EWE: Gake eva trɔ susu emegbe.
ENGLISH: But he later changed his view.

EWE: Nyɔ! talawo bia gbee tso eƒe dɔwo kple dzixɔsewo ŋu.
ENGLISH: Awake! asked him about his work and religious beliefs.

EWE: Nu kawoe wofia wò le ɖevime?
ENGLISH: What teachings were you exposed to as a youth?

EWE: Wofiaa nu le suku si mede la be nɔnɔmetɔtrɔ dzie agbe to va dzɔ, gake ame aɖeke mete ŋu ɖe ale si agbea wɔ hafi dze egɔme me o.
ENGLISH: My school taught the theory of evolution, but no one explained how life itself began.

EWE: Esi dzinyelawo va zu Tao subɔsubɔha me tɔwo la, meva nɔ to ɖom woƒe subɔsubɔhakplɔlawo ƒe nufiafiawo eye mebiaa nya geɖe wo.
ENGLISH: When my parents became Taoists, I used to listen to their religious instructors and ask them a lot of questions.

EWE: Gake nye biabia ʋɛ aɖewo ŋu koe wote ŋu ɖo nam nyuie.
ENGLISH: But I received few answers that satisfied me.

EWE: Aleke wòdzɔe be nèva zu akɔntanyala?
ENGLISH: Why did you become a mathematician?

EWE: Esime menɔ gɔmedzesuku la, akɔntasɔsrɔ̃ doa dzidzɔ nam.
ENGLISH: When I was in elementary school, I became fascinated with mathematics.

EWE: Esi meyi yunivɛsiti la, meyi akɔntasɔsrɔ̃ kple ale si woawɔ numekuku tso nuwo ŋu si doa dzidzɔ nam la dzi.
ENGLISH: This fascination continued when I went to university, where I especially enjoyed courses in mathematics and probability.

EWE: Le gonyeme la, akɔnta si wobu wòkpɔ kuxi aɖe gbɔ la doa dzidzɔ nam.
ENGLISH: To me, a concise mathematical proof can be both beautiful and elegant.

EWE: Aleke wòdzɔe be nèva tsɔ ɖe le Biblia me nyawo me?
ENGLISH: How did you become interested in the Bible?

EWE: Le ƒe 1978 me la, Yehowa Ðasefowo va te Biblia sɔsrɔ̃ kple srɔ̃nye Jinghuei, eye ɣeaɖewoɣi la mekpɔa gome le nusɔsrɔ̃a me.
ENGLISH: In 1978 my wife, Jinghuei, began studying the Bible with Jehovah’s Witnesses, and occasionally I shared in the discussions.

EWE: Míenɔ Amerika ɣemaɣi.
ENGLISH: By then, we were living in the United States.

EWE: Srɔ̃nye Jinghuei wu yunivɛsiti nu eye wòzu dzɔdzɔmeŋusẽwo ŋuti nunyalagã eye nye hã menɔ akɔntabubu srɔ̃m le yunivɛsiti aɖe le Indiana, Amerika.
ENGLISH: Jinghuei had just received her doctorate in physics, and I was studying statistics at Purdue University in Indiana.

EWE: Aleke nèbua Bibliae?
ENGLISH: What did you think of the Bible?

EWE: Nya si Biblia gblɔ tso ale si wotrɔ asi le anyigbaa ŋu be agbe nanya nɔ le edzi la wɔ dɔ ɖe dzinye.
ENGLISH: I was impressed by its account of how the earth was prepared for human life.

EWE: Togbɔ be ŋkeke ade siwo Mose Ƒe Agbalẽ Gbãtɔ gblɔ be wotsɔ wɔ nuwoe dze nu bɔbɔe hã la, susu le eme eye mele abe ale si blemaxotutuwo gblɔe ene o.
ENGLISH: The six creative periods described in Genesis, albeit in simple language, seemed to fit the facts​ unlike ancient mythologies.

EWE: Togbɔ be ele alea hã la, hena ƒe geɖe la, nyemexɔe se be Wɔla aɖee wɔ nuwo o.
ENGLISH: Still, for many years I did not commit to belief in a Creator.

EWE: Nu ka tae wòsesẽ be nàxɔe ase be Wɔla aɖee wɔ nuwo?
ENGLISH: Why was that an issue for you?

EWE: Ne mexɔe se be Wɔla aɖee wɔ nuwo katã la, efia be megbe nu le nu si wofiam tso ɖevime gbɔ
ENGLISH: Believing in a Creator meant rejecting my childhood religion

EWE: Ema bia be mawɔ nyametsotso sesẽ aɖe.
ENGLISH: My feelings were involved.

EWE: Ne mexɔe se be Wɔla aɖee wɔ nuwo katã la, efia be megbe nu le nu si wofiam tso ɖevime gbɔ, elabena Tao subɔsubɔha si me menɔ fiaa nu be Mawu ɖeka si nye Wɔla si wɔ nuwo katã aɖeke meli o.
ENGLISH: Believing in a Creator meant rejecting my childhood religion, because traditional Taoism does not teach that there is a personal God, or Creator.

EWE: Gake èva trɔ susu emegbe.
ENGLISH: Later, though, your viewpoint changed.

EWE: Nu kae gbɔe wòtso?
ENGLISH: Why was that?

EWE: Zi ale si meyi edzi le ŋugble dem tso ale si agbe dze egɔmee ŋu la, zi nenemae meva ka ɖe edzi be nu gbagbe gbãtɔ anya wɔ nuku ŋutɔ.
ENGLISH: The more I thought about the origin of life, the more I became convinced that the first living thing must have been very complex.

EWE: Le kpɔɖeŋu me, enye nu sesẽ be nu gbagbe nadzi etɔgbi, eye hafi esia nadzɔ la ele be wòanɔ te ɖe nyatakaka siwo le eme siwo ŋu dɔ wòawɔ la dzi, eye ele be ɖoɖo aɖe hã nanɔ anyi si dzi wòazɔ ɖo adzi etɔgbia pɛpɛpɛ.
ENGLISH: For example, it had to be able to reproduce, which requires genetic information and a mechanism for accurately replicating that information.

EWE: Azɔ hã, nu gbagbevi suetɔ kekeake gɔ̃ hã hiã nu siwo awɔ dɔ le eme abe mɔ̃ ene hafi wòate ŋu awɔ lãmenugbagbevi yeye ƒe akpa vovovoawo, eye ele be ŋutete nanɔ eŋu be wòate ŋu afia mɔ dɔ siwo wòawɔ.
ENGLISH: Also, even the simplest living cell needs molecular machines for building all the parts of a new cell, as well as the means to harness and direct energy.

EWE: Aleke lãmenugbagbevi ƒe dɔwɔwɔ si wɔ nuku alea la awɔ adzɔ le eɖokui si ne menye ame aɖekee wɔe o?
ENGLISH: How could such complex mechanisms assemble randomly from nonliving matter?

EWE: Abe akɔntanyala ene la, mekpɔe be Wɔla aɖee wɔ nuwo.
ENGLISH: As a mathematician, I could not accept that assumption.

EWE: Elabena nu wɔnuku sia ƒe dɔwɔwɔ mate ŋu adzɔ le eɖokui si o.
ENGLISH: It asks far too much of random processes.

EWE: Nu kae ʋã wò be nèva dzro Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe nufiafiawo me nyuie?
ENGLISH: What was it that moved you to examine more closely the teachings of Jehovah’s Witnesses?

EWE: Ɣeaɖewoɣi mesrɔ̃a nu kple Yehowa Ðasefoawo gadzudzɔna.
ENGLISH: I had studied with the Witnesses on and off.

EWE: Ke le ƒe 1995 me la, mezɔ mɔ yi Taiwan, eye le afi ma la, medze dɔ vevie.
ENGLISH: Then, in 1995, while visiting Taiwan, I fell sick and needed help.

EWE: Srɔ̃nye si le Amerika la ƒo ka na Yehowa Ðasefo siwo le Taiwan be woakpe ɖe ŋunye.
ENGLISH: From the United States, my wife contacted Jehovah’s Witnesses in Taiwan.

EWE: Hafi woava ke ɖe ŋunye la menɔ kɔ aɖe dzi gake esi dɔnɔwo yɔ abatiawo katã dzi ta la, womekpɔ teƒe nam o; nu te ŋunye ŋutɔ.
ENGLISH: They found me exhausted outside a hospital where there were no available beds.

EWE: Ðasefoawo dometɔ ɖeka kplɔm yi amedzrodzeƒe be maɖi ɖe eme.
ENGLISH: One of the Witnesses took me to a hotel to rest.

EWE: Sẽ kple sẽ ko eva kpɔm ɖa, emegbe ekplɔm yi kɔ bubu aɖe dzi be woakpɔ gbɔnye.
ENGLISH: He kept checking on me and then took me to a clinic for treatment.

EWE: Ale si wokpe ɖe ŋunye lɔlɔ̃tɔe la wɔ dɔ ɖe dzinye ŋutɔ, esia na mede ŋugble tso ale si Yehowa Ðasefowo nyo dɔme na nye ƒomea zi geɖe le mɔ vovovowo nu va yi la ŋu.
ENGLISH: That genuine concern deeply touched me, and I reflected on how often Jehovah’s Witnesses had shown kindness to my family on other occasions.

EWE: Ðasefoawo ƒe xɔse na woto vovo.
ENGLISH: The Witnesses’ faith made them different.

EWE: Eya ta mena wogadze Biblia sɔsrɔ̃ gɔme kplim.
ENGLISH: So I resumed my study of the Bible with them.

EWE: Le ƒe si kplɔe ɖo me la, wonyrɔm ɖe tsi me.
ENGLISH: The following year I was baptized.

EWE: Ðe nu siwo ŋu nèkena ɖo le sukunusɔsrɔ̃a me la tsi tsitre ɖe wò xɔse yeyea ŋua?
ENGLISH: Does your faith conflict with your secular studies?

EWE: Kura o!
ENGLISH: Not at all!

EWE: Le ƒe ʋɛ siwo va yi me la, mewɔ akɔntabubu aɖewo tsɔ kpe ɖe dzɔdzɔmeŋutinunyala siwo srɔ̃a nu tso ale si DNA wɔa dɔe ŋu la ŋu.
ENGLISH: In recent years I have provided mathematical support for scientists who study gene function.

EWE: Ale si DNA wɔa nyatakaka siwo le eme la ŋu dɔe kpe ɖe mía ŋu míegava se nu geɖe gɔme tso agbe ŋu gɔmesese sia na Wɔlaa ƒe nunya wɔa nuku nam.
ENGLISH: The study of genetics provides insight into the mechanisms of life​ an insight that fills me with awe for the Creator’s wisdom.

EWE: Àte ŋu aƒo nu tso nunya ma ƒe kpɔɖeŋu aɖe ŋu na mía?
ENGLISH: Give an example of that wisdom.

EWE: Na míade ŋugble tso ale si nu gbagbewo dzinae ŋu kpɔ.
ENGLISH: Consider reproduction.

EWE: Menye atsu kple nɔ ƒe gododo dzie nugbagbevi aɖewo abe amoeba ene tona hafi dzina o.
ENGLISH: Some organisms, such as amoebas, don’t have male and female counterparts.

EWE: Ne nugbagbevi sia di be yeadzi bubu la, ɖeko wòmana, eye wòwɔa nyatakaka siwo le eƒe DNA me la ƒe kɔpi ɖe esi dzim wòle la me.
ENGLISH: These single-cell microbes simply make a copy of their genetic information and divide​ a process called asexual reproduction.

EWE: Gake le lãwo kple ati geɖe gome la, atsu kple nɔ ye doa go hafi wodzia bubu, eye esia wɔnɛ be nu si wodzina la nyia nɔnɔme aɖewo dome tsoa edzila eveawo gbɔ.
ENGLISH: Most animals and plants, however, reproduce sexually, combining genetic information from male and female parents.

EWE: Nu ka tae nu gbagbe siwo nye atsu kple nɔ ƒe gododo hafi adzi la wɔ nuku?
ENGLISH: Why is sexual reproduction remarkable?

EWE: Nɔnɔmetɔtrɔ dzixɔselawo fiaa nu be nu gbagbe ƒe mama dzie nugbagbeviwo tona dzina hena ƒe gbogbo aɖe si ame aɖeke menya o, emegbe nu gbagbe siwo nye atsu kple nɔ ƒe gododo adzi bubu va dzɔ tso esia me, ɖe susu le numeɖeɖe sia mea?
ENGLISH: Why would a system of reproduction in which one organism simply divides into two​ and has done this very well for who knows how long ​develop into a system in which two things combine to form one?

EWE: Elabena le atsu kple nɔ ƒe gododo hafi adzi ya gome la, ebia be atsu kple nɔ siwo le go dom la naɖo nyatakaka siwo le woƒe DNA me la ɖa sɔsɔe woava do go wo nɔewo azu nu ɖeka, eye ale si esia dzɔnae me ɖeɖe zua taɖui na dzɔdzɔmeŋutinunyala siwo xɔ nɔnɔmetɔtrɔ dzi se.
ENGLISH: The mechanisms required to take half the genetic information from the male and half from the female and combine them are immensely complex, presenting a huge problem to evolutionary biologists.

EWE: Le nye susu nu la, ɖikeke aɖeke mele eme o be ale si nu gbagbe siwo nye atsu kple nɔ doa go hafi dzina la nye Mawu ƒe nunya si wɔ nuku.
ENGLISH: In my view, gender-based reproduction points unequivocally to the mind of God.

EWE: Saŋkuƒola Aɖe Ƒe Xɔse
ENGLISH: A Classical Pianist Explains His Faith

EWE: Eldar Nebolsin si tso Uzbekistan nye saŋkuƒola si ƒe ŋkɔ de du ŋutɔ.
ENGLISH: Eldar Nebolsin of Uzbekistan is an internationally acclaimed pianist.

EWE: Eƒo saŋku le London, Moscow, St. Petersburg, New York, Paris, Rome, Sydney, Tokyo kple Vienna, eye eya ɖeka ƒoa saŋku le haƒohawo ŋgɔ.
ENGLISH: He has played as a soloist with orchestras in London, Moscow, St. Petersburg, New York, Paris, Rome, Sydney, Tokyo, and Vienna.

EWE: Soviet Union ye Eldar tsi le eye wònye mawudzimaxɔsela.
ENGLISH: Eldar grew up in the Soviet Union as an atheist.

EWE: Gake eva ƒo nya ta emegbe be Wɔla lɔ̃ame aɖee wɔ amegbetɔwo.
ENGLISH: But later he concluded that humans are the work of a loving Creator.

EWE: Nyɔ! magazinea talawo bia gbee tso haƒoƒo kple eƒe xɔse ŋu.
ENGLISH: Awake! asked him about his music and his faith.

EWE: Aleke nèwɔ va zu haƒola?
ENGLISH: How did you become a musician?

EWE: Dzinyelawo nye saŋkuƒolawo.
ENGLISH: My parents are both pianists.

EWE: Wote saŋkuƒoƒo fiafiam esime mexɔ ƒe atɔ̃ ko.
ENGLISH: They began teaching me when I was five years old.

EWE: Emegbe mede hasrɔ̃suku deŋgɔ si le Tashkent.
ENGLISH: Later, I studied at the advanced school of music in Tashkent.

EWE: Ƒo nu tso kuxi siwo nèdoa goe ne èle saŋku ƒom kple haƒoha ŋu na mí.
ENGLISH: Tell us about the challenges of playing with an orchestra.

EWE: Haƒoha aɖeke mesɔ kple bubu o.
ENGLISH: No two orchestras are alike.

EWE: Haƒoha ɖe sia ɖe le ko abe haƒonu gã si "ƒom " haƒoha ƒe ŋgɔnɔla le ene.
ENGLISH: They are like giant musical instruments that are "played " by their conductors.

EWE: Ðewohĩ nu si koŋ sesẽna na saŋkuƒola ɖekɛ wue nye ale si wòaƒo saŋkua wòawɔ ɖeka kple haƒoha ƒe ŋgɔnɔla ƒe atidada.
ENGLISH: Perhaps the main challenge for the soloist is to achieve balanced interaction with the conductor.

EWE: Abe ale si xɔlɔ̃wo ɖoa dze ene la, ele be saŋkuƒola kple haƒoha ƒe ŋgɔnɔla nawɔ nu aduadu.
ENGLISH: It’s like a conversation between friends rather than one always taking the lead, each should yield to the other.

EWE: Zi geɖe la, numetoto ɖeka alo eve koe míetea ŋu wɔna tsɔ srɔ̃na ale si míawɔ nu woasɔ ɖe mía nɔewo tɔ dzi.
ENGLISH: Usually, you have only one or two rehearsals in which to develop this rapport.

EWE: Ɣeyiɣi didi kae nètsɔ toa saŋkuƒoƒoa me?
ENGLISH: How much time do you spend practicing?

EWE: Mezãa gaƒoƒo etɔ̃ ya teti, eye menye haa ƒe akpa siwo sesẽ la me koe mezãa ɣeyiɣi sia tsɔ tonae o.
ENGLISH: At least three hours a day and that isn’t just to practice difficult passages.

EWE: Mesrɔ̃a ɖoɖo si nu woɖo haa ɖo hã evɔ nyemeƒoa haa ŋutɔ le ɣeyiɣi sia me o.
ENGLISH: I also study the structure of the piece I’m preparing but without actually playing it.

EWE: Nu bubu siwo mewɔna ye nye be meɖoa to hakpala ma ƒe ha bubuwo eye esia wɔnɛ be mesea ha si srɔ̃m mele la gɔme ɖe edzi wu.
ENGLISH: Another thing I do is listen to the composer’s other works, which gives me more insight into the present piece.

EWE: Nu kae ɖea dzesi le saŋkuƒola bibi ŋu?
ENGLISH: What would you say distinguishes a fine pianist?

EWE: Eyae nye ale si wòtea ŋu nana saŋku "dzia ha. "
ENGLISH: His ability to make a piano "sing. "

EWE: Maɖe eme miase.
ENGLISH: Let me explain.

EWE: Saŋku nye haƒonu si wotsɔa asi ƒona.
ENGLISH: The piano is a kind of percussion instrument.

EWE: Ne wote asi ɖe saŋku ƒe kpevi dzi la, ɖeko eƒe ɖiɖi yia to; mele abe haƒonu siwo me woɖoa ƒuƒu ɖo alo amegbetɔ ƒe gbe si tea ŋu yia dzi alo nɔa ɖeka ene o.
ENGLISH: After a note is struck, the sound can only decrease in volume unlike that of wind instruments or the human voice, which can hold a note or even increase its volume.

EWE: Kuxi si dzi wòhiãna be saŋkuƒola naɖue nye ale si wòakpɔ egbɔ be haa ƒe ɖiɖi aɖe nagayi to o.
ENGLISH: The challenge for pianists is to overcome the tendency of a note to fade.

EWE: Ewɔa esia to eƒe asibidewo kple alɔtsinuwo ʋaʋã to saŋkukpeviwo dzi aɖaŋutɔe me tsɔ kpe ɖe afɔɖoɖo gbeɖiɖitrɔnu ɖusimetɔ dzi le ɣeyiɣi si sɔ me eye esia wɔnɛ be wòléa gbea ƒe ɖiɖi ɖe te eteƒe didina, eye wòtea ŋu trɔa gbeɖiɖi vovovowo.
ENGLISH: They do this by subtle movement of their fingers and wrists, along with the complex interaction of the right pedal, which extends the duration of a note and varies its timbre.

EWE: Ne saŋkuƒola te ŋu ɖu tu na aɖaŋu siawo siwo sɔsrɔ̃ mele bɔbɔe o nyuie vɔ la, ate ŋu aƒo saŋku wòaɖi abe dze, kpẽ alo haƒoha tɔ ene.
ENGLISH: When pianists master these difficult techniques, they can make the piano sound like a flute, a horn, or even an orchestra.

EWE: Ate ŋu ana hã be saŋku naɖi abe amegbetɔ ƒe gbe, si nye gbeɖiɖi nyuitɔ kekeake ene.
ENGLISH: They can also make it resemble the finest musical instrument of all the human voice.

EWE: Edze kɔtɛe be èlɔ̃a haƒoƒo ŋutɔ.
ENGLISH: It’s obvious that you have a deep love for music.

EWE: Le gonyeme la, mebunɛ be haƒoƒo nye gbegbɔgblɔ si tea ŋu ɖea seselelãme siwo mele bɔbɔe be woagblɔ kple nu o la gblɔna tẽe wu.
ENGLISH: For me, music is the language that most directly expresses and evokes feelings that are difficult, if not impossible, to communicate in words.

EWE: Nu kae na nèva tsɔ ɖe le mawusubɔsubɔ me?
ENGLISH: What aroused your interest in spiritual matters?

EWE: Míaƒe aƒe me yɔ fũu kple agbalẽ siwo fofonye tsɔ tso Moscow gbɔe.
ENGLISH: Our house was always full of books, which my father brought from Moscow.

EWE: Agbalẽ si do dzidzɔ nam wue nye esi me Biblia me ŋutinya siwo ku ɖe amegbetɔ ƒe ŋutinya ƒe gɔmedzedze kple Israel-viwo ƒe ŋutinya ŋu la le.
ENGLISH: A book that especially interested me contained Bible stories about the dawn of history and the experiences of the Israelites.

EWE: Agbalẽ si hã ŋu meke ɖoe nye Ate Ŋu Anɔ Agbe Tegbee le Paradiso me le Anyigba Dzi, si Yehowa Ðasefowo ta.
ENGLISH: Another book I came across was You Can Live Forever in Paradise on Earth, published by Jehovah’s Witnesses.

EWE: Ale si woɖe Biblia ƒe nufiafiawo me wo me kɔ nyuie le eme la wɔ dɔ ɖe dzinye ŋutɔ.
ENGLISH: Its clear presentation of Bible teachings fascinated me.

EWE: Esi meʋu yi Spain le ƒe 1991 me be maɖasrɔ̃ haƒoƒo la, metsɔ agbalẽ sia ɖe asi eye mexlẽe zi geɖe.
ENGLISH: When I moved to Spain in 1991 to study music, I took that book with me and read it several times.

EWE: Meva de dzesii be xɔse si ŋu agbalẽ sia ƒo nu tsoe la nye esi ŋu kpeɖodzi le si nɔ te ɖe nuŋububu nyui dzi, ke menye seselelãme dzro aɖe ko o.
ENGLISH: I discovered a faith based not merely on emotion but also on sound reasoning and convincing evidence.

EWE: Nufiafia si wɔ dɔ ɖe dzinye wue nye ŋugbe si Biblia do be amegbetɔwo ate ŋu anɔ agbe tegbee le anyigba dzi.
ENGLISH: A teaching that really intrigued me was the Bible’s promise that humans can live forever on earth.

EWE: Susu le nya sia me ŋutɔ!
ENGLISH: That made so much sense!

EWE: Gake va se ɖe ɣemaɣi la, nyemekpɔ do go Yehowa Ðasefo aɖeke o.
ENGLISH: I might add that I still had not met Jehovah’s Witnesses.

EWE: Ke hã metso nya me be ne medo go wo dometɔ aɖe la, mabia tso esi be wòasrɔ̃ Biblia kplim.
ENGLISH: But I resolved that when I did meet them, I would ask for Bible lessons.

EWE: Aleke nèwɔ va ke ɖe Ðasefowo ŋu?
ENGLISH: How did you meet the Witnesses?

EWE: Kwasiɖa ʋɛ aɖewo le nye nyametsotso ma megbe la, medo go ɖetugbui eve aɖewo siwo lé Biblia ɖe asi.
ENGLISH: A few days after I made that mental resolution, I saw two ladies, each with a Bible in hand.

EWE: Megblɔ le susu me be: ‘Ame siawo ɖi ame siwo ŋu mexlẽ nu tsoe le nye agbalẽa me.
ENGLISH: ‘They look like the people I’ve read about in my book,’ I thought.

EWE: Wonɔ gbeƒã ɖem abe ale si ko Kristotɔ siwo nɔ anyi le Biblia-ŋlɔɣiwo la wɔe ene.’
ENGLISH: ‘They are preaching just as Christians did in Bible times.’

EWE: Eteƒe medidi o, Ðasefo aɖe te Biblia sɔsrɔ̃ kplim.
ENGLISH: Soon, I was studying the Bible with a Witness.

EWE: Egbea la, nu si doa dzidzɔ nam wue nye be makpe ɖe amewo ŋu woasrɔ̃ ŋu tso mía Wɔla la ŋu.
ENGLISH: Today, my greatest joy is helping others to learn about our Creator.

EWE: Nu kae na nèva xɔe se be Wɔla aɖe li, evɔ mawudzimaxɔselae nenye tsã?
ENGLISH: What convinced you, a former atheist, to believe in a Creator?

EWE: Haƒoƒo hã kpe ɖe ŋunye.
ENGLISH: Music itself did.

EWE: Amegbetɔwo katã kloe kpɔa dzidzɔ ɖe haƒoƒo ŋu, si nye nu si lãwo ya mate ŋu awɔ o.
ENGLISH: Almost everybody appreciates music, and in a way that no animal can.

EWE: Wotea ŋu ɖea dzidzɔ, kakaɖedzi, tufafa kple seselelãme ƒomevi ɖe sia ɖe kloe fiana le haƒoƒo me.
ENGLISH: Music can express joy, confidence, tenderness, and almost every other emotion.

EWE: Le dzɔdzɔme nu la, míeʋãna ɖe haƒoƒo ƒe ɖiɖi dzi.
ENGLISH: We naturally move to the rhythms in music.

EWE: Gake ɖe haƒoƒo hiã kokoko hafi míate ŋu anɔ agbea?
ENGLISH: But is music necessary for our survival?

EWE: Ðe haƒoƒo wɔa akpa aɖe le nufiafia si nye be "ŋusẽtɔ lae tsia agbe " abe ale si ame siwo fia nu be ɖe nuwo dzɔ le wo ɖokui si la fianɛ ene la mea?
ENGLISH: Does it play a role in the "survival of the fittest, " as evolutionists teach?

EWE: Gbeɖe!
ENGLISH: I think not.

EWE: Le nye susu nu la, nunya mele eme be míaƒo nya ta be amegbetɔ ƒe ahɔhɔ̃, si ŋu ŋutete le be wòate ŋu akpa ha alo ase vivi na haƒoƒowo abe Mozart kple Beethoven ƒe haƒoƒo ene la, dzɔ le eɖokui si o.
ENGLISH: In my view, it’s unreasonable to conclude that the human brain, with its ability to create and appreciate music like that of Mozart and Beethoven, is the product of evolution.

EWE: Numeɖeɖe si me susu le wue nye be Wɔla nyanu lɔ̃ame aɖee wɔ míaƒe ahɔhɔ̃ la.
ENGLISH: A far more reasonable explanation is that our brain is the product of a wise and loving Creator.

EWE: Nu kae na nèva xɔe se be Biblia tso Mawu gbɔ?
ENGLISH: What led you to believe that the Bible is from God?

EWE: Agbalẽ suesuesue 66 ye le Biblia me eye ame 40 ye ŋlɔe eye eŋɔŋlɔ xɔ ƒe 1,600 kple edzivɔwo.
ENGLISH: The Bible is a collection of 66 smaller books written over some 1,600 years by about 40 men.

EWE: Mebia ɖokuinye be: ‘Ame kae ate ŋu ana woaŋlɔ agbalẽ deŋgɔ sia si me nyawo wɔ ɖeka alea?’
ENGLISH: I asked myself, ‘Who could have orchestrated the writing of this unified masterpiece?’

EWE: Ŋuɖoɖo si me susu le koe nye be Mawue na woŋlɔe.
ENGLISH: The only reasonable answer is God.

EWE: Le nye susu nu la, Biblia le ko abe hadzidzi si me nyawo le ɖoɖo nyui aɖe si de ŋgɔ ŋutɔ nu ene, eye gbedeasi siwo le eme la wɔa dɔ ɖe ameƒomevi ɖe sia ɖe dzi.
ENGLISH: In my mind, the Bible is like a symphony with an elegant structure, a masterful arrangement, and a moving message for all mankind.

EWE: "Mexɔe Se Be Mawue Wɔ Nu Gbagbewo "
ENGLISH: "I Am Convinced That Life Was Designed by God "

EWE: Brett Schenck nye nutomeŋutinunyala si xɔ dzudzɔ le United States.
ENGLISH: Brett Schenck is a retired environmental consultant in the United States.

EWE: Esrɔ̃ nu tso ale si atiwo, lãwo kple nutoa me hiãa wo nɔewoe la ŋu.
ENGLISH: He studied the interdependency of plants, animals, and the environment.

EWE: Nu ka tae wòxɔe se be Wɔla aɖe li?
ENGLISH: Why does he believe in a Creator?

EWE: Nyɔ! magazinea talawo bia gbee tso dzɔdzɔmeŋutinunya kple eƒe dzixɔse ŋu.
ENGLISH: Awake! asked him about his science and his faith.

EWE: Ƒo nu tso ɖokuiwò ŋu na mí.
ENGLISH: What is your background?

EWE: Fofonye nye mɔ̃ɖaŋudɔwɔla.
ENGLISH: My father was a mechanical engineer.

EWE: Eɖoa dze nam tso akɔntabubu kple dzɔdzɔmeŋutinunya ŋu vividoɖenuŋutɔe.
ENGLISH: He often talked enthusiastically to me about math and science.

EWE: Esi menɔ ɖevime la, mekpɔa dzidzɔ ɖe nu miemiewo, lãwo, tɔsisiwo kple ta siwo le míaƒe nutoa me le New Paris, Ohio, le United States la ŋu.
ENGLISH: As a boy, I was fascinated by the plants and animals in the creeks and pools near my home in New Paris, Ohio, U.S.A. So when I went to Purdue University, I chose to study ecology.

EWE: Ðe nèlɔ̃a mawusubɔsubɔa?
ENGLISH: Did religion interest you?
Yes, it did.

EWE: Papa dea dzi ƒo nam be masrɔ̃ nu tso míaƒe Luther subɔsubɔha ŋu.
ENGLISH: Dad encouraged me to study our Lutheran religion.

EWE: Mesrɔ̃ Koine (Helagbe si wodona wu), si nye gbegbɔgblɔ siwo me woɖe Biblia gɔme ɖo zi gbãtɔ la dometɔ ɖeka.
ENGLISH: I studied Koine (common) Greek, one of the languages in which the Bible was first written.

EWE: Esia wɔe be meva dea asixɔxɔ gã aɖe Biblia ŋu.
ENGLISH: I developed deep respect for the Bible.

EWE: Aleke nèbua nufiafia si nye be ɖeko nuwo dzɔ le wo ɖokuiwo si lae?
ENGLISH: How did you view the theory of evolution?

EWE: Míaƒe sɔlemeha la da asi ɖe edzi.
ENGLISH: My church accepted it.

EWE: Nye dɔwɔhatiwo hã xɔe se.
ENGLISH: My colleagues believed it.

EWE: Eya ta nyemeke ɖii kpɔ o.
ENGLISH: So I never questioned it.

EWE: Gake megaxɔ Mawu hã dzi se.
ENGLISH: But I also believed in God.

EWE: Ewɔna nam be dzixɔse eve siawo wɔ ɖeka.
ENGLISH: I had a foggy notion that the two beliefs were compatible.

EWE: Togbɔ be medea asixɔxɔ Biblia ŋu hã la, nyemebunɛ be Mawu gbɔe wòtso o.
ENGLISH: Although I respected the Bible, I didn’t think it came from God.

EWE: Nu kae na ale si nèbua Bibliae la va trɔ?
ENGLISH: What made you change your view of the Bible?

EWE: Yehowa Ðasefo eve siwo ŋkɔwoe nye Steve kple Sandy va srã nye kple srɔ̃nye Debbie kpɔ.
ENGLISH: Two of Jehovah’s Witnesses, Steve and Sandy, visited my wife, Debbie, and me.

EWE: Wona míede dzesii be togbɔ be Biblia menye dzɔdzɔmeŋutinunyagbalẽ o hã la, emenyawo wɔ ɖeka kple dzɔdzɔmeŋutinunya.
ENGLISH: They showed us that the Bible, though not a science textbook, is scientifically accurate.

EWE: Le kpɔɖeŋu me, egblɔ le Mawu ŋu be: "Eya, ame si le xexea me godoo tame. "
ENGLISH: For example, it says of God: "There is One who is dwelling above the circle of the earth. "

EWE: (Yesaya 40:22) Egblɔ hã be: "Meku anyigba ɖe naneke ŋu o. "
ENGLISH: (Isaiah 40:22) It also says: "He is . . . hanging the earth upon nothing. "

EWE: (Hiob 26:7) Ɣemaɣi la, mezãa foto siwo wotsɔ yamenutomeɖemɔ̃ ɖe tsɔ srɔ̃a nu tso kadodo si nɔa nu gbagbewo kple nutoa me dome ŋu, eya ta mawunyakpukpui siawo wɔ dɔ ɖe dzinye ŋutɔ.
ENGLISH: (Job 26:7) At that time, I was using satellite photographs to study ecology, so these scriptures impressed me.

EWE: Woŋlɔ nya siawo ɖi gbe aɖe gbe ʋĩ ke hafi amewo va ɖe fotowo hekpɔe be anyigba la le nogoo eye womekui ɖe naneke ŋu o.
ENGLISH: They were written long before anyone photographed the circle of the earth hanging on nothing.

EWE: Esi Steve kple Sandy nɔ Biblia srɔ̃m kpli mí la, míesrɔ̃ nu tso Biblia me nyagblɔɖi siwo va eme kple Biblia ƒe aɖaŋuɖoɖo siwo ɖea vi ŋu, eye woƒe numeɖeɖewo me kɔ nam.
ENGLISH: As my wife and I studied the Bible with Steve and Sandy, I learned of prophecies that had come true, advice that works, and explanations that satisfied me.

EWE: Vivivi la, meva ka ɖe edzi be Mawu ƒe Nyae Biblia la nye.
ENGLISH: Gradually, I became convinced that the Bible is the Word of God.

EWE: Ɣekaɣie nèva trɔ susu ku ɖe ale si agbe wɔ va dzɔ ŋu?
ENGLISH: When did you change your mind about the origin of life?

EWE: Mlɔeba la, Steve tsɔ nya si Biblia gblɔ eme kɔ ƒãa la fiam, si nye be: "Yehowa Mawu tsɔ anyi mè ame. " (1 Mose 2:7) Woŋlɔ ale si ame gbãtɔ wɔ va dzɔ la ŋu nyawo ɖi.
ENGLISH: Eventually, Steve showed me the Bible’s clear statement: "Jehovah God proceeded to form the man out of dust from the ground. " (Genesis 2:7) The first man has a documented life history.

EWE: Esia fɔ nyabiase sia ɖe te be: Ðe Biblia wɔ ɖeka kple dzɔdzɔmeŋutinunya?
ENGLISH: This raised the question: Is the Bible in harmony with scientific facts?

EWE: Steve de dzi ƒo nam be maku nya ma me, eye mewɔe nenema hã.
ENGLISH: Steve encouraged me to research the matter, so I did.

EWE: Nu kae nèsrɔ̃ tso nufiafia si nye be ɖeko nuwo dzɔ le wo ɖokui si la ŋu?
ENGLISH: What did you learn about evolution?

EWE: Mesrɔ̃ nu geɖe.
ENGLISH: Many things.

EWE: Wo dometɔ ɖekae nye ale si nu sia fialawo dzea agbagba be yewoaɖe ale si nu gbagbewo wɔ va dzɔ la me.
ENGLISH: To mention just one, the evolution theory attempts to explain the origin of species.

EWE: Ŋutinu siwo wɔa dɔ nyuie hele ɖoɖo nu, abe dzi, dzitodzito kple ŋku ene, le nu gbagbewo si.
ENGLISH: Living things are made up of efficient organs, such as the heart, lungs, and eyes.

EWE: Eye ne wotsɔ mɔ̃ kpɔ nu gbagbewo ƒe lãmenugbagbeviwo me la, àkpɔ ‘mɔ̃’ wɔnukuwo le wo me.
ENGLISH: Also, at the microscopic level, we see marvelously designed ‘machines’ within cells.

EWE: Aleke wòdzɔe be mɔ̃ mawo le lãmenugbagbeviwo me?
ENGLISH: Where do the designs for those come from?

EWE: Ame siwo fiaa nu be ɖeko nuwo dzɔ le wo ɖokuiwo si gblɔ be ɖeko mɔ̃ mawo ŋutɔwo dzɔ le wo ɖokui si, elabena nu gbagbe siwo me wole lae tsia agbe.
ENGLISH: Evolutionists claim that the best mechanisms are automatically selected because the living things that have them survive better.

EWE: Gake numeɖeɖe ma meɖo nyabiase si nye, Aleke wòdzɔe be mɔ̃ siawo le lãmenugbagbeviwo me? la ŋu o.
ENGLISH: But that idea does not answer the question: Where do the mechanisms come from?

EWE: Meva nya be dzɔdzɔmeŋutinunyala geɖe mexɔe se be woate ŋu anɔ te ɖe nufiafia sia dzi aɖo nya ma ŋu o.
ENGLISH: I learned that many scientists do not believe that the evolution theory answers that question.

EWE: Lãwo ŋuti nunyala aɖe ʋu eme nam be yemexɔ nufiafia si nye be ɖeko nuwo dzɔ le wo ɖokuiwo si la dzi se o.
ENGLISH: A professor of zoology confided to me that he did not believe any of the theories of evolution.

EWE: Ke hã esi wònɔ vɔvɔ̃m be dɔ ava gblẽ na ye ta la, mekɔ nu le edzi o.
ENGLISH: However, he did not air his views for fear of losing his job.

EWE: Ðe nusɔsrɔ̃ tso nu gbagbewo kple nutoa me ŋu do ŋusẽ wò xɔsea?
ENGLISH: Does your knowledge of ecology strengthen your faith?
Yes, it does.

EWE: Mesrɔ̃a nu tso ale si nu gbagbewo hiãa wo nɔewo hafi woate ŋu anɔ agbe la ŋu.
ENGLISH: My work involved studying how living things depend on each other.

EWE: Nu gbagbe siwo katã le anyigba dzi hiãa wo nɔewo hafi woate ŋu anɔ agbe.
ENGLISH: On earth, all living things depend on something else.

EWE: Bu seƒoƒowo kple anyiwo ŋu kpɔ.
ENGLISH: Consider flowers and bees, for example.

EWE: Wowɔ seƒoƒowo ale be woƒe amadedewo, woƒe ʋeʋẽ lililiwo, wo me tsiwo kple woƒe wɔwɔme tea ŋu hea anyiwo, eye anyiwo kpɔa seƒoƒoŋuwɔ gbogbo aɖewo le wo dzi.
ENGLISH: The color, fragrance, nectar, and structure of flowers are designed to attract bees and to sprinkle them with pollen.

EWE: Wowɔ anyiwo be woano seƒoƒometsiwo, eye woalɔ seƒoƒoŋuwɔwo le seƒoƒo aɖe dzi ayi na ati bubu ale be wòate ŋu aƒo se.
ENGLISH: Bees are designed to extract nectar and to take one flower’s pollen to another plant for fertilization.

EWE: Edze kɔtɛe be ɖe wowɔ seƒoƒowo kple anyiwo be woakpɔ wo nɔewo ƒe nuhiahiãwo gbɔ.
ENGLISH: Clearly, the flowers and bees are designed to supply what the other needs.

EWE: ‘Ale si nu gbagbewo kple afi si wole ɖɔa wo ɖokuiwo ɖo la na mexɔe se be Mawue wɔ nu gbagbewo’
ENGLISH: ‘The resilience of the entire system of life on earth convinces me that life was designed by God’

EWE: Le nutoa me la, míekpɔe be nu gbagbewo hiãa wo nɔewo le mɔ geɖewo nu.
ENGLISH: In an ecosystem, we see interdependence on a vast scale.

EWE: Nuto si míewɔnɛ la fia nu gbagbe akpe geɖewo, abe lãwo, nu miemiewo kple hlo ƒomeviwo ene, kple afi si wole.
ENGLISH: An ecosystem is an environment with a community of perhaps thousands of types of animals, plants, bacteria, and fungi.

EWE: Lãwo katã hiãa gbe kple ya si woyɔna be ɔksidzin hafi woate ŋu anɔ agbe, eye nenema ke ati siwo ƒoa se la dometɔ akpa gãtɔ hiã lãwo hafi woate ŋu anɔ agbe.
ENGLISH: All animals depend on plants for food and oxygen, and most flowering plants depend on animals.

EWE: Togbɔ be ale si lãwo kple nu miemiewo hiã wo nɔewo gɔme sese sesẽ ŋutɔ, eye edze abe wo dome ate ŋu agblẽ bɔbɔe ene hã la, woayi edzi anɔ anyi ƒe akpe.
ENGLISH: Although ecosystems are exceedingly complex and the organisms in them are fragile, they may continue surviving for millennia.

EWE: Ne edzɔ be ɖiƒoƒo gblẽ nu le nuto aɖe ŋu gɔ̃ hã la, nu gbagbe gbogbo aɖewo agate ŋu adzi ɖe nuto ma me ne ɖiƒoƒoa nu yi.
ENGLISH: Even after damage by pollution, once the source of pollution is gone, a complex ecosystem soon develops again.

EWE: Ne mebu ale si nu gbagbewo kple afi si wole tea ŋu ɖɔa wo ɖokuiwo ɖoe ŋu la, mexɔe se be Mawue wɔ nu gbagbewo.
ENGLISH: When I think about the resilience of the entire system of life on earth, I am convinced that life was designed by God.

EWE: Nu ka tae nèzu Yehowa Ðasefo?
ENGLISH: Why did you become one of Jehovah’s Witnesses?

EWE: Metsi dzi vevie ɖe ale si ameƒomea le anyigbadzinuwo dome gblẽmee la ŋu.
ENGLISH: I was deeply concerned about the way human society is ruining the environment.

EWE: Menyae be togbɔ be nu gbagbewo kple nuto siwo me wole ate ŋu aɖɔ wo ɖokuiwo ɖo hã la, mefia be wo dome mate ŋu agblẽ ɖikaa o.
ENGLISH: I knew that although ecosystems are resilient, they are not indestructible.

EWE: Yehowa Ðasefowo fiam le Ŋɔŋlɔawo me be Mawu ahe "gbegblẽ ava ame siwo le anyigba la gblẽm la dzi. "
ENGLISH: I learned from Jehovah’s Witnesses that, according to the Scriptures, God will "bring to ruin those ruining the earth. "

EWE: (Nyaɖeɖefia 11:18) Nya mawo nɔ vevie nam ŋutɔ.
ENGLISH: (Revelation 11:18) Those words were important to me.

EWE: Esi meyi Biblia sɔsrɔ̃ dzi la, meva de dzesii be mɔkpɔkpɔ si ŋu nya Biblia gblɔ nye nu ŋutɔŋutɔ.
ENGLISH: As I continued studying the Bible, I gradually realized that the hope that the Bible presents is sure.

EWE: Nuƒoƒo na amewo tso nye dzixɔsewo ŋu dzɔa dzi nam, eye mesrɔ̃ Biblia kple dzɔdzɔmeŋutinunyala aɖewo.
ENGLISH: I enjoy sharing my beliefs with others, and I have studied the Bible with some scientists.

EWE: Esi mexɔ ƒe 55 la, mexɔ dzudzɔ le dɔ me togbɔ be nye dzudzɔxɔɣi meɖo o hã, ale be mate ŋu azã ɣeyiɣi geɖe atsɔ akpe ɖe amewo ŋu woase Ame si wɔ nu gbagbewo kple eƒe tameɖoɖo ku ɖe anyigba dzeani sia ŋu la gɔme.
ENGLISH: At age 55, I took early retirement to spend more time helping people to understand the Creator of life and his purpose for our magnificent earth.

EWE: Ŋutete Si Le Amegbetɔ Ƒe Ŋutilãa Ŋu Be Wòawu Abi
ENGLISH: The Human Body’s Ability to Repair Wounds

EWE: Abiteƒe si wotsɔ plasta tre
ENGLISH: A bandage on a hand

EWE: NU VOVOVO siwo wɔe be amegbetɔ nɔa agbe la dometɔ ɖekae nye ŋutete si le ŋutilãa ŋu be wòawu abi, eye wòana lãmenu siwo gblẽ le teƒe si wɔ abi la nagaɖɔ ɖo.
ENGLISH: AMONG the numerous mechanisms that make human life possible is the body’s ability to heal wounds and regenerate damaged tissue.

EWE: Ne ŋutilãa ƒe akpa aɖe nya xɔ abi ko la, nu siwo ana abia naku la dzea dɔ gɔme enumake.
ENGLISH: The process begins as soon as an injury occurs.

EWE: Bu nya siawo ŋu kpɔ: Lãmenugbagbevi gbogbo aɖewo ƒe dɔwɔwɔ wɔnuku aɖe dzie abi ƒe kuku dzea egɔme tsona abe esiwo gbɔna ene:
ENGLISH: Consider: The healing process is made possible by a cascade of complex cellular functions:

EWE: Ʋumenu gbabɛwo va nɔa abia me, eye wonaa ʋua blana hetrea ʋuka siwo le ʋu ɖuɖum la nu.
ENGLISH: Platelets adhere to tissues around a wound, forming a blood clot and sealing damaged blood vessels.

EWE: Abia ƒe tete vie kpɔa eta tsoa dɔlékuiwo si me eye wòɖea "ɖiwo " ɖa le eme.
ENGLISH: Inflammation protects against infection and removes any "debris " caused by the injury.

EWE: Le ŋkeke ʋɛ aɖewo megbe la, ŋutilã la dzea lãmenu siwo gblẽ le abiteƒea ɖɔliɖɔli gɔme, enana abia miana eye wòɖɔa ʋuka siwo gblẽ la ɖo.
ENGLISH: Within days, the body begins to replace injured tissue, make the wound contract, and repair damaged blood vessels.

EWE: Mlɔeba la, lãmenu siwo gblẽ la ɖɔna ɖo hezua abikukuteƒe eye ŋusẽ ɖoa teƒea ŋu.
ENGLISH: Finally, scar tissue remodels and strengthens the damaged area.

EWE: Numekulawo kpɔe be yewoate ŋu anɔ te ɖe ale si ʋu blanae dzi awɔ aŋenu siwo ne wogbã la woate ŋu aɖɔ ɖo le wo ɖokui si.
ENGLISH: Inspired by blood clotting, researchers are developing plastics that can "heal " damage to themselves.

EWE: Le aŋenu sia si woawɔ me la, pɔmpi suesuesue aɖewo anɔ eme siwo me atike ƒomevi eve aɖewo anɔ siwo ado ne aŋenua ƒe akpa aɖe gbã.
ENGLISH: Such regenerating materials are equipped with tiny parallel tubes containing two chemicals that "bleed " when any damage occurs.

EWE: Ne aŋenua ƒe akpa aɖe gbã la, atike eveawo ado ava bla ɖe teƒea eye wòaɖɔ gbagbãƒea ɖo.
ENGLISH: As the two chemicals mix, they form a gel that spreads across the damaged areas, closing cracks and holes.

EWE: Ne atike eve siwo tsaka le teƒea le ƒuƒum la, alia eye wòana teƒea naɖɔ ɖo abe ale si wònɔ tsã ene.
ENGLISH: As the gel solidifies, it forms a tough substance that restores the material’s original strength.

EWE: Numekula aɖe gblɔ be, "Míekpɔ ale si nu gbagbe aɖewo wɔna ɖɔa woƒe ŋutilã ɖo ne woxɔ abi dzi be míawɔ aŋenu siwo me agbe mele o be woawo hã nate ŋu aɖɔ wo ɖokuiwo ɖo ne wogbã. "
ENGLISH: One researcher admits that this synthetic healing process currently under development is "reminiscent " of what already exists in nature.

EWE: Nu kae nèsusu?
ENGLISH: What do you think?

EWE: Ðe ŋutete si le amegbetɔ ƒe ŋutilãa ŋu be wòawu abi la dzɔ le eɖokui sia?
ENGLISH: Did the body’s ability to repair wounds come about by evolution?

EWE: Alo Wɔla lae wɔea?
ENGLISH: Or was it designed?

EWE: Nyatakaka Si Gbegbe Nɔa Domenyiŋusẽfianu Me
ENGLISH: The Storage Capacity of DNA

EWE: Dzɔdzɔmeŋutinunyalawo le mɔ kpɔm be yewoahe tɔtrɔ gã aɖe ava nyatakakadzadzraɖo ƒe mɔnuwo me.
ENGLISH: COMPUTER users generate enormous amounts of digital data that has to be stored for access as needed.

EWE: Woƒe susue nye be yewoanɔ te ɖe dzɔdzɔme nyatakakadzraɖonu si de ŋgɔ sãsãsã la ƒe ŋutete dzi awɔ yewo tɔa. Dzɔdzɔmenu mae nye domenyiŋusẽfianu (DNA alo ADN).
ENGLISH: Scientists are hoping to revolutionize current methods for digital storage by imitating a far superior data-storage system found in nature DNA.

EWE: Bu nya siawo ŋu kpɔ: Nyatakaka miliɔn akpe geɖewoe nɔa nu gbagbewo ƒe domenyiŋusẽfianuwo me.
ENGLISH: Consider: DNA, found in living cells, holds billions of pieces of biological information.

EWE: Aƒetɔ Nick Goldman si wɔa dɔ le Europatɔwo ƒe dɔwɔƒe aɖe (European Bioinformatics Institute) gblɔ be: "Míate ŋu aɖe wo tso atiglinyi ƒomevi aɖewo siwo nɔ anyi le blema ƒe ƒuwo me . . . ahase nyatakaka siwo le wo me la gɔme.
ENGLISH: "We can extract it from bones of woolly mammoths . . . and make sense of it, " says Nick Goldman of the European Bioinformatics Institute.

EWE: Ðe woate ŋu adzra nyatakaka siwo ŋu amegbetɔwo trɔ asi le la ɖo ɖe domenyiŋusẽfianuwo dzia?
ENGLISH: "It’s also incredibly small, dense and does not need any power for storage, so shipping and keeping it is easy. "

EWE: Numekulawo ɖo eŋu be ɛ̃, woate ŋui.
ENGLISH: Could DNA store man-made data?

ENGLISH: Various theories as to the cause of this disease had been proposed, yet no one had solved the mystery.

ENGLISH: Troubled by the spectacle of numerous mothers suffering a slow, agonizing death, Semmelweis determined to find the cause of the disease and prevent it.

ENGLISH: Hence, Semmelweis thought that perhaps what he termed "poisons " from cadavers were infecting pregnant patients, thus causing childbed fever.

ENGLISH: The results he obtained challenged the theories concerning childbed fever held by his superior, who also found Semmelweis’ insistent manner irritating.

ENGLISH: Fact: Although God never causes suffering, he sometimes allows it temporarily.

EWE: Nu ka tae Mawu ɖe mɔ Nazitɔwo tsrɔ̃ Yudatɔwo o?
ENGLISH: Why did God allow the Holocaust?

EWE: Susu si tae Mawu ɖe mɔ amegbetɔwo katã le fu kpem ɖo la ke tae wòɖe mɔ Nazitɔwo tsrɔ̃ Yudatɔwo ɖo: be woakpɔ ŋuɖoɖo na nyui kple vɔ̃ ƒe nya si fɔ ɖe te gbe aɖe gbe ʋĩ ke la.
ENGLISH: God allowed the Holocaust for the same reason that he has permitted all human suffering: to settle moral issues that were raised long ago.

EWE: Biblia ɖee fia kɔtɛe be Abosam ye le xexea dzi ɖum egbea, menye Mawu ye o.
ENGLISH: The Bible clearly indicates that at present the Devil, not God, rules the world.

EWE: (Luka 4:1, 2, 6; Yohanes 12:31) Togbɔ be nyati si ƒe kadodo nàkpɔ le tanya sia te ɖe nu si tae Mawu ɖe mɔ ɖe fukpekpe ŋu me tsitotsito hã la, nyateƒenya eve aɖewo dze le Biblia me siwo akpe ɖe mía ŋu míase nu si tae Mawu ɖe mɔ Nazitɔwo tsrɔ̃ Yudatɔwo ɖo la gɔme.
ENGLISH: (Luke 4:1, 2, 6; John 12:31) Two basic facts from the Bible can help explain why God allowed the Holocaust.

EWE: Ame ka gbɔe wòtso be Nazitɔwo tsrɔ̃ Yudatɔwo?
ENGLISH: God created humans with free will.

EWE: Mawu gblɔ nu si wòdi tso amegbetɔ gbãtɔ siwo nye Adam kple Xawa si la na wo, gake mezii ɖe wo dzi o.
ENGLISH: God told the first humans, Adam and Eve, what he expected of them, but he did not force them to obey.

EWE: Wotiae be yewo ŋutɔwo yewoaɖo nu si nye nyui kple nu si nye vɔ̃ na yewo ɖokuiwo, eye nenema ko amegbetɔ bubuawo hã le ewɔm le ƒe gbogbo siwo kplɔe ɖo me.
ENGLISH: They chose to decide for themselves what was good and bad, and their bad choice and similar choices by people throughout history has brought horrible consequences to mankind.

EWE: (1 Mose 2:17; 3:6; Romatɔwo 5:12) Ðeko wòle abe ale si agbalẽ aɖe gblɔe ene be: "Fukpekpe siwo le xexea me ƒe akpa gãtɔ tso ale si mímewɔa tiatiawɔblɔɖe si wona mí la ŋu dɔ nyuie o gbɔ. "
ENGLISH: (Genesis 2:17; 3:6; Romans 5:12) It is as the book Statement of Principles of Conservative Judaism says: "Much of the world’s suffering directly results from our misuse of the free will granted to us. "

EWE: (Statement of Principles of Conservative Judaism) Mawu mexɔ tiatiawɔblɔɖe le mía si o, ke boŋ ɖe wòna ɣeyiɣi amegbetɔwo be woawo ŋutɔwo woakpɔ woƒe nyawo gbɔ le wo ɖokuiwo si ye Mawu manɔmee.
ENGLISH: Rather than revoke our free will, God has given humans time to try to manage their affairs independent of him.

EWE: Mawu ate ŋu aɖɔ nu siwo Nazitɔwo gblẽ le Yudatɔwo ŋu la ɖo eye awɔe hã.
ENGLISH: God can and will undo all the damage of the Holocaust.

EWE: Mawu do ŋugbe be yeafɔ ame miliɔn geɖe siwo ku la ɖe tsitre eye Yudatɔ siwo Nazitɔwo wu hã anɔ eme.
ENGLISH: God promises to bring back to life millions who have died, including Holocaust victims.

EWE: Aɖe veve si ame siwo tsi agbe le Nazitɔwo ƒe ametsɔtsrɔ̃ ma me sena ne woɖo ŋku nu dziŋɔ siwo me woto dzi la hã ɖa.
ENGLISH: He will also eliminate the pain that Holocaust survivors feel because of horrific memories.

EWE: (Yesaya 65:17; Dɔwɔwɔwo 24:15) Lɔlɔ̃ si le Mawu si na amegbetɔƒomea nye kpeɖodzi be awɔ ɖe eƒe ŋugbedodo siawo dzi.
ENGLISH: (Isaiah 65:17; Acts 24:15) God’s love for mankind guarantees that he will fulfill these promises.

EWE: Yohanes 3:16.
ENGLISH: John 3:16.

EWE: Ame siwo tsi agbe le Nazitɔwo ƒe ametsɔtsrɔ̃ ma me la dometɔ geɖe te ŋu va xɔ Mawu dzi se eye woƒe dzi dze eme le agbe me esi wova se nu si tae Mawu ɖe mɔ vɔ̃ɖinyenye kpɔtɔ li kple tame si wòɖo be yeaɖɔ nu siwo vɔ̃ɖinyenye gblẽ le amewo ŋu la katã ɖo la gɔme.
ENGLISH: Many Holocaust victims and survivors were able to maintain their faith and find meaning in life by understanding why God has allowed evil and how he purposes to undo its effects.

EWE: Fukpekpe Nu Ayi Kpuie!
ENGLISH: The End of Suffering Is at Hand!

EWE: Tsɔe be èle xexe si me nu siwo nana míekpea fu, abe nu vlo wɔwɔ, aʋawɔwɔ, dɔléle kple dzɔdzɔmefɔkuwo ene mele o la me.
ENGLISH: Imagine living in a world free of suffering a world without crime, warfare, sickness, and natural disasters.

EWE: Kpɔe ɖa le susu me be ne èfɔ ŋdi sia ŋdi la, mètsia dzimaɖi le vovototodedeameme, ameteteɖeanyi nuwɔna, alo ganyawo ƒe kemalimali ta o.
ENGLISH: Imagine waking up every morning without having to worry about discrimination, oppression, or economic uncertainty.

EWE: Ðe wòwɔ na wò be drɔ̃e gbɔlo koe nya siawo nyea?
ENGLISH: Does all of this sound too good to be true?

EWE: Enye nyateƒe be amegbetɔ alo amegbetɔwo ƒe habɔbɔ aɖeke mate ŋu ahe tɔtrɔ mawo ava xexea me o.
ENGLISH: Granted, no human or man-made organization can bring about such conditions.

EWE: Gake Mawu do ŋugbe be yeaɖe nu siwo katã nana amegbetɔwo kpea fu la ɖa; esiwo me míedzro le nyati si do ŋgɔ me la hã le eme.
ENGLISH: But God has promised to do away with all causes of human suffering, including those discussed in the preceding article.

EWE: De ŋugble le Mawu ƒe ŋugbedodo siawo siwo dze le eƒe Nya, Biblia, me la ŋu kpɔ:
ENGLISH: Note the following promises from God’s Word, the Bible:

EWE: DZIÐUÐU NYUI AVA
ENGLISH: THE RULE OF GOOD GOVERNMENT

EWE: "Dziƒo ƒe Mawu la aɖo fiaɖuƒe aɖe anyi, si matsrɔ̃ gbeɖegbeɖe o, eye eƒe fiaɖuƒe mayi ɖe dukɔ bubu aɖeke si me o; agbã fiaɖuƒe mawo katã, eye wòagblẽ wo, ke eya ŋutɔ anɔ anyi tegbee. "
ENGLISH: "The God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be brought to ruin. And the kingdom itself will not be passed on to any other people. It will crush and put an end to all these kingdoms, and it itself will stand to times indefinite. "

EWE: Daniel 2:44.
ENGLISH: Daniel 2:44.

EWE: Mawu Fiaɖuƒea nye dziɖuɖu si woɖo anyi le dziƒo.
ENGLISH: The Kingdom of God is a heavenly government.

EWE: Yesu Kristo, si nye Dziɖula si Mawu tia la axɔ ɖe amegbetɔwo ƒe dziɖuɖuwo teƒe eye wòakpɔ egbɔ be wole Mawu ƒe lɔlɔ̃nu wɔm le dziƒo kple anyigba dzi afi sia hã.
ENGLISH: Its chosen Ruler, Jesus Christ, will take the place of all human rulership and will ensure that God’s will is done not only in heaven but also here on earth.

EWE: (Mateo 6:9, 10) Amegbetɔ ƒe dziɖuɖu aɖeke mava xɔ ɖe dziɖuɖu sia teƒe o, elabena "mía Aƒetɔ kple Ðela Yesu Kristo ƒe fiaɖuƒe mavɔ " ye wònye.
ENGLISH: (Matthew 6:9, 10) This government will not be replaced by any human government because it is "the everlasting kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. "

EWE: Ŋutifafa axɔ aƒe ɖi tegbee le dziɖuɖu ma te.
ENGLISH: Lasting peace will be assured.

EWE: 2 Petro 1:11.
ENGLISH: 2 Peter 1:11.

EWE: ALAKPASUBƆSUBƆ MAGANƆ ANYI O
ENGLISH: NO MORE FALSE RELIGION

EWE: "Satana ŋutɔ yia edzi trɔa eɖokui wɔa kekeli ƒe dɔla.
ENGLISH: "Satan himself keeps transforming himself into an angel of light.

EWE: Eya ta menye nu gã aɖekee wònye, ne eƒe subɔlawo hã yia edzi trɔa wo ɖokuiwo dzɔdzɔenyenye ƒe subɔlawo o.
ENGLISH: It is therefore nothing great if his ministers also keep transforming themselves into ministers of righteousness.

EWE: Gake woƒe nuwuwu anɔ ɖe woƒe dɔwɔwɔwo nu. " 2 Korintotɔwo 11:14, 15.
ENGLISH: But their end shall be according to their works. " 2 Corinthians 11:14, 15.

EWE: Woaklo nu le alakpasubɔsubɔ dzi wòadze gaglãa be Abosam ƒe dɔwɔwɔe wònye, eye woaɖee ɖa keŋkeŋ le anyigba dzi.
ENGLISH: False religion will be exposed as the work of the Devil and will be eliminated from the earth.

EWE: Fuléle si subɔsubɔhawo dona ɖe ŋgɔ kple woƒe ʋukɔkɔɖi nu ayi.
ENGLISH: Gone will be all religious bigotry and bloodshed.

EWE: Esia ana mɔnukpɔkpɔ ame siwo katã lɔ̃ "Mawu gbagbe vavã " la be woasubɔe le "xɔse ɖeka " me, le "gbɔgbɔ kple nyateƒe " me.
ENGLISH: This will allow all lovers of the "living and true God " to worship him in "one faith " and "with spirit and truth. "

EWE: Ŋutifafa kple ɖekawɔwɔ ka gbegbee nye esi wòanye! 1 Tesalonikatɔwo 1:9; Efesotɔwo 4:5; Yohanes 4:23.
ENGLISH: What peace and unity! 1 Thessalonians 1:9; Ephesians 4:5; John 4:23.

EWE: AMEGBETƆWO ƑE BLIBOMADEMADE NU AYI
ENGLISH: HUMAN IMPERFECTION WILL BE NO MORE

EWE: "Mawu ŋutɔ anɔ anyi kpli wo.
ENGLISH: "God himself will be with them.

EWE: Eye wòatutu aɖatsi sia aɖatsi ɖa le woƒe ŋkume, eye ku maganɔ anyi o, eye konyifafa kple ɣlidodo kple vevesese hã maganɔ anyi o.
ENGLISH: And he will wipe out every tear from their eyes, and death will be no more, neither will mourning nor outcry nor pain be anymore.

EWE: Nu siwo nɔ anyi tsã la nu va yi. "
ENGLISH: The former things have passed away. "

EWE: Nyaɖeɖefia 21:3, 4.
ENGLISH: Revelation 21:3, 4.

EWE: Yehowa Mawu ana esia nava eme to Via, Yesu, ame si tsɔ eƒe agbe sa vɔe ɖe ameƒomea ta la dzi.
ENGLISH: Jehovah God makes this possible by means of his Son, Jesus, who gave his life for the world of mankind.

EWE: (Yohanes 3:16) Le Yesu ƒe mɔfiafia te la, woana amegbetɔwo nagava zu ame deblibowo ake, abe ale si wònɔ le gɔmedzedzea me ene.
ENGLISH: (John 3:16) Under Jesus’ direction, humankind will be brought to perfection.

EWE: Fukpekpe aɖeke maganɔ anyi o, elabena "Mawu ŋutɔ anɔ anyi kpli wo " eye atutu "aɖatsi sia aɖatsi ɖa le woƒe ŋkume. "
ENGLISH: There will no longer be any suffering because "God himself will be with them " and will erase "every tear from their eyes. "

EWE: Eteƒe madidi o, amegbetɔ ƒe blibomademade kple fukpekpe azu gbe aɖe gbe nya; "ame dzɔdzɔewo anyi anyigba la dome, eye woanɔ edzi tegbee. "
ENGLISH: Human imperfection and suffering will soon be a thing of the past; "the righteous themselves will possess the earth, and they will reside forever upon it. "

EWE: Psalmo 37:29.
ENGLISH: Psalm 37:29.

EWE: GBƆGBƆ VƆ̃WO MAGANƆ ANYI O
ENGLISH: WICKED SPIRITS WILL BE GONE

EWE: "[Yesu Kristo] lé ʋɔ driba, si nye da xoxo la, si nye Abosam kple Satana, eye wòblae hena ƒe akpe ɖeka.
ENGLISH: "He [Jesus Christ] seized the dragon, the original serpent, who is the Devil and Satan, and bound him for a thousand years.

EWE: Eye wòtsɔe ƒu gbe ɖe aʋli la me, eye wòtu nu ɖe enu, eye wòtre enu, bene wòagakplɔ dukɔwo atrae azɔ o. "
ENGLISH: And he hurled him into the abyss and shut it and sealed it over him, that he might not mislead the nations anymore. "

EWE: Nyaɖeɖefia 20:2, 3.
ENGLISH: Revelation 20:2, 3.

EWE: Ne wolé Satana kple gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃wo de "aʋli la " si nye dɔmawɔmawɔ ƒe nɔnɔme me me vɔ la, womagakpɔ ŋusẽ ɖe amewo dzi azɔ o.
ENGLISH: All satanic influence will be gone when Satan and the demons are bound and hurled into "the abyss, " a state of total inactivity.

EWE: Ɣemaɣi la, gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃wo magakpɔ ŋusẽ gbegblẽ ɖe amegbetɔwo ƒe ɖoɖowo dzi le mɔ aɖeke nu o.
ENGLISH: They will no longer exercise their evil control over human affairs.

EWE: Gbɔdzɔe ka gbegbee nye esi wòanye be míanɔ agbe le xexe si me Satana kple gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃wo ƒe fuɖename maganɔ o la me!
ENGLISH: What a relief it will be to live in a world free from the influence of Satan and the wicked spirits!

EWE: "ŊKEKE MAMLƐAWO " AWU ENU
ENGLISH: "THE LAST DAYS " WILL BE OVER

EWE: "Ŋkeke mamlɛawo " awu enu ne "xaxa gã " si ŋu Yesu ƒo nu tsoe la va.
ENGLISH: "The last days " will end with what Jesus called the "great tribulation. "

EWE: Egblɔ be: "Ɣemaɣi la, xaxa gã ava, si tɔgbi meva kpɔ o, ao, meva kpɔ tso xexea ƒe gɔmedzedze va se ɖe fifia o, eye magava ake o. "
ENGLISH: He said: "Then there will be great tribulation such as has not occurred since the world’s beginning until now, no, nor will occur again. "

EWE: Mateo 24:21.
ENGLISH: Matthew 24:21.

EWE: Anye xaxa gã le gɔmesesea nu be nɔnɔme sesẽ siwo tɔgbi meva kpɔ o lae ava.
ENGLISH: The tribulation will be great in the sense that unprecedented calamities will occur.

EWE: Awu enu kple "Mawu Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la ƒe ŋkeke gã la ƒe aʋawɔwɔ, " si woyɔna be "Harmagedon. "
ENGLISH: These will climax at "the war of the great day of God the Almighty, " better known as "Armageddon. "

EWE: Nyaɖeɖefia 16:14, 16.
ENGLISH: Revelation 16:14, 16, footnote.

EWE: Le xexea me godoo la, ame siwo lɔ̃ nu nyui wɔwɔ la le mɔ kpɔm na nuɖoanyi vɔ̃ɖi sia ƒe nuwuwu vevie.
ENGLISH: People everywhere who love what is right look forward to the end of this wicked system of things.

EWE: Bu yayra siwo le wo lalam le Mawu Fiaɖuƒea ƒe dziɖuɖu te la dometɔ ʋɛ aɖewo ko ŋu kpɔ.
ENGLISH: Consider just a few of the blessings that await them under God’s Kingdom.

EWE: YAYRA BUBUWO AGATSO MAWU GBƆ!
ENGLISH: GOD WILL DO EVEN MORE!

EWE: Woakpɔ "ameha gã aɖe " ta woage ɖe ŋutifafa ƒe xexe yeye me: Mawu ƒe Nya la gblɔ be "ameha gã " aɖe si womenya xexlẽme na o la "[ado] go tso xaxa gã la me " eye woakpɔ wo ta woage ɖe xexe yeye si me dzɔdzɔenyenye anɔ la me.
ENGLISH: "A great crowd " will be preserved into a peaceful new world: God’s Word says that an unnumbered "great crowd " of people will "come out of the great tribulation " and be preserved alive into a righteous new world.

EWE: (Nyaɖeɖefia 7:9, 10, 14; 2 Petro 3:13) Woalɔ̃ ɖe edzi be Yesu Kristo, "Mawu ƒe Alẽvi si le xexea ƒe nu vɔ̃ ɖem ɖa " la dzie woto ɖe yewo.
ENGLISH: (Revelation 7:9, 10, 14; 2 Peter 3:13) They will attribute their salvation to Jesus Christ, "the Lamb of God that takes away the sin of the world. "

EWE: Yohanes 1:29.
ENGLISH: John 1:29.

EWE: Nufiame si tso Mawu gbɔ aɖe vi geɖe: Le xexe yeyea me la, ‘sidzedze Yehowa axɔ anyigba la dzi.’
ENGLISH: Great benefits will come from divine education: In the new world, "the earth will certainly be filled with the knowledge of Jehovah. "

EWE: (Yesaya 11:9) Ale si amewo anɔ anyi kple wo nɔewo le ŋutifafa me ahalé be na anyigba la hã le nufiame si atso Mawu gbɔ la me.
ENGLISH: (Isaiah 11:9) This divine education will include instruction on how to live in peace with all people and in harmony with the environment.

EWE: Mawu do ŋugbe be: "Nye Yehowa, wò Mawu, enye ame si fia nu si nyo na wò la wò, nyee akplɔ wò to mɔ, si dzi nàto la. "
ENGLISH: God promises: "I, Jehovah, am your God, the One teaching you to benefit yourself, the One causing you to tread in the way in which you should walk. "

EWE: Yesaya 48:17.
ENGLISH: Isaiah 48:17.

EWE: Woafɔ ame kukuwo ɖe tsitre: Esime Yesu nɔ anyigba dzi la, efɔ exɔlɔ̃ Lazaro si ku la ɖe tsitre.
ENGLISH: Dead loved ones will be raised from the grave: While on earth, Jesus raised his friend Lazarus from the dead.

EWE: (Yohanes 11:1, 5, 38-44) Eto esia dzi ɖe nu si wòato Mawu Fiaɖuƒea dzi awɔ le xexea me godoo la fia.
ENGLISH: (John 11:1, 5, 38-44) Thus he demonstrated what he will do on a much larger scale under God’s Kingdom arrangement.

EWE: Yohanes 5:28, 29.
Ŋutifafa kple dzɔdzɔenyenye anɔ anyi tegbee: Le Kristo ƒe dziɖuɖu te la, sedzimawɔmawɔ azu gbe aɖe gbe nya.
ENGLISH: Peace and righteousness will prevail forever: Under Christ’s rulership, lawlessness will be a thing of the past.

EWE: Aleke míewɔ nya?
ENGLISH: How do we know that?

EWE: Elabena ŋutete le Yesu si be wòanya nu si le ame ƒe dzi me, eye awɔ ŋutete ma ŋu dɔ atsɔ adrɔ̃ ʋɔnu ame dzɔdzɔewo kple ame vɔ̃ɖiwo.
ENGLISH: Because Jesus is able to read hearts, and he will use that ability to judge between the righteous and the wicked.

EWE: Womaɖe mɔ na ame siwo gbe be yewomatrɔ le yewoƒe mɔ vɔ̃wo dzi o la be woayi edzi anɔ agbe le Mawu ƒe xexe yeyea me o.
ENGLISH: Those who refuse to change their wicked ways will not be allowed to live in God’s new world.

EWE: Psalmo 37:9, 10; Yesaya 11:3, 4; 65:20; Mateo 9:4.
ENGLISH: Psalm 37:9, 10; Isaiah 11:3, 4; 65:20; Matthew 9:4.

EWE: Nu siwo me míedzro la nye Biblia me nyagblɔɖi siwo ƒo nu tso ɣeyiɣi nyui si le ŋgɔ gbɔna ŋu la dometɔ ʋɛ aɖewo ko.
ENGLISH: We have considered just a few of the many Bible prophecies that point to the wonderful time to come.

EWE: Ne Mawu Fiaɖuƒea le anyigba dzi ɖum la, "ŋutifafa gbogbo " axɔ aƒe ɖi tegbee.
ENGLISH: When God’s Kingdom exercises rulership over the earth, an "abundance of peace " will prevail forever.

EWE: (Psalmo 37:11, 29) Woaɖe nu siwo hea vevesese kple fukpekpe siwo me tom amegbetɔwo le vɛ la katã ɖa.
ENGLISH: (Psalm 37:11, 29) All the causes of pain and suffering that have plagued mankind will be undone.

EWE: Mawu ŋutɔe do ŋugbe esi wògblɔ be: "Kpɔ ɖa!
ENGLISH: We have God’s own word on it: "Look!

EWE: Mele nuwo katã wɔm yeyee. . . .
ENGLISH: I am making all things new. . . .

EWE: Nya siawo nye nyateƒenyawo kple nya vavãwo. "
ENGLISH: These words are faithful and true. "

EWE: Nyaɖeɖefia 21:5.
ENGLISH: Revelation 21:5.

EWE: Ne Wò Ame Vevi Aɖe Ku
ENGLISH: When a Loved One Dies

EWE: "Bebe, Mawu nya nu si nyo na mí. . . .
ENGLISH: "God knows best, baby. . . .

EWE: Èseea? . . . Mègafa avi o. "
ENGLISH: Don’t . . . you . . . cry. "

EWE: Nya mawoe ame aɖe gblɔ ɖe to me na nyɔnu aɖe si ŋkɔe nye Bebe, si fofo ku le ʋufɔku aɖe me la, le kua teƒe.
ENGLISH: Those words were whispered into the ear of a woman named Bebe. She was at the funeral of her father, who had died in a car accident.

EWE: Tsi metoa Bebe kple fofoa dome o.
ENGLISH: Bebe had been very close to her father.

EWE: Wo xɔlɔ̃ aɖe si nya ƒomea nyuie lae gblɔ nya mawo be yeatsɔ afa akɔ nɛ, gake nya mawo mefa akɔ na Bebe o, ke boŋ ɖeko wogado nuxaxa nɛ.
ENGLISH: The remark came from a well-meaning family friend, but Bebe found it more cutting than comforting.

EWE: Bebe nɔ egbɔgblɔ dzi be, "Eƒe kua menye nu si nyo nam o. "
ENGLISH: "His death wasn’t for the best, " she kept repeating to herself.

EWE: Nu si Bebe ŋlɔ ɖe agbalẽ aɖe me tso nudzɔdzɔa ŋu le ƒe aɖewo megbe la ɖee fia kɔtɛ be egakpɔtɔ nɔ fofoa ƒe ku fam kokoko.
ENGLISH: It was clear that when Bebe recounted the incident in a book years later, she was still grieving.

EWE: Abe ale si Bebe kpɔe dze sii ene la, etea ŋu xɔa ƒe geɖe hafi ame si dzi ku dzɔ ɖo la dzudzɔa nuxaxa, vevietɔ ne woa kple ame si ku la dome nɔ kplikplikpli.
ENGLISH: As Bebe came to see, it can take a long time for someone to overcome grief, especially when the bereaved person was very close to the deceased.

EWE: Esɔ nyuie be woyɔ ku le Biblia me be "futɔ mamlɛtɔ. " (1 Korintotɔwo 15:26) Ðeko wòva dzea mí kpoyi le vo me, míetea ŋu wɔa naneke le eŋu o, eye wòkplɔa míaƒe ame veviwo dzonɛ.
ENGLISH: In the Bible, death is aptly described as "the last enemy. " (1 Corinthians 15:26) It breaks into our lives with irresistible force, often when we are completely unprepared, and it robs us of those we hold dear.

EWE: Mía dometɔ aɖeke mate ŋu asi le nu si ku gblẽna le ame ŋu la nu o.
ENGLISH: None of us are immune to its ravages.

ENGLISH: Of course, not everyone grieves in the same way.

ENGLISH: So if you do not outwardly display sorrow, this does not mean that you are suppressing your emotions or that you should force tears.

ENGLISH: Rather than dwelling on sayings that hurt, follow the Bible’s wise advice: "Do not take to heart every word that people say. "

ENGLISH: Ronaldo says: "At Ecclesiastes 9:5, the Bible shows that the dead are not suffering, and that fact gives me an inner peace.

EWE: Eya ta mebua nye ame vevi siwo ku la abe ɖeko wozɔ mɔ ene. "
ENGLISH: So I think of the loved ones I have lost in death as if they were away on a trip. "

EWE: Dɔwɔwɔwo 24:15.

EWE: Yesaya 25:8.

ENGLISH: This series of articles discusses how you can cope with tragedy.

ENGLISH: For Bible-based information on the reasons for human suffering, see the series of articles "Why Do Bad Things Happen to Good People? " in the July 1, 2014, issue of our companion journal, The Watchtower.

EWE: Ale Si Nàwɔ Anɔ Te Ðe Nuxaxa Nu Nu Si Nàte Ŋu Awɔ Egbea
ENGLISH: Coping With Grief​ What You Can Do Today

EWE: Ne èdi aɖaŋuɖoɖo tso ale si nàwɔ anɔ te ɖe nuxaxa nu ŋu la, ɖewohĩ àke ɖe gbogbo aɖewo ŋu, eye ɖewo aɖe vi wu bubuwo.
ENGLISH: If you look for advice on dealing with grief, you will likely find a myriad of ideas​ some more helpful than others.

ENGLISH: They are frequently cited by grief counselors, and they echo timeless principles found in an ancient book of wisdom, the Bible.

EWE: 1: NA WÒ ƑOMETƆWO KPLE XƆLƆ̃WO NAKPE ÐE ŊUWÒ
ENGLISH: 1: ACCEPT SUPPORT FROM FAMILY AND FRIENDS

EWE: Ame aɖewo le fefem le ƒuta eye wole foto ɖem
ENGLISH: People at the seashore fly a kite and take pictures

EWE: Aɖaŋuɖola bibi aɖewo bui be esia nye mɔ vevi siwo dzi woato anɔ te ɖe nuxaxa nu la dometɔ ɖeka.
ENGLISH: Some experts consider this to be the most important factor in getting through grief.

EWE: Ke hã ɣeaɖewoɣia màdi be ame aɖeke nanɔ ye ŋu o.
ENGLISH: Yet, at times, you may want to be alone.

EWE: Àte ŋu ado dziku ɖe ame siwo le agbagba dzem be yewoakpe ɖe ŋuwò la ŋu gɔ̃ hã.
ENGLISH: You may even feel irritated at those who are trying to help you.

EWE: Naneke megblẽ le eŋu o.
ENGLISH: This is normal.

EWE: Mègasusu be ele be amewo nanɔ ye ŋu ɣesiaɣi o, gake mèganya wo ɖa keŋkeŋ le ɖokuiwò ŋu hã o.
ENGLISH: Do not feel that you must always be around others, but do not completely push them away either.

EWE: Àva hiã woƒe kpekpeɖeŋu emegbe.
ENGLISH: After all, you may need their support in the future.

EWE: Gblɔ nu si nèdi be woawɔ na ye kple nu si mèdi o la na wo.
ENGLISH: Kindly let others know what you need at the moment and what you do not.

EWE: Togbɔ be àdi be amewo nawɔ nanewo na ye alo woagawɔ nanewo na ye o hã, ele be nàda asɔ be nàte ŋu akpɔ ɣeyiɣi na amewo hã.
ENGLISH: According to your needs, find a balance between time with other people and time alone.

EWE: MƆFIAME: "Ne ame le eve la, enyo wu ame ɖeka, . . .
ENGLISH: PRINCIPLE: "Two are better than one . . .

EWE: Elabena ne wo dometɔ ɖeka dze anyi la, evelia afɔe ɖe tsitre. " Nyagblɔla 4:9, 10.
ENGLISH: For if one of them falls, the other can help his partner up. "​ Ecclesiastes 4:9, 10.

EWE: 2: LÉ ŊKU ÐE WÒ NUÐUÐU ŊU, EYE NÀDI ƔEYIƔI ADE KAME
ENGLISH: 2: WATCH YOUR DIET, AND MAKE TIME FOR EXERCISE

EWE: Ne èɖua nu nyuie la, akpe ɖe ŋuwò nàte ŋu anɔ te ɖe nuxaxa nu.
ENGLISH: A balanced diet will help with the stress that comes from dealing with grief.

EWE: Dze agbagba be yeanɔ atikutsetsewo, amagbewo kple nuɖuɖu siwo me protein le la ɖum.
ENGLISH: Try to eat a variety of fruits, vegetables, and lean proteins.

EWE: No tsi sɔgbɔ eye nàno nunono bubu siwo dea lãmesẽ dzi hã.
ENGLISH: Drink plenty of water and other healthful liquids.

EWE: Ne nu menya le ɖuɖum na wò o la, ekema ɖui vivivi edziedzi.
ENGLISH: If your appetite is low, eat small portions more frequently.

EWE: Azɔ hã, àte ŋu agblɔ na wò ɖɔkta be wòana nunyiametikewo wò.
ENGLISH: You may also ask your doctor about nutrition supplements.

EWE: Azɔlizɔzɔ atsɔ ade kame kple kamedede bubuwo ate ŋu ana ame matsi dzi fũu o.
ENGLISH: Brisk walks and other forms of exercise can lessen negative emotions.

EWE: Kamedede ate ŋu akpe ɖe ŋuwò nàde ŋugble le ale si nuwo trɔ na wò fifia la ŋu alo ana nàɖe susu ɖa le nu si dzɔa dzi vie.
ENGLISH: Exercise can provide time to reflect on your loss or to take a break from thinking about it.

ENGLISH: PRINCIPLE: "No one has ever hated his own body but he feeds it and takes care of it. "​ Ephesians 5:29, NET Bible.

ENGLISH: 3: GET PLENTY OF SLEEP

ENGLISH: A bed

ENGLISH: Sleep is always important, but this is especially so for those who are grieving, as grief can bring extra fatigue.

EWE: Mègano nu siwo me caffeine le fũu o eye mèganɔ aha hã nom fũu o elabe woate ŋu agblẽ alɔ̃ me na wò.
ENGLISH: Be careful with the amount of caffeine and alcohol you consume, as both can interfere with your sleep.

EWE: MƆFIAME: "Gbɔɖeme asiʋlo ɖeka nyo wu dɔ sesẽ wɔwɔ kple dagbadagba ɖe yame asiʋlo eve. " Nyagblɔla 4:6.
ENGLISH: PRINCIPLE: "Better is a handful of rest than two handfuls of hard work and chasing after the wind. "​ Ecclesiastes 4:6.

EWE: 4: DA SƆ
ENGLISH: 4: BE FLEXIBLE

EWE: Nyɔnu aɖe si le nu xam la le nu ƒom tso eƒe kuxia ŋu na exɔlɔ̃
ENGLISH: A grieving woman expresses herself to a friend

ENGLISH: Ultimately, you will need to determine the strategy that works best for you.

EWE: Ame geɖe kpɔe be ne yewoƒo nu tso yewoƒe nuxaxa ŋu na ame bubuwo la, ekpena ɖe yewo ŋu yewonɔa te ɖe enu, gake ame bubuwo ya medina be yewoaƒo nu tso eŋu o.
ENGLISH: Many find that expressing their grief to others helps them deal with it, while others prefer not to express their grief.

EWE: Eŋuti aɖaŋuɖolawo ƒe susu mesɔ le nya sia ŋu o.
ENGLISH: Experts have various opinions as to whether expressing one’s feelings is vital to success in coping with grief.

ENGLISH: If you need to confide in someone but are hesitant to do so, you might find it easier to start small by expressing some of your feelings to a close friend.

EWE: Le ame aɖewo gome la, wokpɔe be ne yewofa avi la, ekpena ɖe yewo ŋu yewonɔa te ɖe nuxaxa nu, gake ame bubuwo ya tea ŋu nɔa te ɖe enu ne womefa avi boo o hã.
ENGLISH: Some people find that crying helps them deal with their grief, while others seem to cope even though they cry less.

EWE: MƆFIAME: "Ame ƒe dzi nya eya ŋutɔ ƒe vevesese. " Lododowo 14:10.
ENGLISH: PRINCIPLE: "Each heart knows its own bitterness. "​ Proverbs 14:10, New International Version.

ENGLISH: 5: AVOID SELF-DESTRUCTIVE HABITS

ENGLISH: Such "escape " is self-destructive.

EWE: Ðeko aha kple atike vɔ̃wo nana ame kpɔa gbɔdzɔe hena ɣeyiɣi vi aɖe ko, gake emegbe emetsonuawo gblẽa nu vevie.
ENGLISH: Any relief a person may feel is short-lived, only to be followed by major negative consequences.

EWE: Di mɔ siwo dzi nàto anɔ te ɖe nuxaxa nu evɔ magblẽ nu le ŋuwò o.
ENGLISH: Try harmless ways to calm your anxieties.

EWE: MƆFIAME: "Mina míakɔ mía ɖokui ŋu tso . . . ɖiƒoƒo sia ɖiƒoƒo me. " 2 Korintotɔwo 7:1.
ENGLISH: PRINCIPLE: "Let us cleanse ourselves of every defilement. "​ 2 Corinthians 7:1.

EWE: 6: ZÃ WÒ ƔEYIƔIWO NYUIE
ENGLISH: 6: BALANCE YOUR TIME

EWE: Ame geɖe kpɔe be eɖea vi ne yewowɔ nanewo be yewoaɖe susu ɖa le nuxaxaa ŋu ahawɔ nu siwo ana yewoƒe susu nadze akɔ anyi ale be wòaɖe yewoƒe vevesesea dzi akpɔtɔ vie.
ENGLISH: Many find it helpful to alternate periods of grieving (experiencing and dealing with their emotions) with temporary breaks (activities that temporarily distance them from their pain).

EWE: Wò dzi adze eme vie ne èdze xɔlɔ̃ nyuiwo, srɔ̃ asinudɔ yeye aɖe alo ɖe modzaka.
ENGLISH: You may find temporary relief by forming or strengthening friendships, learning new skills, or engaging in recreation.

EWE: Ne ɣeyiɣiawo va le yiyim la, àva trɔ ɖe nɔnɔmea ŋu.
ENGLISH: As time passes, the balance will likely change.

EWE: Àva kpɔe be wò nuxaxaa maganɔ abe tsã ene o, edzi anɔ ɖeɖem kpɔtɔ eye esia akpe ɖe ŋuwò nànɔ te ɖe kuxia nu.
ENGLISH: You may notice that your breaks from grieving become longer and more frequent​ a natural part of the healing process.

EWE: MƆFIAME: "Ɣeyiɣi li na nu sia nu, . . . avifaɣi li, eye nukoɣi li; konyifaɣi li, eye ɣeɖuɣi li. " Nyagblɔla 3:1, 4.
ENGLISH: PRINCIPLE: "There is an appointed time for everything, . . . a time to weep and a time to laugh; a time to wail and a time to dance. "​ Ecclesiastes 3:1, 4.

EWE: 7: YI NU SIWO NÈWƆNA DZI
ENGLISH: 7: KEEP A ROUTINE

EWE: Nyɔnu aɖe le ɖoɖo wɔm ɖe nu siwo wòawɔ ŋu
ENGLISH: A woman uses a calendar to plan her routine

EWE: Ne anya wɔa, yi nu siwo nèwɔna dzi.
ENGLISH: As soon as possible, resume a normal routine.

EWE: Ne èmlɔa anyi ɖe game dzi, wɔa dɔ, eye nèwɔa nu bubuwo la, nuwo ava nɔ na wò abe tsã ene.
ENGLISH: When you hold to a routine for sleep, work, and other activities, you will likely regain a sense of normalcy.

EWE: Ne ètrɔ ɖe dɔ bubuwo ŋu la, ana nàɖe veve si kua do na wò la dzi akpɔtɔ.
ENGLISH: Keeping yourself occupied with positive activities can help to mitigate painful emotions.

EWE: MƆFIAME: "Ƒãa hafi wògabua eƒe agbemeŋkekewo ƒe yiyi ŋu, le esi Mawu vavã la na eƒe susu katã le eƒe dzi ƒe dzidzɔkpɔkpɔ ŋu ta. " Nyagblɔla 5:20.
ENGLISH: PRINCIPLE: "He will hardly notice the passing days of his life, because the true God keeps him preoccupied with the rejoicing of his heart. "​ Ecclesiastes 5:20.

EWE: 8: MÈGATSƆ DZITSITSI WƆ NYAMETSOTSOWO O
ENGLISH: 8: AVOID MAKING BIG DECISIONS TOO SOON

ENGLISH: Many who make big decisions soon after losing a loved one later regret those decisions.

EWE: Ne anya wɔ la, lala ɣeyiɣi aɖe hafi aʋu, adi dɔ yeye alo atsɔ wò ame vevi si ku la ƒe nanewo aƒu gbe.
ENGLISH: If possible, wait for a reasonable length of time before moving, changing jobs, or discarding your loved one’s belongings.

EWE: MƆFIAME: "Veviedola ƒe ɖoɖowo hea dzidzedzekpɔkpɔ vanɛ, ke ame sia ame si tsia klokloklo la, hiã atui. " Lododowo 21:5.
ENGLISH: PRINCIPLE: "The plans of the diligent surely lead to success, but all who are hasty surely head for poverty. "​ Proverbs 21:5.

EWE: 9: MÈGAŊLƆ WÒ AME VEVI SI KU LA BE O
ENGLISH: 9: REMEMBER YOUR LOVED ONE

EWE: Ŋutsu aɖe tsɔ srɔ̃a si ku la ƒe fotowo le amewo fiam
ENGLISH: A man shows friends pictures of his deceased wife

EWE: Ame geɖe siwo ame ku na kpɔe be eɖea vi ne yewowɔa nu siwo akpe ɖe yewo ŋu be yewoaɖo ŋku yewoƒe ame si ku la dzi.
ENGLISH: Many bereaved ones feel it is beneficial to do things that help keep alive their memory of the person who has died.

EWE: Àkpɔe be wò dzi adze eme ne èdzra foto alo ŋkuɖodzinu aɖewo ɖo loo alo ŋlɔ nudzɔdzɔ vevi aɖewo siwo màdi be yeaŋlɔ be o la ɖi.
ENGLISH: You might find it therapeutic to collect pictures or mementos or to create a journal of events and stories you wish to recall.

EWE: KUXIA
ENGLISH: THE CHALLENGE

EWE: Viwò si xɔ ƒe ade bia wò be: "Ta, wò hã ègbɔna kuku gea? "
ENGLISH: Your six-year-old asks, "Are you going to die someday? "

ENGLISH: Startled by his question, you wonder: ‘Is my child old enough to understand the answer?

EWE: Aleke maɖe nu me nɛ tso ku ŋu?’
ENGLISH: How can I talk to him about death?’

EWE: NU SI WÒLE BE NÀNYA
ENGLISH: WHAT YOU SHOULD KNOW

EWE: Ðeviwo bua tame tso ku ŋu.
ENGLISH: Children do think about death.

EWE: Ne wole fefem la, wo dometɔ aɖewo wɔa aye be yewoku gɔ̃ hã.
ENGLISH: Some even play games in which someone pretends to die.

EWE: Eya ta mele be nàƒo asa na nuƒoƒo tso ku ŋu na viwòa o, eye ne ebia nya aɖe wò tso ku ŋu la, lɔ̃ faa nàɖe eme nɛ.
ENGLISH: Therefore, death should not be considered a taboo subject, and you should welcome any questions your child may have about it.

EWE: Ne èƒoa nu tso ku ŋu na viwòa ɣeaɖewoɣi la, awɔe be mavɔ̃ agbɔ eme ne miaƒe ame vevi aɖe ku o.
ENGLISH: By occasionally talking openly about death, you help your child learn how to cope with the loss of a loved one.

EWE: Nuƒoƒo tso ku ŋu mana viwò navɔ̃ agbɔ eme o.
ENGLISH: Talking about death will not cause your child to have morbid thoughts.

EWE: Ke boŋ aɖe eƒe vɔvɔ̃a dzi akpɔtɔ.
ENGLISH: Rather, it will help him alleviate fears.

EWE: Ke hã ehiã be nàɖɔ eƒe susu ɖo le nanewo gome.
ENGLISH: However, you may need to correct some misunderstandings.

EWE: Le kpɔɖeŋu me, numekula aɖewo gblɔna be ɖevi siwo mekpɔ xɔ ƒe ade haɖe o la dometɔ geɖe bunɛ be ame ate ŋu aku agafɔ enumake.
ENGLISH: For example, some experts say that many children under the age of six do not view death as final.

EWE: Ne ɖeviwo le fefem la, wo dometɔ aɖewo kua ayeku, eye kaka nàkpɔ la, woawoe nye ema gafɔ.
ENGLISH: In their games, a child will be "dead " one moment and "alive " the next.

EWE: Gake ne ɖeviawo va tsi vie wu la, wova nɔa tame bum tso ku ŋu vevie, esiae wɔnɛ be wonɔa nya geɖewo biam, wotsia dzi eye wovɔ̃na gɔ̃ hã, vevietɔ ne woƒe ame vevi aɖe ku.
ENGLISH: When they get a little older, however, children begin to grasp the seriousness of death a fact that may cause them to have questions, concerns, or even fears, especially if a loved one has died.

EWE: Eya ta ele vevie be miadzro nu me tso ku ŋu kpli wo.
ENGLISH: Therefore, it is vital that you discuss the subject.

ENGLISH: Mental-health expert Marion Haza points out: "A child will develop anxieties related to death if he feels that he is not allowed to talk about this subject at home. "

EWE: Mehiã be nàtsi dzi fũu ɖe nya si nàgblɔ nɛ ŋuti o.
ENGLISH: You need not worry excessively about what to say.

EWE: Le numekuku aɖe nu la, nu si ko ɖeviwo "dinae nye be woagblɔ nyateƒea na yewo tufafatɔe. "
ENGLISH: According to one study, children just want to "hear the truth expressed in kind words. "

EWE: Nyae be ɖeviwo mebiaa nya ne womesu te na ŋuɖoɖoa sese o.
ENGLISH: Be assured that a child will usually not ask a question unless he is ready to hear the answer.

EWE: NU SI NÀTE ŊU AWƆ

ENGLISH: Take advantage of opportunities to talk about death.

EWE: Ne viwòa kpɔ xevi kuku aɖe le mɔ to alo miaƒe aƒemelã aɖe ku la, àte ŋu abia nya bɔbɔe aɖewoe siwo ana wòagblɔ eƒe susu.
ENGLISH: If your child sees a dead bird on the side of the road or if a beloved pet dies, use simple questions to encourage him to talk.

EWE: Le kpɔɖeŋu me, àte ŋu abiae be: "Ðe lã kukua le fu kpema?
ENGLISH: For example, you could ask: "Does a dead animal suffer?

EWE: Ðe vuvɔ le ewɔma?
ENGLISH: Is it cold or hungry?

EWE: Ðe dɔ le ewuma? Aleke nàwɔ anya be ame alo lã aɖe ku? "
ENGLISH: How do you know that an animal or a person is dead? "

ENGLISH: Bible principle: Ecclesiastes 3:1, 7.

EWE: Mègaɣla nyateƒea ɖee o.
ENGLISH: Do not hide the truth.

ENGLISH: When an acquaintance or a relative has died, avoid using confusing euphemisms such as "He has gone away. "

EWE: Viwòa asusui vodadatɔe be ame si ku la agatrɔ agbɔ kpuie.
ENGLISH: Your child might wrongly conclude that the deceased will soon return home.

EWE: Ke boŋ zã nya siwo gɔme sese le bɔbɔe nàtsɔ aɖe nu me nɛ.
ENGLISH: Instead, use simple and direct words.

EWE: Àte ŋu agblɔ nɛ be: "Esi mama kua, eƒe ŋutilã megale dɔ wɔm o.
ENGLISH: For example, you might say: "When Grandma died, her body stopped working.

ENGLISH: We can’t talk to her, but we will never forget her. "

EWE: Biblia ƒe mɔfiame: Efesotɔwo 4:25.
ENGLISH: Bible principle: Ephesians 4:25.

ENGLISH: Since a young child might think that death is contagious, assure him that he is safe

EWE: Ka ɖe edzi nɛ be menye eƒe vodadae o.
ENGLISH: Reassure your child.

EWE: Ate ŋu asusui be yee wɔ nane alo yee susu nane tae amea ku.
ENGLISH: He might think that his actions or thoughts caused someone’s death.

ENGLISH: Instead of just saying that he is not responsible for what happened, you could ask, "What makes you think that it is your fault? "

EWE: Ðo to nyuie nàse eƒe nyawo, eye mègada eƒe nyawo ɖe anyi o.
ENGLISH: Listen carefully, without belittling his feelings.

EWE: Esi ɖeviwo susunɛ be ne wole nu ƒom tso ku ŋu la ɖe wokuna ta la, ka ɖe edzi nɛ be naneke mele ewɔ ge o.
ENGLISH: Also, since a young child might think that death is contagious, assure him that he is safe.

EWE: Na viwòa nagblɔ eƒe susu.
ENGLISH: Draw out your child.

EWE: Miɖo dze tso miaƒe ame vevi siwo ku, siwo dometɔ aɖewo nye miaƒe ƒometɔ siwo viwòa mekpɔ kpɔ o, la ŋu.
ENGLISH: Talk freely about loved ones who have died, including relatives whom your child has never met.

EWE: Àte ŋu agblɔ nu nyui siwo mia tasi, nyrui, mama alo tɔgbui aɖe wɔ kpɔ la nɛ, eye miagblɔ nu ɖikokoe aɖe si amea wɔ kpɔ hã nɛ.
ENGLISH: You might evoke fond memories of an aunt, an uncle, or a grandparent and relate amusing anecdotes.

EWE: Ne mieƒoa nu tso ame siawo tɔgbi ŋu la, akpe ɖe viwòa ŋu wòakpɔe be mele be yeaƒo asa na wo ŋu bubu alo nuƒoƒo tso wo ŋu o.
ENGLISH: When you openly discuss such people, you help your child understand that he need not avoid talking or thinking about them.

EWE: Gake mègazi viwòa dzi be wòaƒo nu kokoko o.

EWE: Àte ŋu ado nyaa ɖa ɣebubuɣi si nèkpɔ be asɔ wu.
ENGLISH: You can always broach the subject later, when you feel the time is right.
