EWE: Gblɔ wò dzimenyawo na wò ƒometɔ alo xɔlɔ̃ si dzi nèka ɖo.
ENGLISH: Confide in a family member or trusted friend.

EWE: Menye ɖeko ƒometɔwo kple xɔlɔ̃ kplikplikpliwo aɖo to wò ko o, ke boŋ woate ŋu ade dzi ƒo na wò eye woakpe ɖe ŋuwò hã.
ENGLISH: In addition to providing a listening ear, family members or close friends can provide words of encouragement and give practical help.

EWE: Wò susu nenɔ ɣeyiɣi si me nuwo aɖɔ ɖo ŋu.
ENGLISH: Look ahead to better times.

EWE: "Míele dziƒo yeye kple anyigba yeye, siwo me dzɔdzɔenyenye anɔ la, lalam le [Mawu ƒe] ŋugbedodo la nu. " 2 Petro 3:13.
ENGLISH: "There are new heavens and a new earth that we are awaiting according to [God’s] promise, and in these righteousness is to dwell. "​ 2 Peter 3:13.

EWE: Nya Kae Biblia Gblɔ Tso Dzɔdzɔmefɔkuwo Ŋu?
ENGLISH: What Does the Bible Say About Natural Disasters?

EWE: Ale si Biblia ɖo eŋui
ENGLISH: The Bible’s answer

EWE: Menye Mawu gbɔe dzɔdzɔmefɔku siwo dzɔna egbea la tso o, gake etsɔa ɖe le eme na ame siwo ŋu dzɔdzɔmefɔkuwo gblẽ nu le.
ENGLISH: God does not cause the natural disasters occurring today, but he is concerned about people who are affected by them.

EWE: Gake fifia gɔ̃ hã la, Mawu faa akɔ na ame siwo ŋu dzɔdzɔmefɔkuwo gblẽ nu le.
ENGLISH: Natural disasters are one of the causes of suffering that God’s Kingdom will eliminate.

EWE: 2 Korintotɔwo 1:3. Nu ka tae míate ŋu aka ɖe edzi be dzɔdzɔmefɔkuwo menye tohehe tso Mawu gbɔ o?
ENGLISH: In the meantime, God provides comfort for those who are affected by natural disasters.​ 2 Corinthians 1:3.

EWE: Ðe dzɔdzɔmefɔkuwo nye dzesi be míele ŋkeke mamlɛawo mea?
ENGLISH: Why can we be sure that natural disasters are not punishment from God?

EWE: Aleke Mawu kpena ɖe ame siwo ŋu dzɔdzɔmefɔkuwo gblẽ nu le la ŋu?
ENGLISH: Are natural disasters a sign of the times?

EWE: Ðe Biblia ate ŋu akpe ɖe mía ŋu be míadzra ɖo ɖe dzɔdzɔmefɔkuwo ŋua?
ENGLISH: How does God help victims of natural disasters?

EWE: Nu ka tae míate ŋu aka ɖe edzi be dzɔdzɔmefɔkuwo menye tohehe tso Mawu gbɔ o?
ENGLISH: Can the Bible help with natural-disaster preparedness?

EWE: Mawu zã dzɔdzɔmeŋusẽwo tsɔ he to na amewo le blema.
ENGLISH: Bible verses to comfort victims of natural disasters

EWE: Gake ne Mawu zã dzɔdzɔmeŋusẽwo tsɔ he to na amewo la, ekpɔa egbɔ be ame vɔ̃ɖiwo koe tsrɔ̃na.
ENGLISH: Why can we be sure that natural disasters are not punishment from God?

EWE: (1 Mose 19:29, 30) Mawu kpɔ du mawo me tɔwo ƒe dziwo me, eye wòtsrɔ̃ ame siwo wòkpɔ be wovɔ̃ɖi la ɖeɖe ko.
ENGLISH: Natural disasters differ from God’s use of natural forces, as recorded in the Bible.

EWE: Zi geɖe la, dzɔdzɔmefɔkuwo dzɔna le vo me.
ENGLISH: Natural disasters kill and maim indiscriminately.

EWE: Gake hafi Mawu nazã dzɔdzɔmeŋusẽwo atsɔ ahe to na ame vɔ̃ɖiwo la, exlɔ̃a nu wo do ŋgɔ.
ENGLISH: In contrast, God’s acts of judgment recorded in the Bible were selective.

EWE: Eya ta mɔnukpɔkpɔ sua ame siwo ɖo to nuxlɔ̃amea la si be woasi le afɔkua nu.
ENGLISH: For example, when God destroyed the ancient cities of Sodom and Gomorrah, he spared the good man Lot and his two daughters.
(Genesis 19:29, 30) God read the hearts of the individuals of that time and destroyed only those he deemed wicked.​ Genesis 18:23-​32; 1 Samuel 16:7.

EWE: Amegbetɔwo ƒe nuwɔnawo hã le eme tae dzɔdzɔmefɔkuwo dzɔna alo gblẽa nu le amewo ŋu.
ENGLISH: On the other hand, God gave warnings to the wicked before using natural forces against them.

EWE: Le mɔ ka nu?
ENGLISH: How?

EWE: Wogblẽa dzɔdzɔmenuwo dome eye wotua xɔ ɖe teƒe siwo anyigbaʋuʋu, tsiɖɔɖɔ kple ya sesẽwo ate ŋu agblẽ nu le bɔbɔe.
ENGLISH: By damaging the natural environment and by building in areas prone to earthquakes, floods, and extreme weather.

EWE: (Nyaɖeɖefia 11:18) Mele be míabu fɔ Mawu ɖe tiatia mawo siwo amewo wɔna la ta o. Lododowo 19:3.
ENGLISH: (Revelation 11:18) God is not to blame for such human choices.​ Proverbs 19:3.

EWE: Ðe dzɔdzɔmefɔkuwo nye dzesi be míele ŋkeke mamlɛawo mea?
ENGLISH: Are natural disasters a sign of the times?

EWE: Ɛ̃, Biblia gblɔe ɖi be afɔkuwo adzɔ le "nuɖoanyia ƒe nuwuɣi, " alo "ŋkeke mamlɛawo me. "
ENGLISH: Yes, Bible prophecies suggest that there would be disasters during "the conclusion of the system of things, " or "the last days. "

EWE: (Mateo 24:3; 2 Timoteo 3:1) Le kpɔɖeŋu me, Yesu gblɔ tso míaƒe ŋkekea ŋu be: "Nuɖuɖu ave le teƒeteƒewo, eye anyigba aʋuʋu le teƒeteƒewo. "
ENGLISH: (Matthew 24:3; 2 Timothy 3:1) For example, concerning our time, Jesus said: "There will be food shortages and earthquakes in one place after another. "

EWE: (Mateo 24:7) Eteƒe madidi o, Mawu aɖe dzɔdzɔmefɔkuwo kple nu siwo katã nana míesea veve eye míekpea fu la ɖa le anyigba dzi. Nyaɖeɖefia 21:3, 4.
ENGLISH: (Matthew 24:7) Soon, God will rid the earth of all causes of pain and suffering, including natural disasters.​ Revelation 21:​3, 4.

EWE: Aleke Mawu kpena ɖe ame siwo ŋu dzɔdzɔmefɔkuwo gblẽ nu le la ŋu?
ENGLISH: How does God help victims of natural disasters?

EWE: Mawu toa eƒe Nya, Biblia, dzi faa akɔ na ame siwo ŋu dzɔdzɔmefɔkuwo gblẽ nu le.
ENGLISH: God comforts victims with his Word, the Bible.

EWE: Biblia ka ɖe edzi na mí be Mawu tsɔ ɖe le eme na mí eye wòsea veve ɖe mía nu ne míele fu kpem.
ENGLISH: The Bible assures us that God cares for us and that he feels for us when we suffer.

EWE: (Yesaya 63:9; 1 Petro 5:6, 7) Biblia na míekpɔe hã be Mawu do ŋugbe be ɣeyiɣi aɖe ava si me dzɔdzɔmefɔkuwo magadzɔ azɔ o. Kpɔ aɖaka si nye " Mawunyakpukpui siwo ate ŋu afa akɔ na ame siwo ŋu dzɔdzɔmefɔkuwo gblẽ nu le. "
ENGLISH: (Isaiah 63:9; 1 Peter 5:​6, 7) It also reveals his promise of a time when natural disasters will not happen anymore.​ See " Bible verses to comfort victims of natural disasters. "

EWE: Mawu toa esubɔlawo dzi kpena ɖe ame siwo ŋu dzɔdzɔmefɔkuwo gblẽ nu le la ŋu.
ENGLISH: God helps victims by means of his worshippers.

EWE: Mawu ʋãa esubɔla siwo le anyigba dzi be woasrɔ̃ kpɔɖeŋu si Yesu ɖo.
ENGLISH: God uses his worshippers on earth to imitate the example set by Jesus.

EWE: Biblia gblɔe ɖi be Yesu afa akɔ na "ame siwo ƒe dzi gbã " kple "konyifalawo katã. "
ENGLISH: It was prophesied that Jesus would comfort "the brokenhearted " and "all who mourn. "

EWE: (Yesaya 61:1, 2) Mawu subɔlawo hã dzea agbagba be yewoawɔ nenema ke. Yohanes 13:15.
ENGLISH: (Isaiah 61:​1, 2) Worshippers of God strive to do the same.​ John 13:15.

EWE: Mawu gatoa esubɔlawo dzi naa kpekpeɖeŋu siwo hiã la ame siwo ŋu dzɔdzɔmefɔkuwo gblẽ nu le. Dɔwɔwɔwo 11:28-30; Galatiatɔwo 6:10.
ENGLISH: God also uses his worshippers to provide practical relief to victims of natural disasters.​ Acts 11:28-30; Galatians 6:​10.

EWE: Yehowa Ðasefowo le aƒe aɖe dzram ɖo le Puerto Rico
ENGLISH: Jehovah’s Witnesses repair a home in Puerto Rico

EWE: Yehowa Ðasefowo le kpekpeɖeŋu nam ame siwo ŋu ahom sesẽ aɖe gblẽ nu le le Puerto Rico
ENGLISH: Jehovah’s Witnesses providing practical relief to hurricane victims in Puerto Rico

EWE: Ðe Biblia ate ŋu akpe ɖe mía ŋu be míadzra ɖo ɖe dzɔdzɔmefɔkuwo ŋua?
ENGLISH: Can the Bible help with natural-disaster preparedness?
Yes.

EWE: Togbɔ be menye dzadzraɖo ɖe dzɔdzɔmefɔkuwo ŋu tae woŋlɔ Biblia ɖo o hã la, mɔfiamewo le eme siwo ate ŋu akpe ɖe mía ŋu.
ENGLISH: Although the Bible is not a manual for disaster preparedness, it contains principles that can help.

EWE: Wo dometɔ aɖewoe nye esiawo:
ENGLISH: For example:

EWE: Nɔ dzadzraɖoɖi ɖe afɔkuwo ŋu.
ENGLISH: Plan ahead for potential disasters.

EWE: Biblia gblɔ be: "Aɖaŋudzela kpɔa afɔku gbɔna eye wòɣlaa eɖokui. "
ENGLISH: "The shrewd one sees the danger and conceals himself, " says the Bible.

EWE: (Lododowo 22:3) Nunya le eme be míadzra ɖo ɖe afɔkuwo ŋu do ŋgɔ.
ENGLISH: (Proverbs 22:3) We are wise to prepare an emergency plan in advance.

EWE: Dzadzraɖo do ŋgɔ abia be nàƒo nu vevi siwo nàhiã ne afɔku dzɔ kpata la nu ƒu ɖe akplo me ahana wòanɔ asitsɔƒe na wò, eye wò kple wò ƒomea miadzro nu me ahalɔ̃ ɖe afi si miava do go le ne afɔku dzɔ la dzi.
ENGLISH: Such planning may include assembling an emergency kit that is ready to go in case of an emergency and rehearsing with one’s family where to meet if a disaster occurs.

EWE: Agbea nenɔ vevie na wò wu kesinɔnuwo.
ENGLISH: Value life over possessions.

EWE: Biblia gblɔ be: "Míetsɔ naneke va xexea me o, eye míate ŋu atsɔ naneke adzoe hã o. " (1 Timoteo 6:7, 8) Ele be míanɔ klalo be míagblẽ míaƒe aƒe kple kesinɔnuwo ɖi ale be míasi le afɔku nu.
ENGLISH: The Bible acknowledges: "We have brought nothing into the world, and neither can we carry anything out. " (1 Timothy 6:​7, 8) We need to be willing to leave our home and possessions in order to escape disaster.

EWE: Ehiã be míaɖo ŋku edzi be míaƒe agbe le vevie wu nunɔamesi ɖe sia ɖe. Mateo 6:25.
ENGLISH: We do well to remember that our life is more important than any material things.​ Matthew 6:​25.

EWE: Mawunyakpukpui siwo ate ŋu afa akɔ na ame siwo ŋu dzɔdzɔmefɔkuwo gblẽ nu le
ENGLISH: Bible verses to comfort victims of natural disasters

EWE: 1 Mose 18:25: ‘Meka ɖe edzi be Mawu mawɔ nu ma, awu ame dzɔdzɔe kple ame vɔ̃ɖi siaa gbeɖe o.
ENGLISH: Genesis 18:25: "It is unthinkable that [God] would act in this manner by putting the righteous man to death with the wicked one . . .

EWE: Ðe anyigba blibo la ƒe Ʋɔnudrɔ̃la la mawɔ nu dzɔdzɔe oa?’
ENGLISH: Will the Judge of all the earth not do what is right? "

EWE: Nu si wòfia: Mawu wɔa nu si le eteƒe ɣesiaɣi; mele be míabu fɔe ne ame nyuiwo ku le dzɔdzɔmefɔkuwo me o.
ENGLISH: Meaning: God always does what is right; he is not to blame when good people die because of natural disasters.

EWE: Psalmo 46:1, 2: "Mawu nye míaƒe sitsoƒe kple míaƒe ŋusẽ, eyae nye xɔnametɔ si li ɖaa le xaxaɣiwo.
ENGLISH: Psalm 46:​1, 2: "God is our refuge and strength, a help that is readily found in times of distress.

EWE: Esia tae míavɔ̃ o, togbɔ be anyigba la ƒe nɔnɔme le tɔtrɔm hã. "
ENGLISH: That is why we will not fear, though the earth undergoes change. "

EWE: Nu si wòfia: Nu ka kee ɖadzɔ le afi si míele o, míate ŋu aɖo ŋu ɖe Mawu ŋu be wòakpe ɖe mía ŋu míanɔ te sesĩe.
ENGLISH: Meaning: No matter what may happen around us, God is a reliable Source of strength.

EWE: Yesaya 63:9: "Le woƒe vevesesewo katã me la, eya hã se veve. "
ENGLISH: Isaiah 63:9: "During all their distress it was distressing to him. "

EWE: Nu si wòfia: Mawu sea veve ɖe mía nu ne míele fu kpem.
ENGLISH: Meaning: God has empathy​ he feels for us when we suffer.

EWE: Yohanes 5:28, 29: "Gaƒoƒo la gbɔna, esime ame siwo katã le ŋkuɖodziyɔdowo me la ase [Yesu ƒe] gbe, eye woado go. "
ENGLISH: John 5:​28, 29: "The hour is coming in which all those in the memorial tombs will hear [Jesus’] voice and come out. "

EWE: Nu si wòfia: Míele mɔ kpɔm be míava kpɔ míaƒe ame vevi siwo ku la ake, elabena Mawu ana ŋusẽ Yesu be wòafɔ wo ɖe tsitre.
ENGLISH: Meaning: We can have the hope of seeing our dead loved ones again because God will empower Jesus to bring them back to life.

EWE: 1 Petro 5:6, 7: "Eya ta mibɔbɔ mia ɖokui ɖe Mawu ƒe asi sesẽ la te . . . esime miedro miaƒe dzimaɖitsitsiwo katã ɖe edzi, elabena eléa be na mi. "
ENGLISH: 1 Peter 5:​6, 7: "Humble yourselves, therefore, under the mighty hand of God . . . while you throw all your anxiety on him, because he cares for you. "

EWE: Nu si wòfia: Mawu tsɔ ɖe le eme na mí vevie eye wòdi be míado gbe ɖa na ye tso míaƒe dzimaɖitsitsiwo ŋu.
ENGLISH: Meaning: God has deep concern for us and wants us to pray to him about our anxieties.

EWE: Nyaɖeɖefia 21:4: "[Mawu] atutu aɖatsi sia aɖatsi ɖa le woƒe ŋkume, eye ku maganɔ anyi akpɔ o, konyifafa kple ɣlidodo kpakple vevesese hã maganɔ anyi o.
ENGLISH: Revelation 21:4: "[God] will wipe out every tear from their eyes, and death will be no more, neither will mourning nor outcry nor pain be anymore.

EWE: Nu siwo nɔ anyi tsã la nu va yi. "
ENGLISH: The former things have passed away. "

EWE: Nu si wòfia: Mawu aɖe dzɔdzɔmefɔkuwo kple nu siwo katã nana míekpea fu la ɖa.
ENGLISH: Meaning: God will eliminate all causes of suffering, including natural disasters.

EWE: Lãmesẽ
ENGLISH: Health

EWE: Ðe Mawu tsɔ ɖe le míaƒe lãmesẽnyawo mea?
ENGLISH: Does God care about how we treat our bodies?

EWE: "Meganɔ wain tsu nolawo kple lã tsu ɖulawo dome o. "
ENGLISH: "Do not come to be among heavy drinkers of wine, among those who are gluttonous eaters of flesh. "

EWE: Lododowo 23:20.
ENGLISH: Proverbs 23:20.

EWE: NU KA TAE WÒLE VEVIE?
ENGLISH: WHY DOES IT MATTER?

EWE: Biblia menye atikewɔgbalẽ o; eye mede se ku ɖe amegbetɔ ƒe agbemenuwɔna ɖe sia ɖe hã ŋu o.
ENGLISH: The Bible is not a medical textbook; nor does it regulate every aspect of human behavior.

EWE: Ke hã ale si Mawu bua lãmesẽnyawoe xexlẽ le Biblia me aɖe vi na wò.
ENGLISH: Still, you can benefit from understanding God’s view of health as expressed in the Bible.

EWE: NU SI BIBLIA GBLƆ
ENGLISH: WHAT THE BIBLE SAYS

EWE: Mawunyakpukpui geɖe ƒo nu tso ale si Mawu bua ale si míewɔa nu ɖe míaƒe ŋutilã ŋu la ŋu.
ENGLISH: Numerous Bible passages shed light on how God feels about the way we treat our bodies.

EWE: Le kpɔɖeŋu me, Biblia ƒo nu tsi tre ɖe nu siwo ate ŋu agblẽ nu le míaƒe ŋutilã ŋu, abe ahamumu kple nu tsu ɖuɖu ene ŋu.
ENGLISH: For instance, the Bible condemns harmful excesses, including drunkenness and gluttony.

EWE: (Lododowo 23:20) Se si Mawu de na blema Israel dukɔa dometɔ aɖewo ku ɖe nu siwo woawɔ atsɔ alé dɔlélewo nu alo axe mɔ ɖe wo nu kura la ŋu.
ENGLISH: (Proverbs 23:20) God’s Law code given to ancient Israel included measures that would control and in some cases even prevent diseases.

EWE: Dedienɔnɔ ŋuti mɔfiame aɖewo koŋ le Sea me siwo akpe ɖe ame ŋu wòaƒo asa na afɔkuwo.
ENGLISH: The Law also incorporated specific safety regulations for the prevention of injuries.

EWE: (5 Mose 22:8) Edze kɔtɛe be Biblia de dzi ƒo na mí be míalé be na mía ɖokuiwo eye míaɖe afɔ siwo sɔ atsɔ akpɔ míaƒe lãmesẽ ta.
ENGLISH: (Deuteronomy 22:8) Clearly, the Bible encourages us to take care of our bodies and take reasonable measures to protect our health.

EWE: Le Biblia ƒe nya nu la, nu ka gbɔe wòtso be míedzea dɔ?
ENGLISH: According to the Bible, why do we get sick?

EWE: "To ame ɖeka dzi nu vɔ̃ ge ɖe xexea me, eye to nu vɔ̃ me ku la va. "
ENGLISH: "Through one man sin entered into the world and death through sin. "

EWE: Romatɔwo 5:12.
ENGLISH: Romans 5:12.

EWE: NYA SI AMEWO GBLƆNA
ENGLISH: WHAT PEOPLE SAY

EWE: Ame geɖe xɔe se be dɔléle nye nane si dzɔ le eɖokui si esime amegbetɔwo nɔ tɔtrɔm.
ENGLISH: Many believe that sickness is simply a quirk of human evolution.

EWE: Ame bubuwo susui be vivimeŋusẽwo, abe gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃wo ene, gbɔe míaƒe lãmesẽkuxiwo tsona.
ENGLISH: Others think that mysterious forces, such as evil spirits, are the cause of our health problems.

EWE: NYA SI BIBLIA GBLƆ
ENGLISH: WHAT THE BIBLE SAYS

EWE: Le Biblia ƒe nya nu la, esi amegbetɔ gbãtɔwo dze aglã ɖe Mawu ŋu tae míedzea dɔ ɖo.
ENGLISH: According to the Bible, we get sick as a result of the first human rebellion against God.

EWE: (Romatɔwo 5:12) Mía dzila gbãtɔ Adam kple Xawa nɔ lãmesẽ blibo me hafi wova dze aglã ɖe Mawu ŋu.
ENGLISH: (Romans 5:12) Before their rebellion, our first parents, Adam and Eve, enjoyed perfect health.

EWE: Wonyae be ne yewogbe Mawu ƒe beléname si me lɔlɔ̃ le la, yewoaku.
ENGLISH: They knew that they would die if they withdrew from God’s loving care.

EWE: (1 Mose 2:16, 17) Ke hã woɖoe koŋ tso xɔlɔ̃wɔwɔ si nɔ wo kple Mawu dome la me, ale wobu woƒe blibodedea.
ENGLISH: (Genesis 2:16, 17) Still, they willfully severed their friendship with God and lost their perfection.

EWE: Míenyi blibomademade ƒe dome tso mía dzila gbãtɔ siwo dze aglã ɖe Mawu ŋu la gbɔ.
ENGLISH: The flawed nature of our rebellious first human parents has been passed on to us.

EWE: Eya ta togbɔ be ameƒomea le agbagba dzem kpem be yeaɖe dɔléle ɖa hã la, gbeɖegbeɖea koe.
ENGLISH: Hence, despite all efforts to eliminate human maladies, we still get sick.

EWE: NU KAE NÀWƆ?
ENGLISH: WHAT CAN YOU DO?

EWE: Biblia fia nu be ne èwɔ ɖe Mawu ƒe mɔfiame siwo me nunya le dzi tsɔ dzra wò kplii dome ɖo la, àva nɔ agbe le paradiso me le anyigba dzi le lãmesẽ blibo me.
ENGLISH: The Bible teaches that if you become reconciled to God by obeying his wise principles, you will eventually enjoy perfect health in an earthly paradise.

EWE: (Yesaya 33:24) Mawu do ŋugbe be yeaɖe vevesese, dɔléle kple ku ɖa.
ENGLISH: (Isaiah 33:24) God promises to eliminate pain, sickness, and death.

EWE: Nyaɖeɖefia 21:3, 4.
ENGLISH: Revelation 21:3, 4.

EWE: Ðe Biblia xe mɔ ɖe atikewɔwɔ nua?
ENGLISH: Does the Bible discourage medical treatment?

EWE: "Ame siwo le lãmesẽ me la mehiã atikewɔla o, gake ame siwo le dɔ lém la hiãe. "
ENGLISH: "Persons in health do not need a physician, but the ailing do. "

EWE: Mateo 9:12.
ENGLISH: Matthew 9:12.

EWE: NYA SI AMEWO GBLƆNA
ENGLISH: WHAT PEOPLE SAY

EWE: Ame aɖewo gblɔna be gbɔgbɔmegbedada (si wogayɔna be xɔsegbedada) la nyo wu atikewɔwɔ.
ENGLISH: Some promote spiritual healing (also known as faith healing) over medical treatment.

EWE: NYA SI BIBLIA GBLƆ
ENGLISH: WHAT THE BIBLE SAYS

EWE: Mawu ɖe mɔ atikewɔlawo nɔ eƒe ame siwo nɔ anyi le Biblia ƒe ɣeyiɣiwo me la dome.
ENGLISH: God allowed health-care practitioners to operate among his people in Bible times.

EWE: (1 Mose 38:28; Kolosetɔwo 4:14) Naneke mele Biblia me si ɖee fia be Mawu mekpɔ ŋudzedze ɖe atikewɔla mawo ƒe gbewo, dɔmiwo kple nuɖuɖu aɖewo koŋ tsitsri kple dɔdamɔnu bubuwo zazã ŋu o.
ENGLISH: (Genesis 38:28; Colossians 4:14) There is nothing in the Bible that would indicate that God was displeased with their use of medicinal plants, ointments, prescribed diets, and other health treatments.

EWE: Le nyateƒe me la, Yesu gblɔ be "ame siwo le lãmesẽ me la mehiã atikewɔla o, gake ame siwo le dɔ lém la hiãe. "
ENGLISH: In fact, Jesus acknowledged that "persons in health do not need a physician, but the ailing do. "

EWE: Mateo 9:12.
ENGLISH: Matthew 9:12.

EWE: Ke hã Biblia meda asi ɖe dɔdamɔnu ɖe sia ɖe ƒomevi dzi o.
ENGLISH: Yet, the Bible does not endorse the pursuit of health at all costs.

EWE: Le kpɔɖeŋu me, Biblia meda asi ɖe xɔsegbedada siwo li egbea la dzi o.
ENGLISH: For instance, the Bible does not endorse the modern-day practice of faith healing.

EWE: Eye Mawu meda asi ɖe dɔdamɔnu siwo lɔ gbɔgbɔyɔyɔ ɖe eme hã dzi o.
ENGLISH: And cures that involve spiritistic practices are not approved by God.

EWE: (Galatiatɔwo 5:19-21) To vovo na dɔdamɔnu siwo Biblia tsri la, nu nyuitɔ si wòle be míawɔ ne míedze dɔe nye be míadi dɔdamɔnu si sɔ kaba ne ɖe li.
ENGLISH: (Galatians 5:19-21) Aside from practices that the Bible condemns, the sensible thing to do when faced with infirmities would be to seek appropriate health care promptly, if it is available.

EWE: Nu Siwo Nàwɔ Be Nànɔ Lãmesẽ Me Wu
ENGLISH: Ways to Improve Your Health

EWE: AME kae dina be yealé dɔ?
ENGLISH: WHO wants to be sick?

EWE: Dɔléle doa nuxaxa na ame eye wògblẽa ga na ame hã.
ENGLISH: At the very least, an illness is an inconvenience and an expense.

EWE: Ana be dzi madzɔ wò o, eye màte ŋu ayi suku alo awɔ dɔ akpɔ ga o, eye màte ŋu akpɔ wò ƒomea dzi hã o.
ENGLISH: You not only feel bad, but when you are sick, you may not be able to go to work or school, earn any money, or look after your family.

EWE: Ahiã gɔ̃ hã be ame aɖe nakpɔ dziwò eye nàzã ga gbogbo aɖe ɖe atikewo kple dɔdada ŋu.
ENGLISH: You may even need someone to look after you, and you may have to pay for expensive medicines and treatment.

EWE: Màte ŋu aƒo asa na dɔléle aɖewo ya o.
ENGLISH: Well has it been said that "Prevention is better than cure. "

EWE: Gake nu geɖewo li nàte ŋu awɔ be dɔlélewo makpɔ ŋusẽ boo ɖe dziwò o alo aƒo asa na wo keŋkeŋ.
ENGLISH: Some illnesses cannot be avoided.

EWE: Elabena dzeaʋaɖia, aʋa mesinɛ o.
ENGLISH: Still, there is much you can do to slow down or even prevent the onset of illness.

EWE: Kpɔ nu atɔ̃ siwo nàte ŋu awɔ tso egbea dzi be nànɔ lãmesẽ me la ɖa.
ENGLISH: Consider five things that you can do today to get on the road to better health.

EWE: 1 WƆ NU SI ANA NÀNƆ DZADZƐE
ENGLISH: 1 PRACTICE GOOD HYGIENE

EWE: Nu siwo wozãna tsɔ kpɔa ŋutilãmedzadzɛnyenye gbɔ
ENGLISH: Items used for good physical and dental hygiene

EWE: Kɔdzi si woyɔna be Mayo gblɔ be, "mɔ nyuitɔ siwo dzi ame ato aƒo asa na dɔlélewo kple dɔlékuiwo kaka la dometɔ ɖekae " nye asikɔklɔ.
ENGLISH: According to the Mayo Clinic, "one of the best ways to avoid getting sick and spreading illness " is to wash your hands.

EWE: Mɔ siwo dzi ame tona xɔa kpeƒoame alo dzamezã ƒe dɔlékuiwo bɔbɔe ye nye be wòatsɔ asi si ŋu dɔlékuiwo le anɔ ŋɔtinu alo ŋku lilim.
ENGLISH: One of the easiest ways to catch a cold or influenza is to rub your nose or your eyes when your hands have been contaminated by germs.

EWE: Mɔ nyuitɔ si dzi nàto aƒo asa na esia ye nye be nànɔ asi klɔm edziedzi.
ENGLISH: Your best defense against such contamination is to wash your hands regularly.

EWE: Beléle na ame ɖokui ahanɔ dzadzɛe ate ŋu axe mɔ ɖe dɔ vɔ̃ɖi aɖewo kaka nu, wo dometɔ aɖewoe nye axamedɔ kple mitsinyenyedɔwo, dɔ siawo wua ɖevi siwo mekpɔ xɔ ƒe atɔ̃ haɖe o la dometɔ miliɔn eve aɖewo ƒe sia ƒe.
ENGLISH: Good hygiene can also prevent the spread of more serious conditions, such as pneumonia and diarrheal diseases, which every year cause the death of over two million children under the age of five.

EWE: Asikɔklɔ ate ŋu aɖe dɔ vɔ̃ɖi si ŋkɔe nye Ebola gɔ̃ hã ƒe kaka dzi akpɔtɔ.
ENGLISH: Even the spread of deadly Ebola can be minimized by the simple habit of washing hands.

EWE: Asikɔklɔ le vevie le ɣeyiɣi aɖewo koŋ me be míakpɔ míawo ŋutɔwo kple ame bubuwo ƒe lãmesẽ ta.
ENGLISH: There are certain times when hand washing is particularly important to protect your own health and that of others.

EWE: Ele be nàklɔ asi:
ENGLISH: You should wash your hands:

EWE: Ne ède afɔdzi.
ENGLISH: After using the toilet.

EWE: Ne èɖɔli godui na viwò alo ne ede afɔdzi nèkpɔ egbɔ.
ENGLISH: After changing diapers or helping a child to use the toilet.

EWE: Hafi nàkpɔ abi gbɔ, eye ne èkpɔ abia gbɔ vɔ hã.
ENGLISH: Before and after treating a wound or a cut.

EWE: Hafi nàyi dɔnɔ aɖe gbɔ, eye ne èdzo le egbɔ hã.
ENGLISH: Before and after being with someone who is sick.

EWE: Hafi nàɖa nu, nàtsɔ nuɖuɖu aɖo kplɔ̃e alo aɖu nu.
ENGLISH: Before preparing, serving, or eating food.

EWE: Ne ènyè, èkpe kpe alo fi mitsi.
ENGLISH: After sneezing, coughing, or blowing your nose.

EWE: Ne èka asi lã aɖe ŋu alo lãmi aɖe ŋu.
ENGLISH: After touching an animal or animal waste.

EWE: Ne èbla gbeɖuɖɔ alo tsɔe ƒu gbe.
ENGLISH: After handling garbage.

EWE: Mele be nàklɔ asi ɖewoɖewoe o.
ENGLISH: And do not take it for granted that you are cleaning your hands properly.

EWE: Numekukuwo ɖee fia be ame siwo yia dugazewo la dometɔ akpa gãtɔ meklɔa asi nyuie ne wode afɔdzi o eye ame aɖewo meklɔnɛ gɔ̃ hã o.
ENGLISH: Studies have shown that a large percentage of those who use public toilets do not wash their hands afterward or do not wash them correctly.

EWE: Aleke wòle be nàklɔ asie?
ENGLISH: How should you wash your hands?

EWE: Kɔ tsi dzadzɛ ɖe asi dzi eye nàwɔ adzalẽ ɖe asi me.
ENGLISH: Wet your hands in clean running water and apply soap.

EWE: Nɔ asiawo klɔm, ɖo ŋku edzi nàɖe fetuwo kple degblefetsuwo me nyuie, klɔ wò asimegbewo kple asitomewo.
ENGLISH: Rub your hands together to make a lather, not forgetting to clean your nails, your thumbs, the backs of your hands, and between your fingers.

EWE: Wɔe sekɛnd 20 ya teti.
ENGLISH: Keep rubbing for at least 20 seconds.

EWE: Azɔ kɔ tsi ɖe asi dzi nàkpalae.
ENGLISH: Rinse in clean running water.

EWE: Tsɔ asitutunu kɔkɔe alo pepatakuvi tutu asi.
ENGLISH: Dry with a clean cloth or a paper towel.

EWE: Mɔnu siawo le bɔbɔe gake woate ŋu akpɔ tawò tso dɔléle si me eye wòakpɔ wò agbe ta.
ENGLISH: Such measures are simple but can avert illness and save lives.

EWE: 2 ZÃ TSI SI LE DZADZƐE
ENGLISH: 2 USE A SAFE WATER SUPPLY

EWE: Kɔpo si me tsi dzadzɛ le kple dɔŋuti tsotsoe
ENGLISH: A glass of clean water and pieces of lemon

EWE: Le dukɔ aɖewo me la, avu kple kɔe wònyena na ƒome aɖewo be woakpɔ tsi nyui azã.
ENGLISH: Obtaining sufficient clean water for one’s family is a regular chore in some countries.

EWE: Ke hã, tsi nyui kpɔkpɔ ate ŋu azu kuxi le xexemedukɔ ɖe sia ɖe me, elabena tɔɖɔɖɔ, ahom, pɔmpiwo ƒe gbagbã kple nu bubuwo ate ŋu ana tsi nyui siwo amewo nona la me naƒo ɖi.
ENGLISH: Yet, access to clean water can become a concern in any part of the world when a main supply that is usually good to drink becomes contaminated as a result of a flood, a storm, a pipe break, or some other issue.

EWE: Ne afi si wokpɔa tsiawo tso alo nu siwo me wokɔa wo ɖo me mele dzadzɛe o la, ate ŋu ana amewo nalé dɔ siwo nye koléra, mitsinyenyedɔ siwo tea ŋu wua ame, asrã sesẽ, aklãdɔ kple dɔléle bubuwo.
ENGLISH: If water does not come from a safe source or is not stored correctly, it can cause parasite infestation, as well as cholera, life-threatening diarrhea, typhoid, hepatitis, and other infections.

EWE: Wobu akɔnta be tsi nyui ƒe anyimanɔmanɔ nana ame miliɔn 1,700 xɔa mitsinyenyedɔwo ƒe sia ƒe.
ENGLISH: Unsafe drinking water is one of the causes of an estimated 1.7 billion cases of diarrheal disease every year.

EWE: Nu geɖewo li nàte ŋu awɔ be dɔlélewo makpɔ ŋusẽ boo ɖe dziwò o alo nàƒo asa na wo keŋkeŋ
ENGLISH: There is much you can do to slow down or prevent the onset of illness

EWE: Zi geɖe la, amewo xɔa koléra nenye be wono tsi siwo me ame siwo ŋuti dɔ sia le la de afɔdzi ɖo alo ɖu nu siwo tsi siawo ƒomevi ƒo ɖii.
ENGLISH: Cholera is most often contracted when a person drinks water or eats food that is contaminated with fecal matter from infected people.

EWE: Nu kawoe nàte ŋu awɔ atsɔ akpɔ ɖokuiwò ta tso dɔ sia kple bubuwo si me nenye be dzɔdzɔmefɔkuwo dzɔ teti gɔ̃ hã?
ENGLISH: What steps can you take to protect yourself, even in the immediate aftermath of a disaster, from this and other types of water contamination?

EWE: Kpɔ egbɔ be tsi siwo nèzãna na numekɔklɔ, nuɖuɖuwo kple agbawo kɔklɔ, nuɖaɖa alo tsikpewɔwɔ la le dzadzɛe, ate ŋu anye pɔmpitsi si woléa be na nyuie alo aŋetukpametsi siwo adzɔha siwo ŋu kakaɖedzi le la wɔ.
ENGLISH: Ensure that all your drinking water including the water used for brushing teeth, making ice, washing food and dishes, or cooking comes from a safe source, such as an adequately treated public supply or sealed bottles from a reputable firm.

EWE: Ne ewɔ na wò be yewoƒe pɔmpitsia mele dzadzɛe o la, ke ɖa tsia alo de atike siwo wua dɔlékui le tsi me la tsia me hafi nàzãe.
ENGLISH: If there is any possibility that your piped supply has been contaminated, boil your water before use or treat it with an appropriate chemical product.

EWE: Ne èbe yeazã atike siwo wotsɔ dzaa tsi me abe klorine kple esia tɔgbi ene la, wɔ ɖe atikeawo wɔlawo ƒe mɔfiamewo dzi pɛpɛpɛ.
ENGLISH: When using chemicals, such as chlorine or water-purifying tablets, follow the maker’s directions carefully.

EWE: Zã tsitsyɔnu adodoewo ne ɖe li alo ne womexɔ asi fũu akpa o.
ENGLISH: Use quality water filters, if available and affordable.

EWE: Ne nu siwo wotsɔ dzaa tsi me meli o la, ke de ɖiɖetike (bleach alo l’eau de Javel) gege toŋtoŋ eve ɖe tsi lita ɖeka me, blu tsia me nyuie, eye nàda tsia ɖi miniti 30 hafi nàzãe.
ENGLISH: If no water-treatment products are available, add household bleach, eight drops per gallon of water (two drops per liter), mix well, and then let the water stand for 30 minutes before using it.

EWE: Kɔ tsi nyuiwo alo tsi siwo nèɖa la ɖe nu siwo me kɔ me eye nàtu nu wo nu nyuie ale be dɔlékui aɖeke nagage ɖe wo me o.
ENGLISH: Always store treated water in clean, covered containers to protect it from possible recontamination.

EWE: Kpɔ egbɔ be nu sia nu si nàtsɔ aku tsi le tsigoa me la le dzadzɛe.
ENGLISH: Ensure that any vessel used to take water from your stored supply, such as a ladle, is clean.

EWE: Asiwò nekɔ hafi nàlé nu siwo me tsi dzadzɛwo le eye mègade asi tsi nono me o.
ENGLISH: Handle water containers with clean hands, and do not dip your hands or fingers into water used for drinking.

EWE: 3 LÉ ŊKU ÐE WÒ NUÐUÐUWO ŊU
ENGLISH: 3 WATCH WHAT YOU EAT

EWE: Agblemenuku nyui vovovowo
ENGLISH: A variety of wholesome foods from different food groups

EWE: Mímate ŋu anɔ lãmesẽ me ne mímeɖua nu nyuie o, eye nuɖuɖu nyuie bia be míaɖu nu siwo me nunyiame vovovowo le.
ENGLISH: Good health is impossible without good nutrition, and for good nutrition you need a healthy, balanced diet.

EWE: Ele be nàlé ŋku ɖe dze, ami, sukli kple nuɖuɖu agbɔsɔsɔme si nèɖuna ŋu.
ENGLISH: You may need to consider your intake of salt, fats, and sugar, and you should watch your portion sizes.

EWE: Nɔ atikutsetsewo kple amagbewo ɖum, eye nɔ nu vovovowo ɖum.
ENGLISH: Include fruits and vegetables in your diet, and vary what you eat.

EWE: Ne èxlẽa nu siwo woŋlɔ ɖe nuɖuɖuwo abe yevubolo, nukuwo, makaroni alo mɔlu ene dzi hafi ƒlea wo la, akpe ɖe ŋuwò nàtia nuɖuɖu siwo wowɔ kple nuku blibowo.
ENGLISH: Reading the packaging will help you to select whole-grain foods when buying bread, cereals, pasta, or rice.

EWE: Nunyiame kple ŋutilãtuɖonu geɖe nɔa nuɖuɖu siwo wotsɔ nuku blibowo wɔ la me wu nuɖuɖu siwo wotsɔ nuku siwo ŋu wotrɔ asi le la wɔ.
ENGLISH: These are richer in nutrients and fiber than the alternatives made from refined grain.

EWE: Ðu ʋulã alo koklolã ƒe akpa siwo ami menɔna o la ƒe sue aɖe eye nàdze agbagba aɖu tɔmelã zi eve le kwasiɖaa me ne anya wɔ.
ENGLISH: As for proteins, eat small and lean portions of meat and poultry and try to eat fish a couple of times a week, if possible.

EWE: Le dukɔ aɖewo me la, woate ŋu akpɔ nunyiame siwo nɔa lãwo me le amagbewo hã me.
ENGLISH: In some lands it is also possible to find protein-rich foods from vegetable sources.

EWE: Ne èɖua suklinu alo aminu akpa la, ate ŋu ana nàlolo.
ENGLISH: If you eat too many sugars and solid fats, you risk becoming overweight.

EWE: Eya ta no tsi ɖe aha viviwo teƒe.
ENGLISH: To minimize this risk, drink water instead of sweet beverages.

EWE: Ðu atikutsetse geɖe wu numeɖenu viviwo.
ENGLISH: Eat more fruit instead of sugary desserts.

EWE: Ðe sausage (saucisse), ʋulã, nyinotsi babla kple akpɔnɔviviwo ɖuɖu dzi kpɔtɔ ale be ami magasɔ gbɔ ɖe lãme na wò o.
ENGLISH: Limit your intake of solid fats from such items as sausages, meat, butter, cakes, cheese, and cookies.

EWE: Le esi nàzã ami kpekewo atsɔ aɖa nu teƒe la, zã ami siwo dea lãmesẽ dzi boŋ.
ENGLISH: And instead of using solid fats for cooking, you may want to use healthier oils.

EWE: Dzeɖuɖu fũu ate ŋu ana nàxɔ ʋusɔgbɔdɔ.
ENGLISH: Too much salt, or sodium, in the diet can raise your blood pressure to an unhealthy level.

EWE: Eya ta ne èɖua dze fũu la, ke xlẽ nu si woŋlɔ ɖe nuɖuɖuawo ƒe akpa dzi ne nàkpɔ dze agbɔsɔsɔ si wode wo me ale be dze nagasɔ gbɔ fũu ɖe lãme na wò o.
ENGLISH: If this is your problem, use the information on food packaging to keep your sodium intake low.

EWE: Eya ta zã amagbewo kple nu ʋeʋĩwo ɖe dze teƒe.
ENGLISH: Instead of salt, use herbs and spices to flavor your meals.

EWE: Nu agbɔsɔsɔ si nèɖuna hã le vevie ko abe nu siwo nèɖuna ke ene.
ENGLISH: How much you eat can be as important as what you eat.

EWE: Eya ta ne nuɖuɖua le nuwò vivim hã la, mègayi eɖuɖu dzi ne èɖi ƒo o.
ENGLISH: So, while enjoying your food, do not keep eating after you are no longer hungry.

EWE: Nu bubu si ŋu wòle be nàlé ŋku ɖo le wò nuɖunyawo gome hãe nye nuɖuɖu siwo me dɔlékuiwo le.
ENGLISH: An issue tied to nutrition is the risk of food poisoning.

EWE: Ne womeɖa nuwo nyuie alo lé be na wo nyuie o la, dɔlékuiwo ate ŋu anɔ wo me agblẽ nu le ŋuwò.
ENGLISH: Any food can poison you if it is not prepared and stored properly.

EWE: Ƒe sia ƒe la, Amerikatɔ 1 le 6 me xɔa dɔlékuiwo le nu siwo woɖuna me.
ENGLISH: Every year, 1 out of every 6 Americans falls sick from food poisoning.

EWE: Wo dometɔ akpa gãtɔ hayana ya, gake wo dometɔ aɖewo hã kuna.
ENGLISH: Most recover without lasting ill effects, but some die from it.

EWE: Nu kae nàte ŋu awɔ atsɔ aɖe afɔku sia dzi akpɔtɔ?
ENGLISH: What can you do to minimize the risk?

EWE: Wotea ŋu tsɔa lãmiwo nyroa anyigba hafi doa amagbewo ɖe wo dzi, eya ta hafi nàɖu amagbewo la, klɔ wo nyuie.
ENGLISH: Vegetables grow in soil that may have been treated with manure, so wash these items carefully before preparing them.

EWE: Tsɔ tsi dzodzoe kple adzalẽ klɔ asi, nuɖanuwo kple agbawo nyuie eye nàklɔ kplɔ̃wo kple nu siwo dzi nètso nuɖuɖu aɖe le la dzi nyuie hafi nàgazãe na nu bubu le nua ɖaɣi.
ENGLISH: Wash your hands, cutting board, utensils, dishes, and countertops with hot, soapy water before preparing each item.

EWE: Be nàƒo asa na dɔlékuiwo kaka la, mègada nuɖuɖu ɖe nu si dzi nèda nuɖuɖu siwo womeɖa o abe koklozi mumu, koklolã, ʋulã kple tɔmelãwo ene la dzi ne mèklɔ edzi o.
ENGLISH: To avoid cross-contamination, never put food on a surface or plate that was previously in contact with raw eggs, poultry, meat, or fish, without first washing that surface.

EWE: Ða nuwo woabi nyuie, eye nàde nuɖuɖu siwo gblẽna kaba siwo màɖu enumake o la nufamɔ̃ me.
ENGLISH: Cook until the food reaches the right temperature, and promptly refrigerate any perishable items that are not going to be eaten immediately.

EWE: Tsɔ nuɖuɖu siwo gblẽna kaba dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe si wogblẽ ɖe nuvo wòwu gaƒoƒo eve la ƒu gbe, eye ne wogblẽ nuɖuɖu aɖe ɖe nuvo ɖe afi si yame ƒe dzoxɔxɔ sɔ gbɔ wu Celsius 32 wòde gaƒoƒo ɖeka la, tsɔe ƒu gbe.
ENGLISH: Discard perishable items left at room temperature for more than two hours or one hour if air temperature exceeds 90 degrees Fahrenheit (32°C).

EWE: 4 NƆ KAME DEM
ENGLISH: 4 STAY PHYSICALLY ACTIVE

EWE: Bɔl kple bɔlƒofɔkpa eve
ENGLISH: A soccer ball and a pair of soccer shoes

EWE: Ƒe ka kee nèɖaxɔ o, ehiã be nànɔ kame dem be nànɔ lãmesẽ me.
ENGLISH: Regardless of your age, you need regular physical activity to stay in good shape.

EWE: Egbea la, ame geɖewo medea kame fũu o.
ENGLISH: Many people today do not exercise enough.

EWE: Nu ka tae kamedede le vevie?
ENGLISH: Why is exercise important?

EWE: Kamedede ate ŋu:
ENGLISH: Staying physically active can help you to:

EWE: Ana nàdɔ alɔ̃ nyuie.
ENGLISH: Sleep well.

EWE: Ana agbe nanɔ mewò.
ENGLISH: Stay mobile.

EWE: Ana be ŋusẽ nanɔ wò ƒuwo kple lãkusiwo ŋu.
ENGLISH: Maintain strong bones and muscles.

EWE: Ana be mànɔ lolom ɖe edzi o.
ENGLISH: Maintain or achieve a healthy weight.

EWE: Aɖe blanuiléle dzi akpɔtɔ.
ENGLISH: Lower your risk of suffering from depression.

EWE: Aɖe kukpokuku dzi akpɔtɔ.
ENGLISH: Lower your risk of premature death.

EWE: Ne mèdea kame o la, ate ŋu:
ENGLISH: If you do not stay physically active, you are more likely to:

EWE: Ana be nàxɔ dzidɔ.
ENGLISH: Suffer from heart disease.

EWE: Ana nàxɔ suklidɔ alo aɖuɖɔvividɔ.
ENGLISH: Suffer from type 2 diabetes.

EWE: Ana nàxɔ ʋusɔgbɔdɔ.
ENGLISH: Develop high blood pressure.

EWE: Ana be ami nasɔ gbɔ ɖe lãme na wò.
ENGLISH: Develop high cholesterol.

EWE: Ana nàxɔ gbagbadɔ.
ENGLISH: Suffer a stroke.

EWE: Kamedefefe si asɔ na wò la anɔ te ɖe ƒe si nèxɔ kple wò lãmesẽ dzi. Eya ta anyo be nàdzro eme kple wò ɖɔkta hafi nàte kamedefefe yeyewo kpɔ.
ENGLISH: The kind of physical activity that is right for you depends on your age and your health, so it would be wise to consult your doctor before beginning any new exercise program.

EWE: Atikeŋutinunyala geɖewo ɖo aɖaŋu be ele be ɖeviwo kple sɔhɛwo nakpɔ gome le kamedefefe bɔbɔewo kple sesẽwo siaa me miniti 60 ya teti gbe sia gbe.
ENGLISH: According to various recommendations, children and adolescents should get at least 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous activity every day.

EWE: Eye ame tsitsiwo ya nakpɔ gome le kamedefefe bɔbɔewo me miniti 150 alo kamedefefe sesẽwo me miniti 75 kwasiɖa sia kwasiɖa.
ENGLISH: Adults should get 150 minutes of moderate activity or 75 minutes of vigorous activity every week.

EWE: Tia kamedefefe si doa dzidzɔ na wò.
ENGLISH: Choose an activity that is fun.

EWE: Wo dometɔ aɖewoe nye baskɛtbɔlƒoƒo, tenis-ƒoƒo, afɔbɔlƒoƒo, azɔlizɔzɔ sesĩe, gasɔdodo, abɔdɔwɔwɔ, nakedzedze, tsiƒuƒu, tɔdziʋukuku, duƒuƒu kple bubuwo.
ENGLISH: You might consider basketball, tennis, soccer, brisk walking, cycling, gardening, chopping wood, swimming, canoeing, jogging, or other aerobic exercise.

EWE: Aleke nàwɔ ade vovototo kamedefefe bɔbɔewo kple kamedefefe sesẽwo dome?
ENGLISH: How can you tell whether an activity is moderate or vigorous?

ENGLISH: At first, Juliza was pessimistic about her lot in life.

EWE: Gake etrɔ eƒe susu.
ENGLISH: But that changed.

EWE: Nu kae kpe ɖe eŋu?
ENGLISH: What helped?

EWE: Juliza gblɔ be, "Hafi dzinyelawo nawɔ asitɔtrɔ le woƒe agbenɔnɔ ŋu wòanyo la, Biblia kpe ɖe ŋunye mɔkpɔkpɔ su asinye le agbe me.
ENGLISH: "Even before my parents overcame their difficulties, " Juliza says, "the Bible helped me to improve my outlook.

EWE: Va se ɖe egbea la, Biblia me nyawo kpena ɖe ŋunye be nyemebua dziɖeleameƒonuwo ŋu o.
ENGLISH: And to this day, thoughts from the Bible keep my thinking from spiraling downward.

EWE: Fifia ne amewo ɖe nɔnɔme manyomanyo aɖe fia la, medzea agbagba be mase nu si ta wowɔ nu nenema ɖo la gɔme. "
ENGLISH: Now, when people display traits I don’t like, I try to understand why they behave the way they do. "

EWE: Abe ale si Juliza va srɔ̃e ene la, mɔfiame nyui geɖewo le Biblia me.
ENGLISH: As Juliza learned, the Bible is a book of sound principles.

EWE: Eƒe aɖaŋuɖoɖowo ate ŋu akpe ɖe ŋuwò nànɔ te ɖe nɔnɔme madeamedziwo nu.
ENGLISH: Its advice can help you to cope with negative circumstances.

EWE: Le kpɔɖeŋu me, Biblia gblɔ le Efesotɔwo 4:23 be: "Minɔ miaƒe tamesusu ƒe nɔnɔme si kpɔa ŋusẽ ɖe mia dzi wɔm yeyee. "
ENGLISH: For example, Ephesians 4:23 says: "Continue to be made new in your dominant mental attitude. "

EWE: Abe ale si mawunyakpukpui sia gblɔe ene la, àte ŋu awɔ nane le wò nɔnɔmewo ŋu.
ENGLISH: As that verse implies, your outlook is not set in stone.

EWE: Àte ŋu anɔ nɔnɔme si kpɔa ŋusẽ ɖe dziwò la "wɔm yeyee. "
ENGLISH: You can "be made new " in your thinking.

EWE: Eya ta tɔtrɔwo wɔwɔ nye nu si wòle be nànɔ wɔwɔm ɖaa.
ENGLISH: However, making such a change is an ongoing process.

EWE: Esia tae mawunyakpukpuia gblɔ be míayi edzi anɔ míaƒe ‘tamesusu ƒe nɔnɔme si kpɔa ŋusẽ ɖe mía dzi wɔm yeyee.’
ENGLISH: That is why the verse says that we should "continue to be made new. "

EWE: 2 WÒ SUSU NÈNƆ NU NYUIWO ŊU
ENGLISH: 2 FOCUS ON THE POSITIVE

EWE: BIBLIA GBLƆ BE: "Ame si le fu kpem la ƒe ŋkekewo katã nye vɔ̃, ke ame si ƒe dzi le dzidzɔ kpɔm la tua aglo ɣesiaɣi. "
ENGLISH: THE BIBLE SAYS: "All the days of the afflicted one are bad, but the one with a cheerful heart has a continual feast. "

EWE: Lododowo 15:15.
ENGLISH: Proverbs 15:15.

EWE: NU SI WÒFIA: Ne èbua nɔnɔme ɖe sia ɖe be made ame dzi o la, ekema "nuxaxa " axɔ aƒe ɖe mewò eye ŋkeke sia ŋkeke anye "vɔ̃ " na wò.
ENGLISH: WHAT IT MEANS: If you see everything negatively, you will feel "afflicted " and every day will appear "bad, " or gloomy.

EWE: Gake ne wò susu le nu nyuiwo ŋu la, wò ‘dzi akpɔ dzidzɔ’ eye àtso aseye gɔ̃ hã.
ENGLISH: But if you focus on positive things, you will have "a cheerful heart " and even feel joyful.

EWE: Wò ŋutɔe awɔ tiatiaa.
ENGLISH: The choice is yours.

EWE: Yanko
ENGLISH: Yanko

EWE: KPƆÐEŊU: Wowɔ dɔ heɖe nutete le ahɔhɔ̃ me na Yanko zi geɖe. Eye esia gblẽ nu le eƒe lãmesẽ kple nuƒoƒo ŋu.
ENGLISH: EXAMPLE: After several surgeries to remove a brain tumor, Yanko had physical limitations that affected his movement and speech.

EWE: Esi Yanko kpɔe be esia awɔe be yemaɖo yeƒe taɖodzinuwo gbɔ o la, dzi ɖe le eƒo hena ƒe geɖe.
ENGLISH: Feeling that these would stop him from reaching his goals, Yanko was deeply discouraged for years.

EWE: Emegbe etrɔ susu.
ENGLISH: Then he changed.

EWE: Aleke wòtrɔe?
ENGLISH: How?

EWE: Egblɔ be, "Le esi teƒe be mana nye susu nanɔ nɔnɔme madeamedziwo ŋu la, mesrɔ̃ ale si manɔ nu siwo ade dzi ƒo nam la ŋu bum boŋ. "
ENGLISH: "Instead of focusing on my limitations, " he says, "I learned to occupy my mind with encouraging subjects. "

EWE: Mɔ ɖeka aɖe si dzi wòwɔna esia toe nye ale si wòxlẽa Biblia me nyawo.
ENGLISH: One way Yanko does this is by reading passages from the Bible.

EWE: Egblɔ be: "Esia naa nye susu nɔa nu nyuiwo ŋu.
ENGLISH: "This keeps my thoughts positive, " he says.

EWE: Nyemeŋlɔ taɖodzinu siwo gbɔ medi be maɖo le etsɔme la be o, gake nye susu le esiwo gbɔ mate ŋu aɖo fifia la ŋu.
ENGLISH: "I haven’t totally put aside my long-term goals, but I’m focusing on the smaller goals that I can reach now.

EWE: Ne dziɖeleameƒonuwo va susu me nam la, medea ŋugble tsoa susu geɖe siwo ta wòle be makpɔ dzidzɔ ɖo la ŋu. "
ENGLISH: When discouraging thoughts creep into my mind, I reflect on the many reasons I have to be happy. "

EWE: Abe ale si Yanko wɔe ene la, àte ŋu adzudzɔ dziɖeleameƒonuwo ŋu bubu ahanɔ nu siwo ade dzi ƒo na wò la ŋu bum.
ENGLISH: Like Yanko, you can confront your pessimistic thoughts and replace them with something positive.

EWE: Ne èle akɔ kpem kple nɔnɔme sesẽwo ɖewohĩ lãmesẽkuxiwo abe Yanko ene la, bia ɖokuiwò be: ‘Ðe nɔnɔmea nye esi ŋu nyemate ŋu awɔ naneke le kura oa?
ENGLISH: If you are dealing with negative circumstances perhaps a health problem, as was the case with Yanko ask yourself: ‘Is the situation really hopeless?

EWE: Ðe wòvɔ nama, alo mɔxenu aɖe koe wònyea?’
ENGLISH: Have I reached a dead end, or is this merely a roadblock?’

EWE: Srɔ̃ ale si nàdzudzɔ dziɖeleameƒonuwo ŋu bubu ahanɔ nu siwo atu wò ɖo boŋ la ŋu bum.
ENGLISH: Learn to keep negative thoughts out by concentrating on something constructive.

EWE: 3 WƆ NU SI AÐE VI NA AMEWO
ENGLISH: 3 DO THINGS FOR OTHERS

EWE: BIBLIA GBLƆ BE: "Dzidzɔ geɖe le nunana me wu nuxɔxɔ. "
ENGLISH: THE BIBLE SAYS: "There is more happiness in giving than there is in receiving. "

EWE: Dɔwɔwɔwo 20:35.
ENGLISH: Acts 20:35.

EWE: NU SI WÒFIA: Nunana amewo tso dzi me faa naa ame kpɔa dzidzɔ.
ENGLISH: WHAT IT MEANS: Unselfish giving brings deep satisfaction to the giver.

EWE: Nu ka tae?
ENGLISH: Why?

EWE: Elabena wowɔ mí be míawɔ nu wòaɖe vi na amewo wu be míaƒe susu nanɔ míawo ŋutɔwo ƒe nuhiahiãwo ko ŋu.
ENGLISH: Because we were created to do more than simply look after our own needs.

EWE: (Filipitɔwo 2:3, 4; 1 Yohanes 4:11) Dzidzɔ si míakpɔ tso nunana amewo me ate ŋu akpe ɖe mía ŋu míanɔ te ɖe nɔnɔme sesẽ siwo míado goe le agbe me la nu.
ENGLISH: (Philippians 2:3, 4; 1 John 4:11) Experiencing the joy of giving can do much to help us cope with negative circumstances in life.

EWE: Josué
ENGLISH: Josué

EWE: KPƆÐEŊU: Dzimeƒudɔ sesẽ aɖe ɖe fu na Josué.
ENGLISH: EXAMPLE: Josué suffers from spina bifida, a severe defect in his spinal column.

EWE: Esia na wòsea veve ale gbegbe.
ENGLISH: He is often racked with pain.

EWE: Gake Josué wɔa nu si ɖea vi na amewo si naa wòkpɔa dzidzɔ.
ENGLISH: But Josué enjoys a productive life helping others.

EWE: Josué gblɔ be, "le esi magblɔ be, ‘nyemate ŋu awɔ esi kple ekemɛ o’ teƒe la, mebua mɔ ŋutɔŋutɔ siwo dzi mato akpe ɖe amewo ŋu gbe sia gbe la ŋu.
ENGLISH: "Rather than say, ‘I can’t do that,’ " says Josué, "I enjoy thinking of practical ways to help people with their daily needs.

EWE: Media mɔ siwo dzi mato awɔ nu siwo aɖe vi na amewo, eye esia naa mekpɔa dzidzɔ. "
ENGLISH: I find ways to do things for others, and this fills my life with happiness. "

EWE: NU SI NÀTE ŊU AWƆ
ENGLISH: WHAT YOU CAN DO

EWE: Josué le dzidzɔ kpɔm kple ƒome aɖe esime wòle agba klɔm
ENGLISH: Josué washes dishes while he enjoys the company of a young family

EWE: Di mɔ siwo dzi nàto akpe ɖe amewo ŋu.
ENGLISH: Look for opportunities to be self-sacrificing.

EWE: Le kpɔɖeŋu me, ɖe nàte ŋu aɖa nu na aƒelika aɖe si dze dɔa?
ENGLISH: For example, can you prepare a meal for a sick neighbor?

EWE: Ðe nàte ŋu akpe ɖe ame tsitsi aɖe si hiã kpekpeɖeŋu be wòadzra eƒe aƒe me ɖo la ŋua?
ENGLISH: Do you know elderly ones who need help with tasks around the home?

EWE: Trɔ asi le wò nɔnɔme ŋu wòanyo ɖe edzi abe ale si nànɔ be lém na abɔ ene.
ENGLISH: Care for your attitude in the same way you would cultivate a garden.

EWE: Ho aɖigbe siwo nye dziɖeleameƒonuwo ɖa le susu me.
ENGLISH: Root out the poisonous weeds of pessimism and negativity.

EWE: Eye nàƒã nu nyui siwo anɔ wò tum ɖo si ana nɔnɔme nyui nanɔ asiwò.
ENGLISH: Sow seeds of realistic optimism, and fertilize your life with actions that produce positive emotions.

EWE: Ne èwɔe alea la, àŋe nu siwo awɔe be nàkpɔ dzidzɔ le agbe me.
ENGLISH: You will reap an emotional crop that will make your life much more rewarding.

EWE: Eye esia aɖo kpe edzi be nɔnɔme si anɔ asiwò ye ana nàkpɔ dzidzɔ.
ENGLISH: And it will confirm the fact that attitude makes a difference!

EWE: Ame aɖewo dzudzɔ nanewo ɖuɖu le woƒe lãmesẽ ta, nenema ke wò hã àte ŋu aɖe asi le nɔnɔme manyomanyowo ŋu
ENGLISH: For the sake of their health, some people learn to say no to certain foods; you can do the same with negative attitudes

EWE: Míaƒe Seselelãmewo
ENGLISH: Emotional Health

EWE: Biblia xlɔ̃ nu mí tso seselelãme siwo ate ŋu agblẽ nu le mía ŋu la ŋu, eye wòde dzi ƒo na mí be míatu esiwo aɖe vi na mí la ɖo.
ENGLISH: The Bible warns against emotions that are harmful and encourages us to cultivate those that are beneficial.

EWE: DZIKU
ENGLISH: ANGER

EWE: BIBLIA ƑE MƆFIAME: "Ame si gbɔa dzi ɖi blewu la nyo wu kalẽtɔ. " Lododowo 16:32.
ENGLISH: BIBLE PRINCIPLE: "The one slow to anger is better than a mighty man. "​ Proverbs 16:32.

EWE: NU SI WÒFIA: Ne míetea ŋu ɖua míaƒe seselelãmewo dzi la, eɖea vi na mí.
ENGLISH: WHAT IT MEANS: We benefit when we develop the strength to control our emotions.

EWE: Togbɔ be asɔ ɣeaɖewoɣi be míado dziku hã la, ne míeɖua míaƒe dziku dzi o la, egblẽa nu.
ENGLISH: Although some anger may be justified at times, uncontrolled anger is destructive.

EWE: Numekuku siwo wowɔ nyitsɔ laa ɖo kpe edzi be ne ame aɖe do dziku la, zi geɖe la, egblɔa nya alo wɔa nu siwo va venɛ emegbe.
ENGLISH: Modern researchers point out that in the heat of the moment, angry people often say or do things that they will later regret.

EWE: NU SI NÀTE ŊU AWƆ: Srɔ̃ ale si nàɖu wò dziku dzi hafi wòana nàwɔ nu gbegblẽ.
ENGLISH: WHAT YOU CAN DO: Learn to control your anger before it controls you.

EWE: Togbɔ be ame geɖe bua dzikudodo be ènye kalẽwɔwɔ hã, míawo ya míenyae be gbɔdzɔgbɔdzɔ ƒe dzesi boŋue wònye.
ENGLISH: While some people think that uncontrolled anger is a sign of strength, we are wise to recognize that it is really a sign of weakness.

EWE: Biblia gblɔ be: "Ame si meɖua eƒe dziku dzi o la le abe du si ŋu wogbã gli le wòtsi nuvo ene. "
ENGLISH: "As a city broken through, without a wall, is the man who cannot control his temper, " says the Bible.

EWE: (Lododowo 25:28) Mɔ ŋutɔŋutɔ aɖe si dzi nàto aɖu wò dziku dzie nye be nànya nyateƒe bliboa hafi aɖe afɔ.
ENGLISH: (Proverbs 25:28) A practical way to control your anger is to get the facts before reacting.

EWE: "Ame si sea nu gɔme nyuie la, medoa dziku kabakaba o. "
ENGLISH: "The insight of a man certainly slows down his anger. "

EWE: (Lododowo 19:11) Anyo be míanya nyaa ƒe akpa sia akpa, esia ana míase nuwo gɔme nyuie eye wòana míalé mía ɖokui.
ENGLISH: (Proverbs 19:11) We do well to listen carefully to both sides of a matter, which may provide insight that can steady our emotions.

EWE: NYE AKPEDALA
ENGLISH: GRATITUDE

EWE: BIBLIA ƑE MƆFIAME: "Minye akpedalawo. " Kolosetɔwo 3:15.
ENGLISH: BIBLE PRINCIPLE: "Show yourselves thankful. "​ Colossians 3:15.

EWE: NU SI WÒFIA: Wogblɔna zi geɖe be ame siwo nye akpedalawo la kpɔa dzidzɔ.
ENGLISH: WHAT IT MEANS: It has been said that only a grateful person can be happy.

EWE: Ame siwo to nɔnɔme sesẽ aɖewo me kpɔ gɔ̃ hã lɔ̃ ɖe nya sia dzi.
ENGLISH: Even those who have gone through tremendous loss can attest to this.

EWE: Wogblɔ be nu si koŋ kpe ɖe yewo ŋu yewote ŋu nɔ te ɖe nɔnɔmea nue nye be menye nu siwo bu na yewo ŋue yewotsɔ susu ɖo o, ke ɖe nu siwo ta yewoate ŋu ada akpe ɖo boŋ ŋue.
ENGLISH: They point out that the key to their emotional survival has been to focus on​ not what they lost ​but what they have to be grateful for.

EWE: NU SI NÀTE ŊU AWƆ: Gbe sia gbe la, ŋlɔ nu siwo ta nàda akpe ɖo la ɖi.
ENGLISH: WHAT YOU CAN DO: Each day, make a list of the things that you are grateful for.

EWE: Mele be nu siawo nanye nu gãwo kokoko o.
ENGLISH: These do not have to be major things.

EWE: De ŋugble le nu suesuesuewo abe agu ƒe dzedze, dze nyui si wò kple ame vevi aɖe mieɖo, alo esi agbeŋu bubu gake ɖe wò ene ta.
ENGLISH: Reflect on even the small things, such as a beautiful sunrise, a pleasant conversation with a loved one, or simply having another day of life.

EWE: Ne èdea dzesi nu siawo eye nèbua wo ŋu hedaa akpe ɖe wo ta la, ana nàkpɔ dzidzɔ.
ENGLISH: These positive things can do much to boost your emotional health​ if you take the time to notice and appreciate them.

EWE: Aɖe vi geɖe ŋutɔ na wò ne èbu susu siwo tae nàda akpe ɖe wò ƒomea kple xɔ̃wòwo ta la ŋu.
ENGLISH: It can be especially beneficial to think about why you are grateful for your family and friends.

EWE: Ne ède dzesi nu si dzɔa dzi na wò tso amewo ŋu la, na woanya to egbɔgblɔ na amea ŋutɔ tẽe, to lɛta, e-mail alo to text message dzi.
ENGLISH: When you have identified what you appreciate about other people, tell them about it, either in person or in a letter, an e-mail, or a text message.

EWE: Esia ana wò kple amea ƒe ƒomedodo me nasẽ ɖe edzi, eye àkpɔ dzidzɔ si dona tsoa nunana me. Dɔwɔwɔwo 20:35.
ENGLISH: This will likely strengthen your relationships and enable you to experience the happiness that comes from giving.​ Acts 20:35.

ENGLISH: OTHER BIBLE PRINCIPLES

ENGLISH: A mother listens to an audio recording of the Bible while she folds her little girl’s clothes

ENGLISH: "Beginning a fight is like opening a floodgate; before the quarrel breaks out, take your leave. "​ PROVERBS 17:14.

ENGLISH: AVOID UNNECESSARY WORRY ABOUT THE FUTURE.

ENGLISH: "Never be anxious about the next day, for the next day will have its own anxieties.

ENGLISH: Physical Health and Resilience

ENGLISH: Ulf’s experience reminds us that none of us have complete control over our health.

ENGLISH: Still, we can take reasonable measures to reduce the risk of ill health.

ENGLISH: "Do not be among those who drink too much wine, among those who gorge themselves on meat, for a drunkard and a glutton will come to poverty. "​ Proverbs 23:20, 21.

ENGLISH: It reminds me that my suffering​ and the suffering of others as well ​is just temporary.

ENGLISH: Thinking about scriptures like that helps strengthen my faith in God’s promise of a bright future​ not just for those who suffer with chronic illnesses but for everyone.

ENGLISH: Jehovah ‘Daily Carries the Load for Me’

EWE: Maretha du Raan
ENGLISH: Maretha du Raan

ENGLISH: Despite an uncertain health condition that might have seemed unbearable, I have felt the loving support of our dear heavenly Father throughout my life.

ENGLISH: And for more than 20 years, I have found special joy serving Jehovah as a pioneer.

ENGLISH: Because the neural tube in my spine failed to close completely, nerve damage has made it difficult for me to walk and has caused other serious health problems.

ENGLISH: Some time before my birth, missionaries of Jehovah’s Witnesses started to study the Bible with my parents.

EWE: Eya ta míesrɔ̃a nu siwo woasrɔ̃ le hame ƒe kpekpewo me la abe ƒome ene.
ENGLISH: Hence, we considered the material for congregation meetings as a family.

ENGLISH: At age seven, I had a urostomy, an operation performed to create an artificial opening in my body so that I could pass urine.

EWE: Esi mexɔ ƒe 14 la, meva nɔ kpeŋuidɔ (adzigbo) hã lém.
ENGLISH: At age 14, I developed epilepsy.

EWE: Esi sekɛndrisuku (lycée) si le míaƒe nutoa me la didi tso mía gbɔ eye mehiã dzinyelawo ƒe beléle tɔxɛ ta la, nyemete ŋu wu enu o.
ENGLISH: Because the nearest high school was far away and I needed special care from my parents, I could not complete my schooling.

EWE: Ke hã, meɖoe be mana nye kple Yehowa dome ƒomedodoa me nasẽ.
ENGLISH: Nevertheless, I decided to fortify myself spiritually.

EWE: Wometa míaƒe Kristotɔwo ƒe agbalẽ geɖe ɖe mía degbe Afrikaans me o.
ENGLISH: Many of our Christian publications were not yet available in Afrikaans, my mother tongue.

ENGLISH: So I learned to read English in order to study a number of our books.

ENGLISH: I became a Kingdom publisher and got baptized at age 19.

ENGLISH: During the following four years, I had many health problems and emotional difficulties.

EWE: Tsɔ kpe ɖe eŋu la, esi kadodo kplikplikpli le míaƒe kɔƒea me tɔwo dome ta la, amegbetɔvɔvɔ̃ xe mɔ nam be nyemete ŋu nɔ geɖe wɔm le subɔsubɔdɔa me o.
ENGLISH: Moreover, in the close-knit community in my hometown, fear of man prevented me from having a zealous share in the ministry.

ENGLISH: During my early 20’s, we moved from Namibia to South Africa, and for the first time, I was able to associate with a congregation.

EWE: Dzidzɔ ka gbegbee nye esi!
ENGLISH: How wonderful that was!

ENGLISH: However, I had to undergo surgery again this time a colostomy.

EWE: Le ɣeyiɣi aɖe megbe la, mese nutome sue dzikpɔla ƒe nuƒo si woƒo tso mɔɖeɖedɔa wɔwɔ ŋu.
ENGLISH: Some time later, I heard a circuit overseer speak on the subject of pioneering.

EWE: Nya siwo wògblɔ la wɔ dɔ ɖe dzinye.
ENGLISH: His remarks touched my heart.

ENGLISH: I knew that my health was less than ideal, but I had seen how Jehovah had carried me through many difficulties.

ENGLISH: So I applied to be a regular pioneer.

EWE: Ke hã, metso nya me be mawɔ nye ŋutete katã le Fiaɖuƒegbeƒãɖeɖedɔa me.
ENGLISH: Still, I decided to give Kingdom preaching my best effort.

ENGLISH: With the help of my mother and others, I managed to devote pioneer hours to the ministry over a period of six months.

EWE: Esia ɖe ale si meɖoe kplikpaa be mawɔ mɔɖeɖedɔa fia, eye ena wòdze ƒãa be mate ŋu awɔe togbɔ be lãmesẽkuxiwo le ŋunye hã.
ENGLISH: That proved my determination to pioneer and showed that my health problems were manageable.

EWE: Megade asi mɔɖeɖedɔ ƒe dɔbiagbalẽvia te ake, eye fifia ya woda asi ɖe edzi.
ENGLISH: I applied again, and this time my application was approved.

EWE: Le September 1, 1988 dzi la, mezu gbesiagbe mɔɖela.
ENGLISH: On September 1, 1988, I became a regular pioneer.

EWE: Abe mɔɖela ene la, mekpɔa Yehowa ƒe ŋusẽdoame ɣesiaɣi.
ENGLISH: As a pioneer, I have constantly experienced Jehovah’s support.

EWE: Nyateƒea fiafia ame yeyewo kpɔ tanye, enyim, eye wòkpe ɖe ŋunye metsi le gbɔgbɔ me, ale be nyemetsɔa susu ɖoa nye nɔnɔmea ŋu o.
ENGLISH: Teaching new ones the truth instead of focusing on my own situation has protected me, nurtured me, and helped me to grow spiritually.

EWE: Mekpe ɖe ame gbogbo aɖewo ŋu woɖe adzɔgbe xɔ nyɔnyrɔ, eye esia he dzidzɔ manyagblɔ vɛ nam.
ENGLISH: I have derived immense joy from helping a number of individuals to dedication and baptism.

EWE: Nye lãmesẽnyawo tea ŋu trɔna kpata.
ENGLISH: My health remains uncertain.

ENGLISH: But Jehovah ‘daily carries the load for me.’

ENGLISH: My father made a swing for me, and I loved running around the garden.

ENGLISH: My mother started to weep.

ENGLISH: Though I understood little as a ten-year-old girl, I realized that the news was bad.

ENGLISH: On my arrival, the austere building dismayed me.

ENGLISH: The nuns found it hard to understand why I refused.

ENGLISH: I implored Jehovah not to abandon me, and I soon felt his protective arm around me, like the warm, firm hug of a loving father.

ENGLISH: Children normally could not have their own books, but the nuns allowed me to keep them along with my Bible, which I read every day.

EWE: Meɖoa dze tso mɔkpɔkpɔ si le asinye be mava nɔ agbe tegbee le Paradiso me le anyigba dzi, afi si ame aɖeke magadze dɔ le o, la ŋu na mía tɔ nyɔnuviawo.
ENGLISH: I also talked to other girls about my hope of living forever in the earthly Paradise, where nobody would get sick.

ENGLISH: (Revelation 21:3, 4) Despite feeling sad and lonely at times, I was glad that my faith and trust in Jehovah were growing stronger.

EWE: Ɣleti ade sɔŋ megbe la, ɖɔktawo ɖe asi le ŋunye be matrɔ ayi aƒe me.

ENGLISH: My illness had not relented, but I felt happy to be back with my parents.

ENGLISH: However, I sometimes felt disappointed in him. "Why me?

EWE: Mèle fu siwo kpem mele la kpɔm oa? "

ENGLISH: I fondly remember Alicia​ 20 years older than I am ​who became a true friend.

EWE: Ekpe ɖe ŋunye be maganɔ nye dɔlélea ŋu bum fũu akpa o, eye be matsɔ ɖe le eme na ame bubuwo tsɔ wu be manɔ nye kuxiwo ŋu bum atraɖii.
ENGLISH: She helped me to look beyond my illness and to take an interest in others rather than brooding on my own problems.

ENGLISH: But I asked Jehovah for help, and with support from my family and friends, I did it.

ENGLISH: That hectic month passed quickly, and I found that I had overcome my fears and embarrassment.

ENGLISH: I enjoyed it so much that in 1996 I decided to become a regular pioneer​ spending a set number of hours each month in the ministry.

ENGLISH: Often I close my eyes and open my private "window " into the new world that God promises

ENGLISH: So when someone loses his sight, he comes to rely more heavily on other senses​ hearing, smell, touch, and taste.

ENGLISH: As one of Jehovah’s Witnesses, how do you personally study the Bible?

EWE: Esi mɔ̃ɖaŋunu siwo ŋkunɔwo zãna mebɔ tsã o la, srɔ̃nye Loli xlẽa Biblia kple Biblia srɔ̃gbalẽwo nam.
ENGLISH: When technology for the blind was limited, Loli read the Bible and Bible study aids to me.

EWE: Srɔ̃nyea kpena ɖe ŋunye ale gbegbe.
ENGLISH: She was a great help.

EWE: Esia wɔnɛ be metea ŋu wɔa dɔdeasiwo le hamea ƒe kpekpewo me.
ENGLISH: As a result, I was even able to give talks at congregation meetings.

EWE: Gake fifia la, metea ŋu xlẽa nu le ɖokuinye si elabena Biblia kple Biblia-srɔ̃gbalẽ siwo wota na ŋkunɔwo la le asinye.
ENGLISH: Nowadays, though, I can read for myself because I have the Bible and study aids in Braille.

EWE: Metea ŋu yia Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe nyatakakadzraɖoƒe si nye jw.org ɖawɔa nu siwo woxlẽ lé ɖe mɔ̃ dzi ƒe kɔpiwo.
ENGLISH: I can also go to the website established by Jehovah’s Witnesses​ jw.org​ where I download audio recordings.

EWE: Nane le kɔmpiutaa ŋu na ŋkunɔwo si kpena ɖe ŋunye metea ŋu xlẽa nu siwo dzena le kɔmpiutaa dzi.
ENGLISH: And I have a Braille display, which enables me to read what is on my computer monitor.

EWE: Gavi suesuesue siwo nye ŋkunɔwo ƒe nuxexlẽdzesiwo dzena le nu sia si le kɔmpiuta ŋu la dzi.
ENGLISH: The display has small pins that pop up in groups to form Braille characters.

EWE: Enye nane si wɔ nuku ŋutɔ!
ENGLISH: It’s quite amazing!

EWE: Mɔnukpɔkpɔ nyui aɖe si su asinye ye nye ale si mekpea asi ɖe eŋu ne wole agbalẽwo wɔm na ŋkunɔwo le Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe alɔdzedɔwɔƒe si le Madrid, Spain.
ENGLISH: A privilege I have especially enjoyed is assisting with Braille transcription at the Spain branch office of Jehovah’s Witnesses in Madrid.

EWE: Esi wodi be agbalẽ siwo wɔm wole na ŋkunɔwo naɖe vi geɖe na wo ta la, ame siwo le ewɔm la biaa aɖaŋuɖoɖo tsoa ŋkunɔwo gbɔ.
ENGLISH: In order to improve the quality of Braille publications, those preparing them value suggestions from the blind.

EWE: Eya ta mate ŋu agblɔ tso dzi me be nye gbɔgbɔmenɔviwo lɔ̃m hedea asixɔxɔ ŋunye.
ENGLISH: So I can honestly say that I feel both loved and appreciated by my spiritual brothers and sisters.

EWE: Ðe hadede kple ame bubuwo doa dzidzɔ na wòa?
ENGLISH: Do you enjoy interacting with others?

EWE: Ɛ̃, vevietɔ nye ƒometɔ kplikplikpliwo kple hati Ðasefowo, ame siwo nye kpli wo míeyina ɖaɖea gbeƒã na amewo tso aƒe me yi aƒe me.
ENGLISH: Yes, especially with my immediate family and fellow Witnesses, with whom I also go out preaching from door to door.

EWE: Nye gbɔgbɔmenɔviwo wɔa nu ɖe ŋunye nyuie abe ale si wowɔa nu ɖe ame bubuwo ŋu ene.
ENGLISH: My spiritual brothers and sisters treat me the way they treat anybody else.

EWE: Le nyateƒe me la, ɣeaɖewoɣi la, woŋlɔna be be ŋkunɔe menye!
ENGLISH: In fact, they sometimes forget that I’m blind!

EWE: Tsɔ kpe ɖe eŋu la, gbeƒãɖeɖedɔa wɔwɔ naa megblɔa mɔkpɔkpɔ xɔasi si le Biblia me ŋu nya na amewo.
ENGLISH: I might add that the ministry enables me to share with others the precious hope found in the Bible.

EWE: Le kpɔɖeŋu me, Yesaya 35:5 gblɔ be ne Mawu Fiaɖuƒea va le anyigba dzi ɖum la, "ŋkuagbãtɔwo ƒe ŋku aʋu. "
ENGLISH: For example, at Isaiah 35:5, we read that under God’s Kingdom government, "the eyes of the blind will be opened. "

EWE: Esime Yesu nɔ anyigba dzi la, eʋu ŋku na ŋkunɔwo tsɔ ɖe nu si wòava wɔ le etsɔme fia.
ENGLISH: When Jesus Christ was on the earth, he cured the blind, giving us a preview of that future time.

EWE: (Mateo 15:30, 31) Ŋkutsitsi kple dɔléle bubu ɖe sia ɖe nu ayi kpuie.
ENGLISH: (Matthew 15:30, 31) Blindness, therefore, is a temporary problem, which is true of all disabilities.

EWE: Ne anyigba va zu Paradiso la, ame aɖeke magblɔ be ‘Mele dɔ lém alo menye nuwɔametɔ o.’ Yesaya 33:24; Luka 23:43.
ENGLISH: In the earthly Paradise to come, no one will say, ‘I am sick or disabled.’​ Isaiah 33:24; Luke 23:43.

EWE: Jairo Ƒe Ŋkuwoe Kpena Ðe Eŋu Wòsubɔa Mawu
ENGLISH: Jairo’s Eyes His Way to Serve God

EWE: Abe ale si nɔviaŋutsu Samuel Ruiz-León Arroyo gblɔe ene
ENGLISH: As told by his brother Samuel Ruiz-León Arroyo

EWE: Ðe nàte ŋu abu ale si agbea anɔ na wò nenye be màte ŋu aʋã wò abɔwo kple afɔwo o, negbe wò ŋkuwo ko ŋu kpɔa?
ENGLISH: Can you imagine having no control of your body except for your eyes?

EWE: Nɔnɔme ma mee nɔvinyeŋutsu Jairo le.
ENGLISH: My brother Jairo is in such a predicament.

EWE: Ke hã taɖodzinu le eƒe agbe ŋu.
ENGLISH: Yet, he enjoys a meaningful life.

EWE: Hafi maƒo nu tso nu si tae Jairo kpɔe be enyo be yele agbe ŋu la, anyo be magblɔ eƒe agbemeŋutinya.
ENGLISH: Before I explain why he has found his life to be worth living, let me tell you his story.

EWE: Esi wodzi Jairo la, ahɔhɔ̃medɔ si nye cerebral palsy, si nana ame ƒe abɔwo kple afɔwo siaa tuna, si woyɔna be spastic quadriplegia la, le eŋu.
ENGLISH: Jairo was born with a type of cerebral palsy called spastic quadriplegia.

EWE: Esia wɔe be mekpɔ ŋusẽ ɖe eƒe abɔɖeɖe kple afɔɖeɖe dzi o.
ENGLISH: As a result, he has no control over most of his body.

EWE: Eƒe ahɔhɔ̃ metea ŋu fiaa mɔ eƒe lãkusiwo o, eya ta eƒe afɔwo dana hetrona le wo ɖokui si.
ENGLISH: His brain cannot send clear signals to his muscles, so his limbs twist, or writhe, uncontrollably.

EWE: Ale si Jairo ƒe abɔwo kple afɔwo ŋutɔwo ʋãna le wo ɖokuiwo si alea nana wòwɔa nu vevi eɖokui ɣeaɖewoɣi.
ENGLISH: Sometimes, Jairo’s unpredictable jerking movements even cause him to hurt himself.

EWE: Ne ame siwo tsɔ ɖe egbɔ mele ŋudzɔ o la, ate ŋu awɔ nu vevi woawo hã.
ENGLISH: People nearby may also get hurt if they are not alert.

EWE: Nublanuitɔe la, ele be woabla eƒe abɔwo kple afɔwo ɖe eƒe bunɔkekea ŋu be wòagawɔ nu vevi amewo o.
ENGLISH: Sadly, his arms and legs must often be tied to his wheelchair to prevent such accidents.

EWE: FU SIWO WÒKPE ESI WÒNƆ TSITSIM
ENGLISH: PAINFUL PATH TO ADULTHOOD

EWE: Esi Jairo nɔ tsitsim la, ekpe fu ale gbegbe.
ENGLISH: Jairo’s physical growth has been very painful.

EWE: Esi wòxɔ ɣleti etɔ̃ ye eƒe dɔa ƒe dzesiwo dze egɔme; edzea ti eye esia nana wòyia ɖi me.
ENGLISH: When he was three months old, he started to have seizures that left him unconscious.

EWE: Zi geɖe la, Dada fanae ɖe akɔnu hedea afɔ du me yia kɔdzi. Eya ŋutɔ susuna be eku vɔ.
ENGLISH: All too often, Mum would hold him tightly and rush him to the hospital, convinced that he was dead.

EWE: Esi wònye be Jairo ƒe abɔwo kple afɔwo me hena hetrona ta la, ewɔe be eƒe ƒuwo glɔ̃.
ENGLISH: Because of all the tightening and contracting, in time Jairo’s bones became deformed.

EWE: Esi wòxɔ ƒe 16 la, eɖɔli eƒe aligo, si wɔe be ehiã be woawɔ dɔ sesẽ aɖe nɛ ako eƒe ata, ali, kple eƒe aligo siaa.
ENGLISH: At the age of 16, he dislocated his pelvis and required major surgery to his thigh, hip, and pelvis.

EWE: Megaɖoa ŋku ale si Jairo nɔa avi fam zã sia zã esi wonɔ hayahayam la dzi kokoko.
ENGLISH: I still remember Jairo crying out in pain every night during his recovery.

EWE: Jairo ƒe dɔa na be amewoe wɔa nu sia nu nɛ, abe nuɖuɖu, awudodo, kple ekɔkɔ ada ɖe aba dzi ene.
ENGLISH: Jairo’s severe disability makes him totally reliant on others to carry out daily functions, such as eating, getting dressed, and getting to bed.

EWE: Dada kple Papa ye kpɔa eƒe hiahiã mawo gbɔ nɛ.
ENGLISH: Mum and Dad usually perform these tasks.

EWE: Togbɔ be Jairo hiã kpekpeɖeŋu ɣeawokatãɣi hã, mía dzilawo ɖoa ŋku edzi nɛ ɣesiaɣi be menye amegbetɔwo si me koe eƒe agbe le o, ke boŋ Mawue lé eƒe agbe ɖe te.
ENGLISH: Though Jairo needs constant help, our parents always remind him that his life depends not only on humans but also on God.

EWE: WOVA KE ÐE DZEÐOÐO ƑE MƆNU AÐE ŊU
ENGLISH: A WAY OF COMMUNICATION OPENS

EWE: Yehowa Ðasefowoe mía dzilawo nye, eye woxlẽa Biblia me ŋutinyawo na Jairo tso eƒe ɖevime ke.
ENGLISH: Our parents are Jehovah’s Witnesses, and they have been reading Bible stories to Jairo ever since he was a baby.

EWE: Wonya nyuie be tameɖoɖo nɔa ame ƒe agbe ŋu wu ne ƒomedodo le woa kple Mawu dome.
ENGLISH: They always knew that life is more meaningful when one has a relationship with God.

EWE: Ðeko wòdzɔ be Jairo ƒe ametia, si ʋãna enuenu la mede edzi o, gake etsɔmemɔkpɔkpɔ nyui si ŋu kakaɖedzi le ate ŋu asu esi.
ENGLISH: Jairo was trapped in a frail body that jerked continually, but he could have a bright, solid hope for the future.

EWE: Ke hã womeka ɖe edzi nenye be Jairo ate ŋu ase Biblia me nyateƒea gɔme o.
ENGLISH: However, they often wondered if Jairo could grasp Bible knowledge.

EWE: Gbe ɖeka, le Jairo ƒe ɖevime la, Papa biae be, "Jairo, meɖe kuku, àte ŋu aƒo nu nama? "
ENGLISH: One day, when Jairo was a child, Dad asked him, "Jairo, can you please talk to me? "

EWE: Eyome wògblɔ nɛ be, "Ne èlɔ̃m vavã la, àƒo nu nam! "
ENGLISH: Then he added, "If you really love me, you will! "

EWE: Esi Papa ɖe kuku nɛ be wòagblɔ nya ɖeka pɛ ko na ye la, aɖatsi lólo ɖe ŋku dzi na Jairo enumake.
ENGLISH: As Dad begged him to say at least one word, tears welled up in Jairo’s eyes.

EWE: Togbɔ be Jairo dze agbagba be yeaɖe yeƒe seselelãmewo agblɔ hã la, ɖeko nàsee be ete gbe me.
ENGLISH: Though he tried to express his feelings with words, he could only mutter guttural sounds.

EWE: Ete ɖe Papa dzi be yena Jairo fa avi.
ENGLISH: Father felt bad for having made Jairo cry.

EWE: Ke hã nudzɔdzɔ ma na Papa kpɔe be Jairo se nya si yegblɔ la gɔme.
ENGLISH: But that reaction showed that Jairo understood what Father had said.

EWE: Gake kuxiae nye be mate ŋu aƒo nu o.
ENGLISH: The problem was that he could not speak.

EWE: Eteƒe medidi o, mía dzilawo de dzesii be ɣeaɖewoɣi la, Jairo ʋãa eƒe ŋkuwo kabakaba abe ɖe wòle agbagba dzem be yeagblɔ nya aɖe ene.
ENGLISH: Before long, our parents noticed that Jairo at times moved his eyes rapidly in an apparent attempt to convey his thoughts and feelings.

EWE: Etena ɖe Jairo dzi ŋutɔ be ame aɖeke metea ŋu sea nya si yedi be yeagblɔ la gɔme o.
ENGLISH: It was frustrating for Jairo that he could not always make himself understood.

EWE: Gake ne dzinyelawo te ŋu se dzesi siwo wɔm wòle kple nu si ta wòle ŋku ɖem ɖo gɔme la, enumake Jairo ɖoa nukomo gã aɖe.
ENGLISH: But when my parents learned to decipher his eye signals and get him what he needed, Jairo’s face would beam with a broad grin.

EWE: Ema dzi wòtona daa akpe na wo.
ENGLISH: It was his way of saying thank you.

EWE: Nuƒoƒoŋutete ŋuti aɖaŋuɖola aɖe ɖo aɖaŋu na mí be, be ƒomea nate ŋu aɖo dze kplii nyuie la, anyo be míado míaƒe asiwo ɖe dzi ne míele nya aɖe si ƒe ŋuɖoɖo anye ɛ̃ alo ao biamee.
ENGLISH: A speech therapist suggested that for better communication, we should raise both hands in the air when asking him a yes-or-no question.

EWE: Nuɖusi afia ɛ̃, eye miasi afia oa.
ENGLISH: The right hand means yes, the left hand no.

EWE: Ne míewɔe alea la, ana míanya nu si dim wòle ne etrɔ eƒe ŋkuwo ɖe abɔ si alo ekemɛ ŋu.
ENGLISH: Thus, he could express his wishes by fixing his eyes on the proper hand.

EWE: NU ÐEDZESI AÐE LE JAIRO ƑE AGBE ME
ENGLISH: A MILESTONE IN JAIRO’S LIFE

EWE: Yehowa Ðasefowo dea takpekpewo zi etɔ̃ le ƒea me, eye le takpekpe mawo me la, woƒoa nuƒo siwo me woɖea Biblia me na nyasela gbogbowo le.
ENGLISH: Three times a year, Jehovah’s Witnesses hold assemblies and conventions, where Bible talks are presented to large audiences.

EWE: Ɣesiaɣi si wole nuƒo siawo ƒomevi ƒom na ame siwo di be yewoaxɔ nyɔnyrɔ la, dzi dzɔa Jairo ale gbegbe.
ENGLISH: Jairo always got excited during the talk that was addressed to baptism candidates.

EWE: Gbe ɖeka, esime Jairo xɔ ƒe 16 la, Papa biae be, "Jairo, àdi be yeaxɔ nyɔnyrɔa? "
ENGLISH: One day, when Jairo was 16, Father asked him, "Jairo, do you want to get baptized? "

EWE: Ðeko wòtrɔ eƒe ŋkuwo ɖe Papa ƒe nuɖusi ŋu enumake, eye esia ɖee fia be edi be yeaxɔ nyɔnyrɔ.
ENGLISH: At once, his decisive look at Dad’s right hand revealed his desire to take that step.

EWE: Eyome Papa biae be, "Ðe nèdo gbe ɖa na Mawu hedo ŋugbe nɛ be yeasubɔe tegbeea? "
ENGLISH: Then Dad added, "Have you promised God in prayer to serve him forever? "

EWE: Jairo gatrɔ eƒe ŋkuwo ɖe Papa ƒe nuɖusi ŋu ake.
ENGLISH: Once again, Jairo gazed straight at Dad’s right hand.

EWE: Eme kɔ ƒãa be Jairo tsɔ eƒe agbe ɖe adzɔgbe na Yehowa xoxo.
ENGLISH: It was clear that Jairo had already dedicated his life to Jehovah.

EWE: Esi wowɔ Biblia me numedzodzro vovovowo kplii megbe la, esia hã ɖee fia be Jairo se nu si ta wòle vevie be Kristotɔ naxɔ nyɔnyrɔ la gɔme.
ENGLISH: After several Bible discussions, it was also clear that Jairo understood the significance of Christian baptism.

EWE: Esia wɔe be Jairo va ɖo biabia vevitɔ si wobiae kpɔ la ŋu, le ƒe 2004 me, esi wobiae be, "Ðe nètsɔ ɖokuiwò ɖe adzɔgbe na Mawu be yeawɔ eƒe lɔlɔ̃nua? "
ENGLISH: So, in 2004, he answered the most important question he was ever asked, "Have you dedicated yourself to God to do his will? "

EWE: Jairo trɔ eƒe ŋkuwo kpɔ dziƒo.
ENGLISH: Jairo answered this question by raising his eyes upward.

EWE: Emae nye nyaŋuɖoɖo be ɛ̃ ƒe ɖoɖo si wowɔ nɛ do ŋgɔ.
ENGLISH: It was his prearranged way of saying yes.

EWE: Esia wɔe be, wòxɔ nyɔnyrɔ hezu Yehowa Ðasefo esime wòxɔ ƒe 17.
ENGLISH: Thus, at age 17, he got baptized as one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.

EWE: EƑE ŊKUWO LE MAWU ƑE NUWO ŊU
ENGLISH: EYES FOCUSED ON THE THINGS OF GOD

EWE: Le ƒe 2011 me la, mɔ yeye aɖe si dzi Jairo ato aɖo dze kple amewo la ʋu ɖi nɛ azɔ si nye kɔmpiuta si wotsɔa ŋku fiaa mɔe.
ENGLISH: In 2011, a new way to communicate opened up for Jairo an eye-controlled computer.

EWE: Mɔ̃ɖaŋunu sia tea ŋu dea dzesi afi sia afi si ame trɔ eƒe ŋku yibɔea ɖo.
ENGLISH: This device tracks the movements of his iris so that he can activate icons on the screen.

EWE: Ne eɖe ŋku ɖe nutata aɖe le kɔmpiutaa dzi alo ƒo aɖaba ɖee ko la, ewɔa dɔ abe ɖe wòzi edzi kple asi ene.
ENGLISH: Blinking or staring at an icon is like clicking a mouse on a computer.

EWE: Eya ta wowɔ kɔmpiutakpe aɖe si dzi nutata vovovowo le la na Jairo be wòakpe ɖe eŋu wòate ŋu aɖo dze kple amewo.
ENGLISH: A board consisting of pictograms was created to help Jairo communicate.

EWE: Ne ele nutatawo dometɔ aɖe kpɔm eye wòƒo aɖaba zi ɖeka ko la, ɖoɖo siwo wowɔ ɖe mɔ̃a me la nana kɔmpiutaa gblɔa nya siwo wolé ɖe mɔ̃a dzi.
ENGLISH: When he blinks at one of them, the built-in software converts a written message into an electronic voice.

EWE: Jairo le eƒe kɔmpiuta si wòtsɔa ŋku fiaa mɔe la zãm
ENGLISH: Jairo using his eye-controlled computer

EWE: Esi Jairo va le Biblia gɔme sem ɖe edzi la, edi vevie be yeakpe ɖe ame bubuwo ŋu woasrɔ̃ nu tso Mawu ŋu.
ENGLISH: As Jairo’s understanding of the Bible increased, so did his desire to help others spiritually.

EWE: Ne míaƒe ƒomea le Biblia srɔ̃m abe ale si míewɔnɛ Kwasiɖa sia Kwasiɖa ene la, sẽe kple sẽe la, eɖea ŋku ɖem hekpɔa kɔmpiutaa dzi, eye wòwɔa esia enuenu.
ENGLISH: During our weekly family Bible study, he often looks back and forth between me and his computer.

EWE: Aleae wòɖoa ŋku edzi nam be maŋlɔ ale si yeaɖo nya ŋui ne míeyi Kristotɔwo ƒe kpekpewo la ɖe mɔ̃a dzi na ye.
ENGLISH: This is his way of reminding me that I should write down comments that he can offer during question-and-answer sessions at meetings of our Christian congregation.

EWE: Ne míeyi nusrɔ̃ƒe la, egbɔa dzi ɖi kpɔa kɔmpiutaa dzi heƒoa aɖaba ɖe nutata si sɔ la le kɔmpiutakpea dzi, eye enumake mɔ̃a ŋutɔ gblɔa nya si wòdi be yeagblɔ la ame sia ame sena.
ENGLISH: At the meeting, he patiently navigates through the screen to click on the appropriate icon, and then his electronic voice is heard by everyone.

EWE: Ɣesiaɣi si wòte ŋu de dzi ƒo na hamea me tɔwo le mɔ sia nu la, ekoa alɔgbɔnu gã aɖe.
ENGLISH: He smiles broadly every time he encourages the members of the congregation in this way.

EWE: Jairo xɔlɔ̃ siwo nye sɔhɛwo dometɔ ɖeka si ŋkɔe nye Alex gblɔ be, "Ɣesiaɣi si Jairo ɖo nya ŋu ku ɖe Biblia me nyatia aɖe ŋu mese la, ewɔa dɔ ɖe dzinye ŋutɔ. "
ENGLISH: Alex, one of Jairo’s young friends, observes, "It always impresses me when I hear Jairo’s comments on a Bible subject. "

EWE: [Nɔnɔmetata ŋu nya siwo le axa 10, 11]
ENGLISH: Jairo using his computer to make a comment at a meeting

EWE: Jairo le eƒe kɔmpiutaa zãm tsɔ le nya ŋu ɖom le nusrɔ̃ƒe
ENGLISH: Jairo uses his eye-controlled computer and its electronic voice to comment at meetings and to share his beliefs with others

EWE: Jairo zãa eƒe ŋkuwo tsɔ gblɔa eƒe dzixɔsewo na ame bubuwo hã.
ENGLISH: Jairo also uses his eyes to tell others about his beliefs.

EWE: Mɔ aɖe si dzi wòtona wɔa esia ye nye be eƒoa aɖaba ɖe nutata si nye abɔ dama si me lãwo kple ame ƒomevi vovovowo le le ŋutifafa me.
ENGLISH: One way he does this is by clicking a pictogram that portrays a garden where animals and people of all races live in peaceful conditions.

EWE: Ne eƒo aɖaba alea ko la, eƒe kɔmpiutaa ŋutɔ gblɔna be, "Mɔkpɔkpɔ si ŋu Biblia ƒo nu tsoe nye be anyigba ava zu paradiso, afi si dɔléle kple ku maganɔ azɔ o, Nyaɖeɖefia 21:4. "
ENGLISH: When he activates this, his computer voice proclaims, "The hope of the Bible is that the earth will be a paradise where there will be no more sickness and death, Revelation 21:4. "

EWE: Ne nyaa do dzidzɔ na ame si wòle gbeƒã ɖem na la, egaƒoa aɖaba ɖe nutata bubu eye eƒe kɔmpiutaa gblɔna be, "Àdi be masrɔ̃ Biblia kpli yea "?
ENGLISH: If the listener shows interest, another click causes his computer to say, "Would you like to study the Bible with me? "

EWE: Nukutɔe la, mía tɔgbui lɔ̃ be wòasrɔ̃ Biblia kpli ye.
ENGLISH: Surprisingly, our grandfather accepted this invitation.

EWE: Ewɔa dɔ ɖe ame dzi ŋutɔ be wòakpɔ ale si Jairo srɔ̃a nu kple tɔgbui blewuu esime hati Ðasefo aɖe le kpekpem ɖe eŋu la teƒe!
ENGLISH: It is thrilling to see Jairo, assisted by a fellow Witness, slowly teaching Grandpa the Bible!

EWE: Dzidzɔtɔe la, Tɔgbui xɔ nyɔnyrɔ le nutome gã takpekpe si wowɔ le Madrid, le August 2014 me la me.
ENGLISH: Happily, Grandpa got baptized at the regional convention in Madrid in August 2014.

EWE: Jairo le gbeƒã ɖe nya nyuia le dutoƒo
ENGLISH: Jairo sharing in the public ministry

EWE: Jairo ƒe sukunufialawo gɔ̃ hã de dzesi ale si gbegbe wòlɔ̃ Mawui.
ENGLISH: Jairo’s devotion to God does not go unnoticed by the teachers at his school.

ENGLISH: Does my mate resent me for being sick?

EWE: Kazuko gblɔ be: "Ele be mawɔ nu sia nu na srɔ̃nye.

ENGLISH: As a result of caring for him, my neck, shoulders, and arms ache, and I am an outpatient at an orthopedic hospital.

ENGLISH: Despite the difficulties, however, Kazuko says: "Our bond as a couple has become stronger. "

ENGLISH: For one thing, those who retain a healthy measure of satisfaction and contentment in their marriage view the illness as an assault not only on the ailing spouse but on the two of them as a couple.

EWE: Nya lae nye be ne srɔ̃tɔ ɖeka dze dɔ la, wo ame evea katã kpea fu le mɔ aɖe nu godoo.
ENGLISH: After all, if one mate is sick, both are deeply affected, even if in different ways.

ENGLISH: This interdependent relationship between a husband and wife is described at Genesis 2:24: "A man will leave his father and his mother and he must stick to his wife and they must become one flesh. "

EWE: Eya ta ne dɔmavɔleameŋu dze srɔ̃tɔ ɖeka dzi la, ele be wo ame evea woawɔ nu adudu le akɔkpekpe kple kuxia me.
ENGLISH: Thus, when a spouse has an ongoing physical ailment, it is critical that both husband and wife work together to meet the challenge.

ENGLISH: Additionally, research shows that couples who maintain a good relationship in the face of chronic illness accept their situation and learn effective ways to adapt to it.

ENGLISH: Many of the coping skills that they have learned echo the timeless advice found in the Bible.

ENGLISH: Why?

ENGLISH: Do you ‘raise your partner up’ with expressions of appreciation?

EWE: Ðe miete ŋu dia mɔnu siwo dzi miato ana kpekpeɖeŋu mia nɔewoa?
ENGLISH: Are you able to look for ways to be of practical assistance to each other?

ENGLISH: If I want to go outside and view the beautiful scenery, I ask her if she would like to join me.

ENGLISH: We are sharing the pain and enduring the situation together. "

ENGLISH: Now her husband endeavors to be more communicative in this regard.

ENGLISH: It could be something as simple as reading to each other or as challenging as learning a new language.

ENGLISH: At times, balance becomes a problem for caregiving spouses.

EWE: Wo dometɔ aɖewo ƒoa wo ɖokuiwo ɖe dɔ geɖe akpa wɔwɔ me, si wɔnɛ be nu nɔa wo ŋu tem vivivi, eye wògblẽa nu le woƒe lãmesẽ ŋu.
ENGLISH: Some take on too much work, slowly wear down, and endanger their own health.

ENGLISH: Eventually, they may even render themselves unable to continue providing care for their beloved mate.

ENGLISH: So if you are taking care of a chronically ill spouse, do not ignore your personal needs.

ENGLISH: Instead of overanalyzing them, ask yourself, ‘What is the simplest, most obvious way to improve the situation?’

ENGLISH: Remember that in this world, all happiness is limited in some way.

ENGLISH: The key here is to accept your situation and make the best of it.

ENGLISH: Take delight in even the smallest improvements in your health.

ENGLISH: Find things to look forward to, and set reachable goals together.
