EWE: Nu Si Wòle Be Nànya Tso Kpeŋuidɔ Ŋu
ENGLISH: What You Should Know About Epilepsy

EWE: WÒ AME nyanyɛ aɖe dze anyi hebu ɖe eɖokui.
ENGLISH: AN ACQUAINTANCE falls to the ground, unconscious.

EWE: Ametia lia goŋgoŋ eye eƒe ta, asiwo kple afɔwo le ƒoƒom tititi.
ENGLISH: His body stiffens, and his head and limbs begin to convulse.

EWE: Ne ènya be kpeŋuidɔ, si wogayɔna be dzeanyigblo alo adzigbo le eŋu la, àte ŋu ana kpekpeɖeŋu si sɔ lae hafi anɔ mɔ kpɔm na dɔdalawo ƒe kpekpeɖeŋu.
ENGLISH: If you know that the person suffers from epilepsy, you can provide adequate assistance while waiting for help.

EWE: Na míakpɔ nyateƒenya siwo ku ɖe dɔléle sia si gɔme ame geɖewo mesena o la ŋu.
ENGLISH: Let us explore some basic facts about this often misunderstood disorder.

EWE: Nu kae nye kpeŋuidɔ?
ENGLISH: What is epilepsy?

EWE: Kpeŋuidɔ nye ahɔhɔ̃medɔ si nana ame buna ɖe eɖokui hena ɣeyiɣi kpui aɖe.
ENGLISH: Epilepsy is a brain disorder that produces brief attacks called seizures.

EWE: Zi geɖe ne edze ame dzi la, medea miniti atɔ̃ hafi amea gagbugbɔna ɖoa eɖokui me o.
ENGLISH: The entire seizure usually lasts less than five minutes.

EWE: Nudzɔdzɔ si míeɖɔ le nyati sia ƒe gɔmedzedze lae woyɔna zi geɖe be dzeanyigblo, elabe enana amea dzea anyi.
ENGLISH: The situation described at the outset of this article is typical of what is called a grand mal seizure.

EWE: Nu kae nana dɔ sia hona na ame?
ENGLISH: What causes seizures?

EWE: Numekulawo xɔe se be ahɔhɔ̃mekawo ƒe dɔmawɔmawɔ nyuie gbɔe wòtsona.
ENGLISH: Researchers believe that seizures occur when there is an abnormal surge of electrical activity between brain cells.

EWE: Gake nu si nana ahɔhɔ̃mekawo doa kpo dɔwɔwɔ nyuie gɔme sese zu taɖui na numekulawo.
ENGLISH: Just why this happens remains unclear.

EWE: Ne kpeŋuidɔ ho na ame aɖe la, kpekpeɖeŋu kae mate ŋu anae?
ENGLISH: If I see someone with epilepsy having a grand mal seizure, what should I do?

EWE: Numekugbalẽ aɖe ɖo aɖaŋu be "ele be woaɖe asi le ame si ku kpeŋui la ŋu wòanɔ anyi ʋuu eƒe mo nakɔ, gake ahiã be woakpɔ egbɔ be ele gbɔgbɔm nyuie eye ŋku nanɔ eŋu be wòagawɔ nu vevi eɖokui o. "
ENGLISH: "Bystanders should let the attack run its course and not interfere with the patient, beyond checking to make sure the person is in no physical danger and can breathe, " says The Encyclopedia of the Brain and Brain Disorders.

EWE: (The Encyclopedia of the Brain and Brain Disorders) Agbalẽ ma ke gblɔ yi edzi be: "Nenye be amea bu ɖe eɖokui wògbɔ miniti atɔ̃ ŋu, alo kasia eƒe mo nakɔ ko bubu gadze edzi alo megbugbɔ ɖo eɖokui me o miniti ʋɛ aɖewo esime wòdzudzɔ ƒoƒo tititi megbe la, ele be woadi dɔnɔkɔʋu ne wòakɔe ayi kɔdzi. "
ENGLISH: On the other hand, the book says: "An ambulance should be called if the seizure continues for more than five minutes, if another seizure immediately follows the first, or if the person does not regain consciousness a few minutes after the seizure ends. "

EWE: Aleke mate ŋu akpe ɖe ame si ku kpeŋui la ŋu?
ENGLISH: How can I help the patient while he is having a seizure?

EWE: Tsɔ nu bɔbɔe aɖe de eƒe ta te, eye nàɖe lãnuwo ɖa le eƒe ta gbɔ.
ENGLISH: Place a soft object between his head and the floor, and move sharp objects away from his head.

EWE: Ne edzudzɔ ƒoƒo tititi la, trɔe ɖe eƒe axa dzi abe ale si wòdze le nɔnɔmetata si le axa sia me ene.
ENGLISH: When the convulsions stop, turn the patient on his side as shown in the accompanying diagram.

EWE: Nu kae mawɔ ne amea ƒe mo kɔ?
ENGLISH: What should I do after the patient awakens?

EWE: Gbã la, gblɔ nɛ be megavɔ̃ o.
ENGLISH: First, assure him that everything is all right.

EWE: Azɔ lée tsi tre eye nàkplɔe ayi afi si wòate ŋu aɖi ɖe eme le.
ENGLISH: Then help him to stand upright and guide him to a place where he can get needed rest.

EWE: Ame akpa gãtɔ tɔtɔna eye alɔ̃ tsɔa wo ne woɖo wo ɖokui me; gake ame aɖewo ya ƒe mo kɔna kaba eye wogatea ŋu yia nu si wɔm wole hafi ku kpeŋuia la wɔwɔ dzi.
ENGLISH: Most people are confused and sleepy after a seizure; others recover quickly and can continue what they were doing before the attack.

EWE: Kpeŋuikulawo katãe ƒona tititia?
ENGLISH: Do all epileptic seizures include convulsions?

EWE: Ao.
ENGLISH: No.

EWE: Ame aɖewo buna ɖe wo ɖokui sẽe, gake womedzea anyi o.
ENGLISH: Some patients experience a moment of impaired awareness without even falling to the ground.

EWE: Kpeŋui sia ƒomevi menɔa anyi eteƒe didina o, ne kpeŋuia nu tso na amea ko la eƒe mo kɔna zi ɖeka.
ENGLISH: This is called a petit mal seizure (or absence seizure), which is usually brief with no lingering aftereffects.

EWE: Gake kpeŋui sia ƒomevi kula aɖewo ƒe kpeŋuikukua nɔa anyi eteƒe didina, eye wòxɔa miniti geɖewo.
ENGLISH: Some people with epilepsy undergo prolonged petit mal seizures, lasting several minutes.

EWE: Ne edzɔ alea la, amea nɔa tsatsam le eƒe xɔ me, nɔa awu hem le eɖokui ŋu, alo nɔa nu tramatrama wɔm.
ENGLISH: In such a case, the patient may wander around the room, tug at his clothing, or otherwise behave strangely.

EWE: Ne eƒe mo kɔ la, esena le eɖokui me be yeƒe ta katã le wodzoe.
ENGLISH: After the seizure, he may feel light-headed.

EWE: Aleke agbea nɔna na ame si ŋu kpeŋuidɔ le?
ENGLISH: What is it like to live with epilepsy?

EWE: Enye nyateƒe be ame siwo ŋu kpeŋuidɔ le la tsia dzi vevie esi womenya ɣekaɣi dɔ sia agaho na yewo o ta.
ENGLISH: Understandably, many people with epilepsy contend with a nagging fear of when and where the next seizure will occur.

EWE: Esi womedi be yewoado ŋukpe yewo ɖokui o ta la, womelɔ̃na be yewoayi ame dome o.
ENGLISH: To avoid embarrassment, they may tend to avoid social situations.

EWE: Aleke mate ŋu akpe ɖe ame si ŋu kpeŋuidɔ le la ŋu?
ENGLISH: How can I give support to someone who has epilepsy?

EWE: De dzi ƒo nɛ be wòaɖe eƒe seselelãmewo agblɔ na ye faa.
ENGLISH: Encourage him not to bottle up his feelings.

EWE: Ðo to nyuie ne ele nu ƒom.
ENGLISH: Be a good listener.

EWE: Biae be ne dɔa ho nɛ la, kpekpeɖeŋu kae yeate ŋu anae mahã.
ENGLISH: Ask him what he would like you to do if he has a seizure.

EWE: Esi wònye ame siwo ŋu kpeŋuidɔ le dometɔ geɖe mekua ʋu o ta la, àte ŋu adoe ɖa be yeakɔe ɖe ʋu me ayi afi si wòadi be yeayi alo ayi aɖaƒle asi nɛ.
ENGLISH: Since many people with epilepsy do not drive, perhaps you could offer a ride or run some errands for him.

EWE: Ðe woate ŋu alé kpeŋuidɔ ƒe hoho na ame nu alo axe mɔ ɖe enu kura?
ENGLISH: Can seizures be reduced or even prevented?

EWE: Nɔnɔme aɖewo nana be kpeŋuidɔ tea ŋu hona na ame kabakaba, esiawo dometɔ aɖewoe nye nuteɖeamedzi kple alɔ̃madɔmadɔ.
ENGLISH: Some factors increase the likelihood of a seizure, such as stress and lack of sleep.

EWE: Dɔléle sia ŋuti nunyalawo dea dzi ƒo na ame siwo ŋu dɔ sia le la be woaɖi ɖe eme nyuie, eye woanɔ kame dem edziedzi ale be nu naganɔ tetem ɖe wo dzi boo o.
ENGLISH: Experts therefore encourage epileptics to get proper rest and to exercise regularly in order to reduce stress.

EWE: Le go aɖewo me la, atike aɖewo zazã te ŋu xe mɔ ɖe dɔ sia ƒe hoho na ame nu kura.
ENGLISH: In some cases, medications have also been effective in preventing seizures.

EWE: Esi wònye be kpeŋuidɔ le ɖekakpui Sello si le South Africa ŋu ta la, edzudzɔ sukudede le eƒe ɖevime.
ENGLISH: Because of his epilepsy, a young man in South Africa named Sello was dismissed from school at an early age.

EWE: Esi wòtsi la, menya agbalẽ o, eye atike aɖeke hã mele esi wòtsɔ léa eƒe dɔlélea nu o.
ENGLISH: He grew up without an education and without medication to control his epilepsy.

EWE: Gake edi be yeanya Biblia eye Yehowa Ðasefowo kpe ɖe eŋu.
ENGLISH: But he wanted to understand the Bible, and Jehovah’s Witnesses helped him.

EWE: Wosrɔ̃ Biblia kplii eye wofia nuxexlẽ hãe.
ENGLISH: They not only studied the Bible with him but also taught him to read.

EWE: Sello gblɔ be: "Yehowa Ðasefowo nye Kristotɔ siwo si lɔlɔ̃ akuakua le na wo haviwo. "
ENGLISH: Additionally, a Witness medical doctor helped him get medication along with a social disability grant.

EWE: Fifia, Sello ŋutɔ hã zu Yehowa Ðasefo eye wòkpɔa dzidzɔ ɖe xexe yeye si ƒe ŋugbe Mawu do si me dɔléle maganɔ o la ŋu nya gbɔgblɔ na amewo ŋu.
ENGLISH: "Jehovah’s Witnesses are truly loving Christians, " says Sello, who is now a Witness himself and enjoys sharing with others God’s promise of a new world where sickness will be no more.

EWE: Nyaɖeɖefia 21:3-5.
ENGLISH: Revelation 21:3-5.

EWE: Nu Siwo Nàte Ŋu Awɔ
ENGLISH: The Recovery Position

EWE: Esi wòdzudzɔ ƒoƒo tititi megbe . . .
ENGLISH: After convulsing has stopped . . .

EWE: Dze klo ɖe dɔnɔa xa, eye lé eƒe abɔklugui nàtrɔ eƒe alɔ do ɖe eƒe ta gbɔ lɔƒo
ENGLISH: Kneel beside the patient and bend his arm at the elbow, pointing it upward

EWE: He eƒe asi blewu ale be eƒe tome nanɔ eƒe asi dzi
ENGLISH: Gently tuck the hand of the patient’s other arm underneath his cheek

EWE: Tsɔ asi evelia he amea ƒe klo va ɖokuiwò gbɔ, eye nàtrɔe blewu.
ENGLISH: With your other hand, pull the patient’s knee toward you, slowly rolling him over.

EWE: He eƒe klo va ŋgɔ ale be eƒe klo nanɔ anyigba
ENGLISH: Then move the patient’s knee in front of his body so that it rests on the floor

EWE: Trɔ eƒe ta yi dzi ale be gbɔgbɔ nagati eƒo o
ENGLISH: Tilt the patient’s head up to allow for unobstructed breathing

EWE: Aɖulãdɔ Ele Fu Ðem Na Wòa?
ENGLISH: Gum Disease Are You at Risk?

EWE: ENYE dɔléle siwo bɔ wu la dometɔ ɖeka.
ENGLISH: IT IS one of the most common oral diseases in the world.

EWE: Ke hã dɔ sia menya kpɔna dzea si le gɔmedzedzea me o.
ENGLISH: Yet, this disease in its initial stages may not cause any immediate symptoms.

EWE: Dɔléle vɔ̃ɖi si nye aɖulãdɔ míewɔnɛ.
ENGLISH: This dangerous subtlety is characteristic of gum disease.

EWE: Agbalẽ aɖe gblɔ be aɖulãdɔ nye numedɔléle siwo "gblẽa nu le ame ƒe lãmesẽ ŋu vevie " la dometɔ ɖeka.
ENGLISH: The International Dental Journal lists periodontal disease among oral disorders that pose "a serious public-health problem. "

EWE: (International Dental Journal) Agbalẽ ma ke gblɔ kpee be numedɔlélewo gblẽa nu geɖe le "ame ɖekaɖekawo kple amehaawo ŋu, wonana ame kpea fu hesea veve vevie, nuɖuɖu zua dɔ nɛ eye megasea vivi na agbea o. "
ENGLISH: It adds that the impact of oral disease "on individuals and communities in terms of pain and suffering, impairment of function and reduced quality of life, is considerable. "

EWE: Numedzodzro tso dɔléle sia si ɖe kpe na ame geɖewo ŋu akpe ɖe ŋuwò nànya ale si nàwɔ aƒo asa nɛ.
ENGLISH: A discussion of this widespread condition may help you reduce your risk of gum disease.

EWE: Nya Vevi Aɖewo Tso Aɖulãdɔ Ŋuti
ENGLISH: Facts About Gum Disease

EWE: Aɖulãdɔ ƒe akpa vovovowoe li.
ENGLISH: There are different stages of gum disease.

EWE: Le gɔmedzedzea la, enana aɖulãwo alo nyèdewo tena.
ENGLISH: The initial stage, called gingivitis, is an inflammation of the gums.

EWE: Ne aɖulãwo toa ʋu la, ate ŋu anye aɖulãdɔ ƒe dzesie.
ENGLISH: Bleeding gums may be a sign of this stage.

EWE: Esia tea ŋu dzɔna ne ame le nu me klɔm alo le aɖutɛ me ɖem, alo aɖulãwo ŋutɔ nanɔ anyi ko ato ʋu.
ENGLISH: This may occur during brushing and flossing or for no apparent reason.

EWE: Ne aɖudɔdalawo le aɖua dom kpɔ ko wòto ʋu la, efia be aɖulãdɔ ƒe gɔmedzedzee nye ema.
ENGLISH: Also, bleeding during a gum examination may be indicative of gingivitis. Gum disease that progresses from this stage is called periodontitis.

EWE: Ne aɖulãdɔ le tsitsim la, aɖuwo ƒe lãkusiwo kple aɖuŋuƒu siwo léa aɖuawo ɖe te la dome tea gbegblẽ.
ENGLISH: At this point, oral structures that support your teeth, such as bone and gum tissue, begin to be destroyed.

EWE: Aɖulãdɔ sia menana dzesi aɖeke o va se ɖe esime wòtsi nyuie.
ENGLISH: This form of gum disease may not cause symptoms until it reaches an advanced stage.

EWE: Ne aɖulãdɔ tsi va ɖo afi aɖe la, etea ŋu nana aɖulãwo tena ɖa le aɖuawo ŋu, aɖuawo gbɔdzɔna, eye wo dome kena, enana ame ƒe nu me ʋẽna, aɖulã alo nyèdewo nɔa nyinyim henana aɖuawo dzena abe ɖe wodidi ŋutɔ ene, eye aɖulãwo nɔa ʋu tom.
ENGLISH: Some signs of periodontitis may be gum pockets; loose teeth; gaps forming between teeth; bad breath; receding gums, that is, gums that are pulling away from the teeth, giving the teeth a longer appearance; and bleeding gums.

EWE: Nu geɖewo gbɔe aɖulãdɔ tsona.
ENGLISH: Cause and Effect of Gum Disease

EWE: Aɖuawo tea ŋu ƒoa sogo alo ƒoa ba.
ENGLISH: Several factors can increase the risk of gum disease.

EWE: Sogo alo aɖuŋuba, si nye nugbagbevi nyaŋuinyaŋui siwo léna ɖe aɖuwo ŋu edziedzi gbɔ koŋue dɔ sia tsona.
ENGLISH: Dental plaque, which is a thin film of bacteria that regularly forms on the teeth, is the most common cause.

EWE: Ne womeɖe sogoawo ɖa le aɖuawo ŋu o la, woate ŋu ana aɖulãawo nate.
ENGLISH: If plaque is not removed, the bacteria can cause gum swelling.

EWE: Le ɣeyiɣi aɖe megbe la, aɖulãawo va nɔa tetem ɖa le aɖuawo ŋu si nana be mɔ va tsia aɖuawo kple aɖulãawo dome.
ENGLISH: As this process progresses, the gums start to separate from the teeth, allowing the bacteria-laden plaque to grow under the gum line.

EWE: Eye sogoawo va ɖoa wo dome. Ne sogoawo nya ɖo wo dome ko la, wotea lãkusiawo kple aɖuŋuƒuawo dome gbegblẽ.
ENGLISH: Once the bacteria has infiltrated to this point, the inflammatory process advances by destroying bone and gum tissue.

EWE: Eɖanye aɖuawo ŋue sogoawo le loo alo wo domee wole o, wotea ŋu va sesẽna ŋutɔ.
ENGLISH: Dental plaque, either above or below the gum line, can harden into calculus (or what is commonly known as tartar).

EWE: Nugbagbevi nyaŋuinyaŋuiwo tsyɔa sogo sesẽ siawo hã dzi, eye esi wònye sogo siawo léna ɖe aɖuawo ŋu kpaɖii ta la, wo ɖeɖe le aɖuawo ŋu zua dɔ.
ENGLISH: Calculus is also covered with bacteria, and because of its hardness and adherence to the teeth, it is not as easily removed as plaque.

EWE: Esia ate ŋu awɔe be nugbagbevi siawo nayi edzi agblẽ nu le aɖulãawo ŋu vevie.
ENGLISH: Therefore, bacteria can continue to affect the gums adversely.

EWE: Aɖulãdɔ tea ŋu tsoa nu bubuwo hã gbɔ.
ENGLISH: There are other factors that can contribute to your risk of having gum disease.

EWE: Nu siwo gbɔ wòtsona dometɔ aɖewo ate ŋu anye bemalémale na ame ƒe nu me, atike siwo tsia dɔlélenutsiŋutete ƒe dɔwɔwɔ nu, dɔlékuiwo, nuteɖeamedzi, suklidɔ (alo aɖuɖɔvividɔ) si ŋu womele ŋku lém ɖo o, aha tsu nono kple sigarɛtnono kpakple lãmetsiwo ƒe tɔtrɔ si fufɔfɔ hena vɛ.
ENGLISH: These may include poor oral hygiene, medications that suppress the immune system, viral infections, stress, uncontrolled diabetes, excessive alcohol consumption, tobacco use, and hormonal changes because of pregnancy.

EWE: Aɖulãdɔ ate ŋu agblẽ nu le ŋuwò le go bubuwo hã me.

ENGLISH: I’m normally a caring person, but when I’m depressed, I care little about anyone or anything. "

EWE: Ðeko Anna kple Julia ɖo woƒe sɔhɛ me teti koe nye ma blanuiléledɔ ɖe fu na wo zi gbãtɔ.
ENGLISH: Anna and Julia were in their early teens when they first experienced depression.

EWE: Togbɔ be sɔhɛwo tea ŋu léa blanui vie ɣeaɖewoɣi hã, Anna kple Julia ƒe blanuilélea ya xɔ kwasiɖa aɖewo alo ɣleti aɖewo gɔ̃ hã.
ENGLISH: While other young people might occasionally feel down, Anna and Julia had periods of depression that persisted for weeks or months at a time.

EWE: Anna gblɔ be: "Ðeko wòle abe nàxaxa ɖe do globoo doviviti aɖe si me màte ŋu ado le o me ene.
ENGLISH: "It’s like being stuck in a deep, dark hole with no way out, " Anna says.

EWE: Awɔ na wò abe ɖe wò tagbɔ le gbegblẽm eye mègale ame me o ene. "
ENGLISH: "You feel like you are losing your mind, losing who you are. "

EWE: Menye Anna kple Julia koe kuxi sia ɖea fu na o.
ENGLISH: Anna and Julia’s situation is not uncommon.

EWE: Sɔhɛ geɖewo va le blanuiléledɔ lém fifia ŋutɔ, eya ta Xexea Me Lãmesẽ Habɔbɔ ka nya ta be, "blanuiléle koŋ gbɔe wòtsona be ŋutsuvi kple nyɔnuvi siwo xɔ tso ƒe 10 va se ɖe 19 la ƒe lãme gblẽna, wogbɔdzɔna eye woƒe susu mewɔa dɔ nyuie o. "
ENGLISH: The diagnosis of depression among the young appears to be increasing at an alarming rate, and depression is "the predominant cause of illness and disability for both boys and girls aged 10 to 19 years, " says the World Health Organization (WHO).

EWE: Blanuiléledɔ ƒe dzesi siwo ate ŋu adze le ɖevi si le sɔhɛ me ɖom ŋu ƒe ɖewoe nye alɔ̃dɔdɔ fũu, alɔ̃madɔmadɔ nyuie, nuɖuɖu fũu akpa, numaɖumaɖu nyuie kple lolo alo kuɖiɖi.
ENGLISH: The symptoms of depression can appear during adolescence and may include changes in sleep patterns, appetite, and weight.

EWE: Bubuwo hã ate ŋu anye dzodzodzoetsitsi, mɔkpɔkpɔbuɖeame, nuxaxa kple sese le ame ɖokui me be yemeɖi naneke o.
ENGLISH: Feelings of despair, hopelessness, sadness, and worthlessness may also appear.

EWE: Ðewo hãe nye ame ɖokui ɖeɖe ɖe aga, susu ƒe nu ŋu manɔmanɔ alo nuŋlɔbe, ame ɖokui wuwu ƒe susuwo alo nuwɔna kple nɔnɔme siwo ŋu ɖɔktawo menya nu tsoe o.
ENGLISH: Other signs include social withdrawal, trouble concentrating or remembering, suicidal thoughts or actions, and medically unexplained symptoms.

EWE: Dzesi aɖewo siwo dzena le ame ŋu hena kwasiɖawo eye wonana ame ƒe gbe sia gbe nuwɔna trɔna dzie tagbɔdɔdalawo nɔa te ɖo ƒoa nya ta be blanuiléledɔe le fu ɖem na ame.
ENGLISH: When mental-health professionals suspect depression, they usually look for groups of symptoms that persist for weeks and that disrupt a person’s everyday life.

EWE: NU SIWO GBƆ SƆHƐWO ƑE BLANUILÉLEDƆ ATE ŊU ATSO
ENGLISH: POSSIBLE CAUSES OF TEEN DEPRESSION

EWE: Xexea Me Lãmesẽ Habɔbɔa gblɔ be: "Nu siwo me ame to, nu siwo dome wònyi kple nu siwo ŋu wòbuna gbɔe blanuiléledɔ tsona. "
ENGLISH: According to WHO, "depression results from a complex interaction of social, psychological and biological factors. "

EWE: Esiawo dometɔ aɖewoe nye:
ENGLISH: These may include the following.

EWE: Ƒome si me ame tso, atike muamewo zazã.
ENGLISH: Physical factors.

EWE: Abe ale si wòle le Julia gome ene la, blanuiléledɔ le ƒome aɖewo me si wɔnɛ be zi geɖe la, ƒome mawo me tɔwo tea ŋu léa dɔa.
ENGLISH: As was true in Julia’s case, depression often runs in families, suggesting that genetics can play a role, perhaps affecting chemical activity in the brain.

EWE: Nu bubu siwo hã gbɔ dɔa tsonae nye dzidɔ alo ʋukamedɔléle aɖewo siwo nana lãmetsi aɖewo mewɔa dɔ nyuie o kple atikemuamewo zazã ɣeyiɣi didi hã ate ŋu ana dɔa nanyra.
ENGLISH: Other physical risk factors include cardiovascular disease and changing hormone levels, as well as ongoing substance abuse, which may intensify depression, if not give rise to it.

EWE: Nuteɖeamedzi.
ENGLISH: Stress.

EWE: Megblẽ naneke ne nu te ɖe sɔhɛ aɖe dzi vie o, gake ne nu te ɖe edzi ɣeyiɣi didi alo vevie la, ate ŋu agblẽ nu le eƒe ametia kple susua ŋu, esia wɔnɛ be ɣeaɖewoɣia sɔhɛ siwo le seselelãmekuxiwo me tom xoxo, alo esiwo blanuiléledɔ le ƒome na la nalé dɔa.
ENGLISH: While a little stress can be healthy, chronic or excessive stress can be physically and psychologically harmful, sometimes to the point of plunging a susceptible, or biologically vulnerable, teen into depression.

EWE: Togbɔ be ele alea hãa, ame aɖeke menya nu si gbɔ tututu blanuiléledɔ tsona o, ɖewohĩ nu geɖewo gbɔe wòtsona abe ale si míegblɔe va yi ene.
ENGLISH: That said, the exact causes of depression remain unclear and may involve a combination of factors, as mentioned earlier.

EWE: Nu siwo nana nu tena ɖe ame dzi wòléa blanui ate ŋu anye ame dzilawo ƒe wo nɔewo gbegbe alo kaklã ɖa, ame vevi ƒe ku, ameƒoƒo alo ame gbɔ dɔdɔ sesẽe, afɔku sesẽ aɖe dzedze, dɔléle alo ne ɖevi aɖe menyaa nu o, eye vevietɔ ne ɖevia sena le eɖokui me be wometsɔa ɖeke le eme na ye o.
ENGLISH: Stress-related factors linked to depression may include parental divorce or separation, the death of a loved one, physical or sexual abuse, a serious accident, illness, or a learning disability especially if a child feels rejected as a result.

EWE: Nu bubu hã ate ŋu anye ne dzilawo kpɔa mɔ be wo vi aɖe nawɔ nu siwo gbɔ eƒe ŋutete ŋu, ɖewohĩ le eƒe agbalẽsrɔ̃nyawo me.
ENGLISH: A related factor may be unrealistically high parental expectations, perhaps in regard to scholastic achievement.

EWE: Ðewo hãe nye ne wowɔa ŋlɔmi le ame ŋu, ne ame tsi dzi ɖe etsɔme ŋu kple ame dzila si le blanuiléledɔ lém la ƒe nuwɔwɔ ɖe ame ŋu tramatrama.
ENGLISH: Other possible causes are bullying, uncertainty about the future, emotional estrangement by a depressed parent, and parental unpredictability.

EWE: Ne ɖevi aɖe lé blanui le nu siawo dometɔ aɖe ta la, nu kae ate ŋu akpe ɖe eŋu?
ENGLISH: If depression results, what may help a teen to cope?

EWE: LÉ BE NA WÒ AMETIA KPLE WÒ SUSU
ENGLISH: CARE FOR YOUR MIND AND BODY

EWE: Wotea ŋu tsɔa atike aɖewo siwo tagbɔdɔléleŋutinunyalawo nana kple woƒe aɖaŋuɖoɖowo léa blanuiléledɔ si nu sẽ la nu.
ENGLISH: Moderate to severe depression is usually managed with medication and counseling by a mental-health professional.

EWE: Yesu Kristo gblɔ be: "Ame siwo le lãmesẽ me la mehiã gbedala o, negbe ame siwo le dɔ lém ko. "
ENGLISH: Jesus Christ said: "Those who are strong do not need a physician, but those who are ill do. "

EWE: (Marko 2:17) Eya ta dɔléle ate ŋu aɖe fu na míaƒe ametia ƒe akpa sia akpa, ate ŋu aɖe fu na míaƒe susu hã!
ENGLISH: (Mark 2:17) And illness can affect any part of our body, including our brain!

EWE: Anyo hã be míaɖe asi le agbe aɖewo siwo míenɔna tsã la ŋu le esi susua kple ametiae wɔa dɔ aduadu ta.
ENGLISH: Lifestyle changes may also be advisable because our mind and body are closely connected.

EWE: Ne èle blanuiléledɔ lém la, dze agbagba nànɔ nu siwo ana wò susu nawɔ dɔ nyuie eye nànɔ lãmesẽ me la wɔm.
ENGLISH: If you suffer from depression, take reasonable measures to care for your physical and mental health.

EWE: Le kpɔɖeŋu me, ɖu nu siwo me amenyinu le, dɔ alɔ̃ wòasu wò nyuie eye nànɔ kame dem edziedzi.
ENGLISH: For instance, eat wholesome meals, get sufficient sleep, and exercise regularly.

EWE: Kamedede nana lãmetsi siwo nana dzi dzɔa ame dzana ɖe lãme na ame, enana ŋusẽ ɖoa ame ŋu eye wònana wodɔa alɔ̃ nyuie.
ENGLISH: Exercise releases chemicals that can lift your mood, increase your energy, and improve your sleep.

EWE: Ne anya wɔ la, dze agbagba nàde dzesi nu siwo hoa dɔ sia na wò eye nàwɔ nu siwo nàtsɔ alé enu la ŋuti ɖoɖo ɖi.
ENGLISH: If possible, try to recognize triggers and early warning signs of a depressive mood and create a suitable plan of action.

EWE: Gblɔ wò dɔlélea ŋu nya na ame aɖe si dzi nèka ɖo.
ENGLISH: Confide in someone you trust.

EWE: Wò ƒomea me tɔwo kple xɔlɔ̃wo ƒe alɔdodo wò ate ŋu akpe ɖe ŋuwò nànɔ te ɖe dɔlélea nu eye ɖewohĩ ana wòaka ɖe eme na wò gɔ̃ hã.
ENGLISH: A supportive network of close family members and friends may help you to cope more effectively with your depression, possibly reducing symptoms.

EWE: Ŋlɔ nu siwo vaa susu me na wò kple wò seselelãmewo ɖe agbalẽ aɖe me nu siae kpe ɖe Julia si ƒe nya míegblɔ va yi la ŋu.
ENGLISH: Record your thoughts and feelings in a journal a practice that helped Julia, quoted earlier.

EWE: Vevietɔ wu la, kpɔ egbɔ be wò kple Mawu dome le nyuie.
ENGLISH: Above all, be sure to address your spiritual need.

EWE: Esia ate ŋu ana mɔkpɔkpɔ nasu asiwò le agbe me geɖe wu.
ENGLISH: This can greatly improve your outlook on life.

EWE: Yesu Kristo gblɔ be: "Dzidzɔtɔwoe nye ame siwo nyae be gbɔgbɔmenuwo hiã yewo. "
ENGLISH: Jesus Christ said: "Happy are those conscious of their spiritual need. "

EWE: Mateo 5:3.
ENGLISH: Matthew 5:3.

EWE: Nyɔnuvi sɔhɛ aɖe le nu ɖum kple edzilawo, ele kame dem, eye wòmlɔ anyi
ENGLISH: A teenage girl has a meal with her parents, exercises, and sleeps

EWE: Ðu nu siwo me amenyinu le, dɔ alɔ̃ wòasu wò nyuie eye nànɔ kame dem edziedzi
ENGLISH: Eat well, stay active, and get sufficient sleep

EWE: Nyɔnuvi sɔhɛ aɖe le Biblia xlẽm
ENGLISH: A teenage girl reads the Bible

EWE: Ðu nu siwo me amenyinu le, de kame edziedzi eye dɔ alɔ̃ nyuie, Ne wò kple Mawu dome le nyuie la, ana wò dzi nadze eme
ENGLISH: You can find comfort by satisfying your spiritual need

EWE: Anna kple Julia siaa ɖo kpe Yesu ƒe nya mawo dzi.
ENGLISH: Both Anna and Julia attest to Jesus’ words.

EWE: Anna gblɔ be: "Dɔ siwo ku ɖe mawusubɔsubɔ ŋu wɔwɔ nana nye susu nɔa ame bubuwo hã ŋu ke menye nye kuxiwo ɖeɖe ko ŋu o.
ENGLISH: Anna says: "Spiritual activities make me focus on other people, not just on my own problems.

EWE: Esia wɔwɔ menɔa bɔbɔe ɣesiaɣi o gake ne mewɔea enana mekpɔa dzidzɔ. "
ENGLISH: That isn’t always easy, but I am much happier as a result. "

EWE: Gbedodoɖa kple Biblia xexlẽ ye faa akɔ na Julia.
ENGLISH: Julia finds comfort in prayer and Bible reading.

EWE: Egblɔ be: "Nye dzimenyawo gbɔgblɔ na Mawu le gbedodoɖa me nana meɖea dzi ɖi.
ENGLISH: "Pouring out my heart to God in prayer calms me, " she says.

EWE: Biblia kpe ɖe ŋunye mekpɔe be mexɔ asi le Mawu ŋkume eye be eléa be nam.
ENGLISH: "And the Bible helps me to see that I am valuable in God’s eyes and that he really cares about me.

EWE: Biblia xexlẽ na kakaɖedzi su asinye ɖe etsɔme ŋu. "
ENGLISH: Bible reading also gives me a positive view of the future. "

EWE: Esi Yehowa Mawue wɔ mí ta la, ese ale si hehe si míexɔ, míaƒe agbemenuteƒekpɔkpɔwo kple nu siwo dome míenyi kpɔa ŋusẽ ɖe míaƒe agbenɔnɔ kple seselelãme dzii la gɔme bliboe.
ENGLISH: As our Creator, Jehovah God fully understands how our upbringing, experiences in life, and genetic makeup influence our outlook and emotions.

EWE: Eya ta etea ŋu naa kpekpeɖeŋu kple akɔfafa si míehiã la mí ɣeaɖewoɣi to mía havi amegbetɔ siwo sea veve ɖe ame nu hesea nu gɔme na ame dzi.
ENGLISH: He is therefore able to supply needed support and comfort, perhaps doing so through compassionate and understanding fellow humans.

EWE: Azɔ hã, ɣeyiɣi aɖe gbɔna si Mawu ada míaƒe dɔlélewo katã na mí.
ENGLISH: Moreover, the time will come when God will heal us of all our illnesses, physical or mental.

EWE: Yesaya 33:24 gblɔ be: "Dua me tɔ aɖeke magblɔ be, ‘Mele dɔ lém o.’ "
ENGLISH: "No resident will say: ‘I am sick,’ " says Isaiah 33:24.

EWE: Ɛ̃, Biblia do ŋugbe be Mawu "atutu aɖatsi sia aɖatsi ɖa le [míaƒe] ŋkume, eye ku maganɔ anyi akpɔ o, konyifafa kple ɣlidodo kpakple vevesese hã maganɔ anyi o. "
ENGLISH: Yes, the Bible promises that God "will wipe out every tear from [our] eyes, and death will be no more, neither will mourning nor outcry nor pain be anymore. "

EWE: (Nyaɖeɖefia 21:4) Nya sia faa akɔ henaa kakaɖedzi ame lo!
ENGLISH: (Revelation 21:4) How comforting and reassuring that is!

EWE: Ne èdi be yeasrɔ̃ nu geɖe tso Mawu ƒe tameɖoɖo na amegbetɔ ŋu la, ekema míeɖe kuku yi jw.org nyatakakadzraɖoƒea.
ENGLISH: If you would like to learn more about God’s purpose for mankind and the earth, please visit us at jw.org.

EWE: Àkpɔ Biblia nyui aɖe kple nyati gbogbo siwo ƒo nu tso nu vovovo siwo dome blanuiléledɔ hã le la ŋu le afi ma.
ENGLISH: There you will find an excellent online Bible, as well as articles on a broad range of topics, including depression.

EWE: Nu Siwo Dzilawo Ate Ŋu Awɔ
ENGLISH: What Parents Can Do

EWE: Dzilawo, minyae be esesẽna na sɔhɛ siwo lé blanui be woagblɔ ale si wole sesem le wo ɖokuiwo me eye ɖewohĩ womase nu si le fu ɖem na wo la gɔme o.
ENGLISH: Recognize that depressed teens may find it hard to express their feelings or may not understand what is happening to them.

EWE: Anɔ eme be womanya gɔ̃ hã be blanuiléledɔe le fu ɖem na yewo o.
ENGLISH: They may not even be aware of the symptoms of depression.

EWE: Sɔhɛ siwo blanuiléledɔ le fu ɖem na ƒe nuwɔna toa vovo na ame tsitsi siwo le dɔ ma lém la tɔ, eya ta nɔ ŋudzɔ ɖe tɔtrɔ siwo ava viwòa ƒe nuwɔnawo, eƒe nuɖuɖu, eƒe dzidzɔkpɔkpɔ, alɔ̃dɔdɔ alo hadomenuwɔnawo me la ŋu, vevietɔ ne tɔtrɔawo li hena kwasiɖa geɖewo.
ENGLISH: Teens tend to express their depression in ways different from those of adults, so be alert to major changes in your child’s behavior, eating habits, moods, sleep patterns, or social interactions especially if the changes persist for weeks.

EWE: Mègabui fefenyae ne viwòa gblɔ nya aɖe alo wɔ nane si fia be edi be yeawu ye ɖokui o.
ENGLISH: Take seriously any comments or hints regarding suicide.

EWE: Ne ewɔ na wò be blanuiléledɔe di be yeaɖe fu nɛ la kplɔe yi kɔdzi ne woadoe kpɔ, (menye blanuiléle vie ƒe nya gblɔm míele o).
ENGLISH: If you suspect depression (not just the blues), consider getting a professional diagnosis.

EWE: Kpe ɖe viwòa ŋu wòazã atike siwo ɖɔktaa nae la nyuie eye ne dɔa meka ɖe eme nɛ o alo ne atikeawo le fu ɖem nɛ la, ele be nàna ɖɔktaa nanya.
ENGLISH: Help your teen adhere to the doctor’s prescribed treatment, and consult the doctor if you see no improvement or observe unpleasant side effects.

EWE: Na wò ƒomea naɖu nu nyuie, minɔ kame dem eye midɔ alɔ̃ nyuie.
ENGLISH: Have a stable family routine for eating, exercising, and sleeping.

EWE: Nɔ dze ɖom kple viwòa ɣesiaɣi eye nàkpe ɖe eŋu wòanɔ te ɖe nu manyomanyo siwo amewo wɔna alo gblɔna ɖe blanuiléledɔlélawo ŋu la nu.
ENGLISH: Maintain good communication with your teen, and help him or her to deal with any stigma associated with depression.

EWE: Esi blanuiléledɔ nana ame sena le eɖokui me be yetsi akogo, ŋukpe lé ye alo viɖe mele ye ŋu o ta la, na viwòa naka ɖe edzi be wò ya elɔ̃ ye ɣesiaɣi.
ENGLISH: Because depression can make one feel alone, ashamed, or worthless, regularly reassure your teen of your love.

EWE: Ŋlɔ Nu Siwo Nàwɔ Ne Dɔa Ho Na Wò La Ði
ENGLISH: Create a "First-Aid Kit " for Your Emotions

EWE: Nu siwo nàwɔ ne dɔa ho na wo la dometɔ aɖewoe nye, ŋkuɖodzinu, mawunyakpukpuiwo, hadzidziwo, nyatiwo kple nuteƒekpɔkpɔwo
ENGLISH: An emotional first-aid kit, including positive and upbuilding momentos, scriptures, songs, articles, and experiences

EWE: Ne blanuiléledɔ le ŋuwò la, nu si akpe ɖe ŋuwò nànɔ te ɖe enue nye be nàŋlɔ nu siwo nàwɔ ne dɔa ho la ɖi.
ENGLISH: If you suffer from depression, a practical suggestion to help you control your thoughts and feelings is to create what has been called an emotional first-aid kit.

EWE: Nu siwo nàŋlɔ siwo ŋu nàte ŋu anɔ asi trɔm le ɣeaɖewoɣi dometɔ aɖewoe nye nu siwo dze le axa sia:
ENGLISH: The kit, which can be adjusted as you see fit, might include the items on this page.

EWE: Ŋlɔ ame siwo nàte ŋu ayɔ alo aƒo ka na ne èlé blanui la ƒe ŋkɔwo ɖi
ENGLISH: Contact information of people to call when you feel down

EWE: Ŋlɔ ha siwo doa dzidzɔ na wò eye wotua wò ɖo la ɖi
ENGLISH: Favorite songs that are positive and upbuilding

EWE: Ŋlɔ nyagbɔgblɔ kple nyati siwo dea dzi ƒo na wò la ɖi
ENGLISH: Inspirational sayings and encouraging articles

EWE: Ŋlɔ nya fakɔname siwo tso Biblia me siwo tua ame ɖo abe Psalmo 34:18; 51:17; 94:19; Filipitɔwo 4:6, 7 ene la ɖi
ENGLISH: A list of comforting and upbuilding sayings from the Bible, such as Psalm 34:18; 51:17; 94:19; Philippians 4:6, 7

EWE: Dzra ŋkuɖodzinu siwo ame siwo lɔ̃ wò na wò la ɖo eye nànɔ wo ŋu dɔ wɔm
ENGLISH: Mementos to remind you of people who love you

EWE: Nɔ nuteƒekpɔkpɔ nyui kple nu nyui siwo nèsusuna siwo nèŋlɔ ɖi la xlẽm
ENGLISH: A journal containing your positive thoughts as well as positive experiences you have enjoyed

EWE: Nu Siwo Gbɔ Nyɔnuviwo Ƒe Blanuiléledɔ Tsona
ENGLISH: Depression and Teenage Girls

EWE: Edze abe blanuiléledɔ ɖea fu na nyɔnuviwo wu ŋutsuviwo ene.
ENGLISH: The incidence of depression in teenage girls appears to be higher than that of boys.

EWE: Nu siwo gbɔ wòtsona dometɔ ɖekae nye be, zi geɖe la, eva hiãna be nyɔnuviwo nanɔ te ɖe seselelãme, ŋutilãme alo gbɔdɔnya siwo wotsɔ ɖea fu na wo la nu.
ENGLISH: One factor may be the stress resulting from emotional, physical, or sexual harassment or abuse, which girls often have to cope with.

EWE: Aƒenɔ Sharon Hersh si nye aɖaŋuɖola bibi aɖe ŋlɔ bena: "Ne nu manyomanyo siwo me tom wole le aƒe me alo suku kple woawo ŋutɔwo ƒe seselelãmewo go do la, ewua tsɔtsɔ na wo eye wotɔtɔna. "
ENGLISH: "When a scary external world and a chaotic internal world collide, " wrote professional counselor Sharon Hersh, "the result is often overwhelming and confusing. "

EWE: Nu siwo nyadzɔdzɔgblɔmɔnuwo hã gblɔna be eyae ana ame ƒe "dzedzeme " nanya kpɔ la kpɔa ŋusẽ ɖe wo dzi madzemadzee.
ENGLISH: Girls may also be unduly influenced by media portrayals of the "ideal " body.

EWE: Nyɔnuvi si buna be yemedze tugbe o alo di be yeƒe nu nadze ye xɔlɔ̃wo ŋu la ate ŋu alé blanuiléledɔ bɔbɔe.
ENGLISH: A girl who sees herself as physically undesirable or who is overly concerned about peer approval may be more vulnerable to depression.

EWE: Nu Kae Mawɔ Be Madzudzɔ Blanuiléle?
ENGLISH: How Can I Stop Being So Sad?

EWE: "Ne ame bubuwo le nɔnɔme sesẽwo me tom la, mekpena ɖe wo ŋu hedea dzi ƒo na wo.
ENGLISH: "When everyone else falls apart, I’m there to fix their problems and make them feel better.

EWE: Gake ame ʋɛ aɖewoe koe nya be ne meyi aƒe me la, menɔa xɔ me hefaa avi. "​ ⁠Kellie.
ENGLISH: But then​ and this is the part that few people see I go home to my room and cry. "​ Kellie.

EWE: "Ne melé blanui la, meɖea ɖokuinye ɖe aga.
ENGLISH: "When I’m down, I isolate myself.

EWE: Ne wokpem na wɔna aɖe la, medoa taflatsɛ.
ENGLISH: If I get invited somewhere, I come up with an excuse not to go.

EWE: Metea ŋu ɣlaa nye blanuilélea ale gbegbe be ƒonyemetɔwo menyana kura be melé blanui o.

EWE: Ne mele nu si li ke ŋu bum la nye susu yia nane si sesẽ goŋgoŋ, glikpɔ sesẽ, si naneke mate ŋu aŋɔ o dzi.
ENGLISH: When I think of something that is fortified, I think of something impenetrable, a structure with stone walls.

ENGLISH: In 2011, Mme. Bazizane Maheshe, the Minister of Education for North Kivu Province, published a provincial circular entitled "Ban Placed on Discrimination Based on Religion, " which described the situation as "deplorable. "

EWE: Wogblɔ tso nyaa ŋu tẽe le agbalẽvia me be: "Woɖea ŋku tɔa sukuvi siwo le suku siwo subɔsubɔhawo doa alɔe me la le esi wogbe be yewomakpɔ gome le subɔsubɔwɔna siwo woɖo le sukuawo me o la ta, eye woŋea aɖaba ƒua Congo-dukɔa ƒe sededewo dzi. "
ENGLISH: The circular addressed the issue clearly by stating: "Students of some religious confessions are subject to discrimination based on internal school rules in disregard of regulations in force in the DR Congo. "

EWE: Nya sia de du le dukɔa me le September (Anyɔnyɔ) 4, 2013 dzi, esi Mwangu Famba, Congo-dukɔa ƒe Dudɔwɔƒe Si Kpɔa Sukudenyawo Gbɔ de se aɖe si bla sukuwo katã le dukɔa me.
ENGLISH: The issue received national attention on September 4, 2013, when Mwangu Famba, the Minister of Education for the Democratic Republic of Congo, published a decree applying to all schools in all districts.

EWE: Wogblɔ le "Sedede Ðe Ŋkutɔtɔ Ame Le Mawusubɔsubɔnyawo Ta Nu Ŋuti Gbalẽvi " la me tẽe be: "Gome le sukuvi ɖe sia ɖe si le sukuwo katã me, eye medze be woatɔ ŋku wo dometɔ aɖeke le eƒe mawusubɔsubɔ ta o. "
ENGLISH: The "Circular on the Prohibition of Discrimination Based on Religion " unequivocally stated: "All children have the right to apply to any school without adverse distinction based on religion. "

EWE: Wogagblɔ le sededea me hã be sukuviwo nyanya le suku le woƒe mawusubɔsubɔ ta nye "dada le Congo-dukɔa ƒe ɖoɖowo kple sewo dzi. "
ENGLISH: The decree also stated that expulsion of students on religious grounds was "in total violation of the standards and laws in force in the Democratic Republic of Congo. "

EWE: Suku geɖewo wɔ ɖe dziɖuɖua ƒe sededea dzi eye wogbugbɔ sukuvi Ðasefoawo xɔ ɖe woƒe sukuawo me.
ENGLISH: Many schools have obeyed the official directives and have welcomed Witness students back into the classroom.

EWE: Gake suku ʋɛ aɖewo gbe.
ENGLISH: A few schools, however, have resisted.

EWE: Eya ta le June (Masa) 12, 2014 dzi la, Dudɔwɔƒe Si Kpɔa Sukudenyawo Gbɔ ɖe nyatakaka aɖe ɖe go le September (Anyɔnyɔ) 2013 me si gado ŋusẽ sedede tsãtɔa eye wòhe susu yi se yeye si Congo Dukplɔla de ku ɖe sukudenyawo ŋu la dzi.
ENGLISH: Thus, on June 12, 2014, the Ministry of Education published a memorandum reinforcing the September 2013 decree and citing the new framework law on education that was issued by the President of the DRC.

EWE: Ŋkuɖodzinya siawo tɔ asi nu si tutu le megbe na kuxi sia dzi eye wona eme kɔ tẽe be ele be woatso ɖe ŋkutɔtɔ ame le eƒe mawusubɔsubɔ ta ŋu eye wòɖo kpe edzi hã be dukɔa kple xexemedukɔwo ƒe sewo le ŋgɔ na sukuwo ŋutɔwo ƒe sededewo.
ENGLISH: This reminder addressed the root cause of the problem by highlighting the importance of fighting discrimination and stressed the primacy of national and international laws over internal school rules.

EWE: Dudɔnunɔla Si Kpɔa Sukudenyawo Gbɔ ɖo nyagɔmekulawo be woaku nya gɔme le suku siwo le dukɔa me godoo ale be woakpɔ ale si wole sedede sia dzi wɔmee.
ENGLISH: The Minister of Education also appointed investigators to visit schools throughout the country to ensure that they abide by the decree.

EWE: Ðikeke mele eme o be nu nyuiwo ado tso dziɖuɖua ƒe afɔɖeɖe siawo me eye wòakpɔ kuxi sia gbɔ eteƒe nadidi.
ENGLISH: No doubt, these measures taken by the government will bring long-standing, positive results.

EWE: Eɖe Vi Na Ame Geɖewo
ENGLISH: Benefits to Many

EWE: Suku siwo le Congo wɔ ɖe sedede sia dzi eye sukuviwo katã ate ŋu akpɔ mɔ be womagatɔ ŋku yewo le suku le yewoƒe mawusubɔsubɔ ta azɔ o.
ENGLISH: As Congolese schools act in accordance with the law, all students can expect to receive an education unencumbered by religious intolerance.

EWE: Sukuviwo asrɔ̃ ale si woade bubu ame sia ame ŋuti, eɖanye subɔsubɔha ka mee wòle o.
ENGLISH: School children will learn to accord respect to all people, regardless of their beliefs.

EWE: Esia ana be Congo Dukplɔsea kple Dudɔwɔƒe Si Kpɔa Sukudenyawo Gbɔ ƒe sededewo dzi ko woawɔ le sukuwo me, eye woɖo ameŋkumemakpɔmakpɔ ƒe kpɔɖeŋu nyui aɖe na dukɔa me sɔhɛwo hã.
ENGLISH: In so doing, Congolese schools will not only uphold the Constitution of the DRC and the decree from the Minister of Education but also set an example of fairness for its young people.

EWE: Wole Ga Me Ƒe Blaevee Nye Esia Le Eritrea​ Enu Ava Yi Gbe Ðeka?
ENGLISH: Twenty Years of Imprisonment in Eritrea​ Will It Ever End?

EWE: Ƒe blaevee nye esi va yi la, Eritrea dziɖuɖumegãwo lé ɖekakpuivi etɔ̃ aɖewo de ga le Sawa Gakpɔ me, wole nɔnɔme madeamedziwo me, eye wogakpɔtɔ le gakpɔa me va se ɖe egbe.
ENGLISH: Twenty years ago, Eritrean authorities arrested three young men and detained them in harsh conditions in the Sawa prison camp, where they remain until this day.

EWE: Wometsɔ nya aɖeke ɖe wo ŋu o, eye womena mɔnukpɔkpɔ aɖeke wo hã be woaɖe wo ɖokuiwo nu le ʋɔnu o.
ENGLISH: They have never been charged with a crime, nor have they been given the opportunity to defend themselves in a court of law.

EWE: Nu ka tae wolé wo de ga madzemadzee?
ENGLISH: Why have they been unjustly imprisoned?

EWE: Paulos Eyassu, Negede Teklemariam kple Isaac Mogos nye Yehowa Ðasefowo, eye wogbe be yewomaxɔ asrafo ƒe hehe o le woƒe mawusubɔsubɔ si womefena kple o ta.
ENGLISH: Paulos Eyasu, Negede Teklemariam, and Isaac Mogos are Jehovah’s Witnesses and conscientiously object to performing military service because of their strongly held religious beliefs.

EWE: Ne ɖe wodrɔ̃ ʋɔnu wo hebu fɔ wo be wowɔ "nu gbegblẽ " le esi wogbe be yewomaxɔ asrafo ƒe hehe o ta la, anye ne woka ƒe aɖe koŋ na wo be woanɔ ga me.
ENGLISH: Had they been formally charged with the "crime " of refusing military service, they would have been sentenced to a fixed prison term.

EWE: Fifia Paulos xɔ ƒe 41, Negede xɔ ƒe 40 eye Isaac hã xɔ ƒe 38, eye wo katã wozã woƒe sɔhɛmenɔɣia katã le ga me.
ENGLISH: Paulos, Negede, and Isaac, now aged 41, 40, and 38 respectively, have spent their youth in confinement.

EWE: Woxɔ srɔ̃ɖeɖe, vidzidzi, wo dzilawo dzi kpɔkpɔ alo agbenɔnɔ ale si woawo ŋutɔ wodii ƒe mɔnukpɔkpɔ le wo si.
ENGLISH: They have been denied the opportunity to marry and have children, give support to their aging parents, or live their lives as they choose.

EWE: Eye woxɔ tadede agu ɖekae kple woƒe haxɔsetɔwo ƒe mɔnukpɔkpɔ hã le wo si.
ENGLISH: They have also been denied the opportunity to worship with their fellow believers.

EWE: Esi wolé Paulos, Negede kple Isaac le September 24, 1994 dzi yi Sawa Gakpɔ me la, gakpɔa dzi kpɔlawo sẽ ŋuta le wo ŋu vevie hewɔ funyafunya wo gɔ̃ hã.
ENGLISH: After their arrest on September 24, 1994, Paulos, Negede, and Isaac were treated severely, even tortured, by authorities in the Sawa prison camp.

EWE: Gake le ƒe ʋɛ siwo va yi me la, womegasẽa ŋuta le wo ŋu ale o, eye womegawɔa funyafunya wo hã o. Ale si woɖoe kplikpaa be yewomaɖe asi le yewoƒe mawudzixɔse ŋu o la na be gakpɔa dzi kpɔlawo dea bubu wo ŋu.
ENGLISH: In recent years, however, the harsh treatment has ended, and their firm determination to remain loyal to their religious beliefs has earned them the respect of the prison guards.

EWE: Ðasefo Bubu Siwo Wolé De Ga Le Nɔnɔme Sesẽwo Me
ENGLISH: Other Witnesses imprisoned in harsh conditions

EWE: Eritrea yee wole Yehowa Ðasefowo yome tim kutɔkutɔe le wu le xexea me godoo.
ENGLISH: It is in Eritrea, more than anywhere else in the world, that Jehovah’s Witnesses experience the most intense persecution.

EWE: Esime míele nyati sia ŋlɔm la, Ðasefo 73 le ga me, nyɔnuwo, ɖeviwo kple ame tsitsiwo hã le wo dome.
ENGLISH: As of this writing, 73 Witnesses are in prison, including women, children, and the elderly.

EWE: Wo dometɔ geɖe le te nɔm ɖe gbedadaƒo ƒe nɔnɔme sesẽ mawo nu, womekpɔa nu nyui ɖuna o, womekpɔa tsi nona wosua wo o, eye gakpɔa dzi kpɔlawo wɔa fu wo vevie.
ENGLISH: Many have endured under harsh desert conditions, lacking a balanced diet and sufficient water and being mistreated by prison officials.

EWE: Wolé Ðasefo etɔ̃ bubu aɖewo hã de ga le Sawa Gakpɔa me ƒe ewo kple edzivɔe nye ema, gake Paulos, Negede kple Isaac le ga me wòdidi wu Ðasefo ɖe sia ɖe le Eritrea.
ENGLISH: Three other Witness men have been imprisoned for more than ten years in the Sawa camp, but Paulos, Negede, and Isaac have been in detention the longest of any other Witnesses in Eritrea.

EWE: Xexemedukɔwo Le Biabiam Tso Eritrea Si Be Wòadzudzɔ Mawusubɔlawo Yome Titi
ENGLISH: International community calls on Eritrea to end religious persecution

EWE: Xexemedukɔwo nyae nyuie be Eritrea dziɖuɖua wɔa fu Yehowa Ðasefowo kple subɔsubɔha sue bubuwo me tɔwo.
ENGLISH: The international community is well-aware of Eritrea’s mistreatment of Jehovah’s Witnesses and other religious minorities.

EWE: Tso ƒe 2004 me la, United States (États-Unis) Dukɔa Ƒe Dɔwɔƒe yɔa Eritrea be enye "dukɔ si ƒe nuwɔna ɖe fu etɔxɛe. " Wozãa "nya sia na dukɔ siwo ƒe dziɖuɖuwo ɖoe koŋ yi edzi xea mɔ ɖe mawusubɔsubɔ ƒe ablɔɖe nu megbemakpɔmakpɔe. "
ENGLISH: Every year since 2004, the U.S. Department of State has designated Eritrea as a "country of particular concern, " which refers to "any country whose government engages in or tolerates particularly severe violations of religious freedom that are systematic, ongoing and egregious. "

EWE: Amegbetɔwo Ƒe Gomenɔamesinyawo Gbɔkpɔha tsi dzi vevie le ale si "Eritrea dziɖuɖumegãwo yi edzi le afɔkpo tum woƒe dukɔmeviwo ƒe gomenɔamesiwo " la ŋu.
ENGLISH: The United Nations Human Rights Council has expressed deep concern at the "grave violations of human rights by the Eritrean authorities against their own population and fellow citizens. "

EWE: Ebia tso Eritrea dziɖuɖua si be wòade bubu "ame sia ame ƒe . . . tamebubu, dzitsinya, mawusubɔsubɔ kple dzixɔse ƒe ablɔɖe ŋu. "
ENGLISH: It calls upon the Eritrean government "to respect everyone’s right to freedom . . . of thought, conscience and religion or belief. "

EWE: United States dukɔa ƒe Dukɔwo Dome Mawusubɔsubɔ Ƒe Ablɔɖe Gbɔkpɔha gblɔ le eƒe ƒe 2014 ƒe Ƒe Sia Ƒe Nyatakaka me be: "Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe mawusubɔsubɔ ƒe ablɔɖe . . . ɖo afɔku me vevie ŋutɔ. "
ENGLISH: The U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom stated in its Annual Report for 2014: "The religious freedom situation is particularly grave for . . . Jehovah’s Witnesses. "

EWE: Amegbetɔ ƒe Gomenɔamesi Dzikpɔha gblɔ le eƒe Ƒe 2013 Xexea Me Ƒe Nyatakaka me be Eritrea dziɖuɖua gakpɔtɔ le mawusubɔsubɔha siwo dzi dziɖuɖua "meda asi ɖo o " la me tɔwo lém hele fu wɔm wo, eye Yehowa Ðasefowo koŋue wotɔ ŋkui.
ENGLISH: In its World Report 2013, Human Rights Watch acknowledged that the Eritrean government continues to arrest, detain, and torture members of "unrecognized " religions and that "Jehovah’s Witnesses are especially victimized. "

EWE: Le December 2005 me la, Afrika Ƒe Amegbetɔwo Kple Dukɔwo Ƒe Gomenɔamesi Ƒe Hakplɔɖoɖowo da asi ɖe Nyametsotso Ku Ðe Amegbetɔ Ƒe Gomenɔamesinyawo Le Eritrea Ŋu dzi eye wòbia tso Eritrea dziɖuɖua si be "wòakpɔ egbɔ be wodrɔ̃ ʋɔnu amewo ameŋkumemakpɔtɔe, woana ame ƒe susu gbɔgblɔ kple nuƒoƒo kpakple kpekpewo wɔwɔ le ŋutifafa me ɣesiaɣi ƒe ablɔɖe amewo. "
ENGLISH: In December 2005 the African Commission on Human and Peoples’ Rights adopted Resolution on the Human Rights Situation in Eritrea, which called on Eritrea to "guarantee, at all times, the right to a fair trial, freedom of opinion and expression as well as the right to peaceful assembly. "

EWE: Philip Brumley, si nye Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe senyawo gbɔ kpɔla gbãtɔ na xexea me godoo gblɔ be: "Míele mɔ kpɔm vevie be Eritrea dziɖuɖua aɖe asi le Yehowa Ðasefo siwo katã le ga me la ŋu, tsɔ kpe ɖe ŋutsu etɔ̃ siawo siwo le ga me ƒe 20 ye nye esia la hã ŋu, eye woadzudzɔ míaƒe haxɔsetɔwo yome titi. "
ENGLISH: Philip Brumley, general counsel for Jehovah’s Witnesses, spoke for Witnesses worldwide when he said: "It is our fervent hope that the government of Eritrea will release all Witness prisoners, including these three men who have been detained for 20 years, and bring an end to the persecution of our fellow believers. "

EWE: Yehowa Ðasefowo Wu Woƒe Dɔwɔƒegã Yeyea Tutu Dɔa Ƒe Akpa Vevitɔ Nu
ENGLISH: Jehovah’s Witnesses Complete Peak Construction Phase of New World Headquarters

EWE: NEW YORK Tso August (Dasiamime) va se ɖe October (Kele) 2015 me la, Yehowa Ðasefowo wu woƒe dɔwɔƒegã yeyea tutu ƒe dɔ si wode to me le Warwick le New York ƒe akpa vevitɔ nu, eye lɔlɔ̃nu faa dɔwɔla 3,800 aɖewoe kpɔa gome le dɔa me gbe sia gbe.
ENGLISH: NEW YORK From August to October 2015, the building of Jehovah’s Witnesses’ new world headquarters in Warwick, New York, was at peak construction, with 3,800 volunteer workers assisting with the project each day.

EWE: Esime dɔa ɖo eƒe ami me la, wotsɔ bɔsu siwo ade 40 lɔa lɔlɔ̃nu faa dɔwɔla 3,800 aɖewo tsɔ yia dɔa wɔƒe galɔa wo yia wo nɔƒewo gbe sia gbe.
ENGLISH: During peak construction, approximately 40 buses were used to help transport some 3,800 volunteers to and from the site each day.

EWE: Woɖaa nu na lɔlɔ̃nu faa dɔwɔlawo le nuɖaƒe enyi siwo woɖo hena dɔa wɔwɔ.
ENGLISH: As many as eight temporary dining rooms have been used to provide meals for the volunteers.

EWE: Tso esime wodze dɔa gɔme le July (Siamlɔm) 2013 me la, Ðasefo 18,000 kple edzivɔwo tso Amerika-dukɔa ƒe du vovovowo me kpɔ gome le dɔa me, wo dometɔ aɖewo tso keke Alaska kple Hawaii gɔ̃ hã.
ENGLISH: Since breaking ground in July 2013, over 18,000 Witnesses have traveled from every state including Alaska and Hawaii to work on the project.

EWE: Dɔwɔla 400 va se ɖe 500 lɔƒo vaa dɔa wɔƒe le kwasiɖanuwuwu ɖe sia ɖe, eye esi woɖo dɔa ƒe ami me ya la, woƒe agbɔsɔsɔme dzi ɖe edzi va ɖo 700 kple edzivɔwo kwasiɖanuwuwu ɖe sia ɖe eye esia yi edzi kwasiɖa ene sɔŋ.
ENGLISH: Approximately 400-500 workers arrive each weekend, although this jumped to well over 700 during the peak phase. A large part of the workforce has volunteered for assignments lasting from one to four weeks.

EWE: Aƒetɔ Richard Devine, si nye Ðasefowo ƒe Warwick Xɔtukɔmitia ƒe zimenɔla gblɔ be: "Esi wònye ame akpe geɖe vaa dɔa me gbe sia gbe ta la, ele be bɔbɔe be amewo nava sɔ gbɔ ɖe dɔa wɔƒe kpaŋkpaŋ.
ENGLISH: Richard Devine, chairman of the Witnesses’ Warwick Construction Project Committee (CPC), explains: "With thousands of people on the job each day, worksites could easily get overcrowded.

EWE: Eya ta míeɖe ame 400 le ŋkekemedɔwɔlawo dzi be woawɔ dɔ tso ŋdɔ ga 3 va se ɖe fɔŋli ga 2 ale be nuwo nanɔ ɖoɖo nu le dɔa wɔƒe. "
ENGLISH: To keep things organized and efficient, we took about 400 from the day shift and assigned them to work from 3 p.m. to 2 a.m. "

EWE: Ame siawo wɔ dɔ tso May (Damɛ) va se ɖe September (Anyɔnyɔ).
ENGLISH: That second shift lasted from May through September.

EWE: Woɖe foto afi si anye Ðasefowo ƒe dɔwɔƒegã yeyea ƒe mɔnu la le anyinufaɣi.
ENGLISH: A view at sunset of what will be the main entrance to the Witnesses’ new world headquarters complex.

EWE: Aƒetɔ Richard Devine gblɔ be woawu mlɔƒe eneawo dometɔ eve tututu nu le January (Dzove) 2016 me abe ale si woɖoe ene.
ENGLISH: The CPC reports that two of the four residence buildings will be completed by January 2016, as originally planned.

EWE: Aƒetɔ Devine gagblɔ be, "ale si ame gbogbo aɖewo kpe asi ɖe dɔa ŋu ta la, dɔ bliboa do ŋgɔ na ɣeyiɣi si wòle be wòawu enu la ɣleti ene sɔŋ. "
ENGLISH: However, according to Mr. Devine, "the overall project is four months ahead of schedule thanks to what has been a huge coordinated effort. "

EWE: Woɖoe be woawu mlɔƒe susɔeawo, dɔwɔxɔawo kple nudzraɖoƒea nu le September (Anyɔnyɔ) 1, 2016 dzi.
ENGLISH: The remaining residence, office, and maintenance buildings are now scheduled for completion by September 1, 2016.

EWE: Dɔwɔƒegã yeye tuƒe si wonɔ yame ɖe foto.
ENGLISH: Aerial view of the new world headquarters site.

EWE: Kadodowo:
ENGLISH: Contact(s):

EWE: Ðasefowo Te Woƒe Teƒe Siwo Le Brooklyn Dzadzra
ENGLISH: Witnesses Begin Highly Anticipated Sale of Brooklyn Properties

EWE: NEW YORK Yehowa Ðasefowo le woƒe teƒe siwo le Dumbo kple Brooklyn Heights si le Brooklyn le New York, siwo amewo le mɔ kpɔm na vevie be yewoaƒle la dzram.
ENGLISH: NEW YORK Jehovah’s Witnesses are selling some of the most sought-after properties in Dumbo and Brooklyn Heights in Brooklyn, New York.

EWE: Asiƒoƒo ƒe wɔnawo dze egɔme ku ɖe teƒe si nye 85 Jay Street si nye Brooklyn ƒe akpa gãtɔ siwo dzi womewɔ dɔ ɖo o la dometɔ ɖeka kple mlɔƒe si nye dziƒoxɔ dzisasrã-ewo si le 124 Columbia Heights la ŋu.
ENGLISH: The competitive offering process has begun for 85 Jay Street, one of Brooklyn’s largest undeveloped sites, and the ten-story residence at 124 Columbia Heights.

EWE: Wole afi si woƒe dɔwɔƒegã le fifia si nye 25/30 Columbia Heights la hã dzram.
ENGLISH: The current location of their world headquarters, 25/30 Columbia Heights, is also on the market.

EWE: Gbetakpɔxɔ Habɔbɔa Ƒe Nunɔamesiwo Dzadzra Ƒe Dɔwɔƒee le teƒe etɔ̃ siawo dzadzra ƒe ɖoɖoa dzi kpɔm, eye wokpɔ mɔ be adzra wo vovovo.
ENGLISH: The three properties are being offered by the Watchtower Real Estate Office and are expected to sell in separate transactions.

EWE: Richard Devine, si nye Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe nyanuɖela aɖe, gblɔ tso anyigba si ƒe kekeme nye meta 12,500 togodo si le 85 Jay Street ŋu be: "Teƒea xɔ Dumbo-nutoa ƒe akpa gã aɖe eye teƒe si woxɔ mɔɖeɖe be woate ŋu awɔ dɔ ɖo la keke meta 93,000 togodo kloe. "
ENGLISH: Richard Devine, a spokesman for Jehovah’s Witnesses, states concerning the 135,000-square-foot (12,542 sq m) parcel at 85 Jay Street: "The site spans an entire city block in the dynamic Dumbo neighborhood and has nearly one million square feet of development rights. "

EWE: Teƒe si nye 85 Jay Street la le Manhattan Ana gbɔ le Dumbo-nuto si me amewo sɔa gbɔ ɖo fũu.
ENGLISH: The 85 Jay Street property sits at the base of the Manhattan Bridge in the vibrant Dumbo neighborhood.

EWE: Ðasefowo ƒe mlɔƒe aɖe le teƒe si keke meta 14,000 togodo le 124 Columbia Heights si le afi si amewo ɖia tsa le le Brooklyn Heights nuto ɖedzesi la me.
ENGLISH: The Witnesses’ 152,000-square-foot (14,121 sq m) residential building at 124 Columbia Heights is located on the promenade in the acclaimed Brooklyn Heights Historic District.

EWE: Aƒetɔ Devine gblɔ be: "Enye xɔ ɖedzesi aɖe, eye ne wole Brooklyn Ana dzi, Ablɔɖe Ƒe Kpetata kple Anyigbe Manhattan kpɔe la, enya kpɔna ŋutɔ. "
ENGLISH: "It’s a remarkable building with spectacular views of the Brooklyn Bridge, the Statue of Liberty, and the impressive Lower Manhattan skyline, " states Mr. Devine.

EWE: Xɔ si nye 124 Columbia Heights le Brooklyn Heights nuto ɖedzesi la me.
ENGLISH: 124 Columbia Heights is located in the historic Brooklyn Heights neighborhood.

EWE: Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe dɔwɔƒegã la le 25/30 Columbia Heights (foto etametɔ) ƒe geɖee nye esia, eye New York dua me tɔ geɖewo nyae nyuie le Gbetakpɔxɔ ƒe dzesi ɖedzesi la kple gaƒoɖokui si le afi ma la ta.
ENGLISH: The world headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses has been located at 25/30 Columbia Heights (top image) for decades and is familiar to many New Yorkers for its marquee Watchtower sign and clock.

EWE: Xɔ sia xɔ teƒe si keke wu meta 68,000 togodo la xɔ dua ƒe xɔ tsrala eve kloe xɔƒe, eye ame siwo le Brooklyn Ana dzi la tea ŋu kpɔnɛ nyuie.
ENGLISH: The property, totaling over 733,000 square feet (68,098 sq m), covers almost two city blocks and offers unobstructed views of the Brooklyn Bridge.

EWE: Aƒetɔ Devine gblɔ tso taɖodzinu vevitɔ si le Ðasefoawo si ŋu be, "Teƒe siawo dzadzra nye ɖoɖo si míewɔ be míaɖe míaƒe dɔwɔƒegã la ayi Warwick le New York ƒe akpa aɖe ko. "
ENGLISH: Commenting on the larger scope of the Witnesses’ plans, Mr. Devine adds, "These sales are the next steps in relocating our world headquarters to Warwick, New York. "

ENGLISH: The mayor of Vienna’s Meidling District, Gabriele Votava, was the key speaker at the curbside unveiling of the plaque affixed to the outside of the Steinacher family’s former residence in Meidling, Vienna at Lägenfeldgasse 68.

EWE: Wɔnaa ƒe tanyae nye "Nyemate ŋu ada tu o. " Nya siae aƒetɔ Steinacher gblɔ esime wònɔ biabiam be woakpɔ nublanui na ye.
ENGLISH: The program bore the theme "I just can’t shoot, " the explanation Mr. Steinacher uttered during his petition for clemency.

ENGLISH: Equipped with medicine supplied by Witnesses in Bangladesh, India, and Japan, as well as mobile equipment for surgery and intensive care, this team from Europe worked with the Nepal Disaster Relief Committee to treat patients at Kingdom Halls in the earthquake zone.

ENGLISH: The relief team is based in a Kingdom Hall in Kathmandu where Witness victims are given food and shelter.

ENGLISH: Gamaliel Camarillo, a spokesman for Jehovah’s Witnesses in Mexico, states, "During the four days that we operated the booth, we had over 10,000 visitors and distributed almost 29,000 pieces of literature, free of charge.

ENGLISH: The branch office of Jehovah’s Witnesses in Chile reported that no Witnesses were killed or seriously injured.

ENGLISH: One Kingdom Hall, a place of worship, was completely destroyed and two others were damaged by the flooding.

ENGLISH: Property destroyed in the city of Diego de Almagro, a town severely damaged by the floods.

EWE: Le Copiapó, si nye du siwo me tsiɖɔɖɔa gblẽ nu le wu dometɔ ɖeka me la, Yehowa Ðasefowo ɖo kpekpeɖeŋunakɔmitiwo be woaxɔ nyatakakawo eye woadzra teƒeawo ɖo.
ENGLISH: In Copiapó, one of the cities hardest hit by the floods, Jehovah’s Witnesses formed a relief committee to gather information and organize the cleanup efforts.

ENGLISH: Witnesses from the cities of Antofagasta, Arica, Calama, Caldera, Iquique, and La Serena immediately sent supplies to support their fellow worshippers in need.

ENGLISH: Our efforts are also focused on providing comfort and encouragement to everyone devastated by the floods. "

EWE: Yehowa Ðasefowo Ðo Amerika Tokunɔgbegɔmeɖeƒe Le Florida

ENGLISH: The Witnesses make their ASL videos available online at jw.org and on DVD.

ENGLISH: He continues: "There are some 45 countries where ASL is used and, as is the case with spoken languages, deaf people have regional accents when signing.
