EWE: Esi wose be Ebola dɔlélea le Guinea eye be ekaka enumake ɖe dukɔ siwo nye Liberia kple Sierra Leone me la, Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe alɔdzedɔwɔƒe siwo le dukɔ siawo me ŋlɔ lɛta ɖo ɖe hame siwo le dukɔ siawo me be woanɔ ŋudzɔ.
ENGLISH: Upon learning that the Ebola virus had been found in Guinea and had quickly spread to nearby Liberia and Sierra Leone, branch offices of Jehovah’s Witnesses in the region immediately sent letters to alert all congregations in the three countries.

EWE: Le lɛtaa me la, woŋlɔ dziɖuɖudɔwɔƒe ƒe mɔfiamewo kple aɖaŋuɖoɖo siwo ku ɖe dɔlékuia, ale si wòkakanae kple nu si woate ŋu awɔ be dɔlékuia nagakaka o la ŋu.
ENGLISH: Incorporating guidelines and suggestions provided by local government agencies, the letters explained the dangers of the virus, how the virus is transmitted, and what precautionary measures should be taken to prevent the spread of the disease.

EWE: Aƒetɔ Collin Attick, si nye Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe nyanuɖela le Sierra Leone, gblɔ be: "Míele dukɔ aɖe si me amewo mesea dɔlélewo gɔme nyuie o eye wokakaa aʋatsonyawo tso Ebola dɔlélea ŋu la me, eya ta amewo tɔtɔ le gɔmedzedzea me eye womenya nu si woawɔ o.
ENGLISH: "Being in an area where medical diseases are not well understood and where false rumors about the source of Ebola were widespread, many people were initially confused about what to do, " states Collin Attick, spokesman for Jehovah’s Witnesses in Sierra Leone.

EWE: Gake esi woxlẽ lɛtaa me mɔfiamewo na hameawo la, wotso enumake wɔ ɖe mɔfiameawo dzi. "
ENGLISH: "But when our congregation members heard the instructions at their Kingdom Hall, they responded promptly and positively. "

EWE: Le July me la, wowɔ ɖoɖo tɔxɛ aɖe be dzikpɔla mɔzɔlawo nayi aɖasrã hame siwo le Sierra Leone kple Guinea la kpɔ ŋkeke eve.
ENGLISH: In July, traveling representatives of Jehovah’s Witnesses began making special two-day visits to each congregation in Sierra Leone and Guinea.

EWE: Sasrãkpɔa ƒe nuƒoa ƒe tanyae nye "Toɖoɖo Kpɔa Ame Ta, " be woatsɔ akpe ɖe wo nɔviwo ŋu woakpɔ wo ɖokuiwo ta tso dɔlélea si me eye woado ŋusẽ wo woayi edzi awɔ ɖe mɔfiame yeye siwo wona wo la dzi.
ENGLISH: The visits feature a talk entitled "Obedience Saves Lives, " with the objective of increasing awareness of practical safeguards against the disease as well as encouraging continued adherence to the latest guidelines available.

EWE: Sasrãkpɔ sia ayi edzi va se ɖe November 2014 me.
ENGLISH: These visits will continue through November 2014.

EWE: Tsɔ kpe ɖe eŋu la, Ðasefoawo da tsi si me wokɔ dɔlékuiwutike (bleach alo l’eau de Javel) ɖo la ɖe woƒe tadeaguƒewo (siwo woyɔna be Fiaɖuƒe Akpatawo) ƒe mɔnu le Guinea, Liberia kple Sierra Leone.
ENGLISH: Additionally, the Witnesses provided hand-washing stations containing water mixed with bleach at the entrance of each of the Witnesses’ places for worship (known as Kingdom Halls) in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone.

EWE: Ðasefo geɖe siwo le dukɔ siawo me le zɔzɔm ɖe asikɔklɔ ƒe ɖoɖo sia ke nu le woƒe aƒewo me.
ENGLISH: Most Witnesses in these countries are following that example, providing a hand-washing station at their home.

EWE: Ðasefowo ƒe ƒome aɖe wɔ ɖe se si wode be ame aɖeke megayi Dolo-nuto, si le Monrovia ƒe ɣedzeƒe le Liberia la, me o alo ado le eme o la dzi.
ENGLISH: As a precaution, a Witness family cooperates with an area quarantine in Dolo’s Town, a community east of Monrovia, Liberia.

EWE: Woɖe mɔxeɖenu sia ɖa le September 8, 2014 dzi.
ENGLISH: The quarantine was lifted on September 8, 2014.

EWE: Xexea Me Lãmesẽ Habɔbɔ ka nya ta le October 1, 2014 dzi be ame 7,178 xɔ Ebola le Ɣetoɖoƒe Afrika eye ame 3,300 kple edzivɔe dɔlélea wu, gake wokpɔ mɔ be xexlẽmea adzi ɖe edzi.
ENGLISH: According to a report by the World Health Organization dated October 1, 2014, there have been 7,178 cases reported and more than 3,300 victims have died in the current outbreak of Ebola in West Africa, although the numbers are expected to increase.

EWE: Va se ɖe October 2 la, Ðasefo 2,800 siwo le Guinea kple Sierra Leone dometɔ ɖeka si nye nyɔnu dɔnɔdzikpɔla aɖe koe xɔ Ebola dɔlélea, eye wòku le September 25, 2014 dzi.
ENGLISH: As of October 2, of the 2,800 Witnesses in Guinea and Sierra Leone, one female Witness who was a nurse contracted the Ebola virus and died on September 25, 2014.

EWE: Le Ðasefo 6,365 siwo le Liberia dome la, ame 10 ye ku le dɔlélea si me; ame 6 nye lãmesẽdɔwɔlawo.
ENGLISH: Of the 6,365 Witnesses in Liberia, 10 have died as a result of the disease; 6 were health workers.

EWE: Togbɔ be dɔlékuia kaka va Nigeria nyitsɔ laa hã la, Ðasefo siwo le afi ma la dometɔ aɖeke mexɔ dɔlélea o.
ENGLISH: Although the virus has also spread into Nigeria recently, none of the Witnesses there have contracted the disease.

EWE: Gakpe ɖe eŋu la, Ðasefo dutanyanyuigblɔla (mawunyadɔgbedela) siwo le dukɔ siawo me dometɔ aɖeke mexɔ dɔa o, elabena esi dɔa nɔ kakam la, dutanyanyuigblɔlaawo yi mɔkeke eye ɖewo hã yi takpekpe le Europa kple Amerika.
ENGLISH: Additionally, no Witness missionaries in these countries are reported to be infected; as the virus was spreading, a number of these missionaries were away on vacation or attending conventions in Europe and the United States.

EWE: Ame aɖewo trɔ yi woƒe dɔwo dzi eye wole wɔwɔm ɖe afɔɖoƒe kple mɔfiame vevi siwo alɔdzedɔwɔƒea na hamewo la dzi.
ENGLISH: Some have recently returned to their missionary activity and are heeding necessary precautions and instructions from the local branch office.

EWE: Dutanyanyuigblɔla bubuwo hã di be yewoagbɔ, gake esi womekpɔ ɖe mɔ na yameʋuwo be woava du mawo me o hekpe ɖe nɔnɔme bubu aɖewo ŋuti ta la, womegbɔ haɖe o.
ENGLISH: Other missionaries are waiting to return due to flight restrictions or other circumstances.

EWE: Asiklɔƒe si le Fiaɖuƒe Akpata aɖe nu le Sierra Leone.
ENGLISH: A hand-washing station at a Kingdom Hall in Sierra Leone.

EWE: Ðasefowo ƒe lɔlɔ̃nu faa dɔwɔlawo ƒe kɔmitiwo le kpekpem ɖe Ðasefo siwo le Ɣedzeƒe Afrika-dukɔ, siwo me Ebola gblẽ nu le vevie la ŋu, wole woƒe ƒomewo kple woƒe haxɔsetɔwo ƒe nuhiahiãwo gbɔ kpɔm.
ENGLISH: Relief committees of Witness volunteers are assisting local Witnesses in caring for the needs of their families and fellow worshippers in the West African countries hardest hit by Ebola.

EWE: Aƒetɔ Thomas Nyain, si nye Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe nyanuɖela le Liberia, gblɔ be: "Wɔwɔ ɖe Biblia ƒe aɖaŋuɖoɖo siwo ku ɖe dzadzɛnyenye kple dɔnɔwo ɖeɖe ɖe aga dzi le kpekpem ɖe mía ŋu míele te nɔm ɖe nɔnɔme siawo nu.
ENGLISH: "Following Bible principles of cleanliness and quarantine is helping us to deal with this situation, " states Thomas Nyain, Sr., spokesman for Jehovah’s Witnesses in Liberia.

EWE: Esi wònye Yehowa Ðasefowoe míenye ta la, míeƒoa asa na ameɖiɖikɔnu siwo mewɔ ɖeka kple Biblia o.
ENGLISH: "As Jehovah’s Witnesses, we also avoid unscriptural burial practices.

EWE: Esia le míaƒe hameviwo ta kpɔm, vevietɔ le ɣeyiɣi dziŋɔ sia me. "
ENGLISH: This is proving to be a protection for all of our members, especially during this critical time. "

EWE: Le Sierra Leone la, wogblɔ nu vovovo siwo Yehowa Ðasefowo wɔ tsɔ kpe ɖe woƒe hameviwo kple nutoa me tɔ bubuwo ŋu woƒo asa na Ebola dɔlélea le nutoa me ƒe radio aɖe dzi.
ENGLISH: In Sierra Leone, an announcement aired on a local radio station outlining how Jehovah’s Witnesses helped their members and non-Witnesses in the community to avoid the Ebola virus.

EWE: Dziɖuɖumegã siwo le afi ma hã bia tso Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe kpekpeɖeŋunakɔmitia me tɔwo si be woakpe asi ɖe dziɖuɖu ƒe dɔwɔha siwo le nutoa me la ŋu.
ENGLISH: The authorities there also requested that the Witnesses’ relief committee assist the government’s agencies in the region.

EWE: Aƒetɔ J. R. Brown, si nye Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe nyanuɖela le woƒe dɔwɔƒegã le New York, gblɔ be: "Dzi ɖo mía ƒo esi míekpɔ ale si míaƒe haxɔsetɔ siwo le Ɣetoɖoƒe Afrika la ɖɔa ŋu ɖo ne wole woƒe mawusubɔsubɔdɔwo kple Biblia-fiafiadɔwo wɔm ale si woate ŋui.
ENGLISH: "We are encouraged to see our fellow believers in West Africa exercising caution while continuing their spiritual activities and Bible education work to the extent possible, " comments J. R. Brown, international spokesman at the Witnesses’ world headquarters in New York.

EWE: Ehiã vevie be míanɔ gbe dom ɖa ɖe míaƒe haxɔsetɔwo kple ame bubu siwo ŋu Ebola dɔlélea gblẽ nu le la ta. "
ENGLISH: "Our spiritual brothers and sisters and others coping with the impact of this Ebola virus are in our thoughts and prayers. "

EWE: Dukɔwo Dome Takpekpe Ŋuti Nyatakakawo: Ðasefowo Wɔ Takpekpe Ðedzesiwo Le MetLife Bɔlƒoƒea
ENGLISH: International Convention Coverage: Witnesses Hold Historic Conventions at MetLife Stadium

EWE: NEW YORK Le June 20 va se ɖe 22 kple June 27 va se ɖe 29, 2014 dzi la, Yehowa Ðasefo gbogbo aɖewo va ƒo ƒu ɖe MetLife Bɔlƒoƒea le Ɣedzeƒe Rutherford le New Jersey hena "Yi Edzi Nànɔ Mawu Fiaɖuƒea Dim Gbã! "
ENGLISH: NEW YORK On June 20-22 and June 27-29, 2014, Jehovah’s Witnesses packed the MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, for the "Keep Seeking First God’s Kingdom! "

EWE: Dukɔwo Dome Takpekpe siwo woawɔ, eye wowɔ takpekpea le Eŋlisigbe kple Spainiagbe me.
ENGLISH: International Convention series, with programs presented in English and Spanish respectively.

EWE: Ame siwo de takpekpea le kwasiɖanuwuwu eveawo ƒe agbɔsɔsɔe nye 118,000, takpekpe gã eve siawo na míeɖo ŋku takpekpe gã siwo wowɔ kpɔ le New York du gãwo me ƒe geɖewoe nye ema va yi la dzi.
ENGLISH: With a peak attendance for both weekends totaling over 118,000, these two gatherings represented the Witnesses’ largest convention in the New York metropolitan area in decades.

EWE: Woto videokadodo dzi na ame 407,000 kple edzivɔ siwo ƒo ƒu ɖe nuto bubuwo me la hã kpɔ gome le wɔnaa ƒe akpa vevi aɖewo me si wɔe be ameawo katã ƒe agbɔsɔsɔ va nye 525,500.
ENGLISH: Over 407,000 in other cities were tied in by video to select portions of the programs, bringing the total combined attendance to over 525,500.

EWE: Wɔnaa ƒe akpa geɖewo lɔ nuteƒekpɔkpɔwo wɔwɔ fia kple video siwo ɖe ale si Biblia me mɔfiamewo ɖea vie me la fia.
ENGLISH: Many program parts featured reenactments and videos demonstrating the practical application of Bible principles.

EWE: Dɔdzikpɔhaa me tɔe ƒoa ŋkeke ɖe sia ɖe ƒe nuƒo mamlɛtɔ.
ENGLISH: Both conventions concluded each day with a lecture from a member of the Governing Body of Jehovah’s Witnesses.

EWE: David Splane ye ƒo nu le takpekpe si wowɔ tso June 20 va se ɖe 22 me; eye Geoffrey Jackson ye ƒoe tso June 27 va se ɖe 29 dzi.
ENGLISH: David Splane spoke on June 20-22; Geoffrey Jackson, on June 27-29.

EWE: Wonyrɔ amewo le takpekpe siawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe me.
ENGLISH: Each convention also included a baptism.

EWE: Ame siwo wonyrɔ le takpekpewɔƒeawo ƒe agbɔsɔsɔe nye 1,255, eye ame siwo wonyrɔ le teƒe bubu siwo amewo ƒo ƒu ɖoe nye ame 2,930 si wɔe be nyɔnyrɔxɔlawo katã ƒe agbɔsɔsɔ va le 4,185.
ENGLISH: A total of 1,255 people were baptized in the stadium, and another 2,930 were baptized at satellite locations, bringing the total number of those baptized to 4,185.

EWE: Vavalwo dometɔ aɖewo tso Argentina, Australia, Belize, Britain, Chile, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Germany, Greece, Guatemala, Honduras, Italy, Malaysia, Mexico, Nicaragua, Panama, Peru, Spain kple Venezuela.
ENGLISH: Attendees included delegates invited from Argentina, Australia, Belize, Britain, Chile, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Germany, Greece, Guatemala, Honduras, Italy, Malaysia, Mexico, Nicaragua, Panama, Peru, Spain, and Venezuela.

EWE: Aƒetɔ J. R. Brown, si nye Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe nyanuɖela gblɔ be: "Takpekpe sia ɖo ŋku takpekpe ɖedzesi si wowɔ le New York le ƒe 1958 me dzi na mía dometɔ geɖe.
ENGLISH: J. R. Brown, a spokesman for Jehovah’s Witnesses, states: "This event reminded many of us of our historic convention in New York back in 1958.

EWE: Le takpekpe siwo wowɔ le Yankee Stadium kple teƒe si woyɔna tsã be Polo Grounds la, valawo wu ame 253,000.
ENGLISH: Between Yankee Stadium and the then existing Polo Grounds, over 253,000 attended that event.

EWE: Takpekpe siwo míewɔ le MetLife Bɔlƒoƒea le ƒe sia me la ɖe dzesi ŋutɔ le Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe ŋutinya me. "
ENGLISH: The conventions at MetLife Stadium this year will certainly be considered milestones in the history of Jehovah’s Witnesses. "

EWE: Xlẽ nyati si nye The Record si ƒo nu tso dukɔwo dome takpekpe si wowɔ le MetLife Bɔlƒoƒea ŋu.
ENGLISH: Read an article from The Record covering the international conventions in MetLife Stadium.

EWE: Amewo nyɔnyrɔ ƒe foto si dze le nyadzɔdzɔgbalẽ aɖe ƒe ŋgɔgbekpa dzi.
ENGLISH: A photo of the baptism was featured on the front page of the newspaper (pictured).

EWE: Yehowa Ðasefowo Ƒo Zi Ðe MetLife Bɔlƒoƒea Kpaŋkpaŋ (PDF)
ENGLISH: Jehovah’s Witnesses Pack MetLife Stadium (PDF)

EWE: Wowɔ Ŋkuɖodziwɔna Aɖe Le Sachsenhausen Tsɔ De Bubu Yehowa Ðasefo Aɖe Si Nazitɔwo Wu Ŋu
ENGLISH: Sachsenhausen Memorial to Honor One of Jehovah’s Witnesses Executed by Nazis

EWE: SELTERS, Germany Le September 16, 2014 dzi la, Brandenburg Ŋkuɖodzi Ƒe Habɔbɔ awɔ wɔna vevi aɖe atsɔ aɖo ŋku kufia si wotso na August Dickmann hewui le Sachsenhausen fuwɔamegakpɔ me la ƒe ƒe 75 lia dzi.
ENGLISH: SELTERS, Germany On September 16, 2014, the Brandenburg Memorials Foundation will host a special event to remember the 75th anniversary of the execution of August Dickmann in the Sachsenhausen concentration camp.

EWE: Aƒetɔ August Dickmann ye nye ame gbãtɔ si gbe asrafodɔwɔwɔ ɖe dzitsinya ta eye Nazitɔwo wui le dutoƒo le Xexemeʋa II me.
ENGLISH: He was the first conscientious objector publicly executed by the Nazis in World War II.

EWE: August Dickmann, ƒe 1936 lɔƒo.
ENGLISH: August Dickmann, circa 1936.

EWE: Wolé Aƒetɔ Dickmann de ga le October 1937 me le Sachsenhausen fuwɔamegakpɔ me le Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe dzixɔse siwo me wòlé ɖe asi ta.
ENGLISH: In October 1937, Mr. Dickmann was imprisoned in the Sachsenhausen concentration camp because of his beliefs as one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.

EWE: Esi Xexemeʋa II dze egɔme le ƒe 1939 me ƒe ŋkeke etɔ̃ megbe la, adzamekpovitɔwo lé Aƒetɔ Dickmann eye wobia tso esi be wòade asi asrafogbalẽvi te ahazu Germanytɔwo ƒe asrafo.
ENGLISH: Three days after the outbreak of World War II in 1939, the Gestapo summoned Mr. Dickmann and asked him to sign a military identification card, which would have enlisted him in the German army.

EWE: Esi Aƒetɔ Dickmann gbe la, wolée de ame ɖekɛ gaxɔ me eye gaxɔdzikpɔla bia tso SS-srafowo ƒe amegã si be wòaɖe mɔ na ye yeawu Aƒetɔ Dickmann le etɔ gamenɔlawo katã ŋkume.
ENGLISH: When Mr. Dickmann refused, he was placed in solitary confinement and the camp commander sought permission from the head of the SS to execute Mr. Dickmann in the presence of all other camp inmates.

EWE: Le September 15, 1939 dzi la, wozi Yehowa Ðasefo alafa geɖe siwo dome Aƒetɔ Dickmann nɔvi kpamkpam Heinrich hã le la dzi be woakpɔ ewuwu teƒe.
ENGLISH: On September 15, 1939, hundreds of Jehovah’s Witnesses, including Mr. Dickmann’s fleshly brother Heinrich, were forced to watch the execution.

EWE: Le ŋkeke eve megbe la, nyadzɔdzɔgbalẽ si nye The New York Times gblɔ tso Germany be: "Asrafowo da tu August Dickmann si xɔ 29 . . . wòku. "
ENGLISH: Two days later, The New York Times reported from Germany: "August Dickmann, 29 years old, . . . has been shot here by a firing squad. "

EWE: Nyadzɔdzɔgbalẽa gblɔ kpee be esi wògbe be yemawɔ asrafodɔ o "le eƒe mawusubɔsubɔ tae " wowui ɖo.
ENGLISH: The newspaper further noted that he was sentenced for refusing military service "because of religious scruples. "

EWE: Le September 18, 1999 dzi la, wowɔ ŋkuɖodzikpe aɖe ɖe Sachsenhausen fuwɔamegakpɔ si me wònɔ tsã la ƒe gli aɖe ŋu tsɔ de bubu Yehowa Ðasefo 890 kple edzivɔ siwo wode ga le afi ma la ŋu.
ENGLISH: On September 18, 1999, a plaque honoring the over 890 Jehovah’s Witnesses imprisoned in Sachsenhausen was placed on the outer wall of the former concentration camp.

EWE: Wogawɔ ŋkuɖodzikpe bubu aɖe hã tsɔ de bubu Aƒetɔ Dickmann ŋu.
ENGLISH: Additionally, a memorial stone was unveiled in honor of Mr. Dickmann.

EWE: Woadze ŋkuɖodzizã 75 lia gɔme le afi si Aƒetɔ Dickmann ƒe ŋkuɖodzikpea le, eyome woava ƒo nuƒo aɖewo le afi si gamenɔlawo ƒe nuɖaƒe nɔ tsã.
ENGLISH: The 75th anniversary event will begin at the site of Mr. Dickmann’s memorial, followed by speeches made in the former prisoners’ kitchen.

EWE: Wokpe amegã Detlef Garbe, ame si ɖo Neuengamme Fuwɔamegakpɔ Ƒe Ŋkuɖodzi, si ganye edzikpɔla la be wòava ƒo nuƒo le afi sia.
ENGLISH: Dr. Detlef Garbe, author and director of the Neuengamme Concentration Camp Memorial, will be the guest lecturer.

EWE: Lillian Gobitas Klose, Sukuvi Si Ŋuti Ʋɔnudrɔ̃ƒe Kɔkɔtɔ Ƒe Nyadɔdrɔ̃ Ðedzesi Aɖe Ku Ðo Le Ƒe 1940 Me La Ku Le Eƒe Ƒe 90 Lia Xɔxɔ Me
ENGLISH: Lillian Gobitas Klose, Schoolgirl at Center of Historic 1940 Supreme Court Case, Dies at 90

EWE: NEW YORK​ Lillian Gobitas Klose, si tso nya me be yemado gbe na aflaga o eye wodrɔ̃ ʋɔnu ɖedzesi aɖee le Amerika Ƒe Ʋɔnudrɔ̃ƒe Kɔkɔtɔ la, ku le eƒe aƒe me le Fayetteville si le Georgia le August 22, 2014 dzi.
ENGLISH: NEW YORK Lillian Gobitas Klose, whose personal decision not to salute the flag placed her in the center of a landmark United States Supreme Court case, died in her home in Fayetteville, Georgia on August 22, 2014.

EWE: Exɔ ƒe 90.
ENGLISH: She was 90 years of age.

EWE: William Henry Gobitas (miame ɖaa), Walter Gobitas kple Lillian Gobitas esime wonya ɖeviwo le suku esi wogbe be yewomado gbe na aflaga o ta le ƒe 1935 me.
ENGLISH: William Henry Gobitas (far left), Walter Gobitas, and Lillian Gobitas after the children were expelled from school for not saluting the flag in 1935.

EWE: Lɛta si Lillian Gobitas ŋlɔ na Minersville Sukutatɔwo le ƒe 1935 me tsɔ ʋli eƒe xɔse tae.
ENGLISH: Letter that Lillian Gobitas wrote to the Minersville School Board in 1935, defending her faith.

EWE: Lillian Gobitas kple nɔvia ŋutsu William tso nya me be yewomagado gbe na aflaga azɔ o esi wose dukɔa ƒe radio dzi wɔna aɖe le October 6, 1935 dzi, si ƒo nu tso se si Biblia de ku ɖe trɔ̃subɔsubɔ ŋu vɔ megbe.
ENGLISH: Lillian Gobitas and her younger brother William, both Jehovah’s Witnesses, personally decided to stop saluting the flag after hearing a national radio broadcast on October 6, 1935, that focused on Biblical commands against idolatry.

EWE: Yehowa Ðasefowoe wo ame evea siaa nye.
ENGLISH: A few weeks later they were expelled from school for their stand.

EWE: Le kwasiɖa ʋɛ aɖewo megbe la, wonya wo le suku esi wogbe be yewomado gbe na aflaga o.
ENGLISH: Their father, Walter, filed suit to protect the rights of his children and won in the local courts.

EWE: Wo fofo, Walter, tsɔ nya yi nutomeʋɔnudrɔ̃ƒewo heʋli ɖeviawo ƒe gomenɔamesi ta eye wòɖu dzi.
ENGLISH: The school board appealed to the Supreme Court and on June 3, 1940, the resulting court case, Minersville School District v. Gobitis (the family name was misspelled in the court records), was decided against the Gobitases.

EWE: Sukutatɔwo tsɔ nyaa yi Ʋɔnudrɔ̃ƒe Kɔkɔtɔ le June 3, 1940 dzi be woagbugbɔ nyaa adrɔ̃ na yewo. Esi wogbugbɔ nya sia si wona ŋkɔe be Minersville Nutomesuku kple Gobitis (womeŋlɔ tɔgbuiŋkɔa nyuie le ʋɔnudrɔ̃ƒea ƒe nuŋlɔɖiwo me o) drɔ̃ la, nya la va yi Gobitas ƒomea dzi.
ENGLISH: Three years later, on Flag Day, June 14, 1943, the Supreme Court overturned the 1940 Gobitis ruling, in its decision of West Virginia State Board of Education v. Barnette, allowing Witness children to return to school.

EWE: Esiae nye zi gbãtɔ Amerika Ʋɔnudrɔ̃ƒe Kɔkɔtɔ trɔ nyametsotso si wòwɔ le ɣeyiɣi kpui aɖe me.
ENGLISH: This marked the first time in U.S. history that the Supreme Court reversed itself in such a short period of time.

EWE: Aƒetɔ Walter Gobitas kple srɔ̃a Ruth dzi Lillian Gobitas le Minersville le Pennsylvania le November 2, 1923 dzi.
ENGLISH: Lillian Gobitas was born in Minersville, Pennsylvania, to Walter and Ruth Gobitas on November 2, 1923.

EWE: Wonyrɔe wòzu Yehowa Ðasefo le March 14, 1935 dzi.
ENGLISH: She was baptized as one of Jehovah’s Witnesses on March 14, 1935.

EWE: Esi aƒenɔ Gobitas xɔ ƒe 20 la, eva zu ɣeyiɣiawo katã ƒe Biblia-fiala (si Yehowa Ðasefowo yɔna be gbesiagbe mɔɖela) eye emegbe wòva subɔ le Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe dɔwɔƒegã le Brooklyn si le New York tso February 1946 va se ɖe April 1953 me.
ENGLISH: At the age of 20, Ms. Gobitas became a full-time Bible instructor (referred to by Witnesses as a regular pioneer) and later worked at the world headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses in Brooklyn, New York, from February 1946 to April 1953.

EWE: Lillian kple srɔ̃a Erwin Klose, esime wonye dutanyanyuigblɔlawo le Vienna si le Austria le ƒe 1954 me.
ENGLISH: Lillian and her husband, Erwin Klose, as missionaries in Vienna, Austria, in 1954.

EWE: Esi aƒenɔ Gobitas de Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe takpekpe aɖe le Europa le ƒe 1951 me la, edo go aƒetɔ Erwin Klose le Ðasefowo ƒe alɔdzedɔwɔƒe si le Germany.
ENGLISH: While attending conventions of Jehovah’s Witnesses in Europe in 1951, Ms. Gobitas met Erwin Klose at the Witnesses’ branch office in Germany.

EWE: Xɔlɔ̃wɔwɔ yi edzi le wo dome hafi aƒetɔ Klose va de Gbetakpɔxɔ Habɔbɔa Ƒe Gilead Biblia Suku, si nye dutanyanyuigbɔgblɔlawo, siwo wogayɔna be mawunyadɔgbedelawo ƒe suku si wowɔ le South Lansing si le New York.
ENGLISH: They continued their acquaintance while Mr. Klose attended the Watchtower Bible School of Gilead, the Witnesses’ missionary school, held in South Lansing, New York.

EWE: Ewu sukua nu le ƒe 1952 me, eye woɖoe ɖe Vienna le Austria (Autriche).
ENGLISH: He graduated in 1952 and accepted an assignment to Vienna, Austria.

EWE: Aƒenɔ Gobitas hã wu mawunyadɔgbedelawo ƒe suku nu le February 1954 me.
ENGLISH: Ms. Gobitas also graduated from the Witnesses’ missionary school in February 1954.

EWE: Le March 24, 1954 dzi la, eya kple aƒetɔ Klose ɖe wo nɔewo le Vienna eye woyi woƒe dutanyanyuigbɔgblɔdɔa dzi le Austria.
ENGLISH: On March 24, 1954, she and Mr. Klose were married in Vienna and continued missionary work together in Austria.

EWE: Wotrɔ va Amerika le ƒe ma ƒe nuwuwu le aƒetɔ Klose ƒe lãmesẽkuxi si nɔ gã dom ɖe edzi ta. Elabena Nazitɔwo wɔ funyafunya aƒetɔ Klose le fuwɔamegaxɔ me le esi wònye Yehowa Ðasefo ta, eye esia gblẽ nu le eƒe lãmesẽ ŋu vevie.
ENGLISH: They returned to the United States at the end of that year due to the deteriorating health of Mr. Klose, who was still suffering the effects of the brutal treatment he received in a Nazi concentration camp for being one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.

EWE: Emegbe wodzi vi eve siwo ŋkɔwoe nye Stephen Paul kple Judith Deborah.
ENGLISH: They later had two children, Stephen Paul and Judith Deborah.

EWE: Le ƒe 1967 me la, aƒetɔ Klose kple eƒe ƒomea ʋu yi Riverdale le Georgia afi si wokeke woƒe Biblia-fiafiadɔ ɖe enu le.
ENGLISH: In 1967, the Klose family moved to Riverdale, Georgia where they expanded their Bible education ministry as a family.

EWE: Aƒenɔ Gobitas Klose gblẽ via nyɔnu Judith Klose; nɔvia nyɔnu eve siwo ŋkɔwoe nye Jeanne Fry kple Grace Reinisch; kple nɔvia ŋutsu Paul Gobitas ɖe megbe.
ENGLISH: Ms. Gobitas Klose is survived by her daughter, Judith Klose; two sisters, Jeanne Fry and Grace Reinisch; and a brother Paul Gobitas.

EWE: Srɔ̃a kple via Stephen Paul Klose, edzilawo, nɔvia ŋutsu William Gobitas kpakple nɔvia nyɔnu Joy Yubeta ku do ŋgɔ nɛ.
ENGLISH: She was preceded in death by her husband, her parents, her brother William Gobitas, her sister Joy Yubeta, and her son, Stephen Paul Klose.

EWE: Ðasefowo Ado Boblo JW.ORG Nyatakakadzraɖoƒe Si Le Gbegbɔgblɔ Gbogbotɔ Kekeake Me
ENGLISH: Witnesses Campaign to Advertise World’s Most Translated Website, JW.ORG

EWE: NEW YORK Le August 1, 2014 dzi la, Yehowa Ðasefowo adze trakt yeye aɖe si ƒe tanyae nye Afi Kae Míakpɔ Ŋuɖoɖo Na Agbe Me Biabia Vevitɔwo Le? mama gɔme si axɔ ɣleti ɖeka atsɔ ado boblo woƒe internet dzi nyatakakadzraɖoƒe si nye jw.org.
ENGLISH: NEW YORK On August 1, 2014, Jehovah’s Witnesses will begin a month-long global distribution of a new tract entitled Where Can We Find Answers to Life’s Big Questions? to raise awareness of their official website, jw.org.

EWE: Nyatakakadzraɖoƒe sia le gbegbɔgblɔ 500 aɖewo me, eye woate ŋu awɔ agbalẽ kple nu bubu siwo le edzi la ƒe kɔpi le gbegbɔgblɔ 700 kloe me.
ENGLISH: Accessible in about 500 languages, with publications available for download in almost 700 languages, jw.org is the world’s most translated website.

EWE: Ame miliɔn ɖeka kple edzivɔwo ʋua jw.org nyatakakadzraɖoƒea gbe sia gbe.
ENGLISH: Over one million unique visitors go to jw.org each day.

EWE: Nyatiwo kple videowo le nyatakakadzraɖoƒea, siwo aɖe vi na ame siwo xɔ ƒe vovovowo, ame ƒomevi vovovowo kple ame siwo le nɔnɔme vovovowo me.
ENGLISH: The site features articles and videos offering practical advice to people of all ages, backgrounds, and circumstances.

EWE: Video siawo dometɔ ɖeka ƒe tanyae nye Nu Ka Tae Wònyo Be Nàsrɔ̃ Biblia?, eye àte ŋu azã QR-xlẽnu ƒe kadodoa si dze le trakt yeyea dzi atsɔ aʋui.
ENGLISH: One of these videos, entitled Why Study the Bible?, will be linked to a QR code found on the new tract.

EWE: Wozã agbemenudzɔdzɔ ŋutɔŋutɔwo le video sia me tsɔ ɖe nu si tae wòanyo be míasrɔ̃ Biblia la fia.
ENGLISH: This video merges live-action elements and animation to illustrate the practical benefits of studying the Bible.

EWE: Ele gbegbɔgblɔ 450 me fifia, eye amewo wɔ eƒe kɔpi miliɔn 4 tso esime woɖee ɖe go le November 18, 2013 dzi.
ENGLISH: It is currently available in over 450 languages and has been downloaded nearly 4 million times since it was released on November 18, 2013.

EWE: J. R. Brown, si nye Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe nyanuɖela le woƒe dɔwɔƒegã si le Brooklyn le New York, gblɔ be: "Míele mɔ kpɔm na boblododo sia vevie.
ENGLISH: J. R. Brown, a spokesman for Jehovah’s Witnesses at their world headquarters in Brooklyn, New York, explains: "We are excited about this campaign.

EWE: Yehowa Ðasefo miliɔn enyie le xexea me godoo, eye mí katã míagblɔ nyatakakadzraɖoƒe sia ŋu nya na míaƒe aƒelikawo.
ENGLISH: There are some eight million of Jehovah’s Witnesses around the world, and all of us will be speaking to our neighbors about this website.

EWE: Ðewohĩ esiae anye boblodododɔ gãtɔ si míewɔ kpɔ. "
ENGLISH: This may be the most extensive campaign that we have ever organized. "

EWE: Geoffrey Jackson, si nye Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe Dɔdzikpɔhaa me tɔ gblɔ be: "Tso esime jw.org nyatakakadzraɖoƒe sia dze dɔ gɔme ƒe evee nye esi va yi la, ame siwo tso xexea me godoo kpɔe be nyatakaka siwo ŋu viɖe le la le afi sia.
ENGLISH: Geoffrey Jackson, a member of the Governing Body of Jehovah’s Witnesses, states: "Since its launch two years ago, people all over the world have found jw.org to be an invaluable resource.

EWE: Le nyatakakadzraɖoƒe sia la, àte ŋu akpɔ video siwo akpe ɖe viwòwo ŋu, nyati siwo ate ŋu akpe ɖe wò ƒomea ŋu, eye àte ŋu axlẽ Biblia gɔ̃ hã.
ENGLISH: On this site, you can watch videos that can help your children, consult articles that can help your family, and even read the Bible online.

EWE: Míedi be jw.org nyatakakadzraɖoƒea naɖe vi na ame gbogbotɔ kekeake, esia tae míede boblododo ƒe ɖoɖo sia to me ɖo. "
ENGLISH: We want as many as possible to benefit from jw.org, and that’s why we initiated this special campaign. "

EWE: Yehowa Ðasefowo Le Kpekpeɖeŋu Nam Amewo Le Balkan-nutowo Me
ENGLISH: Witnesses Mobilize Relief Efforts in the Balkans

EWE: ZAGREB, Croatia Kpekpeɖeŋunakɔmiti siwo me tɔwo nye lɔlɔ̃nu faa dɔwɔlawo kple Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe alɔdzedɔwɔƒe si le Germany ƒe ame dɔdɔwo le kpekpem ɖe ame siwo ŋu tsiɖɔɖɔ dziŋɔtɔ si teƒe wokpɔ kpɔ le Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia kple Serbia la gblẽ nu le la ŋu.
ENGLISH: ZAGREB, Croatia Disaster relief committees of Witness volunteers, assisted by representatives from the branch office of Jehovah’s Witnesses located in Germany, took action to aid victims of the worst flooding ever recorded in Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia, and Serbia.

EWE: Tsi gã aɖe si dza le Balkan-nutowo me tso May 13 va se ɖe May 15, 2014 dzi na tsi ɖɔ ɖe nutoa eteƒe mekɔ o eye agaɖevi (si fia agakpe siwo fli le towo ŋu) 3,000 aɖewo hã gblẽ nu le nutoa me.
ENGLISH: Torrential rainfall in the Balkans from May 13-15, 2014, caused massive flooding and triggered some 3,000 landslides.

EWE: Kpekpeɖeŋunakɔmitiawo wɔ ɖoɖo ɖe mɔzɔnyawo, nuɖuɖu, nudodo kple teƒe siwo woanɔ gbɔ la ŋu enumake.
ENGLISH: The disaster relief committees immediately provided transportation, food, clothing, and temporary housing to those displaced.

EWE: Togbɔ be Ðasefo aɖeke meku o eye nu vevi mewɔ ɖeke o hã la, woƒe aƒe 14 ya teti dome gblẽ.
ENGLISH: While none of Jehovah’s Witnesses were killed or injured as a result of the disaster, at least 14 of their homes were completely destroyed or severely damaged.

EWE: Gakpe ɖe eŋu la, Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe tadeaguƒe ɖeka gbã.
ENGLISH: Also, one house of worship used by the Witnesses was destroyed.

EWE: Kɔmitiawo gbugbɔ le aƒe siwo gbã kple esiwo ŋu nu gblẽ le la ɖɔm ɖo, eye wole xɔ siwo me ame siwo ƒe aƒewo dome gblẽ la anɔ gbɔ la hã tum.
ENGLISH: The committees are now coordinating the repair and renovation of damaged homes as well as the building of simple pre-fabricated houses for those whose homes were lost.

EWE: Aƒetɔ Josip Liović, si nye Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe nyanuɖela le Croatia, gblɔ be: "Míaƒe dzi dze eme esi míese be nu vevi mewɔ míaƒe haxɔsetɔ aɖeke o, gake míese veve ɖe ame siwo le nu xam ɖe woƒe ƒometɔwo kple wo xɔlɔ̃wo ƒe ku ta la ŋu.
ENGLISH: Josip Liović, a spokesman for the branch office of Jehovah’s Witnesses in Croatia, states: "We are relieved to hear that none in our congregations were harmed in this tragic event, yet our hearts go out to all who are grieving over the loss of family members and friends.

EWE: Míele agbagba dzem etɔxɛe be míakpe ɖe amewo ŋu le Balkan-nuto bliboa me.
ENGLISH: Throughout the Balkans, we are making a special effort to comfort our neighbors.

EWE: Míeda akpe na mía xɔlɔ̃ siwo tso Germany va kpe ɖe mía ŋu míewɔ ɖoɖo ɖe kpekpeɖeŋunu siwo ahiã le kwasiɖa kple ɣleti siwo gbɔna me la ŋu. "
ENGLISH: We are also grateful to our friends from Germany who have come to help us organize the relief efforts that will be needed in the coming weeks and months. "

EWE: Wode Bubu Yehowa Ðasefowo Ŋu Le Gusen Fuwɔamegakpɔ Ƒe Ŋkuɖodziƒe La Me
ENGLISH: Jehovah’s Witnesses Honored at the Gusen Concentration Camp Memorial

EWE: SELTERS, Germany (Allemagne)​ Le Kwasiɖa, April 13, 2014 dzi la, woɖe ŋkuɖodzikpe aɖe fia le Gusen Fuwɔamegakpɔ Ƒe Ŋkuɖodziƒe si le Austria (Autriche) la me tsɔ ɖo ŋku Yehowa Ðasefo 450 siwo Nazitɔwo lé de ga le Mauthausen fuwɔamegakpɔ kple eƒe Gusen gakpɔ sue me la dzi.
ENGLISH: SELTERS, Germany On Sunday, April 13, 2014, the Gusen Concentration Camp Memorial in Austria unveiled a memorial plaque in recognition of some 450 Jehovah’s Witnesses who were imprisoned by the Nazis in the Mauthausen concentration camp and its subcamp in Gusen.

EWE: Ame 130 kple edzivɔe va wɔnaa teƒe.
ENGLISH: More than 130 visitors were present for the ceremony.

EWE: Ŋkuɖodzikpe aɖe si woɖe fia le wɔna aɖe si wowɔ le Gusen Fuwɔamegakpɔ Ƒe Ŋkuɖodziƒe me le April 13, 2014 dzi.
ENGLISH: Commemorative plaque unveiled during a public ceremony held at the Gusen Concentration Camp Memorial on April 13, 2014.

EWE: Esi wokplɔ Ðasefoawo va Mauthausen fuwɔamegakpɔa me la, gaxɔa ƒe amegã do ŋɔdzi na wo be: "Biblia Nusrɔ̃vi aɖeke madzo le afi sia agbagbee o. "
ENGLISH: When the Witnesses arrived at the Mauthausen concentration camp, the command leader threatened them: "No Bible Student will come out of here alive. "

EWE: Aƒetɔ Martin Poetzinger si nɔ ga me le Dachau, Mauthausen kple Gusen hena ƒe asieke eye emegbe wòva zu Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe Dɔdzikpɔhaa me tɔ le Brooklyn le New York la gblɔ tso esime wònɔ ga me le Mauthausen ŋu be: "Adzamekpovitɔwo wɔ nu sia nu si woate ŋui be yewoana míaƒe xɔse me nagbɔdzɔ. "
ENGLISH: Martin Poetzinger, who survived nine years of imprisonment in Dachau, Mauthausen, and Gusen and later served as a member of the Governing Body of Jehovah’s Witnesses in Brooklyn, New York, said of his time in Mauthausen: "The Gestapo tried every method to induce us to break our faith. "

EWE: May 1945: Gusen Fuwɔamegakpɔ.
ENGLISH: May 1945: Gusen Concentration Camp.

EWE: Martin Poetzinger (nɔ anyi ɖe ŋgɔgbezikpuia dzi, evelia tso miame) ɖe foto sia kple ame 23 siwo tsi agbe la le asiɖeɖe le wo ŋu megbe kpuie.
ENGLISH: Martin Poetzinger (seated front row, second from left) poses with 23 other survivors shortly after their release.

EWE: Wokplɔ Ðasefo siwo le Mauthausen gakpɔa me la dometɔ aɖewo yi Gusen gakpɔ me emegbe.
ENGLISH: Some of the Witnesses in Mauthausen were later transferred to the subcamp at Gusen.

EWE: "Amewusaɖa " koŋue Gusen gakpɔ la nye, elabena woɖonɛ koŋ wua amewo le afi ma gbe sia gbe.
ENGLISH: Gusen’s primary function was a "murder camp, " where deliberate and planned killings were part of the daily routine.

EWE: Ðasefoawo kpena le hatsotso suesuewo me le zã me dzroa Biblia ƒe akpa siwo wolé ɖe susu me la me ale be wòado ŋusẽ woƒe xɔse.
ENGLISH: To keep their faith strong, the Witnesses met in small groups at night to discuss Bible texts from memory.

EWE: Gbe ɖeka Biblia va ka wo si.
ENGLISH: On one occasion, they obtained a Bible.

EWE: Woma Biblia la me ɖe akpa vovovo me, eye ne ɖe ɖo ame aɖe gbɔ la eya hã ɖonɛ ɖe nɔvia.
ENGLISH: It was divided into parts, and each Witness took turns sharing the pages.

EWE: Wobena ɖe woƒe abatiwo te xlẽnɛ le vovoɣi vi siwo sua wo si la me.
ENGLISH: Hiding underneath their beds, they would read during what little free time they had.

EWE: Ðasefoawo gblɔa Biblia me gbedeasia na amewo hã ŋuɖɔɖotɔe.
ENGLISH: The Witnesses also discreetly shared the Bible’s message with others.

EWE: Ðasefoawo srɔ̃ Biblia kple Polandtɔ atɔ̃ aɖewo esi wonɔ ga me eye woxɔ nyɔnyrɔ le adzame le atigo aɖe si wokpa hena esia wɔwɔ la me.
ENGLISH: Five Polish prisoners studied the Bible with the Witnesses and secretly got baptized in a wooden trough specially made for that purpose.

EWE: Ðasefo aɖe si ŋkɔe nye Franz Desch gblɔ Biblia me gbedeasia na SS-srafo aɖe eye eya hã va zu Yehowa Ðasefo.
ENGLISH: One Witness named Franz Desch shared the Bible’s message with an SS officer who later became one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.

EWE: Aƒetɔ Wolfram Slupina, si nye Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe nyanuɖela le Austria, gblɔ be: "Edzɔ dzi na mí ŋutɔ be woɖo ŋku Ðasefo siwo nɔ Mauthausen kple Gusen gakpɔwo me la dzi le woƒe xɔse kple dzinɔameƒo siwo woɖe fia le gakpɔ siawo me ta.
ENGLISH: Wolfram Slupina, a spokesman for Jehovah’s Witnesses in Austria, states: "We are grateful that the Witnesses are being remembered for their faith and courage while in the Mauthausen and Gusen camps.

EWE: Ale si woɖoe kplikpaa be yewoaɖe Kristotɔwo ƒe veveseseɖeamenu kple dɔmenyonyo afia ame sia ame la nye vɔ̃dziɖuɖu si dzi wòle be woaɖo ŋkui ahasrɔ̃. "
ENGLISH: Their determination to treat everyone with Christian empathy and kindness was a triumph over evil that is worthy of commemoration and imitation. "

EWE: Nyatakaka Ku Ðe Ðasefo Siwo Le Ukraine Kple Crimea Ŋu
ENGLISH: Report on Witnesses in Ukraine and Crimea

EWE: LVIV, Ukraine​ Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe alɔdzedɔwɔƒe si le Ukraine ka nya ta be le June 17, 2014 dzi la, Ðasefo aɖe si le Ukraine ƒe ɣedzeƒedu si woyɔna be Kramatorsk me ku esi bɔmb aɖe wó le eƒe ʋu gbɔ.
ENGLISH: LVIV, Ukraine The branch office of Jehovah’s Witnesses in Ukraine reports that on June 17, 2014, one Witness in the eastern Ukrainian city of Kramatorsk was killed when a bomb exploded next to his car.

EWE: Yehowa Ðasefo bubu aɖeke meku o, eye nu vevi mewɔ ɖeke hã le dukɔmeviʋa si le edzi yim le dukɔa me ɣleti ʋɛ aɖewoe nye esia me o.
ENGLISH: No other Witnesses have been killed or seriously injured as a result of the civil unrest in the country that started a few months ago.

EWE: Ke hã, Ðasefo alafa geɖewo ʋu le nuto siwo me dukɔmeviʋa le edzi yim le le Ukraine ƒe ɣedzeƒenuto me la me.
ENGLISH: However, hundreds of Witnesses have been evacuated from the affected areas of eastern Ukraine.

EWE: Ame siwo ʋu le woƒe aƒewo me la yi ɖatsi woƒe haxɔsetɔwo gbɔ.
ENGLISH: Those displaced are taking refuge with fellow worshippers.

ENGLISH: Despite ongoing violence, the Witnesses in Ukraine continue sharing the Bible’s comforting message with their neighbors.

EWE: Tso June 2014 ƒe gɔmedzedze va se ɖe eƒe domedome la, Ðasefowo wɔ takpekpe gã geɖewo le ŋutifafa me le Ukraine ƒe ɣedzeƒenutoa me. Woƒo nuƒo siwo wotu ɖe Biblia dzi, eye wowɔ wɔwɔfia siwo ɖe ale si woawɔ ɖe Biblia me nyawo dzi le gbe sia gbe nuwɔnawo me fia hã.
ENGLISH: During the first half of June 2014, the Witnesses hosted several large, peaceful gatherings in eastern Ukraine, which included Bible-based talks and demonstrations of how to apply the Bible’s advice in everyday situations.

EWE: Ame 5,200 kple edzivɔe de takpekpe siawo.
ENGLISH: Over 5,200 were in attendance.

EWE: Ðasefoawo awɔ nutome gã takpekpe 40 le Ukraine kple Crimea, eye woaƒo nu tso nya si Biblia gblɔ tso ale si Mawu Fiaɖuƒea ahe ŋutifafa vae le etsɔme ŋu la ŋu.
ENGLISH: The Witnesses will host some 40 regional conventions in Ukraine and Crimea, which will highlight Biblical statements about a peaceful future under God’s Kingdom.

EWE: Wole mɔ kpɔm be ame 165,000 kple edzivɔwo ade wɔna siawo. Wokpɔ mɔ be wo dometɔ 7,500 adee le Crimea
ENGLISH: More than 165,000 are expected to attend these events, including 7,500 in Crimea.

EWE: Ðasefowo Kpɔ Gome Le Agbalẽɖeɖefia Si Wowɔ Le Mexico City Le Ƒe 2014 Me La Me
ENGLISH: Witnesses Participate in the 2014 Mexico City Books and Magazines Expo

EWE: MEXICO CITY Yehowa Ðasefowo hã nɔ agbalẽtaƒe 150 siwo wokpe be woava kpɔ gome le agbalẽɖeɖefia aɖe si woyɔ be Expo Publica Agbalẽɖeɖefia me la dome. Mexico Dukɔa Ƒe Dɔwɔƒe Si Kpɔa Agbalẽtatadɔwo dzi lae wɔ ɖoɖo ɖe agbalẽɖeɖefia sia ŋu.
ENGLISH: MEXICO CITY Jehovah’s Witnesses were among 150 publishing houses sharing in the first Expo Publica Book Fair, coordinated by the National Chamber for the Mexican Publishing Industry (CANIEM).

EWE: Dɔwɔƒea wɔ agalẽɖeɖefia sia le Mexico Dukɔwo Dome Asitsaƒe tso April 25 va se ɖe May 4, 2014 dzi be yeatsɔ aɖu yeƒe ƒe 50 ƒe azã.
ENGLISH: The expo, held at the World Trade Center in Mexico City from April 25 to May 4, 2014, marked the 50th anniversary of CANIEM.

EWE: Ame siwo va wɔna sia teƒe ade 20,000.
ENGLISH: Approximately 20,000 people attended the event.

EWE: Ðasefowo ɖe woƒe agbalẽwo, magazinewo kple video vovovo siwo wotu ɖe Biblia dzi la fia.
ENGLISH: The Witnesses showcased their wide variety of Bible-based books, magazines, and videos.

EWE: Wodo boblo woƒe nyatakakadzraɖoƒe si nye www.jw.org, afi si woate ŋu awɔ woƒe agbalẽ siwo le gbe 650 kple edzivɔwo me la ƒe kɔpi le.
ENGLISH: They also featured their official website, www.jw.org, where downloadable versions of their publications are available in over 650 languages.

EWE: Vavalawo xɔ Ðasefowo ƒe agbalẽ siwo wu 1,600, eye wo dometɔ aɖewo bia be woava srɔ̃ Biblia kpli yewo le yewo ƒe me.
ENGLISH: Visitors selected more than 1,600 pieces of literature from the Witnesses, and some requested a personal visit in their home.

EWE: Ann-Jacqueline Frieser kple Richard Rudolph, si ƒe agbemeŋutinya na wòɖu dzi le ƒe 2009 me.

ENGLISH: For decades, Richard Rudolph made it his aim to share the Bible’s message with others and to share lessons he learned from the past about the harmful effects of discrimination.

ENGLISH: Wolfram Slupina, a spokesman for Jehovah’s Witnesses in Germany, states: "Richard Rudolph was not only a dear friend and fellow worshiper but also an invaluable historical resource.

ENGLISH: His life of remarkable faith and courage is an example for all of us. "

EWE: Agaɖeviwo Gblẽ Nu Le Washington State
ENGLISH: Devastating Mudslide in Washington State

EWE: Agaɖeviwo na aƒewo nyrɔ ɖe ba me le Snohomish County si le Washington le United States (États-Unis) le March 22, 2014 dzi.
ENGLISH: A mile-wide mudslide buried homes in Snohomish County, Washington, USA on March 22, 2014.

EWE: Nutoa me dziɖuɖumegãwo ka nya ta be ame 90 aɖewoe bu eye wogblɔ be ame 17 ku.
ENGLISH: Local officials state that up to 90 people are still missing and 17 people have been confirmed dead.

EWE: Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe alɔdzedɔwɔƒe si le United States ka nya ta be nyɔnu Ðasefo ɖeka le ame siwo bu la dome.
ENGLISH: The United States branch office of Jehovah’s Witnesses reports that one female Witness is among the missing.

EWE: Ðasefo atsu kple asi aɖe ƒe vinyɔnu kple woƒe mamayɔvi hã ku le nudzɔdzɔ sia me.
ENGLISH: One Witness couple lost both their daughter and great-granddaughter in the mudslide.

EWE: Eva hiã be Ðasefo eve naʋu le woƒe aƒewo me; Ðasefo bubu aɖe ya ƒe aƒe dome gblẽ keŋkeŋ.
ENGLISH: Two Witnesses had to evacuate their homes; the home of another Witness was completely destroyed.

EWE: Ðasefowo ƒe hamemetsitsi siwo le nutoa me le kpekpeɖeŋu kple akɔfafa nam ame siwo ŋu afɔku sia gblẽ nu le.
ENGLISH: Local Witness elders are providing comfort and support to those affected by the disaster.

EWE: Aƒetɔ Guy H. Pierce Si Nye Yehowa Ðasefowo Ƒe Dɔdzikpɔha Me Tɔ Ku
ENGLISH: Guy H. Pierce, Member of the Governing Body of Jehovah’s Witnesses, Dies

EWE: NEW YORK​ Guy H. Pierce, si nye Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe Dɔdzikpɔha me tɔ le woƒe Dɔwɔƒegã si le Brooklyn le New York la ku le Braɖa, March 18 dzi le eƒe ƒe 79 lia xɔxɔ me.
ENGLISH: NEW YORK Guy H. Pierce, a member of the Governing Body of Jehovah’s Witnesses at their world headquarters in Brooklyn, New York, died on Tuesday, March 18. He was 79 years of age.

EWE: Aƒetɔ Pierce wɔ dɔ le kɔmiti vovovo siwo kpɔa Ðasefowo ƒe dɔwo kple Biblia-fiafiadɔ si wowɔna le xexea me godoo dzi la me.
ENGLISH: Mr. Pierce served on various committees that supervise activities related to the Witnesses and their international Bible-education work.

EWE: Dɔ siwo wòwɔna le woƒe habɔbɔa me bia be wòanɔ mɔ zɔm edziedzi eye wòtoa esia dzi dea dzi ƒo na Yehowa Ðasefowo le xexea me godoo.
ENGLISH: His organizational responsibilities required that he travel extensively, and he used these occasions to provide encouragement for Jehovah’s Witnesses throughout the world.

EWE: Togbɔ be dɔ geɖe nɔ edzi hã la, ekpɔa vovo ɖe ame siwo hiã eƒe kpekpeɖeŋu alo aɖaŋuɖoɖo la ŋu, eye ale si wòkoa alɔgbɔnu hedoa nukokoe na ame la nana be amewo ɖea dzi ɖi le egbɔ.
ENGLISH: Despite his workload, he was well-known for never being too busy to listen to those needing assistance or advice, and he put others at ease with his warm smile and good sense of humor.

EWE: Exɔlɔ̃ veviwo kpɔe le eŋu be ame ɖe sia ɖe ƒomevi tea ŋu tena ɖe eŋu bɔbɔe.
ENGLISH: His closest associates noted that people from different backgrounds or cultures were naturally drawn to him.

EWE: Aƒetɔ Pierce gblɔ tso eɖokui ŋuti le nuƒo aɖe si wòƒo le ame siwo wɔa subɔsubɔdɔa ɣeyiɣiawo katã la ƒe sukunuwuwɔna aɖe me be dzidzenu si nu yenɔa agbe ɖoe nye be: "Lé dzidzenu dzɔdzɔewo me ɖe asi sesĩe, gake wò nya me megasẽ kpaɖi o.
ENGLISH: In a discourse at a graduation program for full-time ministers, Mr. Pierce made remarks that he was known to exemplify: "Be firm for right principles, but be flexible.

EWE: Mègado vlo ame siwo nàdo goe le wò subɔsubɔdɔa me o le esi woƒe dekɔnuwo to vovo ta o. "
ENGLISH: Do not look down on those in your assignment because their culture is different. "

EWE: Wodzi Guy Hollis Pierce le Auburn si le California le November 6, 1934 dzi.
ENGLISH: Guy Hollis Pierce was born in Auburn, California, on November 6, 1934.

EWE: Exɔ nyɔnyrɔ hezu Yehowa Ðasefo le August 14, 1955 dzi esime wòxɔ ƒe 20.
ENGLISH: He was baptized as one of Jehovah’s Witnesses on August 14, 1955, at the age of 20.

EWE: Eɖe eƒe haxɔsetɔ Ðasefo aɖe si ŋkɔe nye Penelope (Penny) Wong le May 30, 1977 dzi eye wohe wo viwo ɖekae.
ENGLISH: He married a fellow Witness, Penelope (Penny) Wong, on May 30, 1977, and the two raised a family together.

EWE: Aƒetɔ kple aƒenɔ Pierce va zu ame siwo fia Biblia amewo ɣeyiɣiawo katã (siwo Yehowa Ðasefowo yɔna be gbesiagbe mɔɖelawo).
ENGLISH: Mr. and Mrs. Pierce became full-time Bible instructors (referred to by Witnesses as regular pioneers).

EWE: Emegbe eva zu dzikpɔla mɔzɔla, eyina ɖasrãa Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe hamewo kpɔ le Amerika-dukɔa me godoo, eye wòdoa ŋusẽ ame siwo fiaa Biblia amewo ɣeyiɣiawo katã kple ame bubuwo le hame siwo me wòyina la me.
ENGLISH: Later, he became a traveling minister of Jehovah’s Witnesses, visiting congregations of Jehovah’s Witnesses throughout the United States to provide spiritual encouragement to other full-time Bible instructors and local congregation members.

EWE: Le ƒe 1997 me la, wokpe aƒetɔ kple aƒenɔ Pierce be woava wɔ dɔ le Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe alɔdzedɔwɔƒe si le Amerika la ɣeyiɣiawo katã.
ENGLISH: In 1997, the Pierces were invited to work full-time at the United States branch office of Jehovah’s Witnesses.

EWE: Le October 2, 1999 me la, woɖe gbeƒãe be aƒetɔ. Pierce zu Dɔdzikpɔha la me tɔ.
ENGLISH: On October 2, 1999, Mr. Pierce was announced as a new member of the Governing Body.

EWE: Aƒetɔ Pierce ye nye Gbetakpɔxɔ Biblia Kple Trakt Habɔbɔ si le Pennsylvania ƒe ƒe sia ƒe takpekpe 129 lia ƒe wɔnawo ƒe zimenɔla le October 5 kple 6, 2013 ƒe kwasiɖanuwuwua me.
ENGLISH: Mr. Pierce was the chairman for the 129th annual meeting of the Watch Tower Bible and Tract Society of Pennsylvania, on the weekend of October 5 and 6, 2013.

EWE: Ame 1,413,676 ye kpɔ gome le wɔnaa me le dukɔ 31 me, wo dometɔ aɖewo de wɔnaa wɔƒe ŋutɔ eye bubuwo hã kpɔe to internet-kadodowo dzi.
ENGLISH: A total audience of 1,413,676 in 31 countries attended the event either in person or via webcast.

EWE: Le Ðasefowo ƒe nyatakakadzraɖoƒea ƒe nya nu la, esiae nye Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe kpekpe gãtɔ kekeake si wowɔ kpɔ.
ENGLISH: According to the Witnesses’ official website, this was the largest gathering of Jehovah’s Witnesses to date.

EWE: Aƒetɔ Pierce gblẽ srɔ̃a Penny, via dzidzi ade, tɔgbuiyɔviwo kple tɔgbuitɔgbuiyɔvi geɖewo ɖe megbe.
ENGLISH: In addition to his wife, Penny, Mr. Pierce is survived by his six children, several grandchildren, and great-grandchildren.

EWE: Yehowa Ðasefo siwo le xexea me godoo siwo wòbuna be wonye yeƒe ƒometɔwo la hã ɖoa ŋku edzi vevie.
ENGLISH: He will also be fondly remembered by Jehovah’s Witnesses around the world whom he regarded as family.

EWE: Ehati Dɔdzikpɔha me tɔ bubuwo ƒo nu tso "xɔse sẽŋu si le esi kple ale si wòléa Yehowa ƒe sewo kple dzidzenuwo me ɖe asi sesĩe " la ŋu. Wogblɔ kpee be: "Ŋkuɖoɖo eƒe dzinɔameƒo kple nuteƒewɔwɔ dzi le eƒe anyigbadzinɔɣi dzi ayi edzi anɔ ŋusẽ dom mí hena ƒe geɖe. "
ENGLISH: In a statement, his fellow members of the Governing Body commented on "his solid faith and firm stand for Jehovah’s laws and principles, " adding: "Our memories of his courageous and faithful earthly life course will continue to strengthen us for years to come. "

EWE: Yehowa Ðasefowo Le Amewo Kpem Le Xexea Me Godoo Na Kristo Ƒe Ku Ƒe Ŋkuɖodzia
ENGLISH: Jehovah’s Witnesses to Launch Global Invitation Campaign for the Memorial of Christ’s Death

EWE: NEW YORK​ Le Memleɖa, March 22, 2014 dzi la, Yehowa Ðasefowo adze amewo kpekpe le xexea me godoo be woava kpɔ Kristo ƒe ku ƒe Ŋkuɖodziwɔna, si nye wɔna vevitɔ na Ðasefowo le ƒea me la teƒe.
ENGLISH: NEW YORK On Saturday, March 22, 2014, Jehovah’s Witnesses will launch a global campaign inviting the public to an event the Witnesses consider to be the most important of the year: the Memorial of Christ’s death.

EWE: Le ƒe si va yi me la, ame 19,241,252 ye kpe ta hena wɔna tɔxɛ sia.
ENGLISH: Last year, there were 19,241,252 that gathered for this special observance.

EWE: Ðasefoawo le mɔ kpɔm be ame gbogbotɔ ade wɔnaa teƒe le ƒe sia me. Woawɔe le Dzoɖa, April 14, le ɣeɖoto megbe.
ENGLISH: The Witnesses hope to reach a new all-time peak in attendance for this year’s Memorial, which will be held on Monday, April 14, after sundown.

EWE: J. R. Brown, si nye Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe nyanuɖela le woƒe dɔwɔƒegã le New York gblɔ be: "Míeka ɖe edzi be ame siwo katã ade Ŋkuɖodzia kpli mí la akpɔ ŋudzedze ɖe eŋu eye wòaɖe vi na wo hã.
ENGLISH: "We are sure that all who attend the Memorial with us will enjoy this occasion and benefit from it, " states J. R. Brown, a spokesman for Jehovah’s Witnesses at their world headquarters in New York.

EWE: Esia tae míele amewo kpem vevie hena wɔna kɔkɔe sia. "
ENGLISH: "That prospect is motivating us to invite as many as possible to join us for this sacred event. "

EWE: Guy H. Pierce Si Nye Yehowa Ðasefowo Ƒe Dɔdzikpɔha Me Tɔ Ku Le Eƒe 79 Lia Xɔxɔ Me
ENGLISH: Guy H. Pierce, Member of the Governing Body of Jehovah’s Witnesses, Dies at 79

EWE: Guy H. Pierce, si nye Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe Dɔdzikpɔha me tɔ le woƒe Dɔwɔƒegã si le Brooklyn le New York la ku le Braɖa, March 18 dzi le eƒe ƒe 79 lia xɔxɔ me.
ENGLISH: Guy H. Pierce, a member of the Governing Body of Jehovah’s Witnesses at their world headquarters in Brooklyn, New York, died on Tuesday, March 18. He was 79 years of age.

EWE: Aƒetɔ Pierce gblẽ srɔ̃a Penny, via dzidzi ade, tɔgbuiyɔviwo kple tɔgbuitɔgbuiyɔvi geɖewo ɖe megbe.
ENGLISH: In addition to his wife, Penny, Mr. Pierce is survived by his six children, several grandchildren, and great-grandchildren.

EWE: Yehowa Ðasefo siwo le xexea me godoo siwo wòbuna be wonye yeƒe ƒometɔwo la hã ɖoa ŋku edzi vevie.
ENGLISH: He is also fondly remembered by Jehovah’s Witnesses around the world whom he regarded as family.

EWE: Ehati Dɔdzikpɔha me tɔ bubuwo gblɔ tso eŋu be: "Ŋkuɖoɖo eƒe dzinɔameƒo kple nuteƒewɔwɔ dzi ayi edzi anɔ ŋusẽ dom mí hena ƒe geɖe. "
ENGLISH: In a statement, his fellow members of the Governing Body commented: "Our memories of his courageous and faithful earthly life course will continue to strengthen us for years to come. "

EWE: Yehowa Ðasefowo Ðe Biblia Yeyea Ƒe Nuŋɔŋlɔ Lolotɔ Ðe Go
ENGLISH: Jehovah’s Witnesses Release Newly Revised Bible in a Large-Size Edition

EWE: NEW YORK​ Yehowa Ðasefowo le agbagba dzem be Biblia nasu ame gbogbotɔ kekeake si. Eya ta woɖe Ŋɔŋlɔ Kɔkɔeawo​ Xexe Yeye Gɔmeɖeɖe Biblia yeyea ƒe nuŋɔŋlɔ lolotɔ hã ɖe go.
ENGLISH: NEW YORK In their ongoing efforts to make the Bible accessible to as many people as possible, Jehovah’s Witnesses are releasing a large-size edition of the revised New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures.

EWE: Wowɔ ɖoɖo be Biblia sia ƒe gbãtɔ siwo woata le Amerika kple Japan siaa ƒe agbɔsɔsɔ nanye 424,000.
ENGLISH: This edition, which is being printed in the United States and Japan, is scheduled to have a combined initial printing of 424,000 copies.

EWE: Ðasefoawo ɖe Xexe Yeye Gɔmeɖeɖe Biblia yeye sia ƒe tata si ame geɖe zãna la ɖe go le kpekpe tɔxɛ aɖe si wowɔ tso October 5 va se ɖe 6, 2013 dzi me, eye amewo kpɔ gome le kpekpe sia me to internet-kadodo dzi le dukɔ 31 me.
ENGLISH: The Witnesses released the regular-size revised New World Translation during a special meeting that was broadcast on October 5-6, 2013, to 31 countries.

EWE: Enye ƒe 1984 ƒe tata si ŋu wotrɔ asi le eme kɔ wu. Tso October 7, 2013 dzi la, Ðasefowo to dɔwɔnu si nye JW Library si nana be wotea ŋu zãa Biblia sia le mɔ̃ vovovowo dzi la vɛ, eye amewo zã dɔwɔnu sia tsɔ wɔ Biblia sia ƒe kɔpi miliɔn ɖeka akpe alafa ene kloe le internet dzi.
ENGLISH: The 2013 revision represents the most comprehensive update of the translation since 1984. On October 7, 2013, the Witnesses made this translation of the Bible available in a multiplatform app, JW Library, which has already had close to 1.4 million downloads.

EWE: Xexe Yeye Gɔmeɖeɖe Biblia le fɔmat vovovowo hã me le internet dzi nyatakakadzraɖoƒe si nye www.jw.org.
ENGLISH: The revised New World Translation is also available in a variety of electronic formats online at www.jw.org.

EWE: Titinanuŋɔŋlɔ siwo ade 60,000 kloe hã le eme siwo kpena ɖe Biblia-xlẽlawo ŋu wosea Biblia me nuŋlɔɖiwo gɔme nyuie.
ENGLISH: The revised New World Translation in all formats includes nearly 60,000 marginal references, which help readers to understand better the context of Bible accounts.

EWE: Tsɔ kpe ɖe eŋu la, foto siwo le amadede vovovowo me, Biblia me nyigbawo ƒe nɔnɔmetatawo kple aɖaka siwo ɖe ale si amewo nɔ agbee le Biblia-ŋlɔɣiwo me la me tsitotsito hã le eme.
ENGLISH: Also included are full-color diagrams, maps of Biblical lands, and charts illustrating details of daily life during Bible times.

EWE: Eƒe akpa si nye megbenyawo ƒo nu tso nyatiwo abe Biblia gɔme ɖeɖe ŋuti mɔfiamewo kple ale si woŋlɔ Biblia hekpɔ etae ŋu.
ENGLISH: An appendix explains such topics as the principles of Bible translation and the history of how the Bible was written and preserved.

EWE: Wona Mawu ƒe ŋkɔa dze le ƒe 1984 ƒe Xexe Yeye Gɔmeɖeɖe Biblia me le teƒe 7,000 sɔŋ.
ENGLISH: The 1984 edition of the New World Translation already included God’s personal name some 7,000 times in the text.

EWE: Tsɔ kpe ɖe eŋu la, Mawu ƒe ŋkɔa gadze le asinuŋɔŋlɔgbalẽ xoxotɔ kekeake siwo ŋu wova ke ɖo nyitsɔ laa ƒe akpa bubu aɖewo hã, eye wodee le akpa siawo hã le ƒe 2013 ƒe tata yeye sia me.
ENGLISH: However, the 2013 revision also reflects current research on where the name of God appears in the oldest Bible manuscripts.

EWE: Elabena esi woku nu me tso Ƒukukua ƒe Agbalẽxatsaxatsawo kple asinuŋɔŋlɔgbalẽ xoxotɔwo me la, wokpɔe be Mawu ƒe ŋkɔa gadze le teƒe ade bubuwo, eye wodee teƒe mawo katã le Xexe Yeye Gɔmeɖeɖe Biblia yeye sia me.
ENGLISH: Based on further examination of the Dead Sea Scrolls and other ancient manuscripts, the revised New World Translation includes six additional occurrences of the divine name.

EWE: Wodze le Ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo 19:18; 1 Samuel 2:25; 6:3; 10:26; 23:14, 16.
ENGLISH: They are found at Judges 19:18; 1 Samuel 2:25; 6:3; 10:26; 23:14; 23:16.

EWE: Megbenyawo gaƒo nu tso ale si wozã Mawu ƒe ŋkɔa le blema Hebrigbe kple Helagbe me kpakple ale si wòdze le Biblia-gɔmeɖeɖe siwo le egbegbe gbegbɔgblɔ vovovowo mee me la ŋu.
ENGLISH: An appendix further discusses the use of the divine name in ancient Hebrew and Greek, as well as its appearance in Bible translations in several modern dialects and languages.

EWE: Tso gbe aɖe gbe kee Ðasefowo ɖea Xexe Yeye Gɔmeɖeɖe Biblia gɔme, tanɛ hemana na amewo, eye agbalẽnyalagãwo dea asixɔxɔ Biblia sia ŋu ŋutɔ ɖe ale si wòde pɛpɛpɛ ta.
ENGLISH: The Witnesses have a long history of printing, distributing, and translating the New World Translation, which has been well-regarded by scholars for its accuracy.

EWE: Woɖe Biblia sia ƒe bliboa ɖe go zi gbãtɔ le ƒe 1961 me le Eŋlisigbe me.
ENGLISH: The complete text of this translation was first made available in English in 1961.

EWE: Le ƒe 1963 me la, nyadzɔdzɔgbalẽ aɖe (The New York Times) ka nya ta be abe ale si woɖe gbeƒãe le Ðasefowo ƒe takpekpe si wowɔ le Yankee Stadium ene la, woaɖe Xexe Yeye Gɔmeɖeɖe Biblia gɔme ɖe gbegbɔgblɔ ade bubuwo me.
ENGLISH: In 1963, The New York Times reported that the New World Translation would be available in six additional languages, as announced at a Witness convention held at Yankee Stadium.

EWE: Tso ɣemaɣi la, Ðasefowo ta Biblia sia ɖe gbegbɔgblɔ 120 kple edzivɔwo me.
ENGLISH: Since then, the Witnesses have provided this translation in over 120 languages.

EWE: Nyitsɔ laa la, Xexe Yeye Biblia Gɔmeɖeɖe Kɔmitia ɖoe be yeagbugbɔ asi trɔ le Xexe Yeye Gɔmeɖeɖe Biblia ŋu ale be wòasɔ ɖe egbegbe Eŋlisigbe nu eye emenya aɖewo gɔme sese nanɔ bɔbɔe wu, ale be eme nakɔ eye exexlẽ nanɔ bɔbɔe wu.
ENGLISH: In recent years, the New World Bible Translation Committee chose to revise the New World Translation to respond to changes in modern language and to clarify certain Biblical expressions, thus enhancing readability and understanding.

EWE: Eye alea tututue wotrɔ asi le eŋui.
ENGLISH: The revised New World Translation embodies these latest advances in Bible translation.

EWE: Aƒetɔ J. R. Brown, si nye Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe nyanuɖela le woƒe dɔwɔƒegã la, gblɔ be: "Dzidzɔ gã aɖee wònye ɣemaɣi esi woxɔ Xexe Yeye Gɔmeɖeɖe Biblia gbãtɔ ƒe 50 aɖewoe nye esi va yi, gake dzi dzɔ mí wu gbɔgblɔ esi míexɔ gɔmeɖeɖe yeye sia.
ENGLISH: "It was thrilling to receive the first editions of the New World Translation over 50 years ago, and it is even more thrilling to have the latest revised edition, " states J. R. Brown, a spokesman for Jehovah’s Witnesses at their world headquarters.

EWE: Míaƒe taɖodzinue nye be míaɖe Ŋɔŋlɔ Kɔkɔeawo gɔme wo gɔme sese nanɔ bɔbɔe na ame sia ame, evɔ míazã nya siwo de pɛpɛpɛ, nya siwo ŋu bubu le siwo amewo zãna egbea le nuƒoƒo me. "
ENGLISH: "Our intent is to make the Holy Scriptures understandable to all, using language that is accurate, dignified, and contemporary. "

EWE: Ale Si Nyaa Va Yii: Agbagba Si Wodze Be Woaxe Mɔ Ðe JW.ORG Nu Medze Edzi O
ENGLISH: Expanded Coverage: Attempt to Ban JW.ORG Fails

EWE: ST.
ENGLISH: ST.

EWE: PETERSBURG, Russia Yehowa Ðasefowo ɖu dzi gã aɖe le ʋɔnudrɔ̃nya aɖe me le January 22, 2014 dzi, esi nyagbugbɔdrɔ̃ƒea te fli ɖe nutomeʋɔnudrɔ̃ƒe suetɔ ƒe nyametsotso be woaxe mɔ ɖe jw.org, si nye Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe nyatakakadzraɖoƒea nu le Russia-dukɔa me godoo.
ENGLISH: PETERSBURG, Russia Jehovah’s Witnesses won a major court victory on January 22, 2014, when an appellate court reversed a lower court’s ruling that banned jw.org, the official website of Jehovah’s Witnesses, throughout Russia.

EWE: Tver Nutomeʋɔnudrɔ̃ƒe te fli ɖe Tsentralniy nutomeʋɔnudrɔ̃ƒe suetɔ ƒe nyametsotsoa me le August 7, 2013 dzi.
ENGLISH: The Tver Regional Court overturned the August 7, 2013, decision of the Tsentralniy District Court.

EWE: Tver Nutomeʋɔnudrɔ̃ƒea de dzesii be nutomeʋɔnudrɔ̃ƒe suetɔa ƒe nyametsotso be woaxe mɔ ɖe Yehowa Ðasefowo ƒe nyatakakadzraɖoƒea nu mele se nu o, elabena womeɖe mɔ na Yehowa Ðasefowo, ame siwo tɔ nyatakakadzraɖoƒe sia nye la be woakpɔ ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃a teƒe o.
ENGLISH: The regional court determined that the district court was unjustified in banning the website because Jehovah’s Witnesses, the owners, had not been given an opportunity to participate in the hearing.

EWE: Nutoa me ʋɔnudrɔ̃la amesamala si le Tver tsɔ nya ɖe jw.org nyatakakadzraɖoƒea ŋu be agbalẽ siwo Russia dziɖuɖua tso nya me be wodea "aglãdzedze ƒe dzi ƒo " la le edzi.
ENGLISH: The local prosecutor in Tver brought the case to court because jw.org contained publications that Russian courts have ruled to be "extremist. "

EWE: Esi Yehowa Ðasefowo nya se nutomeʋɔnudrɔ̃ƒe suetɔ ƒe nyametsotsoa ko la, woɖe agbalẽ siwo ŋu nyaa ku ɖo la le jw.org si amewo ʋuna le Russia la dzi.
ENGLISH: As soon as Jehovah’s Witnesses learned of the district court’s ruling, they removed these publications from jw.org in Russia.
