ENGLISH: Bible writers had scientific knowledge that was beyond the understanding of their contemporaries.

EWE: Le kpɔɖeŋu me, le blema la, ame geɖewo xɔe se be lã aɖewo dzie míaƒe anyigba la le, eye wogblɔna be lã siawo dometɔ aɖewoe nye atiglinyi, gbeha alo nyitsu.
ENGLISH: For example, in ancient times many peoples believed that the earth was supported by an animal, such as an elephant, a boar, or an ox.

EWE: Gake Biblia ya gblɔ be Mawu "meku anyigba la ɖe naneke ŋu o. "
ENGLISH: In contrast, the Bible says that God is "suspending the earth upon nothing. "

EWE: (Hiob 26:7) Nenema ke Biblia ɖɔ anyigba ƒe nɔnɔme wòde pɛpɛpɛ be ele "nogoo " alo "godoo. "
ENGLISH: (Job 26:7) Similarly, the Bible correctly describes the shape of the earth as a "sphere, " or "globe. "

EWE: (Yesaya 40:22, Eʋegbe Biblia) Ame geɖe xɔe se be nu si tae Biblia-ŋlɔlawo te ŋu nya nu mawo siwo ŋu wo ŋɔlimetɔwo menya naneke tsoe o gblɔ lae nye be Mawue ɖee fia wo.
ENGLISH: (Isaiah 40:22, footnote; Douay Version) Many people feel that the most reasonable explanation for such advanced understanding is that Bible writers received their information from God.

EWE: Biblia ɖo nyabiase sesẽ geɖe siwo ate ŋu awɔe be ame nazu mawudzimaxɔsela ne mekpɔ ŋuɖoɖo na wo o la ŋu.
ENGLISH: The Bible answers many difficult questions, the type of questions that when not satisfactorily answered can lead a person to atheism.

EWE: Nyabiase siawo dometɔ aɖewoe nye, Ne Mawu lɔ̃ ame eye wònye ŋusẽkatãtɔ la, ke nu ka tae fukpekpe kple nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ bɔ ɖe xexea me alea gbegbe?
ENGLISH: For example: If God is loving and all-powerful, why is there suffering and evil in the world?

EWE: Nu ka tae zi geɖe la, mawusubɔsubɔhawo wɔe be amewo wɔa nu vɔ̃ esi woana be amewo nawɔ nu nyui boŋ?​ Tito 1:​16.
ENGLISH: Why is religion so often an influence for bad rather than for good?​ Titus 1:​16.

EWE: Ŋusẽ Dzro Aɖe Koe Mawu Nyea?
ENGLISH: Is God an Impersonal Force?

EWE: Ale si Biblia ɖo eŋui
ENGLISH: The Bible’s answer

EWE: Mawu zãa ŋusẽ si ƒo ɖe sia ɖe ta le xexea me godoo.
ENGLISH: God exercises unsurpassed force throughout the universe.

EWE: Esi Biblia nɔ nu ƒom tso ale si Mawu wɔ ɣletivi gbogbo manyaxlẽ miliɔn akpe geɖewo ŋu la, egblɔ be: "Mifɔ mo dzi, ne miakpɔ nu!
ENGLISH: Regarding the way he created the countless billions of stars, the Bible says: "Raise your eyes high up and see. Who has created these things?

EWE: Ame ka wɔ nu siawo, eye wòkplɔa eŋu nuwo doa goe dedie?
ENGLISH: It is the One who is bringing forth the army of them even by number, all of whom he [God] calls even by name.

EWE: Eyɔa wo katã ŋkɔ, eye wo dometɔ aɖeke mesusɔna o le eƒe ŋusẽ geɖe kple alɔkame sesẽ la nu. "
ENGLISH: Due to the abundance of dynamic energy, he also being vigorous in power, not one of them is missing. "

EWE: Yesaya 40:25, 26.
ENGLISH: Isaiah 40:25, 26.

EWE: Gake menye ŋusẽ dzro aɖe koe Mawu nye o.
ENGLISH: But God is much more than a powerful force.

EWE: Biblia gblɔ be seselelãmewo, abe lɔlɔ̃ kple fuléle ene, le esi.
ENGLISH: The Bible says that he has feelings, such as love and hate.

EWE: (Psalmo 11:5; Yohanes 3:16) Biblia ɖee fia hã be ale si amegbetɔwo nɔa agbee la ate ŋu ana Mawu nakpɔ dzidzɔ alo ado dziku.
ENGLISH: (Psalm 11:5; John 3:16) It also reveals that the way humans act can affect God’s emotions.

EWE: Psalmo 78:40, 41.
Ðe Nɔƒe Aɖe Koŋ Le Mawu Sia?
ENGLISH: Does God Live in a Specific Location?

EWE: Ale si Biblia ɖo eŋui
ENGLISH: The Bible’s answer
Yes.

EWE: Nɔƒe aɖe koŋ le Mawu si, eyae nye dziƒowo.
ENGLISH: God lives in a specific place the heavens.

EWE: Ðe ŋugble tso Biblia me nuŋlɔɖi siawo ŋu kpɔ:
ENGLISH: Consider these Bible passages:

EWE: Salomo gblɔ le gbedodoɖa me be: "Nàsee le nɔwòƒe le dziƒo. " 1 Fiawo 8:43.
ENGLISH: In a prayer, King Solomon said: "May you yourself listen from the heavens, your established place of dwelling. " 1 Kings 8:43.

EWE: Yesu fia eƒe nusrɔ̃lawo be woado gbe ɖa na wo "Fofo si le dziƒowo. "
ENGLISH: Jesus Christ taught his disciples to address their prayers to their "Father in the heavens. "

EWE: Mateo 6:9.
ENGLISH: Matthew 6:9.

EWE: Esi wofɔ Yesu ɖe tsitre la, "dziƒo ŋutɔŋutɔ wòge ɖo, bene wòado ɖe Mawu ŋutɔ ŋkume. "
ENGLISH: After Jesus was resurrected, he entered "into heaven itself, now to appear before the person of God. "

EWE: Hebritɔwo 9:24.
ENGLISH: Hebrews 9:24.

EWE: Mawunyakpukpui siawo ɖee fia be ame ŋutɔŋutɔe Yehowa Mawu nye eye be mele afi sia afi o, ke boŋ dziƒo koe nye enɔƒe.
ENGLISH: Those verses clearly indicate that Jehovah God is a real person and that he dwells, not everywhere, but only in heaven.

EWE: Ðe Ame Aɖe Kpɔ Mawu Kpɔa?
ENGLISH: Has Anyone Ever Seen God?

EWE: Ale si Biblia ɖo eŋui
ENGLISH: The Bible’s answer

EWE: Amegbetɔ aɖeke mekpɔ Mawu ŋkume-kple-ŋkume kpɔ o.
ENGLISH: No human has literally seen God.

EWE: (2 Mose 33:20; Yohanes 1:18; 1 Yohanes 4:12) Biblia gblɔ be "Mawu nye Gbɔgbɔ, " si fia agbe ƒomevi aɖe si amegbetɔ ƒe ŋku mate ŋu akpɔ o.​ Yohanes 4:24; 1 Timoteo 1:17.
ENGLISH: (Exodus 33:20; John 1:​18; 1 John 4:​12) The Bible says that "God is a Spirit, " a form of life that is invisible to the human eye.​ John 4:​24; 1 Timothy 1:​17.

EWE: Ke hã mawudɔlawo tea ŋu kpɔa Mawu ŋkume-kple-ŋkume elabena gbɔgbɔe woawo hã wonye.
ENGLISH: God can be seen directly by angels, though, because they are spirit creatures.

EWE: (Mateo 18:10) Gawu la, woafɔ ame siwo ku la dometɔ aɖewo be woayi dziƒo eye gbɔgbɔŋutilã asu wo si, eye woate ŋu akpɔ Mawu ŋkume-kple-ŋkume.​ Filipitɔwo 3:20, 21; 1 Yohanes 3:2.
ENGLISH: (Matthew 18:10) Moreover, some humans who die will be raised to life in heaven with a spirit body and will then be able to see God.​ Philippians 3:​20, 21; 1 John 3:2.

EWE: Mɔ si nu nàte ŋu akpɔ Mawu le egbea
ENGLISH: How to "see " God now

EWE: Biblia zã nya nukpɔkpɔ tsɔ wɔa kpɔɖeŋu na nugɔmesese.
ENGLISH: The Bible often uses the idea of seeing figuratively, to represent enlightenment.

EWE: (Yesaya 6:10; Yeremiya 5:21; Yohanes 9:39-41) Le gɔmesese sia nu la, amegbetɔwo ate ŋu akpɔ Mawu fifia kple woƒe "dzi me ŋkuwo " ne xɔse le wo si eye wonya eya amea hekpɔa ŋudzedze ɖe eƒe nɔnɔme nyuiwo ŋu.
ENGLISH: (Isaiah 6:​10; Jeremiah 5:​21; John 9:​39-​41) In this sense, a person can see God now with "the eyes of [his] heart " by having faith so as to know Him and appreciate His qualities.

EWE: (Efesotɔwo 1:18) Biblia gblɔ nu siwo wòle be míawɔ be xɔse sia ƒomevi nasu mía si la na mí.
ENGLISH: (Ephesians 1:​18) The Bible describes steps to build this kind of faith.

EWE: Srɔ̃ nu tso Mawu ƒe nɔnɔmewo abe lɔlɔ̃, dɔmenyo, nunya kple ŋusẽ ene ŋu to eƒe asinudɔwɔwɔwo dzi.
ENGLISH: Learn about God’s qualities, such as his love and generosity as well as his wisdom and power, through his creation.

EWE: (Romatɔwo 1:20) Esi wohe nuteƒewɔla Hiob ƒe susu yi Mawu ƒe asinudɔwɔwɔwo dzi la, ese le eɖokui me abe ɖe Mawu le eŋkume ŋutɔŋutɔ ene.​ Hiob 42:5.
ENGLISH: (Romans 1:​20) After being reminded of God’s creative works, the faithful man Job felt as though God were right before his eyes.​ Job 42:5.

EWE: Àte ŋu anya Mawu to Biblia-sɔsrɔ̃ me.
ENGLISH: Get to know God by studying the Bible.

EWE: Biblia na kakaɖedzi mí be: "Ne [èdi Mawu] la, ekema ana nàke ɖe eŋu. "​ 1 Kronika 28:9; Psalmo 119:2; Yohanes 17:3.
ENGLISH: "If you search for [God], he will let himself be found by you, " the Bible assures us.​ 1 Chronicles 28:9; Psalm 119:2; John 17:3.

EWE: Àte ŋu asrɔ̃ nu tso Mawu ŋu to nusɔsrɔ̃ tso Yesu ƒe agbenɔnɔ ŋu me.
ENGLISH: Learn about God through the life of Jesus.

EWE: Esi wònye be Yesu ɖe Fofoa ƒe nɔnɔmewo fia bliboe ta la, Yesu te ŋu gblɔ wòsɔ be: "Ame si kpɔm la, ekpɔ Fofo la hã. "​ Yohanes 14:9.
ENGLISH: Since Jesus perfectly reflected the personality of his Father, Jehovah God, he could rightly say: "Whoever has seen me has seen the Father also. "​ John 14:9.

EWE: Nɔ nu siwo ana wò nu nadze Mawu ŋu la wɔm, eye àkpɔ ale si wòakpe ɖe ŋuwòe.
ENGLISH: Live in a way that pleases God, and see how he acts in your behalf.

EWE: Yesu gblɔ be: "Dzidzɔtɔwoe nye ame siwo dza le dzi me, elabena woakpɔ Mawu. "
ENGLISH: Jesus said: "Happy are the pure in heart, since they will see God. "

EWE: Abe ale si míegblɔe va yi ene la, woafɔ ame siwo ƒe nuwɔna dze Mawu ŋu la dometɔ aɖewo woayi dziƒo, eye "woakpɔ Mawu " le afi ma.​ Mateo 5:8; Psalmo 11:7.
ENGLISH: As noted earlier, some who please God will be resurrected to heaven and will thus "see God " there.​ Matthew 5:8; Psalm 11:7.

EWE: Ðe Mose, Abraham kple ame bubuwo mekpɔ Mawu ŋkume-kple-ŋkume oa?
ENGLISH: Did not Moses, Abraham, and others actually see God?

EWE: Le Biblia me nudzɔdzɔ siwo me wòdze le abe ɖe amegbetɔwo kpɔ Mawu ŋutɔŋutɔ ene la, nya siwo ƒo xlã nya mawo ɖee fia be mawudɔla aɖe si le Mawu teƒee wokpɔ loo alo eɖe eɖokui fia wo le ŋutega me.
ENGLISH: In accounts where it might seem that the Bible says that humans literally saw God, the context shows that God was represented by an angel or appeared by means of a vision.

EWE: Mawudɔlawo.
ENGLISH: Angels.

EWE: Le blema la, Mawu dɔa mawudɔlawo wonyea eteƒenɔlawo dzena na amegbetɔwo eye woƒoa nu le eƒe ŋkɔ me.
ENGLISH: In ancient times, God sent angels as his representatives to appear to humans and to speak in his name.

EWE: (Psalmo 103:20) Le kpɔɖeŋu me, Mawu ƒo nu na Mose gbe ɖeka le ŋuve aɖe si nɔ bibim me, eye Biblia gblɔ be: "Mose ɣla eƒe ŋkume, elabena ele vɔvɔ̃m na Mawu vavã la kpɔkpɔ. " (2 Mose 3:4, 6) Mose mekpɔ Mawu ŋutɔŋutɔ o, elabe nya siwo ƒo xlã nya ma ɖee fia be "Yehowa ƒe dɔla " ye wòkpɔ.​ 2 Mose 3:2.
ENGLISH: (Psalm 103:20) For example, God once spoke to Moses from a burning bush, and the Bible says that "Moses hid his face, because he was afraid to look at the true God. " (Exodus 3:​4, 6) Moses did not literally see God, though, for the context shows that he actually saw "Jehovah’s angel. "​ Exodus 3:2.

EWE: Nenema kee esi Biblia gblɔ be Mawu "ƒoa nu kple Mose ŋkume kple ŋkume " la, efia be Mawu ɖoa dze kple Mose abe exɔlɔ̃a ene.
ENGLISH: Similarly, when the Bible says that God "spoke to Moses face-to-face, " it means that God conversed with Moses intimately.

EWE: (2 Mose 4:10, 11; 33:11) Mose mekpɔ Mawu kple ŋku ŋutɔŋutɔ o elabena exɔ gbedeasi la "to mawudɔlawo dzi. "
ENGLISH: (Exodus 4:​10, 11; 33:11) Moses did not actually see God’s face, for the information he received from God "was transmitted through angels. "

EWE: (Galatiatɔwo 3:19; Dɔwɔwɔwo 7:53) Ke hã, Mose xɔ Mawu dzi se ale gbegbe be Biblia gblɔ tso eŋu be ɖeko wòle abe ɖe wònɔ "Ame si womekpɔna o la kpɔm " ene.​ Hebritɔwo 11:27.
ENGLISH: (Galatians 3:​19; Acts 7:​53) Still, Moses’ faith in God was so strong that the Bible described him as "seeing the One who is invisible. "​ Hebrews 11:27.

EWE: Mawu ƒo nu na Abraham hã to mawudɔla aɖe dzi abe ale si ko wòwɔ le Mose gome ene.
ENGLISH: In the same way that he spoke to Moses, God communicated with Abraham through angels.

EWE: Enye nyateƒe be ne mède ŋugble tso Biblia ƒe akpa sia ŋu nyuie o la, àsusui be ɖe Abraham kpɔ Mawu ŋutɔŋutɔ.
ENGLISH: Granted, a casual reading of the Bible might give the impression that Abraham literally saw God.

EWE: (1 Mose 18:1, 33) Ke hã, nya siwo ƒo xlã kpukpui siawo ɖee fia be mawudɔla siwo Mawu dɔe "ŋutsu etɔ̃ " siwo wòkpɔ la nye.
ENGLISH: (Genesis 18:​1, 33) However, the context shows that the "three men " who came to Abraham were actually angels sent by God.

EWE: Abraham kpɔe dze sii be Mawu teƒenɔlawo wonye, eya ta wònɔ nu ƒom na wo abe Yehowa ŋutɔe wònɔ nyaa gblɔm na tẽe ene.​ 1 Mose 18:2, 3, 22, 32; 19:1.
ENGLISH: Abraham recognized them as God’s representatives and addressed them as if he were speaking directly to Jehovah.​ Genesis 18:​2, 3, 22, 32; 19:1.

EWE: Ŋutegawo.
ENGLISH: Visions.

EWE: Mawu ɖe eɖokui fia amegbetɔwo le ŋutegawo hã me.
ENGLISH: God has also appeared to humans through visions, or scenes presented to a person’s mind.

EWE: Le kpɔɖeŋu me, esi Biblia gblɔ be Mose kple Israel-vi bubuwo "wokpɔ Israel ƒe Mawu la " la, nu si dzɔ ŋutɔŋutɔe nye be "wokpɔ Mawu vavã la le ŋutega me. " (2 Mose 24:9-11) Nenema kee Biblia gblɔna ɣeaɖewoɣi be nyagblɔɖilawo ‘kpɔ Yehowa.’
ENGLISH: For instance, when the Bible says that Moses and other Israelites "saw the God of Israel, " they really "saw a vision of the true God. " (Exodus 24:​9-​11) Likewise, the Bible sometimes says that prophets "saw Jehovah. "

EWE: (Yesaya 6:1; Daniel 7:9; Amos 9:1) Le go siawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe me la, nya siwo ƒo xlã kpukpui mawo ɖenɛ fiana be ŋutega mee wokpɔ Mawu le, ke womekpɔ Mawu ŋkume-kple-ŋkume o.​ Yesaya 1:1; Daniel 7:2; Amos 1:1.
ENGLISH: (Isaiah 6:1; Daniel 7:9; Amos 9:1) In each case, the context shows that they were given a vision of God rather than a direct view of him.​ Isaiah 1:1; Daniel 7:2; Amos 1:1.

EWE: Ðe Mawu Nye Mawuɖekaetɔ̃ Alo Trinitaa?
ENGLISH: Is God a Trinity?

EWE: Ale si Biblia ɖo eŋui
ENGLISH: The Bible’s answer

EWE: Sɔlemeha vovovowo gblɔna be Mawu nye Mawuɖekaetɔ̃ alo Trinita Kɔkɔe.
ENGLISH: Many Christian denominations teach that God is a Trinity.

EWE: Gake de dzesi nya si agbalẽ aɖe (Encyclopædia Britannica) gblɔ: "Trinita alo eŋuti nufiafia gobii aɖeke medze le Nubabla Yeyea me o . . .
ENGLISH: However, note what the Encyclopædia Britannica states: "Neither the word Trinity nor the explicit doctrine appears in the New Testament . . .

EWE: Nufiafia sia dze egɔme vivivi eye wònye nya wohe ʋuu hafi va ɖoe anyi le ƒe alafa geɖewo megbe. "
ENGLISH: The doctrine developed gradually over several centuries and through many controversies. "

EWE: Le nyateƒe me la, Biblia ƒe afi aɖeke meɖɔ Mawu kpɔ enye Mawuɖekaetɔ̃ ƒe akpa aɖe o.
ENGLISH: In fact, the God of the Bible is never described as being part of a Trinity. Note these Bible passages:

EWE: De dzesi mawunyakpukpui siawo me nyawo:
ENGLISH: "Jehovah our God is one Jehovah. "

EWE: "Yehowa, mía Mawu la, Yehowa ɖeka koe! " 5 Mose 6:4.
ENGLISH: Deuteronomy 6:4.

EWE: "Ŋkɔwòe nye Yehowa, eye wò ɖeɖe koe ɖo kpo ɖe anyigba blibo la dzi! "
ENGLISH: "You, whose name is Jehovah, you alone are the Most High over all the earth. "

EWE: Psalmo 83:19.
ENGLISH: Psalm 83:18.

EWE: "Esiae nye agbe mavɔ la bena, woanya wò, Mawu vavã ɖeka la, kple Yesu Kristo, si nèdɔ ɖa la. "
ENGLISH: "This means everlasting life, their taking in knowledge of you, the only true God, and of the one whom you sent forth, Jesus Christ. "

EWE: Yohanes 17:3, Eʋegbe Biblia.
ENGLISH: John 17:3.

EWE: "Mawu ɖeka koe. "
ENGLISH: "God is only one. "

EWE: Galatiatɔwo 3:20.
ENGLISH: Galatians 3:20.

EWE: Nu ka tae sɔlemeha geɖewo fiaa nu be Mawu nye Mawuɖekaetɔ̃ alo Trinita Kɔkɔe?
ENGLISH: Why do most Christian denominations say that God is a Trinity?

EWE: Ðe Mawu Trɔa Susua?
ENGLISH: Does God Change His Mind?

EWE: Ale si Biblia ɖo eŋui
ENGLISH: The Bible’s answer

EWE: Ɛ̃, etrɔa susu le mɔ sia nu be ne amewo trɔ woƒe nuwɔnawo la eya hã trɔa nɔnɔme ɖe wo ŋu.
ENGLISH: Yes, he does, in the sense that he changes his attitude when people change their behavior.

EWE: Le kpɔɖeŋu me, esi Mawu dɔ nyagblɔɖila aɖe be wòayi aɖagblɔ ʋɔnudrɔ̃gbedeasi aɖe na blema Israel-viwo la, egblɔ be: "Ðewohĩ woasee, eye ame sia ame atrɔ tso eƒe mɔ vɔ̃ dzi, ekema matrɔ susu, eye nyemagahe vɔ̃ si meɖo ɖe wo ŋu le woƒe nuwɔna vɔ̃ɖiwo ta la ava wo dzi o. "​ Yeremiya 26:3.
ENGLISH: For example, when God sent a judgment message to the people of ancient Israel, he said: "Perhaps they will listen and each one will turn back from his evil way, and I will change my mind concerning the calamity that I intend to bring on them because of their evil deeds. "​ Jeremiah 26:3.

EWE: Woɖe nya sia gɔme le Biblia aɖewo me be Mawu "trɔ dzi me " le vɔ̃ si wòɖo be yeawɔ la gome. Woƒe nya sia ate ŋu afia be Mawu da vo.
ENGLISH: Many Bible translations render this verse as saying that God would "repent " over the intended calamity, which could be understood to mean that he had made a mistake.

EWE: Gake Hebrigbe me nya si gɔme woɖe la ate ŋu afia "trɔ susu alo trɔ tame. "
ENGLISH: However, the original Hebrew word can mean "change of mind or intention. "

EWE: Agbalẽnyala gã aɖe ŋlɔ bena: "Ne amewo trɔ woƒe nuwɔna la, Mawu hã trɔa ʋɔnu si wòɖo be yeadrɔ̃ wo la. "
ENGLISH: One scholar wrote: "A change in man’s conduct brings about a change in God’s judgment. "

EWE: Ke hã, ele be míade dzesii be togbɔ be Mawu tea ŋu trɔa susu hã la, mezi edzi be wòatrɔ susu ɣesiaɣi o.
ENGLISH: Of course, just because God can change his mind does not mean that he must change it.

EWE: Kpɔ Biblia me nudzɔdzɔ siwo me Mawu metrɔ susu le o la dometɔ aɖewo ɖa:
ENGLISH: Consider some situations where the Bible says that God has not changed his mind:

EWE: Mawu meɖe mɔ Balak na wòtrɔ susu heƒo fi de Israel-dukɔ la o.​ 4 Mose 23:18-20.
ENGLISH: God did not allow Balak to make Him change His mind and curse the nation of Israel.​ Numbers 23:18-​20.

EWE: Esi Israel fia Saul tsɔ nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ ɖo dɔe la, Mawu metrɔ tame si wòɖo be yeagbee la o.​ 1 Samuel 15:28, 29.
ENGLISH: Once King Saul of Israel became firmly set in badness, God did not change his mind about rejecting him as king.​ 1 Samuel 15:28, 29.

EWE: Mawu awɔ ɖe ŋugbe si wòdo be yeana ye Vi nanye nunɔla tegbee la dzi.
ENGLISH: God will fulfill his promise to make his Son a priest forever.

EWE: Mawu matrɔ susu o.​ Psalmo 110:4.
ENGLISH: God will not change His mind.​ Psalm 110:4.

EWE: Ðe Biblia megblɔ be Mawu metrɔna oa?
ENGLISH: Doesn’t the Bible say that God never changes?

EWE: Ɛ̃, Mawu gblɔ le Biblia me be: "Nye Yehowa nyemetrɔ o. "
ENGLISH: Yes, the Bible records God as saying: "I am Jehovah; I do not change. "

EWE: (Malaki 3:6) Nenema kee Biblia gblɔ be Mawu "metrɔna abe vɔvɔli ene o. "
ENGLISH: (Malachi 3:6) Similarly, the Bible says that God "does not vary or change like the shifting shadows. "

EWE: (Yakobo 1:17) Gake nya sia metsi tsitre ɖe nya si Biblia gblɔ be Mawu trɔ susu la ŋu o.
ENGLISH: (James 1:​17) This, however, does not contradict what the Bible says about God changing his mind.

EWE: Mawu metrɔna o le susu sia nu be eƒe nɔnɔmewo kple eƒe dzidzenu ku ɖe lɔlɔ̃ kple dzɔdzɔenyenye ŋu metrɔna gbeɖe o.
ENGLISH: God is unchangeable in that his personality and standards of love and justice never alter.

EWE: (5 Mose 32:4; 1 Yohanes 4:8) Gake etea ŋu naa mɔfiame vovovowo amewo le ɣeyiɣi vovovowo me.
ENGLISH: (Deuteronomy 32:4; 1 John 4:8) Still, he can give different instructions to people at different times.

EWE: Le kpɔɖeŋu me, Mawu na mɔfiame vovovowo Fia David le aʋa eve aɖewo me, gake mɔfiame eveawo katã kpɔ dzidzedze.​ 2 Samuel 5:​18-​25.
ENGLISH: For instance, God gave opposite instructions to King David for fighting two consecutive battles, yet both methods succeeded.​ 2 Samuel 5:​18-​25.

EWE: Ðe wòve Mawu be yewɔ amegbetɔwoa?
ENGLISH: Is God sorry that he created humans?

EWE: Ao, togbɔ be evenɛ be ame akpa gãtɔ meɖoa to ye o hã.
ENGLISH: No, although he does regret that most people ignore or reject him.

EWE: Biblia gblɔ tso ale si nɔnɔmeawo nɔ le anyigba dzi do ŋgɔ na Noa ƒe ŋkekea me Tsiɖɔɖɔa ŋu be: "Eve Yehowa bena, wòwɔ ame ɖe anyigba dzi, eye wòɖu dzi nɛ. " (1 Mose 6:6) Dɔwɔnya si wozã le kpukpui sia me be "eve " nye Hebrigbe me nya aɖe si ate ŋu afia "trɔ susu. "
ENGLISH: Describing conditions before the global Flood of Noah’s day, the Bible says: "Jehovah regretted that he had made men on the earth, and his heart was saddened. " (Genesis 6:6) In this verse, the word "regretted " comes from the Hebrew word that can mean "change of mind. "

EWE: Mawu trɔ susu ku ɖe ame siwo nɔ anyigba dzi do ŋgɔ na Tsiɖɔɖɔa dometɔ akpa gãtɔ ŋu le woƒe nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ ta.
ENGLISH: God changed his mind about most of the people who lived before the Flood because they had become wicked.

EWE: (1 Mose 6:5, 11) Togbɔ be etena ɖe Mawu dzi be amewo tsɔ nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ ɖo dɔe hã la, metrɔ susu ku ɖe amegbetɔƒome bliboa ŋu o.
ENGLISH: (Genesis 6:​5, 11) Even though he was saddened that they chose to follow a bad course, he did not change his attitude toward the entire human race.

EWE: Le nyateƒe me la, ekpɔ amegbetɔƒomea ta le Tsiɖɔɖɔa me esi wòna Noa kple eƒe ƒomea tsi agbe.​ 1 Mose 8:21; 2 Petro 2:5, 9.
ENGLISH: In fact, he preserved mankind through the Flood by means of Noah and his family.​ Genesis 8:​21; 2 Peter 2:​5, 9.

EWE: Nu Kae Nye Gbɔgbɔ Kɔkɔe La?
ENGLISH: What Is the Holy Spirit?

EWE: Ale si Biblia ɖo eŋui
ENGLISH: The Bible’s answer

EWE: Gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔeae nye Mawu ƒe ŋusẽ ɖeɖe fia alo eƒe dɔwɔŋusẽ.
ENGLISH: The holy spirit is God’s power in action, his active force.

EWE: (Mika 3:8; Luka 1:35) Mawu ɖoa eƒe gbɔgbɔa ɖe teƒewo le mɔ sia nu be eɖoa eƒe ŋusẽ ɖe teƒe mawo ale be eƒe lɔlɔ̃nu nava eme.​ Psalmo 104:30; 139:7.
ENGLISH: (Micah 3:8; Luke 1:​35) God sends out his spirit by projecting his energy to any place to accomplish his will.​ Psalm 104:30; 139:7.

EWE: Nya si gɔme woɖe le Biblia me be "gbɔgbɔ " la nye Hebrigbe me nya ruach kple Helagbe me nya pneuma.
ENGLISH: In the Bible, the word "spirit " is translated from the Hebrew word ruach and the Greek word pneuma.

EWE: Zi geɖe la nya mawo fiaa Mawu ƒe dɔwɔŋusẽ alo gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔe la.
ENGLISH: Most often, those words refer to God’s active force, or holy spirit.

EWE: (1 Mose 1:2) Gake Biblia zãa nya mawo wofia nu bubuwo hã abe:
ENGLISH: (Genesis 1:2) However, the Bible also uses those words in other senses:

EWE: Gbɔgbɔ (ŋɔtimegbɔgbɔ).​ Habakuk 2:19; Nyaɖeɖefia 13:15.
ENGLISH: Breath.​ Habakkuk 2:​19; Revelation 13:15.

EWE: Ya (yaƒoƒo).​ 1 Mose 8:1; Yohanes 3:8.
ENGLISH: Wind.​ Genesis 8:1; John 3:8.

EWE: Agbegbɔgbɔ alo ŋusẽ si nana be nu gbagbewo ʋãna.​ Hiob 34:14, 15.
ENGLISH: The vital, or animating, force in living creatures.​ Job 34:14, 15.

EWE: Ame ƒe agbenɔnɔ alo eƒe nɔnɔme.​ 4 Mose 14:24.
ENGLISH: A person’s disposition or attitude.​ Numbers 14:24.

EWE: Gbɔgbɔmemewo, siwo lɔ Mawu kple mawudɔlawo ɖe eme.​ 1 Fiawo 22:21; Yohanes 4:24.
ENGLISH: Spirit persons, including God and the angels.​ 1 Kings 22:21; John 4:​24.

EWE: Gbɔgbɔ ƒe gɔmesese siawo katã fia nane si ƒe dɔwɔwɔ dzena amegbetɔwo kpɔna gake wometea ŋu kpɔa gbɔgbɔa ŋutɔ kple ŋku o.
ENGLISH: These meanings all share the sense of something invisible to humans that produces visible effects.

EWE: Nenema kee Mawu ƒe gbɔgbɔa hã "le abe ya ke ene, enye nu makpɔmakpɔ sẽŋu aɖe. "​ An Expository Dictionary of New Testament Words, si W. E. Vine ta.
ENGLISH: Similarly, the spirit of God, "like the wind, is invisible, immaterial and powerful. "​ An Expository Dictionary of New Testament Words, by W. E. Vine.

EWE: Biblia yɔ Mawu ƒe gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔea be ‘asi’ alo "asibidɛwo. "
ENGLISH: The Bible also refers to God’s holy spirit as his "hands " or "fingers. "

EWE: (Psalmo 8:3; 19:1; Luka 11:20; tsɔe sɔ kple Mateo 12:28.)
ENGLISH: (Psalm 8:3; 19:1; Luke 11:20; compare Matthew 12:28.)

EWE: Abe ale si ko aɖaŋudɔwɔla zãa eƒe asi alo asibidɛwo tsɔ wɔa nuwoe ene la, Mawu hã zãa eƒe gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔea tsɔ wɔ alo tsɔ wɔa nu siwo gbɔna:
ENGLISH: Just as a craftsman uses his hands and fingers to do his work, God has used his spirit to produce such results as the following:

EWE: Xexea.​ Psalmo 33:6; Yesaya 66:1, 2.
ENGLISH: The universe.​ Psalm 33:6; Isaiah 66:​1, 2.

EWE: Biblia la.​ 2 Petro 1:20, 21.
ENGLISH: The Bible.​ 2 Peter 1:​20, 21.

EWE: Nukunu siwo esubɔla siwo nɔ anyi le blema wɔ kple ale si woɖe gbeƒã dzonɔamemetɔe.​ Luka 4:18; Dɔwɔwɔwo 1:8; 1 Korintotɔwo 12:4-11.
ENGLISH: The miracles performed by his ancient servants and their zealous preaching.​ Luke 4:​18; Acts 1:8; 1 Corinthians 12:​4-​11.

EWE: Nɔnɔme nyui siwo ame siwo ɖoa toe ɖena fiana.​ Galatiatɔwo 5:22, 23.
ENGLISH: The fine qualities displayed by people who obey him.​ Galatians 5:​22, 23.

EWE: Menye amee gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔe la nye o
ENGLISH: The holy spirit is not a person

EWE: Esi Biblia yɔ Mawu ƒe gbɔgbɔa be eƒe ‘asi’ alo "asibidɛwo " alo "ŋɔtimegbɔgbɔ " la, eɖee fia be menye amee gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔe la nye o.
ENGLISH: By referring to God’s spirit as his "hands, " "fingers, " or "breath, " the Bible shows that the holy spirit is not a person.

EWE: (2 Mose 15:8, 10) Aɖaŋudɔwɔlaa ƒe asiwo mate ŋu awɔ dɔ eƒe susu kple eƒe ŋutilã ƒe akpa bubuwo manɔmee o; nenema kee ne Mawu fia mɔ gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔea ko hafi wòtea ŋu wɔa dɔ.
ENGLISH: (Exodus 15:​8, 10) A craftsman’s hands cannot function independent of his mind and body; likewise, God’s holy spirit operates only as he directs it.

EWE: (Luka 11:13) Biblia tsɔ Mawu ƒe gbɔgbɔa sɔ kple tsi eye wòtsɔe do ƒome kple nuwo abe xɔse kple sidzedze ene hã.
ENGLISH: (Luke 11:13) The Bible also compares God’s spirit to water and associates it with such things as faith and knowledge.

EWE: Esiawo katã ɖee fia be menye amee gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔea nye o. Yesaya 44:3; Dɔwɔwɔwo 6:5; 2 Korintotɔwo 6:6.
ENGLISH: These comparisons all point to the impersonal nature of the holy spirit.​ Isaiah 44:3; Acts 6:5; 2 Corinthians 6:6.

EWE: Woyɔ Yehowa Mawu kple Via Yesu Kristo ŋkɔ na mí le Biblia me, gake gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔea ƒe ŋkɔ medze le afi aɖeke le Biblia me o.
ENGLISH: The Bible gives the names of Jehovah God and of his Son, Jesus Christ; yet, nowhere does it name the holy spirit.

EWE: (Yesaya 42:8; Luka 1:31) Esi Kristotɔ Stefano si wowu ɖe eƒe xɔse ta kpɔ dziƒo nukutɔe le ŋutega aɖe me la, ame eve ko wòkpɔ le afi ma, menye ame etɔ̃ o.
ENGLISH: (Isaiah 42:8; Luke 1:​31) When the Christian martyr Stephen was given a miraculous heavenly vision, he saw only two persons, not three.

EWE: Biblia gblɔ be: "Esi gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔe yɔe fũu la, ekpɔ dziƒo gãa, eye wòkpɔ Mawu ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe kple Yesu wòle tsitre ɖe Mawu ƒe ɖusime. "
ENGLISH: The Bible says: "He, being full of holy spirit, gazed into heaven and caught sight of God’s glory and of Jesus standing at God’s right hand. "

EWE: (Dɔwɔwɔwo 7:55) Gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔe lae nye Mawu ƒe ŋusẽ si wòtsɔ kpe ɖe Stefano ŋu wòkpɔ ŋutega ma.
ENGLISH: (Acts 7:​55) The holy spirit was God’s power in action, enabling Stephen to see the vision.

EWE: Alakpanya siwo amewo gblɔna ku ɖe gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔea ŋu
ENGLISH: Misconceptions about the holy spirit

EWE: Nyakpakpa: Gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔe la nye ame ŋutɔŋutɔ eye wònye Mawuɖekaetɔ̃ (Trinita Kɔkɔe) la ƒe akpa aɖe abe ale si wodze le 1 Yohanes 5:7, 8 le Eʋegbe Biblia me ene.
ENGLISH: Misconception: The "Holy Ghost, " or holy spirit, is a person and is part of the Trinity, as stated at 1 John 5:​7, 8 in the King James version of the Bible.

EWE: Nyateƒea: Nya siwo dze le Eʋegbe Biblia me le 1 Yohanes 5:7, 8 ƒe ɖewoe nye "le dziƒo: Fofo la, Nya la kple Gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔe la, eye ame etɔ̃ siawo le ɖeka.
ENGLISH: Fact: The King James version of the Bible includes at 1 John 5:​7, 8 the words "in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one.

EWE: Eye ame etɔ̃e li, ame siwo le ɖase ɖim le anyigba dzi. "
ENGLISH: And there are three that bear witness in earth. "

EWE: Gake numekulawo va kpɔe be menye apostolo Yohanes ye ŋlɔ nya siawo o, eya ta menye Biblia me nyawoe wonye o.
ENGLISH: However, researchers have found that those words were not written by the apostle John and so do not belong in the Bible.

EWE: Nufialagã Bruce M. Metzger ŋlɔ bena: "Nya siawo nye nyakpakpawo eye enye nyateƒe be mesɔ be woatsɔ wo akpe ɖe Nubabla Yeyea ŋu o. "​ A Textual Commentary on the Greek New Testament.
ENGLISH: Professor Bruce M. Metzger wrote: "That these words are spurious and have no right to stand in the New Testament is certain. "​ A Textual Commentary on the Greek New Testament.

EWE: Nyakpakpa: Biblia ƒoa nu tso gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔea ŋu abe amee wònye ene, eya ta efia be amee wònye.
ENGLISH: Misconception: The Bible personifies the holy spirit, and this proves that it is a person.

EWE: Nyateƒea: Enye nyateƒe be ŋɔŋlɔawo ƒoa nu tso gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔea ŋu ɣeaɖewoɣi abe amee wònye ene ya, gake esia mefia be amee wònye o.
ENGLISH: Fact: The Scriptures do at times personify the holy spirit, but this does not prove that the holy spirit is a person.

EWE: Biblia ƒoa nu tso nunya, ku, kple nu vɔ̃ hã ŋu abe amewoe wonye ene.
ENGLISH: The Bible also personifies wisdom, death, and sin.

EWE: (Lododowo 1:20; Romatɔwo 5:17, 21) Le kpɔɖeŋu me, woƒo nu tso nunya ŋu be ewɔa ‘dɔ’ eye "viwo " le esi, eye woɖɔa nu vɔ̃ be eblea ame nu, ewua ame eye wòbiãa ŋu.​ Mateo 11:19; Luka 7:35; Romatɔwo 7:8, 11.
ENGLISH: (Proverbs 1:​20; Romans 5:​17, 21) For example, wisdom is said to have "works " and "children, " and sin is depicted as seducing, killing, and working out covetousness.​ Matthew 11:19; Luke 7:​35; Romans 7:​8, 11.

EWE: Nenema kee esime apostolo Yohanes yɔ Yesu ƒe nyawo la, eƒo nu tso gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔe la ŋu abe amee wònye ene esi wògblɔ be enye "kpeɖeŋutɔ " si ana kpeɖodzi, afia mɔ, aƒo nu, ase nu, eye wòagblɔ nya, akafu ahaxɔ nya.
ENGLISH: Similarly, when the apostle John quoted Jesus, he personified the holy spirit as a "helper " (paraclete) that would give evidence, guide, speak, hear, declare, glorify, and receive.

EWE: Nyakpakpa: Amewo nyɔnyrɔ ɖe gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔe la ƒe ŋkɔ me ɖee fia be amee wònye.
ENGLISH: He used masculine personal pronouns such as "he " or "him " when referring to that "helper. "

EWE: Nyateƒea: Biblia zãa "ŋkɔ " ɣeaɖewoɣi tsɔ fia ŋusẽ alo ɖoƒe.
ENGLISH: Fact: The Bible sometimes uses "name " to stand for power or authority.

EWE: (5 Mose 18:5, 19-22; Esta 8:10) Wogblɔa nya sia tɔgbi le Eŋlisigbe me be le "sea ƒe ŋkɔ me, " gake esia mefia be amee se la nye o.
ENGLISH: (Deuteronomy 18:​5, 19-​22; Esther 8:​10) This is similar to its use in the English expression "in the name of the law, " which does not mean that the law is a person.

EWE: Ame si wonyrɔ le "gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔe la ƒe ŋkɔ me " lɔ̃na ɖe gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔea ƒe ŋusẽ kple akpa si wòwɔna be Mawu ƒe tameɖoɖo nava eme la dzi.​ Mateo 28:19.
ENGLISH: A person who is baptized "in the name of " the holy spirit recognizes the power and role of the holy spirit in accomplishing God’s will.​ Matthew 28:19.

EWE: Nyakpakpa: Yesu ƒe apostolowo kple eƒe nusrɔ̃la gbãtɔ bubuwo xɔe se be amee gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔea nye.
ENGLISH: Misconception: Jesus’ apostles and other early disciples believed that the holy spirit was a person.

EWE: Nyateƒea: Esia ƒe kpeɖodzi aɖeke mele Biblia alo ŋutinya me o.
ENGLISH: Fact: The Bible does not say that, nor does history.

EWE: Numekugbalẽ aɖe (Encyclopædia Britannica) gblɔ be: "Konstantinople ƒe Aɖaŋuɖotakpekpe si wowɔ le ƒe 381 Do Ŋgɔ Na Yesu . . . mee woto nufiafia si nye be Gbɔgbɔ Kɔkɔea hã nye Mawu la vɛ. "
ENGLISH: The Encyclopædia Britannica states: "The definition that the Holy Spirit was a distinct divine Person . . . came at the Council of Constantinople in ad 381. "

EWE: Esia nye ƒe 250 kple edzivɔ le apostolo mamlɛtɔ ƒe ku megbe.
ENGLISH: This was over 250 years after the last of the apostles had died.

EWE: Ðe Ŋkɔ Le Mawu Sia?
ENGLISH: Does God Have a Name?

EWE: Ale si Biblia ɖo eŋui
ENGLISH: The Bible’s answer

EWE: Ŋkɔ le ame sia ame si.
ENGLISH: Humans all have personal names.

EWE: Ðe mesɔ be ŋkɔ nanɔ Mawu hã si oa?
ENGLISH: Wouldn’t it be reasonable for God to have a name?

EWE: Ame nɔewo ŋkɔnyanya kple eyɔyɔ wɔa kpa vevie aɖe le xɔlɔ̃kadodowo me.
ENGLISH: Having and using personal names is a vital part of human friendships.

EWE: Ðe mele be wòanɔ alea le xɔlɔ̃wɔwɔ kple Mawu hã gome oa?
ENGLISH: Should it be different when it comes to our friendship with God?

EWE: Mawu gblɔ le Biblia me be: "Nyee nye Yehowa, ŋkɔnyee. "
ENGLISH: In the Bible, God says: "I am Jehovah. That is my name. "

EWE: (Yesaya 42:8) Togbɔ be dzesideŋkɔ geɖewo, abe "Mawu ŋusẽkatãtɔ, " "Aƒetɔ Dziɖulagã " kple "Wɔla " le Mawu si hã la, ede bubu esubɔlawo ŋu esi wòbia tso wo si be woayɔ ye ŋkɔ ŋutɔ.
ENGLISH: (Isaiah 42:8) Although he also has many titles, such as "God Almighty, " "Sovereign Lord, " and "Creator, " he honors his worshippers by inviting them to address him by his personal name.

EWE: 1 Mose 17:1; Dɔwɔwɔwo 4:24; 1 Petro 4:19.
ENGLISH: Genesis 17:1; Acts 4:24; 1 Peter 4:19.

EWE: Mawu ƒe ŋkɔ dze le Biblia gɔmeɖeɖe geɖewo me le 2 Mose 6:3.
ENGLISH: Many translations of the Bible contain God’s personal name at Exodus 6:3.

EWE: Afi ma gblɔ be: "Nyee ɖe ɖokuinye fia Abraham, Isak kple Yakob abe Mawu ŋusẽkatãtɔ ene; ke nyemeɖe nye ŋkɔ Yehowa fia wo o. "
ENGLISH: That passage says: "I used to appear to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob as God Almighty, but as respects my name Jehovah I did not make myself known to them. "

EWE: Yehowa ye nye ale si woyɔa Mawu ƒe ŋkɔe le Eʋegbe me ƒe alafa geɖewoe nye esia.
ENGLISH: Jehovah is a rendering of God’s name in English that has been used for centuries.

EWE: Togbɔ be agbalẽnyala geɖewo lɔ̃a "Yahweh " zazã hã la, Yehowa ye ame akpa gãtɔ ya zãna.
ENGLISH: While many scholars prefer the spelling "Yahweh, " Jehovah is the form of the name that is most widely recognized.

EWE: Hebrigbe mee woŋlɔ Biblia ƒe akpa gbãtɔ ɖo. Le gbe sia me la, woxlẽa nu tso ɖusime yia miame me, eye mele abe Eʋegbe ene o.
ENGLISH: The first part of the Bible was written not in English but in Hebrew, a language that is read from right to left.

EWE: Le Hebrigbea me la, xaxagbeɖiɖi ene, siwo nye יהוה ye wotsɔ ŋlɔa Mawu ƒe ŋkɔe.
ENGLISH: In that language, the divine name appears as four consonants, יהוה.

EWE: Amewo lɔ̃a Hebrigbe me ŋɔŋlɔdzesi ene mawo, siwo nye YHWH le míaƒe ŋɔŋlɔdzesi nu la yɔyɔ be Hebrigbe me ŋɔŋlɔdzesi ene.
ENGLISH: Those four Hebrew characters transliterated YHWH are known as the Tetragrammaton.

EWE: Mawu Ŋkɔe Nye Yesua?
ENGLISH: Is God’s Name Jesus?

EWE: Ale si Biblia ɖo eŋui
ENGLISH: The Bible’s answer

EWE: Yesu yɔ eɖokui be "Mawu ƒe Vi. "
ENGLISH: Jesus referred to himself as "God’s Son " or "the Son of God. "

EWE: (Yohanes 10:36; 11:4) Yesu megblɔ kpɔ be yenye Mawu Ŋusẽkatãtɔ o.
ENGLISH: (John 10:36; 11:4) Jesus never identified himself as Almighty God.

EWE: Gawu la, Yesu do gbe ɖa na Mawu.
ENGLISH: Moreover, Jesus prayed to God.

EWE: (Mateo 26:39) Esi Yesu nɔ gbedodoɖa fiam eyomedzelawo la, egblɔ be: "Mía Fofo si le dziƒowo, wò ŋkɔ ŋuti nakɔ. "
ENGLISH: (Matthew 26:39) And while teaching his followers how to pray, Jesus said: "Our Father in the heavens, let your name be sanctified. "

EWE: Mateo 6:9.
ENGLISH: Matthew 6:9.

EWE: Yesu ɖe Mawu ƒe ŋkɔ ɖe go esi wòyɔ nya tso blema Ŋɔŋlɔ aɖe me hegblɔ be: "Oo Israel, see, Yehowa mía Mawu la, Yehowa ɖeka koe. "
ENGLISH: Jesus revealed God’s name when he quoted an ancient passage of Scripture and said: "Hear, O Israel, Jehovah our God is one Jehovah. "

EWE: Marko 12:29; 5 Mose 6:4.
ENGLISH: Mark 12:29; Deuteronomy 6:4.

EWE: Ame Kae Nye Yehowa?
ENGLISH: Who Is Jehovah?

EWE: Ale si Biblia ɖo eŋui
ENGLISH: The Bible’s answer

EWE: Yehowae nye Mawu vavã si ŋu woƒo nu tsoe le Biblia me, eyae nye nuwo katã Wɔla.
ENGLISH: Jehovah is the true God of the Bible, the Creator of all things.

EWE: (Nyaɖeɖefia 4:11) Nyagblɔɖila siwo ŋkɔe nye Abraham kple Mose subɔ eya amea, eye Yesu hã subɔe.
ENGLISH: (Revelation 4:​11) The prophets Abraham and Moses worshipped him, as did Jesus.

EWE: (1 Mose 24:27; 2 Mose 15:1, 2; Yohanes 20:17) Eyae nye "anyigba blibo la katã " ƒe Mawu, ke menye dukɔ ɖeka aɖe ko tɔ o. Psalmo 47:2.
ENGLISH: (Genesis 24:27; Exodus 15:1, 2; John 20:17) He is the God, not just of one people, but of "all the earth. "​ Psalm 47:2.

EWE: Biblia na míenya be Yehowa ye nye Mawu ƒe ŋkɔ ɖeka kolia.
ENGLISH: Jehovah is God’s unique name as revealed in the Bible.

EWE: (2 Mose 3:15; Psalmo 83:18) Ŋkɔ sia tso Hebrigbe me dɔwɔnya "evaa eme " me, eye agbalẽnyalagã geɖewo gblɔ be ŋkɔa gɔmee nye "Enana Wòvaa Eme. "
ENGLISH: (Exodus 3:​15; Psalm 83:18) It comes from a Hebrew verb that means "to become, " and a number of scholars suggest that the name means "He Causes to Become. "

ENGLISH: Reasons to know and use God’s name

EWE: Mawu ƒe ŋkɔ ŋutɔŋutɔ si nye Yehowa la le vevie nɛ elabe ena woŋlɔ ŋkɔa zi gbɔ zi akpe geɖe ɖe Biblia me.​ Malaki 1:11.
ENGLISH: God must feel that his personal name, Jehovah, is important, because he included it thousands of times in the Bible.​ Malachi 1:​11.

ENGLISH: For instance, he prayed to Jehovah: "Let your name be sanctified. "​ Matthew 6:9; John 17:6.

EWE: Ame siwo va nyaa Mawu ƒe ŋkɔa hezãnɛ la wɔ afɔɖeɖe gbãtɔ siwo ana be xɔlɔ̃wɔwɔ nanɔ woawo kple Yehowa dome.
ENGLISH: Those who come to know and use God’s name take the first steps in building a friendship with Jehovah.

EWE: (Psalmo 9:10; Malaki 3:16) Ƒomedodo sia wɔnɛ be Mawu ƒe ŋugbedodo sia ate ŋu aɖe vi na wo, egblɔ be: "Esi melɔ̃a nu le gbɔnye o ta la, nye hã maɖee.
ENGLISH: (Psalm 9:​10; Malachi 3:​16) Such a relationship enables them to benefit from God’s promise: "Because he has affection for me, I will rescue him.

EWE: Makpɔ eta, elabena enya nye ŋkɔ. "​ Psalmo 91:14.
ENGLISH: I will protect him because he knows my name. "​ Psalm 91:14.

EWE: Biblia lɔ̃ ɖe edzi be: "Nu siwo woyɔna be mawuwo li, eɖanye le dziƒo alo le anyigba dzi o, abe ale si ‘mawu’ geɖewo kple ‘aƒetɔ’ geɖewo li ene. " (1 Korintotɔwo 8:5, 6) Ke hã, ena eme kɔ ƒãa be Mawu vavã ɖeka si ŋkɔe nye Yehowa koe li.​ Psalmo 83:18.
ENGLISH: The Bible acknowledges: "There are so-called gods, whether in heaven or on earth, just as there are many ‘gods’ and many ‘lords.’ " (1 Corinthians 8:​5, 6) Yet it clearly identifies the one true God by his name, Jehovah.​ Psalm 83:18.

EWE: Tame Kae Mawu Ðo Ðe Nye Agbe Ŋu?
ENGLISH: What Is the Will of God for My Life?

EWE: Ale si Biblia ɖo eŋui
ENGLISH: The Bible’s answer

EWE: Mawu ƒe lɔlɔ̃nue nye be nàva nya ye be Ame ŋutɔŋutɔe yenye, nàte ɖe ye ŋu, alɔ̃ ye eye nàsubɔ ye kple wò dzi blibo.
ENGLISH: God’s will is that you come to know him as a Person, draw close to him, and then love and serve him with your whole heart.

EWE: (Mateo 22:37, 38; Yakobo 4:8) Àte ŋu asrɔ̃ ale si nàwɔ Mawu ƒe lɔlɔ̃nu ne èsrɔ̃ nu tso Yesu ƒe agbenɔnɔ kple eƒe nufiafiawo ŋu.
ENGLISH: (Matthew 22:37, 38; James 4:8) You can learn how to do God’s will from the life and teachings of Jesus.

EWE: (Yohanes 7:16, 17) Menye ɖeko Yesu ƒo nu tso Mawu ƒe lɔlɔ̃nu ŋu na amewo o, eya ŋutɔ hã nɔ agbe ɖe enu.
ENGLISH: (John 7:16, 17) Jesus didn’t just talk about the will of God he lived it.

EWE: Eya tae Yesu gblɔ gɔ̃ hã be tameɖoɖo si le yeƒe agbe ŋu ‘menye be yeawɔ ye ŋutɔ yeƒe lɔlɔ̃nu o, ke boŋ yeawɔ ame si dɔ ye ɖa la ƒe lɔlɔ̃nu.’
ENGLISH: In fact, Jesus said that his purpose in life was "to do, not my will, but the will of him that sent me. "

EWE: Yohanes 6:38.
ENGLISH: John 6:38.

EWE: Ðe wòhiã be makpɔ dzesi tɔxɛ, ŋutega alo axɔ yɔyɔ tɔxɛ aɖe hafi anya tame si Mawu ɖo ɖe ŋunyea?
ENGLISH: Do I need a special sign, vision, or calling to know what the will of God is for me?

EWE: Ao, elabe gbedeasi si le Mawu si na ameƒomea la le Biblia me.
ENGLISH: No, because the Bible contains God’s message to mankind.

EWE: Nu sia nu si nèhiã be ‘nàdze bliboe, eye nànɔ dzadzraɖoɖi keŋkeŋ na dɔ nyui sia dɔ nyui wɔwɔ’ la le eme. (2 Timoteo 3:16, 17) Mawu di be nàzã Biblia kple wò "tamebubu ŋutete " atsɔ anya tame si yeɖo ɖe ŋuwò.
ENGLISH: It has what you need to be "completely equipped for every good work. " (2 Timothy 3:16, 17) God wants you to use the Bible along with your "power of reason " to learn his will for you.

EWE: Romatɔwo 12:1, 2; Efesotɔwo 5:17.
ENGLISH: Romans 12:1, 2; Ephesians 5:17.

EWE: Ðe mate ŋu awɔ Mawu ƒe lɔlɔ̃nu ŋutɔŋutɔa?
ENGLISH: Can I really do God’s will?

EWE: Ɛ̃, àte ŋui, elabe Biblia gblɔ be Mawu ƒe "seawo mesesẽ o. " (1 Yohanes 5:3, Eʋegbe Biblia) Esia mefia be Mawu ƒe sewo dzi wɔwɔ nɔa bɔbɔe ɣesiaɣi o.
ENGLISH: Yes, you can, for the Bible says: "God’s commands are not too hard for us. " (1 John 5:3, Easy-to-Read Version) That’s not to say that obeying God’s commands is always easy.

EWE: Gake vi siwo Mawu ƒe sewo dzi wɔwɔ ɖena na ame la ƒo agbagba siwo ame dzena hafi wɔa wo dzi la ta sãsãsã.
ENGLISH: But the benefits you will gain far outweigh the effort you must put forth.

EWE: Yesu ŋutɔ gblɔ be: "Dzidzɔtɔwoe nye ame siwo le Mawu ƒe nya la sem, eye wole edzi wɔm! " Luka 11:28.
ENGLISH: Jesus himself said: "How happy are those who hear the word of God and obey it! "

EWE: Nu Kae Biblia Gblɔ Tso Tiatiawɔblɔɖe Ŋu?
ENGLISH: Luke 11:28, Good News Translation.

EWE: Ðe Mawu Ðo Ame Si Nàva Zu Le Etsɔme Ðia?
ENGLISH: What Does the Bible Say About Free Will?

EWE: Ale si Biblia ɖo eŋui
ENGLISH: Is God in Control?

EWE: Mawu de bubu mía ŋu hena tiatiawɔblɔɖe mí.
ENGLISH: The Bible’s answer

EWE: Tiatiawɔblɔɖe nye ablɔɖe si Mawu na mí be míawo ŋutɔwo míatso nya me ke menye be Mawu alo dzɔgbese naɖo ale si míava nɔ agbee la ɖi na mí o.
ENGLISH: God dignifies us with free will, the power to make decisions of our own rather than having God or fate predetermine what we do.

EWE: Bu Biblia ƒe nufiafia siawo ŋu kpɔ.
ENGLISH: Consider what the Bible teaches.

EWE: Mawu wɔ amegbetɔwo ɖe eƒe nɔnɔme nu.
ENGLISH: God created humans in his image.

EWE: (1 Mose 1:26) Mía Wɔla wɔ mí ɖe eƒe nɔnɔme nu le mɔ sia nu be ŋutete le mía si míeɖea eƒe nɔnɔmewo, abe lɔlɔ̃ kple dzɔdzɔnyenye ene fiana.
ENGLISH: (Genesis 1:26) Unlike animals, which act mainly on instinct, we resemble our Creator in our capacity to display such qualities as love and justice.

EWE: Míele abe lãwo ene o elabena lãwo ya wɔa nu ɖe woƒe lãmenusese ko nu.
ENGLISH: And like our Creator, we have free will.

EWE: Eye abe mía Wɔla ene la, tiatiawɔblɔɖe le mía si.
ENGLISH: To a great extent, we can determine our future.

EWE: Biblia de dzi ƒo na mí be ‘mitia agbe eye miɖo to Mawu ƒe gbe,’ si fia be míalɔ̃ be míawɔ eƒe sewo dzi.
ENGLISH: The Bible encourages us to "choose life . . . by listening to [God’s] voice, " that is, by choosing to obey his commands.

EWE: (5 Mose 30:19, 20) Nya sia anye dzodzro kple tagbɔsesẽ le ame ŋu ne ŋutete mele mía si be míate ŋu atia nu si míawɔ la o.
ENGLISH: (Deuteronomy 30:19, 20) This offer would be meaningless, even cruel, if we lacked free will.

EWE: Le esi Mawu nazi nu si wòdi la ɖe mía dzi teƒe la, ɖe wòkpe mí lɔlɔ̃tɔe hegblɔ be: "Ðe wònye ɖe nèɖo to nye seawo la, anye ne wò ŋutifafa anɔ abe tɔsisi ene. "
ENGLISH: Instead of forcing us to do what he says, God warmly appeals to us: "O if only you would actually pay attention to my commandments! Then your peace would become just like a river. "

EWE: Yesaya 48:18.
ENGLISH: Isaiah 48:18.

EWE: Menye dzɔgbese aɖekee kpɔa ŋusẽ ɖe míaƒe dzidzedzekpɔkpɔ alo kpododonu dzi o.
ENGLISH: Our success or failure is not determined by fate.

EWE: Ne míedi be míakpɔ dzidzedze le míaƒe agbagbadzedzewo me la, ke ele be míawɔ dɔ sesĩe.
ENGLISH: If we want to succeed at an endeavor, we must work hard.

EWE: Biblia gblɔ be: "Nu sia nu si wò asi ate ŋu awɔ la, wɔe kple wò ŋusẽ. "
ENGLISH: "All that your hand finds to do, " says the Bible, "do with your very power.

EWE: (Nyagblɔla 9:10) Egblɔ hã be: "Veviedola ƒe tameɖoɖo hea viɖe vɛ. "
ENGLISH: "(Ecclesiastes 9:10) It also says: "The plans of the diligent one surely make for advantage. "

EWE: Lododowo 21:5.
ENGLISH: Proverbs 21:5.

EWE: Nunana xɔasie tiatiawɔblɔɖe nye Mawu na mí, elabena esia nana míelɔ̃nɛ kple míaƒe "dzi blibo, " le esi míetiae be míalɔ̃e ta.
ENGLISH: Free will is a precious gift from God, for it lets us love him with our "whole heart " because we want to.

EWE: Mateo 22:37.
ENGLISH: Matthew 22:37.

EWE: Ðe Mawu kpɔa ŋusẽ ɖe nu sia nu dzia?
ENGLISH: Doesn’t God control all things?

EWE: Biblia fia nu be Mawue nye Ŋusẽkatãtɔ, si fia be ame aɖeke ƒe ŋusẽ megbɔ etɔ nu o.
ENGLISH: The Bible does teach that God is Almighty, that his power is not limited by anyone other than himself.

EWE: (Hiob 37:23; Yesaya 40:26) Gake mezãa eƒe ŋusẽa tsɔ kpɔa ŋusẽ ɖe nu sia nu dzi o.
ENGLISH: (Job 37:23; Isaiah 40:26) However, he does not use his power to control everything.

EWE: Le kpɔɖeŋu me, esi Mawu nɔ nu wɔm kple blema Babilontɔ siwo nye eƒe amewo ƒe futɔwo la, egblɔ be "mezi ɖokuinye dzi. "
ENGLISH: For example, the Bible says that God was "exercising self-control " toward ancient Babylon, an enemy of his people.

EWE: (Yesaya 42:14) Nenema kee egbea hã, Mawu zi eɖokui dzi heɖe mɔ amewo le woƒe tiatiawɔblɔɖea zãm tsɔ le nu gblẽm le ame bubuwo ŋu.
ENGLISH: (Isaiah 42:14) Similarly, for now, he chooses to tolerate those who misuse their free will to harm others.

EWE: Gake Mawu mazi eɖokui dzi ɖaa o.
ENGLISH: But God will not do so indefinitely.

EWE: Psalmo 37:10, 11.
Mawue Nana Míekpea Fua?
ENGLISH: Is God to Blame for Our Suffering?

EWE: Ale si Biblia ɖo eŋui
ENGLISH: The Bible’s answer

EWE: Biblia ɖo eŋu eme kɔ ƒãa be, ao.
ENGLISH: The Bible emphatically answers no!

EWE: Yehowa Mawu meɖoe kura be amegbetɔwo nakpe fu o.
ENGLISH: Suffering was not part of Jehovah God’s purpose for mankind.

EWE: Ke hã atsu kple asi gbãtɔ dze aglã ɖe Mawu ƒe dziɖuɖu ŋu, eye wotiae be yewo ŋutɔwo yewoatso nya me le nyui kple vɔ̃ ŋu na yewo ɖokuiwo.
ENGLISH: However, the first human couple rebelled against God’s rulership, choosing to set their own standards of good and bad.

EWE: Woɖe wo ɖokuiwo ɖa le Mawu ŋu eye wokpɔ emetsonuawo hã.
ENGLISH: They turned away from God and suffered the consequences.

EWE: Egbea míele tiatia gbegblẽ si ame eve mawo wɔ la ƒe fu kpem.
ENGLISH: Today we are experiencing the effects of their bad choice.

EWE: Eya ta amegbetɔwo ƒe fukpekpe metso Mawu gbɔ kura o.
ENGLISH: But in no way did God originate human suffering.

EWE: Biblia gblɔ be: "Ne ame aɖe le tetekpɔ me tom la, negagblɔ be: ‘Mawue le teyem kpɔ’ o.
ENGLISH: The Bible says: "When under trial, let no one say: ‘I am being tried by God.’

EWE: Elabena womate ŋu atsɔ nu vɔ̃ɖiwo ate Mawu kpɔ o, eye eya ŋutɔ hã metea ame aɖeke kpɔ o. "
ENGLISH: For with evil things God cannot be tried nor does he himself try anyone. "

EWE: (Yakobo 1:13) Fukpekpe ate ŋu aɖe kpe na ame sia ame, ame siwo ŋu Mawu kpɔa ŋudzedze le gɔ̃ hã meto le eme o.
ENGLISH: (James 1:13) Suffering can afflict anyone even those who are favored by God.

EWE: Amegbetɔwo Ƒe Nunyae Le Biblia Mea?
ENGLISH: Is the Bible a Book of Human Wisdom?

EWE: Ale si Biblia ɖo eŋui
ENGLISH: The Bible’s answer

EWE: Nya siwo me nunya le dometɔ geɖe le Biblia alo Ŋɔŋlɔ Kɔkɔeawo me.
ENGLISH: The Bible, also known as the Holy Scriptures, does contain many wise sayings.

EWE: Ke hã de dzesi nya si Biblia gblɔ tso eɖokui ŋu: "Ŋɔŋlɔ blibo la tso Mawu ƒe gbɔgbɔ me. " (2 Timoteo 3:16) Kpeɖodzi geɖe le nya sia ŋu.
ENGLISH: However, note the claim that the Bible makes for itself: "All Scripture is inspired of God. " (2 Timothy 3:16) There is much evidence to back up that claim.

EWE: Wo dometɔ aɖewoe nye esiawo:
ENGLISH: Consider the following:

EWE: Amewo tee kpɔ be yewoake ɖi ale si ŋutinya si le Biblia me la de pɛpɛpɛ, gake wo katã wodo kpo nu.
ENGLISH: No one has ever successfully challenged the historical accuracy of the Bible.

EWE: Ame siwo ŋlɔ Biblia la nye ŋutsu anukwaretɔ siwo ŋlɔ nuwo le nyateƒe me.
ENGLISH: The Bible writers were honest men who wrote with openness of heart.

EWE: Woƒe anukwareɖiɖi na wòdze ƒãa be woƒe nuŋlɔɖiawo nye nyateƒenyawo.
ENGLISH: Their candor gives their writing the clear ring of truth.

EWE: Tanya vevi ɖekae le Biblia si. Eyae nye ale si Mawu koe dze aɖu amegbetɔƒomea dzi la ta ʋiʋli kple ale si wòato eƒe Dziƒofiaɖuƒea dzi ana eƒe tameɖoɖo nava eme.
ENGLISH: The Bible has one central theme: the vindication of God’s right to rule mankind and the fulfillment of his purpose by means of his heavenly Kingdom.

EWE: Togbɔ be woŋlɔ Biblia ƒe akpe geɖewoe nye esi va yi hã la, susu totro siwo nɔ dzɔdzɔmeŋutinunyalawo si le blema siwo dzi ame geɖewo da asi ɖo la ƒe ɖeke mele Biblia me o.
ENGLISH: Although written thousands of years ago, the Bible is free of mistaken scientific ideas that had gained wide acceptance in ancient times.

EWE: Blemanudzɔdzɔ siwo ŋu woku nu me le la ɖo kpe edzi be Biblia me nyagblɔɖiwo va eme pɛpɛpɛ.
ENGLISH: Documented historical evidence proves that Bible prophecies, or predictions, have come true.

EWE: Mawu Ƒe Susuwoe Woŋlɔ Ðe Biblia Mea?
ENGLISH: Is the Bible a Record of God’s Thoughts?

EWE: Ale si Biblia ɖo eŋui
ENGLISH: The Bible’s answer

EWE: Biblia-ŋlɔla geɖewo gblɔ be Mawue gblɔ nu siwo yewoŋlɔ la na yewo.
ENGLISH: Many Bible writers state that God directed what they wrote.

EWE: Kpɔ eƒe kpɔɖeŋu aɖewo ɖa:
ENGLISH: Note these examples:

EWE: Fia David: "Yehowa ƒe [gbɔgbɔ] ƒo nu to dzinye, eye eƒe nya le nye aɖe dzi. " 2 Samuel 23:1, 2.
ENGLISH: King David: "The spirit of Jehovah it was that spoke by me, and his word was upon my tongue. " 2 Samuel 23:1, 2.

EWE: Nyagblɔɖila Yesaya: "Ale Aƒetɔ, Yehowa Zebaot, gblɔ esi. "
ENGLISH: The prophet Isaiah: "This is what the Sovereign Lord, Jehovah of armies, has said. "

EWE: Yesaya 22:15.
ENGLISH: Isaiah 22:15.

EWE: Apostolo Yohanes: "Nyaɖeɖefia, si Yesu Kristo ɖe fia, si Mawu tsɔ nae. "
ENGLISH: The apostle John: "A revelation by Jesus Christ, which God gave him. "

EWE: Nyaɖeɖefia 1:1.
ENGLISH: Revelation 1:1.

EWE: Mose Ye Ŋlɔ Biblia?
ENGLISH: Did Moses Write the Bible?

EWE: Ale si Biblia ɖo eŋui
ENGLISH: The Bible’s answer

EWE: Mawu na Mose ŋlɔ Biblia ƒe agbalẽ atɔ̃ gbãtɔwo: Mose Ƒe Agbalẽ Gbãtɔ, Mose Ƒe Agbalẽ Evelia, Mose Ƒe Agbalẽ Etɔ̃lia, Mose Ƒe Agbalẽ Enelia kple Mose Ƒe Agbalẽ Atɔ̃lia.
ENGLISH: God used Moses to write the first five books of the Bible: Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, and Deuteronomy.

EWE: Eye anɔ eme be eya kee ŋlɔ Hiob ƒe agbalẽa kple Psalmo 90 lia.
ENGLISH: He also likely wrote the book of Job and Psalm 90.

EWE: Gake ŋutsu 40 siwo Mawu zã woŋlɔ Biblia la dometɔ ɖeka koe Mose nye.
ENGLISH: But Moses was only one of some 40 people whom God used to write the Bible.

EWE: Ðe Míate Ŋu Anya Ame Siwo Tututu Ŋlɔ Biblia?
ENGLISH: Can Anyone Know Who Really Wrote the Bible?

EWE: Ale si Biblia ɖo eŋui
ENGLISH: The Bible’s answer

EWE: Wogblɔ na ame geɖewo be míate ŋu anya ame siwo ŋlɔ Biblia o.
ENGLISH: Many people are told that we can’t be sure who wrote the Bible.

EWE: Gake zi geɖe la, Biblia me nuŋlɔɖiwo nana míenyaa ame siwo ŋlɔ wo.
ENGLISH: But the Bible is often clear about who penned its contents.

EWE: Eƒe akpa aɖewo dze egɔme ale: "Nexemya . . . ƒe ŋutinyawo nye esi, " "ŋutega, si Yesaya . . . kpɔ " kple "Yehowa ƒe gbe, si va na Yoel. "
ENGLISH: Some parts begin with such phrases as "the words of Nehemiah, " "the vision of Isaiah, " and "the word of Jehovah that occurred to Joel. "

EWE: Nexemiya 1:1; Yesaya 1:1; Yoel 1:1.
ENGLISH: Nehemiah 1:1; Isaiah 1:1; Joel 1:1.

EWE: Biblia-ŋlɔla geɖewo gblɔ be Yehowa, Mawu vavã la ƒe ŋkɔ mee yewoŋlɔ yewoƒe agbalẽawo le, eye eyae fia mɔ yewo.
ENGLISH: Most Bible writers acknowledged that they wrote in the name of Jehovah, the one true God, and that they were guided by him.

EWE: Nyagblɔɖila siwo ŋlɔ Hebri Ŋɔŋlɔawo gblɔ wu zi 300 be: "Ale Yehowa gblɔ esi. "
ENGLISH: Prophets who wrote the Hebrew Scriptures proclaimed more than 300 times: "This is what Jehovah has said. "

EWE: (Amos 1:3; Mixa 2:3; Naxum 1:12) Biblia-ŋlɔla bubuwo xɔ Mawu ƒe gbedeasia to mawudɔlawo dzi.
ENGLISH: (Amos 1:3; Micah 2:3; Nahum 1:12) Other writers received God’s message through angels.

EWE: Zaxarya 1:7, 9.
ENGLISH: Zechariah 1:7, 9.

EWE: Ŋutsu 40 aɖewoe ŋlɔ Biblia, eye Biblia-ŋɔŋlɔ xɔ ƒe 1,600 kple edzivɔwo.
ENGLISH: The Bible was written by some 40 men over the course of 1,600 years.

EWE: Ŋutsu siawo dometɔ aɖewo ŋlɔ Biblia-gbalẽ geɖe.
ENGLISH: Some men were used to write more than one book of the Bible.

EWE: Ne míagblɔe la, Biblia nye agbalẽdzraɖoƒe sue si me agbalẽ 66 le.
ENGLISH: In fact, the Bible is a miniature library of 66 books.

EWE: Agbalẽ 39 ye le Biblia ƒe akpa si nye Hebri Ŋɔŋlɔawo, si ame geɖewo yɔna be Nubabla Xoxoa me, eye agbalẽ 27 ye le Kristotɔwo Ƒe Hela Ŋɔŋlɔawo, si amewo yɔna zi geɖe be Nubabla Yeyea me.
ENGLISH: It consists of the 39 books of the Hebrew Scriptures, called by many the Old Testament, and the 27 books of the Christian Greek Scriptures, often called the New Testament.

EWE: Ðe Wotrɔ Biblia Me Nyawoa?
ENGLISH: Has the Bible Been Changed or Tampered With?

EWE: Ao.
ENGLISH: No.

EWE: Blemasinuŋɔŋlɔgbalẽwo tsɔtsɔ sɔ kple wo nɔewo ɖee fia be wometrɔ naneke le Biblia me o togbɔ be wogbugbɔ ŋlɔe zi akpe geɖe ɖe nu siwo tea ŋu nyunyɔna dzi hã.
ENGLISH: A comparison of ancient manuscripts shows that the Bible is basically unchanged despite millenniums of recopying on perishable materials.

EWE: Ðe wòfia be womewɔ vodada aɖeke kura esi wogbugbɔ nɔ eŋlɔm oa?
ENGLISH: Does this mean that mistakes in copying were never made?

EWE: Woke ɖe Biblia ƒe blemasinuŋɔŋlɔgbalẽ akpe geɖe ŋu.
ENGLISH: Thousands of ancient Bible manuscripts have been found.

EWE: Vovototo aɖewo dze le wo dometɔ aɖewo me si fia be egbugbɔŋlɔlawo wɔ vodada aɖewo.
ENGLISH: Some of these contain a number of differences, indicating that mistakes were made in copying.

EWE: Vovototo siawo ƒe akpa gãtɔ nye vodada suesuesue siwo metrɔ gɔmesese si le nyawo ŋu o.
ENGLISH: Most of these differences are minor and do not change the meaning of the text.

EWE: Ke hã woke ɖe vodada ɖedzesi aɖewo ŋu eye wo dometɔ aɖewo dze abe ame aɖewoe ɖoe koŋ le blema be yewoatrɔ Biblia ƒe gbedeasia ene.
ENGLISH: However, a few significant differences have been discovered, some of which appear to be deliberate attempts made long ago to alter the Bible’s message.

EWE: Kpɔ eƒe kpɔɖeŋu eve aɖewo ɖa:
ENGLISH: Consider two examples:

EWE: Le 1 Yohanes 5:7 la, Biblia gɔmeɖeɖe xoxo aɖewo gblɔ be: "ame siwo le ɖase ɖim le dziƒo: Fofo la, Nya la kple gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔe la, eye ame etɔ̃ siawo le ɖeka. "
ENGLISH: At 1 John 5:7, some older Bible translations contain the following words: "in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one. "

EWE: Gake asinuŋɔŋlɔgbalẽ siwo ŋu kakaɖedzi le la ɖo kpe edzi be nya siawo mele blemasinuŋɔŋlɔgbalẽ xoxoawo me o.
ENGLISH: However, reliable manuscripts confirm that these words were not in the original text.

EWE: Emegbee wode wo eme.
ENGLISH: They were added later.

EWE: Eya ta woɖe wo ɖa le egbegbe Biblia gɔmeɖeɖe siwo ŋu kakaɖedzi le la me.
ENGLISH: Thus, reliable modern Bible translations have excluded them.

EWE: Mawu ƒe ŋkɔ dze zi akpe geɖe le Biblia ƒe asinuŋɔŋlɔgbalẽ xoxotɔwo me.
ENGLISH: God’s personal name appears thousands of times in ancient manuscripts of the Bible.

EWE: Ke hã Biblia gɔmeɖeɖe geɖewo tsɔ dzesideŋkɔwo abe "Aƒetɔ " alo "Mawu " ene ɖo ŋkɔa teƒe.
ENGLISH: Yet, numerous Bible translations have replaced it with titles such as "Lord " or "God. "

EWE: Aleke míawɔ anya be vodada bubu geɖe mekpɔtɔ le eme o?
ENGLISH: How can we be sure that there are not many more errors waiting to be found?

EWE: Va se ɖe fifia la, woke ɖe asinuŋɔŋlɔgbalẽ gbogbo aɖewo ŋu si wɔe be ele bɔbɔe wu tsã be woade dzesi vodadawo.
ENGLISH: At this point, so many manuscripts have been discovered that it is easier than ever before to detect errors.

EWE: Nu kae agbalẽ vovovo siawo tsɔtsɔ sɔ kple wo nɔewo ɖe fia ku ɖe ale si gbegbe Biblia de pɛpɛpɛ egbeae ŋu?
ENGLISH: What has a comparison of these documents revealed regarding the accuracy of the Bible today?

EWE: Agbalẽnyala si ŋkɔe nye William H. Green gblɔ tso Hebri Ŋɔŋlɔawo si amewo yɔna egbea be "Nubabla Xoxoa " ŋu be: "Míate ŋu agblɔe kakaɖedzitɔe be blemagbalẽ aɖeke meli si me nyawo woŋlɔ ɖi wòde pɛpɛpɛ alea kpɔ o. "
ENGLISH: Commenting on the text of the Hebrew Scriptures (commonly called the "Old Testament "), scholar William H. Green stated: "It may be safely said that no other work of antiquity has been so accurately transmitted. "

EWE: Ku ɖe Kristotɔwo Ƒe Hela Ŋɔŋlɔawo alo "Nubabla Yeyea " ŋu la, Biblia-nyala F. F. Bruce gblɔ be: "Míaƒe Nubabla Yeye la ŋuti kpeɖodzi siwo ŋu woke ɖo la de ŋgɔ sãsãsã wu agbalẽŋlɔla bubu geɖe ƒe nuŋlɔɖiwo, eye ame aɖeke meku drɔ̃e kpɔ be yeake ɖi le wo me nyawo ƒe dede pɛpɛpɛ ŋu gbeɖe o. "
ENGLISH: Regarding the Christian Greek Scriptures, or "New Testament, " Bible scholar F. F. Bruce wrote: "The evidence for our New Testament writings is ever so much greater than the evidence for many writings of classical authors, the authenticity of which no one dreams of questioning. "

EWE: Aƒetɔ Frederic Kenyon, si nye asinuŋɔŋlɔgbalẽwo ŋutinunyala gblɔ be, ame "ate ŋu atsɔ kakaɖedzi agblɔ be Biblia si yelé ɖe asi la nye agbalẽ si nye Mawu ƒe Nya, si wotsɔ na mí si me nya veviwo metrɔ o tso dzidzime yi dzidzime hena ƒe alafa geɖe. "
ENGLISH: Sir Frederic Kenyon, a noted authority on Bible manuscripts, stated that one "can take the whole Bible in his hand and say without fear or hesitation that he holds in it the true Word of God, handed down without essential loss from generation to generation throughout the centuries. "

EWE: Susu bubu kawoe gali siwo ta míeka ɖe edzi be Biblia nye agbalẽ si de pɛpɛpɛ?
ENGLISH: What additional reasons are there for confidence that the Bible has been transmitted with accuracy?

EWE: Yudatɔ kple Kristotɔ nugbugbɔgaŋlɔlawo siaa kpɔ ŋutinya siwo klo nu le vodada gã siwo Mawu ƒe amewo wɔ dzi la ta.
ENGLISH: Both Jewish and Christian copyists preserved accounts that expose the serious mistakes made by God’s people.

EWE: (4 Mose 20:12; 2 Samuel 11:2-4; Galatiatɔwo 2:11-14) Nenema kee wogakpɔ Biblia ƒe akpa siwo bu fɔ Yuda dukɔa ɖe woƒe tomaɖomaɖo kple nu siwo klo nu le amegbetɔwo ƒe dzixɔse totrowo ŋu la ta.
ENGLISH: (Numbers 20:12; 2 Samuel 11:​2-4; Galatians 2:​11-​14) Likewise, they preserved passages that condemn the Jewish nation’s disobedience and that expose man-made doctrines.

EWE: (Hosea 4:2; Malaki 2:8, 9; Mateo 23:8, 9; 1 Yohanes 5:21) Esi wogbugbɔ ŋlɔ ŋutinya siawo ɖi wòde pɛpɛpɛ ta la, nugbugbɔgaŋlɔlaawo ɖe ale si gbegbe míate ŋu aka ɖe wo dzii kple ale si wobua Mawu ƒe Nya nu kɔkɔee la fia.
ENGLISH: (Hosea 4:2; Malachi 2:​8, 9; Matthew 23:​8, 9; 1 John 5:​21) By copying these accounts accurately, the copyists showed their trustworthiness and their high regard for God’s sacred Word.

EWE: Ðe susu mele eme be míaxɔe ase be Mawu si ŋlɔ Biblia la akpɔ eta be wòade pɛpɛpɛ oa?
ENGLISH: Is it not reasonable that God, having inspired the Bible in the first place, would also preserve its accuracy?

EWE: (Yesaya 40:8; 1 Petro 1:24, 25) Le nyateƒe me la, menye ame siwo nɔ anyi le blema koe wòdi be eme nyawo naɖe vi na o ke na mí ame siwo li egbea hã.
ENGLISH: (Isaiah 40:8; 1 Peter 1:​24, 25) After all, he intended it to benefit not only people of long ago but also us today.

EWE: (1 Korintotɔwo 10:11) Le nyateƒe me la, "nu siwo katã woŋlɔ ɖi tsã la, woŋlɔ wo ɖi be woatsɔ afia nu mí, ale be to míaƒe dzidodo kple akɔfafa si míekpɔ tso Ŋɔŋlɔawo me dzi la, mɔkpɔkpɔ nasu mía si. "​ Romatɔwo 15:4.
ENGLISH: (1 Corinthians 10:11) In fact, "all the things that were written beforehand were written for our instruction, so that through our endurance and through the comfort from the Scriptures we might have hope. "​ Romans 15:4.

EWE: Yesu kple eyomedzelawo yɔ nya tso Hebri Ŋɔŋlɔawo me kple kakaɖedzi eye womeke ɖi be blemanuŋɔŋlɔ mawo mede pɛpɛpɛ o.​ Luka 4:16-21; Dɔwɔwɔwo 17:1-3.
ENGLISH: Jesus and his followers quoted from copies of the Hebrew Scriptures without expressing any concern about the accuracy of those ancient texts.​ Luke 4:​16-​21; Acts 17:​1-3.

EWE: Ðe Biblia Me Nyawo Wɔ Ðeka Kple Dzɔdzɔmeŋutinunya?
ENGLISH: Does Science Agree With the Bible?

EWE: Ale si Biblia ɖo eŋui
ENGLISH: The Bible’s answer

EWE: Ɛ̃, togbɔ be Biblia menye dzɔdzɔmeŋutinyagbalẽ o hã, emenyawo de pɛpɛpɛ nenye be eƒo nu tso dzɔdzɔmeŋutinunya ŋu.
ENGLISH: Yes, for although the Bible is not a science textbook, it is accurate when it mentions matters of science.

EWE: Bu kpɔɖeŋu siwo ɖee fia be Biblia me nyawo wɔ ɖeka kple dzɔdzɔmeŋutinunya, eye be nyateƒenya siwo ku ɖe dzɔdzɔmeŋutinunya ŋu le Biblia me, siwo to vovo kura na dzixɔse siwo nɔ ame siwo nɔ anyi le Bibliaŋlɔɣi la si ŋu kpɔ.
ENGLISH: Consider some examples showing that science and the Bible agree and that the Bible contains scientific facts that differed greatly from the beliefs of many people living at the time it was written.

EWE: Gɔmedzedze li na xexea.
ENGLISH: The universe had a beginning.

EWE: (1 Mose 1:1) Gake blema nyakpakpa geɖewo gblɔ be menye ɖe wowɔ xexea o, ke boŋ edzɔ tso zitɔtɔ manɔɖoɖonu aɖe me.
ENGLISH: (Genesis 1:1) In contrast, many ancient myths describe the universe, not as being created, but as being organized from existing chaos.

EWE: Babilontɔwo xɔe se be mawu siwo na xexea dzɔ la tso atsiaƒu gbahoo eve me.
ENGLISH: The Babylonians believed that the gods that gave birth to the universe came from two oceans.

EWE: Blemaxotutu aɖewo hã gblɔ be azi gã aɖe mee xexea dzɔ tso.
ENGLISH: Other legends say that the universe came from a giant egg.

EWE: Dzɔdzɔmesewo dzie xexea zɔna ɖo gbe sia gbe, ke menye mawu aɖewo siwo wɔa nu eŋumabumabui woe kpɔ ŋusẽ ɖe xexe gbahoo la dzi o.
ENGLISH: The universe is governed day-to-day by rational natural laws, not by the whims of deities.

EWE: (Hiob 38:33; Yeremiya 33:25) Nyakpakpawo le xexea ƒe akpa vovovowo, siwo fiana be wɔna aɖeke mele amegbetɔwo ŋu le mawu siwo dzi womate ŋu aka ɖo o eye nublanuikpɔkpɔ hã mele woƒe nuwɔnawo me o, la si me o.
ENGLISH: (Job 38:33; Jeremiah 33:25) Myths from around the world teach that humans are helpless before the unpredictable and sometimes merciless acts of the gods.

EWE: Womeku anyigba ɖe naneke ŋu o.
ENGLISH: The earth is suspended in empty space.

EWE: (Hiob 26:7) Ame geɖe siwo nɔ anyi le blema xɔe se be anyigba la le gbadzaa eye ame dzɔtsu alo lã gã aɖe, abe to alo klo ene, dzie wònɔ.
ENGLISH: (Job 26:7) Many ancient peoples believed that the world was a flat disk supported by a giant or an animal, such as a buffalo or a turtle.

EWE: Ɣea hea tsi tsoa atsiaƒu kple tsi bubuwo me yia yame eye wòtrɔna zua tsi, sno alo kpetsi dzana ɖe anyigba dzi eye wogasina yia tɔsisiwo kple tsidzɔƒewo me.
ENGLISH: Rivers and springs are fed by water that has evaporated from the oceans and other sources and then has fallen back to earth as rain, snow, or hail.

EWE: (Hiob 36:27, 28; Nyagblɔla 1:7; Yesaya 55:10; Amos 9:6) Gake blema Helatɔwo susui be tsi siwo le anyigbaa gɔmee ŋɔna yia tɔsisiwo me, susu sia nɔ amewo si kaka va ɖo ƒe alafa 18-awo me.
ENGLISH: (Job 36:27, 28; Ecclesiastes 1:7; Isaiah 55:10; Amos 9:6) The ancient Greeks thought that rivers were fed by underground ocean water, and this idea persisted into the 18th century.

EWE: Towo hona ɖe dzi eye wogabuna, eye to siwo li egbea nɔ atsiaƒu gɔme kpɔ.
ENGLISH: The mountains rise and fall, and today’s mountains were once under the ocean.

EWE: (Psalmo 104:6, 8) Gake nyakpakpa geɖewo gblɔna be mawuawoe wɔ to siwo li egbea.
ENGLISH: (Psalm 104:​6, 8) In contrast, several myths say that the mountains were created in their current form by the gods.

EWE: Dzadzɛnyenye kpɔa ame ƒe lãmesẽ ta.
ENGLISH: Sanitary practices protect health.

EWE: Ðoɖo aɖewo nɔ Se si wotsɔ na Israel-dukɔa me, siwo bia tso wosi be woaklɔ wo ɖokuiwo ŋu nenye be woka asi nukuku alo amekuku aɖe ŋu, woaɖe ame siwo ŋu dɔxɔleameŋu le la ɖe aga, eye woaɖi woƒe nugodowo ɖe do me.
ENGLISH: The Law given to the nation of Israel included regulations for washing after touching a dead body, quarantining those with infectious disease, and disposing of human waste safely.

EWE: (3 Mose 11:25-28; 13:1-5; 5 Mose 23:13) To vovo na ema la, esime wona se sia Israel-dukɔa, Egiptetɔwo wɔa atike aɖe si me amegbetɔwo ƒe nugodo le tsɔ ɖoa abi.
ENGLISH: (Leviticus 11:28; 13:​1-5; Deuteronomy 23:13) By contrast, one of the Egyptian remedies in use when these commands were given called for applying to an open wound a mixture that included human excrement.

EWE: Ðe vodadawo le nya siwo Biblia gblɔ tso dzɔdzɔmeŋutinunya ŋua?
ENGLISH: Are there scientific errors in the Bible?

EWE: Biblia me dzodzro yi ŋgɔe ɖee fia kɔtɛe be vodadawo mele eme o.
ENGLISH: A reasonable examination of the Bible shows the answer to be no.

EWE: Nyakpakpa: Biblia gblɔ be ŋkeke ade siwo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe nye gaƒoƒo 24 ye wotsɔ wɔ xexea katã.
ENGLISH: Here are some common misconceptions about the scientific accuracy of the Bible:

EWE: Nyateƒea: Biblia megblɔ ɣeyiɣi tututu si me Mawu wɔ xexea o.
ENGLISH: Myth: The Bible says that the universe was created in six 24-hour days.

EWE: (1 Mose 1:1) Azɔ hã, nuwo wɔwɔ ƒe ŋkeke si ŋu woƒo nu tsoe le Mose Ƒe Agbalẽ Gbãtɔ la nye ɣeyiɣi agbɔsɔsɔ me si womeyɔ o.
ENGLISH: Fact: According to the Bible, God created the universe in the indefinite past.

EWE: Le nyateƒe me la, woyɔ ɣeyiɣi si wotsɔ wɔ anyigba kple dziƒo la katã hã be "ŋkeke " ɖeka.​ 1 Mose 2:4.
ENGLISH: (Genesis 1:1) Also, the days of creation described in chapter 1 of Genesis were epochs whose length is not specified.

EWE: Nyakpakpa: Biblia gblɔ be wowɔ numiemiewo hafi va wɔ ɣea, ale be numiemiewo nazã ɣea ƒe ŋusẽ atsɔ awɔ woƒe nuɖuɖu.​ 1 Mose 1:11, 16.
ENGLISH: Myth: The Bible says that vegetation was created before the sun existed to support photosynthesis.​ Genesis 1:​11, 16.

EWE: Nyateƒea: Biblia ɖee fia be wowɔ ɣea, si nye ɣletivi siwo le "dziƒo " la dometɔ ɖeka hafi va wɔ numiemiewo.
ENGLISH: Fact: The Bible shows that the sun, one of the stars that make up "the heavens, " was created before vegetation.

EWE: (1 Mose 1:1) Kekeli si tso ɣea gbɔ la ɖo anyigba dzi flukpee le nuwɔwɔ ƒe "ŋkeke " gbãtɔ dzi.
ENGLISH: (Genesis 1:1) Diffused light from the sun reached the earth’s surface during the first "day, " or epoch, of creation.

EWE: Esi yame nɔ kɔkɔm va ɖo nuwɔwɔ ƒe "ŋkeke " etɔ̃lia dzi la, ɣea ƒe keklẽ nu sẽ va ɖo afi si numiemiewo te ŋu zãe tsɔ wɔ woƒe nuɖuɖu.
ENGLISH: As the atmosphere cleared, by the third "day " of creation, the light was strong enough to support photosynthesis.

EWE: (1 Mose 1:3-5, 12, 13) Ɣeyiɣi aɖe megbe ko hafi ɣea va te dzedze nyuie.​ 1 Mose 1:16.
ENGLISH: (Genesis 1:​3-5, 12, 13) Only later did the sun become distinctly visible from the surface of the earth.​ Genesis 1:​16.

EWE: Nyakpakpa: Biblia gblɔ be ɣea ƒoa ɣla anyigba la.
ENGLISH: Myth: The Bible says that the sun revolves around the earth.

EWE: Nyateƒea: Nyagblɔla 1:5 gblɔ be: "Ɣe dzena, eye wòɖoa to, eye wòɖea abla gatrɔna yia afi si wòdzena tso. "
ENGLISH: Fact: Ecclesiastes 1:5 says: "The sun rises, and the sun sets; then it hurries back to the place where it rises again. "

EWE: Ke hã, ɖeko nya sia le ale si amegbetɔwo kpɔa ɣea wòtsona ɣedzeƒe va yina ɣetoɖoƒe la ɖɔm.
ENGLISH: However, this statement merely describes the apparent motion of the sun as viewed from the earth.

EWE: Egbea gɔ̃ hã, amegbetɔwo tea zãa nya siwo nye "ɣe dze " kple "ɣe ɖo to, " evɔ wonyae be anyigbae ƒoa xla ɣea.
ENGLISH: Even today, a person can use the words "sunrise " and "sunset, " yet he knows that the earth revolves around the sun.

EWE: Nyakpakpa: Biblia gblɔ be anyigba la le gbadzaa.
ENGLISH: Myth: The Bible says that the earth is flat.

EWE: Nyateƒea: Biblia zã nyagbe si nye "anyigba ƒe seƒe ke, " gake mefia be anyigba la le gbadzaa alo seƒe le eŋu o.
ENGLISH: Fact: The Bible uses the phrase "the ends of the earth " to mean "the most distant part of the earth "; this does not imply that the earth is flat or that it has an edge.

EWE: (Dɔwɔwɔwo 1:8) Nenema kee nyagbe si nye "anyigba ƒe go eneawo " nye kpɔɖeŋunyagbɔgblɔ si fia anyigba dzi godoo; eye ame aɖe ate ŋu azã taɖoƒefianu (compass alo la boussole) ƒe dzesi eneawo wòafia kpɔɖeŋunyagbɔgblɔ ma ke.​ Yesaya 11:12; Luka 13:29.
ENGLISH: (Acts 1:8; footnote) Likewise, the expression "the four corners of the earth " is a figure of speech referring to the entire surface of the earth; today a person might use the four points of the compass as a similar metaphor.​ Isaiah 11:12; Luke 13:29.

EWE: Nyakpakpa: Biblia gblɔ be togodo ƒe ɣlaƒoƒo ɖeka ƒe dzidze nye fli si tso eƒe toga ɖeka yi kemea ƒe teƒe etɔ̃ pɛpɛpɛ, gake togodo ƒe ɣlaƒoƒo ƒe dzidze ŋutɔŋutɔ anɔ abe 3.1416 si nye (pi alo π).
ENGLISH: Myth: The Bible says that the circumference of a circle is exactly three times its diameter, but the correct value is pi (π), or about 3.1416.

EWE: Nyateƒea: "Gazɔ gã la " si ƒe nya wogblɔ le 1 Fiawo 7:23 kple 2 Kronika 4:2 ɖee fia be eƒe didime tso to ɖeka yi kemea nye abɔklugui ewo eye "ka didime abɔklugui blaetɔ̃e " hiã hafi "akpee ɖo. "
ENGLISH: Fact: The measurements of "the Sea of cast metal " given at 1 Kings 7:​23 and 2 Chronicles 4:2 indicate that it had a diameter of 10 cubits and that "it took a measuring line 30 cubits long to encircle it. "

EWE: Ate ŋu anɔ eme be woatsɔ nu sue aɖe kpe xexlẽme siawo alo aɖee le eme hafi woade pɛpɛpɛ.
ENGLISH: These dimensions might have been merely the nearest round numbers.

EWE: Anɔ eme hã be gazɔa ƒe togodo kple eƒe didime tso eƒe toga ɖeka yi kemea tsi tsitre ɖi na gazɔa me kple egodo ƒe dzidze.
ENGLISH: It is also possible that the circumference and diameter represented inner and outer measurements of the basin respectively.

EWE: Ðe Biblia Fia Nu Be Anyigba La Le Gbadzaa?
ENGLISH: Does the Bible Teach That the Earth Is Flat?

EWE: Ale si Biblia ɖo eŋui
ENGLISH: The Bible’s answer

EWE: Ao, Biblia mefia nu be anyigba la le gbadzaa o.
ENGLISH: No, the Bible does not teach that the earth is flat.

EWE: Menye dzɔdzɔmeŋutinunyagbalẽe Biblia nye o.
ENGLISH: The Bible is not a science textbook.

EWE: Ke hã, Biblia me nya aɖeke metsi tre ɖe dzɔdzɔmeŋutinunya si ŋu kakaɖedzi le ŋu o.
ENGLISH: At the same time, nothing in the Bible contradicts proved science.

EWE: Míate ŋu "aɖo ŋu ɖe " nya siwo Biblia gblɔ la "ŋu ɖaa tegbee. " Psalmo 111:8.
ENGLISH: What the Bible says is "always reliable, now and forever. "​ Psalm 111:8.

EWE: Nya si Biblia gblɔ be "anyigba ƒe go eneawo " gɔme ɖe?
ENGLISH: What does the Bible mean by "the four corners of the earth "?

EWE: Ke tetekpɔ si Abosam he va Yesu dzi ya ɖe?
ENGLISH: What about the Devil’s temptation of Jesus?

EWE: Nya si Biblia gblɔ be "anyigba ƒe go eneawo " gɔme ɖe?
ENGLISH: What does the Bible mean by "the four corners of the earth "?

EWE: Mele be míase nyagbɔgblɔ "anyigba ƒe go eneawo " kple "anyigba ƒe mlɔenuwo " si Biblia zã la gɔme ɖe nyagbeawo ŋutɔŋutɔ nu abe ɖe dzogoe ene le anyigba si alo abe ɖe seƒe le anyigba si ene o.
ENGLISH: The expressions "the four corners of the earth " and "the ends of the earth " used in the Bible are not to be taken literally, as if the earth were square or had ends.

ENGLISH: At Ecclesiastes 1:4, the Bible says that "the earth remains forever, " which to some apparently conflicts with its statement that "the elements will be destroyed by heat​ with the earth. " (2 Peter 3:​10, Beck) In the Bible, however, the word "earth " is used both literally, referring to our planet, and figuratively, referring to the people who live on it.

EWE: (1 Mose 1:1; 11:1) "Anyigba " la tsɔtsrɔ̃ si ŋu woƒo nu tsoe le 2 Petro 3:​10 mefia be míaƒe anyigba si dzi míele la ŋutɔŋutɔ afiã le dzo me o, ke boŋ "ame mavɔ̃mawuwo ƒe ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃ kple tsɔtsrɔ̃ " ye wowɔnɛ.​ 2 Petro 3:7.
ENGLISH: (Genesis 1:1; 11:1) The destruction of the "earth " described at 2 Peter 3:​10 refers, not to the burning up of our planet, but to the "destruction of the ungodly people. "​ 2 Peter 3:7.

EWE: Mɔfiame 5: Woate ŋu agblɔ be ame aɖe wɔ nane evɔ menye eya ŋutɔe wɔe tẽe o
ENGLISH: Principle 5: Attribution

EWE: Le Kapernaum la, ame kae va bia kpekpeɖeŋu tso Yesu gbɔ na asrafomegã?
ENGLISH: In Capernaum, who brought the centurion’s request to Jesus?

EWE: Mateo 8:​5, 6 gblɔ be asrafomegã ŋutɔe yi Yesu gbɔ evɔ Luka 7:3 ya gblɔ be Yudatɔwo ƒe dumegãwoe asrafomegã la dɔ ɖe Yesu gbɔ.
ENGLISH: Matthew 8:​5, 6 says that the centurion (army officer) himself came to Jesus, while Luke 7:3 says that the centurion sent older men of the Jews to make his request.

EWE: Nu si wòfia koe nye be asrafomegã ŋutɔ gblɔ be woabia kpekpeɖeŋu tso Yesu gbɔ na ye, gake edɔ dumegãwo ɖo ɖe Yesu gbɔ abe eteƒenɔlawo ene.
ENGLISH: This apparent Bible contradiction can be understood in that the army officer initiated the request, but he sent the older men as his representatives.

EWE: Mɔfiame 6: Biblia gɔmeɖeɖe si de pɛpɛpɛ
ENGLISH: Principle 6: Accurate translation

EWE: Ðe mí katã míewɔa nu vɔ̃a?
ENGLISH: Do we all sin?

EWE: Biblia na míenya be mí katã míenyi nu vɔ̃ dome tso ŋutsu gbãtɔ Adam gbɔ.
ENGLISH: The Bible teaches that we all inherit sin from the first man, Adam.

EWE: (Romatɔwo 5:​12) Ale si woɖe Biblia aɖewo gɔme la di be yeatsi tre ɖe nya sia ŋu, esi wogblɔ le wo me be ame nyui "mewɔa nu vɔ̃ o. " (1 Yohanes 3:6, Eʋegbe Biblia) Gake fifiɣeyiɣi mee Helagbe me nya si gɔme woɖe be "nu vɔ̃ " le 1 Yohanes 3:6 la le. Eye ne wozã fifiɣeyiɣi le gbe ma me la, efiaa nuwɔna aɖe si le edzi yim.
ENGLISH: (Romans 5:​12) Some translations seem to contradict this by saying that a good person "does no sin " or "sinneth not. " (1 John 3:6, The Bible in Basic English; King James Version) In the original language, though, the Greek verb for "sin " at 1 John 3:6 is in the present tense, which in that language normally indicates a continuous action.

EWE: Vovototo le nu vɔ̃ si ƒe dome míenyi kple nu vɔ̃ ɖowɔe, si fia be ame naɖoe koŋ anɔ Mawu ƒe sewo dzi dam la dome.
ENGLISH: There is a difference between inherited sin, which we cannot avoid, and the deliberate, continuous practice of disobeying God’s laws.

EWE: Eya ta Biblia-gɔmeɖela aɖewo dze agbagba de vovototo nu vɔ̃ ƒomevi eve siawo dome ale be magadze abe ɖe Biblia tsi tsitre ɖe eɖokui ŋu ene o, eye woɖe kpukpui ma gɔme wòde pɛpɛpɛ be "metsɔa nu vɔ̃ wɔwɔ ɖoa dɔe o " alo "meyia edzi nɔa nu vɔ̃ wɔm o. "​ Xexe Yeye Gɔmeɖeɖe; Phillips.
ENGLISH: Thus, some translations clear up this seeming contradiction by accurately using phrases such as "does not practice sin " or "does not habitually sin. "​ New World Translation; Phillips.

EWE: Mɔfiame 7: Zã Biblia, ke menye sɔlemehawo ƒe nufiafiawo o
ENGLISH: Principle 7: The Bible, not dogma

EWE: Ðe Yesu sɔ kple Mawu loo alo ɖe Mawu lolo wu Yesua?
ENGLISH: Is Jesus equal to God or lesser than God?

EWE: Yesu gblɔ gbe ɖeka bena: "Nye kple Fofo la míele ɖeka. " Ewɔna na ame aɖewo be eƒe nya siawo tsi tsitre ɖe nya bubu si wògblɔ be "Fofo la lolo wum " la ŋu.
ENGLISH: Jesus once said: "I and the Father are one, " which seems to contradict his statement that "the Father is greater than I am. "

EWE: (Yohanes 10:30; 14:28) Hafi míate ŋu ase eƒe nya mawo gɔme nyuie la, ele be míadzro nya siwo tututu Biblia gblɔ tso Yehowa kple Yesu ŋu me, ke manye be míadze agbagba be míaɖe Biblia me wòasɔ ɖe sɔlemehawo ƒe nufiafia si nye Mawuɖekaetɔ̃ alo Trinita Kɔkɔea, si wometu ɖe Biblia dzi o la, nu o.
ENGLISH: (John 10:30; 14:28) To understand those verses correctly, we must examine what the Bible really says about Jehovah and Jesus rather than try to harmonize the verses with the Trinity dogma, which is not based on the Bible.

EWE: Biblia ɖee fia be Yehowae nye Yesu Fofo eye wòganye eƒe Mawu hã. Yehowa ye Yesu ŋutɔ gɔ̃ hã dea ta agu na.
ENGLISH: The Bible shows that Jehovah is not only Jesus’ Father but also Jesus’ God, the One whom even Jesus worships.

EWE: (Mateo 4:10; Marko 15:34; Yohanes 17:3; 20:17; 2 Korintotɔwo 1:3) Yesu mesɔ kple Mawu o.
ENGLISH: (Matthew 4:​10; Mark 15:34; John 17:3; 20:17; 2 Corinthians 1:3) Jesus is not equal to God.

EWE: Nya si Yesu nɔ gbɔgblɔm hafi gblɔ be "nye kple Fofo la míele ɖeka " ɖee fia be ale si eƒe susu wɔ ɖeka kple Fofoa Yehowa Mawu ƒe tameɖoɖowo ye wòwɔnɛ.
ENGLISH: The context of Jesus’ statement "I and the Father are one " shows that he was talking about the oneness of purpose that he shared with his Father, Jehovah God.

EWE: Yesu gblɔ emegbe be: "Fofo la wɔ ɖeka kplim, eye nye hã mewɔ ɖeka kple Fofo la. "
ENGLISH: Jesus later said: "The Father is in union with me and I am in union with the Father. "

EWE: (Yohanes 10:38) Yesu kple eƒe nusrɔ̃lawo hã wɔ ɖeka le tameɖoɖo ma ke gome, elabe edo gbe ɖa na Mawu le wo ta be: "Metsɔ ŋutikɔkɔe si nètsɔ nam la na wo, ne woazu ɖeka, abe ale si míele ɖeka ene.
ENGLISH: (John 10:38) Jesus shared this unity of purpose with his followers as well, for he prayed to God about them: "I have given them the glory that you have given me, in order that they may be one just as we are one.

EWE: Mewɔ ɖeka kpli wo, eye nèwɔ ɖeka kplim. "​ Yohanes 17:22, 23.
ENGLISH: I in union with them and you in union with me. "​ John 17:22, 23.

EWE: Ame Kae Alo Nu Kae Nye Mawu Ƒe Nya La?
ENGLISH: Who or What Is the Word of God?

EWE: Ale si Biblia ɖo eŋui
ENGLISH: The Bible’s answer

EWE: Zi geɖe la, nyagbɔgblɔ "Mawu ƒe nya " fiaa Mawu ƒe gbedeasi alo nya siwo wògblɔ.
ENGLISH: The expression "the word of God " usually refers to a divine message or to a collection of those messages.

EWE: (Luka 11:28) Wozãa "Mawu Ƒe Nya " alo "Nya La " le teƒe ʋɛ aɖewo wònyea dzesideŋkɔ.​ Nyaɖeɖefia 19:13; Yohanes 1:14.
ENGLISH: (Luke 11:28) In a few places, "The Word of God " or "the Word " is used as a personal title.​ Revelation 19:13; John 1:​14.

EWE: Mawu ƒe gbedeasi.
ENGLISH: A divine message.

EWE: Nyagblɔɖilawo gblɔna zi geɖe be gbedeasi siwo yewogblɔna la nye Mawu ƒe nya.
ENGLISH: The prophets often stated that the messages they delivered were God’s word.

EWE: Le kpɔɖeŋu me, Yeremiya dze eƒe nyagblɔɖi gbedeasia gɔme be, "Yehowa ƒe gbe va nam. "
ENGLISH: For example, Jeremiah introduced his prophetic messages with the expression "the word of Jehovah came to me. "

EWE: (Yeremiya 1:4, 11, 13; 2:1) Hafi nyagblɔɖila Samuel nagblɔ na Saul be Mawu tiae be wòanye fia la, nyagblɔɖilaa gblɔ be: "Tɔ ne magblɔ Mawu ƒe gbe na wò. "​ 1 Samuel 9:27.
ENGLISH: (Jeremiah 1:​4, 11, 13; 2:1) Before telling Saul that God had chosen him as king, the prophet Samuel said: "Stand still now, so that I may let you hear the word of God. "​ 1 Samuel 9:​27.

EWE: Dzesideŋkɔ.
ENGLISH: A personal title.

EWE: Biblia zã "Nya la " wònye dzesideŋkɔ na Yesu Kristo esime wònye gbɔgbɔmenuwɔwɔ le dziƒo kple esime wònye amegbetɔ nɔ anyigba dzi.
ENGLISH: "The Word " also appears in the Bible as a title for Jesus Christ, both as a spirit in heaven and as a human on earth.

EWE: Kpɔ susu siwo tae míate ŋu aƒo nya ta alea ɖo la ɖa:
ENGLISH: Consider some reasons for this conclusion:

EWE: Nya la nɔ agbe do ŋgɔ na nuwɔwɔ bubuwo katã.
ENGLISH: The Word lived before all other creation.

EWE: "Le gɔmedzedzea me, Nya la li, . . .
ENGLISH: "In the beginning was the Word . . .

EWE: Ame sia nɔ anyi kple Mawu le gɔmedzedzea me. "
ENGLISH: This one was in the beginning with God. "

EWE: (Yohanes 1:1, 2) Yesue nye "nuwɔwɔwo katã ƒe gbãtɔ . . .
ENGLISH: (John 1:​1, 2) Jesus is "the firstborn of all creation . . .

EWE: Etre dzɔdzɔ na nu bubuwo katã hã. "​ Kolosetɔwo 1:13-15, 17.
ENGLISH: He is before all other things. "​ Colossians 1:​13-​15, 17.

EWE: Nya la va anyigba dzi abe amegbetɔ ene.
ENGLISH: The Word came to earth as a human.

EWE: "Nya la va zu amegbetɔ, enɔ mía dome. "
ENGLISH: "The Word became flesh and resided among us. "

EWE: (Yohanes 1:14) Kristo Yesu ‘ɖi gbɔlo eɖokui, eye wòtsɔ kluvi ƒe nɔnɔme heva zu amegbetɔ.’​ Filipitɔwo 2:5-7.
ENGLISH: (John 1:​14) Christ Jesus "emptied himself and took a slave’s form and became human. "​ Philippians 2:​5-7.

EWE: Nya la nye Mawu ƒe Vi.
ENGLISH: The Word is God’s Son.

EWE: Esi apostolo Yohanes gblɔ be "Nya la va zu amegbetɔ " vɔ la, eyi edzi be: "Míekpɔ eƒe ŋutikɔkɔe si le abe tenuvi ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe tso fofoa gbɔ ene. "
ENGLISH: After stating that "the Word became flesh, " as quoted above, the apostle John continued: "We had a view of his glory, a glory such as belongs to an only-begotten son from a father. "

EWE: (Yohanes 1:14) Yohanes gaŋlɔ hã be: "Yesu Kristoe nye Mawu ƒe Vi la. "​ 1 Yohanes 4:15.
ENGLISH: (John 1:​14) John also wrote: "Jesus is God’s Son. "​ 1 John 4:​15.

EWE: Mawu ƒe nɔnɔmewo le Nya la si.
ENGLISH: The Word possesses godlike attributes.

EWE: "Nya la nye mawu aɖe. "
ENGLISH: "The Word was a god, " or "was divine. "

EWE: (Yohanes 1:1) Yesu "ɖe Mawu ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe fia eye wònye eƒe amenyenye ƒe nɔnɔme pɛpɛpɛ. "​ Hebritɔwo 1:2, 3.
ENGLISH: (John 1:1; An American Translation) Jesus is "the reflection of God’s glory and the exact representation of his very being. "​ Hebrews 1:​2, 3.

EWE: Nya la nye fia.
ENGLISH: The Word rules as a king.

EWE: Biblia gblɔ be "fiakuku geɖewo le ta " na Mawu ƒe Nya la.
ENGLISH: The Bible states that on the head of the Word of God are "many royal headbands. "

EWE: (Nyaɖeɖefia 19:12, 13) Wogayɔ Nya la be "fiawo dzi Fia kple aƒetɔwo dzi Aƒetɔ. "
