ENGLISH: Stress is your body’s response to a demanding situation.

EWE: Wò ahɔhɔ̃ nana lãmetsi aɖewo dzina ɖe lãme na wò.
ENGLISH: Your brain causes hormones to flood your system.

EWE: Esia wɔnɛ be wò dzi ƒona kabakaba, wò ʋu sina kabakaba, wò dzitodzito vuna alo mĩana eye wò lãmekawo liana.
ENGLISH: These increase your heart rate, regulate your blood pressure, expand or constrict the capacity of your lungs, and tense your muscles.

EWE: Kaka nànya la, ametia le klalo anɔ te ɖe nɔnɔmea nu.
ENGLISH: Before you are fully aware of what is happening, your body is primed for action.

EWE: Ne nu si he nuteɖeamedzia vɛ nu yi ko la, wò ametia gawɔa dɔ ale si dze.
ENGLISH: When a stressful episode is over, your body comes off "high alert " and returns to normal.

EWE: NUTEÐEAMEDZI ATE ŊU AÐE VI ALO AGBLẼ NU
ENGLISH: GOOD AND BAD STRESS

EWE: Nuteɖeamedzi nye mɔ aɖe si dzi ame tona nɔa te ɖe nɔnɔme sesẽwo alo afɔkuwo nu le dzɔdzɔmenu.
ENGLISH: Stress is a natural response that enables you to deal with challenging or dangerous situations.

EWE: Tenɔnɔ ɖe nɔnɔmea nu dzea egɔme tso ahɔhɔ̃a me.
ENGLISH: The stress response begins in your brain.

EWE: Nuteɖeamedzi si ɖea vi la ana nawɔ nu kpata.
ENGLISH: Beneficial stress enables you to act or react quickly.

EWE: Nuteɖeamedzi si megbɔ eme o ate ŋu ana nàɖo wò taɖodzinuwo gbɔ alo ana nàwɔ dɔ nyuie, ɖewohĩ le dodokpɔ me, ne èle dɔ dim, alo le kamedefefe aɖe me.
ENGLISH: A certain amount of stress can also help you to reach your goals or to perform better, perhaps during an exam, a job interview, or a sporting event.

EWE: Ke hã, ne nu te ɖe dziwò eteƒe didi, alo wògbɔ eme la, ate ŋu agblẽ nu le ŋuwò.
ENGLISH: However, prolonged, extreme, or chronic stress can harm you.

EWE: Ne ètsia dzodzodzoe edziedzi la, ate ŋu agblẽ nu le wò ametia, wò seselelãme kple wò susu ŋu.
ENGLISH: When your body is repeatedly or constantly on "high alert, " you may begin to suffer physically, emotionally, and mentally.

EWE: Wò nɔnɔme kple ale si nèwɔa nu ɖe amewo ŋu ate ŋu atrɔ.
ENGLISH: Your behavior, including the way you treat others, may change.

EWE: Nuteɖeamedzi si nu sẽ ate ŋu ana ame natsɔ aha nono, atike vɔ̃ɖiwo zazã kple nuwɔna gbegblẽ bubuwo aɖo dɔe be yeatsɔ anɔ te ɖe enu.
ENGLISH: Chronic stress can also lead to substance abuse and other unhealthy means of coping.

EWE: Ate ŋu ana ame nalé blanuiléledɔ, nu nati kɔ na ame, alo wòana ame nadi be yeawu ye ɖokui gɔ̃ hã.
ENGLISH: It may even spiral into depression, burnout, or thoughts of suicide.

EWE: Togbɔ be ame sia ame kple ale si wòwɔa nui ne nu te ɖe edzi hã la, nuteɖeamedzi ate ŋu ahe dɔléle vovovowo ava ame dzi.
ENGLISH: While stress may not affect everyone in the same way, it can contribute to a wide range of diseases.

EWE: Eye ate ŋu akpɔ ŋusẽ ɖe ametia ƒe akpa sia akpa kloe dzi.
ENGLISH: And it can affect nearly every part of the body.

EWE: ŊUSẼ SI NUTEÐEAMEDZI ATE ŊU AKPƆ ÐE WÒ AMETIA DZI
ENGLISH: HOW STRESS CAN AFFECT YOUR BODY

EWE: Ahɔhɔ̃mekawo ƒe dɔwɔwɔ.
ENGLISH: Nervous system.

EWE: Ŋutsu aɖe ɖo asi ŋgonu, le nuteɖeamedzi ta.
ENGLISH: A man, holding his hand to his forehead, feeling the effects of stress.

EWE: Wò ahɔhɔ̃mekawo nana wò ametia dzia lãmetsiwo abe adrenaline kple cortisol ene.
ENGLISH: Your nervous system causes hormones such as adrenaline and cortisol to be released.

EWE: Esia nana wò dzi ƒona kabakaba, wò ʋu sina kabakaba, eye sukli si le wò ʋu me hã dzina ɖe edzi nu siawo katã kpena ɖe ametia ŋu wòɖea afɔ kaba ne afɔku gbɔna.
ENGLISH: These increase your heart rate, your blood pressure, and the glucose levels in your blood​ all of which enable you to respond quickly to danger.

EWE: Gake nuteɖeamedzi si gbɔ eme ate ŋu ahe
ENGLISH: Too much stress can lead to

EWE: dzikudodo, dzimaɖitsitsi, blanuiléledɔ, taɖuame kple alɔ̃madɔmadɔ vɛ
ENGLISH: irritability, anxiety, depression, headaches, insomnia

EWE: Lãmekawo kple ƒuwo.
ENGLISH: Musculoskeletal system.

EWE: Wò lãmekawo liana ale be woakpɔ tawò be nu vevi nagawɔ wò o.
ENGLISH: Your muscles tense up to protect you from injury.

EWE: Gake nuteɖeamedzi si gbɔ eme ate ŋu ahe
ENGLISH: Too much stress can lead to

EWE: lãmevee, taɖuame kple vevesese le lãmekawo me vɛ
ENGLISH: body aches and pains, tension headaches, muscle spasms

EWE: Dzitodzito ƒe dɔwɔwɔ.
ENGLISH: Respiratory system.

EWE: Dzitodzito ƒe dɔwɔwɔ kabakaba nana ame gbɔna ɔksidzin-ya nyuie wu.
ENGLISH: You breathe faster to take in more oxygen.

EWE: Gake nuteɖeamedzi si gbɔ eme ate ŋu ana
ENGLISH: Too much stress can lead to

EWE: gbɔgbɔtsixe natsi ame ƒo alo gbɔgbɔ masu ame o, eye le ame aɖewo gome la, enana dzidzi ƒoa wo
ENGLISH: hyperventilation and shortness of breath, as well as panic attacks in those who are prone to them

EWE: Dzi kple ʋukawo ƒe dɔwɔwɔ.
ENGLISH: Cardiovascular system.

EWE: Wò dzi ƒona sesĩe kabakaba ale be ʋu nate ŋu asi le lãme na wò nyuie.
ENGLISH: Your heart beats faster and harder to distribute blood throughout your body.

EWE: Ʋukawo me vuna alo mĩana ale be ʋu nate ŋu asi ayi ametia ƒe akpa siwo hiãe wu, le kpɔɖeŋu me, ʋu sina yia lãkusiwo me ne ehiã le afi ma wu.
ENGLISH: Blood vessels dilate or constrict to direct blood where your body needs it the most, such as in your muscles.

EWE: Gake nuteɖeamedzi si gbɔ eme ate ŋu ahe
ENGLISH: Too much stress can lead to

EWE: ʋusɔgbɔdɔ, dzidɔ kple gbagbadɔ vɛ
ENGLISH: high blood pressure, heart attack, stroke

EWE: Lãmenu siwo wɔa lãmetsiwo ƒe dɔwɔwɔ.
ENGLISH: Endocrine system.

EWE: Wò lãmenu aɖewo wɔa lãmetsiwo abe adrenaline kple cortisol ene siwo kpena ɖe ametia ŋu wòtea ŋu nɔa te ɖe nuteɖeamedzi nu.
ENGLISH: Your glands produce the hormones adrenaline and cortisol, which help the body react to stress.

EWE: Wò aklã nana sukli si le wò ʋu me la dzina ɖe edzi be wòado ŋusẽ wò.
ENGLISH: Your liver increases your blood-sugar level to give you more energy.

EWE: Gake nuteɖeamedzi si gbɔ eme ate ŋu ana
ENGLISH: Too much stress can lead to

EWE: ame nalé suklidɔ, ŋusẽ maganɔ ametia ŋu wòawɔ avu kple dɔlékuiwo o, si ana ame nànɔ dɔ dzem kabakaba, eƒe seselelãme nanɔ tɔtrɔm, eye wòava nɔ lolom fũu akpa
ENGLISH: diabetes, lower immunity and increased illness, mood swings, weight gain

EWE: Dɔgbo ƒe dɔwɔwɔ.
ENGLISH: Gastrointestinal system.

EWE: Nuteɖeamedzi ate ŋu ana wò dɔgbo ƒe dɔwɔwɔ me natɔtɔ.
ENGLISH: The way your body processes food is disrupted.

EWE: Nuteɖeamedzi si gbɔ eme ate ŋu ana
ENGLISH: Too much stress can lead to

EWE: dzigbɔ nanɔ ame tsɔm, ame nanɔ xe ɖem, ame nanɔ mitsi nyem alo ame mate ŋu anɔ afɔdzi dem o
ENGLISH: nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation

EWE: Vidzidzi ŋutete.
ENGLISH: Reproductive system.

EWE: Nuteɖeamedzi ate ŋu ana gbɔdɔdɔ ƒe dzodzro kple ŋutete nu naɖiɖi.
ENGLISH: Stress can affect sexual desire and function.

EWE: Nuteɖeamedzi si gbɔ eme ate ŋu ana
ENGLISH: Too much stress can lead to

EWE: ame nagbɔdzɔ le ŋutsu me, eye nyɔnu ƒe asiɖoɖoanyi me natɔtɔ
ENGLISH: impotence, disrupted menstrual cycle

EWE: Ale Si Nàwɔ Anɔ Te Ðe Nuteɖeamedzi Nu
ENGLISH: How to Deal With Stress

EWE: Be nàte ŋu anɔ te ɖe nuteɖeamedzi nu dzidzedzetɔe la, ele be nàbu wò lãmesẽ, ale si nèwɔa nu kple ame bubuwo, wò taɖodzinuwo kple nu siwo nètsɔ ɖoa nɔƒe gbãtɔ, siwo nye nu siwo le vevie na wò wu le agbe me la ŋu.
ENGLISH: To deal effectively with stress, you need to think about your physical health, the way you interact with others, and your goals and priorities in life​ that is, what you consider to be truly important.

EWE: Nyati sia aƒo nu tso mɔfiame ŋutɔŋutɔ siwo ate ŋu akpe ɖe ŋuwò be nànɔ te ɖe nuteɖeamedzi nu nyuie wu eye be nàɖe edzi akpɔtɔ gɔ̃ hã la ŋu.
ENGLISH: This article will review some practical principles that can help you to deal better with stress and perhaps even reduce it.

EWE: Bu Ŋkeke Ðe Sia Ðe Ko Ƒe Hiahiãwo Ŋu
ENGLISH: Try to Live One Day at a Time

EWE: Nyɔnu aɖe le dzidzɔ kpɔm eye dzi le eƒo le dugã aɖe me
ENGLISH: A happy and confident woman walking in a big city.

EWE: "Migatsi dzimaɖi gbeɖe le etsɔ si gbɔna ŋu o, elabena etsɔ si gbɔna la kple eya ŋutɔ ƒe dzimaɖitsitsiwoe. "​ MATEO 6:34.
ENGLISH: "Never be anxious about the next day, for the next day will have its own anxieties. "​ MATTHEW 6:34.

EWE: Nu si wòfia: Gbe sia gbe dzimaɖitsitsi nye agbea ƒe akpa aɖe.
ENGLISH: Meaning: Daily anxieties are a part of life.

EWE: Gake mègatsɔ etsɔ ƒe dzimaɖitsitsiwo kpe ɖe egbe tɔwo ŋu o.
ENGLISH: But do not increase today’s anxieties by adding tomorrow’s to them.

EWE: Bu ŋkeke ɖe sia ɖe ko ƒe hiahiãwo ŋu.
ENGLISH: Try to live one day at a time.

EWE: Nuteɖeamedzi ate ŋu ana ame natsi dzimaɖi.
ENGLISH: Stress can cause anxiety.

EWE: Eya ta te esia kpɔ: Gbã la, se egɔme be màte ŋu aƒo asa na nuteɖeamedzi aɖewo ya o.
ENGLISH: So try this: First, recognize that some stress is inevitable.

EWE: Ðeko dzitsitsi ɖe nu siwo ŋu màte ŋu awɔ naneke le o la, adzi wò nuteɖeamedzia ɖe edzi.
ENGLISH: Fretting over things you cannot prevent increases your stress.

EWE: Evelia, zi geɖe la nu siwo ŋu míetsia dzi ɖo la, medzɔna ŋutɔŋutɔ o.
ENGLISH: Second, understand that quite often things do not turn out the way we may fear they will.

EWE: Ðo Taɖodzinu Siwo Le Bɔbɔe
ENGLISH: Set Reasonable Standards

EWE: "Nunya si tso dziƒo la, . . . esea nu gɔme. "​ YAKOBO 3:17.
ENGLISH: "The wisdom from above is . . . reasonable. "​ JAMES 3:17.

EWE: Nu si wòfia: Mèganye ame si dia blibodede o.
ENGLISH: Meaning: Do not be a perfectionist.

EWE: Mègaɖo taɖodzinu siwo gbɔ manya ɖo na wò ŋutɔ alo ame bubuwo o.
ENGLISH: Avoid setting unrealistically high standards for yourself or others.

EWE: Da sɔ, ɖo taɖodzinu siwo le bɔbɔe, nya afi si wò ŋutɔ kple ame bubuwo sia ƒe ŋutetewo se ɖo.
ENGLISH: Be modest, set reasonable standards, and know both your limitations and those of others.

EWE: Ne èwɔ esiawo la, ke àɖe nuteɖeamedzi dzi akpɔtɔ eye nu nyuiwo ado tso eme.
ENGLISH: When you do this, you will reduce stress all around and even encourage greater success.

EWE: Azɔ hã, tsɔ nanewo wɔ nukokoe.
ENGLISH: Also, keep a sense of humor.

EWE: Ne nanewo meyi edzi nyuie o gɔ̃ hã gake nètsɔe wɔ nukokoe la, ana nàɖe nuteɖeamedzia dzi akpɔtɔ eye wòana wò dzi nadze eme.
ENGLISH: When you laugh​ even when something goes wrong ​you relieve tension and brighten your mood.

EWE: Nya Nu Siwo Nana Nu Tena Ðe Dziwò
ENGLISH: Know What Stresses You

EWE: "Nugɔmesela gbɔa dzi ɖi blewu. " LODODOWO 17:27.
ENGLISH: "A discerning man will remain calm. "​ PROVERBS 17:27.

EWE: Nu si wòfia: Seselelãme gbegblẽwo ate ŋu akpɔ ŋusẽ ɖe ale si nèbua nuwoe dzi, eya ta gbɔ dzi ɖi blewu.
ENGLISH: Meaning: Negative emotions can cloud clear thinking, so try to stay calm.

EWE: De dzesi nu siwo nana nu tena ɖe dziwò kple ale si nèwɔa nui.
ENGLISH: Identify what stresses you, and note your response.

EWE: Le kpɔɖeŋu me, ne nu te ɖe dziwò la, de dzesi wò nuŋububuwo, seselelãmewo kple nuwɔnawo, eye àte ŋu aŋlɔ wo ɖi gɔ̃ hã.
ENGLISH: For example, when you feel stressed, note your thoughts, feelings, and behavior, perhaps even making a record of them.

EWE: Ne èva nya ale si nèwɔa nui ne nu te ɖe dziwò la, ate ŋu akpe ɖe ŋuwò be nànɔ te ɖe nuteɖeamedzia nu nyuie wu.
ENGLISH: By becoming more aware of your response to stress, you may be able to deal with it more effectively.

EWE: Azɔ hã, de ŋugble tso mɔ siwo dzi nàto aɖe nu siwo nana nu tena ɖe dziwò le agbe me la ɖa kura.
ENGLISH: Also, think of ways to eliminate stressful things from your life.

EWE: Ne manyawɔ be nàɖe wo ɖa o la, di mɔ siwo dzi nàto anɔ te ɖe wo nu, ɖewohĩ anyo be nàwɔ ɖoɖo ɖe wò dɔwo alo wò ɣeyiɣi ŋu nyuie.
ENGLISH: If that is unrealistic, look for ways to reduce their impact, perhaps by managing your tasks or time more efficiently.

EWE: Trɔ ale si nèbua nuwo ŋui.
ENGLISH: Try to see things in a different light.

EWE: Nu siwo nana nu tena ɖe dziwò la, mana nu nate ɖe ame bubu dzi o.
ENGLISH: What stresses you may not stress someone else.

EWE: Esia ate ŋu atso ale si nèbua nuwoe gbɔ.
ENGLISH: The difference may be in viewpoint.

EWE: Bu aɖaŋuɖoɖo etɔ̃ siawo ŋu kpɔ:
ENGLISH: Consider these three suggestions:

EWE: Mèganɔ susu vɔ̃wo bum ɖe amewo ŋu kabakaba o.
ENGLISH: Do not be quick to assume bad motives.

EWE: Ame aɖe ate ŋu ava tso ŋgɔ na wò le fli me.
ENGLISH: A person may cut ahead of you in a line.

EWE: Ne èbu eƒe nuwɔnaa be enye ameŋumabumabu la, ana wò dzi naho.
ENGLISH: If you attribute his act to rudeness, you may become upset.

EWE: Ðe ema teƒe la, nu ka tae màbui be susu nyui aɖe tae wòwɔe ɖo o?
ENGLISH: Instead, why not assume that his motive was good?

EWE: Anɔ eme hã be susu nyui aɖe tae!
ENGLISH: You may be right!

EWE: Susu nyui nenɔ asiwò ɖe nɔnɔmea ŋu.
ENGLISH: See the positive side of a situation.

EWE: Ne èle lalam be yeakpɔ ɖɔkta alo le yameʋudzeƒe ɣeyiɣi didi aɖe la, anɔ bɔbɔe be nàdo dzi alala ne èzã ɣeyiɣi ma tsɔ xlẽ nane, awɔ ɖoɖo ɖe dɔ ŋu alo atsɔ axlẽ wò e-mailwo.
ENGLISH: A long wait at a doctor’s office or an airport is easier to bear if you use the time to do some reading or to catch up on work or e-mail.

EWE: Kpɔ nu yi ŋgɔe.
ENGLISH: Keep the big picture in mind.

EWE: Bia ɖokuiwò be, ‘Ðe kuxi sia ava do ga ɖe edzi le ŋkeke aɖewo megbea?’
ENGLISH: Ask yourself, ‘Will this problem be a big issue tomorrow or next week?’

EWE: De dzesi kuxi siwo nye sueawo alo esiwo anɔ anyi ɣeyiɣi kpuie aɖe kple esiwo nye ŋkubiãnyawo.
ENGLISH: Distinguish between minor or short-term issues and more serious ones.

EWE: Na Wò Nuwo Nanɔ Ðoɖo Nu
ENGLISH: Try to Be Orderly

EWE: Nyɔnu aɖe lé fon ɖe asi, eye wòle ɖoɖo wɔm ɖe ŋkekea ŋu.
ENGLISH: A woman holding her smartphone, using a daily planning application.

EWE: "Mina nuwo katã nayi edzi nyuie ɖe ɖoɖo nu. " 1 KORINTOTƆWO 14:40.
ENGLISH: "Let all things take place decently and by arrangement. "​ 1 CORINTHIANS 14:40.

EWE: Nu si wòfia: Dze agbagba nàna wò nuwo nanɔ ɖoɖo nu.
ENGLISH: Meaning: Try to maintain order in your life.

EWE: Edzɔa dzi na mí ne nuwo le ɖoɖo nu.
ENGLISH: We like a reasonable amount of order in life.

EWE: Nu ɖeka aɖe si ate ŋu ana nuwo manɔ ɖoɖo nu o, eye wòana nu nate ɖe mía dzi ye nye ne míehea megbelele, esia awɔe be dɔ nali kɔ ɖe mía dzi.
ENGLISH: One thing that can contribute to disorder​ and stress ​is procrastination, and this may lead to a growing list of unfinished tasks.

EWE: Ðe manyo be nàte aɖaŋuɖoɖo eve siawo kpɔ oa?
ENGLISH: Why not try these two suggestions?

EWE: Wɔ ɖoɖo aɖe koŋ eye nàzɔ ɖe edzi.
ENGLISH: Make a practical schedule, and stick to it.

EWE: De dzesi nu siwo nana nèhea megbelele eye nàwɔ nane tso wo ŋu.
ENGLISH: Identify and correct any attitudes that cause you to procrastinate.

EWE: Da Sɔ Le Agbe Me
ENGLISH: Pursue a Balanced Lifestyle

EWE: "Gbɔɖeme asiʋlo ɖeka nyo wu dɔ sesẽ wɔwɔ kple dagbadagba ɖe yame asiʋlo eve. " NYAGBLƆLA 4:6.
ENGLISH: "Better is a handful of rest than two handfuls of hard work and chasing after the wind. "​ ECCLESIASTES 4:6.

EWE: Nu si wòfia: Ame siwo vuna ɖe dɔ ŋu fũu la, mekpɔa viɖe aɖeke tsoa woƒe "dɔ sesẽ wɔwɔ . . . asiʋlo eve " la me o.
ENGLISH: Meaning: Workaholics can deprive themselves of the benefits of their "two handfuls of hard work. "

EWE: Edzɔna be ɣeyiɣi alo lãmesẽ gɔ̃ hã meva nɔa wo si be woase vivi na nu si ŋu wokpe fu ɖo o.
ENGLISH: They may have no time or energy left to enjoy what they worked for.

EWE: Susu nyui nenɔ asiwò ɖe dɔ kple ga ŋu.
ENGLISH: Have a realistic view of work and money.

EWE: Ne ga geɖe le ame si la, mefia be akpɔ dzidzɔ geɖe alo nu mate ɖe edzi o.
ENGLISH: More money does not mean more happiness or less stress.

EWE: Le nyateƒe me la, ate ŋu ana ame makpɔ dzidzɔ o eye nu nate ɖe edzi boŋ.
ENGLISH: In fact, the opposite can be true.

EWE: Nyagblɔla 5:12 gblɔ be: "Nu gbogbo siwo le kesinɔtɔ si la menana wòdɔa alɔ̃ o. "
ENGLISH: "The plenty belonging to the rich one does not permit him to sleep, " says Ecclesiastes 5:12.

EWE: Eya ta nɔ agbe ɖe nu si le asiwò la nu.
ENGLISH: So try to live within your means.

EWE: Di ɣeyiɣi nàɖi ɖe eme.
ENGLISH: Make time to relax.

EWE: Ne èwɔa nu siwo doa dzidzɔ na wò la, àɖe nuteɖeamedzi dzi akpɔtɔ.
ENGLISH: You relieve stress when you do things you enjoy.

EWE: Ke hã, modzaka siwo nànɔ anyi ko aɖe, abe Television kpɔkpɔ ene made dziwò o.
ENGLISH: However, passive recreation, such as watching TV, may not help.

EWE: Zã mɔɖaŋunuwo nyuie.
ENGLISH: Keep technology in its place.

EWE: Ƒo asa na e-mail, text message kple internet dzi hahoo kadodowo zazã edziedzi.
ENGLISH: Avoid constantly checking e-mail, texts, or social media sites.

EWE: Mèganɔ e-mail siwo ku ɖe dɔ ŋu xlẽm ne mèle dɔ me o, negbe ɖe wòhiã vevie ko hafi.
ENGLISH: Unless circumstances require it, do not check work-related e-mail outside of working hours.

EWE: Kpɔ Wò Lãmesẽ Ta
ENGLISH: Take Care of Your Health

EWE: Ðekakpui aɖe le du ƒum eye wòle nu kom.
ENGLISH: A young man smiling as he is running outdoors.

EWE: "Ŋutilãmamla nyo. " 1 TIMOTEO 4:8.
ENGLISH: "Physical training is beneficial. "​ 1 TIMOTHY 4:8.

EWE: Nu si wòfia: Kamedede edziedzi nana míenɔa lãmesẽ me.
ENGLISH: Meaning: Regular exercise promotes better health.

EWE: Wɔ nu siwo ade wò lãmesẽ dzi.
ENGLISH: Develop healthful habits.

EWE: Kamedede ate ŋu ade wo lãmesẽ dzi eye wòana wò ametia nanɔ te ɖe nuteɖeamedzi nu.
ENGLISH: Physical activity can lift your mood and improve your body’s response to stress.

EWE: Ðu nu siwo me nunyiame le, eye nànɔ nu ɖum ɖe ɖoɖo nu.
ENGLISH: Eat nutritious food, and try to avoid skipping meals.

EWE: Dze agbagba nàɖi ɖe eme wòasu wò.
ENGLISH: Be sure to get enough rest.

ENGLISH: Yet, it promotes a healthful course of life.

EWE: Bu Biblia ƒe mɔfiame aɖewo siwo akpe ɖe ŋuwò be nànɔ lãmesẽ me la ŋu kpɔ.
ENGLISH: Consider some Bible principles that can improve your life physically.

EWE: LÉ BE NA WÒ AMETIA
ENGLISH: TAKE CARE OF YOUR BODY

EWE: BIBLIA ƑE MƆFIAME: "Ame aɖeke melé fu eya ŋutɔ ƒe ŋutilã kpɔ o, ke boŋ enyinɛ, eye wòléa be nɛ nyuie. " Efesotɔwo 5:29.
ENGLISH: BIBLE PRINCIPLE: "No man ever hated his own body, but he feeds and cherishes it. "​ Ephesians 5:29.

EWE: NU SI WÒFIA: Biblia ƒe mɔfiame sia de dzi ƒo na mí be míawɔ mía tɔ sinua alé be na mía ɖokui.
ENGLISH: WHAT IT MEANS: This Bible principle encourages us to do what we can to care for our physical health.

EWE: Numekuku aɖe ɖee fia be ale si ame akpa gãtɔ nɔa gbee gbɔe lãmesẽkuxi geɖewo tsona.
ENGLISH: One study shows that many health problems are related to personal lifestyle choices.

EWE: Eya ta ale si nènɔa agbee la ate ŋu ana nànɔ lãmesẽ nyuie me.
ENGLISH: Hence, making the right personal choices can lead to better health.

EWE: NU SI NÀTE ŊU AWƆ:
ENGLISH: WHAT YOU CAN DO:

EWE: Ðu Nu Si Me Nunyiame Le.
ENGLISH: Nutrition.

EWE: Ðu nu siwo me nunyiame le eye nànɔ tsi nom sɔ gbɔ.
ENGLISH: Take charge of your nutrition by eating healthful foods and drinking enough water.

EWE: Nɔ Kame Dem.
ENGLISH: Stay Active.

EWE: Ƒe ka kee nèɖaxɔ o, èɖanye nuwɔametɔ alo dɔléle sesẽ aɖe le ŋuwò o, kamedede ana nànɔ lãmesẽ me.
ENGLISH: Physical activity can improve your health regardless of your age, even if you are disabled or limited by chronic illness.

EWE: Togbɔ be ame siwo lɔ̃ wò kple ɖɔktawo aɖo aɖaŋu nyuiwo na wò hã la, wò ŋutɔe awɔ edzi be wòaɖe vi na wò!
ENGLISH: While loved ones and health practitioners can assist you with your exercise program, only you can make it work!

EWE: Dɔ Alɔ̃ Wòasu Wò.
ENGLISH: Get Enough Sleep.

EWE: Ne mèdɔa alɔ̃ wòsua wò o la, ate ŋu ana nàva dze dɔ vevie emegbe.
ENGLISH: Prolonged sleep deprivation is associated with risks for serious illnesses.

EWE: Ame aɖewo tsɔa nu geɖe doa agba na wo ɖokuiwo le alɔ̃dɔɣiwo.
ENGLISH: As a result of the choices they make, many people do not get enough sleep.

EWE: Ke hã ne ètiae be yeadɔ alɔ̃ wòasu ye nyuie la, ànɔ lãmesẽ me.
ENGLISH: Yet, by choosing to sleep enough, you choose to live better.

EWE: TSRI NUMAME GBEGBLẼWO
ENGLISH: AVOID HARMFUL HABITS

EWE: BIBLIA ƑE MƆFIAME: "Mina míakɔ mía ɖokui ŋu tso ŋutilã kple gbɔgbɔ ƒe ɖiƒoƒo sia ɖiƒoƒo me. " 2 Korintotɔwo 7:1.
ENGLISH: BIBLE PRINCIPLE: "Let us cleanse ourselves of every defilement of flesh and spirit. "​ 2 Corinthians 7:1.

EWE: NU SI WÒFIA: Eɖea vi na mí ŋutɔ ne míetsri nu siwo gblẽa nu le mía ŋu abe atama kple nu bubu siwo nye nu siwo koŋ gblẽa nu le míaƒe lãmesẽ ŋu eye wohea ku vɛ.
ENGLISH: WHAT IT MEANS: We benefit from not polluting our bodies with harmful substances such as tobacco products, which are known to be a major cause of disease and death.

EWE: NU SI NÀTE ŊU AWƆ: Ðo ɣeyiɣi si nàdzudzɔ keŋkeŋ eye nàde dzesii ɖi.
ENGLISH: WHAT YOU CAN DO: Set a date to quit, and mark it on your calendar.

EWE: Hafi ŋkeke ma naɖo la, tsɔ sigaretwo, dzowɔgbawo, dzosinuwo kple nu bubu siwo do ƒome kplii la ƒu gbe.
ENGLISH: Just before that day, dispose of cigarettes, ashtrays, lighters, and other paraphernalia associated with this harmful habit.

EWE: Mèganɔ teƒe siwo amewo aƒoe ɖe nuwò be nàƒo ɖokuiwò ɖe nuwɔna siawo me yim o.
ENGLISH: Avoid places where others engage in habits like this.

EWE: Gblɔ ale si nètso nya mee na xɔlɔ̃ siwo di be nàtrɔ ne woakpe ɖe ŋuwò.
ENGLISH: Tell supporting friends about your decision.

EWE: BIBLIA ƑE MƆFIAME BUBUWO
ENGLISH: OTHER BIBLE PRINCIPLES

EWE: Ŋutsu aɖe le Biblia xlẽm
ENGLISH: A man reads the Bible

EWE: Bia Yehowa Ðasefo siwo le miaƒe nutoa me dometɔ aɖe ne wòana Biblia ɖeka wò
ENGLISH: You may obtain a printed copy of the Bible by contacting one of Jehovah’s Witnesses in your community

EWE: WƆ NU SIWO ANA NÀNƆ DEDIE.
ENGLISH: BE SAFETY CONSCIOUS.

EWE: "Ne ètso aƒe yeye la, tɔ kpɔ ɖe xɔa tame, bena ame aɖeke magage le edzi, eye nàna wò aƒe naɖi ʋufɔ o. " 5 MOSE 22:8.
ENGLISH: "If you build a new house, you must also make a parapet for your roof, so that you may not bring bloodguilt on your house because of someone falling from it. "​ DEUTERONOMY 22:8.

EWE: ÐU WÒ DZIKU DZI.
ENGLISH: CONTROL YOUR ANGER.

EWE: "Ame si medoa dziku kabakaba o la, nugɔmesese bɔ ɖe esi, ke ame si megbɔa dzi ɖi o la ɖea eƒe bometsitsi fiana. " LODODOWO 14:29.
ENGLISH: "The one who is slow to anger has great discernment, but the impatient one displays his foolishness. "​ PROVERBS 14:29.

EWE: TSRI NU TSU ÐUÐU.
ENGLISH: AVOID OVEREATING.

EWE: ‘Mèganɔ nu tsu ɖulawo dome o.’ LODODOWO 23:20.
ENGLISH: "Do not be . . . among those who gorge themselves. "​ PROVERBS 23:20.

EWE: Ƒomegbenɔnɔ Kple Xɔlɔ̃wo
ENGLISH: Family Life and Friendships

EWE: Esesẽna na ame geɖe be woadze xɔlɔ̃wo eye woana wo kpli wo dome navivi.
ENGLISH: Many find it daunting to maintain strong personal relationships.

EWE: Bu Biblia ƒe mɔfiame siwo ate ŋu akpe ɖe ŋuwò be nàna wò kple amewo dome navivi ŋu kpɔ.
ENGLISH: Consider some Bible principles that can help you improve your life socially.

EWE: MÈGADI ÐOKUIWÒ TƆ O
ENGLISH: BE UNSELFISH

EWE: BIBLIA ƑE MƆFIAME: ‘Miganɔ miawo ŋutɔ miaƒe nyonyo ko dim o, ke midi ame bubuwo hã ƒe nyonyo.’ Filipitɔwo 2:4.
ENGLISH: BIBLE PRINCIPLE: "Look out not only for your own interests, but also for the interests of others. "​ Philippians 2:4.

EWE: NU SI WÒFIA: Mía kple amewo dome anyo ɖe edzi wu ne míenana míaƒe susu nɔa nu si míate ŋu awɔ na wo, tsɔ wu nu si woawɔ na mí ŋu.
ENGLISH: WHAT IT MEANS: Successful relationships are more about giving than about receiving.

EWE: Ne ɖokuiwò tɔ ko nèdina la, wò kple amewo dome agblẽ.
ENGLISH: If you follow a selfish course of life, you can damage your relationships with others.

EWE: Le kpɔɖeŋu me, ate ŋu adzɔ be srɔ̃tɔ si dia eɖokuitɔ la, mawɔ nuteƒe na srɔ̃a o.
ENGLISH: For example, a selfish marriage mate may be disloyal to his or her partner.

EWE: Azɔ hã, ame aɖeke medina be yeadze xɔ̃ ame si dana le nu siwo le esi ta alo le nu si wònya ta o.
ENGLISH: Additionally, nobody wants to make friends with a person who always boasts about what he owns or knows.

EWE: Agbalẽ aɖe (The Road to Character) gblɔ be, "ame siwo dia wo ɖokui ɖeɖe ko tɔ la va toa kuxi vovovowo me. "
ENGLISH: Thus, as the book The Road to Character says, "self-centeredness leads in several unfortunate directions. "

EWE: NU SI NÀTE ŊU AWƆ:
ENGLISH: WHAT YOU CAN DO:

EWE: Kpe ɖe amewo ŋu.
ENGLISH: Help others.

EWE: Kakaɖedzi kple ɖokuitsɔtsɔna ye nana xɔlɔ̃wo dome sẽna ɖe edzi.
ENGLISH: Strong friendships stem from a sense of commitment and trust.

EWE: Numekuku aɖe ɖee fia be ame siwo kpena ɖe amewo ŋu la meléa blanuiléledɔ kaba o, eye enana amewo dea bubu wo ŋu.
ENGLISH: Some studies indicate that people who help others suffer less from depression and boost their own self-esteem.

EWE: Se veve ɖe amewo nu.
ENGLISH: Show empathy.

EWE: Woɖe veveseɖeamenu gɔme be enye vevesese si sem ame bubu le la sese le wò dzi me.
ENGLISH: Empathy has been described as feeling another person’s pain in your heart.

EWE: Ne èsea veve ɖe ame nu la, awɔe be mànɔ hatsekanya siwo tɔa ame gblɔm ɖe amewo ŋu be wòave wo o.
ENGLISH: If you show empathy, you will be less likely to use biting sarcasm, that is, sharp and often ironic expressions intended to hurt the feelings of another person.

EWE: Ne èsea veve ɖe amewo nu la, màna woƒe nuwɔnawo nanɔ fu ɖem na wò o.
ENGLISH: When you show empathy, you also become tolerant of others.

EWE: Veveseseɖeamenu akpe ɖe ŋuwò be màbu nazã ɖe amewo ŋu o, azɔ hã, àdze xɔlɔ̃ ame siwo tso dukɔ kple teƒe vovovowo faa.
ENGLISH: Thus, empathy can help you to avoid being prejudiced and also to make friends from different cultures or backgrounds.

EWE: Kpɔ vovo ɖe amewo ŋu.
ENGLISH: Give of your time.

EWE: Ne èkpɔa vovo ɖe amewo ŋu la, awɔe be nànya wo nyuie wu.
ENGLISH: The more time you spend with others, the better you will get to know them.

EWE: Ahiã be nàɖo dze tuameɖowo kple amewo, esia awɔe be nàte ŋu adze xɔ̃ wo.
ENGLISH: You need to have meaningful conversations with others to make real friends.

EWE: Eya ta nye toɖola nyui.
ENGLISH: So be a good listener.

EWE: Ðee fia xɔ̃wòa be yetsɔ ɖe le eme nɛ.
ENGLISH: Show interest in your friends’ concerns.

EWE: Numekuku aɖe si wowɔ nyitsɔ laa gblɔ be "dze tuameɖowo ɖoɖo kple amewo nana wokpɔa dzidzɔ. "
ENGLISH: A recent study states that "deep conversations may actually make people happier. "

EWE: TIA WÒ ZƆHƐWO LE NUNYA ME
ENGLISH: CHOOSE FRIENDSHIPS WISELY

EWE: BIBLIA ƑE MƆFIAME: "Hadede vɔ̃wo gblẽa nɔnɔme nyuiwo. " 1 Korintotɔwo 15:33.
ENGLISH: BIBLE PRINCIPLE: "Bad associations corrupt good morals. "​ 1 Corinthians 15:33, footnote.

EWE: NU SI WÒFIA: Ame siwo nèdea ha kplii la ate ŋu akpɔ ŋusẽ nyui alo ŋusẽ gbegblẽ ɖe dziwò.
ENGLISH: WHAT IT MEANS: The people you spend time with have a great influence on you​ for good or for bad.

EWE: Ame siwo srɔ̃a nu tso amegbetɔwo ƒe nɔnɔmewo ŋu lɔ̃ ɖe edzi be ame siwo míedea ha kplii la kpɔa ŋusẽ gã ɖe mía dzi.
ENGLISH: Sociologists agree that such influence can affect your life.

EWE: Akpatɔgbɔnɔla mesea akpa dzena o, le kpɔɖeŋu me, ne èdea ha kple ame siwo noa sigaret alo ame siwo gbea wo srɔ̃wo la, wò hã adze sigaret yɔyɔ alo àdi be yeagbe ye srɔ̃.
ENGLISH: For example, they say that if you surround yourself with people who smoke or who are getting divorced, you may be more likely to start smoking or to want a divorce.

EWE: NU SI NÀTE ŊU AWƆ: Dze xɔ̃ ame siwo dea asixɔxɔ nu siwo ŋu nèdea asixɔxɔe siwo ɖea nɔnɔme siwo dzea ŋuwò fiana alo nàdi be yeasrɔ̃ la.
ENGLISH: WHAT YOU CAN DO: Make friends with people who display qualities and have values you admire or want to imitate.

EWE: Le kpɔɖeŋu me, dze xɔ̃ ame siwo ɖɔa ŋu ɖo, dea bubu ame ŋu, nye dɔmenyolawo kple amedzrowɔlawo.
ENGLISH: For instance, seek association with people who are tactful, respectful, generous, and hospitable.

EWE: BIBLIA ƑE MƆFIAME BUBUWO
ENGLISH: OTHER BIBLE PRINCIPLES

EWE: Nyɔnu aɖe le Biblia me video aɖe ɖem na nyɔnuvi sue aɖe
ENGLISH: A woman shows a little girl a Bible-based video

EWE: Srɔ̃tɔwo, sɔhɛwo kple ɖeviwo ate ŋu akpɔ video siwo wotu ɖe Biblia dzi be wòakpe ɖe wo ŋu le ƒomea me
ENGLISH: Watch Bible-based videos designed to help married couples, teenagers, and young children improve their family life

EWE: TSRI NYA TƆAMEWO GBƆGBLƆ.
ENGLISH: AVOID HURTFUL SPEECH.

EWE: "Nuƒoƒo eŋumabumabui le abe yitɔame ene. " LODODOWO 12:18.
ENGLISH: "Thoughtless speech is like the stabs of a sword. "​ PROVERBS 12:18.

EWE: NYO DƆME.
ENGLISH: BE GENEROUS.

EWE: "Eme anyo na dɔmenyotɔ. " LODODOWO 11:25.
ENGLISH: "The generous person will prosper. "​ PROVERBS 11:25.

EWE: WƆ NU ÐE AMEWO ŊU ABE ALE SI NÀDI BE WOAWƆ NA YE ENE.
ENGLISH: TREAT OTHERS AS YOU WANT TO BE TREATED.

EWE: "Nu sia nu si miedina be amewo nawɔ na mi la, miawo hã miwɔ nenema ke na wo. "
ENGLISH: "All things . . . that you want men to do to you, you also must do to them. "​ MATTHEW 7:12.

EWE: MATEO 7:12. Gazazã
ENGLISH: Financial Stability

EWE: Biblia ƒe mɔfiamewo le kpekpem ɖe ame geɖewo ŋu wole ga zãm nyuie wu.
ENGLISH: Many people have minimized their money problems by applying Bible principles.

EWE: WƆ ÐOÐO NYUI
ENGLISH: HAVE A GOOD PLAN

EWE: BIBLIA ƑE MƆFIAME: "Veviedola ƒe ɖoɖowo hea dzidzedzekpɔkpɔ vanɛ, ke ame sia ame si tsia klokloklo la, hiã atui. " Lododowo 21:5.
ENGLISH: BIBLE PRINCIPLE: "The plans of the diligent surely lead to success, but all who are hasty surely head for poverty. "​ Proverbs 21:5.

EWE: NU SI WÒFIA: Nu vevi si akpe ɖe ŋuwò nàkpɔ dzidzedzee nye be nàzɔ ɖe ɖoɖo siwo nèwɔ dzi.
ENGLISH: WHAT IT MEANS: Diligently sticking to your plans is an important key to success.

EWE: Eya ta wɔ ɖoɖo ɖe gazazã ŋu.
ENGLISH: Therefore, plan before spending.

EWE: Ðo ŋku edzi be menye nu sia nu si ŋu nèke ɖo koe nàƒle o.
ENGLISH: Remember, you likely cannot buy everything you want.

EWE: Eya ta zã ga le nunya me.
ENGLISH: Thus, spend your money wisely.

EWE: NU SI NÀTE ŊU AWƆ:
ENGLISH: WHAT YOU CAN DO:

EWE: Wɔ ɖoɖo eye nàzɔ ɖe edzi.
ENGLISH: Stick to a budget.

EWE: Ŋlɔ wò gazazãwo katã ɖi, eye nàma wo ɖe nu vovovoawo nu.
ENGLISH: Write down all your expenses, and put them in categories.

EWE: Eyome ma ga ɖe nuawo nu.
ENGLISH: Then allocate funds for each expense.

EWE: Ne èzã ga ɖe nanewo ŋu wu la, ɖee le ɖewo ŋu nàtsɔ aɖo ema teƒe.
ENGLISH: If you overspend in one category, take money from another to cover the difference.

EWE: Le kpɔɖeŋu me, ne èzã ga fũu ɖe mɔ̃memi ŋu la, ɖe gaa tso nu bubu siwo mele vevie tututu o abe awuƒlega ene ŋu nàtsɔ aɖo eteƒe.
ENGLISH: For example, if you spent more than you planned on automobile fuel, take money set aside for a less important purpose​ for example, dining out.

EWE: Ƒo asa na fenyinyi.
ENGLISH: Avoid unnecessary debt.

EWE: Dze agbagba ɖe sia ɖe nàtsri fenyinyi.
ENGLISH: To the extent possible, avoid going into debt.

EWE: Ðe ema teƒe la, dzra ga ɖo nàtsɔ aƒle nu siwo hiã wò la.
ENGLISH: Instead, save up to buy the items you need.

EWE: Ne èzãa agbananuƒlegbalẽvi la, dze agbagba nàxe ga siwo katã susɔ ɣleti sia ɣleti be màganɔ deme xem na wo o.
ENGLISH: If you use a credit card, try to pay off your balance in full each month to avoid paying interest.

EWE: Ne fe le ŋuwò la, wɔ ɖoɖo ɖe exexe ŋu eye nàzɔ ɖe edzi.
ENGLISH: If you are in debt, set up a repayment plan, and then stick to it.

EWE: Numekuku aɖe ɖee fia be ne amewo tsɔ agbananuƒlegbalẽvi le nu ƒlem la, woƒlea nu wògbɔa eme.
ENGLISH: One study suggests that when paying with a credit card, people are prone to spend more.

EWE: Eya ta ne agbananuƒlegbalẽvi le asiwò la, nya ale si nàzãe.
ENGLISH: So if you have a credit card, use it with restraint.

EWE: KPƆ NYUIE LE NUMAME GBEGBLẼWO ŊU
ENGLISH: BEWARE OF HARMFUL ATTITUDES

EWE: BIBLIA ƑE MƆFIAME: "Kuviatɔ medea agble le vuvɔŋɔli o, eya ta abia nu le nuŋeɣi, esi naneke mele esi o ta. " Lododowo 20:4.
ENGLISH: BIBLE PRINCIPLE: "The lazy one does not plow in winter, so he will be begging during the harvest when he has nothing. "​ Proverbs 20:4.

EWE: NU SI WÒFIA: Kuviawɔwɔ ate ŋu ana ame naɖi hiã.
ENGLISH: WHAT IT MEANS: Laziness can contribute to poverty.

EWE: Eya ta do vevie dɔ, eye ne anya wɔ la, nàwɔ ɖoɖo ɖe ale si nàzã ga fifia kple etsɔme ŋu.
ENGLISH: Therefore, be a diligent worker, and to the extent possible, plan your financial future.

EWE: NU SI NÀTE ŊU AWƆ:
ENGLISH: WHAT YOU CAN DO:

EWE: Wɔ dɔ sesĩe.
ENGLISH: Work hard.

EWE: Lé fɔ ɖe dɔ si nèwɔna ŋu eye nànye ame si dzi woate ŋu aka ɖo.
ENGLISH: Protect your source of income by being industrious and dependable at your job.

EWE: Dɔtɔwo lɔ̃a ame siwo doa vevie dɔ.
ENGLISH: Employers appreciate diligence.

EWE: Ði anukware.
ENGLISH: Be honest.

EWE: Mèganɔ ame si nèle dɔ wɔm na fim o.
ENGLISH: Do not steal from your employer.

EWE: Anukwaremaɖimaɖi agblẽ wò ŋkɔ eye asesẽ hafi nàgakpɔ dɔ.
ENGLISH: Dishonesty could mar your reputation and make it difficult for you to find employment later on.

EWE: Mègaklẽ ŋu o.
ENGLISH: Avoid greed.

EWE: Ne èklẽa ŋu ɖe ga ŋu la, ava gblẽ nu le wò lãmesẽ ŋu eye wòana wò kple ame bubuwo dome nagblẽ.
ENGLISH: An unbalanced approach to money can eventually damage your health and your relationships with others.

EWE: Ðo ŋku edzi be agbe xɔ asi wu ga.
ENGLISH: Remember, there is more to life than money.

EWE: BIBLIA ƑE MƆFIAME BUBUWO
ENGLISH: OTHER BIBLE PRINCIPLES

EWE: Ŋutsu aɖe le Biblia xlẽm le internet dzi
ENGLISH: A man reads the Bible online

EWE: Àte ŋu axlẽ Biblia le internet dzi le gbegbɔgblɔ alafa geɖe me le jw.org
ENGLISH: Read the Bible online, available in hundreds of languages on jw.org

EWE: MÈGAZÃ ƔEYIƔI KPLE GA ÐE NUMAME GBEGBLẼWO ŊU O.
ENGLISH: DO NOT WASTE TIME AND RESOURCES ON BAD HABITS.

EWE: "Ahamula kple nu tsu ɖula la, ada ahe, eye akɔlɔ̃edɔdɔ ɖe wònana wotsia ɖovu me. "
ENGLISH: "A drunkard and a glutton will come to poverty, and drowsiness will clothe one with rags. "​ PROVERBS 23:21.

EWE: LODODOWO 23:21.
ENGLISH: AVOID UNDUE STRESS.

EWE: MÈGATSI DZI FŨU AKPA ÐE GA ŊU O. "Midzudzɔ dzimaɖitsitsi ɖe miaƒe agbewo ŋu le nu si miaɖu alo nu si miano ŋuti, alo le miaƒe ŋutilãwo ŋu le nu si miado ŋuti. "
ENGLISH: "Stop being anxious about your lives as to what you will eat or what you will drink, or about your bodies as to what you will wear. "​ MATTHEW 6:25.

EWE: MATEO 6:25.
ENGLISH: AVOID ENVY.

EWE: MÈGABIÃ ŊU O. "Ŋubiãla le yɔyɔm ɖe kesinɔnuwo ŋu, ke menya be hiã ava tu ye o. " LODODOWO 28:22.
ENGLISH: "An envious man is eager for wealth, not knowing that poverty will overtake him. "​ PROVERBS 28:22.

EWE: Mawusubɔsubɔ
ENGLISH: Spirituality

EWE: Abe ale si míekpɔe le nyati gbãtɔ me ene la, ame geɖe bua Biblia be enye agbalẽ kɔkɔe.
ENGLISH: As noted at the outset, many people consider the Bible to be a sacred book.

EWE: Wova kpɔe be ne yewoxlẽe, wɔ ɖe eƒe aɖaŋuɖoɖowo dzi la, enana yewotena ɖe Mawu ŋu eye wova sea nu si tae míele agbe ɖo la gɔme.
ENGLISH: They find that when they read it and apply its guidance, they feel uplifted spiritually and come to understand their purpose in life.

EWE: Biblia zã nya "gbɔgbɔmenuwo " tsɔ fia nɔnɔme si le ame si alo ale si wòbua agbee.
ENGLISH: The Bible uses the word "spirituality " to refer to an attitude or an approach to life.

EWE: (Yuda 18, 19) To vovo na ame si ƒe susu katã nɔa ŋutilãmenu siwo ade eya ɖeɖe ko dzi ŋu la, ame si tsia dzi ɖe gbɔgbɔmenuwo ŋu ya dea asixɔxɔ Mawu ƒe nudidiwo ŋu. Efesotɔwo 5:1.
ENGLISH: (Jude 18, 19) Unlike a fleshly-minded person, who focuses more on self, those with a spiritual outlook value God’s standards.​ Ephesians 5:1.

EWE: NU KA TAE ÐOKUIBƆBƆ LE VEVIE?
ENGLISH: WHY IS HUMILITY IMPORTANT?

EWE: Ðokuibɔbɔ nana kadodowo me nyona.
ENGLISH: Humility benefits relationships.

EWE: Agbalẽ aɖe (The Narcissism Epidemic) gblɔ be, "Zi geɖe la, ɖokuibɔbɔla tea ŋu dzea xɔ̃wo bɔbɔe. "
ENGLISH: "Overall, humble people are more connected to others, " says the book The Narcissism Epidemic.

EWE: Eyi edzi gblɔ be: "Enɔa bɔbɔe be wòade ha kple amewo le afi sia afi. "
ENGLISH: It adds that such people find it "easier to relate to other people and the wider world. "

EWE: Ðokuibɔbɔ ate ŋu aɖe vi na viwòa le etsɔme.
ENGLISH: Humility benefits your child’s future.

EWE: Ne viwò srɔ̃ ɖokuibɔbɔ la, akpe ɖe eŋu fifia kple etsɔme le kpɔɖeŋu me, ne eyi dɔ diƒe.
ENGLISH: Learning to be humble will help your child both now and later in life​ for example, when seeking employment.

EWE: Agbalẽnyalagã Leonard Sax gblɔ be: "Sɔhɛ si doa eɖokui ɖe dzi, evɔ medea dzesi eƒe gbɔdzɔgbɔdzɔwo o la, metea ŋu ɖoa nyawo ŋu wòdea dzi gbɔ na dɔtɔ ne ele dɔ dim eye wole gbe biamee o.
ENGLISH: "The young person with bloated self-esteem, unaware of her own deficiencies, is unlikely to do well in the job interview, " writes Dr. Leonard Sax.

EWE: Gake sɔhɛ si di tso dzi me be yeanya nu si le vevie na dɔtɔa la, ƒe asi tea ŋu sua dɔa dzi bɔbɔe wu. "
ENGLISH: "But the young person who is genuinely interested in what the recruiter has to say is more likely to get the job. "

EWE: ALE SI NÀFIA ÐOKUIBƆBƆ VIWÒ
ENGLISH: HOW TO TEACH HUMILITY

EWE: Kpe ɖe viwòa ŋu be wòagabu eɖokui ŋu fũu o.
ENGLISH: Encourage a balanced view of self.

EWE: BIBLIA ƑE MƆFIAME: "Ne ame aɖe susuna be yenye nane, evɔ menye naneke o la, eɖokui ko blem wòle. " Galatiatɔwo 6:3.
ENGLISH: BIBLE PRINCIPLE: "If anyone thinks he is something when he is nothing, he is deceiving himself. "​ Galatians 6:3.

EWE: Mègaɖɔ kesekuku nɛ o.
ENGLISH: Avoid misleading maxims.

EWE: Nyawo abe "Wò asi ate ŋu asu nu sia nu dzi " kple "Àte ŋu ava nye nu sia nu si nèdi be yeava nye " ene gbɔgblɔ, adze dzideƒonyawo, gake zi geɖe la, eto vovo na ale si agbea ŋutɔ nɔna.
ENGLISH: Sayings like "All your dreams can come true " and "You can be anything that you want to be " might sound inspiring, but they often do not prove true in real life.

EWE: Ke hã, ne eɖoa taɖodzinu nyui siwo gbɔ wòate ŋu aɖo eye wòdzea agbagba be yeaɖo wo gbɔ la, ate ŋu ava kpɔ dzidzedze.
ENGLISH: Your children will likely be more successful if they have reasonable goals and work hard to achieve them.

EWE: Kafui ɖe nane koŋ ta.
ENGLISH: Praise specific actions.

EWE: Ne ègblɔ na viwò be "ède ŋgɔ ŋutɔ " la, makpe ɖe eŋu wòabɔbɔ eɖokui o.
ENGLISH: Simply telling a child that he or she is "awesome " does not encourage humility.

EWE: Kafukafua neku ɖe nane koŋ ŋu.
ENGLISH: Be specific.

EWE: Mègana wòazã Internet dzi hahoo kadodowo fũu akpa o.
ENGLISH: Limit your child’s use of social media.

EWE: Zi geɖe la, Internet dzi hahoo kadodowo nana ame hea susu va eɖokui dzi enana ame doa boblo eƒe ŋutetewo kple nu siwo wòte ŋu wɔna, eye esia fia be ame mebɔbɔ eɖokui o.
ENGLISH: Often, social media is linked with self-promotion​ broadcasting a person’s talents and accomplishments ​the very opposite of humility.

EWE: Fia viwòa be wòanye ame si ɖea kuku kaba.
ENGLISH: Encourage your child to apologize quickly.

EWE: Kpe ɖe viwòa ŋu wòakpɔ afi siwo wòdze agɔ le, eye wòalɔ̃ ɖe edzi.
ENGLISH: Help your child to see where he is wrong and to acknowledge it.

EWE: Fiae be wòakpɔ ŋudzedze ɖe nu ŋu.
ENGLISH: Promote gratitude.

EWE: BIBLIA ƑE MƆFIAME: "Minye akpedalawo. " Kolosetɔwo 3:15.
ENGLISH: BIBLE PRINCIPLE: "Show yourselves thankful. "​ Colossians 3:15.

EWE: Fiae be wòakpɔ ŋudzedze ɖe Mawu ƒe nuwɔwɔwo ŋu.
ENGLISH: Gratitude for creation.

EWE: Ele be ɖevi nasrɔ̃ ale si wòakpɔ ŋudzedze ɖe nuwɔwɔwo ŋu kple ale si gbegbe woɖea vi na míi.
ENGLISH: Children should appreciate nature and how much we depend on it for survival.

EWE: Míehiã ya agbɔ, tsi ano kple nuɖuɖu be míaɖu.
ENGLISH: We need air to breathe, water to drink, and food to eat.

EWE: Zã kpɔɖeŋu siawo nàtsɔ aƒã ale si viwòa nakpɔ ŋudzedze ɖe Mawu ƒe nuwɔwɔ wɔnuku siwo le xexea me ŋu la ɖe eme, eye wòada akpe ɖe wo ta.
ENGLISH: Use these examples to instill appreciation, awe, and gratitude for the wonders of the natural world.

EWE: Fiae be wòakpɔ ŋudzedze ɖe amewo ŋu.
ENGLISH: Gratitude for people.

EWE: Ðo ŋku edzi na viwòa be ame bubuwo nyo wui le mɔ aɖe nu eye le esi wòaʋã ŋu wo le woƒe ŋutetewo kple nu siwo wote ŋu wɔna ŋu teƒe la, ate ŋu asrɔ̃ nu tso wo gbɔ boŋ.
ENGLISH: Remind your child that everyone is superior to him in one way or another and that instead of being jealous of others’ skills and abilities, he can learn from them.

EWE: Fiae be wòanye akpedala.
ENGLISH: Expressing gratitude.

EWE: Fia viwòa wòasrɔ̃ ale si wòagblɔ be "akpe, " gake menye be wòagblɔe kple nu ko o, ke boŋ wòatso dzi me nɛ.
ENGLISH: Teach your children to say "thank you, " not just with words but with genuine appreciation.

EWE: Ne míekpɔa ŋudzedze ɖe nu ŋu la, enana míebɔbɔa mía ɖokui.
ENGLISH: A grateful spirit has been called a building block of humility.

EWE: Kpe ɖe viwòa ŋu be wòawɔ nu si aɖe vi na ame bubuwo.
ENGLISH: Teach your children that there is value in serving others.

EWE: BIBLIA ƑE MƆFIAME: "Mitsɔ ɖokuibɔbɔ bu ame bubuwo be wonye gã wu mi, ale be miaganɔ miawo ŋutɔ miaƒe nyonyo ko dim o, ke miadi ame bubuwo hã ƒe nyonyo. " Filipitɔwo 2:3, 4.
ENGLISH: BIBLE PRINCIPLE: "With humility consider others superior to you, as you look out not only for your own interests, but also for the interests of others. "​ Philippians 2:3, 4.

EWE: De aƒemedɔwo asi na viwòa.
ENGLISH: Expect your child to do chores.

EWE: Ne mèdea aƒemedɔwo asi na viwòa le ƒomea me o la, ke èle gbɔgblɔm nɛ be, ‘Èle vevie wu dɔ mawo!’
ENGLISH: Exempting your child from family chores might give him the message, ‘You are too important to do this!’

EWE: Kpe ɖe eŋu wòawɔ aƒemedɔwo vɔ hafi afe fefe.
ENGLISH: Family duties should come first, and playing second.

EWE: Ƒo nu tso ale si aƒemedɔwo ɖea vi na ame bubuwoe kple ale si wokpɔa ŋudzedze ɖe dɔa kpakple ewɔla siaa ŋu la ŋu nɛ.
ENGLISH: Point out how chores benefit others and how others will appreciate and respect him for doing them.

EWE: Te gbe ɖe ale si wònyo be woakpe ɖe ame bubuwo ŋu la dzi nɛ.
ENGLISH: Emphasize that serving others is a privilege.

EWE: Kpekpe ɖe ame bubuwo ŋu ana wòatsi le susu me.
ENGLISH: Doing so is a primary way to develop maturity.

EWE: Eya ta kpe ɖe viwòa ŋu be eƒe susu nanɔ ame siwo hiã na kpekpeɖeŋu la ŋu.
ENGLISH: Therefore, encourage your child to identify those in need.

EWE: Gblɔ nu siwo wòate ŋu awɔ atsɔ akpe ɖe wo ŋu la nɛ.
ENGLISH: Discuss with him what he can do to help them.

EWE: Ne ekpe ɖe ame aɖe ŋu la, kafui eye nàde dzi ƒo nɛ.
ENGLISH: Commend and support your child as he serves others.

EWE: Ŋutsuvi aɖe tsɔ gbeɖuɖɔ le gbeɖuɖɔgo me dem
ENGLISH: A boy puts trash in a bin

EWE: NA HEHEE FIFIA
ENGLISH: TRAIN NOW

EWE: Ðevi si srɔ̃ ale si wòawɔ aƒemedɔ tsɛwo la va zua ame tsitsi si tea ŋu wɔa dɔ kple ame bubuwo faa
ENGLISH: A child who learns to perform humble tasks at home is more likely to work well with others as an adult

EWE: Ðo Kpɔɖeŋu Nyui
ENGLISH: Teach by Example

EWE: Ðe menana vinyewo nyana be ɣeaɖewoɣi la, nye ŋutɔ hã mehiãna na ame bubuwo ƒe kpekpeɖeŋua?
ENGLISH: Do I let my children know that at times I also need help from others?

EWE: Ðe meƒoa nu nyui tso amewo ŋu eye mekpɔa ŋudzedze ɖe wo ŋu loo alo ɖe medaa wo ɖe anyia?
ENGLISH: Do I speak positively and appreciatively about others, or do I belittle them?

EWE: Ðe vinyewo kpɔnɛ be edzɔa dzi nam be makpe ɖe amewo ŋua?
ENGLISH: Do my children see that I value serving others?

EWE: Nu Si Míewɔna . . .
ENGLISH: What We Did . . .

EWE: "Mía vinyɔnua gblɔ na mí be yeƒe sukuxɔmehati aɖe mewɔa nu ɖe amewo ŋu nyuie o, eya ta amewo melɔ̃a eƒe nya o.
ENGLISH: "Our daughter told us about a classmate who, she said, is mean to others and is not liked.

EWE: Megblɔ na mía via be wòabu nu siwo me wòanya nɔ totom le aƒe me ŋu kpɔ.
ENGLISH: I told her to think of what that girl might be going through at home.

EWE: Le nyateƒe me la, menye ame sia ame ŋue wowɔa nu ɖo nyuie le aƒe me o.
ENGLISH: After all, not everybody has a good family life.

EWE: Esia kpe ɖe mía via ŋu wòkpɔe be yemenyo wu ame bubuwo o.
ENGLISH: That helped our daughter to see that she is not better than others.

EWE: Ðeko nuwo de ye dzi wu. " Karen.
ENGLISH: She may just have better circumstances. "​ Karen.

EWE: "Míedea dzi ƒo na mía vinyɔnuawo be woalé fɔ ɖe woƒe sukunusɔsrɔ̃wo ŋu eye woawɔ wo tɔ sinua eye woagatsɔ wo ɖokuiwo anɔ sɔsɔm kple wo tɔ bubuwo o.
ENGLISH: "We encourage our daughters to enjoy what they learn in school and simply to do their best without comparing themselves to others.

EWE: Míenana wonyana be míawo hã míatsɔ wo asɔ kple ame bubuwo o. " Marianna.
ENGLISH: We want them to know that we will not compare them to others either. "​ Marianna.

EWE: Ale Si Wòanɔ Te Ðe Nu Nu
ENGLISH: How to Be Resilient

EWE: NU KAE WÒFIA BE WOANƆ TE ÐE NU NU?
ENGLISH: WHAT IS RESILIENCE?

EWE: Ame si nɔa te ɖe nu nu nye ame si tea ŋu trɔna ɖe nɔnɔmeawo ŋu bɔbɔe eye wògakpɔa dzidzɔ.
ENGLISH: A resilient person bounces back from obstacles and disappointments.

EWE: Nanewo me toto ye nana nɔnɔme sia va sua ame si.
ENGLISH: This skill is acquired through experience.

EWE: Ale si ko ɖevi si le azɔlizɔzɔ srɔ̃m megbea anyidzedze o la, nenemae agbe madze edzi na ɖevi ne mesrɔ̃ ale si wòanɔ te ɖe kuxiwo nu o.
ENGLISH: Just as a child cannot learn how to walk without an occasional fall, he cannot learn how to succeed in life without experiencing occasional setbacks.

EWE: NU KA TAE TENƆNƆ ÐE NU NU LE VEVIE?
ENGLISH: WHY IS RESILIENCE IMPORTANT?

EWE: Dzi ɖena le ɖevi aɖewo ƒo ne wodo kpo nu, wole nɔnɔme sesẽ aɖe me tom, alo wohe nya ɖe wo ŋu.
ENGLISH: Some children get discouraged when they meet with failure, adversity, or criticism.

EWE: Ðewo ya naa ta kura.
ENGLISH: Others give up entirely.

EWE: Ke hã, ele be wòase nyateƒenya vevi siawo gɔme:
ENGLISH: However, they need to understand the following facts:

EWE: Míado kpo nu le nanewo me godoo. Yakobo 3:2.
ENGLISH: Failure is inevitable in some endeavors.​ James 3:2.

EWE: Ame sia ame toa nɔnɔme sesẽ aɖe me ɣeaɖewoɣi. Nyagblɔla 9:11.
ENGLISH: Adversity affects everyone at some point.​ Ecclesiastes 9:11.

EWE: Ðɔɖɔɖo hiã be míate ŋu asrɔ̃ nu geɖe. Lododowo 9:9.
ENGLISH: Correction is vital for learning.​ Proverbs 9:9.

EWE: Tenɔnɔ ɖe nu nu akpe ɖe viwòa ŋu be dzi nanɔ eƒo wòakpe akɔ kple agbemekuxiwo.
ENGLISH: Resilience will help your child face life’s challenges with confidence.

EWE: ALE SI NÀFIA VIWÒA BE WÒANƆ TE ÐE NU NU
ENGLISH: HOW TO TEACH RESILIENCE

EWE: Ne viwòa do kpo nu le nane me.
ENGLISH: When your child fails.

EWE: BIBLIA ƑE MƆFIAME: "Ne ame dzɔdzɔe dze anyi zi adre hã la, agafɔ. " Lododowo 24:16.
ENGLISH: BIBLE PRINCIPLE: "The righteous one may fall seven times, and he will get up again. "​ Proverbs 24:16.

EWE: Kpe ɖe viwòa ŋu be wòada nuwo akpɔ nyuie.
ENGLISH: Help your child put things in perspective.

EWE: Le kpɔɖeŋu me, nu kae wòawɔ ne ege le sukudodokpɔ aɖe me?
ENGLISH: For example, what would he do if he failed a test at school?

EWE: Ðewohĩ ana ta agblɔ be, "Nye ya nyemate ŋu awɔ naneke wòanyo o! "
ENGLISH: He might give up, saying, "I can’t do anything right! "

EWE: Be nàfia ale si wòanɔ te ɖe nu nui la, kpe ɖe eŋu wòakpɔe ɖa be nu kae yeawɔ be dodokpɔa nanyo ɣebubuɣi hã.
ENGLISH: To teach resilience, help your child work out a strategy that will help him to improve.

EWE: Ne èwɔe elea la, viwòa ŋutɔ ate ŋu akpɔ kuxia gbɔ, wu be kuxia naɖu edzi.
ENGLISH: In this way, he will take charge of the problem rather than become a victim of it.

EWE: Gake wò ŋutɔ mègakpɔ kuxia gbɔ nɛ o.
ENGLISH: At the same time, avoid fixing the problem for your child.

EWE: Kpe ɖe eŋu be eya ŋutɔ boŋ nadi mɔ si dzi wòato akpɔ egbɔ.
ENGLISH: Instead, help him create his own plan.

EWE: Àte ŋu abiae be: "Nu kae nèsusu be yeate ŋu awɔ be yeagase nyati ma gɔme nyuie wu ne wole efiam? "
ENGLISH: You might ask him, "What can you do to improve your understanding of the subject that is being taught? "

EWE: Ne nya vɔ̃ aɖe dzɔ.
ENGLISH: When adversity strikes.

EWE: BIBLIA ƑE MƆFIAME: "Mienya ale si miaƒe agbe anɔ etsɔ o. " Yakobo 4:14.
ENGLISH: BIBLE PRINCIPLE: "You do not know what your life will be like tomorrow. "​ James 4:14.

EWE: Ame aɖeke menya nu si adzɔ etsɔ o.
ENGLISH: Life is unpredictable.

EWE: Ame si nye gatɔ egbea ate ŋu ava zu hiãtɔ etsɔ; ame si le lãmesẽ me egbea ate ŋu ava zu dɔnɔ etsɔ.
ENGLISH: A person who is rich today might be poor tomorrow; a person who is healthy today might be sick tomorrow.

EWE: Biblia gblɔ be: "Dziɖuɖu le duɖimekeke me mele afɔ ɖeablɛ me ɣesiaɣi o, dziɖuɖu le aʋa me mele kalẽwɔwɔ me ɣesiaɣi o . . . elabena azãgbe kple nuɖiɖeame li na wo katã. " Nyagblɔla 9:11.
ENGLISH: "The swift do not always win the race, nor do the mighty win the battle, " says the Bible, "because time and unexpected events overtake them all. "​ Ecclesiastes 9:11.

EWE: Esi nènye dzila ta la, èwɔa tɔwò sinua be yeakpɔ ye via ta tso afɔku me.
ENGLISH: As a parent, you rightly take reasonable steps to protect your child from danger.

EWE: Gake manya wɔ be nàkpɔ viwòa ta tso kuxi ɖe sia ɖe me o.
ENGLISH: Realistically, though, it is not possible to shield your child from all of life’s adversities.

EWE: Enye nyateƒe be viwòa metsi ase nu si wòfia be dɔ nagblẽ na ame alo be ame nanɔ gakuxiwo me tom gɔme o.
ENGLISH: Of course, your child may not be old enough to experience the loss of a job or a financial reversal.

EWE: Ke hã, àte ŋu akpe ɖe eŋu be wòanɔ te ɖe kuxi bubuwo abe, ne eya kple exɔlɔ̃ aɖe ƒe ƒomedodo me gblẽ alo ne miaƒe ƒometɔ aɖe ku ene nu.
ENGLISH: Still, you can help him cope with other adversities​ for example, the loss of a friendship or the death of a family member.

EWE: Ne wogbe nya na viwòa le nu gbegblẽ aɖe si wòwɔ ta.
ENGLISH: When your child receives constructive criticism.

EWE: BIBLIA ƑE MƆFIAME: "Se aɖaŋuɖoɖo . . . ne nàdze nunya le etsɔ si gbɔna me. " Lododowo 19:20.
ENGLISH: BIBLE PRINCIPLE: "Listen to counsel . . . in order to become wise in your future. "​ Proverbs 19:20.

EWE: Ne ame aɖe gbe nya na viwò la, menye ŋlɔmi wɔm wòle le eŋu o; ke boŋ ele kpekpem ɖe eŋu be wòaɖe asi le nu gbegblẽ alo nɔnɔme gbegblẽ aɖe ŋu.
ENGLISH: Constructive criticism is not bullying; it is guidance that addresses an action or an attitude that needs to change.

EWE: Ne èfia viwòa be wòalɔ̃ woaɖɔe ɖo la, aɖe vi na mi ame evea siaa.
ENGLISH: When you teach your child to accept correction, both of you are spared much grief.

EWE: Vifofo aɖe si ŋkɔe nye John gblɔ be: "Ne ètsoa viwòwo xɔna le vodada ɖe sia ɖe si wowɔna me la, womasrɔ̃ nu gbeɖe o.
ENGLISH: "If children are always rescued from their errors, " says a father named John, "they will never learn.

EWE: Nu gbegblẽ wɔwɔ dzi koe woanɔ, eye gbe sia gbe la, ànɔ woƒe kuxiwo nu lém.
ENGLISH: They will jump from one problem to the next, and you will spend your life following them, stomping out the fires that they cause.

EWE: Esia ana agbea nati dzilawo kple ɖeviawo siaa. "
ENGLISH: That makes life miserable for the parents and the child. "

EWE: Aleke nàte ŋu akpe ɖe viwòa ŋu be wòalɔ̃ woagbe nya nɛ?
ENGLISH: How can you help your child benefit from constructive criticism?

EWE: Ne wogbe nya na viwòa, le suku alo teƒe bubu aɖe la, ɖu ɖokuiwò dzi be màgagblɔ be mesɔ be woaɖɔe ɖo o.
ENGLISH: When your child receives it​ whether at school or anywhere else ​resist the urge to say that the correction is unfair.

EWE: Ðe ema teƒe la, àte ŋu abiae be:
ENGLISH: Instead, you could ask:

EWE: "Èsusu be nu ka tae woɖɔ wò ɖo? "
ENGLISH: "Why do you think the correction was given? "

EWE: "Ðe nàte ŋu awɔ asitɔtrɔ aɖewoa? "
ENGLISH: "How can you improve? "

EWE: "Ne ègakpɔ ɖokuiwò le nɔnɔme sia me ɣebubuɣi la, nu kae nàwɔ? "
ENGLISH: "What will you do the next time you are in this situation? "

EWE: Ðo ŋku edzi be ne wogbea nya na viwòa la, aɖe vi nɛ fifia kple ne eva tsi.
ENGLISH: Remember, constructive criticism will serve your child well, not only now but also in adulthood.

EWE: Dzi le nyɔnuvi aɖe kum elabe nane si wòmè la gblẽ, gake dadaa le kpekpem ɖe eŋu
ENGLISH: A mother helps her daughter who is frustrated because a cake she baked turned out poorly

ENGLISH: TRAIN NOW

ENGLISH: A child who is able to bounce back from disappointments and mistakes is more likely to persevere when learning skills and to become proficient at them

ENGLISH: Teach by Example

ENGLISH: Do I admit my mistakes, or do I blame others?

EWE: Ðe meƒoa nu tso nu siwo me medo kpo nu le kple nu si mesrɔ̃ tso eme ŋua?
ENGLISH: Do I talk about my failures and what I learned from them?

EWE: Ðe meɖua fewu le ame bubuwo ŋu ne woda voa?
ENGLISH: Do I ridicule others for their mistakes?

ENGLISH: What We Did . . .

ENGLISH: "We did not protect our children from every challenge, failure, or mistake.

EWE: Esi wònye be menɔ te ɖe nɔnɔme mawo tɔgbi nu le nye ɖevime ta la, ekpe ɖe ŋunye metu nɔnɔme nyuiwo ɖo.
