Eya ta se ɖe mɔ be woawɔ nu nyui le Sabat dzi. " 13 Eye wògblɔ na ŋutsua be: "Mlo asi. " Eye wòmloe, eye asi la ɖɔ ɖo keŋkeŋ abe asi kemɛa ene. 14 Ke Farisitɔwo do go, eye wode adaŋu be yewoawui. 15 Esi Yesu kpɔ esia dze sii la, edzo le afi ma.
ENGLISH: 12 And after the removal to Babylon Jeconiah had a son Shealtiel; and Shealtiel, Zerubbabel; 13 and Zerubbabel, Abihud; and Abihud, Eliakim; and Eliakim, Azzur; 14 and Azzur, Sadok; and Sadok, Jachin; and Jachin, Elihud; 15 and Elihud, Eleazar; and Eleazar, Mattan; and Mattan, Jacob; 16 and Jacob, Joseph, the husband of Mary who had for her son Jesus, known as the Messiah.

EWE: Ame geɖewo hã dze eyome, eye wòda gbe le dɔnɔ siwo katã le wo dome la ŋu, 16 ke ede se na wo vevie be woagana woadze si ye o, 17 ne nya si wogblɔ ɖi to nyagblɔɖila Yesaya dzi la nava eme, ame si gblɔ be:
ENGLISH: 17 So there are in all fourteen generations from Abraham down to David, and fourteen generations from David down to the removal to Babylon, and fourteen generations from the removal to Babylon down to the Messiah.

EWE: 18 "Kpɔ ɖa! Nye subɔla si metia, si gbɔ nyemelɔ̃a nu le o, si ƒe nu dze ŋunye! Matsɔ nye gbɔgbɔ la ada ɖe edzi, eye ana dukɔwo nase nu si dzɔdzɔenyenye fia la gɔme.
ENGLISH: 18 And the birth of Jesus Christ was thus: His mother Mary being engaged to Joseph, before they came together it was found that she was pregnant by the Holy Spirit.

EWE: 19 Mawɔ dzre o, mado ɣli o, eye ame aɖeke mase eƒe gbe le ablɔwo dzi hã o.
ENGLISH: 19 And Joseph her husband, being an honest man and unwilling to make a spectacle of her, wanted to divorce her privately.

EWE: 20 Maɖe aƒla si ŋe vɔ kloe la ɖa le enu o, eye matsi ɖovu bibi si le tsitsim la o, va se ɖe esime wòna dzɔdzɔenyenye ɖu dzi.
ENGLISH: 20 But while he was thinking of this, lo, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying "Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take your wife Mary.

EWE: 21 Vavãe, eƒe ŋkɔ ana mɔkpɔkpɔ dukɔwo. "
ENGLISH: For what has been generated in her is by the Holy Spirit; 21 and she shall bear a son, and you shall name him Jesus, for he shall save his people from their sins.

EWE: 22 Eye wokplɔ ŋkuagbãtɔ aɖe si nye aɖetututɔ, si me gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃ le la, va egbɔ, eye wòda gbe le eŋu, ale be aɖetututɔ la ƒo nu hekpɔ nu.
ENGLISH: 22 And all this has come to pass in order that what was said by the Lord through the prophet in the words 23 ‘Lo, the maiden shall be pregnant and bear a son, and they shall name him Immanuel’ " which means "God-is-with-us " "should be fulfilled. " 24 And on waking from his sleep Joseph did as the angel of the Lord directed him, and took his wife 25 and did not know her until she bore a son, and named him Jesus. Matthew

EWE: 23 Ale ameha blibo la ƒe nu ku eye wobia be: "Manye David Vi lae nye esia oa? " 24 Esi Farisitɔwo se esia la, wogblɔ be: "Gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃wo ƒe fia Beelzebul dzie ame sia tona nyaa gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃wo. " 25 Esi wònya woƒe susuwo ta la, egblɔ na wo be: "Fiaɖuƒe ɖe sia ɖe si ma ɖe eɖokui ŋu la zua aƒedo, eye du sia du alo aƒe sia aƒe si ma ɖe eɖokui ŋu la mate ŋu ali ke o.
ENGLISH: 2:1-23 2 And after Jesus was born at Bethlehem in Judea in the days of Herod the king, lo, magi from the East arrived in Jerusalem 2 saying "Where is the King of the Jews that has been born? for we saw his star coming up and have come to do him reverence. " 3 And at hearing it King Herod was alarmed, and all Jerusalem with him; 4 and he called together all the chief priests and scribes of the people, and inquired of them where the Messiah was to be born.

EWE: 26 Nenema kee ne Satana nyaa Satana doa goe la, ekema ema ɖe eɖokui ŋu; ke aleke eƒe fiaɖuƒea awɔ ali ke? 27 Eye ne Beelzebul dzie metona nyaa gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃wo doa goe la, ekema ame ka dzie mia viwo ya tona nyaa wo doa goe? Esia tae mia viwo adrɔ̃ ʋɔnu mi ɖo.
ENGLISH: 5 And they said to him "At Bethlehem in Judea; for so it is written through the prophet, 6 ‘And you, Bethlehem, land of Judah, are by no means least among the chieftains of Judah; for out of you shall come a ruler who shall govern my people Israel.’ " 7 Then Herod called the magi privately and got from them the precise time of the star’s appearing, 8 and sent them to Bethlehem and said "Go and learn the precise facts about the child, and when you find him bring word to me, so that I may come myself and do him reverence. " 9 And they listened to the king and went; and lo, the star that they had seen coming up went ahead of them till it came and stood still over where the child was; 10 and when they saw the star they were glad, and their gladness was very great.

EWE: 28 Ke ne Mawu ƒe gbɔgbɔ dzie metona nyaa gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃wo doa goe la, ekema Mawu Fiaɖuƒe la ɖi ɖe mi ŋutɔŋutɔ.
ENGLISH: 11 And they came to the house and saw the child with Mary his mother, and prostrated themselves and did him reverence; and they opened their coffers and offered gifts to him, gold and frankincense and myrrh.

EWE: 29 Alo aleke ame awɔ age ɖe ame sesẽ aɖe ƒe aƒe me aha eƒe nuwo, ne mebla ame sesẽ la gbã hafi o?
ENGLISH: 12 And, it being revealed to them in a dream that they should not go back to Herod, they withdrew to their own country by another route.

EWE: Ema ko hafi wòate ŋu aha eƒe aƒe la. 30 Ame si mele dzinye o la, tsi tsitre ɖe ŋunye, eye ame si meƒoa amewo nu ƒu kplim o la kaa wo hlẽna.
ENGLISH: 16 Then Herod was greatly enraged at seeing that he had been made a fool of by the magi, and sent and took the lives of all the boys in Bethlehem and in all its territory, from two years old down, to correspond to the precise time which he had got from the magi.

EWE: 31 "Esia ta mele egblɔm na mi be, woatsɔ nu vɔ̃ kple busunyagbɔgblɔ ɖe sia ɖe ake amewo, ke womatsɔ busunya si wogblɔ ɖe gbɔgbɔa ŋu ya ake o.
ENGLISH: 17 Then what was said through the prophet Jeremiah in the words 18 "A sound was heard in Ramah, weeping and much lamenting Rachel weeping for her children and not letting herself be comforted, because they are not " was fulfilled.

EWE: 32 Le kpɔɖeŋu me, ame sia ame si aƒo nu atsi tsitre ɖe Amegbetɔvi la ŋu la, woatsɔe akee; ke ame sia ame si aƒo nu atsi tsitre ɖe gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔe la ŋu la, womatsɔe akee gbeɖe o, womatsɔe akee le nuɖoanyi sia me loo alo esi gbɔna la me o.
ENGLISH: 19 And after Herod’s death, lo, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in Egypt in a dream, 20 saying "Rise, take the child and his mother, and go to the land of Israel; for those who were seeking the child’s life are dead. " 21 And he rose, took the child and his mother, and came into the land of Israel.

EWE: 33 "Mido ati nyui la, eye eƒe kutsetse anyo, alo mido ati manyomanyo, eye eƒe kutsetse manyo o, elabena ati ƒe kutsetsee wotsɔna dzea sii. 34 Dzakpatawo ƒe dzidzimeviwo, aleke miate ŋu agblɔ nya nyuiwo, esi mienye ame vɔ̃ɖiwo?
ENGLISH: 22 But, hearing that Archelaus was king of Judea in place of his father Herod, he was afraid to go there, and, a revelation being made to him in a dream, he withdrew to the parts of Galilee, 23 and came and settled in a city called Nazareth, so that what was said through the prophets, "He shall be called a Nazarene, " should be fulfilled.

EWE: Elabena nya si wu dzi lae nu gblɔna.
ENGLISH: Matthew 3:1-17

EWE: 35 Ame nyui ɖea nu nyuiwo ɖe go tso eƒe nu nyui dzraɖoƒe, ke ame vɔ̃ɖi ɖea nu vɔ̃ɖiwo ɖe go tso eƒe nu vɔ̃ɖi dzraɖoƒe.
ENGLISH: 5 Then Jerusalem and all Judea and all the region of the Jordan went out to him 6 and had themselves baptized in the river Jordan by him, confessing their sins.

EWE: 36 Mele egblɔm na mi be, nya dzodzro sia nya dzodzro si amewo gblɔna la, woabu akɔnta le eŋuti le Ʋɔnudrɔ̃gbe la; 37 elabena wò nyawoe woatsɔ atso afia na wò, eye wò nyawoe woatsɔ abu fɔ wò. "
ENGLISH: 10 And the ax is already lying at the root of the trees, so every tree that does not produce good fruit is to be cut out and thrown into a fire.

EWE: 38 Eye agbalẽfiala aɖewo kple Farisitɔ aɖewo gblɔ nɛ be: "Nufiala, míedi be nàwɔ dzesi aɖe míakpɔ. " 39 Eɖo eŋu na wo be: "Dzidzime vɔ̃ɖi wɔahasi le dzesi dim, ke womele dzesi aɖeke na gee o, negbe nyagblɔɖila Yona ƒe dzesi la ko.
ENGLISH: 11 I am baptizing you in water to repentance, but he who is coming behind me is stronger than I, whose shoes I am not fit to carry: he will baptize you in Holy Spirit and fire 12 he whose winnowing-fork is in his hand, and who will clean up his threshing-floor and gather his wheat into his barn, but burn up the chaff with inextinguishable fire. " 13 Then came Jesus from Galilee to John at the Jordan to be baptized by him.

EWE: 40 Elabena ale si Yona nɔ tɔmelã gã la ƒe dɔ me ŋkeke etɔ̃ kple zã etɔ̃ la, nenema kee Amegbetɔvi la hã anɔ anyigba tume ŋkeke etɔ̃ kple zã etɔ̃.
ENGLISH: 14 But John checked him, saying "I need to be baptized by you, and are you coming to me? " 15 But Jesus answered him "Let me now, for it befits us to fulfill all righteousness thus. "

EWE: 41 Niniwetɔwo afɔ ɖe tsitre le ʋɔnudrɔ̃ɣi la kpe ɖe dzidzime sia ŋu, eye woabu fɔe, elabena wotrɔ dzi me le nya siwo Yona ɖe gbeƒãe la ta.
ENGLISH: Then he let him. 16 And when Jesus was baptized, at once he came up from the water, and lo, the sky opened and he saw God’s Spirit come down like a dove and come upon him; 17 and lo, a voice out of the sky saying "This is my dear son in whom I take pleasure. "

EWE: Ke kpɔ ɖa, ame si lolo wu Yona la le afii.
ENGLISH: Matthew 4:1-25

EWE: 42 Woafɔ anyiehefianyɔnu la ɖe tsitre le ʋɔnudrɔ̃ɣi la kpe ɖe dzidzime sia ŋu, eye wòabu fɔe; elabena etso keke anyigba seƒe ke va be yease Salomo ƒe nunyanyawo.
ENGLISH: 4 Then Jesus was brought up to the wilderness by the Spirit to be tempted by the Devil.

EWE: Ke kpɔ ɖa, ame si lolo wu Salomo la le afii!
ENGLISH: 2 And upon fasting forty days and forty nights he afterward grew hungry.

EWE: 43 "Ne gbɔgbɔ makɔmakɔ aɖe do go le ame aɖe me la, etsana le teƒe siwo ƒu kplakplakpla nɔa gbɔɖemeƒe dim, eye ne mekpɔ ɖeke o la, 44 egblɔna be: ‘Matrɔ ayi nye aƒe, si me medzo le la me,’ eye ne eva ɖo la, ekpɔnɛ be aƒea me le ƒuƒlu, gake wokplɔ eme heɖo atsyɔ̃ nɛ. 45 Eye wòyina ɖakplɔa gbɔgbɔ adre bubu siwo vɔ̃ɖi wu eya ŋutɔ la kpena ɖe eɖokui ŋu, eye ne woyi ɖe eme la, wonɔa afi ma; eye ame ma ƒe nɔnɔme mlɔetɔ va gblẽna wu gbãtɔ.
ENGLISH: 12 But upon hearing that John was committed to prison he retired to Galilee, 13 and left Nazareth and came and settled in Capernaum on the seacoast, in the territory of Zebulun and Naphtali, 14 that what was said through the prophet Isaiah in the words 15 "The land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, seaward on the other side of the Jordan, Galilee of the nations 16 the people that was sitting in darkness has seen a great light, and to those who were sitting in the country and shadow of death a light has risen, " might be fulfilled.

EWE: Nenema kee wòanɔ na dzidzime vɔ̃ɖi sia hã. "
ENGLISH: 17 Thenceforth Jesus began to proclaim "Repent, for the Reign of Heaven is almost here. "

EWE: 46 Esi wògale nu ƒom na amehawo la, dadaa kple nɔviaŋutsuwo va tɔ ɖe xexe le didim be yewoaƒo nu kplii. 47 Eye ame aɖe gblɔ nɛ be: "Kpɔ ɖa!
ENGLISH: 18 And in walking by the Sea of Galilee he saw two brothers, Simon, the one who is known as Peter, and his brother Andrew, throwing a casting-net in the sea for they were fishermen 19 and said to them "Come here after me, and I will make you fishers of men "; 20 and they left their nets at once and followed him.

EWE: Dawò kple nɔviwòŋutsuwo le tsitre ɖe xexe le didim be yewoaƒo nu kpli wò. " 48 Ke eɖo eŋu na ame si gblɔ nyaa nɛ la be: "Ame kae nye danye, eye ame kawoe nye nɔvinyeŋutsuwo? " 49 Eye esi wòfia asi eƒe nusrɔ̃lawo la, egblɔ be: "Kpɔ ɖa!
ENGLISH: 21 And he went on from there and saw two other brothers, James the son of Zebedee and his brother John, in their boat with their father Zebedee putting their nets to rights, and called them; 22 and they left the boat and their father at once and followed him.

EWE: Danye kple nɔvinyeŋutsuwoe nye esiawo! 50 Elabena ame sia ame si wɔa Fofonye si le dziƒo la ƒe lɔlɔ̃nu la, eyae nye nɔvinyeŋutsu kple nɔvinyenyɔnu kpakple danye. "
ENGLISH: 23 And he went around in all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues and proclaiming the gospel of the Reign and curing every disease and every ailment among the people.

EWE: Mateo
ENGLISH: Matthew

EWE: 13 Yesu do go le aƒea me gbe ma gbe, eye wòyi ɖabɔbɔ nɔ ƒua nu. 2 Eye ameha gã aɖe ƒo ƒu ɖe eŋu, eya ta ege ɖe tɔdziʋu aɖe me, eye wòbɔbɔ nɔ anyi, ke ameha blibo la le tsitre ɖe ƒua nu.
ENGLISH: 5 And when he saw the crowds he went up on the mountainside; and he sat down, and his disciples came to him, 2 and he opened his mouth and taught them, saying

EWE: 3 Eye wògblɔ nya geɖewo na wo le lododowo me be: "Mikpɔ ɖa!
ENGLISH: 3 "Happy are the poor at heart, because the Reign of Heaven is theirs.

EWE: 4 Esi wòle nukua wum la, nuku aɖewo ge ɖe mɔ to, eye xeviwo va fɔ wo mi.
ENGLISH: 4 Happy are mourners, because they shall be comforted.

EWE: 5 Bubuwo ge ɖe kpenyigba dzi, afi si womekpɔ anyi sɔgbɔ le o, eye womie enumake, elabena anyia mede to o.
ENGLISH: 5 Happy are the meek, because they shall inherit the earth.

EWE: 6 Esi ŋdɔ ʋu la, ŋdɔkutsu ɖu wo, eye woyrɔ, elabena woƒe ke meyi to o.
ENGLISH: 6 Happy are the hungry and thirsty for righteousness, because they shall have their meal.

EWE: 7 Bubuwo hã ge ɖe ŋùwo me, eye ŋùawo vu tsyɔ wo dzi.
ENGLISH: 7 Happy are the pitiful, because they shall be pitied.

EWE: 8 Bubu aɖewo hã ge ɖe anyigba nyui dzi, eye wode asi tsetse me, ɖewo teƒe alafa ɖeka, ɖewo blaade, ɖewo blaetɔ̃.
ENGLISH: 8 Happy are the clean in mind, because they shall see God.

EWE: 9 Ame si to li na la, nesee. "
ENGLISH: 9 Happy are peacemakers, because they shall be called sons of God.

EWE: 10 Eye nusrɔ̃lawo va biae be: "Nu ka tae nèƒoa nu na wo le lododowo me? " 11 Eɖo eŋu na wo be: "Miawo la, wona mi be miase Dziƒofiaɖuƒe la ƒe nya ɣaɣla kɔkɔeawo gɔme, ke womena woawo ya o.
ENGLISH: 10 Happy are the persecuted who have been persecuted on account of righteousness, because the Reign of Heaven is theirs.

EWE: 12 Elabena ame si si nu le la, woatsɔ geɖe akpee nɛ, eye wòagba go nɛ; gake ame si si nu mele o la, woaxɔ nu si le esi la gɔ̃ hã le esi.
ENGLISH: 11 Happy are you when they twit you and persecute you and say everything vile about you falsely on my account; 12 be glad and exult, because your reward is great in heaven, for thus they persecuted the prophets who came before you.

EWE: 13 Esia tae meƒoa nu na wo le lododowo me ɖo; elabena togbɔ be wole nu kpɔm hã la, dzodzroe wole ekpɔm, eye togbɔ be wole nu sem hã la, dzodzroe wole esem, eye womesea egɔme o.
ENGLISH: 13 "You are the salt of the earth; but if salt loses its strength, with what shall it be salted? it will no longer do for anything but to be thrown out and trodden underfoot by men.

EWE: 15 Elabena dukɔ sia ƒe dzi ku atri; wose nu kple woƒe towo, ke womewɔ edzi o, eye womia woƒe ŋkuwo, ne woagakpɔ nu kple woƒe ŋkuwo, eye woase nu kple woƒe towo ahase nu gɔme kple woƒe dziwo, eye woatrɔ, ne mada gbe le wo ŋu o.’
ENGLISH: 14 You are the light of the world; a city located on a mountaintop cannot be hidden, 15 nor do they light a lamp and put it under the peck measure, but on the stand and it shines for everybody in the house.

EWE: 16 "Ke dzidzɔtɔwo mienye, elabena miaƒe ŋkuwo kpɔa nu eye miaƒe towo hã sea nu.
ENGLISH: 16 Let your light shine thus before men, so that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven.

EWE: 17 Elabena vavã mele egblɔm na mi be, nyagblɔɖila kple ame dzɔdzɔe geɖewo di vevie be yewoakpɔ nu siwo kpɔm miele la, gake womekpɔ wo o, eye wodi be yewoase nya siwo sem miele la, gake womese wo o.
ENGLISH: 17 "Do not suppose that I came to tear down the law or the prophets; I did not come to tear down but to fill up.

EWE: 18 "Azɔ miɖo to miase nukuwula ŋuti lododoa ƒe gɔmeɖeɖe.
ENGLISH: 18 For I tell you verily, till the heavens and the earth pass away, not the dot of an i nor the cross of a t in the law shall pass away, till everything is done.

EWE: 19 Ne ame aɖe se Fiaɖuƒea ŋuti nya la gake mesea egɔme o la, vɔ̃ɖitɔ la va ɖea nu si wowu ɖe eƒe dzi me la dzonae; nuku siae nye esi ge ɖe mɔ to la.
ENGLISH: 19 So whoever breaks one of the pettiest of those commandments, and teaches men so, shall be called petty in the Reign of Heaven; but whoever does them and teaches them shall be called great in the Reign of Heaven.

EWE: 20 Ke nuku si ge ɖe kpenyigba dzi la, eyae nye ame si le nya la sem, eye wòxɔnɛ enumake kple dzidzɔ.
ENGLISH: 20 For I tell you that unless your righteousness outdoes the scribes and Pharisees you shall not get into the Reign of Heaven.

EWE: 21 Gake meli ke le eɖokui me o, enɔa anyi ɣeyiɣi aɖe ko, eye ne xaxa alo yometiti va le nya la ta ko la, edea megbe enumake. 22 Ke nuku si ge ɖe ŋùwo me la, esiae nye ame si le nya la sem, gake nuɖoanyi sia me dzimaɖitsitsi kple kesinɔnuwo ƒe amebleŋusẽ vuna tsyɔa nya la dzi, eye metsea ku o.
ENGLISH: 21 "You have heard that it was said to the ancients ‘You shall not commit murder; and whoever commits murder shall be liable to judgment.’ 22 But I tell you that anyone who is angry with his brother shall be liable to judgment; and whoever says ‘Raka’ to his brother shall be liable to the Sanhedrin Court; and whoever says ‘You fool’ shall be liable to the fire of hell.

EWE: 23 Eye nuku si ge ɖe anyigba nyui dzi lae nye ame si le nya la sem, eye wòsea egɔme, eye wòtsea ku geɖe, ɖewo teƒe alafa ɖeka, ɖewo teƒe blaade, ɖewo teƒe blaetɔ̃. " 24 Egado lo bubu na wo be: "Dziƒofiaɖuƒe la le abe ame aɖe si wu nuku nyui ɖe eƒe agble me ene.
ENGLISH: 23 So, if you are offering your gift on the altar and there remember that your brother has something against you, 24 leave your gift there before the altar and go and make up with your brother first; then come and offer your gift.

EWE: 25 Esi amewo dɔ alɔ̃ la, eƒe futɔ va wu gbe vɔ̃ɖi ɖe luawo dome, eye wòdzo. 26 Esi luawo to aŋgba hetse la, gbe vɔ̃ɖiawo hã do.
ENGLISH: 25 Be quick to make friends with your antagonist while you are on the road to court with him, for fear your antagonist should hand you over to the judge, and the judge to the officer, and you be thrown into prison; 26 I tell you verily, you shall not get out from there till you pay the last copper.

EWE: 27 Eye aƒetɔ la ƒe kluviwo va gblɔ nɛ be: ‘Aƒetɔ, menye nuku nyui ye nèwu ɖe wò agblea me oa? Aleke wɔ gbe vɔ̃ɖiwo va le eme?’ 28 Egblɔ na wo be: ‘Futɔ aɖee wɔ nu sia.’
ENGLISH: 27 "You have heard that it was said ‘You shall not commit adultery.’ 28 But I tell you that anyone who looks at a woman to desire her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.

EWE: Kluviawo biae be: ‘Ekema èdi be míayi aɖaho woa?’ 29 Eɖo eŋu be: ‘Ao; elabe ne miele gbe vɔ̃ɖiawo hom la, ɖewohĩ miaho luawo hã akpe ɖe wo ŋu.
ENGLISH: 29 And if your right eye is tripping you up, take it out and throw it from you; for it is well for you that one of your organs should perish and not your whole body be thrown into hell.

EWE: 30 Mina wo kple evea siaa natsi va se ɖe nuŋeɣi la, eye ne nuŋeɣia ɖo la, magblɔ na nuŋelawo be: Miho gbe vɔ̃ɖiawo gbã, eye miabla wo tatata atɔ dzo wo, emegbe miaƒo lu la nu ƒu ɖe nye nudzraɖoƒe.’ "
ENGLISH: 30 And if your right hand is tripping you up, cut it away and throw it from you; for it is well for you that one of your organs should perish and not your whole body go to hell.

EWE: 31 Egado lo bubu na wo be: "Dziƒofiaɖuƒe la le abe sinapi-ku si ame aɖe ƒã ɖe eƒe agble me ene. 32 Le nyateƒe me la, eyae nye nuku suetɔ, ke ne etsi la, eyae nyea abɔ me nu miemie si lolona wu, eye wòzua ati, ale be dziƒoxewo va nɔa eƒe alɔwo me. "
ENGLISH: 31 "And it was said ‘Whoever divorces his wife, let him give her a certificate of divorce.’ 32 But I tell you that anyone who divorces his wife, except on grounds of unchastity, causes her to commit adultery, and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery.

EWE: 33 Egado lo bubu na wo be: "Dziƒofiaɖuƒe la le abe amɔwɔʋãnu si nyɔnu aɖe tsɔ de amɔwɔ dzidzenu gã etɔ̃ me va se ɖe esime amɔwɔ bliboa ʋã la ene. " 34 Yesu gblɔ nya siawo katã na ameha la le lododowo me. Le nyateƒe me la, meƒoa nu na wo ne menye le lododo me o, 35 ale be nya si wogblɔ ɖi to nyagblɔɖila la dzi nava eme, egblɔ be: "Make nu aƒo nu le lododowo me; magblɔ nu siwo le ɣaɣla tso keke gɔmeɖoanyiɣi ke. "
ENGLISH: 33 "Again, you have heard that it was said to the ancients ‘You shall not perjure yourself, but discharge your oaths to the Lord.’ 34 But I tell you not to swear at all; neither by heaven, because it is God’s throne, 35 nor by the earth, because it is the footstool of his feet, nor by Jerusalem, because it is the city of the great King.

EWE: 36 Esi wòɖe asi le amehaa ŋu vɔ la, eyi aƒe me.
ENGLISH: 36 And do not swear by your head either, because you cannot make one hair white or black.

EWE: Nuŋeɣi lae nye nuɖoanyi aɖe ƒe nuwuɣi, eye nuŋelaawoe nye mawudɔlawo.
ENGLISH: 37 But let your language be yes, yes, no, no; anything in excess of this is so much of bad.

EWE: 40 Eya ta abe ale si woho gbe vɔ̃ɖiawo hetɔ dzo woe ene la, nenema kee wòanɔ le nuɖoanyia ƒe nuwuɣi. 41 Amegbetɔvi la adɔ eƒe dɔlawo ɖa, eye woaƒo amenuɖianuwo kple sedzimawɔlawo nu ƒu tso eƒe Fiaɖuƒe la me, 42 eye woatsɔ wo aƒu gbe ɖe kpodzo bibi la me. Afi mae woafa avi ahaɖu aɖukli le.
ENGLISH: 38 "You have heard that it was said ‘an eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth.’ 39 But I tell you not to oppose the bad; but whoever slaps you on your right cheek, turn him the other too, 40 and when a man wants to sue you and get your shirt let him have your cloak too, 41 and go two miles with whoever requisitions you for one.

EWE: 43 Ɣemaɣi la, ame dzɔdzɔewo aklẽ abe ɣe ene le wo Fofo ƒe Fiaɖuƒe la me.
ENGLISH: 42 Give to him who asks you, and do not turn your back on him who wants to borrow from you.

EWE: Ame si to li na la, nesee. 44 "Dziƒofiaɖuƒe la le abe kesinɔnu aɖe si woɣla ɖe anyigba aɖe me ene, eye ame aɖe va ke ɖe eŋu hetsɔe ɣla; eye le dzidzɔ si wòkpɔ ta la, eyi ɖadzra eƒe nuwo katã eye wòƒle anyigba ma. 45 "Dziƒofiaɖuƒe la gale abe asitsala mɔzɔla aɖe si le dzonu nyuiwo dim la ene.
ENGLISH: 43 "You have heard that it was said ‘you shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’ 44 But I tell you, love your enemies and pray for your persecutors, 45 so as to act as sons of your Father in heaven, because he makes his sun rise on bad and good, and sends rain on honest men and rascals.

EWE: 46 Esi wòke ɖe dzonu xɔasi aɖe ŋu la, eyi ɖadzra eƒe nuwo katã enumake eye wòƒlee. 47 "Dziƒofiaɖuƒe la gale abe ɖɔ si woɖi ɖe ƒu me, si ɖe tɔmelã ɖe sia ɖe ƒomevi la ene.
ENGLISH: 46 For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? do not even customhouse officers do the same? 47 and if you salute only your brothers, what are you doing that is special? do not even the heathen do the same?

EWE: 48 Esi ɖɔa yɔ la, wohee va gota, eye wonɔ anyi heƒo tɔmelã nyuiawo nu ƒu ɖe nugowo me, ke wotsɔ manyomanyoawo ƒu gbe.
ENGLISH: 48 "So you are to be thorough as your heavenly Father is thorough.
Matthew

EWE: 16 Farisitɔwo kple Zadukitɔwo va Yesu gbɔ be yewoatee kpɔ eye wobiae be wòaɖe dzesi aɖe afia yewo tso dziƒo.
ENGLISH: 6 But beware of doing your righteousness before men, to be viewed by them; if you do, you have no reward with your Father in heaven.

EWE: 17 Le ŋkeke ade megbe la, Yesu kplɔ Petro, Yakobo kple nɔvia Yohanes kpe ɖe eɖokui ŋu, eye woawo ɖeɖe woyi to kɔkɔ aɖe dzi. 2 Eye eƒe dzedzeme trɔ le wo ŋkume, eƒe mo klẽ abe ɣe ene, eye eƒe awuwo fu tititi abe kekeli ene.
ENGLISH: 2 So when you give charity do not have a trumpet blown before you as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, so that they may be glorified by men; I tell you verily, they have got their reward.

EWE: 3 Eye kpɔ ɖa, Eliya kple Mose dze wokpɔ eye wole dze ɖom kplii. 4 Eya ta Petro gblɔ na Yesu be: "Aƒetɔ, enyo na mí be míanɔ afi sia.
ENGLISH: 3 But at your giving charity let your left hand not find out what your right is doing, 4 so that your charity may be under cover, and your Father who sees under cover will repay you.

EWE: Ne èlɔ̃ la, matu agbadɔ etɔ̃ ɖe afi sia, ɖeka na wò, ɖeka na Mose, eye ɖeka na Eliya. " 5 Esi wògale nuƒoƒo dzi la, kpɔ ɖa, alilikpo keklẽ aɖe do vɔvɔli ɖe wo dzi, eye gbe aɖe ɖi tso alilikpoa me be: "Ame siae nye Vinye, si gbɔ nyemelɔ̃a nu le o, si ƒe nu dzea ŋunye.
ENGLISH: 5 "And when you pray you are not to be as the hypocrites are; for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and at the corners of the main streets, so that they may be visible to men; I tell you verily, they have got their reward.

EWE: Miɖo toe. " 6 Esi nusrɔ̃lawo se nya sia la, wotsyɔ mo anyi, eye vɔvɔ̃ ɖo wo ŋutɔ.
ENGLISH: 6 But do you, when you pray, go into your closet, and shut the door and pray to your Father who is present in hidden places; and your Father who sees in hidden places will reward you.

EWE: 7 Eye Yesu te ɖe wo ŋu eye wòka asi wo ŋu gblɔ be: "Mifɔ.
ENGLISH: 7 And in praying do not parrot off words like the heathen; for they think they will get themselves listened to by the quantity of what they say.

EWE: Migavɔ̃ o. " 8 Esi wofɔ mo dzi la, womekpɔ ame aɖeke o, negbe Yesu ɖeka ko.
ENGLISH: 8 So do not be like them; for your Father knows the things you need before you ask him.

EWE: 9 Esi wole ɖiɖim tso toa dzi la, Yesu de se na wo be: "Migagblɔ ŋutega la na ame aɖeke o, va se ɖe esime wofɔ Amegbetɔvi la tso ame kukuwo dome hafi. " 10 Ke nusrɔ̃lawo biae be: "Ekema nu ka tae agbalẽfialawo gblɔna be ele be Eliya nava gbã? " 11 Eɖo eŋu be: "Vavãe, ele be Eliya nava, eye wòaɖɔ nuwo katã ɖo.
ENGLISH: 9 Do you, then, pray in this way: ‘Father in heaven, may thy name be kept holy, 10 thy reign come, than will be done on earth as in heaven; 11 give us today our next day’s bread, 12 and forgive us our debts as we too have forgiven our debtors, 13 and do not have us fall under temptation but deliver us from evil.’ 14 For if you forgive men their offenses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you; 15 but if you do not forgive men, no more will your Father forgive your offenses.

EWE: 12 Ke mele egblɔm na mi be Eliya va xoxo, gake womedze sii o, eye wowɔ nu si dze wo ŋu la ɖe eŋu. Nenema kee Amegbetɔvi la hã akpe fu le wo si me. " 13 Ale nusrɔ̃lawo se egɔme be Yohanes Amenyrɔɖetsimela ŋu nya gblɔm wòle na yewo.
ENGLISH: 16 "And when you are fasting do not be lugubrious like the hypocrites; for they make their faces unsightly so that it may be seen by men that they are fasting; I tell you verily, they have got their reward.

EWE: 14 Esi wogbɔna ameha la gbɔ la, ŋutsu aɖe te ɖe eŋu hedze klo ɖe eŋkume gblɔ be: 15 "Aƒetɔ, kpɔ nublanui na vinyeŋutsuvi, elabena kpeŋuidɔ le eŋu, eye dɔa nu sẽ. Edzea dzo me enuenu, eye wòdzea tsi me enuenu.
ENGLISH: 17 But do you in fasting put oil on your head and wash your face, 18 so that it may not be seen by men that you are fasting but by your Father who is present in secret places; and your Father who sees in secret places will reward you,

EWE: 16 Mekplɔe va wò nusrɔ̃lawo gbɔ, ke womete ŋu da gbe le eŋu o. " 17 Yesu ɖo eŋu be: "Oo, dzidzime maxɔse totro kpaɖikpaɖi, ɣeyiɣi didi kae manɔ mia gbɔ ase ɖo? Ɣeyiɣi didi kae mado dzi atsɔ miaƒe nuwɔnawo ase ɖo?
ENGLISH: 19 "Do not lay up stores for yourselves on earth where moth and decay consume, and where thieves break in and steal, 20 but lay up stores for yourselves in heaven where neither moth nor decay consumes and where thieves do not break in nor steal; 21 for where your stores are, there your heart too will be.

EWE: Mikplɔe va gbɔnye afii. " 18 Yesu blu ɖe gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃ la ta eye wòdo go le eme, ale ŋutsuvi la ƒe lãme sẽ enumake. 19 Eye nusrɔ̃lawo ɖeɖe va Yesu gbɔ va biae be: "Aleke wɔ míawo ya míete ŋu nyae do goe o? " 20 Eɖo eŋu na wo be: "Le miaƒe xɔse ʋɛ la tae.
ENGLISH: 22 The lamp of the body is the eye; therefore if your eye is free your whole body will be light, 23 but if your eye is mean your whole body will be dark, so if the light in you is darkness, what must the darkness be! 24 No one can belong to two masters, for he will either hate the one and love the other or be attentive to the one and despise the other: you cannot belong to God and money.

EWE: Elabena vavã mele egblɔm na mi be: Ne xɔse le mia si de sinapi-ku ƒe lolome nu la, ekema miagblɔ na to sia be: ‘Ho le afi sia nàyi aɖadze afi mɛ!’ eye wòaho ayi, eye naneke mate ŋu awu wɔwɔ na mi o. " 21
ENGLISH: 25 For this reason I tell you, do not fret over your soul what you shall eat or what you shall drink, nor over your body what you shall put on; is not the soul more than the food, and the body than the garment? 26 Look at the birds of the air, that they do not sow nor reap nor gather into barns, and your heavenly Father feeds them; are you not more important than they? 27 and which of you by fretting can add to his height one foot? 28 And why do you fret about dress?

EWE: 22 Esime Yesu kple eƒe nusrɔ̃lawo ƒo ƒu ɖe Galilea la, egblɔ na wo be: "Wole Amegbetɔvi la de ge asi na amewo, 23 eye woawui, ke woafɔe ɖe tsitre le ŋkeke etɔ̃a gbe. "
ENGLISH: Observe the lilies of the field, how they grow: they do not labor nor spin, 29 but I tell you not even Solomon in all his glory was clad like one of these.

EWE: Esia na woxa nu vevie. 24 Esi wova ɖo Kapernaum la, ame siwo xɔa drakma eve ƒe adzɔ le amewo si la te ɖe Petro ŋu hebiae be: "Ðe miaƒe nufiala ya medzɔa drakma eve la oa? " 25 Eɖo eŋu be: "Edzɔnɛ. "
ENGLISH: 30 But if God robes the plants in the field so, that are there today and are thrown in a firepot tomorrow, will he not much more you, little-faiths? 31 So do not fret and say ‘What shall we eat?’ or ‘What shall we drink?’ or ‘What shall we wrap ourselves in?’ 32 for the foreigners hunt after all this.

EWE: Ke esi wòge ɖe aƒea me la, Yesu do ŋgɔ biae be: "Simon, nu kae nèsusu?
ENGLISH: For your heavenly Father knows that you want all this.

EWE: Ame kawo sie anyigbadzifiawo xɔa adzɔ alo nudzɔdzɔ le?
ENGLISH: 33 But seek first the Reign, and his righteousness, and you will have all this added.

EWE: Wo viwo si loo alo ame bubuwo sia? " 26 Esi wòɖo eŋu be, "Le ame bubuwo si " la, Yesu gblɔ nɛ be: "Ekema mehiã be viwo naxe adzɔ o ɖe! 27 Ke be míagaɖia wo nu o la, yi ƒuta, nàda ƒu, eye lã gbãtɔ si nàɖe la, lée, eye ne èke eƒe nu me la, àkpɔ klosalogaku. Tsɔe yi ɖana wo ɖe nye kpli wò nu. "
ENGLISH: 34 So do not fret over tomorrow, for to morrow will do its own fretting; a day’s evil is a sufficiency for that day.

EWE: Mateo
ENGLISH: Matthew

EWE: 18 Le gaƒoƒo ma me la, nusrɔ̃lawo te ɖe Yesu ŋu biae be: "Ame ka tututue nye gãtɔ le Dziƒofiaɖuƒe la me? " 2 Ale wòyɔ ɖevi aɖe va eɖokui gbɔ, kplɔe va wo dome 3 hegblɔ be: "Vavã mele egblɔm na mi be: Ne mietrɔ hezu abe ɖevi suewo ene o la, miele yiyi ge ɖe Dziƒofiaɖuƒe la me akpɔ o.
ENGLISH: 7 "Do not be judging, 2 that you may not be judged; for the judgments that you pass shall be passed upon you, and the measure that you give shall be given to you.

EWE: 4 Eya ta ame sia ame si abɔbɔ eɖokui abe ɖevi sia ene la, eyae anye gãtɔ le Dziƒofiaɖuƒe la me; 5 eye ame sia ame si xɔa nenem ɖevi siawo tɔgbi ɖeka le nye ŋkɔ ta la, exɔa nye hã.
ENGLISH: 3 And why is it that you can see the particle of straw in your brother’s eye, but do not observe the beam of timber in your own eye? 4 or how will you say to your brother ‘Let me get the particle out of your eye,’ when in your eye there is the timber? 5 Hypocrite, first get the timber out of your eye, and then you will have good eyesight to get the particle out of your brother’s eye.

EWE: 6 Ke ame sia ame si aɖia ɖevi sue siawo, siwo xɔ dzinye se dometɔ aɖe nu la, ade edzi wu be woatsɔ té, si tedziwo trona, atsi ɖe kɔ nɛ, eye woatsɔe aƒu gbe ɖe atsiaƒu me.
ENGLISH: 6 "Do not give sacred things to the dogs, nor throw your pearls before the hogs, for fear they should trample them with their feet and turn and tear you to pieces.

EWE: 7 "Baba na xexea le nu siwo nana amewo dzea nu vɔ̃ me la ŋuti!
ENGLISH: 7 "Ask, and you will have things given to you; look, and you will find; knock, and you will be opened to.

EWE: Nu siwo ana amewo nadze nu vɔ̃ me la ava godoo ya, ke baba na ame si ana amewo nadze nu vɔ̃ me! 8 Eya ta ne wò asi alo wò afɔ hea wò dea nu vɔ̃ me la, lãe ɖa eye nàtsɔe ƒu gbe.
ENGLISH: 8 For every asker receives, and the seeker finds, and the knocker will be opened to.

EWE: 9 Eye ne wò ŋku hea wò dea nu vɔ̃ me la, hoe le eto me nàtsɔ aƒu gbe. Enyo na wò be nàge ɖe agbe la me kple ŋku ɖeka wu be ŋku eve nanɔ asiwò, evɔ woatsɔ wò aƒu gbe ɖe Gehena ƒe dzo la me. 10 Mikpɔ nyuie be miagado vlo ɖevi siawo dometɔ ɖeka pɛ hã o, elabena mele egblɔm na mi be, woƒe mawudɔla siwo le dziƒo la kpɔa Fofonye si le dziƒo la ƒe mo ɣesiaɣi.
ENGLISH: 9 Or what man is there of you that his son will ask for bread and he will hand him a stone? 10 or ask for a fish and he will hand him a snake? 11 So if you, being bad, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask him!

EWE: 11 12 "Nu kae miesusu?
ENGLISH: 12 "Everything that you want to have men do to you, then, do so yourselves to them; for this is the law and the prophets.

EWE: Ne alẽ alafa ɖeka le ame aɖe si, eye wo dometɔ ɖeka bu la, ɖe magblẽ blaasieke vɔ asieke la ɖe towo dzi, eye wòayi aɖadi ɖeka si bu la oa? 13 Eye ne ekpɔe la, vavã mele egblɔm na mi be, akpɔ dzidzɔ ɖe eŋu wu ale si wòakpɔe ɖe blaasieke vɔ asieke siwo mebu o la ŋu.
ENGLISH: 13 "Enter by the narrow gate, because wide and spacious is the road that leads to perdition, and many are they who enter it, 14 because narrow is the gate and contracted the road that leads to life, and few are they who find it.

EWE: 15 "Ne nɔviwò wɔ nu vɔ̃ ɖe ŋuwò la, yi nàɖe eƒe vodada fiae le wò kplii ɖeɖe ko dome.
ENGLISH: 15 Beware of pretended prophets who come to you in the garb of sheep but are rapacious wolves inside.

EWE: Ne eɖo to wò la, ekema èɖe nɔviwò. 16 Ke ne meɖo to wò o la, kplɔ ame ɖeka alo eve kpe ɖe ɖokuiwò ŋu, ale be le ɖasefo eve alo etɔ̃ ƒe ɖaseɖiɖi nu la, miaɖo kpe nya sia nya dzi. 17 Ne meɖo to woawo hã o la, ekema gblɔe na hamea.
ENGLISH: 16 You will recognize them by their fruits: do people pick grapes from thorns or figs from cockleburs? 17 thus every good tree produces good fruit, but a foul tree produces bad fruit.

EWE: 18 "Vavã mele egblɔm na mi be: Nu sia nu si miabla le anyigba dzi la anye nu si wobla xoxo le dziƒo, eye nu sia nu si miatu le anyigba dzi la anye nu si wotu xoxo le dziƒo.
ENGLISH: 18 A good tree cannot bear bad fruit, nor a foul tree good fruit.

EWE: 19 Megale egblɔm na mi hã be: Ne mia dometɔ eve wɔ ɖeka le anyigba dzi ɖe kuku bia nane si hiã vevie la, Fofonye si le dziƒo la ana wòava eme.
ENGLISH: 19 Every tree that does not produce good fruit is cut out and thrown into a fire.

EWE: 20 Elabena afi si ame eve alo etɔ̃ ƒo ƒu ɖo le nye ŋkɔ me la, mele wo dome le afi ma. "
ENGLISH: 20 Hence you will recognize them by their fruits.

EWE: 21 Eye Petro va biae be: "Aƒetɔ, zi nenie nɔvinye awɔ nu vɔ̃ ɖe ŋunye eye matsɔe akee? Va se ɖe zi adre loo? " 22 Yesu gblɔ nɛ be: "Nyemegblɔ na wò be va se ɖe zi adre o, ke boŋ va se ɖe zi blaadre vɔ adre. 23 "Esia tae wotsɔ Dziƒofiaɖuƒe la sɔ kple fia aɖe si di be yeabu akɔnta kple yeƒe kluviwo.
ENGLISH: 21 Not everyone who says to me ‘Lord, Lord’ will get into the Reign of Heaven, but he who does the will of my Father in heaven: 22 many will say to me in that day ‘Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy by your name and expel demons by your name and work many miracles by your name?’ 23 and then ‘I will avow to them ‘I never knew you; begone from me, you that practice wickedness.’

EWE: 24 Esi wòte akɔntaa bubu la, wokplɔ ŋutsu aɖe si nyi talento akpe ewo ƒe fe le eŋu la vɛ. 25 Ke esi naneke mele esi wòatsɔ axe fea o ta la, eƒe aƒetɔ ɖe gbe be woadzra eya ŋutɔ, srɔ̃a kple viawo kpakple nu siwo katã le esi la atsɔ axe fe lae.
ENGLISH: 24 "So everyone who hears these words of mine and does them will resemble a sensible man who built his house on the rock; 25 and the rain came down and the rivers ran and the winds blew, and they struck against that house and it did not fall, for it was founded on the rock.

EWE: 26 Ale kluvi la bɔbɔ ɖe eŋkume ɖe kuku nɛ gblɔ be, ‘Meɖe kuku, gbɔ dzi ɖi nam, mele nu sia nu xe ge na wò.’ 27 Esi kluvi ma ƒe nu wɔ nublanui na eƒe aƒetɔa la, eɖe asi le eŋu hetsɔ fe la kee.
ENGLISH: 26 And everyone that hears these words of mine and does not do them will resemble a foolish man who built his house on the sand; 27 and the rain came down and the rivers ran and the winds blew, and they beat against that house and it fell, and its fall was great. "

EWE: 31 Esi ehati kluviwo kpɔ nu si dzɔ la, eve wo ŋutɔ, eye woyi ɖagblɔ nu siwo katã dzɔ la na woƒe aƒetɔ. 32 Eya ta eƒe aƒetɔa yɔe va eɖokui gbɔ gblɔ nɛ be: ‘Kluvi vɔ̃ɖi, esi nèɖe kuku nam la, metsɔ fe mawo katã ke wò.
ENGLISH: 28 And when Jesus had finished these words the crowds were astonished at his teaching; 29 for he taught them as having authority, and not like their scribes.

EWE: Mateo
ENGLISH: Matthew

EWE: 2 Ameha geɖewo hã dze eyome, eye wòda gbe le wo ŋu le afi ma.
ENGLISH: 8 And when he came down from the mountain great crowds followed him.

EWE: Eya ŋuti nu si Mawu bla ɖekae la, ame aɖeke megama eme o. " 7 Wogblɔ nɛ be: "Ke nu ka tae Mose de se be woana srɔ̃gbegbalẽ nyɔnua eye woagbee? " 8 Egblɔ na wo be: "Miaƒe dzimesesẽ tae Mose ɖe mɔ na mi be miagbe mia srɔ̃wo ɖo, gake menye nenemae wòle tso gɔmedzedzea me o.
ENGLISH: 2 And lo, a leper approached him and did him reverence, saying "Sir, if you will you can cleanse me. " 3 And he reached out his hand and touched him, saying "I will; be cleansed "; and at once his leprosy was cleansed.

EWE: 9 Mele egblɔm na mi be, ame sia ame si gbe srɔ̃a, ne menye le ahasiwɔwɔ ta o, eye wòɖe bubu la, ewɔ ahasi. "
ENGLISH: 4 And Jesus said to him "See that you do not tell anybody, but go show yourself to the priest and offer the gift that Moses directed, for an attestation to them. "

EWE: 10 Nusrɔ̃lawo gblɔ nɛ be: "Ne aleae ŋutsu kple srɔ̃a dome nya le la, ekema manyo be woaɖe srɔ̃ o ɖe! " 11 Yesu gblɔ na wo be: "Menye amewo katãe tea ŋu wɔna ɖe nya sia dzi o, negbe ame siwo si nunana ma le la ko.
ENGLISH: 5 And when he came into Capernaum a centurion approached him, appealing to him with the words 6 "Sir, my boy is in the house down with paralysis and suffering frightful tortures. " 7 He said to him "I will come and cure him. " 8 But the centurion answered "Sir, I am not fit to have you come under my roof, but just say the word and my boy will be healed.

EWE: 12 Elabena ame tata aɖewo li siwo wodzi nenema, eye ame tata aɖewo li siwo amewo ta, eye ame tata aɖewo hã li siwo wɔ wo ɖokuiwo ame tatawoe le Dziƒofiaɖuƒe la ta.
ENGLISH: 9 For I too am a man under authority, with soldiers under me; and I say to this one ‘Go,’ and he goes; and to another ‘Come,’ and he comes; and to my servant ‘Do this,’ and he does it. " 10 And at hearing it Jesus wondered, and said to those who were following "I tell you verily, I have not found in Israel so much faith shown by anyone.

EWE: Ame si ate ŋui la, newɔe. " 13 Azɔ wokplɔ ɖevi suewo va egbɔ be wòada asi ɖe wo dzi eye wòado gbe ɖa ɖe wo ta, ke nusrɔ̃lawo blu ɖe wo ta.
ENGLISH: 11 But I tell you many will come from the east and the west and go to the table with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob in the Reign of Heaven, 12 but the native sons of the Reign will be put out into the outside darkness; there will the weeping and the grinding of teeth be. " 13 And Jesus said to the centurion "Go, have it as you believed "; and the boy was healed at that moment.

EWE: 14 Gake Yesu gblɔ be: "Miɖe asi le ɖeviawo ŋu, mina woava gbɔnye, eye migaxe mɔ na wo o, elabena ame siawo ƒomevi tɔe nye Dziƒofiaɖuƒe la. " 15 Eda asi ɖe wo dzi, eye wòdzo le afi ma.
ENGLISH: 14 And Jesus came into Peter’s house and saw his mother-in-law down with a fever; 15 and he touched her hand, and the fever left her, and she rose and waited on his needs.

EWE: 16 Azɔ kpɔ ɖa, ame aɖe va egbɔ hebiae be: "Nufiala, nu nyui kae wòle be mawɔ be makpɔ agbe mavɔ? " 17 Egblɔ nɛ be: "Nu ka tae nèle nya biamem tso nu si nye nyui ŋu? Ame ɖeka pɛ koe nye ame nyui.
ENGLISH: 16 And when evening was come they brought him many demoniacs; and he expelled the spirits by his word, and cured all that were ill, 17 so that what was said through the prophet Isaiah in the words "He took our sicknesses and carried our diseases " should be fulfilled.

EWE: Ke ne èdi be yeayi ɖe agbe la me la, yi edzi nànɔ seawo dzi wɔm. " 18 Ebiae be: "Kawo? "
ENGLISH: 18 But Jesus, seeing a crowd around him, gave the word to go off to the other side.

EWE: Yesu gblɔ be: "Woawoe nye: Mègawu ame o, mègawɔ ahasi o, mègafi fi o, mègaɖi aʋatsoɖase o, 19 bu fofowò kple dawò, kple lɔ̃ hawòvi abe wò ŋutɔ ɖokuiwò ene. " 20 Ðekakpui la gblɔ nɛ be: "Mewɔa se siawo katã dzi; nu kae gasusɔ nam? " 21 Yesu gblɔ nɛ be: "Ne èdi be yeazu blibo la, yi nàdzra nu siwo le asiwò la nàtsɔ ga la ana ame dahewo, ekema kesinɔnuwo anɔ asiwò le dziƒo; eye nàva dze yonyeme. " 22 Esi ɖekakpuia se nya sia la, edzo kple nuxaxa, elabena nu geɖe le esi.
ENGLISH: 19 And a scribe approached him and said to him "Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go. " 20 And Jesus said to him "The foxes have dens and the birds of the air have roosts, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head. " 21 And another of his disciples said to him "Sir, permit me first to go and bury my father. " 22 But Jesus said to him "Follow me, and leave the dead to bury their dead. "

EWE: 23 Eye Yesu gblɔ na eƒe nusrɔ̃lawo be: "Vavã mele egblɔm na mi be, asesẽ na kesinɔtɔ be wòayi ɖe Dziƒofiaɖuƒe la me.
ENGLISH: 23 And when he got into the boat his disciples followed him.

EWE: 24 Megale egblɔm na mi hã be: Ele bɔbɔe na kposɔ be wòato abui ƒe vo me wu be kesinɔtɔ nayi ɖe Mawu Fiaɖuƒe la me. "
ENGLISH: 24 And lo, there came a great commotion in the sea, so that the boat was being covered by the waves; and he was asleep.

EWE: 25 Esi nusrɔ̃lawo se nya sia la, ewɔ nuku na wo ŋutɔ, eye wobia be: "Ke ame ka gɔ̃e ate ŋu akpɔ ɖeɖe? " 26 Yesu kpɔ woƒe ŋkume dũu, eye wògblɔ na wo be: "Amegbetɔwo gbɔ la, manya wɔ be woawɔ esia o; ke Mawu ya tea ŋu wɔa nu sia nu. "
ENGLISH: 25 And they approached him and roused him, saying "Help, sir! we are lost! " 26 And he said to them "Why are you timorous, little-faiths? " Then he rose and rebuked the winds and the sea, and there came a great calm.

EWE: 27 Eye Petro biae be: "Kpɔ ɖa!
ENGLISH: 27 But the men wondered, saying "What a man this is, that even the winds and the sea obey him! "

EWE: Míegblẽ nuwo katã ɖi hedze yowòme; ke nu kae ava nye mía tɔ? " 28 Yesu gblɔ na wo be: "Vavã mele egblɔm na mi be: Le nuwo gbugbɔwɔɣi, ne Amegbetɔvi la bɔbɔ nɔ eƒe ŋutikɔkɔefiazikpui dzi la, mi ame siwo dze yonyeme hã mianɔ anyi ɖe fiazikpui wuieve dzi adrɔ̃ ʋɔnu Israel to wuieveawo.
ENGLISH: 28 And when he came to the other side, to the country of the Gadarenes, there met him two demoniacs coming out of the tombs, exceedingly intractable, so that nobody was able to pass along that road; 29 and lo, they screamed out "What have we to do with you, Son of God? have you come here to torture us before it is time? " 30 And a long way off from them there was a numerous herd of hogs feeding; 31 and the demons appealed to him with the request "If you are expelling us, send us into the herd of hogs. " 32 And he said to them "Go. "

EWE: 29 Eye ame sia ame si gblẽ aƒewo alo nɔviŋutsuwo alo nɔvinyɔnuwo alo fofo alo dada alo viwo alo agblewo ɖi le nye ŋkɔ ta la, akpɔ wo ɖe eteƒe zi alafa, eye wòanyi agbe mavɔ dome.
ENGLISH: And they came out and went into the hogs, and lo, all the herd bolted down the steep bank into the sea, and lost their lives in the water; 33 and the men who were tending them ran away, and went to the city and reported everything, including the part about the demoniacs.

EWE: 30 "Ke ame geɖe siwo nye gbãtɔwo azu mlɔetɔwo, eye mlɔetɔwo azu gbãtɔwo.
ENGLISH: 34 And out came all the city to meet Jesus; and when they saw him they appealed to him to pass on away from their territory;

ENGLISH: Matthew

EWE: 20 "Elabena Dziƒofiaɖuƒe la le abe aƒetɔ aɖe si do go ŋdi kanya be yeaɖadi apatɔwo woawɔ dɔ le yeƒe waingble me ene.
ENGLISH: 9 and he got into a boat and crossed over and came to his own city.

EWE: 2 Esi wòƒo asi kple dɔwɔlawo eye wolɔ̃ be wòaxe denario ɖeka na yewo ŋkeke ɖeka vɔ la, eɖo wo ɖe eƒe waingble la me.
ENGLISH: 2 And lo, they brought him a paralyzed man lying helpless on a couch.

EWE: 3 Esi wògado go le gaƒoƒo etɔ̃lia me lɔƒo la, ekpɔ ame bubuwo le tsitre ɖe asi me siwo mele dɔ aɖeke wɔm o; 4 eye wògblɔ na wo be: ‘Miawo hã miyi waingble la me, eye maxe fe si dze la na mi.’ 5 Eya ta woyi. Egado go le gaƒoƒo adelia kple asiekelia me lɔƒo, eye wòwɔ nenema ke. 6 Mlɔeba le gaƒoƒo wuiɖekɛlia me lɔƒo la, edo go, eye wòkpɔ ame bubuwo le tsitre ɖi, eye wòbia wo be, ‘Nu ka tae miele tsitre ɖe afi sia ŋkeke bliboa katã dɔ aɖeke mawɔmawɔe?’ 7 Woɖo eŋu nɛ be: ‘Elabena ame aɖeke metsɔ mí be míawɔ dɔ na ye o.’
ENGLISH: And Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralyzed man "It is all right, my child, your sins are forgiven. " 3 Said some of the scribes to themselves, "This man is blaspheming. " 4 And Jesus, knowing their thoughts, said "What are you inwardly thinking wicked thoughts for? 5 why, which is easier, to say ‘your sins are forgiven’ or to say ‘rise and walk’? 6 But, that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins " then he said to the paralyzed man, "Rise, take up your couch and go home. " 7 And he rose and went off to his home.

EWE: Egblɔ na wo be: ‘Miawo hã miyi waingble la me.’
ENGLISH: 8 And at this sight the crowds were afraid and glorified God who had given such authority to men.

EWE: 8 "Esi fiẽsi ɖo la, waingbletɔa gblɔ na eƒe nuwo dzi kpɔla be, ‘Yɔ dɔwɔlawo nàxe fe na wo, eye nàdze egɔme tso ame mlɔetɔwo dzi va se ɖe gbãtɔwo dzi.’ 9 Esi gaƒoƒo wuiɖekɛlia me tɔwo va la, wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe xɔ denario ɖeka.
ENGLISH: 9 And in passing on his way from there Jesus saw sitting in a customhouse office a man known as Matthew, and said to him "Follow me "; and he rose and followed him.

EWE: 10 Eya ta esi ame gbãtɔwo va la, wosusu be yewoaxɔ wòasɔ gbɔ wu, ke woxe denario ɖekaɖeka na woawo hã.
ENGLISH: 10 And as he was eating a meal in the house, there came to the table with Jesus and his disciples many customhouse officers and people of bad character.

EWE: 11 Esi woxɔe la, woto nyatoƒoe le aƒetɔ la ŋu 12 be: ‘Ame mlɔetɔ siawo wɔ dɔ gaƒoƒo ɖeka ko; ke èna wosɔ kple mí ame siwo kpe fu wɔ dɔ sesĩe le ŋdɔgbe ŋkeke bliboa katã!’ 13 Ke eɖo eŋu na wo dometɔ ɖeka be: ‘Xɔ̃, nyemedze agɔ le dziwò o ɖe.
ENGLISH: 11 And the Pharisees, seeing it, said to his disciples "Why does your teacher eat with the customhouse officers and people of bad character? " 12 But he, hearing it, said "Not the able-bodied, but the ill, need a physician.

EWE: Denario ɖeka dzie nye kpli wò míelɔ̃ ɖoe? 14 Xɔ tɔwò nàdzo.
ENGLISH: 13 But go and learn what ‘I want pity, and not sacrifice’ is; for I have not come to call saints, but sinners. "

EWE: Melɔ̃ be maxe fe na ame mlɔetɔ siawo abe ale si mexee na wòe ene. 15 Ðe nyemekpɔ mɔ azã nye ŋutɔ nye nuwo ale si melɔ̃ oa?
ENGLISH: 14 Then John’s disciples came to him with the words "Why is it that we and the Pharisees fast, but your disciples do not? " 15 And Jesus said to them "Can the wedding guests mourn, as long as the bridegroom is with them? but there will come days, when the bridegroom is taken from them, and then they will fast.

EWE: Alo nyui si mewɔ lae na nèle ŋu ʋãma?’ 16 Aleae mlɔetɔwo azu gbãtɔwo, eye gbãtɔwo azu mlɔetɔwo. "
ENGLISH: 16 But nobody puts a patch of unfulled cloth on an old cloak; for the filler takes away some from the cloak, and a worse hole is made.

EWE: Yesu ɖo eŋu na wo be: "Ɛ̃. Ðe miexlẽe kpɔ be, ‘Ðeviwo kple vi nonowo ƒe nu me nèdzra kafukafu ɖo’ oa? " 17 Eye wògblẽ wo ɖi hedo go le dua me yi Betania, eye wòtsi afi ma dɔ.
ENGLISH: 17 Neither do they put new wine in old skins; if they do, the skins burst, and the wine runs out and the skins are wasted; but they put new wine into fresh skins, and both together are preserved. "

EWE: 18 Esi wòtrɔ yina dua me le ŋdi kanya la, dɔ wui. 19 Ekpɔ gboti aɖe le mɔ to eye wòte ɖe eŋu, ke mekpɔ naneke le edzi o negbe aŋgbawo ko, eye wògblɔ nɛ be: "Màgatse akpɔ gbeɖegbeɖe o. " Eye gboti la yrɔ enumake.
ENGLISH: 18 While he was telling them this, lo, a ruler approached him and did him reverence, saying "My daughter is just passing away; but come and lay your hand on her, and she will live. " 19 And Jesus and his disciples rose and followed the man.

EWE: 20 Esi nusrɔ̃lawo kpɔ esia la, ewɔ nuku na wo, eye wobia be: "Aleke wɔ gboti la yrɔ enumake? " 21 Yesu ɖo eŋu na wo be: "Vavã mele egblɔm na mi be: Ne xɔse le mia si, eye mieke ɖi o la, menye nu si mewɔ gboti la ɖeɖe koe miawɔ o, ke boŋ ne miegblɔ na to sia be, ‘Ho nàyi aɖadze atsiaƒu me’ la, ava eme.
ENGLISH: 20 And lo, a woman who had had a flow of blood for twelve years came up behind and touched the tassel of his cloak; 21 for she said to herself, "If I only touch his cloak I shall be made well. " 22 But Jesus turned and saw her and said "It is all right, daughter, your faith has made you well. "

EWE: 22 Eye ne xɔse le mia si la, nu sia nu si miado gbe ɖa abia la, miaxɔe. "
ENGLISH: And the woman was well from that moment.

EWE: 23 Ke esi wòyi gbedoxɔa me hele nu fiam la, nunɔlawo ƒe tatɔwo kple dumegãwo va egbɔ, eye wobiae be: "Ŋusẽ kae nètsɔ wɔa nu siawo? Eye ame kae na ŋusẽ sia wò? " 24 Yesu ɖo eŋu na wo be: "Nye hã mabia nya ɖeka mi.
ENGLISH: 23 And when Jesus came into the ruler’s house and saw the flute-players, and the crowd making a commotion, 24 he said "Stand aside, for the girl is not dead but asleep "; and they laughed at him.

EWE: Ne mieɖo eŋu nam la, ekema nye hã magblɔ ŋusẽ si metsɔ wɔa nu siawoe la na mi: 25 Yohanes ƒe amenyɔnyrɔ ɖe tsi me la ɖe, afi kae wòtso?
ENGLISH: 25 But when the crowd was put out he went in and grasped her hand, and the girl woke up.

EWE: Dziƒoe wòtso loo alo amegbetɔwo gbɔe? "
ENGLISH: 26 And the rumor of this went out to that whole land.

EWE: Ke woda nyaa kpɔ le wo nɔewo dome gblɔ be: "Ne míegblɔ be, ‘Dziƒoe wòtso’ la, abia mí be, ‘Ekema nu ka tae miexɔ edzi se o?’ 26 Ke ne míegblɔ be, ‘Etso amewo gbɔ la,’ ke míedɔ̃ le ameha la si me, elabena wo katã wobua Yohanes nyagblɔɖilae. " 27 Eya ta woɖo eŋu na Yesu be: "Míenya o. "
ENGLISH: 27 And as Jesus was passing on his way from there two blind men followed him, crying out "Take pity on us, Son of David. " 28 And when he came into the house the blind men came up to him; and Jesus said to them "Do you believe I can do this? "

EWE: Vi eve le ŋutsu aɖe si. Eye wòyi gbãtɔ gbɔ ɖagblɔ nɛ be, ‘Vinye, yi ɖawɔ dɔ le waingble la me egbe.’ 29 Eɖo eŋu be, ‘Nyemayi o,’ ke emegbe la evee eye wòyi.
ENGLISH: They said to him "Yes, sir. " 29 Then he touched their eyes, saying "Have it as you have faith for "; 30 and their eyes were opened.

EWE: Eya ɖo eŋu be, ‘Mayi,’ ke meyi o. 31 Ame eve siawo dometɔ kae wɔ fofoa ƒe lɔlɔ̃nu? " Woɖo eŋu be: "Gbãtɔe. "
ENGLISH: And Jesus said to them sternly "See that nobody finds it out. " 31 But they went out and spread the report about him in that whole land.

EWE: Yesu gblɔ na wo be: "Vavã mele egblɔm na mi be, adzɔxɔlawo kple gbolowo atre Mawu Fiaɖuƒe la me yiyi na mi. 32 Elabena Yohanes va mia gbɔ be yeafia dzɔdzɔenyenyemɔ la mi, ke miexɔ edzi se o.
ENGLISH: 32 And as these were going out, lo, they brought him a dumb man who was demon-ridden; 33 and when the demon was expelled the dumb man spoke.

EWE: 33 "Mise lododo bubu ɖa: Aƒetɔ aɖe de waingble, eye wòtɔ kpɔ ƒo xlãe, ewɔ wainfiãƒe ɖe eme, eye wòtu agbledzɔxɔ ɖe eme; etsɔe de asi na agbledelawo, eye wòzɔ mɔ yi duta. 34 Esi nuŋeɣi ɖo la, edɔ eƒe kluviwo ɖe agbledelawo gbɔ be woaxɔ yeƒe kutsetsewo avɛ.
ENGLISH: And the crowds wondered, saying "Never was the like seen in Israel "; 34 but the Pharisees said "It is by having the head of the demons that he expels the demons. "

EWE: 35 Ke agbledelaawo lé eƒe kluviawo, woƒo ɖeka, wowu ɖeka, eye woƒu kpe bubu wòku.
ENGLISH: 35 And Jesus went the round of all the cities and villages, teaching in their synagogues and proclaiming the gospel of the Reign and curing every disease and every ailment.

ENGLISH: 37 Then he said to his disciples "The crop to harvest is great, but the workers are few; 38 so beg the owner of the crop to send out workers to his harvest ";

EWE: Mateo
ENGLISH: Matthew

EWE: 22 Yesu gado lo bubu na wo be: 2 "Dziƒofiaɖuƒe la le abe fia aɖe si ɖo srɔ̃ɖekplɔ̃ na via ene.
ENGLISH: 10 and, calling to him his twelve disciples, he gave them authority over unclean spirits to expel them, and to cure every disease and every ailment.

EWE: 3 Eye wòdɔ eƒe kluviwo be woaɖayɔ ame siwo wokpe la ava srɔ̃ɖekplɔ̃a ŋu, gake womelɔ̃ be yewoava o. 4 Egadɔ kluvi bubuwo ɖa gblɔ be, ‘Migblɔ na ame kpekpeawo be: "Kpɔ ɖa, ŋdɔnuɖuɖua sɔ gbe vɔ, wowu nye nyitsuwo kple lã damiwo, eye nu sia nu sɔ gbe.
ENGLISH: 2 And these are the names of the twelve apostles: first Simon known as Peter, and his brother Andrew, and James the son of Zebedee and his brother John, 3 Philip and Bartholomew, Thomas and Matthew the customhouse officer, James the son of Alpheus and Thaddeus, 4 Simon the Kananee and Judas Iscariot the same who was the agent in his arrest.

EWE: Miva srɔ̃ɖeŋkekenyuia ɖuƒe. "’ 5 Ke wometsɔ ɖeke le eme o, eye wodzo, ame ɖeka yi eƒe agble me, bubu yi eƒe adzɔ do ge; 6 ke mamlɛawo lé eƒe kluviawo, wɔ fu wo eye wowu wo.
ENGLISH: 5 These twelve Jesus sent out, instructing them thus:

EWE: 7 "Ale fia la do dziku, eye wòdɔ eƒe aʋakɔwo ɖa woyi ɖawu amewula mawo eye wotɔ dzo woƒe du la.
ENGLISH: "Do not go off on any route among the nations nor into a city of the Samaritans; 6 go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, 7 and as you go proclaim that the Reign of Heaven is almost here.

EWE: 8 Eye wògblɔ na eƒe kluviawo be, ‘Nu sia nu sɔ gbe na srɔ̃ɖeŋkekenyuia ɖuɖu, gake ame siwo wokpe la medze o.
ENGLISH: 8 Cure sick men, raise dead men, cleanse lepers, expel demons. You received gratis, give gratis.

EWE: 9 Eya ta miyi dua ƒe mɔ gãwo dzi ne miakpe ame sia ame si miakpɔ la va srɔ̃ɖeŋkekenyuia ɖuƒe.’ 10 Ale kluvi mawo do go yi mɔwo dzi, eye woƒo ame siwo katã wokpɔ la nu ƒu, ame vɔ̃ɖiwo kple ame nyuiwo siaa; ale amewo yɔ srɔ̃ɖekplɔ̃a ŋu fũu le xɔ si me wole srɔ̃a ɖem le la me.
ENGLISH: 9 Do not get gold nor silver nor copper to take in your belts, 10 no traveling-wallet nor two coats nor shoes nor a walking-stick; for a worker deserves his food.

EWE: 11 "Esi fia la va be yealé ŋku ɖe ame kpekpeawo ŋu la, ekpɔ ŋutsu aɖe si medo srɔ̃ɖewu o la le afi ma.
ENGLISH: 11 And whatever city or village you come into, find out who in it is deserving, and stay there till you come out.

EWE: Ke mete ŋu ke nu o. 13 Eye fia la gblɔ na eƒe subɔviwo be, ‘Mibla eƒe asiwo kple afɔwo, eye mitsɔe ƒu gbe ɖe viviti la me le xexe.
ENGLISH: 12 And in coming into the house salute it; 13 and if the house is deserving let your peace come upon it, but if it is not deserving let your peace come back to you.

EWE: Afi mae wòafa avi ahaɖu aɖukli le.’ 14 "Elabena ame geɖewoe wokpe, ke ame ʋɛ aɖewo koe wotia. " 15 Eye Farisitɔwo dzo yi ɖade adaŋu, ne woatsɔ eya ŋutɔ ƒe nyagbɔgblɔ atre mɔ̃ nɛ alée.
ENGLISH: 14 And whoever does not receive you nor hear your words, shake out the dust from your feet in coming out from that house or city; 15 I tell you verily, it will be more bearable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment than for that city.

EWE: 16 Eya ta wodɔ woƒe nusrɔ̃lawo kple Herodes habɔbɔ me nɔlawo ɖe egbɔ gblɔ be: "Nufiala, míenyae be ètoa nyateƒe, èfiaa Mawu ƒe mɔ la le nyateƒe me, eye mèdea ame dzi o, elabena mèwɔa nu ɖe ale si amewo dzena le gotae la nu o. 17 Eya ta gblɔe na mí: Nu kae nèsusu?
ENGLISH: 16 "Here I am sending you out like sheep among wolves; so be as cunning as snakes and as innocent as doves.

EWE: Ðe se ɖe mɔ be míaxe adzɔ na Kaisaro loo alo se meɖe mɔ o? " 18 Ke esi Yesu kpɔ woƒe vɔɖivɔ̃ɖi dze sii la, egblɔ be: "Alakpanuwɔlawo, nu ka tae miele mɔ̃ trem nam? 19 Mitsɔ gaku si wotsɔna xea adzɔ la vɛ makpɔ. "
ENGLISH: 17 But beware of men; for they will have you arrested and taken into court, and flogged in their synagogues; 18 and you will be brought before governors and kings on my account, for an attestation to them and the nations.

EWE: Wotsɔ denario ɖeka vɛ nɛ. 20 Eye wòbia wo be: "Ame ka ƒe nɔnɔmetata kple nuŋɔŋlɔe nye esia? " 21 Wogblɔ be: "Kaisaro tɔe. "
ENGLISH: 19 But when they have you arrested, do not fret over how or what you are to speak; for it will be given to you at that moment what to speak, 20 for it is not you that speak but your Father’s Spirit that speaks in you.

EWE: Eye wògblɔ na wo be: "Ekema mitsɔ nu siwo nye Kaisaro tɔ la na Kaisaro, ke mitsɔ nu siwo nye Mawu tɔ la na Mawu. " 22 Esi wose esia la, woƒe nu ku, eye wogblẽe ɖi dzo.
ENGLISH: 21 "And a brother will have a brother arrested and put to death, and a father a child; and children will stand up against parents and have them put to death; 22 and you will be hated by all because of my name; but he who holds out to the end, he will come safe through.

EWE: 23 Gbe ma gbe Zadukitɔwo, ame siwo gblɔna be tsitretsitsi aɖeke meli o la, va biae be: 24 "Nufiala, Mose gblɔ be: ‘Ne ŋutsu aɖe ku, evɔ vi mele esi o la, nɔviaŋutsu naxɔ srɔ̃a aɖe ne wòado ƒome ɖi nɛ.’ 25 Nɔviŋutsu adre nɔ mía dome.
ENGLISH: 23 But when they persecute you in this city flee to the other; for I tell you verily you will not finish the cities of Israel till the Son of Man comes. 24 "A pupil is not above his teacher nor a servant above his master.

EWE: Gbãtɔa ɖe srɔ̃ eye wòku, gake esi medzi vi aɖeke o ta la, nɔvia xɔ nyɔnua ɖe.
ENGLISH: 25 It is sufficient for the pupil that he be made like his teacher, and the servant like his master.

EWE: 26 Nu ma kee dzɔ ɖe evelia kple etɔ̃lia dzi va se ɖe wo ame adrea katã dzi.
ENGLISH: If they have dubbed the head of the house Beelzebul, how much more will they the rest of his family! 26 So do not fear them.

EWE: 27 Mlɔeba nyɔnua hã ku.
ENGLISH: 27 What I tell you in the dark, say in the light; and what you hear whispered in your ear, proclaim on the roofs.

EWE: 28 Eya ta le tsitretsitsia me ɖe, ŋutsu adreawo dometɔ ka srɔ̃ wòanye? Elabena wo katã woɖee kpɔ. "
ENGLISH: 28 And do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul, but fear rather him who can destroy both soul and body in hell.

EWE: 29 Yesu ɖo eŋu na wo be: "Mieda ƒu, elabena mienya Ŋɔŋlɔawo loo alo Mawu ƒe ŋusẽ la o; 30 elabena le tsitretsitsia me la, ŋutsuwo maɖe srɔ̃ o, eye womatsɔ nyɔnuwo ana be woaɖe o, ke boŋ woanɔ abe mawudɔla siwo le dziƒo la ene.
ENGLISH: 29 Why, sparrows are sold two for a penny, and not one of them will fall to the earth without your Father; 30 but of your heads even the hairs are all counted; 31 so do not fear, you are more important than a great many sparrows.

EWE: 31 Ke le ame kukuwo ƒe tsitretsitsi ŋuti la, ɖe miexlẽ nya si Mawu gblɔ na mi be: 32 ‘Nyee nye Abraham ƒe Mawu, Isak ƒe Mawu kple Yakob ƒe Mawu’ la oa?
ENGLISH: 32 Everyone who shall acknowledge me before men, then, I myself will acknowledge before my Father in heaven; 33 but whoever repudiates me before men I myself will repudiate before my Father in heaven.

EWE: Menye ame kukuwo ƒe Mawue wònye o, ke boŋ agbagbeawo tɔe. " 33 Esi amehaawo se nya siawo la, woƒe nu ku le ale si wòfia nui ta. 34 Esi Farisitɔwo se be etsi nya ɖe Zadukitɔwo nu la, wolɔ hoo va.
ENGLISH: 34 "Do not suppose that I came to launch peace on the earth: I did not come to launch peace, but the sword, 35 for I came to put a man in antagonism to his father and a daughter to her mother and a daughter-in-law to her mother-in-law, 36 and the members of a man’s family shall be his enemies.

EWE: 35 Esi wo dometɔ ɖeka si nya Sea nyuie la di be yeadoe kpɔ la, ebiae be: 36 "Nufiala, sedede kae nye gãtɔ le Se la me? " 37 Egblɔ nɛ be: "‘Lɔ̃ Yehowa wò Mawu kple wò dzi blibo kple wò luʋɔ blibo kpakple wò tamesusu blibo.’ 38 Esiae nye sedede gãtɔ kple gbãtɔ.
ENGLISH: 37 He who loves father or mother above me is not worthy of me; and he who loves son or daughter above me is not worthy of me; 38 and he who does not take his cross and follow after me is not worthy of me.

EWE: 39 Evelia si ɖii lae nye esi: ‘Lɔ̃ hawòvi abe wò ŋutɔ ɖokuiwò ene.’ 40 Wotu Se blibo la katã kple nyagblɔɖilawo ƒe nyawo ɖe sedede eve siawo dzi. "
ENGLISH: 39 He who finds his self shall lose it, and he who loses his self on my account shall find it. 40 "He who receives you is receiving me, and he who receives me is receiving him who sent me.

EWE: 41 Ke esi Farisitɔwo ƒo ƒu la, Yesu bia wo be: 42 "Nu kae miesusu le Kristo la ŋu? Ame ka vie wònye? " Woɖo eŋu nɛ be: "David vie. " 43 Egabia wo be: "Ekema aleke wɔ gbɔgbɔ ʋã David wòyɔe be ‘Aƒetɔ,’ esi wògblɔ be: 44 ‘Yehowa gblɔ na nye Aƒetɔ be: "Bɔbɔ nɔ nye ɖusime va se ɖe esime matsɔ wò futɔwo ade wò afɔ te "’? 45 Azɔ ne David yɔe be ‘Aƒetɔ’ ɖe, ke aleke wɔ wònye via? " 46 Ame aɖeke mete ŋu ɖo nya ŋu nɛ o, eye tso gbe ma gbe la, ame aɖeke mete ŋu do dzi gabia nya bubu aɖekee o.
ENGLISH: 41 He who receives a prophet as being a prophet shall get a prophet’s reward, and he who receives a saint as being a saint shall get a saint’s reward; 42 and anybody who gives one of these little ones just a cup of cold water to drink as being a disciple, I tell you verily, shall not lose his reward. "

EWE: Mateo
ENGLISH: Matthew

EWE: 3 Eya ta miwɔ nu siwo katã wogblɔna na mi la, eye milé wo me ɖe asi, ke migakpɔ woƒe nuwɔna miawɔ o, elabena wogblɔnɛ, gake womewɔa nu si wogblɔna la dzi o.
ENGLISH: 11 And when Jesus had finished giving directions to his twelve disciples he passed on from there to teach and make the proclamation in their cities.

EWE: 4 Woblaa agba kpekpewo tsɔ ɖoa amewo ƒe abɔta, gake woawo ŋutɔwo medina be yewoƒe asibidɛ ɖeka teti naka wo ŋu o. 5 Dɔ siwo katã wowɔna la, wowɔnɛ be amewo nakpɔ; elabena wowɔa nugoe siwo me ŋɔŋlɔawo le la wòkekena eye woblaa wo ɖe ŋgonu kple abɔ be woakpɔ yewo ta, eye wowɔa woƒe awu togawo wòdidina.
ENGLISH: 2 And John, hearing in his prison the deeds of the Messiah, sent by his disciples 3 and said to him "Are you the Coming One or are we to expect another? " 4 And Jesus answered them "Go and report to John what you hear and see: 5 blind men are recovering their sight and cripples are walking, lepers are being cleansed and deaf men are hearing, and dead men are being raised and poor men are being given the gospel; 6 and happy is anyone who is not staggered over me. "

EWE: 6 Wolɔ̃a bubunɔƒewo nɔnɔ le fiẽnuɖuƒewo kple ŋgɔgbezikpuiwo dzi nɔnɔ le ƒuƒoƒewo, 7 eye wodina be amewo nado gbe na yewo bubutɔe le ablɔwo me, eye woayɔ yewo be Rabi. 8 Ke miawo la, migana woayɔ mi be Rabi o, elabena ame ɖeka koe nye miaƒe Nufiala, ke mi katã la, nɔviwo mienye.
ENGLISH: 7 And while these were on their way Jesus began to say to the crowds about John "What did you go out into the wilderness for? to gaze at reeds shaking in the wind? 8 But what did you go out for? to see a man robed in soft fabrics? for the wearers of soft fabrics, go to kings’ houses.

EWE: 9 Eye migayɔ ame aɖeke be mia fofo le anyigba dzi hã o, elabena ame ɖekae nye mia Fofo, Ame si le dziƒo.
ENGLISH: 9 But what did you go out for? to see a prophet?

EWE: 10 Eye womegayɔ mi be kplɔlawo hã o, elabena ame ɖekae nye miaƒe Kplɔla, eyae nye Kristo la. 11 Ke ame si nye gãtɔ le mia dome la nanye miaƒe subɔla.
ENGLISH: Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet; 10 this is he of whom it is written ‘Lo, I am sending before your face my messenger who shall prepare your road before you,’ 11 I tell you verily, there has not arisen among all that are born of women a greater than John the Baptist; but the littlest in the Reign of Heaven is greater than he.

EWE: 12 Ame si doa eɖokui ɖe dzi la, woabɔbɔe ɖe anyi, eye ame si bɔbɔa eɖokui la, woadoe ɖe dzi.
ENGLISH: 12 But from John the Baptist’s days till now the Reign of Heaven is being forced and violent men are pouncing on it.

EWE: 16 "Baba na mi, mɔfiala ŋkuagbãtɔwo, mi ame siwo gblɔna be, ‘Ne ame aɖe tà gbedoxɔa la, mehiã be wòawɔ edzi o; ke ne ame aɖe tà sika si le gbedoxɔa me ya la, ele be wòawɔ eƒe atam la dzi godoo.’ 17 Movitɔwo kple ŋkuagbãtɔwo! Mibu eŋu kpɔ, kae le vevie wu, sika la loo alo gbedoxɔ si na sika la ŋuti kɔ yea? 18 Miegblɔna hã be, ‘Ne ame aɖe tà vɔsamlekpuia la, mehiã be wòawɔ edzi o; ke ne ame aɖe tà nunana si le edzi ya la, ele be wòawɔ edzi godoo.’ 19 Ŋkuagbãtɔwo! Mibu eŋu kpɔ, kae le vevie wu, nunana la loo alo vɔsamlekpui si na nunana la ŋuti kɔ yea? 20 Eya ta ame si tà vɔsamlekpuia la, età vɔsamlekpuia kple nu siwo katã le edzi la siaa; 21 eye ame si tà gbedoxɔa la, età gbedoxɔa kple Ame si le eme la siaa; 22 eye ame si tà dziƒo la, età Mawu ƒe fiazikpui kple Ame si bɔbɔ nɔ edzi la siaa.
ENGLISH: 13 For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John’s coming; 14 and if you are willing to have it, he is the Elijah who was to come; 15 let him who has ears hear! 16 But to what shall I compare this generation? it is like children sitting in the marketplaces, that call out to the others 17 and say ‘We played to you and you did not dance, we lamented and you did not wail.’ 18 For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say ‘He has a demon’; 19 the Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say ‘Here is a gormandizer and a drinker, a friend of customhouse officers and people of bad character’; and wisdom is justified by her works. " 20 Then he began to reproach the cities in which most of his miracles had been done, because they did not repent: 21 "Woe to you, Chorazin! woe to you, Bethsaida! because if the miracles that have been done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon they would have repented in sackcloth and ashes long ago; 22 I tell you, though, it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon at the day of judgment than for you.

EWE: 23 "Baba na mi, agbalẽfialawo kple Farisitɔwo, alakpanuwɔlawo! Elabena mienaa ahamɛ, sikɔni kple adrike ƒe ewolia, ke mieŋea aɖaba ƒua Se la me nu vevitɔwo, siwo nye dzɔdzɔenyenye kple nublanuikpɔkpɔ kpakple nuteƒewɔwɔ dzi. Ehiã be miawɔ nu mawo, gake miagaŋe aɖaba aƒu esiawo hã dzi o. 24 Mɔfiala ŋkuagbãtɔ siwo tsyɔa nu dzodzoe sue, gake mia kposɔ ya!
ENGLISH: 23 And you, Capernaum, are you to be lifted up to heaven? you are to go down to the world of the dead, because if the miracles that have been done in you had been done in Sodom it would have lasted till today; 24 I tell you, though, it will be more bearable for Sodom at the day of judgment than for you. "

EWE: 25 "Baba na mi, agbalẽfialawo kple Farisitɔwo, alakpanuwɔlawo! Elabena mieklɔa kplu kple agba ŋuti, gake wo me yɔ fũu kple ŋukeklẽ kple nu gbɔme wɔwɔ. 26 Farisitɔ ŋkuagbãtɔ, klɔ kplu kple agba la me gbã, ekema eŋu hã aɖi.
ENGLISH: 25 At that time Jesus answered "I give thee praise, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that thou didst hide these things from the wise and discerning and disclose them to infants; 26 yes, Father, because such was thy pleasure.

EWE: 27 "Baba na mi, agbalẽfialawo kple Farisitɔwo, alakpanuwɔlawo! Elabena mieɖi yɔdo siwo wosi akalo na, siwo nya kpɔ ŋutɔ le gota, ke wo me yɔ fũu kple ame kuku ƒuwo kple makɔmakɔnyenye ɖe sia ɖe ƒomevi.
ENGLISH: 27 Everything has been committed to me by my Father; and no one is acquainted with the Son except the Father, nor is anyone acquainted with the Father except the Son and he to whom the Son chooses to disclose him.

EWE: 28 Nenemae miedzena ame dzɔdzɔewoe le gota le amewo ŋkume, gake mia me yɔ fũu kple alakpanuwɔwɔ kple sedzimawɔmawɔ.
ENGLISH: 28 Come to me, all you toilers, all who are loaded down, and I will give you rest.

EWE: 29 "Baba na mi, agbalẽfialawo kple Farisitɔwo, alakpanuwɔlawo!
ENGLISH: 29 Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me, because I am meek and lowly in heart; and you shall find rest for your souls.

EWE: 38 Kpɔ ɖa! Woagblẽ miaƒe aƒe la ɖi na mi.
ENGLISH: 30 For my yoke is easy, and my load light. "

EWE: Mateo
ENGLISH: Matthew

EWE: 2 Egblɔ na wo be: "Miele nu siawo katã kpɔma?
ENGLISH: 12 At that time Jesus went through the grainfields on the sabbath.

EWE: Vavã mele egblɔm na mi be, womele kpe aɖeke gblẽ ge ɖe kpe dzi le afi sia si womamu aƒu anyi o. " 3 Esi wòbɔbɔ nɔ Amitoa dzi la, nusrɔ̃lawo ɖeɖe va egbɔ hebiae be: "Gblɔe na mí, ɣekaɣie nu siawo adzɔ, eye nu kae anye wò anyinɔɣi kple nuɖoanyia ƒe nuwuɣi la ƒe dzesi? " 4 Yesu ɖo eŋu na wo be: "Mikpɔ nyuie be ame aɖeke nagaflu mi o, 5 elabena ame geɖewo ava yɔ nye ŋkɔ ɖe wo ɖokuiwo ŋu agblɔ be, ‘Nyee nye Kristo la,’ eye woakplɔ ame geɖewo atrae. 6 Miase aʋawɔwɔwo kple aʋawɔwɔwo ŋu nyawo. Gake dzika megatso mia ƒo o, elabena ele be nu siawo nava eme godoo, gake nuwuwu la meɖo haɖe o.
ENGLISH: And his disciples grew hungry and began to pick ears and eat them; 2 and the Pharisees, seeing it, said to him "There, your disciples are doing what it is not lawful to do on a Sabbath. " 3 But he said to them "Have you not read what David did when he and those who were with him were hungry? 4 how he went into the house of God and they ate the showbread, which it was not allowable for him to eat nor for those who were with him, but only for the priests? 5 or have you not read in the law that on the sabbath the priests in the temple profane the sabbath and are guiltless? 6 but I tell you there is something greater than the temple here.

EWE: 7 "Elabena dukɔ atso ɖe dukɔ ŋu, eye fiaɖuƒe ɖe fiaɖuƒe ŋu, nuɖuɖu ave le teƒeteƒewo, eye anyigba aʋuʋu le teƒeteƒewo.
ENGLISH: 7 But if you knew what ‘I want pity, and not sacrifice’ is, you would not have condemned the guiltless; 8 for the Son of Man is master of the sabbath. "

EWE: 8 Nu siawo katã nye fuɖuame ƒe gɔmedzedze. 9 "Eye amewo atsɔ mi ade asi be woawɔ fu mi, woawu mi, eye dukɔwo katã alé fu mi le nye ŋkɔ la ta. 10 Ame geɖewo atra ɖa le xɔse la gbɔ, eye woade wo nɔewo asi ahalé fu wo nɔewo.
ENGLISH: 9 And he passed from that place to their synagogue; 10 and lo, there was a man there with a shriveled hand, and they put the question to him "Is it lawful to cure on the sabbath? " that they might arraign him.

EWE: 11 Aʋatsonyagblɔɖila geɖewo ado eye woakplɔ ame geɖewo atrae; 12 eye le sedzimawɔmawɔ ƒe dzidziɖedzi ta la, ame akpa gãtɔ ƒe lɔlɔ̃ ayi to.
ENGLISH: 11 But he said to them "What man will there be of you that will have one sheep, and if that falls into a pit on the sabbath will not catch hold of it and get it on its feet? 12 How much more important, then, is a man than a sheep!

EWE: 13 Ke ame si do dzi va se ɖe nuwuwu la, eyae akpɔ ɖeɖe.
ENGLISH: So that it is lawful to do a good turn on the sabbath. " 13 Then he said to the man "Stretch out your hand "; and he stretched it out and it was restored, sound like the other.

EWE: 14 Eye woaɖe gbeƒã Fiaɖuƒe ŋuti nya nyui sia le anyigba blibo la katã dzi be wòanye ɖaseɖiɖi na dukɔwo katã, eye ekema nuwuwu la ava.
ENGLISH: 14 But the Pharisees went out and laid a plot against him to make away with him; 15 but Jesus, finding it out, retired from that place.

EWE: 15 "Eya ta ne miekpɔ ‘ŋunyɔnu si ahe aƒedozuzu vɛ’ la le kɔkɔeƒe la, abe ale si nyagblɔɖila Daniel gblɔe ene la, (nuxlẽla newɔ gɔmesese ŋu dɔ) 16 ekema ame siwo le Yudea la nasi ayi towo dzi.
ENGLISH: And many followed him, and he cured them all, 16 and told them peremptorily not to make him known, 17 that what was said through the prophet Isaiah in the words 18 "Here is my servant whom I like well, my dear one in whom my soul takes pleasure; I will put my Spirit upon him, and he shall announce judgment to the nations.

EWE: 17 Ame si le xɔ ta la megaɖi be yeatsɔ naneke tso yeƒe xɔ me ayii o, 18 eye ame si le agble la megatrɔ gbɔ be yeatsɔ yeƒe awudziwui o.
ENGLISH: 19 He will not wrangle, nor shout, nor will anyone hear his voice on the streets.

EWE: 19 Baba na funɔwo kple ame siwo le no nam vi le ŋkeke mawo me! 20 Minɔ gbedodoɖa dzi be miaƒe sisi nagadze vuvɔŋɔli alo Sabat ŋkeke dzi o; 21 elabena ɣemaɣi la, xaxa gã si tɔgbi meva kpɔ tso xexea ƒe gɔmedzedze va se ɖe fifia o la ava, eye etɔgbi megale vava ge ake o.
ENGLISH: 20 He will not break a crushed reed, and will not put out smoldering flax, till he brings judgment out to victory; 21 and in his name shall nations hope " should be fulfilled.

EWE: 22 Le nyateƒe me la, ne wometso ŋkeke mawo dzi o la, ŋutilã aɖeke makpɔ ɖeɖe o; ke le ame tiatiawo ta woatso ŋkeke mawo dzi.
ENGLISH: 22 Then there was brought to him a blind and dumb demoniac; and he cured him, so that the dumb man spoke and saw.

EWE: 23 "Ekema ne ame aɖe gblɔ na mi be, ‘Kpɔ ɖa, Kristo la le afii!’ alo ‘Ele afi mɛ!’ la, migaxɔe se o. 24 Elabena aʋatsokristowo kple aʋatsonyagblɔɖilawo ado, eye woawɔ dzesi gãwo kple nukunuwo bena, ne woate ŋui la, woaflu ame tiatiawo gɔ̃ hã. 25 Kpɔ ɖa, mexlɔ̃ nu mi do ŋgɔ. 26 Eya ta ne wogblɔ na mi be, ‘Kpɔ ɖa! Ele gbedzi’ la, migayi o; ‘Kpɔ ɖa! Ele xɔgã me’ la, migaxɔe se o. 27 Elabena ale si ko dzi kea dzo le ɣedzeƒe eye eƒe keklẽ dea ɣetoɖoƒe ke la, nenema kee Amegbetɔvi la ƒe anyinɔɣi hã anɔ.
ENGLISH: 23 And all the crowds were surprised and said "Can it be that this is the Son of David? " 24 But the Pharisees, hearing it, said "It is simply by Beelzebul the head of the demons that this man expels the demons. " 25 But he, knowing their thoughts, said to them "Any kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and any city or family divided against itself will not be kept up; 26 and if Satan is expelling Satan, he is divided against himself so how shall his kingdom be kept up? 27 And if it is by Beelzebul that I expel the demons, by whom do your sons expel them? accordingly they shall be your judges.

EWE: 28 Afi si nu kuku le la, afi mae hɔ̃wo aƒo ƒu ɖo.
ENGLISH: 28 But if I expel the demons by the Spirit of God, then the Reign of God has overtaken you.

EWE: 29 "Le xaxa si ava le ŋkeke mawo me megbe teti ko la, ɣe ado viviti, eye ɣleti magaɖi o, ɣletiviwo age tso dziƒo, eye woaʋuʋu dziƒowo ƒe ŋusẽwo.
ENGLISH: 29 Or how can one enter a strong man’s house and carry off his goods unless he first binds the strong man? and then he shall plunder his house.

EWE: 30 Ɣemaɣi la, Amegbetɔvi la ƒe dzesi adze le dziƒo, eye anyigbadziƒomewo katã afa konyi vevie, eye woakpɔ Amegbetɔvi la le dziƒolilikpowo dzi gbɔna kple ŋusẽ kpakple ŋutikɔkɔe gã.
ENGLISH: 30 He who is not with me is against me, and he who does not gather with me scatters.

EWE: 31 Eye wòadɔ eƒe dɔlawo ɖa kple kpẽ ƒe ɖiɖi gã aɖe, eye woaƒo eƒe ame tiatiawo nu ƒu tso ya eneawo dzi, tso dziƒo ƒe go ɖeka dzi yi eƒe go kemɛ dzi.
ENGLISH: 31 Accordingly I tell you, men will be forgiven every sin and blasphemy, but not the blasphemy of the Spirit.

EWE: 32 "Ke misrɔ̃ nu sia tso gboti ŋu: Ne edze alɔ fẽwo, eye wònya to aŋgbawo ko la, mienyana be dzomeŋɔli gogo.
ENGLISH: 32 And anyone who says a thing against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but one who says it against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven either in this or in the future age.

EWE: 33 Nenema kee miawo hã, ne miekpɔ nu siawo katã la, minyae be Amegbetɔvi la gogo ʋɔtruawo nu.
ENGLISH: 33 Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree foul and its fruit foul; for the tree is known by the fruit.

EWE: 34 Vavã mele egblɔm na mi be, dzidzime sia nu mele yiyi ge akpɔ o, va se ɖe esime nu siawo katã va eme.
ENGLISH: 34 Spawn of vipers, how can you be bad and speak good? for what the mouth speaks comes out of what is overflowing in the heart.

EWE: 35 Dziƒo kple anyigba nu ava yi, ke nye nyawo ya nu mava yi akpɔ o.
ENGLISH: 35 A good man brings out good things from his good stock, and a bad man brings out bad things from his bad stock.

EWE: 36 "Le ŋkeke ma kple gaƒoƒo ma ŋuti la, ame aɖeke menyae o, mawudɔla siwo le dziƒo la menyae o, eye Vi la hã menyae o, negbe Fofo la ko. 37 Elabena ale si Noa ƒe ŋkekeawo nɔ la, nenema kee Amegbetɔvi la ƒe anyinɔɣi la hã anɔ.
ENGLISH: 36 But I tell you, every idle word that men shall speak they shall account for at the day of judgment; 37 for you shall be acquitted on your own words and condemned on your own words. "
