EWE: Woxɔnɛ sena ɣeyiɣi aɖe ko, ke le dodokpɔ ƒe ɣeyiɣi me la, wodea megbe. 14 Ke esiwo ge ɖe ŋùwo me la woe nye ame siwo see, gake esi agbe sia me dzimaɖitsitsiwo, kesinɔnuwo kple dzidzɔdonamenuwo he wo hevu tsyɔ wo dzi keŋkeŋ ta la, wometsina tsena o. 15 Ke esiwo ge ɖe anyigba nyui dzi la, woawoe nye ame siwo sea nya la kple dzi nyui si nyo, eye woléa eme ɖe asi, eye wotsea ku le dzidodo me.
ENGLISH: The seed is the word of God; 12 and the ones on the roadside are those who hear and then the devil comes and takes away the word from their hearts, that they may not believe and be saved; 13 and the ones on the rock are those who, when they hear, accept the word with joy, while they have no root who believe temporarily and quit in testing-time; 14 and what fell among the thorns, these are the ones who hear, and, as they go on, are stifled by life’s anxieties and riches and pleasures, and do not ripen a crop; 15 and what was in soil that was all right, these are those who hear and retain the word in a right and good heart, and bear their crop by holding out.

EWE: 16 "Ame aɖeke mesia akaɖi hetsyɔa nu edzi alo danɛ ɖe abati te o, ke boŋ etsɔnɛ dana ɖe akaɖiti dzi be wòaklẽ na ame siwo vaa aƒea me la.
ENGLISH: 16 "But nobody after lighting a lamp covers it with a jar or sets it under a couch, but sets it on a stand so that those who enter can see the light.

EWE: 17 Elabena womeɣla naneke si womava ɖe ɖe go o, eye wometsyɔ nu naneke dzi si womava nya alo ava dze le gaglãgbe o.
ENGLISH: 17 For there is no secret thing that will not be laid open, nor a thing concealed that shall not be found out and brought to light.

EWE: 18 Eya ta milé ŋku ɖe ale si mieɖoa toe ŋu nyuie; elabena ame si si nu le la, woatsɔ geɖe akpee nɛ, ke ame si si nu mele o la, woaxɔ nu si wòsusu be ele ye si la gɔ̃ hã le esi. "
ENGLISH: 18 So look out how you hear; for to one who has, more shall be given, and from one who has not, even what he seems to have shall be taken away. "

EWE: 19 Azɔ dadaa kple nɔviawo va egbɔ, gake womete ŋu te ɖe eŋu o le ameha la ta. 20 Ke amewo gblɔ nɛ be: "Dawò kple nɔviwòwo le tsitre ɖe xexe le didim be yewoakpɔ wò. " 21 Eɖo eŋu na wo be: "Danye kple nɔvinyewoe nye ame siawo, siwo sea Mawu ƒe nya la, eye wowɔa edzi. "
ENGLISH: 19 And his mother and his brothers came to him, and could not get at him because of the crowd; 20 and he was told "Your mother and your brothers are standing outside wanting to see you. " 21 But he answered them "My mother and my brothers, they are those who listen to God’s word and do it. "

EWE: 22 Gbe ɖeka la, Yesu kple eƒe nusrɔ̃lawo ge ɖe tɔdziʋu aɖe me, eye wògblɔ na wo be: "Mina míayi ta la ƒe go kemɛ dzi. " Ale wodze mɔ. 23 Esi wole tɔdziʋua me yina la, edɔ alɔ̃.
ENGLISH: 22 And on one of the days he and his disciples had got into a boat, and he said to them "Let us go across to the other side of the lake, " and they started; 23 and during the passage he fell asleep.

EWE: Ke ahom sesẽ aɖe tu le ta la dzi, tsi de asi tɔdziʋu la yɔyɔ me, eye woƒe agbe ɖo afɔku me. 24 Eya ta wova egbɔ henyɔe gblɔ be: "Nufiala, Nufiala, míeku vɔ! "
ENGLISH: And a squall of wind came down on the lake, and they were getting swamped and were in danger; 24 and they approached him and roused him up, saying "Master, master, we are lost. "

EWE: Eye wòfɔ heblu ɖe ahom la kple tsi dzeagbo la ta, ale wodze akɔ anyi, eye ɖoɖoe zi toŋtoŋtoŋ.
ENGLISH: But when he was roused he rebuked the wind and the surging of the water, and they stopped and there was a calm.

EWE: 25 Azɔ ebia wo be: "Afi kae miaƒe xɔse le? "
ENGLISH: 25 And he said to them "Where is your faith? "

EWE: Elabena eɖea gbe na yaƒoƒo kple tsi gɔ̃ hã, eye woɖoa toe. " 26 Emegbe wova ɖi go ɖe Gerasa nuto, si dze ŋgɔ Galilea la me.
ENGLISH: And they were afraid and wondered, saying to each other "Who then is this, that he gives orders to the winds and the water and they obey him? " 26 And they came to land in the country of the Gerasenes, which is on the opposite side from Galilee.

EWE: 27 Esi wòdo le ʋua me la, ŋutsu aɖe si me gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃wo le la do tso dua me va do goe. Ɣeyiɣi didi aɖee nye ema megado awu kpɔ o, eye menɔa aƒe me o, ke boŋ yɔdowo dome koe wònɔna.
ENGLISH: 27 And when he had landed there met him a certain man out of the city who had demons, and had not for a considerable time had on a garment, and did not stay in a house but in the tombs.

EWE: 28 Esi wòkpɔ Yesu la, edo ɣli sesĩe hedze klo ɖe eŋkume, eye wògblɔ sesĩe be: "Nya kae le nye kpli wò dome, Yesu, Mawu Dziƒoʋĩtɔ la ƒe Vi?
ENGLISH: 28 And at seeing Jesus he screamed out and threw himself down before him and said in a loud voice "What have I to do with you, Jesus, Son of the Most High God?

EWE: Meɖe kuku na wò, mègawɔ fum o. " 29 (Elabena Yesu ɖe gbe na gbɔgbɔ makɔmakɔ la be wòado go le amea me.
ENGLISH: I beg you, do not torture me "; 29 for he was enjoining the unclean spirit to come out of the man.

EWE: Ekpɔ ŋusẽ ɖe edzi zi geɖe, eye enuenu wodea kɔsɔkɔsɔ kple kunyowui hedzɔa eŋu, gake etsoa kɔsɔkɔsɔawo heŋea kunyowuawo, eye gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃ la nyanɛ ɖona ɖe teƒe tsoabowo.) 30 Yesu biae be: "Ŋkɔwò ɖe? " Eɖo eŋu be: "Aʋakɔ, " elabena gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃ geɖewoe ge ɖe eme.
ENGLISH: For at many times it had seized him, and he used to be manacled with fetters and chains and kept under guard, and he would burst the fastenings and be driven to the wildernesses by the demon. 30 And Jesus put the question to him "What is your name? " and he said "Brigade, " because many demons had entered him.

EWE: 31 Eye woɖe kuku nɛ be meganya yewo ɖo ɖe aʋli la me o.
ENGLISH: 31 And they were appealing to him not to order them to go to the abyss.

EWE: Eye wòɖe mɔ na wo. 33 Ale gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃awo do go le ame la me, eye woyi ɖe haawo me, eye haawo si du kplikplikpli to to la dzi ge dze ta la me doo, eye wono tsi ku. 34 Ke esi hakplɔviawo kpɔ nu si dzɔ la, wosi, eye wova gblɔe na amewo le dua me kple agbletawo.
ENGLISH: 32 Now there was there a considerable herd of hogs feeding on the mountainside; and they appealed to him to permit them to enter those; and he gave them permission, 33 and the demons came out of the man and entered the hogs, and the herd bolted down the steep bank into the lake and were drowned.

EWE: 35 Eya ta amewo do go yi be yewoakpɔ nu si dzɔ. Wova Yesu gbɔ hekpɔ ŋutsu si me gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃awo do go le la wònɔ anyi ɖe Yesu ƒe afɔnu, ele awu me eye eƒe mo kɔ nyuie, eye vɔvɔ̃ ɖo wo.
ENGLISH: 34 And the men who were tending them, at seeing what had happened, ran away and reported it in the city and in the fields; 35 and they came out to see what had happened, and came to Jesus and found the man from whom the demons had come out sitting at Jesus’s feet, clothed and sane, and they were afraid.

EWE: 36 Ame siwo kpɔ nu si dzɔ la gblɔ ale si wòyɔ dɔ ŋutsu si me gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃ nɔ la na wo.
ENGLISH: 36 And those who had seen it reported to them how the demon-ridden man had been brought to himself.

EWE: 37 Eya ta ame gbogbo siwo tso Gerasa nutoa me la katã gblɔ na Yesu be wòadzo le yewo gbɔ, elabena vɔvɔ̃ gã aɖe lé wo. Eya ta eɖo tɔdziʋu la hetrɔ dzo.
ENGLISH: 37 And the entire populace of the region of the Gerasenes asked him to go away from their country, because they were under the strain of a great fear; and he got into a boat and returned.

EWE: 38 Ke ŋutsu si me gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃wo do go le la ɖe kuku nɛ be yeakplɔe ɖo, gake edo mɔ ŋutsua gblɔ be: 39 "Trɔ yi aƒe me, eye nànɔ nu siwo katã Mawu wɔ na wò la gblɔm. " Ale ŋutsu la dzo hele gbeƒã ɖem nu siwo Yesu wɔ nɛ la le du bliboa me.
ENGLISH: 38 And the man from whom the demons had come out begged to be with him; but he dismissed him, saying 39 "Return home and tell what things God has done for you "; and he went off through the whole city proclaiming what things Jesus had done for him.

EWE: 40 Esi Yesu trɔ gbɔ la, ameha la xɔe nyuie, elabena wo katã wole mɔ kpɔm nɛ.
ENGLISH: 40 And at Jesus’s return the crowd was there to welcome him; for they were all expecting him.

EWE: 41 Ke kpɔ ɖa, ŋutsu aɖe si ŋkɔe nye Yairo, si nye ƒuƒoƒea dzi kpɔlawo dometɔ ɖeka la, va dze klo ɖe Yesu ƒe afɔnu heɖe kuku nɛ vevie be wòava yeƒe aƒe me, 42 elabena vianyɔnuvi ɖekɛ si xɔ abe ƒe wuieve ene la ɖo kudo nu.
ENGLISH: 41 And there came a man whose name was Jair and he was a director in the synagogue and threw himself down at Jesus’s feet and appealed to him to come to his house, 42 because he had an only daughter, about twelve years old, and she was dying.

EWE: Esi Yesu yina la, amehawo mimii ɖo. 43 Nyɔnu aɖe le ʋusisidɔ lém ƒe wuieve sɔŋ, eye ame aɖeke mete ŋu dae nɛ o. 44 Nyɔnu sia zɔ to emegbe va ka asi eƒe awu toga, enumake ʋu si le sisim le eŋu la nu tso. 45 Eye Yesu bia be: "Ame kae ka asi ŋunye? "
ENGLISH: And while he was on the way the crowds were suffocating him; 43 and a woman who had been having a flow of blood for twelve years, who had not succeeded in getting cured by anybody, 44 came up behind and touched the tassel of his cloak, and immediately her flow of blood stopped.

EWE: Esi wo katã wogblɔ be menye yewoe o la, Petro gblɔ be: "Nufiala, ameha la ƒo xlã wò hemimi wò ɖoe. " 46 Ke Yesu gblɔ be: "Ame aɖe ka asi ŋunye, elabena mede dzesii be ŋusẽ do le menye. " 47 Esi nyɔnu la kpɔe be Yesu nya nu si yewɔ la, enɔ dzodzom nyanyanya va dze klo ɖe eŋkume hegblɔ nu si ta wòka asi eŋu kple ale si dɔa vɔ nɛ enumake la le ameawo katã ŋkume. 48 Ke Yesu gblɔ nɛ be: "Vinyenyɔnu, wò xɔse na nèhaya. Dzo yi le ŋutifafa me. "
ENGLISH: 45 And Jesus said "Who was it that touched me? " but everybody denied it, while Peter said "Master, the crowds are hemming you in and crushing you. " 46 But Jesus said "Somebody touched me; for I felt that a power had gone out from me. " 47 And the woman, seeing that she had not escaped notice, came trembling and threw herself down before him and told him before all the people the reason why she touched him, and how she was healed immediately; 48 and he said to her "Daughter, your faith has made you well; go, and good betide you. "

EWE: 49 Esi wògale nuƒoƒo dzi la, ƒuƒoƒea dzi kpɔla ƒe ame dɔdɔ va gblɔ be: "Viwònyɔnuvi la ku; mègaxa ɖe fu na Nufiala la o. " 50 Esi Yesu se nya sia la, eɖo eŋu nɛ be: "Mègavɔ̃ o, xɔe se ko, eye woaɖee. " 51 Esi wòɖo aƒea me la, meɖe mɔ na ame aɖeke be wòage ɖe xɔa me kpli ye o, negbe Petro, Yohanes, Yakobo kpakple nyɔnuvi la fofo kple dadaa ko.
ENGLISH: 49 While he was still speaking, someone came from the director’s house saying "Your daughter is dead; do not put the teacher out anymore. " 50 But Jesus, hearing it, answered him "Do not be afraid, only believe, and she shall get well. " 51 And when he came to the house he would not let anyone go in with him but Peter and John and James and the girl’s father and mother.

EWE: 52 Ke ameawo katã le avi fam hele nu xam le ɖevi la ta. Eya ta egblɔ be: "Midzudzɔ avifafa, elabena meku o, ke boŋ alɔ̃ dɔm wòle. " 53 Ale wode asi ekoko me, elabena wonya be eku.
ENGLISH: 52 And everybody was weeping and wailing for her; but he said "Do not weep, she is not dead but asleep. " 53 And they laughed at him, knowing that she was dead.

EWE: 54 Gake elé nyɔnuvi la ƒe alɔnu, eye wòyɔe gblɔ be: "Nyɔnuvi, tsi tsitre! " 55 Ale wògbɔ agbe, eye wòtsi tsitre enumake, eye wògblɔ be woana nanee wòaɖu.
ENGLISH: 54 But he grasped her hand and called "Girl, rise "; 55 and her spirit came back, and she stood up immediately; and he directed that she should be given something to eat.

EWE: 56 Eye nyɔnuvia dzilawo gli kple dzidzɔ, gake ede se na wo be womegagblɔ nu si dzɔ la na ame aɖeke o.
ENGLISH: 56 And her parents were astounded; but he instructed them to tell nobody what had taken place.

EWE: Luka
ENGLISH: Luke

EWE: 9 Eyɔ Ame Wuieveawo ƒo ƒu hena ŋusẽ kple ŋutete wo be woanya gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃wo katã ado goe, eye woada dɔlélewo. 2 Eye wòdɔ wo be woaɖe gbeƒã Mawu Fiaɖuƒe la ahada dɔlélewo, 3 eye wògblɔ na wo be: "Migatsɔ naneke ɖe asi na mɔzɔzɔa o, eɖanye atizɔti alo nuɖuɖukotoku alo abolo alo ga o; eye migatsɔ awu eve o.
ENGLISH: 9 And he called together the Twelve and gave them power and authority over all demons and to cure diseases, 2 and sent them to proclaim the Reign of God and to heal, 3 and said to them "Do not take anything for the journey, neither a walking-stick nor a wallet nor bread nor money, nor have two shirts to a man.

EWE: 4 Ne mieyi du aɖe me la, minɔ aƒe si me miedze la me va se ɖe esime miadzo le dua me.
ENGLISH: 4 And whatever house you go into, stay there and come out from there.

EWE: 5 Eye afi sia afi si womexɔ mi le o la, ne miele dzodzom le du ma me la, miʋuʋu ke le miaƒe afɔwo ŋu ɖe anyi wòanye ɖaseɖiɖi ɖe wo ŋu. " 6 Eye wodze mɔ yi ɖatsa le nutoawo katã me tso kɔƒe me yi kɔƒe me, eye wole gbeƒã ɖem nya nyui la hele dɔlélewo dam le afi sia afi.
ENGLISH: 5 And whatever people do not receive you, in coming out of that city shake off the dust from your feet for an attestation against them. " 6 And they went out and went along through the villages, preaching the gospel and curing people of sickness everywhere.

EWE: 7 Ke esi nutodziɖula Herodes se nu siwo katã le dzɔdzɔm la, etɔtɔ ŋutɔ, elabena ame aɖewo le gbɔgblɔm be wofɔ Yohanes tso ame kukuwo dome, 8 bubuwo be Eliya ye va do, ke bubu aɖewo hã be blemanyagblɔɖilawo dometɔ ɖekae tsi tsitre.
ENGLISH: 7 And the tetrarch Herod heard of all that was going on, and was puzzled, because it was said by some that John had risen from the dead, and by some that Elijah had appeared, 8 and by others that some old-time prophet had arisen.

EWE: 9 Herodes gblɔ be: "Yohanes la, metso ta le enu. Ke ame kae nye esia si ŋuti mele nya siawo sem le? "
ENGLISH: 9 But Herod said "John I beheaded; but who is this about whom I hear such things? " and tried to get a chance to see him.

EWE: Eya ta edi be yeakpɔe. 10 Esi apostoloawo trɔ gbɔ la, wogblɔ nu siwo katã wowɔ la na Yesu.
ENGLISH: 10 And the apostles returned and told him the story of everything they had done; and he took them and withdrew with them by himself to a city named Bethsaida.

EWE: Eye wòkplɔ wo woawo ɖeɖe woyi du aɖe si woyɔna be Betsaida me. 11 Ke esi amehaawo nya la, wotii yi afi ma.
ENGLISH: 11 But the crowds, finding it out, followed him; and he made them welcome and spoke to them about the Reign of God, and healed those who needed a cure.

EWE: Exɔ wo nyuie, eye wòte nuƒoƒo na wo tso Mawu Fiaɖuƒe la ŋu, eye wòda dɔ na dɔnɔwo katã. 12 Azɔ esi fiẽsi le ɖoɖom la, Ame Wuieveawo va egbɔ hegblɔ nɛ be: "Ðe asi le ameha la ŋu ne woayi kɔƒewo me kple agbleta siwo ƒo xlã mí la, ne woadi dzeƒe kple nuɖuɖu, elabena teƒe sia tso abo. " 13 Ke egblɔ na wo be: "Miawo ŋutɔwo mina nu wo woaɖu. "
ENGLISH: 12 But the day began to decline; and the Twelve came to him and said to him "Dismiss the crowd, so that they may go to the villages and farmlands round about and get lodged and find provisions, because here we are in an uninhabited place. " 13 But he said to them "Give them something to eat yourselves. "

EWE: Wogblɔ be: "Naneke mele mía si wu abolo atɔ̃ kple tɔmelã eve o, negbe ɖeko míawo ŋutɔwo míayi aɖaƒle nuɖuɖu na ame siawo katã. " 14 Evɔ woanɔ abe ŋutsu akpe atɔ̃ ene.
ENGLISH: And they said "We have no more than five cakes of bread and two fishes, unless it is for us to go and buy eatables for all these people " 14 for there were about five thousand men.

EWE: Eye wògblɔ na eƒe nusrɔ̃lawo be: "Mina woanɔ anyi ɖe hatsotsowo me, eye hatsotso ɖe sia ɖe nanye ame blaatɔ̃ lɔƒo. " 15 Eye wowɔe nenema, eye wona wo katã wonɔ anyi.
ENGLISH: But he said to his disciples "Have them lie down by groups of about fifty each "; 15 and they did so, and got them one and all lying down.

EWE: 16 Ke esi wòtsɔ abolo atɔ̃awo kple tɔmelã eveawo la, efɔ mo dzi kpɔ dziƒo, yra ɖe wo dzi. Eŋe wo me, eye wòtsɔ wo na eƒe nusrɔ̃lawo be woatsɔ aɖo ameha la kɔme. 17 Ale wo katã woɖu nu ɖi ƒo, eye woƒo kakɛ siwo susɔ la nu ƒu wòde kusi wuieve.
ENGLISH: 16 And he took the five cakes and the two fishes, and looked up to the sky and blessed them and broke them up and gave them to the disciples to set before the crowd; 17 and they all ate and had their fill, and there were taken up what they had of fragments left over, twelve baskets.

EWE: 18 Emegbe esi eya ɖeka le gbe dom ɖa la, nusrɔ̃lawo va egbɔ, eye wòbia wo be: "Ame kae amehaawo le gbɔgblɔm be menye? " 19 Woɖo eŋu nɛ be: "Yohanes Amenyrɔɖetsimela, bubuwo be Eliya, bubuwo hã be blemanyagblɔɖilawo dometɔ ɖekae tsi tsitre. " 20 Azɔ ebia wo be: "Ke miawo ya ɖe, ame kae miegblɔna be menye? "
ENGLISH: 18 And there was a time, while he was praying in private, that the disciples were with him and he put the question to them "Who do the crowds say I am? " 19 And they answered "John the Baptist and others, Elijah and others, that one of the old-time prophets has arisen. " 20 And he said to them "And who do you say I am? "

EWE: Petro ɖo eŋu be: "Mawu ƒe Kristo la. " 21 Ke ede se na wo vevie be womegagblɔ nya sia na ame aɖeke o, 22 egblɔ hã be: "Ele na Amegbetɔvi la be wòakpe fu geɖe, eye dumegãwo kple nunɔlawo ƒe tatɔwo kple agbalẽfialawo agbee, eye woawui, ke woafɔe ɖe tsitre le ŋkeke etɔ̃a gbe. "
ENGLISH: And Peter answered "God’s Messiah. " 21 But he peremptorily enjoined them not to tell this to anyone, 22 saying that the Son of Man must suffer a great deal, and be rejected by the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and rise on the third day.

EWE: 23 Eye wògblɔ na wo katã be: "Ne ame aɖe di be yeadze yonyeme la, negbe nu le eɖokui gbɔ, eye wòatsɔ eƒe fuwɔameti la gbe sia gbe, eye wòadze yonyeme.
ENGLISH: 23 And he said to all "If anyone wishes to come after me, let him repudiate himself and take up his cross daily and follow me.

EWE: 24 Elabena ame sia ame si dina be yeaɖe yeƒe agbe la abui; ke ame sia ame si abu eƒe agbe le tanye la, aɖee.
ENGLISH: 24 For whoever wishes to save his self will lose it; but whoever loses his self on my account, he will save it.

EWE: 25 Le nyateƒe me la, viɖe kae wòanye na ame, ne xexe blibo la katã zu etɔ, gake wòbu eƒe agbe alo tsrɔ̃? 26 Elabena ame sia ame si nye kple nye nyawo kpea ŋu na la, Amegbetɔvi la hã akpe ŋui ne eva ɖo le eya ŋutɔ kple Fofoa kpakple mawudɔla kɔkɔeawo ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe me.
ENGLISH: 25 For what good will a man get by making a profit of the whole world and a loss of himself? 26 For whoever is ashamed of me and my words, of him the Son of Man will be ashamed when he comes in his glory and his Father’s and the holy angels’.

EWE: 27 Ke vavã mele egblɔm na mi be, ame aɖewo le ame siwo le tsitre ɖe afi sia dome, siwo maɖɔ ku kpɔ gbeɖe o, va se ɖe esime wokpɔ Mawu Fiaɖuƒe la hafi. "
ENGLISH: 27 But I tell you truly, there are some of those who stand here who shall not taste death till they see the Reign of God. "

EWE: 28 Le nyateƒe me la, anɔ ŋkeke enyi le nya siawo gbɔgblɔ megbe la, ekplɔ Petro kple Yohanes kpakple Yakobo ɖe asi yi to aɖe dzi be yeado gbe ɖa.
ENGLISH: 28 And about a week after these things he took with him Peter and John and James and went up on the mountainside to pray.

EWE: 29 Eye esi wòle gbe dom ɖa la, eƒe mo ƒe dzedzeme trɔ, eye eƒe awu fu tititi hele dzo dam. 30 Eye kpɔ ɖa, ŋutsu eve, siwo nye Mose kple Eliya, le dze ɖom kplii. 31 Ame siawo dze le ŋutikɔkɔe me, eye wole dze ɖom tso eƒe dzodzo si ava eme le Yerusalem la ŋu.
ENGLISH: 29 And while he was praying the look of his face became different and his clothes flashing white; 30 and lo, there were two men talking with him; it was Moses and Elijah, 31 who, appearing in glory, spoke of his departure which he was to consummate at Jerusalem.

EWE: 32 Ke Petro kple ame siwo kpe ɖe eŋu la le alɔ̃ dɔm, gake esi wonyɔ keŋkeŋ la, wokpɔ eƒe ŋutikɔkɔe kple ŋutsu eve siwo le tsitre ɖe egbɔ.
ENGLISH: 32 But Peter and those who were with him were weighed down with sleep, but when they waked up they saw his glory and the two men that were standing with him.

EWE: 33 Eye esi ame siawo le dzodzom le Yesu gbɔ la, Petro gblɔ nɛ be: "Nufiala, enyo na mí be míanɔ afi sia. Eya ta na míatu agbadɔ etɔ̃, ɖeka na wò, ɖeka na Mose, eye ɖeka na Eliya. "
ENGLISH: 33 And while those were parting from him Peter said to Jesus "Master, it is a good thing we are here: let us make three booths, one for you and one for Moses and one for Elijah " not knowing what he was saying.

EWE: Gake eya ŋutɔ menya nya ka gblɔm wòle o. 34 Ke esi wòle nya siawo gblɔm la, alilikpo do, eye wòdo vɔvɔli ɖe wo dzi.
ENGLISH: 34 And as he was saying these things there was a cloud, and it overshadowed them; and they were afraid when they entered the cloud.

EWE: 35 Eye gbe aɖe ɖi tso alilikpoa me gblɔ be: "Ame siae nye Vinye si metia la. Miɖo toe. " 36 Eye esi gbea ɖi la, Yesu ɖeka koe wokpɔ.
ENGLISH: 35 And there came a voice out of the cloud, "This is my chosen son: listen to him. " 36 And as the voice came, Jesus alone was to be found.

EWE: Ke womia nu ɖe nya la dzi, eye womeka nu siwo wokpɔ la dometɔ aɖeke ta na ame aɖeke le ŋkeke mawo me o.
ENGLISH: And they kept silence and did not report any of the things they had seen to anybody in those days.

EWE: 39 Eye kpɔ ɖa, gbɔgbɔ aɖe dzea edzi, eye kasia wòdoa ɣli, eye wònana wòƒona tititi, eye futukpɔ dona le enu, eye ne ewɔ nu vevii vɔ hã la, bebli hafi wòdzona le edzi. 40 Meɖe kuku na wò nusrɔ̃lawo be woanyae do goe, ke womete ŋui o. " 41 Yesu ɖo eŋu be: "Oo, dzidzime maxɔse totro kpaɖikpaɖi, ɣeyiɣi didi kae manɔ mia gbɔ ahado dzi atsɔ miaƒe nuwɔnawo ase ɖo? Kplɔ viwòa va afii. " 42 Gake esi ɖevia le egogom la, gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃ la xlãe ɖe anyi hena wòƒo tititi ŋutɔ. Ke Yesu ka mo na gbɔgbɔ makɔmakɔ la, eye wòda gbe le ŋutsuvi la ŋu, eye wòtsɔe na fofoa.
ENGLISH: 37 And when they came down off the mountain on the next day he encountered a great crowd; 38 and a man shrieked out from the crowd "Teacher, I beg you to take notice of my son, because he is the only one I have, 39 and here a spirit takes him and all of a sudden he screams, and it convulses him and raises a foam, and it is with great difficulty that it can be got to come away from him, breaking him all to pieces; 40 and I begged your disciples to expel it and they could not. " 41 And Jesus answered "O unbelieving and perverse generation, how long shall I be among you and bear with you? bring your son here. " 42 But even while he was coming the demon struck him down and threw him into a convulsion; but Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit and healed the boy and gave him back to his father.

EWE: 43 Ale wo katã ƒe nu ku le Mawu ƒe ŋusẽ gã la ŋuti.
ENGLISH: 43 And all were astonished at the grandeur of God.

EWE: Esi nu siwo katã wɔm wòle la na wo katã ƒe mo wɔ yaa la, egblɔ na eƒe nusrɔ̃lawo be: 44 "Miɖo to nya siawo nyuie ne woatsi susu me na mi, elabena woade Amegbetɔvi la asi na amewo. " 45 Ke womese nya si gblɔm wòle la gɔme o. Le nyateƒe me la, woɣlae ɖe wo be woagase egɔme o, eye wole vɔvɔ̃m be yewoabia nyae tso nya sia ŋu.
ENGLISH: But while all were wondering at all that he was doing he said to his disciples 44 "Lodge these words in your ears: for the Son of Man is to be given up into the hands of men. " 45 But they did not know what to make of this saying, and it was veiled from them so that they should not apprehend it; and they were afraid to ask him about this saying.

EWE: 46 Azɔ nyaʋiʋli ɖo wo dome le wo dometɔ si nye gãtɔ la ŋuti.
ENGLISH: 46 And the question came up among them which of them was greatest.

EWE: 47 Esi Yesu nya woƒe dzimesusuwo ta la, ekplɔ ɖevi aɖe vɛ hena wòtɔ ɖe egbɔ, 48 eye wògblɔ na wo be: "Ame sia ame si xɔa ɖevi sia le nye ŋkɔ ta la, exɔa nye hã; eye ame sia ame si xɔam la, exɔa Ame si dɔm ɖa la hã. Elabena ame si wɔa eɖokui suetɔ le mi katã mia dome lae nye gãtɔ. "
ENGLISH: 47 But Jesus, knowing their inward questioning, took a child and had it stand at his side, 48 and said to them "Anybody who receives this child in my name is receiving me, and anybody who receives me is receiving him who sent me; for he who is smallest among you all, he is greatest. "

EWE: 49 Eye Yohanes gblɔ nɛ be: "Nufiala, míekpɔ ame aɖe wòle gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃wo nyam do goe le wò ŋkɔ me, eye míegbe nɛ, elabena menye mía dometɔ ɖekae wònye o. " 50 Ke Yesu gblɔ nɛ be: "Migagbe nɛ o, elabena ame si metsi tsitre ɖe mia ŋu o la, le mia dzi. "
ENGLISH: 49 And John answered "Master, we saw somebody expelling demons in your name and we stopped him because he does not follow with us. " 50 But Jesus said to him "Do not stop him, because he who is not against us is for us. "

EWE: 51 Ke esi ɣeyiɣi si woakɔ Yesu ayi dziƒo le aƒe tum la, eɖoe kplikpaa be yeayi Yerusalem. 52 Eya ta edɔ dɔlawo ɖo ɖe eŋgɔ.
ENGLISH: 51 And when the days for his being taken up came around, he set his face to go to Jerusalem 52 and sent messengers ahead of him; and they went, and came into a village of Samaritans to make preparations for him; 53 and they did not receive him, because he was headed toward Jerusalem.

EWE: Eye wodze mɔ va ɖo Samariatɔwo ƒe kɔƒe aɖe me be woadzra ɖo na eƒe vava. 53 Gake womexɔe o, le esi wòɖoe kplikpaa be yeayi Yerusalem ta.
ENGLISH: 54 And when the disciples James and John saw it they said "Sir, will you have us say the word for fire to come down out of the sky and consume them? " 55 But he turned and rebuked them, 56 and they went to another village.

EWE: 54 Esi nusrɔ̃la Yakobo kple Yohanes kpɔ esia la, wobiae be: "Aƒetɔ, èlɔ̃ be míana dzo nage tso dziƒo ava tsrɔ̃ woa? " 55 Ke etrɔ heka mo na wo. 56 Ale wodzo yi kɔƒe bubu me.
ENGLISH: 57 And while they were going along somebody said to him on the road "I will follow you wherever you go. " 58 And Jesus said to him "The foxes have dens and the birds of the air perches, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head. "

EWE: 57 Ke esi wole mɔa dzi yina la, ame aɖe gblɔ nɛ be: "Madze yowòme ayi afi sia afi si nàyi. " 58 Yesu gblɔ nɛ be: "Do le abeiwo si, eye atɔ le dziƒoxewo si, ke teƒe aɖeke mele Amegbetɔvi la ya si wòaziɔ ta ɖo o. " 59 Eye wògblɔ na ame bubu be: "Dze yonyeme. "
ENGLISH: 59 And he said to another "Follow me "; but he said "Permit me first to go and bury my father. " 60 And he said to him "Leave the dead to bury their dead, but for your part go and advertise the Reign of God. "

EWE: Amea gblɔ be: "Aƒetɔ, ɖe mɔ nam mayi aɖaɖi fofonye gbɔ. " 60 Ke egblɔ nɛ be: "Na ame kukuwo naɖi woƒe ame kukuwo, ke wò la, yi nàɖe gbeƒã Mawu Fiaɖuƒe la. " 61 Eye ame bubu hã gblɔ be: "Aƒetɔ, madze yowòme; gake na mayi aɖaklã nye aƒemetɔwo gbã. " 62 Yesu gblɔ nɛ be: "Ame si tsɔ eƒe asi ɖo kodzi dzi, eye wògale nu siwo le megbe kpɔm la, medze na Mawu Fiaɖuƒe la o. "
ENGLISH: 61 And still another said "I will follow you, sir; but first permit me to bid farewell to the people at home. " 62 But Jesus said to him "Nobody who puts his hand to a plow and looks back is fit for the Reign of God. "

EWE: Luka
ENGLISH: Luke

EWE: 10 Le nu siawo megbe la, Aƒetɔ la tia ame blaadre bubuwo, eye wòdɔ wo eveeve ɖo ɖe eŋgɔ ɖe duwo me kple teƒe siwo katã to ge eya ŋutɔ gbɔna la.
ENGLISH: 10 And after this the Lord designated seventy-two others and sent them out ahead of him two by two to every city and place where he himself was going to come.

EWE: 2 Eye wògblɔ na wo be: "Nyateƒee, nuŋeŋe la sɔ gbɔ, ke dɔwɔlawo ya mede ha o.
ENGLISH: 2 And he said to them "The harvest is great, but the workers are few; so beg the owner of the harvest to send out workers to his harvest.

EWE: Eya ta miɖe kuku na nuŋeŋe ƒe Aƒetɔ la be wòaɖo dɔwɔlawo ɖe eƒe nuŋeŋe la me. 3 Miheyi!
ENGLISH: 3 Go; here I am sending you out like lambs among wolves.

EWE: 4 Migatsɔ gakotoku alo nuɖuɖukotoku alo afɔkpa o, eye migado gbe na ame aɖeke le mɔ dzi o.
ENGLISH: 4 Carry no purse, no wallet, no shoes, and salute no one on the road.

EWE: 5 Ne miege ɖe aƒe aɖe me la, gbã la, migblɔ be: ‘Ŋutifafa na aƒe sia.’ 6 Eye ne ŋutifafalɔ̃la aɖe le afi ma la, miaƒe ŋutifafa anɔ edzi. Ke ne ɖeke meli o la, ekema agbugbɔ ava mia dzi.
ENGLISH: 5 And whatever house you enter, first say ‘Peace to this house’; 6 and if there be a man for peace there, your peace shall rest upon him, but if not it shall come back to you.

EWE: 7 Minɔ aƒe ma ko me, eye miaɖu nu ahano nu si wona mi, elabena dɔwɔla dze na eƒe fetu.
ENGLISH: 7 And stay in that same house, eating and drinking what they furnish, for a worker deserves his pay.

EWE: Miganɔ ʋuʋum tso aƒe me yi aƒe me o.
ENGLISH: Do not move from house to house.

EWE: 8 "Ne mieyi ɖe du aɖe me, eye woxɔ mi la, miɖu nu si woatsɔ aɖo mia kɔme, 9 mida gbe le dɔnɔ siwo le eme la ŋu, eye migblɔ na wo be: ‘Mawu Fiaɖuƒe la gogo mi.’ 10 Ke ne miege ɖe du aɖe me, eye womexɔ mi o la, miyi ɖe eƒe ablɔwo me, eye miagblɔ be: 11 ‘Míele ʋuʋudedi si lé ɖe míaƒe afɔwo ŋu le miaƒe dua me la kura gɔ̃ hã ʋuʋum ɖi na mi. Gake nenɔ susu me na mi be, Mawu Fiaɖuƒe la gogo.’ 12 Mele egblɔm na mi be, anɔ bɔbɔe na Sodom le ŋkeke ma dzi wu ale si wòanɔ na du ma. 13 "Baba na wò, Korazin!
ENGLISH: 8 And whatever city you come into and they receive you, eat what is set before you, 9 and cure the sick in it, and say to them ‘The Reign of God is almost upon you.’ 10 And whatever city you come into and they do not receive you, come out into its main streets and say 11 ‘We wipe off the very dust that has stuck to our feet out of your city; know this though, that the Reign of God is almost here.’ 12 I tell you it will be more bearable for Sodom in that day than for that city.

EWE: Baba na wò, Betsaida! Elabena ne ɖe wowɔ ŋusẽdɔ siwo wowɔ le mewò la le Tiro kple Sidon la, anye ne wotrɔ dzi me hebɔbɔ nɔ akpanya kple dzofi me gbe aɖe gbe ke. 14 Eya ta anɔ bɔbɔe na Tiro kple Sidon le ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃ la me wu mi.
ENGLISH: 13 Woe to you, Chorazin! woe to you, Bethsaida! because if the miracles that have been done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes; 14 it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment, though, than for you.

EWE: 15 Ke wò Kapernaum, ɖe woado wò ɖe dzi yi ɖatɔ dziƒo loo?
ENGLISH: 15 And you, Capernaum, are you to be lifted up to heaven? you are to go down to the world of the dead.

EWE: Keke Tsiẽƒe kee nàva do ɖo! 16 "Ame sia ame si ɖoa to mi la, ɖoa to nye hã. Ame sia ame si gbea mi la, gbea nye hã. Eye ame sia ame si gbeam la, gbea Ame si dɔm ɖa la hã. "
ENGLISH: 16 He who listens to you is listening to me, and he who disregards you is disregarding me; and he who disregards me is disregarding him who sent me. "

EWE: 17 Eye ame blaadreawo trɔ gbɔ kple dzidzɔ va gblɔ be: "Aƒetɔ, gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃wo gɔ̃ hã naa ta mí ne míeyɔ wò ŋkɔ la. " 18 Eye wògblɔ na wo be: "Mekpɔ Satana wòge xoxo abe dzikedzo ene tso dziƒo.
ENGLISH: 17 And the seventy-two returned with joy, saying "Sir, even the demons submit to us at your name. " 18 But he said to them "I saw Satan fall from heaven like lightning.

EWE: 19 Kpɔ ɖa!
ENGLISH: 19 Lo, I have empowered you to tread upon snakes and scorpions and on all the Enemy’s power, and nothing shall injure you.

EWE: Mena ŋusẽ mi be miaɖo afɔ dawo kple dziɖegbewo dzi, eye miaɖu futɔ la ƒe ŋusẽwo katã dzi, eye naneke mawɔ nu vevi mi o.
ENGLISH: 20 Do not rejoice at this, though, that the spirits submit to you; but rejoice because your names are enrolled in heaven. "

EWE: Ɛ̃, Fofo, elabe nenemae dze ŋuwò. 22 Fofonye tsɔ nuwo katã de asi nam, eye ame aɖeke menya ame si Vi la nye o, negbe Fofo la ko, eye ame aɖeke menya ame si Fofo la nye o, negbe Vi la, kple ame si Vi la lɔ̃ be yeaɖee afia la ko. "
ENGLISH: 21 At that same time he exulted in the Holy Spirit and said "I give thee praise, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that thou didst conceal these things from the wise and discerning and disclose them to infants; yes, Father, because such was thy pleasure.

EWE: 23 Eye wòtrɔ ɖe nusrɔ̃lawo ɖeɖe ŋu gblɔ be: "Dzidzɔtɔwoe nye ame siwo ƒe ŋku le nu siwo kpɔm miele la kpɔm. 24 Elabena mele egblɔm na mi be, nyagblɔɖila kple fia geɖewo di vevie be yewoakpɔ nu siwo kpɔm miele la, gake womekpɔ wo o, eye wodi be yewoase nya siwo sem miele la, gake womese wo o. "
ENGLISH: 22 Everything has been committed to me by my Father; and no one knows who the Son is except the Father, nor who the Father is except the Son and he to whom the Son chooses to disclose him. " 23 And he turned to his disciples and said to them by themselves "Happy are the eyes that see what you see; 24 for I tell you many prophets and kings wanted to see what you see and to hear what you hear, and did not. "

EWE: 25 Eye kpɔ ɖa, ŋutsu aɖe si nya Sea nyuie la tso be yeadoe kpɔ hegblɔ be: "Nufiala, nu kae wòle be mawɔ be manyi agbe mavɔ la dome? " 26 Ebiae be: "Nu kae woŋlɔ ɖe Se la me? Aleke nèse egɔmee? " 27 Eɖo eŋu nɛ be: "‘Lɔ̃ Yehowa wò Mawu kple wò dzi blibo, wò luʋɔ blibo, wò ŋusẽ blibo, kple wò tamesusu blibo,’ eye nàlɔ̃ ‘hawòvi abe wò ŋutɔ ɖokuiwò ene.’ " 28 Egblɔ nɛ be: "Èɖo eŋu nyuie; nɔ esia wɔm, ekema àkpɔ agbe. " 29 Ke esi ŋutsua di be yeaɖee afia be yele dzɔdzɔe ta la, ebia Yesu be: "Ame ka tututue nye hanyevi? " 30 Yesu ɖo eŋu be: "Ame aɖe tso Yerusalem ɖi abu yina Yeriko, eye wòdze adzodalawo si me, woɖe nu sia nu le eŋu, woƒoe wòku afã kple afã eye wogblẽe ɖi hedzo.
ENGLISH: 25 And up stood a legist to put him to a test, saying "Teacher, what should I do to inherit eternal life? " 26 And he said to him "What is written in the law? what do you read? " 27 And he answered "You shall love the Lord your God out of all your heart, and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind, and your neighbor as yourself. " 28 And he answered him "You have answered right: do this and you shall live. " 29 But he, wanting to vindicate himself, said to Jesus "And who is my neighbor? " 30 Jesus rejoined "Once upon a time a man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and he fell among robbers; who stripped him and gave him a clubbing, and went off leaving him half dead.

EWE: 31 Ke eva eme be, nunɔla aɖe to mɔ ma ɖi abu gbɔna, ke esi wòkpɔe la, edze to mɔa ƒe akpa kemɛ dzo.
ENGLISH: 31 And by chance a certain priest was going down by that road, and saw him and went past on the other side.

EWE: 32 Nenema kee esi Lewitɔ aɖe hã va ɖo afi ma, eye wòkpɔe la, edze to mɔa ƒe akpa kemɛ dzo.
ENGLISH: 32 And similarly a Levite came to the place and saw and went past on the other side.

EWE: 33 Ke Samariatɔ aɖe si le mɔa zɔm la va ke ɖe eŋu, eye esi wòkpɔe la, eƒe nu wɔ nublanui nɛ. 34 Ale wòte ɖe eŋu, kɔ ami kple wain ɖe eƒe abiawo me hebla wo nɛ. Emegbe ekɔ amea ɖe eya ŋutɔ ƒe tedzi dzi yi amedzrodzeƒe, eye wòkpɔ edzi.
ENGLISH: 33 But a certain wayfaring Samaritan came where he was, and saw him and was moved to pity, 34 and went up to him and bandaged his wounds, pouring on oil and wine; and he set him on his own beast and brought him to an inn and took care of him.

EWE: 35 Esi ŋu ke la, etsɔ denario eve na amedzrodzeƒea dzi kpɔla hegblɔ be: ‘Kpɔ edzi, eye nu sia nu si nàgagblẽ akpee la, maxee na wò ne metrɔ va.’ 36 Ame etɔ̃ siawo dometɔ kae nèsusu be ewɔ eɖokui havi na ame si dze adzodalawo si me? " 37 Egblɔ be: "Ame si kpɔ nublanui nɛ lae. " Eye Yesu gblɔ nɛ be: "Heyi, eye wò hã nàwɔ nenema ke. " 38 Ke esi wole woƒe mɔzɔzɔa dzi la, eyi kɔƒe aɖe me.
ENGLISH: 35 And in the morning he pulled out two denarii and gave them to the landlord and said ‘Take care of him, and what more you spend I will pay you when I am coming back.’ 36 Which of these three do you think showed himself neighbor to the man who had fallen among the robbers? " 37 And he said "The one that did him the kindness. "

EWE: Eye nyɔnu aɖe si ŋkɔe nye Marta la xɔe ɖe eƒe me. 39 Nɔvinyɔnu aɖe le nyɔnu sia si, eŋkɔe nye Maria; ke eya bɔbɔ nɔ Aƒetɔ la ƒe afɔnu hele to ɖom eƒe nyawo. 40 Ke Marta ya tsi dzi ɖe nu geɖewo gbɔ kpɔkpɔ ŋu. Eya ta eva Yesu gbɔ va gblɔ be: "Aƒetɔ, mètsɔ ɖeke le eme be nɔvinyea gblẽ dɔawo katã ɖe nye ɖeka dzinye oa?
ENGLISH: And Jesus said to him "Go and do like that yourself. " 38 And once while they were traveling along he had come into a village, and a woman, Martha by name, had taken him into her house; 39 and this woman had a sister named Mary, who had seated herself at the Lord’s feet and was listening to his words; 40 but Martha was having to bustle this way and that with a great deal to be done for the guests.

EWE: Gblɔe nɛ ne wòava kpe ɖe ŋunye. " 41 Aƒetɔ la ɖo eŋu nɛ be: "Marta, Marta, ètsi dzimaɖi hele fu ɖem na ɖokuiwò le nu geɖewo ŋuti. 42 Ke hã nu ʋɛ aɖewo koe hiã, alo ɖeka pɛ ko.
ENGLISH: And she came and stood before him and said "Sir, do you not care that my sister has left me to attend to things alone? so tell her to take hold and help me. " 41 But the Lord answered her "Martha, Martha, you are fretting and getting worried about many things, 42 but what is wanted is only a few, or one.

EWE: Maria ya tia nyuia gome, eye womele exɔ ge le esi o. "
ENGLISH: For Mary has chosen the good portion, which will not be taken away from her. "

EWE: Luka
ENGLISH: Luke

EWE: 11 Gbe ɖeka Yesu le gbe dom ɖa le teƒe aɖe, eye esi wòwu enu la, eƒe nusrɔ̃lawo dometɔ ɖeka gblɔ nɛ be: "Aƒetɔ, fia gbedodoɖa mí abe ale si Yohanes hã fia eƒe nusrɔ̃lawoe ene. " 2 Eya ta egblɔ na wo be: "Ne miele gbe dom ɖa la, migblɔ be: ‘Fofo, wò ŋkɔ ŋuti nakɔ. Wò Fiaɖuƒe nava. 3 Na abolo si asu mía nu gbe sia gbe la mí.
ENGLISH: 11 And as he was in a certain place praying, one of his disciples said to him when he ceased "Sir, teach us to pray, the same as John taught his disciples. " 2 And he said to them "When you pray, say ‘Father, may thy name be kept holy, thy reign come; 3 give us our next day’s bread day by day.

EWE: 4 Eye tsɔ míaƒe nu vɔ̃wo ke mí, elabena míawo ŋutɔwo hã míetsɔna kea ame sia ame si nyi fe le mía ŋu; eye mègakplɔ mí yi tetekpɔ me o.’ "
ENGLISH: 4 And forgive us our sins, for so do we forgive everyone who owes us anything.

EWE: Metu ʋɔa xoxo, eye nye kple vinyewo míemlɔ anyi.
ENGLISH: And do not have us fall under temptation.’ "

EWE: Nyemate ŋu afɔ ana naneke wò o.’ 8 Mele egblɔm na mi be: Ne mafɔ ana nanekee le esi wònye exɔlɔ̃ ta o la, afɔ godoo le esi wòle ebiam atraɖii ta, eye wòatsɔ nu siwo hiãe la anɛ. 9 Eya ta mele egblɔm na mi be, minɔ ebiabia dzi, eye woana mi; minɔ edidi dzi, eye miakpɔe; minɔ ʋɔƒoƒo dzi, eye woaʋui na mi.
ENGLISH: 5 And he said to them "Which of you shall have a friend and go to him at midnight and say to him ‘Friend, lend me three cakes of bread, 6 since a friend of mine has arrived at my house and I have nothing to set before him,’ 7 and he shall answer from inside ‘Do not bother me; the door is locked now, and my children are in the bed with me; I cannot get up and give you anything’ 8 I tell you, even if he shall not get up and give him anything because of being his friend, for his unashamedness he will rise and give him whatever he wants.

EWE: 10 Elabena ame sia ame si le nu biam la, exɔnɛ; ame sia ame si le nu dim la, ekpɔnɛ; eye ame sia ame si le ʋɔ ƒom la, woaʋui nɛ.
ENGLISH: 9 And I tell you, ask and you will have things given to you; look and you will find; knock and you will be opened to; 10 for every asker receives, and the seeker finds, and the knocker will be opened to.

EWE: 11 Le nyateƒe me la, vifofo kae le mia dome si ne via bia tɔmelãe la, wòatsɔ da ade esi ɖe tɔmelã teƒe? 12 Alo ne ebia koklozii la, wòatsɔ dziɖegbe anɛ? 13 Eya ta ne mi ame vɔ̃ɖiwo kura gɔ̃ hã, mienya ale si miana nu nyuiwo mia viwo la, ɖe Fofo si le dziƒo la mana gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔe ame siwo bianɛ la geɖe wu oa? "
ENGLISH: 11 And which of you that is a father will his son ask for a fish and he hand him a snake instead of a fish? 12 or ask for an egg and he hand him a scorpion? 13 So if you, being bad, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father from heaven give Holy Spirit to those who ask him! "

EWE: 14 Emegbe enya gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃ aɖe si na ame aɖe zu mumu la do goe le amea me.
ENGLISH: 14 And he was expelling a demon, a dumb one, and when the demon had gone out the dumb man spoke.

EWE: 15 Ke wo dometɔ aɖewo gblɔ be: "Gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃wo ƒe fia Beelzebul dzie wòtona nyaa gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃wo. " 16 Ke ame bubuwo doe kpɔ hebiae be wòawɔ dzesi tso dziƒo yewoakpɔ.
ENGLISH: And the crowds wondered; 15 but some of them said "It is by Beelzebul the head of the demons that he expels the demons, " 16 and others, to test him, tried to get from him a token out of heaven.

EWE: 17 Esi wònya woƒe susuwo ta la, egblɔ na wo be: "Fiaɖuƒe ɖe sia ɖe si ma ɖe eɖokui ŋu la gbãna, eye aƒe si ma ɖe eɖokui ŋu la gbãna.
ENGLISH: 17 But he, knowing their ideas, said to them "Any kingdom that is divided against itself is laid waste, and house falls upon house.

EWE: 18 Nenema kee ne Satana hã ma ɖe eɖokui ŋu ɖe, aleke eƒe fiaɖuƒe awɔ ali ke? Elabena miebe Beelzebul dzie metona nyaa gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃wo doa goe.
ENGLISH: 18 And if Satan too is divided against himself how shall his kingdom be kept up? since you say it is by Beelzebul that I expel the demons.

EWE: 19 Ne Beelzebul dzie metona nyaa gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃wo doa goe la, ekema ame ka dzie mia viwo ya tona nyaa wo doa goe? Esia tae mia viwo adrɔ̃ ʋɔnu mi ɖo.
ENGLISH: 19 But if it is by Beelzebul that I expel the demons, by whom do your sons expel them? accordingly they shall be your judges.

EWE: 20 Ke ne Mawu ƒe asibidɛ dzie metona nyaa gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃wo doa goe la, ekema Mawu Fiaɖuƒe la ɖi ɖe mi ŋutɔŋutɔ.
ENGLISH: 20 But if I expel the demons by the finger of God, then the Reign of God has overtaken you.

EWE: 21 Ne ame sesẽ aɖe kpla eƒe aʋawɔnuwo katã hele eƒe fiasã ŋu dzɔm la, eƒe nunɔamesiwo nɔa dedie. 22 Ke ne ame si sesẽ wui va dze edzi heɖu edzi la, etsɔa eƒe aʋawɔnu blibo si ŋu wòle dzi ɖom ɖo la dzonɛ, eye wòmaa eƒe nu siwo wòlɔ le egbɔ la.
ENGLISH: 21 When a strong man, armed, guards his own premises, his property is in safety; 22 but when a stronger man comes on and defeats him he takes from him the weapons and armor in which he had trusted, and gives away the spoils.

EWE: 23 Ame si mele dzinye o la, tsi tsitre ɖe ŋunye, eye ame si meƒoa amewo nu ƒu kplim o la kaa wo hlẽna.
ENGLISH: 23 He who is not with me is against me, and he who does not gather with me scatters.

EWE: 24 "Ne gbɔgbɔ makɔmakɔ aɖe do go le ame aɖe me la, etsana le teƒe siwo ƒu nɔa gbɔɖemeƒe dim, eye ne mekpɔ ɖeke o la, egblɔna be, ‘Matrɔ ayi nye aƒe si me medzo le la me.’ 25 Eye ne etrɔ va aƒea me la, ekpɔna be wokplɔ eme heɖo atsyɔ̃ nɛ. 26 Azɔ eyina ɖakplɔa gbɔgbɔ adre bubu siwo vɔ̃ɖi wu eya ŋutɔ la kpena ɖe eɖokui ŋu, eye woyina ɖe eme henɔa afi ma. Eye ame ma ƒe nɔnɔme mlɔetɔwo va gblẽna ɖe edzi wu gbãtɔwo. "
ENGLISH: 24 When an unclean spirit comes out of a man it goes through waterless tracts looking for a resting-place, and upon not finding one it says ‘I will return to my home that I came from’; 25 and when it gets there it finds it swept and put in order; 26 then it goes and takes with it seven other spirits viler than itself, and they go in and live there, and that man’s last stage comes to be worse than his first. "

EWE: 27 Ke esi wòle nya siawo gblɔm la, nyɔnu aɖe do ɣli le ameha la dome gblɔ be: "Dzidzɔtɔe nye nyɔnu si ƒe vidzidɔ me nènɔ kple no si nèno! " 28 Ke egblɔ be: "Ao, ke boŋ dzidzɔtɔwoe nye ame siwo le Mawu ƒe nya la sem, eye wole edzi wɔm! "
ENGLISH: 27 And while he was saying this, a woman in the crowd raised her voice and said to him "Happy the body in which you were carried, and the breasts that you sucked! " 28 But he said "Nay, happy are those who listen to God’s word and live up to it. "

EWE: 29 Esi amehawo va le ƒu ƒom la, ede asi gbɔgblɔ me be: "Dzidzime vɔ̃ɖie dzidzime sia nye; ele dzesi dim, ke womele dzesi aɖeke na gee o, negbe Yona ƒe dzesi la ko. 30 Elabena ale si ko Yona zu dzesi na Niniwetɔwoe la, nenema ke Amegbetɔvi la hã anye dzesi na dzidzime siae.
ENGLISH: 29 And while the crowds were collecting round him he began to say "This generation is a wicked generation; it is looking for a token and will be given none but the token of Jonah; 30 for as Jonah was a token to the Ninevites, so will the Son of Man be to this generation.

EWE: 31 Woafɔ anyiehefianyɔnu la ɖe tsitre le ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃ la me kpe ɖe dzidzime sia me tɔwo ŋu, eye wòabu fɔ wo; elabena etso keke anyigba seƒe ke va be yease Salomo ƒe nunyanyawo.
ENGLISH: 31 The queen of the south shall indict the men of this generation and convict them, because she came from the ends of the earth to listen to Solomon’s wisdom, and now here is more than Solomon.

EWE: Ke kpɔ ɖa, ame si lolo wu Salomo la le afii! 32 Niniwetɔwo afɔ le ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃ la me kpe ɖe dzidzime sia ŋu, eye woabu fɔe; elabena wotrɔ dzi me le nya siwo Yona ɖe gbeƒãe la ta.
ENGLISH: 32 The men of Nineveh shall indict this generation and convict it, because they repented at Jonah’s proclamation and now here is more than Jonah.

EWE: Kpɔ ɖa, ame si lolo wu Yona la le afii! 33 Ame aɖeke mesia akaɖi dana ɖe ɣaɣlaƒe alo kusi te o, ke edanɛ ɖe akaɖiti dzi boŋ, be wòaklẽ na ame siwo vaa aƒea me la.
ENGLISH: 33 Nobody after lighting a lamp puts it in a cupboard or under the peck measure, but on the stand, that those who step in may see the glow.

EWE: 34 Wò ameti la ƒe akaɖie nye wò ŋku. Ne wò ŋku nɔa nu ɖeka ŋu la, ekema wò ameti blibo la katã me akɔ, ke ne wò ŋku biãa ŋu la, wò ameti blibo la katã hã me ado viviti.
ENGLISH: 34 Your eye is the body’s lamp: when your eye is free your whole body too is light, but when it is mean your body too is dark.

EWE: 35 Eya ta kpɔ nyuie be kekeli si le mewò la nagazu viviti o.
ENGLISH: 35 So be looking to see whether the light in you is not darkness.

EWE: 36 Eya ta ne wò ameti blibo la me kɔ, eye eƒe akpa aɖeke medo viviti o la, ekema ameti bliboa me akɔ abe ale si akaɖi ƒe keklẽ naa kekeli wòe ene. "
ENGLISH: 36 If, then, your body is all light, not having any part dark, it shall be all light as when the lamp lights you with its blaze. "

EWE: 37 Esi wògblɔ nya siawo la, Farisitɔ aɖe kpee be wòava ɖu nu kpli ye. Eya ta eyi, eye wòbɔbɔ nɔ kplɔ̃a ŋu.
ENGLISH: 37 And while he was speaking a Pharisee asked him to lunch with him; and he went in and took his place at the table.

EWE: 38 Ke ewɔ moyaa na Farisitɔ la be meklɔ asi gbã hafi be yeaɖu nua o.
ENGLISH: 38 And at seeing this the Pharisee wondered that he had not first dipped in water before lunch.

EWE: 39 Ke Aƒetɔ la gblɔ nɛ be: "Mi Farisitɔwo, mieklɔa kplu kple agba ŋu, ke miaƒe dzi me yɔ fũu kple ŋukeklẽ kpakple vɔɖivɔ̃ɖi.
ENGLISH: 39 But the Lord said to him "At present you Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and the plate, but your inside is full of rapacity and rascality.

EWE: 40 Mi movitɔwo! Menye ame si wɔ eŋuti la kee wɔ eme hã oa? 41 Ke mitsɔ nu siwo le eme la nyo dɔme na ame dahewo, eye kpɔ ɖa, nu bubuwo katã ŋu akɔ na mi! 42 Ke baba na mi Farisitɔwo, elabena mienaa ahamɛ kple ƒãglo kpakple amagbe bubuwo katã ƒe ewolia, gake mieŋea aɖaba ƒua Mawu ƒe dzɔdzɔenyenye kple eƒe lɔlɔ̃ ya dzi!
ENGLISH: 40 Silly men, did not the maker of the outside make the inside too? 41 Instead, give in charity what is in the dishes, and you have everything clean. 42 But woe to you Pharisees, because you tithe the mint and the rue and every vegetable and you slight justice and the love of God; but you ought to have done these and not let those slip.

EWE: Ele be miawɔ nu mawo, gake miagaŋe aɖaba aƒu esiawo hã dzi o.
ENGLISH: 43 Woe to you Pharisees, because you love the first seat in synagogues, and greetings in the marketplaces.

EWE: 43 Baba na mi Farisitɔwo, elabena mielɔ̃a ŋgɔgbezikpuiwo dzi nɔnɔ le ƒuƒoƒewo eye miedina be amewo nado gbe na yewo le ablɔwo me! 44 Baba na mi, elabena miele abe yɔdo siwo mele dzedzem nyuie o, eye amewo zɔa wo dzi, evɔ womenyana o la ene! "
ENGLISH: 44 Woe to you because you are like unmarked tombs that men walk over without knowing it. "

EWE: 45 Eya ta ame siwo nya Sea nyuie la dometɔ ɖeka gblɔ nɛ be: "Nufiala, esi nègblɔ nya siawo la, èdzu míawo hãe. " 46 Eye wògblɔ be: "Baba na mi ame siwo nya Sea nyuie la hã, elabena miedoa agba kpekpe siwo manya tsɔ o la na amewo, ke miawo ŋutɔwo mietsɔa miaƒe asibidɛ ɖeka pɛ hã kaa agbaawo ŋu o!
ENGLISH: 45 And one of the legists answered him "Teacher, in saying these things you are insulting us too. " 46 But he said "Woe to you too, you legists, because you load men down with loads hard to carry and do not touch the loads yourselves with one of your fingers.

EWE: 47 "Baba na mi, elabena miedzraa nyagblɔɖilawo ƒe yɔdowo ɖo, evɔ wònye mia tɔgbuiwoe wu wo! 48 Nyateƒee, mienye ɖasefowo le mia tɔgbuiwo ƒe nuwɔnawo ŋu, gake mieda asi ɖe wo dzi, elabena ame siawoe wu nyagblɔɖilawo, eye miawo miele woƒe yɔdowo dzram ɖo.
ENGLISH: 47 Woe to you because you build the tombs of the prophets, and your fathers killed them; 48 you are witnesses, then, and approve of your fathers’ deeds, because they killed them and you build.

EWE: 49 Esia ta Mawu ƒe nunya gblɔ hã be: ‘Madɔ nyagblɔɖilawo kple apostolowo ɖe wo, woawu wo dometɔ aɖewo eye woati bubuwo yome, 50 bena woabia nyagblɔɖila siwo katã ƒe ʋu wokɔ ɖe anyi tso xexea ƒe gɔmeɖoanyiɣi la tso dzidzime sia si me, 51 tso Abel ƒe ʋu dzi va se ɖe Zakariya, ame si wowu ŋutasesẽtɔe le vɔsamlekpui la kple xɔ la dome ƒe ʋu dzi.’
ENGLISH: 49 Accordingly God’s wisdom has said ‘I will send among them prophets and apostles, and some they will kill and will persecute, 50 that this generation may answer for the blood of all the prophets, shed since the foundation of the world, 51 from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zachariah who perished between the altar and the house:’ yes, I tell you, this generation shall answer for it.

EWE: Ɛ̃, mele egblɔm na mi be: Woabu fɔ dzidzime sia ɖe woƒe ʋu ta. 52 "Baba na mi ame siwo nya Sea nyuie la, elabena mietsɔ sidzedze ƒe safui la dzoe.
ENGLISH: 52 Woe to you legists, because you have taken away the key of knowledge; you did not go in yourselves and you prevented those who were going in. "

EWE: 53 Esi wòdo go le afi ma la, agbalẽfialawo kple Farisitɔwo tsi tsitre ɖe eŋu vevie hele nya geɖewo biamee tsɔ le aɖe dem nu me nɛ, 54 eye wole eɖiam, be yewoalée le eƒe nuƒoƒo me.
ENGLISH: 53 And when he came out from there the scribes and the Pharisees began to be savagely hostile and to quiz him about numerous things, 54 watching him for a chance to snap up something out of his mouth;

EWE: Luka
ENGLISH: Luke

EWE: 12 Le ɣeyiɣi sia me la, ame akpeakpewo va ƒo ƒu, ale gbegbe be wole afɔ ɖom wo nɔewo dzi. Yesu ƒo nu na eƒe nusrɔ̃lawo gbã gblɔ be: "Mikpɔ nyuie le Farisitɔwo ƒe amɔwɔʋãnu si nye alakpanuwɔwɔ la ŋuti.
ENGLISH: 12 during which the crowds gathered round by tens of thousands so that they trampled each other, and he began to say to his disciples "First and foremost beware of Pharisee yeast; that is, hypocrisy.

EWE: 2 Wometsyɔ nu naneke dzi, si womava ɖe ɖe go o, eye womeɣla naneke, si womava nya o. 3 Eya ta nya siwo miegblɔna le viviti me la, woava see le kekeli nu, eye nya si miedo dalĩ gblɔ le xɔgã me la, woaɖe gbeƒãe le xɔwo tame.
ENGLISH: 2 But there is nothing covered up that will not be uncovered, or secret that will not be found out; 3 on the contrary, whatever you have said in the dark will be heard in the light, and what you have spoken into someone’s ear in the closets will be proclaimed on the roofs.

EWE: 4 Xɔ̃nyewo, mele egblɔm na mi hã be, migavɔ̃ ame siwo wua ŋutilã, eye le esia megbe la womegatea ŋu wɔa naneke wu ema o la o. 5 Ke mafia ame si miavɔ̃ la mi: Mivɔ̃ Ame si, ne ewu ame vɔ la, ŋusẽ le esi be wòatsɔe aƒu gbe ɖe Gehena. Ɛ̃, mele egblɔm na mi be, mivɔ̃ Ame sia boŋ.
ENGLISH: 4 And I say to you friends of mine, do not fear those who kill the body and after that are not able to do anything further; 5 but I will let you know whom to fear fear him who has authority after killing to send to hell: yes, I tell you, fear him.

EWE: 6 Ðe womedzraa atsutsrɔe atɔ̃ xɔa gaku eve siwo ƒe home le sue oa? Gake Mawu meŋlɔa wo dometɔ ɖeka pɛ gɔ̃ hã be o. 7 Ke woxlẽ miaƒe taɖawo katã gɔ̃ hã.
ENGLISH: 6 Why, sparrows are sold nine for twopence, and not one of them is forgotten before God, 7 but even the hairs of your heads are all counted.

EWE: Migavɔ̃ o; miexɔ asi sãsãsã wu atsutsrɔe geɖewo.
ENGLISH: Do not fear, you are more important than a great many sparrows.

EWE: 8 "Eya ta mele egblɔm na mi be, ame sia ame si ʋua menye le amewo ŋkume la, Amegbetɔvi la hã aʋu eme le mawudɔlawo ŋkume. 9 Ke ame si gbe nu le gbɔnye le amewo ŋkume la, nye hã magbe nu le egbɔ le mawudɔlawo ŋkume. 10 Eye ame sia ame si gblɔ nya vlo aɖe ɖe Amegbetɔvi la ŋu la, woatsɔe akee, ke ame si gblɔ busunya ɖe gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔea ŋu la, womatsɔe akee o.
ENGLISH: 8 But I tell you, everyone who acknowledges me before men the Son of Man will in his turn acknowledge before the angels of God, 9 but he who repudiates me before men will be disowned before the angels of God; 10 and everyone who says a thing against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but he who blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.

EWE: 11 Ne wokplɔ mi yi amehawo, dziɖulawo kple ŋusẽtɔwo ŋkume la, migatsi dzimaɖi le nya si miatsɔ aʋli mia ɖokui ta alo le nya si miagblɔ la ŋuti o, 12 elabena gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔe la afia nya si miagblɔ le gaƒoƒo ma tututu me la mi. "
ENGLISH: 11 But when they bring you in before synagogues and governments and authorities, do not fret over how you shall make your defense or what it shall be or what you shall say; 12 for the Holy Spirit will teach you at the moment what you must say. "

EWE: 13 Eye ame aɖe tso ameha la dome gblɔ nɛ be: "Nufiala, gblɔ na nɔvinye ne wòama domenyinu la kplim. " 14 Ebiae be: "Ŋutsu, ame kae ɖom ʋɔnudrɔ̃la alo nyametsola ɖe mi ame evea nu? " 15 Eye wògblɔ na wo be: "Mina miaƒe ŋkuwo nanɔ ʋuʋu, eye mikpɔ nyuie le ŋukeklẽ ɖe sia ɖe ƒomevi ŋu, elabena ne nu gbogbo aɖewo le ame si hã la, nu siawo mana agbee o. " 16 Ale wòdo lo sia na wo be: "Kesinɔtɔ aɖe ƒe anyigba wɔ nu nyuie.
ENGLISH: 13 And one of the crowd said to him "Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me. " 14 But he said to him "Man, who has set me as a judge or divider over you? " 15 And he said to them "See that you keep clear of all overreaching, because it is not by having an oversupply that one has his living out of his property. "

EWE: 17 Eya ta ebu le eɖokui me be, ‘Esi teƒe aɖeke megale asinye madzra nye agblemenukuwo ɖo o ɖe, nu ka wɔ ge mala?’ 18 Eya ta egblɔ be, ‘Menya nu si mawɔ: Mamu nye nudzraɖoƒewo, eye matu esiwo lolo wu; afi mae madzra nye nukuwo katã kple nye nuwo katã ɖo, 19 eye magblɔ na ɖokuinye be: "Èdzra nu nyui geɖe ɖo ɖi hena ƒe geɖewo; ɖe dzi ɖi, ɖu nu, no nu, eye nàɖu agbe. "’ 20 Ke Mawu gblɔ nɛ be: ‘Movitɔ, zã sia me ke woabia wò agbe le asiwò me. Ekema ame ka tɔe nu siwo nèdzra ɖo ɖi la azu?’ 21 Nenemae wònɔna na ame si ƒo kesinɔnuwo nu ƒu na eɖokui, gake menye kesinɔtɔ le Mawu gbɔ o. "
ENGLISH: 16 And he told them a parable: "Once upon a time a rich man’s lands bore a great crop, 17 and he was going over the question to himself ‘What shall I do, because I have nowhere to put my crops when I gather them?’ 18 and he said ‘This is what I will do: pull down my barns and build larger ones, and put all my wheat and the rest of my good things in them, 19 and say to my soul "Soul, you have a great stock of good things laid up for years: rest, eat, drink, be gay "’; 20 but God said to him ‘Silly man, this night your soul is to be called for, and who will have what you have got ready?’ 21 That is what the man is like who lays by for himself and is not rich toward God. "

EWE: 22 Eye wògblɔ na eƒe nusrɔ̃lawo be: "Esia tae mele egblɔm na mi be, midzudzɔ dzimaɖitsitsi ɖe miaƒe agbe ŋu le nu si miaɖu ŋuti, alo le miaƒe ŋutilãwo ŋu le nu si miado ŋuti. 23 Elabena agbe la wu nuɖuɖu, eye ŋutilã la wu nudodo.
ENGLISH: 22 And he said to his disciples "For this reason I tell you, do not fret over your soul what you shall eat, nor over your body what you shall put on; 23 for the soul is more than the food, and the body than the garment.

EWE: Ðe miexɔ asi sãsãsã wu xeviwo oa? 25 Mia dometɔ kae ne ele dzimaɖi tsim la, wòate ŋu atsɔ abɔklugui ɖeka akpe eƒe agbenɔƒe? 26 Eya ta ne miate ŋu awɔ nu sue sia teti gɔ̃ hã o la, ke nu ka tae miatsi dzimaɖi ɖe nu susɔeawo ŋu? 27 Mibu ale si dzogbenyawo tsinae la ŋu kpɔ: Womewɔa dɔ alo trea ɖeti o; gake mele egblɔm na mi be, le Salomo ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe la katã me gɔ̃ hã la, meɖo atsyɔ̃ kpɔ abe esiawo dometɔ ɖeka ene o.
ENGLISH: 24 Observe the ravens, that they neither sow nor reap, they who have no storeroom nor barn, and God feeds them: how much more important you are than the birds! 25 And which of you by fretting can add a foot to his height? 26 so if you cannot do even a trifling thing why do you fret about the rest? 27 Observe the lilies, how they neither spin nor weave, but, I tell you, not even Solomon in all his glory was clad like one of these.

EWE: 28 Ke ne Mawu ɖoa atsyɔ̃ na gbe si le gbe me egbe, eye etsɔ ko woatsɔe aƒu gbe ɖe dzo me la, ɖe maɖo atsyɔ̃ na miawo ya geɖe wu oa? Mi xɔseʋɛtɔwo! 29 Eya ta migatsi dzimaɖi ɖe nu si miaɖu kple nu si miano la ŋu o, eye midzudzɔ dzimaɖitsitsi fũu akpa; 30 elabena nu siawo yomee xexemedukɔwo tina vevie, ke mia Fofo nyae be nu siawo hiã mi.
ENGLISH: 28 But if in the field God so attires the plants, that are there today and are thrown in a firepot tomorrow, how much more he will you, little-faiths! 29 And do not you be seeking things to eat and to drink, and do not be nervous; 30 for the nations of the world hunt after all this, but your Father knows that you want this.

EWE: 31 Ke minɔ eƒe Fiaɖuƒe la didi dzi boŋ, eye woatsɔ nu siawo akpee na mi.
ENGLISH: 31 But do seek his Reign, and you will have this added.

EWE: 32 "Alẽha sue, mègavɔ̃ o, elabena edze mia Fofo la ŋu be yeatsɔ Fiaɖuƒe la na mi.
ENGLISH: 32 "Do not be afraid, little flock; because your Father has been pleased to give you the kingship.

EWE: Mitɔ gakotoku siwo megblẽna o, siwo nye nu xɔasi siwo nu mayi o la, na mia ɖokui ɖe dziƒowo, afi si fiafitɔ megogona o, eye agbagblaʋui hã megblẽa nu le o. 34 Elabena afi si wò nu xɔasiwo le la, afi mae wò dzi hã anɔ.
ENGLISH: 33 Sell your property and give charity: make yourselves purses that do not grow old, an inexhaustible store in heaven where thief does not come near and moth does not spoil; 34 for where your stores are, there your heart too will be.

EWE: 35 "Midzra ɖo, minɔ klalo, eye miaƒe akaɖiwo nenɔ bibim, 36 eye minɔ abe ame siwo le woƒe aƒetɔ lalam be wòagbɔ tso srɔ̃ɖeƒe, ale be ne eva ɖo eye wòƒo ʋɔa la, yewoaʋui nɛ enumake la ene.
ENGLISH: 35 Let your loins be girded and your lamps lighted, 36 and you like men watching for their master, for the time when he comes away from the wedding, that when he comes and knocks they may open to him at once.

EWE: 37 Dzidzɔtɔwoe nye kluvi mawo siwo aƒetɔ la akpɔ be wole ŋudzɔ ne eva ɖo!
ENGLISH: 37 Happy are those servants whom the master, when he comes, shall find awake: I tell you verily he will put on an apron and send them to the table and come and wait on them.

EWE: Vavã mele egblɔm na mi be, eya ŋutɔ abla ali dzi, eye wòana woanɔ kplɔ̃ ŋu, eye wòasubɔ wo.
ENGLISH: 38 And if he comes in the second watch and finds them so, and if in the third, happy are they.

EWE: 38 Dzidzɔtɔwoe woanye ne eva le ŋudzɔɣi evelia, alo etɔ̃lia gɔ̃ hã me, eye wòkpɔ wo wole ŋudzɔ! 39 Ke minya esia be, ne ɖe aƒea tɔ anya gaƒoƒo si dzi fiafitɔ ava la, anye ne maɖe mɔ nɛ wòadze kpɔ age ɖe eƒe me o.
ENGLISH: 39 But be sure of this, that if the man of the house had known at which hour the thief was coming he would not have let his house be broken into.

EWE: 40 Miawo hã minɔ dzadzraɖoɖi, elabena Amegbetɔvi la ava le gaƒoƒo si miesusu o la dzi. "
ENGLISH: 40 Be ready yourselves, because it will be at the hour when you are not thinking of it that the Son of Man comes. "

EWE: 41 Eye Petro biae be: "Aƒetɔ, míawo koe nèle lo sia dom na loo alo amewo katã? " 42 Eye Aƒetɔ la ɖo eŋu be: "Ame ka tututue nye aƒedzikpɔla nuteƒewɔla, si dze aɖaŋu, si eƒe aƒetɔ aɖo eƒe subɔviwo ƒe ha la nu, be wòanɔ nuɖuɖu si asu na wo la nam wo le ɣeyiɣi nyuitɔ dzi? 43 Dzidzɔtɔe kluvi ma anye ne eƒe aƒetɔ gbɔ va kpɔe wòle ewɔm nenema! 44 Vavã mele egblɔm na mi be, atsɔe aɖo eƒe nuwo katã nu.
ENGLISH: 41 And Peter said "Sir, are you telling this parable with reference to us ourselves or to everybody? " 42 And the Lord said "Who, then, is the intelligent faithful steward whom the master will set over his help to give them their rations punctually? 43 Happy is that servant whom his master, when he comes, shall find doing thus: 44 I tell you truly he will set him over all his property.

EWE: 45 Ke ne kluvi ma agblɔ le eƒe dzi me be, ‘Nye aƒetɔ mele gbɔgbɔm kaba o,’ eye wòade asi subɔviŋutsuwo kple subɔvinyɔnuwo ƒoƒo me, eye wòaɖu nu ano nu eye wòamu aha la, 46 kluvi ma ƒe aƒetɔ ava le gbe si gbe mele mɔ kpɔm nɛ o kple gaƒoƒo si menya o la me, eye wòahe to nɛ vevie ahana gomee kpe ɖe ame mawɔnuteƒewo ŋu. 47 Ekema woaƒo kluvi ma si nya eƒe aƒetɔ ƒe lɔlɔ̃nu, gake menɔ dzadzraɖoɖi alo wɔ nu si eƒe aƒetɔa gblɔ o la geɖe. 48 Ke ame si menya o, eye wòwɔ nu si dze ƒoƒo la, woaƒoe ʋɛ. Vavãe, ame sia ame si wona nu geɖe la, woabia nu geɖe tso esi, eye ame si wotsɔ ɖo nu geɖe nu la, woabia nu geɖe wu tso esi.
ENGLISH: 45 But if that servant says to himself ‘My master is late about coming’ and begins to beat the men and the maids, and to eat and drink and get drunk, 46 that servant’s master will come on a day when he does not expect it and at an hour that he does not know, and will cut him up and allot him a part among the faithless; 47 and that servant who knew his master’s wishes and did not get things ready or do in accordance with his wishes will have many strokes of the whip, 48 but the one who did not know and did things that deserve whipping will have few; and everyone to whom much was given will be called on for much, and on him to whom they entrusted most they will make most of a demand.

EWE: 49 "Ðe meva dzo do ge ɖe anyigba dzi, eye ne dzoa lé xoxo ɖe, nu kae magadi? 50 Nyateƒee, nyɔnyrɔ aɖe li wòle be maxɔ, eye aleke metsi dzodzodzoe va se ɖe esime wòawu enue nye esi! 51 Ðe miesusu be ŋutifafa na gee meva le anyigba dzia?
ENGLISH: 49 "I came to throw out fire on the earth, and how I wish it was already kindled! 50 And I have a water to plunge in, and what a pressure I am under till it is done! 51 Do you think I have come to give peace on earth? no, I tell you, but disunion.

EWE: Gbeɖe, mele egblɔm na mi be, mama boŋ ye. 52 Elabena tso fifia dzi la, ame atɔ̃ anɔ aƒe ɖeka me, eye wo dome ama, etɔ̃ atsi tsitre ɖe eve ŋu, eye eve ɖe etɔ̃ ŋu. 53 Fofo kple viŋutsu dome ama, eye viŋutsu kple fofoa dome ama, vidada kple vianyɔnu dome ama, eye vinyɔnu kple dadaa dome ama, lɔ̃xo kple lɔ̃xoyɔvi dome ama, eye lɔ̃xoyɔvi kple lɔ̃xoa dome ama. "
ENGLISH: 52 For from now on five in one family will be parted three against two and two against three; 53 they will part so that father will be against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against her mother, mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law. "

EWE: 54 Eye wògblɔ na amehawo hã be: "Ne miekpɔ alilikpo le dodom le ɣetoɖoƒe la, miegblɔna enumake be: ‘Tsi gã aɖe gbɔna,’ eye wòvaa eme hã. 55 Eye ne miekpɔ be ya ƒo tso anyiehe la, miegblɔna be: ‘Xexea me le dzo xɔ ge,’ eye wòvaa eme hã.
ENGLISH: 54 And to the crowds too he said "When you see a cloud rising in the west, at once you say ‘there is a shower coming,’ and so it does; 55 and when you see the wind in the south you say ‘there will be a scorcher,’ and there is.

EWE: 56 Alakpanuwɔlawo, mienya ale si mialé ŋku ɖe anyigba kple dziŋgɔli ƒe nɔnɔme ŋu, ke aleke wɔ mienya ale si mialé ŋku ɖe ɣeyiɣi sia tututu ya ŋu o? 57 Eye nu ka tae mietsoa nya me le nu si le dzɔdzɔe la ŋuti na mia ɖokui o? 58 Le kpɔɖeŋu me, ne wò kple wò ketɔ si tsɔ nya ɖe ŋuwò mieyina dziɖula aɖe ŋkume la, dze agbagba nàdzra mia dome ɖo le mɔa dzi, ne magakplɔ wò ayi ʋɔnudrɔ̃la ŋkume, ale be ʋɔnudrɔ̃la la natsɔ wò ade asi na kpovitɔ, eye kpovitɔ la nade wò gaxɔ me o. 59 Mele egblɔm na wò be, màdo go le afi ma akpɔ o, va se ɖe esime nàxe wò gaku suetɔ mamlɛa hafi. "
ENGLISH: 56 You hypocrites, you know enough to judge of the face of the earth and the face of the sky, how is it you fail to judge of these times? 57 And why do you not of yourselves decide on the right? 58 While you are going with your antagonist to appear before a magistrate, make it an object to get clear of him on the road, for fear he should drag you to the judge and the judge should hand you over to the officer and the officer should put you in prison: 59 I tell you, you shall not get out from there till you pay the very last copper. "

EWE: Luka
ENGLISH: Luke

EWE: 13 Ɣemaɣi la, ame aɖewo siwo le afi ma la gblɔ ale si Pilato wu Galileatɔ aɖewo siwo nɔ vɔ sam eye wòtsɔ woƒe ʋu tsaka woƒe vɔsalãwo ƒe ʋu la ŋu nya nɛ. 2 Eya ta ebia wo be: "Ðe miesusu be Galileatɔ siawo nye nu vɔ̃ wɔlawo wu Galileatɔ bubuawo le esi nu sia dzɔ ɖe wo dzi ta? 3 Gbeɖe, mele egblɔm na mi be, ne mietrɔ dzi me o la, woatsrɔ̃ mi katã nenema ke.
ENGLISH: 13 And at that very time there were some present who reported to him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices; 2 and he answered them "Do you think these Galileans had been bigger sinners than any of the Galileans, that they suffered this 3 no, I tell you, but if you do not repent all of you will perish similarly.

EWE: 4 Alo ɖe miesusu be ame wuienyi siwo dzi Siloam-mɔ́ la mu dze woku la, woawoe ɖi fɔ wu Yerusalemtɔ bubuawo katã mahã? 5 Gbeɖe, mele egblɔm na mi be, ne mietrɔ dzi me o la, woatsrɔ̃ mi katã nenema ke. "
ENGLISH: 4 Or those eighteen on whom the tower fell in Siloam and killed them, do you think they had more of an account standing against them than any of the people that live in Jerusalem? 5 no, I tell you, but if you do not repent you will all perish in the same way. "

EWE: 6 Eye wòdo lo sia be: "Ame aɖe do gboti ɖe eƒe waingble me, eye wòva di kutsetse le edzi, ke mekpɔ ɖeke o.
ENGLISH: 6 And he told this parable: "A man had a fig-tree planted in his orchard, and came looking for fruit on it and did not find any.

EWE: Lãe ƒu anyi! Nu ka ŋuti wòaxɔ anyigba la dzodzro?’ 8 Eɖo eŋu nɛ be, ‘Aƒetɔ, na wòaganɔ anyi ƒe ɖeka kpɔ, ne maɖe do aƒo xlãe ahado aɖu ɖe ete. 9 Ne eva tse le etsɔme la, enyo; ke ne mele nenema o la, nàlãe aƒu anyi.’ "
ENGLISH: 7 And he said to the orchardman ‘Here it is three years since I have been coming to look for fruit on this tree and not finding any: cut it away, what is it keeping the land idle for into the bargain?’ 8 And he answered him ‘Sir, let it be this one year more till I dig around it and put in manure; 9 and if it does produce fruit for the coming year well, if not, you shall cut it away.’ "

EWE: 10 Azɔ ele nu fiam le ƒuƒoƒeawo dometɔ ɖeka le Sabat dzi. 11 Eye kpɔ ɖa, nyɔnu aɖe si me gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃ aɖe le, eye wòna wòzu dɔnɔ ƒe wuienyi sɔŋ; eye wòxa gobaa ale be metea ŋu dzɔna kura o la le afi ma.
ENGLISH: 10 And he was teaching in one of the synagogues on the sabbath, 11 and there was a woman who had had a sickness-spirit eighteen years, and was bent over and unable to stand perfectly erect.

EWE: 12 Esi Yesu kpɔe la, eyɔe gblɔ nɛ be: "Nyɔnu, wotu ka wò tso wò dɔléle la me. " 13 Eye wòda eƒe asiwo ɖe edzi, enumake nyɔnua dzɔ kã, eye wòde asi Mawu kafukafu me.
ENGLISH: 12 And Jesus, seeing her, called out to her and said "Woman, you are released from your sickness, " 13 and laid his hands on her; and immediately she straightened up and glorified God.

EWE: 14 Ke ƒuƒoƒea dzi kpɔlaa do dziku vevie le esi Yesu da gbe le amea ŋu le Sabat dzi ta, eye wògblɔ na ameha la be: "Ŋkeke adee li, siwo dzi wòle be ame nawɔ dɔ le, eya ta miva ne woada gbe le mia ŋu le ŋkeke mawo dzi, ke menye le Sabat la dzi o. " 15 Ke Aƒetɔ la ɖo eŋu nɛ be: "Alakpanuwɔlawo, ɖe mia dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe meɖea ka eƒe nyitsu alo eƒe tedzi le lãkpo me le Sabat dzi, eye wòkplɔnɛ yia tsinoƒe oa? 16 Ðe ɣeyiɣi mede be woaɖe ka nyɔnu sia, si nye Abraham vi, eye Satana blae ƒe wuienyi sɔŋ la le Sabat ŋkeke dzi oa? " 17 Esi wògblɔ nya siawo la, ŋukpe lé ame siwo tsi tsitre ɖe eŋu la katã, ke ameha blibo la de asi dzidzɔkpɔkpɔ me le nu wɔnuku siwo katã wòwɔ la ta.
ENGLISH: 14 But the director of the synagogue, taking offense at Jesus’s having cured on the sabbath, answered by saying to the crowd "There are six days in which work ought to be done: so come in them and be cured, and not on the sabbath day. " 15 But the Lord answered him "Hypocrites, does not each of you on the sabbath untie his ox or ass from the manger, and lead it away and water it? 16 and ought not this woman, a daughter of Abraham whom Satan had tied up these eighteen years, to be untied from this tether on the sabbath day? " 17 And as he said this all his opponents were put to shame, and all the crowd rejoiced over all the magnificent things that were being done by him.

EWE: 18 Eya ta egblɔ be: "Nu kae Mawu Fiaɖuƒe la ɖi, eye nu kae matsɔe asɔ kplii? 19 Ele abe sinapi-ku si ame aɖe ƒã ɖe eƒe abɔ me, eye wòtsi va zu ati, eye dziƒoxewo va wɔ atɔ ɖe eƒe alɔwo me la ene. "
ENGLISH: 18 So he said "What is the Reign of God like, and to what shall I compare it? 19 it is like a grain of mustard which a man took and dropped into his garden, and it grew and became a tree, and the birds of the air perched in its branches. "

EWE: 20 Egagblɔ be: "Nu kae matsɔ Mawu Fiaɖuƒe la asɔ kplii? 21 Ele abe amɔwɔʋãnu si nyɔnu aɖe tsɔ blu amɔwɔ dzidzenu gã etɔ̃ va se ɖe esime amɔwɔ bliboa ʋã la ene. "
ENGLISH: 20 And again he said "To what shall I compare the Reign of God? 21 it is like a bit of yeast which a woman took and hid in forty quarts of flour till it all grew yeasty. "

EWE: 22 Eye wòyi ɖato duwo kple kɔƒewo me hele nu fiam, eye wòle mɔzɔzɔa dzi ɖo ta Yerusalem. 23 Ke ame aɖe biae be: "Aƒetɔ, ame ʋɛ aɖewo koe akpɔ ɖeɖea? " Eɖo eŋu na wo be: 24 "Miʋli sesĩe be miato agbo xaxɛ la nu age ɖe eme, elabena mele egblɔm na mi be: Ame geɖewo adi be yewoage ɖe eme, ke womate ŋui o.
ENGLISH: 22 And he was passing through city after city and village after village teaching and traveling toward Jerusalem, 23 and someone said to him "Sir, are there few who are saved? " and he said to them 24 "Push to get in through the narrow gate; because, I tell you, a great many will try to get in and not be able.

EWE: 25 Ne aƒea tɔ tso do ʋɔa la, miatɔ ɖe xexe anɔ ʋɔa ƒom anɔ gbɔgblɔm be, ‘Aƒetɔ, ʋui na mí,’ ekema aɖo eŋu na mi be: ‘Nyemenya afi si mietso o.’ 26 Ekema miade asi gbɔgblɔ me be, ‘Míeɖu nu heno nu le ŋkuwòme, eye nèfia nu le míaƒe ablɔwo dzi ɖe.’ 27 Ke agblɔ na mi be, ‘Nyemenya afi si mietso o.
ENGLISH: 25 After the head of the house rises and shuts the door, and you begin to stand outside and knock on the door, saying ‘Open to us, sir,’ and he shall answer you ‘I do not know you to tell where you are from,’ 26 then you will begin to say ‘We have eaten and drunk before you, and you have taught in our streets’; 27 and he will tell you ‘I do not know where you are from: take yourselves away from me, all you doers of wrong.’ 28 There will the weeping and the grinding of teeth be, when you see Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets in the Reign of God and yourselves put out.

EWE: Mite ɖa le gbɔnye, mi nu madzɔmadzɔ wɔlawo katã!’ 28 Afi mae miafa avi ahaɖu aɖukli le, ne miekpɔ Abraham, Isak, Yakob kple nyagblɔɖilawo katã le Mawu Fiaɖuƒe la me, ke wotsɔ miawo ya ƒu gbe ɖe xexe.
ENGLISH: 29 And they will come from east and west and from north and south and go to the table in the Reign of God; 30 and there are last who will be first and there are first who will be last. "

EWE: 29 Amewo atso ɣedzeƒe, ɣetoɖoƒe, dziehe kple anyiehe, eye woabɔbɔ nɔ kplɔ̃ ŋu le Mawu Fiaɖuƒe la me.
ENGLISH: 31 At that moment certain Pharisees approached him saying "Go out and away from here, because Herod is wanting to kill you. " 32 And he said to them "Go and tell that fox ‘I am expelling demons and performing cures today and tomorrow, and the third day I come to my consummation.

EWE: 30 Eye kpɔ ɖa, ame mlɔetɔ aɖewo li, siwo ava zu gbãtɔwo, eye ame gbãtɔ aɖewo li, siwo ava zu mlɔetɔwo. "
ENGLISH: 33 I must go on my way, though, today and tomorrow and the next day, because it is not possible that a prophet should perish outside Jerusalem.

EWE: 34 Yerusalem, Yerusalem, si wu nyagblɔɖilawo, eye wòƒu kpe ame siwo wodɔ ɖo ɖe egbɔ zi nenie nyemehedi be maƒo viwòwo nu ƒu abe ale si koklonɔ ƒoa viawo nu ƒu ɖe eƒe aʋalawo te ene o! Ke mielɔ̃ o! 35 Kpɔ ɖa! Wogblẽ miaƒe aƒe la ɖi na mi.
ENGLISH: 34 Jerusalem, Jerusalem, killer of the prophets and stoner of those that are sent to her how many times I have wished to gather her children as a bird gathers her brood under her wings, and you would not! 35 Lo, your house is left to you.

EWE: Mele egblɔm na mi be: Miegale kpɔ ye ge o va se ɖe esime miagblɔ be: ‘Woayra ame si gbɔna le Yehowa ƒe ŋkɔ me!’ "
ENGLISH: And I tell you, you shall not see me until there comes the time when you say ‘Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.’ "

EWE: Luka
ENGLISH: Luke

EWE: 14 Ɣebubuɣi la, Yesu yi Farisitɔwo ƒe kplɔla aɖe ƒe me le Sabat dzi be yeaɖu nu, eye wonɔ ŋku lém ɖe eŋu vevie. 2 Eye kpɔ ɖa, ŋutsu aɖe si le tetedɔ lém la le eŋgɔ.
ENGLISH: 14 And when he came into the home of one of the heads of the Pharisees on a sabbath to eat a meal, they were watching him, 2 and there before him was a man with the dropsy.

EWE: 3 Eya ta Yesu bia ame siwo nya Sea nyuie la kple Farisitɔwo be: "Ðe se ɖe mɔ be woada dɔ le Sabat dzi loo alo se meɖe mɔ o? " 4 Ke wozi kpi.
ENGLISH: 3 And Jesus answered by saying to the legists and Pharisees "Is it lawful on the sabbath to cure, or not? " 4 but they made no move.

EWE: Ale wòka asi amea ŋu heda gbe le eŋu, eye wòdo mɔe. 5 Ebia wo be: "Mia dometɔ kae li, ne viaŋutsu alo eƒe nyitsu ge ɖe vudo me le Sabat dzi la, maɖee enumake o? " 6 Eye womete ŋu ɖo nya sia ŋu o.
ENGLISH: And he took him and healed him and dismissed him, 5 and said to them "Which one of you, if his son or his steer falls into a well, will not at once pull him out on the sabbath day? " 6 And they were not able to reply to that.

EWE: 7 Esi wòkpɔ ale si ame kpekpeawo le bubunɔƒewo tiam na wo ɖokuiwo la, egblɔ na wo be: 8 "Ne ame aɖe kpe wò va srɔ̃ɖekplɔ̃ ŋu la, mègava nɔ bubunɔƒe gãtɔ o. Ðewohĩ ekpe ame aɖe si nye bubume wu wò la hã vɛ. 9 Eye ame si kpe wò kplii la ava gblɔ na wò be: ‘Tsɔ wò nɔƒe na ame sia.’ Ekema àtsɔ ŋukpe ayi aɖanɔ nɔƒe mlɔetɔ. 10 Ke boŋ ne wokpe wò la, yi ɖanɔ anyi ɖe nɔƒe mlɔetɔ, ale be ne ame si kpe wò la va la, wòagblɔ na wò be: ‘Xɔ̃nye, yi ɖanɔ nɔƒe si ŋu bubu le wu.’ Ekema anye bubu na wò le ame kpekpe susɔeawo katã ŋkume.
ENGLISH: 7 And he told the guests a parable, noticing how they were choosing the first places at the table: 8 "When you are invited to a wedding by anybody, do not take the first place, for fear there may have been invited by him a man of more account than you, 9 and the one who invited you and him shall come and say to you ‘Make room for this man,’ and then you will begin to occupy the last place with humiliation; 10 but when you are invited go and take the last place, in order that when the one who has invited you comes he may say to you ‘Friend, come further up’ then it will redound to your honor before all who are at the table with you.

EWE: 11 Elabena ame sia ame si doa eɖokui ɖe dzi la, woabɔbɔe ɖe anyi, eye ame sia ame si bɔbɔa eɖokui la, woadoe ɖe dzi. "
ENGLISH: 11 For everyone who lifts himself up will be put down, and he who puts himself down will be lifted up. "

EWE: Elabena ɖewohĩ woawo hã woava kpe wò gbe ɖeka, eye ema azu teƒeɖoɖo na wò. 13 Ke boŋ ne èɖo kplɔ̃ la, kpe ame dahewo, nuwɔametɔwo, bunɔwo kple ŋkuagbãtɔwo; 14 ekema àkpɔ dzidzɔ, le esi naneke mele wo si woatsɔ aɖo eteƒe na wò o la ta. Ke woaɖo eteƒe na wò le ame dzɔdzɔewo ƒe tsitretsitsi la me. " 15 Esi ame siwo hã wokpe dometɔ ɖeka se nya siawo la, egblɔ nɛ be: "Dzidzɔtɔe nye ame si aɖu nu le Mawu Fiaɖuƒe la me. "
ENGLISH: 12 And he also said to the one who had invited him "When you give a lunch or a dinner, do not call your friends nor your brothers nor your relatives nor rich neighbors, for fear they should return the invitation themselves and you should have a compensation; 13 but when you give a banquet invite poor men, maimed men, cripples, blind men, 14 and happy shall you be, because they are not able to compensate you; for you shall be compensated at the resurrection of the righteous. "

EWE: 16 Yesu gblɔ nɛ be: "Ame aɖe ɖo fiẽnuɖukplɔ̃ gã aɖe, eye wòkpe ame geɖewo. 17 Esi fiẽnuɖuɣia ɖo la, edɔ eƒe kluvi ɖa be wòayi aɖagblɔ na ame kpekpeawo be, ‘Miva, elabena nu sia nu sɔ gbe.’ 18 Ke wo katã wodo taflatsɛ. Ame gbãtɔ gblɔ nɛ be, ‘Meƒle agble, eye ele nam be mayi aɖakpɔe ɖa; eya ta meɖe kuku, nyemate ŋu ava o.’ 19 Eye ame bubu gblɔ be, ‘Meƒle nyi eveeve teƒe atɔ̃, eye meyina wo do ge kpɔ, eya ta meɖe kuku, nyemate ŋu ava o.’ 20 Ame bubu hã gblɔ be, ‘Ðeko meɖe srɔ̃e nye esia, eya ta nyemate ŋu ava o.’ 21 Eye kluvi la trɔ gbɔ va gblɔ nya siawo na eƒe aƒetɔ la.
ENGLISH: 15 And one of his fellow-guests heard this and said to him "Happy is he who shall eat bread in the Reign of God. " 16 But he said to him "Once upon a time there was a man who gave a great dinner and invited many; 17 and he sent his servant at the hour for the dinner to tell the invited guests ‘Come, it is ready now.’ 18 And right off they all began to excuse themselves: the first said to him ‘I have bought a field and am obliged to go out and see it; pray excuse me’; 19 and another said ‘I have bought five yoke of oxen and am on my way to see what they are worth; pray excuse me’; 20 and another said ‘I have got married and consequently cannot come’; 21 and the servant came and reported it to his master.

EWE: Ale eƒe aƒetɔ do dɔmedzoe, eye wògblɔ na eƒe kluvi la be, ‘Netsɔ, yi dua ƒe ablɔwo me kple kpɔdomeewo, eye nàkplɔ ame dahewo, nuwɔametɔwo, ŋkuagbãtɔwo kple bunɔwo vɛ.’ 22 Le ɣeyiɣi aɖe megbe la, kluvi la gbɔ va gblɔ be, ‘Aƒetɔ, mewɔ nu si nèɖo nam la, gake nɔƒe gali.’ 23 Eya ta aƒetɔ la gblɔ na kluvi la be, ‘Yi mɔwo dzi kple ablɔwo me, eye nàƒoe ɖe amewo nu be woava, ne nye aƒea me nayɔ. 24 Elabena mele egblɔm na mi be, ame mawo, siwo mekpe hafi wogbe la, dometɔ aɖeke maɖɔ nye fiẽnuɖuɖu la kpɔ o.’ "
ENGLISH: Then the host was angry, and said to his servant ‘Go right out to the streets and alleys of the city and bring the poor and maimed and crippled and blind in here.’ 22 And the servant said ‘Sir, what you ordered has been done and there is still room.’ 23 And the master said to the servant ‘Go out to the highways and hedges and make people come in, so that my house shall be full; 24 for I tell you none of those guests that were invited shall taste my dinner.’ "

EWE: 25 Ke ameha gã aɖe le mɔ zɔm kplii gbe ɖeka, eye wòtrɔ gblɔ na wo be: 26 "Ne ame aɖe va gbɔnye, eye melé fu fofoa, dadaa, srɔ̃a, viawo, nɔviaŋutsuwo kple nɔvianyɔnuwo, ɛ̃, ne melé fu eya ŋutɔ ƒe agbe kekeake gɔ̃ hã o la, mate ŋu anye nye nusrɔ̃la o.
ENGLISH: 25 And great crowds were going along with him, and he turned and said to them 26 "If one comes to me and does not hate his father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, and his own self besides, he cannot be a disciple of mine.

EWE: 27 Ame si metsɔ eƒe fuwɔameti hedze yonyeme o la mate ŋu anye nye nusrɔ̃la o.
ENGLISH: 27 Whoever does not carry his cross and come after me cannot be a disciple of mine.

EWE: 28 Le kpɔɖeŋu me, mia dometɔ kae li ne edi be yeatu xɔ la, manɔ anyi abu eŋu kɔnta gbã ahakpɔ ɖa be nu sɔ gbɔ ɖe ye si yeate ŋu awu enu o mahã? 29 Ne menye nenema o la, aɖo egɔme anyi, gake mate ŋu awu enu o, eye ame siwo katã kpɔe la aɖu fewu le eŋu 30 agblɔ be: ‘Ame sia dze xɔtutu gɔme, gake mete ŋu wu enu o.’ 31 Alo fia kae li, eye ne eyina aʋa kpe ge kple fia bubu la, manɔ anyi abu eŋuti gbã, ne ate ŋu atsɔ asrafo akpe ewo anɔ te ɖe ame si gbɔna aʋa kpe ge kplii la ƒe asrafo akpe blaeveawo nu oa? 32 Ne ekpɔe be manya wɔ o la, ekema ne ame kemɛa le adzɔge ʋĩi gbɔna la, adɔ eƒe amewo ɖa be woawɔ ŋutifafa kplii.
