ENGLISH: 28 And as they did not think well of recognizing God, God gave them up to a mind that cannot be thought well of, to do what ought not to be done, 29 crammed with all injustice, villainy, greed, viciousness, full of envy, murder, quarreling, fraud, malice; whisperers, 30 detractors, God-haters, bullies, proud, pretentious, inventors of vices, disobedient to parents, 31 senseless, faithless, loveless, pitiless 32 who, aware of God’s verdict that those who commit such things deserve death, not only do the things but even approve of doing them.

EWE: Romatɔwo
ENGLISH: Romans

EWE: 2 Eya ta Oo, ame, ame ka kee nèɖanye o, ne èdrɔ̃a ʋɔnu amewo la, ekema taflatsɛdodo aɖeke mele asiwò o; elabena ne èdrɔ̃ ʋɔnu ame aɖe la, èbua fɔ ɖokuiwò, elabena wò, ame si drɔ̃a ʋɔnu la, wò ŋutɔ hã èwɔa nu mawo ke.
ENGLISH: 2 Wherefore you are inexcusable, man, any man that passes judgment; for in the judgment you pass on the other man you are condemning yourself, for you who pass it are committing the same things.

EWE: 2 Ke míenyae be ame siwo wɔa nu siawo la, Mawu drɔ̃a ʋɔnu wo ɖe eteƒe le nyateƒe la nu.
ENGLISH: 2 And we know that God’s judgment is truthfully against those who commit such things.

EWE: 3 Oo ame, ke esi nèdrɔ̃a ʋɔnu ame siwo wɔa nu siawo, evɔ wò ŋutɔ hã nèwɔa wo la, ɖe nèsusu be yeate ŋu asi le Mawu ƒe ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃ nua? 4 Alo esi mènya be ɖe Mawu le didim be yeakplɔ wò ayi dzimetɔtrɔ gbɔ le eƒe dɔmenyonyo la ta o tae nèdoa vlo eƒe dɔmenyonyo kple dzidodo kpakple dzigbɔgbɔ blewu laa? 5 Ke esi nèsẽ dzi me hegbe dzimetɔtrɔ ta la, èle dziku dzram ɖo ɖi na ɖokuiwò le Mawu ƒe dɔmedzoedogbe si dzi wòadrɔ̃ ʋɔnu dzɔdzɔe le. 6 Aɖo eteƒe na ame sia ame ɖe eƒe dɔwɔwɔwo nu: 7 ana agbe mavɔ ame siwo le ŋutikɔkɔe kple bubu kpakple magblemagblẽ dim to dzidodo le dɔ nyui wɔwɔ me dzi; 8 gake ame siwo lɔ̃a dzrewɔwɔ, eye womeɖoa to nyateƒe la o, ke boŋ wonɔa nu madzɔmadzɔ wɔwɔ yome la, dziku kple dɔmedzoe ava wo dzi. 9 Xaxa kple vevesese ava ame sia ame si wɔa nu vɔ̃ɖi la dzi, ava Yudatɔ dzi gbã, kple Helatɔ hã dzi; 10 ke ŋutikɔkɔe, bubu kple ŋutifafa anye ame sia ame si wɔa nu nyui la tɔ, Yudatɔ gbã, kple Helatɔ hã. 11 Elabena Mawu mekpɔa ame ŋkume o. 12 Elabena ame siwo katã wɔ nu vɔ̃ se manɔ wo sii la, woaku se manɔ wo sii; ke ame siwo katã wɔ nu vɔ̃ esi wole se te la, se lae woatsɔ adrɔ̃ ʋɔnu wo.
ENGLISH: 3 And do you count on this, man passing judgment on those who commit such things and doing them, that you will escape God’s judgment? 4 or do you despise his wealth of kindness and tolerance and patience, ignorant of the fact that God’s kindness is leading you toward repentance, 5 but with your stiffness and unrepenting heart store up for yourself anger on the day of God’s anger and revelation of just judgment? 6 who will repay each man according to his deeds: 7 those who seek for glory and honor and immortality by way of steadfastness in good work, with eternal life; 8 but those who act by self-interest and disobey the truth, but obey wrong, with anger and wrath; 9 distress and anguish upon every soul of evil-doing man, Jew first and Greek too, 10 but glory and honor and peace for everyone who does what is good, Jew first and Greek too, 11 for there is no favoritism with God.

EWE: 13 Elabena menye ame siwo kea to sea se lae nye ame dzɔdzɔewo le Mawu ŋkume o, ke boŋ ame siwo wɔa se dzi lae woabu ame dzɔdzɔewoe. 14 Elabena ne dukɔ siwo si se mele o la me tɔwo wɔa nu le dzɔdzɔme nu wòsɔna ɖe se nu, togbɔ be se mele wo si o hã la, wozu se na wo ɖokuiwo.
ENGLISH: 12 For as many as sinned without law will perish without law, and as many as sinned under the law will be judged by the law; 13 for it is not the audience of the law that are righteous with God, but it is the doers of the law that are justified.

EWE: 15 Ame siawo tututue ɖee fia be woŋlɔ se la ƒe mɔfiamewo ɖe yewoƒe dziwo me, esi woƒe dzitsinya hã ɖia ɖase, eye woawo ŋutɔwo ƒe tamesusuwo bua fɔ wo alo tsoa afia na wo be wo tɔ dzɔ. 16 Esia adzɔ le ŋkeke si dzi Mawu adrɔ̃ ʋɔnu amegbetɔwo ƒe nuwɔna siwo le ɣaɣla to Kristo Yesu dzi le nya nyui si mele gbeƒã ɖemee la nu.
ENGLISH: 14 For when heathens who do not have the law do by nature what the law commands, these, not having the law, are a law for themselves, 15 displaying as they do the work of the law in writing on their hearts, their own consciences joining in the testimony and their mutual thoughts bringing accusations or, as the case may be, defenses, 16 on the day in which God is going to judge what is covered up in men, in accordance with my gospel, through Christ Jesus.

EWE: 17 Eya ta ne ŋkɔ le ŋuwò be nènye Yudatɔ, eye nèɖoa ŋu ɖe se ŋu hedana be Mawu tɔ yenye, 18 nènya eƒe lɔlɔ̃nu, eye nèlɔ̃ ɖe nu siwo nyo wu sãsãsã la dzi le esi wofia Se la wò ta, 19 nèka ɖe edzi be yenye ŋkuagbãtɔwo ƒe mɔfiala, kekeli na ame siwo le viviti me, 20 ame si ɖɔa ame masenugɔmewo ɖo, ame si fiaa nu ɖevi suewo, ame si si sidzedze kple nyateƒe la ƒe nɔnɔme si le Sea me la le 21 ekema wò, ame si le nu fiam ame bubu la, ɖe mèfiaa nu ɖokuiwò oa? Wò, ame si le gbeƒã ɖem be, "Mègafi fi o " la, wòe fia fia? 22 Wò, ame si le gbɔgblɔm be, "Mègawɔ ahasi o " la, wòe wɔa ahasia? Wò, ame si nyɔa ŋu trɔ̃wo la, wòe daa adzo trɔ̃xɔwoa? 23 Wò, ame si ƒoa adegbe le se ŋu la, ɖe nèdoa vlo Mawu to Se la dzi dada mea? 24 Elabena "wole busunya gblɔm ɖe Mawu ƒe ŋkɔ la ŋu le dukɔwo dome le mia ta "; abe ale si woŋlɔe ɖi ene.
ENGLISH: 17 But if you wear the name of Jew, and rest on the law, and boast of God, 18 and know his will and are a judge of the things he cares about, being schooled out of the law, 19 and feel assured that you are a guide for blind men, a light for those who are in the dark, 20 a preceptor for silly men, a teacher for infants, having in the law the formulation of knowledge and truth, 21 then do you who are teaching somebody else not teach yourself? do you who preach not to steal steal? 22 do you who tell them not to commit adultery commit adultery? do you who abominate idols rob temples? 23 do you who boast of the law dishonor God by violation of the law? 24 for God’s name gets vilified among the nations because of you, as is written.

EWE: 25 Le nyateƒe me la, ne èwɔa se dzi ko hafi viɖe le wò aʋatsotso ŋu; ke ne ènye sedzidala la, ekema wò aʋatsotso la zu aʋamatsomatso.
ENGLISH: 25 For circumcision is worth while if you live up to the law; but if you are a violator of the law your circumcision is turned to uncircumcision.

EWE: 26 Eya ta ne aʋamatsomatsotɔ léa Se la ƒe nudidi dzɔdzɔeawo me ɖe asi la, ɖe womabu eƒe aʋamatsomatso la aʋatsotsoe oa? 27 Eye ne ame si nye aʋamatsomatsotɔ le ŋutilã nu wɔa Se la dzi la, ekema adrɔ̃ ʋɔnu wò, ame si wotso aʋa na eye woŋlɔ sea na wò evɔ nènye sedzidala. 28 Elabena menye ame si nye Yudatɔ le gota lae nye Yudatɔ o, eye menye nu si le gota le ŋutilã ŋu lae nye aʋatsotso o. 29 Ke boŋ ame si nye Yudatɔ le ememe lae nye Yudatɔ akuakua, eye eƒe aʋatsotso la nye dzimeʋatsotso le gbɔgbɔ me, ke menye to se si woŋlɔ ɖi me o. Menye amewo gbɔe ame sia ƒe kafukafu tsona o, ke boŋ Mawu gbɔe.
ENGLISH: 26 So if uncircumcision keeps the prescriptions of the law, will not his uncircumcision be counted as circumcision, 27 and natural uncircumcision, fulfilling the law, pass judgment on you who with letter and circumcision are a violator of the law? 28 For it is not the one who is visibly such that is a Jew, nor is it the visible, in the flesh, that is circumcision, 29 but the Jew who is such in what is out of sight, and heart-circumcision in spirit, not in a literal sense; of which the praise comes not from men but from God.

EWE: Romatɔwo
ENGLISH: Romans

EWE: 3 Ekema viɖe kae le Yudatɔnyenye ŋu, alo viɖe kae le aʋatsotso ŋu? 2 Wosɔ gbɔ le mɔ sia mɔ nu.
ENGLISH: 3 Then what is the Jew’s special privilege, or what is the good of circumcision? 2 Much every way.

EWE: Gbã la, woawoe wotsɔ Mawu ƒe nya kɔkɔeawo de asi na. 3 Ekema nya lae nye ka? Ne xɔse mele wo dometɔ aɖewo si o la, ɖe woƒe dzimaxɔse la ana Mawu hã nagbe nuteƒewɔwɔa? 4 Gbeɖe!
ENGLISH: For, in the first place, that they had God’s revelation entrusted to them 3 for what if some were faithless? is their faithlessness to abrogate God’s faith? 4 away with the thought, but let God prove true, and every man a liar! as it is written, "so that thou mayest be found to have been in the right in thy words, and mayest win when thou comest into court. "

EWE: Ke boŋ Mawu nanye nyateƒetɔ, ne ame sia ame nye aʋatsokala gɔ̃ hã, abe ale si woŋlɔe ɖi ene be: "Ne tɔwò nadzɔ, eye nàɖu dzi ne wodrɔ̃ ʋɔnu wò. " 5 Ke ne míaƒe nu madzɔmadzɔ wɔwɔ na Mawu ƒe dzɔdzɔenyenye dze ƒãa ɖe, ekema nya kae míagblɔ? Ne Mawu ɖe eƒe dziku ɖe go la, ɖe wòfia be etɔ medzɔ oa?
ENGLISH: 5 But if our wrongness brings out God’s righteousness, what, shall we say? is God doing a wrong when he comes down with anger?

EWE: (Mele nu ƒom abe amegbetɔ ene.) 6 Gbeɖe!
ENGLISH: I speak from a human point of view.

EWE: Ne menye nenema o ɖe, aleke Mawu awɔ adrɔ̃ ʋɔnu xexea? 7 Ke ne nye aʋatsokaka wɔe be Mawu ƒe nyateƒe la dze ƒãa hena eƒe ŋutikɔkɔe la, ekema nu ka tae wogale ʋɔnu drɔ̃mem abe nu vɔ̃ wɔla ene ɖo? 8 Eye nu ka tae míagblɔ boŋ be, "Mina míawɔ nu vɔ̃ɖiwo, ne nu nyuiwo nado tso eme, " abe ale si ame aɖewo daa alakpa ɖe mía si be míawoe gblɔa nya ma ene o?
ENGLISH: 6 Away with the thought, for how is God to judge the world? 7 But if by my lie God’s truth came out the more abundant to his glory, why am even I any longer judged as a sinner, 8 and not as the gibe against us goes, and as some do assert that we say, "Let us do the bad things so that we may have the good consequences, " on whom judgment is well-deserved.

EWE: Ʋɔnu si woadrɔ̃ ame siawo la le eteƒe. 9 Ekema nu kae?
ENGLISH: 9 What follows then? are we outranked? no, decidedly.

EWE: Kpao! Elabena míegblɔe xoxo be Yudatɔwo kple Helatɔwo siaa le nu vɔ̃ te; 10 abe ale si woŋlɔe ɖi ene be: "Ame dzɔdzɔe aɖeke meli o, ɖeka hɔ̃ hã meli o; 11 ame aɖeke meli si sea nu gɔme nyuie o; ame aɖeke meli si dia Mawu o. 12 Amegbetɔwo katã tra mɔ, wo katã wozu ame maɖinuwo; ame aɖeke meli si nyoa dɔme o, ɖeka pɛ hã meli o. " 13 "Woƒe vehlo le abe yɔdo si le nuvo ene; wotsɔ woƒe aɖewo blea ame. " "Dzakpata ƒe aɖi le woƒe nu me. " 14 "Eye ɖiŋudodo kple nya veamewo yɔ woƒe nu me fũu. " 15 "Woƒe afɔwo tsɔna ɖe ʋukɔkɔɖi ŋu. " 16 "Gbegblẽ kple xaxa le woƒe mɔwo dzi, 17 eye womenya ŋutifafamɔ la o. " 18 "Mawuvɔvɔ̃ aɖeke mele mo na wo o. " 19 Ke míenyae be nu siwo katã Se la gblɔ la, ame siwo le Se la tee wògblɔ wo na, ale be ɖoɖoe nazi le ame sia ame nu, eye xexe blibo la katã nadze na Mawu ƒe tohehe. 20 Eya ta womabu ame aɖeke be ele dzɔdzɔe le eŋkume to se ƒe dɔwɔwɔwo me o, elabena se dzie wotona nyaa nu si tututu nu vɔ̃ nye.
ENGLISH: For we previously indicted both Jews and Greeks as being all under sin, 10 as it is written "There is not one single right-doer, 11 none that understands, none that seeks God; 12 all have gone wrong, together they are good for nothing; there is none that is acting humanely, not even one "; 13 "their throat is an open grave, they have used their tongues insidiously, " "there is cobras’ venom under their lips, " 14 "whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness, " 15 "their feet are swift to shed blood, 16 havoc and wretchedness are along their roads, 17 and they have not known the road to peace, " 18 "there is no fear of God before their eyes. " 19 And we know that in anything that the law says it is speaking to those who are within the law’s jurisdiction, in order that every mouth may be stopped and all the world become liable to judgment by God, 20 because out of deeds under the law no mortal will be justified before him.

EWE: Elabena medea vovototo aɖeke ame me o.
ENGLISH: For through the law comes recognition of sin.

EWE: 23 Elabena wo katã wɔ nu vɔ̃, eye wometea ŋu ɖoa Mawu ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe la gbɔ o, 24 eye nunana faa wònye be woto tafe si Kristo Yesu xe la dzi na ablɔɖe wo, eye wobu wo be wole dzɔdzɔe le eƒe amenuveve me. 25 Mawu tsɔe na be wòanye avulévɔsa to eƒe ʋu la dzi xɔxɔ se me. Ewɔ esia be wòatsɔ aɖe eya ŋutɔ ƒe dzɔdzɔenyenye afia, elabena Mawu nɔ dzi gbɔm ɖi eye wòtsɔ nu vɔ̃ siwo wowɔ va yi la nɔ kekem. 26 Ewɔ esia be wòatsɔ aɖe eya ŋutɔ ƒe dzɔdzɔenyenye afia le ɣeyiɣi sia me, ale be wòanye dzɔdzɔetɔ, ne ebu ame si xɔ Yesu dzi se la ame dzɔdzɔe.
ENGLISH: 21 But now apart from the law a righteousness of God’s has been disclosed, attested by the law and the prophets, 22 but a righteousness of God’s through faith in Jesus Christ to reach all who believe; for there is no distinction, 23 for all have sinned and come short of God’s glory, 24 getting their justification gratuitously by his grace through the redemption by Christ Jesus, 25 whom God put forward to be propitiatory through faith by his blood for a display of his righteousness, because of the way in which under God’s forbearance previous sins had been let pass; 26 with a view to the displaying of his righteousness at the present time, so that he should be righteous and be justifying the one who lives by faith in Jesus.

EWE: 27 Ekema susu ka tae míaƒo adegbe ɖo? Susu aɖeke meli o.
ENGLISH: 27 So what becomes of boasting? it is shut off.

EWE: Kpao, ke xɔse ƒe se la boŋ ye. 28 Elabena míelɔ̃ ɖe edzi be wobua ame be ele dzɔdzɔe to xɔse me, menye to se ƒe dɔwɔwɔwo me o.
ENGLISH: By what law? of deeds? no, but by the law of faith, 28 for we count that a man is justified by faith apart from deeds under the law.

EWE: 29 Alo Yudatɔwo ɖeɖe ko ƒe Mawue wònyea? Ðe menye dukɔwo me tɔwo hã ƒe Mawu oa?
ENGLISH: 29 Or is God the God of the Jews only? is he not of the nations too?

EWE: Ɛ̃, dukɔwo me tɔwo hã tɔe wònye. 30 Esi wònye be Mawu ɖeka koe li ta la, abu aʋatsotsotɔwo be wole dzɔdzɔe le woƒe xɔse ta, eye wòabu aʋamatsomatsotɔwo hã be wole dzɔdzɔe le woƒe xɔse ta.
ENGLISH: Yes, of the nations too, 30 if it be true that God is one, who will justify circumcised men on the basis of faith and uncircumcised by means of faith.

EWE: 31 Ekema ɖe míetsɔa míaƒe xɔse ɖea se ɖa?
ENGLISH: 31 Are we superseding the law by faith, then? away with the thought, we are making good the law.

EWE: Gbeɖe!
ENGLISH: Romans

EWE: 4 Esi wòle alea ɖe, ekema viɖe kae míagblɔ be Abraham, ame si nye mía tɔgbui le ŋutilã nu la, kpɔ? 2 Le kpɔɖeŋu me, ne ɖe wobu Abraham be ele dzɔdzɔe le dɔwɔwɔwo ta la, anye ne susu aɖe anɔ anyi si ta wòaƒo adegbe ɖo hafi; gake menye le Mawu gbɔ o.
ENGLISH: 4 Then what shall we say that Abraham, our forefather in the way of flesh, had found? 2 For if Abraham was justified as the outcome of deeds, he does have something to boast of.

EWE: 3 Elabena nya kae ŋɔŋlɔ la gblɔ?
ENGLISH: But not to God, 3 for what does the text say?

EWE: 5 Gake ame si menɔa te ɖe dɔwɔwɔwo dzi o, ke boŋ wòxɔa Ame si bua ame mavɔ̃mawu ame dzɔdzɔe dzi sena la, wobua eƒe xɔse la dzɔdzɔenyenye nɛ. 6 Abe ale si David hã ƒo nu le dzidzɔ si ame kpɔna ne Mawu bu dzɔdzɔenyenye nɛ, menye to dɔwɔwɔwo me o, la ŋuti ene be: 7 "Dzidzɔtɔwoe nye ame siwo ƒe dzidadawo wotsɔ ke, ame siwo ƒe nu vɔ̃wo dzi wotsyɔ nui; 8 dzidzɔtɔe nye ame si ƒe nu vɔ̃ Yehowa mabu nɛ kura o. " 9 Ekema aʋatsotsotɔwo ɖeɖe koe kpɔa dzidzɔ sia loo alo aʋamatsomatsotɔwo hã kpɔnɛa? Elabena míele gbɔgblɔm be: "Wobu Abraham ƒe xɔse dzɔdzɔenyenye nɛ. " 10 Ekema nɔnɔme kawo mee wobui dzɔdzɔenyenye nɛ le? Esime wotso aʋa nɛ loo, alo esime wometso aʋa nɛ o? Menye esime wotso aʋa nɛ o, ke boŋ esime wometso aʋa nɛ o.
ENGLISH: "And Abraham believed God, and it was counted righteousness for him. " 4 But one who works does not have the pay counted to him in the way of grace but of debt; 5 but one who does not work but puts faith in him who justifies an impious man has his faith counted for righteousness, 6 in the same way as David tells of the happy state of the man to whom God counts righteousness apart from works: 7 "Happy they whose wickednesses are forgiven and whose sins are covered up; 8 happy a man for whom the Lord does not count sin. " 9 Is this happy state, then, pronounced upon circumcision, or upon uncircumcision too? for we are saying "Faith was counted righteousness for Abraham. " 10 How was it counted then, when he was in circumcision or in uncircumcision?

EWE: 11 Eye wòxɔ dzesi, si nye aʋatsotso, abe dzɔdzɔenyenye ƒe nutrenu ene le xɔse si nɔ esi hafi wòva tso aʋa la ta, ale be wòanye ame siwo katã si xɔse le togbɔ be wonye aʋamatsomatsotɔwo hã la fofo, be woabui dzɔdzɔenyenye na wo; 12 eye be wòanye vi siwo katã wotso aʋa na la fofo, menye na ame siwo de aʋatsotso dzi la ɖeɖe ko o, ke na ame siwo hã zɔna le ɖoɖo nu le xɔse ƒe mɔ ma, si nɔ mía fofo Abraham si esi wometso aʋa nɛ o la, ke nu.
ENGLISH: Not in circumcision but in uncircumcision; 11 and he got the token of circumcision as a seal of his righteousness of faith in uncircumcision, so that he should be father of all who believe while uncircumcised so that righteousness should be counted to them, 12 and father of circumcision for those who are not of circumcision only but who also walk in the tracks of the faith our father Abraham had during uncircumcision.

EWE: 13 Elabena menye to se mee Abraham alo eƒe dzidzimevi la xɔ ŋugbedodo le be wòanye xexe aɖe ƒe domenyila o, ke boŋ dzɔdzɔenyenye si to xɔse me la mee.
ENGLISH: 13 For it is not through the law that there is the promise to Abraham or to his descendants, that he is to be heir of the world, but through righteousness of faith.

EWE: 14 Elabena ne ame siwo lé se me ɖe asi lae nye domenyilawo la, ekema viɖe aɖeke megale xɔse ŋu o, eye woɖe ŋugbedodo la ɖa. 15 Le nyateƒe me la, Se la hea dziku vanɛ, gake afi si se mele o la, sedzidada hã menɔa anyi o.
ENGLISH: 14 For if those who are on the basis of law are heirs, faith is nullified and the promise is superseded; 15 for the law evolves anger, and where there is not law there is not violation either.

EWE: Mawu, Ame si dzi wòxɔ se la ŋkumee woɖo kpe esia dzi le, ame si gbɔa agbe ame kukuwo, eye wòyɔa nu siwo meli o la abe ɖe woli ene. 18 Togbɔ be naneke menɔ anyi si ta mɔkpɔkpɔ nanɔ Abraham si ɖo o hã la, le mɔkpɔkpɔ ta la, exɔe se be yeazu dukɔ geɖewo fofo le nya si wogblɔ ɖi la nu be: "Aleae wò dzidzimeviwo anɔ. " 19 Eye togbɔ be megbɔdzɔ le xɔse me o hã la, ebu eya ŋutɔ ƒe ŋutilã ya abe ɖe wòku xoxo ɣemaɣi ene (elabena exɔ abe ƒe alafa ɖeka ene), eye wòbu Sara ƒe vidzidɔ hã be eku. 20 Ke le Mawu ƒe ŋugbedodo ta la, meke ɖi abe xɔsemanɔsitɔ ene o; ke boŋ esẽ ŋu le xɔse me, eye wòtsɔ ŋutikɔkɔe na Mawu 21 eye wòka ɖe edzi bliboe be nu si ŋugbe Mawu do la, ate ŋu awɔe hã. 22 Esia tae "wobui dzɔdzɔenyenye nɛ " ɖo.
ENGLISH: 16 Hence, on the basis of faith in order to be in the way of grace, so that the promise may be securely settled to all the descendants, not only the line which is based on the law but also that which is based on Abraham’s faith, his who is father of all of us 17 (as it is written "I have made you father of many nations ") before the God whom he believed, him who brings the dead to life and calls what does not exist as though it did; 18 his who in a hopeless case had the hopefulness to believe, so as to become father of many nations in accordance with what it says, "Such shall your descendants be, " 19 and did not weaken in faith as he observed his own body gone dead, he being a hundred years or so old, and the deadening of Sarah’s womb; 20 but he did not unbelievingly doubt at God’s promise, but had his faith invigorated, giving glory to God 21 and feeling convinced that what he has promised he is able to go on and do; 22 which is why it was counted for righteousness to him.

EWE: 23 Gake nya si woŋlɔ ɖi be ‘wobui nɛ’ la, menye eya ɖeɖe ko tae woŋlɔe ɖi ɖo o, 24 ke mí ame siwo woava bui na la hã tae, elabena míexɔ Ame si fɔ Yesu, mía Aƒetɔ la, tso ame kukuwo dome la dzi se. 25 Wotsɔe na ɖe míaƒe vodadawo ta, eye wofɔe ɖe tsitre be woabu mí ame dzɔdzɔewoe.
ENGLISH: 23 And it was not written on his account only that it was counted to him, 24 but on ours too, to whom it is going to be counted, us who believe on the one that raised from the dead our Lord Jesus, 25 who was handed over to death on account of our offenses and was raised on account of our justification.

EWE: Romatɔwo
ENGLISH: Romans

EWE: 5 Esi wobu mí ame dzɔdzɔewoe azɔ to xɔse me ta la, mina míanɔ ŋutifafa me kple Mawu to mía Aƒetɔ Yesu Kristo dzi. 2 To eya dzi la, mɔ ʋu na mí be amenuveve sia su mía si fifia to xɔse me; eye mina míatso aseye le Mawu ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe ƒe mɔkpɔkpɔ la ta.
ENGLISH: 5 So, being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ, 2 by whose agency we have also had the introduction into this grace in which we stand, and boast of the hope of God’s glory.

EWE: 3 Menye ema ɖeɖe ko o, ke mina míatso aseye le xaxawo me hã, elabena míenyae be xaxa hea dzidodo vanɛ; 4 dzidodo hã hea ŋudzedzekpɔkpɔ ɖe ame ŋu vanɛ; ŋudzedzekpɔkpɔ ɖe ame ŋu hã hea mɔkpɔkpɔ vanɛ, 5 eye mɔkpɔkpɔ menana ame ɖua ŋukpe o; elabena wokɔ Mawu ƒe lɔlɔ̃ la ɖe míaƒe dziwo me to gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔe si wona mí la dzi.
ENGLISH: 3 And not only this, but we also boast of our distresses, knowing that distress develops endurance; 4 and endurance, positive experience; and positive experience, hope; 5 and hope does not put us to shame, because God’s love has been poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit that was given to us.

EWE: 6 Le nyateƒe me la, esime míeganye gbɔdzɔgbɔdzɔtɔwo la, Kristo ku ɖe ame mavɔ̃mawuwo ta le ɣeyiɣi ɖoɖi la dzi.
ENGLISH: 6 For while we still were weak Christ died for impious men in time of need.

EWE: 7 Elabena bebli hafi ame aɖe aku ɖe ame dzɔdzɔe ta; ame nyui ya la ɖewohĩ ame aɖe ado dzi aku ɖe eta. 8 Ke Mawu ɖe eya ŋutɔ ƒe lɔlɔ̃ na mí fia le esia me be, esime míeganye nu vɔ̃ wɔlawo la, Kristo ku ɖe mía ta. 9 Eya ta esi wonɔ te ɖe eƒe ʋu dzi bu mí ame dzɔdzɔewoe azɔ ta la, woaɖe mí tso dziku la me geɖe wu to edzi.
ENGLISH: 7 For one will scarcely die for a saint for a good man maybe someone does even venture to die 8 but God vouches for his own love to us in that while we were still sinful Christ died for us; much more, 9 then, now that we have been justified by his blood we shall be saved from God’s anger through him.

EWE: 10 Elabena ne woto Via ƒe ku dzi dzra mía kple Mawu dome ɖo esime míenye eƒe futɔwo la, ekema woaɖe mí geɖe wu to eƒe agbe la me esi wova dzra mía kplii dome ɖo azɔ. 11 Eye menye ema ɖeɖe ko o, ke míele aseye tsom hã le Mawu me to mía Aƒetɔ Yesu Kristo dzi, ame si dzi woto dzra mía dome ɖo azɔ.
ENGLISH: 10 For if when enemies we were reconciled to God by his Son’s death, much more when reconciled shall we be saved in his life; 11 and not only saved but also boasting of Cod through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we did now receive the reconciliation.

EWE: 12 Esia tae ale si ko to ame ɖeka dzi nu vɔ̃ va xexea me, eye to nu vɔ̃ me ku la va, ale ku la kaka ɖe amewo katã dome, esi wo katã wɔ nu vɔ̃ ŋuti . . . 13 Elabena hafi Se la nava la, nu vɔ̃ nɔ xexea me, gake wometsoa ame aɖeke nu be ewɔ nu vɔ̃ ne se meli o. 14 Ke ku ɖu fia tso Adam dzi va ɖo Mose dzi, ɖe ame siwo mewɔ nu vɔ̃ si sɔ kple Adam ƒe dzidada o la gɔ̃ hã dzi, eya, ame si ɖi ame si ava va la.
ENGLISH: 12 For this reason, just as it was through one man that sin came into the world, and, through sin, death, and thus death went on to all men inasmuch as all sinned 13 for until the law there was sin in the world, but sin is not charged in the account when there is no law, 14 yet death reigned from Adam to Moses even over those who had not sinned in a way parallel to the violation by Adam, who is a type of the one that was to be.

EWE: 15 Gake nunana la mele abe vodada la ene o.
ENGLISH: 15 But the act of grace is not just as the offense was.

EWE: Elabena ne ame ɖeka ƒe vodadae na ame geɖewo ku la, ekema ɖe Mawu ƒe amenuveve kple eƒe nunana faa la kpakple amenuveve si to ame ɖeka si nye Yesu Kristo dzi la, masɔ gbɔ fũu na ame geɖewo wu oa! 16 Eye nu si nunana faa la hena vanɛ la mele abe nu si ame ɖeka ma ƒe nu vɔ̃ he vɛ la ene o. Elabena vodada ɖeka ye na wodrɔ̃ ʋɔnu hebu fɔ amewo katã, ke nunana si wona ɖe vodada geɖewo ta lae nye be wobu ame geɖewo ame dzɔdzɔewoe.
ENGLISH: For if by the one man’s offense the many died, much more did God’s grace and the gift in grace, the grace of the one man Jesus Christ, come amply to the many. 16 And what is given is not as in the case of the one’s sinning; for the judgment followed from one to condemnation, but the act of grace from many offenses to justification.

EWE: 17 Elabena ne ame ɖeka ƒe vodada wɔe be ku ɖu fia to ame ɖeka ma dzi la, ekema ɖe ame siwo xɔ amenuveve la kple dzɔdzɔenyenye ƒe nunana faa le agbɔsɔsɔ me la maɖu fia geɖe wu le agbe me to ame ɖeka, si nye Yesu Kristo dzi oa!
ENGLISH: 17 For if by the one’s offense death reigned through the one, much more shall those who receive the amplitude of grace and of the gift of righteousness reign in life through the one, Jesus Christ.

EWE: 18 Ale si vodada ɖeka na wobu fɔ amewo katã la, nenema kee nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔ ɖeka na wobu amewo katã be wole dzɔdzɔe hena agbe. 19 Elabena ale si ko ame ɖeka ƒe tomaɖomaɖo na ame geɖewo zu nu vɔ̃ wɔlawoe la, nenema kee to ame ɖeka ƒe toɖoɖo me hã woana ame geɖewo nazu ame dzɔdzɔewo. 20 Azɔ Se la va do, ale be vodada nasɔ gbɔ ɖe edzi.
ENGLISH: 18 So then as through one offense the consequence followed to all men to condemnation, so too through one deed of right it follows to all men to justification into life; 19 for as the many were rendered sinful through the one man’s failure to obey, so too the many will be rendered righteous through the one’s obedience.

EWE: Ke afi si nu vɔ̃ sɔ gbɔ le la, amenuveve ya sɔa gbɔ geɖe wu. 21 Kple susu ka? Ale be ale si ko nu vɔ̃ kple ku ɖu fiae la, amenuveve hã naɖu fia nenema ke to dzɔdzɔenyenye me hena agbe mavɔ to mía Aƒetɔ Yesu Kristo dzi.
ENGLISH: 20 And the law stepped in to play its part so that there should be plenty of the offense; but where there was plenty of sin there was superabundance of grace, 21 in order that as sin did reign in death, so too grace might reign through righteousness to eternal life through our Lord Jesus Christ.

EWE: Romatɔwo
ENGLISH: Romans

EWE: 6 Ekema nya kae míagblɔ? Ðe míakpɔtɔ anɔ nu vɔ̃ wɔm, be amenuveve la nasɔ gbɔ ɖe edzia? 2 Gbeɖe!
ENGLISH: 6 What shall we therefore say? "let us keep on with sin so that there may be plenty of grace "? 2 away with the thought!

EWE: Esi wònye míeku le nu vɔ̃ gome ɖe, aleke wɔ míagakpɔtɔ anɔ agbe le eme? 3 Alo ɖe mienyae be mí ame siwo katã wonyrɔ ɖe Kristo Yesu me la, wonyrɔ mí ɖe eƒe ku me oa? 4 Eya ŋuti esi wonyrɔ mí ɖe eƒe ku me ta la, woɖi mí kpakplii, ale be ale si ko wofɔ Kristo ɖe tsitre tso ame kukuwo dome to Fofo la ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe me la, míawo hã míazɔ nenema ke ɖe agbenɔnɔmɔ yeye nu.
ENGLISH: We who died to sin, how are we to live in it still? 3 Or are you unaware that we, whoever were baptized into Christ Jesus, were baptized into his death? 4 so we were buried together with him through baptism into death, in order that as Christ was raised from the dead through the Father’s glory, so we too should walk on the new footing of life.

EWE: 5 Ne míewɔ ɖeka kplii le ku si tɔgbi wòku me la, ekema míawɔ ɖeka kplii godoo le tsitretsitsi si tɔgbi wòkpɔ la hã me. 6 Elabena míenyae be wohe míaƒe amenyenye xoxo la ɖe ati ŋuti kplii, ale be ŋusẽ aɖeke naganɔ míaƒe nu vɔ̃ ŋutilã la ŋu o, be míagayi edzi anye kluviwo na nu vɔ̃ o. 7 Elabena ame si ku la, wotso afia nɛ ɖee tso eƒe nu vɔ̃ me.
ENGLISH: 5 For if we have come to be twinned with the likeness of his death, yet so shall we of his resurrection; 6 knowing this, that the old man of us was crucified with him in order that sin’s body might be discontinued so that we should no longer belong to sin; 7 for he who has died is acquitted of sin.

EWE: 8 Azɔ hã ne míeku kple Kristo la, míexɔe se be míanɔ agbe hã kpakplii. 9 Elabena míenyae be esi wofɔ Kristo tso ame kukuwo dome azɔ la, magaku akpɔ o; ku magaɖu aƒetɔ ɖe edzi azɔ o. 10 Elabena ku si wòku la, eku na nu vɔ̃ ɖeɖe ɖa zi ɖeka ɖe ɣeyiɣiawo katã nu, ke agbe si wòle la, ele agbe na Mawu.
ENGLISH: 8 And if we died with Christ we believe that we shall also live with him, 9 knowing that Christ risen from the dead does not die anymore; death no longer has jurisdiction over him; 10 because his dying he did to sin, once for all, but his living he is doing to God.

EWE: 11 Nenema kee miawo hã, mibu mia ɖokuiwo be yewoku na nu vɔ̃, ke azɔ yewole agbe na Mawu to Kristo Yesu dzi.
ENGLISH: 11 So you too: count it that you are dead to sin but alive to God in Christ Jesus.

EWE: 13 Eye migatsɔ miaƒe ŋutilãwo nɔ nu vɔ̃ nam abe nu madzɔmadzɔ wɔwɔ ƒe aʋawɔnuwo ene hã o, ke boŋ mitsɔ mia ɖokuiwo na Mawu abe ame siwo wogbɔ agbe tso ame kukuwo dome ene, eye mitsɔ miaƒe ŋutilãwo hã na Mawu abe nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔ ƒe aʋawɔnuwo ene.
ENGLISH: 12 So let sin not reign in your mortal body to have you obey its desires, 13 and do not present your organs to be sin’s instruments for wrong-doing, but present yourselves to God like men alive from the dead and your organs to be God’s instruments for right-doing.

EWE: 14 Mele be nu vɔ̃ naɖu aƒetɔ ɖe mia dzi o, elabena miele se te o, ke amenuveve tee miele.
ENGLISH: 14 For sin is not to have jurisdiction over you; for you are not under the law but under grace.

EWE: Esi míele se te o, ke boŋ amenuveve tee míele tae míanɔ nu vɔ̃ wɔma? Gbeɖe! 16 Ðe mienyae be ne mietsɔa mia ɖokuiwo wɔa kluvii na ame aɖe be yewoaɖo toe la, ekema miezu ame si mieɖoa toe la ƒe kluviwo, eɖanye nu vɔ̃ ƒe kluviwo hena ku, alo toɖoɖo ƒe kluviwo hena dzɔdzɔenyenye oa? 17 Ke woada akpe na Mawu be mienye nu vɔ̃ ƒe kluviwo tsã, ke mieva zu ame siwo ɖoa to nufiafia si tɔgbi wotsɔ de asi na mi la tso dzi me.
ENGLISH: 15 What then? are we to sin because we are not under the law but under grace? away with the thought! 16 Do you not know that to whom you present yourselves as his for obedience, his you are, his whom you obey? either sin’s, for death, or obedience’s, for righteousness.

EWE: 18 Ɛ̃, esi wona ablɔɖe mi tso nu vɔ̃ me ta la, mieva zu dzɔdzɔenyenye ƒe kluviwo. 19 Mele nu ƒom abe amegbetɔ ene le miaƒe ŋutilã ƒe gbɔdzɔgbɔdzɔ ta; elabena ale si ko mietsɔ miaƒe ŋutinuwo wɔ kluviwoe na makɔmakɔnyenye kple sedzimawɔmawɔ si na mienye sedzimawɔlawo tsã la, nenema ke mitsɔ miaƒe ŋutinuwo wɔ kluviwoe na dzɔdzɔenyenye azɔ be mianye ame kɔkɔewo.
ENGLISH: 17 But thanks be to God that you were slaves to sin but obeyed with goodwill the pattern of teaching under which you were put, 18 and, set free from sin, were enslaved to righteousness 19 I use human language in view of the weakness of your flesh; for, as you did present your organs in servitude to uncleanness and wickedness for wickedness, so now present your organs in servitude to righteousness for sanctification.

EWE: 20 Elabena esi mienye nu vɔ̃ ƒe kluviwo tsã la, dzɔdzɔenyenye ƒe nya aɖeke metsɔ mia gbɔ o. 21 Ekema kutsetse kae do tso eme na mi ɣemaɣi? Nu siwo va le ŋu kpem na mi azɔ lae. Elabena nu mawo ƒe nuwuwue nye ku.
ENGLISH: 20 For when you were in servitude to sin you were free as regards righteousness; 21 so what fruit did you have then? things you are now ashamed of.

EWE: 22 Ke azɔ esi wona ablɔɖe mi tso nu vɔ̃ me, eye mieva zu Mawu ƒe kluviwo ta la, kutsetse si kpɔm miele lae nye kɔkɔenyenye, eye le nuwuwu la, miakpɔ agbe mavɔ.
ENGLISH: For the end of those things is death; 22 but now, set free from sin but enslaved to God, you have your fruit for sanctification, and the end eternal life.

EWE: 23 Elabena nu vɔ̃ ƒe fetue nye ku, ke Mawu ƒe nunanae nye agbe mavɔ to Kristo Yesu mía Aƒetɔ la dzi.
ENGLISH: 23 For sin’s pay is death, but God’s gracious gift is eternal life in our Lord Christ Jesus.

EWE: Romatɔwo
ENGLISH: Romans

EWE: 7 Nɔviwo, alo ɖe mienyae be Se la ɖua aƒetɔ ɖe ame dzi zi ale si wòle agbe oa? (elabena mi ame siwo nya se lae mele nu ƒom na.) 2 Le kpɔɖeŋu me, se bla nyɔnu srɔ̃tɔ ɖe srɔ̃a ŋu ŋkeke ale si ŋutsua le agbe; ke ne ŋutsua ku la, ekema wotu nyɔnua tso srɔ̃a ƒe se la me.
ENGLISH: 7 Or are you unaware, brothers (for I am speaking to men who know the law), that the law has jurisdiction over man so long as he is alive? 2 For the wedded woman is bound to the living husband by the law; but if the husband dies she is disengaged from the husband’s law.

EWE: 3 Eya ta ne srɔ̃a le agbe hafi wòva zu ŋutsu bubu tɔ la, woayɔe be ahasiwɔla. Ke ne srɔ̃a ku la, ekema evo tso eƒe se la me, ale be ne eva zu ŋutsu bubu tɔ la, meganye ahasiwɔla o.
ENGLISH: 3 So while the husband is alive she will be called an adulteress if another man gets her; but if the husband dies she is free from the law so as not to be an adulteress when another man does get her.

EWE: 4 Eya ta nɔvinyewo, wona miawo hã miezu ame kukuwo le Se la gome to Kristo la ƒe ŋutilã me, ale be miazu ame bubu, si nye ame si wofɔ tso ame kukuwo dome la tɔ, ale be míatse ku na Mawu.
ENGLISH: 4 Hence, my brothers, you too were brought into death to the law through the Christ’s body so that another might get you, he who rose from the dead, in order that we may bear fruit for God.

EWE: 5 Elabena esi míenɔ agbe nɔm le ŋutilã nu la, nu vɔ̃ ƒe dzodzro sesẽ siwo Se la nyɔna ɖe míaƒe ŋutilãwo me la nɔ dɔ dzi, ale be míatse ku na ku. 6 Ke azɔ wotu mí tso Se la me, elabena míeku na nu si de ga mí la, be míazu kluviwo le gɔmesese yeye nu to gbɔgbɔ la me, eye menye le gɔmesese xoxo la nu to se si woŋlɔ ɖi la me o.
ENGLISH: 5 For when we were in the flesh the susceptibilities to sin that come by the law were at work in our organism so that we should bear fruit for death, 6 but now we have been disengaged, having died, from the law in which we were held under, so that we serve in the new relation of spirit and not in the old relation of letter.

EWE: 7 Ekema nya kae míagblɔ? Ðe Se la nye nu vɔ̃a? Gbeɖe! Le nyateƒe me la, ne menye Se lae o la, anye ne nyemenya nu si nu vɔ̃ nye o.
ENGLISH: 7 What shall we therefore say? "the law is sin "? away with the thought! but I should not have known sin except through the law.

EWE: Le kpɔɖeŋu me, nyemanya nu si ŋubiabiã nye o, ne menye ɖe Se la gblɔ be: "Mègabiã ŋu o. " 8 Ke esi nu vɔ̃ la kpɔ mɔnu to sedede la me ta la, ena ŋubiabiã ɖe sia ɖe ƒomevi va nyɔ ɖe menye, elabena ne se meli o la, ekema nu vɔ̃ hã ku.
ENGLISH: For I should not know about coveting if the law did not say "You shall not covet. " 8 But sin, getting a start by the commandment, produced in me a coveting of everything.

EWE: 9 Nyateƒee, tsã la, menɔ agbe esi se menɔ anyi o.
ENGLISH: For without the law sin is dead; 9 and I was alive without the law once.

EWE: Ke esi sedede la va ɖo la, nu vɔ̃ gagbɔ agbe, ke nye ya meku. 10 Eye se si wode be wòakplɔ ame ayi agbe me la, nye ya mekpɔe be ekplɔa ame yia ku me. 11 Elabena esi nu vɔ̃ la kpɔ mɔnu to sedede la me ta la, eble nunye heto edzi wum.
ENGLISH: But when the commandment came sin came to life, and I died; 10 and for me the commandment, the very thing that led to life, was found to lead to death, 11 since sin, getting a start by the commandment, tricked me, and killed me through it.

EWE: 12 Evɔ Se la le kɔkɔe, eye sededeawo hã le kɔkɔe, le dzɔdzɔe eye wònyo hafi.
ENGLISH: 12 Consequently: the law is holy, and the commandment holy and just and good.

EWE: 13 Ekema ɖe nu nyui la zu ku nama? Gbeɖe! Gake nu vɔ̃ ye zui, ne wòadze ƒãa be nu vɔ̃ ye wɔ nu nyui ŋu dɔ tsɔ he ku vɛ nam, ale be nu vɔ̃ la nagadze gaglãa wu to sedede la me.
ENGLISH: 13 Then did the good become death for me? away with the thought, but sin did, in order that it might appear as sin, producing death for me through the good, in order that sin might come out supremely sinful through the commandment.

EWE: 14 Elabena míenyae be gbɔgbɔmenue Se la nye; ke ŋutilãmeme si wodzra na nu vɔ̃e nye ya menye.
ENGLISH: 14 For we know that the law is spiritual; but I am of flesh, sold under sin.

EWE: 15 Elabena nye ŋutɔ nyemesea nye nuwɔna gɔme o.
ENGLISH: 15 For I do not know the product I am working out.

EWE: Elabena nu si medina la, menye eyae mewɔna o, ke nu si melé fui la boŋue mewɔna. 16 Ke ne nu si nyemedina o lae mewɔna la, ekema melɔ̃ ɖe edzi be Se la nyo.
ENGLISH: For it is not just what I have a will for that I am busy at, it is just what I hate that I am doing; 16 but if I am doing just what I have no will for, I agree that the law is fine.

EWE: 17 Ke meganye nyee le ewɔm o, ke boŋ nu vɔ̃ si le menye lae.
ENGLISH: 17 And now it is no longer I that work out what ensues, but my inmate sin.

EWE: 18 Elabena menyae be le menye, si nye le nye ŋutilã me la, nu nyui aɖeke meli o; elabena nu nyui wɔwɔ ƒe didia le menye, ke ŋutetea ya meli o. 19 Elabena nu nyui si medina la, nyemewɔnɛ o, ke nu vɔ̃ɖi si nyemedina o la, eya boŋ mewɔna.
ENGLISH: 18 For I know that there does not reside in me, that is, in my flesh, anything good; for to will is within my reach, but to work out what would be a fine thing is not, 19 for I do not do the good thing which I will, but it is just the bad thing which I do not will that I am busy at.

EWE: 20 Ke ne nu si nyemedina o lae mewɔna la, ekema meganye nyee le ewɔm o, ke boŋ nu vɔ̃ si le menye lae.
ENGLISH: 20 But if it is just what I do not will that I do, it is no longer I that work out what ensues, but sin residing in me.

EWE: 21 Ke nye la, mekpɔ se sia le gonyeme be: Ne medi be mawɔ nu si sɔ la, nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ ƒe didi nɔa menye.
ENGLISH: 21 I find the law, then, for me who have the will to do the fine thing, that the bad is what is laid out for me.

EWE: 22 Mekpɔa dzidzɔ le Mawu ƒe se la ŋu ŋutɔ le ame si menye le ememe la gome, 23 ke mekpɔ se bubu aɖe le menye, si le aʋa wɔm kple se si le nye susu me, eye wòléam aboyoe yina na nu vɔ̃ ƒe se si le nye ŋutilã me.
ENGLISH: 22 For I am in sympathy with the law of God as to my inward man, 23 but I see another law in my organism waging war with the law of my mind and taking me prisoner to the law of sin that is in my organism.

EWE: 24 Oo, nye nu wɔ nublanui lo! Ame kae aɖem tso kuŋutilã sia si me? 25 Meda akpe na Mawu to Yesu Kristo, mía Aƒetɔ la dzi!
ENGLISH: 24 Wretched man I! who will deliver me out of the body that carries this death? 25 thanks be to God through our Lord Jesus Christ!

EWE: Eya ta le nye susu me la, menye kluvi na Mawu ƒe se la, ke le nye ŋutilã me la, menye kluvi na nu vɔ̃ ƒe se la.
ENGLISH: So then I myself belong in mind to the service of God’s law, but in flesh to that of sin’s law.

EWE: Romatɔwo
ENGLISH: Romans

EWE: 8 Eya ta fɔbubu aɖeke meli na ame siwo wɔ ɖeka kple Kristo Yesu o. 2 Elabena gbɔgbɔ ma, si naa agbe ame si wɔ ɖeka kple Kristo Yesu la, ƒe se la na ablɔɖe wò tso nu vɔ̃ kple ku ƒe se la me.
ENGLISH: 8 Then there is no condemnation now for those who are in Christ Jesus, 2 for the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has given freedom from the law of sin and of death.

EWE: 3 Nu si Se la mete ŋu wɔ o le esi ŋutilã la na wògbɔdzɔ ta la, Mawu wɔe esi wòdɔ eya ŋutɔ Via ɖo ɖa le nu vɔ̃ ŋutilã ƒe nɔnɔme me, be wòaɖe nu vɔ̃ ɖa, eye Mawu to esia me bu fɔ nu vɔ̃ le ŋutilã me, 4 ale be Se la ƒe nudidi dzɔdzɔe la nava eme le mí ame siwo le zɔzɔm le gbɔgbɔ la nu ke menye le ŋutilã nu o la gome.
ENGLISH: 3 For, what was impossible to the law in that it was weak by the flesh, God, sending his own son in the likeness of sinning flesh and on account of sin, condemned sin in the flesh 4 in order that the prescription of the law might be fully realized in us who walk along the line not of flesh but of spirit.

EWE: 5 Elabena ame siwo nɔa agbe ɖe ŋutilã nu la tsɔa woƒe susuwo ɖoa ŋutilã la ƒe nuwo ŋu, ke ame siwo nɔa agbe ɖe gbɔgbɔ la nu la tsɔa woƒe susuwo ɖoa gbɔgbɔ la ƒe nuwo ŋu.
ENGLISH: 5 For those who are along the line of flesh are of the flesh’s mind, but those who are along the line of spirit are of the Spirit’s.

EWE: 6 Susu ɖoɖo ŋutilã la ŋu hea ku vanɛ, ke susu ɖoɖo gbɔgbɔ la ŋu hea agbe kple ŋutifafa vanɛ; 7 elabena susu ɖoɖo ŋutilã la ŋu fia Mawu ƒe futɔnyenye, elabena mebɔbɔ ɖe Mawu ƒe se la te o, eye le nyateƒe me la, mate ŋui hã o.
ENGLISH: 6 For the flesh’s mind is death, but the Spirit’s mind is life and peace.

EWE: 8 Eya ta ame siwo nɔa agbe ɖe ŋutilã nu la mate ŋu adze Mawu ŋu o.
ENGLISH: 7 For the flesh’s mind is enmity to God, for it does not submit itself to God’s law, it even cannot; 8 and those who are in flesh cannot please God.

EWE: 9 Ke miawo la, ne Mawu ƒe gbɔgbɔ la le mia me ŋutɔŋutɔ la, ekema menye ŋutilã la nue miele agbe ɖo o, ke ɖe gbɔgbɔ la nu boŋ.
ENGLISH: 9 But you are not in flesh but in spirit, if God’s Spirit does reside in you; but if anybody does not have Christ’s Spirit, that man is not his.

EWE: 10 Ke ne Kristo le ɖekawɔwɔ me kpli mi la, ekema ŋutilã la ku le nu vɔ̃ ta, ke gbɔgbɔ la nye agbe le dzɔdzɔenyenye ta.
ENGLISH: 10 But if Christ is in you, the body is dead on account of sin, but the spirit is life on account of righteousness.

EWE: 11 Ne ame si fɔ Yesu tso ame kukuwo dome la ƒe gbɔgbɔ le mia me la, ekema ame si fɔ Kristo Yesu tso ame kukuwo dome la, ana miaƒe ŋutilã si kuna la hã nagbɔ agbe to eƒe gbɔgbɔ si le mia me la dzi.
ENGLISH: 11 And if the Spirit of him who raised Jesus from the dead resides in you, he who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will bring to life your mortal bodies too through his Spirit your inmate.

EWE: 12 Eya ta nɔviwo, menye ŋutilã la ŋue míenyi fe le be míanɔ agbe ɖe ŋutilã nu o; 13 elabena ne mienɔa agbe ɖe ŋutilã nu la, ekema miaku godoo; ke ne miewua ŋutilã ƒe dɔwɔwɔwo to gbɔgbɔ la ƒe kpekpeɖeŋu me la, mianɔ agbe.
ENGLISH: 12 So then, brothers, we are debtors not to the flesh to live along the line of flesh, 13 for if you live along the line of flesh you are going to die; but if by spirit you bring the body’s practices to their death you will live.

EWE: 14 Elabena ame siwo katã Mawu ƒe gbɔgbɔ fiaa mɔe lae nye Mawu ƒe viwo.
ENGLISH: 14 For as many as are led by God’s Spirit, these are sons of God.

EWE: 15 Elabena menye kluvinyenye ƒe gbɔgbɔ si ana miaganɔ vɔvɔ̃m ake lae miexɔ o, ke boŋ vinyenye ƒe gbɔgbɔ ye miexɔ, eye gbɔgbɔ sia ʋãa mí míedoa ɣli be: "Abba, Fofo! " 16 Gbɔgbɔ la ŋutɔ ɖia ɖase kpena ɖe míaƒe gbɔgbɔ ŋu be Mawu ƒe viwo míenye. 17 Ke ne viwoe míenye la, ekema domenyilawo hãe míenye Mawu ƒe domenyilawo, kple Kristo ƒe hadomenyilawo ne míekpe fu kplii ko, ale be woakɔ mía ŋu hã kpakplii.
ENGLISH: 15 For you did not receive a spirit of slavery, back into fear, but you received a spirit of adoption, in which we cry Abba, "Father. " 16 The Spirit itself joins with our spirit in testifying that we are children of God 17 and if children, heirs too: heirs of God, and co-heirs with Christ, if we are indeed his co-sufferers in order that we may share also his glory.

EWE: 18 Eya ta mekpɔe be ɣeyiɣi sia me fukpekpewo meɖi naneke kura ne wotsɔe sɔ kple ŋutikɔkɔe si woava ɖe afia le mía gome la o.
ENGLISH: 18 For I figure that the sufferings of the present are not worth counting in comparison with the glory that is going to be revealed for us.

EWE: 19 Elabena nuwɔwɔ la le mɔ kpɔm vevie na Mawu ƒe viwo ƒe ɖeɖefia la.
ENGLISH: 19 For the expectancy of all creation is awaiting the revelation of the sons of God.

EWE: 20 Elabena wobɔbɔ nuwɔwɔ la ɖe toflokonyenye te, menye le eya ŋutɔ ƒe lɔlɔ̃nu me o, ke boŋ to ame si bɔbɔe ɖe anyi la dzi, hena mɔkpɔkpɔ 21 be woaɖe nuwɔwɔ la ŋutɔ hã tso gbegblẽ ƒe kluvinyenye la me, eye wòakpɔ Mawu ƒe viwo ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe ƒe ablɔɖe la.
ENGLISH: 20 For the creation became subject to futility not of its own free will, but for the purposes of him who created it, with the hope 21 that creation itself is to be set free out of slavery to decay, into the liberty of the glory of God’s children.

EWE: 23 Menye ema ɖeɖe koe o, ke boŋ míawo ŋutɔwo hãe, mí ame siwo si kutsetse gbãtɔ si nye gbɔgbɔ la le, ɛ̃, míawo hã míele ŋeŋem le mía ɖokui me, esime míele lalam vevie be woaxɔ mí abe viwo ene, be woaɖe mí tso míaƒe ŋutilã me to tafe la dzi.
ENGLISH: 22 For we know that all creation together is in groans and pangs up to now; 23 and not only this, but we ourselves too, having as we do the firstfruits of the Spirit, are groaning in ourselves as we await adoption, the redemption of our body.

EWE: 24 Elabena mɔkpɔkpɔ siae na woɖe mí; ke ne wokpɔ nu si wole mɔ kpɔm na xoxo la, womegayɔnɛ be mɔkpɔkpɔ o, elabena nu si kpɔm wole la, ɖe wogakpɔa mɔ nɛa? 25 Ke ne míele mɔ kpɔm na nu si míekpɔna o la, míetsɔa dzidodo nɔa elalam vevie.
ENGLISH: 24 For we were saved by hope; but a seen hope is not a hope (for who hopes for what he sees?), 25 but if we are hoping for what we do not see we await it steadily.

EWE: 26 Nenema kee gbɔgbɔ la hã kpena ɖe mía ŋu le míaƒe gbɔdzɔgbɔdzɔ me; elabena míenya nu si wòle be míado gbe ɖa abia abe ale si wòdze be míawɔe ene o, gake gbɔgbɔ la ŋutɔ xɔa míaƒe ŋeŋe siwo míeɖe gblɔ o la ɖe akɔ.
ENGLISH: 26 And in the same way the Spirit too takes hold to help our weakness; for we do not know what prayers to make as we need to, but the Spirit itself intercedes by groans which cannot be put into words.

EWE: 27 Ke ame si dzroa dziwo me kpɔ la sea gbɔgbɔ la gɔme, elabena exɔa ame kɔkɔewo ƒe nya ɖe akɔ ale si dzea Mawu ŋu.
ENGLISH: 27 And he who searches the hearts knows what is the Spirit’s mind, that he is interceding in God’s way for God’s people.

EWE: 28 Míenyae be Mawu naa eƒe nuwɔnawo katã zɔna aduadu ɖe ɖoɖo nu hena ame siwo lɔ̃a Mawu la ƒe nyonyo, ame siwo nye ame yɔyɔwo le eƒe tameɖoɖo la nu; 29 elabena ame siwo ŋu wòtrɔ ɖo gbã la, eɖoe ɖi hã do ŋgɔ be woanɔ ye Vi la ƒe nɔnɔme me, be wòanye ŋgɔgbevi le nɔvi geɖewo dome. 30 Azɔ hã, ame siwo wòɖo ɖi do ŋgɔ la, woawoe wòyɔ; eye ame siwo wòyɔ la, woawo kee wòbu ame dzɔdzɔewoe. Mlɔeba la, ame siwo wòbu ame dzɔdzɔewoe la, woawo hã ŋutie wòkɔ.
ENGLISH: 28 And we know that to those who love God, God gives all cooperation for good, to those who, as suited his purpose, are called 29 because those whom he foreknew he did also foreordain to be shaped into the image of his Son so that he should be firstborn among many brothers; 30 and those whom he foreordained, these he also called; and those whom he called, these he also justified; and those whom he justified, these he also glorified.

EWE: 31 Ekema nya kae míagblɔ le esiawo ŋu?
ENGLISH: 31 So what shall we say to these things?

EWE: Ne Mawu le mía dzi la, ame kae atsi tsitre ɖe mía ŋu? 32 Esi meve nu le eya ŋutɔ Via gɔ̃ hã ŋu o, ke boŋ wòtsɔe na ɖe mí katã ta la, nu ka tae eya kple Vi sia womalɔ̃ faa atsɔ nu bubuawo katã hã akpe ɖe eŋuti na mí o? 33 Ame kae atso Mawu ƒe ame tiatiawo nu? Mawue nye Ame si bua wo ame dzɔdzɔewoe. 34 Ame kae abu fɔ wo?
ENGLISH: If God is for us, who is against us? 32 He who did not stop short of his own Son, but gave him up for us all, how should he do otherwise than bestow everything on us with him? 33 Who will bring charges against God’s chosen? it is God that justifies, 34 who is it that condemns?

EWE: Kristo Yesue nye ame si ku, ɛ̃, nu si gawue nye be, wofɔe ɖe tsitre tso ame kukuwo dome, ame si le Mawu ƒe ɖusime, ame si hã xɔa míaƒe nya ɖe akɔ. 35 Ame kae ama mí ɖa tso Kristo la ƒe lɔlɔ̃ gbɔ? Fukpekpe loo alo xaxa alo yometiti alo dɔwuame alo amamanɔnɔ alo afɔku alo yia? 36 Abe ale si woŋlɔe ɖi ene be: "Tawòe wole mía wuwu dzi ŋkeke bliboa katã; wobu mí abe alẽ siwo woyina wuwu ge ene. " 37 Gake le nu siawo katã me la, míeɖua dzi bliboe to ame si lɔ̃ mí la dzi.
ENGLISH: It was Christ that died, or rather rose, he who is at God’s right hand, he who is even interceding for us; 35 who will separate us from Christ’s love? will distress or anguish or persecution or hunger or nakedness or danger or the sword, 36 as it is written "On your account we are being done to death all day, we were rated like sheep for slaughtering "? 37 but in all these things we are overwhelmingly victorious through him who loved us.

EWE: 38 Elabena meka ɖe edzi bliboe be, eɖanye ku o, eɖanye agbe o, eɖanye mawudɔlawo o, eɖanye dziɖuɖuwo o, eɖanye nu siwo li fifia o, eɖanye nu siwo le vava ge o, eɖanye ŋusẽwo o, 39 eɖanye kɔkɔƒe o, eɖanye gogloƒe alo nuwɔwɔ bubu aɖe o, mate ŋu ama mí ɖa tso Mawu ƒe lɔlɔ̃ si le Kristo Yesu, mía Aƒetɔ, me la gbɔ o.
ENGLISH: 38 For I am convinced that neither death nor life nor angels nor governments nor present conditions nor future nor powers 39 nor height nor depth nor any other creature will be able to separate us from God’s love in our Lord Christ Jesus.

EWE: Romatɔwo
ENGLISH: Romans

EWE: 9 Nyateƒe tom mele, elabena menye Kristo tɔ; nyemele aʋatso kam o, elabena nye dzitsinya wɔ ɖeka kple gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔe la le ɖase ɖim nam, 2 be mele nu xam vevie hele veve sem ɖaasi le nye dzi me.
ENGLISH: 9 I am speaking the truth in Christ, I am not lying, as in Holy Spirit my conscience bears me out in attesting, 2 that I have a great grief and my heart an unceasing ache.

EWE: 3 Elabena ɖe madi be woaɖe nye ŋutɔ ɖa le Kristo la ŋu abe fiƒodeme ene le nɔvinyewo, ame siwo nye ƒonyemeawo le ŋutilã nu, ta hafi, 4 wo, ame siwo nye Israel-viwo. Woawoe woxɔ be woanye viwo eye woakpɔ ŋutikɔkɔe, eye woawoe wotsɔ nubablawo, Se la, subɔsubɔdɔ kɔkɔe la kple ŋugbedodoawo na. 5 Wonye tɔgbuiawo ƒe dzidzimeviwo, eye woawo mee Kristo la dzɔ tso le ŋutilã nu. Woakafu Mawu, ame si ƒo nuwo katã ta la, yi mavɔmavɔ me.
ENGLISH: 3 For I could pray that I might myself be for God’s doom cutting me off from Christ in favor of my brothers, my kinsfolk in the way of flesh, 4 who are Israelites, to whom belong the adoption and the glory and the covenants and the gift of the law and the divine service and the promises; 5 whose are the fathers, and from whom in the way of flesh comes the Christ, he who is over everything, God blessed forever Amen!

EWE: Amen. 6 Gake menye ɖe Mawu ƒe nya la do kpo nu hafi o.
ENGLISH: 6 But it is not any such thing as that God’s word has fallen through.

EWE: Elabena menye ame siwo katã dzɔ tso Israel me lae nye "Israel " viwo ŋutɔŋutɔ o.
ENGLISH: For it is not just everybody who comes from Israel that are Israel.

EWE: 7 Eye menye esi wonye Abraham ƒe dzidzimeviwo tae wo katã wonye viwo o, hafi boŋ: "Ame si woayɔ be ‘wò dzidzimevi’ la adzɔ tso Isak me. " 8 Efia be, ŋutilãmeviwo menye Mawu ƒe viwo ŋutɔŋutɔ o, ke boŋ ŋugbedodo la ƒe viwoe nye dzidzimeviawo.
ENGLISH: 7 Neither because they are Abraham’s issue are all of them children, but "it will be by Isaac that issue shall be called yours "; 8 that is, it is not just the children of the flesh that are children of God’s, but the children of the promise are counted as issue; 9 for this word, "at this date I will come and Sarah shall have a son, " is one of promise.

EWE: 9 Elabena ŋugbedodonya la yi ale: "Magava le ƒe si gbɔna ƒe ɣealewoɣi, eye viŋutsuvi anɔ Sara si. " 10 Ke menye ema koe o, ke esime Rebeka fɔ venɔviwo ƒe fu na mía tɔgbui Isak hã; 11 elabena esi womekpɔ dzi wo o, eye womewɔ nyui alo vɔ̃ aɖeke haɖe o la, be Mawu ƒe tameɖoɖo le tiatiawɔwɔ ŋu nakpɔtɔ anɔ te ɖe Eya ame si yɔa ame la dzi, ke menye ɖe dɔwɔwɔwo dzi o ta la, 12 wogblɔ nɛ be: "Tsitsitɔ anye kluvi na ɖevitɔ. " 13 Abe ale si woŋlɔe ɖi ene be: "Melɔ̃ Yakob, ke melé fu Esau ya. " 14 Ekema nya kae míagblɔ?
ENGLISH: 10 And not only this, but Rebecca too, having impregnation by one man, our father Isaac, 11 for when they were not yet born nor had done any good or evil act, in order that God’s purpose in the way of choice might remain in force not on the basis of deeds but on the basis of him who gave the call, 12 she was told "the senior shall be enslaved to the junior, " 13 as it is written "I loved Jacob, but Esau I hated. "

EWE: Ðe Mawu wɔa nu madzɔmadzɔa? Gbeɖe! 15 Elabena egblɔ na Mose be: "Makpɔ nublanui na ame si medi be makpɔ nublanui na, eye mave ame si nu medi be mave la nu. " 16 Eya ta metso ame si le didim alo ame si le ʋiʋlim la ƒe lɔlɔ̃nu me o, ke boŋ etso Mawu, ame si kpɔa nublanui la, ƒe lɔlɔ̃nu me.
ENGLISH: 14 What shall we therefore say? is there injustice with God? away with the thought! 15 For he says to Moses "I will take pity on whom I do take pity on, and have compassion for whom I do have compassion for. " 16 So then it belongs not to the one who has the will nor to the one who does the running, but to God who takes pity.

EWE: 17 Elabena Ŋɔŋlɔ la gblɔ na Farao be: "Susu sia tae meɖe mɔ nèkpɔtɔ li ɖo: be maɖe nye ŋusẽ afia le ŋuwò, ale be woaɖe gbeƒã nye ŋkɔ le anyigba blibo la dzi. " 18 Eya ta ekpɔa nublanui na ame si wòdi be yeakpɔe na, ke ame si ŋu wòdi be yeaɖe asi le wòasẽ dzi me la, eɖea asi le eŋu. 19 Eya ta àbiam be: "Ekema nu ka tae wògabua fɔ ame ɖo?
ENGLISH: 17 For the text says to the Pharaoh "I raised you up for this sake, for the sake of showing my power on you, and of having my fame told of throughout the earth. " 18 So then he takes pity on whom he will, but whom he will he hardens.

EWE: Ðe nu si womè la agblɔ na ame si mèe la be: "Nu ka tae nèwɔm alea? " 21 Nu ka? Ðe ŋusẽ mele zemela si ɖe tsu dzi be wòatsɔ anyi si wònya la ƒe ɖe amè ze si ŋu bubu le, eye wòagatsɔ eƒe ɖe amè ze si ŋu bubu mele o la oa? 22 Ekema ne Mawu di be yeaɖe yeƒe dɔmedzoe afia, eye yeana woanya yeƒe ŋusẽ, evɔ wògbɔ dzi ɖi heɖe mɔ ɖe dziku ƒe ze siwo wodzra ɖo ɖi na tsɔtsrɔ̃ la ŋu ɖe? 23 Eye ne ewɔ esia be yeana woanya ŋutikɔkɔe ƒe agbɔsɔsɔ si le ye si ɖe nublanuikpɔkpɔ ƒe ze siwo wòdzra ɖo ɖi do ŋgɔ hena ŋutikɔkɔe la ŋu, 24 siwo nye míawo, ame siwo wòyɔ, menye tso Yudatɔwo ɖeɖe ko dome o, ke boŋ tso dukɔwo hã dome la, ekema nya kae míagblɔ le eya ŋu? 25 Ele abe ale si wògblɔe le Hosea ƒe agbalẽ me hã ene be: "Ame siwo menye nye dukɔ o la, mayɔ wo be ‘nye dukɔ,’ kple nyɔnu si nyemelɔ̃ tsã o la be ‘lɔlɔ̃tɔ’; 26 eye afi si wogblɔ na wo le be, ‘Menye nye dukɔe mienye o’ la, afi mae woayɔ wo le be ‘Mawu gbagbe la ƒe viwo.’ " 27 Azɔ hã, Yesaya do ɣli gblɔ le Israel ŋu be: "Togbɔ be Israel-viwo ƒe xexlẽme anɔ abe ƒutake ene hã la, ame ʋɛ siwo susɔ koe woaɖe. 28 Elabena Yehowa abia akɔnta le anyigba dzi, awɔe ade goe, eye awɔe kaba. " 29 Eye abe ale si Yesaya gblɔe ɖi ene la: "Ne ɖe aʋakɔwo ƒe Yehowa mekpɔtɔ dzidzime aɖeke ɖi na mí o la, anye ne míezu abe Sodom ene, anye ne míeɖi Gomora. "
ENGLISH: 19 So you will say to me "Why does he go on finding fault? for who stands up against his wish? " 20 Rather, man, who are you that answer back to God? is the product to say to the manufacturer "Why did you make me like this? " 21 Or does the potter not have a right to manage the clay, to make out of the same mass part into a vessel destined for honor and part into one for ignominy? 22 And if God, having a will to show his anger and make known what he could do, endured with great patience vessels for anger, adapted to go to destruction; 23 and, in order to make known the richness of his glory upon vessels for mercy which he had prepared for glory, 24 us whom he also called not only out of the Jews but out of the nations too 25 the same as he says to Hosea "I will call him who was not my people my people, and her who was not loved loved, 26 and in the place where they were told ‘you are not my people,’ there they shall be called sons of the living God. " 27 And Isaiah cries out about Israel "If the number of the sons of Israel be like the sand of the sea, the remnant will be saved, 28 for the Lord will put a word in effect sweepingly and summarily on earth. " 29 And, as Isaiah had said before, "if the Lord of Sabaoth had not left us seed we should have come to be like Sodom and a parallel to Gomorrah. "

EWE: 30 Ekema nya kae míagblɔ?
ENGLISH: 30 So what shall we say?

EWE: Eyae nye be, togbɔ be dukɔwo me tɔwo menɔ dzɔdzɔenyenye yome o hã la, woƒe asi su dzɔdzɔenyenye dzi, si nye dzɔdzɔenyenye si tso xɔse me; 31 gake togbɔ be Israel nɔ dzɔdzɔenyenye ƒe se yome hã la, eƒe asi mesu se ma dzi o. 32 Nu ka tae?
ENGLISH: That foreign nations, those that did not go in for righteousness, arrived at righteousness, but the righteousness that comes of faith; 31 but Israel, going in for the law of righteousness, did not attain to the law.

EWE: Elabena meti eyome le xɔse me o, ke boŋ abe ɖe wònɔ te ɖe dɔwɔwɔwo dzi ene. Wokli "nukikli ƒe kpe " la; 33 abe ale si woŋlɔe ɖi ene be: "Kpɔ ɖa! Mele nukikli ƒe kpe kple nuɖiaɖia ƒe agakpe ɖom anyi le Zion, ke ame si ziɔ eƒe xɔse ɖe eŋu maɖu ŋukpe o. "
ENGLISH: 32 Why? because they were not trying on the basis of faith, but as if on that of deeds; they struck on the "stone to strike against, " 33 as it is written "Here I am laying in Sion a stone to strike against and a rock to stumble over; and he who believes in him will not be put to shame. "

EWE: Romatɔwo
ENGLISH: Romans

EWE: 10 Nɔviwo, nye dzimedidi kple nye kukuɖeɖe na Mawu ɖe wo tae nye be woakpɔ ɖeɖe.
ENGLISH: 10 Brothers, my heart’s goodwill and entreaty to God is in their favor for their salvation.

EWE: 2 Elabena mele ɖase ɖim le wo ŋu be, dzo le wo me ɖe Mawu ŋu, ke menye le sidzedze vavãtɔ nu o. 3 Elabena esi womenya Mawu ƒe dzɔdzɔenyenye o, ke boŋ wole didim be yewoaɖo yewo ŋutɔ tɔ anyi ta la, womebɔbɔ wo ɖokuiwo ɖe Mawu ƒe dzɔdzɔenyenye la te o.
ENGLISH: 2 For I testify that they have zeal for God, but not with insight; 3 for, not knowing about God’s righteousness and trying to make good their own, they did not let themselves depend on God’s righteousness.

EWE: 4 Elabena Kristoe nye Se la ƒe nuwuwu, ale be ame sia ame si xɔna sena la ƒe asi nasu dzɔdzɔenyenye dzi.
ENGLISH: 4 For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every believer.

EWE: 5 Elabena Mose ŋlɔe ɖi le dzɔdzɔenyenye si tso Se la me ŋu be: "Ame si wɔa nu siawo la, anɔ agbe to wo me. " 6 Ke dzɔdzɔenyenye si tso xɔse me la gblɔ be: "Mègagblɔ le wò dzi me be, ‘Ame kae alia ayi dziƒo?’ be wòana Kristo naɖi ava, 7 alo, ‘Ame kae aɖi ayi aʋli me?’ be wòakplɔ Kristo tso ame kukuwo dome avɛ hã o. " 8 Ke nya kae wògblɔ?
ENGLISH: 5 For Moses writes of righteousness on the basis of law "the man who does the things will have life " by it; 6 but righteousness on the basis of faith says thus: "Do not say to yourself ‘Who will go up to the sky?’ " (that is, to bring Christ down;) 7 "or ‘Who will go down into the abyss?’ " (that is, to bring Christ up from the dead). 8 But what does it say?

EWE: "Nya la tsɔ ɖe gbɔwò, ele wò ŋutɔ wò nu me kple wò ŋutɔ wò dzi me "; eyae nye xɔse ƒe "nya, " si míele gbeƒã ɖemee la. 9 Elabena ne ètsɔ wò nu ɖea gbeƒã le dutoƒo be Yesu nye Aƒetɔ, eye nèxɔna sena le wò dzi me be Mawu fɔe ɖe tsitre tso ame kukuwo dome la, ekema àkpɔ ɖeɖe.
ENGLISH: "The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart "; that is, the word of faith which we are proclaiming; 9 because if by your mouth you acknowledge Jesus to be Lord, and in your heart you believe that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.

EWE: 10 Elabena wotsɔa dzi xɔna sena hena dzɔdzɔenyenye, ke wotsɔa nu ʋua eme le dutoƒo hena ɖeɖekpɔkpɔ.
ENGLISH: 10 For it is with a heart believing is done leading to righteousness, and it is with a mouth acknowledgment is made leading to salvation.

EWE: 11 Ŋɔŋlɔ la gblɔ be: "Ame sia ame si ziɔ eƒe xɔse ɖe eŋu la maɖu ŋukpe o. " 12 Elabena vovototo aɖeke mele Yudatɔ kple Helatɔ dome o. Aƒetɔ ɖekae le wo katã nu, eye wònaa nu geɖe ame siwo katã yɔnɛ la.
ENGLISH: 11 For the text says "Anyone who believes in him will not be put to shame "; 12 for there is no distinction between Jew and Greek, for the same one is Lord of all, rich toward all who call on him; 13 for "everyone who shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved. "

EWE: 13 Elabena "ame sia ame si yɔa Yehowa ƒe ŋkɔ la, woaɖee. " 14 Ke aleke woawɔ ayɔ ame si dzi womexɔ se o la?
ENGLISH: 14 How are they then to call on him in whom they have not believed?

EWE: Eye aleke woawɔ axɔ ame si ŋu nya womese kpɔ o la dzi ase?
ENGLISH: And how are they to believe in him of whom they have not heard?

EWE: Eye aleke woawɔ asee, ne ame aɖeke meɖea gbeƒã o? 15 Eye aleke woawɔ aɖe gbeƒã, ne womedɔ wo ɖa hafi o? Abe ale si woŋlɔe ɖi ene be: "Ame siwo ɖea gbeƒã nu nyuiwo ŋuti nya nyui la ƒe afɔwo nya kpɔ loo! "
ENGLISH: And how are they to hear without a proclaimer? 15 And how are they to proclaim unless they are sent? as it is written "How beautiful are the feet of those who bring the news of good! "

EWE: 16 Gake menye wo katãe ɖo to nya nyui la o. Elabena Yesaya gblɔ be: "Yehowa, ame kae xɔ nya si wose tso mía gbɔ la dzi se? " 17 Eya ta nu si wose la mee xɔse tsona. Eye wosenɛ ne wogblɔ Kristo ŋu nya na wo. 18 Ke mele biabiam be, Menye ɖe womesee o ɖe?
ENGLISH: 16 But they did not all listen to the good news; for Isaiah says "Lord, who believed what they heard from us? " 17 Then believing comes out of hearing; and hearing, through Christ’s word.

EWE: Nya lae nye be, "woƒe gbe ɖi hoo le anyigba blibo la dzi, eye nya si wogblɔ la de xexea ƒe afi sia afi. " 19 Ke megale biabiam be, Menye ɖe Israel menyae o ɖe?
ENGLISH: 18 But I say, did they not hear? why, "the noise of them went out into all the earth and their words to the ends of the world. " 19 But I say, did Israel not know?

EWE: Gbã la, Mose gblɔ be: "Mato dukɔ maɖinu dzi ana miaʋã ŋu; mato dukɔ tsibome dzi ana miado dziku vevie. " 20 Ke dzi ɖo Yesaya ƒo ŋutɔ wògblɔ be: "Ame siwo medim o lae kpɔm; mena ame siwo mebia tanye se o la va nyam. " 21 Ke egblɔ le Israel ya ŋu be: "Meke nye abɔwo me ɖo ɖe dukɔ si meɖoa to o, eye wonye dzimesesẽtɔwo la, ŋkeke bliboa katã. "
ENGLISH: First Moses says "I will challenge your jealousy with what is not a people, provoke you with an insensate nation. " 20 And Isaiah comes out boldly and says "I was found by those who were not looking for me, I showed myself to those who were not inquiring of me. " 21 But as to Israel he says "all day I have spread out my hands to a disobedient and dissident people. "

EWE: Romatɔwo
ENGLISH: Romans

EWE: 11 Azɔ mele biabiam be, Ðe Mawu gbe eƒe dukɔ la?
ENGLISH: 11 So I am saying, Did God reject his people?

EWE: Gbeɖe! Elabena Israel-vie nye hã menye, Abraham ƒe dzidzimevi, tso Benyamin-toa me.
ENGLISH: Away with the thought! for I am an Israelite myself, a descendant of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.

EWE: 2 Mawu megbe eƒe dukɔ si ŋu wòtrɔ susu ɖo gbã la o.
ENGLISH: 2 God did not reject his people whom he foreknew.

EWE: Ðe mienya nu si ŋɔŋlɔ la gblɔ le Eliya ŋu, ale si wòtso Israel nu na Mawu oa? 3 "Yehowa, wowu wò nyagblɔɖilawo, wogbã wò vɔsamlekpuiwo gudugudu, nye ɖeka koe susɔ, eye fifia wole didim be yewoaɖe nye agbe ɖa. " 4 Ke nya kae Mawu gblɔ nɛ?
ENGLISH: Or do you not know in the story of Elijah what the text says, when he is expostulating with God against Israel 3 "Lord, they killed thy prophets, they demolished thy altars, and I was the only one left, and they are after my life " 4 but what does the divine voice say to him?

EWE: "Mesusɔ ame akpe adre ɖi na ɖokuinye, ame siwo medze klo na Baal o. " 5 Eya ta nenema kee le fifi ɣeyiɣia me hã la, ame susɔe aɖewo li siwo wotia to amenuveve me.
ENGLISH: "I left myself seven thousand men who did not bend a knee to the Baal. " 5 Thus then at the present time too there are leavings in accordance with the choice made by grace.

EWE: 6 Ke ne amenuveve tae la, ekema meganye to dɔwɔwɔwo dzie o; ne menye nenema o la, ke amenuveve la meganye amenuveve o.
ENGLISH: 6 But if it is by grace it is no longer on the basis of deeds, else grace would no longer be grace.

EWE: 7 Ekema nu kae?
ENGLISH: 7 What then?

EWE: Nu si tututu dim Israel le vevie la, eƒe asi mesu edzi o, ke ame siwo wotia ya ƒe asi su edzi. Wo dometɔ susɔeawo na woƒe nugɔmesese yi to, 8 abe ale si woŋlɔe ɖi ene be: "Mawu trɔ alɔ̃ tsu dɔdɔ ƒe gbɔgbɔ kɔ ɖe wo dzi, ena ŋku si mekpɔa nu o kple to si mesea nu o la wo va se ɖe egbe sia. " 9 David hã gblɔ be: "Na woƒe kplɔ̃ nazu ɖɔ, mɔ̃, nukikli kple tohehe na wo. 10 Na woƒe ŋkuwo dzi natsyɔ ne woagakpɔ nu o, eye na woƒe dzimegbe naxa gobaa ɣeawokatãɣi. "
ENGLISH: The very thing that Israel is hunting after, this thing it did not win: the chosen ones did win it, but the rest turned callous, 8 as it is written "God gave them a spirit of trance, eyes not to see and ears not to hear, up to this day "; 9 and David says "Let their table become a trap and toils and the bait on a trigger and retribution to them, 10 let their eyes be darkened out of seeing, and break down their back all the time. "

EWE: 11 Eya ta mele biabiam be, Ðe wokli nu hedze anyi keŋkeŋua?
ENGLISH: 11 So I am saying, Did they stumble in order that they might fall?

EWE: Gbeɖe! Ke boŋ woƒe afɔ baɖa ɖeɖe la zu ɖeɖekpɔkpɔ na dukɔwo me tɔwo, ale be wòana woaʋã ŋu.
ENGLISH: Away with the thought; but by their falling into offense the foreign nations get salvation to stir their jealousy.

EWE: 12 Ke ne woƒe afɔ baɖa ɖeɖe la he yayra vɛ na xexea, eye ne wo dzi si ɖe kpɔtɔ la he yayra vɛ na dukɔwo me tɔwo ɖe, ekema ɖe woƒe xexlẽme blibo la mahee vɛ geɖe wu oa? 13 Azɔ mele nu ƒom na mi ame siwo nye dukɔwo me tɔwo. Esi menye apostolo na dukɔwo ta la, medoa nye subɔsubɔdɔ la ɖe dzi, 14 ne mato mɔ aɖe dzi ana nye ŋutɔ nye amewo naʋã ŋu, ale be maɖe wo dometɔ aɖewo.
ENGLISH: 12 But if their falling into offense is wealth to the world and their failure is wealth to the nations, how much more their full coming in! 13 But to you foreigners I say, Then so far as I am an apostle to foreigners I make much of my office 14 in the hope that I may stir the jealousy of my kindred and save some of them.

EWE: 15 Elabena ne wo gbegbe la na wodzra xexea kple Mawu dome ɖo la, ekema nu kae wo xɔxɔ la anye, ne menye wo ɖeɖe tso ku me ava agbe me o? 16 Eye ne amɔwɔ ƒe akpa si nye kutsetse gbãtɔ la le kɔkɔe la, ekema amɔwɔ la katã hã le kɔkɔe; eye ne ke la le kɔkɔe la, ekema alɔawo hã le kɔkɔe.
ENGLISH: 15 For if throwing them overboard means reconciliation for the world, what will taking them in be but life from the dead? 16 And if the piece taken out first is sacred, so is the batch; and if the root is sacred, so are the branches.

EWE: 17 Ke ne wolã alɔawo dometɔ aɖewo ɖa, eye wotsɔ wò, si nye gbemiti do ɖe susɔeawo dzi, eye nèzu gomekpɔla le amiti la ƒe ke si me nunyiame le me la, 18 ekema mèganɔ ɖokuiwò dom ɖe dzi ɖe alɔawo ŋu o.
ENGLISH: 17 And if some of the branches were broken out, and you, being a piece of wild olive, were grafted in among them and came to share with them the root of the olive-tree’s fatness, 18 do not flout the branches; if you do, it is not you that are carrying the root but the root that is carrying you.

EWE: Ke ne èle ɖokuiwò dom ɖe dzi ɖe wo ŋu la, ɖo ŋku edzi be menye wòe lé ke la ɖe te o, ke boŋ ke lae lé wò ɖe te. 19 Azɔ àgblɔ be: "Wolã alɔwo ɖa, ale be woatsɔm ado ɖe wo teƒe. " 20 Enyo! Woƒe dzimaxɔse tae wolã wo ɖa ɖo, ke wò ya wò xɔsee na nèle tsitre. Mèganɔ ɖokuiwò dom ɖe dzi o, ke nɔ vɔvɔ̃m boŋ.
ENGLISH: 19 Then will you say "Branches were broken out to have me grafted in "? 20 All right: they were broken out by unbelief, and you stand by faith; do not get lofty ideas, but have fears, 21 for if God did not spare the natural branches neither will he spare you.

EWE: 21 Elabena ne Mawu mekpɔ nublanui na alɔ siwo nye atia ŋutɔ ƒe dzɔdzɔmetɔwo o la, ekema makpɔ nublanui na wò hã o. 22 Eya ta kpɔ Mawu ƒe dɔmenyonyo kple ale si eƒe asi sẽna ɖe ame dzii ɖa.
ENGLISH: 22 See, then, a kindness and a rigorousness of God’s: toward those who fell rigorousness, but toward you God’s kindness if you keep in touch with the kindness else you too will be cut out.

EWE: 23 Eye woawo gɔ̃ hã, ne womeyi edzi tsi woƒe dzimaxɔse la me o la, ekema woatsɔ wo ado ɖe edzi; elabena Mawu agate ŋu ado wo ɖe edzi ake.
ENGLISH: 23 And they, if they do not stick to unbelief, will be grafted in; for God is able to graft them in again.

EWE: 24 Elabena ne wolã wò tso amiti si nye gbemetɔ tso dzɔdzɔme la ŋu, eye wotsɔ wò do ɖe amiti si nye abɔmetɔ dzi, si mele dzɔdzɔme nu o la, ekema ɖe womatsɔ esiawo, siwo nye dzɔdzɔmetɔ la, ado ɖe woawo ŋutɔwo ƒe amiti la dzi geɖe wu oa?
ENGLISH: 24 For if you were cut out of the natural wild tree and grafted unnaturally into a quality tree, how much more shall these, the natural ones, be grafted on their own tree!

EWE: 25 Nɔviwo, nyemedi be nya ɣaɣla kɔkɔe sia nanɔ manyamanya na mi o, ne miagabu mia ɖokuiwo nunyalawoe o: Israel ƒe nugɔmesese yi to va se ɖe esime dukɔwo me tɔwo ƒe xexlẽme blibo la de, 26 eye aleae woana ɖeɖe Israel blibo la. Abe ale si woŋlɔe ɖi ene be: "Ðela la atso Zion, eye wòaɖe mawumavɔmavɔ̃ ɖa tso Yakob gbɔ. 27 Eye esiae nye nubabla si anɔ nye kpli wo dome, ne meɖe woƒe nu vɔ̃wo ɖa. " 28 Nyateƒee, le nya nyui la gome la, wonye futɔwo le miaƒe viɖe ta; ke le Mawu ƒe tiatia la gome la, wonye lɔlɔ̃tɔwo le wo tɔgbuiwo ta. 29 Mawu ƒe nunanawo kple yɔyɔ la mavee o.
ENGLISH: 25 For I do not want you to be without the knowledge of this secret, brothers, in order that you may not feel sagacious, that there has come to Israel a partial callousing until the fullness of the nations gets in, 26 and thus all Israel will be saved, as it is written "He will come out of Sion who shall execute deliverance; he will turn away crimes from Jacob; 27 and this is the covenant from me for them, when I remove their sins. " 28 As to the gospel they are enemies on your account, but as to the choice they are dear on account of the fathers; 29 for God’s gracious gifts and his call are not liable to a change of mind.

EWE: 30 Elabena ale si ko mieɖo to Mawu tsã o, ke wokpɔ nublanui na mi azɔ le woƒe tomaɖomaɖo ta la, 31 nenema kee ame siawo hã meɖo to fifia o, eye nublanuikpɔkpɔ do tso eme na miawo, ale be woakpɔ nublanui na woawo hã azɔ.
ENGLISH: 30 For as you were formerly disobedient to God but now have come to receive mercy by the disobedience of these, 31 so it was that these too were disobedient now in order that by the mercy to you they too may receive mercy.

EWE: 32 Elabena Mawu tu nu ɖe wo katã nu ɖe tomaɖomaɖo me, ale be wòakpɔ nublanui na wo katã.
ENGLISH: 32 For God locked everybody up into disobedience in order that he may have mercy on everybody.

EWE: 33 Oo, Mawu ƒe kesinɔnuwo kple nunya kpakple sidzedze me goglo loo! Aleke eƒe ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃wo me dzodzro tsitotsito meli o, eye eƒe mɔwo mele nyanya me o ale! 34 Elabena "ame kae va nya Yehowa ƒe tamesusu, alo ame kae zu eƒe aɖaŋuɖola? " 35 Alo, "ame kae na nui gbã, ne wòaɖo eteƒe nɛ? " 36 Elabena nuwo katã tso egbɔ, eyae tsɔ wo na, eye wonye etɔ.
ENGLISH: 33 O the vastness of God’s wealth in both wisdom and knowledge! how unsearchable are his judgments and how untraceable his courses! 34 "For who has known the Lord’s mind? or who has been adviser to him? " 35 "or who has advanced any sum to him and is to have it paid back? " 36 because out of him and through him and into him comes everything.

EWE: Etɔ nanye ŋutikɔkɔe yi mavɔmavɔ me.
ENGLISH: To him be glory forever; amen.

EWE: Amen.
ENGLISH: Romans

EWE: 12 Eya ta nɔviwo, mele kuku ɖem na mi vevie to Mawu ƒe dɔmetɔtrɔ me be miatsɔ miaƒe ŋutilãwo ana wòanye vɔsa gbagbe, si le kɔkɔe, si dzea Mawu ŋu, wòanye subɔsubɔdɔ kɔkɔe si me miazã miaƒe tamebubuŋutete le. 2 Eye midzudzɔ agbenɔnɔ ɖe nuɖoanyi sia ƒe nɔnɔme nu, ke boŋ mitrɔ miaƒe nɔnɔme to miaƒe tamesusu wɔwɔ yeyee me, ne miawo ŋutɔwo miate ŋu akpɔ kakaɖedzi le Mawu ƒe lɔlɔ̃nu nyui dzeameŋu si le blibo la ŋu.
ENGLISH: 12 So, brothers, I urge you by God’s compassion to present your bodies a holy living sacrifice acceptable to God, your rational form of worship; 2 and do not shape yourselves to fit in with these times, but be transformed by reconstitution of your mind so that you may be judges of what is God’s good and acceptable and perfect will.

EWE: 3 Elabena to amenuveve si wonam me la, mele egblɔm na mia dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe be wòagabu eɖokui ŋu wu ale si dze o, ke boŋ be wòabu ale si wòanɔ ŋute le susu me ŋu, ame sia ame le xɔse ƒe dzidze si Mawu nɛ la nu.
ENGLISH: 3 For through the grace given to me let me tell each man among you not to be more lofty-minded than is right, but to mind that he keeps in his right mind, each as God has allotted him a measure of faith.

EWE: 4 Elabena ale si ko ŋutinu geɖewo le ŋutilã ɖeka ŋu na mí, gake ŋutinuawo katã mewɔa dɔ ɖeka ƒomevi o la, 5 nenema kee míawo hã, togbɔ be míesɔ gbɔ hã la, ŋutilã ɖekae míenye le Kristo me, gake ŋutinuwoe mía dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe nye na nɔvia. 6 Eya ta esi wònye nunana vovovowoe le mía si le amenuveve si wona mí nu ta la, ne nyagbɔgblɔɖie la, mina míagblɔ nya ɖi le xɔse ale si nu wona mí la nu; 7 alo ne subɔsubɔdɔe la, mina míanɔ subɔsubɔdɔ sia dzi; alo ame si fiaa nu la, nenɔ eƒe nufiafia la dzi; 8 alo ame si dea dzi ƒo la, nenɔ eƒe dzidede ƒo na ame la dzi; ame si naa nu la, nenɔ nu nam kple dzi faa; ame si le amewo nu la, nedo vevie nu le ewɔwɔ me; ame si kpɔa nublanui la, nenɔ edzi kple dzidzɔ. 9 Migana alakpanuwɔwɔ aɖeke nanɔ miaƒe lɔlɔ̃ la me o. Minyɔ ŋu nu vɔ̃ɖi; milé ɖe nu si nyo la ŋu. 10 Miaƒe nɔvilɔlɔ̃ nade to abe dadavilɔlɔ̃ ene. Mitre mia nɔewo bubu. 11 Mitsɔ dzo ɖe dɔ ŋu, migawɔ kuvia o. Mixɔ dzo le gbɔgbɔ la me. Misubɔ Yehowa abe kluviwo ene. 12 Dzi nedzɔ mi le mɔkpɔkpɔ me. Mido dzi le xaxa me. Minɔ gbedodoɖa dzi ɖaa. 13 Mina nu ame kɔkɔewo le woƒe hiahiãwo nu. Minɔ amedzrowɔwɔ dzi.
ENGLISH: 4 For as we have many organs in one body, but the organs do not all have the same function, 5 so we who are so many are one body in Christ, and individually organs of each other, 6 but having different gifts according to the grace given to us 7 be it prophecy in proportion to faith, be it servitorship in serving, be it the teacher in teaching, 8 be it the exhorter in exhortation; the giver of his goods in largeheartedness, the manager of affairs in devotion to duty, the comforter of misfortunes in cheeriness; 9 love with no sham about it; detesting what is wicked, sticking tight to what is good; 10 in brotherliness mutually affectionate, in honor showing mutual deference, 11 in earnestness not slack, enthusiastic in spirit, conscious of being bound to the Lord’s service, 12 blithe in hope, steadfast in distress, devoted to prayer, 13 showing solidarity with the needs of God’s people, forward in hospitality.

EWE: 14 Minɔ ame siwo tia mia yome la yram; miyra ame, migaƒo fi de ame o.
ENGLISH: 14 Bless your persecutors: bless and do not curse.

EWE: 15 Mikpɔ dzidzɔ kple ame siwo le dzidzɔ kpɔm; mifa avi kple ame siwo le avi fam.
ENGLISH: 15 Gladness with men who are being glad, weeping with weepers.

EWE: 16 Miwɔ nu ɖe amewo ŋu abe ale si miewɔnɛ ɖe mia ɖokuiwo ŋu ene; miganɔ nu gãwo ŋu bum o, ke minɔ nu siwo bɔbɔ ɖe anyi la yome boŋ. Migabu mia ɖokuiwo nunyalawoe o. 17 Migaɖo vɔ̃ vɔ̃ teƒe na ame aɖeke o. Miwɔ nu siwo nyo le amewo katã ƒe nukpɔkpɔ nu.
ENGLISH: 16 Interested along the same line, for each other; not occupied with thoughts of high things, but drawn into the interests of lowly people; do not feel as if you were great thinkers.

EWE: 18 Ne anya wɔ, eye wòanye nu si atso mia gbɔ la, minɔ anyi kple amewo katã le ŋutifafa me. 19 Lɔlɔ̃tɔwo, migabia hlɔ̃ na mia ɖokuiwo o, ke miɖe mɔ na dziku la boŋ; elabena woŋlɔ ɖi be: "‘Tɔnyee nye hlɔ̃biabia’; nye la, maɖo eteƒe, Yehowa ye gblɔe. " 20 Ke boŋ "ne dɔ le wò futɔ wum la, na nui wòaɖu; ne tsikɔ le ewum la, na tsii wòano; elabena ne èwɔ esia la, àƒo dzoka xɔxɔwo nu ƒu ɖe eƒe ta dzi. " 21 Mègaɖe mɔ nu vɔ̃ɖi naɖu dziwò o, ke boŋ yi edzi nàtsɔ nu nyui anɔ nu vɔ̃ɖi dzi ɖum.
ENGLISH: 17 Not paying anybody back a bad turn for a bad, keeping in mind what is going to be good before all men; 18 if possible, as far as depends on you, keeping at peace with all men; 19 not taking your own revenges, dear ones, but leave room for God’s anger; for it is written "Mine is vengeance, I will requite, says the Lord. " 20 But "if your enemy is hungry feed him, if he is thirsty give him a drink, for in doing this you will be piling live coals on his head. " 21 Do not be beaten by the bad, but beat the bad with the good.

EWE: Romatɔwo
ENGLISH: Romans

EWE: 13 Ame sia ame nebɔbɔ eɖokui ɖe ŋusẽtɔwo te, elabena ŋusẽ aɖeke meli o, negbe esi tso Mawu gbɔ la ko; ŋusẽtɔ siwo li la, Mawue ɖe mɔ wole woƒe nɔƒe siwo seɖoƒe li na la. 2 Eya ta ame si tsia tsitre ɖe ŋusẽtɔ ŋu la, etsia tsitre ɖe Mawu ƒe ɖoɖo ŋu; ame siwo tsia tsitre ɖe eŋu la, woahe ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃ ava wo ɖokuiwo dzi.
ENGLISH: 13 Let every soul be submissive to superior authorities; for there is no authority except by God, and those that there are are given their positions by God, 2 so that he who sets himself against authority is opposing God’s institution; and those who oppose it will have judgment passed on them.

EWE: 3 Elabena ŋɔdzi le dziɖulawo ŋu, menye na nu nyui wɔlawo o, ke na nu gbegblẽ wɔlawo boŋ. Eya ta ɖe mèdi be yeavɔ̃ ŋusẽtɔ oa? Ekema nɔ nu nyui wɔm, eye àkpɔ kafukafu tso egbɔ; 4 elabena Mawu ƒe dɔla wònye na wò le wò nyonyo ta.
ENGLISH: 3 For rulers are not a terror to the good deed but to the bad; and you want not to be afraid of the authority? do the good, and you will have praise from it, 4 for it is to you an agent of God’s for the good.

EWE: Mawu ƒe dɔla si hea to na nu gbegblẽ wɔla le dɔmedzoe me lae wònye. 5 Eya ta ehiã vevie be miabɔbɔ mia ɖokui ɖe wo te, menye le dɔmedzoedodo ma ɖeɖe ko ta o, ke le miaƒe dzitsinya hã ta.
ENGLISH: But if you do the bad, do be afraid, for it is not for nothing he wears his sword; for he is an avenging agent of God’s for anger to him who commits the bad deed; 5 for which reason it is necessary to be submissive not only on account of his anger but also on account of your conscience.

EWE: 6 Esia tae miexea adzɔ hã ɖo; elabena Mawu ƒe dutoƒo subɔlawo wonye, eye wosubɔna ɣesiaɣi le tameɖoɖo sia tututu ta.
ENGLISH: 6 For this is why you pay taxes too; for they are servitors of God’s steadily at work for that very purpose.

EWE: 7 Mitsɔ nu si ame sia ame dze na la nɛ: ame si dze na adzɔ la, mixe adzɔ nɛ; ame si dze na nudzɔdzɔ la, midzɔ nu nɛ; ame si dze na vɔvɔ̃ la, mivɔ̃e; ame si dze na bubu la, mibui.
ENGLISH: 7 Pay everybody what is due him: for whom it is the tax, the tax; for whom the tariff, the tariff; for whom fear, fear; for whom honor, honor.

EWE: 8 Miganyi naneke ƒe fe le ame aɖeke ŋu o, negbe mia nɔewo lɔlɔ̃ ƒe fe ko; elabena ame si lɔ̃a ehavi la, ewu se la nu.
ENGLISH: 8 Do not owe anybody anything, except to love each other; for he who loves the other has fulfilled the law.

EWE: 9 Elabena se la me nya siwo nye, "Mègawɔ ahasi o, Mègawu ame o, Mègafi fi o, Mègabiã ŋu o, " kpakple se bubu ɖe sia ɖe si li la, woƒo wo katã nu ƒu ɖe nya sia me be: "Lɔ̃ hawòvi abe wò ŋutɔ ɖokuiwò ene. " 10 Lɔlɔ̃ la mewɔa vɔ̃ ɖe ehavi ŋu o; eya ta lɔlɔ̃e nye sedziwɔwɔ.
ENGLISH: 9 For "You shall not commit adultery, " "You shall not murder, " "You shall not steal, " "You shall not covet, " and any other commandment, are summed up in this sentence, "You shall love your neighbor as yourself. " 10 Love does not do anything bad to a neighbor; so love is fulfillment of the law.

EWE: 11 Miwɔ esia hã, elabena mienya ɣeyiɣi si me míele la be, gaƒoƒo la de xoxo be mianyɔ tso alɔ̃ me, elabena míaƒe ɖeɖekpɔkpɔ gogo fifia wu ale si wònɔ esime míezu xɔsetɔwo la. 12 Zã do eteƒe didi; ŋu ƒe keke gogo.
ENGLISH: 11 And this knowing the crisis, that it is already time you woke up out of sleep, for salvation is nearer us now than when we first believed.

EWE: Eya ta mina míaɖe viviti me dɔwɔwɔwo ɖa, eye mina míado kekeli ƒe aʋawɔnuwo. 13 Mina míazɔ nyuie abe ale si dze le ŋkeke me ene; menye le kplɔ̃ɖoɖo siwo gbɔ eme kple ahamumuwo me o, menye le gbɔdɔdɔ manɔsenuwo kple ŋukpenanuwɔwɔ dzimesesẽtɔe me o, menye le dzrewɔwɔ kple ŋuʋaʋã me o. 14 Ke boŋ mido Aƒetɔ Yesu Kristo, eye miganɔ ɖoɖo wɔm ɖe kɔɖiɖi na ŋutilã ƒe nudzodzrowo ŋu o.
ENGLISH: 12 It is far on in the night, and day is almost here; so let us throw off the activities of darkness and put on the armor of light; 13 let us behave respectably, as in daylight, not with wild parties and getting drunk, not with sexualism and indecency, not with quarreling and jealousy; 14 but put on the Lord Jesus Christ and do not make arrangements for the flesh for gratifications.

EWE: Romatɔwo
ENGLISH: Romans

EWE: 2 Xɔse le ame aɖe si be wòaɖu nu sia nu, ke amagbewo koe ame si ƒe xɔse mesẽ ŋu o ya ɖuna. 3 Ame si ɖua nu sia nu faa la megado vlo ame si meɖua nu sia nu o la o, eye ame si meɖua nu sia nu o hã megadrɔ̃ ʋɔnu ame si ɖua nu sia nu o, elabena Mawu xɔ ame ma.
