ENGLISH: 32 Have nothing about you that either Jew or Greek or the church of God could stub their toes on, 33 in the same way as I am pleasing everybody about everything, not looking out for my own interests but for those of the many, that they may be saved.

EWE: 1 Korintotɔwo
ENGLISH: 1 Corinthians

EWE: 11 Mizu srɔ̃nyelawo, abe ale si nye hã menye Kristo srɔ̃la ene.
ENGLISH: 11 Be imitators of me in the same way as I am of Christ.

EWE: 2 Mele mia kafum, elabena mieɖoa ŋku dzinye le nuwo katã me, eye mielé ɖoɖoawo me ɖe asi goŋgoŋ abe ale si metsɔ wo de mia sii ene.
ENGLISH: 2 And I praise you that you thoroughly remember me and stick to the correct line as I passed it on to you.

EWE: 3 Ke medi be mianyae be ŋutsu sia ŋutsu ƒe tae nye Kristo; nyɔnu hã ƒe tae nye ŋutsu; eye Kristo hã ƒe tae nye Mawu.
ENGLISH: 3 But I want you to know that every man’s head is the Christ, and a woman’s head the man, and the Christ’s head God.

EWE: 4 Ŋutsu sia ŋutsu si tsyɔa nu ta hafi doa gbe ɖa alo gblɔa nya ɖi la, doa ŋukpe eƒe ta; 5 ke nyɔnu sia nyɔnu si metsyɔa nu ta hafi doa gbe ɖa alo gblɔa nya ɖi o la, doa ŋukpe eƒe ta, elabena ele ko abe nyɔnu si wolũ ta na ene.
ENGLISH: 4 Any man praying or prophesying with anything on his head is disgracing his head. 5 But a woman praying or prophesying with her head uncovered is disgracing her head, for it is one and the same thing as a shaved woman.

EWE: 6 Elabena ne nyɔnu aɖe metsyɔa nu ta o la, ekema nekpa ɖa boŋ; ke ne enye ŋukpe na nyɔnu aɖe be wòakpa ɖa alo alũ ta la, ekema netsyɔ nu ta.
ENGLISH: 6 For if a woman is not covered, let her have her hair cut too; but if having her hair cut or shaved is disgraceful for a woman, let her be covered.

EWE: 7 Ke medze be ŋutsu natsyɔ nu ta o, elabena Mawu ƒe nɔnɔme kple ŋutikɔkɔe wònye, ke nyɔnue nye ŋutsu ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe. 8 Elabena ŋutsu metso nyɔnu me o, nyɔnu boŋ ye tso ŋutsu me. 9 Eye womewɔ ŋutsu le nyɔnu ta hã o, nyɔnu boŋ ye wowɔ le ŋutsu ta.
ENGLISH: 7 For a man ought not to have his head covered, he being the image and glory of God; but woman is the glory of man, 8 for man does not have his being out of woman but woman out of man; 9 for, also, man was not created on account of the woman but a woman on account of the man.

EWE: 10 Esia tae wòle be ŋusẽ ƒe dzesi nanɔ ta na nyɔnu, le mawudɔlawo ta.
ENGLISH: 10 For this reason the woman ought to have a safeguard over her head because of the angels.

EWE: 11 Hekpe ɖe eŋu la, le Aƒetɔ la me la, nyɔnu meli ŋutsu manɔmee o, eye ŋutsu hã meli nyɔnu manɔmee o. 12 Elabena ale si ko nyɔnu tso ŋutsu me la, nenema kee ŋutsu hã to nyɔnu dzi va; ke nuwo katã tso Mawu me.
ENGLISH: 11 There is not in the Lord, though, woman apart from man nor man apart from woman; 12 for as the woman comes out of the man, so does the man too come through the woman; and everything comes out of God.

EWE: 13 Miawo ŋutɔwo mibu eŋu kpɔ: Ðe wòsɔ be nyɔnu nado gbe ɖa na Mawu ne metsyɔ nu ta oa? 14 Ðe miekpɔe be le dzɔdzɔme nu la, ne ɖa legbe le ta na ŋutsu la, enye ŋukpe nɛ, 15 ke ne ɖa legbe le ta na nyɔnu la, enye atsyɔ̃ nɛ oa? Elabena wotsɔ ɖa nɛ ɖe tatsyɔnu teƒe.
ENGLISH: 13 Judge in your own consciences: is it proper for a woman to pray uncovered to God? 14 Does not even nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair it is a dishonor to him, 15 but if a woman has long hair it is a glory to her, because she is given her hair to serve as a wrap?

EWE: 16 Gake ne ame aɖe le nya hem be ɖoɖo bubu aɖe li le nya sia ŋu la, bubu aɖeke mele mía si o, eye ɖeke mele Mawu ƒe hameawo hã si o.
ENGLISH: 16 But if anybody sees fit to be disputatious, we do not have such a custom, and neither do God’s churches.

EWE: 17 Ke le mɔfiame siwo gbɔna ŋu la, nyemele mia kafum o, elabena ne miekpe ta la, nuwo menyona ɖe edzi o, ɖe wogblẽna ɖe edzi boŋ. 18 Elabena gbã la, mese be ne mieva kpe ta le hamea me la, mamawo nɔa mia dome; eye mexɔ edzi se le go aɖe me. 19 Elabena kɔmamawo anɔ mia dome godoo, ale be ame siwo ŋu wokpɔ ŋudzedze ɖo la nadze ƒãa le mia dome.
ENGLISH: 17 But this injunction I give without praise for your way of coming together not for the better but for the worse: 18 for, in the first place, when you come together in a church meeting I hear there are divisions among you; and to some extent I believe it, 19 for there do have to be factions among you in order that it may become apparent among you which ones are of the right kind.

EWE: 20 Eya ta ne mieva kpe ta la, menye Aƒetɔ ƒe Fiẽnuɖuɖu lae mieɖuna o. 21 Elabena ne eɖo edzi be miaɖui la, mia dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe ɖua eya ŋutɔ ƒe fiẽnuɖuɖu doa ŋgɔ, ale be dɔ nɔa ame aɖewo wum, evɔ ame bubuwo ya mua aha.
ENGLISH: 20 So when you meet together there is no eating a supper of the Lord’s, 21 for each one is getting a start in the eating to take his own supper, and one goes hungry and another has had too much drink.

EWE: 22 Ðe aƒewo mele mia si be miaɖu nu ahano nu le wo me oa?
ENGLISH: 22 Why, have you no houses for eating and drinking? or are you despising the church of God and shaming those who have nothing?

EWE: Alo ɖe miedoa vlo Mawu ƒe hame la, eye miedoa ŋukpe ame siwo si naneke mele o laa?
ENGLISH: What am I to say to you? am I to praise you over this?

EWE: Makafu mia?
ENGLISH: I do not.

EWE: Nyemele mia kafum le nu sia me o. 23 Elabena nu si mexɔ tso Aƒetɔ la gbɔ lae metsɔ de asi na mi, be le zã si me woade Aƒetɔ Yesu asi la, etsɔ abolo, 24 eye esi wòda akpe ɖe eta vɔ la, eŋe eme gblɔ be: "Esia le tsitre ɖi na nye ŋutilã si wotsɔ na ɖe mia ta. Minɔ esia wɔm hena ŋkuɖoɖo dzinye. " 25 Nenema kee wòtsɔ kplu la hã le fiẽnuɖuɖu la megbe gblɔ be: "Kplu sia le tsitre ɖi na nubabla yeye si wowɔ to nye ʋu dzi la. Minɔ esia wɔm, ɣesiaɣi si mianoe, hena ŋkuɖoɖo dzinye. " 26 Elabena ɣesiaɣi si mieɖua abolo sia henoa nu le kplu sia nu la, miele gbeƒã ɖem Aƒetɔ la ƒe ku va se ɖe esime wòava.
ENGLISH: 23 For I received from the Lord that same thing that I handed on to you, that the Lord Jesus, on the night when he was to be arrested, took bread 24 and gave thanks and broke it and said "This is my body that goes for you; do this in remembrance of me "; 25 in the same way the cup too, after eating the supper, saying "This cup is the new covenant in my blood; do this, as often as you drink, in remembrance of me. " 26 For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you are announcing the death of the Lord, until he come.

EWE: 27 Eya ta ame sia ame si ɖua abolo la, alo noa nu le Aƒetɔ la ƒe kplu la nu madzemadzee la, aɖi fɔ le Aƒetɔ la ƒe ŋutilã kple eƒe ʋu ŋu.
ENGLISH: 27 Consequently one who eats the Lord’s bread or drinks his cup in unworthy fashion will be liable for the body and blood of the Lord.

EWE: 28 Ele be ame nadzro eɖokui me kpɔ nyuie gbã be yedze hã, ema ko hafi wòaɖu abolo la ƒe ɖe ahano nu le kplu la nu. 29 Elabena ame si medzro nu si ŋutilã la fia me kpɔ nyuie hafi ɖunɛ alo nonɛ o la, eɖua ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃ henoa ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃ na eɖokui.
ENGLISH: 28 But let a man see how he is to be rated, and in such fashion eat from the loaf and drink from the cup; 29 for he who eats and drinks is eating and drinking a judgment upon himself when he does not distinguish the body.

EWE: 30 Esia tae mia dometɔ geɖewo gbɔdzɔ, eye wodze dɔ, eye geɖewo hã le alɔ̃ dɔm le ku me.
ENGLISH: 30 That is why there are among you many weakly and sick, and a number have gone to their rest.

EWE: 31 Ke ne míedzro mía ɖokui me kpɔ nyuie la, womadrɔ̃ ʋɔnu mí o. 32 Gake ne wodrɔ̃ ʋɔnu mí la, Yehowae le mía ɖɔm ɖo, ale be woagabu fɔ mí kpe ɖe xexea ŋu o.
ENGLISH: 31 But if we saw how we stood, we should not be judged; 32 but in being judged we are being disciplined by the Lord, in order that we may not be condemned with the world.

EWE: 33 Eya ta nɔvinyewo, ne mieva kpe ta be yewoaɖui la, milala mia nɔewo.
ENGLISH: 33 Consequently, my brothers, when you come together to eat wait for each other.

EWE: 34 Ne dɔ le ame aɖe wum la, neɖu nu le aƒe me, ale be ne mieva kpe ta la, woagadrɔ̃ ʋɔnu mi o.
ENGLISH: 34 If anybody is hungry let him eat at home, in order that your coming together may not run you into judgment.

EWE: Ke ne meva ɖo mia gbɔ hã la, makpɔ nya susɔeawo gbɔ.
ENGLISH: And as to the rest I will give directions when I shall come.

EWE: 1 Korintotɔwo
ENGLISH: 1 Corinthians

EWE: 12 Ke le gbɔgbɔmenunanawo ŋu la, nɔviwo, nyemedi be wòanɔ manyamanya na mi o.
ENGLISH: 12 And about the workings of the Spirit, brothers, I do not wish you to be ignorant.

EWE: 2 Mienyae be esime mienye dukɔwo me tɔwo la, woflu mi kplɔ mi trae yi legba maƒonuwo gbɔ, eye mienɔa wo yome yia afi sia afi.
ENGLISH: 2 You know when you were heathen you were carried away to the voiceless idols, however it was done.

EWE: 3 Eya ta medi be mianyae be, ame aɖeke meƒoa nu to Mawu ƒe gbɔgbɔ dzi gblɔna be, "Yesu nye fiƒodeme! " o, eye ame aɖeke mate ŋu agblɔ be, "Yesu nye Aƒetɔ! " o, negbe to gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔe dzi ko.
ENGLISH: 3 For this reason I make it known to you that nobody speaking in the Spirit of God says "Jesus is accursed, " and nobody can say "Jesus is Lord " except in Holy Spirit.

EWE: 4 Ke nunana vovovowoe li, gake gbɔgbɔ ɖeka ma ke koe; 5 eye subɔsubɔdɔ vovovowoe li, gake Aƒetɔ ɖeka ma ke koe; 6 eye dɔ vovovowoe li, gake Mawu ɖeka ma kee wɔa dɔawo katã to amewo katã dzi.
ENGLISH: 4 But there are different lines of gifts, but the same Spirit; 5 and there are different lines of service and the same Lord; 6 and there are different lines of divine workings and the same God, he who works everything in everybody.

EWE: 7 Ke gbɔgbɔ la dzena wokpɔna le ame sia ame me hena taɖodzinu si ŋu viɖe le.
ENGLISH: 7 But each one is given such a manifestation of the Spirit as will be advantageous.

EWE: 8 Elabena woto gbɔgbɔ la dzi na ale si woaƒo nu nunyatɔe la ame aɖe, eye woto gbɔgbɔ ma ke dzi na nuƒoƒo ŋuti sidzedze ame bubu, 9 woto gbɔgbɔ ma ke dzi na xɔse ame bubu, eye woto gbɔgbɔ ɖeka ma ke dzi na dɔdada ƒe nunana ame bubu, 10 eye wona ŋusẽdɔwo wɔwɔ ame bubu hã, wona nyagbɔgblɔɖi ame bubu, wona nya siwo tso gbɔgbɔ me la gɔme sese ame bubu, wona gbe bubuwo dodo ame bubu, eye wona gbewo gɔme ɖeɖe ame bubu.
ENGLISH: 8 For one through the Spirit is given words of wisdom, and another words of knowledge after the same Spirit, 9 somebody else faith, in the same Spirit, and another gifts of healing, in the one Spirit, 10 and another miracle-workings, another prophecy, another discrimination between spirits, somebody else different kinds of languages, and another the translating of languages.

EWE: 11 Ke gbɔgbɔ ɖeka ma kee wɔa dɔ siawo katã, eye wòmaa wo na ame sia ame ale si wòlɔ̃.
ENGLISH: 11 But in all these one and the same Spirit is at work, distributing to each individually as it wishes.

EWE: 12 Ale si ko ametia nye nu ɖeka gake ŋutinu geɖewo le eŋu, eye ameti ma ƒe ŋutinuwo sɔ gbɔ gake woƒo ƒu wɔ ameti ɖeka la, nenema kee Kristo la hã le. 13 Elabena gbɔgbɔ ɖeka me woto nyrɔ mí katã ɖe ŋutilã ɖeka me, míeɖanye Yudatɔwo alo Helatɔwo o, míeɖanye kluviwo alo ablɔɖemewo o, eye wona mí katã míeno gbɔgbɔ ɖeka.
ENGLISH: 12 For just as the body is one and has many organs, but all the organs of the body, many as they are, are one body, so it is with the Christ; 13 for we too were all baptized in one Spirit into one body, be we Jews or Greeks, be we slaves or freemen, and were all given one Spirit to drink in.

EWE: 14 Le nyateƒe me la, ametia menye ŋutinu ɖeka o, ke boŋ ŋutinu geɖewoe.
ENGLISH: 14 For neither is the body one organ, but many.

EWE: 15 Ne afɔ agblɔ be, "Esi nyemenye asi o ta la, nyemenye ametia ƒe akpa aɖeke o " la, ema mewɔe be meganye ametia ƒe akpa aɖeke o. 16 Eye ne to agblɔ be, "Esi nyemenye ŋku o ta la, nyemenye ametia ƒe akpa aɖeke o " la, ema mewɔe be meganye ametia ƒe akpa aɖeke o.
ENGLISH: 15 If the foot says "Because I am not a hand I am no part of the body " it is not on that account no part of the body, 16 and if the ear says "Because I am not an eye I am no part of the body " it is not on that account no part of the body.

EWE: Ne wo katã nye nusese ɖe, ekema afi kae nuʋeʋẽse anɔ? 18 Ke Mawu ɖo ŋutinuawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe wo teƒe le ametia ŋu abe ale si wòdi ene. 19 Ne wo katã nye ŋutinu ɖeka ɖe, ekema afi kae ametia anɔ? 20 Ke azɔ wonye ŋutinu geɖewo, gake ameti ɖeka.
ENGLISH: 17 If the body were wholly eye, where would be the hearing? if wholly ear, where the smelling? 18 But now God did put the organs each one of them in the body as he chose; 19 and if all were one organ, where would be the body? 20 but now there are many organs but one body.

EWE: 21 Ŋku mate ŋu agblɔ na asi be, "Nyemehiã wò o "; eye ta hã mate ŋu agblɔ na afɔwo be, "Nyemehiã mi o. " 22 Ke boŋ ametia ƒe ŋutinu siwo dze abe ɖe wogbɔdzɔ wu ene la hiã vevie, 23 eye ametia ƒe akpa siwo míesusuna be bubu boo aɖeke mele wo ŋu o la, woawo ŋue míedea bubui wu, ale ŋutinu siwo menya kpɔ o la ŋue míetrɔa asi le nyuie wu, 24 evɔ ŋutinu siwo nya kpɔ la mehiã naneke o.
ENGLISH: 21 And the eye cannot say to the hand "I have no need of you, " or again the head to the feet "I have no need of you, " 22 but, much rather, what seem to be weak organs of the body are necessary, 23 and it is just what we think are less honorable parts of the body that we invest with special honor, and the indecorous parts of us have special decorum, 24 but the decorous parts of us stand in no need.

EWE: Gake Mawu fɔ ametia ƒe ŋutinuwo kpe, eye wòna bubu geɖe akpa siwo hiã bubu la, 25 ale be mama aɖeke naganɔ ametia me o, ke boŋ ŋutinuawo nalé be na wo nɔewo sɔsɔe. 26 Eye ne ŋutinu ɖeka le fu kpem la, ŋutinu bubuawo katã kpea fu kplii; alo ne wodo ŋutinu ɖeka ɖe dzi la, ŋutinu bubuawo katã kpɔa dzidzɔ kplii.
ENGLISH: But God commingled the body, giving special honor to what came short, 25 in order that there might not be division in the body, but the organs might feel the same solicitude for each other; 26 and be it that one organ suffers, all the organs suffer with it; be it that one organ is decorated, all the organs rejoice with it.

EWE: 27 Ke miawoe nye Kristo ƒe ŋutilã, eye mia dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe nye ŋutinuawo dometɔ aɖe. 28 Eye Mawu de dɔ asi na ame vovovowo le hamea me: gbã la, apostolowo; evelia nyagblɔɖilawo; etɔ̃lia nufialawo; emegbe ŋusẽdɔwɔwɔwo; dɔdada ƒe nunana; kpekpeɖeŋunadɔwo; mɔfiafiaŋutetewo; gbe bubuwo dodo. 29 Amewo katãe nye apostolowoa? Amewo katãe nye nyagblɔɖilawoa?
ENGLISH: 27 And you are Christ’s body, and, individually, organs; 28 and in the church God has put some, first, as apostles; secondly, as prophets; thirdly, as teachers; then miracles, then gifts of healing, assistance, management, different kinds of languages.

EWE: Amewo katãe nye nufialawoa? Amewo katãe wɔa ŋusẽdɔwoa? 30 Amewo katã sie dɔdada ƒe nunanawo lea? Amewo katãe ƒoa nu le gbegbɔgblɔ bubuwo mea?
ENGLISH: 29 Are all apostles? are all prophets? are all teachers? do all work miracles? 30 do all have gifts of healing? do all speak languages? do all translate?

EWE: Amewo katãe nye nyagɔmeɖelawoa? 31 Ke miyi edzi mianɔ nunana siwo lolo wu la dim vevie.
ENGLISH: 31 But aspire to the greater gifts.

EWE: Ke azɔ mafia mɔ aɖe si de ŋgɔ wu la mi.
ENGLISH: And let me point out to you an even preeminent course.

EWE: 1 Korintotɔwo
ENGLISH: 1 Corinthians

EWE: 2 Ne nyagblɔɖi ƒe nunana le asinye, eye menya nya ɣaɣla kɔkɔewo katã kple sidzedzewo katã, eye xɔse le asinye ale gbegbe be mate ŋu aho towo, gake lɔlɔ̃ mele asinye o la, nyemenye naneke o. 3 Eye ne metsɔ nye nunɔamesiwo katã na be woatsɔ anyi ame bubuwo, eye metsɔ nye ametia na, ale be maƒo adegbe, gake lɔlɔ̃ mele asinye o la, meɖe vi aɖeke kura nam o. 4 Lɔlɔ̃ gbɔa dzi blewu, eye wònyoa dɔme. Lɔlɔ̃ meʋãa ŋu o. Meƒoa adegbe o, medoa eɖokui ɖe dzi glodzoo o, 5 mewɔa nu si medze o, media eya ŋutɔ tɔ o, mebia dzi o.
ENGLISH: 13 If I speak the languages of men and angels but do not have love, I turn into a gong sounding or a cymbal clashing; 2 and if I have prophecy and know all secrets and all knowledge, and if I have all faith so as to move mountains, but do not have love, I am nothing; 3 and if I give all my possessions in charity, and if I give up my body in order to boast, but do not have love, I am none the better.

EWE: Meléa vɔ̃ siwo wowɔ ɖe eŋu la ɖi o. 6 Mekpɔa dzidzɔ ɖe nu madzɔmadzɔ ŋu o, ke ekpɔa dzidzɔ ɖe nyateƒe boŋ ŋu. 7 Enɔa te ɖe nuwo katã nu, exɔa nuwo katã dzi sena, ekpɔa mɔ na nuwo katã, edoa dzi le nuwo katã me. 8 Lɔlɔ̃ nu metsina gbeɖe o.
ENGLISH: 4 Love is patient, kind; love is not jealous; love does not show off, does not get inflated, 5 does not shock people, does not look out for its own interests, does not get provoked, does not count its injuries, 6 is not glad at a wrong deed but glad to have the truth made glad, 7 stands everything, believes everything, hopes everything, holds out through everything.

EWE: Ke ne nyagbɔgblɔɖi ƒe nunanawo li la, woava ɖe wo ɖa; ne gbegbɔgblɔ bubuwo gbɔgblɔ li la, woadzudzɔ; ne sidzedze li la, woava ɖee ɖa. 9 Elabena sidzedze afãafã ye le mía si, eye míegblɔa nya ɖi afãafã, 10 ke ne nu si le blibo la va ɖo la, woaɖe nu afãafã la ɖa.
ENGLISH: 8 Love never drops away; but as for prophecies they will be superseded, as for languages they will come to a stop, as for knowledge it will be superseded; 9 for it is in part that we know and in part that we prophesy, 10 but when the complete comes the partial will be superseded.

EWE: 11 Esime menye ɖevi la, meƒoa nu abe ɖevi ene, mebua tame abe ɖevi ene, mebua nuwo ŋu abe ɖevi ene; ke azɔ esi metsi la, meɖe asi le ɖevimenuwo ŋu.
ENGLISH: 11 When I was a child I used a child’s language, took a child’s views, made a child’s calculations; since I have become a man I have superseded the child’s ways.

EWE: 12 Elabena fifia la, míekpɔa nu flukpee to gahuhɔ̃e aɖe me, ke ɣemaɣi la, anye ŋkume kple ŋkume. Fifia la, menya nu afãafã, ke ɣemaɣi la, manya nu sia nu nyuie abe ale si wonyam nyuie ene.
ENGLISH: 12 For we see now by a mirror, as a puzzle to be guessed at, but then face to face; now I know in part, but then I shall be aware in the same way as he was aware of me.

EWE: 13 Ke azɔ la, nu etɔ̃ siawoe kpɔtɔ li: xɔse, mɔkpɔkpɔ, lɔlɔ̃; ke esi ƒo wo tae nye lɔlɔ̃.
ENGLISH: 13 And now there remain faith, hope, love these three. And greatest of these is love.

EWE: 1 Korintotɔwo
ENGLISH: 1 Corinthians

EWE: 14 Miti lɔlɔ̃ yome, ke minɔ gbɔgbɔmenunanawo dim vevie, gake vevietɔ la, be miagblɔ nya ɖi.
ENGLISH: 14 Aim at love; but aspire to the manifestations of the Spirit, but preferably that you should prophesy.

EWE: 2 Elabena ame si tsɔa gbegbɔgblɔ bubu ƒoa nu la, menye amewoe wòƒoa nu na o, ke boŋ Mawue, elabena ame aɖeke mesenɛ o, ke boŋ egblɔa nya ɣaɣla kɔkɔewo to gbɔgbɔ la dzi. 3 Ke ame si gblɔa nya ɖi la tua ame ɖo, eye wòdea dzi ƒo na ame hefaa akɔ na amewo to eƒe nuƒoƒo dzi.
ENGLISH: 2 For he who speaks a language is speaking not to men but to God, for nobody understands, but in spirit he is speaking secrets; 3 but he who prophesies is speaking upbuilding and exhortation and comfort for men.

EWE: 4 Ame si tsɔa gbegbɔgblɔ bubu ƒoa nu la tua eya ŋutɔ ɖokui ɖo, ke ame si gblɔa nya ɖi la tua hame la ɖo.
ENGLISH: 4 He who speaks a language is building himself up; but he who prophesies is building up the church.

EWE: 5 Ðe madi be mi katã miado gbegbɔgblɔ bubuwo hafi, ke medi be miagblɔ nya ɖi boŋ. Le nyateƒe me la, ame si gblɔa nya ɖi la de ŋgɔ wu ame si tsɔa gbegbɔgblɔ bubuwo ƒoa nui, negbe ɖe wòɖe egɔme, ale be wòatu hamea ɖo.
ENGLISH: 5 And I want to have you all speak languages, but preferably to have you prophesy; and he who prophesies is superior to him who speaks languages, except in case he translates so that the church may get an upbuilding.

EWE: Ke ne metsɔ nyaɖeɖefia alo sidzedze alo nyagbɔgblɔɖi alo nufiafia boŋ ƒo nu na mi la, ɖe maɖe vi wu oa? 7 Nenemae wòle le nu siwo me agbe mele o la ƒe ɖiɖime gome, eɖanye dze alo saŋku o. Ne woƒe ɖiɖi meto vovo o ɖe, aleke woawɔ anya nu si kum dze la le alo nu si ƒom saŋku la le? 8 Elabena ne kpẽ ƒe ɖiɖime mekɔ nyuie o ɖe, ame kae adzra ɖo ɖe aʋa ŋu? 9 Nenema kee miawo hã, ne mietsɔa aɖe gblɔa nya siwo gɔme anya se bɔbɔe o ɖe, aleke ame awɔ anya nya si gblɔm miele?
ENGLISH: 6 And now, brothers, if I come to you speaking languages what good shall I do you unless I speak to you either in revelation or in knowledge or in prophecy or teaching? 7 It is the same with lifeless sound-producers: be it flute or be it harp, if it does not make a distinction in the notes how will the tune that is being played be known? 8 For, again, if a trumpet makes an unclear sound, who will get ready for war? 9 So with you too: if by your tongues you do not produce plain speech, how will the meaning that is being spoken be known? for you will be talking into the air.

EWE: Le nyateƒe me la, anye nuƒoƒo ɖe yame. 10 Anye be gbegbɔgblɔ vovovowo le xexea me, gake wo dometɔ aɖeke meli, si ŋu gɔmesese mele o. 11 Elabena ne nyemese nya si wogblɔ la gɔme o la, ekema mezu dutagbedola na ame si le nu ƒom, eye ame si le nu ƒom hã zu dutagbedola nam.
ENGLISH: 10 There are so many kinds, say, of sounds in the world, and none unvocal; if, then, 11 I do not know the force of the sound, I shall be senseless to the speaker and the speaker senseless to me.

EWE: 12 Eya ta miawo hã, esi miele gbɔgbɔ la ƒe nunanawo dim vevie ta la, midze agbagba miagba go le nunana siwo atu hamea ɖo la me.
ENGLISH: 12 In the same way you: since you are aspirants to spirit-gifts, try to excel for the upbuilding of the church.

EWE: 13 Eya ta ame si tsɔa gbegbɔgblɔ bubu ƒoa nu la nedo gbe ɖa be yeate ŋu aɖe egɔme.
ENGLISH: 13 Wherefore, let him who speaks a language pray that he may translate.

EWE: 14 Elabena ne metsɔa gbegbɔgblɔ bubu doa gbe ɖae la, gbɔgbɔ ƒe nunana si le asinye lae le gbea dom ɖa, ke nye susu ya meɖe vi aɖeke o.
ENGLISH: 14 For if I pray in a language, my spirit is praying but my mind is not fruiting.

EWE: 15 Ekema nu kae mawɔ?
ENGLISH: 15 So what is the thing to do?

EWE: Matsɔ gbɔgbɔ ƒe nunana la ado gbe ɖa, eye magatsɔ nye susu hã ado gbe ɖa. Matsɔ gbɔgbɔ ƒe nunana la adzi kafukafuha, eye magatsɔ nye susu hã adzi kafukafuha.
ENGLISH: I will pray with the spirit, and I will pray with the mind too; I will sing with the spirit, and I will sing with the mind too.

EWE: 16 Ne menye nenema o la, ne ètsɔa gbɔgbɔ ƒe nunana la gblɔa kafukafunyawo ɖe, aleke ame tsɛ si le mia dome la ate ŋu agblɔ "Amen " ɖe wò akpedada dzi, esi menya nya si gblɔm nèle o? 17 Nyateƒee, èdaa akpe le mɔ nyui nu, gake metua ame kemɛa ɖo o.
ENGLISH: 16 Since if you bless in spirit, how is he who occupies the commoner’s place to say the Amen to your thanks, since he does not know what you are saying? 17 you are giving thanks well, but the other man is not being built up.

EWE: 18 Medaa akpe na Mawu be metsɔa gbegbɔgblɔ bubuwo ƒoa nui wu mi katã. 19 Gake madi be matsɔ nye susu agblɔ nya atɔ̃ le hamea me, ale be mafia nu ame bubuwo hã, wu be magblɔ nya akpe ewo le gbegbɔgblɔ bubu me.
ENGLISH: 18 I thank God, I speak languages more freely than any of you; 19 but in meeting I had rather speak five sentences with my mind, in order to enlighten others too, than ten thousand sentences in a language.

EWE: 20 Nɔviwo, miganye ɖevi suewo le nugɔmesese me o, ke boŋ minye ɖevi suewo le nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ me; ke mizu ame siwo tsi bliboe le nugɔmesese me.
ENGLISH: 20 Brothers, do not be children in intelligence; as to viciousness do be childlike, but in intelligence be adult.

EWE: 21 Woŋlɔ ɖe Se la me be: "‘Dutagbedolawo ƒe aɖe kple du bubu me tɔwo ƒe nuyiwo matsɔ aƒo nu na dukɔ sia, ke hã, woagbe toɖoɖom,’ Yehowa ye gblɔe. " 22 Eya ta gbegbɔgblɔ bubuwo dodo menye dzesi na xɔsetɔwo o, ke boŋ na dzimaxɔsetɔwo, eye nyagbɔgblɔɖi meli na dzimaxɔsetɔwo o, ke boŋ na xɔsetɔwo.
ENGLISH: 21 In the law it stands written "By men of alien language and by alien lips I will speak to this people, and not even so will they listen to me, says the Lord. " 22 Consequently languages are for a token not to believers but to unbelievers, but prophecy not to unbelievers but to believers.

EWE: 23 Eya ta ne hame blibo la katã va kpe ta ɖe afi ɖeka, eye wo katã wotsɔ gbegbɔgblɔ bubuwo le nu ƒom, eye ame tsɛwo alo dzimaxɔsetɔwo va la, ɖe womagblɔ be miaƒe tagbɔe le gbegblẽm oa? 24 Ke ne mi katã miele nya gblɔm ɖi, eye dzimaxɔsetɔ aɖe alo ame tsɛ aɖe va la, ekema miaƒe nyawo katã azu mokaka nɛ, eye wòatsɔ wo adzro eɖokui me. 25 Eƒe dzimenya ɣaɣlawo adze ƒãa, ale be wòatsyɔ mo anyi ade ta agu na Mawu agblɔ be: "Mawu le mia dome vavã. "
ENGLISH: 23 If then the whole church meets together and all are speaking languages, and commoners or unbelievers come in, will they not say you are crazy? 24 But if all are prophesying, and some unbeliever or commoner comes in, he is reproved by all, he is put through an examination by all, 25 the things hidden in his heart come out; and thus he will throw himself down on his face and do reverence to God, declaring that God really is among you.

EWE: 26 Ekema nɔviwo, nu kae miawɔ?
ENGLISH: 26 So what is the thing to do, brothers?

EWE: Miwɔ nuwo katã hena tutuɖo. 27 Eye ne ame aɖe tsɔa gbegbɔgblɔ bubu ƒoa nu la, ke woanye ame eve alo ne ede ƒãa la, ame etɔ̃, eye woaƒo nu ɖekaɖeka, eye ame aɖe naɖe egɔme. 28 Ke ne gbegɔmeɖela aɖeke meli o la, nezi ɖoɖoe le hame la me, eye wòaƒo nu na eɖokui kple Mawu.
ENGLISH: When you come together, each has a psalm, has a teaching, has a revelation, has a language, has a translation let everything be so done as to build up: 27 suppose somebody is speaking a language, let it be done by twos or at most threes, and one after another, and one translate; 28 but if there is no translator, let him keep silence in meeting, and speak to himself and to God.

EWE: 29 Nyagblɔɖila eve alo etɔ̃ ko naƒo nu, eye ame bubuwo nadi egɔmesese. 30 Ke ne woɖe nane fia ame bubu aɖe si nɔ anyi ɖe afi ma la, ke ame gbãtɔ si le nu ƒom la nazi ɖoɖoe.
ENGLISH: 29 And of prophets let two or three speak and the others assess; 30 but if a revelation comes to another who is in the seats, let the first keep silence.

EWE: 31 Elabena mi katã miate ŋu agblɔ nya ɖi ɖekaɖeka, ale be ame sia ame nasrɔ̃ nane, eye wòade dzi ƒo nɛ. 32 Eye nyagblɔɖilawo nakpɔ egbɔ be wozã gbɔgbɔ ƒe nunana la le ɖoɖo nu. 33 Elabena Mawu menye nyamanyamawɔwɔ ƒe Mawu o, ke ŋutifafa ƒe Mawu boŋ.
ENGLISH: 31 For you can all prophesy one at a time, in order that all may learn and all receive exhortation; 32 and prophets’ spirits subordinate themselves to prophets, 33 for God is not a God of disorder but of peace.

EWE: Abe ale si wòle le ame kɔkɔewo ƒe hamewo katã me ene la, 34 nyɔnuwo nazi ɖoɖoe le hameawo me, elabena womeɖe mɔ na wo be woaƒo nu o. Ke boŋ woabɔbɔ wo ɖokuiwo, abe ale si Se la hã gblɔe ene.
ENGLISH: As in all meetings of God’s people, 34 let the women keep silence in the meetings; for it is not permissible for them to speak, but let them subordinate themselves, as the law too says.

EWE: 35 Ke ne wodi be yewoasrɔ̃ nane la, woabia wo srɔ̃wo le aƒe me, elabena enye ŋukpe be nyɔnu naƒo nu le hamea me.
ENGLISH: 35 But if they wish to find out something, let them put questions to their husbands at home; for it is disgraceful for a woman to speak in meeting.

EWE: 36 Mia gbɔe Mawu ƒe nya la dzɔ tsoa, alo miawo ɖeɖe gbɔ koe wòɖoa? 37 Ne ame aɖe susu be yenye nyagblɔɖila alo be wona gbɔgbɔ ƒe nunana ye la, ekema nelɔ̃ ɖe edzi be nya siwo ŋlɔm mele na mi la nye Aƒetɔ la ƒe sedede. 38 Ke ne ame aɖe metsɔ ɖe le eme o la, ekema womatsɔ ɖe le eya hã me o.
ENGLISH: 36 Or was it from you that the word of God started, or did it arrive at you alone? 37 If anybody is supposed to be a prophet or gifted with the Spirit, let him recognize what I am writing to you as being a commandment of the Lord; 38 but if somebody discredits it, discredit that.

EWE: 39 Eya ta nɔvinyewo, miyi edzi mianɔ nyagbɔgblɔɖi ƒe nunana la dim vevie, gake migade se ɖe gbegbɔgblɔ bubuwo dodo nu o. 40 Ke mina nuwo katã nayi edzi nyuie ɖe ɖoɖo nu.
ENGLISH: 39 Consequently, brothers, aspire to prophesying, and do not bar speaking languages; 40 but let everything be done in a respectable and orderly way.

EWE: 1 Korintotɔwo
ENGLISH: 1 Corinthians

EWE: 15 Ke nɔviwo, mele ŋku ɖom nya nyui si megblɔ na mi, si hã miexɔ helé eme ɖe asi sesĩe la dzi na mi. 2 Miakpɔ ɖeɖe hã ne mielé nya nyui si megblɔ na mi la me ɖe asi sesĩe ko, negbe ɖe mieva zu xɔsetɔwo dzodzro. 3 Elabena nu gbãtɔ siwo metsɔ de asi na mi lae nye nu siwo nye hã mexɔ, be Kristo ku ɖe míaƒe nu vɔ̃wo ta le Ŋɔŋlɔawo nu; 4 eye woɖii, ɛ̃, wofɔe ɖe tsitre le ŋkeke etɔ̃a gbe le Ŋɔŋlɔawo nu; 5 eye eɖe eɖokui fia Kefas, emegbe la, Ame Wuieveawo. 6 Le ema megbe la, eɖe eɖokui fia nɔvi siwo wu alafa atɔ̃ zi ɖeka, ame siwo dometɔ akpa gãtɔ kpɔtɔ le mía dome, ke wo dometɔ aɖewo hã dɔ alɔ̃ le ku me. 7 Emegbe eɖe eɖokui fia Yakobo, eyome eɖe ɖokui fia apostoloawo katã.
ENGLISH: 15 But, brothers, let me make you acquainted with the gospel I preached to you, the same that you received, the same that you stand on, 2 the same that you are saved by, in what terms I preached it to you, if you are holding to it except in case you believed for nothing! 3 For I handed on to you as a foremost thing the same thing I received, that Christ died for our sins in accordance with scripture, 4 and that he was buried, and that he rose the third day in accordance with scripture, 5 and that he appeared to Cephas, then to the Twelve; 6 then he appeared to above five hundred brothers at a time, of whom the majority are with us until now, but some have gone to their rest; 7 then he appeared to James, then to all the apostles; 8 and last of all, as it were to the runt born by abortion, he appeared to me too.

EWE: 8 Ke mlɔeba eɖe eɖokui fia nye hã, abe ame si ƒe ŋkeke mede hafi wodzii o ene. 9 Nyee nye suetɔ le apostoloawo dome, eye nyemedze woayɔ be apostolo o, elabena meti Mawu ƒe hame la yome. 10 Ke le Mawu ƒe amenuveve me la, mezu nu si menye egbea.
ENGLISH: 9 For I am the most insignificant of the apostles, not fit to be called an apostle, because I persecuted God’s church; 10 but by the grace of God I am what I am, and his grace to me was not a failure, but I out-toiled all of them yet not I, but God’s grace with me.

EWE: 11 Gake eɖanye nyee o, eɖanye woawoe o, nu siae míeɖea gbeƒãe, eye nu siae na mieva xɔe se.
ENGLISH: 11 So, be it I or they, we preach that way and you believed that way.

EWE: 12 Ke ne wole gbeƒã ɖem be wofɔ Kristo ɖe tsitre tso ame kukuwo dome la, aleke wɔ mia dometɔ aɖewo le gbɔgblɔm be ame kukuwo ƒe tsitretsitsi aɖeke meli o? 13 Ne vavãe ame kukuwo ƒe tsitretsitsi aɖeke meli o la, ekema womefɔ Kristo ɖe tsitre o. 14 Ke ne womefɔ Kristo ɖe tsitre o la, ekema míaƒe gbeƒãɖeɖe la nye dzodzro nyateƒe, eye miaƒe xɔse hã nye dzodzro. 15 Azɔ hã, woakpɔ mí be míenye aʋatsoɖasefowo ɖe Mawu ŋu elabena míeɖia ɖase tsia tsitre ɖe Mawu ŋuti be efɔ Kristo la ɖe tsitre, evɔ ne vavãe womefɔa ame kukuwo ɖe tsitre o la, ekema mefɔe ɖe tsitre hafi o. 16 Elabena ne womafɔ ame kukuwo ɖe tsitre o la, ekema womefɔ Kristo hã ɖe tsitre o.
ENGLISH: 12 But if Christ is preached to have risen from the dead, how do some among you say there is no such thing as resurrection of the dead? 13 But if there is no such thing as resurrection of the dead, not even Christ has risen; 14 and if Christ has not risen, then our preaching has nothing in it, your faith has nothing in it either, 15 and into the bargain we are found to be false witnesses against God, because we testified as to God that he raised the Christ, whom he did not raise if we are to take it that the dead do not rise.

EWE: 17 Eye ne womefɔ Kristo ɖe tsitre o la, ekema viɖe aɖeke mele miaƒe xɔse la ŋu o; miegakpɔtɔ le miaƒe nu vɔ̃wo me.
ENGLISH: 16 For if the dead do not rise, not even Christ has risen; 17 and if Christ has not risen, your faith is futile, you are still in your sins.

EWE: 18 Ekema ame siwo dɔ alɔ̃ le ku me le Kristo me hã tsrɔ̃.
ENGLISH: 18 Then those who have gone to their rest in Christ perished too.

EWE: 19 Ne agbe sia ɖeɖe ko mee míekpɔ mɔ na Kristo le la, ekema míaƒe nue wɔ nublanui wu.
ENGLISH: 19 If we are hoping in Christ in this life only, we are most pitiable of all men.

EWE: 20 Gake azɔ wofɔ Kristo ɖe tsitre tso ame kukuwo dome, eye wònye ame siwo dɔ alɔ̃ le ku me la ƒe kutsetse gbãtɔ.
ENGLISH: 20 But now Christ has risen from the dead, first to come in of those who have gone to their rest.

EWE: 21 Elabena esi wònye ame dzie ku to va ta la, ame kukuwo ƒe tsitretsitsi la hã to ame dzi va.
ENGLISH: 21 For since death came through a man, resurrection of the dead came through a man too.

EWE: 22 Elabena ale si ko amewo katã kuna le Adam me la, nenema kee woagbɔ agbe wo katã hã le Kristo me. 23 Ke ame sia ame le eƒe ɖoɖo nu: Kristoe nye kutsetse gbãtɔ, emegbe la, ame siwo nye Kristo la tɔ le eƒe anyinɔɣi la. 24 Azɔ nuwuwu la ava, esime wòatsɔ Fiaɖuƒe la ade asi na eƒe Mawu, si nye Fofoa, ne eɖe dziɖuɖu katã kple amegãnyenye katã kpakple ŋusẽ katã ɖa vɔ. 25 Elabena ele be wòaɖu fia va se ɖe esime Mawu natsɔ futɔwo katã ade eƒe afɔ te.
ENGLISH: 22 For as by Adam all are dying, so too by the Christ all are going to be brought to life, 23 but each when his turn comes: Christ the first to come in; then those who belong to Christ, at his coming; 24 then the end, when he hands the empire over to God the Father, when he has superseded every government and every authority and power, 25 for he has to reign "until he has put all enemies under his feet. " 26 Last of the enemies death is superseded.

EWE: 26 Futɔ mamlɛtɔ si woaɖe ɖa lae nye ku. 27 Elabena Mawu "tsɔ nuwo katã de eƒe afɔ te. " Ke esi wògblɔ be ‘wotsɔ nuwo katã de ete’ la, edze ƒãa be Ame si tsɔ nuwo katã de ete ya mele eme o.
ENGLISH: 27 For "he has subjected everything under his feet "; but, when it says "everything " is subjected, evidently exclusive of him who subjected everything to him.

EWE: 28 Ke ne wotsɔ nuwo katã de ete vɔ la, ekema Vi la ŋutɔ hã atsɔ eɖokui ade Ame si tsɔ nuwo katã de ete la te, ale be Mawu nanye nuwo katã na ame sia ame.
ENGLISH: 28 But when everything has been subjected to him, then the Son himself too will be subjected to him who subjected everything to him, in order that God may be everything in everything.

EWE: 29 Ne menye nenema o la, nu kae ame siwo nyrɔm wole yi ɖe ku me la awɔ? Ne womafɔ ame kukuwo ɖe tsitre kura o ɖe, ekema nu ka tae wole wo nyrɔm kple taɖodzinu ma? 30 Nu ka tae míawo hã míeɖoa afɔku me ɣesiaɣi ɖo? 31 Medzea ŋgɔ ku gbe sia gbe.
ENGLISH: 29 Because what will those who get baptized for the dead do? if dead men do not rise anyhow, why go the length of getting baptized for them? 30 Why, too, do we ourselves run risks every moment? 31 I am dying day after day, I swear it by the boast of you, brothers, which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord.

EWE: Nɔviwo, aseye si metsona le mia ta le mía Aƒetɔ Kristo Yesu me lae metsɔ le kpe ɖom nya sia dzi. 32 Ne mewɔ avu kple lã wɔadãwo le Efeso abe ame bubuwo ene ɖe, viɖe kae wònye nam? Ne womafɔ ame kukuwo ɖe tsitre o la, ekema "mina míaɖu nu, eye míano nu, elabena etsɔ míele kuku ge. " 33 Migana woaflu mi o. Hadede vɔ̃wo gblẽa nɔnɔme nyuiwo.
ENGLISH: 32 If as far as men were concerned I fought the beasts in Ephesus, what good does it do me? if dead men do not rise, "let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die. " 33 Make no mistake; "keeping bad company spoils good characters "; 34 sober up honestly and do not sin; for some folks are sheer materialists I speak to stir your sense of shame.

EWE: Nu si nèƒãna la megbɔa agbe o, negbe ɖe wòku gbã. 37 Eye nu si nèƒãna la, menye ati si amie tso eme lae nèƒãna o, ke boŋ nuku gbɔlo ko, ate ŋu anye lu alo nuku bubu ɖe sia ɖe; 38 ke Mawu naa nɔnɔmee ale si wòlɔ̃, eye wònaa nukuawo ŋutɔ ƒe nɔnɔme wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe.
ENGLISH: 35 But somebody will say "How do the dead rise? and with what sort of body do they come? " 36 Silly man, what you yourself sow does not come to life unless it dies; 37 and of what you sow you sow not the body that is to come but a naked grain, of wheat say or some one of the rest; 38 and God gives it a body as he has willed, and to each of the seeds a body of its own.

EWE: 39 Menye ŋutilãwo katãe nye ŋutilã ɖeka ƒomevi o, ke boŋ amegbetɔwo tɔ li, lãfɔnewo ƒe ŋutilã li, xewo ƒe ŋutilã li eye tɔmelãwo tɔ hã li.
ENGLISH: 39 Flesh is not all of it the same flesh, but there is one of men, and another flesh of cattle, and another flesh of fowl, and another of fishes.

EWE: 40 Dziƒoŋutilãwo li, eye anyigbadziŋutilãwo hã li; ke dziƒoŋutilãwo ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe le vovo, eye anyigbadziŋutilãwo hã tɔ le vovo.
ENGLISH: 40 And there are heavenly bodies and earthly bodies, but the glory of the heavenly is of one type and that of the earthly is other: 41 one glory of the sun and another glory of the moon and another glory of the stars, for star differs from star in glory.

EWE: 41 Ɣe ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe le vovo, ɣleti ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe le vovo, eye ɣletiviwo ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe hã le vovo; le nyateƒe me la, ɣletivi ɖe sia ɖe ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe to vovo na nɔvia tɔ.
ENGLISH: 42 So too the resurrection of the dead: it is sowed in dissolution, it rises in imperishability; 43 it is sowed in ignominy, it rises in glory; it is sowed in weakness, it rises in power; 44 it is sowed an animal body, it rises a spiritual body.

EWE: 42 Nenema kee ame kukuwo ƒe tsitretsitsi hã le.
ENGLISH: If there is an animal body there is a spiritual too.

EWE: Ne ŋutilã si míekpɔna li la, ekema gbɔgbɔŋutilã hã li. 45 Woŋlɔ ɖi be: "Ame gbãtɔ Adam zu ame gbagbe. "
ENGLISH: 45 It is written so too, the first man Adam "became a living soul "; the last Adam, a life-giving spirit.

EWE: Adam mamlɛtɔ zu gbɔgbɔ si naa agbe. 46 Gake menye gbɔgbɔmetɔe gbãtɔ nye o.
ENGLISH: 46 But there is not first the spiritual, but the animal, then the spiritual.

EWE: 47 Ame gbãtɔ la tso anyigba me, eye anyi wotsɔ mèe; ame evelia ya tso dziƒo.
ENGLISH: 47 The first man was out of the earth, a figure of clay; the second man, out of heaven.

EWE: 48 Ame siwo wowɔ kple anyi la le ko abe ame si wotsɔ anyi mè la ene; eye ame siwo le dziƒo la le ko abe ame si tso dziƒo va la ene. 49 Eye ale si ko ame si wotsɔ anyi mè la ƒe nɔnɔme le mía si la, nenema kee ame si tso dziƒo va la ƒe nɔnɔme hã anɔ mía si.
ENGLISH: 48 Such as the figure of clay, such also are those who are of clay, and such as the heavenly one, such also are those who are heavenly; 49 and as we have worn the likeness of the figure of clay, let us wear the likeness of the heavenly one also.

EWE: 50 Ke nɔviwo, esia gblɔm mele be, ŋutilã kple ʋu mate ŋu anyi Mawu Fiaɖuƒe la dome o, eye gbegblẽ mate ŋu anyi magblemagblẽ dome o.
ENGLISH: 50 But this I do say, brothers, that flesh and blood cannot inherit the Reign of God, nor does dissolution inherit imperishability.

EWE: 51 Kpɔ ɖa! Mele nya ɣaɣla kɔkɔe aɖe gblɔm na mi: Menye mí katãe adɔ alɔ̃ le ku me o, ke boŋ woatrɔ mí katã míaƒe nɔnɔme 52 enumake, le aɖabaƒoƒo ɖeka me, le kpẽkuku mamlɛa me. Elabena kpẽ la aɖi, eye woafɔ ame kukuwo ɖe tsitre magblemagblẽe, eye woatrɔ míaƒe nɔnɔme.
ENGLISH: 51 Here I tell you a secret: we shall not all go to our rest, but we shall all be changed in an instant, 52 in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet; for the trumpet will sound, and the dead will rise imperishable, and we shall be changed.

EWE: 53 Elabena ele be nu sia, si gblẽna la, nadó magblemagblẽ, eye nu sia, si kuna la, nadó makumaku.
ENGLISH: 53 For this that is perishable has to dress itself in imperishability, and this that is mortal to dress itself in immortality.

EWE: 54 Ke ne nu sia si gblẽna la dó magblemagblẽ, eye nu sia si kuna la dó makumaku la, ekema nya si woŋlɔ ɖi la ava eme be: "Womi ku tegbee. " 55 "Ku, wò dziɖuɖu ɖe?
ENGLISH: 54 But when this that is mortal does dress itself in immortality, then the words that are written will come true, 55 "Death has been swallowed up in victory. "

EWE: Ku, afi kae wò ti si nètsɔ le ame tém la le? " 56 Ti si hea ku vanɛ lae nye nu vɔ̃, eye nu vɔ̃ ƒe ŋusẽe nye Se la.
ENGLISH: Where is your victory, death? where is your sting, death? 56 But the sting of death is sin. And the power of sin is the law.

EWE: 57 Ke woada akpe na Mawu be ena dziɖuɖu mí to mía Aƒetɔ Yesu Kristo dzi!
ENGLISH: 57 And thanks be to God who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.

EWE: 58 Eya ta nɔvinye lɔlɔ̃tɔwo, minɔ te sesĩe, maʋamaʋã, eye miwɔ geɖe le Aƒetɔ la ƒe dɔ la me ɣesiaɣi, elabena mienyae be miaƒe agbagbadzedze le Aƒetɔ la me menye dzodzro o.
ENGLISH: 58 Consequently, dear brothers, be firm in your footing, not easy to knock about, always abundant in work for the Lord, knowing that your labor does not come to nothing in the Lord.

EWE: 1 Korintotɔwo
ENGLISH: 1 Corinthians

EWE: 16 Ke le nudzɔdzɔ si woaɖo ɖe ame kɔkɔeawo ŋuti la, miwɔ ɖe mɔfiame siwo mena hame siwo le Galatia la dzi. 2 Le kwasiɖa ɖe sia ɖe ƒe ŋkeke gbãtɔ dzi la, mia dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe nadzra nane ɖo le eƒe ŋutete nu, ale be mahiã be mava ɖo hafi miadzɔ nu o.
ENGLISH: 16 And as to the collection for the members of the church, do the same as I directed the churches of Macedonia: 2 the first day of every week let each of you lay by to accumulate whatever he is prospered to, in order that when I come there may not be taking up of collections then.

EWE: 3 Ke ne meva ɖo la, madɔ ŋutsu siwo dzi mieda asi ɖo le miaƒe agbalẽawo me la be woatsɔ miaƒe dɔmenyonunana la ayi Yerusalem. 4 Gake ne esɔ be nye hã mayi la, ekema woayi kplim.
ENGLISH: 3 And when I arrive, whomever you approve I will send with letters to take your kindness to Jerusalem; 4 and if it is worth while for me to go too, they shall go with me.

EWE: 5 Ke ne metso Makedonia la, mava mia gbɔ, elabena Makedonia to ge mele; 6 eye ɖewohĩ manɔ mia gbɔ vie, alo matsi mia gbɔ le vuvɔŋɔli la gɔ̃ hã, ale be miaɖom ɖa vie ne mayi afi si wòle be magayi.
ENGLISH: 5 But I will come to you when I have been through Macedonia; for I am going through Macedonia, 6 but with you I shall maybe stay a while or over the winter, in order that you may give me a send-off wherever I may be going.

EWE: 7 Nyemedi be makpɔ mi fifia ne metso eme va yina o, elabena mele mɔ kpɔm be ne Yehowa ɖe mɔ la, mava nɔ mia gbɔ vie.
ENGLISH: 7 For I do not want to pay you a passing visit now; for I hope to stay with you some time, if the Lord permits.

EWE: 8 Ke manɔ Efeso va se ɖe Pentekoste Ŋkekenyui la dzi, 9 elabena woʋu dɔwɔwɔ ƒe ʋɔtru gã aɖe nam, gake tsitretsiɖeŋula geɖewo li.
ENGLISH: 8 But I shall stay in Ephesus till Pentecost; 9 for a great door for effective work has been opened to me, and there are many opponents.

EWE: 10 Ne Timoteo va ɖo la, mikpɔ egbɔ be vɔvɔ̃ nagaɖoe le mia dome o, elabena Yehowa ƒe dɔ wɔmee wòle abe nye ke ene. 11 Eya ta ame aɖeke megado vloe o.
ENGLISH: 10 But if Timothy comes, see to it that he is free from fear among you; for he is working at the Lord’s work the same as I am, 11 so let nobody scorn him, but start him on his way in peace to come to me, for I am expecting him with the brothers.

EWE: Mikplɔe ɖo ɖa le ŋutifafa me, ne wòava gbɔnye afi sia, elabena mele eya kple nɔviawo lalam. 12 Ke le mía nɔvi Apolo ŋuti la, meɖe kuku nɛ vevie be eya kple nɔviawo nava mia gbɔ.
ENGLISH: 12 But as to Brother Apollos, I strongly urged him to come to you with the brothers, and it positively was not willed that he should come now, but he will when he gets a chance.

EWE: 13 Minɔ ŋudzɔ, minɔ tsitre sesĩe le xɔse la me, miwɔ ŋutsu, misẽ ŋu.
ENGLISH: 13 Keep awake, stand firm in the faith, be manly, take on strength.

EWE: 14 Miwɔ miaƒe nuwo katã le lɔlɔ̃ me.
ENGLISH: 14 Let everything you are concerned in be done in love.

EWE: 15 Ke mele nu xlɔ̃m mi, nɔviwo: Mienyae be Stefana ƒe aƒe lae nye kutsetse gbãtɔ le Akaya, eye wotsɔ wo ɖokuiwo ɖo anyi hena ame kɔkɔewo subɔsubɔ. 16 Miawo hã miyi edzi miabɔbɔ mia ɖokui na ame siawo tɔgbi kple ame siwo katã le asi kpem ɖe dɔa ŋu aduadu hele kutri kum.
ENGLISH: 15 But I urge you, brothers, you know Stephanas’s family, how it was the first to come in in Achaea and they charged themselves with service to God’s people, 16 that you too put yourselves at the disposal of folks like that and of everybody who cooperates and does the hard work.

EWE: 17 Ke mekpɔ dzidzɔ le Stefana, Fortunato kple Akaiko ƒe anyinɔnɔ ŋuti, elabena esi miele afi sia o la, woxɔ ɖe mia teƒe. 18 Elabena wofa akɔ na nye gbɔgbɔ kple miawo hã mia tɔ.
ENGLISH: 17 And I am glad of the arrival of Stephanas and Fortunatus and Achaicus because these filled out the shortage of you; 18 for they set my spirit at rest, and yours too.

EWE: Eya ta mikpɔ ŋudzedze ɖe ame siawo tɔgbi ŋu.
ENGLISH: So recognize folks like that.

EWE: 19 Hame siwo le Asia la do gbe na mi.
ENGLISH: 19 The churches of Asia send you greetings.

EWE: Akwila kple Priskila kpakple hame si le woƒe aƒe me la do gbe na mi vevie le Aƒetɔ la me.
ENGLISH: Aquila and Prisca, with the meeting at their home, send you many greetings in the Lord.

EWE: 20 Nɔviawo katã do gbe na mi.
ENGLISH: 20 All the brothers send you greetings.

EWE: Mitsɔ nugbugbɔ kɔkɔe do gbe na mia nɔewo.
ENGLISH: Give my greetings to each other with a holy kiss.

EWE: 21 Nye Paulo ƒe gbedoname, si metsɔ nye ŋutɔ nye asi ŋlɔ lae nye esi.
ENGLISH: 21 Greeting with my own hand from me, Paul.

EWE: 22 Ne ame aɖe melɔ̃ Aƒetɔ la o la, neɖi eŋu kpékpekpe.
ENGLISH: 22 If anyone does not love the Lord, let him be for God’s destruction.

EWE: Oo, mía Aƒetɔ, va! 23 Mía Aƒetɔ Yesu ƒe amenuveve nanɔ kpli mi.
ENGLISH: Maran atha. 23 The grace of the Lord Jesus be with you.

EWE: 24 Nye lɔlɔ̃ nanɔ kpli mi katã le Kristo Yesu me.
ENGLISH: 24 My love is with you all in Christ Jesus.

EWE: 2 Korintotɔwo
ENGLISH: 2 Corinthians

EWE: 1 Paulo, Kristo Yesu ƒe apostolo to Mawu ƒe lɔlɔ̃nu me, kple mía nɔvi Timoteo, le esia ŋlɔm na Mawu ƒe hame si le Korinto kple ame kɔkɔe siwo le Akaya nutoa katã me: 2 Amenuveve kple ŋutifafa si tso Mawu mía Fofo kple Aƒetɔ Yesu Kristo gbɔ la woana mi.
ENGLISH: 1 Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through God’s will, and Brother Timothy, to God’s church at Corinth with all the people of God in all Achaea; 2 grace to you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

EWE: 3 Woakafu mía Aƒetɔ Yesu Kristo ƒe Mawu, si nye Fofoa, ame si nye dɔmetɔtrɔ Fofo kple akɔfafawo katã ƒe Mawu, 4 ame si faa akɔ na mí le míaƒe tetekpɔwo katã me, ale be míato akɔfafa si míekpɔ tso Mawu gbɔ la dzi afa akɔ na ame siwo le tetekpɔ ɖe sia ɖe ƒomevi me tom la. 5 Elabena ale si ko míaƒe fukpekpewo le Kristo la ta sɔ gbɔe la, nenema kee akɔfafa si míekpɔna la hã sɔ gbɔ to Kristo dzi.
ENGLISH: 3 Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of compassion and God of all encouragement, 4 who encourages us upon all our distress so that we may be able to encourage those who are in any distress with the encouragement that is given to us ourselves by God, 5 because as the Christ’s sufferings are coming plentifully to us, so through the Christ our encouragement too comes in plentiful measure.

EWE: 6 Ne míele tetekpɔwo me tom la, esi míedi be miakpɔ akɔfafa kple ɖeɖe tae; eye ne wofa akɔ na mí la, ale si miawo hã miakpɔ akɔfafa, be miate ŋu ado dzi le fu siwo ke míawo hã míekpena me la tae. 7 Ale mɔkpɔkpɔ si le mía si le mia ŋuti la li ke sesĩe, esi míenyae be, ale si ko miawo hã mietoa fukpekpewo me la, nenema kee woafa akɔ na miawo hã. 8 Elabena nɔviwo, míedi be xaxa si me míeto le Asia nutoa me la nanɔ manyamanya na mi o. Womimi mí ɖo wòwu tsɔtsɔ na mí ale gbegbe be míegaka ɖe edzi be míatsi agbe gɔ̃ hã o.
ENGLISH: 6 And be it that we are distressed, this is for your encouragement and salvation; or be it that we are encouraged, this is for your encouragement, which takes effect in the steadfast endurance of the same sufferings that we too undergo, 7 and our hope is firm for you, knowing as we do that as you are included in the sufferings, so too you are included in the encouragement.

EWE: 9 Le nyateƒe me la, míesusu be wotso kufia na mí. Eva eme alea, ale be míagaɖo dzi ɖe mía ɖokuiwo ŋu o, ke boŋ ɖe Mawu, ame si fɔa ame kukuwo ɖe tsitre la ŋu. 10 Eɖe mí tso ku ƒe ŋɔdzi gã aɖe me, eye agaɖe mí, eye míele mɔ kpɔm be agayi edzi aɖe mí.
ENGLISH: 8 For we do not want you to go without the knowledge, brothers, as to our distress in Asia, that we had an extraordinarily hard time, too hard for our powers, so that we had no prospect of even living, 9 but have had in our own selves the answer of death, in order that we may not be confident in ourselves but in God who raises the dead, 10 who delivered us out of that awful death and will do so; on whom we have set our hope.

EWE: 11 Miawo hã miate ŋu akpe ɖe mía ŋu aƒo koko ɖe mía ta, ale be ame geɖewo nada akpe ɖe mía ta, le ale si wove mía nui heɖo ame geɖewo ƒe gbedodoɖa ɖe mía ta ŋu la ŋuti.
ENGLISH: And he will deliver us still, 11 while you cooperate helpfully on our behalf by petition, in order that from many faces thanks for the favor bestowed on us may be given through many on our behalf.

EWE: 12 Elabena nu si ŋu míeƒoa adegbe lee nye esi, be míaƒe dzitsinya ɖia ɖase be míenɔ agbe le xexea me, vevietɔ le mia dome, le kɔkɔenyenye kple anukwareɖiɖi si dzea Mawu ŋu la nu, menye ɖe ŋutilã ƒe nunya nu o, ke boŋ ɖe Mawu ƒe amenuveve nu.
ENGLISH: 12 For this is our boast, the testimony of our conscience that it was in God’s holiness and candor, not in fleshly wisdom but in the grace of God, that we lived the life we did in the world; and very specially in relation to you.

EWE: 13 Elabena míele nya bubu aɖeke ŋlɔm ɖo ɖe mi o, negbe nu siwo miate ŋu axlẽ ase wo gɔme la ko; eye mele mɔ kpɔm be miayi edzi anɔ nu siawo gɔme sem bliboe, 14 abe ale si ko miese egɔme xoxo va se ɖe afi aɖe ene, be miatsɔ mí aƒo adegbee, abe ale si ko míawo hã míatsɔ mi aƒo adegbee le mía Aƒetɔ Yesu ƒe ŋkeke la dzi ene.
ENGLISH: 13 For we do not write anything else to you but what you read or even recognize, and we hope will recognize to the full, 14 as you did in part recognize us to be your boast, the same as you are ours on the day of our Lord Jesus.

EWE: 15 Eya ta esi kakaɖedzi sia su asinye ta la, meɖoe gbã be mava mia gbɔ ale be dzi nagadzɔ mi zi evelia; 16 elabena meɖoe be mava kpɔ mi ɖa ne meyina Makedonia, eye magatrɔ tso Makedonia ava mia gbɔ, eye miaɖom ɖa mayi Yudea.
ENGLISH: 15 And in this assurance I wanted to come first to you, in order that you might have a second glad time, 16 and to go through to Macedonia by way of you and come from Macedonia to you again and have you see me off for Judea.

EWE: Alo ɖe meɖoa tame le ŋutilã ƒe didi nu, ale be nye nyawo nyea "Ɛ̃, ɛ̃, " eye wògatrɔna zua "Ao, ao " mahã? 18 Ke esi miate ŋu aka ɖe Mawu dzi godoo ta la, nya si míegblɔ na mi la menye "ɛ̃ " ganye "ao " o.
ENGLISH: 17 Wanting to do this, then, did I act capriciously? or is it in the way of flesh that I plan what I plan, so that with me there should be "O yes " and "O no "? 18 But, as God is faithful, our words to you are not yes-and-no.

EWE: 19 Elabena Mawu ƒe Vi, Yesu Kristo, ame si woɖe gbeƒãe le mia dome to nye ŋutɔ kple Silvano kpakple Timoteo dzi la, menye "ɛ̃, " ganye "ao " o, ke boŋ "ɛ̃ " nye "ɛ̃ " le eya gome.
ENGLISH: 19 For God’s Son Jesus Christ, who was proclaimed among you through us, Silvanus and Timothy and me, has not shown himself a yes-and-no, but in him there has been a Yes.

EWE: 20 Elabena aleke gbegbee Mawu ƒe ŋugbedodowo ɖasɔ gbɔe o, wo katã nye "ɛ̃ " to eya amea dzi. Eya ta to eya amea dzi kee míegblɔa "Amen " na Mawu bena míahe ŋutikɔkɔe avɛ na Mawu.
ENGLISH: 20 For in him is the Yes to as many promises of God as there are; for which reason through him also comes the Amen for glory to God through us.

EWE: 21 Ke ame si ɖo kpe edzi be míawo kple miawo míenye Kristo tɔ, eye wòsi ami na mí lae nye Mawu. 22 Eɖo eƒe nutrenu mía ŋu hã, eye wòna nu si ava va la ƒe kpeɖodzi sue aɖe mí, si nye gbɔgbɔ la, le míaƒe dziwo me.
ENGLISH: 21 And the one who brings us with you into a settled position in Christ and has anointed us is God, 22 the same who sealed us and gave us the Spirit in our hearts as earnest-money.

EWE: 23 Meyɔ Mawu be wòanye ɖasefo nam be, fafam mele na mi be miagaxa nu akpa o tae nyemeva Korinto haɖe o.
ENGLISH: 23 But I call God as witness against my own self that it was out of consideration for you I broke off coming to Corinth.

EWE: 24 Menye be míeɖua aƒetɔ ɖe miaƒe xɔse dzi o, ke boŋ míenye hadɔwɔlawo hena miaƒe dzidzɔ, elabena miaƒe xɔsee na miele tsitre.
ENGLISH: 24 Not that we have any control over your faith, but we are cooperators in your joy; for it is by faith you stand.

EWE: 2 Korintotɔwo
ENGLISH: 2 Corinthians

EWE: 2 Ke meɖoe be nyemagatsɔ nuxaxa ava mia gbɔ azɔ o.
ENGLISH: 2 But I made this resolution, not to come to you with an annoyance again.

EWE: 2 Elabena ne mena miexa nu la, ekema ame kae gali ado dzidzɔ nam, ne menye ame si medo nuxaxa na lae oa? 3 Meŋlɔ nya mawo ɖo ɖe mi, ale be ne meva la, nyemagaxa nu le ame siwo ta wòle be makpɔ dzidzɔ ɖo hafi la ŋuti o, elabena kakaɖedzi le asinye be nu si hea dzidzɔ vanɛ nam la hea dzidzɔ vanɛ na mi katã hã.
ENGLISH: 2 For if I annoy you, then who is it that gladdens me but the one who is annoyed by me? 3 And I wrote that very thing in order that I might not, when I come, have annoyance from those over whom I ought to be rejoicing, being confident of you all that my joy is that of all of you.

EWE: 4 Elabena xaxa kple dzi kpekpe ye na metsɔ aɖatsi geɖe ŋlɔ nu ɖo ɖe mi, menye be mana miaxa nu o, ke boŋ ne mianya lɔlɔ̃ si gbegbe le asinye na mi.
ENGLISH: 4 For in much distress and heartache I wrote to you with many tears, not in order that you might be annoyed but in order that you might know the love I specially feel toward you.

EWE: 5 Ke ne ame aɖe he nuxaxa vɛ la, menye nyee wòdo nuxaxa na o, ke boŋ le mɔ aɖe nu la, mi katãe.
ENGLISH: 5 And if anyone has caused an annoyance he has caused it not to me but in part, not to come down too hard, to all of you.

EWE: Ke nyemedi be nye nyawo nu nasẽ akpa o. 6 Tohehe sia si mia dometɔ akpa gãtɔ miena ŋutsu sia la sɔ gbɔ nɛ; 7 azɔ la, mitsɔe kee faa, eye mifa akɔ nɛ, ale be nuxaxa akpa nagamii o.
ENGLISH: 6 For such a one this rebuke by the majority is sufficient; 7 so that on the contrary you should rather be condoning and encouraging, for fear such a one should be crushed with excessive grief.

EWE: 8 Eya ta mele nu xlɔ̃m mi be, miɖee fiae be mielɔ̃e. 9 Esia ta meŋlɔ agbalẽ ɖo ɖe mi, ne manya ne miele klalo aɖo to le nuwo katã me.
ENGLISH: 8 For which reason I urge you to take the line of love toward him; 9 for this was what I wrote for, in order to ascertain your quality, whether you are obedient on all points.

EWE: 10 Ne mietsɔ ame aɖe ƒe nu si wòwɔ kee la, nye hã metsɔe kee. Le nyateƒe me la, nu sia nu si metsɔ ke (ne metsɔ nane ke) la, miaƒe viɖe tae metsɔe ke ɖo le Kristo ŋkume, 11 ale be Satana ƒe asi nagasu mía dzi o, elabena eƒe ayemɔwo mele ɣaɣla ɖe mí o.
ENGLISH: 10 But to him to whom you condone anything, so do I for what I have condoned, if anything I have, has been on your account before Christ’s face, 11 in order that we may not be overreached by Satan; for we are not unacquainted with his contrivances.

EWE: 12 Ke esi meva ɖo Troa be magblɔ Kristo la ŋu nya nyuia, eye woʋu ʋɔtru nam le Aƒetɔ la me la, 13 nye gbɔgbɔ tsi dzodzodzoe le menye, elabena nyemekpɔ nɔvinye Tito o. Eya ta meklã nusrɔ̃la siwo le afi ma hedze Makedonia mɔ.
ENGLISH: 12 But when I came to Troas to preach Christ’s gospel, and had a door opened for me in the Lord, 13 I did not have any relief for my spirit owing to my not finding my brother Titus, but bade them farewell and went out to Macedonia.

EWE: 14 Ke woada akpe na Mawu, ame si nɔa ŋgɔ na mí ɣesiaɣi le aʋadziɖuɖu ƒe gbɔlɔlɔ gã aɖe me ɖekae kple Kristo, eye wòtoa mía dzi kakaa eŋuti sidzedze ƒe ʋeʋẽ lilili le afi sia afi! 15 Elabena míenye Kristo ƒe ʋeʋẽ lilili na Mawu le ame siwo xɔm wole ɖe agbe kple ame siwo le tsɔtsrɔ̃m la dome; 16 míenye ku ƒe ʋeʋẽ si kplɔa ame yia ku me na ame siwo le tsɔtsrɔ̃m, eye míenye agbe ƒe ʋeʋẽ lilili si kplɔa ame yia agbe me na ame siwo xɔm wole ɖe agbe la.
ENGLISH: 14 But thanks be to God who is always leading us about in his triumph and through us diffusing in every place the odor of the knowledge of him, 15 because we are Christ’s genial scent to God among those who are being saved and among those who are being lost 16 to these an odor from death, to death, but to those an odor from life, to life.

EWE: Eye ame kae dze nyuie na nu siawo wɔwɔ? 17 Míawoe, elabena míetsɔa Mawu ƒe nya la tsaa asi abe ale si ame geɖewo wɔnɛ ene o, ke boŋ míeƒoa nu le anukwareɖiɖi me abe ame siwo Mawu dɔ ene; ɛ̃, le Mawu ŋkume, le ɖekawɔwɔ me kple Kristo.
ENGLISH: And for this who is adequate? 17 For we are not like so many, peddling God’s word for a living; it is as in honor bound, it is as from God, in God’s presence, in Christ, that we speak.

EWE: 2 Korintotɔwo
ENGLISH: 2 Corinthians

EWE: 3 Elabena mieɖee fia be miawoe nye Kristo ƒe agbalẽ si mí subɔlawo míeŋlɔ, menye kple agbalẽŋlɔtsi o, ke boŋ kple Mawu gbagbe la ƒe gbɔgbɔ, menye ɖe kpe ŋutɔŋutɔwo dzi o, ke boŋ ɖe esiwo nye ŋutilã dzi, ɖe dziwo dzi. 4 Kakaɖedzi sia le mía si le Mawu me to Kristo dzi.
ENGLISH: 3 Are we beginning to recommend ourselves again? or do we want, as some folks do, letters of commendation to you or from you? 2 You are our letter, inscribed on our hearts, known and read by all men, 3 manifested to be a letter of Christ’s delivered by us, inscribed not in ink but in Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on heart-tablets of flesh.

EWE: 5 Menye be míawo ŋutɔwo míedze nyuie asusu be míawo gbɔe nane tso o, ke boŋ míaƒe dzedze nyuie la tsoa Mawu gbɔ, 6 ame si na míedze nyuie be míanye nubabla yeye aɖe ƒe subɔlawo, menye se siwo woŋlɔ ɖi la tɔwo o, ke boŋ gbɔgbɔ la tɔwo; elabena se siwo woŋlɔ ɖi la tsoa kufia na ame, ke gbɔgbɔ la gbɔa agbe ame.
ENGLISH: 4 But we have such assurance through the Christ toward God, 5 not that we are adequate of ourselves to count anything as from ourselves, but our adequacy is from God, 6 the same who made us adequate as servitors of a new covenant not of letter but of spirit; for the letter kills but the spirit brings to life.

EWE: 7 Azɔ ne Se si hea kufiatsotso vanɛ, si wotsɔ ŋɔŋlɔdzesiwo ŋlɔ ɖe kpewo dzi la, va le ŋutikɔkɔe ma gbegbe me be Israel-viwo mete ŋu kpɔ Mose ƒe mo o le ŋutikɔkɔe si dze le eƒe mo ta, evɔ wònye ŋutikɔkɔe si woava ɖe ɖa la, 8 ekema ɖe gbɔgbɔ la ƒe subɔsubɔdɔ manɔ ŋutikɔkɔe geɖe wu me oa? 9 Elabena ne ŋutikɔkɔe nɔ Se si hea fɔbubu vanɛ ŋu la, ekema ŋutikɔkɔe ka gbegbee nye esi anɔ subɔsubɔdɔ si hea dzɔdzɔenyenye vanɛ la ŋu! 10 Le nyateƒe me la, woɖe ŋutikɔkɔe ɖa le nu si wodo ŋutikɔkɔe na tsã la gɔ̃ hã ŋu, le ŋutikɔkɔe si ƒo eta sãa la ta.
ENGLISH: 7 And if the service of death, in letters, imprinted in stones, came in glory so that the sons of Israel could not fix their eyes on Moses’s face because of that glory of his face which was being superseded, 8 how shall the service of the Spirit not be more greatly in glory? 9 For if the service of condemnation is glory, much more surpassing in glory is the service of righteousness; 10 for the glorified is even gloryless in this aspect, on account of the glory that outdoes it.

EWE: 11 Elabena ne nu si woava ɖe ɖa la va le ŋutikɔkɔe me la, ekema aleke gbegbe nu si anɔ anyi ya ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe alolo wue nye esi!
ENGLISH: 11 For if what is superseded comes in glory, much more does what remains stand in glory.

EWE: 12 Esi mɔkpɔkpɔ sia le mía si ta la, míevo aƒo nu faa, 13 eye míawo ya míewɔa nu si Mose wɔ esi wòtsɔa motsyɔnu tsyɔa mo be Israel-viwo nagakpɔ nu si woava ɖe ɖa la ƒe nuwuwu o. 14 Ke woƒe susu wɔ dɔ̃ɔ. Elabena va se ɖe egbegbe la, ne wole nubabla xoxoa xlẽm la, motsyɔnu ma gali kokoko, elabena Kristo dzi ko wotona ɖenɛ ɖa. 15 Le nyateƒe me la, va se ɖe egbegbe la, ɣesiaɣi si woxlẽ Mose ƒe nuŋlɔɖiwo la, motsyɔnu tsyɔa woƒe dziwo dzi.
ENGLISH: 12 So, having such a hope, we practice great frankness, 13 and do not do as Moses did when he put a veil over his face so that the sons of Israel should not set eyes on the end of what was being superseded; 14 but their senses became callous, for to this very day the same veil remains over the reading of the old covenant, not thrown back because it is superseded in Christ, 15 but to this day when Moses is read a veil lies over their heart.

EWE: 16 Ke ne wotrɔ ɖe Yehowa ŋu la, ekema woɖea motsyɔnu la ɖa.
ENGLISH: 16 But when he returns to the Lord the veil is taken off.

EWE: 17 Azɔ la, Yehowa nye Gbɔgbɔ; eye afi si Yehowa ƒe gbɔgbɔ le la, afi mae ablɔɖe le.
ENGLISH: 17 And the Lord is the Spirit; and where the Lord’s Spirit is, freedom is.

EWE: 18 Eye esi mí katã míetsɔa mo siwo wometsyɔ nui o ɖea Yehowa ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe fiana abe ahuhɔ̃ewo ene ta la, wotrɔa míaƒe nɔnɔme ɖe nɔnɔme ma ke me tso ŋutikɔkɔe me yi ŋutikɔkɔe si de ŋgɔ wu me, abe ale si tututu Yehowa, Gbɔgbɔ la, wɔe ene.
ENGLISH: 18 But we all of us, viewing the reflection of the Lord’s glory with face freed from its veil, are transfigured into the same likeness, from glory into glory, as should be the case from the Lord’s Spirit.

EWE: 2 Korintotɔwo
ENGLISH: 2 Corinthians

EWE: 4 Eya ta esi wokpɔ nublanui na mí hetsɔ subɔsubɔdɔ sia de asi na mí ta la, míenaa ta o. 2 Ke boŋ míegbea nu le ŋukpenanu ɣaɣlawo gbɔ, míewɔa ayemenu o, eye míetɔa tsi Mawu ƒe nya la hã o; ke boŋ le Mawu ŋkume la, míehea nyateƒea ɖe go eye míekpɔa ŋusẽ nyui ɖe amewo katã ƒe dzitsinya dzi.
ENGLISH: 4 For this reason, having this service to perform as mercy was granted to us, we do not give up trying, 2 but have renounced the concealments of shame, not walking in trickery nor adulterating God’s word, but by giving publicity to the truth commending ourselves to every human conscience before God.

EWE: 3 Ke ne wotsyɔ nu nya nyui si gblɔm míele la dzi vavã la, ame siwo le tsɔtsrɔ̃m lae wotsyɔ nu edzi na, 4 ale nuɖoanyi sia ƒe mawu gbã ŋku na dzimaxɔsetɔ siawo ƒe tamesusu, ale be Kristo, si nye Mawu ƒe nɔnɔme la, ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe nya nyui la ƒe kekeli nagaklẽ na wo o.
ENGLISH: 3 And if our gospel be veiled, it is veiled in the case of those who are being lost, 4 in whose case the god of this world has blinded unbelievers’ senses so that they should not eye the refulgence of the gospel of the glory of the Christ, who is image of God.

EWE: 5 Elabena míele gbeƒã ɖem mía ɖokui o, ke boŋ Yesu Kristo, be eyae nye Aƒetɔ la, eye míawo míenye miaƒe kluviwo le Yesu ta. 6 Elabena Mawu ame si gblɔ be, "Kekeli neklẽ tso viviti me " lae klẽ ɖe míaƒe dziwo me be wòana Mawu ŋuti sidzedze wɔnuku la naklẽ ɖe wo me to Kristo ƒe mo dzi.
ENGLISH: 5 For we are not preaching ourselves, but Jesus Christ as Lord and ourselves servants to you on Jesus’s account, 6 because it was God, he who said "Light shall shine out of darkness, " that shone in our hearts to produce the refulgence of the knowledge of God’s glory in the face of Christ.

EWE: 7 Gake nu xɔasi sia le mía si le anyigoewo me, ale be ŋusẽ si gbɔ dzɔdzɔmetɔ ŋu la nanye Mawu tɔ, eye menye mía gbɔ wòatso o. 8 Womimi mí ɖo le go sia go me, ke menye ale gbegbe be míedo kpo ʋaʋã o; míetɔtɔ, ke menye be míenya nu si míawɔ kura o; 9 wotia mía yome, ke womegblẽ mí ɖi o; woxlã mí ɖe anyi, ke wometsrɔ̃ mí o.
ENGLISH: 7 But we have this treasure in earthen jars, in order that the surpassing power may be God’s and not out of us: 8 every way hard pressed but not cornered, perplexed but not baffled, 9 persecuted but not deserted, felled but not ended, 10 always carrying about in our body Jesus’s deadness in order that Jesus’s life too may be made visible in our body.

EWE: 11 Elabena mí, ame siwo le agbe la, míedzea ŋgɔ ku ɣesiaɣi le Yesu ta, ale be Yesu ƒe agbe nadze hã le míaƒe ŋutilã si kuna la ŋu. 12 Ale ku le dɔ wɔm le mía me, gake agbe le dɔ wɔm le miawo me.
ENGLISH: 11 For we who are alive are all the time being sent to death on Jesus’s account, in order that Jesus’s life too may be made visible in our mortal flesh, 12 so that death is at work in us but life in you.

EWE: 13 Ke esi xɔse ma ke si ŋu woŋlɔ le be, "Mexɔe se, eya tae meƒo nu ɖo "; ƒe gbɔgbɔ le mía me ta la, míawo hã míexɔe se, eya tae míeƒoa nu ɖo, 14 elabena míenyae be Ame si fɔ Yesu ɖe tsitre la afɔ míawo hã ɖe tsitre kpe ɖe Yesu ŋu, eye wòaɖe míawo kple miawo siaa afia.
ENGLISH: 13 And, having the same spirit of faith, in accordance with the written words "I believed, for that reason I spoke, " we too believe and it is for that reason we speak, 14 knowing that he who raised Jesus will raise us too with Jesus and present us together with you.

EWE: 15 Elabena wowɔ nu siawo katã le mia ta, ale be amenuveve si dzi ɖe edzi la, nasɔ gbɔ ɖe edzi le ame geɖe wu ƒe akpedada ta, hena Mawu ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe.
ENGLISH: 15 For everything is on your account, in order that the grace, growing vaster by the greater number, may make thanksgiving the more abundant to the glory of God.

EWE: 16 Eya ta míenaa ta o, ke ne ame si míenye le gota gome le gbegblẽm hã la, kakaɖedzi li be ame si míenye le ememe ya le yeye zum gbe sia gbe. 17 Elabena togbɔ be ɣeyiɣi vi aɖe ƒe xaxa si nu mesẽ o koe wònye hã la, ehea ŋutikɔkɔe gã mavɔ si ƒoa nu sia nu ta sãsãsã la vanɛ na mí; 18 esi míenana míaƒe ŋkuwo nɔa nu siwo wokpɔna la ŋu o, ke boŋ nu siwo womekpɔna o la ŋu.
ENGLISH: 16 Wherefore we do not give up trying, but though our outer man be perishing our inner is renewed day by day, 17 for the light pressure of our present distress is producing for us in unparalleled richness an unequaled weight of eternal glory; 18 while we look not to the seen but to the unseen, for what is seen is temporary but what is unseen is eternal.

EWE: 2 Korintotɔwo
ENGLISH: 2 Corinthians

EWE: 5 Elabena míenyae be ne wogbã míaƒe anyigbadzixɔ, si nye agbadɔ sia, gɔ̃ hã la, xɔ si tso Mawu gbɔ la anɔ mía si, xɔ si wometsɔ asi tu o, si li tegbee le dziƒo.
ENGLISH: 5 For we know that if our earthly housing in the tent is pulled down we have a building that comes from God, an eternal unmanufactured house, in the heavens.

EWE: 2 Le nyateƒe me la, míeŋena le xɔ sia si me míele la me, eye míele didim vevie be míado xɔ si nye mía tɔ, si tso dziƒo la, 3 ale be ne míeva doe la, míagatsi amama o. 4 Le nyateƒe me la, mí ame siwo le agbadɔ sia me la míeŋena, eye nu tea mía ŋu, elabena míedi be míaɖe esia ada ɖi o, ke boŋ be míado ekemɛa, ale be agbe nami nu si kuna la.
ENGLISH: 2 For this is what we groan about, longing to be clothed with the overgarment of our habitation from heaven, 3 if we are to have put it on and not be found naked 4 for we who are in the tent are weighed down and groan over our wish not to be stripped but to be clothed with an overgarment in order that mortality may be engulfed by life.

EWE: 5 Ke ame si dzra mí ɖo na nu sia lae nye Mawu, ame si na gbɔgbɔ si nye nu si ava va la ƒe kpeɖodzi mí.
ENGLISH: 5 And the one that framed us to this very end was God, he who gave us the Spirit as earnest-money.

EWE: 6 Eya ta dzideƒo geɖe le mía si ɣesiaɣi, eye míenya be zi ale si míaƒe aƒe kpɔtɔ le ŋutilã me la, míele Aƒetɔ la gbɔ o, 7 elabena míezɔna le xɔse me, ke menye le nukpɔkpɔ me o. 8 Ke dzideƒo geɖe le mía si, eye míedi be míakpɔtɔ anɔ ŋutilã la me o, ke boŋ míayi aɖanɔ Aƒetɔ la gbɔ. 9 Eya ta míele egbɔ loo alo míeɖale egbɔ o, míeɖoe kplikpaa be míaƒe nu nadze eŋu.
ENGLISH: 6 So, being always ready for anything, and knowing that while at home in the body we are abroad from the Lord 7 for we are walking by faith, not by a sight, 8 but we are ready for anything and willing, more willing, to be abroad from the body and at home with the Lord; 9 for this reason we make it our ambition too, whether at home or abroad, to be pleasing to him.

EWE: 10 Elabena ele na mí katã be míado ɖe Kristo ƒe ʋɔnudrɔ̃zikpui la ŋgɔ, ale be ame sia ame naxɔ nu si wòdze na ɖe nu siwo wòwɔ le ŋutilã me la nu, eɖanye nyui alo vɔ̃ o.
ENGLISH: 10 For we all have to come out to the bar of the Christ, each to get the payment for what he has done with his body, be it a good thing or a bad thing.

EWE: 11 Eya ta esi míenya ale si woavɔ̃ Aƒetɔ lae ta la, míeyia edzi fiaa nu amewo be woatrɔ susu, ke Mawu nya ame siwo míenye la nyuie.
ENGLISH: 11 So, knowing the fear of the Lord, we are persuading men but are displayed in our true colors to God, and, I hope, in your consciences too.

EWE: 12 Menye ɖe míegale mía ɖokuiwo kafum na mi ake o, ke boŋ míele nu si ana miatsɔ mí aƒo adegbee la nam mi, ale be miate ŋu aɖo nya ŋu na ame siwo ƒoa adegbe le gota gome ko ŋuti, ke menye le nu si le dzi me la ŋuti o.
ENGLISH: 12 We are not recommending ourselves to you again, but giving you material for boasting about us, in order that you may have something to say to those who boast of what they have to show and not of what is in them.

EWE: 13 Ne míaƒe tame da la, Mawu tae; ne míaƒe susu le te la, miawo tae.
ENGLISH: 13 For if we are out of our senses it looks toward God, and if we are of sound mind it looks toward you.

EWE: 14 Elabena Kristo ƒe lɔlɔ̃ la ƒonɛ ɖe mía nu, elabena nu si dzi míelɔ̃ ɖoe nye esi, be ame ɖeka ku ɖe wo katã ta; eye ale wo katã ku. 15 Eye wòku ɖe wo katã ta, ale be ame siwo le agbe la naganɔ agbe na wo ɖokuiwo azɔ o, ke woanɔ agbe na ame si ku ɖe wo ta, eye wofɔe ɖe tsitre la boŋ. 16 Eya ta tso esia dzi la, míenya ame aɖeke le ŋutilã nu o.
ENGLISH: 14 For Christ’s love puts a pressure on us, our conclusion being that one died for all, hence all died, 15 and he died for all in order that those who are alive may no longer be alive looking toward themselves but toward the one who died and rose for them, 16 so that we, from now on, do not know anybody in the way of flesh.

EWE: Ne míenya Kristo le ŋutilã nu tsã hã la, míeganyae nenema kura azɔ o.
ENGLISH: Even though we have known Christ in the way of flesh, yet now we no longer do.

EWE: 17 Eya ta ne ame aɖe wɔ ɖeka kple Kristo la, ezu nuwɔwɔ yeye; nu xoxowo nu va yi; kpɔ ɖa, nu yeyewo va li.
ENGLISH: 17 So that if one is in Christ it is a new creation, what originally existed is bygone, here have new things come into existence.

EWE: 18 Ke nuwo katã tso Mawu gbɔ, eya, ame si dzra mía kplii dome ɖo to Kristo dzi, eye wòtsɔ subɔsubɔdɔ si dzraa amewo kple Mawu dome ɖo la de asi na mí, 19 si nye be Mawu to Kristo dzi nɔ eya kple xexea dome dzram ɖo, ale be megabu woƒe vodadawo na wo o, eye wòtsɔ nya si dzraa eya kple amewo dome ɖo la de asi na mí.
ENGLISH: 18 But everything is from God, who reconciled us to himself through Christ and gave us the errand of communicating the reconciliation, 19 how God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, not counting their offenses against them, and consigning to us the word of the reconciliation.

EWE: 20 Eya ta míenye amedɔdɔwo le Kristo teƒe, abe ɖe Mawu to mía dzi le kuku ɖem ene.
ENGLISH: 20 So we come as ambassadors for Christ, as if it were God appealing to you by us; speaking for Christ we beg you, be reconciled to God.

EWE: Abe Kristo teƒenɔlawo ene la, míeɖea kuku be: "Mina woadzra mia kple Mawu dome ɖo. " 21 Ena ame si ŋu nu vɔ̃ mele o la zu nuvɔ̃vɔsa ɖe mía ta, be to eya dzi la, míazu ame dzɔdzɔewo le Mawu ŋkume.
ENGLISH: 21 Him who had not known sin he made into sin for us in order that we may become righteousness of God’s in him.

EWE: 2 Korintotɔwo
ENGLISH: 2 Corinthians

EWE: 6 Esi míenye Mawu ƒe hadɔwɔlawo ta la, míele nu xlɔ̃m mi hã be miagaxɔ Mawu ƒe amenuveve la evɔ ada taɖodzinu si le eŋu ya ƒu o. 2 Elabena egblɔ be: "Meɖo to wò le amenuveɣi, eye mekpe ɖe ŋuwò le xɔxɔgbe. "
ENGLISH: 6 And in cooperation too we appeal to you not to give God’s grace such a reception as will make it amount to nothing; 2 for he says "At a time of acceptance I listened to you and on a day of salvation I helped you. "

EWE: Kpɔ ɖa! Fifia koŋ ye nye amenuveɣi la. Kpɔ ɖa!
ENGLISH: Here is the time of acceptance now, here is the day of salvation now.

EWE: Fifiae nye xɔxɔgbe la. 3 Míewɔa naneke si azu nuɖiaɖia le mɔ aɖeke nu o, ale be woagakpɔ vodada aɖeke le míaƒe subɔsubɔdɔ la ŋu o; 4 ke boŋ míeɖea mía ɖokui fiana le mɔ sia mɔ nu be míenye Mawu ƒe subɔlawo, le dzidodo geɖe me, le xaxawo me, le hiãkamewo me, le fukpekpewo me, 5 le ƒoƒowo me, le gamenɔnɔwo me, le zitɔtɔwo me, le dɔ sesẽ wɔwɔ me, le zãdomadɔlɔ̃e me, le dɔmeɣeɣiwo me; 6 to dzadzɛnyenye me, to sidzedze me, to dzigbɔgbɔ blewu me, to dɔmenyonyo me, to gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔe me, to lɔlɔ̃ si me alakpa mele o me, 7 to nyateƒetoto me, to Mawu ƒe ŋusẽ me; to dzɔdzɔenyenye ƒe aʋawɔnu siwo le ɖusi kple mia me la me, 8 to bubudeameŋu kple bubumadeameŋu me, to nya vɔ̃ kple nya nyui gbɔgblɔ tso mía ŋu me. Wobua mí ameblelawoe, evɔ nyateƒetɔwoe míenye, 9 wobua mí abe ame siwo womedze sii o ene, evɔ wodze si mí hafi, wobua mí abe ame siwo le kukum ene, gake kpɔ ɖa, míele agbe, wohe to na mí, gake wometsɔ mí de asi na ku o, 10 wobua mí abe ame siwo le nu xam ene, gake míekpɔa dzidzɔ ɣesiaɣi, abe ame dahewo ene, gake míenaa ame geɖewo zua kesinɔtɔwo, abe ame siwo si naneke mele o ene, evɔ nuwo katã le mía si hafi.
ENGLISH: 3 And we do not give anything for people to object to in any case, in order that the business we are on may not be found fault with, 4 but in every case are commending ourselves as agents of God, in holding out through many hard things, in distresses, in necessities, in tight pinches, 5 in beatings, in imprisonments, in mobbings, in hard work, in sleepless nights, in foodless days, 6 in integrity, in knowledge, in patience, in kindness, in Holy Spirit, in unfeigned love, 7 in words of truth, in God’s power, by the right-hand and left-hand armament of righteousness; 8 through glory and dishonor, through denunciation and commendation; as deceivers and truthful, 9 as unknown and noted, as dying and here we are alive, as punished for discipline and not put to death, 10 as grieving but always glad, as poor but enriching many, as not having anything but in possession of everything.

EWE: 11 Míeke nu gblɔ nya sia nya na mi, Korintotɔwo, eye míeʋu míaƒe dziwo na mi gbadzaa.
ENGLISH: 11 Our mouth is open to you, Corinthians, our heart is expanded.

EWE: 12 Míexaxa le míaƒe lɔlɔ̃ na mi me o, ke boŋ miawoe xaxa le miaƒe lɔlɔ̃ na mí me.
ENGLISH: 12 You are not narrowed down in us but narrowed down in your own sympathies.

EWE: 13 Eya ta mele nu ƒom na mi abe vinyewo ene be, nu si miawɔ atsɔ aɖo eteƒee nye be, miawo hã miʋu miaƒe dziwo me gbadzaa na mí.
ENGLISH: 13 But in due requital, I say as speaking to children of mine, be expanded yourselves.

EWE: Alo ɖekawɔwɔ kae le kekeli kple viviti dome? 15 Azɔ hã, ɖekawɔwɔ kae le Kristo kple Belial dome? Alo kadodo kae le xɔsetɔ kple dzimaxɔsetɔ dome? 16 Eye ɖekawɔwɔ kae le Mawu ƒe gbedoxɔ kple trɔ̃wo dome? Elabena Mawu gbagbe la ƒe gbedoxɔ míenye; abe ale si Mawu gblɔe ene be: "Manɔ wo dome, eye mazɔ wo dome, manye woƒe Mawu, eye woanye nye dukɔ. " 17 "‘Eya ta mido go le wo dome, eye miɖe mia ɖokui ɖa,’ Yehowa ye gblɔe, ‘eye midzudzɔ asikaka nu makɔmakɔ la ŋu’ "; "‘eye maxɔ mi.’ " 18 "‘Eye manye mia fofo, eye mianye vinyeŋutsuwo kple vinyenyɔnuwo,’ Yehowa Ŋusẽkatãtɔ lae gblɔe. "
ENGLISH: 14 Do not be in incongruous yoking with unbelievers; for what have righteousness and wickedness in common? or what solidarity has light with darkness? 15 and what agreement between Christ and Belial is there? or what does a believer share with an unbeliever? 16 and what unity is there between a temple of God and idols? for we are a temple of the living God, as God said "I will live among them and walk among them, and will be their God and they shall be my people; 17 wherefore come out from their midst and separate yourselves, says the Lord, and do not touch an unclean thing, 18 and I will take you in and be father to you, and you shall be sons and daughters to me, says the Lord Almighty. "

EWE: 2 Korintotɔwo
ENGLISH: 2 Corinthians

EWE: 7 Esi ŋugbedodo siawo le mía si ta la, lɔlɔ̃tɔwo, mina míakɔ mía ɖokui ŋu tso ŋutilã kple gbɔgbɔ ƒe ɖiƒoƒo sia ɖiƒoƒo me, eye míanɔ kɔkɔe geɖe wu le mawuvɔvɔ̃ me.
ENGLISH: 7 So, dear friends, having these promises, let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of flesh and spirit, working out holiness in the fear of God.

EWE: 2 Mikɔ dzi me ɖe mía ŋu.
ENGLISH: 2 Find room for us; we did not wrong anybody, wreck anybody, overreach anybody.

EWE: Míeda vo ɖe ame aɖeke ŋu o, míegblẽ nu le ame aɖeke ŋu o, míeba ame aɖeke o. 3 Nyemele esia gblɔm be mabu fɔ mi o.
ENGLISH: 3 I am not saying it by way of condemnation; for I have said before that you are in our hearts to live and die with us.

EWE: 5 Le nyateƒe me la, esi míeva ɖo Makedonia la, míaƒe ŋutilã mekpɔ gbɔdzɔe aɖeke o, ke boŋ woyi edzi wɔ fu mí le mɔ sia mɔ nu ʋiʋliwo nɔ egodo, vɔvɔ̃ nɔ ememe. 6 Ke Mawu, ame si faa akɔ na ame siwo ƒo dzi ɖe le la, na Tito ƒe vava fa akɔ na mí. 7 Eye menye eƒe vava la ɖeɖe koe o, ke ale si miena eƒe dzi dze eme hãe, elabena eva gblɔ ale si miedi vevie be yewoakpɔm, ale si miele nu xam ɖe tanye, kple ale si mietsɔ ɖe le eme nam vevie la nam; eye esia na megakpɔ dzidzɔ geɖe wu. 8 Elabena ne nye agbalẽa na miexa nu hã la mevem o. Ne evem gbã hã la, (mekpɔe be agbalẽ ma do nuxaxa na mi, gake ɣeyiɣi vi aɖe koe), 9 azɔ mele dzidzɔ kpɔm, menye esi wòdo nuxaxa na mi ta o, ke esi wòna miexa nu hena dzimetɔtrɔ ta boŋ.
ENGLISH: 4 I have great confidence in speaking to you, great boasts on your account; I am filled full of encouragement, I have superabundant gladness with all our distress 5 for when we came to Macedonia our human nature had no relief; but in distress at every point outwardly fights, inwardly fears 6 but he who encourages those that are brought low, God, encouraged us with Titus’s arrival, 7 and not only his arrival but also the encouragement he had over you as he reported to us your longing, your lamenting, your jealousy for me, so that I had more of gladness; 8 because if I did grieve you in my letter, I do not regret it; if I did regret it (I see that that letter did, if only momentarily, grieve you) 9 I am glad now, not that you were grieved but that you were grieved into repentance.

EWE: Elabena ena miexa nu le Mawu me, ale be míegblẽ naneke le mia ŋu o. 10 Elabena mawumenuxaxa nana wotrɔa dzi me hena ɖeɖekpɔkpɔ, eye esia mevea ame o; ke xexe sia ƒe nuxaxa hea ku vanɛ.
ENGLISH: For you were grieved in God’s way, in order that you might not be in any respect the worse off by us; 10 for grief that is felt in God’s way causes repentance into salvation, which there is no regretting, but the world’s grief produces death.

EWE: 11 Mikpɔ nu si gbegbe do tso miaƒe mawumenuxaxa me la ɖa, ɛ̃, ena miekɔ mia ɖokui ŋu, ɛ̃, ena mielé fu nu manyomanyo, ɛ̃, ena vɔvɔ̃ ɖo mi, ɛ̃, ena didi vevie nɔ mia me, ɛ̃, ena mietsɔ dzo ɖe nu ŋu, ɛ̃ ena mieɖɔ nu si gblẽ la ɖo!
ENGLISH: 11 For look what earnestness, nay, words of self-defense, nay, indignation, nay, fear, nay, longing, nay, jealousy, nay, castigation! every way you kept your skirts clean in the matter.

EWE: Mieɖee fia le go sia go me be yewole dzadzɛ le nya sia me. 12 Togbɔ be meŋlɔ agbalẽ na mi hã la, menye ame si da vo alo ame si ŋu woda vo ɖo tae meŋlɔe ɖo o, ke boŋ be miaƒe veviedodo le mía ŋuti la nadze ƒãa le mia dome le Mawu ŋkume.
ENGLISH: 12 So then if I did write to you it was not on account of the one who did the wrong nor of the one who was wronged, but for the sake of having your earnestness on our behalf made apparent to yourselves before God.

EWE: 13 Esia tae wofa akɔ na mí ɖo. Ke hekpe ɖe míaƒe akɔfafa sia ŋu la, míegakpɔ dzidzɔ geɖe wu le dzidzɔ si Tito kpɔ la ta, elabena mi katã miena eƒe gbɔgbɔ kpɔ dzidzeme. 14 Ne meƒo adegbe le mia ŋu le eŋkume la, mezu ŋukpe nam o; ke boŋ ale si nya siwo katã míegblɔ na mi nye nyateƒe la, nenema kee ale si metsɔ mi ƒo adegbee na Tito la hã nye nyateƒe.
ENGLISH: 13 For this reason we have felt encouraged; and along with our encouragement we were all the gladder at Titus’s gladness because his spirit has been set at rest by all of you, 14 because if I have made any boast to him about you I was not put to shame, but as we told you everything truthfully, so too our boasting before Titus proved true.
