ENGLISH: 14 Do not neglect the gift you have in you, which was given to you through a prophecy with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery.

EWE: 15 De ŋugble le nu siawo ŋu; lé fɔ ɖe wo ŋu, ale be wò ŋgɔgbedede nadze ƒãa na amewo katã.
ENGLISH: 15 Practice on these things, take up your time with these, in order that your progress may be evident to everybody.

EWE: 16 Kpɔ ɖokuiwò kple wò nufiafia dzi nyuie ɣeawokatãɣi. Do vevie nu le nu siawo me, elabena ne èwɔ esia la, àxɔ ɖokuiwò kple ame siwo ɖoa to wò la siaa ɖe agbe.
ENGLISH: 16 Attend to yourself and to the teaching; keep on with them; for in doing this you will save both yourself and your hearers.

EWE: 1 Timoteo
ENGLISH: 1 Timothy

EWE: 5 Mègahe nya ɖe ame tsitsi ŋu o. Ke boŋ xlɔ̃ nui abe fofo ene, ɖekakpuiwo abe nɔviŋutsuwo ene, 2 nyɔnu tsitsiwo abe dadawo ene, ɖetugbuiwo abe nɔvinyɔnuwo ene le dzadzɛnyenye blibo me.
ENGLISH: 5 Do not rebuke an elderly man but appeal to him as a father; younger men as brothers, 2 older women as mothers, younger ones as sisters in all purity.

EWE: 3 Bu ahosi siwo nye ahosi ŋutɔŋutɔwo la ŋu.
ENGLISH: 3 Honor widows who really are widows.

EWE: 4 Ke ne viwo alo mamayɔviwo le ahosi aɖe si la, na ame siawo nasrɔ̃ ale si woawɔ nu si dzea Mawu ŋu le woawo ŋutɔwo ƒe aƒe me gbã, eye woaɖo eteƒe na wo dzilawo, wo tɔgbuiwo kple wo mamawo ale si dze, elabena esia sɔ le Mawu ŋkume.
ENGLISH: 4 But if any widow has children or grandchildren let them learn first to show piety toward their own family and to make returns to their progenitors; for this is a thing welcome to God.

EWE: 5 Ke nyɔnu si nye ahosi ŋutɔŋutɔ, eye naneke mele esi o la, tsɔa eƒe mɔkpɔkpɔ ɖoa Mawu dzi, eye wònɔa kokoƒoƒowo kple gbedodoɖawo dzi zã kple keli.
ENGLISH: 5 But the real widow, left alone in the world, has her hope set on God and keeps up her petitions and prayers night and day; 6 but the self-indulgent one is dead while she is alive.

EWE: 7 Eya ta yi edzi nànɔ mɔfiame siawo nam, ale be woanye mokakamanɔŋutɔwo.
ENGLISH: 7 Give these injunctions too, in order that they may be unimpeachable.

EWE: 8 Le nyateƒe me la, ne ame aɖe mekpɔa eya ŋutɔ tɔwo ƒe nu hiahiãwo gbɔ o, vevietɔ eya ŋutɔ ƒe aƒemetɔwo ƒe nu hiahiãwo gbɔ o la, egbe xɔse la, eye wòvɔ̃ɖi wu dzimaxɔsetɔ.
ENGLISH: 8 But if one does not look out for his own, and especially those of his immediate family, he has disowned the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.

EWE: 9 Ahosi si woatia la naxɔ tso ƒe blaade heyi, ame si nye ŋutsu ɖeka srɔ̃, 10 ame si ŋu woɖi ɖase le le eƒe dɔwɔwɔ nyuiwo ta, ne ehe viawo nyuie, ne ewɔa amedzro, ne eklɔa afɔ na ame kɔkɔewo, ne ena kpekpeɖeŋu ame siwo ɖo xaxa me, ne ekpɔa gome le dɔ nyui sia dɔ nyui wɔwɔ me.
ENGLISH: 9 Let a widow be listed as such when she is not less than sixty years old, widow of one husband, 10 well attested for good works, if she has brought up children, if she has practiced hospitality, if she has washed the feet of people of God’s, if she has assisted persons in distress, if she has been assiduous in every good work.

EWE: 11 Ke mègatia ahosi siwo metsi o, elabena ne woƒe gbɔdɔdɔ ƒe dzodzrowo va zu mɔxeɖenu na woƒe subɔsubɔdɔ wɔwɔ na Kristo la, wodina be yewoaɖe srɔ̃.
ENGLISH: 11 But decline younger widows; for when they get too high-strung for the Christ, they want to marry, 12 incurring a judgment because they slighted their first faith.

EWE: 13 Eye wogbea dɔwɔwɔ hã, nɔa tsatsam tso aƒe me yi aƒe me; ɛ̃, menye ɖeko wogbea dɔwɔwɔ o, ke wonɔa ame ŋu nya hã gblɔm, eye wonɔa nu dem amewo ƒe nyawo me henɔa nya siwo mele be woagblɔ o la gblɔm.
ENGLISH: 13 And at the same time they also learn to be idlers going the rounds of the houses, and not only idlers but also chatterers and busybodies, talking of what they ought not.

EWE: 14 Eya ta medi be ahosi siwo metsi o la naɖe srɔ̃, adzi vi, akpɔ aƒe dzi, ale be woagana mɔ tsitretsiɖeŋula la wòakpɔ nya vlo aɖeke agblɔ tso mía ŋu o.
ENGLISH: 14 So I would have younger ones marry, bear children, keep house, not give the opponent any opening toward abusive talk; 15 for some have already turned off to follow Satan.

EWE: 15 Le nyateƒe me la, wo dometɔ aɖewo trɔ dze Satana yome hã xoxo. 16 Ne nyɔnu xɔsetɔ aɖe ƒe ƒometɔ aɖe nye ahosi la, nena kpekpeɖeŋui, ne wòaganye agba na hame la o.
ENGLISH: 16 If any believing woman has widows, let her assist them and the church not be burdened, in order that it may assist the real widows.

EWE: 17 Hamemetsitsi siwo wɔa woƒe dzikpɔkpɔdɔa nyuie la dze na bubu teƒe eve, vevietɔ wo dometɔ siwo doa vevie nu le nuƒoƒo kple nufiafia me.
ENGLISH: 17 Let elders who have done well in management be deemed to deserve double honor, especially those who exert themselves in speaking and teaching.

EWE: 18 Elabena ŋɔŋlɔ la gblɔ be, "Mègabla nu na nyitsu ne ele nuku tugum o, " eye be, "Dɔwɔla dze na eƒe fetu. " 19 Ne wotso ame tsitsi aɖe nu la, mègaxɔe o, negbe le ɖaseɖila eve alo etɔ̃ ƒe nya nu ko.
ENGLISH: 18 For the text says "You shall not muzzle a threshing beast "; and a worker deserves his pay. 19 Do not accept an accusation against an elder unless on the word of two or three witnesses.

EWE: 20 Ka mo na ame siwo tsɔ nu vɔ̃ wɔwɔ ɖo dɔe la le amewo katã ŋkume, ne ame mamlɛawo nakpɔe ne woavɔ̃.
ENGLISH: 20 Reprove publicly those who sin, in order that the rest may on their part have something to be afraid of.

EWE: 21 Mele eɖom dziwò le Mawu kple Kristo Yesu kpakple mawudɔla tiatiawo ŋkume be, nàlé mɔfiame siawo me ɖe asi nazãbubu kple ameŋkumekpɔkpɔ aɖeke manɔmee.
ENGLISH: 21 I notify you before God and Christ Jesus and the chosen angels to take care of these things without prejudging, not doing anything in the way of favor.

EWE: 22 Mègatsɔ dzitsitsi ada asi ɖe ame aɖeke dzi gbeɖe o; eye mègakpɔ gome le ame bubuwo ƒe nu vɔ̃wo me o; lé ɖokuiwò dzadzɛ.
ENGLISH: 22 Do not be quick to lay hands on anybody, nor share other people’s sins; keep yourself pure.

EWE: 23 Mèganɔ tsi ɖeɖe ko nom o, ke boŋ no wain vi aɖe le wò dɔgbo kple wò lãmegbegblẽ enuenu la ta.
ENGLISH: 23 Do not keep on with water-drinking, but use a little wine on account of your stomach and your frequent illnesses.

EWE: 24 Ame aɖewo ƒe nu vɔ̃wo dzena gaglã, si nana wodrɔ̃a ʋɔnu wo enumake, ke ame aɖewo hã tɔ va dzena emegbe.
ENGLISH: 24 Some men’s sins are obvious, going ahead of them to judgment, and some their sins follow up.

EWE: 25 Nenema kee dɔwɔwɔ nyuiwo hã dzena gaglã, ke esiwo medze o la, mate ŋu anɔ ɣaɣla ɖaa o.
ENGLISH: 25 In the same way good works too are obvious, and such as are otherwise cannot be hidden.

EWE: 1 Timoteo
ENGLISH: 1 Timothy

EWE: 6 Ame siwo le kluvinyenye ƒe kɔkuti te la nayi edzi ade bubu blibo woƒe aƒetɔwo ŋu, be woagagblɔ nya vɔ̃ tso Mawu ƒe ŋkɔ kple nufiafia la ŋu gbeɖe o.
ENGLISH: 6 Let as many as are under a yoke in servitude regard their masters as entitled to all honor, in order that God’s name and the teaching may not be vilified.

EWE: 2 Azɔ hã, ame siwo ƒe aƒetɔwo nye xɔsetɔwo la nagatsɔ wo aba hae le esi wonye nɔviwo ta o. Ke boŋ woalɔ̃ faa asubɔ wo, elabena woƒe dɔ nyui wɔwɔ ɖea vi na ame siwo nye xɔsetɔwo kple lɔlɔ̃tɔwo.
ENGLISH: 2 And let those who have believing masters not be disrespectful to them because they are brothers, but be the more their servants because those who enjoy the benefit are believers and loved ones.

EWE: Enye ame si nyaʋiʋliwo kple glãkahehewo flu tagbɔ na.
ENGLISH: These things teach, and exhort to these.

EWE: Nu siawo hea ŋubiabiã, dzrewɔwɔ, amegɔmezɔzɔ, susu vɔ̃wo bubu ɖe ame ŋu, 5 kple nyahehe ɣesiaɣi le nya maɖinyawo ŋu, siwo ame siwo ƒe susu gblẽ eye nyateƒea to wo ŋu yi la dona ɖe ŋgɔ, ame siwo susuna be ɖokuitsɔtsɔ na Mawu nye viɖedidi ƒe mɔnu. 6 Nyateƒee, ɖokuitsɔtsɔ na Mawu nye viɖenu gã, nenye be nu si le mía si la dzea mía ŋu.
ENGLISH: 3 If one teaches erratic notions and does not apply himself to sound words, those of our Lord Jesus Christ, and to the teaching that is along the line of piety, 4 he is conceit-ridden, not knowing anything, but infatuated about arguments and disputed technicalities, out of which come grudges, quarreling, vilification, base suspicions, 5 frictions between men unsound in mind and bereft of the truth who suppose piety to be an economic resource.

EWE: 7 Elabena míetsɔ naneke va xexea me o, eye míate ŋu atsɔ naneke adzoe hã o. 8 Eya ta ne nuɖuɖu kple nudodo le mía si la, míana nu siawo nadze mía ŋu.
ENGLISH: 6 But a great resource is piety with contentment; 7 for we brought nothing into the world, because neither can we carry anything out; 8 but when we have food to sustain us and coverings to protect us we shall be well enough off.

EWE: 9 Ke ame siwo ɖoe kplikpaa be yewoazu kesinɔtɔwo la gena ɖe tetekpɔ kple mɔ̃tetre kpakple movidzɔdzɔ ƒe nudzodzro geɖe, siwo wɔa nu vevi ame eye wonyrɔa ame ɖe tsɔtsrɔ̃ kple gbegblẽ me la me.
ENGLISH: 9 But those who want to be rich fall into temptation and a trap and many stupid and harmful desires which sink men into destruction and perdition.

EWE: 10 Elabena nu vɔ̃ɖi ƒomeviwo katã ƒe ke ɖekae nye galɔlɔ̃, eye esi ame aɖewo ti lɔlɔ̃ sia yome la, wotra mɔ tso xɔse la gbɔ, eye wotsɔ vevesese geɖe ŋɔ wo ɖokuiwo flofloflo.
ENGLISH: 10 For the love of money is the root of all things bad; hankering for it, some have strayed away from the faith and stabbed themselves with many pains.

EWE: 11 Ke wò la, Oo, Mawu ƒe ame, sí le nu siawo nu. Ke boŋ ti dzɔdzɔenyenye, mawusosroɖa, xɔse, lɔlɔ̃, dzidodo kple tufafa yome.
ENGLISH: 11 But for your part, man of God, keep clear of these things; and aim at honesty, piety, faith, love, constancy, meekness under provocation.

EWE: 12 Ʋli xɔse ƒe ʋiʋli nyui la; na wò asi nasu agbe mavɔ si ta woyɔ wò ɖo eye nèʋu eme nyuie le dutoƒo le ɖasefo geɖewo ŋkume la dzi.
ENGLISH: 12 Play the great game of faith, grasp the eternal life to which you were called and made the good confession before many witnesses.

EWE: 13 Mawu, ame si léa nuwo katã ƒe agbe ɖe te, kple Kristo Yesu, ame si ɖi ɖase heʋu eme nyuie le dutoƒo le Pontio Pilato ŋkume la, ŋkumee mele nu xlɔ̃m wò le 14 be nàwɔ sedede sia dzi kpɔtsɔtsɔ kple mokaka manɔŋui va se ɖe mía Aƒetɔ Yesu Kristo ƒe ɖeɖefiaɣi la, 15 si Ŋusẽtɔ Gã kple dzidzɔtɔ ɖeka kolia la ana amewo nakpɔ adze sii le eya ŋutɔ ƒe ɣeyiɣi ɖoɖi la dzi, eya, ame si nye fiawo katã ƒe Fia kple aƒetɔwo katã ƒe Aƒetɔ la, 16 ame si ko si makumakunyenye le, ame si le kekeli si ŋu womate ŋu ate ɖo o la me, ame si amegbetɔ aɖeke mekpɔ kpɔ alo ate ŋu akpɔ o. Eya tɔ nanye bubu kple ŋusẽ mavɔ. Amen.
ENGLISH: 13 I enjoin you before God who gives everything its life, and Christ Jesus who before Pontius Pilate bore his witness to the good confession, 14 to keep the commandment spotlessly, irreproachably, till the oncoming of our Lord Jesus Christ; 15 which, when the right time comes, the blessed only Potentate will display, the King of all who reign and Lord of all who rule, 16 he who alone has immortality, who inhabits unapproachable light, whom none of men have seen nor can see; to whom belong honor and might eternal; amen.

EWE: 17 Xlɔ̃ nu ame siwo nye kesinɔtɔwo le fifi nuɖoanyi sia me be, woagado wo ɖokuiwo ɖe dzi o, eye woagatsɔ woƒe mɔkpɔkpɔ aziɔ ɖe kesinɔnu siwo dzi womate ŋu aka ɖo o la ŋu o, ke boŋ ɖe Mawu, ame si naa nuwo katã mí fũu be wòado dzidzɔ na mí la ŋu. 18 Gblɔ na wo be woawɔ nyui, woanye kesinɔtɔwo le dɔ nyuiwo wɔwɔ me, woaʋu asi me, woalɔ̃ faa ana nu ame, 19 ale be woadzra kesinɔnu ɖo ɖi dedie na wo ɖokuiwo, wòanye gɔmeɖoanyi nyui na etsɔ si gbɔna, be woƒe asi nasu agbe vavã la dzi.
ENGLISH: 17 Enjoin those who are rich in the present world not to have lofty ideas and not to have their hopes set on uncertainty of wealth, but on God, him who lets us have everything in rich measure to use and enjoy; 18 to practice beneficence, be rich in good works, ready in sharing what they have, loyal in solidarity, 19 laying away for themselves a good foundation toward the future that they may have a hold on the life that is life.

EWE: 20 Timoteo, kpɔ nu si wotsɔ de asiwò la dzi, eye nàgbe dzeɖoɖo ƒuƒlu siwo medea asixɔxɔ nu kɔkɔewo ŋu o, kple nu si woyɔna alakpatɔe be "sidzedze " la ƒe glãkahehewo. 21 Adegbeƒoƒo le sidzedze sia ƒomevi ŋu na ame aɖewo tra mɔ tso xɔse la gbɔ.
ENGLISH: 20 Timothy, safeguard the deposit, turning off from the unsanctified nonsense and counter-propositions of what is miscalled knowledge, 21 which some have promised and therein missed the mark of the faith.

EWE: Mawu ƒe amenuveve nanɔ kpli mi.
ENGLISH: Grace be with you and yours.

EWE: 2 Timoteo
ENGLISH: 2 Timothy

EWE: 1 Paulo, Kristo Yesu ƒe apostolo to Mawu ƒe lɔlɔ̃nu me, le agbe si ŋugbe wodo to Kristo Yesu dzi la nu, 2 le esia ŋlɔm na vinye lɔlɔ̃a Timoteo: Amenuveve, nublanuikpɔkpɔ kple ŋutifafa si tso Mawu, Fofo la, kple Kristo Yesu mía Aƒetɔ gbɔ la, nanɔ kpli wò.
ENGLISH: 1 Paul, apostle of Christ Jesus through God’s will in accordance with the promise that we are to have life in Christ Jesus, 2 to my dear child Timothy: grace, mercy, peace, from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.

EWE: 3 Medaa akpe na Mawu, ame si metsɔ dzitsinya dzadzɛ le subɔsubɔdɔ kɔkɔe wɔm na, abe ale si tɔgbuinyewo wɔe ene, be nyemedzudzɔ ŋkuɖoɖo dziwò le nye kokoƒoƒowo me zã kple keli o. 4 Ne meɖo ŋku wò aɖatsiwo dzi la, edzroam vevie be makpɔ wò, ale be dzidzɔ nayɔm fũu. 5 Elabena meɖoa ŋku wò xɔse si me alakpa mele o, si nɔ mamawò Lois kple dawò Eunike me gbã, eye meka ɖe edzi be ele wò hã mewò, la dzi.
ENGLISH: 3 I thank God, to whom I perform service with a clear conscience as did my fathers, that I keep the mention of you so uninterrupted in my prayers, night and day 4 longing to see you, remembering your tears in order that I may be filled with joy 5 by getting a reminiscence of the unfeigned faith you have in you, which resided first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, and does, I am persuaded, in you too.

EWE: 6 Susu sia tae mele ŋku ɖom edzi na wò be, nàde dzo Mawu ƒe nunana si le mewò si nèxɔ esi meda nye asi ɖe dziwò la me. 7 Elabena Mawu mena vɔvɔ̃gbɔgbɔ mí o, ke ŋusẽ kple lɔlɔ̃ kpakple ŋuɖɔɖo ƒe gbɔgbɔ boŋ.
ENGLISH: 6 For which reason I am reminding you to brighten up the fire of the gift of God which you have in you through the laying on of my hands; 7 for God did not give us a spirit of timorousness but of power and love and discipline.

EWE: 8 Eya ta ŋu megakpe wò le ɖaseɖiɖi le mía Aƒetɔ la ŋu o, alo le nye, ame si nye gamenɔla le eta la ŋuti o, ke boŋ kpe fu le xaxa me faa le nya nyui la ta eye nàɖo ŋu ɖe Mawu ƒe ŋusẽ la ŋu. 9 Eɖe mí, eye wòkpe mí hena ame yɔyɔ kɔkɔe la, menye le míaƒe dɔwɔwɔwo ta o, ke boŋ le eya ŋutɔ ƒe tameɖoɖo kple amenuveve ta.
ENGLISH: 8 So do not be ashamed of testifying to our Lord nor of me his man in prison, but in the hardships of the gospel work take a share appropriate to the power of God, 9 who saved us and gave us a holy call in accordance not with our deeds but with an intent and grace of his own, given to us in Christ Jesus eternities ago 10 but now made apparent by the oncoming of our Savior Christ Jesus, who superseded death and gave the illumination of life and imperishability through the gospel.

EWE: Wona esia mí le Kristo Yesu me tso gbe aɖe gbe ke, 10 ke azɔ la, wona wòdze ƒãa to mía Ðela, Kristo Yesu, ƒe ɖeɖefia la me, ame si ɖe ku ɖa gake wòna kekeli klẽ ɖe agbe kple magblemagblẽ dzi to nya nyui la dzi, 11 nya nyui si ƒe gbeƒãɖela kple apostolo kpakple nufiala woɖom. 12 Esia tae nye hã mele nu siawo ƒe fu kpem ɖo, gake ŋu mekpeam o.
ENGLISH: 11 For which I was appointed a herald and apostle and teacher; 12 for which same cause I am suffering these things; but I am not abashed, for I know him whom I have believed, and am persuaded that he is able to guard for that day what I left in his care.

EWE: 13 Yi edzi nàlé nya siwo le blibo, siwo nèse le gbɔnye kple xɔse kpakple lɔlɔ̃ si le Kristo Yesu me la ƒe kpɔɖeŋu me ɖe asi. 14 Dzra nu nyui sia si míetsɔ de asi na wò to gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔe si le mía me dzi la ɖo nyuie.
ENGLISH: 13 Have an outline of sound words heard from me; in faith and the love that is in Christ Jesus 14 safeguard the good deposit through the Holy Spirit our inmate.

EWE: 15 Ènya esia, be ame siwo katã le Asia nutoa me la trɔ ɖa le ŋunye, ame siwo dome Figelo kple Hermogene hã le.
ENGLISH: 15 You know this, that everybody in the province of Asia turned his back on me; among whom are Phygelus and Hermogenes.

EWE: 16 Aƒetɔ la nekpɔ nublanui na Onesiforo ƒe aƒe la, elabena efa dzi nam enuenu, eye nye kɔsɔkɔsɔwo mekpe ŋu nɛ o. 17 Ke boŋ esi wòva Roma la, eku kutri dim vevie hekpɔm. 18 Aƒetɔ la nena Yehowa nakpɔ nublanui nɛ le ŋkeke ma dzi.
ENGLISH: 16 The Lord grant mercy to Onesiphorus’s family, because he heartened me up over and over, and was not ashamed of my chains 17 but, when he was in Rome, took pains to hunt me up and found me; 18 the Lord grant him to find mercy from the Lord on that day.

EWE: Subɔsubɔdɔ siwo katã wòwɔ le Efeso la, ènya wo nyuie.
ENGLISH: And what services he rendered in Ephesus you know right well.

EWE: 2 Timoteo
ENGLISH: 2 Timothy

EWE: 2 Eya ta vinye, yi edzi nànɔ ŋu sẽm le amenuveve si le Kristo Yesu me la me; 2 eye nu siwo nèse le gbɔnye, siwo dzi ɖasefo geɖewo hã ɖo kpee la, tsɔ nu siawo de asi na nuteƒewɔlawo, ekema woawo hã woadze nyuie afia nu ame bubuwo.
ENGLISH: 2 So for your part, my child, be valiant in the grace that there is in Christ Jesus; 2 and what you heard from me with many witnesses, those things commit to trustworthy men who shall be competent in turn to teach others.

EWE: 3 Esi nènye Kristo Yesu ƒe asrafo nyui ta la, lɔ̃ faa nàkpe fu le xaxa me.
ENGLISH: 3 Take your share of hardships like a good soldier of Christ Jesus.

EWE: 4 Ame si le asrafodɔ wɔm la megaƒoa eɖokui ɖe asitsadɔ siwo amewo wɔna le agbe me la me o, ale be wòadze ame si xɔe ɖe asrafodɔa me la ŋu.
ENGLISH: 4 Everybody in military service keeps clear of entanglement in the businesses of daily life so as to satisfy the one who enlisted him.

EWE: 5 Eye ne ame aɖe le ho ʋlim la, mexɔa dziɖuɖukuku la o, negbe ɖe wòʋli ho la le seawo nu hafi.
ENGLISH: 5 Or if one goes into an athletic contest either, he gets no wreath unless he contends according to the rules.

EWE: 6 Agbledela si doa vevie nu lae atre kutsetseawo ɖuɖu.
ENGLISH: 6 The hardworking husbandman has to be the first to enjoy a part of the crop.

EWE: 7 De ŋugble le nya si gblɔm mele la ŋu ɣeawokatãɣi; Aƒetɔ la ana gɔmesese wò le nuwo katã me.
ENGLISH: 7 Note what I say, for the Lord will give you insight into everything.

EWE: 8 Ðo ŋku edzi be wofɔ Yesu Kristo ɖe tsitre tso ame kukuwo dome, eye wònye David ƒe dzidzimevi, le nya nyui si meɖea gbeƒãe la nu, 9 nya nyui si ta mele fu kpem eye woblam de gae abe nu vɔ̃ wɔla ene ɖo. Gake womebla Mawu ƒe nya la ya o. 10 Esia tae meyi edzi le dzi dom le nu sia nu me le ame tiatiawo ta, be woawo hã woakpɔ ɖeɖe to Kristo Yesu dzi hekpe ɖe ŋutikɔkɔe mavɔ ŋuti.
ENGLISH: 8 Remember Jesus Christ, risen from the dead, a descendant of David, in accordance with my preaching, 9 in which I am having hardships to the extent of imprisonment as a criminal; but God’s word is not imprisoned; 10 for this reason I hold on through everything for the sake of such as are chosen, in order that they too may come in for the salvation that there is in Christ Jesus with eternal glory.

EWE: 11 Nyateƒenyae nya sia nye: Ne míeku kpakplii la, ekema míanɔ agbe hã kpakplii; 12 ne míeyi edzi do dzi la, míaɖu fia hã kpakplii; ne míegbe nu le egbɔ la, eya hã agbe nu le mía gbɔ; 13 ne míenye nuteƒewɔlawo o hã la, eya kpɔtɔ nye nuteƒewɔla, elabena mate ŋu agbe nu le eɖokui gbɔ o.
ENGLISH: 11 The saying is a trustworthy one, "For if we died with him, so shall we live with him; 12 if we are bearing the brunt, so shall we reign with him; if we disown him, so will he disown us; 13 if we are distrustful, he remains trusty, for he cannot disown himself. "

EWE: 14 Yi edzi nànɔ ŋku ɖom nu siawo dzi na wo, eye nàfia wo le Mawu ŋkume be woaganɔ nyaʋa wɔm o, elabena meɖea vi aɖeke o, ke boŋ egblẽa nu le ame siwo senɛ la ŋu.
ENGLISH: 14 Remind people of these things, admonishing them before God not to wrangle over technicalities to no useful purpose, upsetting the listeners.

EWE: 15 Wɔ wò ŋutete ɖe sia ɖe nàɖe ɖokuiwò afia Mawu abe ame si dze eŋu, dɔwɔla si ƒe dɔ mekpea ŋu nɛ le mɔ aɖeke nu o, ame si wɔa nyateƒenya la ŋu dɔ pɛpɛpɛ ene. 16 Ke gbe dzeɖoɖo ƒuƒlu makɔmakɔwo, elabena ɖeko woana mawumavɔmavɔ̃ naxɔ aƒe ɖi geɖe wu, 17 eye woƒe nya la akeke ta abe abi vɔ̃ ene. Himenayo kple Fileto le ame siawo dome.
ENGLISH: 15 Make a point of presenting yourself to God tried and true, a worker with nothing to be ashamed of, keeping the straight line of the word of truth; 16 but stand away from outpourings of unsanctified nonsense; for they will go further in irreligiousness, 17 and their talk will spread like a gangrene, among whom are Hymenaeus and Philetus, 18 who missed the mark of truth, saying that there has already been a resurrection, and are wrecking some people’s faith.

EWE: 18 Ame siawo tra mɔ tso nyateƒe la gbɔ hele gbɔgblɔm be tsitretsitsia va yi xoxo, eye wotrɔa ame aɖewo ƒe xɔse bua anyi. 19 Ke hã, Mawu ƒe gɔmeɖoanyi sesẽ la li ke, eye woɖe nuŋɔŋlɔ sia ɖe eŋu be: "Yehowa nya ame siwo nye etɔwo, " eye: "Ame sia ame si yɔa Yehowa ƒe ŋkɔ la, nete ɖa le nu madzɔmadzɔ wɔwɔ gbɔ. " 20 Ke le aƒe gã me la, menye sikanuwo kple klosalonuwo ɖeɖe koe li o, ke boŋ atinuwo kple anyinuwo hã li, ɖewo li na nu si ŋu bubu le, ke ɖewo hã li na nu si ŋu bubu mele o.
ENGLISH: 19 However, God’s solid foundation still stands, having this seal, "The Lord knows the ones that belong to him " and "Let everybody who names the Lord’s name keep clear of wrong. " 20 And in a great house there is not only gold and silver ware but also woodenware and crockery, and some pieces destined for honor, some for ignominy; 21 so if one cleans himself out from these things he will be a piece for honor, consecrated, useful to the owner, prepared for every good work.

EWE: 22 Eya ta si le sɔhɛmenɔɣi ƒe nudzodzrowo nu, ke boŋ ti dzɔdzɔenyenye, xɔse, lɔlɔ̃ kple ŋutifafa yome hekpe ɖe ame siwo yɔa Aƒetɔ la tso dzi dzadzɛ me la ŋu.
ENGLISH: 22 But tear yourself away from the desires of youth, and aim at righteousness, faith, love, peace, with those who call on the Lord out of a pure heart.

EWE: 23 Eye gbe bometsinyahehe siwo me susu aɖeke mele o, elabena ènyae be dzre ko wohena vanɛ. 24 Elabena mele be Aƒetɔ la ƒe kluvi nawɔ dzre o, ke boŋ wòafa tu na amewo katã, wòanya nufiafia, wòaɖu eɖokui dzi ne wowɔ vɔ̃ ɖe eŋu, 25 wòafia nu tsitretsiɖeŋulawo le tufafa me; elabena ɖewohĩ Mawu ana woatrɔ dzi me ava nyateƒe ƒe sidzedze vavãtɔ gbɔ, 26 eye woanyɔ le wo ɖokuiwo me ado le Abosam ƒe mɔ̃tetre me, esi wokpɔe be ɖe wòlé yewo agbagbee hena eƒe lɔlɔ̃nu wɔwɔ ta.
ENGLISH: 23 But try to keep out of foolish and half-educated arguments, knowing that they breed quarrels; 24 and a servant of the Lord’s must not quarrel but be gentle toward everybody, a good teacher, a man to put up with hard treatment, 25 educating opponents by mild methods in case God should give them repentance into recognition of the truth 26 and they should sober up out of the Devil’s trap, captured by him, into His will.

EWE: 2 Timoteo
ENGLISH: 2 Timothy

EWE: 3 Ke nya esia be le ŋkeke mamlɛawo me la, ɣeyiɣi sesẽ siwo me nɔnɔ asesẽ la ava. 2 Elabena amewo anye ɖokuilɔ̃lawo, galɔ̃lawo, adegbeƒolawo, dadalawo, busunyagblɔlawo, ame maɖoto dzilawo, ame madakpewo, ame mawɔnuteƒewo, 3 ame siwo melɔ̃a ame ƒe nya o, ame siwo melɔ̃na ɖe ɖoɖo aɖeke dzi o, ameŋugblẽlawo, ame siwo meɖua wo ɖokuiwo dzi o, ame wɔadãwo, ame siwo melɔ̃a nu nyui o, 4 yomemɔfialawo, totrilawo, ame siwo doa wo ɖokuiwo ɖe dzi glodzoo, ame siwo lɔ̃a dzidzɔkpɔkpɔ le esi teƒe be woalɔ̃ Mawu, 5 ame siwo ŋu ɖokuitsɔtsɔ na Mawu ƒe nɔnɔme dzena le, gake womenana wòkpɔa ŋusẽ ɖe woƒe agbe dzi o; te ɖokuiwò ɖa tso ame siawo gbɔ.
ENGLISH: 3 But know this, that in the last days difficult times will come on; 2 for men will be selfish, money-mad, pretentious, proud, scurrilous, disobedient to parents, thankless, graceless, 3 loveless, implacable, slanderers, slaves of appetite, ferocious, disinclined to goodness, 4 traitorous, headstrong, conceited, more devoted to pleasure than to God, 5 having a formulation of piety but denying its efficacy; eschew these too.

EWE: 6 Elabena ame siawo dometɔ aɖewo bena dzaa gena ɖe aƒewo me heɖea aboyo nyɔnu gbɔdzɔgbɔdzɔtɔ siwo nu vɔ̃ do agba na eye nudzodzro vovovowo hea wo la, 7 eye ame siawo nɔa nusɔsrɔ̃ dzi ɣesiaɣi, evɔ wometea ŋu kena ɖe nyateƒe ƒe sidzedze vavãtɔ la ŋu hã gbeɖe o.
ENGLISH: 6 For to this class belong those who slip into houses and get into their hands females loaded up with sins, led along by miscellaneous desires, 7 always learning and never able to come to awareness of truth.

EWE: 8 Ke ale si Yane kple Yambre tsi tsitre ɖe Mose ŋui la, nenema kee ame siawo hã le tsitre tsim ɖe nyateƒe la ŋu. Ame siawo ƒe susu gblẽ keŋkeŋ, eye woƒe nu medze Mawu ŋu le xɔse la me o. 9 Ke womagate ŋu ayi ŋgɔ o, elabena woƒe movidzɔdzɔ la adze gaglã na amewo katã, abe ale si ko ame eve mawo tɔ dzee ene.
ENGLISH: 8 And in just the same way as Jannes and Jambres opposed themselves to Moses these too oppose themselves to the truth, men of ruined mind, incompetent for matters of faith; 9 but they will make no further progress, for their senselessness will be evident to everybody, just as those men’s came to be.

EWE: 10 Ke wò la, èdze nye nufiafia, nye agbenɔnɔ, nye tameɖoɖo, nye xɔse, nye dzigbɔgbɔ blewu, nye lɔlɔ̃ kple nye dzidodo yome pɛpɛpɛ, 11 eye nènya nu tso yometiti kple fu siwo tɔgbi mekpe le Antiokia, Ikonio kple Listra la ŋu.
ENGLISH: 10 But you observed my teaching, conduct, purpose, faith, patience, love, steadiness, 11 persecutions, sufferings, what things happened to me at Antioch, at lconium, at Lystra, what persecutions I underwent and the Lord delivered me out of all.

EWE: Medo dzi le yometiti siawo me, eye Aƒetɔ la ɖem tso wo katã me. 12 Le nyateƒe me la, ame siwo katã dina be yewoanɔ agbe ɖe ɖokuitsɔtsɔ na Mawu nu le Kristo Yesu me la, woati woawo hã yome tsã.
ENGLISH: 12 And all who propose to live piously in Christ Jesus will also be persecuted; 13 but scoundrels and impostors will make progress for the worse, misguiding and misguided.

EWE: 14 Ke wò la, nɔ nu siwo nèsrɔ̃, eye nèkpɔ kakaɖedzi le wo ŋu hexɔ wo dzi se la me, elabena ènya ame siwo gbɔ nèsrɔ̃ wo le, 15 eye be tso ɖevime kee nènya ŋɔŋlɔ kɔkɔeawo, siwo ate ŋu ana nàdze nunya hena ɖeɖekpɔkpɔ to Kristo Yesu dzixɔse me.
ENGLISH: 14 But as for you, remain in what you learned and were given assurance of, knowing from whom you learned it 15 and that ever since you were a baby you have known sacred literature such as could give you the wisdom for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.

EWE: 16 Ŋɔŋlɔ blibo la tso Mawu ƒe gbɔgbɔ me, eye wònyo na nufiafia, na mokaka, na ɖɔɖɔɖo, na amehehe le dzɔdzɔenyenye me, 17 ale be Mawu ƒe ame la nadze bliboe, eye wòanɔ dzadzraɖoɖi keŋkeŋ na dɔ nyui sia dɔ nyui wɔwɔ.
ENGLISH: 16 Every text is inspired by God and useful for teaching, for reproof, for correction, for training in doing right, 17 in order that the man of God may be a whole man, rounded out to fitness for every good work.

EWE: 2 Timoteo
ENGLISH: 2 Timothy

EWE: 4 Mele eɖom dziwò le Mawu kple Kristo Yesu, ame si woɖo be wòadrɔ̃ ʋɔnu agbagbeawo kple kukuawo la ŋkume, to eƒe ɖeɖefia kple Fiaɖuƒe la dzi be, 2 ɖe gbeƒã nya la, nɔ edzi vevie, le ɣeyiɣi deamedziwo kple ɣeyiɣi madeamedziwo me, ka mo, gbe nya, xlɔ̃ nu le dzigbɔgbɔ blewu kple nufiafiaɖaŋu me.
ENGLISH: 4 I notify you before God and Christ Jesus who is to judge living men and dead men, and by his oncoming and his reign, 2 proclaim the word; push in with a good opening or without, reprove, rebuke, exhort, with all patience and along every line of teaching.

EWE: 3 Elabena ɣeyiɣi le vava ge esime womalɔ̃ ɖe nufiafia nyuitɔ la dzi o, ke boŋ le woawo ŋutɔwo ƒe nudzodzrowo nu la, woaƒo nufialawo nu ƒu na wo ɖokuiwo, be woalũ to me na wo. 4 Woaɖe to ɖa le nyateƒe la ŋu, eye woatrɔ ɖe gliwo ŋu.
ENGLISH: 3 For there will be a time when they will not stand sound teaching, but to suit their own desires will pile up teachers for themselves as they get their ears tickled, 4 and avert their ears from the truth and turn off to the fictions.

EWE: 5 Ke wò la, nɔ mo xexi le nuwo katã me, do dzi le nɔnɔme sesẽwo me, wɔ nya nyui gbɔgblɔ dɔ, wɔ wò subɔsubɔdɔ la bliboe.
ENGLISH: 5 But for your part be sober in every respect, bear hardships, do a gospel preacher’s work, do your service thoroughly.

EWE: 6 Elabena wotrɔm le kɔkɔm ɖi abe nunovɔsa ene xoxo, eye asiɖeɖe le ŋunye ƒe ɣeyiɣi la gogo.
ENGLISH: 6 For as for me, I am a cup that is already being poured on the sacrifice, and it is almost time for me to be getting away.

EWE: 8 Tso esia dzi la, wodzra dzɔdzɔenyenye ƒe dziɖuɖukuku la ɖo ɖi nam, si Aƒetɔ la si nye ʋɔnudrɔ̃la dzɔdzɔe la, atsɔ aɖo eteƒe nam le ŋkeke ma dzi, ke menye na nye ɖeɖe ko o, ke boŋ na ame siwo katã lɔ̃ eƒe ɖeɖefia la hã.
ENGLISH: 7 I have played the great game, I have run the race through, I have kept the faith: 8 what is left is that I have awaiting me the wreath of righteousness, which the Lord, the just judge, will deliver to me on that day.

EWE: 9 Dze agbagba ɖe sia ɖe nàva gbɔnye kaba.
ENGLISH: And not only to me but also to all who have been in love with his oncoming.

EWE: 10 Elabena Dema gblẽm ɖi le esi wòlɔ̃ fifi nuɖoanyi sia ta, eye wòdzo yi Tesalonika; Kreske yi Galatia, Tito yi Dalmatia. 11 Luka ɖeɖe koe le gbɔnye.
ENGLISH: 9 Try hard to come to me right off; 10 for Demas left me in the lurch, falling in love with the present world, and went to Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia; Titus to Dalmatia; 11 Luke is the only one with me.

EWE: Kplɔ Marko ɖe asi vɛ, elabena enye kpeɖeŋutɔ nyui aɖe nam le subɔsubɔdɔ la me.
ENGLISH: Pick up Mark and bring him with you, for he is valuable to me for errands.

EWE: 12 Ke medɔ Tikiko ɖe Efeso.
ENGLISH: 12 And Tychicus I sent to Ephesus.

EWE: 13 Ne ègbɔna la, tsɔ awu ʋlaya si megblẽ ɖe Troa ɖe Karpo gbɔ kple agbalẽawo, vevietɔ esiwo wowɔ kple lãgbalẽ, ɖe asi vɛ.
ENGLISH: 13 When you come bring the poncho I left at Troas with Carpus, and the books, especially the parchments.

EWE: 14 Aleksandro, akɔblinutula la, wɔ nu vevi geɖem. Yehowa aɖo eteƒe nɛ ɖe eƒe nuwɔnawo nu.
ENGLISH: 14 Alexander the coppersmith injured me in many ways; the Lord will repay him in accordance with his deeds.

EWE: 15 Wò hã kpɔ ɖokuiwò dzi nyuie le eŋu, elabena etsi tsitre ɖe míaƒe gbedeasia ŋu vevie ŋutɔ.
ENGLISH: 15 Be on your guard against him yourself, for he opposed our words much.

EWE: 16 Le ɖokuinye ta ʋiʋli gbãtɔ me la, ame aɖeke mede dzinye o, ke boŋ wo katã wogblẽm ɖi Mawu megabu esia na wo vevie o.
ENGLISH: 16 At my first defense nobody rallied to me, everybody left me in the lurch; may it not be counted against them.

EWE: 17 Ke Aƒetɔ la tsi tsitre ɖe gbɔnye, eye wòdo ŋusẽm, ale be woawɔ gbeƒãɖeɖedɔ la ade goe to dzinye, ne dukɔwo katã nasee; eye woɖem tso dzata ƒe nu me.
ENGLISH: 17 But the Lord stood by me and put power into me in order that through me the proclamation might be consummated and all the nations might hear, and I was rescued out of a lion’s mouth.

EWE: 18 Aƒetɔ la aɖem tso vɔ̃wo katã me, eye wòaxɔm ɖe eƒe Fiaɖuƒe si le dziƒo la me. Eya tɔ nanye ŋutikɔkɔe tso mavɔ me yi mavɔ me.
ENGLISH: 18 The Lord will rescue me out of the way of every deed of evil and will save me into his heavenly kingdom; to whom be glory forever and ever.

EWE: Amen.
ENGLISH: Amen.

EWE: 19 Do gbe na Priskila kple Akwila kpakple Onesiforo ƒe aƒe la nam.
ENGLISH: 19 Give my greetings to Prisca and Aquila and Onesiphorus’s family.

EWE: 20 Erasto tsi Korinto, ke megblẽ Trofimo ɖe Mileto, elabena ele dɔ lém.
ENGLISH: 20 Erastus stayed at Corinth; and Trophimus I left at Miletus sick.

EWE: 21 Dze agbagba ɖe sia ɖe nàva ɖo hafi vuvɔŋɔli naɖo.
ENGLISH: 21 Try hard to come before winter.

EWE: Eubulo do gbe na wò, eye Pude, Lino, Klaudia kple nɔviawo katã hã do gbe na wò.
ENGLISH: Eubulus sends you greetings, and Pudens and Linus and Claudia and all the brothers.

EWE: 22 Aƒetɔ la nenɔ anyi kple gbɔgbɔ si nèɖena fiana la.
ENGLISH: 22 The Lord be with your spirit.

EWE: Eƒe amenuveve nanɔ kpli mi.
ENGLISH: Grace be with you and yours.

EWE: Tito
ENGLISH: Titus

EWE: 1 Paulo, Mawu ƒe kluvi kple Yesu Kristo ƒe apostolo, le Mawu ƒe ame tiatiawo ƒe xɔse kple nyateƒe la ƒe sidzedze vavãtɔ le ɖokuitsɔtsɔ na Mawu nu, 2 si wotu ɖe agbe mavɔ ƒe mɔkpɔkpɔ si ƒe ŋugbe Mawu, ame si mate ŋu aka aʋatso o la, do tso gbe aɖe gbe ʋĩi ke la dzi; 3 esi wòna wonya eƒe nya la le eya ŋutɔ ƒe ɣeyiɣi dzi to gbeƒãɖeɖedɔ si wode asi nam la dzi le Mawu, mía Xɔla, ƒe sedede la nu; 4 le esia ŋlɔm ɖo ɖe Tito, vinye vavã si le xɔse ɖeka me kplim: Amenuveve kple ŋutifafa si tso Mawu Fofo la kple Kristo Yesu mía Ðela gbɔ la nanɔ kpli wò.
ENGLISH: 1 Paul, servant of God, and Jesus Christ’s delegate for the matter of the faith of God’s chosen and their awareness of truth along the line of piety 2 in the hope of eternal life, which God, who has no falsehoods, promised ages ago 3 but disclosed his word at the right time by a proclamation with which I was entrusted by order of God our savior, 4 to Titus my very own child by common faith, grace and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Savior.

EWE: 5 Megblẽ wò ɖe Kreta be nàɖɔ nu siwo gblẽ la ɖo, eye nàɖo hamemetsitsiwo tso du me yi du me, abe ale si meɖoe na wò ene be: 6 ne ame aɖe li, si ŋu nutsotso aɖeke mele o, ame si nye nyɔnu ɖeka srɔ̃, ame si si vi xɔsetɔ siwo nu wometso ɖe agbe baɖa nɔnɔ alo aglãdzedze ta o la le.
ENGLISH: 5 I left you in Crete for this purpose, to have you straighten out what remained to be seen to and appoint elders in the different cities as I directed you 6 anyone who is of blameless reputation, husband of one wife, having believing children not under accusations of debauchery nor insubordinate.

EWE: 7 Elabena abe Mawu ƒe aƒedzikpɔla ene la, ele be dzikpɔla nanye ame si ŋu nutsotso aɖeke mele o, wòaganye ɖokuiŋudzela o, wòaganye ame si doa dɔmedzoe kabakaba o, wòaganye ahamula o, wòaganye ŋutasẽla o, wòaganye ame si klẽa ŋu ɖe viɖe ƒoɖi kpɔkpɔ ŋu o, 8 ke boŋ wòanye amedzrowɔla, nu nyui lɔ̃la, ame ɖɔŋuɖo, ame dzɔdzɔe, nuteƒewɔla, ɖokuidziɖula, 9 ame si léna ɖe nyateƒenya la ŋu goŋgoŋ le eƒe nufiafiaɖaŋu me, ale be wòatsɔ nufiafia si le blibo la ade dzi ƒo na ame eye wòaka mo na ɖeklemiɖelawo.
ENGLISH: 7 For the church visitor must be of blameless reputation as God’s steward, not high and mighty, not hot-tempered, not disorderly over his wine, not apt to come to blows, not mercenary, 8 but hospitable, loving whatever is good, discreet, honest, godly, master of his appetites, 9 in touch with the trustworthy ideas that agree with the teaching, in order that he may be able both to exhort in sound instruction and to confute opponents.

EWE: 10 Elabena aglãdzelawo, nya dzodzro gblɔlawo kple ameblela geɖewoe li, vevietɔ wo dometɔ siwo lé aʋatsotso ƒe nufiafia la me ɖe asi. 11 Ehiã be woatsi nya ɖe ame siawo nu, elabena woyi edzi le ƒome blibowo ƒe susu trɔm tu, to nu siwo medze be woafia o la fiafia me le viɖe ƒoɖi ta.
ENGLISH: 10 For there are many, insubordinate gabblers and delusionists, especially those of the circumcision, 11 whom one must silence, people who wreck whole families, teaching from mercenary motives what ought not to be taught.

EWE: 12 Wo dometɔ ɖeka, si nye woawo ŋutɔwo ƒe nyagblɔɖila aɖe, gblɔ be: "Kretatɔwo nye aʋatsokalawo ɖaa, lã wɔadã vɔ̃ɖiwo, nu tsu ɖula kuviatɔwo. "
ENGLISH: 12 One of them, a prophet of their very own, said

EWE: 13 Ðaseɖiɖi sia nye nyateƒe.
ENGLISH: "The Cretans, ever liars, vile cattle, idle maws. " 13 This testimony is a true one.

EWE: Le susu sia tututu ta la, yi edzi nànɔ mo kam na wo vevie, ne woanɔ te sesĩe le xɔse la me, 14 be woaganɔ to ɖom Yudatɔwo ƒe gliwo kple ame siwo trɔ le nyateƒe la yome ƒe sededewo o.
ENGLISH: For which reason show up their errors rigorously in order that they may be sound in the faith, 14 not giving their attention to Jewish fictions and the commandments of human beings who turn their backs on the truth.

EWE: 15 Nuwo katã le dzadzɛ na ame dzadzɛwo; ke ame ƒoɖiwo kple dzimaxɔsetɔwo ya la, naneke mele dzadzɛ na wo o, elabena woƒe susu kple dzitsinya siaa ƒo ɖi.
ENGLISH: 15 Everything is clean for clean men; but for polluted unbelievers nothing is clean, but both their mind and their conscience are polluted.

EWE: 16 Woʋua eme be yewonya Mawu, ke wotsɔa woƒe nuwɔnawo ɖenɛ fiana be yewogbe nu le egbɔ, elabena wonye ame nyɔŋuwo kple tosẽlawo, eye womedze na dɔ nyui aɖeke wɔwɔ o.
ENGLISH: 16 They avow that they know God, but in their acts they disavow it, being abominated and disobedient and worthless for any good purpose.

EWE: Tito
ENGLISH: Titus

EWE: 2 Ŋutsu tsitsiwo nada asɔ le nuwɔna me, woalé fɔ ɖe nu ŋu, woaɖɔ ŋu ɖo, woasẽ ŋu le xɔse me, le lɔlɔ̃ me, le dzidodo me. 3 Nenema kee nyɔnu tsitsiwo hã nawɔ nu le mawuvɔvɔ̃ me, woaganye ameŋugblẽlawo o, eye woaganye aha geɖe nolawo hã o, woanye nu nyui fialawo, 4 ne woaxlɔ̃ nu ɖetugbuiwo be woalɔ̃ wo srɔ̃wo, woalɔ̃ wo viwo, 5 woanye ame ɖɔŋuɖowo, agbe dzadzɛ nɔlawo, aƒemedɔwɔlawo, nyuiwɔlawo, ame siwo bɔbɔa wo ɖokuiwo na woawo ŋutɔwo srɔ̃wo, ale be woagagblɔ nya vlo ɖe Mawu ƒe nya la ŋu o.
ENGLISH: 2 But as for you, speak what is appropriate to sound teaching: 2 that aged men be sober, dignified, discreet, sound in faith, in love, in constancy; 3 aged women, in the same way, saintlike in demeanor, not scandalmongers nor slaves to drink, good advisers 4 in order that they may train the young women to be affectionate to their husbands, affectionate to their children, 5 discreet, pure, homemakers, kind, submissive to their husbands, in order that God’s word may not be made a butt for vilification.

EWE: 6 Nenema kee yi edzi nànɔ nu xlɔ̃m ɖekakpuiwo be woaɖɔ ŋu ɖo; 7 nàɖo kpɔɖeŋu nyui le dɔ nyuiwo wɔwɔ me le nu sia nu me. Fia nu si dza la moveviɖoɖotɔe, 8 na wò nuƒoƒo nanyo, ale be woagakpɔ nya aɖeke le eŋu agblɔ o; ale be ŋu nakpe tsitretsiɖeŋulawo le esi womekpɔ nya gbegblẽ aɖeke agblɔ le mía ŋu o ta. 9 Kluviwo nabɔbɔ wo ɖokuiwo na woƒe aƒetɔwo le nu sia nu me, woadze agbagba adze woƒe aƒetɔwo ŋu, eye woaganɔ nya hem kpli wo o, 10 woaganɔ wo fim o, ke boŋ woanye ame siwo dzi woate ŋu aka ɖo bliboe, ale be woaɖo atsyɔ̃ na Mawu, mía Xɔla, ƒe nufiafia la le nu sia nu me. 11 Elabena Mawu ɖe eƒe amenuveve fia, eye esia hea ɖeɖekpɔkpɔ vɛ na ame ƒomeviwo katã.
ENGLISH: 6 In the same way exhort the younger men to be discreet about everything, 7 setting an example of good works yourself, presenting in your teaching untaintedness, dignity, 8 irreprovable sound words, in order that he who takes the opposite side may be shamed by not having anything harsh to say about us; 9 servants to be submissive to their masters in everything, to be pleasant, not talking back, 10 not purloining but showing all good faithfulness, in order that they may in every respect adorn the teaching of God our savior.

EWE: 12 Esia fia mí be míatsri mawumavɔmavɔ̃ kple xexea me nudzodzrowo, eye be míanɔ agbe le ŋuɖɔɖo kple dzɔdzɔenyenye kpakple ɖokuitsɔtsɔ na Mawu me le fifi nuɖoanyi sia me, 13 esime míele dzidzɔmɔkpɔkpɔ kple Mawu gã la kpakple mía Ðela Yesu Kristo ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe ƒe ɖeɖefia la lalam, 14 ame si tsɔ eɖokui na ɖe mía ta, be wòaɖe mí tso sedzimawɔmawɔ ɖe sia ɖe me, eye wòakɔ dukɔ si nye eya ŋutɔ tɔ, si le tɔxɛ nɛ, si doa vevie nu le dɔ nyuiwo wɔwɔ me, la ŋu na eɖokui.
ENGLISH: 11 For God’s grace has come on the scene with salvation for all men, 12 schooling us to disown impiety and mundane desires and live discreetly and honestly and piously in the present world, 13 watching for the blessed hope and oncoming of the glory of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ, 14 who gave himself for us to redeem us from all wickedness and cleanse for himself a people specially his own, zealous for good works.

EWE: 15 Yi edzi nànɔ nya siawo gblɔm, eye nàxlɔ̃ nu ahaka mo le ŋusẽ blibo si wona wò la nu. Mègana ame aɖeke nado vlo wò o.
ENGLISH: 15 Speak these things and exhort to them and see to people’s conformity to them, with all imperativeness; let nobody make light of you.

EWE: Tito
ENGLISH: Titus

EWE: 3 Yi edzi nànɔ ŋku ɖom edzi na wo be woabɔbɔ wo ɖokuiwo na dziɖuɖuwo kple ŋusẽtɔwo, eye woaɖo to wo, eye woanɔ dzadzraɖoɖi na dɔ nyui sia dɔ nyui wɔwɔ, 2 be woagagblɔ nya vɔ̃ ɖe ame aɖeke ŋu o, woaganye dzrewɔlawo o, ke boŋ woanye nugɔmeselawo, woafa tu na amewo katã.
ENGLISH: 3 Remind them to be submissive and obedient to governments and authorities, to be ready for every good work, 2 to vilify nobody, to keep out of fights, to be reasonable and show all gentleness toward all men.

EWE: 3 Elabena tsã la, míawo hã míenye movitɔwo, tosẽlawo, ame siwo tra mɔ, nudzodzro kple vivisese vovovowo ƒe kluviwo, míenɔ nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ kple ŋubiabiã dzi, eye míenye ame nyɔŋuwo kple ame siwo léa fu wo nɔewo. 4 Ke esi Mawu, mía Xɔla la ɖe eƒe dɔmenyonyo kple ale si wòlɔ̃ ameƒomea ɖe go la, 5 eɖe mí (menye le dzɔdzɔenyenyedɔ si míawo míewɔ la ta o, ke boŋ le eƒe nublanuikpɔkpɔ ta), to tsilename si na agbe mí kple mía wɔwɔ yeyee to gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔe me la me. 6 Ekɔ gbɔgbɔ sia ɖe mía dzi fũu to Yesu Kristo, mía Ðela la dzi, 7 ale be esi wobu mí ame dzɔdzɔewoe to eƒe amenuveve me vɔ la, míazu domenyilawo le agbe mavɔ ƒe mɔkpɔkpɔ la nu.
ENGLISH: 3 For we ourselves were once stupid, disobedient, drifters, in servitude to varied desires and pleasures, leading a life of viciousness and envy, odious, hating each other; 4 but when kindness and goodwill came on from our savior God, 5 not as the outcome of deeds in righteousness that we did but in the way of his mercy he saved us by the bath of rebirth and renovation by the Holy Spirit, 6 which he poured out on us richly through Jesus Christ our Savior, 7 in order that being justified by his grace we might become heirs with hope of eternal life.

EWE: 8 Kakaɖedzi le nya siawo ŋu, eye medi be nàte gbe ɖe nya siawo dzi ɣesiaɣi ale be ame siwo xɔ Mawu dzi se la ƒe susu nanɔ dɔ nyuiwo wɔwɔ ŋu. Nu siawo nyo, eye viɖe le wo ŋu na ame.
ENGLISH: 8 The saying is a trustworthy one, and about these things I want you to be positive, in order that those who have believed God may take care to practice good works.

EWE: 9 Ke mègade nu bometsinyawo ʋiʋli kple dzidzimewo xexlẽ fia kple nyahehewo kpakple dzrewɔwɔ me le Se la ŋu o, elabena womeɖea vi aɖeke o, eye wonye nu dzodzrowo.
ENGLISH: These things are good and useful to men; 9 but stand away from foolish arguments and tracings of genealogies and quarreling and fights over the law, for they are useless and futile.

EWE: 10 Ne èxlɔ̃ nu ame si doa kɔmama ɖe ŋgɔ zi gbãtɔ kple zi evelia vɔ la, nàgbe nu le egbɔ, 11 nyae be ame sia tra mɔ, eye wòle nu vɔ̃ wɔm hebu fɔ eɖokui.
ENGLISH: 10 Have nothing more to do with a troublemaker after one and a second admonition, 11 knowing that such a man is perverted and is sinning when he is self-condemned.

EWE: 12 Ne medɔ Artemas alo Tikiko ɖe gbɔwò la, dze agbagba ɖe sia ɖe nàva gbɔnye le Nikopoli, elabena afi mae meɖo be manɔ le vuvɔŋɔli la.
ENGLISH: 12 When I send Artemas to you, or Tychicus, try to come to me promptly at Nicopolis; for I have decided to be there through the winter.

EWE: 13 Wɔ nu sia nu si nàte ŋui adi nu siwo katã Zena, ame si nya Se la nyuie, kple Apolo hiã la na wo ale be naneke nagahiã wo le woƒe mɔzɔzɔa me o.
ENGLISH: 13 Give Zenas the legist and Apollos your best send-off so that they shall have no lack of anything.

EWE: 14 Ke na míaƒe amewo hã nasrɔ̃ ale si woanɔ dɔ nyuiwo wɔwɔ dzi, ale be woate ŋu akpɔ woƒe nuhiahiã veviwo gbɔ, ne woagazu ame matsekuwo o.
ENGLISH: 14 And let our people also learn to practice good works for occasions of emergency, so that they may not be unfruitful.

EWE: 15 Ame siwo katã le gbɔnye la do gbe na wò.
ENGLISH: 15 All who are with me send you greetings.

EWE: Do gbe na ame siwo katã lɔ̃ mí le xɔse la me nam.
ENGLISH: Give my greetings to those who love us in faith.

EWE: Mawu ƒe amenuveve nanɔ kpli mi katã.
ENGLISH: Grace be with you all.

EWE: Filemon
ENGLISH: Philemon

EWE: 1 Paulo, ame si le ga me le Kristo Yesu ta, kple mía nɔvi Timoteo le esia ŋlɔm na Filemon, míaƒe hadɔwɔla lɔlɔ̃a, 2 kple mía nɔvinyɔnu Apia kple mía hatisrafo Arkipo kpakple hame si le aƒewò me: 3 Amenuveve kple ŋutifafa si tso Mawu mía Fofo kple Aƒetɔ Yesu Kristo gbɔ la, nanɔ kpli mi.
ENGLISH: 1 Paul, Christ Jesus’s man in prison, and Brother Timothy, to our dearly loved friend and co-worker Philemon 2 and Sister Apphia and our fellow-soldier Archippus and the meeting at your house: 3 grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

EWE: 4 Medaa akpe na nye Mawu ɣesiaɣi si meyɔ ŋkɔwò le nye gbedodoɖawo me, 5 esi meyi edzi le wò xɔse kple lɔlɔ̃ si le asiwò ɖe Aƒetɔ Yesu kple ame kɔkɔewo katã ŋu la ŋuti nya sem ta. 6 Mele gbe dom ɖa be wò xɔse si me nèlé ɖe asi naʋã wò nàlɔ̃ ɖe nu nyui sia nu nyui si su mía si to Kristo dzi la dzi.
ENGLISH: 4 I always thank my God as I make mention of you in my prayers, 5 hearing of the love and faith you cherish toward the Lord Jesus and to all the people of God, 6 that your solidarity in the faith may take effect in the knowledge of every good thing that there is in us toward Christ.

EWE: 7 Elabena nɔviŋutsu, mekpɔ dzidzɔ kple akɔfafa geɖe esi mese wò lɔlɔ̃ ŋu nya, elabena èna ame kɔkɔewo ƒe dzi dze eme.
ENGLISH: 7 For I felt great gladness and encouragement over your love, because the hearts of God’s people have been set at rest through you, brother.

EWE: 8 Le susu sia tututu ta, togbɔ be mekpɔ mɔ le Kristo me agblɔe na wò kã be nàwɔ nu si sɔ hã la, 9 le lɔlɔ̃ ta, medi be maɖe kuku na wò boŋ.
ENGLISH: 8 Wherefore, though I have in Christ plenty of claim to enjoin you to do the right thing, 9 for love’s sake I prefer to appeal to your goodwill.

EWE: 12 Megbugbɔ le eɖom ɖe wò, ɛ̃, eya, ame si nye nye ŋutɔ nye dzi. 13 Madi be mana wòanɔ gbɔnye, ale be wòayi edzi anɔ subɔyem ɖe tewòƒe le nye gaxɔmenɔnɔ me le nya nyui la ta hafi. 14 Ke nyemedi be mawɔ naneke ne mèda asi ɖe edzi hafi o, ale be nu nyui si nàwɔ la naganye le dzizizi ta o, ke boŋ wòanye esi wò ŋutɔ nèlɔ̃ faa be yeawɔ.
ENGLISH: Being such as I am, Paul, an old man and now a prisoner for Jesus Christ besides, 10 I am appealing to you about my child who has been born to me in my chains, Onesimus, 11 the one who was once good for nothing for you but is now good for a great deal both for you and for me; 12 whom I am sending back to you, him who is the heart of my heart 13 whom I wanted to retain with me in order that he might take your place in doing services for me during my imprisonment for the gospel; 14 but I was not willing to do anything without word from you, in order that your goodness might not be in a sense compulsory but in a voluntary way.

EWE: 15 Ðewohĩ esia tututu tae wòdzo le gbɔwò ɣeyiɣi vi aɖe ɖo, ale be wòagbugbɔ ava nɔ gbɔwò tegbee, 16 meganye kluvi ko o, ke boŋ ede ŋgɔ wu kluvi, ezu nɔvi lɔlɔ̃tɔ, vevietɔ na nye ŋutɔ, ke ezu esia na wò ya geɖe wu le ŋutilã me kple Aƒetɔ la me siaa.
ENGLISH: 15 For maybe it was for this purpose he was parted from you for a moment, in order that you might have him back eternally yours, 16 no longer as a slave but above that, a dear brother, dear to me but how much dearer to you both in flesh and in the Lord!

EWE: 17 Eya ta ne èbum xɔ̃wòe la, ekema kɔ dɔme nàxɔe faa abe ale si nàxɔm ene.
ENGLISH: 17 So if you count me as a comrade, receive him as you would me.

EWE: 18 Eye ne eda vo aɖe ɖe ŋuwò alo nyi nane ƒe fe le ŋuwò la, bui nam. 19 Nye Paulo ŋutɔe tsɔ nye asiwo le nya siawo ŋlɔm be: maɖo eteƒe nyemedi be magblɔ be ènyi wò ŋutɔ ɖokuiwò hã ƒe fe le ŋunye o.
ENGLISH: 18 And if he did you any injury or owes anything, charge that to me; 19 I Paul write it with my own hand, I will pay to say nothing of your owing your own self to me into the bargain.

EWE: 20 Ɛ̃, nɔviŋutsu, wɔ esia nam le Aƒetɔ la ta; na nye dzi nadze eme le Kristo me.
ENGLISH: 20 Yes, brother, let me have joy of you in the Lord; set my heart at rest in Christ.

EWE: 21 Meka ɖe dziwò be àwɔ esia, eya ta mele agbalẽ sia ŋlɔm na wò, eye menyae be àwɔ geɖe wu esiwo megblɔ gɔ̃ hã.
ENGLISH: 21 I write you in assurance of your obedience, knowing that you will do even beyond what I say.

EWE: 22 Hekpe ɖe ema ŋu la, dzra dzeƒe ɖo ɖi nam, elabena mele mɔ kpɔm be to miaƒe gbedodoɖawo me la, woaɖe asi le ŋunye na mi.
ENGLISH: 22 But, at the same time, get a room ready for me; for I hope that through your prayers I shall be granted to you.

EWE: 23 Epafra, si le gaxɔ me kplim le Kristo Yesu me, do gbe na wò. 24 Marko, Aristarko, Dema kple Luka, siwo nye nye hadɔwɔlawo, hã do gbe na wò.
ENGLISH: 23 Epaphras my fellow-prisoner in Christ Jesus, 24 and Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, Luke, my co-workers, send you greetings.

EWE: 25 Aƒetɔ Yesu Kristo ƒe amenuveve nanɔ anyi kple gbɔgbɔ si mieɖena fiana la.
ENGLISH: 25 The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirits.

EWE: Hebritɔwo
ENGLISH: Hebrews

EWE: 1 Le blema me la, Mawu ƒo nu zi geɖe na mía tɔgbuiwo to nyagblɔɖilawo dzi le mɔ vovovowo nu. 2 Azɔ le ŋkeke siawo ƒe nuwuwu la, eƒo nu na mí to Vi si wòtia be wòanyi nuwo katã dome, ame si dzi wòto wɔ nuɖoanyiawo la dzi. 3 Eyae ɖe Mawu ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe fia eye wònye eƒe amenyenye ƒe nɔnɔme pɛpɛpɛ, eye wòléa nuwo katã ɖe te to eƒe nya si ŋu ŋusẽ le dzi. Eye esi wòkɔ mía ŋu tso míaƒe nu vɔ̃wo me vɔ la, ebɔbɔ nɔ Bubutɔ Gã la ƒe ɖusime le dziƒowo. 4 Ale wòva de ŋgɔ wu mawudɔlawo, elabena enyi ŋkɔ si ƒo wo tɔ ta sãsãsã la dome.
ENGLISH: 1 Fragmentarily and variously did God of old speak to the fathers in the prophets, 2 but has in these latter days spoken to us in a Son whom he has appointed heir to everything, through whom also he made the universe; who, 3 being beam of his glory and imprint of his essence, and actuating all things by his word of power, took his seat at the right hand of the Majesty on high when he had made purgation of sins, 4 becoming as much better than the angels as he has inherited a more transcendent name than they.

EWE: 5 Le kpɔɖeŋu me, mawudɔlawo dometɔ kae Mawu gblɔ na kpɔ be: "Vinyee nènye; mezu fofowò egbe "? Eye be: "Mazu fofoa, eye eya azu vinye "? 6 Ke egblɔ le ɣeyiɣi si me wòagaɖo eƒe Ŋgɔgbevi la ɖe anyigba dzi ŋu be: "Mawu ƒe dɔlawo katã nebɔbɔ ɖe eŋkume. " 7 Egblɔ le mawudɔlawo hã ŋu be: "Ewɔ eƒe dɔlawo wonye gbɔgbɔwo kple eƒe subɔlawo wonye dzo flafla. " 8 Ke egblɔ le Via ya ŋu be: "Mawue nye wò fiazikpui ɖaa tegbee, wò Fiaɖuƒe ƒe fiatikplɔ nye nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔ ƒe fiatikplɔ. 9 Èlɔ̃ nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔ, eye nèlé fu nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ.
ENGLISH: 5 For to which of the angels did he ever say "You are my son, I have this day brought you to birth, " and again "I will be father to him and he shall be son to me "? 6 and when he shall again bring in the firstborn into the world of men he says "and let all God’s angels do him reverence. " 7 And as to the angels he says "he who makes his angels winds, and his servitors flame "; 8 but as to the Son "God is your throne forever and ever, and the scepter of integrity is the scepter of his reign.

EWE: 11 Wo nu ava yi, ke wò ya ànɔ anyi; wo katã woanyunyɔ abe avɔ ene, 12 eye àŋlɔ wo abe awu ene, abe avɔ ene, woaɖɔli wo. Ke wò la, nenema ko nèle, eye nuwuwu meli na wò ƒewo gbeɖe o. " 13 Ke mawudɔlawo dometɔ ka ŋue wògblɔ le kpɔ be: "Bɔbɔ nɔ nye ɖusime, va se ɖe esime matsɔ wò futɔwo awɔ wò afɔɖodzinui "? 14 Alo menye gbɔgbɔwoe wo katã wonye hena subɔsubɔdɔ kɔkɔe wɔwɔ, eye wodɔa wo ɖa be woasubɔ ame siwo anyi ɖeɖekpɔkpɔ dome la oa?
ENGLISH: 9 You loved rectitude and hated wickedness; for this reason God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of joy beyond your fellows, " 10 and "You at the beginning, Lord, laid the foundations of the earth, and the heavens are works of your hands: 11 they will perish, but you abide; and all of them will grow old as a cloak does, 12 and like a mantle you will roll them up like a cloak, too, will they be changed; but you are the same and your years will not come short. " 13 But as to which of the angels has he ever said "Sit at my right hand till I make your enemies the footstool for your feet "? 14 Are they not, all of them, servient spirits that are sent on errands in behalf of those who are to inherit salvation?

EWE: Hebritɔwo
ENGLISH: Hebrews

EWE: 2 Esia tae wòle vevie na mí be míalé to ɖe nu siwo míesena la ŋu geɖe wu, ale be míagatra mɔ gbeɖe o.
ENGLISH: 2 For this reason we must pay special attention to what we have heard, for fear we should drop away.

EWE: 2 Elabena ne nya si wogblɔ to mawudɔlawo dzi la nye esi ŋu kakaɖedzi le, eye dzidada ɖe sia ɖe kple tomaɖomaɖo ɖe sia ɖe xɔ eŋuti tohehe le dzɔdzɔenyenye nu la, 3 ekema aleke míawɔ asi, ne míetsɔ ɖeke le ɖeɖekpɔkpɔ gã sia gbegbe me o?
ENGLISH: 2 For if the word spoken through angels proved sure, and every violation or nonobservance received due requital, 3 how shall we escape after neglecting such a great salvation? which, having begun to be spoken through the Lord, was confirmed to us by those who had heard it, 4 God adding his attestation by tokens and wonders and varied miracles and grants of the Holy Spirit according to his will.

EWE: Elabena esia ŋuti nya mía Aƒetɔ la gblɔ gbã, eye ame siwo see la ɖo kpe edzi na mí, 4 esime Mawu ŋutɔ hã tsɔ dzesiwo kple nukunuwo kple ŋusẽdɔ vovovowo kpakple gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔe ƒe nunana siwo wòna le eya ŋutɔ ƒe lɔlɔ̃nu nu la, ɖi ɖase kpe ɖe wo ŋuti. 5 Elabena menye mawudɔlawo tee wòtsɔ xexe si gbɔna, si ŋu míele nu ƒom tsoe la, de o. 6 Ke ɖasefo aɖe gblɔ le afi aɖe be: "Nu kae amegbetɔ nye, be nèɖoa ŋku edzi, alo amegbetɔvi nye, be nèléa be nɛ? 7 Èwɔe wòbɔbɔ ɖe anyi vie wu mawudɔlawo; eye nèɖɔ ŋutikɔkɔe kple bubu nɛ, eye nètsɔe ɖo wò asinudɔwɔwɔwo nu. 8 Ètsɔ nuwo katã de eƒe afɔ te. " Esi Mawu tsɔ nuwo katã de ete la, megblẽ naneke ɖi, si metsɔ de ete o. Gake fifia la, medze ƒãa na mí haɖe be nuwo katã le ete o. 9 Ke míekpɔ Yesu, ame si wobɔbɔ ɖe anyi vie wu mawudɔlawo la, fifia woɖɔ ŋutikɔkɔe kple bubu nɛ esi wòkpe fu heku, ale be to Mawu ƒe amenuveve me la, wòaɖɔ ku kpɔ ɖe amewo katã ta.
ENGLISH: 5 For not to angels did he subject the future earth of which we are speaking; 6 because someone has somewhere testified in these words: "What is a man, that thou rememberest him? or a son of man, that thou dost look after him? 7 Thou didst make him a little inferior to the angels, didst garland him with glory and honor, 8 didst subject everything underneath his feet, " For in subjecting everything to him he has left nothing unsubjected to him, but now we do not yet see everything subjected to him; 9 but him who was made a little inferior to the angels, Jesus, we do see garlanded with glory and honor so that by God’s grace he may taste death for everyone.

EWE: 10 Elabena esɔ be ame si ta nuwo katã va li, ame si me nuwo katã to va la, esi wòkplɔ vi geɖewo yi ŋutikɔkɔe me la, ena woƒe Kplɔla Vevitɔ si dzi wotona kpɔa ɖeɖe la zu blibo to fukpekpewo me.
ENGLISH: 10 For it befitted him for whom everything exists and through whom everything exists that in bringing many sons to glory he should perfect through suffering their leader in salvation.

EWE: 11 Elabena ame si le amewo ŋu kɔm kple ame siwo ŋu kɔm wole la siaa dzɔ tso ame ɖeka me, eye le esia ta ŋu mekpee be wòayɔ wo be nɔviwo o, 12 esi wògblɔ be: "Maɖe gbeƒã wò ŋkɔ la na nɔvinyewo; madzi ha akafu wò le amehawo dome. " 13 Egagblɔ hã be: "Maɖo ŋu ɖe eŋu. " Eye wògagblɔ be: "Kpɔ ɖa! Nye kple vi siwo Yehowa nam lae nye esi. " 14 Eya ta esi wònye ‘viawo’ nye gomekpɔlawo le ʋu kple ŋutilã me ta la, eya hã kpɔ gome le nu mawo ke me, ale be wòato eƒe ku la dzi axɔ ŋusẽ le ame si ate ŋu ahe ku vɛ la si, si nye Abosam, 15 eye be wòana ablɔɖe ame siwo katã zu kluviwo le woƒe agbenɔɣi katã le vɔvɔ̃ na ku ta.
ENGLISH: 11 For the sanctifier and the sanctified all come of one; for which reason he is not ashamed of calling them brothers, 12 saying "I will announce thy name to my brothers, in the midst of the congregation I will hymn thy praise, " 13 and again "I will rest my confidence in him, " and again "Lo, I and the children God has given me. " 14 So, since the children have been sharing flesh and blood, he himself similarly participated in the same, that through death he might quell him who wields the might of death that is, the Devil 15 and deliver those who for the fear of death were doomed to slavery all their lives.

EWE: 16 Elabena le nyateƒe me la, menye mawudɔlawo ŋue wòle kpekpem ɖo kura o, ke Abraham ƒe dzidzimevi la boŋ ŋue.
ENGLISH: 16 For he does not take up angels, methinks, but takes up the descendants of Abraham.

EWE: 17 Eya ta eva hiã be wòava nɔ abe "nɔviawo " ene le goawo katã me, be wòazu nunɔlagã nublanuikpɔla kple nuteƒewɔla le nu siwo ku ɖe Mawu ƒe subɔsubɔdɔa ŋu me, ne wòasa avulévɔ ɖe dukɔ la ƒe nu vɔ̃wo ta.
ENGLISH: 17 Whence he had to be made in all respects like his brothers, that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest for our relations to God, to make propitiation for the people’s sins.

EWE: 18 Esi eya ŋutɔ kpe fu esi wotee kpɔ ta la, ate ŋu akpe ɖe ame siwo wotena kpɔna la ŋu.
ENGLISH: 18 For by the fact that he himself has suffered from temptation he is able to help the tempted.

EWE: Hebritɔwo
ENGLISH: Hebrews

EWE: 3 Eya ŋuti nɔvi kɔkɔewo, dziƒoyɔyɔ ƒe gomekpɔlawo, mibu apostolo kple nunɔlagã si me míeʋuna la ŋu si nye Yesu. 2 Ewɔ nuteƒe na Ame si ɖoe, abe ale si Mose hã wɔ nuteƒe le Ame ma ƒe aƒe la katã me ene.
ENGLISH: 3 Hence, holy brothers, participants in the celestial call, look at Jesus the apostle and high priest of our confession, 2 faithful to the one who appointed him in the same way as Moses was faithful in his house.

EWE: 3 Elabena wobu eya amea be edze na ŋutikɔkɔe geɖe wu Mose, elabena ame si tso aƒe la dze na bubu gã wu aƒea.
ENGLISH: 3 For he has been awarded more glory than Moses insofar as he who constructed the house has more honor than the house.

EWE: 4 Nyateƒee, aƒe sia aƒe la, amee tsonɛ, ke ame si wɔ nuwo katãe nye Mawu. 5 Ke Mose, si nye subɔvi, la wɔ nuteƒe le Ame ma ƒe aƒe la katã me be wòanye ɖaseɖiɖi le nya siwo woava gblɔ emegbe la ŋu. 6 Ke Kristo, ame si le Mawu ƒe aƒe la nu, wɔ nuteƒe abe vi ene.
ENGLISH: 4 For every house is constructed by somebody; but he who constructed everything is God, 5 and Moses was faithful in all his house as a servant for a testimony of what was to be spoken, 6 but Christ as a son over his house; whose house we are if we retain our confidence and prideful hope.

EWE: 7 Eya ta abe ale si gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔe la gblɔe ene la, "Egbe ne miese eƒe gbe la, 8 migasẽ dzi me, abe ale si wowɔ le ɣeyiɣi si me wodo dɔmedzoe nam vevie le ŋkeke si wodom kpɔ le gbea dzi, 9 afi si mia tɔgbuiwo dom kpɔ hetem kpɔ le, togbɔ be wokpɔ nye dɔwɔwɔwo ƒe blaene sɔŋ hafi la ene o. 10 Esia tae dzidzime ma ƒe nu nyɔ ŋu nam, eye megblɔ be: ‘Woƒe dzi traa mɔ ɣesiaɣi, eye womenya nye mɔwo o.’ 11 Eya ta meka atam le nye dziku me be: ‘Womayi ɖe nye dzudzɔ la me o.’ " 12 Nɔviwo, mikpɔ nyuie be dzi vɔ̃ɖi maxɔse nagaɖo mia dometɔ aɖeke me, le esi wòle tetem ɖa le Mawu gbagbe la gbɔ ta o; 13 ke boŋ miyi edzi mianɔ dzi dem ƒo na mia nɔewo gbe sia gbe, zi ale si woyɔnɛ be "Egbe, " ale be nu vɔ̃ ƒe amebleŋusẽ nagana mia dometɔ aɖeke ƒe dzi me nasẽ o. 14 Elabena ne míelé kakaɖedzi si le mía si le gɔmedzedzea me la me ɖe asi sesĩe va se ɖe nuwuwu ko hafi míazu gomekpɔlawo ŋutɔŋutɔ kple Kristo. 15 Wogblɔ be, "Egbe ne miese eƒe gbe la, migasẽ dzi me, abe ale si wowɔ le ɣeyiɣi si me wodo dɔmedzoe nɛ vevie ene o. " 16 Elabena ame kawoe see, evɔ wodo dɔmedzoe nɛ vevie? Alo menye ame siwo katã Mose kplɔ dzoe le Egipte lae oa? 17 Azɔ hã, ame kawo ƒe nue nyɔ ŋu na Mawu ƒe blaene sɔŋ? Alo menye ame siwo wɔ nu vɔ̃, siwo ƒe kukuawo tsi gbea dzi lae oa? 18 Eye ame kawoe wòka atam gblɔ na be, womade yeƒe dzudzɔ la me o? Ðe menye ame siwo sẽ to lae oa? 19 Eya ta míekpɔe be womete ŋu yi ɖe eme o le dzimaxɔse ta.
ENGLISH: 7 Wherefore, as the Holy Spirit says "Today, if you hear his voice, 8 do not harden your hearts as at the embittering, as on the day of the testing in the wilderness, 9 where your fathers made a test for approval and saw my deeds for forty years, 10 wherefore I was disgusted with that generation and said ‘They are wrong-headed all the time and do not know my ways,’ 11 as I swore in my anger ‘They shall not come into my rest,’ " 12 look to it, brothers, that there shall not be in any one of you a vicious heart of unbelief in breaking away from the living God, 13 but exhort each other each day as long as "today " is so called, in order that there may not any one of you be hardened by the deceits of sin; 14 for we have become the Christ’s "fellows " if we hold firm to the end the resolution we began with, 15 while it is said "Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as at the embittering. " 16 For who did the embittering when they had heard? why, was it not all who had come out of Egypt by Moses’s agency? 17 and with whom was he disgusted for forty years? was it not with those who had sinned, whose limbs dropped in the wilderness? 18 and to whom did he swear that they should not come into his rest except to those who had disbelieved? 19 and we see that they could not come in because of unbelief.

EWE: Hebritɔwo
ENGLISH: Hebrews

EWE: 4 Eya ta esi eƒe dzudzɔ la me yiyi ƒe ŋugbedodo kpɔtɔ li ta la, mina míanɔ ŋudzɔ, ne menye nenema o la, ato mia dometɔ aɖewo ŋu. 2 Elabena wogblɔ nya nyui la na míawo hã, abe woawo ke ene; ke nya si wose la meɖe vi na wo o, elabena woƒe xɔse mewɔ ɖeka kple ame siwo see la tɔ o.
ENGLISH: 4 So let us be afraid lest when there is left a promise of coming into his rest any one of you should perchance appear to have fallen short 2 for we have heard a gospel, as they too had, but the words they heard did them no good, they not meeting the hearers with faith.

EWE: 3 Mí ame siwo xɔe se la, míeyina ɖe dzudzɔ la me, abe ale si wògblɔ ene be: "Eya ta meka atam le nye dziku me be, ‘Womayi ɖe nye dzudzɔ la me o,’ " togbɔ be ewu eƒe dɔwɔwɔwo nu tso xexea ƒe gɔmeɖoanyiɣi ke hã.
ENGLISH: 3 For we believers come into rest, as he says "as I swore in my anger ‘They shall not come into my rest’ " though it was back at the foundation of the world that the works were done.

EWE: 4 Elabena egblɔ le afi aɖe le ŋkeke adrelia ŋu be: "Eye Mawu dzudzɔ tso eƒe dɔwɔwɔwo katã me le ŋkeke adrelia dzi, " 5 eye wògagblɔ le afi sia be: "Womayi ɖe nye dzudzɔ la me o. " 6 Eya ta esi wòsusɔ be ame aɖewo nayi ɖe eme, eye ame siwo wogblɔ nya nyui la na gbã la meyi ɖe eme o le tomaɖomaɖo ta la, 7 egaɖo ŋkeke ɖi, esi wògagblɔ emegbe ʋĩi le David ƒe psalmo aɖe me be "Egbe "; abe ale si míegblɔe va yi ene be, "Egbe ne miese eƒe gbe la, migasẽ dzi me o. " 8 Elabena ne ɖe Yosua kplɔ wo yi dzudzɔƒe la, anye ne Mawu magaƒo nu tso ŋkeke bubu ŋu emegbe o.
ENGLISH: 4 For he somewhere says like this about the seventh day, "And God rested on the seventh day from all his works, " 5 and in this passage again "They shall not come into my rest "; 6 so since it remains that some come into it, and those who heard the gospel before did not come in because of disobedience, 7 he again defines a certain day, "today, " saying in David so long afterward, as aforesaid, "Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts. " 8 For if Joshua had brought them to rest he would not be speaking about another day afterward.

EWE: 9 Eya ta sabat ƒe dzudzɔ aɖe gakpɔtɔ li na Mawu ƒe amewo.
ENGLISH: 9 So then there remains a sabbath for God’s people.

EWE: 10 Elabena ame si yi ɖe Mawu ƒe dzudzɔ me la, eya hã dzudzɔ tso eya ŋutɔ ƒe dɔwɔwɔwo me, abe ale si ko Mawu hã dzudzɔ tso eya ŋutɔ tɔwo me ene.
ENGLISH: 10 For he who has come into his rest is resting from his own works just as God did from his.

EWE: 11 Eya ta mina míawɔ míaƒe ŋutete ɖe sia ɖe be míayi ɖe dzudzɔ ma me, ale be ame aɖeke nagadze tomaɖomaɖo ƒe nuwɔna ma tɔgbi me o.
ENGLISH: 11 So let us make it our concern to come into that rest, in order that no one may fall by the same pattern of disobedience.

EWE: 12 Elabena Mawu ƒe nya la le agbe, eye ŋusẽ le eŋu, eye wòɖana wua yi nuevee sia yi nuevee, eye wòƒona ɖe ame yi ɖamaa keke luʋɔ kple gbɔgbɔ me, kpakple ƒunukpeƒewo kple ƒutomemi me, eye wòtea ŋu dzea si tamesusuwo kple dzimedidiwo. 13 Eye nuwɔwɔ aɖeke mele ɣaɣla ɖee o, ke boŋ woklo nu le nuwo katã dzi eye wotsi ƒeƒle le ame si míabu akɔnta na la ŋkume.
ENGLISH: 12 For God’s word is living and effective and a surer cutter than any two-edged sword, and penetrative to the dissection of soul and spirit, of joints and marrows, and a judge of a heart’s thoughts and conceptions; 13 and not a creature escapes his notice, but everything is naked and thrown flat on its back for his eyes of whom we are speaking.

EWE: 14 Azɔ esi nunɔlagã, si nye Yesu, Mawu ƒe Vi, si yi dziƒo la le mía si ta la, mina míayi edzi alé eya amea me ʋuʋu me ɖe asi sesĩe le dutoƒo.
ENGLISH: 14 So, having a great high priest who has gone past the skies, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold on to our confession.

EWE: 15 Elabena menye nunɔlagã si mate ŋu ase veve ɖe míaƒe gbɔdzɔgbɔdzɔwo nu o lae le mía si o, ke boŋ ame si wodo kpɔ le go sia go me abe míawo ke ene, ke nu vɔ̃ koe mele eŋu o.
ENGLISH: 15 For we do not have a high priest that cannot feel our weaknesses, but one who has met temptations of like nature in all respects without sin.

EWE: 16 Eya ta mina dzi nanɔ mía ƒo míate ɖe amenuvevezikpui la ŋu aƒo nu faa, ale be wòakpɔ nublanui na mí, eye wòave mía nu le hiahiãgbe.
ENGLISH: 16 So let us come to the throne of grace with confidence in order that we may obtain mercy and find grace for timely help.

EWE: Hebritɔwo
ENGLISH: Hebrews

EWE: 5 Elabena nunɔlagã ɖe sia ɖe si wotia tso amegbetɔwo dome la, woɖonɛ be wòawɔ Mawu ƒe subɔsubɔdɔ ɖe amewo nu, ale be wòatsɔ nunanawo ana, eye wòasa vɔ ɖe nu vɔ̃wo ta. 2 Etea ŋu sea veve ɖe ame siwo wɔa nu le manyamanya me kple ame siwo daa vo la nu, le esi gbɔdzɔgbɔdzɔ le eya ŋutɔ hã ŋu ta, 3 eye esia tae wòle nɛ be wòasa vɔ ɖe eya ŋutɔ ƒe nu vɔ̃wo ta abe ale si ko wòwɔnɛ ɖe dukɔ la ta ene.
ENGLISH: 5 For every high priest, taken from among men, is appointed on men’s behalf in their relations to God, to offer gifts and sacrifices for sins, 2 being able to take a reasonable attitude toward those who blunder and stray since he too is beset by weakness 3 and because of it is obliged to offer sin-offerings on his own account just as he does on the people’s.

EWE: 4 Ame aɖeke metiaa bubunɔƒe sia na eɖokui o, negbe ɖe Mawu yɔe ko hafi, abe ale si wòyɔ Aron ene.
ENGLISH: 4 And one does not take the honor to himself but enters upon it at God’s call in the same way as Aaron did.

EWE: 5 Nenema kee Kristo la hã medo eɖokui ɖe dzi heɖo eɖokui nunɔlagãe o, ke boŋ Ame si gblɔ nɛ be: "Vinyee nènye; mezu fofowò egbe, " lae doe ɖe dzi. 6 Abe ale si wògagblɔ le teƒe bubu hã be, "Nunɔlae nènye abe Melkizedek ene tegbee. "
ENGLISH: 5 In this same way the Christ did not glorify himself into the office of high priest, but he who spoke to him in the words "You are my son, I have this day brought you to birth, " 6 as he says in another passage too "You are a priest forever in such station as Melchisedek’s was. "

EWE: 7 Le Kristo ƒe anyigbadzigbenɔnɔ me la, etsɔ ɣlidodo sesĩwo kple aɖatsiwo ƒo koko heɖe kuku vevie na Ame si te ŋu ɖee tso ku me la, eye wòɖo toe le eƒe mawuvɔvɔ̃ ta. 8 Togbɔ be vi wònye hã la, esrɔ̃ toɖoɖo le fu siwo wòkpe la me. 9 Eye esi wona wòzu blibo vɔ la, eva zu ame si dzi ame siwo katã ɖoa toe la tona kpɔa ɖeɖe mavɔ, 10 elabena Mawu ŋutɔe da ŋkɔ ɖe edzi be enye nunɔlagã abe Melkizedek ene.
ENGLISH: 7 Who, having in his days of flesh offered with strong outcries and tears both petitions and supplications to him who could save him from death, and having been listened to for his godliness, 8 learned obedience by suffering, Son though he was, 9 and, perfected, became for all who obey him the author of an eternal salvation, 10 being addressed by God as a high priest "in such station as Melchisedek’s was. "

EWE: 11 Nya geɖewo li míagblɔ tso eya amea ŋu, gake wo me ɖeɖe sesẽ, le esi nugɔmesese zu dɔ na mi ta. 12 Elabena va ɖo fifia la, ɖe wòle be mianye nufialawo hafi, gake egahiã be woafia Mawu ƒe gbedeasi kɔkɔeawo ƒe gɔmedzenuwo mi tso nu gbãtɔwo dzi, eye miegatrɔ zu ame siwo hiã notsi, ke menye nuɖuɖu sesẽ o.
ENGLISH: 11 About whom we have much to say, and hard to explain in the saying, since you have come to be dull-eared 12 for when you ought to be teachers on account of the time that has elapsed, you are again in need of having someone teach you the primary elements of God’s oracles, and have come to be in need of milk, not of solid food.

EWE: 13 Elabena ame sia ame si gakpɔtɔ noa notsi la, menya naneke le dzɔdzɔenyenye ƒe nya la ŋu o, elabena ɖevi ko wòganye. 14 Ke ame tsitsiwo tɔe nye nuɖuɖu sesẽ, ame siwo na hehe woƒe nugɔmeseseŋutetewo to wo zazã me, be woate ŋu ade vovo nyui kple vɔ̃ dome.
ENGLISH: 13 For anyone who takes milk is unversed in the discussion of righteousness; for he is an infant, 14 but solid food is for grown men, those who from experience have their senses exercised for discrimination between good and bad.

EWE: Hebritɔwo
ENGLISH: Hebrews

EWE: 6 Eya ta esi míegblẽ Kristo la ŋuti gɔmedzenufiafiawo ɖi la, mina míayi ŋgɔ aɖo tsitsinyenye gbɔ, eye míaganɔ gɔmeɖoanyi ɖom ake o, si nye dzimetɔtrɔ tso dɔwɔwɔ kukuwo me kple Mawu dzi xɔxɔ se, 2 nyɔnyrɔxɔxɔwo ŋuti nufiafia kple asidada ɖe ame dzi, ame kukuwo ƒe tsitretsitsi kple ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃ mavɔ.
ENGLISH: 6 Wherefore let us drop primary propositions about the Christ and push on to adult work, not re-laying a foundation of repentance from dead works and of faith in God, 2 instruction about baptisms and laying on of hands, resurrection of the dead and eternal judgment.

EWE: 3 Ɛ̃, míayi ŋgɔ aɖo tsitsinyenye gbɔ ne Mawu lɔ̃.
ENGLISH: 3 And this we will do if God permits.

EWE: 4 Elabena ame siwo kekeli la klẽ na kpɔ, eye woɖɔ dziƒo ƒe nunana faa la kpɔ, eye woxɔ gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔe la, 5 eye woɖɔ Mawu ƒe nya nyui la kple nuɖoanyi si gbɔna la ƒe ŋusẽwo kpɔ, 6 gake wode megbe la, manya wɔ be woagawɔ wo yeye hena dzimetɔtrɔ o, elabena wogahe Mawu ƒe Vi la ɖe ati ŋu ake na wo ɖokui, eye wodoa ŋukpee le gaglãgbe.
ENGLISH: 4 For it is impossible to renew again to repentance those who were once lighted up and tasted the heavenly gift and became partakers in the Holy Spirit 5 and tasted God’s good word and the powers of a future age, 6 and have gone off the track; men that are recrucifying the Son of God for themselves and making a spectacle of him.

EWE: 7 Elabena anyigba la xɔa yayra tso Mawu gbɔ, ne enoa tsi si dzana ɖe edzi enuenu, eye wòmiea nu siwo ɖea vi na ame siwo ŋlɔe la. 8 Ke ne emiea ŋùwo kple srẽwo la, woɖea asi le eŋu, eye ɖeko wòle abe ɖe woƒo fi dee ene, eye mlɔeba wotɔa dzoe.
ENGLISH: 7 For land that has drunk the rain which came repeatedly upon it and brings forth vegetation fit for the purposes of those on whose account it is worked enjoys a blessing from God, 8 but such as puts out thorns and thistles is worthless and close to a curse, coming in the end to burning.

EWE: 9 Ke lɔlɔ̃tɔwo, togbɔ be míele nu ƒom alea hã, le miawo ya gome la, míeka ɖe nu siwo nyo wu la dzi, siwo nye nu siwo hea ɖeɖekpɔkpɔ vanɛ.
ENGLISH: 9 But we are persuaded of better things about you, dear friends, and things that go with salvation, though we do speak thus.

EWE: 10 Elabena Mawu menye madzɔmadzɔtɔ, be wòaŋlɔ miaƒe dɔwɔwɔ kple lɔlɔ̃ si mieɖe fia le eƒe ŋkɔ la ta, esi miesubɔ ame kɔkɔewo, eye miegale edzi le wo subɔm la be o.
ENGLISH: 10 For God is not unjust, to forget your work and the love you have displayed toward his name in the services you have rendered and are rendering to his people.

EWE: 11 Ke míedi be mia dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe naɖe veviedodo ma ke afia, ne mɔkpɔkpɔ ƒe kakaɖedzi blibo la nanɔ mia si va se ɖe nuwuwu, 12 ale be miaganye kuviatɔwo o, ke boŋ mianye ame siwo to xɔse kple dzigbɔɖi me nyi ŋugbedodowo dome la srɔ̃lawo.
ENGLISH: 11 But we wish each of you might display the same earnestness with reference to certitude of hope to the end, 12 in order that you may not come out dullards but imitators of those who through faith and patience were granted the promises.

EWE: 13 Elabena esime Mawu do ŋugbe na Abraham la, esi ame aɖeke melolo wui wòatsɔ aka atam o ta la, etsɔ eɖokui ka atam 14 gblɔ be: "Mayra wò godoo, eye mana nàdzi asɔ gbɔ ɖe edzi. " 15 Eya ta esi Abraham gbɔ dzi ɖi la, eƒe asi su ŋugbedodo sia dzi.
ENGLISH: 13 For in giving Abraham the promise God, since he had no way to swear by any greater, swore by himself 14 "Verily I will bless you and make you numerous. " 15 And thus when he had been patient he won the promise.

EWE: 16 Elabena ame si lolo wu lae wotsɔna kaa atam, eye woƒe atamkaka la nyea nyahehe ɖe sia ɖe ƒe nuwuwu, elabena enyea kpeɖodzinu le se nu na wo. 17 Nenema kee esime Mawu ɖoe be yeaɖee afia ŋugbedodo la ƒe domenyilawo kɔtɛ wu be yeƒe tameɖoɖo metrɔna o la, eka atam tsɔ ɖo kpe edzi, 18 ale be le nu eve siwo metrɔna o, siwo me Mawu mate ŋu aka aʋatso le o me la, dzideƒo sẽŋu nanɔ mí ame siwo sii tso la si be míalé mɔkpɔkpɔ si woɖo mía ŋkume la me ɖe asi sesĩe.
ENGLISH: 16 For men swear by the greater, and the oath is for them the assuring end of all contradiction; 17 which being so, God, wishing particularly to show the grantees of the promise the immutability of his plan, interposed with an oath, 18 in order that by two immutable things in which it is impossible for God to lie we might have a strong encouragement, we who have sought refuge in grasping the hope that lies before us.

EWE: 19 Mɔkpɔkpɔ sia le mía si abe seke ene na míaƒe luʋɔwo, kakaɖedzi le eŋu, eye wòli ke, eye wòto xɔmetsovɔ la me yi, 20 afi si ŋgɔdola la yi ɖe mía ta le, si nye Yesu, ame si zu nunɔlagã abe Melkizedek ene yi mavɔmavɔ me.
ENGLISH: 19 Which hope we have as an anchor for the soul, safe and firm and going inside the curtain, 20 where Jesus went in for us in advance when he became high priest forever in such station as Melchisedek’s was.

EWE: Hebritɔwo
ENGLISH: Hebrews

EWE: 7 Elabena Melkizedek sia, si nye Salem-fia, Mawu Dziƒoʋĩtɔ la ƒe nunɔla, va do go Abraham esime wòtrɔ tso fiawo siƒe gbɔna, eye wòyrae, 2 eye Abraham tsɔ nuwo katã ƒe ewolia nɛ. Gbã la, eƒe ŋkɔ gɔmee nye "Dzɔdzɔenyenyefia, " eye wòganye Salem-fia hã, si gɔmee nye "Ŋutifafafia. " 3 Esi wònye tɔ kple nɔ kpakple dzidzime ŋuti nuŋlɔɖi aɖeke mele esi o, eye eƒe dzidzi alo ku ŋuti nuŋlɔɖi aɖeke meli o, ke boŋ wona wòle abe Mawu ƒe Vi la ene ta la, enye nunɔla tso mavɔ me yi mavɔ me.
ENGLISH: 7 For this Melchisedek, king of Salem, priest of God Most High, who came to meet Abraham as he returned from the defeat of the kings and blessed him, 2 to whom also Abraham apportioned a tithe of everything, translated, in the first place, "King of Righteousness, " and then also "king of Salem, " which is "king of peace, " 3 fatherless, motherless, pedigreeless, not having either a beginning of days or an end of life but put in like condition with the Son of God, remains a priest in perpetuity.

EWE: 4 Mikpɔ ale si gbegbe ame sia, si ƒome ƒe ta Abraham tsɔ nu siwo wòha la ƒe nyuitɔwo ƒe ewolia na la, nye ame vevii ɖa. 5 Nyateƒee, le Se la nu la, wogblɔ na Lewi viwo dometɔ siwo woɖoa nunɔlawoe la be woaxɔ nuwo ƒe ewolia tso dukɔ si nye wo nɔviwo si, togbɔ be woawo hã wonye Abraham ƒe dzidzimeviwo hã. 6 Ke ame sia si medzɔ tso woƒe ƒomea me o la, xɔ nuwo ƒe ewolia le Abraham si, eye wòyra ame si si ŋugbedodoawo le la.
ENGLISH: 4 And see what a man this was, to whom Abraham, the founder of the nation, gave a tithe out of the spoils! 5 and those of the sons of Levi who receive the priesthood have orders to tithe the people in accordance with the law, that is, to tithe their brothers even though they have come out of Abraham’s loins; 6 but he who does not count his ancestry from them has tithed Abraham and blessed him who had the promises.

EWE: 7 Ðikeke aɖeke mele eme o be, ame si nye gãtɔ lae yra ame si nye suetɔ la.
ENGLISH: 7 And beyond any dispute the lesser is blessed by the better.

EWE: 8 Le Lewi viwo gome la, woxɔa nuwo ƒe ewolia eye wonye ame siwo kuna, ke le ame evelia si xɔ nuwo ƒe ewolia ya gome la, Ŋɔŋlɔawo ɖi ɖase le eŋu be ele agbe.
ENGLISH: 8 And here men who die receive tithes, but there one who has it attested that he lives.

EWE: 9 Eye woate ŋu agblɔ be Lewi, ame si xɔa nuwo ƒe ewolia, gɔ̃ hã to Abraham dzi na nuwo ƒe ewolia, 10 elabena tɔgbuia medzii haɖe o esime Melkizedek va kpee.
ENGLISH: 9 And, so to speak, through Abraham even Levi, he who receives tithes, has been tithed; 10 for he was still in his father’s loins when Melchisedek came to meet him.

EWE: 11 Eya ta ne ɖe woate ŋu aɖo blibodede gbɔ to Lewitɔwo ƒe nunɔlanyenye dzi (elabena ekpe ɖe se si wotsɔ na dukɔa ŋu) la, ekema nu ka tae wògahiã be nunɔla bubu nado, ame si ŋu wogblɔ le be ele abe Melkizedek ene, ke menye abe Aron ene o? 12 Elabena esi wole nunɔlanyenyea ɖɔlim ta la, eva hiã be woaɖɔli Se la hã.
ENGLISH: 11 So if perfection was attainable through the Levitical priesthood (for the people has its legislation on that basis), what more need was there that another priest be set up in such station as Melchisedek’s was and not be said to be in such station as Aaron’s? 12 for when the priesthood is shifted there necessarily comes a shift of law too.

EWE: 13 Elabena ame si ŋuti wogblɔ nya siawo le la nye to bubu me tɔ, tso ame siwo mesubɔ le vɔsamlekpuia gbɔ kpɔ o la dome. 14 Eme kɔ ƒãa be mía Aƒetɔ la do tso Yuda-toa me, evɔ Mose megblɔ nya aɖeke be to ma me tɔwo anye nunɔlawo o.
ENGLISH: 13 For he of whom these things are said is a member of another tribe, from which nobody has tended the altar; 14 for it is a conspicuous fact that our Lord has arisen out of Judah, with reference to which tribe Moses spoke nothing about priests.

EWE: 15 Eye esia me gakɔ ɖe edzi ƒãa esi nunɔla bubu si le abe Melkizedek ene la do, 16 ame si va zu alea, menye abe ale si sea bia be wòanɔ le ŋutilã me ƒomedodo nu la ene o, ke boŋ le agbe si womate ŋu atsrɔ̃ o la ƒe ŋusẽ nu. 17 Elabena woɖi ɖase le eŋu be: "Nunɔlae nènye abe Melkizedek ene tegbee. "
ENGLISH: 15 And it is all the more evident if in likeness to Melchisedek another priest is set up 16 who has become such not as determined by the law of a commandment for flesh but as determined by the power of indestructible life; 17 for he has the attestation "You are a priest forever in such station as Melchisedek’s was. "

EWE: 18 Eya ta woɖe se si do ŋgɔ la ɖa le esi wògbɔdzɔ eye meɖo eƒe taɖodzinu bliboa gbɔ o ta. 19 Elabena Se la mena naneke de blibo o, ke boŋ mɔkpɔkpɔ si nyo wu, si wotsɔ vɛ, si dzi míeto le tetem ɖe Mawu ŋu lae.
ENGLISH: 18 For there ensues abrogation of a prior commandment because of its weakness and uselessness 19 (for the law did not complete anything) and introduction of a better hope through which we approach God.

EWE: 20 Eye esi wònye womeɖoe nunɔlae atamkaka manɔŋui o 21 (elabena le nyateƒe me la, ame aɖewo li siwo zu nunɔlawo atamkaka manɔŋui, ke ame sia ya zu nunɔla si ŋu atamkaka kpe ɖo, eye Ame si ka atam ma la gblɔ le eŋu be: "Yehowa ka atam, eye matrɔ susu o be, ‘Nunɔla nènye tegbee,’ ") ta la, 22 Yesu hã va zu ame si da megbe na nubabla si nyo wu la.
ENGLISH: 20 And so far as regards its not being without the taking of an oath 21 (for those are priests made such without the taking of an oath, but he with the taking of an oath, through him who says to him "The Lord has sworn, and will not revoke it, ‘You are priest forever’ "), 22 to that extent has Jesus become guarantor of a better covenant.

EWE: 23 Gawu la, ame geɖewo va zu nunɔlawo ɖe wo nɔewo yome le esi ku meɖe mɔ be woayi edzi asubɔ o ta, 24 ke esi eya le agbe yi mavɔmavɔ me ta la, ame aɖeke mexɔna ɖe eƒe nunɔlanyenye la teƒe o. 25 Eya ta ate ŋu aɖe ame siwo le tetem ɖe Mawu ŋu to eya amea dzi la bliboe hã, elabena ele agbe ɣesiaɣi, be wòaxɔ woƒe nya ɖe akɔ.
