ENGLISH: 23 And those have been a number of priests because prevented by death from staying in their place; 24 but he, because of remaining forever, has his priesthood inalienable, 25 wherefore he can totally save those who come to God through him, he being always alive to intercede for them.

EWE: 26 Esɔ be nunɔlagã sia tɔgbie le mía si, ame si nye nuteƒewɔla, ame maɖifɔ, si ŋu ɖiƒoƒo aɖeke mele o, si te ɖa tso nu vɔ̃ ŋu, eye wodoe ɖe dzi boo. 27 Mehiã be wòanɔ vɔ sam gbe sia gbe, gbã ɖe eya ŋutɔ ƒe nu vɔ̃wo ta, eye emegbe ɖe dukɔ la tɔwo ta, abe ale si nunɔlagã mawo wɔnɛ ene o, elabena ewɔ esia zi ɖeka ɖe ɣeyiɣiawo katã nu esime wòtsɔ eɖokui sa vɔe.
ENGLISH: 26 For such a high priest was the right one for us, godly, innocent, unpolluted, separated from sinners and risen to be higher than the heavens, 27 who does not, like the high priests, have daily necessity to offer sacrifices first for his own sins, then for those of the people; for this he did once for all in making the offering of himself.

EWE: 28 Elabena Se la ɖoa ame siwo ŋu gbɔdzɔgbɔdzɔwo le la nunɔlagãwoe, ke atamkanya si va ɖe Se la yome la ya ɖo Vi, si wona wòde blibo tegbee la, ɖoƒe sia.
ENGLISH: 28 For the law appoints men as high priests, men who have weaknesses; but the oath-taking word that came after the law a Son, perfected forever.

EWE: Hebritɔwo
ENGLISH: Hebrews

EWE: 8 Ke nya vevitɔ si le nya si gblɔm míele me lae nye esi: Nunɔlagã sia gbegbee le mía si, eye wòbɔbɔ nɔ Bubutɔ Gã la ƒe fiazikpui ƒe ɖusime le dziƒowo, 2 eye eyae nye kɔkɔeƒe la kple agbadɔ vavã si Yehowa tu, eye menye amee tui o, la ƒe subɔla.
ENGLISH: 8 And, the main point for what we are talking about, we have such a high priest as has taken his seat at the right hand of the throne of majesty in the heavens, 2 a ministrant of the true sanctuary and the true tent which the Lord pitched, not a man.

EWE: 3 Elabena woɖoa nunɔlagã ɖe sia ɖe be wòatsɔ nunanawo ana, eye wòasa vɔ; eya ta ehiã be ame sia hã natsɔ nane ana.
ENGLISH: 3 For every high priest is appointed to offer gifts and sacrifices; whence it is necessary that this one too should have something to offer.

EWE: 4 Ne anyigba dzie wòle la, manye nunɔla o, elabena amewo li, siwo tsɔa nunanawo nana le Se la nu. 5 Ame siawo le subɔsubɔdɔ kɔkɔe wɔm wònye dziƒonuwo ƒe kpɔɖeŋu kple vɔvɔli; abe ale si ko Mawu de se na Mose esime wòle agbadɔa tu ge la ene: Elabena Egblɔ be: "Kpɔ egbɔ be nàwɔ nuawo katã ɖe nɔnɔme si wotsɔ fia wò le toa dzi la nu pɛpɛpɛ. " 6 Ke azɔ subɔsubɔdɔ si nyo wu sãsãsã ye su Yesu si, elabena ezu nubabla si nyo wu ema la ƒe domenɔla, esi woɖo le se nu ɖe ŋugbedodo siwo nyo wu la dzi.
ENGLISH: 4 If then he were on earth he would not be a priest at all, there being those who offer the gifts in accordance with the law, 5 who perform the service of a model and shadow of the heavenly, as Moses had the revelation made to him when he was going to execute the Tent; for it says "See that you make everything in conformity with the figure that was showed you on the mountain. " 6 But now he enjoys a more transcendent ministry insofar as he is also mediator of a better covenant which has its legislation on the basis of better promises.

EWE: 7 Ne ɖe vodada mele nubabla gbãtɔa ŋu o la, anye ne evelia mahiã o.
ENGLISH: 7 For if that first one had been irreproachable there would be no looking for a place for a second.

EWE: 8 Elabena fɔ bumee wòle ameawo esime wògblɔ be: "‘Kpɔ ɖa! Ŋkekewo li gbɔna,’ Yehowa ye gblɔe, ‘esime mabla nu yeye kple Israel ƒe aƒe la kpakple Yuda ƒe aƒe la. 9 Manɔ abe nu, si mebla kple wo tɔgbuiwo le gbe si gbe melé woƒe alɔnu kplɔ wo tso Egipte-nyigba dzi la ene o, elabena womeyi edzi lé nu, si mebla kpli wo la me ɖe asi o, eya ta medzudzɔ beléle na wo,’ Yehowa ye gblɔe. 10 "‘Elabena esiae nye nu, si mabla kple Israel ƒe aƒe la le ŋkeke mawo megbe,’ Yehowa ye gblɔe. ‘Matsɔ nye sewo ade woƒe susu me, eye maŋlɔ wo ɖe woƒe dziwo me. Manye woƒe Mawu, eye woawo woanye nye dukɔ. 11 "‘Eye ame aɖeke magafia nu ehavi kple nɔvia agblɔ be: "Dze si Yehowa! " o. Elabena wo katã woadze sim, tso ɖeviwo dzi va se ɖe tsitsiawo dzi. 12 Elabena makpɔ nublanui na wo le woƒe nu madzɔmadzɔ wɔwɔwo me, eye nyemagaɖo ŋku woƒe nu vɔ̃wo dzi azɔ o.’ " 13 Esi wògblɔ be "nubabla yeye " la, ena gbãtɔ la do xoxo. Ke nu si do xoxo eye enu le yiyim la, eteƒe madidi hafi woaɖee ɖa keŋ o.
ENGLISH: 8 For he says, reproaching them, "Here are days coming, says the Lord, that I will execute regarding the house of Israel and the house of Judah a new covenant 9 not like the covenant I made for their fathers on the day of my taking them by the hand to bring them out of Egypt, because they did not adhere to my covenant and I left them to themselves, says the Lord; 10 because this is the covenant I will establish for the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord, putting my laws into their mind and inscribing them on their hearts, and they shall have me for their God and I will have them for my people, 11 and they shall not be each teaching his fellow-citizen and each his brother ‘Know the Lord,’ because they shall all know me from the least to the greatest of them, 12 because I will be gracious to their wrong-doings and will no longer remember their sins. " 13 In saying "new " he has antiquated the first one; but what is being antiquated and showing its old age is somewhere near disappearance.

EWE: Hebritɔwo
ENGLISH: Hebrews

EWE: 9 Le nubabla tsãtɔ gome la, subɔsubɔdɔ kɔkɔe ŋuti sewo nɔ anyi, eye eƒe kɔkɔeƒe la nɔ anyigba dzi.
ENGLISH: 9 So the first one did have ordinances of service and its sanctuary of a mundane sort.

EWE: 2 Elabena wotu agbadɔ la ƒe akpa gbãtɔ si me akaɖiti kple kplɔ̃ kpakple ŋkumeɖobolowo nɔna la; eye woyɔnɛ be Kɔkɔeƒe la. 3 Ke le xɔmetsovɔ evelia godo la, agbadɔ la ƒe akpa si woyɔna be Kɔkɔeƒewo Ƒe Kɔkɔeƒe la li. 4 Nu siwo le afi siae nye sikadzudzɔdosonu kple nubablaɖaka si ŋu wofa sika ɖo keŋ kpe ɖo, si me sikaze si me mana le la kple Aron ƒe atikplɔ si ƒo se kpakple nubabla ƒe kpe gbadzɛawo le; 5 ke ŋutikɔkɔe ƒe kerubiwo le aɖaka la tame, eye wodo vɔvɔli ɖe avulénutunu la dzi.
ENGLISH: 2 For a tent was constructed, the first one, in which the lampstand and the showbread were, which tent is designated as Holy, 3 and after the second curtain a tent, the one designated as Holiest of the Holy, 4 with a golden altar of incense and the ark of the covenant coated all over with gold, in which there were a gold jar holding the manna, and Aaron’s stick that sprouted, and the tablets of the covenant; 5 and up on top of it cherubim of glory shading the mercy-seat, about which things it is not practicable to tell in detail now.

EWE: Ke menye fifiae míanɔ nu ƒom le nu siawo ŋu tsitotsito o. 6 Esi wotui alea vɔ la, nunɔlawo gena ɖe agbadɔ la ƒe akpa gbãtɔ me edziedzi be woawɔ subɔsubɔdɔ kɔkɔe; 7 ke nunɔlagã la ɖeɖe koe gena ɖe akpa evelia ya zi ɖeka ƒe ɖeka, eye megena ɖe eme o, negbe ɖe wòtsɔ ʋu si wòana ɖe eya ŋutɔ kple dukɔ la ƒe nu vɔ̃ siwo wowɔ le manyamanya me ta la ɖe asi hafi.
ENGLISH: 6 And, these things being thus arranged, into the first tent the priests are all the time coming in to go through with the services, 7 but into the second the high priest only, once a year, not without blood which he offers for the people’s indiscretions, 8 what the Holy Spirit meant to express being this, that the way to the sanctuary had not yet been brought to light while the first tent was still standing.

EWE: 8 Ale gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔe la na wòdze ƒãa be, zi ale si agbadɔ gbãtɔ la gakpɔtɔ li la, womeɖe mɔ si yi kɔkɔeƒe emetɔ la fia o. 9 Agbadɔ sia tututu nye kpɔɖeŋu na nu siwo li le fifi ɣeyiɣi sia me, eye wonaa nunanawo hesaa vɔwo le ɖoɖo sia nu. Gake nu siawo mate ŋu ana ame si le subɔsubɔdɔ kɔkɔe wɔm la ƒe dzitsinya ŋuti nadza bliboe o.
ENGLISH: 9 Which is a parable for the present time; in keeping with which there are being offered gifts and sacrifices that cannot perfect the worshiper as to conscience, 10 only on the score of foods and drinks and different ablutions: ordinances for flesh, imposed till a time of rectification.

EWE: 11 Ke esime Kristo va abe nu nyui siwo va li la ƒe nunɔlagã ene la, ege ɖe agbadɔ si lolo wu hede blibo wu, esi wometsɔ asi tu o, si fia be menye nuwɔwɔ sia ƒe akpa aɖeke o, la me. 12 Menye gbɔ̃wo kple nyitsuwo ƒe ʋu ye wòtsɔ ge ɖe kɔkɔeƒe la zi ɖeka ɖe ɣeyiɣiawo katã nu o, ke boŋ eya ŋutɔ ƒe ʋu ye, eye wòxɔ ɖeɖekpɔkpɔ mavɔ vɛ na mí.
ENGLISH: 11 But when Christ arrived, high priest of good things that had come into existence, by way of the greater and more perfect tent, not man-made, that is, not of this creation, and not by virtue of blood of goats and steers but by his own blood, 12 he entered the holy place once for all, achieving an eternal redemption.

EWE: 13 Elabena ne gbɔ̃wo kple nyitsuwo ƒe ʋu kpakple nyinɔe ƒe afi, si wohlẽna ɖe ame siwo ŋu mekɔ o ŋu la, klɔa ŋutilã la ŋu henana wo ŋu kɔna la, 14 ekema ɖe Kristo la, ame si to gbɔgbɔ mavɔ ƒe dɔwɔwɔ dzi tsɔ eɖokui na Mawu abe vɔsa si ŋu mokaka mele o ene la, ƒe ʋu maklɔ míaƒe dzitsinyawo ŋu tso dɔwɔwɔ kukuwo me geɖe wu, ale be míawɔ subɔsubɔdɔ kɔkɔe na Mawu gbagbe la oa? 15 Esia tae wònye nubabla yeye ƒe domenɔla ɖo, ale be esi wòku be yeaɖe wo tso vodada siwo wowɔ le nubabla tsãtɔ te la me to tafe dzi ta la, ame siwo woyɔ la naxɔ domenyinu mavɔ ƒe ŋugbedodo la.
ENGLISH: 13 For if the blood of goats and bulls, and ashes of a heifer sprinkling the defiled, hallow one as regards the cleanness of the flesh, 14 how much more will the blood of the Christ, who by the working of an eternal Spirit offered himself as a faultless oblation to God, cleanse our conscience from the corpses of our deeds for worshiping a living God! 15 And this is why he is mediator of a new covenant, so that, a death having taken place to cancel the transgressions under the first covenant, those who had been called might receive the promised eternal inheritance.

EWE: 16 Elabena afi si nubabla le la, ele be woaɖo kpe ame si nye nublala la ƒe ku dzi, 17 elabena wonɔa te ɖe ku dzi nana nubabla wɔa dɔ, elabena zi ale si nublala la le agbe la, ŋusẽ mele nubabla la ŋu o.
ENGLISH: 16 For where there is a testament it is necessary that the testator’s death be put in evidence; 17 for it is for the affairs of the dead that a testament is valid, since when the testator is alive it is not at the time in effect.

EWE: 18 Eya ta womeɖo nubabla tsãtɔ la hã anyi ʋu manɔmee o.
ENGLISH: 18 Whence it comes that not even the first one was inaugurated without blood.

EWE: 19 Elabena esime Mose gblɔ Se la ƒe nudidiwo katã na dukɔ bliboa la, etsɔ nyitsuiwo kple gbɔ̃wo ƒe ʋu hekpe ɖe tsi kple alẽfu dzĩ kpakple isop gbe ŋu, eye wòhlẽ wo ɖe nubablagbalẽ la kple dukɔ blibo la ŋu 20 hegblɔ be: "Esiae nye nubabla si ƒe se Mawu de na mi be mialé eme ɖe asi la, ƒe ʋu. " 21 Eye wòhlẽ ʋu la ɖe agbadɔ la kple nu siwo katã wozãna le subɔsubɔdɔ kɔkɔe me la hã ŋu nenema ke. 22 Ɛ̃, wotsɔa ʋu klɔa nu sia nu kloe ŋu le Se la nu, eye ne womekɔ ʋu ɖi o la, tsɔtsɔke aɖeke menɔa anyi o.
ENGLISH: 19 For after every commandment had been spoken to all the people by Moses in accordance with the law, he took the blood of the steers and goats with water and scarlet wool and marjoram and sprinkled the book itself and all the people, 20 saying "This is the blood of the covenant which God commanded for you. " 21 And he likewise sprinkled with the blood the tent and all the vessels for the services; 22 and, broadly speaking, according to the law everything is cleansed with blood, and without the shedding of blood no exoneration takes place.

EWE: 23 Eya ta ehiã vevie be woatsɔ nu siawo akɔ nu siwo nye dziƒonuwo ƒe kpɔɖeŋu la ŋu, gake dziƒonuwo ya hiã vɔsa si nyo wu sãsãsã la.
ENGLISH: 23 So there is a necessity that the models of what is in the heavens be cleansed with these things but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices transcending these.

EWE: 24 Elabena menye kɔkɔeƒe si wotsɔ asi wɔ, si nye vavãtɔ la ƒe kpɔɖeŋu, ye Kristo yi o, ke boŋ dziƒo ŋutɔŋutɔ wòyi, ale be wòado ɖe Mawu ŋkume azɔ le mía ta. 25 Eye menye be wòatsɔ eɖokui anɔ nanam enuenu, abe ale si nunɔlagã la tsɔa ʋu si menye eya ŋutɔ tɔ o gena ɖe kɔkɔeƒe la ƒe sia ƒe ene o. 26 Ne nenemae la, ekema ahiã be wòanɔ fu kpem enuenu tso xexea ƒe gɔmeɖoanyiɣi. Ke azɔ eɖe eɖokui fia zi ɖeka ɖe ɣeyiɣiawo katã nu le nuɖoanyiawo ƒe nuwuɣi, be wòaɖe nu vɔ̃ ɖa esi wòtsɔ eɖokui sa vɔe.
ENGLISH: 24 For it was not into a man-made sanctuary, a reproduction of the true one, that Christ went in, but into heaven itself, to appear in God’s presence now for us; 25 neither was it with a view to offering himself repeatedly as the high priest goes into the sanctuary year after year by another creature’s blood, 26 else he would have had to suffer over and over since the foundation of the world; but now it is once, at the culmination of the ages, that he has shown himself for the annulment of sin by his sacrifice.

EWE: 27 Eye ale si ko wòle na amewo be woaku zi ɖeka ɖe ɣeyiɣiawo katã nu, eye esia megbe ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃ nava la, 28 nenema kee Kristo la hã tsɔ eɖokui na zi ɖeka ɖe ɣeyiɣiawo katã nu be wòatsɔ ame geɖewo ƒe nu vɔ̃wo; eye zi evelia si wòado la, manye ɖe nu vɔ̃ ta o, eye ame siwo le mɔ kpɔm na woƒe ɖeɖekpɔkpɔ vevie lae akpɔe.
ENGLISH: 27 And as surely as it is reserved for men to die once, but after this a judgment, 28 so too the Christ, offered once to take up the sins of many, will appear a second time, clear of sin, for salvation, to those who are awaiting him.

EWE: Hebritɔwo
ENGLISH: Hebrews

EWE: 2 Ne menye nenema o la, ɖe womadzudzɔ vɔsasa oa? Elabena afia be wokɔ ame siwo le subɔsubɔdɔ kɔkɔe wɔm la ŋu zi ɖeka ko evɔ, eye le esia ta womagase le wo ɖokuiwo me be yewonye nu vɔ̃ wɔlawo azɔ o. 3 Ke vɔsa siawo ɖoa ŋku nu vɔ̃ dzi na ame ƒe sia ƒe boŋ, 4 elabena nyitsuwo kple gbɔ̃tsuwo ƒe ʋu mate ŋu aɖe nu vɔ̃wo ɖa o. 5 Esia tae esime wòva xexea me la, egblɔ be: "‘Menye vɔsawo kple nunanawoe nèdina o, ke boŋ èdzra ŋutilã ɖo ɖi nam.
ENGLISH: 10 For the law, having a shadow of the future good, not the very image of the things, can never year by year with the same sacrifices, which they are offering, perfect in perpetuity those who come; 2 else would they not have ceased to be offered because the worshipers, once cleansed, would no longer have had sins on their conscience? 3 but in them there is a remembrance of sins year by year, 4 for it is impossible that blood of goats and bulls should take away sins; 5 for which reason as he comes into the world he says "Sacrifice and offering thou hadst no will for, but a body thou didst fit for me; 6 burnt-offerings and sin-offerings thou didst not approve.

EWE: 6 Numevɔsa blibowo kple nuvɔ̃vɔsa medzea ŋuwò o.’ 7 Eye megblɔ be: ‘Kpɔ ɖa! Meva ɖo (agbalẽ xatsaxatsa la mee woŋlɔ nu ɖo le ŋunye) be, Oo Mawu, wò lɔlɔ̃nu mawɔ.’ " 8 Egblɔ gbã be: "Menye vɔsawo kple nunanawo kple numevɔsa blibowo kpakple nuvɔ̃vɔsawoe nèdina o, eye womedzea ŋuwò hã o " vɔ siwo wosana le Se la nue wòwɔnɛ 9 emegbe egagblɔ be: "Kpɔ ɖa! Meva ɖo be mawɔ wò lɔlɔ̃nu. " Eɖe nu gbãtɔ la ɖa, be wòaɖo evelia anyi.
ENGLISH: 7 Then I said ‘Here I come, in a roll of a book it is written of me, to do thy will, God.’ " 8 Saying above "Sacrifices and offerings and burnt-offerings and sin-offerings thou hadst no will for and didst not approve, " which are offered according to the law, 9 he has then said "Here I come to do thy will "; he abolishes the first to make good the second; 10 in which will we have been sanctified by the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.

EWE: 10 Le eƒe "lɔlɔ̃nu " sia nu la, wokɔ mía ŋu to Yesu Kristo ƒe ŋutilã si wotsɔ na zi ɖeka ɖe ɣeyiɣiawo katã nu la dzi. 11 Azɔ hã nunɔla ɖe sia ɖe nɔa eƒe teƒe gbe sia gbe nɔa subɔsubɔdɔ kɔkɔe wɔm eye wòsaa vɔ mawo ke enuenu, siwo mate ŋu aɖe nu vɔ̃wo ɖa keŋkeŋ gbeɖe o. 12 Ke eya sa vɔ zi ɖeka ɖe nu vɔ̃wo ta ɖe ɣeyiɣiawo katã nu, eye wòbɔbɔ nɔ Mawu ƒe ɖusime, 13 eye tso ɣemaɣi wòle lalam va se ɖe esime woatsɔ eƒe futɔwo awɔ eƒe afɔɖodzinui. 14 Elabena vɔsa ɖeka dzi wòto na ame siwo ŋu wokɔ la de blibo hena ɣeyiɣiawo katã.
ENGLISH: 11 And every priest stands day by day performing his services and repeatedly offering the same sacrifices, which can never remove sins; 12 but this one, having offered one sacrifice for sins, took a seat in perpetuity at God’s right hand, 13 thenceforth waiting till his enemies be made the footstool for his feet, 14 for by one offering he has brought those who were to be sanctified into perfect status in perpetuity.

EWE: 15 Gawu la, gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔe la hã ɖia ɖase na mí, elabena egblɔ gbã be: 16 "‘Esiae nye nu, si mabla kpli wo le ŋkeke mawo megbe,’ Yehowa ye gblɔe. ‘Matsɔ nye sewo ade woƒe dziwo me, eye maŋlɔ wo ɖe woƒe susuwo me.’ " 17 Egagblɔ be: "Eye nyemagaɖo ŋku woƒe nu vɔ̃wo kple woƒe dzidadawo dzi azɔ o. " 18 Ke ne wotsɔ nu siawo ke la, vɔsasa ɖe nu vɔ̃wo ta megali o.
ENGLISH: 15 And the Holy Spirit too gives us testimony; for after having said 16 "this is the covenant I will establish for them after those days, says the Lord, putting my laws on their hearts and inscribing them on their mind, " 17 comes "and will no longer remember their sins and their wickednesses. " 18 But where there is exoneration from these there is no more offering of anything for sin.

EWE: 21 Eye esi nunɔlagã si le Mawu ƒe aƒe la nu le mía si ta la, 22 mina míate ɖe Mawu ŋu kple dzi nyateƒetɔ kple xɔse blibo, esi wohlẽ ʋu ɖe míaƒe dziwo ŋu tsɔ kɔ wo ŋu tso dzitsinya vɔ̃ɖi me, eye wole tsi dzadzɛ na míaƒe ŋutilãwo la ta. 23 Mina míalé míaƒe mɔkpɔkpɔ me ʋuʋu me ɖe asi sesĩe maʋamaʋãe, elabena ame si do ŋugbea la, nuteƒewɔlae wònye. 24 Eye mina míanɔ mía nɔewo ŋu bum, ale be míado ŋusẽ mía nɔewo na lɔlɔ̃ kple dɔ nyuiwo wɔwɔ, 25 eye míaganɔ míaƒe kpekpewo gblẽm ɖi, abe ale si wòzu numame na ame aɖewo ene o, ke boŋ míanɔ dzi dem ƒo na mía nɔewo, eye míawɔe geɖe wu, zi ale si miekpɔ be ŋkeke la le ɖoɖom la.
ENGLISH: 19 So, brothers, having confidence for entrance into the sanctuary by Jesus’s blood, 20 which entrance he inaugurated for us, a fresh and living passage through the curtain (that is, his flesh), 21 and having a great priest over God’s house, 22 let us come with a true heart in certitude of faith, our hearts sprinkled from bad conscience and our bodies washed with clean water; 23 let us hold erect the profession of our faith, for he who made the promises is faithful, 24 and let us observe each other to stimulate us to love and good works, 25 not abandoning our assemblies as some have a way of doing, but cheering on; and the more as you see the day coming nearer.

EWE: 26 Elabena ne nyateƒe la ƒe sidzedze vavãtɔ su mía si hafi míegaɖoe le nu vɔ̃ wɔm la, ekema vɔsasa ɖe nu vɔ̃wo ta aɖeke megali o, 27 ke boŋ ɖeko míanɔ mɔ kpɔm kple vɔvɔ̃ na ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃ kpakple dziku helĩhelĩ si gbɔna tsitretsiɖeŋulawo dzi la.
ENGLISH: 26 For if we sin willfully after having had the recognition of the truth, there no longer remains a sacrifice for sins, 27 but a frightful waiting for judgment, and the jealousy of a fire that is to consume foes.

EWE: 28 Wowua ame sia ame si do vlo Mose ƒe Sea la nublanuimakpɔmakpɔe, le ame eve alo etɔ̃ ƒe ɖaseɖiɖi nu. 29 Tohehe si sesẽ wu kae miesusu be adze na ame si tu afɔ Mawu ƒe Vi la dzi, eye wòbu nubabla ƒe ʋu si wotsɔ kɔ eŋu la nu maɖinui hedo vlo amenuvevegbɔgbɔ la? 30 Elabena míenya Ame si gblɔ be: "Tɔnyee nye hlɔ̃biabia; maɖo eteƒe. " Eye wògagblɔ be: "Yehowa adrɔ̃ ʋɔnu eƒe dukɔ la. " 31 Ŋɔdzinu wònye be ame nadze Mawu gbagbe la ƒe asi me.
ENGLISH: 28 When one has disregarded Moses’s law he dies without mercy at two or three witnesses; 29 how much worse a penalty do you think he will be deemed to deserve who has trampled on the Son of God and has regarded as unholy the covenant blood by which he was sanctified and has affronted the Spirit of grace? 30 For we know who it was that said "Mine is vengeance; I will requite, " and again "The Lord will judge his people. " 31 It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of a living God.

EWE: 32 Gake minɔ ŋku ɖom edzi be le tsãŋkekewo me la, esi miekpɔ kekelia vɔ megbe la, miedo dzi eye mieʋli vevie le fukpekpewo me. 33 Ɣeaɖewoɣi la, wodo ŋukpe mi le dutoƒo, eye mieto xaxawo me, eye ɣebubuɣiwo la, miekpe fu mawo ke kpli wo. 34 Elabena miese veve ɖe ame siwo le gaxɔ me la nu, eye esi woha miaƒe nuwo la, miexɔe kple dzidzɔ, elabena mienyae be nunɔamesi si nyo wu eye wònɔa anyi ɖaa lae le mia si.
ENGLISH: 32 But recollect the earlier days in which after you were given the light you held out through a hard grind of suffering, 33 for one thing being made a spectacle of with insults and distresses, and for another thing showing your solidarity with those who were leading such a life 34 for you shared the suffering of the imprisoned and accepted cheerfully the pillage of your property, knowing that you have better belongings that stay by you.

EWE: 35 Eya ta migatsɔ miaƒe dzideƒo, si teƒeɖoɖo gã li na la, ƒu gbe o.
ENGLISH: 35 So do not throw up your confidence, which has great wages payable.

EWE: 36 Elabena ehiã be miado dzi, ale be ne miewɔ Mawu ƒe lɔlɔ̃nu vɔ la, miaƒe asi nasu ŋugbedodo la dzi.
ENGLISH: 36 For staying power is what it takes, that after doing God’s will you may receive the fulfillment of the promise: 37 "for yet the least moment he who is coming will come and not be belated.

EWE: 37 Elabena "esusɔ vie ko, " eye "ame si gbɔna la ava ɖo, eye mahe ɖe megbe o. " 38 "Ke nye ame dzɔdzɔe la ƒe xɔsee ana wòanɔ agbe, " eye "ne egbugbɔ ɖe megbe la, nyemakpɔ ŋudzedze ɖe eŋu o. " 39 Ke míenye ame siwo gbugbɔna ɖe megbe yia tsɔtsrɔ̃ me la dometɔwo o, ke boŋ ame siwo si xɔse le, si ana woaxɔ mí ɖe agbe la dometɔwoe míenye.
ENGLISH: 38 And my righteous man shall have life out of faith; and if he flinches my soul takes no satisfaction in him. " 39 And we are not for flinching that comes to destruction, but for faith that comes to soul-preservation.

EWE: Hebritɔwo
ENGLISH: Hebrews

EWE: 11 Xɔse nye dziɖoɖo ɖe nu si wole mɔ kpɔm na la ŋu kakaɖedzitɔe kple kpeɖodzi si dze ƒãa be nu siwo kpɔm womele o la li ŋutɔŋutɔ.
ENGLISH: 11 And faith is assuming the validity of hopes, putting unseen things to the test.

EWE: 2 Elabena esia dzie blematɔwo to kpɔ ɖaseɖiɖi na wo ɖokuiwo.
ENGLISH: 2 For it is as to this the old-timers are vouched for.

EWE: 3 Le xɔse me míekpɔe dze sii be woɖo nuɖoanyiwo anyi le Mawu ƒe nya la nu, ale be nu si wokpɔna la dzɔ tso nu siwo medzena wokpɔna o la me.
ENGLISH: 3 It is by faith we apprehend that the worlds were set in order by a word of God’s, so that it is not out of observable things that what we see was made.

EWE: 4 Le xɔse me Abel tsɔ vɔsa si nyo wu Kain tɔ la na Mawu, eye to xɔse sia dzi wòkpɔ ɖaseɖiɖi be enye ame dzɔdzɔe, elabena Mawu xɔ eƒe nunanawo, eye togbɔ be eku hã la, egale nu ƒom to eƒe xɔse me.
ENGLISH: 4 It was by faith Abel offered to God more of a sacrifice than Cain, through which he had himself attested to be righteous, God testifying over his gifts; and it is through it he still speaks after he dies.

EWE: 5 Le xɔse me wokɔ Enok dzoe, be wòagakpɔ ku o, eye womegakpɔe le afi aɖeke o, elabena Mawu kɔe dzoe; elabena hafi woakɔe adzoe la, ekpɔ ɖaseɖiɖi be eƒe nu dze Mawu ŋu nyuie. 6 Gawu la, ne xɔse mele ame si o la, mate ŋu adze Mawu ŋu nyuie o, elabena ele be ame sia ame si tena vaa Mawu gbɔ la naxɔe ase be eli, eye wònyea teƒeɖola na ame siwo dinɛ vevie la.
ENGLISH: 5 It was by faith Enoch was translated so as not to see death, and was not to be found because God had translated him; for before the translation he was vouched for as having pleased God, 6 but without faith it is impossible to please; for he who comes to God has to believe that he is and that to those who seek him he proves a paymaster.

EWE: 7 Le xɔse me Noa, esime Mawu na toklãe tso nu siwo womekpɔ haɖe o ŋu la, eɖe mawuvɔvɔ̃ fia, eye wòkpa aɖakaʋu hena eƒemetɔwo ɖeɖe; eye to xɔse sia me la, ebu fɔ xexea, eye wòzu dzɔdzɔenyenye, si tso xɔse me la, ƒe domenyila.
ENGLISH: 7 It was by faith Noah, receiving a revelation about what could not yet be seen, was on his guard and constructed an ark for the saving of his family, through which he pronounced condemnation on the world and became heir to the righteousness that comes in the way of faith.

EWE: 8 Le xɔse me Abraham, esime woyɔe la, eɖo to hedo go yi teƒe si woɖo be wòaxɔ wòanye eƒe domenyinu la; eye wòdzo, togbɔ be menya afi si yim wòle o hã.
ENGLISH: 8 It was by faith Abraham, when he was called, obeyed to go out to a place he was to get for an inheritance, and did go out, not knowing where he was going.

EWE: 9 Le xɔse me eyi ɖanɔ ŋugbedodonyigba la dzi le dzronyigba dzi abe amedzro ene, eye eya kple Isak kpakple Yakob, ame siwo hã nye ŋugbedodo ma tututu ƒe domenyilawo la, nɔ agbadɔwo me. 10 Elabena enɔ du si gɔmeɖoanyi ŋutɔŋutɔwo li na la lalam, du si ƒe aɖaŋuwɔla kple tsolae nye Mawu.
ENGLISH: 9 It was by faith he lived in an immigrant’s condition in the country he had the promise of as if in a country not his own, living in tents with Isaac and Jacob, the co-heirs of the same promise; 10 for he was waiting for the city that has the foundations, of which God is architect and artisan.

EWE: 11 Le xɔse me wona ŋusẽ Sara hã wòfɔ fu dzi vi, esime wòtsi to vidzidzi me kura gɔ̃ hã, elabena ebu Ame si do ŋugbea la nuteƒewɔlae. 12 Esia tae tso ame ɖeka, si ƒe vidzidziŋutete ku la, mee wodzi vi siwo sɔ gbɔ abe dziƒoɣletiviwo ene, abe ƒutake siwo mele xexlẽ me o la ene.
ENGLISH: 11 It was by faith Sarah herself too received power for founding a line of descendants even out of her time of life, since she regarded the giver of the promise as trustworthy; 12 because of which, also, there were born from one and one who had gone dead, at that descendants numerous as the stars in the sky or as the uncountable sand on the seashore.

EWE: 13 Le xɔse me ame siawo katã ku, togbɔ be woƒe asi mesu ŋugbedodoawo dzi o hã; ke wokpɔ wo le adzɔge ɖaa, eye wodo ɖoaƒe na wo, eye woʋu eme be yewonye amedzrowo kple ame siwo le anyigba la dzi hena ɣeyiɣi kpui aɖe.
ENGLISH: 13 In faith all these died, not having received the promised things but having seen and greeted them at a distance and avowed that on the earth they were strangers living away from their home.

EWE: 14 Elabena ame siwo gblɔe nenema la ɖee fia be yewole teƒe si azu yewo ŋutɔwo tɔ la dim vevie.
ENGLISH: 14 For those who say things of that sort make it manifest that they are wanting a home.

EWE: 15 Ke ne ɖe wona woƒe susu kpɔtɔ nɔ teƒe si woʋu tso dzi la, anye ne mɔnukpɔkpɔ su wo si wogbugbɔ yi. 16 Ke azɔ la, nɔƒe si nyo wu la le wo dzrom, si nye dziƒo tɔ.
ENGLISH: 15 And if they had been remembering that one from which they had gone out, they would have had a suitable time for going back; 16 but as it is, they are bent on a better one, that is, a heavenly one.

EWE: Eya ta mekpe ŋu na Mawu be woayɔ ye be yewoƒe Mawu o, elabena edzra du ɖo ɖi na wo.
ENGLISH: For which reason God is not ashamed of them, of being designated as their God; for he has got a city ready for them.

EWE: 17 Le xɔse me Abraham, esime wodoe kpɔ la, etsɔ Isak na, eya, ame si xɔ ŋugbedodoawo kple dzidzɔ la, tsɔ eƒe tenuvi la sa vɔe kloe, 18 togbɔ be wogblɔ nɛ be, "Ame si woayɔ be ‘wò dzidzimevi’ la adzɔ tso Isak me " hã. 19 Ke ebui be Mawu ate ŋu afɔe ɖe tsitre tso ame kukuwo dome, eye exɔe tso ku me hã le kpɔɖeŋumɔ nu.
ENGLISH: 17 It was by faith Abraham, when put to the test, brought Isaac as a sacrifice, and he who had taken the promises to himself, 18 to whom the word had been spoken "it will be by Isaac that issue shall be called yours, " was sacrificing his only son, 19 counting on it that God is powerful enough to raise from the dead, wherefrom he did, figuratively speaking, receive him.

EWE: 20 Le xɔse me kee Isak yra Yakob kple Esau le nu siwo ava va la ŋu.
ENGLISH: 20 It was by faith, too, Isaac gave Jacob and Esau a blessing about future things.

EWE: 21 Le xɔse me Yakob, esime wòsusɔ vie wòaku la, eyra Yosef viŋutsuawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe, eye wòziɔ ɖe eƒe atizɔti ŋu de ta agu.
ENGLISH: 21 It was by faith Jacob, when dying, blessed each of Joseph’s sons, and did reverence on the top of his staff.

EWE: 22 Le xɔse me Yosef, esime eƒe kuɣi gogo la, eƒo nu tso Israel-viwo ƒe ʋuʋu la ŋu, eye wòde se le eƒe ƒuwo ŋu.
ENGLISH: 22 It was by faith Joseph, when passing away, mentioned the coming out of the sons of Israel from Egypt and gave a command about his bones.

EWE: 23 Le xɔse me, esime wodzi Mose la, edzilawo ɣlae ɣleti etɔ̃ sɔŋ, elabena wokpɔe be ɖevi la dze ɖeka, eye womevɔ̃ fia ƒe sedede la o.
ENGLISH: 23 It was by faith Moses, when born, was hidden three months by his parents because they saw the child was a pretty one, and they were not afraid of the king’s order.

EWE: 24 Le xɔse me Mose, esime wòtsi la, egbe be woagayɔ ye be Farao vinyɔnu la ƒe vi o, 25 eye wòtiae be yeakpe fu kple Mawu ƒe dukɔ la, wu be yease nu vɔ̃ ƒe vivi si nɔa anyi ɣeyiɣi kpui aɖe ko, 26 elabena ebu ŋukpe si wodoe abe Kristo la ene be exɔ asi sãsãsã wu Egipte ƒe kesinɔnuwo, elabena eƒe ŋku nɔ teƒeɖoɖofetu la dzi tututu.
ENGLISH: 24 It was by faith Moses, when he grew up, renounced being known as Pharaoh’s daughter’s son, 25 choosing rather to share the hardships of God’s people than to have temporary enjoyment from a sin, 26 regarding the insults given to the Christ as a greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt; for he had his eye on the wages to be paid.

EWE: 27 Le xɔse me edzo le Egipte, ke mevɔ̃ fia ƒe dziku la o, elabena eyi edzi nɔ te sesĩe, abe ɖe wòle Ame si womekpɔna o la kpɔm ene.
ENGLISH: 27 It was by faith he left Egypt, not fearing the king’s rage, for he bore up as seeing the Invisible One.

EWE: 28 Le xɔse me eɖu Ŋutitotoŋkekenyui la hewɔ ɖe ʋuhehlẽ ƒe ɖoɖo la dzi, ale be nutsrɔ̃la la nagaka asi woƒe ŋgɔgbeviwo ŋu o.
ENGLISH: 28 It was by faith he celebrated the passover and the application of the blood so that the destroyer of the firstborn should not touch them.

EWE: 29 Le xɔse me woto Ƒudzĩ la me abe anyigba ƒuƒui dzi ene, ke esi Egiptetɔwo tee kpɔ la, ƒu la mi wo.
ENGLISH: 29 It was by faith they crossed the Red Sea as if along dry ground; attempting which, the Egyptians were swallowed up.

EWE: 30 Le xɔse me Yeriko gliawo mu esi wozɔ ƒo xlãe ŋkeke adre megbe.
ENGLISH: 30 It was by faith the walls of Jericho fell after seven days of circling around them.

EWE: 31 Le xɔse me Rahab, gbolo la, metsrɔ̃ kpe ɖe tosẽlawo ŋuti o, elabena exɔ ŋkutsalawo le ŋutifafa me. 32 Eye nya kae magagblɔ?
ENGLISH: 31 It was by faith Rahab the prostitute did not perish with those who had been disobedient, she having received the spies with peace.

EWE: Elabena ɣeyiɣi mele asinye be maƒo nu tso Gideon, Barak, Samson, Yefta, David kpakple Samuel kple nyagblɔɖila bubuawo ŋu o. 33 Le xɔse me woɖu fiaɖuƒewo dzi, wowɔ nu dzɔdzɔe, xɔ ŋugbedodowo, mia nu na dzatawo, 34 tsi dzo ƒe ŋusẽ nu, si le yi nu, wona ŋusẽ ɖo wo ŋu le gbɔdzɔgbɔdzɔ me, wowɔ kalẽ le aʋawɔwɔ me, wosi aʋakɔ siwo tso ɖe wo ŋu la keŋkeŋ.
ENGLISH: 32 And why say more? for the time will fail me as I tell about Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, and David and Samuel and the prophets, 33 who through faith put down kingdoms, did service to the right, won promises, stopped lions’ mouths, 34 quenched the power of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, were brought to powerfulness from weakness, became strong in war, routed camps of aliens.

EWE: 35 Wofɔ nyɔnu siwo ƒe amewo ku la ɖe tsitre na wo, ke wowɔ fu ame bubuwo vevie, elabena womelɔ̃ be yewoana ta ale be yewoakpɔ ablɔɖe le mɔ aɖe nu o, be yewoakpɔ tsitretsitsi si nyo wu la. 36 Ɛ̃, ame bubuwo to fewuɖuɖuwo kple ƒoƒowo ƒe tetekpɔwo me, gawu la, wokpe bablawo kple gaxɔmenɔnɔwo ƒe fu.
ENGLISH: 35 Women received their dead in resurrection; and others were beaten to death and did not accept a chance of getting off, in order that a better resurrection might be theirs; 36 and others experienced derisive indignities and lashes, and chains and prison life moreover.

EWE: 37 Woƒu kpe wo, wote wo kpɔ, wodze wo ɖe eve kple laxalaxa, wowu wo kple yi, wonɔ tsatsam le alẽgbalẽwo me, le gbɔ̃gbalẽwo me, esime wole hiã me, le xaxa me, le fuwɔwɔ wo me; 38 eye xexea medze wo o. Wotsa tsaglãla le gbedzi kple towo dzi kpakple anyigba dzi agadowo kple ʋewo me.
ENGLISH: 37 They were stoned, sawed in two, put to the sword; they went about in sheepskins, in goatskins, suffering want, distress, hardship, 38 they of whom the world was not worthy, wandering in deserts and mountains and caves and holes in the ground.

EWE: 39 Togbɔ be ame siawo katã kpɔ ɖaseɖiɖi nyui na wo ɖokuiwo le woƒe xɔse ta hã la, womekpɔ ŋugbedodo la me vava o, 40 elabena Mawu kpɔ nane si nyo wu la da ɖi na mí, ne woagawɔ wo bliboe míawo manɔmee o.
ENGLISH: 39 And all these, though by faith they had themselves vouched for, did not receive what was promised, 40 as God looked forward to something better regarding us, so that they were not to come to completeness apart from us.

EWE: Hebritɔwo
ENGLISH: Hebrews

EWE: 12 Eya ta esi ɖasefowo ƒe alilikpo gã sia gbegbe ƒo xlã mí ta la, mina míaɖe nu kpekpe sia nu kpekpe kple nu vɔ̃ si ɖea to ɖe mí bɔbɔe la ɖa, eye mina míatsɔ dzidodo anɔ duɖimekeke si woɖo na mí la dzi, 2 esi míaƒe ŋku le Yesu, si nye míaƒe xɔse ƒe Kplɔla Vevitɔ kple Ame si na míaƒe xɔse de blibo la ŋu tututu. Le dzidzɔ si wotsɔ ɖo eŋkume ta la, edo dzi kpe fuwɔameti ŋuti fu, eye mebu ŋukpe ɖe naneke me o, eye wòbɔbɔ nɔ Mawu ƒe fiazikpui la ƒe ɖusime.
ENGLISH: 12 Consequently let us too, having around us such a cloud of witnesses, take off everything heavy, and trammeling sin, and run steadily the race that lies before us, 2 looking to him who led the way in faith and brought it to completeness, Jesus, who for the joy that lay before him endured a cross, despising shame, and has taken his seat at the right hand of God’s throne.

EWE: 3 Ɛ̃, mibu ame si do dzi kpe nu vɔ̃ wɔlawo ƒe tsitretsiɖeŋunya si gblẽ nu le woawo ŋutɔwo ŋu ƒe fu la ŋu, ale be ɖeɖi nagate mia ŋu miana ta o.
ENGLISH: 3 For think over the case of him who has endured such opposition from sinners against themselves, so that you may not lose your nerve and give out.

EWE: 4 Le avu si wɔm miele kple nu vɔ̃ me la, miekpɔ ɖo afi si wòhiã be woakɔ miaƒe ʋu ɖi le haɖe o. 5 Eye mieŋlɔ nuxlɔ̃ame si wona mi abe viwo ene la be keŋkeŋ, si nye: "Vinye, mègabu Yehowa ƒe amehehe nu tsɛ o, eye ne eɖɔ wò ɖo la, dzi megaɖe le ƒowò o; 6 elabena ame si Yehowa lɔ̃na la, eyae wòhea to na, le nyateƒe me la, ame sia ame si wòxɔ abe vi ene lae wòƒona. " 7 Ehiã be miado dzi elabena enye mia ɖɔɖɔɖo ƒe akpa aɖe. Ðe Mawu le nu wɔm ɖe mia ŋu abe viwo ene. Elabena vi kae li, si fofoa mehea to na o? 8 Ne ɖe womehe to sia na mi katã o la, anye ne miezu gbɔmeyaviwo, ke menye vi ŋutɔŋutɔwo o. 9 Azɔ hã, míaƒe ŋutilãmefofowo hea to na mí, eye míedea bubu wo ŋu.
ENGLISH: 4 You have not yet stood up to your fight with sin till the blood ran; 5 and you have forgotten the exhortation which reasons with you as sons, "My son, do not slight the Lord’s discipline nor be disheartened when you are corrected by him, 6 for it is the one the Lord loves that he disciplines, and he whips every son that he accepts. " 7 It is for discipline that you have trials to endure; God is treating you as sons; for what son is there that a father does not discipline? 8 but if you are without discipline, of which all have had their share, then you are bastards and not sons.

EWE: Ekema ɖe míalɔ̃ faa abɔbɔ mía ɖokui na Fofo si tsɔ gbɔgbɔ dzi mí la, be míanɔ agbe oa? 10 Elabena woawo hea to na mí ɣeyiɣi kpui aɖe le ale si wokpɔ be enyo la nu, ke eya wɔnɛ le míaƒe viɖe ta, be míakpɔ gome le eƒe kɔkɔenyenye la me.
ENGLISH: 9 And then, we had our bodily fathers as disciplinarians and stood in awe of them; shall we not much more be submissive to the Father of spirits, and live? 10 For they disciplined us for a few days as they saw fit, but he for our advantage so that we shall partake of his holiness.

EWE: 11 Nyateƒee, míebua tohehe aɖeke fifia dzidzɔe o, ke veve boŋ; gake emegbe la, etsea dzɔdzɔenyenye ƒe ŋutifafaku na ame siwo wotsɔe na hehee la.
ENGLISH: 11 Any discipline does not in its present aspect seem to be a thing for gladness but for pain; but afterward it yields a peaceful fruit to those who have had their training by it, the fruit of righteousness.

EWE: 12 Eya ta mido ŋusẽ asi siwo wɔ gblɔdɔɔ kple klo siwo gbɔdzɔ la, 13 eye miyi edzi mianɔ mɔ dzɔdzɔe ɖem na miaƒe afɔwo, ne nu si gli la nagaɖe ɖa le enu o, ke woada gbe le eŋu boŋ.
ENGLISH: 12 Wherefore, brace up the unstrung hands and the palsied knees, 13 and make straight tracks for your feet, in order that what is lame may not get a sprain but may rather heal up.

EWE: 14 Miyi edzi mianɔ ŋutifafa me kple amewo katã, eye miti kɔkɔenyenye yome, elabena eya manɔmee la, ame aɖeke makpɔ Aƒetɔ la o. 15 Mikpɔ nyuie be Mawu ƒe amenuveve la nagage le ame aɖeke si o, ale be kè aɖeke si nye aɖi nagamie aɖe fu na mi, eye wòaƒo ɖi ame geɖewo o; 16 eye ame aɖeke naganye ame si ƒo eɖokui ɖe gbɔdɔdɔ manɔsenu me alo ame si medea asixɔxɔ nu kɔkɔewo ŋu o, abe Esau, ame si tsɔ eƒe ŋgɔgbevinyenye na ɖe nuɖuɖu zi ɖeka ta la ene o.
ENGLISH: 14 Aim at peace with everyone, and sanctification (without which nobody will see the Lord), 15 having an eye to it that nobody coming short of God’s grace, no root of bitterness sending up its sprout, shall make trouble and thereby the rank and file be polluted, 16 no libertine or unsanctified man like Esau, who for one meal sold his rights as eldest son; 17 for you know how when he did afterward want to inherit the blessing he was ruled out; for he did not find a chance to change his mind though he tried for it in tears.

EWE: 17 Elabena mienyae be, emegbe esi wòdi be yeanyi yayra la dome la, wogbe; elabena togbɔ be etsɔ aɖatsiwo di vevie be woatrɔ susu ɖe ye ŋu hã la, medze edzi o. 18 Elabena nu si gbɔ miete va la menye nu si ŋu woate ŋu aka asii o, menye dzo si le bibim vlavlavla, kple alilikpo dodo, kple viviti tsiɖitsiɖi, kple ahom, 19 kple kpẽ ƒe ɖiɖi kpakple nyawo ƒe ɖiɖi, esi tututu ameawo se heɖe kuku be woagagblɔ nya aɖeke akpee na yewo o la o.
ENGLISH: 18 For you have not come to something tangible and burned with fire and to darkness and gloom and thick air, 19 and trumpet-tone, and such a sound of words that the hearers declined to have more said to them, 20 for they could not bear the charge that was given, "if even a beast touches the mountain it shall be stoned, " 21 and, so fearful was the display, Moses said "I quail and quiver "; 22 but you have come to Mount Sion and the city of the living God, heavenly Jerusalem, and tens of thousands of angels 23 in festival throng, and a church of firstborn sons registered in heaven, and God the Judge of all, and the spirits of perfected saints, 24 and Jesus the mediator of a new covenant, and a blood of sprinkling that speaks better than Abel’s.

EWE: 20 Elabena womete ŋu nɔ te ɖe sedede la nu o, se lae nye: "Ne lã aɖe gɔ̃ hã ka toa ŋu la, woaƒu kpee. " 21 Eye nukpɔkpɔ la ɖi vɔvɔ̃ ale gbegbe be Mose gblɔ be: "Mele vɔvɔ̃m hele ƒoƒom kpakpakpa. " 22 Ke nu si gbɔ miawo ya miete va lae nye Zion To kple Mawu gbagbe la ƒe du, dziƒo Yerusalem, kple mawudɔla akpeakpewo 23 ƒe takpekpe gã, kple ŋgɔgbevi siwo ƒe ŋkɔwo woŋlɔ ɖe dziƒowo la ƒe hame, kple Mawu, si nye amewo katã ƒe Ʋɔnudrɔ̃la, kple ame dzɔdzɔe siwo wowɔ bliboe la ƒe agbe si dzi gbɔgbɔa kpɔ ŋusẽ ɖo, 24 kple Yesu si nye nubabla yeye ƒe domenɔla, kpakple ʋu si wohlẽ, si ƒoa nu nyuie wu Abel ƒe ʋu.
ENGLISH: 25 See to it that you do not decline him who speaks; for if those did not escape when they had on earth declined him who was giving the revelation, much more we, who turn our backs on him who is doing it from heaven, 26 whose voice shook the earth then, but now he has promised "One time more I will shake not only the earth but the sky too. " 27 And "one time more " expresses the displacement of the shaken things as of things that have been made, in order that the unshaken may remain. 28 Wherefore, raised to the throne of an unshakable empire, let us have a thankful spirit, through which we shall worship God acceptably; with reverence and fear 29 for our God is a consuming fire.

EWE: Hebritɔwo
ENGLISH: Hebrews

EWE: 13 Mina miaƒe nɔvilɔlɔ̃ nayi edzi ɖaa.
ENGLISH: 13 Let brotherliness persist.

EWE: 2 Migaŋlɔ amedzrowɔwɔ be o, elabena to esia me ame aɖewo wɔ amedzro na mawudɔlawo, evɔ woawo ŋutɔwo menya o.
ENGLISH: 2 Do not forget hospitableness, for by it some men had angels as guests before they knew it.

EWE: 3 Minɔ ŋku ɖom ame siwo le gaxɔ me la dzi abe ɖe miawo hã miele gaxɔ me kpli wo ene, kple ame siwo wole fu wɔmee, esi miawo ŋutɔwo hã miele ŋutilã me ta.
ENGLISH: 3 Remember those in prison, as being fellow-prisoners; those in hardship, as being in a body yourselves.

EWE: 4 Mina bubu nanɔ srɔ̃ɖeɖe ŋu le amewo katã dome, eye woagaƒo ɖi srɔ̃ɖeba la o, elabena Mawu adrɔ̃ ʋɔnu ame siwo ƒoa wo ɖokui ɖe gbɔdɔdɔ manɔsenu me kple ahasiwɔlawo.
ENGLISH: 4 Marriage, highly honored in all respects, and the bed unpolluted; for God will judge libertines and adulterers.

EWE: 5 Mina miaƒe agbenɔnɔ navo tso galɔlɔ̃ me, eye nu siwo le mia si fifia la nadze mia ŋu. Elabena egblɔ be: "Nyemaɖe asi le ŋuwò akpɔ o, eye nyemagblẽ wò ɖi hã akpɔ o. " 6 Ale be dzi naɖo mía ƒo bliboe míagblɔ be: "Yehowa ye nye nye kpeɖeŋutɔ; nyemavɔ̃ o. Nu kae amegbetɔ ate ŋu awɔm? "
ENGLISH: 5 Character, unmercenary; getting along with what there is on hand, for he himself has said "I will not neglect you nor abandon you, " 6 so that we can say stoutly "I have the Lord as helper and will not be frightened; what is a man to do to me? "

EWE: 7 Miɖo ŋku ame siwo le ŋgɔ xɔm le mia dome la dzi, ame siwo gblɔ Mawu ƒe nya la na mi, eye esi miele nu siwo do tso woƒe agbenɔnɔ me ŋu bum la, misrɔ̃ woƒe xɔse.
ENGLISH: 7 Be mindful of your leaders who spoke God’s word to you; whose faith imitate, viewing the way they passed out of the life they had led.

EWE: 8 Ame si Yesu Kristo nye la kee wònye etsɔ kple egbe, yi ɖe mavɔmavɔ me.
ENGLISH: 8 Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today, and forever.

EWE: 9 Migana nufiafia manyatalenu vovovowo nakplɔ mi atrae o, elabena enyo be woatsɔ amenuveve ali ke dzi la, ke menye nuɖuɖu, siwo meɖea vi aɖeke na ame siwo tsɔe ɖo nɔƒe vevitɔ la o.
ENGLISH: 9 Do not be swept along with miscellaneous peculiar doctrines; for it is a good thing that the heart be held firm by grace not by foods, in which those who concern themselves with them did not get any benefit.

EWE: 10 Vɔsamlekpui aɖe le mía si, si ame siwo wɔa subɔsubɔdɔ kɔkɔe le agbadɔa me la mekpɔ mɔ aɖu edzi nu o.
ENGLISH: 10 We have an altar from which those who perform the service of the tabernacle have no right to eat.

EWE: 11 Elabena wotɔa dzo nuvɔ̃vɔsalã siwo ƒe ʋu nunɔlagã la tsɔna yia kɔkɔeƒea la ƒe lã bliboa le asaɖa la godo. 12 Esia tae Yesu hã kpe fu le dua ƒe agbo la godo ɖo, ale be wòatsɔ eya ŋutɔ ƒe ʋu akɔ dukɔ la ŋu.
ENGLISH: 11 For when the blood of animals is brought into the holy place by the high priest on account of sin, the bodies of these are burned up outside the camp; 12 for which reason so did Jesus, in order to sanctify the people by his own blood, suffer outside the gate; 13 well, then, let us come out to him outside the camp, bearing his ignominy.

EWE: 13 Eya ta mina míayi egbɔ le asaɖa la godo, ne woado ŋukpe mí abe ale si wodo ŋukpe eya hã ene, 14 elabena du aɖeke mele mía si le afi sia si anɔ anyi ɖaa o, ke boŋ míele esi gbɔna la dim vevie.
ENGLISH: 14 For we do not have a permanent city here, but are trying for the future one.

EWE: 15 Mina míato eya amea dzi atsɔ kafukafuvɔsa anɔ Mawu nam ɣesiaɣi, si nye míaƒe nuyi si míetsɔ ʋua eƒe ŋkɔ me le dutoƒo la ƒe kutsetse.
ENGLISH: 15 Through him let us offer a sacrifice of praise to God all the time; that is, the fruit of lips making acknowledgments to his name.

EWE: 16 Eye migaŋlɔ nyuiwɔwɔ kple nunana amewo hã be o, elabena nenem vɔsa siawo dzea Mawu ŋu ŋutɔ.
ENGLISH: 16 And do not forget beneficence and solidarity; for with such sacrifices God is pleased.

EWE: 17 Miɖo to ame siwo le ŋgɔ xɔm le mia dome la, eye mibɔbɔ mia ɖokui na wo, elabena wole mia ŋu dzɔm, abe ame siwo ana akɔnta ene, ne woawɔ esia kple dzidzɔ, eye menye kple hũɖeɖe o, elabena esia agblẽ nu le mia ŋu.
ENGLISH: 17 Obey your leaders and defer to them, for they are on the alert night and day in behalf of your souls, expecting to have to account for them; in order that they may do that with gladness, not with groans, for this would not pay you.

EWE: 18 Minɔ gbedodoɖa dzi ɖe mía ta, elabena míeka ɖe edzi be dzitsinya nyui le mía si, elabena míedina be míaɖi anukware le nuwo katã me.
ENGLISH: 18 Pray for us; for we are persuaded that we have a good conscience, intending to lead a good life in every respect.

EWE: 19 Ke mele dzi dem ƒo na mi vevie be mianɔ gbe dom ɖa, ale be woaɖe asi le ŋunye na mi kpuie.
ENGLISH: 19 And I more especially urge you to do this in order that I may be restored to you the more quickly.

EWE: 20 Ŋutifafa ƒe Mawu, ame si fɔ alẽawo ƒe kplɔla gã, si nye mía Aƒetɔ Yesu, tso ame kukuwo dome hekpe ɖe nubabla mavɔ ƒe ʋu la ŋu la, 21 natsɔ nu nyui sia nu nyui adzra mi ɖo, be miawɔ eƒe lɔlɔ̃nu, eye wòawɔ nu si dze eŋu la le mía me to Yesu Kristo dzi, ame si tɔ nanye ŋutikɔkɔe tso mavɔ me yi mavɔ me. Amen.
ENGLISH: 20 And may the God of peace, who by virtue of the blood of an eternal covenant brought up from the dead the great Shepherd of the sheep, our Lord Jesus, 21 make you fit in every good quality for doing his will, bringing about in you what shall be pleasing before him through Jesus Christ, to whom be glory forever and ever; amen.

EWE: 22 Ke mele nu xlɔ̃m mi, nɔviwo, be mialɔ̃ faa axɔ dzideƒonamenya sia, elabena le nyateƒe me la, agbalẽ kpui aɖe koe meŋlɔ na mi.
ENGLISH: 22 But I beg you, brothers, take the word of exhortation in good part for I have given you a short letter.

EWE: 23 Medi be mianyae be woɖe asi le mía nɔvi Timoteo ŋu. Ne eva ɖo kaba la, nye kplii míava kpɔ mi ɖa.
ENGLISH: 23 Know that our brother Timothy has been released; with whom, if he comes pretty soon, I will see you.

EWE: 24 Mido gbe na ame siwo katã le ŋgɔ xɔm le mia dome kple ame kɔkɔewo katã nam.
ENGLISH: 24 Give my greetings to all your leaders and all God’s people.

EWE: Ame siwo le Italia la do gbe na mi.
ENGLISH: The brothers from Italy send you greetings.

EWE: 25 Mawu ƒe amenuveve nanɔ kpli mi katã.
ENGLISH: 25 Grace be with you all.

EWE: Yakobo
ENGLISH: James

EWE: 1 Yakobo, Mawu kple Aƒetɔ Yesu Kristo ƒe kluvi, le esia ŋlɔm ɖo ɖe to wuieve siwo ka hlẽ la:
ENGLISH: 1 James, servant of God and the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes abroad, greeting.

EWE: Medo gbe na mi! 2 Nɔvinyewo, ne miedo go tetekpɔ vovovowo la, mibui dzidzɔ sɔŋ, 3 esi mienyae be miaƒe xɔse ƒe nyonyome sia si wodo kpɔ la hea dzidodo vanɛ ta.
ENGLISH: 2 Think it all gladness, my brothers, when you fall into varied temptations, 3 knowing that the test of your faith produces steadfastness.

EWE: 4 Ke mina dzidodo nawu eƒe dɔwɔwɔ nu bliboe, ale be mianɔ blibo, eye miade keŋkeŋ le goawo katã me, eye naneke nagahiã mi o.
ENGLISH: 4 And let steadfastness take complete effect, that you may be complete, sound all over, not lacking in any respect.

EWE: 5 Eya ta ne mia dometɔ aɖe hiã nunya la, nenɔ Mawu biam, elabena enaa nu amewo katã faa, medoa ŋukpe ame o, eye anɛ.
ENGLISH: 5 But if one of you is lacking in wisdom let him ask of the God who gives wholeheartedly to all and says no more about it.

EWE: 6 Gake nenɔ ebiam le xɔse me, eye megake ɖi kura o, elabena ame si kea ɖi la le abe ƒutsotsoe si ya ƒona yina gbɔna la ene.
ENGLISH: 6 But let him ask in faith, without any doubting; for one who doubts is like a swell at sea blown about and tossing.

EWE: 7 Le nyateƒe me la, ame ma megasusui kura be yeaxɔ nane tso Yehowa gbɔ o; 8 dzimevesusula wònye, melia ke le eƒe mɔwo katã dzi o.
ENGLISH: 7 For let not that man think that he will get anything from the Lord 8 a man of two minds, fickle in all his courses.

EWE: 9 Ke nɔvi si nye ame dahe la natso aseye le esi wodoe ɖe dzi ta, 10 eye kesinɔtɔ hã, le esi wobɔbɔe ɖe anyi ta, elabena enu ava yi abe gbe ƒe seƒoƒo ene.
ENGLISH: 9 But let the lowly brother glory in his loftiness, 10 and the rich in his lowliness, because he shall pass away like field flowers.

EWE: 11 Elabena ale si ɣe dzena kple eƒe dzoxɔxɔ gã henaa gbe yrɔna, eƒe seƒoƒo duduna, eye eƒe atsyɔ̃ nu yina la, nenemae kesinɔtɔ hã ayrɔ le eƒe agbemenuwo yome titi me.
ENGLISH: 11 For the sun rises with the hot wind, and dries up the plants, and their flowers fall off and the beauty of their faces is gone; so the rich man too shall wither in his wayfarings.

EWE: 12 Dzidzɔtɔe nye ame si doa dzi le tetekpɔ me, elabena ne wokpɔ ŋudzedze ɖe eŋu la, axɔ agbefiakuku si ŋugbe Yehowa do na ame siwo lɔ̃nɛ la.
ENGLISH: 12 Happy is the man who endures temptation, because when he has stood the test he shall receive the wreath of life which God has promised to those who love him.

EWE: 13 Ne ame aɖe le tetekpɔ me tom la, megagblɔ be: "Mawue le teyem kpɔ " o. Elabena womate ŋu atsɔ nu vɔ̃ɖiwo ate Mawu akpɔ o, eye eya ŋutɔ hã metea ame aɖeke kpɔna o.
ENGLISH: 13 Let no one, when he is tempted, say "I am being tempted by God "; for God feels no temptations to evil, and himself tempts nobody.

EWE: 14 Ke nu si tea ame sia ame kpɔnae nye eya ŋutɔ ƒe nudzodzro si henɛ eye wòblenɛ. 15 Azɔ ne nudzodzro la fɔ fu la, edzia nu vɔ̃; eye ne wowɔ nu vɔ̃ la, ehea ku vanɛ.
ENGLISH: 14 But each one is tempted by being enticed and allured by his own desire; 15 then desire becomes pregnant and gives birth to sin, and sin grows up and brings forth its offspring death.

EWE: 16 Nɔvinye lɔlɔ̃tɔwo, migana woaflu mi o.
ENGLISH: 16 Do not be misled, my dear brothers.

EWE: 17 Nunana nyuiwo katã kple nunana blibowo katã tso dziƒo, tso kekeliwo Fofo la gbɔ, eye eya metrɔna abe ale si vɔvɔli nɔa tɔtrɔm ene o.
ENGLISH: 17 Every good giving, every perfect gift, is from above, coming down from the Father of Lights, with whom there is no such thing as a variation or the shadowing of a turn.

EWE: 18 Enye eƒe lɔlɔ̃nu be yeatsɔ nyateƒenya la adzi mí, ale be míanye eƒe nuwɔwɔwo dome kutsetse gbãtɔwo.
ENGLISH: 18 Purposely did he, by the word of truth, bring us forth as his offspring, to the end that we should be a sort of firstfruits of his creatures.

EWE: 19 Nɔvinye lɔlɔ̃tɔwo, minya esia: Ame sia ame naɖe abla le nusese me, nanɔ blewu le nuƒoƒo me, nanɔ blewu le dziku me, 20 elabena ame ƒe dziku mewɔa nu si le dzɔdzɔe le Mawu ŋkume o.
ENGLISH: 19 You know it, my dear brothers. But let every man be quick to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger; 20 for man’s anger does not practice God’s righteousness.

EWE: 21 Eya ta miɖe ɖiƒoƒowo katã kple vɔ̃ɖinyenye ɖe sia ɖe ƒomevi ɖa, eye mixɔ nya si ƒãm wole ɖe mia me, si ate ŋu axɔ mi ɖe agbe la, kple dzi faa.
ENGLISH: 21 Wherefore, laying off all befoulment and profusion of malice, receive in meekness the implanted word that is able to save your souls.

EWE: 22 Mizu nyadziwɔlawo, ke menye nyaselawo ko o, ale be miagatsɔ nuŋububu masɔmasɔwo anɔ mia ɖokuiwo blem o. 23 Elabena ne ame aɖe nye nyasela, eye menye nyadziwɔla o la, ame ma le abe ame si le eya ŋutɔ ƒe mo kpɔm le ahuhɔ̃e me la ene.
ENGLISH: 22 But be doers of words, and not merely self-cheating hearers; 23 because whoever is a hearer of a word and not a doer, he is like a man looking in a glass at the face he was born with; 24 for he looks at himself and goes off and forgets at once what he was like.

EWE: 25 Ke ame si léa ŋku ɖe se deblibo si naa ablɔɖe la ŋu, eye wònɔa edzi ɖaa la, ame sia menye nyasela si ŋlɔa nu be o, ke nyadziwɔla boŋ; eye akpɔ dzidzɔ le nu si wòwɔna la me.
ENGLISH: 25 But he who gazes into the perfect law, the law of liberty, and stays by it, not showing himself a forgetful hearer but a doer in act, happy shall he be in his doing.

EWE: 26 Ne ame aɖe bua eɖokui mawusubɔlae, evɔ meléa eƒe aɖe o la, eya ŋutɔ ƒe dzi blem wòle, eye eƒe subɔsubɔ nye dzodzro.
ENGLISH: 26 If one thinks himself devout while not bridling his tongue but deceiving his own heart, that man’s devotions are futile.

EWE: 27 Subɔsubɔ si le dzadzɛ, si ŋu ɖiƒoƒo mele o, le mía Mawu si nye mía Fofo ŋkume lae nye esi: be woakpɔ tsyɔ̃eviwo kple ahosiwo dzi le woƒe xaxa me, eye woadzra ame ɖokui ɖo ɖimaƒomaƒoe tso xexea me.
ENGLISH: 27 Pure and undefiled devotions in the eyes of God the Father are these: to look after orphans and widows in their distress; to keep one’s self unspotted from the world.

EWE: Yakobo
ENGLISH: James

EWE: 2 Nɔvinyewo, ɖe mielé míaƒe ŋutikɔkɔe ƒe Aƒetɔ Yesu Kristo dzi xɔxɔ se me ɖe asi hafi gaɖe mɔ ɖe ameŋkumekpɔkpɔ ŋua? 2 Elabena ne ame aɖe do sikasigɛwo eye wòle awu xɔasiwo me va miaƒe ƒuƒoƒe, eye ame dahe aɖe hã le awu ƒoɖi me va la, 3 ɖe ame si do awu xɔasi la ƒe nu nyoa mia ŋu, ale be miegblɔna be, "Va nɔ anyi ɖe teƒe nyui sia, " eye miegblɔna na ame dahea ya be, "Wò la, nɔ tsitrenu, " alo, "Nɔ anyi ɖe afi ma le nye afɔɖodzinu te " mahã? 4 Ne nenemae la, ɖe miele vovototo dem mia nɔewo dome, eye miezu ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo hele afia gbegblẽwo tsom oa? 5 Nɔvinye lɔlɔ̃tɔwo, mise nya sia.
ENGLISH: 2 My brothers, let it not be with partiality that you hold the faith of our Lord of glory Jesus Christ. 2 For if there comes into a synagogue of yours a man with a gold ring, in splendid dress, and there comes in also a poor man in soiled dress, 3 and you take notice of the one who wears the splendid dress and say "You sit here in a good place, " and say to the poor man "You stand there, or sit under my footstool, " 4 are you not in conflict with yourselves, and have you not shown yourselves judges swayed by base influences? 5 Listen, my dear brothers: did not God choose those who are poor as to the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the royalty which he promised to those who love him? 6 but you have dishonored the poor man.

EWE: Ðe Mawu metia ame siwo nye ame dahewo le xexea ƒe nukpɔkpɔ nu, be woanye kesinɔtɔwo le xɔse me kple domenyilawo le Fiaɖuƒe si ŋugbe wòdo na ame siwo lɔ̃nɛ la me oa? 6 Ke miawo miedo vlo ame dahe la.
ENGLISH: Do not the rich tyrannize over you and do not they drag you before tribunals? 7 do not they blaspheme the goodly name by which you are called?

EWE: Menye kesinɔtɔwoe tea mi ɖe anyi, eye wohea mi yia ʋɔnui oa? 7 Ðe menye woawoe gblɔa busunya ɖe ŋkɔ nyui si woyɔ na mi la ŋuti oa? 8 Ke azɔ, ne miewɔa fiasedede la dzi abe ale si ŋɔŋlɔ la gblɔe ene be, "Lɔ̃ hawòvi abe wò ŋutɔ ɖokuiwò ene " la, ekema miewɔe nyuie.
ENGLISH: 8 If, however, you fulfill the royal law according to the text "You shall love your neighbor as yourself, " you do well; 9 but if you show partiality you are practicing sin, being convicted by the law as violators.

EWE: 10 Elabena ame si wɔa Se la katã dzi, gake wòdana le eƒe nudidi ɖeka dzi la, eda wo katã dzi.
ENGLISH: 10 For whoever keeps the whole law but makes a slip in one point has become guilty of all.

EWE: 11 Elabena ame si gblɔ be: "Mègawɔ ahasi o " la kee gblɔ be: "Mègawu ame o. " Ke ne mèwɔa ahasi o, gake nèwua ame la, ekema èzu sedzidala.
ENGLISH: 11 For he who said "Do not commit adultery " said also "Do not murder "; and if you do not commit adultery but do commit murder you have become a violator of the law.

EWE: 12 Miyi edzi mianɔ nu ƒom eye mianɔ nu wɔm abe ame siwo woatsɔ ablɔɖedukɔ ƒe se adrɔ̃ ʋɔnui ene.
ENGLISH: 12 So speak, and so do, as men who are to be judged by a law of liberty.

EWE: 13 Elabena ame si mekpɔa nublanui na ame o la, womakpɔ nublanui nɛ le ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃ me o.
ENGLISH: 13 For justice is pitiless to him who has not showed pity; pity flouts justice.

EWE: Ðe xɔse ma ate ŋu axɔe ɖe agbea? 15 Ne nɔviŋutsu alo nɔvinyɔnu aɖewo li, awu mele wo si o eye nuɖuɖu si asu na wo le ŋkekea me hã mele wo si o, 16 evɔ mia dometɔ aɖe gblɔ na wo be, "Miheyi le ŋutifafa me; dzo naɖo lãme na mi, eye miɖu nu miaɖi ƒo, " ke miena nu siwo hiã woƒe ŋutilã la wo o ɖe, viɖe kae wònye? 17 Nenema kee xɔse hã, ne dɔwɔwɔ mekpe ɖe eŋu o la, enye nu kuku.
ENGLISH: 14 What is the use, my brothers, if one says he has faith, but does not have deeds? can faith save him? 15 If a brother or sister be naked and in lack of daily food, 16 and one of you say to them "Good luck to you, keep warm and eat heartily, " but you do not give them what is requisite for the body, what is the use? 17 just so faith, if it does not have deeds, is dead in itself.

EWE: 18 Ke ame aɖe agblɔ be: "Xɔse le asiwò, eye dɔwɔwɔwo le nye hã asinye.
ENGLISH: 18 But a man will say "You have faith and I have deeds; show me your faith without deeds, and I will show you my faith by my deeds.

EWE: Fia wò xɔse si ŋu dɔwɔwɔ mekpe ɖo o lam, eye nye hã mafia nye xɔse la wò to nye dɔwɔwɔwo me. " 19 Èxɔe se be Mawu ɖeka koe li ɖe? Èwɔe nyuie.
ENGLISH: 19 You believe that there is one God? you do well: the demons too believe, and shiver.

EWE: Gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃wo hã xɔe se, eye wodzona nyanyanya. 20 Ke wò, ame gbɔlo, ɖe nèdi be yeanya be xɔse dɔwɔwɔ manɔŋui meɖea vi aɖeke oa? 21 Ðe womebu mía fofo Abraham ame dzɔdzɔe to dɔwɔwɔ me, esi wòtsɔ via Isak na le vɔsamlekpui la dzi oa? 22 Èkpɔe be eƒe xɔse zɔ aduadu kple eƒe dɔwɔwɔwo, eye eƒe dɔwɔwɔwo na eƒe xɔse la de blibo; 23 ale ŋɔŋlɔ la va eme, si gblɔ be: "Abraham xɔ Yehowa dzi se, eye wobui dzɔdzɔenyenye nɛ, " eye woyɔe be Yehowa xɔlɔ̃. 24 Miekpɔe be wobua ame be ele dzɔdzɔe to dɔwɔwɔwo me, ke menye to xɔse ɖeɖe ko me o.
ENGLISH: 20 But do you want to know, hollow man, that faith without deeds is idle? 21 Was not Father Abraham justified by deeds, in that he sacrificed his son Isaac on the altar? 22 do you perceive that faith cooperated with his deeds, and faith was perfected by deeds? 23 and the text which says ‘And Abraham believed God, and it was counted as righteousness for him, and he was called God’s friend’ was fulfilled. " 24 You see that a man is justified by deeds and not by faith alone.

EWE: 25 Ðe menye nenema kee wobu Rahab, gbolo la, hã ame dzɔdzɔe to dɔwɔwɔwo me, esi wòxɔ ame dɔdɔawo nyuie hena woto mɔ bubu dzo oa? 26 Ɛ̃, ale si ŋutilã gbɔgbɔ manɔmee nye nu kuku la, nenema kee xɔse dɔwɔwɔ manɔŋui hã nye nu kuku.
ENGLISH: 25 And in the same way was not Rahab the prostitute justified by deeds, when she took in the messengers and sent them out another way? 26 For as the body without a spirit is dead, so also faith without deeds is dead.

EWE: Yakobo
ENGLISH: James

EWE: 3 Nɔvinyewo, mele be mia dometɔ geɖewo nazu nufialawo o, esi mienyae be míakpɔ ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃ si sesẽ wu ta.
ENGLISH: 3 Do not many of you be teachers, my brothers, knowing that we shall come under greater responsibility.

EWE: 2 Elabena mí katã míedaa vo zi geɖe.
ENGLISH: 2 For we one and all make many slips.

EWE: Ne ame aɖe meda vo le nuƒoƒo me o la, enye ame deblibo si ate ŋu ade ga eƒe ŋutilã bliboa hã.
ENGLISH: If anyone does not slip in speech, that man is a complete man, able to bridle the whole body too.

EWE: 3 Ne míedea ga nu na sɔwo be woaɖo to mí la, ekema míekpɔa ŋusẽ ɖe woƒe ŋutilã bliboa hã dzi.
ENGLISH: 3 And if we put bits in horses’ mouths to have them obey us, we bring around their whole body too.

EWE: 4 Kpɔ tɔdziʋuwo hã ɖa: Togbɔ be wololo ŋutɔ, eye ya sesẽ hea wo hã la, kuɖɔ sue aɖe koe kuɖɔɖola la tsɔna kua wo yia afi sia afi si wòdi.
ENGLISH: 4 Ships also, great as they are and driven by hard winds, are brought around by a little helm whichever way the steersman’s push will have it.

EWE: 5 Nenema kee aɖe la hã nye ŋutinu sue aɖe ko, gake wòhekana ɖe nu gãwo ŋu.
ENGLISH: 5 So is the tongue a small organ and boasts a great record. What a great forest the least bit of fire will kindle! and the tongue is a fire.

EWE: Mikpɔ ale si dzo sue aɖe ko tea ŋu tɔa dzo ave gã aɖee ɖa! 6 Aɖe la hã, dzoe wònye.
ENGLISH: 6 The tongue is set among our organs as the world of wrong, what spots the whole body and sets aflame the wheel of birth and is set aflame by hell.

EWE: 7 Elabena womlaa gbemelãwo, xewo, lã siwo tana, kple ƒumelã ƒomeviwo katã, eye amegbetɔwo tea ŋu mlaa wo. 8 Ke aɖe la ya, amegbetɔ aɖeke mate ŋu amlae o. Enye nane si dzi womate ŋu aɖu bɔbɔe o, ewɔa nu vevi ame eye wòyɔ fũu kple aɖi wuame.
ENGLISH: 7 For every species of beasts and of birds, and of reptiles and the creatures of the sea, is and has been subdued by the human species; 8 but the tongue no human being can subdue, unquiet evil that it is, full of death-dealing venom.

EWE: 9 Eyae míetsɔna kafua Yehowa, mía Fofo la, gake eya kee míetsɔna ƒoa fi dea ame siwo wowɔ "ɖe Mawu ƒe nɔnɔme nu " la hã. 10 Nu ɖeka ma ke mee yayra kple fiƒode dona tso.
ENGLISH: 9 With it we bless our Lord and Father, and with it we curse men, who are made in the likeness of God: 10 out of the same mouth come blessing and curse; my brothers, these things ought not to be so done.

EWE: Nɔvinyewo, mesɔ be nuwo nanɔ edzi yim alea o. 11 Ðe vudo dzia tsi nyui kple tsi veve tso do ɖeka ma ke mea? 12 Nɔvinyewo, ɖe gboti ate ŋu atse amititsetsewo, alo wainka natse gbotsetsewoa?
ENGLISH: 11 Does a spring flow sweet and bitter out of the same orifice? 12 can a fig-tree, my brothers, produce olives, or a grapevine figs? neither can salt water produce sweet.

EWE: Nenema kee vudo si dzia dzetsi la magate ŋu adzi tsi vivi hã o. 13 Ame kae nye nunyala kple nugɔmesela le mia dome?
ENGLISH: 13 Who is there among you that is wise and intelligent? let him show his deeds out of a good life, in meekness of wisdom.

EWE: 14 Ke ne ŋuʋaʋã vɔ̃ɖi kple dzrehehe le miaƒe dziwo me la, miganɔ adegbe ƒom ahanɔ aʋatso kam ɖe nyateƒe la si o.
ENGLISH: 14 But if you have bitter jealousy and contest in your hearts, do not flout the truth and tell lies against it.

EWE: 15 Menye nunya si tso dziƒo lae nye esia o; anyigbadzitɔe, lã tɔe, gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃wo tɔe. 16 Elabena afi sia afi si ŋuʋaʋã kple dzrehehe le la, tɔtɔ kple nu gbegblẽ ɖe sia ɖe hã nɔnɛ.
ENGLISH: 15 This wisdom is not heaven-descended but terrestrial, animal, fiendlike; 16 for where jealousy and contests are, there is disorder and every faulty action.

EWE: 17 Ke nunya si tso dziƒo la, gbã la, ele dzadzɛ, azɔ hã, ewɔa ŋutifafa, esea nu gɔme, elɔ̃na faa ɖoa to, nublanuikpɔkpɔ kple kutsetse nyuiwo yɔe fũu, medea vovototo amewo me o, alakpanuwɔwɔ mele eme o.
ENGLISH: 17 But the heaven-descended wisdom is first pure, then peaceable, reasonable, tractable, full of pity and good fruits, with no misgivings and no insincerities; 18 and fruit of righteousness is sowed in peace for those who make peace.

EWE: Yakobo
ENGLISH: James

EWE: 4 Afi kae aʋawɔwɔ kple dzrewɔwɔ siwo le mia dome la tso? Ðe menye miaƒe ŋutilãmenudzodzro siwo wɔa avu le miaƒe ŋutinuwo me la mee wotso oa? 2 Nu dzroa mi, ke miekpɔnɛ o. Miewua ame eye miebiãa ŋu, ke miaƒe asi mesua edzi o. Miewɔa dzre, eye miewɔa aʋa. Ke miekpɔa nu si dim miele o, elabena miebiaa Mawu o.
ENGLISH: 4 What is the origin of wars and fightings among you? is it not this, your pleasures campaigning in your organism? 2 You desire and do not have, you murder and are jealous and cannot obtain you fight and make war.

EWE: 3 Ne miebia la, miexɔnɛ o, elabena susu vɔ̃e mietsɔ le ebiam, ale be miatsɔe aɖi kɔ na miaƒe ŋutilãmenudzodzrowo.
ENGLISH: You do not have because you do not ask; 3 you ask and do not get because you ask wrongly, to spend it in your pleasures.

EWE: 4 Ahasiwɔlawo, ɖe mienyae be xɔlɔ̃dzedze xexea nye futɔnyenye na Mawu oa? Eya ta ame sia ame si dina be yeanye xexea xɔlɔ̃ la, ewɔa eɖokui Mawu ƒe futɔ.
ENGLISH: 4 Adulteresses, do you not know that friendship to the world is enmity to God? so anyone who wishes to be a friend of the world becomes, as such, an enemy of God.

EWE: 5 Alo ɖe miebu be dzodzroe ŋɔŋlɔ la gblɔ be: "Gbɔgbɔ si xɔ aƒe ɖe mía me la dzroa nu le ŋubiabiã me " mahã? 6 Ke amenuveve si Wònana la lolo wu. Eya ta ŋɔŋlɔ la gblɔ be: "Mawu tsia tsitre ɖe dadalawo ŋu, ke evea ɖokuibɔbɔlawo nu. " 7 Eya ŋuti mibɔbɔ mia ɖokui ɖe Mawu te; ke mitsi tsitre ɖe Abosam ŋu, eye asi le mia gbɔ.
ENGLISH: 5 Or do you think it is meaninglessly that the text says "The spirit that he has housed in us longs enviously "? 6 But he gives a greater grace; for which reason it says "God sets himself against the proud but gives grace to the lowly. " 7 So be submissive to God; but stand up against the devil and he will run from you.

EWE: 8 Mite ɖe Mawu ŋu, eye ate ɖe mia ŋu.
ENGLISH: 8 Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you.

EWE: Miklɔ miaƒe asiwo, mi nu vɔ̃ wɔlawo, eye mikɔ miaƒe dziwo ŋu, mi dzimevesusulawo. 9 Mixa nu, mifa konyi, eye mifa avi. Mina miaƒe nukoko natrɔ azu nuxaxa, eye miaƒe aseyetsotso natrɔ azu mɔkpɔkpɔbuɖeame.
ENGLISH: Clean your hands, sinners, and purify your hearts, men of two minds; 9 be miserable, and mourn, and weep; let your laughter be turned to mourning and your gladness to abasement.

EWE: 10 Mibɔbɔ mia ɖokui ɖe anyi le Yehowa ŋkume, ekema ado mi ɖe dzi.
ENGLISH: 10 Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will uplift you.

EWE: 11 Nɔviwo, midzudzɔ nya si medze o la gbɔgblɔ ɖe mia nɔewo ŋu.
ENGLISH: 11 Do not talk disparagingly of each other, brothers.

EWE: Ame si ƒoa nu le nɔvi aɖe ŋu, alo drɔ̃a ʋɔnu nɔvia la, eƒoa nu tsia tre ɖe se la ŋu, eye wòdrɔ̃a ʋɔnu se la.
ENGLISH: He who disparages or judges his brother is disparaging and judging the law; and if you judge the law you are not a doer of the law but a judge.

EWE: 12 Senala kple Ʋɔnudrɔ̃la ɖeka koe li, ame si tea ŋu xɔa ame ɖe agbe, eye wòtea ŋu tsrɔ̃a ame.
ENGLISH: 12 There is one lawgiver and judge, he who can save and can destroy; but who are you, you who judge your neighbor?

EWE: Ke wò la, ame kae nènye be nèle ʋɔnu drɔ̃m hawòvi? 13 Azɔ misee, mi ame siwo gblɔna be: "Egbe alo etsɔ la, míayi du si me, eye míanɔ afi ma ƒe ɖeka, eye míatsa asi akpɔ viɖe, " 14 evɔ mienya ale si miaƒe agbe anɔ etsɔ o. Elabena afu si dona ɣeyiɣi vi aɖe eye emegbe wòbuna ko mienye. 15 Ele be miagblɔ boŋ be: "Ne Yehowa lɔ̃ la, míanɔ agbe awɔ esi alo ekemɛ. " 16 Ke azɔ miele dadam hele adegbe ƒuƒlu ƒom. Adegbeƒoƒo sia katã nye vɔ̃.
ENGLISH: 13 Come now, you who say "Today or tomorrow we will go to such a city and spend a year there and trade and make profits " 14 when you do not know what the future holds; for what is your life? for you are vapor, that appears for a little while and then just disappears 15 instead of saying "If the Lord will we shall both live and do this or that. " 16 But now you are glorying in your great claims; any such glorying is wicked.

EWE: 17 Eya ta ame si nya nu nyui gake mewɔe o la, enye nu vɔ̃ nɛ.
ENGLISH: 17 So, when one knows enough to do right and does not, it is a sin of his.

EWE: Yakobo
ENGLISH: James

EWE: 5 Azɔ misee, mi kesinɔtɔwo, mifa avi eye miƒu asi nu le xaxa siwo gbɔna mia dzi la ta.
ENGLISH: 5 Come on now, rich men, weep and howl over your miseries to come.

EWE: 2 Miaƒe kesinɔnuwo nyunyɔ, eye agbagblaʋuiwo ɖu miaƒe awuwo. 3 Miaƒe sika kple klosalo lé ɣebia, eye woƒe ɣebialéle aɖi ɖase le mia ŋu ahaɖu miaƒe ŋutilã.
ENGLISH: 2 Your wealth has rotted and your garments have become moth-eaten, 3 your gold and silver have rusted and their rust will be a testimony to you and will eat your flesh like fire.

EWE: Nu si miedzra ɖo ɖi le ŋkeke mamlɛawo me anɔ abe dzo ene. 4 Kpɔ ɖa!
ENGLISH: 4 You have been hoarding in the last days; here the delayed pay of the laborers who reaped your acres is crying out, and the clamor of the harvesters has entered the ears of the Lord of Sabaoth.

EWE: Dɔwɔla siwo ŋe miaƒe agblemenuwo na mi la ƒe fetu siwo dzi miezi la le ɣlidodo dzi, eye nuŋelawo ƒe ɣlidodo be woaxɔ na yewo la va ɖo aʋakɔwo ƒe Yehowa ƒe towo me. 5 Mieɖu agbe eye miedo dzidzɔ na mia ɖokuiwo le anyigba dzi. Miena miaƒe dziwo da ami le wuwugbe la kura gɔ̃ hã. 6 Miebu fɔ ame, eye miewu ame dzɔdzɔe la. Ðe metsi tsitre ɖe mia ŋu oa?
ENGLISH: 5 You have been living in luxury and self-indulgence on the earth, you have been feeding your hearts in a day of slaughter; 6 you have been condemning the man who was in the right, murdering him he does not make any stand against you.

EWE: 7 Eya ta nɔviwo, migbɔ dzi ɖi va se ɖe Aƒetɔ la ƒe anyinɔɣi la.
ENGLISH: 7 So, brothers, have patience till the Lord’s coming.

EWE: Kpɔ ɖa! Agbledela nɔa anyigba ƒe nuku xɔasi la lalam eye wògbɔa dzi ɖi va se ɖe esime adatsi kple keletsi dza. 8 Miawo hã migbɔ dzi ɖi; mido ŋusẽ miaƒe dziwo, elabena Aƒetɔ la ƒe anyinɔɣi gogo.
ENGLISH: How the farmer waits for the precious crops of the soil, having patience over them till they get the early rains and the late rains! 8 Have patience yourselves, fortify your hearts, because the Lord’s coming is almost here.

EWE: 9 Nɔviwo, miganɔ tse ɖum ɖe mia nɔewo ŋu o, ale be woagadrɔ̃ ʋɔnu mi o. Kpɔ ɖa! Ʋɔnudrɔ̃la la le tsitre ɖe ʋɔtrua nu.
ENGLISH: 9 Do not sigh against each other, brothers, that you may not be judged: here is the judge standing at the doors.

EWE: 10 Nɔviwo, mina nyagblɔɖila siwo ƒo nu le Yehowa ƒe ŋkɔ me la ƒe fukpekpewo, kple woƒe dzigbɔgbɔ blewu la, nanye kpɔɖeŋu na mi.
ENGLISH: 10 Take as an example of fortitude and patience, brothers, the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.

EWE: 11 Kpɔ ɖa! Míeyɔa ame siwo doa dzi la be dzidzɔtɔwo. Miese Hiob ƒe dzidodo ŋu nya, eye miekpɔ ale si Yehowa na nuwo va wu enu nɛ, be Yehowa ƒe dɔme trɔna ɖe ame ŋu geɖe, eye wòkpɔa nublanui na ame.
ENGLISH: 11 How we admire the condition of those who endured! you have heard of Job’s endurance, and seen the Lord’s ending, that the Lord is tenderhearted and compassionate.

EWE: 12 Gawu la, nɔvinyewo, midzudzɔ nutàta, eɖanye dziƒo alo anyigba alo nu bubu aɖe o, migatà wo dometɔ aɖeke o. Ke boŋ mina miaƒe "Ɛ̃ " nanye ɛ̃, eye miaƒe "Ao " nanye ao, ale be miagadze ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃ me o.
ENGLISH: 12 And above all, my brothers, do not swear, neither by heaven nor by the earth nor any other oath; but let your yes be yes and your no no, that you may not come under judgment.

EWE: 13 Ðe mia dometɔ aɖe le xaxa me toma? Neyi edzi wòanɔ gbe dom ɖa.
ENGLISH: 13 Is anyone among you having hardships? let him pray.

EWE: Ðe dzi le ame aɖe dzɔma? Nedzi kafukafuha.
ENGLISH: Is anyone feeling cheery? let him sing hymns.

EWE: 14 Ðe mia dometɔ aɖe le dɔ léma? Neyɔ hamemetsitsiwo woava egbɔ, eye woado gbe ɖa ɖe eta ahasi ami nɛ le Yehowa ƒe ŋkɔ me. 15 Eye xɔse ƒe gbedodoɖa ana dɔnɔ la ƒe lãme nasẽ, eye Yehowa afɔe ɖe te. Eye ne ewɔ nu vɔ̃ la, woatsɔe akee.
ENGLISH: 14 Is anyone among you sick? let him call in the elders of the church, and let them pray over him, putting oil on him in the name of the Lord, 15 and the prayer of faith shall make the sufferer well, and the Lord shall raise him; and if he has committed sins he shall be forgiven.

EWE: 16 Eya ta miʋu miaƒe nu vɔ̃wo me na mia nɔewo, eye mido gbe ɖa ɖe mia nɔewo ta, be miahaya.
ENGLISH: 16 So confess your sins to each other and pray for each other that you may be healed.

EWE: Ŋusẽ le ame dzɔdzɔe ƒe kokoƒoƒo ŋu, eye wòwɔa dɔ.
ENGLISH: Great is the efficacy of a righteous man’s strenuous prayer.

EWE: 17 Eliya nye amegbetɔ si ƒe seselelãmewo sɔ kple mía tɔwo, gake edo gbe ɖa vevie be tsi nagadza o, eye tsi medza ɖe anyigba la dzi o ƒe etɔ̃ kple ɣleti ade. 18 Eye wògado gbe ɖa, eye tsi dza tso dziƒo, eye anyigba gawɔ nu.
ENGLISH: 17 Elijah was a man subject to the same limitations as we are, and he specially prayed that it might not rain, and it did not rain on the earth three years and six months; 18 and he prayed again and the sky gave showers and the earth started to grow crops.

EWE: 19 Nɔvinyewo, ne mia dometɔ aɖe tra mɔ tso nyateƒe la gbɔ, eye ame bubu gatrɔe gbɔe la, 20 minyae be ame si trɔ nu vɔ̃ wɔla la tso eƒe mɔtatra dzi la, axɔe tso ku me, eye wòatsyɔ nu nu vɔ̃ geɖe dzi.
ENGLISH: 19 My brothers, if one among you strays from the truth and someone brings him back, 20 let him know that he who brings a sinner back from his straying course will save him from death and cover a multitude of sins.

EWE: 1 Petro
ENGLISH: 1 Peter

EWE: 1 Petro, Yesu Kristo ƒe apostolo, le esia ŋlɔm ɖo ɖe amedzro siwo kaka ɖe Ponto, Galatia, Kapadokia, Asia kple Bitinia nutowo me. Ame siwo nye ame tiatiawo 2 le Mawu, Fofo la, ƒe nunyanya do ŋgɔ la nu, eya, ame si tsɔ gbɔgbɔ la kɔ wo ŋu be woanye toɖolawo, ame siwo ŋu wohlẽ Yesu Kristo ƒe ʋu ɖo la: Amenuveve kple ŋutifafa nasɔ gbɔ ɖe edzi na mi.
ENGLISH: 1 Peter, apostle of Jesus Christ, to the chosen who are living abroad among the Jewish colonies of Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia, 2 according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, in sanctification of the Spirit, to obedience and sprinkling of Jesus Christ’s blood: Grace and peace be yours in abundance.

EWE: 3 Woakafu mía Aƒetɔ Yesu Kristo ƒe Mawu, si nye Fofoa, elabena le eƒe nublanuikpɔkpɔ geɖe me la, edzi mi yeyee to Yesu Kristo ƒe tsitretsitsi tso ame kukuwo dome dzi hena mɔkpɔkpɔ gbagbe, 4 be míaxɔ domenyinu magblemagblẽ, maƒoɖi, si nu meyina o. Wodzrae ɖo ɖe dziƒo na mi, 5 ame siwo ŋu dzɔm Mawu le kple eƒe ŋusẽ la le miaƒe xɔse ta, ale be miakpɔ xɔxɔ si woava ɖe ɖe go kpuie le ɣeyiɣi mamlɛa me. 6 Miele aseye tsom le esia ta, togbɔ be tetekpɔ vovovowo doa nuxaxa na mi fifia hena ɣeyiɣi vi aɖe hã, 7 ale be miaƒe xɔse si wodo kpɔ, si xɔ asi sãsãsã wu sika si gblẽna togbɔ be wodonɛ kpɔ kple dzo hã la, nahe kafukafu kple ŋutikɔkɔe kpakple bubu avɛ le Yesu Kristo ƒe ɖeɖefia la me. 8 Togbɔ be miekpɔe kpɔ o hã la, mielɔ̃e. Togbɔ be miele ekpɔm fifia o hã la, miexɔa edzi sena, eye miekpɔa dzidzɔ gã manyagblɔ hetsoa aseye, 9 esi mieɖo miaƒe xɔse ƒe taɖodzinu si nye miaƒe ɖeɖekpɔkpɔ la gbɔ ta.
ENGLISH: 3 Blessed be our Lord Jesus Christ’s God and Father, he who in accordance with his great mercy has given us rebirth into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, 4 into an imperishable, undefiled, unfading inheritance that has been kept in heaven for you 5 who by the power of God are guarded through faith for a salvation ready to be disclosed at the last 6 wherein you exult, though for a little while now, if need be, you have been saddened in various trials, 7 that the quality of your faith may be found more valuable than gold (which is a perishable thing, but is tested by fire) for praise and glory and honor at the manifestation of Jesus Christ, 8 whom you love without having seen him; believing in whom, without now seeing him, you exult in ineffable and glorified gladness, 9 obtaining the end of faith, soul-salvation.

EWE: 10 Xɔxɔ sia tututu ŋue nyagblɔɖila siwo gblɔ nya ɖi le amenuveve si miava kpɔ ŋuti la, dzro nu me vevie hewɔ numekuku tsitotsito le. 11 Wodzro nu me vevie tso ɣeyiɣi si tututu alo azãgbe si gbɔgbɔ si le wo me la le asi fiamee tso Kristo ŋuti, esime wòle ɖase ɖim do ŋgɔ le fu siwo Kristo akpe kple ŋutikɔkɔe si adze eyome la ŋuti. 12 Woɖee fia wo be menye woawo ŋutɔ ɖokuiwoe wonɔ subɔsubɔdɔ wɔm na o, ke boŋ miawoe wonɔ ewɔm na; nu siawoe ame siwo ɖe gbeƒã nya nyui la na mi to gbɔgbɔ kɔkɔe, si woɖo ɖa tso dziƒo, dzi la gblɔ na mi azɔ. Nu siawo tututu me kpɔkpɔ tsitotsito dzroa mawudɔlawo.
ENGLISH: 10 Concerning which salvation prophets sought and searched, who prophesied of the grace that has reached you, 11 searching to find out what time or what sort of time Christ’s spirit in them was pointing to in testifying beforehand the sufferings to which Christ was destined and the glory after these; 12 to whom it was disclosed that they were dispensing them not to themselves but to you, the things that have now been announced to you through those who brought the gospel to you in the Holy Spirit sent from heaven, things that angels desire to look into.

EWE: 13 Eya ta midzra miaƒe susuwo ɖo hena dɔwɔwɔ; minɔ mo xexi bliboe; mitsɔ miaƒe mɔkpɔkpɔ ɖo amenuveve si miakpɔ le Yesu Kristo ƒe ɖeɖefia me la dzi.
ENGLISH: 13 Wherefore, girding up the loins of your mind, keep absolutely sober and hope in the grace that is being brought you in the manifestation of Jesus Christ.

EWE: 14 Abe vi ɖotowo ene la, migana nudzodzro siwo ɖu mia dzi tsã le numanyamanya me la nayi edzi anɔ miaƒe nɔnɔme trɔm o, 15 ke boŋ miawo hã minɔ kɔkɔe le miaƒe agbenɔnɔ katã me abe Kɔkɔetɔ si yɔ mi la ke ene, 16 elabena woŋlɔ ɖi be: "Minɔ kɔkɔe, elabena nye la, mele kɔkɔe. " 17 Eye ne mieyɔa Fofo la, ame si drɔ̃a ʋɔnu ame sia ame ameŋkumemakpɔmakpɔtɔe ɖe eƒe dɔwɔwɔ nu la, ekema minɔ agbe le vɔvɔ̃ me le ɣeyiɣi si mienye amedzrowo la me. 18 Elabena mienyae be menye nu siwo gblẽna, klosalo alo sika, ye wotsɔ ɖe mi tso agbenɔnɔ maɖevi si mia tɔgbuiwo gblẽ ɖi na mi la me o. 19 Ke boŋ ʋu xɔasi ye wotsɔ ɖe mi, abe alẽvi si nu mewɔ afi aɖeke na o, si ŋu kpɔtsɔtsɔ mele o la tɔ ene, si nye Kristo ƒe ʋu. 20 Nyateƒee, wonyae ɖi do ŋgɔ na xexea ƒe gɔmeɖoanyiɣi, ke ɣeyiɣiawo ƒe nuwuwue woɖee fia le mia ta. 21 Eya dzie mieto xɔ Mawu, ame si fɔe ɖe tsitre tso ame kukuwo dome hetsɔ ŋutikɔkɔe nɛ la, dzi se, ale be miaƒe xɔse kple mɔkpɔkpɔ nanɔ Mawu dzi.
ENGLISH: 14 Like children of obedience, not conforming to your old-time desires that you had during your ignorance, 15 but like the Holy One who called you, be holy yourselves in all your life, 16 since it is written "You shall be holy, because I am holy. " 17 And if you invoke a Father who judges impartially according to each one’s doing, live a life of fear for the time of your stay, 18 knowing that it was not with perishable things, silver or gold, that you were redeemed from the futile life your fathers handed down to you, 19 but with precious blood as if of a lamb without defect or spot, Christ’s blood, 20 who had been foreknown before the foundation of the world but had made his appearance at the latter end of time for the sake of you 21 who through him are believers in God who raised him from the dead and gave him glory, so that your faith and hope are in God.

EWE: 22 Azɔ esi miekɔ mia ɖokuiwo ŋu to toɖoɖo nyateƒea me, ale be nɔvilɔlɔ̃ si me alakpa mele o va le mia dome la, milɔ̃ mia nɔewo vevie tso dzi me ke. 23 Elabena wodzi mi yeyee, menye to dzidzi si gblẽna me o, ke to esi megblẽna o boŋ me, to Mawu gbagbe si nɔa anyi ɖaa ƒe nya la dzi. 24 Elabena "ŋutilãwo katã le abe gbe ene, eye woƒe atsyɔ̃ la katã le abe gbe ƒe seƒoƒo ene; gbe yrɔna, eye seƒoƒo duduna, 25 ke Yehowa ƒe nya ya nɔa anyi tegbee. " Eye "nya " siae nye nya nyui si wogblɔ na mi la.
ENGLISH: 22 Having purified your spirits by obedience to the truth for unfeigned brotherliness, love each other ardently from your hearts, 23 reborn not from perishable seed but from imperishable, through the living word of God living and abiding, 24 because "all flesh is like the herbage of the field, and all its glory like field flowers: the herbage withers and the flowers fall off; 25 but the word of the Lord abides forever, " and this is the word that has been brought to you as gospel.

EWE: 1 Petro
ENGLISH: 1 Peter

EWE: 2 Eya ta miɖe vɔ̃ɖinyenye katã, beble, alakpanuwɔwɔ, ŋubiabiã kple ameŋugbegblẽ ɖe sia ɖe ƒomevi ɖa. 2 Abe vidzĩwo ene la, mina nya la ƒe notsi tsimatɔ nadzro mi vevie, ale be miato edzi atsi ahakpɔ ɖeɖe, 3 esi mieɖɔe kpɔ hekpɔ be Aƒetɔ la ƒe dɔme nyo. 4 Azɔ esi mieva eya, si nye kpe gbagbe si amewo gbe gake wòhenye kpe tiatia xɔasi na Mawu ya gbɔ la, 5 miawo ŋutɔwo hã miezu kpe gbagbe siwo wotsɔ le gbɔgbɔmexɔ tum hena nunɔlanyenye kɔkɔe, ale be miato Yesu Kristo dzi asa gbɔgbɔmevɔ siwo dzea Mawu ŋu. 6 Elabena Ŋɔŋlɔ la gblɔ be: "Kpɔ ɖa!
ENGLISH: 2 So, laying off all malice and all trickery, and insincerities and grudges and all detraction, 2 long like newborn babies for unadulterated intellectual milk, that on it you may grow to salvation, 3 if you have tasted that the Lord is kind; 4 coming to whom, a living stone condemned by men but in God’s estimation select and noble, 5 you too as living stones are being built to a spiritual house, for a holy priesthood to offer spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.

EWE: Mele kpe tiatia aɖe ɖom anyi le Zion, si nye gɔmeɖoanyi ƒe dzogoedzikpe xɔasi, eye ame sia ame si xɔa edzi sena la maɖu ŋukpe akpɔ o.
