ENGLISH: 7 And the people worshiped Jehovah throughout Joshuaʽ’s life, and throughout the life of the elders who outlived Joshuaʽ, who had seen all Jehovah’s great work that he did for Israel.

EWE: 8 Eye Yehowa ƒe subɔla Yosua, Nun vi la, ku esi wòxɔ ƒe alafa ɖeka kple ewo.
ENGLISH: 8 And Jehovah’s servant Joshuaʽ the son of Nun died at the age of a hundred and ten years,

EWE: 9 Eye woɖii ɖe anyigba si dome wònyi la dzi le Timna-Heres le Efrayim tonuto la me le Gaas To la ƒe dziehe gome.
ENGLISH: 9 and they buried him on his estate at Timnath-Heres in the highland of Ephraim, to the north of Gaash Mountain.

EWE: 10 Dzidzime ma katã ku eye wotsɔ wo kpe ɖe wo tɔgbuiwo ŋu, eye dzidzime bubu va ɖe wo yome, ame siwo medze si Yehowa alo nya dɔ siwo wòwɔ na Israel la o.
ENGLISH: 10 And so were all that generation gathered to their fathers, and there arose after them another generation that did not know Jehovah nor the work that he did for Israel.

EWE: 11 Eya ta Israel-viwo wɔ nu si nye vɔ̃ le Yehowa ŋkume, eye wosubɔ Baalwo.
ENGLISH: 11 And the sons of Israel did what displeased Jehovah, and worshiped the Baals;

EWE: 12 Ale wogblẽ Yehowa, wo fofowo ƒe Mawu, ame si kplɔ wo tso Egipte-nyigba dzi la ɖi. Wodze mawu bubuwo, siwo nye dukɔ siwo ƒo xlã wo godoo la ƒe mawuwo yome, eye wode ta agu na wo tsɔ do dziku na Yehowa.
ENGLISH: 12 and they left their fathers’ God Jehovah, who had brought them out of Egypt, and followed other gods from among the gods of the peoples around them, and did reverence to them, and provoked Jehovah;

EWE: 13 Wogblẽ Yehowa ɖi hesubɔ Baal kple Astoret legbawo.
ENGLISH: 13 and they left Jehovah and worshiped the Baal and the ʽAshtarts.

EWE: 14 Yehowa ƒe dɔmedzoe bi ɖe Israel ŋu, ale be wòtsɔ wo de asi na adzohawo woda adzo wo. Etsɔ wo dzra na woƒe futɔ siwo ƒo xlã wo la, eye womegate ŋu nɔ te ɖe woƒe futɔwo nu o.
ENGLISH: 14 And Jehovah was angry with Israel and gave them into the hands of pillagers, and they pillaged them; and he sold them into the hands of their enemies on all sides, and they could no longer stand before their enemies.

EWE: 15 Afi sia afi si woyi la, Yehowa ƒe asi sẽna ɖe wo dzi, ale be vɔ̃ tua wo, abe ale si Yehowa gblɔ na wo kple ale si Yehowa ka atam na woe ene, eye woɖo xaxa me ŋutɔ.
ENGLISH: 15 In everything they undertook Jehovah’s hand was on them for mischief, as Jehovah had threatened and as Jehovah had sworn to them; and they were in great straits.

EWE: 16 Eya ta Yehowa ɖoa ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo na wo, ame siwo ɖea wo tso adzohawo si me.
ENGLISH: 16 And Jehovah raised up judges, and they saved them out of the hands of their pillagers;

EWE: 17 Gake wogbe toɖoɖo ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo gɔ̃ hã, wowɔa ahasi kple mawu bubuwo, eye wodea ta agu na wo.
ENGLISH: 17 and neither did they listen to their judges, but prostituted themselves to follow other gods and did reverence to them.

EWE: Wotrɔ ɖa kaba tso mɔ si dzi wo tɔgbuiwo, ame siwo ɖo to Yehowa ƒe sededewo, zɔ la dzi. Womewɔ nu abe wo tɔgbuiwo ene o.
ENGLISH: They quickly left the road their fathers had gone in, obeying Jehovah’s commandments; they did not do so.

EWE: 18 Ɣesiaɣi si Yehowa ɖo ʋɔnudrɔ̃la na wo la, Yehowa nɔa anyi kple ʋɔnudrɔ̃laa, eye wòɖea wo tso woƒe futɔwo si me le ʋɔnudrɔ̃la la ƒe ŋkekewo katã me; elabena ewɔa nublanui na Yehowa ne ame siwo te wo ɖe anyi kple ame siwo sẽ ŋuta le wo ŋu na wole hũ ɖem.
ENGLISH: 18 And when Jehovah raised up judges for them Jehovah was with the judge and saved them out of the hands of their enemies throughout the time of the judge, because Jehovah repented at their groaning over their oppressors and molesters.

EWE: 19 Ke ne ʋɔnudrɔ̃la la ku la, wogawɔa nu gbegblẽ ɖe edzi wu wo fofowo, wodzea mawu bubuwo yome, eye wosubɔa wo hedea ta agu na wo. Womeɖea asi le woƒe nuwɔnawo kple woƒe tosesẽ la ŋu o.
ENGLISH: 19 And at the judge’s death they went back to doing more viciously than their fathers, following other gods, worshiping them and doing them reverence; they did not drop any part of their practices, and of their stubborn course.

EWE: 20 Mlɔeba Yehowa ƒe dɔmedzoe bi ɖe Israel ŋu wògblɔ be: “Esi dukɔ sia tu nu, si mebla kpli wo tɔgbuiwo, eye womeɖo to nye gbe o ta la,
ENGLISH: 20 And Jehovah was angry with Israel and said “Since this nation have violated my covenant which I commanded their fathers, and not been obedient to me,

EWE: 21 nye hã nyemanya dukɔ siwo Yosua kpɔtɔ ɖi hafi ku la dometɔ ɖeka pɛ hã ɖa le wo ŋgɔ o.
ENGLISH: 21 I on my part will not dispossess before you any more of the nations that Joshuaʽ left when he died,”

EWE: 22 Ne matsɔ wo ado Israel kpɔ be woalé ŋku ɖe Yehowa ƒe mɔ ŋu ahazɔ edzi, abe ale si tututu wo fofowo lé ŋku ɖe eŋu ene loo, alo womalé ŋku ɖe eŋu o hã.” 23 Eya ta Yehowa ɖe mɔ dukɔ siawo tsi anyi.
ENGLISH: 22 in order to test Israel by them, whether they kept his ways, walking in them, as their fathers had kept them, or not.

EWE: Menya wo ɖa zi ɖeka o, eye metsɔ wo de asi na Yosua o.
ENGLISH: 23 And Jehovah left these nations, not dispossessing them quickly, and did not give them into Joshuaʽ’s hands.

EWE: Ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo
ENGLISH: Judges

EWE: 3 Dukɔ siwo Yehowa kpɔtɔ ɖi be yeatsɔ ado Israel-vi siwo katã mekpɔ aʋa siwo wowɔ kple Kanaantɔwo teƒe o la kpɔ
ENGLISH: 3 And these are the nations that Jehovah left to test Israel by, all who had not known any of the Canaanite wars;

EWE: 2 (ewɔ esia be Israel-viwo ƒe dzidzime siwo ava emegbe la nakpɔ aʋa teƒe, ne wòatsɔ afia aʋawɔwɔ ame siwo mekpɔ aʋa teƒe kpɔ o) la woe nye:
ENGLISH: 2 only for the sake of the generations of the sons of Israel, to teach them war only those who had not known them before:

EWE: 3 Filistitɔwo ƒe kplɔla atɔ̃awo, Kanaantɔwo, Sidontɔwo, kple Hivitɔwo, siwo katã le Lebanon Towo dzi tso Baal-Hermon To gbɔ va se ɖe Lebo-Hamat ke.
ENGLISH: 3 the Five Sarns of the Philistines, and all the Canaanites and the Phenicians and the Hivvites that live on Mount Lebanon, from Mount Baal-Hermon to Lebo-Hamath;

EWE: 4 Wotsɔ wo do Israel kpɔ ne woakpɔe ɖa be Israel aɖo to Yehowa ƒe se siwo wòde na wo fofowo to Mose dzi hã.
ENGLISH: 4 and they were to test Israel by, to know whether they would obey Jehovah’s commandments which he had given to their fathers by Moses.

EWE: 5 Eya ta Israel-viwo nɔ Kanaantɔwo, Hititɔwo, Amoritɔwo, Perizitɔwo, Hivitɔwo kple Yebusitɔwo dome.
ENGLISH: 5 And the sons of Israel lived in the midst of the Canaanites, the Hittites and the Amorites and the Perizzites and the Hivvites and the Jebusites,

EWE: 6 Woɖe wo vinyɔnuwo, eye wotsɔ wo vinyɔnuwo na wo viŋutsuwo woɖe, eye wosubɔ woƒe mawuwo.
ENGLISH: 6 and took their daughters for wives and gave their own daughters to their sons, and worshiped their gods.

EWE: 7 Ale Israel-viwo wɔ nu si nye vɔ̃ le Yehowa ŋkume, woŋlɔ Yehowa woƒe Mawu la be, eye wosubɔ Baalwo kple Aserawo.
ENGLISH: 7 And the sons of Israel did what displeased Jehovah, and forgot their God Jehovah and worshiped the Baals and the Asherahs;

EWE: 8 Eya ta Yehowa ƒe dɔmedzoe bi ɖe Israel ŋu, ale be wòtsɔ wo dzra na Mesopotamia-fia Kusan-Risatayim. Israel-viwo subɔ Kusan-Risatayim ƒe enyi.
ENGLISH: 8 and Jehovah was angry with Israel and sold them into the hands of Cushan-Risheathaim, the king of Aram-Naharaim; and the sons of Israel were subject to Cushan-Risheathaim eight years.

EWE: 9 Esi Israel-viwo yɔ Yehowa be wòaxɔ na yewo la, Yehowa ɖo xɔla na Israel-viwo, si nye Otniel, Kaleb ƒe tsɛ Kenaz ƒe vi, be wòaɖe wo.
ENGLISH: 9 And the sons of Israel cried to Jehovah, and Jehovah raised up for the sons of Israel a deliverer who saved them, Ghothniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother;

EWE: 10 Eye Yehowa ƒe gbɔgbɔ va edzi, ale wòzu Israel ƒe ʋɔnudrɔ̃la. Esi wòho aʋa la, Yehowa tsɔ Mesopotamia-fia Kusan-Risatayim de asi nɛ, eye wòɖu Kusan-Risatayim dzi.
ENGLISH: 10 and the spirit of Jehovah came upon him, and he judged Israel and went out to war, and Jehovah gave King Cushan-Risheathaim of Aram into his hands, and his hands bore hard on Cushan-Risheathaim;

EWE: 11 Ema megbe la, anyigba la kpɔ gbɔdzɔe ƒe blaene.
ENGLISH: 11 and the country was quiet forty years.

EWE: Emegbe Otniel, Kenaz vi la ku.
ENGLISH: And Ghothniel the son of Kenaz died,

EWE: 12 Eye Israel-viwo gade asi nu si nye vɔ̃ wɔwɔ me le Yehowa ŋkume. Eya ta Yehowa ɖe mɔ Moab-fia Eglon ɖu Israel dzi, elabena wowɔ nu si nye vɔ̃ le Yehowa ŋkume.
ENGLISH: 12 and the sons of Israel did more of what displeased Jehovah, and Jehovah strengthened King ʽEglon of Moab against Israel because of their doing what displeased Jehovah;

EWE: 13 Azɔ hã, ekplɔ Amonitɔwo kple Amalektɔwo va ƒu wo. Wodze Israel dzi eye woxɔ devedu la.
ENGLISH: 13 and he drew together around him the Bene-ʽAmmon and ʽAmalek, and went and defeated Israel and took possession of the City of Palms;

EWE: 14 Israel-viwo subɔ Moab-fia Eglon ƒe wuienyi.
ENGLISH: 14 and the sons of Israel were subject to King ʽEglon of Moab eighteen years.

EWE: 15 Eye Israel-viwo yɔ Yehowa be wòaxɔ na yewo.
ENGLISH: 15 And the sons of Israel cried to Jehovah, and Jehovah raised them up a deliverer, Ehud the son of Gera the Benjamite, a left-handed man.

EWE: Eya ta Yehowa ɖo xɔla na wo, si nye Ehud, Gera vi, enye Benyamintɔ miawɔla aɖe.
ENGLISH: And the sons of Israel were sending a tribute by him to King ʽEglon of Moab;

EWE: 16 Ehud tu adekpui nuevee, si didi abɔklugui ɖeka, eye wòtae ɖe ɖusiklito le eƒe awu te.
ENGLISH: 16 and Ehud made himself a sword with two edges, a foot long, and belted it on under his brigandine, on his right hip.

EWE: 17 Etsɔ adzɔ la vɛ na Moab-fia Eglon. Eglon nye ame lolo dami aɖe.
ENGLISH: 17 And he presented the tribute to King ʽEglon of Moab (who was a very fat man);

EWE: 18 Esi Ehud tsɔ adzɔa na vɔ la, eya kple ame siwo tsɔ adzɔa vɛ la trɔ dzo.
ENGLISH: 18 and when he had finished presenting the tribute he dismissed the people who carried the tribute,

EWE: 19 Ke esi woɖo kpetatawo gbɔ le Gilgal la, etrɔ va gblɔ na fia la be: “Oo fia, nya ɣaɣla aɖe le asinye na wò.” Eya ta fia la gblɔ be: “Ðoɖoe nezi!” Ale eƒe subɔviwo katã do go le egbɔ.
ENGLISH: 19 but he turned back from the carved stones at the Gilgal and said “Your majesty, I have some private business with you”; and he said “Quiet!” and all who were standing in his presence went out from it,

EWE: 20 Eye Ehud va egbɔ, esime eya ɖeka nɔ eƒe xɔtaxɔ si me wòxɔa ya fafɛ le la me.
ENGLISH: 20 and Ehud went in to him, he sitting in his cool roof-chamber alone.

EWE: Eye Ehud gblɔ be: “Mexɔ gbedeasi aɖe tso Mawu gbɔ vɛ na wò.”
ENGLISH: And Ehud said “I have an errand from God to you”; and he rose from his chair.

EWE: Ale wòtso le eƒe fiazikpui la dzi. 21 Azɔ Ehud do eƒe miasi ɖa ɖe adekpui la le ɖusiklito heƒo ɖe dɔme nɛ flo.
ENGLISH: 21 And Ehud put his left hand in and took the sword from his right hip and ran it into ʽEglon’s abdomen,

EWE: 22 Eye adekpui la kple eƒe asiléƒea siaa bu ɖe eme, eye ami nyè tsyɔ adekpui la, elabena meɖe adekpui la le dɔme nɛ o, eye mĩ do go.
ENGLISH: 22 and it went in hilt and all, and the fat closed over the blade, because he had not drawn the sword out of the abdomen;

EWE: 23 Ehud to akpata la me do, etu xɔtaxɔ la ƒe ʋɔtruawo le emegbe, eye wòde ga wo me.
ENGLISH: 23 and Ehud went out on the ledge, and shut the doors of the roof-chamber on him and locked them.

EWE: 24 Esi wòdzo la, fia ƒe subɔviwo va eye wokpɔ be wode ga xɔtaxɔ la ƒe ʋɔtruwo me. Eya ta wogblɔ be: “Anya nɔ afɔdzi le xɔ emetɔ me le yaxɔƒe la.”
ENGLISH: 24 And when he had gone out ʽEglon’s servants came and saw how the doors of the roof-chamber were locked, and thought “He must be easing himself in the cool closet”;

EWE: 25 Wolala ʋuu va se ɖe esime wotsi yaa, gake esi wokpɔe be mele xɔtaxɔ la ƒe ʋɔtruawo ʋum o la, wotsɔ safui ʋu wo, eye wokpɔ woƒe aƒetɔ la ku ɖe anyigba!
ENGLISH: 25 and they waited till they felt uncomfortable, and found that he did not open the doors of the roof-chamber; and they took the key and opened them, and found their sovereign down on the ground dead.

EWE: 26 Ehud si dzo esime wonɔ hehem ɖe megbe, eye wòto kpetatawo gbɔ va do ɖe Seira dedie.
ENGLISH: 26 And Ehud made his escape while they were delaying, and had passed the carved stones and got safe to Seʽirah.

EWE: 27 Esi wòɖo afi ma la, eku kpẽ le Efrayim tonuto la me; eye Israel-viwo ɖi tso toawo dzi dze eyome, eye eya ŋutɔ dze wo ŋgɔ.
ENGLISH: 27 And when he got there he blew the ram-horn in the highland of Ephraim, and the sons of Israel came down from the highland with him, he at their head;

EWE: 28 Eye wògblɔ na wo be: “Midze yonyeme, elabena Yehowa tsɔ miaƒe futɔ siwo nye Moabtɔwo de asi na mi.” Eye wodze eyome heva xe mɔ le Yordan tɔtsoƒewo be Moabtɔwo nagatso tɔa o, eye womeɖe mɔ na ame aɖeke be wòatsoe o.
ENGLISH: 28 and he said to them “Come down after me, because Jehovah has given your enemies the Moabites into your hands,” and they came down after him and took the fords of the Jordan against the Moabites and did not let a man cross,

EWE: 29 Ɣemaɣi la, wowu Moabtɔ siwo anɔ ame akpe ewo, wo katã wonye ŋutsu kakowo kple kalẽtɔwo; ame ɖeka hɔ̃ hã mesi o.
ENGLISH: 29 and made havoc of the Moabites at that time, killing about ten thousand men every man of standing and every man of energy; not one escaped;

EWE: 30 Wobɔbɔ Moab ɖe Israel ƒe asi te gbe ma gbe; eye anyigba la kpɔ gbɔdzɔe ƒe blaenyi sɔŋ.
ENGLISH: 30 and Moab was humbled under the hands of Israel on that day. And the country was quiet eighty years.

EWE: 31 Samgar, Anat vi va ɖe eyome, etsɔ nyikplɔti wu Filistitɔ alafa ade; eya hã ɖe Israel.
ENGLISH: 31 And after him was Shamgar the son of ʽAnath, and he made havoc of the Philistines, killing six hundred men with an oxgoad; and he too saved Israel.

EWE: Ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo
ENGLISH: Judges

EWE: 4 Ke le Ehud ƒe ku megbe la, Israel-viwo gawɔ nu si nye vɔ̃ le Yehowa ŋkume.
ENGLISH: 4 And the sons of Israel did more of what displeased Jehovah, Ehud being dead,

EWE: 2 Eya ta Yehowa tsɔ wo dzra na Kanaan-fia Yabin, si ɖu fia le Hazor. Eƒe aʋafiae nye Sisera, ame si nɔ dukɔwo ƒe Haroset.
ENGLISH: 2 and Jehovah sold them into the hands of Jabin, the king of the Canaanites, who reigned at Hasor; his general was Sisera, whose residence was Harosheth-haggoyim;

EWE: 3 Israel-viwo do ɣli na Yehowa, elabena aʋatasiaɖam siwo ƒe afɔtiwo ŋu lãnuwo le alafa asieke le Yabin si, eye wòte Israel-viwo ɖe anyi vevie ƒe blaeve sɔŋ.
ENGLISH: 3 and the sons of Israel cried out to Jehovah, because he had nine hundred iron chariots; and for twenty years he oppressed the sons of Israel by main force.

EWE: 4 Ke nyɔnunyagblɔɖila Debora, Lapidot srɔ̃, nɔ ʋɔnu drɔ̃m Israel ɣemaɣi.
ENGLISH: 4 And Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth, judged Israel at that time:

EWE: 5 Enɔa Debora ƒe deti te le Rama kple Betel dome le Efrayim tonuto la me; eye Israel-viwo yia egbɔ wòdrɔ̃a ʋɔnu na wo.
ENGLISH: 5 she sat under Deborah’s Palms between Ramah and Bethel, in the highland of Ephraim, and the sons of Israel went up to her for justice.

EWE: 6 Edɔ woyi ɖayɔ Barak, Abinoam vi, tso Kedes-Naftali vɛ, eye wògblɔ nɛ be: “Ðe Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la, mede se oa? ‘Ho yi Tabor To la dzi, nàɖe ame akpe ewo tso Naftali viwo kple Zebulon viwo dome kpe ɖe ɖokuiwò ŋu.
ENGLISH: 6 And she sent and called Barak the son of Abinoʽam from Kedesh in Naphtali, and said to him “The order has come from Israel’s God Jehovah, ‘Go march on Mount Tabor, taking with you ten thousand men of the sons of Naphtali and of the sons of Zebulun;

EWE: 7 Makplɔ Sisera, Yabin ƒe aʋafia kple eƒe aʋatasiaɖamwo kpakple eƒe aʋakɔ la vɛ na wò le Kison-tɔsisi la nu, eye matsɔe ade asi na wò.’”
ENGLISH: 7 and I will draw to you, to Kishon Arroyo, Jabin’s general Sisera and his chariots and his host, and I will give them into your hands.’”

EWE: 8 Ke Barak gblɔ nɛ be: “Ne àyi kplim la, ekema mayi; ke ne màyi kplim o la, nye hã nyemayi o.”
ENGLISH: 8 And Barak said to her “If you go with me I will go, but if you do not I will not.”

EWE: 9 Eɖo eŋu be: “Mayi kpli wò godoo. Ke hã, aʋa si kpe ge miele la ƒe bubu mava na wò o, elabena nyɔnu aɖe si mee Yehowa atsɔ Sisera ade.”
ENGLISH: 9 And she said “Go with you I will; there will be no glory for you, though, in the campaign on which you go, because Jehovah will sell Sisera into a woman’s hands.”

EWE: Ale Debora tso yi Kedes kpe ɖe Barak ŋu.
ENGLISH: And Deborah rose and went with Barak to Kedesh;

EWE: 10 Barak yɔ Zebulon kple Naftali va ƒo ƒu ɖe Kedes, eye ŋutsu akpe ewo dze eyome. Debora hã yi kplii.
ENGLISH: 10 and Barak called out Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh; and ten thousand men went up at his back, and Deborah went up with him.

EWE: 11 Edzɔ be Kenitɔ Heber dzo le Kenitɔ siwo nye Mose to Hobab ƒe dzidzimeviwo gbɔ, eye wòva tu eƒe agbadɔ ɖe ati gã la xa le Zaananim le Kedes.
ENGLISH: 11 And Heber the Cainite had separated from the Cainites, the sons of Moses’s father-in-law Hobab, and pitched his tent up to the Besaʽanim Oak near Kedesh.

EWE: 12 Wova gblɔ na Sisera be Barak, Abinoam vi, yi Tabor To la dzi.
ENGLISH: 12 And they told Sisera that Barak the son of Abinoʽam had gone up to Mount Tabor;

EWE: 13 Enumake Sisera ƒo eƒe aʋatasiaɖamwo katã aʋatasiaɖam siwo ƒe afɔtiwo ŋu lãnuwo le alafa asieke kple eƒe aʋakɔ blibo la nu ƒu tso dukɔwo ƒe Haroset, eye woho yi Kison-tɔsisi la nu.
ENGLISH: 13 and Sisera called out all the chariots he had, nine hundred iron chariots, and all the men he had with him, from Harosheth-haggoyim to Kishon Arroyo.

EWE: 14 Azɔ Debora gblɔ na Barak be: “Tso, elabena egbee Yehowa atsɔ Sisera ade asi na wò. Ðe Yehowa medze ŋgɔwò oa?”
ENGLISH: 14 And Deborah said to Barak “Up, for this is the day Jehovah has given Sisera into your hands Jehovah has gone out before you!”

EWE: Ale Barak ɖi tso Tabor To la dzi, eye ŋutsu akpe ewoawo dze eyome.
ENGLISH: And down went Barak from Mount Tabor, with ten thousand men behind him;

EWE: 15 Eye Yehowa tsɔ yi de tɔtɔ Sisera kple eƒe aʋatasiaɖamwo katã kple aʋakɔ blibo la katã dome le Barak ŋgɔ.
ENGLISH: 15 and Jehovah routed Sisera and all his chariots and all his army unsparingly before Barak, and Sisera dismounted from his chariot and fled on foot,

EWE: Mlɔeba Sisera ɖi le eƒe tasiaɖam la me heto afɔ si. 16 Barak nya aʋatasiaɖamawo kple aʋakɔ la ɖe nu va se ɖe dukɔwo ƒe Haroset ke.
ENGLISH: 16 while Barak pursued the chariots and the army clear to Harosheth-haggoyim, and all Sisera’s army fell without quarter: not one was left.

EWE: 17 Ke Sisera to afɔ si yi nyɔnu aɖe si ŋkɔe nye Yael, Kenitɔ Heber srɔ̃ ƒe agbadɔ gbɔ, elabena ŋutifafa le Hazor-fia Yabin kple Kenitɔ Heber ƒe aƒe la dome.
ENGLISH: 17 And Sisera fled on foot to the tent of Jael the wife of Heber the Cainite, because King Jabin of Hasor and the family of Heber the Cainite were at peace.

EWE: 18 Eye Yael do yi ɖakpe Sisera gblɔ nɛ be: “Nye aƒetɔ, ge ɖe eme, va dze gbɔnye. Mègavɔ̃ o.” Eya ta eyi eƒe agbadɔ la me, eye wòtsyɔ kuntru nɛ.
ENGLISH: 18 And Jael went out to meet Sisera and said to him “In here, sir, in here with me; do not be afraid”; and Sisera went in with her into the tent, and she covered him with the rug;

EWE: 19 Eye wògblɔ na nyɔnua be: “Meɖe kuku, na tsi vi aɖem mano, elabena tsikɔ le wuyem.” Eya ta eʋu lãgbalẽgolo si me notsi le, eye wòna ɖee wòno, emegbe wògatsɔ kuntru la tsyɔ nɛ.
ENGLISH: 19 and he said to her “Let me have a drink of water, I am thirsty,” and she opened the bag of milk and let him drink and covered him up.

EWE: 20 Egblɔ nɛ be: “Yi ɖatɔ ɖe agbadɔ la nu, eye ne ame aɖe va bia wò be: ‘Ŋutsu aɖe le afi sia?’ hã la, gblɔ be: ‘Ao!’”
ENGLISH: 20 And he said to her “Stand at the door of the tent, and if anyone comes and asks you ‘Is there anyone here?’ say ‘No.’”

EWE: 21 Ke Yael, Heber srɔ̃ tsɔ agbadɔtsyoti kple zu ɖe asi. Eye esi ɖeɖi te Sisera ŋu belibeli wòyi alɔ̃ me ʋĩi la, ete ɖe eŋu dzaa eye wòƒo tsyoti la ɖe tonu nɛ heƒoe wòdo ɖe anyigba, ale wòku.
ENGLISH: 21 And Jael the wife of Heber the Cainite got her tent-peg, and took the hammer in her hand, and went in quietly where he was and drove the peg into his temples, and through into the ground, while he was fast asleep and exhausted, and killed him.

EWE: 22 Barak ti Sisera yome yi afi ma, eye Yael do yi ɖakpee hegblɔ nɛ be: “Va mafia ame si dim nèle la wò.” Ale eya kplii woge ɖe eme, eye wòkpɔ Sisera wòku ɖi, tsyoti la ƒo ɖe tonu nɛ.
ENGLISH: 22 And up came Barak pursuing Sisera, and Jael went out to meet him and said to him “Come, and I will show you the man you are looking for”; and he went into her tent and found Sisera lying dead with the peg in his temple.

EWE: 23 Ale Mawu bɔbɔ Kanaan-fia Yabin ɖe anyi le Israel-viwo ŋkume gbe ma gbe.
ENGLISH: 23 And Jehovah humbled King Jabin of the Canaanites that day before the sons of Israel;

EWE: 24 Eye Israel-viwo ƒe asi nɔ sesẽm ɖe Kanaan-fia Yabin dzi va se ɖe esime wotsrɔ̃ Kanaan-fia Yabin ɖa keŋkeŋ.
ENGLISH: 24 and the hands of the sons of Israel pressed harder and harder on King Jabin of the Canaanites till they had wiped out King Jabin of the Canaanites.

EWE: Ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo
ENGLISH: Judges

EWE: 5 Debora kple Barak, Abinoam vi, dzi ha sia gbe ma gbe be:
ENGLISH: 5 And Deborah and Barak the son of Abinoam sang on that day

EWE: 2 “Mikafu Yehowa, Elabe wogblẽ taɖa ɖi ʋluya le Israel, Elabe dukɔ la tsɔ eɖokui na faa!
ENGLISH: 2 “For untrimmed hair in Israel,for ready volunteers, bless Jehovah!

EWE: 3 Mi fiawo, misee; mi dziɖulawo, miƒu to anyi! Mele ha dzi ge na Yehowa.
ENGLISH: 3 Listen, kings; give ear, potentates; I will sing to Jehovah, I!

EWE: Madzi kafukafuha na Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la.
ENGLISH: I will make music to Israel’s God Jehovah.

EWE: 4 Yehowa, esi nèdo tso Seir, Esi nèho tso Edom-nyigba dzi la, Anyigba ʋuʋu, tsi dza tso dziƒowo bababa, Alilikpowo ɖuɖu tsi yoyoyo.
ENGLISH: 4 Jehovah, when you came out from Seir, when you paced forth from the wolds of Edom, The earth quaked; aye, the heavens tossed; aye, the clouds dripped water,

EWE: 5 Towo lólo le Yehowa ŋkume, Sinai kekeake hã lólo le Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la ŋkume.
ENGLISH: 5 The mountains streamed at Jehovah’s presence, this is Sinai,at the presence of Israel’s God Jehovah.

EWE: 6 Le Samgar, Anat vi ŋɔli, Le Yael ŋɔli la, mɔwo dzi ɖi gbɔlo; Mɔzɔlawo katã toa gbememɔwo.
ENGLISH: 6 In the days of Shamgar the son of ʽAnath,in the days of Jael, roads ceased and wayfarers went by devious roads;

EWE: 7 Amewo megale Israel ƒe kɔƒewo me o; Womegali o va se ɖe esime nye, Debora, metso, Va se ɖe esime metso abe vidada ene le Israel.
ENGLISH: 7 Prowess ceased in Israel, ceased till you arose, Deborah, till you arose, mother in Israel.

EWE: 8 Wotia mawu yeyewo; Aʋa nɔ agbowo me ɣemaɣi. Womekpɔ akpoxɔnu alo akplɔ aɖeke Le ame akpe blaene dome le Israel o.
ENGLISH: 8 He would choose new gods; then barley bread; Shield was not to be seen, nor spear, among forty thousand in Israel.

EWE: 9 Nye dzi ku ɖe Israel ƒe kplɔlawo ŋu, Ame siwo tsɔ wo ɖokui na faa yi kple dukɔ la. Mikafu Yehowa!
ENGLISH: 9 My heart goes out to the marshals of Israel, who volunteered among the people; bless Jehovah!

EWE: 10 Mi ame siwo do tedzinɔ hẽwo, Mi ame siwo bɔbɔ nɔ kuntru nyuiwo dzi, Kple mi ame siwo zɔa mɔ dzi, Mibu eŋu kpɔ!
ENGLISH: 10 Riders of roan asses, sitters on carpets, walkers by the way, review it!

EWE: 11 Wose tsikulawo ƒe gbe le lãwo ƒe tsinoƒe; Wole Yehowa ƒe nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔwo gblɔm le afi ma, Eƒe ame siwo le Israel kɔƒewo me ƒe nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔwo.
ENGLISH: 11 At the sound of archers between the water-holes there they shall celebrate Jehovah’s loyal work, his loyal work of prowess in Israel.

EWE: Ɣemaɣie Yehowa ƒe amewo ɖi va agboawo nu.
ENGLISH: Then Jehovah’s people went down to the gates!

EWE: 12 Nyɔ, nyɔ, Oo Debora! Nyɔ, nyɔ, nàdzi ha! Tso, Barak, Abinoam vi, nàkplɔ wò aboyomewo adzoe!
ENGLISH: 12 Arouse, arouse, Deborah; rouse, rouse, chant your song; up, Barak; take your captives, son of Abinoʽam!

EWE: 13 Eye ame siwo susɔ la ɖi va bubumewo gbɔ; Yehowa ƒe dukɔ la ɖi va gbɔnye ɖe kalẽtɔ la ŋu.
ENGLISH: 13 Then survivors came down for heroes, Jehovah’s people came down for me among champions:

EWE: 14 Efrayim mee wodzɔ tso, wo ame siwo le bali la me, Wodze yowòme, Oo Benyamin, wole wò amewo dome. Kplɔlawo ɖi abu tso Makir, Eye ame siwo si aʋawɔlawo tiala ƒe atikplɔ le la tso Zebulon.
ENGLISH: 14 Out of Ephraim those whose root is in the vale,your brother Benjamin among your kinsfolk; Out of Makir marshals came down, and out of Zebulun wielders of the mustering-baton.

EWE: 15 Isakar ƒe amegãwo nɔ Debora ŋu, Ale si Isakar wɔ la, nenemae Barak hã wɔ. Wodɔe wòto afɔ yi bali la me.
ENGLISH: 15 And the chiefs in Issacar were with Deborah, and Issacar, so Barak; in the vale they poured along at his back.

EWE: Wodzro dziwo me kpɔ vevie le Ruben ƒe hatsotsowo dome.
ENGLISH: At Reuben’s water-channels great were the resolves of minds.

EWE: 16 Nu ka tae nèbɔbɔ nɔ sɔkpa si ŋu kotoku eve le dzi, Hele to ɖom lãkplɔlawo ƒe dze si kum wole na lãhawo?
ENGLISH: 16 Why did you sit in the fork of the paths to hear the whistles of the flocks?

EWE: Ruben ƒe hatsotsowo de adaŋu vevie.
ENGLISH: By Reuben’s water-channels great were the searchings of minds.

EWE: 17 Gilead tsi Yordan godo; Eye nu ka tae Dan tsi tɔdziʋuwo gbɔ? Aser nɔ anyi ɖi ɖe ƒuta, Eye wòtsi eƒe tɔdziʋudzeƒewo.
ENGLISH: 17 Gilead was settled on the other side of the Jordan, and Dan was on foreign ships;Asher was living by the beach,settled at its landings.

EWE: 18 Zebulon nye dukɔ si tsɔ eƒe agbe ke ku faa; Naftali hã wɔ nenema le gbadzaƒe si le towo dzi.
ENGLISH: 18 Zebulun was a people that flouted their lives to die,and Naphtali, on the heights of the range.

EWE: 19 Fiawo va wɔ aʋa; Kanaan fiawo kpe aʋa Le Taanak, le Megido-tɔ la nu ɣemaɣi. Womekpɔ klosalo aɖeke ha o.
ENGLISH: 19 Kings came, they fought; then fought the kings of the Canaanites at Taʽanac by the Megiddo Water;no winnings of silver did they take.

EWE: 20 Ɣletiviwo wɔ aʋa tso dziƒo; Wonɔ woƒe mɔwo dzi kpe aʋa kple Sisera.
ENGLISH: 20 The stars fought out of the sky,out of their orbits they fought with Sisera.

EWE: 21 Kison-tɔʋu la kplɔ wo dzoe, Blematɔʋu, Kison-tɔʋu la. Oo nye luʋɔ, ètu afɔ ŋusẽtɔwo dzi.
ENGLISH: 21 The Kishon torrent swept them off,streaked with their blood was the Kishon torrent,stout souls were set on their way.

EWE: 22 Ɣemaɣie sɔwo ƒe afɔziwo nɔ ɖiɖim kpitikpitikpiti, Esi eƒe sɔtsuwo nɔ du dzi vevie.
ENGLISH: 22 Then they pounded the ponies’ heels,his heroes went galloping, galloping.

EWE: 23 Yehowa ƒe dɔla be: ‘Neɖi Meroz ŋu, ‘Ɛ̃, neɖi emenɔlawo ŋu, Elabe womeva kpe ɖe Yehowa ŋu o, Womekplɔ kalẽtɔwo ɖo va kpe ɖe Yehowa ŋu o.’
ENGLISH: 23 Curse Meroz, says Jehovah’s Angel, curse its inhabitants with a downright curse, Because they did not come to help Jehovah,to help Jehovah among the champions.

EWE: 24 Woyra Yael, Kenitɔ Heber srɔ̃ Geɖe wu le nyɔnuwo dome; Woyrae geɖe wu le nyɔnu agbadɔmenɔlawo dome.
ENGLISH: 24 Most blessed of women be Jael the wife of Heber the Cainite, of women in tents most blessed:

EWE: 25 Tsie wòbia; ke notsie wònae. Eku notsi kpekẽ ɖe bubumewo ƒe kplu me vɛ.
ENGLISH: 25 Water he asked, milk she has given, in a noble bowl she has brought clabber.

EWE: 26 Edo asi ɖa tsɔ tsyoti, Edo nuɖusi ɖa tsɔ dɔwɔla ƒe zu. Eye wòda zu ɖe Sisera dzi, egbã ta nɛ, Eye wògbã eƒe tonuƒuiwo heŋɔe.
ENGLISH: 26 Her hand she puts to the peg, her right hand to the toilers’ mallet,And strikes Sisera, smashes his head, shatters and drives through his temple-bone.

EWE: 27 Etsra wɔɔ ɖe eƒe afɔnu; etsi anyigba kpoo; Etsra ɖe eƒe afɔnu, etsi anyigba; Afi si wòtsra ɖo la, afi mae wòku ɖo.
ENGLISH: 27 Between her legs he plunged, fell, lay; between her legs he plunged, fell; where he plunged, there he fell smitten.

EWE: 28 Nyɔnu aɖe le nu kpɔm to fesre nu, Sisera dadae nɔ nu kpɔm to adzrala me, ‘Nu ka tae eƒe tasiaɖam meva ɖo kpɔ o? Nu ka tae eƒe tasiaɖamfɔwo ƒe ɖiɖi tsi megbe ale?’
ENGLISH: 28 At the window, at the lattice,Sisera’s mother stood looking out and talking all the time:‘Why is it his chariotry is so long in coming?why is it the hoofbeats of his chariots are so late?’

EWE: 29 Eƒe nyɔnu bubume siwo dze nunya wu ɖoa eŋu nɛ; Eye eya ŋutɔ hã gblɔna na eɖokui be:
ENGLISH: 29 The wisest of her ladies answered her,she herself echoed back her words,

EWE: 30 ‘Woanya nɔ aboyonu siwo wokpɔ la mam, Nyɔnuvi ɖeka, nyɔnuvi eve na aʋawɔla ɖe sia ɖe, Sisera ƒe aboyonu nanye avɔ siwo wode amae, aboyonu la nanye avɔ si wode amae, Kple awu si me wolɔ̃ atsyã ɖo, avɔ si wode amae ɖeka, awu siwo me wolɔ̃ atsyã ɖo eve Na nuhalawo ƒe kɔ.’
ENGLISH: 30 ‘O, they are finding booty, dividing it, a slave-girl or two per man, A booty of dyed cloths for Sisera,a booty of dyed cloths, embroidery,a dyed cloth, double embroidery, for my neck booty!’

EWE: 31 Oo Yehowa, wò futɔwo katã nu neyi, Gake na ame siwo lɔ̃a wò la nanɔ abe ɣe si dze le eƒe atsyɔ̃ɖoɖo gã me ene.”
ENGLISH: 31 So may all your enemies perish, Jehovah! and may those who love him be like the rising of the sun at its brightest!”

EWE: Eye anyigba la kpɔ gbɔdzɔe ƒe blaene sɔŋ.
ENGLISH: And the country was quiet forty years.

EWE: Ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo
ENGLISH: Judges

EWE: 6 Ke Israel-viwo gawɔ nu si nye vɔ̃ le Yehowa ŋkume, eya ta Yehowa tsɔ wo de asi na Midian ƒe adre.
ENGLISH: 6 And the sons of Israel did what displeased Jehovah, and Jehovah gave them into the hands of the Midianites seven years.

EWE: 2 Midian ƒe asi kpe Israel dzi. Eye le Midian ta Israel-viwo wɔ bebeƒewo na wo ɖokuiwo ɖe towo dzi, ɖe agadowo me kple teƒe siwo yiyi sesẽ.
ENGLISH: 2 And the Midianites’ hand bore hard on Israel: for fear of the Midianites the sons of Israel made themselves the tunnels in the mountains, and the caves and the fastnesses.

EWE: 3 Ne Israel ƒã nu la, Midian, Amalek kple Ɣedzeƒetɔwo va dzea wo dzi.
ENGLISH: 3 And if Israel sowed a crop, up would come the Midianites and the ʽAmalekites and the Eastern Beduins, and come up over them;

EWE: 4 Wova ƒua asaɖa anyi ɖe wo ŋu, eye wogblẽa anyigba la dzi nukuwo dome va se ɖe Gaza ke, eye womegblẽa nuɖuɖu, alẽ, nyi alo tedzi aɖeke ɖi na Israel o.
ENGLISH: 4 and they camped on them and pastured off the growth of the country, till you come to Ghaza; and they would leave no subsistence in Israel, nor sheep nor ox nor donkey.

EWE: 5 Elabena ɖe wova dona bibibi kple woƒe lãhawo kpakple woƒe agbadɔwo abe ʋetsuviwo ene, eye woawo ŋutɔwo kple woƒe kposɔwo mele xexlẽme o, ɖe wovaa anyigba la dzi be yewoagblẽe.
ENGLISH: 5 For they would come up stock and all, and their tents would come in as thick as grasshoppers; and they came into the country to pasture it off.

EWE: 6 Ale Israel va da ahe kolikoli le Midian ta; eye Israel-viwo yɔ Yehowa be wòaxɔ na yewo.
ENGLISH: 6 And Israel was brought very low because of the Midianites, and the sons of Israel cried to Jehovah.

EWE: 7 Esi Israel-viwo yɔ Yehowa be wòaxɔ na yewo le Midian ta la,
ENGLISH: 7 And when the sons of Israel cried to Jehovah about the Midianites

EWE: 8 Yehowa dɔ nyagblɔɖila aɖe ɖo ɖe Israel-viwo wòva gblɔ na wo be: “Ale Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la, gblɔe nye esi, ‘Mekplɔ mi dzoe le Egipte, eye meɖe mi tso kluvinyenyeƒe me.
ENGLISH: 8 Jehovah sent a prophet to the sons of Israel, and he said to them “Says Israel’s God Jehovah, ‘I brought you out from the slave-quarters,

EWE: 9 Ale meɖe mi tso Egipte kple ame siwo katã tea mi ɖe anyi la si me, eye menya miaƒe futɔwo ɖa le mia ŋgɔ hetsɔ woƒe anyigba na mi.
ENGLISH: 9 and delivered you out of the hands of all your oppressors, and drove them out before you and gave you their country;

EWE: 10 Eye megblɔ na mi hã be: “Nyee nye Yehowa mia Mawu. Migavɔ̃ Amoritɔ siwo ƒe anyigba dzi miele la ƒe mawuwo o.”
ENGLISH: 10 and I said to you “I am your God Jehovah: you shall not fear the gods of the Amorites in whose country you are settling” and you did not obey me.’”

EWE: Ke mieɖo tom o.’” 11 Emegbe Yehowa ƒe dɔla va bɔbɔ nɔ ati gã si le Ofra, si nye Yoas, Abi-Ezer vi tɔ la te. Via Gideon nɔ lu ƒom le wainfiãƒe be Midiantɔwo nagakpɔe o.
ENGLISH: 11 And the Angel of Jehovah came and stood under the terebinth-tree at Ghophrah, that belonged to Joash the Abiʽezrite; and when his son Gideon was beating out wheat in the winepress to get it out of the way of the Midianites,

EWE: 12 Yehowa ƒe dɔlaa ɖe eɖokui fiae gblɔ be: “Yehowa li kpli wò, wò aʋakalẽtɔ.”
ENGLISH: 12 the Angel of Jehovah appeared to him and said “Jehovah is with you, brave champion.”

EWE: 13 Ke Gideon gblɔ nɛ be: “Meɖe kuku, nye aƒetɔ, ne Yehowa li kpli mí ɖe, nu ka tae nu siawo katã dzɔ ɖe mía dzi ɖo? Eye afi kae eƒe nukudɔ siwo ŋu mía fofowo ƒo nu le na mí hegblɔ be, ‘Ðe Yehowa meɖe mí tso Egipte oa?’ la le? Azɔ Yehowa gblẽ mí ɖi, eye wòtsɔ mí de asi na Midian.”
ENGLISH: 13 And Gideon said to him “Well, sir, if Jehovah is with us, why has all this come upon us? and where are all his wonders that our fathers have told us of, saying ‘Did not Jehovah bring us up out of Egypt?’ but now Jehovah has abandoned us and put us into Midian’s hands.”

EWE: 14 Yehowa dze ŋgɔe hegblɔ be: “Yi le ŋusẽ si le asiwò la me, eye àɖe Israel tso Midian si me.
ENGLISH: 14 And Jehovah turned to him and said “Go with that strength of yours and save Israel out of Midian’s hands I send you!”

EWE: Alo menye nyee dɔ wò oa?” 15 Gake Gideon ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Meɖe kuku, Yehowa. Aleke mawɔ aɖe Israel? Kpɔ ɖa!
ENGLISH: 15 And he said to him “O, sir, with what shall I save Israel? my thousand is the weakest in Manasseh, and I the most insignificant of my family.”

EWE: 16 Ke Yehowa gblɔ nɛ be: “Manɔ kpli wò, eye àsi Midiantɔwo abe ame ɖekae wonye ene.”
ENGLISH: 16 And Jehovah said to him “Because I will be with you, and you shall strike Midian down like one man.”

EWE: 17 Eye wògblɔ nɛ be: “Ne ève nunye la, ekema ɖe dzesi aɖe fiam, ne manya be wòe le nu ƒom kplim.
ENGLISH: 17 And he said to him “If I have found favor in your eyes, let me have a token that it is you talking with me:

EWE: 18 Meɖe kuku, mègadzo le afi sia o, va se ɖe esime matrɔ ava gbɔwò atsɔ nye nunana aɖo akɔwòme.”
ENGLISH: 18 do not stir from here till I come to you bringing out my offering and lay it before you”; and he said “I will stay till you come back.”

EWE: Eɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Manɔ afi sia va se ɖe esime nàtrɔ agbɔ.” 19 Eye Gideon yi ɖawu gbɔ̃vi ɖeka, eye wòtsɔ wɔ efa ɖeka mè amɔwɔ maʋamaʋã boloe. Efɔ lã la de kusi me, eye wòku detsi la ɖe nuɖaze me tsɔ yi nɛ le ati gã la te, eye wòtsɔe ɖo ekɔme.
ENGLISH: 19 And Gideon went in and killed and cooked a kid and made a bushel of meal into matzoth; the flesh he put in his basket and the broth in his pot, and brought it out to him under the terebinth-tree and presented it.

EWE: 20 Eye Mawu vavã la ƒe dɔla gblɔ nɛ be: “Tsɔ lã la kple amɔwɔ maʋamaʋã bolo la da ɖe kpe gã ma dzi, eye nàtrɔ detsia kɔ ɖi.”
ENGLISH: 20 And the Angel of God said to him “Take the flesh and the matzoth and lay them on yonder rock, and pour out the broth”; and he did so.

EWE: Eye wòwɔe nenema. 21 Eye Yehowa ƒe dɔla tsɔ atikplɔ si le esi la ƒe nugbɔ tɔ lã la kple amɔwɔ maʋamaʋã boloa, eye dzo do tso agakpe la me fiã lã la kple amɔwɔ maʋamaʋã bolo la. Eye Yehowa ƒe dɔlaa bu vĩi le eŋkume.
ENGLISH: 21 And the Angel of Jehovah put out the end of the staff that he had in his hand and touched the flesh and the matzoth, and fire came up out of the stone and consumed the flesh and the matzoth, and the Angel of Jehovah passed away from his sight,

EWE: 22 Gideon kpɔe azɔ be Yehowa ƒe dɔlae.Enumake Gideon do ɣli be: “Aléle, Aƒetɔ Dziɖulagã Yehowa, elabena mekpɔ Yehowa ƒe dɔla ŋkume kple ŋkume!”
ENGLISH: 22 and Gideon saw that it was the Angel of Jehovah. And Gideon said “O, O, my lord Jehovah! I have seen the Angel of Jehovah face to face!”

EWE: 23 Ke Yehowa gblɔ nɛ be: “Ŋutifafa na wò. Mègavɔ̃ o; mèle kuku ge o.”
ENGLISH: 23 And Jehovah said to him “All is well for you: do not be afraid, you shall not die.”

EWE: 24 Eya ta Gideon ɖi vɔsamlekpui na Yehowa ɖe afi ma, eye woyɔa vɔsamlekpui la be Yehowa-Salom va se ɖe egbe sia. Egakpɔtɔ le Abi-Ezertɔwo ƒe Ofra.
ENGLISH: 24 And Gideon built an altar to Jehovah there, and called it “Jehovah All-well”; it exists to this day at Ghophrath-Abi-ha-ʽEzri.

EWE: 25 Le zã ma me la, Yehowa gblɔ nɛ be: “Lé fofowò ƒe nyitsui ɖeka, nàlé nyitsui evelia si xɔ ƒe adre, nàgbã Baal ƒe vɔsamlekpui si nye fofowò tɔ la, eye nàlã Asera-ti si le exa la ƒu anyi.
ENGLISH: 25 And that night Jehovah said to him “Take your father’s wall-steer; and a steer, the second, of seven years, and demolish your father’s altar of the Baal and cut down the asherah over it,

EWE: 26 Eye nàɖo kpewo atsɔ aɖi vɔsamlekpui na Yehowa wò Mawu la ɖe mɔ́ sesẽ sia dzi, eye nàtsɔ nyitsui evelia asa numevɔ ɖe Asera-ti si nàlã la ƒe nakeawo dzi.”
ENGLISH: 26 and build an altar of your God Jehovah on top of this citadel-rock with the coursed stones, and take the second steer and offer a burnt-offering with the wood of the asherah you cut down.”

EWE: 27 Ale Gideon ɖe eƒe subɔviwo dometɔ ewo, eye wòyi ɖawɔe abe ale si tututu Yehowa gblɔ nɛ ene. Ke evɔ̃ fofoa ƒemetɔwo kple dua me ŋutsuwo ale gbegbe be, mewɔe le ŋkeke me o, ke boŋ eyi ɖawɔe le zã me.
ENGLISH: 27 And Gideon took ten men, slaves of his, and did as Jehovah had told him; and, as he was too much afraid of his family and the men of the city to do it by day, he did it by night.

EWE: 28 Esi dua me ŋutsuwo fɔ ŋdi kanya la, wokpɔ be wogbã Baal ƒe vɔsamlekpui la ƒu anyi, wolã Asera-ti si le exa la hã, eye wotsɔ nyitsui evelia sa vɔe ɖe vɔsamlekpui si woɖi la dzi.
ENGLISH: 28 And in the morning the men of the city found that the altar of the Baal had been pulled down and the asherah over it cut down, and the second steer offered on the newly-built altar;

EWE: 29 Wobia wo nɔewo be: “Ame kae wɔ nu sia?”
ENGLISH: 29 and they said to each other “Who did this thing?” and they inquire and investigated, and it was said “Joash’s son Gideon did this thing.”

EWE: Esi woku nyaa me la, wogblɔ be: “Gideon, Yoas vi lae wɔ nu sia.” 30 Eya ta dua me ŋutsuwo gblɔ na Yoas be: “Kplɔ viwò la do goe ne míawui, elabena egbã Baal ƒe vɔsamlekpui la ƒu anyi, eye wòlã Asera-ti si le exa la hã.”
ENGLISH: 30 And the men of the city said to Joash “Bring your son out to die, because he has pulled down the altar of the Baal and cut down the asherah over it.”

EWE: 31 Eye Yoas gblɔ na ame siwo katã tsɔ nyaa tui la be: “Miawoe aʋli Baal taa? Miawoe axɔ nɛa? Ame sia ame si aʋli eta la, woawui ŋdi sia.
ENGLISH: 31 But Joash said to all who stood around him “Are you to contend for the Baal or succor him? let the one who contend for him be put to death.

EWE: Ne mawue wònye la, ekema neʋli eɖokui ta, le esi ame aɖe gbã eƒe vɔsamlekpui ƒu anyi ta.”
ENGLISH: Till morning! if he is a god, let him contend for himself because he pulled down his altar.”

EWE: 32 Eye wòna ŋkɔ Gideon gbe ma gbe be Yerubaal hegblɔ be: “Baal neʋli eɖokui ta, le esi ame aɖe gbã eƒe vɔsamlekpui ƒu anyi ta.”
ENGLISH: 32 And on that day he named him Jerubbaal, meaning “The Baal contend with him, because he pulled down his altar.”

EWE: 33 Eye Midiantɔwo, Amalektɔwo kple Ɣedzeƒetɔwo katã ƒo woƒe aʋawɔlawo nu ƒu; eye wotso tɔ la heva ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Yezreel Bali la me.
ENGLISH: 33 And all the Midianites and the ʽAmalekites and the Eastern Beduins had come together and crossed and encamped in the vale of Jezreʽel;

EWE: 34 Yehowa ƒe gbɔgbɔ va Gideon dzi, eye wòku kpẽ, eye Abi-Ezer viwo ƒo ƒu dze eyome.
ENGLISH: 34 and the spirit of Jehovah took possession of Gideon, and he blew the ram-horn, and the Abiʽezrites came out in arms behind him;

EWE: 35 Edɔ amewo ɖo ɖe Manase blibo la katã, eye woawo hã ƒo ƒu dze eyome. Eye wòdɔ amewo ɖo ɖe Aser, Zebulon kple Naftali hã, eye wova do goe.
ENGLISH: 35 and he sent messengers throughout Manasseh, and the Manassites too came out in arms behind him; and he sent messengers through Asher and Zebulun and Naphtali, and they came up to meet them.

EWE: 36 Eye Gideon gblɔ na Mawu vavã la be: “Ne dzinye to ge nàla aɖe Israel, abe ale si nèdo ŋugbee ene la,
ENGLISH: 36 And Gideon said to God “If you do mean to save Israel by my hands, as you promised,

EWE: 37 ke makeke alẽgbalẽ ɖe nukuƒoƒe la. Ne zãmu dza ɖe alẽgbalẽa ɖeɖe ko dzi, gake anyigba si ƒo xlãe godoo la katã le ƒuƒuie la, ekema madze sii be dzinye to ge nàla aɖe Israel, abe ale si nèdo ŋugbee ene.”
ENGLISH: 37 here I am placing a fleece of wool on the threshing-floor: if there is dew on the fleece alone, and all over the ground it is dry, I shall know that you will save Israel by my hands as you promised.”

EWE: 38 Eva eme nenema tututu. Esi wòfɔ ŋdi kanya hefiã alẽgbalẽa la, zãmu si wòfiã le alẽgbalẽa me la yɔ nuɖugba gã aɖe.
ENGLISH: 38 And it was so: he squeezed the fleece the first thing in the morning and ran out dew out of the fleece, a bowlful of water.

EWE: 39 Ke Gideon gblɔ na Mawu vavã la be: “Mègana wò dɔmedzoe nabi ɖe ŋunye o, ke boŋ ɖe mɔ nam magaƒo nu zi ɖeka pɛ ko.
ENGLISH: 39 And Gideon said to God “Do not be angry with me, and let me speak just once more.

EWE: Meɖe kuku, na magatsɔ alẽgbalẽ la awɔ dodokpɔ ɖeka pɛ ko. Meɖe kuku, na alẽgbalẽa ɖeɖe ko nanɔ ƒuƒuie, ke zãmu naƒo anyigba la katã.”
ENGLISH: Let me try with the fleece only once more: have it dry on the fleece alone, and all over the ground let there be dew.”

EWE: 40 Eye nenemae Mawu wɔ le zã ma me; alẽgbalẽ la ɖeɖe nɔ ƒuƒuie, ke zãmu ƒo anyigba la katã.
ENGLISH: 40 And God did so that night, and it was dry on the fleece alone, and all over the ground there was dew.

EWE: Ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo
ENGLISH: Judges

EWE: 7 Eye Yerubaal, si nye Gideon, kple ame siwo katã le eŋu la fɔ ŋdi kanya va ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Harod-tsidzɔƒe la gbɔ, eye Midiantɔwo ƒe asaɖa la le woƒe dziehe le More togbɛ la gbɔ le bali la me.
ENGLISH: 7 And Jerubbaal (that is, Gideon) and all the people who were with him went in the morning and encamped by Panic Spring; and he had the Midianites’ camp on the north, from Moreh Hill, in the vale.

EWE: 2 Yehowa gblɔ na Gideon be: “Ame siwo le ŋuwò la sɔ gbɔ akpa, be matsɔ Midiantɔwo ade asi na wo. Ne menye nenema o la, Israel ava ƒu asi akɔ ɖe ŋunye agblɔ be: ‘Nye ŋutɔ nye asie xɔ nam.’
ENGLISH: 2 And Jehovah said to Gideon “There are too many of the people that are with you for me to give the Midianites into their hands, for fear Israel should brag against me ‘My own hands gave me the victory’;

EWE: 3 Eya ta meɖe kuku, gblɔ na ameawo be: ‘Ame si ke le vɔvɔ̃m eye dzi mele eƒo o la negbugbɔ yi aƒe.’”
ENGLISH: 3 now proclaim to the people ‘Whoever is afraid and panicky, let him flit back from the highland of Gilead.’”

EWE: Ale Gideon do wo kpɔ. Ame akpe blaeve vɔ eve trɔ dzo, eye ame akpe ewo susɔ.
ENGLISH: And twenty-two thousand of the people went back, and ten thousand were left.

EWE: 4 Ke Yehowa gagblɔ na Gideon be: “Ameawo gasɔ gbɔ akpa kokoko. Kplɔ wo yi tɔ la to, ne mado wo kpɔ na wò le afi ma.
ENGLISH: 4 And Jehovah said to Gideon “There are still too many of the people: have them go down to the water and I will weed them out for you there; and what I tell you shall go with you, shall, and all that I tell you shall not go with you, shall not.”

EWE: Ne megblɔ na wò be, ‘Ame sia ayi kpli wò’ la, eya neyi kpli wò, gake ne megblɔ na wò be, ‘Ame sia mayi kpli wò o’ la, eya megayi o.” 5 Ale wòkplɔ ameawo yi tɔ la to.
ENGLISH: 5 And he had the people go down to the water; and Jehovah said to Gideon “Everyone that laps from the water with his tongue, as a dog does, you shall set apart, and everyone that kneels down to drink.”

EWE: Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Gideon be: “Ðe ame siwo katã ɖuɖɔ tsi la abe avu ene kple ame siwo katã dze klo kpe nu ɖe eme noe la ɖe vovo.” 6 Ke ame siwo ku tsia kple asi no la le ame alafa etɔ̃.
ENGLISH: 6 And the number that lapped with hand to mouth was three hundred men; and all the rest of the people knelt down to drink water.

EWE: Ame mamlɛawo katã dze klo kpe nu ɖe tsia me noe. 7 Yehowa gblɔ na Gideon be: “Matsɔ ame alafa etɔ̃ siwo ku tsia kple asi no la axɔ na mi, eye matsɔ Midiantɔwo ade asi na mi. Ke na ame mamlɛawo katã natrɔ ayi aƒe.”
ENGLISH: 7 And Jehovah said to Gideon “By the three hundred men that lapped I will give you the victory, and give the Midianites into your hands; and let all the people go home to their places.”

EWE: 8 Eya ta woxɔ mɔdzinuɖuɖuwo kple kpẽawo le ameawo si, eye wòɖo Israel ŋutsu mamlɛawo ɖe aƒe, ame alafa etɔ̃awo koe wòkpɔtɔ ɖi.
ENGLISH: 8 And they took the people’s provisions in their hands, and their ram-horns; and he sent home all the men of Israel, and kept the three hundred men.

EWE: Ke Midiantɔwo ƒe asaɖaa le balia me le anyime ɖaa.
ENGLISH: And he had the Midianites’ camp under him in the vale.

EWE: 9 Le zã ma me la, Yehowa gblɔ nɛ be: “Tso nàdze asaɖa la dzi, elabena metsɔe de asi na wò.
ENGLISH: 9 And that night Jehovah said to him “Get up and descend on the camp, because I have given it into your hands.

EWE: 10 Ke ne èle vɔvɔ̃m na wo dzi dzedze la, kplɔ wò dɔla Pura miayi asaɖa la me.
ENGLISH: 10 And if you are afraid to descend on it, you and your man Purah go down to the camp

EWE: 11 Ðo to nya si gblɔm wole, eye dzi aɖo ƒowò nàdze asaɖa la dzi.”
ENGLISH: 11 and hear what they say, and afterward you will have courage and will descend on the camp.”

EWE: Eya ta eya kple eƒe dɔla Pura ɖi yi aʋakɔ siwo ho va la ƒe asaɖa nu.
ENGLISH: And he and his man Purah went down to the edge of the men under arms in the camp.

EWE: 12 Ke Midiantɔwo, Amalektɔwo kple Ɣedzeƒetɔwo katã xɔ bali la me kpaŋkpaŋkpaŋ abe ʋetsuviwo ene; eye woƒe kposɔwo mele xexlẽme o, wosɔ gbɔ abe ƒutake ene.
ENGLISH: 12 And the Midianites and the ʽAmalekites and all the Eastern Beduins had dropped into the vale in numbers like a swarm of locusts: there was no counting their camels, as numerous as the grains of sand on the seashore.

EWE: 13 Esi Gideon va la, ŋutsu aɖe le drɔ̃e lĩm na ehavi be: “Drɔ̃e si meku lae nye esi. Ƒobolo nogoe aɖe mli togotogoe va Midiantɔwo ƒe asaɖa la me. Eva ɖo agbadɔ aɖe gbɔ helɔe sesĩe ale gbegbe be wòmu.
ENGLISH: 13 And when Gideon came, there was a man telling his comrade a dream; and he said “Here I have had a dream that a barley-bread bannock was tumbling over and over in the Midianite camp, and it came to the tent and knocked it upside down.”

EWE: Ɛ̃, elɔ agbadɔa wòtrɔ ta tu hemu gbloo.” 14 Eye ehavia gblɔ be: “Menye nu bubu aɖekee o, ke boŋ Israeltɔ Gideon, Yoas vi la, ƒe yie.
ENGLISH: 14 And his comrade answered “That can be nothing else than the sword of Gideon the son of Joash, the men of Israel; God has given into their hands the Midianites and all the camp.”

EWE: Mawu tsɔ Midiantɔwo kple woƒe asaɖa blibo la katã de asi nɛ.” 15 Esi Gideon nya se drɔ̃e la kple egɔmeɖeɖe ko la, ebɔbɔ de ta agu. Emegbe egbugbɔ va Israel ƒe asaɖa la me gblɔ be: “Mitso, elabena Yehowa tsɔ Midiantɔwo ƒe asaɖa la de asi na mi.”
ENGLISH: 15 And when Gideon heard the account of the dream, and its explanation, he did reverence, and went back to the camp of Israel and said “Get up: Jehovah has given the Midianite camp into your hands.”

EWE: 16 Ema ŋutsu alafa etɔ̃ la ɖe aʋalɔgo etɔ̃ me, eye wòtsɔ kpẽ kple ze ƒuƒlu siwo me akakatiwo le la de wo katã si.
ENGLISH: 16 And he divided the three hundred men into three columns, and gave them all ram-horns to carry, and empty jars, and torches inside the jars;

EWE: 17 Eye wògblɔ na wo be: “Minɔ kpɔyem, eye miwɔ nu si tututu mawɔ. Ne meva ɖo woƒe asaɖaa gbɔ la, miwɔ abe ale si tututu mewɔ ene.
ENGLISH: 17 and he said to them “Take your cue from me, and do the same: when I get to the edge of the camp, do just as I do:

EWE: 18 Ne meku kpẽa, eye ame siwo katã le ŋunye hã kui la, miawo hã miku kpẽawo le asaɖa la ŋu godoo, eye miado ɣli be: ‘Yehowa tɔe, Gideon tɔe!’”
ENGLISH: 18 I and all who are with me will blow the ram-horn, and you shall blow the horns too all around the camp, and say ‘For Jehovah and for Gideon!’”

EWE: 19 Gideon kple ame alafa ɖeka siwo le eŋu la va asaɖa la nu le zãdomeŋudzɔɣi ƒe gɔmedzedze, esi woɖɔli dzɔlawo teti ko.
ENGLISH: 19 And Gideon, and a hundred men who were with him, arrived at the edge of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch; the sentries had just been set; and they blew the ram-horns and smashed the jars they carried.

EWE: Woku kpẽawo, eye wogbã ze siwo le wo si la. 20 Eye aʋalɔgo etɔ̃awo ku kpẽawo hegbã zeawo. Wolé akakatiawo ɖe mia, eye wolé kpẽawo ɖe ɖusi, eye wodo ɣli be: “Yehowa kple Gideon ƒe yie!”
ENGLISH: 20 And the three columns blew the ram-horns and broke the jars, and held the torches in their left hands and in their right hands the ram-horns to blow with, and cried “Charge for Jehovah and for Gideon!”

EWE: 21 Ɣemaɣi katã la, wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe tɔ ɖe eteƒe le asaɖa la ŋu godoo, eye aʋakɔ blibo la katã de afɔ du me nɔ ɣli dom nɔ sisim.
ENGLISH: 21 And they stood still where they were around the camp; and all the camp went to running and shouting to arms and taking flight,

EWE: 22 Ame alafa etɔ̃awo le kpẽawo kum, eye Yehowa na wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe trɔ eƒe yi ɖe nɔvia ŋu le asaɖa blibo la katã me; eye aʋakɔ la si va se ɖe Bet-Sita, ɖo ta Zerera va do ɖe keke Abel-Mehola ƒe golɔgoewo ke le Tabat gbɔ.
ENGLISH: 22 and the three hundred ram-horns blew, and Jehovah set each one’s sword against the next man all through the camp; and the camp fled to Beth-hash-Shittah, toward Seredah, to the bluff of Abel-Meholah by Tabbath.

EWE: 23 Eye woyɔ Israel ŋutsuwo tso Naftali, Aser kple Manase blibo la va ƒo ƒu, eye wonya Midiantɔwo ɖe nu.
ENGLISH: 23 And the men of Israel came out in arms, out of Naphtali and out of Asher and out of all Manasseh, and pursued the Midianites.

EWE: 24 Gideon dɔ ame ɖo ɖe Efrayim tonuto blibo la katã me gblɔ be: “Miyi ɖadze Midiantɔwo dzi, eye miɖaxe mɔ le tɔtsoƒewo va se ɖe keke Bet-Bara kple Yordan nu ke.”
ENGLISH: 24 And Gideon sent messengers through all the highland of Ephraim to say “Come down to head off the Midianites: seize the water against them as far as Beth-Barah, and the Jordan”; and all the men of Ephraim came out in arms and seized the water as far as Beth-Barah, and the Jordan.

EWE: Ale woyɔ Efrayim ŋutsuwo katã ƒo ƒu, eye woyi ɖaxe mɔ le tɔtsoƒeawo va se ɖe keke Bet-Bara kple Yordan nu ke. 25 Wolé Midiantɔwo ƒe amegã eve siwo nye Oreb kple Zeeb hã; wowu Oreb le Oreb-gakpe la dzi, eye wowu Zeeb le Zeeb ƒe wainfiãƒe.
ENGLISH: 25 And they took the two chiefs of the Midianites, Raven and Wolf, and killed Raven at Raven Rock and Wolf at Wolf Winepress, and followed up the Midianites; and they brought the heads of Raven and Wolf to Gideon on the other side of the Jordan,

EWE: Ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo
ENGLISH: Judges

EWE: 8 Eye Efrayim ŋutsuwo biae be: “Nu kae nye esia nèwɔ ɖe mía ŋu? Nu ka tae mèyɔ mí esi nèyina aʋa kpe ge kple Midiantɔwo o?”
ENGLISH: 8 and the men of Ephraim said to him “What is this thing you have done to us, not calling us when you went to attack the Midianites?” and upbraided him sharply.

EWE: Eye wohe nya ɖe eŋu vevie. 2 Gake egblɔ na wo be: “Nu kae mewɔ fifia si de mia tɔ nu? Ðe waintsetse siwo tsi anyi Efrayim fɔ la menyo wu Abi-Ezer ƒe wainxaxa oa?
ENGLISH: 2 But he said to them “What have I done now that was like you? was not Ephraim’s aftermath better than Abiezer’s crop?

EWE: 3 Mia si mee Mawu tsɔ Midian-megã siwo nye Oreb kple Zeeb de, eye nu kae mewɔ si de mia tɔ nu?”
ENGLISH: 3 It was into your hands that God gave the chiefs of the Midianites, Raven and Wolf; and what was I able to do that was like you?”

EWE: Esi wògblɔ nya sia la, woƒe dzi fa.
ENGLISH: Then their ill humor toward him quieted down at his saying this.

EWE: 4 Eye Gideon va Yordan nu eye wòtso tɔa. Ðeɖi te eya kple ŋutsu alafa etɔ̃ siwo le eŋu la ŋu, gake wogati woƒe futɔawo yome kokoko.
ENGLISH: 4 And Gideon came to the Jordan and crossed it, he and the three hundred men that were with him, faint and pressing on the pursuit;

EWE: 5 Eya ta egblɔ na Sukottɔwo be: “Meɖe kuku, mina nuɖuɖu ame siwo le yonyeme la, elabena ɖeɖi te wo ŋu, evɔ mele Midian-fia siwo nye Zeba kple Zalmuna yome tim.”
ENGLISH: 5 and he said to the men of Succoth “Please give some biscuits to the people at my back; for they are faint, and I am in pursuit of Zebah and Salmunnaʽ, the kings of the Midianites.”

EWE: 6 Ke Sukot-megãwo gblɔ be: “Ðe wò asi su Zeba kple Zalmuna dzi xoxo hafi míana nuɖuɖu wò aʋakɔ la?”
ENGLISH: 6 And the captains of Succoth said “Are the hands of Zebah and Salmunnaʽ in your hands already, that we should give your levy bread?”

EWE: 7 Eye Gideon ɖo eŋu be: “Le nya ma ɖeɖe si miegblɔ ta, ne Yehowa tsɔ Zeba kple Zalmuna de asi nam la, matsɔ aŋɔka kple ŋù siwo le gbedadaƒo la aƒo mi vevie.”
ENGLISH: 7 And Gideon said “So when Jehovah gives Zebah and Salmunnaʽ into my hands I will thresh your flesh along with wilderness thorns and thistle-heads.”

EWE: 8 Edzo le afi ma yi Penuel, eye wògabia nuɖuɖu woawo hã, ke Penueltɔwo ɖo eŋu nɛ abe Sukottɔwo ke ene.
ENGLISH: 8 And he went up from there to Penuel and said the like to them, and the men of Penuel answered him as the men of Succoth had;

EWE: 9 Eya ta egblɔ na Penueltɔwo hã be: “Ne metrɔ gbɔ le ŋutifafa me la, magbã mɔ́ sesẽ sia aƒu anyi.”
ENGLISH: 9 and he said to the men of Penuel too “When I come back safe I will pull down this tower.”

EWE: 10 Ke Zeba kple Zalmuna kpakple woƒe aʋawɔla siwo anɔ abe ame akpe wuiatɔ̃ ene la le Karkor. Ame siawo koe susɔ le Ɣedzeƒetɔwo ƒe aʋakɔ blibo la me, elabe ame akpe alafa ɖeka blaeve siwo ta yi la tsi aʋa.
ENGLISH: 10 And Zebah and Salmunnaʽ were at Karkor and their camps with them, about fifteen thousand men, all that were left of the whole camp of the Eastern Beduins; and those who had fallen were a hundred and twenty thousand fighting men.

EWE: 11 Gideon yi ɖato agbadɔmenɔlawo ƒe mɔ le Noba kple Yogbeha ƒe ɣedzeƒe, eye wòva dze aʋakɔ la dzi esime woɖe ŋu ɖi.
ENGLISH: 11 And Gideon went up to the Tent-Dwellers’ Road east of Nobah, and Jogbehah, and attacked the camp while it was off its guard;

EWE: 12 Esi Zeba kple Zalmuna si la, eti wo yome eye wòva lé Zeba kple Zalmuna siwo nye Midian-fia eveawo, eye zi tɔ le asaɖa blibo la me ale gbegbe.
ENGLISH: 12 and Zebah and Salmunnaʽ took flight, and he pursued them. And he took the two kings of the Midianites, Zebah and Salmunnaʽ, and put all the camp to rout.

EWE: 13 Emegbe Gideon, Yoas vi, trɔ tso aʋa la gbɔna, eye wòto Heres-todzimɔ.
ENGLISH: 13 And Gideon the son of Joash came back from battle higher than the sun,

EWE: 14 Elé ɖekakpui aɖe si tso Sukot la le mɔa dzi, eye wòbia gbee. Eye ɖekakpuia ŋlɔ Sukot-megãwo kple eƒe ametsitsiwo ŋkɔwo nɛ; wole ŋutsu blaadre vɔ adre.
ENGLISH: 14 and caught a young man who belonged to Succoth and questioned him, and he wrote down for him the captains and elders of Succoth, seventy-seven men;

EWE: 15 Eye wòyi Sukottɔwo gbɔ hegblɔ be: “Zeba kple Zalmuna, siwo ta mieɖe alɔme le ŋunye le gblɔ be, ‘Ðe wò asi su Zeba kple Zalmuna dzi xoxo hafi míana nuɖuɖu wò ame siwo ŋu ɖeɖi tea?’ mahã la woe nye esi.” 16 Eye wòlé dumemetsitsiawo, eye wòtsɔ aŋɔka kple ŋù siwo wotsɔ tso gbedadaƒo la fia nunya Sukot ŋutsuawo.
ENGLISH: 15 and Gideon came to the men of Succoth and said “Here are Zebah and Salmunnaʽ, about whom you taunted me with the question ‘Are the hands of Zebah and Salmunnaʽ in your hands already, that we should give your fainting men bread?’” 16 and he took the elders of the city and wilderness thorns and thistle-heads and gave the men of Succoth a lesson with them.

EWE: 17 Egbã Penuel mɔ́ la ƒu anyi, eye wòwu dua me ŋutsuwo.
ENGLISH: 17 And he pulled down the tower of Penuel and killed the men of the city.

EWE: 18 Eye wòbia Zeba kple Zalmuna be: “Ŋutsu kawo ƒomevie miewu le Tabor?”
ENGLISH: 18 And he said to Zebah and Salmunnaʽ “What were the men you killed at Tabor like?” and they said “Just like you; either one of them looked like a king’s son.”

EWE: Woɖo eŋu be: “Wole abe wò ene, wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe ɖi fia vi.” 19 Eye wògblɔ be: “Nɔvinyeŋutsuwoe, danye ƒe viwoe.
ENGLISH: 19 And he said “They were my brothers, my mother’s sons; by Jehovah, if you had spared their lives I would not have killed you”;

EWE: 20 Eye wògblɔ na eƒe ŋgɔgbevi Yeter be: “Tso nàwu wo.”
ENGLISH: 20 and he said to his oldest son Jether “Stand up and kill them.”

EWE: Ke ɖekakpui la meɖe eƒe yi o, ele vɔvɔ̃m, elabena ɖekakpui dzaa ko wònye.
ENGLISH: But the boy did not draw his sword; for he was afraid, because he was still a boy.

EWE: 21 Eya ta Zeba kple Zalmuna gblɔ be: “Wò ŋutɔ tso nàwu mí, elabena ŋutsu ƒe ŋusẽ mee wokpɔa eƒe ŋutsunyenye le.”
ENGLISH: 21 And Zebah and Salmunnaʽ said “Stand up yourself and cut us down, because a man has a man’s might”; and Gideon stood up and killed Zebah and Salinunnaʽ and took the crescents on their camels’ necks.

EWE: Ale Gideon tso, eye wòwu Zeba kple Zalmuna, eye wòɖe atsyɔ̃ɖonu gobɛ siwo le kɔ na woƒe kposɔwo.
ENGLISH: 22 And the men of Israel said to Gideon “Rule over us, you and your son and your son’s son, because you have saved us out of the hands of the Midianites”;

EWE: 22 Emegbe Israel ŋutsuwo gblɔ na Gideon be: “Ðu fia ɖe mía dzi, wò ŋutɔ kple viwòŋutsu kpakple wò tɔgbuiyɔvi siaa, elabena wòe ɖe mí tso Midian si me.” 23 Ke Gideon gblɔ na wo be: “Nyemaɖu fia ɖe mia dzi o, eye vinye hã maɖu fia ɖe mia dzi o. Yehowae aɖu fia ɖe mia dzi.”
ENGLISH: 23 and Gideon said to them “I will not rule over you, neither shall my son; Jehovah shall rule over you.”

EWE: 24 Eye Gideon gagblɔ na wo be: “Mabia nu ɖeka mi: mia dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe neɖe ŋɔtigɛ ɖeka le eƒe aboyonuwo me nam.”
ENGLISH: 24 But Gideon said to them “I will make a request of you: give me the earrings in your booty.”

EWE: (Sikaŋɔtigɛwo nɔ ame siwo wosi la si, elabena Ismaeltɔwoe wonye.)
ENGLISH: (For they had golden earrings, because they were Ishmaelites.)

EWE: 25 Woɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Míana wò faa.” Ale wokeke avɔ aɖe ɖi, eye wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe ɖe ŋɔtigɛ ɖeka le eƒe aboyonuawo me da ɖe edzi.
ENGLISH: 25 And they said “That we will”; and he spread out his cloak and they threw in the earrings in their booty;

EWE: 26 Sikaŋɔtigɛ si wòbia la ƒe kpekpeme va le sekel akpe ɖeka alafa adre, womebu atsyɔ̃ɖonu gobɛawo, togɛwo, Midian-fiawo ƒe alẽfuwu dzĩwo kple woƒe kposɔwo ƒe kɔgawo ɖe eme o.
ENGLISH: 26 and the weight of the golden earrings that he got for his asking was nine hundred ounce of gold, besides the crescents and pendants and purple garments that were on the kings of the Midianites, and besides the necklaces on their camels’ necks.

EWE: 27 Gideon tsɔe wɔ kɔmewu, eye wòtsɔe da ɖe wo dedu Ofra me be woakpɔ; eye Israel blibo yia afi ma ɖasubɔnɛ heto esia dzi wɔ gbɔgbɔmehasi, eye wòzu mɔ̃ ɖe Gideon kple eƒe aƒe la.
ENGLISH: 27 And Gideon made it into an ephod and placed it in his city Ghophrah, and all Israel prostituted themselves to go after it there, and it became a snare to Gideon and his family.

EWE: 28 Ale wobɔbɔ Midiantɔwo ɖe anyi le Israel ŋkume, eye womegatso ɖe wo ŋu kpɔ o; eye anyigba la kpɔ gbɔdzɔe ƒe blaene sɔŋ le Gideon ŋɔli.
ENGLISH: 28 But the Midianites were humbled before the sons of Israel, and no longer held their heads high. And the country was quiet forty years in Gideon’s days.

EWE: 29 Eye Yerubaal, Yoas vi, trɔ yi eƒe me, eye wònɔ afi ma.
ENGLISH: 29 And Jerubbaal the son of Joash went to his home and lived there.

EWE: 30 Wodzi ŋutsuvi blaadre na Gideon, elabena srɔ̃ geɖe nɔ esi.
ENGLISH: 30 And Gideon had seventy sons, the issue of his body; for he had many wives.

EWE: 31 Eƒe ahiãvi si le Sekem hã dzi ŋutsuvi nɛ, eye wòna ŋkɔe be Abimelek.
ENGLISH: 31 And his concubine at Shekem also bore him a son, whom he named Abimelec.

EWE: 32 Eye Gideon, Yoas vi la ku esime wònɔ agbe tsi nyuie, eye woɖii ɖe fofoa Yoas ƒe yɔdo me le Abi-Ezertɔwo ƒe Ofra.
ENGLISH: 32 And Gideon the son of Joash died at a good old age, and was buried in the tomb of his father Joash at Ghophrath-Abi-ha-ʽEzri.

EWE: 33 Esi Gideon nya ku ko la, Israel-viwo gade asi Baalwo subɔsubɔ me ake heto esia me wɔ gbɔgbɔmehasi, eye wotsɔ Baal-Berit wɔ woƒe mawui.
ENGLISH: 33 And when Gideon was dead the sons of Israel went back to prostituting themselves to follow the Baals and made Baal-berith their god.

EWE: 34 Israel-viwo meɖo ŋku Yehowa woƒe Mawu, ame si ɖe wo tso woƒe futɔ siwo ƒo xlã wo la katã si me la dzi o;
ENGLISH: 34 And the sons of Israel did not remember their God Jehovah who had delivered them out of the hands of all their enemies on all sides,

EWE: 35 eye womeve Yerubaal, ame si nye Gideon, ƒe aƒe la nu le nyui siwo katã wòwɔ na Israel la ta o.
ENGLISH: 35 did not befriend the family of Jerubbaal Gideon in accordance with all the good he had done to Israel.

EWE: Ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo
ENGLISH: Judges

EWE: 9 Le ɣeyiɣi aɖe megbe la, Abimelek, Yerubaal vi, yi Sekem le nyruiawo gbɔ, eye wògblɔ na wo kple tɔgbuia ƒe ƒome blibo la be:
ENGLISH: 9 And Abimelec the son of Jerubbaal went to his mother’s brothers in Shekem and talked to them and to all the clan of his mother’s family, telling them

EWE: 2 “Meɖe kuku, mibia Sekem kplɔlawo katã be: ‘Kae nyo na mi wu, be Yerubaal viŋutsu blaadreawo katã naɖu fia ɖe mia dzi loo alo be ŋutsu ɖeka ko naɖu fia ɖe mia dzi? Eye miɖo ŋku edzi be nye la miawo ŋutɔ miaƒe ƒu kple ŋutilãe menye.’”
ENGLISH: 2 “Say publicly to the citizens of Shekem ‘Which is better for you, to have seventy men rule over you, the whole company of Jerubbaal’s sons, or to have one man rule over you? and remember that I am your own flesh and blood.’”

EWE: 3 Eya ta nyruiawo gblɔ nya siawo katã na Sekem kplɔlawo ɖe enu, ale woƒe dzi trɔ ɖe Abimelek ŋu be yewoadze eyome, elabena wogblɔ be: “Míawo ŋutɔwo mía nɔvie.”
ENGLISH: 3 And his mother’s brothers said all these things to the citizens of Shekem on his behalf, and they were disposed to second Abimelec, because they said “He is our brother”;

EWE: 4 Eya ta woɖe klosalo blaadre tso Baal-Berit ƒe trɔ̃xɔ me nɛ, eye Abimelek tsɔe di kuviatɔwo kple gbevuwo be woanɔ ye ŋu.
ENGLISH: 4 and they gave him seventy shekels of silver out of the temple of Baal-berith, with which he hired a set of reckless riffraff who went behind him.

EWE: 5 Emegbe eyi fofoa ƒe me le Ofra, eye wòwu nɔviaŋutsu siwo nye Yerubaal viŋutsu blaadreawo ɖe kpe ɖeka dzi. Yotam, si nye Yerubaal viŋutsu ɖevitɔ la koe tsi agbe, elabena eɣla eɖokui.
ENGLISH: 5 And he came to his father’s house at Ghophrah and killed his brothers, Jerubbaal’s sons, seventy men on one stone; but Jerubbaal’s youngest son Jotham survived, because he hid.

EWE: 6 Eye Sekem kplɔlawo kple Bet-Milo nɔlawo katã va ƒo ƒu, eye wotsɔ Abimelek ɖo fiae le ati gã la gbɔ le sɔti si le Sekem la gbɔ.
ENGLISH: 6 And all the citizens of Shekem and all the house of Millo came together and went and made Abimelec king by the Obelisk Oak at Shekem.

EWE: 7 Esi wogblɔe na Yotam la, enumake eyi ɖatɔ ɖe Gerizim To la tame, eye wòdo ɣli sesĩe gblɔ na wo be: “Miɖo tom, mi Sekem kplɔlawo, ne Mawu naɖo to mi:
ENGLISH: 7 And people told Jotham, and he went and stood on the top of Mount Gerizzim and raised his voice and cried out to them “Listen to me, citizens of Shekem, that God may listen to you.

EWE: 8 “Gbe ɖeka atiwo yi be yewoaɖo fia ɖe yewo nu. Eya ta wogblɔ na amiti be: ‘Ðu fia ɖe mía dzi.’
ENGLISH: 8 “The trees went to anoint a king over them, and said to the olive ‘Reign over us’;

EWE: 9 Ke amiti gblɔ na wo be: ‘Ðe maɖe asi le nye ami si wozãna tsɔ kafua Mawu kple amegbetɔwo la ŋu ayi aɖanɔ ya ƒom le ati bubuwo tamea?’
ENGLISH: 9 but the olive said to them ‘Leave off my fatness, I by whom they honor gods and men, and go to sway over the trees?’

EWE: 10 Eye atiawo gblɔ na gboti be: ‘Va ɖu fia ɖe mía dzi.’
ENGLISH: 10 And the trees said to the fig ‘Come, do you reign over us’;

EWE: 11 Ke gboti gblɔ na wo be: ‘Ðe magblẽ nye vivi kple nye kutsetse nyui la ɖi ayi aɖanɔ ya ƒom le ati bubuwo tamea?’
ENGLISH: 11 but the fig said to them ‘Leave off my sweetness and my good crops and go to sway over the trees?’

EWE: 12 Emegbe atiawo gblɔ na wainka be: ‘Va ɖu fia ɖe mía dzi.’
ENGLISH: 12 And the trees said to the grapevine ‘Come, do you reign over us’;

EWE: 13 Wainka ɖo eŋu na wo be: ‘Ðe magblẽ nye wain yeye, si doa dzidzɔ na Mawu kple amegbetɔwo la ɖi ayi aɖanɔ ya ƒom le atiwo tamea?’
ENGLISH: 13 but the grapevine said to them ‘Leave off my juice that gladdens gods and men, and go to sway over the trees?’

EWE: 14 Mlɔeba atiawo katã gblɔ na ŋuve be: ‘Va ɖu fia ɖe mía dzi.’
ENGLISH: 14 And all the trees said to the thornbush ‘Come, do you reign over us’;

EWE: 15 Ŋuve ɖo eŋu na atiawo be: ‘Ne nyateƒee wònye be miebe yewoasi ami nam ne maɖu fia ɖe mia dzi la, ekema miva be ɖe nye vɔvɔli te.
ENGLISH: 15 but the thornbush said to the trees ‘If you are anointing me king over you loyally, come take shelter in my shadow; but if not, let fire go out from the thornbush to devour the cedars of the Lebanon.’

EWE: Ke ne menye nenema o la, ekema dzo nedo tso ŋuve me wòafiã Lebanon ƒe sedertiwo.’ 16 “Azɔ nuteƒe kple nu dzeamee wònye miewɔ be mietsɔ Abimelek ɖo fiaea?
ENGLISH: 16 “And now, if you have acted loyally and honestly in making Abimelec king, and if you have done well by Jerubbaal and his family, and if you have done to him as he deserved,

EWE: Eye ɖe mieɖo eteƒe nɛ abe ale si wòdze nɛ enea? 17 Esi fofonye wɔ aʋa na mi la, etsɔ eƒe agbe de afɔku me heɖe mi tso Midiantɔwo si me.
ENGLISH: 17 when my father had fought for you and taken his life in his hand and delivered you out of the hands of the Midianites,

EWE: 18 Gake egbe la, mietso ɖe fofonye ƒe aƒe la ŋu, eye miewu viaŋutsu blaadre sɔŋ ɖe kpe ɖeka dzi. Eye mietsɔ Abimelek, eƒe kosi ƒe vi, ɖo fiae ɖe Sekem kplɔlawo nu le esi wònye mia nɔvi ta.
ENGLISH: 18 and you have stood up against my father’s family today and killed his sons, seventy men on one stone, and made his slave-girl’s son Abimelec king over the citizens of Shekem because he is your brother,

EWE: 19 Ɛ̃, ne nuteƒe kple nu dzeamee wònye miewɔ ɖe Yerubaal kple eƒe aƒea ŋu egbe la, ekema mikpɔ dzidzɔ ɖe Abimelek ŋu, eye eya hã nekpɔ dzidzɔ ɖe mia ŋu.
ENGLISH: 19 if you have done loyally and honestly by Jerubbaal and his family this day, have joy of Abimelec and may he have joy of you too;

EWE: 20 Ke ne menye nenemae o la, ekema dzo nedo tso Abimelek me ne wòafiã Sekem kplɔlawo kple Bet-Milo, eye dzo nedo tso Sekem kplɔlawo kple Bet-Milo me ne wòafiã Abimelek.”
ENGLISH: 20 but if not, let fire go out from Abimelec to devour the citizens of Shekem and the house of Millo, and let fire go out from the citizens of Shekem and the house of Millo to devour Abimelec.”

EWE: 21 Eye Yotam si yi Beer ɖanɔ afi ma le nɔvia Abimelek ta.
ENGLISH: 21 And Jotham made his escape and fled away, and went to Beer and lived there for fear of his brother Abimelec.

EWE: 22 Abimelek ɖu fia ɖe Israel dzi ƒe etɔ̃.
ENGLISH: 22 And Abimelec held dominion over Israel for three years.

EWE: 23 Eye Mawu na fuléle ɖo Abimelek kple Sekem kplɔlawo dome, eye wotrɔ Abimelek to eme.
ENGLISH: 23 And God sent an evil spirit between Abimelec and the citizens of Shekem, and the citizens of Shekem played Abimelec false,

EWE: 24 Esia dzɔ ale be woabia ŋuta si wosẽ le Yerubaal viŋutsu blaadreawo ŋu la ƒe hlɔ̃, ne woƒe ʋu nava wo nɔvi Abimelek dzi le wo wuwu ta, kple Sekem kplɔlawo dzi le esi wokpe ɖe eŋu wòwu nɔviawo ta.
ENGLISH: 24 that the outrage committed upon the seventy sons of Jerubbaal might come home, and their blood to lay on their brother Abimelec who had killed them and on the citizens of Shekem who had backed him in killing his brothers.

EWE: 25 Eya ta Sekem kplɔlawo ɖe amewo wode xa ɖe towo dzi ɖe eŋu, eye wodaa adzo ame sia ame si va toa wo gbɔ le mɔ ma dzi.
ENGLISH: 25 And the citizens of Shekem laid him ambushes on the mountaintops and robbed everybody who passed by them on the road; and Abimelec was told of it.

EWE: Eye wova gblɔe na Abimelek. 26 Eye Gaal, Ebed vi, kple nɔviawo va Sekem, eye Sekem kplɔlawo ɖo ŋu ɖe eŋu.
ENGLISH: 26 And Goal the son of ʽObed and his brothers came and moved into Shekem, and the citizens of Shekem relied on him.

EWE: 27 Woyi agblewo me ɖaxa woƒe waintsetsewo, wofiã wo tsɔ wɔ wain, eye woɖu azã, emegbe wova woƒe mawu la ƒe me, woɖu nu no nu, eye wodo ɖiŋu na Abimelek.
ENGLISH: 27 And they went out in the country and harvested their vineyards and trod the grapes; and they held a thanksgiving and went to the house of their god and ate and drank and cursed Abimelec,

EWE: 28 Emegbe Gaal, Ebed vi gblɔ be: “Ame kae nye Abimelek, eye ame kae nye Sekem, ne míasubɔe? Ðe menye eyae nye Yerubaal vi, eye Zebul nye eƒe dumegã oa? Misubɔ Hamor, Sekem fofo, ƒe amewo boŋ!
ENGLISH: 28 and Goal the son of ʽObed said “Who is Abimelec and who is Shekem, that we are to be subject to him? why, the son of Jerubbaal and his deputy Zebul were subject to the men of Hamor the father of Shekem, and how comes it we are to be subject to him?

EWE: Ke nu ka tae míasubɔe ɖo? 29 Ne ɖe dukɔ sia le nye kpɔkplɔ te la, anye ne meɖe Abimelek le zi dzi.” Eye wògblɔ na Abimelek be: “Dzi wò aʋakɔ ɖe edzi, eye nàdo va kpem.”
ENGLISH: 29 I wish I had this people in my hands, and I would put Abimelec down!” and to Abimelec he said “Raise your largest levy and come out!”

EWE: 30 Esi dumegã Zebul se Gaal, Ebed vi, ƒe nyawo la, dzi kui vevie.
ENGLISH: 30 And Zebul the captain of the city heard the words of Goal the son of ʽObed, and was angry;

EWE: 31 Eya ta edɔ amewo le adzame ɖo ɖe Abimelek gbɔ be woagblɔ nɛ be: “Kpɔ ɖa! Gaal, Ebed vi, kple nɔviawo va Sekem, eye wole to gblẽm na dua be woatso ɖe ŋuwò.
ENGLISH: 31 and he sent messengers to Abimelec at Bathram with the message “Here are Goal the son of ʽObed and his brothers coming into Shekem; and they are making the city hostile to you.

EWE: 32 Eya ta wò kple wò amewo miva le zã me, ne miade xa ɖe gbe me.
ENGLISH: 32 Now make a night start, you and the people you have with you, and lie in ambush in the field;

EWE: 33 Ne ŋu ke eye ɣe nya dze ko la, tso kaba nàdze dua dzi; eye ne Gaal kple eŋumewo ho ɖe ŋuwò la, wɔ nu sia nu si nàte ŋui ne nàɖu edzi.”
ENGLISH: 33 and the first thing in the morning, at sunrise, make a dash at the city. He and the people he has with him will be coming out to meet you, and you will do with him as you find opportunity.”

EWE: 34 Ale Abimelek kple ame siwo katã le eŋu la fɔ zã, eye wole aʋalɔgo ene me va de xa ɖe Sekem dua ŋu.
ENGLISH: 34 And Abimelec and all the people he had with him made a night start and lay in ambush against Shekem in four columns.

EWE: 35 Esi Gaal, Ebed vi, do va tɔ ɖe dua ƒe agbo nu la, Abimelek kple ame siwo le eŋu la tso le afi si wode xa ɖo.
ENGLISH: 35 And Goal the son of ʽObed went out and stood at the gate of the city; and Abimelec and the people he had with him started from their place of ambush,

EWE: 36 Esi Gaal kpɔ ameawo la, egblɔ na Zebul be: “Kpɔ ɖa! Amewo ɖi tso toawo dzi gbɔna.”
ENGLISH: 36 and Goal saw the people and said to Zebul “There is a body of people coming down from the mountaintops”; and Zebul said to him “The shadows of the mountains look to you like men.”

EWE: Ke Zebul gblɔ nɛ be: “Towo ƒe vɔvɔli kpɔm nèle be amewoe.” 37 Emegbe Gaal gagblɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa! Amewo ɖi tso anyigba la ƒe kɔkɔƒe gbɔna, eye aʋalɔgo ɖeka to Meonenim ƒe ati gã gbɔ mɔ gbɔna.”
ENGLISH: 37 And Goal spoke once more, and said “There are people coming down from by the Land’s Navel, and one column is coming from toward Fortune-Tellers’ Oak.”

EWE: 38 Eye Zebul ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Menye wòe ɖi nu me be: ‘Ame kae nye Abimelek, ne míasubɔe?’ hã oa?
ENGLISH: 38 And Zebul said to him “Where on earth is that mouth of yours, the way you used to say ‘Who is Abimelec that we are to be subject to him?’

EWE: Alo menye ame siawoe nègbe oa? Ho azɔ nàyi aɖakpe aʋa kpli wo.”
ENGLISH: Are not these the people you did not care for? now go out and fight them!”

EWE: 39 Eya ta Gaal dze Sekem kplɔlawo ŋgɔ woyi ɖawɔ aʋa kple Abimelek.
ENGLISH: 39 And Goal went out at the head of the citizens of Shekem and fought Abimelec;

EWE: 40 Abimelek nyae ɖe nu, eye Gaal si le enu, eye wowu ame geɖe kɔ ɖi va se ɖe keke dugbo la nu ke.
ENGLISH: 40 and Abimelec routed him, and he fled before him, and many fell killed, up to the gate.

EWE: 41 Eye Abimelek tsi Aruma, ke Zebul nya Gaal kple nɔviawo ɖa le Sekem.
ENGLISH: 41 And Abimelec remained at Arumah, and Zebul ejected Goal and his brothers from quartering in Shekem.

EWE: 42 Le ŋufɔke la, ameawo do go yi agble, eye ame aɖewo va gblɔe na Abimelek.
ENGLISH: 42 And the next day the people went out to the field, and Abimelec was told of it.

EWE: 43 Ale wòkplɔ eƒe ameawo, ema wo ɖe aʋalɔgo etɔ̃ me, eye wòde xa ɖe gbe me. Esi wòkpɔ be ameawo le dodom tso dua me la, edze wo dzi eye wòwu wo.
ENGLISH: 43 And he took the people and divided them into three columns and lay in ambush in the field; and he saw when the people came out of the city, and started up and struck them,

EWE: 44 Abimelek kple aʋalɔgo si le eŋu la wɔ kaba yi ɖatɔ ɖe dugbo la nu, eye aʋalɔgo eve dze ame siwo katã le agble la dzi, eye wowu wo.
ENGLISH: 44 Abimelec and the column he had with him making a dash and standing at the gate of the city, and the two columns dashing upon all who were in they field and striking them.

EWE: 45 Abimelek wɔ aʋa kple dua ŋkeke ma katã, eye wòxɔ dua. Ewu emenɔlawo, eye wògbã dua hewu dze ɖe edzi.
ENGLISH: 45 And Abimelec attacked the city all that day, and took the city, and killed the people in it, and pulled down the city and sowed it with salt.

EWE: 46 Esi kplɔla siwo katã le Sekem mɔ́ la me se nya sia la, enumake woyi ɖe El-Berit ƒe aƒe ƒe xɔ tamegoba la me.
ENGLISH: 46 And all the citizens of Shekem Tower heard of it, and went into the vault of the house of El-berith;

EWE: 47 Esi wova gblɔe na Abimelek be kplɔla siwo le Sekem mɔ́ la me va ƒo ƒu la,
ENGLISH: 47 and Abimelec was told that all the citizens of Shekem Tower had gathered.

EWE: 49 Eya ta ameawo katã lã atilɔ hedze Abimelek yome. Eye wotsɔ atilɔawo va kɔ ɖe xɔ tamegoba la ŋu, eye wotɔ dzo xɔa ɖe wo dzi. Ale Sekem mɔ́ me nɔlawo katã hã ku; woanɔ ŋutsu kple nyɔnu akpe ɖeka.
ENGLISH: 48 And Abimelec went up on Mount Salmon, he and all the people he had with him; and Abimelec took an ax in his hand and cut a bush of wood, and took it up and put it on his shoulder, and said to the people he had with him “I have done what you saw; be quick and do like me.” 49 And the people too all cut a bush each, and, following Abimelec, went and laid them against the vault and set the vault on fire over the people in it; so all the men of Shekem Tower too came to their death, about a thousand men and women.

EWE: 50 Eye Abimelek ho yi Tebez; eɖe to ɖe Tebez eye wòxɔe.
ENGLISH: 50 And Abimelec went to Tebes, and camped at Tebes and took it.

EWE: 51 Ke mɔ́ sesẽ aɖe le dua titina, eye dua me tɔwo katã, ŋutsuwo kple nyɔnuwo kple dumegãwo katã si yi afi ma. Wodo ʋɔa ɖe wo ɖokuiwo nu, eye wolia mɔ́ sesẽ la yi etame.
ENGLISH: 51 And there was a strong tower in the middle of the city; and all the men and women, and all the citizens of the city, fled to that and locked themselves in, and went up on the roof of the tower.

EWE: 52 Eye Abimelek yi mɔ́ sesẽ la gbɔ ɖadze aʋa ɖe eŋu. Eva mɔ́ sesẽ la ƒe mɔnu be yeatɔ dzoe.
ENGLISH: 52 And Abimelec came to the tower and attacked it, and approached the doorway of the tower to burn it.

EWE: 53 Ke nyɔnu aɖe ɖe asi le tévi ŋu tso dzi wòva dze ta na Abimelek, eye wògbã ta nɛ.
ENGLISH: 53 But one woman threw a quern-stone on Abimelec’s head and cracked his skull;

EWE: 54 Eya ta eyɔ eƒe adekplɔvi gblɔ nɛ be: “Ðe wò yi ne nàwum, ne womagagblɔ le ŋunye be: ‘Nyɔnue wui’ o.” Enumake eƒe adekplɔvi la ƒo yi ɖee wòku.
ENGLISH: 54 and he cried in haste to his squire “Draw your sword and give me my death-stroke, that it may not be said of me ‘a woman killed him’”; and his man ran him through, so that he died.

EWE: 55 Esi Israel ŋutsuwo kpɔ be Abimelek ku la, wo katã wotrɔ yi woƒe aƒewo me.
ENGLISH: 55 And the men of Israel saw that Abimelec was dead, and went home to their places.

EWE: 56 Ale Mawu ɖo vɔ̃ si Abimelek wɔ ɖe fofoa ŋu hewu nɔviaŋutsu blaadreawo teƒe nɛ.
ENGLISH: 56 So God sent back Abimelec’s mischief that he had done to his father in killing his seventy brothers,

EWE: 57 Eye Mawu he vɔ̃ siwo katã Sekem ŋutsuwo hã wɔ va woawo ŋutɔwo ƒe ta dzi. Ale Yotam, Yerubaal vi, ƒe fiƒodea ɖi wo ŋu.
ENGLISH: 57 and the mischief of the men of Shekem God sent back on their own heads, and the curse of Jotham the son of Jerubbaal came upon them.

EWE: Ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo
ENGLISH: Judges

EWE: 10 Le Abimelek megbe la, Tola, Pua vi, Dodo vi, ame si tso Isakar-to la me, do be yeaxɔ na Israel. Enɔ Samir le Efrayim tonuto la me.
ENGLISH: 10 And after Abimelec there stood up to save Israel Tolaʽ the son of Puah the son of Dodo the Issacarite; he lived at Shamir in the highland of Ephraim;

EWE: 2 Edrɔ̃ ʋɔnu na Israel ƒe blaeve vɔ etɔ̃. Emegbe Tola ku, eye woɖii ɖe Samir.
ENGLISH: 2 and he judged Israel twenty-three years, and died and was buried at Shamir.

EWE: 3 Eya megbe Gileadtɔ Yair do, eye wòdrɔ̃ ʋɔnu na Israel ƒe blaeve vɔ eve.
ENGLISH: 3 And after him Jair the Gileadite stood up, and judged Israel twenty-two years;

EWE: 4 Viŋutsu blaetɔ̃ nɔ esi, wodoa tedzi blaetɔ̃, eye du blaetɔ̃ nɔ wo si, woyɔa du siawo be Havot-Yair va se ɖe egbe; wole Gilead-nyigba dzi.
ENGLISH: 4 he had thirty sons who rode on thirty young donkeys, and they had thirty cities (these they call the Havvoth of Jair to this day) in the country of Gilead.

EWE: 5 Emegbe Yair ku, eye woɖii ɖe Kamon.
ENGLISH: 5 And Jair died, and was buried at Kamon.

EWE: 6 Israel-viwo gawɔ nu si nye vɔ̃ le Yehowa ŋkume, eye wosubɔ Baalwo, Astoretwo, Aram mawuwo, Sidon mawuwo, Moab mawuwo, Amonitɔwo ƒe mawuwo kple Filistitɔwo ƒe mawuwo. Ale wogblẽ Yehowa ɖi, eye womesubɔe o.
ENGLISH: 6 And the sons of Israel did more of what displeased Jehovah, and worshiped the Baals and the ʽAshtarts and the gods of Syria and the gods of Phenicia and the gods of Moab and the gods of the Bene-ʽAmmon and the gods of the Philistines, and left Jehovah and did not worship him.

EWE: 7 Eya ta Yehowa ƒe dɔmedzoe bi ɖe Israel ŋu, ale be wòtsɔ wo dzra na Filistitɔwo kple Amonitɔwo.
ENGLISH: 7 And Jehovah was angry with Israel and sold them into the hands of the Philistines and into the hands of the Bene-ʽAmmon,

EWE: 8 Ale wosẽ ŋuta le Israel-viwo ŋu hete wo ɖe anyi vevie le ƒe ma me wote Israel-vi siwo katã le Yordan ƒe go kemɛ dzi le Amoritɔwo ƒe anyigba si le Gilead la dzi ɖe anyi ƒe wuienyi sɔŋ.
ENGLISH: 8 and they mauled and persecuted the sons of Israel that year eighteen years, all the sons of Israel on the other side of the Jordan, in the Amorite country in Gilead.

EWE: 9 Amonitɔwo tsoa Yordan-tɔsisia hã va wɔa aʋa kple Yuda, Benyamin kple Efrayim ƒe aƒe la; eye Israel ɖo xaxa gã aɖe me.
ENGLISH: 9 And the Bene-ʽAmmon crossed the Jordan to attack even Judah and Benjamin and the highland of Ephraim; and Israel was in great straits.

EWE: 10 Eye Israel-viwo yɔ Yehowa be wòaxɔ na yewo hegblɔ be: “Míewɔ nu vɔ̃ ɖe ŋuwò, elabena míegblẽ mía Mawu la ɖi hesubɔ Baalwo.”
ENGLISH: 10 And the sons of Israel cried to Jehovah “We have sinned against you, because we have left our God and worshiped the Baals”;

EWE: 11 Ke Yehowa gblɔ na Israel-viwo be: “Ðe nyemeɖe mi tso Egiptetɔwo, Amoritɔwo, Amonitɔwo, Filistitɔwo,
ENGLISH: 11 and Jehovah said to the sons of Israel “Is not from the Egyptians and the Amorites from the Bene-ʽAmmon and the Philistines?

EWE: 12 Sidontɔwo, Amalektɔwo kple Midiantɔwo si me esime wote mi ɖe anyi oa? Esi miedo ɣli yɔm la, meɖe mi tso wo si me.
ENGLISH: 12 and the Phenicians and ʽAmalek and Maʽon oppressed you, and you cried out to me and I saved you out of their hands;

EWE: 13 Ke miegblẽm ɖi hesubɔ mawu bubuwo. Esia tae nyemagaɖe mi azɔ o.
ENGLISH: 13 but you left me and worshiped other gods; so I will not save you anymore.

EWE: 14 Miyi ɖayɔ mawu siwo mietia la ne woakpe ɖe mia ŋu.
ENGLISH: 14 Go and cry to the gods you have chosen: let them save you in your time of distress.”

EWE: Woneɖe mi le miaƒe xaxaɣi.” 15 Ke Israel-viwo gblɔ na Yehowa be: “Míewɔ nu vɔ̃. Wɔ mí ale si dze ŋuwò. Gake míeɖe kuku, ɖe mí egbe sia.”
