ENGLISH: 15 But the sons of Israel said to Jehovah “We have sinned; do with us yourself just as you think best, only deliver us this day,”

EWE: 16 Eye woɖe dutamawuwo ɖa le wo dome hesubɔ Yehowa, ale be megate ŋu do dzi tsɔ Israel-viwo ƒe fukpekpewo o.
ENGLISH: 16 and removed the foreign gods out of their midst and worshiped Jehovah; and he could not bear Israel’s suffering.

EWE: 17 Emegbe la, Amonitɔwo kpe ta, eye wova ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Gilead.
ENGLISH: 17 And the Bene-ʽAmmon came out in arms and camped at Gilead; and the sons of Israel came together and camped at Mispah.

EWE: Eya ta Israel-viwo hã ƒo ƒu heva ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Mizpa. 18 Eye Gileadtɔwo kple woƒe amegãwo gblɔ na wo nɔewo be: “Ame kae adze ŋgɔ akpe aʋa kple Amonitɔwo? Eyae azu tatɔ ɖe Gileadtɔwo katã nu.”
ENGLISH: 18 And the people, the captains of Gilead, said to each other “Who will be the man that has the nerve to fight the Bene-ʽAmmon? he shall be head of all the population of Gilead.”

EWE: Ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo
ENGLISH: Judges

EWE: 11 Gileadtɔ Yefta nye aʋakalẽtɔ sesẽ aɖe; enye gbolo aɖe ƒe vi, eye Yefta fofoe nye Gilead.
ENGLISH: 11 And Jephthah the Gileadite was a stalwart man who was the son of a prostitute.

EWE: 2 Gilead srɔ̃ dzi ŋutsuvi bubuwo hã nɛ.
ENGLISH: Gilead had begotten Jephthah,

EWE: Esi srɔ̃a ƒe viwo tsi la, wonya Yefta hegblɔ nɛ be: “Domenyinu aɖeke masu asiwò le mía fofo ƒe me o, elabena nyɔnu bubu ƒe vie nènye.” 3 Eya ta Yefta si le nɔviawo nu, eye wòva nɔ Tob-nyigba dzi. Eye ŋutsu dɔaɖekemawɔlawo va wɔ ɖeka kple Yefta, eye wodze eyome.
ENGLISH: 2 and Gilead’s wife bore sons to him, and the wife’s sons, when they grew up, turned Jephthah out and said to him “You shall not inherit in our family, because you are the son of another woman.” 3 And Jephthah left the country on account of his brothers, and lived in the Tob country; and a set of riffraff drew together to Jephthah and went on expeditions with him

EWE: 4 Le ɣeyiɣi aɖe megbe la, Amonitɔwo kpe aʋa kple Israel.
ENGLISH: 4 And after a while the Bene-ʽAmmon made war on Israel;

EWE: 5 Esi Amonitɔwo kpe aʋa kple Israel la, enumake Gilead-metsitsiwo yi be yewoaɖakplɔ Yefta tso Tob-nyigba dzi vɛ.
ENGLISH: 5 and when the Bene-ʽAmmon made war on Israel the elders of Gilead went to fetch Jephthah out of the Tob country.

EWE: 6 Wogblɔ na Yefta be: “Va nye míaƒe aʋafia, ne míawɔ aʋa kple Amonitɔwo.”
ENGLISH: 6 And they said to Jephthah “Come and be our chieftain to make war with the Bene-ʽAmmon.”

EWE: 7 Ke Yefta bia Gilead-metsitsiwo be: “Menye miawoe lé fum vevie henyam le fofonye ƒe me oa?
ENGLISH: 7 And Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead “Why, you hated me and turned me out of my family; how is it you have come to me now when you are in a tight place?”

EWE: Ke nu ka tae mieva gbɔnye azɔ esi mieɖo xaxa me?” 8 Eye Gilead-metsitsiwo gblɔ na Yefta be: “Esia ta míeva gbɔwò ɖo. Ne èyi kpli mí ɖawɔ aʋa kple Amonitɔwo la, àzu mí Gileadtɔwo katã ƒe kplɔla.”
ENGLISH: 8 And the elders of Gilead said to Jephthah “As for that, we have come back to you now, and you are to come with us and fight the Bene-ʽAmmon, and we will have you for head of all the population of Gilead.”

EWE: 9 Eya ta Yefta gblɔ na Gilead-metsitsiawo be: “Ne miekplɔm gbɔe meyi ɖawɔ aʋa kple Amonitɔwo, eye Yehowa ɖu wo dzi nam la, ekema mazu miaƒe kplɔla!”
ENGLISH: 9 And Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead “If you bring me back to fight the Bene-ʽAmmon, and Jehovah gives them to be defeated before me, I shall be your head?”

EWE: 10 Eye Gilead-metsitsiawo ɖo eŋu na Yefta be: “Yehowa nanye ɖasefo le mí kpli wò dome ne míewɔ nya si nègblɔ la dzi o.”
ENGLISH: 10 And the elders of Gilead said to Jephthah “So help us Jehovah, we will do as you have said.”

EWE: 11 Eya ta Yefta yi kple Gilead-metsitsiawo, eye dukɔ la tsɔe ɖo woƒe kplɔla kple aʋafia. Eye Yefta gbugbɔ gblɔ nya siwo wògblɔ la katã le Yehowa ŋkume le Mizpa.
ENGLISH: 11 And Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead, and the people set him over them as head and chieftain; and Jephthah set forth the terms of the pledge before Jehovah at Mispah.

EWE: 12 Eye Yefta dɔ ame ɖo ɖe Amonitɔwo ƒe fia gbɔ be: “Nu kae mewɔ ɖe ŋuwò hafi nèho aʋa ɖe nye anyigba ŋu?”
ENGLISH: 12 And Jephthah sent envoys to the king of the Bene-ʽAmmon to say “What business have you coming into my country to attack me?”

EWE: 13 Amonitɔwo ƒe fia gblɔ na Yefta ƒe ame dɔdɔawo be: “Elabena Israel xɔ nye anyigba esime woʋu tso Egipte va, woxɔe tso Arnon va se ɖe Yabok va ɖo keke Yordan nu ke. Eya ta azɔ la, gbugbɔe nam kpoo.”
ENGLISH: 13 And the king of the Bene-ʽAmmon said to Jephthah’s envoys Because Israel took my country when they came up out of Egypt, from the Arnon to the Jabbok and the Jordan; now restore it peaceably.”

EWE: 14 Ke Yefta gadɔ ame ɖo ɖe Amonitɔwo ƒe fia ake
ENGLISH: 14 And Jephthah again sent envoys to the king of the Bene-’Ammon

EWE: 15 be woagblɔ nɛ be: “Ale Yefta gblɔe nye esi: ‘Israel mexɔ Moabtɔwo ƒe anyigba kple Amonitɔwo ƒe anyigba o,
ENGLISH: 15 and said to him “Says Jephthah, Israel did not take the country of Moab nor that of the Bene-ʽAmmon,

EWE: 16 elabena esime Israel ʋu tso Egipte la, woto gbedzi va ɖo Ƒudzĩ la nu heva Kades.
ENGLISH: 16 but when they were coming up out of Egypt Israel went in the wilderness as far as the Red Sea, and came to Kadesh;

EWE: 17 Eye Israel dɔ ame ɖo ɖe Edom-fia, be woagblɔ nɛ be: “Meɖe kuku, na míato wò anyigba dzi ayi,” ke Edom-fia meɖo toe o. Edɔ ame ɖo ɖe Moab-fia hã, ke eya hã melɔ̃ o.
ENGLISH: 17 and Israel sent envoys to the king of Edom to say ‘Let us pass through your country,’ and the king of Edom did not listen to them; and they sent also to the king of Moab, and he was not willing; so Israel stayed at Kadesh.

EWE: Eye Israel tsi Kades. 18 Esi woto gbea dzi la, wotso Edom-nyigba kple Moab-nyigba ɖi. Woto Moab-nyigba ƒe ɣedzeƒe gome heva ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Arnon nuto la me; womege ɖe Moab ƒe anyigba dzi o, elabena Arnon ye do liƒo na Moab.
ENGLISH: 18 And they went in the wilderness around the country of Edom and that of Moab, and came along east of the country of Moab and camped beyond the Arnon, and did not come within the boundary of Moab, because the Arnon is the boundary of Moab.

EWE: 19 “‘Emegbe Israel dɔ ame ɖo ɖe Amoritɔwo ƒe fia Sihon, si nye Hesbon-fia, eye Israel gblɔ nɛ be: “Meɖe kuku, na míato wò anyigba dzi ayi míawo ŋutɔwo mía nɔƒe.”
ENGLISH: 19 And Israel sent envoys to Sihon the king of the Amorites, the king of Heshbon, and said to him ‘Let us pass through your country to our destination’;

EWE: 20 Ke Sihon meka ɖe Israel-viwo dzi ne wòana woato eƒe anyigba dzi ayi o, eya ta Sihon ƒo eƒe amewo katã nu ƒu heva ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Yahaz, eye wòwɔ aʋa kple Israel.
ENGLISH: 20 but Sihon refused to give Israel passage within his boundary, and Sihon brought together all his people and camped at Jahzah, and fought with Israel.

EWE: 21 Eye Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la, tsɔ Sihon kple eƒe amewo katã de asi na Israel, ale be woɖu wo dzi, eye Israel xɔ Amoritɔ siwo nye anyigba ma dzi tɔwo la ƒe anyigba katã.
ENGLISH: 21 And Israel’s God Jehovah gave Sihon and all his people into Israel’s hands, and they defeated them; and Israel took possession of all the country of the Amorites who inhabited that country;

EWE: 22 Ale woxɔ Amoritɔwo ƒe anyigba la katã wòzu wo tɔ tso Arnon-tɔsisia nu va se ɖe Yabok-tɔsisia nu, tso gbea dzi va se ɖe Yordan nu.
ENGLISH: 22 and they succeeded to all the territory of the Amorites, from the Arnon to the Jabbok and from the wilderness to the Jordan.

EWE: 23 “‘Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu lae nya Amoritɔwo ɖa le eƒe dukɔ Israel ŋgɔ, azɔ wòa nèbe yeanya wo ɖa?
ENGLISH: 23 Now, when Israel’s God Jehovah dispossessed the Amorites before his people Israel, are you to succeed to them?

EWE: 24 Menye nu sia nu si wò mawu Kemos na wò lae nye tɔwò oa?
ENGLISH: 24 You succeed to what your god Kemosh gives you possession of, do you not? and whomever our God Jehovah dispossesses before us, we succeed to them.

EWE: Eya ta ame sia ame si mía Mawu Yehowa nya ɖa le mía ŋgɔ lae míanya ɖa. 25 Azɔ wòe nyo wu Moab-fia Balak, Zipor vi la?
ENGLISH: 25 “And then, are you any better than Balak the son of Sippor, king of Moab? did he bring any claim against Israel, or wage any war with them?

EWE: Ðe wòhe nya kple Israel alo wɔ aʋa kplii kpɔa? 26 Esi Israel nɔ Hesbon kple eŋu duwo, Aroer kple eŋu duwo, kpakple du siwo katã le Arnon ŋu la me ƒe alafa etɔ̃ sɔŋ ɖe, nu ka tae mète kpɔ be yeagbugbɔ xɔe le wo si ɣemaɣi o?
ENGLISH: 26 When Israel settled in Heshbon and its dependencies, and in ʽAroʽer and its dependencies, and in all the cities along the banks of the Arnon, for three hundred years, how is it you did not recover them at that time?

EWE: 27 Nyemewɔ nu vɔ̃ ɖe ŋuwò o, eya ta tɔwò medzɔ be nèho aʋa ɖe ŋunye o.
ENGLISH: 27 And I have committed no offense against you, but you are doing wrong by me in making war on me.

EWE: Yehowa, Ʋɔnudrɔ̃la la, nadrɔ̃e le Israel-viwo kple Amonitɔwo dome egbea.’”
ENGLISH: Jehovah the Judge give judgment today between the sons of Israel and the Bene-ʽAmmon.”

EWE: 28 Ke Amonitɔwo ƒe fia la meɖo to Yefta ƒe nya siwo wògblɔ ɖo ɖee la o.
ENGLISH: 28 But the king of the Bene-ʽAmmon did not listen to the words Jephthah sent to him.

EWE: 29 Ale Yehowa ƒe gbɔgbɔ va Yefta dzi, eye wòto Gilead kple Manase yi Mizpe si le Gilead, eye wòtso Mizpe si le Gilead ɖo ta Amonitɔwo gbɔ.
ENGLISH: 29 And the spirit of Jehovah came upon Jephthah, and he passed through Gilead and Manasseh, and through Mispeh-Gilead; and from Mispeh-Gilead he passed over to the Bene-ʽAmmon.

EWE: 30 Eye Yefta ɖe adzɔgbe na Yehowa gblɔ be: “Ne ètsɔ Amonitɔwo de asi nam la,
ENGLISH: 30 And Jephthah made a vow to Jehovah, “If you give the Bene-ʽAmmon into my hands,

EWE: 31 ekema ame si ado tso nye aƒe ƒe agbo nu ava kpem ne megbɔ tso Amonitɔwo gbɔ le ŋutifafa me la, azu Yehowa tɔ, eye matsɔ ame ma ana abe numevɔsa ene.”
ENGLISH: 31 then any that comes out of my house doors to meet me, when I come safe back from the Bene-ʽAmmon, shall belong to Jehovah, and I will offer that one as a burnt-offering.”

EWE: 32 Ale Yefta yi ɖawɔ aʋa kple Amonitɔwo, eye Yehowa tsɔ wo de asi nɛ.
ENGLISH: 32 And Jephthah passed over to the Bene-ʽAmmon to fight them, and Jehovah gave them into his hands;

EWE: 33 Esi wo hewu wo dometɔ gbogbo aɖewo ŋutɔ tso Aroer yi keke Minit exɔ du blaeve va se ɖe Abel-Keramim ke.
ENGLISH: 33 and he made havoc of them from ʽAroʽer till you come to Minnith, twenty cities, and to Abel-keramim, great havoc.

EWE: Ale wobɔbɔ Amonitɔwo ɖe anyi le Israel-viwo ŋkume.
ENGLISH: And the Bene-ʽAmmon were humbled before the sons of Israel.

EWE: 34 Mlɔeba esi Yefta trɔ gbɔna eƒe me le Mizpa la, kpɔ ɖa, vianyɔnue nye ema do go le axatsɛ ƒom hele ɣe ɖum gbɔna ekpe ge! Ke eya koe nye vi ɖeka hɔ̃ si le esi.
ENGLISH: 34 And Jephthah came to his home at Mispah, and found his daughter coming out to meet him with tambourines and dances; and she was his one only child, he had no son or daughter else.

EWE: Viŋutsu alo vinyɔnu bubu aɖeke megale esi kpe ɖe eŋu o. 35 Esi wòkpɔe la, edze eƒe awuwo hegblɔ be: “Ao, vinye! Ègbã dzi nam, elabe èzu ame si menya de gbe.
ENGLISH: 35 And at seeing her he tore his clothes and said “O, O, my daughter, you have laid me low; you are down on me with the rest! and I have opened my mouth to Jehovah and cannot go back!”

EWE: Elabe meɖe adzɔgbe na Yehowa, eye nyemagate ŋu atrɔe o.” 36 Ke egblɔ nɛ be: “Fofonye, ne èke nu na Yehowa la, ekema wɔm abe ale si nèdo ŋugbee ene, elabena Yehowa bia hlɔ̃ wò futɔ Amonitɔwo na wò.”
ENGLISH: 36 And she said to him “Father, you have opened your mouth to Jehovah: do with me as went out of your mouth, so long as Jehovah has done vengeance on your enemies the Bene-ʽAmmon for you.”

EWE: 37 Eye wògblɔ na fofoa be: “Wɔ nu sia ko nam: Ðe mɔ nam ɣleti eve manɔ ɖokuinye si, ne nye kple xɔ̃nyewo míayi toawo dzi aɖafa nye ɖetugbui leaƒe nyenye.”
ENGLISH: 37 But she said to her father “Let this thing be done for me: let me be for two months to go and range on the mountains and weep for my maidenhood, I and my girl friends.”

EWE: 38 Eye wògblɔ nɛ be: “Heyi!” Ale wòɖe mɔ nɛ wòdzo ɣleti eve, eye eya kple exɔlɔ̃awo yi ɖafa eƒe ɖetugbui leaƒe nyenye le toawo dzi.
ENGLISH: 38 And he said “Go,” and sent her off for two months; and she went, she and her girl friends, and wept for her maidenhood on the mountains.

EWE: 39 Esi ɣleti eveawo wu enu la, etrɔ gbɔ va fofoa gbɔ, eye wòwɔ adzɔgbe si wòɖe le eŋu la dzi. Ke medɔ kple ŋutsu kpɔ o.
ENGLISH: 39 And at the end of two months she came back to her father, and he did with her what he had made the vow to do, when she had not known man.

EWE: Eye wòzu kɔnu le Israel be, 40 ƒe sia ƒe la, Israel ɖetugbuiwo yina ɖakafua Gileadtɔ Yefta ƒe vinyɔnu la, ŋkeke ene le ƒe ɖeka me.
ENGLISH: 40 And it became a usage in Israel that year by year the Israelite girls should go to celebrate the memory of the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite, four days in a year.

EWE: Ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo
ENGLISH: Judges

EWE: 12 Azɔ Efrayim ŋutsuwo kpe ta, eye wotso tɔ la va Zafon, eye wogblɔ na Yefta be: “Nu ka ŋuti nètso tɔ yi ɖawɔ aʋa kple Amonitɔwo, gake mèyɔ mí be míayi kpli wò o?
ENGLISH: 12 And the men of Ephraim came out in arms and crossed to Saphon, and said to Jephthah “How is it you have gone over to fight the Bene-’Ammon and not called us to go with you? we will burn your house down over your head.”

EWE: Míatɔ dzo wò aƒe ɖe dziwò.” 2 Ke Yefta gblɔ na wo be: “Nye kple nye dukɔ míekpe aʋa dziŋɔ aɖe kple Amonitɔwo.
ENGLISH: 2 And Jephthah said to them “I had a quarrel on hand, I and my people, and the Bene-ʽAmmon had committed outrages on me; and I called you to arms and you did not help me against them;

EWE: Meyɔ mi be miava kpe ɖe ŋunye, gake mieva ɖem le wo si me o. 3 Esi mekpɔe be miegbɔna xɔxɔ ge nam o la, meɖoe be matsɔ nye agbe ade afɔku me ahaho ɖe Amonitɔwo ŋu, eye Yehowa tsɔ wo de asi nam.
ENGLISH: 3 so I saw there was nobody to help me, and I took my life in my hand and passed over to the Bene-ʽAmmon, and Jehovah gave them into my hands; then why have you come up to my home this day to fight me?”

EWE: Ke nu ka tae mieva egbea be miawɔ aʋa kplim?” 4 Enumake Yefta ƒo Gilead ŋutsuwo katã nu ƒu, eye wowɔ aʋa kple Efrayim; eye Gilead ŋutsuwo ɖu Efrayimtɔ siwo gblɔ be, “Mi Gileadtɔ siwo le Efrayim kple Manase la, sisilawo koe mienye tso Efrayim” la dzi.
ENGLISH: 4 And Jephthah gathered all the men of Gilead and fought the Ephraimites, and the men of Gilead defeated the Ephraimites.

EWE: 5 Gileadtɔwo va xe mɔ le Yordan tɔtsoƒewo le Efrayim ŋgɔ; eye ne Efrayim ŋutsuwo si va yina la, wogblɔna be, “Mina matso tɔ la”; eye Gilead ŋutsuwo biaa wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe be, “Efrayimtɔe nènyea?”
ENGLISH: 5 And the Gileadites seized the fords of the Jordan against the Ephraimites; and when an Ephraimite fugitive said “Let me cross” and the men of Gilead said to him “Are you an Ephraimite?” and he said “No,”

EWE: Ne eɖo eŋu be, “Ao!” la, 6 wogblɔna nɛ be, “Taflatsɛ, gblɔ be Sibolet.”
ENGLISH: 6 they would say to him “Say shibboleth,” and he would say sibboleth, not getting the pronunciation right, and they would take hold of him and cut his throat, letting the blood run into the fords of the Jordan.

EWE: Ke egblɔna be, “Zibolet,” elabena metea ŋu yɔa nyaa nyuie o.
ENGLISH: And at that time forty-two thousand of the Ephraimites fell.

EWE: 7 Yefta drɔ̃ ʋɔnu na Israel ƒe ade; emegbe Yefta, Gileadtɔ la ku, eye woɖii ɖe wo dedu me le Gilead.
ENGLISH: 7 And Jephthah judged Israel six years; and Jephthah the Gileadite died, and was buried in his city in Gilead.

EWE: 8 Le eyome la, Ibzan si tso Betlehem drɔ̃ ʋɔnu na Israel.
ENGLISH: 8 And after him Ibsan from Beth-lehem judged Israel;

EWE: 9 Viŋutsu blaetɔ̃ kple vinyɔnu blaetɔ̃ le esi. Ena vianyɔnuawo yi ɖaɖe ŋutsu siwo tso hlɔ̃ bubuwo me, eye wòna wokplɔ nyɔnu blaetɔ̃ vɛ na viaŋutsuwo woɖe. Edrɔ̃ ʋɔnu na Israel ƒe adre.
ENGLISH: 9 he had thirty sons, and married off thirty daughters and took in thirty girls from outside as wives for his sons; and he judged Israel seven years.

EWE: 10 Emegbe Ibzan ku, eye woɖii ɖe Betlehem.
ENGLISH: 10 And Ibsan died, and was buried at Beth-lehem.

EWE: 11 Le eyome Elon, Zebulontɔ la, drɔ̃ ʋɔnu na Israel. Edrɔ̃ ʋɔnu Israel ƒe ewo.
ENGLISH: 11 And after him Elon the Zebulonite judged Israel; and he judged Israel ten years.

EWE: 12 Emegbe Elon, Zebulontɔ la ku, eye woɖii ɖe Aiyalon le Zebulon-nyigba dzi.
ENGLISH: 12 And Elon the Zebulonite died, and was buried at Elon in the Zebulonite country.

EWE: 13 Le eyome la, Abdon, Piratontɔ Hilel vi, drɔ̃ ʋɔnu na Israel.
ENGLISH: 13 And after him ʽAbdon the son of Hillel the Pireathonite judged Israel;

EWE: 14 Viŋutsu blaene kple tɔgbuiyɔvi blaetɔ̃ le esi, eye wodoa tedzi blaadre. Edrɔ̃ ʋɔnu na Israel ƒe enyi.
ENGLISH: 14 he had forty sons and thirty grandsons, who rode on seventy young donkeys; and he judged Israel eight years.

EWE: 15 Emegbe Abdon, Piratontɔ Hilel vi la ku, eye woɖii ɖe Piraton le Efrayim-nyigba dzi le Amalektɔwo ƒe to la dzi.
ENGLISH: 15 And ʽAbdon the son of Hillel the Pireathonite died, and was buried at Pireathon in the Ephraimite country, in the ʽAmalekite highland.

EWE: Ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo
ENGLISH: Judges

EWE: 13 Israel-viwo gawɔ nu si nye vɔ̃ le Yehowa ŋkume, eye Yehowa tsɔ wo de asi na Filistitɔwo ƒe blaene.
ENGLISH: 13 And the sons of Israel did more of what displeased Jehovah, and Jehovah gave them into the hands of the Philistines for forty years.

EWE: 2 Ɣemaɣi la, ŋutsu aɖe tso Zora, eŋkɔe nye Manoa tso Dan viwo ƒe ƒomea me. Srɔ̃a tsi ko, eye vi mele esi o.
ENGLISH: 2 Now there was a certain man of Soreah, of the Danite clan, named Manoah; and his wife was barren and had never had a child.

EWE: 3 Gbe ɖeka Yehowa ƒe dɔla ɖe eɖokui fia nyɔnu la hegblɔ nɛ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, ètsi ko, eye vi mele asiwò o. Gake èle fu fɔ ge adzi ŋutsuvi.
ENGLISH: 3 And the Angel of Jehovah appeared to the wife and said to her “You are barren, have never had a child; you shall conceive and have a son.

EWE: 4 Ke kpɔ nyuie be màgano wain alo aha muame aɖeke o, eye mègaɖu nu makɔmakɔ aɖeke o.
ENGLISH: 4 Now take care not to drink wine or beer, nor to eat anything unclean;

EWE: 5 Kpɔ ɖa, èle fu fɔ ge adzi ŋutsuvi, eye talũhɛ maka ta ŋu nɛ o, elabena ɖevi la anye Mawu ƒe Naziritɔ tso edziɣi; eye axɔ ŋgɔ aɖe Israel tso Filistitɔwo si me.”
ENGLISH: 5 for you are conceiving and are to have a son, over whose head no razor shall go, because he shall be God’s devotee from his birth; and he shall begin saving Israel from the Philistines.”

EWE: 6 Eye nyɔnua yi ɖagblɔ na srɔ̃a be: “Mawu vavã la ƒe ame aɖe va gbɔnye, eɖi Mawu vavã la ƒe dɔla, eye ŋɔdzi le eŋu ŋutɔ.
ENGLISH: 6 And the woman went in and told her husband “The man of God came to me, looking like the Angel of God, very awful; and I did not ask him where he was from, and he did not tell me his name; and he said to me

EWE: Nyemebia afi si wòtso lae o, eye meyɔ eŋkɔ hã nam o. 7 Ke egblɔ nam be: ‘Kpɔ ɖa, èle fu fɔ ge adzi ŋutsuvi.
ENGLISH: 7 ‘You are conceiving and are to have a son; now do not drink wine nor beer, nor eat any uncleanness, because the boy shall be God’s devotee from his birth till the day of his death.’”

EWE: Eya ta mègano wain alo aha muame aɖeke o, eye mègaɖu nu makɔmakɔ aɖeke o, elabena ɖevi la anye Mawu ƒe Naziritɔ tso edziɣi va se ɖe eƒe kugbe.’” 8 Eye Manoa ƒo koko na Yehowa vevie be: “Yehowa, meɖe kuku.
ENGLISH: 8 And Manoah invoked Jehovah, and said “O Lord, let the man of God whom you sent come to us again and instruct us what to do with the boy that is to be born.”

EWE: 9 Eya ta Mawu vavã la ɖo to Manoa, eye Mawu vavã la ƒe dɔla gava nyɔnua gbɔ ake esime wòbɔbɔ nɔ agble me; srɔ̃a Manoa mele egbɔ o.
ENGLISH: 9 And God obeyed Manoah, and the Angel of God came to the woman again while she was sitting out on the range and her husband Manoah was not with her;

EWE: 10 Nyɔnua ƒu du kaba yi ɖagblɔ na srɔ̃a be: “Kpɔ ɖa!
ENGLISH: 10 and the woman ran in haste and told her husband “The man that came to me that day has appeared to me.”

EWE: Ŋutsu si va gbɔnye nyitsɔ la gaɖe eɖokui fiam.” 11 Eye Manoa tso kplɔ srɔ̃a ɖo. Esi wòva ŋutsua gbɔ la, ebiae be: “Wòe ƒo nu kple srɔ̃nyea?”
ENGLISH: 11 And Manoah rose and went after his wife, and came to the man and said to him “Are you the man that spoke to the woman?” and he said “Yes.”

EWE: Eɖo eŋu be: “Nyee.” 12 Eye Manoa gblɔ be: “Wò nyawo neva eme! Aleke míanyi ɖevi lae, eye dɔ kae wòawɔ?”
ENGLISH: 12 And Manoah said “At the time your words come true, what shall be the rule for the boy and what shall he do?”

EWE: 13 Eye Yehowa ƒe dɔla la gblɔ na Manoa be: “Ele be srɔ̃wò nakpɔ eɖokui dzi nyuie le nu sia nu si megblɔ nɛ la ŋu.
ENGLISH: 13 And the Angel of Jehovah said to Manoah “The woman must take care about everything that I told her:

EWE: 14 Megaɖu naneke si tso waintsetse me o, megano wain alo aha muame aɖeke o, eye megaɖu nu makɔmakɔ aɖeke hã o. Nu sia nu si ƒe se mede nɛ la, newɔ edzi pɛpɛpɛ.”
ENGLISH: 14 she must not eat anything that comes from the grapevine, nor drink wine or beer, nor eat any uncleanness: she must observe all the instructions I gave her.”

EWE: 15 Azɔ Manoa gblɔ na Yehowa ƒe dɔla la be: “Meɖe kuku, lala vie, ne míaɖa gbɔ̃vi aɖe na wò.”
ENGLISH: 15 And Manoah said to the Angel of Jehovah “Let us have you stop a while, and let us do a kid for you”;

EWE: 16 Ke Yehowa ƒe dɔla la gblɔ na Manoa be: “Ne melala hã la, nyemaɖu wò nu si nàɖa o; gake ne èdi be yeasa numevɔ na Yehowa la, àte ŋu asa vɔa.”
ENGLISH: 16 but the Angel of Jehovah said to Manoah “If you have me stop I will not eat bread of yours, and if you do an animal you must offer it as a burnt-offering to Jehovah.”

EWE: Manoa menya be Yehowa ƒe dɔlae wònye o.
ENGLISH: (For Manoah did not know that it was the Angel of Jehovah.)

EWE: 17 Eye Manoa bia Yehowa ƒe dɔla la be: “Ŋkɔwò ɖe, ale be ne wò nyaa va eme la, ne míade bubu ŋuwò?”
ENGLISH: 17 And Manoah said to the Angel of Jehovah “What is your name? when your words come true we will pay you honor.”

EWE: 18 Ke Yehowa ƒe dɔla la ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Nu ka ŋuti nèle nye ŋkɔ ta biam, evɔ ŋkɔ wɔnuku wònye?”
ENGLISH: 18 But the Angel of Jehovah said to him “What do you ask my name for, when it is mysterious?”

EWE: 19 Manoa tsɔ gbɔ̃vi la kple nuɖuvɔsa la sa vɔ na Yehowa le agakpe la dzi. Eye Mawu wɔ nukunu aɖe Manoa kple srɔ̃a kpɔ.
ENGLISH: 19 And Manoah took the kid and the grain-offering and burned them on the stone as an offering to Jehovah Who Works Mysteriously;

EWE: 20 Esi dzoƒaɖe la de dzi tso vɔsamlekpuia dzi la, Yehowa ƒe dɔla la to vɔsamlekpuia ƒe dzoƒaɖea me yi dzi le Manoa kple srɔ̃a ŋkume wokpɔ. Eye wotsyɔ mo anyi enumake.
ENGLISH: 20 and as the flame went up off the altar to the sky, the Angel of Jehovah went up in the altar-flame, while Manoah and his wife looked on; and they threw themselves flat on their faces;

EWE: 21 Yehowa ƒe dɔla la megaɖe eɖokui fia Manoa kple srɔ̃a kpɔ o.
ENGLISH: 21 and the Angel of Jehovah never again appeared to Manoah and his wife.

EWE: Ale Manoa kpɔe dze sii be Yehowa ƒe dɔlae wònye.
ENGLISH: Then Manoah knew that it was the Angel of Jehovah.

EWE: 22 Eya ta Manoa gblɔ na srɔ̃a be: “Míaku godoo, elabena Mawue míekpɔ.”
ENGLISH: 22 And Manoah said to his wife “We must die, because we have seen God”;

EWE: 23 Ke srɔ̃a gblɔ nɛ be: “Ne ɖe Yehowa di be yeawu mí la, anye ne maxɔ numevɔsa kple nuɖuvɔsa la tso mía si o, maɖe nu siawo katã afia mí o, eye magblɔ nya siawo dometɔ aɖeke na mí o.”
ENGLISH: 23 but his wife said to him “If Jehovah chose to cause our death he would not have taken a burnt-offering and grain-offering at our hands, nor showed us these sights, not to say let us hear such a thing as this.”

EWE: 24 Emegbe nyɔnua dzi ŋutsuvi, eye wòna ŋkɔe be Samson; esi ŋutsuvia tsi la, Yehowa yrae.
ENGLISH: 24 And the woman had a son and named him Samson; and Jehovah blessed the boy as he grew up.

EWE: 25 Le ɣeyiɣi aɖe megbe la, Yehowa ƒe gbɔgbɔ de asi dɔwɔwɔ me ɖe edzi le Mahane-Dan si le Zora kple Estaol dome.
ENGLISH: 25 And the spirit of Jehovah began to stir him at Dan’s Camp, between Soreah and Eshtaol.

EWE: Ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo
ENGLISH: Judges

EWE: 14 Samson yi Timna, eye wòkpɔ Filisti-nyɔnu aɖe le Timna.
ENGLISH: 14 And Samson went down to Timnath; and at Timnath he saw a woman of a Philistine family,

EWE: 2 Eye wòyi ɖagblɔ na fofoa kple dadaa be: “Mekpɔ Filisti-nyɔnu aɖe le Timna, eye medi be miaɖee nam.”
ENGLISH: 2 and he came up and told his father and mother “At Timnath I saw a woman of a Philistine family; now get her for my wife.”

EWE: 3 Ke fofoa kple dadaa biae be: “Màte ŋu akpɔ nyɔnu aɖeke le wò ƒometɔwo kple míaƒe dukɔ bliboa dome aɖe oa? Ðe wòle be nàyi aɖaɖe srɔ̃ le Filistitɔ aʋamatsomatsotɔwo domea?”
ENGLISH: 3 And his father and mother said to him “Is there no such thing as a woman in your own family and in all your people, that you are going and getting a wife from the uncircumcised Philistines?”

EWE: Ke Samson gblɔ na fofoa be: “Ðee nam, elabe eya ƒe nue nyo ŋunye.”
ENGLISH: But Samson said to his father “Get me her, because she suits me”;

EWE: 4 Ke fofoa kple dadaa menya be Yehowa gbɔe esia tso, eye mɔnu dimee wòle le Filistitɔwo ŋu o, elabena Filistitɔwoe nɔ Israel dzi ɖum ɣemaɣi.
ENGLISH: 4 and his father and mother did not know that it was from Jehovah, because he was aiming to start a quarrel against the Philistines. (At that time the Philistines had the rule over Israel.)

EWE: 5 Ale Samson kple fofoa kpakple dadaa woyi Timna. Esi wòva ɖo Timna ƒe waingblewo me la, kpɔ ɖa, dzata aɖe le gbe tem va do goe.
ENGLISH: 5 And Samson and his father and mother went down to Timnath, and came to the Timnath vineyards, and he found a two-year-old lion that met him with a roar;

EWE: 6 Eye Yehowa ƒe gbɔgbɔ do ŋusẽe, eye wòtsɔ asi gbɔlo fee ɖe eve, abe ale si ko ame atsɔ asi gbɔlo afe gbɔ̃vi ɖe eve ene. Ke megblɔ nu si wòwɔ la na fofoa alo dadaa o.
ENGLISH: 6 and the spirit of Jehovah seized upon Samson, and he twisted its legs out of joint as one would with a kid, not having anything in his hand; but he did not tell his father and mother what he had done.

EWE: 7 Eye wòyi ɖaƒo nu kple nyɔnu la; eƒe nu ganyo Samson ŋu kokoko.
ENGLISH: 7 And Samson came down and had a talk with the woman, and she suited him.

EWE: 8 Esi wòtrɔ yina be yeakplɔ nyɔnua ava aƒee la, edze yi afi si dzata kukua le be yeakpɔe ɖa, eye wòkpɔ anyiwo kple anyitsi le dzata kukua me.
ENGLISH: 8 And after some days he came back to take her; and he turned off to see the remains of the lion, and found a swarm of bees in the lion’s body, and honey.

EWE: 9 Eya ta eha anyitsia ɖe asi me, eye wòle enyim le yiyim. Esi wòva tu fofoa kple dadaa la, ena ɖe wo wonyi. Ke megblɔ na wo be dzata kukua mee yeha anyitsia le o.
ENGLISH: 9 And he poked it out into his hands and ate it as he went along, and went to his father and mother and gave them some which they ate, but he did not tell them that it was out of the lion’s body he had gathered the honey.

EWE: 10 Fofoa yi nyɔnu la ƒe me, eye Samson ɖo kplɔ̃ le afi ma, elabena nenemae ɖekakpuiwo wɔna.
ENGLISH: 10 And his father went down to the woman, and Samson made a wassail (for that was the way the young men used to do);

EWE: 11 Esi wokpɔe la, woɖe ehati blaetɔ̃ be woanɔ eŋu.
ENGLISH: 11 and when they saw him they took thirty as comrades, and these were with him.

EWE: 12 Eye Samson gblɔ na wo be: “Meɖe kuku, mato adzo na mi. Ne mieɖe egɔme nam le kplɔ̃ɖoŋkeke adreawo me la, ekema matsɔ aklala biɖibiɖi wu blaetɔ̃ kple atsyɔ̃ɖowu blaetɔ̃ ana mi.
ENGLISH: 12 And Samson said to them “Let me put a riddle to you: if you tell, me the answer in the seven days of the wassail I will give you thirty linen undercloths and thirty dress cloaks,

EWE: 13 Ke ne miete ŋu ɖe egɔme nam o la, ekema miawo boŋ miana aklala biɖibiɖi wu blaetɔ̃ kple atsyɔ̃ɖowu blaetɔ̃m.
ENGLISH: 13 but if you cannot tell me you shall give me thirty linen undercloths and thirty dress cloaks.”

EWE: Woɖo eŋu nɛ be: “To wò adzo la na mí, míedi be míasee.”
ENGLISH: And they said to him “Put your riddle and let us hear it”;

EWE: 14 Eye wògblɔ na wo be: “Nuɖuɖu tso nuɖula me, Eye nu vivi tso ŋusẽtɔ me.”
ENGLISH: 14 and he said to them “Out of the eater came food, and out of mighty came sweet.”

EWE: Womete ŋu ɖe adzo la gɔme o ŋkeke etɔ̃ sɔŋ.
ENGLISH: And they could not answer the riddle in three days;

EWE: 15 Eye le ŋkeke enea gbe la, wogblɔ na Samson srɔ̃ be: “Ble srɔ̃wòa nu, ne wòaɖe adzoa gɔme na mí. Ne menye nenema o la, míatɔ dzo wò kple fofowò ƒe aƒe.
ENGLISH: 15 and on the seventh day they said to Samson’s wife “Inveigle your husband into telling us the answer, if you do not want us to burn you and your family; did you invite us here to beggar us?”

EWE: Ðe miekpe mí va afi sia be yewoaxɔ míaƒe nunɔamesiwoa?” 16 Eya ta Samson srɔ̃ fa avi nɛ gblɔ be: “Ðeko nèlé fum, mèlɔ̃m o. Èto adzo na mía deviwo, ke mèɖe egɔme nam o.”
ENGLISH: 16 And Samson’s wife sobbed at him and said “You just hate me, you do not love me: you have put the riddle to my fellow-countrymen and not told me the answer.”

EWE: Eɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, nyemeɖe egɔme na nye ŋutɔ fofonye kple danye gɔ̃ hã o.
ENGLISH: And he said to her “I have not told my father and mother, and am I to tell you?”

EWE: Ðe maɖe egɔme na wò ya?” 17 Ke enɔ avi fam nɛ le kplɔ̃ɖoŋkeke adreawo ƒe ŋkeke siwo susɔ la me. Mlɔeba le ŋkeke adrea gbe la, eɖe egɔme nɛ, elabena enɔ eƒom ɖe enu.
ENGLISH: 17 but she sobbed at him for the seven days that they held the wassail, and on the seventh day he told her because she nagged him so, and she told her fellow-countrymen;

EWE: Eye nyɔnua yi ɖaɖe adzo la gɔme na wo detɔwo. 18 Eya ta le ŋkeke adrea gbe, hafi ɣe naɖo to la, dua me ŋutsuwo va gblɔ nɛ be: “Nu kae vivina wu anyitsi, Eye nu kae sesẽ wu dzata?” Eɖo eŋu na wo be:
ENGLISH: 18 and the men of the city said to him on the seventh day before he had gone into the chamber “What is sweeter than honey? and what is mightier than a lion?”

EWE: “Ne menye nye nyinɔe mietsɔ ŋlɔ nui o la, Anye ne miete ŋu ɖe nye adzo la gɔme o.”
ENGLISH: And he said to them “If you had not plowed with my heifer you would not have found out my riddle.”

EWE: 19 Eye Yehowa ƒe gbɔgbɔ do ŋusẽe, eye wòyi Askelon ɖawu ŋutsu blaetɔ̃ hetsɔ awu siwo wòɖe le wo ŋu la na adzogɔmeɖelaawo.
ENGLISH: 19 (And the spirit of Jehovah seized upon him, and he went down to Ashkelon and killed thirty of the men there and took their spoils and gave the cloaks to those who had told the answer of the riddle.)

EWE: Eye wòdo dziku vevie hetrɔ dzo yi fofoa ƒe me.
ENGLISH: And he was angry and went up to his father’s home.

EWE: 20 Ke wotsɔ Samson srɔ̃ na ehati siwo nɔ eŋu le eƒe srɔ̃ɖegbea dometɔ ɖeka wòɖe.
ENGLISH: 20 And Samson’s wife became the wife of his comrade who had been best man to him.

EWE: Ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo
ENGLISH: Judges

EWE: 15 Ɣeyiɣi aɖe megbe le luxaɣi la, Samson tsɔ gbɔ̃vi aɖe ɖe asi yina srɔ̃a kpɔ ge ɖa. Egblɔ be: “Medi be mayi srɔ̃nye gbɔ le xɔgã me.”
ENGLISH: 15 And after a while, during the wheat harvest, Samson visited his wife with a kid, and said “I will go into the chamber to my wife”; but her father would not let him go in,

EWE: Ke nyɔnua fofo meɖe mɔ nɛ be wòage ɖe eme o. 2 Ke boŋ fofoa gblɔ be: “Mebu xaa be ɖe nèlé fui kura. Eya ta metsɔe na hawòti si nɔ ŋuwò le wò srɔ̃ɖegbea wòɖe.
ENGLISH: 2 but said “I declare I thought you positively hated her, and I gave her to your comrade; her younger sister is better anyhow have her instead.”

EWE: Meɖe kuku, ɖe eya boŋ.” 3 Ke Samson gblɔ na wo be: “Fifia ya Filistitɔwo mate ŋu abu fɔm ne mewɔ nu vevi wo o.”
ENGLISH: 3 And Samson said to them “This time the Philistines have nothing to complain of if I do them a mischief”;

EWE: 4 Eya ta Samson yi ɖalé abei alafa etɔ̃. Etsɔ akakati, eye wòlé abei eve ɖe sia ɖe ƒe asike kpe heblae, eye wòbla akakati ɖeka ɖe asike eve ɖe sia ɖe dome.
ENGLISH: 4 and Samson went and caught three hundred foxes, and took torches, and turned the foxes tail to tail and put a torch in the middle between every two tails,

EWE: 5 Esi dzo tɔ akakatiawo, eye wòɖe asi le abeiawo ŋu ɖo ɖe Filistitɔwo ƒe nukugblewo me.
ENGLISH: 5 and lighted the torches and turned them loose into the Philistines’ standing crops, and burned stack and standing crop and vineyard and olive-tree.

EWE: Etɔ dzo nu sia nu, nuku bablawo, nuku siwo le bo dzi, waingblewo kple amitibɔwo. 6 Filistitɔwo bia be: “Ame kae wɔ nu sia?” Woɖo eŋu na wo be: “Samson, Timnatɔ la ƒe toyɔvi ye, elabena toa tsɔ srɔ̃a na ehati si nɔ eŋu le eƒe srɔ̃ɖegbea wòɖe.”
ENGLISH: 6 And the Philistines said “Who did that?” and they said “It was Samson, that is son-in-law to the Timnathite, because he took his wife and gave her to his comrade”; and the Philistines came up and burned her and her family.

EWE: Eye Filistitɔwo yi ɖatɔ dzo nyɔnua kple fofoa. 7 Eye Samson gblɔ na wo be: “Ne aleae miewɔ la, mabia hlɔ̃ mi kokoko hafi adzudzɔ.”
ENGLISH: 7 And Samson said to them “O, but if you do things like that I will be revenged on you, and afterward I will let it drop”;

EWE: 8 Eye wòdza wo kɔ ɖi ɖekaɖeka hewu ame gbogbo aɖewo; emegbe edzo yi ɖanɔ Etam-gakpe la ƒe agado aɖe me.
ENGLISH: 8 and he smote them hip and thigh a great slaughter, and went down and lived in the cleft of ʽEtam Cliff.

EWE: 9 Emegbe Filistitɔwo ho va ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Yuda, eye wokaka ɖe Lehi.
ENGLISH: 9 And the Philistines came up and camped in Judah and forayed at the Jawbone;

EWE: 10 Eye Yuda ŋutsuwo bia wo be: “Nu ka ŋuti mieho ɖe mía ŋu?” Woɖo eŋu be: “Samson lé gee míeva, ne míawɔe abe ale si tututu wòwɔ míi ene.”
ENGLISH: 10 and the men of Judah said “Why have you come up against us?” and they said “We have come to tie up Samson, to do to him as he did to us.”

EWE: 11 Eya ta Yuda ŋutsu akpe etɔ̃ yi ɖe Etam-gakpe la ƒe agado la me hebia Samson be: “Mènya be Filistitɔwoe le mía dzi ɖum oa? Ke nu ka tae nèwɔ nu sia ɖe mía ŋu?”
ENGLISH: 11 And three thousand men of Judah went down to the cleft of ʽEtam Cliff and said to Samson “Do you not know that the Philistines have the rule over us? what is this you have done to us?”

EWE: Eɖo eŋu na wo be: “Ale si tututu wowɔm la, nenemae mewɔ wo.”
ENGLISH: And he said to them “As they did to me, so I did to them.”

EWE: 12 Ke wogblɔ nɛ be: “Ðe míeva be míalé wò ade asi na Filistitɔwo.”
ENGLISH: 12 And they said to him “We have come to tie you up, to give you into the hands of the Philistines.”

EWE: Eye Samson gblɔ na wo be: “Mika atam nam be miawo ŋutɔwo miate kpɔ be yewoawɔ nu vevim o.”
ENGLISH: And Samson said to them “Swear to me that you will not cut me down yourselves”;

EWE: 13 Wogblɔ nɛ be: “Ao, ke boŋ ɖeko míabla wò atsɔ ade asi na wo; ke míawu wò o.”
ENGLISH: 13 and they said to him “No, but tie you up and give you into their hands; we will not kill you.”

EWE: Ale wotsɔ ka yeye eve blae hekplɔe do goe tso agado la me.
ENGLISH: And they tied him up with two new ropes and brought him up from the Cliff.

EWE: 14 Esi wòva ɖo Lehi la, Filistitɔwo tso aseye esi wokpɔe. Eye Yehowa ƒe gbɔgbɔ do ŋusẽe, ale be ka siwo le eƒe alɔwo zu abe ɖetika siwo dzo ƒo ene, eye wotso le eƒe alɔnu.
ENGLISH: 14 He had come to Jawbone, and the Philistines had come cheering to meet him, when the spirit of Jehovah seized upon him and the ropes on his arms became like burned-up flax, and his fastenings melted off from his wrists;

EWE: 15 Ekpɔ tedzitsu ƒe glãƒu mumu aɖe; edo asi ɖa tsɔe wu ŋutsu akpe ɖeka.
ENGLISH: 15 and he found a fresh jawbone of a donkey, and reached for it and got it and killed a thousand men with it.

EWE: 16 Eye Samson gblɔ be: “Tedzitsu ƒe glãƒue metsɔ wu wo li kɔ ɖi gleglegle! Tedzitsu ƒe glãƒue metsɔ wu ame akpe ɖeka.”
ENGLISH: 16 And Samson said “With a beast’s jawbone I have been their bane! with a beast’s jawbone killed a thousand men!”

EWE: 17 Eye esi wògblɔ nya siawo vɔ ko la, etsɔ glãƒu la ƒu gbe, eye wòna ŋkɔ teƒea be Ramat-Lehi.
ENGLISH: 17 And when he had said it he dropped the jawbone from his hand; and they call the place Jawbone Fell.

EWE: 18 Ke tsikɔ wui vevie, eye wòyɔ Yehowa gblɔ be: “Wòe tsɔ ɖeɖe gã sia to wò subɔla dzi. Ke azɔ la, ɖe tsikɔ awum maku, eye mage ɖe aʋamatsomatsotɔwo si mea?”
ENGLISH: 18 And he was very thirsty, and called to Jehovah “You have given this great victory into your servant’s hands, and now I shall die with thirst and fall into the hands of the uncircumcised”;

EWE: 19 Eye Mawu fe teƒe aɖe si nyé ɖe eme le Lehi, eye tsi do tso afi ma. Esi wònoe la, ŋusẽ ɖo eŋu, eye agbe gaɖo eme.
ENGLISH: 19 and God ripped open the hollow in the Jawbone, and water came out, and he took a drink, and his spirit came back and he revived.

EWE: Esia tae wòna ŋkɔ teƒea be En-Hakore, si le Lehi va se ɖe egbe sia.
ENGLISH: For this reason it is named Caller Spring, the one that is in the Jawbone to this day.

EWE: 20 Edrɔ̃ ʋɔnu na Israel le Filistitɔwo ŋɔli ƒe blaeve.
ENGLISH: 20 And he judged Israel, in the days of the Philistines, twenty years.

EWE: Ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo
ENGLISH: Judges

EWE: 16 Gbe ɖeka Samson yi Gaza, ekpɔ gbolo aɖe le afi ma, eye wòyi egbɔ.
ENGLISH: 16 And Samson went from there to Ghaza, and saw a prostitute there and went in to her;

EWE: 2 Wova gblɔ na Gazatɔwo be: “Samson va afi sia.” Eya ta woɖe to ɖe teƒea hede xa ɖi nɛ zã bliboa katã le dua ƒe agbo nu.
ENGLISH: 2 and the Ghazites were told “Samson has come here,” and they came around and lay in ambush for him all night at the city gate, and kept quiet all night, saying “Till morning daylight, and we will kill him!”

EWE: Wozi ɖoɖoe zã bliboa katã hegblɔ na wo nɔewo be: “Ne ŋu ke la, míawui.” 3 Ke Samson mlɔ anyi va se ɖe zã titina. Efɔ le zã titina eye wòho du la ƒe agbo kple agbo la ƒe ati eveawo hekpe ɖe gameti la ŋu. Ekɔ wo ɖe abɔta yi to si dze ŋgɔ Hebron la tame.
ENGLISH: 3 But Samson lay abed till midnight, and got up at midnight and took hold of the city gates and the two gateposts and pulled them up bar and all, and put them on his shoulders and took them up to the top of the mountain facing Hebron on the east.

EWE: 4 Le ema megbe la, nyɔnu aɖe si le Sorek Bali me, si ŋkɔe nye Delila la ƒe nu lé dzi nɛ.
ENGLISH: 4 And after that he fell in love with a woman in Sorek Arroyo, whose name was Delilah.

EWE: 5 Eya ta Filistitɔwo ƒe kplɔlawo va nyɔnua gbɔ gblɔ nɛ be: “Ble enu nàdze si nu si naa ŋusẽ triakɔ ma gbegbee kple ale si míawɔ akpe edzi ablae ahabɔbɔe ɖe anyi. Eye mía dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe ana klosalo akpe ɖeka alafa ɖeka wò ɖe esia ta.”
ENGLISH: 5 And the Sarns of the Philistines came up to her and said to her “Inveigle him and see by what means he has the great strength, and by what means we may master him and tie him so as to tame him, and we will each give you eleven hundred shekels of silver.”

EWE: 6 Emegbe Delila gblɔ na Samson be: “Meɖe kuku, gblɔ afi si nèkpɔ wò ŋusẽ gã la tsoe kple nu si woate ŋu atsɔ abla wò abɔbɔ wò ɖe anyi la nam.”
ENGLISH: 6 And Delilah said to Samson “Tell me by what means you have the great strength, and by what means you might be tied up so as to tame you.”

EWE: 7 Samson gblɔ nɛ be: “Ne wotsɔ datimeka mumu adre siwo meƒu haɖe o blam la, magbɔdzɔ azu abe ame bubuwo ke ene.”
ENGLISH: 7 And Samson said to her “If they tie me up with seven fresh undried bowstrings I shall weaken and be like any man.”

EWE: 8 Eya ta Filistitɔwo ƒe kplɔlawo tsɔ datimeka mumu adre siwo meƒu o la vɛ nɛ, eye wòtsɔ wo blae.
ENGLISH: 8 And the Sarns of the Philistines brought up to her seven fresh undried bowstrings, and she tied him with them,

EWE: 9 Azɔ wode xa ɖe xɔgã me, eye wòdo ɣli gblɔ nɛ be: “Samson, Filistitɔwo ƒo ɖe dziwò loo!” Kasia etso datimekawo abe ale si ko ɖetika tsona bɔbɔe ne dzo ƒoe ene.
ENGLISH: 9 while she had the ambuscade waiting in the chamber; and she said to him “The Philistines are on you, Samson!” and he broke the bowstrings as a strand of tow breaks when it scents fire, and his strength was not found out.

EWE: Eye womete ŋu nya eƒe ŋusẽ la tsoƒe o. 10 Emegbe Delila gblɔ na Samson be: “Kpɔ ɖa! èflum, eye nèda alakpa nam.
ENGLISH: 10 And Delilah said to Samson “Here you have been trifling with me and telling me lies; now tell me by what means you might be tied up.”

EWE: 11 Eye wògblɔ nɛ be: “Ne wotsɔ ka yeye siwo wometsɔ wɔ dɔ aɖeke kpɔ o blam la, magbɔdzɔ azu abe ame bubuwo ke ene.”
ENGLISH: 11 And he said to her “If they tie me with new ropes that have never been used, I shall weaken and be like any man.”

EWE: 12 Eya ta Delila tsɔ ka yeyewo blae, eye wògblɔ be: “Samson, Filistitɔwo ƒo ɖe dziwò loo!” (Ɣemaɣi katã la, wode xa ɖe xɔgã me nɛ.) Eye wòtso kaawo le abɔ abe ka lɛ aɖe ko ene.
ENGLISH: 12 And Delilah took new ropes and tied him with them, and said to him “The Philistines are on you, Samson!” while the ambuscade was waiting in the chamber; and he broke them off his arms like a thread.

EWE: 13 Esia megbe la, Delila gblɔ na Samson be: “Èdo movitɔm eye nèda alakpa nam va se ɖe fifi.
ENGLISH: 13 And Delilah said to Samson “You have kept on trifling with me and telling me lies; tell me by what means you might be tied up.”

EWE: Gblɔ nu si woate ŋu atsɔ abla wò la nam.” Eye wògblɔ nɛ be: “Ne ètsɔ avɔlɔ̃ka lɔ̃ ɖakɔ gbigbi adre siwo le ta nam.”
ENGLISH: And he said to her “If you weave the seven braids of hair on my head in with your cloth and drive them down with the stick, I shall weaken and be like any man.”

EWE: 14 Eya ta etsɔ agbatrɔti trɔ ɖakɔawo, eye wògblɔ nɛ be: “Samson, Filistitɔwo ƒo ɖe dziwò loo!”
ENGLISH: 14 And she put him to sleep and wove the seven braids of hair on his head in with her cloth and drove them down with the stick, and said to him “The Philistines are on you, Samson!” and he woke from his sleep and pulled up the stick, the loom and the cloth; and his strength was not found out.

EWE: Ale wòfɔ tso alɔ̃ me heho agbatrɔti la kple avɔlɔ̃ka la. 15 Eye wògblɔ nɛ be: “Aleke wɔ nèbe, ‘yelɔ̃m’ evɔ wò dzi meku ɖe ŋunye o? Zi etɔ̃ sɔŋ nèflum, eye mègblɔ afi si wò ŋusẽ triakɔ la tso nam o.”
ENGLISH: 15 And she said to him “How is it you say ‘I love you’ and do not take me into your confidence? this is three times you have trifled with me and not told me by what means you have the great strength”;

EWE: 16 Esi wòɖea fu nɛ atraɖii, eye wòƒoa nya ɖe enu gbe sia gbe ta la, eva gloe wòdi be yeaku boŋ.
ENGLISH: 16 and when she nagged him with her talk every day and kept the screws on him, he was ready to die with impatience,

EWE: 17 Eya ta egblɔ eƒe dzimenya nɛ be: “Talũhɛ meka nye ta ŋu kpɔ o, elabena Mawu ƒe Naziritɔ menye tso gbe si gbe wodzim. Ne wolũ ta nam la, ekema nye ŋusẽ la ado le menye, eye magbɔdzɔ azu abe ame bubuwo ke ene.”
ENGLISH: 17 and he made a clean breast of it and said to her “No razor has gone over my head, because I have been God’s devotee from my birth; if I am shaved my strength will leave me, and I shall weaken and become like everybody.”

EWE: 18 Esi Delila kpɔ be egblɔ eƒe dzimenya na ye la, edɔ ame enumake be woaɖayɔ Filistitɔwo ƒe kplɔlawo vɛ, eye wògblɔ be: “Miva azɔ, elabena egblɔ eƒe dzimenya nam.”
ENGLISH: 18 And Delilah saw that he had made a clean breast of it, and she sent for the Sarns of the Philistines, saying “This time come up; he has made a clean breast of it”; and the Sarns of the Philistines came up to her, and brought the money up with them.

EWE: Ale Filistitɔwo ƒe kplɔlawo va egbɔ, eye wotsɔ ga la ɖe asi vɛ. 19 Ena wòdɔ alɔ̃ ɖe eƒe ata dzi; eye wòyɔ ŋutsu aɖe wòva lũ ɖakɔ adre siwo le ta nɛ.
ENGLISH: 19 And she put him to sleep in her embrace, and called the man, and shaved off the seven braids of hair on his head, and he began to grow tame, and his strength left him.

EWE: Esia megbe la, nyɔnu la nɔ ŋusẽ kpɔm ɖe edzi, elabena eƒe ŋusẽ la le dodom le eme. 20 Eye wòdo ɣli gblɔ be: “Samson, Filistitɔwo ƒo ɖe dziwò loo!” Enyɔ tso alɔ̃ me gblɔ be: “Mado go abe tsã ene, eye maʋuʋu ɖokuinye avo.”
ENGLISH: 20 And she said “The Philistines are on you, Samson!” and he woke up from his sleep and thought “I shall come off as I did the other times, I shall shake myself loose,” not knowing that his strength had left him.

EWE: Ke menya be Yehowa dzo le ye gbɔ o. 21 Eye Filistitɔwo lée ho eƒe ŋkuwo le to me nɛ. Wokplɔe yi Gaza hede akɔblikunyowu evee, eye wòzu wɔtula le gaxɔ me.
ENGLISH: 21 And the Philistines took hold of him and put out his eyes, and brought him down to Ghaza and put him in irons, and he became a grinder in the prison.

EWE: 22 Ke esi wolũ ta nɛ megbe la, eƒe ɖa gade asi toto me.
ENGLISH: 22 But the hair on his head began to grow as soon as it had been shaved.

EWE: 23 Filistitɔwo ƒe kplɔlawo ƒo ƒu be yewoasa vɔ gã aɖe na yewoƒe mawu Dagon ahatu aglo, elabena wogblɔ be: “Mía mawu tsɔ míaƒe futɔ Samson de asi na mí!” 24 Esi dukɔ la kpɔe la, wokafu woƒe mawu la be: “Mía mawu tsɔ míaƒe futɔ, ame si gblẽ míaƒe anyigba eye wòwu míaƒe ame gbogbo aɖewo la de asi na mí.”
ENGLISH: 23 And the Sarns of the Philistines came together to offer a great sacrifice to their god Dagon and to hold festival, and thought “Our god has given our enemy Samson into our hands”; 24 and the people saw him and praised their god, because, they said, “Our god has given our enemy into our hands, him who made many our dead and laid waste our lands.”

EWE: 25 Esi woƒe dzi le dzidzɔ kpɔm ta la, wogblɔ be: “Miyɔ Samson vɛ ne wòado nukokoe na mí.”
ENGLISH: 25 And when they were jolly they said “Call Samson to give us an exhibition.”

EWE: Ale woyɔ Samson tso gaxɔ la me vɛ be wòaɖe modzaka na yewo; eye wona wòtɔ ɖe sɔtiawo dome.
ENGLISH: And they summoned Samson out of the prison, and he gave an entertainment before them; and they had him stand between the pillars.

EWE: 26 Eye Samson gblɔ na ŋutsuvi si lé eƒe asi le ekplɔm la be: “Na malé sɔti siwo dzi xɔa le la, ne maziɔ ɖe wo ŋu.”
ENGLISH: 26 And Samson said to the young man who held him by the hand “Put me so that I can feel for the pillars the house is supported on and find them, to lean on them,”

EWE: 27 (Ke ŋutsuwo kple nyɔnuwo yɔ xɔ la taŋ. Filistitɔwo ƒe kplɔlawo katã le afi ma, eye ŋutsu kple nyɔnu siwo ade akpe etɔ̃ la le xɔa ta le Samson ƒe nukokoedoname la kpɔm.)
ENGLISH: 27 the house being full of the men and women (and all the Sarns of the Philistine being there, and on the roof about three thousand men and women) who were looking on while Samson gave his exhibition.

EWE: 28 Eye Samson yɔ Yehowa gblɔ be: “Aƒetɔ Dziɖulagã Yehowa, meɖe kuku ɖo ŋku dzinye; Oo Mawu, meɖe kuku do ŋusẽm zi ɖeka sia ko, eye na mabia hlɔ̃ Filistitɔwo ɖe nye ŋku eveawo dometɔ ɖeka ta.”
ENGLISH: 28 And Samson called to Jehovah “Lord Jehovah, remember me and strengthen me just this once, God, so that I may take my revenge on the Philistines for one of my two eyes”;

EWE: 29 Ale Samson lé titinasɔti eve siwo dzi xɔa le la goŋgoŋ, eƒe ɖusi le ɖeka ŋu, eye eƒe miasi le evelia ŋu.
ENGLISH: 29 and Samson twisted the two middle pillars that the house was supported on, and braced himself against them one with his right hand and one with his left.

EWE: 30 Eye Samson do ɣli be: “Maku kple Filistitɔwo!”
ENGLISH: 30 And Samson said “Die myself with the Philistines!” and gave a hard lunge, and down fell the house on the Sarns and on all the people in it.

EWE: Eye wòtutu wo kple eƒe ŋusẽ katã, eye xɔ la mu dze kplɔlaawo kple ame siwo katã le xɔa me la dzi.
ENGLISH: And there were more dead that he had killed at his death than that he had killed in his life.

EWE: Ale wòwu ame geɖe le eƒe kuɣi wu ame siwo wòwu le eƒe agbenɔɣi. 31 Emegbe nɔviawo kple fofoa ƒe ƒometɔwo katã va kɔe dzoe.
ENGLISH: 31 And his brothers and all his family went down and brought him away, and buried him up between Soreah and Eshtaol in the grave of his father Manoah.

EWE: Edrɔ̃ ʋɔnu na Israel ƒe blaeve.
ENGLISH: And he had judged Israel twenty years.

EWE: Ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo
ENGLISH: Judges

EWE: 17 Ŋutsu aɖe tso Efrayim tonuto la me, si ŋkɔe nye Mika.
ENGLISH: 17 Now there was a man of the highland of Ephraim, named Micah:

EWE: 2 Egblɔ na dadaa be: “Wò klosalo akpe ɖeka alafa ɖeka si wotsɔ, eye nèdo ɖiŋu ɖe eŋu mese la, kpɔ ɖa, klosalo la le gbɔnye. Nyee tsɔe.”
ENGLISH: 2 and he said to his mother “The eleven hundred shekels of silver that were taken from you, and you pronounced a curse and said things in my hearing the silver is with me: it was I that took it.”

EWE: Eye dadaa gblɔ be: “Yehowa neyra vinye la.”
ENGLISH: And his mother said “Jehovah bless my son!”

EWE: 3 Ale wògbugbɔ klosalo akpe ɖeka alafa ɖeka la na dadaa, gake dadaa gblɔ be: “Makɔ klosalo si le asinye la ŋu na Yehowa hena vinye la, ne woatsɔe awɔ nu kpakpɛ kple galegba.
ENGLISH: 3 And he returned the eleven hundred shekels of silver to his mother; and his mother said “I hereby dedicate the silver to Jehovah, from my hands exclusively, to make a statue; and now I will return it to you.”

EWE: Azɔ megbugbɔe na wò.” 4 Esi wògbugbɔ klosalo la na dadaa la, dadaa ɖe klosalo alafa eve tsɔ na klosalonutula. Etsɔe wɔ nu kpakpɛ kple galegba; eye wotsɔ wo da ɖe Mika ƒe me.
ENGLISH: 4 And he returned the silver to his mother; and his mother took two hundred shekels of silver and gave it to a silversmith, and he made it into a statue, which was at Micah’s home.

EWE: 5 Mawuxɔ aɖe le Mika si, eye wòwɔ kɔmewu kple terafim legbawo heɖo viaŋutsuwo dometɔ ɖeka be wòanye nunɔla na ye.
ENGLISH: 5 And the man Micah had a chapel, and made an ephod and teraphim, and installed one of his sons, who became priest to him.

EWE: 6 Le ŋkeke mawo me la, fia aɖeke menɔ Israel o.
ENGLISH: 6 In those days there was no king in Israel: each did what suited him.

EWE: Ame sia ame wɔa nu si sɔ le eya ŋutɔ ŋkume. 7 Ðekakpui aɖe tso Betlehem le Yuda, eye wòtso Yuda ƒomea me.
ENGLISH: 7 And there was a youth from Bethlehem in Judah, of the clan of Judah, who was a Levite, and he was living there as an immigrant;

EWE: Enye Lewitɔ va nɔ afi ma vie. 8 Ðekakpui la dzo le Betlehem, le Yuda, be yeayi aɖadi teƒe aɖe anɔ.
ENGLISH: 8 and the man went from the city, from Bethlehem in Judah, to settle as an immigrant wherever he found an opening.

EWE: Ezɔ mɔ va ɖo Mika ƒe aƒe gbɔ le Efrayim tonuto la me.
ENGLISH: And he came to the highland of Ephraim, to Micah’s home, on his errand;

EWE: 9 Eye Mika biae be: “Afi kae nètso?” Eɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Lewitɔ menye tso Betlehem le Yuda, eye meyina be maɖadi teƒe aɖe anɔ.”
ENGLISH: 9 and Micah said to him “Where do you come from?” and he said to him “I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah, and I am out to settle as an immigrant wherever I find an opening.”

EWE: 10 Eye Mika gblɔ nɛ be: “Tsi gbɔnye, nànye fofo kple nunɔla nam, eye mana klosalo ewo wò ƒe sia ƒe hekpe ɖe nudodo kple nuɖuɖu ŋu.” Ale Lewitɔ la ge ɖe eme.
ENGLISH: 10 And Micah said to him “Stay with me and be father and priest to me, and I will give you ten shekels of silver a year and a suit of clothes and your board”; and the Levite went.

EWE: 11 Lewitɔ la lɔ̃ be yeatsi ŋutsua gbɔ, eye ɖekakpui la va zu abe viawo dometɔ ɖeka ene.
ENGLISH: 11 And the Levite consented to stay with the man; and the youth became like one of his sons to him.

EWE: 12 Eye Mika ɖo Lewitɔ la be wòanye nunɔla na ye, eye wònɔ Mika ƒe me.
ENGLISH: 12 And Micah installed the Levite, and the youth became priest to him, and was in Micah’s house.

EWE: 13 Eya ta Mika gblɔ be: “Azɔ menyae nyuie be Yehowa awɔ nyui nam, elabena Lewitɔ la zu nunɔla nam.”
ENGLISH: 13 And Micah said “Now I know that Jehovah will do well by me, since I have got the Levite for priest.”

EWE: Ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo
ENGLISH: Judges

EWE: 18 Le ŋkeke mawo me la, fia aɖeke menɔ Israel o.
ENGLISH: 18 In those days there was no king in Israel.

EWE: Ɣemaɣi la, Dan viwo ƒe to la le anyigba dim, ne woanɔ edzi; elabena va se ɖe ɣemaɣi la, womexɔ domenyinu le Israel-toawo dome o.
ENGLISH: And in those days the Danite tribe was looking for a domain to live in, because till that day nothing had fallen to them as a domain among the tribes of Israel;

EWE: 2 Dan viwo dɔ woƒe ƒomea me tɔ atɔ̃, siwo nye ŋutsu kalẽtɔwo tso Zora kple Estaol, be woayi aɖatsa le anyigba la dzi ahatsa ŋku le edzi. Eye wogblɔ na wo be: “Miheyi ɖatsa le anyigba la dzi.”
ENGLISH: 2 and the children of Dan sent out of their clan five men of all classes, stalwart men from Soreah and Eshtaol, to spy around the country and to examine it, and said to them “Go examine the country”; and they came to Micah’s home in the highland of Ephraim and spent the night there.

EWE: Esi wova ɖo Mika ƒe me le Efrayim tonutoa me la, wotsi afi ma dɔ. 3 Esi wogogo Mika ƒe aƒea la, wodze si ɖekakpui Lewitɔ la ƒe gbe, eya ta woyi egbɔ ɖabiae be: “Ame kae kplɔ wò va afi sia? Nu ka wɔm nèle le teƒe sia?
ENGLISH: 3 They had come opposite Micah’s house when they recognized the Levite youth’s voice and turned in there, and said to him “Who brought you here? what are you doing in these parts? what are you here for?”

EWE: Nu kae na nèva tsi afi sia?” 4 Eɖo eŋu na wo be: “Ale kple ale Mika wɔ nam, eye wòxɔm be manye nunɔla na ye.”
ENGLISH: 4 And he said to them “Micah has done such things for me, and he has hired me to be priest to him.”

EWE: 5 Eye wogblɔ nɛ be: “Míeɖe kuku, bia gbe Mawu kpɔ be mɔ si dzi míele la adze edzi hã.”
ENGLISH: 5 And they said to him “Put the question to God to let us know whether our errand that we are going on will be successful.”

EWE: 6 Eye nunɔla la gblɔ na wo be: “Miheyi le ŋutifafa me.
ENGLISH: 6 And the priest said to them “Go, and good betide you; your errand that you are on is under Jehovah’s eye.”

EWE: Yehowa li kpli mi le miaƒe mɔzɔzɔ la me.” 7 Ale ŋutsu atɔ̃awo yi mɔzɔzɔa dzi va ɖo Lais. Wokpɔ ale si dua me nɔlawo le wo ɖokui si, abe ale si ko Sidontɔwo le ene. Wole tomefafa me heɖe dzi ɖi, eye dziɖula ŋutasẽla aɖeke meva ɖe fu na wo le anyigba la dzi kpɔ o.
ENGLISH: 7 And the five men went on, and came to Laish, and saw the people in it, living off its guard in Phenician fashion, at rest and off their guard, with no one in the country to balk anything, no holder of sway, and they far away from the Phenicians and having no relations with Syria.

EWE: 8 Esi wotrɔ va wo nɔviwo gbɔ le Zora kple Estaol la, wo nɔviawo bia wo be: “Aleke miedee?”
ENGLISH: 8 And they came to their brothers at Soreah and Eshtaol, and their brothers said to them “What is your word?”

EWE: 9 Woɖo eŋu be: “Mina míaho ɖe wo ŋu, elabena míekpɔ be anyigba la nyo ŋutɔ. Nu ka tae miele hehem ɖe megbe?
ENGLISH: 9 and they said “Come on, let us go up against them; for we have seen the city and found it very good; and you are lying still! do not be slack about going to enter and take possession of the country.

EWE: Netsɔ, miyi anyigba la dzi ne miaxɔe wòazu mia tɔ. 10 Ne mieyi la, miakpɔe be dukɔ la ɖe dzi ɖi, eye anyigba la keke ŋutɔ. Mawu tsɔe de asi na mi, enye teƒe si anyigbadzinu ɖe sia ɖe le.”
ENGLISH: 10 When you come you will come to a people off their guard, plenty of elbowroom in their country, because God has given it into your hands: a place where there is no lack of anything the country produces.”

EWE: 11 Ale Dan viwo ƒe ƒomea me ŋutsu alafa ade bla aʋakpa, eye wodze mɔ tso Zora kple Estaol.
ENGLISH: 11 And six hundred men of the Danite clan from Soreah and Eshtaol set out from there in fighting outfit,

EWE: 12 Woyi ɖaƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Kiriat-Yearim le Yuda. Esia tae woyɔa teƒe ma si le Kiriat-Yearim ƒe ɣetoɖoƒe la be Mahane-Dan va se ɖe egbe.
ENGLISH: 12 and went up and camped at Kirjath-Jeʽarim in Judah: that place has consequently been called Dan’s Camp to this day; it lies west of Kirjath-Jeʽarim.

EWE: 13 Woho tso afi ma yi Efrayim tonuto la me, eye wova Mika ƒe aƒe gbɔ.
ENGLISH: 13 And from there they crossed over to the highland of Ephraim, and came to Micah’s home;

EWE: 14 Eye ŋutsu atɔ̃ siwo yi ɖatsa ŋku le Lais-nyigba dzi la gblɔ na wo nɔviwo be: “Mienya be kɔmewu, terafiwo, nu kpakpɛ kple galegba le aƒe siawo mea? Mibu nu si miawɔ la ŋu.”
ENGLISH: 14 and the five men who had gone to spy around the country (Laish) spoke up and said to their brothers “Do you know that in these houses there is an ephod and teraphim and a statue? now make up your minds what you will do.”

EWE: 15 Ale wotɔ ɖe afi ma eye woyi ɖekakpui Lewitɔ la gbɔ le Mika ƒe me, eye wobia eƒe fɔfɔme ta se.
ENGLISH: 15 And they turned in there and went into the Levite youth’s house, Micah’s home, and asked him how he did;

EWE: 16 Ɣemaɣi la, Dan-ŋutsu alafa ade siwo bla aʋakpa la tɔ ɖe agboa nu.
ENGLISH: 16 and while six hundred men in fighting outfit stood at the gate of the place, who belonged to the sons of Dan,

EWE: 17 Eye ŋutsu atɔ̃ siwo yi ɖatsa ŋku le anyigbaa dzi la ge ɖe aƒea me ɖatsɔ nu kpakpɛ la, kɔmewu la, terafim legbaawo kple galegba la. (Nunɔlaa kple ŋutsu alafa ade siwo bla aʋakpa la tɔ ɖe agboa nu.)
ENGLISH: 17 up went the five men who had gone to spy around the country, went in there, took the statue and the ephod and the teraphim, the priest standing at the gate of the place, and the six hundred men in fighting outfit:

EWE: 18 Woge ɖe Mika ƒe me ɖatsɔ nu kpakpɛa, kɔmewua kple terafiawo kpakple legba si wokɔ̀ la.
ENGLISH: 18 those went into Micah’s home and took the statue, the ephod, and the teraphim.

EWE: Eye nunɔla la bia wo be: “Nu ka wɔm miele?”
ENGLISH: And the priest said to them “What are you doing?”

EWE: 19 Ke wogblɔ nɛ be: “Zi ɖoɖoe. Tsyɔ asi nu, eye nàyi kpli mí azu fofo kple nunɔla na mí. Kae nyo wu, be nànye nunɔla na ame ɖeka ƒe aƒe loo alo be nàzu nunɔla na to kple ƒome blibo le Israel?”
ENGLISH: 19 and they said to him “Be still, put your hand over your mouth and go with us and be father and priest to us: is it better for you to be priest to one man’s house or for you to be priest to a tribe and clan in Israel?”

EWE: 20 Esia dze nunɔla la ŋu, ale wòtsɔ kɔmewua kple terafiam legbaawo kpakple nu kpakpɛa, eye wòyi kple dukɔ la.
ENGLISH: 20 And the priest was in high glee, and he took the ephod and the teraphim and the statue and went into the midst of the people.

EWE: 21 Ale wotrɔ be yewoayi mɔzɔzɔa dzi, wona wo viwo kple lãhawo kpakple nu veviwo dze wo ŋgɔ.
ENGLISH: 21 And they turned and went, putting the women and children and the stock and the goods in front.

EWE: 22 Esi wogblẽ Mika ƒe aƒe la ɖe megbe sãa la, ŋutsu siwo nye Mika ƒe aƒelikawo ƒo ƒu, eye wodze Dan viwo yome ɖatu wo.
ENGLISH: 22 They had got to some distance from Micah’s home when the men in the houses near Micah’s came out in arms and overtook the sons of Dan,

EWE: 23 Esi wodo ɣli yɔ Dan viwo la, wotrɔ dze ŋgɔ wo eye wobia Mika be: “Nya kae dzɔ?
ENGLISH: 23 and they called out to the sons of Dan and they faced about and said to Micah “What is the matter, that you have come out in arms?”

EWE: Nu ka tae nèƒo amewo nu ƒu?” 24 Eɖo eŋu be: “Mietsɔ nye mawu siwo mewɔ la, eye miekplɔ nunɔla hã dzo yina. Ke nu kae gasusɔ nam?
ENGLISH: 24 And he said “You have taken my gods that I made, and the priest, and gone off with them; what more have I? what do you mean by saying to me ‘What is the matter?’”

EWE: Aleke wɔ miele biayem be, ‘Nya kae dzɔ ɖe dziwò’ mahã?” 25 Dan viwo ɖo eŋu be: “Mègado ɣli ɖe mía ta o; ne menye nenema o la, ŋutsu siwo do dɔmedzoe la adze mia dzi, eye esia ana nàbu wò agbe kple wò aƒemetɔwo ƒe agbe.”
ENGLISH: 25 And the sons of Dan said to him “Do not let your voice be heard around us, for fear some fellows with bad tempers should get after you, and you should make away with your life and the lives of your family”;

EWE: 26 Eye Dan viwo galé woƒe mɔ; ke esi Mika kpɔe be wosesẽ wu ye la, etrɔ yi aƒe me.
ENGLISH: 26 and the sons of Dan went on their way. And Micah saw that they were too strong for him, and he turned and went back home,

EWE: 27 Esi wotsɔ nu siwo Mika wɔ, eye wokplɔ eƒe nunɔla la dzoe vɔ la, woyi Lais le dukɔ si li le tomefafa me heɖe dzi ɖi la gbɔ. Wowu wo kple yi, eye wotɔ dzo du la.
ENGLISH: 27 while they took that Micah had made and the priest that he had had and came on Laish, on a people at rest and off their guard, and massacred them and burned down the city;

EWE: 28 Ame aɖeke meli axɔ na wo o, elabena wo gbɔ didi tso Sidon, kadodo mele wo kple dukɔ bubu aɖeke dome o, eye du la le Bet-Rehob Bali la me.
ENGLISH: 28 and there was no rescuer because they were far away from Sidon and had no relations with Syria, though it was in the vale that belongs to Beth-Rehob.

EWE: Eye wogbugbɔ du la tso henɔ eme. 29 Azɔ hã, wona ŋkɔ du la be Dan le wo fofo Dan, si wodzi na Israel la, ƒe ŋkɔ nu. Ke tsã la woyɔa du la be Lais.
ENGLISH: 29 And they rebuilt the city and lived in it, and named the city Dan after Dan their ancestor; but Laish was the name of the city originally.

EWE: 30 Emegbe Dan viwo li nu kpakpɛ la na wo ɖokui, eye Yonatan, si nye Mose vi Gersom ƒe vi kple viaŋutsuwo va zu nunɔlawo na Dan viwo ƒe to la, va se ɖe ŋkeke si dzi wokplɔ anyigba la dzi nɔlawo yi aboyo me.
ENGLISH: 30 And the sons of Dan set the statue up for themselves, and Jonathan the son of Gershom the son of Moses, he and his descendants, were priests to the Danite tribe till the day of the deportation of the country.

EWE: 31 Eye woli nu kpakpɛ si Mika wɔ la ɖe afi ma le ŋkeke siwo katã me Mawu vavã la ƒe aƒe la nɔ Silo.
ENGLISH: 31 And they put up for themselves Micah’s statue that he had made, all the time the house of God was at Shiloh.

EWE: Ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo
ENGLISH: Judges

EWE: 19 Le ŋkeke mawo me, esi fia aɖeke menɔ Israel o la, Lewitɔ aɖe si nɔ Efrayim tonuto la ƒe nutotroewo me ɣemaɣi dze ahiã ɖetugbui aɖe si tso Betlehem le Yuda la.
ENGLISH: 19 And in those days, there being no king in Israel, there was a certain Levite living as an immigrant far back in the highlands of Ephraim, and he took as his concubine a woman from Bethlehem in Judah.

EWE: 2 Gake eƒe ahiãvi la mewɔ nuteƒe nɛ o, eye wòdzo le ŋutsua gbɔ ɖanɔ fofoa ƒe me le Betlehem le Yuda.
ENGLISH: 2 And his concubine got into a rage at him, and went from him to her father’s home at Bethlehem in Judah and was there a while, four months.

EWE: Ðetugbuia nɔ afi ma ɣleti ene. 3 Eye srɔ̃a dze eyome be yeaɖaƒo nu nɛ wòatrɔ agbɔ va ye gbɔ; ekplɔ eƒe subɔviŋutsu kple tedzi eve ɖe asi yii. Eye ɖetugbuia kplɔe yi fofoa ƒe me.
ENGLISH: 3 And her husband set out after her to coax her back, taking with him his man and a pair of donkeys; and he came to her father’s home, and the girl’s father saw him and came joyfully to meet him.

EWE: Esi ɖetugbuia fofo kpɔe la, exɔe kple dzidzɔ. 4 Eya ta toa, si nye ɖetugbui la fofo na wòtsi egbɔ ŋkeke etɔ̃; woɖua nu noa nu, eye wòtsia afi ma dɔna.
ENGLISH: 4 And his father-in-law, the girl’s father, held him fast, and he stayed with him three days; and they ate and drank and lodged there for the night.

EWE: 5 Le ŋkeke enea gbe, esi wofɔ ŋdi kanya la, etso be yeadzo, ke ɖetugbuia fofo gblɔ na toyɔvia be: “Ðu nane be wòado ŋusẽ wò, emegbe miate ŋu adzo.”
ENGLISH: 5 And on the fourth day, the first thing in the morning, he rose to go, but the girl’s father said to his son-in-law “Take a bit of bread to brace you up, and after that you shall go.”

EWE: 6 Eya ta wobɔbɔ nɔ anyi, eye wo ame evea woɖu nu no nu; emegbe ɖetugbuia fofo gblɔ na ŋutsua be: “Meɖe kuku, tsi dɔ, eye nàdo dzidzɔ na ɖokuiwò.”
ENGLISH: 6 And the two of them sat down and ate together and drank, and the girl’s father said to the husband “Do stay for the night and be jolly”;

EWE: 7 Esi ŋutsu la tso be yeadzo la, toa nɔ kuku ɖem nɛ, ale wògatsi afi ma dɔ.
ENGLISH: 7 and the husband rose to go, but his father-in-law urged him to stay, and he spent the night there again.

EWE: 8 Esi wòfɔ le ŋkeke atɔ̃lia ƒe ŋdi kanya be yeadzo la, ɖetugbuia fofo gblɔ nɛ be: “Meɖe kuku, ɖu nane be wòado ŋusẽ wò.” Eye woganɔ anyi va se ɖe esime fiẽsi nɔ ɖoɖom.
ENGLISH: 8 And the first thing in the morning on the fifth day he was going, but the girl’s father said “Have something to brace you up” and inveigled him till along in the afternoon, and the two of them were eating.

EWE: Eye wo ame evea wonɔ nu ɖum. 9 Esi ŋutsua tso be yeadzo kple yeƒe ahiãvi kpakple yeƒe subɔvi la, toa, si nye ɖetugbuia fofo gblɔ nɛ be: “Kpɔ ɖa! Fiẽ ɖo vɔ. Meɖe kuku, tsi dɔ. Zã do vɔ. Tsi afi sia dɔ, eye nàdo dzidzɔ na ɖokuiwò.
ENGLISH: 9 And the husband rose to go, he and his concubine and his man, but his father-in-law, the girl’s father, said to him “Here the day is dropping off to evening: stay for the night; here it is the windup of the day: stay here for the night and be jolly, and tomorrow be on your way the first thing in the morning, and go to your home.”

EWE: Etsɔ la, miate ŋu afɔ ŋdi kanya adze mɔ ayi aƒe.” 10 Ke ŋutsua melɔ̃ be yeagatsi adɔ ake o, eya ta edze mɔ va ɖo keke Yebus, si nye Yerusalem ke.
ENGLISH: 10 But the husband would not stay for the night, but started out, and came opposite Jebus (that is, Jerusalem), having with him a pair of saddled donkeys, and his concubine with him.

EWE: Tedzitsu eve siwo wobla akpa na kple eƒe ahiãvi kpakple eƒe subɔvi la le eŋu. 11 Esi wogogo Yebus la, ɣe la yina to ɖo ge. Eya ta subɔvi la gblɔ na eƒe aƒetɔ be: “Míadze ɖe Yebusitɔwo ƒe du sia me atsi afi sia adɔ oa?”
ENGLISH: 11 They were up to Jebus when the day got very low, and the serving-man said to his master “Come, let us turn off to this city of the Jebusites’ and lodge there for the night”;

EWE: 12 Ke eƒe aƒetɔ gblɔ nɛ be: “Míadze ɖe ame tutɔ siwo menye Israel-viwo o la ƒe du aɖeke me o. Ke boŋ míayi ŋgɔ aɖo Gibea.”
ENGLISH: 12 but his master said to him “We will not turn off to a city of foreigners who do not belong to the sons of Israel, but go across to Gibeah.”

EWE: 13 Eye wògblɔ na eƒe subɔvi la be: “Na míadze agbagba aɖo teƒe siawo dometɔ ɖeka; míatsi Gibea alo Rama adɔ.”
ENGLISH: 13 And he said to his man “Come, we will get to one of the places and stay at Gibeah or Ramah for the night”;

EWE: 14 Eya ta woyi mɔzɔzɔa dzi, eye ɣe nɔ to ɖom esi wogogo Benyamin viwo ƒe du si nye Gibea.
ENGLISH: 14 and they crossed over and went on, and the sun went down on them alongside Gibeah of Benjamin,

EWE: 15 Eya ta wotɔ ɖe afi ma, eye woyi Gibea be yewoatsi adɔ.
ENGLISH: 15 and they turned off there to go in and lodge in Gibeah.

EWE: Esi woge ɖe dua me la, wobɔbɔ nɔ dua ƒe ablɔ me, gake ame aɖeke mekplɔ wo yi eƒe me be woatsi adɔ o.
ENGLISH: And he went in and sat down in the square of the city, but there was no man to take them in into his house for the night.

EWE: 16 Mlɔeba la, ŋutsu tsitsi aɖe tso agble gbɔ le fiẽ me. Enye Efrayim tonuto la me tɔ, eye wòle Gibea ɣeyiɣi aɖee nye ema; gake dua me tɔwo nye Benyamin viwo.
ENGLISH: 16 But in came an old man, coming at evening from his work in the field (the man was from the highland of Ephraim and was living in Gibeah as an immigrant, while the men of the place were Benjamites),

EWE: 17 Esi ŋutsu tsitsia fɔ kɔ dzi kpɔ mɔzɔlaa le dua ƒe ablɔ me la, ebiae be: “Afi ka yim nèle, eye afi kae nètso?”
ENGLISH: 17 and he raised his eyes and saw the wayfarer in the square of the city. And the old man said “Where are you going, and where do you come from?”

EWE: 18 Eɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Míetso Betlehem le Yuda yina Efrayim tonutoa ƒe nutotroewo me, eye afi mae metso.
ENGLISH: 18 and he said to him “We are going across from Bethlehem in Judah to the back side of the highland of Ephraim: I am from there, and I have been to Bethlehem in Judah, and I am going home.

EWE: Meva yi Betlehem le Yuda, eye metrɔ yina Yehowa ƒe aƒe la me, gake ame aɖeke meva kplɔm be madze ye gbɔ o.
ENGLISH: But there is no man to take us in into his house.

EWE: 19 Gbe kple nuɖuɖu li na míaƒe tedziawo, eye abolo kple wain hã li na nye kple nyɔnu la kple míaƒe subɔvi la.
ENGLISH: 19 Yet I have with me both straw and feed for the donkeys, and bread and wine too for both your servants, and for the man: we are not in want of anything.”

EWE: Naneke mehiã mí o.” 20 Ke ŋutsu tsitsi la gblɔ be: “Ŋutifafa na wò! Makpɔ nu sia nu si hiã mi la gbɔ.
ENGLISH: 20 And the old man said “All right: just let every want of yours come on me; only do not spend the night in the square,”

EWE: 21 Ale wòkplɔe yi eƒe me, eye wòna nuɖuɖu tedziawo.
ENGLISH: 21 and brought him into his house, and foddered the donkeys.

EWE: Eye woklɔ afɔ ɖu nu no nu. 22 Ke esi wonɔ dzidzɔ dom na wo ɖokuiwo la, dua me ŋutsu yakame aɖewo va ɖe to ɖe aƒea, wonɔ ʋɔa ƒom gbagbagba nɔ gbɔgblɔm na ŋutsu tsitsi si nye aƒea tɔ be: “Kplɔ ŋutsu si va aƒewò me la do goe, ne míadɔ kplii.”
ENGLISH: 22 And they washed their feet and ate and drank. They were having a jolly evening when the men of the city, a set of reprobates, got around the house pounding on the door, and told the old man, the master of the house, “Bring out the man that went into your house, for us to know him.”

EWE: 23 Eye aƒea tɔ do yi ɖagblɔ na wo be: “Ao, nɔvinyewo, migawɔ nu vɔ̃ɖi sia o. Meɖe kuku gbɔnyee ŋutsu sia va dze.
ENGLISH: 23 And the man went out to them, the master of the house, and said to them “Don’t, brothers, don’t do mischief; now that this man has come into my house, don’t do this scandalous thing.

EWE: Migawɔ ŋukpenanu sia o. 24 Vinyenyɔnu ɖetugbui leaƒe kple ŋutsu sia ƒe ahiãvie nye esi. Makplɔ wo ado goe vɛ na mi, ne miaɖi gbɔ wo, ne nenemae miedi.
ENGLISH: 24 Here is my maiden daughter, and his concubine: let me bring them out to you, and outrage them and do what you think best to them, but don’t do this scandalous thing to this man.”

EWE: Ðeko migawɔ ŋukpenanu sia ɖe ŋutsu sia ŋu o.” 25 Gake ŋutsuawo gbe toɖoɖoe. Eya ta ŋutsua lé eƒe ahiãvi la kplɔe do goe yi na wo le xexe. Wodɔ egbɔ, eye wowɔ funyafunyae zã blibo la katã va se ɖe esime ŋu ke. Le fɔŋli la, woɖe asi le eŋu.
ENGLISH: 25 But the men would not listen to him; and the husband took hold of his concubine and took her outside to them, and they knew her and did their will on her all night till morning, and let her go at dawn.

EWE: 26 Le ŋdi kanya la, nyɔnua va dze anyi ɖe ŋutsu si ƒe aƒe me eƒe aƒetɔ le la ƒe ʋɔtru nu, eye wòtsi afi ma va se ɖe esime xexea me kɔ.
ENGLISH: 26 And the woman came when morning was drawing on, and fell down at the door of the man’s house and lay there till daylight.

EWE: 27 Esi eƒe aƒetɔ fɔ ŋdi, eye wòʋu ʋɔtruawo do go be yeayi yeƒe mɔzɔzɔa dzi la, ekpɔ eƒe ahiãvi la wòtsra ɖe aƒe la ƒe mɔnu, eye eƒe asiwo le kpuia dzi.
ENGLISH: 27 And her master rose in the morning and opened the doors of the house and went out to go on his way, and found the woman, his concubine, lying at the door of the house with her hands on the threshold.

EWE: 28 Eye wògblɔ nɛ be: “Tso mídzo.” Ke meɖo eŋu o.
ENGLISH: 28 And he said to her “Get up and let us go,” but nobody answered; and he took her on his donkey.

EWE: Eya ta ŋutsua kɔe ɖo tedzi la dzi, eye wòdze mɔ ɖo ta aƒe. 29 Esi wòva ɖo aƒe me la, etsɔ lãwuhɛ, eye wòfli eƒe ahiãvia ɖe eƒe ƒunuɖeƒewo ɖe akpa wuieve me eye wòɖo akpa ɖeka ɖe Israel-to ɖe sia ɖe.
ENGLISH: 29 And the husband went off to his place; and he went into his house and took the knife, and took hold of his concubine and cut her up joint by joint into twelve pieces, and sent her all through the territory of Israel,

EWE: 30 Ame siwo katã kpɔe la gblɔ be: “Nu sia tɔgbi medzɔ kpɔ o, eye womekpɔ eteƒe kpɔ tso gbe si gbe Israel-viwo ʋu tso Egipte-nyigba dzi va se ɖe egbe sia o. Mibu eŋu, mide adaŋu, ne miagblɔ nu si míawɔ la na mí.”
ENGLISH: 30 and gave the men that he sent the order “You are to say to all the men of Israel ‘Has there happened the like of this thing from the day that the sons of Israel came up out of Egypt to this day? make up your minds to something, and speak’”; and everyone who saw said “There has not happened, nor was ever seen, the like of this, from the day that the sons of Israel came up out of Egypt to this day.”

EWE: Ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo
ENGLISH: Judges

EWE: 20 Eya ta Israel-viwo katã tso Dan va se ɖe Beer-Seba kple Gilead-nyigba dzi va kpe ta ɖekae ɖe Yehowa ŋkume le Mizpa.
ENGLISH: 20 And all the sons of Israel came out to Jehovah at Mispah, and the congregation assembled there like one man, from Dan to Beer-Shebaʽ and the country of Gilead;

EWE: 2 Eye dukɔ la ƒe tatɔwo kple Israel-toawo katã va tɔ ɖe Mawu ƒe amewo ƒe takpekpe la me le wo nɔƒewo, eye aʋawɔla afɔzɔla siwo ta yi la le akpe alafa ene.
ENGLISH: 2 and the headmen of all the people, all the tribes of Israel, took their stand as assembly of the people of God, four hundred thousand fighting men of foot.

EWE: 3 Benyamin viwo se be Israel-viwo ho va Mizpa.
ENGLISH: 3 And the sons of Benjamin heard that the sons of Israel had gone up to Mispah.

EWE: Eye Israel-viwo gblɔ be: “Migblɔe míse, aleke nu dziŋɔ sia dzɔe?”
ENGLISH: And the sons of Israel said “Tell us how this crime happened.”

EWE: 4 Eye Lewitɔ si nye nyɔnu si wowu la srɔ̃ ɖo eŋu be: “Nye kple nye ahiãvi míeva Gibea, si nye Benyamin viwo ƒe du me, be míatsi adɔ.
ENGLISH: 4 And the Levite, the murdered woman’s husband, answered “At Gibeah of Benjamin I and my concubine went in to lodge for the night,

EWE: 5 Gibeatɔwo tso ɖe ŋunye, eye wova ɖe to ɖe aƒe si me menɔ la le zã me. Nyee woɖo be yewoawu hafi, ke wodɔ nye ahiãvi gbɔ wòku.
ENGLISH: 5 and the citizens of Gibeah mobbed me, surrounding the house I was in at night; they thought of killing me, and they outraged my concubine so that she died of it;

EWE: 6 Eya ta mekɔ nye ahiãvi la ƒe kukua, eye meflii heɖo akpa aɖe ɖe Israel-nyigba la ƒe teƒe sia teƒe, elabena wowɔ ŋukpenanu kple vlodonu le Israel.
ENGLISH: 6 and I took my concubine and cut her up and sent her all through the countryside of Israel’s domain, because they had committed a scandal in Israel.

EWE: 7 Azɔ mi Israel-viwo katã, migblɔ miaƒe susu, eye miaɖo aɖaŋu le afi sia.”
ENGLISH: 7 Here you all are, sons of Israel; speak your minds here.”

EWE: 8 Eya ta ameawo katã tso kple tame ɖeka gblɔ be: “Mía dometɔ aɖeke mayi eƒe agbadɔ me alo atrɔ ayi eƒe me o.
ENGLISH: 8 And all the people rose like one man, saying “We will not go to our homes, nor each drop off to his house,

EWE: 9 Azɔ nu si míawɔ Gibea ye nye esi. Míadzidze nu, aho ɖe eŋu.
ENGLISH: 9 but this is the thing we will do to Gibeah now: go up against it by lot,

EWE: 10 Míaɖe ŋutsu ewo le alafa me, ŋutsu alafa ɖeka le akpe ɖeka me, kple ŋutsu akpe ɖeka le akpe ewo me le Israel-toawo katã me, ne woayi aɖadi nuɖuɖu na aʋawɔlawo, ne woaho ɖe Gibea si nye Benyamin viwo ƒe du la ŋu, le ŋukpenanu si wowɔ le Israel la ta.”
ENGLISH: 10 and take ten men to the hundred of all the tribes of Israel, and a hundred to the thousand and a thousand to the myriad, to get provisions for the people, to do to the inmates of Gibeah of Benjamin what all the scandal they have committed in Israel deserves.”

EWE: 11 Ale Israel ŋutsuwo katã ƒo ƒu, eye wobla ɖekae ɖe du la ŋu.
ENGLISH: 11 And all the men of Israel came together to the city, acting in concert like one man.

EWE: 12 Eye Israel-toawo dɔ ame ɖo ɖe Benyamin-to la me tɔwo katã be: “Nu dziŋɔ kae nye esi wowɔ le mia dome?
ENGLISH: 12 And the tribes of Israel sent men through all the tribe of Benjamin to say “What a crime this is that has happened among you!

EWE: 13 Azɔ la, miɖe ŋutsu yakame siwo le Gibea la na ne míawu, ne míaɖe nu vɔ̃ɖi la ɖa le Israel.”
ENGLISH: 13 now give up the reprobate men at Gibeah for us to put to death and rout out crime from Israel.”

EWE: Ke Benyamin viwo gbe toɖoɖo wo nɔvi Israel-viwo.
ENGLISH: But the sons of Benjamin would not obey their brothers the sons of Israel;

EWE: 14 Eye Benyamin viwo tso woƒe duwo me va ƒo ƒu ɖe Gibea be yewoakpe aʋa kple Israel-viwo.
ENGLISH: 14 and the sons of Benjamin came together from their cities to Gibeah to go to war with the sons of Israel.

EWE: 15 Gbe ma gbe la, Benyamin viwo ƒo ŋutsu akpe blaeve vɔ ade siwo ta yi la nu ƒu tso woƒe duawo me hekpe ɖe Gibea ŋutsu tiatia alafa adre hã ŋu.
ENGLISH: 15 And the sons of Benjamin were mustered on that day, from the cities twenty-six thousand fighting men, apart from the inhabitants of Gibeah they were mustered seven hundred picked men.

EWE: 16 Aʋawɔla siawo dometɔ alafa adre nye miawɔla tiatiawo.
ENGLISH: 16 Out of all that body there were seven hundred picked men that were left-handed.

EWE: Ame siawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe tea ŋu daa akafo wòlɔa ɖakui ɖeka gɔ̃ hã, eye medaa dadagbo o.
ENGLISH: All these would sling a stone at a hair and never miss.

EWE: 17 Eye Israel ŋutsu siwo nu woƒo ƒu, siwo ta yi la, le akpe alafa ene, ke Benyamin ya mele eme o, eye wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe nye aʋawɔla bibi.
ENGLISH: 17 And the men of Israel were mustered, apart from Benjamin, four hundred thousand fighting men; all these were men of war.

EWE: 18 Woho yi Betel be yewoabia gbe Mawu.
ENGLISH: 18 And they went up to Bethel.

EWE: Eye Israel-viwo bia be: “Mía dometɔ kae atre hoho ayi aɖawɔ aʋa kple Benyamin viwo?” Yehowa ɖo eŋu be: “Yuda netre hoho.”
ENGLISH: And the sons of Israel put the question to God “Whom shall we have go up to war with the sons of Benjamin to begin with?” and Jehovah said “Judah to begin with.”

EWE: 19 Ale Israel-viwo fɔ ŋdi va ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Gibea ŋu.
ENGLISH: 19 And the sons of Israel started out in the morning and beleaguered Gibeah.

EWE: 20 Eye Israel ŋutsuwo ho yi aʋa wɔ ge kple Benyamin; Israel ŋutsuawo le aʋalɔgowo me va dze aʋa ɖe wo ŋu le Gibea.
ENGLISH: 20 And the men of Israel went out to fight the Benjamites; and the men of Israel gave them battle toward Gibeah;

EWE: 21 Eye Benyamin viwo do tso Gibea va wu Israel ŋutsu akpe blaeve vɔ eve gbe ma gbe.
ENGLISH: 21 and the sons of Benjamin came out of Gibeah and mowed off among the Israelites that day twenty-two thousand men.

EWE: 22 Ke dzi ganɔ Israel ƒe aʋawɔlawo ƒo, eye wogadze aʋa ɖe afi si wodze aʋa ɖo le ŋkeke gbãtɔ dzi la.
ENGLISH: 22 And the people, the men of Israel, took heart and gave battle once more in the same place where they did on the first day.

EWE: 23 Eye Israel-viwo yi ɖafa avi le Yehowa ŋkume va se ɖe fiẽ, eye wobia gbe Yehowa be: “Mígaho aʋa ɖe mía nɔvi Benyamin viwo ŋu akea?” Yehowa ɖo eŋu be: “Miho ɖe wo ŋu.”
ENGLISH: 23 And the sons of Israel went up to Bethel and wept before Jehovah till evening, and put the question to Jehovah “Shall I engage in battle with my brother Benjamin’s sons anymore?” and Jehovah said “Go up against him.”

EWE: 24 Eya ta Israel-viwo te tu Benyamin viwo le ŋkeke evelia dzi.
ENGLISH: 24 And the sons of Israel engaged the Benjamites on the second day;

EWE: 25 Ke Benyamin do tso Gibea va kpe wo le ŋkeke evelia dzi, eye wògawu ŋutsu akpe wuienyi bubu siwo katã ta yi la le Israel-viwo dome.
ENGLISH: 25 and the Benjamites came out of Gibeah to meet them on the second day, and mowed off among the sons of Israel eighteen thousand more; all these were fighting men.

EWE: 26 Eye Israel-viwo katã yi Betel. Wofa avi hebɔbɔ nɔ afi ma le Yehowa ŋkume, wotsi nu dɔ gbe ma gbe va se ɖe fiẽ, eye wosa numevɔwo kple ŋutifafavɔwo le Yehowa ŋkume.
ENGLISH: 26 And all the sons of Israel, and all the people, went up and came to Bethel, and wept and sat there before Jehovah and fasted that day till evening, and offered burnt-offerings and welfare-sacrifices before Jehovah;

EWE: 27 Emegbe Israel-viwo bia gbe Yehowa, elabena Mawu vavã la ƒe nubablaɖaka la le afi ma le ŋkeke mawo me.
ENGLISH: 27 and the sons of Israel put the question to Jehovah (the ark of God’s covenant was there in those days,

EWE: 28 Ke Finehas, Eleazar vi, Aron vi, subɔna le aɖaka la ŋgɔ le ŋkeke mawo me. Wobia be: “Mígaho ɖe mía nɔvi Benyamin viwo ŋu akea, alo mítasia?” Yehowa ɖo eŋu be: “Miyi, elabena etsɔ la, matsɔ wo ade asi na mi.”
ENGLISH: 28 and Pinehas the son of Eleazar the son of Aaron was in charge of its service in those days) “Shall I again go out to battle with my brother Benjamin’s sons, or shall I leave off?” and Jehovah said “Go up, for tomorrow I will give them into your hands.”

EWE: 29 Eye Israel na amewo de xa ɖe Gibea ŋu godoo va kpe.
ENGLISH: 29 And the Israelites laid ambuscades against Gibeah on all sides.

EWE: 30 Israel-viwo ho ɖe Benyamin viwo ŋu le ŋkeke etɔ̃a gbe, eye wodze aʋa ɖe Gibea ŋu abe tsã ene.
ENGLISH: 30 And the sons of Israel went up against the sons of Benjamin on the third day and offered battle as before;
