EWE: 31 Esi Benyamin viwo do go yi be yewoaɖakpe kple aʋawɔlawo la, woble wo yi adzɔge tso dua gbɔ. Eye abe ale si wowɔ tsã ene la, wogadze wo dzi hewu ameawo dometɔ aɖewo le mɔ gã si ɖo ta Betel kple esi ɖo ta Gibea la dzi, Israel ŋutsu siwo ade blaetɔ̃ ku ɖe gbea dzi.
ENGLISH: 31 and the sons of Benjamin came out to meet the people, broke away from the city, and began to stab some of the people as before on the highways that go up one to Bethel and one to Gibeon, in the open, about thirty men among the Israelites.

EWE: 32 Eya ta Benyamin viwo gblɔ be: “Míegale wo sim le mía ŋgɔ abe tsã ene.” Ke Israel-viwo ya gblɔ be: “Míasi le wo nu, eye míable wo ayi adzɔge tso dua gbɔ ayi mɔ gãwo dzi.”
ENGLISH: 32 And the sons of Benjamin thought “They are beaten, the same as the first time”; but the sons of Israel thought “Let us run and break them away from the city into the highways.”

EWE: 33 Israel ŋutsuwo katã tso le wo nɔƒewo va dze aʋa ɖe Baal-Tamar, ɣemaɣi la Israel ŋutsu siwo de xa ɖi ya do tso wo nɔƒewo le Gibea nutoa me.
ENGLISH: 33 And all the men of Israel started up from their place, and formed their line at Baal-Tamar, and the Israelites’ ambuscade burst out from its place to the west of Gebaʽ,

EWE: 34 Ale ŋutsu tiatia akpe ewo tso Israel blibo la va Gibea ŋgɔ, eye aʋa la nu sẽ ŋutɔ.
ENGLISH: 34 and ten thousand picked men out of all Israel went in in front of Gibeah; and the fighting was heavy.

EWE: Ke Benyamin viwo menya be vɔ̃ gogo yewo o.
ENGLISH: But they did not know that disaster was upon them.

EWE: 35 Yehowa si Benyamin le Israel ŋgɔ, eye Israel-viwo wu Benyamin ŋutsu akpe blaeve vɔ atɔ̃ alafa ɖeka, siwo katã ta yi gbe ma gbe.
ENGLISH: 35 And Jehovah caused Israel to beat Benjamin; and the sons of Israel mowed down twenty-five thousand one hundred among the Benjamites that day; all these were fighting men.

EWE: 36 Gake Benyamin viwo susui be yewoaɖu Israel ŋutsuwo dzi esi wosi le Benyamin nu, gake ɖe wosi le wo nu elabena woɖo ŋu ɖe ame siwo de xa ɖe Gibea ŋu la ŋu.
ENGLISH: 36 And the sons of Benjamin saw that they were beaten.And the men of Israel gave way to the Benjamites, because they relied on the ambuscade they had laid against Gibeah;

EWE: 37 Ke xadelawo wɔ kaba ho ɖo ta Gibea.
ENGLISH: 37 and the ambuscade made a hasty dash to Gibeah.

EWE: Wokaka ɖe dua me, eye wowu dua me nɔlawo katã kple yi.
ENGLISH: And the ambuscade poured in and massacred the whole city.

EWE: 38 Ke Israel ŋutsuwo ɖo gbe ɖi kple xadelawo be woana dzudzɔ nade dzi le dua me wòanye dzesi na yewo.
ENGLISH: 38 And the appointment the men of Israel had with the ambuscade was that they should send up a smoke-signal from the city;

EWE: 39 Esi Israel-viwo si le aʋaa nu la, Benyamin ŋutsuwo dze wo dzi wu ame siwo anɔ blaetɔ̃ le Israel ŋutsuwo dome, eye wogblɔ be: “Edze ƒãa be míegale wo dzi ɖum abe ale si wònɔ le aʋa kemɛa me ene.”
ENGLISH: 39 and the men of Israel turned in the battle, and the Benjamites began to stab about thirty men among the men of Israel, because they thought “It must be they are beaten, the same as in the first battle.”

EWE: 40 Gake dzudzɔ babla de dzi le dua me wònye dzesi na wo. Eye esi Benyamin ŋutsuwo trɔ kpɔ megbe la, wokpɔ du bliboa katã le bibim eye dzudzɔ de dzi kɔtɔɔ.
ENGLISH: 40 But the signal began to go up from the city, a pillar of smoke; and the Benjamites turned their eyes back, and found that the holocaust of the city had towered to the sky;

EWE: 41 Azɔ Israel ŋutsuwo trɔ ɖe wo ŋu, eye dzidzi ƒo Benyamin ŋutsuwo, elabena wokpɔe be vɔ̃ tu yewo.
ENGLISH: 41 and the men of Israel had turned; and the men of Benjamin were in consternation because they saw that disaster was upon them.

EWE: 42 Ale wosi le Israel ŋutsuwo nu ɖo ta gbedzi, ke aʋa la yɔ wo ɖe nu, eye ame siwo do tso dua me la va kpe ɖe wo nɔviwo ŋu wowu wo.
ENGLISH: 42 And they turned before the men of Israel toward the wilderness; but the fighting kept up with them, and those who came out of the cities mowed them down in the midst.

EWE: 43 Woɖe to ɖe Benyamin viwo, wonya wo ɖe nu megbemakpɔmakpɔe.
ENGLISH: 43 And they grated away the Benjamites from Nohah to opposite Gebaʽ on the east;

EWE: 44 Mlɔeba Benyamin ŋutsu akpe wuienyi tsi aʋa, wo katã wonye aʋakalẽtɔwo.
ENGLISH: 44 and eighteen thousand men of Benjamin fell, stalwart men all these.

EWE: 45 Benyamin viwo trɔ hesi ɖo ta gbedzi yi Rimon-gakpe la gbɔ, eye Israel-viwo wu wo dometɔ akpe atɔ̃ le mɔ gãwo dzi, eye wonya wo ɖe nu va se ɖe keke Gidom ke; eye wogawu ŋutsu akpe eve kpee.
ENGLISH: 45 And they turned and fled to Rimmon Cliff in the wilderness, and they took an aftermath of five thousand men; and they kept up behind them to Gideom and killed two thousand of them.

EWE: 46 Benyamin vi siwo katã tsi aʋa gbe ma gbe la le ame akpe blaeve vɔ atɔ̃, wo katã wonye aʋakalẽtɔ siwo ta yi.
ENGLISH: 46 The total of the Benjamites that fell was twenty-five thousand men on that day, stalwart men all these;

EWE: 47 Ke ŋutsu alafa ade trɔ hesi yi gbedzi yi Rimon-gakpe la gbɔ, eye wonɔ Rimon-gakpe la dzi ɣleti ene.
ENGLISH: 47 but six hundred men turned and fled to Rimmon Cliff in the wilderness and stayed on Rimmon Cliff four months.

EWE: 48 Israel ŋutsuwo trɔ ɖe Benyamin viwo ŋu, eye wowu duawo me nɔlawo kple yi, amegbetɔwo kple lãwo siaa, nu sia nu si kpɔtɔ le dua me ko. Azɔ hã, wotɔ dzo du siwo katã wokpɔ le afi siwo woto la.
ENGLISH: 48 And the men of Israel went back to the sons of Benjamin and massacred them, from city of men to cattle and everything that was to be found; they also put the torch to all the cities that were to be found.

EWE: Ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo
ENGLISH: Judges

EWE: 21 Azɔ Israel ŋutsuwo ka atam le Mizpa be: “Mía dometɔ aɖeke matsɔ vianyɔnu ana Benyamin ŋutsu wòaɖe o.”
ENGLISH: 21 And the men of Israel had sworn at Mispah “Not a man of us will give his daughter to any of the Benjamites as wife.”

EWE: 2 Eya ta dukɔ la va Betel, eye wobɔbɔ nɔ afi ma le Mawu vavã la ŋkume va se ɖe fiẽ, eye wodo ɣli hefa avi sesĩe.
ENGLISH: 2 And the people came to Bethel and sat down there till evening before God, and raised their voices and wept, making a very great weeping,

EWE: 3 Eye wonɔ gbɔgblɔm be: “Oo Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu, nu ka ŋuti nu sia dzɔ le Israel? Nu ka tae to ɖeka bu egbea le Israel?”
ENGLISH: 3 and said “Why, Jehovah God of Israel, has this thing come to pass in Israel, that one tribe should be missing from Israel today?”

EWE: 4 Le ŋufɔke la, dukɔ la fɔ ŋdi kanya, eye woɖi vɔsamlekpui ɖe afi ma be woasa numevɔwo kple ŋutifafavɔwo.
ENGLISH: 4 and the first thing the next day the people built an altar there, and offered burnt-offerings and welfare-sacrifices.

EWE: 5 Eye Israel-viwo gblɔ be: “Ame kae le Israel-toawo katã dome si meva kpe ta ɖe Yehowa ŋkume o?” elabena woka atam vevie be woawu ame sia ame si mava Yehowa gbɔ le Mizpa o la godoo.
ENGLISH: 5 And the sons of Israel said “Who is there that did not come up to Jehovah in the assembly, of all the tribes of Israel?” because there had been the great oath for whoever did not come up to Mispah to Jehovah, that he must be put to death.

EWE: 6 Israel-viwo xa nu le nu si dzɔ ɖe wo nɔvi Benyamin viwo dzi la ta. Wogblɔ be: “To ɖeka tsrɔ̃ ɖa le Israel egbea.
ENGLISH: 6 And the sons of Israel were sorry about their brother Benjamin, and said “One tribe has been hewn off from Israel today.

EWE: 7 Aleke míawɔ akpɔ nyɔnu na ame siwo susɔ la, elabe míeka atam le Yehowa ŋkume be míatsɔ mía vinyɔnu aɖeke ana wo woaɖe o?”
ENGLISH: 7 What shall we do for wives for them, the ones that are left, when we have sworn by Jehovah not to give them any of our daughters as wives?”

EWE: 8 Wobia be: “Israel-toawo dometɔ kae meva Yehowa gbɔ le Mizpa o?” Eva eme be ame aɖeke metso Yabes-Gilead va asaɖa la me, afi si ha la le o.
ENGLISH: 8 And they said “Who is there at all among the tribes of Israel that did not come to Mispah to Jehovah?” and it was found that not a man from Jabesh in Gilead had come to the camp to the assembly.

EWE: 9 Esi woxlẽ dukɔa la, wokpɔ be Yabes-Gileadtɔ aɖeke mele afi ma o!
ENGLISH: 9 And the people were mustered, and it was found that there was not a man there of the inhabitants of Jabesh in Gilead.

EWE: 10 Eya ta ha la dɔ ame akpe wuieve le aʋakalẽtɔ sesẽwo dome ɖe afi ma. Woɖe gbe na wo be: “Miheyi ɖawu Yabes-Gilead nɔlawo kple yi, nyɔnuwo kple ɖeviwo gɔ̃ hã.
ENGLISH: 10 And the congregation sent there twelve thousand of the most stalwart men, and gave them the order “Go and massacre the inhabitants of Jabesh in Gilead, including the women and children;

EWE: 11 Nu si miawɔe nye esi: Mitsrɔ̃ ŋutsu sia ŋutsu kple nyɔnu siwo katã dɔ ŋutsu gbɔ kpɔ la gbidigbidi.”
ENGLISH: 11 and this is the way you are to do, destroy without quarter every male, and every woman who has known a male’s embrace.”

EWE: 12 Ke wokpɔ nyɔnuvi alafa ene siwo nye ɖetugbui leaƒewo, siwo medɔ ŋutsu gbɔ kpɔ o la, le Yabes-Gileadtɔwo dome. Eye wokplɔ wo va asaɖa la me le Silo, le Kanaan-nyigba dzi.
ENGLISH: 12 And out of the inhabitants of Jabesh in Gilead they found four hundred virgin girls who had not known man in sexual embrace; and they brought them to the camp at Shiloh in the country of Canaan.

EWE: 13 Eye ha blibo la dɔ ame ɖo ɖe Benyamin vi siwo le Rimon-gakpea dzi, eye wodo ŋugbe na wo be yewoawɔ ŋutifafa kpli wo.
ENGLISH: 13 And all the congregation sent word to the sons of Benjamin on Rimmon Cliff, proclaiming peace to them;

EWE: 14 Eya ta Benyamin viwo trɔ gbɔ ɣemaɣi. Eye wotsɔ nyɔnu siwo woxɔ ɖe agbe le Yabes-Gilead nyɔnuwo dome la na wo, ke womede wo nu o.
ENGLISH: 14 and the Benjamites came back at that time, and they gave them the wives they had kept alive out of the women of Jabesh in Gilead, but even so they did not suffice for them.

EWE: 15 Eye dukɔ la xa nu le nu si dzɔ ɖe Benyamin dzi la ta, elabena Yehowa de mama Israel-toawo dome.
ENGLISH: 15 And the people were sorry about the Benjamites, because Jehovah had broken into the tribes of Israel.

EWE: 16 Eye ha la ƒe ametsitsiwo gblɔ be: “Aleke míawɔ akpɔ nyɔnu na ŋutsu siwo susɔ la esi wotsrɔ̃ nyɔnuwo katã le Benyamin?”
ENGLISH: 16 And the elders of the congregation said “What shall we do for wives for the ones that are left?” because womankind had been rooted out from Benjamin;

EWE: 17 Woɖo eŋu be: “Ele be domenyinu nasu Benyamin ƒe agbetsilawo si, ne to ɖeka nu nagayi le Israel dome o.
ENGLISH: 17 and “Benjamin has an estate of survivors, so that a tribe is not to be wiped out from Israel;

EWE: 18 Gake míate ŋu atsɔ mía vinyɔnuwo ana wo o, elabena Israel-viwo ka atam be: ‘Aɖi ame si ana nyɔnu Benyamin la ŋu.’”
ENGLISH: 18 but we cannot give them wives out of our daughters” because the sons of Israel had sworn “Cursed is anyone who gives a wife to the Benjamites.”

EWE: 19 Eye wogblɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa! Woɖua Yehowa ƒe ŋkekenyui ƒe sia ƒe le Silo, le Betel ƒe dziehe, le mɔ gã si tso Betel yi Sekem la ƒe ɣedzeƒe, le Lebona ƒe anyiehe.”
ENGLISH: 19 And they said “Here is the feast of Jehovah at Shiloh annually, north of Bethel, east of the highway that goes up from Bethel to Shekem, and south of Lebonah”;

EWE: 20 Eya ta wogblɔ na Benyamin viwo be: “Miyi ɖade xa ɖe waingbleawo me.
ENGLISH: 20 and they gave the sons of Benjamin the order “Go and lie in ambush in the vineyards,

EWE: 21 Ne miekpɔ Silo ɖetugbuiwo do va be yewoado to aɖu ɣe la, ekema miawo hã miado tso waingbleawo me ava, eye mia dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe nalé Silo ɖetugbui ɖeka wòazu srɔ̃a, eye miatrɔ ayi Benyamin-nyigba dzi.
ENGLISH: 21 and be looking, and if the Shiloh girls come out to dance the dances, come you out of the vineyards and catch yourselves a wife apiece out of the Shiloh girls, and go to the country of Benjamin.

EWE: 22 Ne wo fofowo alo wo nɔviŋutsuwo he nya ɖe mía ŋu la, ekema míawo hã míagblɔ na wo be: ‘Mive mía nu le wo ta, elabena míekpɔ nyɔnu lé le aʋa na ŋutsuawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe wòzu srɔ̃a o, eye miate ŋu atsɔ nyɔnu na wo woaɖe evɔ miaɖi fɔ o.’”
ENGLISH: 22 And when their fathers or brothers come to complain to us, we will say to them “Let them off as a favor to us, because we did not take a wife apiece by fighting, for you did not give to them, then you would have been liable.”

EWE: 23 Ale Benyamin viwo wɔe nenema pɛpɛpɛ, eye wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe lé nyɔnu ɖeka le nyɔnu siwo le ɣe ɖum la dome dzoe wòzu srɔ̃a. Emegbe wogbugbɔ yi woƒe anyigba si dome wonyi la dzi, eye wogbugbɔ duawo tso henɔ wo me.
ENGLISH: 23 And the sons of Benjamin did so, and carried off wives enough for their number out of the dancers they stole, and went home to their domain and rebuilt the cities and lived in them.

EWE: 24 Israel-viwo kaka le afi ma ɣemaɣi, eye ame sia ame yi to si me wòtso kple eƒe ƒome gbɔ, wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe dzo le afi ma yi anyigba si dome wònyi la dzi.
ENGLISH: 24 And upon that the sons of Israel wended their way from there to their several tribes and clans, and they went out from there to their several domains.

EWE: 25 Ɣemaɣi la, fia aɖeke menɔ Israel o. Ame sia ame wɔa nu si sɔ le eya ŋutɔ ŋkume.
ENGLISH: 25 In those days there was no king in Israel: each did what suited him.

EWE: Rut
ENGLISH: Ruth

EWE: 1 Le ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo ƒe ŋkekeawo me la, dɔ to le anyigba la dzi; eye ŋutsu aɖe kple srɔ̃a kpakple viaŋutsu eve ʋu le Betlehem le Yuda be yewoayi aɖanɔ Moab-nyigba dzi.
ENGLISH: 1 And in the time when the judges judged there was a famine in the country, and a man from Bethlehem in Judah went to live as an immigrant in Moab, he and his wife and his two sons;

EWE: 2 Ŋutsua ŋkɔe nye Elimelek, eye srɔ̃a ŋkɔe nye Naomi, viaŋutsu eveawo ŋkɔwoe nye Mahlon kple Kilion.
ENGLISH: 2 the man’s name was Elimelec and his wife’s name was Naomi, and the names of his two sons were Mahlon and Kiljon Ephrathites from Bethlehem in Judah.

EWE: Wonye Efratatɔwo tso Betlehem le Yuda.
ENGLISH: And they went into Moab and were there;

EWE: 3 Le ɣeyiɣi aɖe megbe la, Naomi srɔ̃ Elimelek ku, eye eya kple viaŋutsu eveawo koe susɔ.
ENGLISH: 3 and Naomi’s husband Elimelec died, and she and her two sons remained,

EWE: 4 Emegbe ŋutsuawo ɖe Moab-nyɔnuwo; ɖeka ŋkɔe nye Orpa, eye evelia ŋkɔe nye Rut.
ENGLISH: 4 and she married them to Moabite wives, one named ʽOrpah and the other named Ruth.

EWE: Wonɔ afi ma anɔ ƒe ewo.
ENGLISH: And they lived there about ten years,

EWE: 5 Ke viaŋutsu eveawo, Mahlon kple Kilion, hã va ku, ale be Naomi koe kpɔtɔ, srɔ̃a kple via eveawo ku hegblẽe ɖi.
ENGLISH: 5 and Mahlon and Kiljon died too, both of them, and the woman remained, surviving her two children and her husband.

EWE: 6 Eya ta eya kple lɔ̃xoyɔviawo gbugbɔ tso Moab-nyigba dzi, elabena ese le Moab-nyigba dzi be Yehowa trɔ susu ɖe eƒe amewo ŋu hena nuɖuɖu wo.
ENGLISH: 6 And she broke up her home, she and her daughters-in-law, and was going back out of Moab, because she had heard in Moab that Jehovah had looked after his people, giving them bread;

EWE: 7 Ale wòʋu tso afi si eya kple lɔ̃xoyɔvi eveawo nɔ la. Esi wole mɔ dzi yina Yuda-nyigba dzi la,
ENGLISH: 7 and she went out of the place where she was, and her two daughters-in-law with her, and went along the road to go back to Judah.

EWE: 8 Naomi gblɔ na lɔ̃xoyɔvi eveawo be: “Mitrɔ, eye mia dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe neyi dadaa ƒe me. Yehowa neve mia nu, abe ale si mieve mia srɔ̃ siwo ku kple nye hã nunye ene.
ENGLISH: 8 And Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law “Come on, go back to your mothers’ homes; may Jehovah be kind to you, as you have been to those who are dead and to me.

EWE: 9 Yehowa nena mia dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe nakpɔ dzidzeme le srɔ̃a ƒe me.”
ENGLISH: 9 May Jehovah grant that each of you may find rest in a husband’s home”; and she kissed them.

EWE: Eye wògbugbɔ nu na wo, eye wolé avi me.
ENGLISH: And they raised their voices and wept,

EWE: 10 Eye wonɔ gbɔgblɔm nɛ be: “Ao, ke boŋ míatrɔ kpli wò ayi wò dukɔ gbɔ.”
ENGLISH: 10 and said to her “But we are going back with you to your people.”

EWE: 11 Ke Naomi gblɔ be: “Vinyewo, migbugbɔ! Nu ka tae miayi kplim? Ðe magate ŋu adzi ŋutsuvi siwo ava ɖe mia?
ENGLISH: 11 But Naomi said “Go back, daughters; why should you go with me? do I still have sons in my body who would be husbands for you?

EWE: 12 Vinyewo, migbugbɔ. Miyi elabena metsi akpa be maɖe srɔ̃.
ENGLISH: 12 Go back, daughters, go, because I am too old to marry.

EWE: Nenye be mɔkpɔkpɔ li be maɖe srɔ̃ zã sia me, eye madzi viŋutsuviwo hã la,
ENGLISH: If I said ‘I have hopes’ and actually married tonight, or actually bore sons,

EWE: 13 ɖe mianɔ anyi anɔ lalam va se ɖe esime woatsia? Woawo tae mianɔ anyi srɔ̃maɖemaɖeea?
ENGLISH: 13 would you on that account have patience till they should grow up? would you on that account live single without marrying?

EWE: Kpao, vinyewo, elabena mia tɔ koe le veyem ŋutɔ, be Yehowa do eƒe asi ɖe gbɔnye.”
ENGLISH: No, daughters, though I suffer bitterly because of you; for Jehovah’s hand has gone out against me.”

EWE: 14 Eye wogafa avi sesĩe ɖe edzi, emegbe Orpa gbugbɔ nu na lɔ̃xoa hetrɔ dzo.
ENGLISH: 14 And they raised their voices and wept again, and ʽOrpah kissed her mother-in-law; but Ruth stayed by her.

EWE: Ke Rut ya ku ɖe eŋu. 15 Eya ta Naomi gblɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa! Srɔ̃wòɖia srɔ̃ ahosia trɔ yi eƒe dukɔ kple eƒe mawuwo gbɔ.
ENGLISH: 15 And she said “There, your sister-in-law has gone back to her own people and her own god; go back, follow your sister-in-law.”

EWE: 16 Ke Rut gblɔ nɛ be: “Mègaƒoe ɖe nunye be magblẽ wò ɖi agbugbɔ le yowòme o; elabena afi si nàyi la, afi mae mayi, eye afi si nàtsi adɔ la, afi mae matsi adɔ.
ENGLISH: 16 But Ruth said “Do not pray me to leave you, to go back from following you, because where you go I am going and where you stop for the night I will stop.

EWE: Wò dukɔ anye nye dukɔ, eye wò Mawu anye nye Mawu.
ENGLISH: Your people is my people and your god is my god.

EWE: 17 Afi si nàku ɖo la, afi mae maku ɖo, eye afi mae woaɖim ɖo.
ENGLISH: 17 Where you die I will die, and there I will be buried.

EWE: Yehowa nefiam, ne wòagafiam ɖe edzi, ne menye ku koe aklã nye kpli wò dome o fĩi!”
ENGLISH: Jehovah do so to me, and more, but it shall be death that separates you and me from each other.”

EWE: 18 Esi Naomi kpɔ be Rut ɖoe kplikpaa be yeayi kpli ye la, edzudzɔ eƒoƒo ɖe enu.
ENGLISH: 18 And she saw she was set on going with her, and left off talking to her.

EWE: 19 Eye wo ame evea woyi woƒe mɔzɔzɔa dzi va se ɖe esime woɖo Betlehem.
ENGLISH: 19 And the two of them went till they came to Bethlehem.

EWE: Esi wova ɖo Betlehem teti ko la, du blibo la ƒo zi ɖe wo ŋu, eye nyɔnuawo nɔ biabiam be: “Naomi ye nye esia?”
ENGLISH: And when they came to Bethlehem all the city was in a commotion over them, and they said “Is this Naomi?”

EWE: 20 Ke egblɔna na nyɔnuawo be: “Migayɔm be Naomi o.
ENGLISH: 20 And she said to them “Do not call me Naomi, call me Mara, because Shaddai has made things very bitter for me.

EWE: Miyɔm be Mara, elabena Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la na nye agbenɔnɔ zu veve sɔŋ. 21 Nu nɔ asinye fũu hafi meyi, ke asi ƒuƒlue Yehowa na metrɔ gbɔe.
ENGLISH: 21 I went full and Jehovah brought me back empty; why do you call me Naomi when Jehovah has indicted me and Shaddai has brought evil on me?”

EWE: Nu ka tae miayɔm be Naomi, evɔ Yehowa tso ɖe ŋunye, eye Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la na vɔ̃ dzɔ ɖe dzinye?” 22 Aleae Naomi trɔ gbɔ kple lɔ̃xoyɔvia Rut, Moab-nyɔnu la, tso Moab-nyigba dzi.
ENGLISH: 22 And Naomi came back, and with her Ruth the Moabite, her daughter-in-law, who had followed her back from Moab, and they came to Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest.

EWE: Rut
ENGLISH: Ruth

EWE: 2 Ke Naomi srɔ̃ ƒe ƒometɔ aɖe li, si nye kesinɔtɔ gã aɖe; eŋkɔe nye Boaz, eye wòtso Elimelek ƒe ƒomea me.
ENGLISH: 2 And Naomi had a relative of her husband’s, a stalwart man of Elimelec’s clan, named Boaz.

EWE: 2 Rut, Moab-nyɔnu la, gblɔ na Naomi be: “Meɖe kuku, na mayi agble me aɖafɔ nuku siwo tsi anyigba, le ame sia ame si ave nunye la yome.”
ENGLISH: 2 And Ruth the Moabite said to Naomi “Let me go to the field and glean ears of the grain behind whoever is kind to me”; and she told her “Go, daughter.”

EWE: Eye Naomi gblɔ nɛ be: “Heyi, vinye.” 3 Ale wòdzo yi agble aɖe me ɖale nuku siwo tsi anyi la fɔm le nuŋelawo yome. Eva eme be agble si me wòyi nye Elimelek ƒe ƒometɔ Boaz tɔ.
ENGLISH: 3 And she went off and came and gleaned in the field behind the reapers, and she happened into the section of the field that belonged to Boaz, who was of Elimelec’s clan,

EWE: 4 Ɣemaɣi tututue Boaz tso Betlehem va, eye wògblɔ na nuŋelaawo be: “Yehowa nenɔ kpli mi.” Eye woɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Yehowa neyra wò.”
ENGLISH: 4 and there came Boaz out of Bethlehem and said to the reapers “Jehovah be with you,” and they said to him “Jehovah bless you.”

EWE: 5 Eye Boaz bia ɖekakpui si wòɖo nuŋelawo nu la be: “Ame ka ƒe ɖetugbuie nye ema?”
ENGLISH: 5 And Boaz said to his man who was superintending the reapers “Whose is this girl?”

EWE: 6 Ðekakpui si wòɖo nuŋelawo nu la ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Ðetugbui la nye Moab-nyɔnu si gbɔ kple Naomi tso Moab-nyigba dzi.
ENGLISH: 6 and the man superintending the reapers answered “That is a Moabite girl, the one that came back with Naomi out of Moab;

EWE: 7 Eva biam be: ‘Meɖe kuku, mate ŋu afɔ nuku siwo dzɔ ɖe anyigba le nuŋelaawo yomea?’ Tso ŋdi esi wòva la, eƒe afɔwo dzi ko wòle va se ɖe fifia, eye ɖeko wòyi ɖanɔ anyi ɖe agbadɔa te be yeagbɔ ɖe eme vie koe nye ema.”
ENGLISH: 7 and she said ‘Let me glean and pick up among the shocks behind the reapers,’ and she came and has been on her feet ever since it was daylight till right now; her sitting down in the house has been only a little.”

EWE: 8 Eye Boaz gblɔ na Rut be: “Vinyenyɔnu, ɖo tom. Mègayi ɖafɔ nuku le agble bubu me o, eye mègadzo le teƒe sia o, nɔ nye ɖetugbuiawo ŋu.
ENGLISH: 8 And Boaz said to Ruth “Do you hear, daughter? do not go gleaning in another field, and do not cross over out of this; stick here by my girls;

EWE: 9 Wò ŋku nenɔ agble si me woaŋe nu le la ŋu, eye nàyi kpli wo. Elabena mede se na ɖekakpuiawo be woagaka asi ŋuwò o. Ne tsikɔ le wuwòm la, yi tsizeawo gbɔ nàno tsi si ɖekakpuiawo du la ƒe ɖe.”
ENGLISH: 9 keep your eyes on the field they are reaping and follow them the boys have my orders not to touch you; and when you are thirsty go to the jars and take a drink out of what the boys draw.”

EWE: 10 Eye wòdze klo tsyɔ mo anyi gblɔ nɛ be: “Aleke wɔ nève nunye, eye nèbu ŋunye ale, evɔ wònye amedzroe menye hafi?”
ENGLISH: 10 And she threw herself down on her face and did reverence on the ground, and said to him “How comes it you are kind enough to notice me when I am a foreigner?”

EWE: 11 Boaz ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Wogblɔ nu siwo katã nèwɔ na lɔ̃xowò le srɔ̃wò ƒe ku megbe la kple ale si nègblẽ fofowò kple dawò kpakple wò ƒometɔwo ƒe anyigba ɖi heva dukɔ aɖe si mènya tsã o me la nam tsitotsito.
ENGLISH: 11 And Boaz answered “I have been told all about what you did for your mother-in-law after your husband’s death and how you left your father and mother and your native country and went to a people you had not known before.

EWE: 12 Yehowa neɖo nu si nèwɔ teƒe na wò, eye fetu blibo natso Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu, ame si ƒe aʋala te nèva be ɖo la, gbɔ na wò.”
ENGLISH: 12 May Jehovah requite your actions, and your reward be thorough from Israel’s God Jehovah under whose wings you have come to take shelter.”

EWE: 13 Eye wògblɔ be: “Nye aƒetɔ neve nunye ɖaa, elabena èfa akɔ nam, eye nèƒo nu wòde dzi ƒo na wò dɔlanyɔnu, evɔ nyemenye wò kosiviwo dometɔ aɖeke o hafi.”
ENGLISH: 13 And she said “Thank you, sir, for cheering me up and speaking kindly to your servant, when I am not the like of one of your slave-girls.”

EWE: 14 Eye Boaz gblɔ nɛ le nuɖuɣi be: “Te va afii nàɖu aboloa ƒe ɖe, eye nàtsɔe atɔ wain tsitsi la me.” Ale wòbɔbɔ nɔ nuŋelaawo xa. Eye wòtsɔ nuku tɔtɔe la ƒe ɖe nɛ wòɖu, ale be wòɖi ƒo, eye ɖe gasusɔ.
ENGLISH: 14 And Boaz said to her at eating-time “Come here and have some of the bread and dip your piece in the sauce”; and she sat down beside the reapers, and he passed her roasted grain, and she ate till she had all she wanted, and left some over.

EWE: 15 Esi wòtso be yeayi nukua fɔfɔ dzi la, Boaz de se na eƒe ɖekakpuiawo be: “Mina wòafɔ nuku siwo tsi anyi, eye migaɖe fu nɛ o.
ENGLISH: 15 And she stood up to glean, and Boaz gave the men the order “She is to glean right in between the shocks and you are not to snub her; and, too,

EWE: 16 Milũ ɖewo le bablawo hã me da ɖi wòafɔ, eye migabia nya aɖekee o.”
ENGLISH: 16 you are to pull some out of the armfuls and leave it for her, and she is to glean and you are not to scold her.”

EWE: 17 Eyi nukuawo fɔfɔ dzi le agblea me va se ɖe fiẽ. Esi wòƒo nuku siwo wòfɔ la, anɔ ƒo efa ɖeka.
ENGLISH: 17 And she gleaned in the field till evening; and she beat out what she had gleaned, and it came to about a bushel of barley;

EWE: 18 Etsɔe va dua me, eye lɔ̃xoa kpɔ nu si wòfɔ la.
ENGLISH: 18 and she took it up and went into the city.

EWE: Emegbe Rut ɖe nu si wòɖu susɔ la ɖe go hetsɔe nɛ.
ENGLISH: And her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned, and she took out and gave to her what she had had left over from eating all she wanted.

EWE: 19 Eye lɔ̃xoa biae be: “Afi kae nèfɔ nuku le egbea, eye afi kae nèwɔ dɔ le? Woayra ame si bu ŋuwò alea la.”
ENGLISH: 19 And her mother-in-law said to her “Where did you glean today? on which side did you work? may the one who took notice of you be blessed.”

EWE: Ale wògblɔ ame si ƒe agble me wòwɔ dɔ le la na lɔ̃xoa; eye wògagblɔ be: “Ŋutsu si ƒe agble me mewɔ dɔ le egbea ŋkɔe nye Boaz.”
ENGLISH: And she told her mother-in-law the one with whom she had worked, and said “The name of the man I worked with today is Boaz.”

EWE: 20 Naomi gblɔ na lɔ̃xoyɔvia be: “Yehowa, ame si medzudzɔ agbagbeawo kple kukuawo nuveve o la, nayrae.”
ENGLISH: 20 And Naomi said to her daughter-in-law “Blessed be he of Jehovah, that he has never left off his friendliness with the living and with the dead.”

EWE: Eye Naomi gagblɔ nɛ be: “Míaƒe ƒometɔe ŋutsu la nye. Enye ame siwo agbugbɔ mí aƒle la dometɔ ɖeka.”
ENGLISH: And Naomi said to her “The man is a near relative to us, one of our immediate family.”

EWE: 21 Eye Rut, Moab-nyɔnu la, gblɔ be: “Egblɔ nam hã be: ‘Nɔ nye ɖekakpuiawo ŋu, va se ɖe esime wowu nye nuŋeŋe blibo la katã nu.’”
ENGLISH: 21 And Ruth the Moabite said “Another thing: he said to me ‘You are to stick by my boys till they finish reaping all of the field that is mine.’”

EWE: 22 Naomi gblɔ na lɔ̃xoyɔvia Rut be: “Vinye, enyo be nàyi kple eƒe ɖetugbuiawo, wu be nàyi ame bubu ƒe agble me ne woaɖe fu na wò.”
ENGLISH: 22 And Naomi said to her daughter-in-law Ruth “It is best, daughter, that you go out with his girls and they do not encounter you in another field.”

EWE: 23 Ale wònɔ Boaz ƒe ɖetugbuiawo ŋu, eye wòfɔ nuku va se ɖe esime ƒoŋeɣi kple luŋeɣi siaa wu enu. Eye wònɔ lɔ̃xoa gbɔ.
ENGLISH: 23 And she stuck by Boaz’s girls, gleaning till the barley harvest and the wheat harvest were finished; and she stayed with her mother-in-law.

EWE: Rut
ENGLISH: Ruth

EWE: 3 Eyome lɔ̃xoa Naomi gblɔ nɛ be: “Vinye, ɖe nyemadi gbɔɖemeƒe na wò, ne eme nanyo na wò oa?
ENGLISH: 3 And her mother-in-law Naomi said to her “Daughter, I am to look for a resting-place for you isn’t that right? that will be good for you.

EWE: 2 Míaƒe ƒometɔe Boaz, ame si ƒe ɖetugbuiwo ŋu nènɔ la nye.
ENGLISH: 2 And now Boaz, whose girls you have been with, is our relative, you know.

EWE: Ele ƒo gbɔ ge le nukuƒoƒe zã sia.
ENGLISH: Here will he be winnowing the barley threshing-floor tonight;

EWE: 3 Eya ta le tsi nàsi ami ʋeʋĩ, eye nàdo wò awuwo ne nàyi nukuƒoƒe la. Mègana ŋutsua nanya be nèva o, va se ɖe esime wòɖu nu no nu vɔ.
ENGLISH: 3 take a bath and oil yourself and dress and go down to the threshing-floor; do not disclose yourself to the man till he has finished eating and drinking;

EWE: 4 Ne eyi ɖamlɔ anyi la, lé ŋku ɖe teƒe si wòmlɔ la ŋu, eye nàyi aklo avɔ le eƒe afɔnu ne nàmlɔ afi ma. Ekema agblɔ nu si nàwɔ la na wò.”
ENGLISH: 4 and when he lies down find out the place where he lies and come and lift the blanket at his feet and lie down, and he will tell you what you are to do.”

EWE: 5 Eɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Nu siwo katã nègblɔ nam la, mawɔe.”
ENGLISH: 5 And she said to her “I will do just as you say,”

EWE: 6 Ale wòyi nukuƒoƒe la hewɔ abe ale si tututu lɔ̃xoa gblɔ nɛ ene.
ENGLISH: 6 and went down to the threshing-floor and did just as her mother-in-law had charged her to.

EWE: 7 Ɣemaɣi Boaz ɖu nu, no nu, eye eƒe dzi kpɔ dzidzɔ. Emegbe eyi ɖamlɔ anyi ɖe nuku siwo woli kɔ ɖi la ƒe mlɔenu.
ENGLISH: 7 And Boaz ate and drank and was feeling well, and came to lie down at the edge of the heap of grain, and she came quietly and lifted the blanket at his feet and lay down.

EWE: Azɔ Rut wɔ dzaa va klo nu le eƒe afɔnu hemlɔ anyi. 8 Eye le zãtiƒe la, ŋutsu la dzo nyanyanya.
ENGLISH: 8 And at midnight the man was startled and rolled over and found there was a woman lying at his feet;

EWE: Ebi kɔ, eye wòkpɔ nyɔnu aɖe mlɔ anyi ɖe eƒe afɔnu. 9 Eye wòbiae be: “Wò ame kae?” Eɖo eŋu be: “Nye Rut, wò dɔlanyɔnue.
ENGLISH: 9 and he said “Who are you?” and she said “I am your servant Ruth; spread the flap of your cloak over your servant, because you are next of kin.”

EWE: Keke wò avɔ ɖe wò dɔlanyɔnu la dzi, elabena mía gbugbɔƒlelawo dometɔ ɖekae nènye.” 10 Eye wògblɔ be: “Yehowa neyra wò, vinye.
ENGLISH: 10 And he said “Blessed be you of Jehovah, daughter; you have shown a better friendship last than first, not going after the young men, rich or poor.

EWE: Èɖe wò lɔlɔ̃ vavã fia fifia wu tsã, elabena mèdze ɖekakpuiwo, woɖanye ame tsɛwo alo kesinɔtɔwo o, yome o. 11 Eya ta vinye, mègavɔ̃ o.
ENGLISH: 11 And now, daughter, do not be afraid: I will do for you just as you say, because all the gate of my people knows you are a worthy woman.

EWE: 12 Togbɔ be nyateƒee wònye be mia gbugbɔƒlelawo dometɔ ɖekae menye hã la, mia gbugbɔƒlela aɖe li, si do ƒome kpli mi wum.
ENGLISH: 12 But now the thing is, I certainly am a next of kin, but there is also a next of kin closer than I am.

EWE: 13 Tsi afi sia dɔ, eye ne ŋu ke wòbe yeagbugbɔ wò aƒle la, enyo!
ENGLISH: 13 Stay through the night, and in the morning if he will act as next of kin to you, all right, let him; but if he is not disposed to, then I will do it, as Jehovah lives.

EWE: Negbugbɔ wò ƒle faa.
ENGLISH: Lie still till morning.”

EWE: Wò ya mlɔ afii va se ɖe ŋdi.” 14 Ale wòmlɔ eƒe afɔnu va se ɖe ŋdi, eye wòfɔ hafi xexea me kɔ woayi ame kpɔ ge adze sii.
ENGLISH: 14 And she lay at his feet till morning, and stood up before one man could recognize another; and he thought “It must not be known that the woman had come to the threshing-floor,”

EWE: Eye wògblɔ nɛ be: “Mègana ame aɖeke nanya be nyɔnu aɖe va nukuƒoƒe la o.” 15 Egagblɔ nɛ be: “Tsɔ taɖedzi si le ŋuwò la vɛ, eye nàkeke eme.”
ENGLISH: 15 and said “Let’s have the shawl you have on; hold on to it”; and she held on to it, and he measured out six of barley and set it on her, and went into the city.

EWE: Ale wòkeke eme, eye wòdzidze ƒo dzidzenu ade ɖe eme hedroe nɛ, emegbe ŋutsu la yi dua me. 16 Esi Rut trɔ yi lɔ̃xoa gbɔ la, ebiae be: “Vinye, aleke nèdee?”
ENGLISH: 16 And she came to her mother-in-law, and she said “How did you come out, daughter?” and she told her everything that the man had done with her,

EWE: 17 Rut gblɔ kpee be: “Ƒo dzidzenu ade siae wòtsɔ nam, eye wògblɔ nam be: ‘Mègayi lɔ̃xowò gbɔ asi ƒuƒlu o.’”
ENGLISH: 17 and said “He gave me these six of barley, because he said ‘Do not come to your mother-in-law empty-handed.’”

EWE: 18 Eye wògblɔ be: “Vinye, nɔ anyi ɖe afi sia, ne nàkpɔ ale si nya la ava yii, elabena ŋutsua maɖe dzi ɖi o, va se ɖe esime wòkpɔ nya la gbɔ wu enu egbea hafi.”
ENGLISH: 18 And she said “Stay here, daughter, till you know how things will go, because the man will not stop without finishing the business today.”

EWE: Rut
ENGLISH: Ruth

EWE: 4 Azɔ Boaz yi dugbo la nu hebɔbɔ nɔ afi ma. Eye kpɔ ɖa, gbugbɔƒlela si ƒe nya Boaz gblɔ la va yina. Eye Boaz gblɔ be: “Asimasi, va bɔbɔ nɔ afii.” Ale wòyi ɖanɔ anyi.
ENGLISH: 4 And Boaz had gone up to the gate and sat down there; and along came the next of kin of whom Boaz had spoken, and he said “Come over and sit down here, So-and-so!” and he came over and sat down.

EWE: 2 Eyome Boaz ɖe ŋutsu ewo tso dumemetsitsiawo dome gblɔ be: “Mibɔbɔ nɔ afii.”
ENGLISH: 2 And he took ten men, elders of the city, and said “Sit down here,” and they did.

EWE: Ale wobɔbɔ nɔ anyi. 3 Eye Boaz gblɔ na gbugbɔƒlela la be: “Naomi, ame si gbɔ tso Moab-nyigba dzi la, le mía nɔvi Elimelek ƒe agble la dzram.
ENGLISH: 3 And he said to the next of kin “Naomi, the one that has come back from Moab, has sold out brother Elimelec’s share of the field;

EWE: 4 Eya ta mebu be ele be mana nànya ale be, ‘Nàxɔe aƒle le nye dukɔ la me tɔwo kple eƒe ametsitsiwo ŋkume. Ne àgbugbɔe aƒle la, gbugbɔe ƒle.
ENGLISH: 4 and I thought I would give you notice to buy in the presence of those who are sitting here and of the elders of my people.

EWE: Gake ne màgbugbɔe aƒle o la, gblɔe nam ne manya, elabena wòe wòle be nàgbugbɔe aƒle, eye nyee gakplɔ wò ɖo.’”
ENGLISH: If you will redeem, do so; and if you will not, tell me so that I may know, because there is you to redeem, and I come after you.”

EWE: Eɖo eŋu be: “Melɔ̃ be magbugbɔe aƒle.”
ENGLISH: And he said “I will redeem”;

EWE: 5 Eye Boaz gblɔ be: “Gbe si gbe nàƒle agblea le Naomi si la, àxɔ Rut, Moab-nyɔnu la, ame si srɔ̃ ku, hã aƒle, ne nàna ŋutsu si ku la ƒe ŋkɔ nanɔ eƒe domenyinu la ŋu.”
ENGLISH: 5 and Boaz said “On the day that you get the land out of Naomi’s hands you also get Moabite Ruth, the dead man’s widow, to set up the dead man’s name over his estate.”

EWE: 6 Ke gbugbɔƒlela la gblɔ be: “Nyemate ŋu agbugbɔe aƒle o, ne nye ŋutɔ nye domenyinu dome nagagblẽ o. Mena mɔ wò be nàgbugbɔe aƒle, elabena nyemate ŋu agbugbɔe aƒle o.”
ENGLISH: 6 And the next of kin said “I shall not be able to redeem personally, for fear of impairing my estate; do the redeeming for me yourself, because I shall not be able to redeem.”

EWE: 7 Le blemaɣeyiɣiwo me la, enye kɔnu le Israel be ne ame aɖe agbugbɔ nane aƒle alo aɖɔli nane eye wòdi be kpeɖodzi nanɔ eŋu la, ele be amea naɖe eƒe afɔkpa atsɔ ana ame si le nua xɔm la, eye esia nyea kpeɖoɖo nu dzi le Israel.
ENGLISH: 7 And there was formerly this in Israel for redemption and for substitution, to validate every transaction: a man took off his sandal and gave it to the other party, and this was the attestation in Israel;

EWE: 8 Eya ta esi gbugbɔƒlela la gblɔ na Boaz be, “Xɔe ƒle” la, gbugbɔƒlela la ɖe eya ŋutɔ ƒe afɔkpa.
ENGLISH: 8 and the next of kin said to Boaz “Buy for yourself” and took off his sandal.

EWE: 9 Eye Boaz gblɔ na ametsitsiawo kple dua me tɔwo katã be: “Miawoe nye ɖasefowo egbea be, mexɔ Elimelek ƒe nuwo katã kpakple Kilion kple Mahlon ƒe nuwo katã ƒle le Naomi si.
ENGLISH: 9 And Boaz said to the elders’ and all the people “You are witnesses today that I buy out of Naomi’s hands everything that belonged to Elimelec and everything that belonged to Kiljon and Mahlon,

EWE: 10 Mexɔ Moab-nyɔnu Rut, Mahlon srɔ̃ la, hã wòzu srɔ̃nye, ne mana srɔ̃a si ku la ƒe ŋkɔ nanɔ eƒe domenyinu la ŋu, ale be srɔ̃a kukua ƒe ŋkɔ nagabu le nɔviawo dome kple wo dedu me o.
ENGLISH: 10 and I also buy Mahlon’s widow Moabite Ruth for my wife, to set up the dead man’s name over his estate and not have the dead man’s name disappear from among his brothers and from the gate of his people; you are witnesses today.”

EWE: Miawoe nye ɖasefowo egbea.” 11 Ale ame siwo katã le dugbo la nu kple ametsitsiawo gblɔ be: “Míawoe nye ɖasefowo! Yehowa nena nyɔnu si gbɔna aƒewò me la nanɔ abe Rahel kple Lea ene, nyɔnu eve siwo tsò Israel ƒe aƒe la. Nu nedze edzi na wò le Efrata, eye nàwɔ ŋkɔ nyui na ɖokuiwò le Betlehem.
ENGLISH: 11 And all the people in the gate and the elders said “We are: Jehovah grant the woman who is coming into your house to be like Rachel and Leah, the two that built up the house of Israel; may you earn high standing in Ephrathah and make a name in Bethlehem,

EWE: 12 Vi siwo Yehowa ana ɖetugbui sia nadzi na wò la, nana wò aƒe nanɔ abe Perez, ame si Tamar dzi na Yuda la, tɔ ene.”
ENGLISH: 12 and your family be like the family of Peres whom Tamar bore to Judah, by the issue which Jehovah shall give you out of this girl.”

EWE: 13 Ale Boaz ɖe Rut wòzu srɔ̃a. Edɔ kplii, eye Yehowa na wòfɔ fu dzi ŋutsuvi.
ENGLISH: 13 And Boaz took Ruth and she became his wife; and he went in to her and Jehovah gave her motherhood, and she had a son;

EWE: 14 Eye nyɔnuwo gblɔ na Naomi be: “Woakafu Yehowa, ame si mete gbugbɔƒlela wò egbea o. Woaɖe gbeƒã eƒe ŋkɔ le Israel!
ENGLISH: 14 and the women said to Naomi “Blessed be Jehovah, who has not deprived you today of a next of kin whose name may be called in Israel,

EWE: 15 Eyae zu ame si gbugbɔ wò agbe ɖo te, kple ame si akpɔ dziwò le wò nyagãkuku me, elabena lɔ̃xoyɔviwò si lɔ̃ wò ŋutɔ, si nyo na wò wu viŋutsu adre, ye dzii.”
ENGLISH: 15 and whom you will have as a lifesaver to provide for your old age, because your daughter-in-law who loves you, who is better to you than seven sons, has given him birth.”

EWE: 16 Eye Naomi kɔ ɖevi la ɖe akɔ, eye wòkpɔ edzi.
ENGLISH: 16 And Naomi took the child and laid him in her lap and became caretaker to him.

EWE: 17 Eye nyɔnu aƒelikawo na ŋkɔe. Wogblɔ be, “Wodzi ŋutsuvi na Naomi,” eye woyɔe be Obed. Eyae dzi Isai, David fofo.
ENGLISH: 17 And the neighbor women called him by a name, saying “Naomi has had a son born to her,” and named him ʽObed; he was the father of Jesse the father of David.

EWE: 18 Perez ƒe dzidzimeviwoe nye esi: Perez dzi Hezron;
ENGLISH: 18 And this is Peres’s line. Peres begot Hesron,

EWE: 19 Hezron dzi Ram; Ram dzi Aminadab;
ENGLISH: 19 and Hesron begot Ram, and Ram begot ʽAmminadab,

EWE: 20 Aminadab dzi Nahason; Nahason dzi Salmon;
ENGLISH: 20 and ʽAmminadab begot Nahshon, and Nahshon begot Salmon,

EWE: 21 Salmon dzi Boaz; Boaz dzi Obed;
ENGLISH: 21 and Salmon begot Boaz, and Boaz begot ʽObed,

EWE: 22 Obed dzi Isai; eye Isai dzi David.
ENGLISH: 22 and ʽObed begot Jesse, and Jesse begot David.

EWE: 1 Samuel
ENGLISH: 1 Samuel

EWE: 1 Ŋutsu aɖe tso Ramatayim-Zofim le Efrayim tonuto la me, eŋkɔe nye Elkana, enye Yeroham vi, Elihu vi, Tohu vi, Zuf vi, eye wònye Efrayimtɔ.
ENGLISH: 1 Now there was a certain man of Ramathaim, a Suphite of the highland of Ephraim, named Elkanah, son of Jeroham the son of Elihu the son of Tohu the son of Suph, an Ephrathite.

EWE: 2 Srɔ̃ eve nɔ esi; ɖeka ŋkɔe nye Hana, eye evelia ŋkɔe nye Penina. Penina dzi vi, ke Hana ya medzi vi aɖeke o.
ENGLISH: 2 And he had two wives: one’s name was Hannah and the other’s was Peninnah; and Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no children.

EWE: 3 Ŋutsu sia tsoa wo de ƒe sia ƒe yina ɖadea ta agu hesaa vɔ na aʋakɔwo ƒe Yehowa, le Silo. Afi mae Eli vi eveawo, Hofni kple Finehas, nye nunɔlawo na Yehowa le.
ENGLISH: 3 And this man went up from his city from year to year to do reverence and to sacrifice to Jehovah of Armies at Shiloh; and ʽEli’s two sons Hophni and Pinehas, priests of Jehovah, were there.

EWE: 4 Gbe ɖeka esi Elkana sa vɔ la, ena vɔsalã la ƒe akpa aɖewo srɔ̃a Penina kple viaŋutsuwo kpakple vianyɔnuwo katã,
ENGLISH: 4 And one day Elkanah was sacrificing; and he would give a portion to his wife Peninnah and portions to all her sons and daughters,

EWE: 5 ke ena akpa tɔxɛ aɖe Hana ya, elabena Hana ye wòlɔ̃ wu; gake Yehowa mena wòdzi vi o.
ENGLISH: 5 but would give Hannah one portion in vexation, because he loved Hannah and Jehovah had shut her womb;

EWE: 6 Gawu la, atsusia ɖea alɔme le eŋu atraɖii tsɔ nɔa dziku dom nɛ, le esi Yehowa mena wòdzi vi o ta.
ENGLISH: 6 and her rival provoked her besides, to make her fret, because Jehovah had shut up her womb;

EWE: 7 Aleae wòwɔna ƒe sia ƒe, ne Hana yi Yehowa ƒe aƒea me la, atsusia ɖea alɔme le eŋu ale gbegbe be Hana nɔa avi dzi hegbea nuɖuɖu.
ENGLISH: 7 and thus he did year by year, as often as she went up to Jehovah’s house; thus she provoked her. And Hannah cried and did not eat.

EWE: 8 Ke srɔ̃a Elkana bianɛ be: “Hana, nu ka ta nèle avi fam, nu ka ŋuti nègbe nuɖuɖu, eye nu ka ŋuti nèle nu xam vevie alea?
ENGLISH: 8 And her husband Elkanah said to her “Hannah, why do you cry? why are you not eating? why do you feel badly? am I not more to you than ten sons?”

EWE: Ðe nyemenyo na wò wu viŋutsu ewo oa?” 9 Esi woɖu nu eye wono nu vɔ le Silo la, Hana tso; ɣemaɣi la nunɔla Eli nɔ anyi ɖe zikpui dzi le Yehowa ƒe gbedoxɔ la ƒe ʋɔtru nu.
ENGLISH: 9 And Hannah rose after they had eaten at Shiloh, and went and stood before Jehovah, while Priest ʽEli was sitting on his chair by the doorpost of the temple of Jehovah;

EWE: 10 Eye Hana nɔ nu xam vevie, eye wòde asi gbedodoɖa me na Yehowa hele avi fam hehehe.
ENGLISH: 10 and, she being sore at heart, she prayed to Jehovah and wept tears,

EWE: 11 Eye wòɖe adzɔgbe sia be: “Oo aʋakɔwo ƒe Yehowa, ne èkpɔ wò dɔlanyɔnu la ƒe fukpekpe ɖa, eye nèɖo ŋku dzinye, mèŋlɔ wò dɔlanyɔnu be o, eye nèna ŋutsuvi wò dɔlanyɔnu la, ekema matsɔe ana Yehowa le eƒe agbemeŋkekewo katã me, eye talũhɛ aɖeke made ta ŋu nɛ o.”
ENGLISH: 11 and made a vow and said “Jehovah of Armies, if you look upon your servant’s wretched state and remember me, and do not forget your servant but give your servant a man-child, then I will give him to Jehovah all his life, and no razor shall touch his head.”

EWE: 12 Esi wòle gbe dom ɖa eteƒe didi le Yehowa ŋkume la, Eli nɔ ŋku lém ɖe eƒe nu ŋu.
ENGLISH: 12 And, as she was long praying before Jehovah, ʽEli watched her mouth;

EWE: 13 Hana le nu ƒom le dzi me, eƒe nuyiwo koe nɔ ʋaʋãm butubutu, ke eƒe gbe mele ɖiɖim o.
ENGLISH: 13 and Hannah was speaking inwardly only her lips moved, but her voice was not audible and ʽEli thought she was drunk.

EWE: Eya ta Eli ya bu be ahae wòmu. 14 Eli biae be: “Ɣekaɣie nàmu aha ase ɖo?
ENGLISH: 14 And ʽEli said to her “How long are you going to exhibit your drunkenness?

EWE: Dzudzɔ ahanono dzro.”
ENGLISH: Get rid of your wine.”

EWE: 15 Eye Hana ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Gbeɖe, nye aƒetɔ! Nyɔnu si dzi nu te ɖo vevie menye; nyemeno wain alo aha muame aɖeke o, ke boŋ nye luʋɔe metrɔ ƒo ɖe Yehowa ŋkume.
ENGLISH: 15 But Hannah answered “No, sir, I am a woman in trouble; I have not been drinking wine or beer; I was pouring out my soul before Jehovah.

EWE: 16 Mègabu wò dɔlanyɔnu yakamee o, elabena nye dzimaɖitsitsi kple nye vevesese gbogboawo ŋue mele nu ƒom le va se ɖe fifia.”
ENGLISH: 16 Do not take it as if your servant were a reprobate; it was owing to the greatness of my grievance and provocation that I spoke so long.”

EWE: 17 Eli gblɔ nɛ be: “Heyi le ŋutifafa me, eye Israel ƒe Mawu la nawɔ nu si nèbiae la na wò.”
ENGLISH: 17 And ʽEli answered “Go, and good betide you; and may the God of Israel grant your request that you have asked of him.”

EWE: 18 Eɖo eŋu be: “Ne ève wò dɔlanyɔnu la nu ko.”
ENGLISH: 18 And she said “Thank you, sir.”

EWE: Eye nyɔnua lé eƒe mɔ heyi ɖaɖu nu, eye megaɖo nublanuimo azɔ o.
ENGLISH: And the woman went her way, and ate, and no longer had the look in her face.

EWE: 19 Emegbe wofɔ ŋdi kanya yi ɖade ta agu le Yehowa ŋkume, eye wotrɔ yi aƒe le Rama.
ENGLISH: 19 And when they rose the next morning they did reverence before Jehovah and came back to their home at Ramah.

EWE: Eye Elkana dɔ kple srɔ̃a Hana, eye Yehowa trɔ susu ɖe eŋu.
ENGLISH: And Elkanah knew his wife Hannah, and Jehovah remembered her;

EWE: 20 Ale le ƒea me la, Hana fɔ fu dzi ŋutsuvi, eye wòna ŋkɔe be Samuel, elabena egblɔ be, “Yehowa si mee mebiae le.”
ENGLISH: 20 and at the turn of the year she had a son, and named him Samuel “because I asked Jehovah for him.”

EWE: 21 Le ɣeyiɣi aɖe megbe la, Elkana kple eƒe aƒe blibo la yi be wòasa ƒe sia ƒe vɔ na Yehowa ahana eƒe adzɔgbeɖenunana.
ENGLISH: 21 And the man Elkanah, and all his family, went up to sacrifice to Jehovah the annual sacrifice and his vow.

EWE: 22 Ke Hana ya meyi o, elabena egblɔ na srɔ̃a be: “Ne menya tso no na ɖevia ko la, makplɔe ayii; ne wòado ɖe Yehowa ŋkume, eye wòanɔ afi ma koŋ.”
ENGLISH: 22 But Hannah did not go up; for she said to her husband “Not till the boy is weaned, when I will bring him and he shall appear in the presence of Jehovah and stay there permanently”;

EWE: 23 Eye srɔ̃a Elkana gblɔ nɛ be: “Wɔ nu si nèkpɔ be enyo la. Tsi anyi va se ɖe esime nètso no nɛ. Yehowa newɔ nya si nègblɔ la dzi.”
ENGLISH: 23 and Elkanah her husband said to her “Do what you think best: stay till you wean him; only let Jehovah make good his word.”

EWE: Ale nyɔnu la tsi aƒe, eye wòna no via, va se ɖe esime wòtso no nɛ. 24 Esi wòtso no nɛ ko la, ekplɔe yi Silo. Etsɔ nyitsu si xɔ ƒe etɔ̃ kple wɔ efa ɖeka kpakple wain ze gã ɖeka kpe ɖe eŋuti yi Yehowa ƒe me le Silo.
ENGLISH: 24 And the woman stayed and nursed her son till she weaned him; and when she had weaned him she brought him up with her, with a three-year-old steer and bread and a bushel of flour and a skin of wine, and came to Jehovah’s house at Shiloh, with the boy with them;

EWE: Eye ɖevi la le eŋu. 25 Wowu nyitsu la, eye wokplɔ ɖevi la yi na Eli.
ENGLISH: 25 and they came before Jehovah, and his father made the sacrifice that he made year by year to Jehovah, and brought the boy and slaughtered the steer; and Hannah the boy’s mother brought the boy to ʽEli

EWE: 26 Hana gblɔ nɛ be: “Nye aƒetɔ, meɖe kuku! Zi ale si nèle agbe la, nyee nye nyɔnu si nɔ tsitre ɖe gbɔwò afi sia nɔ gbe dom ɖa na Yehowa.
ENGLISH: 26 and said “O, my lord, as you live, my lord, I am the woman who stood here by you to pray to Jehovah.

EWE: 27 Ðevi sia tae medo gbe ɖa le, eye Yehowa wɔ nu si mebiae la nam.
ENGLISH: 27 It was for this boy that I prayed, and Jehovah has granted me my request that I asked of him.

EWE: 28 Nye hã mele etsɔm na Yehowa. Ŋkeke ale si wòle agbe la, anye ame si wotsɔ na Yehowa.”
ENGLISH: 28 And I on my part have granted him to Jehovah; ever since he has been, he is granted to Jehovah.”

EWE: 1 Samuel
ENGLISH: 1 Samuel

EWE: 2 Eye Hana do gbe ɖa gblɔ be: “Nye dzi le aseye tsom le Yehowa me; Yehowa na nye dzo do biɖaa. Nye nu ke baa ɖe nye futɔwo ŋu, Elabena mele dzidzɔ kpɔm le wò xɔxɔdɔwo me.
ENGLISH: 2 And Hannah prayed and said “My heart exults in Jehovah, my horn is uplifted in Jehovah, my mouth opens wide against my enemies, because I rejoice in your deliverance.

EWE: 2 Ame aɖeke mele kɔkɔe abe Yehowa ene o, Ðeke meli o, negbe wò ko, Eye agakpe aɖeke meli abe mía Mawu la ene o.
ENGLISH: 2 There is no Holy One like Jehovah; for there is none but you; and there is no Rock like our God.

EWE: 3 Miganɔ nu ƒom dadatɔe o; Dadanyawo meganɔ dodom le mia nu o, Elabena sidzedze ƒe Mawue Yehowa nye, Eyae daa nuwɔnawo kpɔna.
ENGLISH: 3 Talk not overmuch loftily, loftily, arrogance coming out of your mouths; for Jehovah is a God of knowledge; and are not deeds measured out?

EWE: 4 Kalẽtɔwo ƒe datiwo ŋe kliklikli, Ke ame beliwo kpɔ ŋusẽ.
ENGLISH: 4 Champions’ bows are shivered, and men who were stumbling have girded themselves with stoutness;

EWE: 5 Ame siwo ɖi ƒo la va le apadɔ wɔm ɖe abolo ta, Ke dɔ megale dɔwuitɔwo ya wum azɔ o. Konɔ dzi vi adre, Ke nyɔnu si dzi vi geɖe la va zu konɔ.
ENGLISH: 5 Well-fed men have hired themselves out for bread, and hungry men have ceased; even the barren has borne seven, and she who had many children is forlorn.

EWE: 6 Yehowa wua ame eye wòkpɔa agbe ta; Edea ame Tsiẽƒe, eye wòfɔa ame ɖe tsitre.
ENGLISH: 6 Jehovah puts to death and brings to life, brings down to the world below, and up.

EWE: 7 Yehowa nana ame daa ahe, eye wònana ame zua kesinɔtɔ; Ebɔbɔa ame ɖe anyi, eye wòdoa ame ɖe dzi.
ENGLISH: 7 Jehovah impoverishes and enriches, abases and exalts,

EWE: 8 Ame si kɔa ame tsɛ ɖe dzi tso ke me; Edoa ame dahe ɖe dzi tso dzofi me, Ne wòana woanɔ anyi kple bubumewo, Eye wònana wobɔbɔ nɔa bubuteƒe. Yehowa tɔe anyigba ƒe anyinɔwo nye, Eye wòtsɔ anyigba wɔnu la ɖo wo dzi.
ENGLISH: 8 Lifts the poor man from the dust, raises the needy man from the rubbish-dump, to seat him with nobles and allot to him a throne of glory; For the pillars of the earth are Jehovah’s, and he has set the world upon them.

EWE: 9 Edzɔa ame siwo wɔa nuteƒe nɛ la ƒe zɔzɔme ŋu, Ke ɖoɖoe azi le ame vɔ̃ɖiwo nu le viviti me, Elabena menye ame ƒe ŋusẽe nana wòɖua dzi o.
ENGLISH: 9 He guards the feet of his godly, and ungodly men are stilled in darkness; for not by strength does a man prevail.

EWE: 10 Yehowa agbã ame siwo tso ɖe eŋu la gudugudu; Aɖe gbe ɖe wo dzi tso dziƒowo.
ENGLISH: 10 Jehovah strikes with dismay the one who contends with him, thunders over him in the sky; Jehovah pronounces judgment for the ends of the earth,

EWE: Yehowa adrɔ̃ ʋɔnu va se ɖe anyigba ƒe mlɔenu, Ana ŋusẽ eƒe fia la, Eye wòado eƒe amesiamina la ƒe dzo ɖe dzi.”
ENGLISH: to give power to his king and uplift the horn of his anointed.”

EWE: 11 Eye Elkana dzo yi eƒe me le Rama, ke ɖevi la subɔ Yehowa le nunɔla Eli gbɔ.
ENGLISH: 11 And she left him there before Jehovah and went to Ramah. And the boy officiated in the service of Jehovah before Priest ʽEli.

EWE: 12 Eli viwo nye ame vɔ̃ɖiwo; womedea bubu aɖeke Yehowa ŋu o.
ENGLISH: 12 And ʽEli’s sons were reprobates who did not know Jehovah

EWE: 13 Aleae wowɔna nunɔlawo ƒe gome si dukɔa tsɔ vanɛ lae nye esi: Ɣesiaɣi si ame aɖe le vɔ sam, eye woɖo lã la dzo dzi la, nunɔla la ƒe subɔvi léa gaflo nuetɔ̃ ɖe asi vana,
ENGLISH: 13 nor the due of the priest from the people; when any man was offering a sacrifice, the priest’s man would come when they were boiling the flesh, with the three-tined fork in his hand,

EWE: 14 eye wòƒonɛ ɖe nuɖagba, nuɖaze alɔeve, gaze alo nuɖaze alɔɖekɛ la me.
ENGLISH: 14 and strike it into the kettle or pipkin or caldron or stewpan; whatever the fork brought up, the priest took to himself.

EWE: Nu sia nu si gaflo la he do goe la, nunɔla la tsɔnɛ.
ENGLISH: Thus they did to all Israel who came there to Shiloh.

EWE: Aleae wowɔna ɖe Israel-vi siwo katã vana Silo la ŋu. 15 Azɔ hã, hafi ame si le vɔ sam la natsɔ lãa ƒe ami ado dzudzɔ la, nunɔla la ƒe subɔvi va gblɔna nɛ be: “Tsɔ lã vɛ woamè na nunɔla. Mele ɖaɖaa dim o, mumua dim wòle.”
ENGLISH: 15 Even before they had burned the fat, the priest’s man would come and say to the man who was sacrificing “Give flesh to roast for the priest, so that he shall not get boiled flesh from you, but raw.”

EWE: 16 Ne amea gblɔ nɛ be: “Na woatsɔ amia ado dzudzɔ gbã, emegbe nàtsɔ nu sia nu si dzro wò” la, egblɔna be: “Kpao, ke boŋ tsɔe nam fifi laa; ne menye nenema o la, matsɔe sesẽe!”
ENGLISH: 16 And the man would say “They have to burn the fat first; then take whatever you like.” And he would say “No, you are to give it now; if not, I take it by force.”

EWE: 17 Ale subɔviawo ƒe nu vɔ̃ va lolo ŋutɔ le Yehowa ŋkume, elabena womede bubu Yehowa ƒe vɔsa la ŋu o.
ENGLISH: 17 And the young men’s sin was very great before Jehovah, because people held Jehovah’s offerings in contempt.

EWE: 18 Ke Samuel subɔna le Yehowa ŋkume, ɖevi dzaa ko wònye, eye wòdoa aklalakɔmewu.
ENGLISH: 18 And Samuel, a boy belted with a white linen ephod, was officiating before Jehovah.

EWE: 19 Azɔ hã, dadaa tɔa awu ʋlaya sue aɖe si ŋu abɔ mele o nɛ, eye wòtsɔnɛ vana nɛ ƒe sia ƒe ne ekplɔ srɔ̃a ɖo va ƒe sia ƒe vɔwo sa ge.
ENGLISH: 19 And his mother made him a little robe and brought it up to him when she came up with her husband to offer the annual sacrifice.

EWE: 20 Eye Eli yra Elkana kple srɔ̃a gblɔ be: “Yehowa nena nyɔnu sia nadzi vi na wò nàtsɔ aɖo esi nèdo na Yehowa la teƒe.”
ENGLISH: 20 And ʽEli blessed Elkanah and his wife, and said “May Jehovah repay you with offspring by this woman for the grant that has been made to Jehovah.”

EWE: Eye wogbugbɔ yi wo nɔƒe.
ENGLISH: And they went to their place.

EWE: 21 Eye Yehowa trɔ susu ɖe Hana ŋu, eye wòfɔ fu; eye wòdzi ŋutsuvi etɔ̃ kple nyɔnuvi eve. Ke Samuel ɖevi la nɔ tsitsim le Yehowa gbɔ.
ENGLISH: 21 And Jehovah visited Hannah, and she conceived and had three sons and two daughters; and the boy Samuel grew up with Jehovah.

EWE: 22 Ke Eli tsi ku amegã, eye wòse nu siwo katã wɔm viawo le ɖe Israel blibo la ŋu kple ale si wole nyɔnu siwo subɔna le takpegbadɔa nu la gbɔ dɔmee.
ENGLISH: 22 And ʽEli, who was very old, used to hear of all that his sons were doing to all Israel, and their lying with the women who did duty at the door of the Tent of Meeting;

EWE: 23 Eye wògblɔna na wo be: “Nu ka tae miele nu siawo wɔm? Elabena nu siwo sem mele tso mia ŋu le ame sia ame nu la menyo o.
ENGLISH: 23 and he said to them “Why do you do such things as these, that I hear these bad things about you from all the people?

EWE: 24 Ao, vinyewo, elabena nya si le ɖiɖim le Yehowa ƒe dukɔ la dome mele sesem la menyo o hee.
ENGLISH: 24 Do not do it, my sons; for the report that I hear Jehovah’s people circulating is not good.

EWE: 25 Ne amegbetɔ wɔ nu vɔ̃ ɖe nɔvia amegbetɔ ŋu la, ame aɖe aɖe kuku na Yehowa ɖe eta; ke ne Yehowa ŋue amegbetɔ wɔ nu vɔ̃ ɖo ɖe, ame kae li ado gbe ɖa ɖe eta?” Ke wogbe toɖoɖo wo fofo, elabena Yehowa ɖoe be yeawu wo.
ENGLISH: 25 If a man sins against a man, God will mediate; but if a man sins against Jehovah, who shall mediate for him?” but his sons would not obey their father, because it was Jehovah’s pleasure to cause their death.

EWE: 26 Le ɣeyiɣi siawo katã me la, Samuel ɖevi la le tsitsim, eye eƒe nu nyo Yehowa kple amegbetɔwo siaa ŋu.
ENGLISH: 26 And the boy Samuel went on pleasing both Jehovah and men.

EWE: 27 Eye Mawu ƒe ame aɖe va Eli gbɔ gblɔ nɛ be: “Ale Yehowa gblɔe nye esi: ‘Meɖe ɖokuinye fia tɔgbuiwò ƒe aƒe la, esime wonye kluviwo na Farao ƒe aƒe la le Egipte.
ENGLISH: 27 And a man of God came to ʽEli and said to him “Says Jehovah, I did reveal myself to your family when they were in Egypt, the Pharaoh’s home,

EWE: 28 Eye metiae tso Israel-toawo katã dome, be wòawɔ nunɔladɔ nam, eye wòalia nye vɔsamlekpui la asa vɔ, ado dzudzɔ ʋeʋĩ, eye wòado kɔmewu le ŋkunyeme; eye metsɔ Israel-viwo ƒe dzovɔsawo katã na tɔgbuiwò ƒe aƒe la.
ENGLISH: 28 and chose it out of all the tribes of Israel to be priests to me, to go up my altar, to burn incense and bear an ephod before me, and gave your family all the fire-offerings of the sons of Israel.

EWE: 29 Nu ka tae miedo vlo nye vɔsa kple nye nunana si ƒe se mede le nye nɔƒe la? Nu ka tae nèle bubu dem viwòwo ŋu wum eye mieɖu nye dukɔ Israel ƒe vɔsalã ƒe akpa nyuitɔwo heda ami?
ENGLISH: 29 Why do you look askance at my sacrifices and offerings which I have ordained, and rank your sons above me, fattening them on the prime of the offerings of Israel my people?

EWE: 30 “‘Eya ta Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la, ƒe numegbee nye esi: “Megblɔe vavã be, wò aƒe kple tɔgbuiwò ƒe aƒe la azɔ le ŋkunyeme ɖaa.”
ENGLISH: 30 So Israel’s God Jehovah quoth, I did say your family, your own and the family you come of, should walk before me forever; but now, quoth Jehovah, away with the thought; for those who honor me I will honor, and those who despise me shall be of little account.

EWE: Ke azɔ la, Yehowa be: “Nede megbe xaa tso gbɔnye, elabena ame siwo buam la, woawoe mabu, eye ame siwo doa vlom la, mado vlo wo.” 31 Kpɔ ɖa!
ENGLISH: 31 Here are days coming when I will hew off your arm and the arm of your kin, that there shall never be an old man in your family in all time.

EWE: 32 Le nu nyui siwo katã mawɔ na Israel dome la, wò ya àkpɔ nu si ana nàʋã ŋu le nɔnyeƒe, eye ame tsitsi aɖeke maganɔ aƒewò me akpɔ o.
ENGLISH: 32 And you will look upon a rival in my dwelling amid all the good that is done to Israel, and never again will there be an old man in your house.

EWE: 33 Gake wò ame si le subɔsubɔm le nye vɔsamlekpuia gbɔ si nyematsrɔ̃ ɖa o la ana wò ŋkuwo natsi, eye wòado nuxaxa na wò; ke wò aƒemetɔ akpa gãtɔ aku ɖe amewo ƒe yi nu.
ENGLISH: 33 But not every man of yours will I cut off from my altar, to consume your eyes and to famish your soul; but all the main body of your family shall die by the sword of men.

EWE: 34 Eye nu si ava dzɔ ɖe viwòŋutsu eveawo, Hofni kple Finehas, dzi la anye dzesi na wò: Wo ame evea woaku gbe ɖeka.
ENGLISH: 34 And this is the token you are to have, what shall come to your two sons Hophni and Pinehas: they shall both die in one day.

EWE: 35 Eye maɖo nunɔla wɔnuteƒe aɖe na ɖokuinye. Awɔ nu ɖe nye dzi ƒe didi nu; matso aƒe si anɔ anyi ɖaa la nɛ, eye wòazɔ le nye amesiamina la ŋkume ɖaa.
ENGLISH: 35 And I will set up for myself a steadfast priest; he shall do as is in my heart and mind; and I will build him a steadfast house, and he shall walk before my anointed for all time.

EWE: 36 Eye ame sia ame si kpɔtɔ ɖe aƒewò me la ava bɔbɔ ɖe eŋkume be wòaxe fe na ye ana abolo ye ahagblɔ be: “Meɖe kuku, de nunɔladɔ aɖe asi nam, ne makpɔ abolo vi aɖe aɖu.”’”
ENGLISH: 36 And whoever is left in your family shall come to do reverence to him for a bit of silver and a biscuit, and shall say ‘Please attach me to one of the priestly offices, so that I can eat a morsel of bread.’”

EWE: 1 Samuel
ENGLISH: 1 Samuel

EWE: 3 Ɣemaɣi la, Samuel ɖevi la nɔ Yehowa subɔm le Eli gbɔ. Le ŋkeke mawo me la, ƒãa hafi Yehowa ƒe gbe nava na ame aɖe, eye ŋutegakpɔkpɔ hã mebɔ o.
ENGLISH: 3 And the boy Samuel was officiating in the service of Jehovah before ʽEli and Jehovah’s word was rare in those days; there was no widespread seeing of visions

EWE: 2 Gbe ɖeka Eli, ame si ƒe ŋkuwo nɔ tsitsim eye meganɔ nu kpɔm o la, mlɔ enɔƒe.
ENGLISH: 2 and on that day, while ʽEli was lying in his place (his eyes had begun to grow dim so that he could not see),

EWE: 3 Womekpɔ tsi Mawu ƒe akaɖi la haɖe o, eye Samuel mlɔ anyi ɖe Yehowa ƒe gbedoxɔ me, le afi si Mawu ƒe Aɖaka la le.
ENGLISH: 3 and the lamp of God had not yet gone out, and Samuel was lying in the temple of Jehovah, where the ark of God was,

EWE: 4 Eye Yehowa yɔ Samuel. Etɔ be: “Nyee nye esi.”
ENGLISH: 4 Jehovah called “Samuel, Samuel!” and he said “Here I am,”

EWE: 5 Eye wòƒu du yi Eli gbɔ gblɔ be: “Nyee nye esi, elabena èyɔm.”
ENGLISH: 5 and ran to ʽEli and said “Here I am, because you called me.”

EWE: Ke egblɔ be: “Nyemeyɔ wò o. Gbugbɔ yi ɖamlɔ anyi.”
ENGLISH: And he said “I did not call; go back and lie down.”

EWE: Ale wòyi ɖamlɔ anyi.
ENGLISH: And he went and lay down.

EWE: 6 Yehowa gayɔe ake be: “Samuel!” Enumake Samuel fɔ yi Eli gbɔ gblɔ be: “Nyee nye esi, elabena èyɔm.” Ke egblɔ be: “Vinye, nyemeyɔ wò o. Gbugbɔ yi ɖamlɔ anyi.”
ENGLISH: 6 And again Jehovah called “Samuel, Samuel!” and he went to ʽEli and said “Here I am, because you called me”; and he said “I did not call, my son; go back and lie down.”

EWE: 7 (Ke Samuel mekpɔ dze si Yehowa nyuie o, eye womeɖe Yehowa ƒe nya fiae haɖe o.)
ENGLISH: 7 (And Samuel did not yet know Jehovah, and Jehovah’s word was not yet revealed to him.)

EWE: 8 Eye Yehowa gayɔe zi etɔ̃lia be: “Samuel!” Enumake wòfɔ yi Eli gbɔ gblɔ be: “Nyee nye esi, elabena èyɔm.”
ENGLISH: 8 And Jehovah called Samuel for the third time; and he ran and went to ʽEli and said “Here I am, because you called me”; and ʽEli perceived that Jehovah was calling the boy.

EWE: Ale Eli kpɔe dze sii be, Yehowae le ɖevi la yɔm. 9 Eya ta Eli gblɔ na Samuel be: “Yi ɖamlɔ anyi. Eye ne egayɔ wò la, nàgblɔ be: ‘Yehowa, ƒo nu, elabena wò subɔla le to dzi.’”
ENGLISH: 9 And ʽEli said to Samuel “Go and lie down, and if he calls to you say ‘Speak, Jehovah, for your servant is listening’”; and Samuel went and lay down in his place.

EWE: Ale Samuel yi ɖamlɔ emlɔƒe. 10 Yehowa va tɔ ɖe afi ma heyɔe abe tsã ene be: “Samuel, Samuel!”
ENGLISH: 10 And Jehovah came and stood and called, as he had before, “Samuel, Samuel!” and Samuel said “Speak, for your servant is listening.”

EWE: Eye Samuel gblɔ be: “Ƒo nu, elabena wò subɔla le to dzi.” 11 Yehowa gblɔ na Samuel be: “Kpɔ ɖa!
ENGLISH: 11 And Jehovah said to Samuel “Lo, I will do such a thing in Israel that when anybody hears of it both his ears will buzz.

EWE: 12 Gbe ma gbee mawɔ nu siwo katã megblɔ ɖe Eli ƒe aƒe ŋu la ɖe eŋu, tso gɔmedzedze va se ɖe nuwuwu.
ENGLISH: 12 On that day I will make good to ʽEli everything that I have denounced against his family, and do it all at once.

EWE: 13 Gblɔ nɛ be mele ʋɔnu drɔ̃ ge eƒe aƒe la tegbee ɖe vodada si ŋu wònya nu le la ta, elabena viawo le busunu wɔm ɖe Mawu ŋu, ke meka mo na wo o.
ENGLISH: 13 And I will tell him that I will execute a perpetual judgment upon his family, because he knew that his sons were insulting God and he did not check them;

EWE: 14 Esia tae meka atam ɖe Eli ƒe aƒe la ŋu be, ne wosa vɔ ɖe Eli ƒe aƒe la ta alo na nu ɖe eta hã la, womagbe tohehe nɛ gbeɖe o.”
ENGLISH: 14 and so I swear to ʽEli’s family that the offense of ʽEli’s family shall not be purged by sacrifice and offering forever.”

EWE: 15 Eye Samuel mlɔ anyi va se ɖe esime ŋu ke; eye wòʋu Yehowa ƒe aƒe la ƒe ʋɔtruwo.
ENGLISH: 15 And Samuel lay abed till morning, and in the morning he opened the door of Jehovah’s house.

EWE: Ke Samuel le vɔvɔ̃m be yeagblɔ ŋutega la na Eli.
ENGLISH: And Samuel was afraid to tell ʽEli the vision.

EWE: 16 Gake Eli yɔ Samuel be: “Vinye Samuel!”
ENGLISH: 16 And ʽEli called Samuel and said “Samuel, my son!” and he said “Here I am.”

EWE: Eye wòtɔ be: “Nyee nye esi.” 17 Ebiae be: “Nya kae wògblɔ na wò? Meɖe kuku, mègaɣlae ɖem o.
ENGLISH: 17 And he said “What was the word that he spoke to you? now do not conceal it from me; Jehovah do so to you, and more, if you conceal from me anything of all the words that he spoke to you.”

EWE: Mawu nefia wò, eye wòagafia wò ɖe edzi, ne èɣla nane ɖem le nya siwo katã wògblɔ na wò la dome!” 18 Ale Samuel gblɔ nya sia nya nɛ, eye meɣla naneke ɖee o. Eli gblɔ be: “Yehowae. Nu si nyo eŋu la, newɔe.”
ENGLISH: 18 And Samuel told him every word, and did not conceal it from him; and he said “It is Jehovah; he will do as he sees fit.”

EWE: 19 Samuel nɔ tsitsim, eye Yehowa ŋutɔ nɔ kplii, eye mena eƒe nyawo dometɔ aɖeke do kpo emevava o.
ENGLISH: 19 And Samuel grew, and Jehovah was with him and did not let any of his words fall to the ground;

EWE: 20 Eye Israel blibo la katã, tso Dan va se ɖe Beer-Seba, va nyae be woɖo Samuel Yehowa ƒe nyagblɔɖilae.
ENGLISH: 20 and all Israel from Dan to Beer-Shebaʽ knew that Samuel was to be depended on as a prophet of Jehovah.

EWE: 21 Eye Yehowa gaɖea eɖokui fiana le Silo, elabena Yehowa gaɖe eɖokui fia Samuel le Silo to Yehowa ƒe nya la dzi.
ENGLISH: 21 And Jehovah continued to appear in Shiloh; for Jehovah revealed himself in Shiloh, by his word, to Samuel;

ENGLISH: 1 Samuel

EWE: 4 Ale Samuel ƒe nya ɖo Israel blibo la gbɔ.
ENGLISH: 4 and all Israel had Samuel’s word.

EWE: Eye Israel ho aʋa ɖe Filistitɔwo ŋu; wova ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Ebenezer gbɔ, eye Filistitɔwo hã va ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Afek.
ENGLISH: And ʽEli grew very old, and his sons went on and on, and their course was displeasing to Jehovah.

EWE: 2 Filistitɔwo va kpe aʋa kple Israel, eye aʋa la mekpa Israel kura o, ale be Filistitɔwo si wo, wowu ame anɔ akpe ene le aʋagbea dzi.
ENGLISH: 2 And the Philistines gave battle to the Israelites, and the battle went badly, and the Israelites were beaten by the Philistines, and they killed about four thousand men in line in the field.

EWE: 3 Esi aʋawɔlaawo va ɖo asaɖa la me la, Israel ƒe ametsitsiwo gblɔ be: “Nu ka tae Yehowa na Filistitɔwo ɖu mía dzi egbea? Mina míakɔ Yehowa ƒe nubablaɖaka la tso Silo ava mía gbɔ, ne wòanɔ mía dome ahaɖe mí tso míaƒe futɔwo si me.”
ENGLISH: 3 And when the men got to camp, the elders of Israel said “Why did Jehovah cause us to be beaten by the Philistines today? let us get the ark of our God from Shiloh, that it may go out in our midst and save us out of the hands of our enemies.”

EWE: 4 Ale wodɔ ame ɖo ɖe Silo woyi ɖakɔ aʋakɔwo ƒe Yehowa, ame si bɔbɔ nɔ kerubiwo tame la, ƒe nubablaɖaka la vɛ. Eye Eli vi eveawo, Hofni kple Finehas, hã va kple Mawu vavã la ƒe nubablaɖaka la.
ENGLISH: 4 And the men sent to Shiloh and carried off from there the ark of Jehovah who sits upon the cherubs; and ʽEli’s two sons were with the ark, Hophni and Pinehas.

EWE: 5 Esi Yehowa ƒe nubablaɖaka la nya va ɖo asaɖaa me ko la, Israel-viwo katã do ɣli sesĩe, ale be anyigba ʋuʋu.
ENGLISH: 5 And when the ark of Jehovah came to the camp all the Israelites gave a great cheer so that the earth quivered;

EWE: 6 Esi Filistitɔwo se ɣlia la, wobia be: “Nu ka ta ɣli sesẽ sia le ɖiɖim le Hebritɔwo ƒe asaɖaa me?”
ENGLISH: 6 and the Philistines heard the sound of the cheering and said “What is this sound of great cheering in the camp of the Hebrews?” and they learned that the ark of Jehovah had come to the camp.

EWE: Mlɔeba wova nya be Yehowa ƒe Aɖaka lae va ɖo asaɖa la me. 7 Eye vɔvɔ̃ ɖo Filistitɔwo, elabena wogblɔ be: “Mawu va asaɖa la me!”
ENGLISH: 7 And the Philistines were afraid; for they said “A god has come to the camp”; and they said “Woe to us! for there has not been anything like this before.

EWE: Eya ta wogblɔ be: “Baba na mí, elabena nu sia tɔgbi medzɔ kpɔ o! 8 Baba na mí! Ame kae aɖe mí tso Mawu gã sia si me? Mawu siae tsɔ fuwɔame vovovowo wu Egiptetɔwo le gbea dzi.
ENGLISH: 8 Woe to us! who shall deliver us out of the hands of these grand gods? these are the gods that struck the Egyptians all those blows in the wilderness.

EWE: 9 Mi Filistitɔwo, milé dzi ɖe ƒo, eye miwɔ ŋutsu, ne miagasubɔ Hebritɔwo, abe ale si ko wosubɔ mi ene o.
ENGLISH: 9 Do your best, be men, Philistines, that you may not be slaves to the Hebrews as they were to you; be men, and fight!”

EWE: Miwɔ ŋutsu, eye miwɔ aʋa la!” 10 Eya ta Filistitɔwo wɔ aʋa la, eye wosi Israel, ale be wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe si yi eƒe agbadɔ me. Ame siwo wowu la sɔ gbɔ ŋutɔ; ale be aʋawɔla afɔzɔla akpe blaetɔ̃ tsi aʋa le Israel-viwo dome.
ENGLISH: 10 And the Philistines fought, and the Israelites were beaten and fled each to his home; and the losses were very great, and there fell of the Israelites three thousand footmen,

EWE: 11 Woxɔ Mawu ƒe Aɖaka la hã, eye wowu Eli vi eveawo, Hofni kple Finehas.
ENGLISH: 11 and the ark of God was taken, and ʽEli’s two sons, Hophni and Pinehas, were killed.

EWE: 12 Eye Benyamintɔ aɖe ƒu du tso aʋagbea dzi va Silo gbe ma gbe; awu vuvu le eŋu, eye ke le tame nɛ.
ENGLISH: 12 And a man of Benjamin ran from the battle and came to Shiloh that same day with his brigandine torn and earth on his head;

EWE: 13 Esi ŋutsua va ɖo la, Eli bɔbɔ nɔ zikpui dzi le mɔ to nɔ mɔ dzi kpɔm, elabena etsi dzimaɖi le Mawu vavã la ƒe Aɖaka la ta.
ENGLISH: 13 and when he came he found ʽEli sitting in his chair at the side of the gate watching along the road, for he felt alarmed for the ark of God.

EWE: Eye ŋutsua ƒu du yi ɖaka nya la ta le dua me, eye du blibo la katã de asi avifafa me.
ENGLISH: And the man went in to tell the news in the city, and all the city raised an outcry;

EWE: 14 Esi Eli se avifafa la, ebia be: “Nu ka ƒe hoowɔwɔe nye ema sem mele?”
ENGLISH: 14 and ʽEli heard the sound of the cry, and said “What is this noise of an uproar?”

EWE: Ŋutsu la ɖe abla yi ɖaka nya la ta na Eli.
ENGLISH: And the man came in haste and told ʽEli;

EWE: 15 (Ke Eli xɔ ƒe blaasieke vɔ enyi, eye eƒe ŋkuwo tsi, eye megale nu kpɔm o.)
ENGLISH: 15 (now ʽEli was ninety-eight years old, and his eyes were set so that he could not see);

EWE: 16 Eye ŋutsua gblɔ na Eli be: “Aʋagbe dzi metso, egbea ko mesi tso aʋagbe dzi!”
ENGLISH: 16 and the man said to ʽEli “I am the one who came from the army; I ran from the battle today.”

EWE: Eye wòbiae be: “Vinye, nu kae dzɔ?”
ENGLISH: And he said “How was it, my son?”

EWE: 17 Ale ame la ɖo eŋu be: “Israel si le Filistitɔwo nu, eye wowu ame geɖe le dukɔ la dome; wò ŋutɔ viwòŋutsu eveawo, Hofni kple Finehas, hã ku, eye woxɔ Mawu vavã la ƒe Aɖaka la hã.”
ENGLISH: 17 And the man with the news answered “The Israelites ran before the Philistines, and there was a great slaughter of our men too, and both your sons are killed too, and the ark of God is taken.”

EWE: 18 Esi wònya yɔ Mawu vavã la ƒe Aɖaka la ŋkɔ ko la, Eli mu tso zikpui la dzi dze anyi ɖe megbe le agboa nu, eye wòtɔ kɔ anyi heku, elabena etsi, eye wòle kpekpem.
ENGLISH: 18 And when he mentioned the ark of God ʽEli fell backward off his chair at the side of the gate, and his neck was broken, and he died for the man was old and heavy.

EWE: Edrɔ̃ ʋɔnu na Israel ƒe blaene.
ENGLISH: And he had judged Israel forty years.

EWE: 19 Ɣemaɣi la, fu nɔ toyɔvia Finehas srɔ̃ ƒo, eye eƒe vidziɣi gogo. Esi wòse be woxɔ Mawu vavã la ƒe Aɖaka la, eye toa kple srɔ̃a hã ku la, ebɔbɔ be yeadzi vi, elabena fu de asi eɖuɖu me enumake.
ENGLISH: 19 And his daughter-in-law, Pinehas’s wife, was on the point of having a child; and she heard the report about the capture of the ark of God and the death of her father-in-law and her husband, and she crouched down and gave birth to her child, because her pains came upon her,

EWE: 20 Eye esi wònɔ kudɔ ƒom la, nyɔnu siwo nɔ egbɔ la gblɔ be: “Mègavɔ̃ o, elabena ŋutsuvie nèdzi.”
ENGLISH: 20 and died forthwith.

EWE: Ke meɖo eŋu o, eye metsɔ ɖeke le eme o.
ENGLISH: And the women who stood over her spoke to her, saying “Do not be afraid, for you have borne a son,” but she made no answer and gave no heed.

EWE: 21 Ke ena ŋkɔ ɖevi la be Ikabod, hegblɔ be: “Ŋutikɔkɔe dzo le Israel yi aboyo me.” Egblɔ esia le Mawu vavã la ƒe Aɖaka si woxɔ kple toa kpakple srɔ̃a ta.
ENGLISH: 21 And she called the boy Icabod, saying “Israel’s glory is gone,” with reference to the capture of the ark of God and to her father-in-law and her husband.

EWE: 22 Egblɔ be: “Ŋutikɔkɔe dzo le Israel yi aboyo me, elabena woxɔ Mawu vavã la ƒe Aɖaka la.”
ENGLISH: 22 And she said “Israel’s glory is gone,” because the ark of God was taken.

ENGLISH: 1 Samuel

EWE: 5 Esi Filistitɔwo xɔ Mawu vavã la ƒe Aɖakaa la, wokɔe tso Ebenezer yi Asdod.
ENGLISH: 5 And the Philistines had taken the ark of God and brought it from the Help Stone to Ashdod.

EWE: 2 Eye Filistitɔwo kɔ Mawu vavã la ƒe Aɖaka la yi Dagon ƒe xɔ me hedae ɖe Dagon xa.
ENGLISH: 2 And the Philistines took the ark of God and brought it into the house of Dagon and placed it beside Dagon.

EWE: 3 Ke esi ŋu ke, eye Asdodtɔwo fɔ ŋdi kanya la, kpɔ ɖa, Dagon ye nye ema tsyɔ mo anyi ɖe Yehowa ƒe Aɖaka la ŋgɔ!
ENGLISH: 3 And the next morning, the first thing, the Ashdodites came into the house of Dagon and found Dagon down on his face on the ground before the ark of Jehovah.

EWE: Eye wofɔ Dagon hegbugbɔe ɖo enɔƒe.
ENGLISH: And they lifted Dagon to his feet and put him back in his place.

EWE: 4 Esi wofɔ ŋdi kanya le ŋkeke si gakplɔe ɖo dzi la, kpɔ ɖa, Dagon tsyɔ mo anyi ɖe Yehowa ƒe Aɖaka la ŋgɔ, eye ta kple asi eveawo fli ɖa le Dagon ŋu ɖe kpuia nu. Negbe eƒe akpa si ɖi tɔmelã koe susɔ.
ENGLISH: 4 And the first thing in the morning on the next day they found Dagon down on his face on the ground before the ark of Jehovah, and Dagon’s head and both his hands knocked off against the threshold.

EWE: 5 Esia tae Dagon ƒe trɔ̃nuawo kple ame siwo dea Dagon ƒe xɔ me la meɖoa afɔ Dagon ƒe kpui la nu o le Asdod va se ɖe egbe sia.
ENGLISH: 5 (This is why the priests of Dagon, and all who go into the house of Dagon, never step on Dagon’s threshold in Ashdod, to this day.)

EWE: 6 Eye Yehowa ƒe asi sẽ ɖe Asdodtɔwo dzi, ale be wòhe gbegblẽ va wo dzi, eye wòna kookoo to ɖe wo ŋu, le Asdod kple eƒe nutowo katã me.
ENGLISH: 6 And Jehovah’s hand was heavy on the Ashdodites, and he desolated them and smote them with buboes, Ashdod and its territory.

EWE: 7 Esi Asdodtɔwo kpɔ nu si nɔ dzɔdzɔm la, wogblɔ be: “Migana Israel ƒe Mawu ƒe Aɖaka la nanɔ mía gbɔ o, elabena eƒe asi sẽ ɖe mía kple mía mawu Dagon dzi.”
ENGLISH: 7 And the men of Ashdod saw that it was so, and went to saying “The ark of the god of Israel must not stay with us, because his hand is hard on us and on our god Dagon”;

EWE: 8 Eya ta wodɔ ame woɖaƒo Filistitɔwo ƒe kplɔlawo katã nu ƒu va wo gbɔ, eye wobia wo be: “Aleke míawɔ Israel ƒe Mawu ƒe Aɖaka lae?” Woɖo eŋu be: “Mina woakɔ Israel ƒe Mawu la ƒe Aɖakaa ayi Gat.”
ENGLISH: 8 and they sent and called together to their city all the Sarns of the Philistines and said “What shall we do with the ark of the god of Israel?” and they said “Let the ark of the god of Israel be brought around to Gath.”

EWE: Ale wokɔ Israel ƒe Mawu ƒe Aɖaka la yi afi ma. 9 Ke esi wokɔe yi afi ma la, Yehowa ƒe asi va du la dzi, ale be dzidzi ƒo wo ŋutɔ. Ewɔ fu dua me tɔwo, ɖeviwo kple tsitsiawo siaa, eye kookoo to ɖe wo ŋu.
ENGLISH: 9 And they brought around the ark of the God of Israel; and after it was brought around Jehovah’s hand was upon the city in a prodigious ravage, and he smote the men of the city, great and small, and buboes broke out on them.

EWE: 10 Eya ta woɖo Mawu vavã la ƒe Aɖaka la ɖe Ekron, gake esi Mawu vavã la ƒe Aɖaka la va ɖo Ekron ko la, Ekrontɔwo de asi ɣlidodo me be: “Wokɔ Israel ƒe Mawu ƒe Aɖaka la va mía gbɔ be wòawu mí kple míaƒe amewo!”
ENGLISH: 10 And they sent the ark of God away to ʽEkron; and when the ark of God came into ʽEkron the ʽEkronites raised an outcry “They have brought the ark of the god of Israel around to me, to kill me and my people”;

EWE: 11 Eya ta wodɔ ame woyi ɖaƒo Filistitɔwo ƒe kplɔlawo katã nu ƒu, eye wogblɔ be: “Miɖo Israel ƒe Mawu ƒe Aɖaka la ɖa, ale be wòagbugbɔ ayi enɔƒe, ne wòagawu mía kple míaƒe dukɔ la o.”
ENGLISH: 11 and they sent and called together all the Sarns of the Philistines and said “Send the ark of the god of Israel away, so that it may go back to its place and not kill me and my people”; for there was a deadly ravage all through the city, Jehovah’s hand was very heavy there.

EWE: Elabena dzidzi ƒo du blibo la be yewoava ku; Mawu vavã la ƒe asi sẽ le afi ma ŋutɔ, 12 eye ame siwo meku o la, kookoo to ɖe wo ŋu.
ENGLISH: 12 And the men who did not die were smitten with the buboes, and the city’s clamor went up to the skies.
