ENGLISH: 29 And the Continuance of Israel will not break his word nor change his mind; for he is not man, to change his mind.”

EWE: 30 Eye wògblɔ be: “Mewɔ nu vɔ̃.
ENGLISH: 30 And he said “I did wrong.

EWE: Ke meɖe kuku, de bubu ŋunye le nye dukɔ la ƒe ametsitsiwo ŋkume kple Israel ŋkume. Gbugbɔ kplim, ne maɖade ta agu na Yehowa wò Mawu la.”
ENGLISH: Now pay honor to me before the elders of my people, and before Israel, and come back with me and let me do reverence to your God Jehovah.”

EWE: 31 Eya ta Samuel gbugbɔ kple Saul yi, eye Saul yi ɖade ta agu na Yehowa.
ENGLISH: 31 And Samuel followed Saul back, and Saul did reverence to Jehovah.

EWE: 32 Eye Samuel gblɔ be: “Mikplɔ Amalek-fia Agag vɛ nam.” Agag zɔ heheɖemegbetɔe yi egbɔ, eye Agag gblɔ na eɖokui be: ‘Nyateƒee, ku ƒe vɔvɔ̃ bú.’
ENGLISH: 32 And Samuel said “Bring Agag the king of the Amalekites to me”; and Agag came to him tottering, and said “Death is bitter, bitter, after all.”

EWE: 33 Ke Samuel gblɔ be: “Ale si ko wò yi na nyɔnuwo zu konɔe la, nenemae dawò hã azu konɔwo ƒe konɔ le nyɔnuwo dome.” Ale Samuel fli Agag kakɛkakɛe le Yehowa ŋkume le Gilgal.
ENGLISH: 33 And Samuel said “As your sword has bereaved women of their children, so shall your mother be the most bereaved of women”; and Samuel cut Agag to pieces before Jehovah at the Gilgal.

EWE: 34 Emegbe Samuel dzo yi Rama, eye Saul hã yi eƒe me le Saul ƒe Gibea.
ENGLISH: 34 And Samuel went to Ramah, and Saul went up to his home at Gibeath-Saul.

EWE: 35 Eye Samuel megakpɔ Saul kpɔ gbeɖe o va se ɖe eƒe kugbe, ke Samuel xa nu le Saul ta. Eve Yehowa be yeɖo Saul fiae ɖe Israel nu.
ENGLISH: 35 And Samuel never again saw Saul till the day of his death, because Samuel mourned over Saul and Jehovah repented of having made Saul king over Israel.

EWE: 1 Samuel
ENGLISH: 1 Samuel

EWE: 16 Mlɔeba Yehowa gblɔ na Samuel be: “Ɣekaɣi nànɔ konyi fam le Saul ta ase ɖo, evɔ wònye megbee be magaɖu fia ɖe Israel dzi o?
ENGLISH: 16 And Jehovah said to Samuel “How long will you keep mourning over Saul, when I have rejected him from reigning over Israel?

EWE: De ami wò lãdzo la me, eye nàdze mɔ. Madɔ wò ɖe Betlehemtɔ Isai gbɔ, elabena metia fia na ɖokuinye le viawo dome.”
ENGLISH: Fill your horn with oil and go, I will send you to Jesse the Bethlehemite; for I have picked out a king among his sons.”

EWE: 2 Ke Samuel gblɔ be: “Aleke mawɔ ayi?
ENGLISH: 2 And Samuel said “How am I to go?

EWE: Ne Saul see la, awum.”
ENGLISH: Saul would hear of it and kill me.”

EWE: Eye Yehowa gblɔ nɛ be: “Kplɔ nyivi aɖe ɖe asi, eye nàgblɔ be: ‘Vɔ sa gee meva na Yehowa.’
ENGLISH: And Jehovah said “You are to take with you a heifer calf, and say ‘I have come to sacrifice to Jehovah,’

EWE: 3 Eye nàkpe Isai va vɔsaƒea; ekema mana nànya nu si nàwɔ.
ENGLISH: 3 and invite Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will let you know what to do; and you are to anoint for me the one I tell you to.”

EWE: Si ami na ame si dzi matɔ asi na wò la nam.” 4 Samuel wɔ nu si Yehowa gblɔ la.
ENGLISH: 4 And Samuel did what Jehovah had said, and came to Bethlehem; and the elders of the city came to meet him in alarm, and said “Your coming means that all is well?”

EWE: Esi wòva ɖo Betlehem eye dumemetsitsiawo kpɔe la, woɖi vo, eya ta wobiae be: “Ŋutifafae nèhe vɛa?” 5 Eɖo eŋu be: “Ŋutifafae. Vɔ sa gee meva na Yehowa. Mikɔ mia ɖokuiwo ŋu, ne miava vɔsaƒea kplim.” Eye wòkɔ Isai kple viawo ŋu hekpe wo va vɔsaƒea.
ENGLISH: 5 and he said “It does; I have come to sacrifice to Jehovah; hallow yourselves and hold festival with me today”; and he hallowed Jesse and his sons and invited them to the sacrifice.

EWE: 6 Esi woge ɖe eme, eye wòkpɔ Eliab la, egblɔ be: “Vavãe Yehowa ƒe amesiamina lae nye esi le eŋkume.”
ENGLISH: 6 And when they came in and he saw Eliab, he thought “It must be Jehovah’s warden, his anointed”;

EWE: 7 Ke Yehowa gblɔ na Samuel be: “Mègakpɔ eƒe dzedzeme kple eƒe atsudzɔdzɔ o, elabena megbee. Elabena menye ale si amegbetɔ kpɔa nue nye ale si Mawu kpɔa nui o, elabena nu si le dzedzem koe amegbetɔ kpɔna, ke Yehowa ya kpɔa keke dzi me ke.”
ENGLISH: 7 but Jehovah said to Samuel “Do not look at his appearance and his tallness, for I have rejected him; for it is not what man sees, for man sees by the eyes but Jehovah sees by the heart.”

EWE: 8 Eye Isai yɔ Abinadab wòva to Samuel ŋkume, ke egblɔ be: “Yehowa metia eya hã o.”
ENGLISH: 8 And Jesse called Abinadab and had him pass before Samuel; and he said “Jehovah has not chosen this one either.”

EWE: 9 Emegbe Isai na Sama va yi, ke egblɔ be: “Yehowa metia eya hã o.”
ENGLISH: 9 And Jesse had Shammah pass; and he said “Jehovah has not chosen this one either.”

EWE: 10 Ale Isai na viawo dometɔ adre va to Samuel ŋkume, gake Samuel gblɔ na Isai be: “Yehowa metia wo dometɔ aɖeke o.”
ENGLISH: 10 And Jesse had all seven of his sons pass before Samuel; and Samuel said to Jesse “Jehovah has not chosen these.”

EWE: 11 Eye Samuel bia Isai be: “Viwò ŋutsuviawo katãe nye esia?” Eɖo eŋu be: “Ekpɔtɔ ɖevitɔ la, eye ele alẽwo kplɔm.”
ENGLISH: 11 And Samuel said to Jesse “Is this all there are of the boys?” and he said “There still remains the youngest: he is out shepherding.”

EWE: Eye Samuel gblɔ na Isai be: “Dɔ woayi aɖakplɔe vɛ, elabena míanɔ anyi aɖu nu o, va se ɖe esime wòva afi sia hafi.”
ENGLISH: And Samuel said to Jesse “Send and get him; for we will not sit down till he is here.”

EWE: 12 Eya ta edɔ woyi ɖakplɔe vɛ. Ðekakpuia biã, eƒe ŋkuwo nya kpɔ, eye wòdze ɖeka.
ENGLISH: 12 And he sent and brought him a ruddy, handsome-eyed, good-looking youth and Jehovah said “There, anoint him: this is the one.”

EWE: Eye Yehowa gblɔ be: “Tso nàsi ami nɛ, elabena eyae!” 13 Eya ta Samuel tsɔ lãdzo si me ami le la, eye wòsi ami nɛ le nɔviawo ŋkume.
ENGLISH: 13 And Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the midst of his brothers; and the spirit of Jehovah seized upon David from that day on.

EWE: Emegbe Samuel tso hedze mɔ yi Rama.
ENGLISH: And Samuel went off to Ramah.

EWE: 14 Eye Yehowa ƒe gbɔgbɔ dzo le Saul dzi, eye gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃ɖi aɖe tso Yehowa gbɔ va le fu ɖem nɛ vevie.
ENGLISH: 14 And the spirit of Jehovah had gone away from Saul, and a bad spirit from Jehovah used to overwhelm him.

EWE: 15 Eye Saul ƒe subɔviwo gblɔ nɛ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃ɖi aɖe tso Mawu gbɔ le fu ɖem na wò.
ENGLISH: 15 And Saul’s officers said to him “There is a bad divine spirit overwhelming you;

EWE: 16 Mía aƒetɔ, míeɖe kuku, ɖe gbe na wò subɔvi siwo le ŋkuwòme, ne woadi ŋutsu aɖe si bi ɖe saŋkuƒoƒo me nyuie la vɛ. Eye ne gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃ɖi si tso Mawu gbɔ la va dziwò la, ekema wòaƒo saŋku, ne wòaka ɖe eme na wò.”
ENGLISH: 16 say the word, sir, your servants are before you, have them look up a man expert as a lyre-player, and when there is a bad divine spirit on you he shall play his music and you will be better.”

EWE: 17 Eya ta Saul gblɔ na eƒe subɔviawo be: “Midi ŋutsu aɖe si nya saŋkuƒoƒo nyuie la nam, eye miakplɔe vɛ nam.”
ENGLISH: 17 And Saul said to his officers “Pick me out a man who plays well and bring him to me.”

EWE: 18 Subɔviawo dometɔ ɖeka gblɔ nɛ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, mekpɔ Isai, Betlehemtɔ la ƒe viwo dometɔ ɖeka si bi ɖe saŋkuƒoƒo me, dzi le eƒo eye wònye aʋakalẽtɔ. Enya nuƒoƒo, eye wòdze ɖeka hã, eye Yehowa li kplii.”
ENGLISH: 18 And one of the henchmen answered “I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite who is expert at playing, and a man of energy and a fighter, and discreet in word, and a fine figure, and Jehovah is with him.”

EWE: 19 Eye Saul dɔ ame ɖo ɖe Isai gbɔ be woagblɔ nɛ be: “Ðo viwò David, si le lãhawo gbɔ la ɖem.”
ENGLISH: 19 And Saul sent messengers to Jesse, and said “Send me your son David, the one who is with the sheep”;

EWE: 20 Ale Isai kplɔ tedzi ɖeka, eye wòtsɔ abolo kple wain lãgbalẽgolo ɖeka kpakple gbɔ̃vi ɖeka, eye wòtsɔ wo kpe ɖe via David ŋu ɖo ɖe Saul.
ENGLISH: 20 and Jesse took a load of bread and a bag of wine and one kid and sent them to Saul by his son David.

EWE: 21 Ale David va Saul gbɔ, eye wòsubɔe. Saul va lɔ̃e ŋutɔ, eye wòzu eƒe adekplɔvi.
ENGLISH: 21 And David came to Saul and presented himself before him, and Saul took a great liking to him and had him as squire.

EWE: 22 Eya ta Saul dɔ ame ɖo ɖe Isai gbɔ be woagblɔ nɛ be: “Meɖe kuku, na David nanɔ gbɔnye asubɔm, elabena eƒe nu nyo ŋunye.”
ENGLISH: 22 And Saul sent word to Jesse “Let David be in my service, because I like him.”

EWE: 23 Eye ne Mawu ƒe gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃ɖi la va Saul dzi la, ekema David ƒoa saŋku, ale be Saul kpɔa gbɔdzɔe, eye wòkana ɖe eme nɛ, eye gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃ɖi la dzona le edzi.
ENGLISH: 23 And when there was a divine spirit on Saul David would take his lyre and play his music, and Saul would be easier and better, and the bad spirit would go away from him.

EWE: 1 Samuel
ENGLISH: 1 Samuel

EWE: 17 Eye Filistitɔwo ƒo woƒe aʋakɔwo nu ƒu be yewoawɔ aʋa. Woƒo ƒu ɖe Yuda du, si nye Soko la me, eye wova ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Soko kple Azeka dome le Efes-Damim.
ENGLISH: 17 And the Philistines brought their armies together for war, and they met at Socoh, which belongs to Judah, and camped between Socoh and ʽAzekah, at Ephes-Dammim;

EWE: 2 Saul kple Israel ŋutsuwo hã ƒo ƒu heva ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Ela Bali la me, eye woho le aʋalɔgowo me yi aʋa kpe ge kple Filistitɔwo.
ENGLISH: 2 and Saul and the men of Israel came together and camped in Terebinth Vale, and offered battle to the Philistines,

EWE: 3 Filistitɔwo le to la ƒe akpa ɖeka, eye Israel-viwo hã le to la ƒe akpa kemɛ, eye bali la tso wo dome.
ENGLISH: 3 the Philistines standing on the mountain on this side and the Israelites on the mountain on that side, with the valley between them.

EWE: 4 Eye aʋakalẽtɔ aɖe do go tso Filistitɔwo ƒe asaɖa la me; eŋkɔe nye Goliat, etso Gat, eye wòkɔ abɔklugui ade kple asi ɖeka.
ENGLISH: 4 And a man came out between them from the Philistine line of battle, named Goliath, from Gath; he was nine and a half feet tall,

EWE: 5 Eɖɔ akɔbligakuku, eye wòdo gawu si le abe tɔmelãtsro ene. Eƒe gawu la ƒe kpekpeme le akɔbli sekel akpe atɔ̃.
ENGLISH: 5 and he had a bronze helmet on his head and wore a hauberk of scales, the hauberk weighing a hundred and eighty pounds of bronze,

EWE: 6 Edo akɔblikpoxɔnuwo ɖe eƒe akpaligbe, eye wòkpla akɔbliŋutrɔ aɖe ɖe dzime.
ENGLISH: 6 and he had bronze greaves on his legs and a bronze javelin between his shoulders;

EWE: 7 Eƒe akplɔti le abe avɔlɔ̃lawo ƒe agbabɔ ene, eye akplɔ si le enu la ƒe kpekpeme nye gayibɔ sekel alafa ade; eye eƒe akpoxɔnutsɔla dze eŋgɔ.
ENGLISH: 7 and the shaft of his spear was like a weaver’s pole, and the iron spearhead weighed twenty pounds, and his shield-carrier went in front of him.

EWE: 8 Eye wòtɔ hedo ɣli ɖo ɖe Israel ƒe aʋalɔgoawo be: “Nu ka tae mieho heva dze aʋa ɖi?
ENGLISH: 8 And he stood and called out to the Israelite line of battle “Why have you come out to offer battle?

EWE: Alo menye Filistitɔe menye, eye miawo mienye Saul ƒe subɔviwo oa?
ENGLISH: I am the Philistine, you are subjects of Saul, select a man to come down to me:

EWE: Mitia ŋutsu ɖeka, ne wòava kpe kplim. 9 Ne ete ŋu wɔ aʋa kplim, eye wòwum la, ekema míazu miaƒe subɔviwo. Ke ne mede enu hewui la, ekema miawo hã miazu subɔviwo na mí asubɔ mí.”
ENGLISH: 9 if he can fight me, and kills me, we will be subject to you; but if I overcome him and kill him, you shall be subject to us and behave as such.”

EWE: 10 Eye Filistitɔ la gagblɔ be: “Meɖe alɔme le Israel ƒe aʋalɔgowo ŋu egbea.
ENGLISH: 10 And the Philistine said “I this day flout Israel’s ranks: give me a man to fight with.”

EWE: Miɖe ŋutsu ɖeka nam, ne nye kplii míawɔ aʋa!” 11 Esi Saul kple Israel blibo la se Filistitɔ la ƒe nya siawo la, ŋɔdzi lé wo, eye wovɔ̃ ŋutɔ.
ENGLISH: 11 And Saul and all the Israelites heard these words of the Philistine’s, and were dismayed and greatly afraid.

EWE: 12 Ke David nye Efratatɔ, si tso Betlehem le Yuda, si ŋkɔe nye Isai la, ƒe vi.
ENGLISH: 12 And David, the son of an Ephrathite (that is, from Bethlehem in Judah) whose name was Jesse, who had eight sons, and who was in Saul’s days an old man, advanced in years,

EWE: Viŋutsu enyi le Isai si, eye le Saul ŋɔli la, enye amegãɖeɖi. 13 Isai vi tsitsi etɔ̃awo kplɔ Saul ɖo yi aʋa la. Via etɔ̃ siwo yi aʋa la ƒe ŋkɔwoe nye Eliab, si nye ŋgɔgbevi la, eveliae nye Abinadab, eye etɔ̃liae nye Sama.
ENGLISH: 13 Jesse’s three oldest sons were gone to the war, following Saul; the names of his three sons who were gone to the war were Eliab the eldest, and Abinadab the second eldest, and Shammah the third;

EWE: 14 David ye nye ɖevitɔ, eye tsitsitɔ etɔ̃awo dze Saul yome.
ENGLISH: 14 David was the youngest, and the three oldest were gone to the war, following Saul,

EWE: 15 Ke David dzona le Saul gbɔ yina ɖakplɔa fofoa ƒe alẽwo le Betlehem gatrɔna gbɔna.
ENGLISH: 15 David was gone, had gone back from Saul’s service to tend his father’s sheep at Bethlehem.

EWE: 16 Ke Filistitɔ la vana ŋdi kple fiẽ va tɔna ɖi, ŋkeke blaene sɔŋ.
ENGLISH: 16 And the Philistine approached the first thing in the morning and again in the evening, and stood ready, forty days.

EWE: 17 Eye Isai gblɔ na via David be: “Meɖe kuku, netsɔ nàtsɔ nuku tɔtɔe efa ɖeka sia kple abolo ewo siawo yi na fowòwo le asaɖa la me.
ENGLISH: 17 And Jesse said to his son David “Take this bushel of roasted grain for your brothers, and ten cakes of bread, and get them to your brothers at the camp quick;

EWE: 18 Eye nàtsɔ notsi babla ewo siawo ayi na aʋakplɔla si le ame akpe ɖeka nu la; azɔ hã, nàbia nɔviwòwo ƒe fɔfɔme ta se, eye nàxɔ gbe tso wo gbɔ vɛ nam.”
ENGLISH: 18 and bring these ten cuts of curd to the captain of the thousand, and make sure how your brothers are doing, and get the token from them;

EWE: 19 Woawo kple Saul kpakple Israel ŋutsu bubuawo katã le Ela Bali la me be yewoawɔ aʋa kple Filistitɔwo.
ENGLISH: 19 Saul and they, and all the men of Israel, are in Terebinth Vale, fighting the Philistines.”

EWE: 20 Ale David fɔ ŋdi kanya hegblẽ alẽawo ɖe ame aɖe gbɔ; eye wòdo agba hedze mɔ abe ale si tututu Isai de se nɛ ene. Esi wòva ɖo asaɖaa me la, aʋakɔawo do yina aʋakpeƒea, eye wodo aʋaɣli.
ENGLISH: 20 And the first thing in the morning David left the sheep with a keeper and loaded himself up and went, as Jesse had ordered him; and he came to the cart-stand, and the force going out to form the line gave a cheer for the fighting;

EWE: 21 Israel kple Filistitɔwo dze aʋa, eye aʋalɔgo dze ŋgɔ aʋalɔgo.
ENGLISH: 21 and the Israelites and the Philistines formed their lines facing each other.

EWE: 22 Enumake David dro agba la da ɖe agbadzikpɔla la gbɔ heƒu du yi aʋakpeƒea. Esi wòɖo la, ebia nɔviawo ƒe fɔfɔme ta se.
ENGLISH: 22 And David put down the things and left them with the supply-keeper, and ran to the front and came and asked how his brothers were doing.

EWE: 23 Esi wòle nu ƒom kpli wo la, Filistitɔwo ƒe aʋakalẽtɔ si ŋkɔe nye Goliat, tso Gat, lae nye ema do. Etso Filistitɔwo ƒe aʋalɔgowo dome gbɔna, eye wògblɔ nya siwo wògblɔna tsã la David se.
ENGLISH: 23 And as he was talking with them, up came a man between the fronts out of the Philistine line, named Goliath the Philistine, from Gath, and spoke these words, and David heard him.

EWE: 24 Esi Israel ŋutsuwo katã kpɔ ŋutsua la, wovɔ̃ ŋutɔ eye wosi le enu.
ENGLISH: 24 And all the men of Israel, when they saw the man, fled before him and were in great fear;

EWE: 25 Eye Israel ŋutsuwo gblɔ be: “Miekpɔ ŋutsu ma si do gbɔnaa? Alɔme ɖe gee wògbɔna le Israel ŋu.
ENGLISH: 25 and the men of Israel said “Do you see this man that has come up? it is to flout Israel he has come up; and the king will make the man that kills him a very rich man and give him his daughter, and make his family free in Israel.”

EWE: Ame si awui la, fia la ana kesinɔnu geɖee, atsɔ eya ŋutɔ vianyɔnu nɛ, eye fofoa ƒe aƒe magadzɔ nu alo awɔ dudɔ le Israel o.” 26 Eye David bia ŋutsu siwo tɔ ɖe egbɔ la be: “Nu kae woawɔ na ame si awu Filistitɔ ma ahaɖe vlododo ɖa le Israel dzi?
ENGLISH: 26 And David said to the men that were standing with him “What will be done for the man who kills yonder Philistine and takes away the flout from Israel? for who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he has flouted the ranks of a living God?”

EWE: 27 Eye ŋutsuawo gblɔ nya mawo ke, si wogblɔ tsã la nɛ be: “Ale kple ale woawɔ na ame si awui la.”
ENGLISH: 27 And the people told him the same thing: “so it will be done for the man who kills him.”

EWE: 28 Esi nɔvia tsitsitɔ Eliab see wònɔ nu ƒom kple ŋutsuawo la, dzi ku Eliab ɖe David ŋu vevie eye wògblɔ be: “Nu ka wɔ gee nèva? Eye ame ka gbɔe nègblẽ alẽ ʋɛ mawo ɖo le gbea dzi?
ENGLISH: 28 And his oldest brother Eliab heard when he spoke to the men; and Eliab was angry at David, and said “What did you come down for, and whom did you leave those few sheep in the wilderness with?

EWE: Menya be ɖe nètsona le ɖokuiwò si wɔa nu, eye susu vlo le dzi me na wò; aʋa teƒe kpɔ gee nèva.”
ENGLISH: I know your headstrongness and cantankerousness, that it was in order to see the fighting you came down.”

EWE: 29 David ɖo eŋu be: “Nu ka mehewɔ fifia? Menye nya ko mebia oa?”
ENGLISH: 29 And David said “What have I been doing now? it was talk, wasn’t it?”

EWE: 30 Eye wòtrɔ ɖa le eŋu te ɖe ame bubu ŋu gabia nya mawo ke, eye ameawo gaɖo eŋu nɛ abe tsã ene.
ENGLISH: 30 and went from beside him around to another section of the front, and said the same thing; and the people gave him the same answer as before.

EWE: 31 Wose nya siwo David gblɔ la, eye woyi ɖagblɔe na Saul. Eya ta ena wokplɔe vɛ.
ENGLISH: 31 But the things David was saying were overheard and reported before Saul; and he had him brought.

EWE: 32 Eye David gblɔ na Saul be: “Dzika megatso ame aɖeke ƒo o. Wò subɔvi ayi aɖawɔ aʋa kple Filistitɔ ma.”
ENGLISH: 32 And David said to Saul “Do not be downhearted, sir; your servant will go and fight this Philistine.”

EWE: 33 Ke Saul gblɔ na David be: “Màte ŋu ayi aɖawɔ aʋa kple Filistitɔ ma o, elabena ɖevi ko nènye, ke eya la, aʋawɔla wònye tso eƒe ɖekakpui me ke.”
ENGLISH: 33 But Saul said to David “You cannot go against this Philistine to fight him, because you are a boy and he has been a fighting man from his boyhood up.”

EWE: 34 Eye David gblɔ na Saul be: “Wò subɔvi nɔ fofoa ƒe alẽhawo kplɔm eye dzata aɖe va lé alẽ ɖeka le lãha la dome, ɣebubuɣi sisiblisi aɖe hã va lé alẽ ɖeka.
ENGLISH: 34 But David said to Saul “Your servant was tending sheep for his father, and there would come a lion or a bear and carry off a sheep out of the flock,

EWE: 35 Ale meti wo yome, eye meƒo wo ƒu anyi heɖee le woƒe nu me. Esi dzata la tso ɖe ŋunye la, melé eƒe kɔdza, eye meƒoe ƒu anyi hewui.
ENGLISH: 35 and I would go out after it and beat it and recover the creature out of its mouth; and one would stand up against me and I would hold its mane and strike it dead.

EWE: 36 Wò subɔvi ƒo dzata kple sisiblisi la siaa ƒu anyi, eye anɔ na Filistitɔ aʋamatsomatsotɔ sia hã abe wo dometɔ ɖeka ene, elabena eɖe alɔme le Mawu gbagbe la ƒe aʋalɔgowo ŋu.”
ENGLISH: 36 Both the lion and the bear your servant killed, and this uncircumcised Philistine will be like one of them, because he has flouted the ranks of a living God.”

EWE: 37 Eye David gblɔ kpee be: “Yehowa, ame si ɖem tso dzata kple sisiblisi ƒe fewo me la, aɖem tso Filistitɔ sia si me.”
ENGLISH: 37 And David said “Jehovah, who brought me off safe from the lion and the bear, he will bring me off safe from this Philistine.”

EWE: Eya ta Saul gblɔ na David be: “Heyi, eye Yehowa nenɔ kpli wò.”
ENGLISH: And Saul said to David “Go, and Jehovah be with you.”

EWE: 38 Eye Saul do eƒe awuwo na David, eɖɔ akɔbligakuku ɖe ta nɛ, eye wòdo gawu nɛ.
ENGLISH: 38 And Saul dressed David in his own brigandine and put a bronze helmet on his head,

EWE: 39 Eye David ta eƒe yi ɖe awuawo dzi, eye wòdze agbagba be yeaɖe zɔ, gake mete ŋui o, elabena medo wo kpɔ o.
ENGLISH: 39 and belted his own sword on David over his brigandine; and David had trouble in walking, because he had not practiced.

EWE: David gblɔ na Saul be: “Nyemate ŋu anɔ nu siawo me ayi o, elabena nyemedo wo kpɔ o.” Eya ta David ɖe wo ɖi.
ENGLISH: And David said to Saul “I cannot walk in these, because I have not practiced”; and they took them off him.

EWE: 40 Etsɔ eƒe lãkplɔti ɖe asi, edi kpe zɔzrɔ̃e atɔ̃ le tɔʋu la me tsɔ de eƒe alẽkplɔlawo ƒe akplo la me, eƒe akafo la le esi eye wòzɔ ɖe Filistitɔ la dzi.
ENGLISH: 40 And he took his staff in his hand, and chose five pebbles out of the bed of the arroyo and put them in his shepherd’s wallet, his yalkut, and had his sling in his hand; and he approached the Philistine,

EWE: 41 Eye Filistitɔ la le tetem ɖe David ŋu hele egogom, eye eƒe akpoxɔnutsɔla dze eŋgɔ.
ENGLISH: 41 and the Philistine went on, drawing nearer and nearer to David, with the man that was his shield-carrier in front of him.

EWE: 42 Esi Filistitɔ la fɔ kɔ dzi kpɔ David la, edo vloe, elabena ɖevi ko wònye, ebiã, eye wòdze ɖeka.
ENGLISH: 42 And the Philistine looked and saw David, and despised him because he was a boy, a ruddy youth and a beauty;

EWE: 43 Eya ta Filistitɔ la bia David be: “Avue menye hafi nètsɔ kpowo gbɔna gbɔnyea?”
ENGLISH: 43 and the Philistine said to David “Am I a dog, that you are coming at me with staves?”

EWE: Eye Filistitɔ la yɔ eƒe mawuwo tsɔ ƒo fi de David.
ENGLISH: And the Philistine cursed David by his gods;

EWE: 44 Filistitɔ la gblɔ na David be: “Wò ya te va gbɔnye ko, eye matsɔ wò lã ana dziƒoxewo kple gbemelãwo.”
ENGLISH: 44 and the Philistine said to David “Come to me and have me give your flesh to the birds of the air and the beasts of the range.”

EWE: 45 David ɖo eŋu na Filistitɔ la be: “Wò ya ètsɔ yi, akplɔ kple aŋutrɔ gbɔna gbɔnye, ke nye ya megbɔna gbɔwò le aʋakɔwo ƒe Yehowa, Israel ƒe aʋalɔgowo ƒe Mawu, si ŋu nèɖe alɔme le la, ƒe ŋkɔ me.
ENGLISH: 45 But David said to the Philistine “You are coming at me with sword and spear and javelin, but I am coming at you with the name of Jehovah of Armies, the God of Israel’s ranks which you have flouted.

EWE: 46 Yehowa atsɔ wò ade asi nam egbea, eye mawu wò ahatso ta le nuwò; eye matsɔ Filistitɔwo ƒe aʋakɔ la ƒe kukuawo ana dziƒoxewo kple gbemelãwo egbea; eye anyigbadzitɔwo katã anyae be Mawu aɖe le Israel.
ENGLISH: 46 This day Jehovah will put you into my hands, and I shall kill you and take off your head and give your corpse and the corpses of the Philistine army to the birds of the air and the wild beasts of the earth today, that all the land may know that Israel has a God:

EWE: 47 Eye ame siwo katã ƒo ƒu ɖe afi sia adze sii be menye yi alo akplɔ ye Yehowa tsɔna xɔna na ame o, elabena Yehowa tɔe nye aʋa la, eye eyae atsɔ mi katã ade asi na mí.”
ENGLISH: 47 that all this assembly may know that victory is not by sword and spear, but battle belongs to Jehovah, and he will give you into our hands.”

EWE: 48 Eye Filistitɔ la zɔ ɖe David dzi, David wɔ kaba ƒu du ɖo ta aʋakpeƒea, be yeakpe kple Filistitɔ la.
ENGLISH: 48 And when the Philistine stood up and came on, drawing nearer to David, David ran in haste toward the line of battle to meet the Philistine;

EWE: 49 David ƒo asi ɖe eƒe akploa me ɖe kpe ɖeka hedae kple eƒe akafo wòyi ɖalɔ Filistitɔ la ƒe ŋgonu. Kpe la ŋɔ eƒe ŋgonu yi eme, eye wòmu tsyɔ mo anyi.
ENGLISH: 49 and David reached into his wallet and took a stone out of it and slung, and hit the Philistine in the forehead, and the stone sank into his forehead and he fell on his face on the ground;

EWE: 50 Ale David tsɔ akafo kple kpe ɖeka ɖu Filistitɔ la dzi; eƒo Filistitɔ la ƒu anyi hewui; togbɔ be yi menɔ David si o hã.
ENGLISH: 50 and David outfought the Philistine with sling and stone, and struck the Philistine dead without having any sword in his hand.

EWE: 51 David ƒu du yi ɖatɔ ɖe Filistitɔ la dzi. Eye wòɖe Filistitɔ la ƒe yi le aku me, tso ta le enu. Esi Filistitɔwo kpɔ be yewoƒe aʋakalẽtɔa ku la, wosi.
ENGLISH: 51 And David ran and stood by the Philistine and took his sword and drew it from its sheath and finished killing him, cutting off his head with it; and the Philistines saw that their champion was dead, and they ran.

EWE: 52 Enumake Israel kple Yuda ŋutsuwo ho kple ɣli heti Filistitɔwo yome tso bali la me va ɖo keke Ekron ƒe agbowo nu ke, eye Filistitɔ siwo wowu la kaka ɖe mɔa dzi tso Saarayim va se ɖe Gat kple Ekron ke.
ENGLISH: 52 And the men of Israel and Judah started up and gave a cheer, and pursued the Philistines till you come to Gath and to the gates of ʽEkron; and the killed Philistines fell from the Shagharaim road to Gath and ʽEkron;

EWE: 53 Esi Israel-viwo trɔ le Filistitɔwo yome la, wova ha Filistitɔwo ƒe asaɖawo.
ENGLISH: 53 and the sons of Israel came back from chasing the Philistines, and pillaged their camp.

EWE: 54 Eye David tsɔ Filistitɔ la ƒe ta va Yerusalem, ke etsɔ Filistitɔ la ƒe aʋawɔnuawo da ɖe eƒe agbadɔ me.
ENGLISH: 54 And David took the Philistine’s head and brought it to Jerusalem, and put his outfit in his tent.

EWE: 55 Esi Saul kpɔ David wòyina Filistitɔa kpe ge la, ebia aʋafia Abner be: “Abner, ame ka ƒe vie ɖevi la nye?” Abner ɖo eŋu be: “Oo fia, metà wò agbe, nyemenyae o!”
ENGLISH: 55 And when Saul saw David go out to meet the Philistine he said to Abner, the general of the army, “Whose son is the boy, Abner?” and Abner said “By your life, king, I do not know.”

EWE: 56 Fia la gblɔ be: “Yi ɖabia ame si ƒe vi ɖekakpuia nye ta se.”
ENGLISH: 56 And the king said “Ask whose son the young fellow is yourself.”

EWE: 57 Eya ta esi David wu Filistitɔ la vɔ hetrɔ gbɔ ko la, Abner kplɔe yi Saul ŋkume, eye Filistitɔ la ƒe ta le esi.
ENGLISH: 57 And when David came back from killing the Philistine, Abner took him and brought him before the king with the Philistine’s head in his hand.

EWE: 58 Eye Saul biae be: “Ðekakpui, ame ka ƒe vie nènye?” David ɖo eŋu be: “Wò subɔvi Betlehemtɔ Isai ƒe vie menye.”
ENGLISH: 58 And Saul said to him “Whose son are you, boy?” and David said “Son to your servant Jesse the Bethlehemite.”

EWE: 1 Samuel
ENGLISH: 1 Samuel

EWE: 18 Esi David ƒo nu kple Saul vɔ ko la, David ƒe nu lé dzi na Yonatan, eye Yonatan lɔ̃e abe eɖokui ene.
ENGLISH: 18 And when he had finished talking to Saul, Jonathan’s soul was tied fast to David’s, and Jonathan loved him as he loved himself.

EWE: 2 Tso gbe ma gbe dzi la, Saul xɔe eye meɖe mɔ nɛ wògbugbɔ yi fofoa ƒe me o.
ENGLISH: 2 And Saul took him that day and would not let him go back to his father’s house.

EWE: 3 Eye Yonatan kple David bla nu, elabena elɔ̃e abe eɖokui ene.
ENGLISH: 3 And Jonathan and David pledged themselves to each other, in the love that he had for him as he loved himself;

EWE: 4 Yonatan ɖe eƒe awu ʋlaya si ŋu abɔ mele o tsɔ na David, etsɔ eƒe aʋawu, yi, dati kple eƒe alidziblanu hã nɛ.
ENGLISH: 4 and Jonathan stripped off the robe he had on and gave it to David, and his brigandine, and even his sword and bow and belt.

EWE: 5 Eye afi sia afi si Saul dɔ David ɖo la, edzea edzi nɛ. Eya ta Saul tsɔe ɖo aʋawɔlawo nu, eye esia nyo dukɔ blibo la kple Saul ƒe subɔviwo hã ŋu.
ENGLISH: 5 And David went out on whatever missions Saul sent him on, and did well; and Saul set him over the soldiers, and it pleased all the people, and Saul’s officers too.

EWE: 6 Ne David kple aʋawɔlawo trɔ gbɔna tso Filistitɔwo wuƒe la, nyɔnuwo doa go tso Israel duwo katã me nɔa ha dzim nɔa ɣe ɖum eye wotsɔa axatsɛwo kple kasaŋkuwo nɔa aseye tsom va kpea fia Saul.
ENGLISH: 6 And when they came in, at David’s return from killing the Philistine, the women came out from all the cities of Israel for song and dances, to meet King Saul, with tambourines and festivity and triangles;

EWE: 7 Eye nyɔnu siwo nɔa aseye tsom la nɔa ha dzim be: “Saul wu ame akpewo, David ya wu ame akpe ewowo.”
ENGLISH: 7 and the merrymaking women sang “Saul struck down his thousands, David his tens of thousands.”

EWE: 8 Esia na dzi ku Saul vevie, elabena ha la mevivi enu o, eya ta egblɔ be: “Wotsɔ akpe ewowo na David, ke wotsɔ akpewo na nye ya. Fianyenye la koe susɔ woatsɔ anɛ!”
ENGLISH: 8 And Saul was very angry, and regarded this as a bad thing, and said “They have given David tens of thousands and me the thousands; he has nothing left but the kingship”;

EWE: 9 Tso gbe ma gbe la, Saul va nɔ susu vɔ̃ bum ɖe David ŋu.
ENGLISH: 9 and Saul took to looking askance at David from that day on.

EWE: 10 Esi ŋu ke la, gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃ɖi aɖe tso Mawu gbɔ va Saul dzi, ale be wòle nu wɔm tramatrama le aƒea me, esime David le kasaŋku ƒom abe ale si wòwɔna tsã ene. Saul lé akplɔ ɖe asi,
ENGLISH: 10 And on the next day a bad divine spirit seized upon Saul, and he fell under the power in the house, while David was playing his music as he did on any day;

EWE: 11 kasia Saul da akplɔ la hegblɔ be: ‘Matɔ David amimii ɖe gli ŋu!’ ke David de axae zi eve.
ENGLISH: 11 and Saul had a spear in his hand. And Saul hurled the spear and thought “I will pin David to the wall,” but David dodged away from him, twice.

EWE: 12 Eye Saul de asi David vɔvɔ̃ me, elabena Yehowa li kplii, ke egblẽ Saul ya ɖi.
ENGLISH: 12 And Saul was afraid of David, because Jehovah was with him and had gone away from Saul;

EWE: 13 Eya ta Saul ɖe David ɖa le eɖokui ŋu hetsɔe ɖo aʋawɔla akpe ɖeka nu ale be wòkplɔa dukɔ la yia aʋae.
ENGLISH: 13 and Saul removed him from his presence and appointed him captain over a thousand, and he went out and came in before the people.

EWE: 14 Nu sia nu si David wɔna la dzea edzi nɛ, eye Yehowa nɔ kplii.
ENGLISH: 14 And David did well on all his errands, and Jehovah was with him.

EWE: 15 Esi Saul kpɔe be nu sia nu dzea edzi nɛ la, evɔ̃e ŋutɔ.
ENGLISH: 15 And Saul saw how very well he did, and he quailed before him;

EWE: 16 Ke Israel kple Yuda blibo la katã lɔ̃ David ƒe nya, elabena enɔa ŋgɔ na wo le woƒe aʋahohowo me.
ENGLISH: 16 but all Israel and Judah loved David, because he went out and came in before them.

EWE: 17 Emegbe Saul gblɔ na David be: “Kpɔ ɖa, vinyenyɔnu tsitsitɔ Merab ye nye esi. Matsɔe na wò nàɖe. Gake wɔ kalẽ nam, eye nàwɔ Yehowa ƒe aʋawo ko.” Ke Saul gblɔ le eɖokui me be: ‘Matsi nye asi me o, ke boŋ netsi Filistitɔwo si me.’
ENGLISH: 17 And Saul said to David “Here is my oldest daughter Merab, I will give you her as wife only show yourself a man of energy, and fight Jehovah’s battles,” Saul’s thought being “Let it not be my hand that comes on him, but the hands of the Philistines.”

EWE: 18 Ke David gblɔ na Saul be: “Ame kae menye, eye ame kae ƒonyemetɔwo kple fofonye ƒe ƒomea nye le Israel, ne mahayi fia ƒe to nye ge?”
ENGLISH: 18 And David said to Saul “Who am I, and who are my sib (father’s clan), in Israel, that I should marry the princess?”

EWE: 19 Ke esi ɣeyiɣi de be woatsɔ Saul vinyɔnu Merab ana David la, wotsɔe na Adriel Meholatɔ la xoxo wòɖe.
ENGLISH: 19 But when the time for giving Saul’s daughter Merab to David came, she had been given to ʽAdriel the Meholathite as wife.

EWE: 20 Ke Saul vinyɔnu Mikal lɔ̃ David, eye wova gblɔe na Saul, eye nya la dzɔ dzi nɛ.
ENGLISH: 20 And Saul’s daughter Mical fell in love with David; and they told Saul, and the thing suited him.

EWE: 21 Eye Saul gblɔ be: “Matsɔe nɛ, ne wòazu mɔ̃ nɛ, ale be wòatsi Filistitɔwo si me.”
ENGLISH: 21 And Saul thought “I will give her to him and have her be a bait to trap him, and the hands of the Philistines come on him.”

EWE: Eya ta Saul gblɔ na David zi evelia be: “Àzu tonye egbea.”
ENGLISH: And Saul said to David “On two conditions you shall marry the princess today.”

EWE: 22 Eye Saul de se na eƒe subɔviwo be: “Miɖe kpɔ David ne miagblɔ nɛ be: ‘Kpɔ ɖa! Wò nu nyo fia la ŋu, eye eƒe subɔviwo katã hã lɔ̃ wò.
ENGLISH: 22 And Saul gave his officers the order “Tell David quietly ‘Here, the king likes you and all his officers love you now marry the princess.’”

EWE: Eya ta lɔ̃ nàzu fia ƒe toyɔvi.’” 23 Esi Saul ƒe subɔviwo va gblɔ nya siawo na David la, David ɖo eŋu be: “Nu tsɛ wònye le mia ŋkume be, nye ame dahe si mele ɖeke me o la, nanye fia ƒe toa?”
ENGLISH: 23 And Saul’s officers said these things in conversation with David; but David said “Does it look to you like a simple thing to marry the princess, I being a poor and obscure man?”

EWE: 24 Eye Saul ƒe subɔviwo va gblɔe nɛ be: “Ale kple ale David gblɔ.”
ENGLISH: 24 And Saul’s officers reported to him “These were David’s words.”

EWE: 25 Eye Saul gblɔ be: “Ale miagblɔ na David ye nye esi: ‘Fia la mele srɔ̃ɖenu aɖeke dim o, ke boŋ Filistitɔwo ƒe aʋanuyi alafa ɖeka, ne wòatsɔ abia hlɔ̃ fia ƒe futɔwo.’” Ke tame vɔ̃e Saul ɖo, be yeana David natsi Filistitɔwo si me.
ENGLISH: 25 And Saul said “Say to David ‘The king does not care for any purchase-money but a hundred Philistine foreskins, to get revenge on the king’s enemies,’” Saul’s plan being to have David fall by the hands of the Philistines.

EWE: 26 Eya ta eƒe subɔviawo va gblɔ nya la na David, eye nya la dze David ŋu be yeanye fia ƒe to.
ENGLISH: 26 And Saul’s officers reported these things; and the idea of marrying the princess suited David,

EWE: Esi ŋkeke si woɖo la mekpɔ de haɖe o la, 27 David kple eƒe amewo yi ɖawu Filistitɔ alafa eve, eye David tsɔ woƒe aʋanuyiawo katã vɛ na fia la, ne wòazu fia ƒe to. Ale Saul tsɔ vianyɔnu Mikal nɛ wòɖe.
ENGLISH: 27 and David went off, he and his men, and killed two hundred of the Philistines, and David brought their foreskins and paid the king in full, to marry the princess; and Saul gave him his daughter Mical as wife.

EWE: 28 Saul kpɔe dze sii be Yehowa li kple David, eye be ye vinyɔnu Mikal hã lɔ̃e.
ENGLISH: 28 And Saul saw and knew that Jehovah was with David; and Saul’s daughter Mical loved him.

EWE: 29 Ale Saul gavɔ̃ David ɖe edzi, eye Saul va zu David ƒe futɔ le eƒe agbemeŋkekewo katã me.
ENGLISH: 29 And Saul was more and more afraid of David; and Saul became a persistent enemy to David.

EWE: 30 Ɣesiaɣi si Filistitɔwo ƒe amegãwo ho yi aʋa la, David ɖua wo dzi wu Saul ƒe subɔviwo katã; eye eƒe ŋkɔ de du ŋutɔ.
ENGLISH: 30 And the captains of the Philistines came out; and as often as they came out David did better than any of Saul’s officers, and his name was held in high honor.

EWE: 1 Samuel
ENGLISH: 1 Samuel

EWE: 19 Emegbe Saul gblɔ na via Yonatan kple eƒe subɔviwo katã be yele David wu ge.
ENGLISH: 19 And Saul proposed to his son Jonathan and to all his officers that they should kill David.

EWE: 2 Esi David ƒe nu nyoa Saul vi Yonatan ŋu ŋutɔ ta la, Yonatan gblɔ na David be: “Fofonye Saul le didim be yeana woawu wò.
ENGLISH: 2 But Saul’s son Jonathan liked David very much; and Jonathan told David “Saul, my father, is looking for a chance to kill you; now in the morning look out for yourself, stay in concealment and hide,

EWE: Eya ta meɖe kuku, kpɔ ɖokuiwò dzi nyuie etsɔ ŋdi, eye nàdi ɣaɣlaƒe aɖe abe ɖo. 3 Ke nye la, mayi aɖatsi tsitre ɖe fofonye gbɔ le gbedzi, afi si nèbe ɖo.
ENGLISH: 3 and I will go out and stand at my father’s side in the field where you are, and I will talk of you to my father, and see what there is, and tell you.”

EWE: Eye maƒo nu le ŋuwò na fofonye, ne mede dzesi nane la, mava gblɔe na wò.” 4 Eya ta Yonatan ƒo nu nyuie le David ŋu na fofoa Saul. Egblɔ nɛ be: “Fia megawɔ vɔ̃ ɖe eƒe subɔvi David ŋu o, elabena mewɔ vɔ̃ aɖeke wò o; dɔ nyui siwo wòwɔ na wò la ɖe vi na wò.
ENGLISH: 4 And Jonathan spoke in David’s favor to his father Saul, and said to him “Take care not to do any wrong in the matter of David, sir, because he has done you no wrong and his deeds have been very good for you;

EWE: 5 Etsɔ eƒe agbe de afɔku me heyi ɖawu Filistitɔ la, ale be Yehowa to esia me he dziɖuɖu gã aɖe vɛ na Israel katã.
ENGLISH: 5 and he took his life in his hand and killed the Philistine, and Jehovah made a great victory for all Israel.

EWE: Èkpɔe, eye dzi dzɔ wò. Ekema nu ka tae nàwɔ nu vɔ̃ ɖe ʋu maɖifɔ ŋu ahana woawu David dzodzro?”
ENGLISH: You saw it and were glad; and why should you do the wrong of shedding innocent blood, in putting David to death for nothing?”

EWE: 6 Ale Saul ɖo to Yonatan ƒe gbe, eye Saul ka atam be: “Zi ale si Yehowa le agbe la, womawui o.”
ENGLISH: 6 And Saul listened to Jonathan, and Saul swore “By Jehovah, he shall not be put to death.”

EWE: 7 Emegbe Yonatan yɔ David, eye Yonatan gblɔ nya siawo katã nɛ. Eya ta Yonatan kplɔ David vɛ na Saul wònɔ egbɔ abe tsã ene.
ENGLISH: 7 And Jonathan called David, and Jonathan told him all these things, and Jonathan brought David to Saul and he was in his presence as he had formerly been.

EWE: 8 Emegbe aʋa gadzɔ, eye David do go yi ɖawɔ aʋa kple Filistitɔwo, eye wòsi wo hewu wo dometɔ gbogbo aɖewo, ale be wosi le enu.
ENGLISH: 8 And there was more of the war, and David went out and fought the Philistines and killed a great number of them, and they fled before him.

EWE: 9 Eye Yehowa ƒe gbɔgbɔ vɔ̃ɖi va Saul dzi esime wòbɔbɔ nɔ aƒe me, eye eƒe akplɔ le esi, eye David nɔ kasaŋku ƒom nɛ.
ENGLISH: 9 And there was a bad divine spirit on Saul while he was sitting in the house, spear in hand, and David was playing his music;

EWE: 10 Saul di be yeatɔ akplɔ David amimii ɖe gli ŋu, ke ede axa na Saul, eye akplɔ si wòda la yi ɖatɔ gli. Eye David si dzo le zã ma me.
ENGLISH: 10 and Saul tried to pin David to the wall with the spear, but David got out of Saul’s way and he struck the spear into the wall; and David fled and made his escape.

EWE: 11 Emegbe Saul dɔ amewo ɖe David ƒe me, be woadzɔ eŋu, ale be ne ŋu ke la, woawui, ke David srɔ̃ Mikal gblɔ nɛ be: “Ne mèsi zã sia o la, ekema àzu ame kuku etsɔ.”
ENGLISH: 11 And that night Saul sent scouts to David’s house to watch it, so as to put him to death in the morning; and David’s wife Mical told him “If you do not get your life into safety tonight you will be put to death tomorrow”;

EWE: 12 Enumake Mikal na David ɖi to fesre nu be wòasi adzo.
ENGLISH: 12 and Mical let David down through the window, and off he went, and fled away and made his escape.

EWE: 13 Eye Mikal tsɔ terafim legba da ɖe aba dzi, eye wòtsɔ avɔ si wolɔ̃ kple gbɔ̃fu ɖo ɖe eƒe tade hetsyɔ avɔ nɛ.
ENGLISH: 13 And Mical took the teraphim and put it in the bed, and put the goat’s-hair netting at its head, and covered it with the blanket.

EWE: 14 Eye Saul dɔ amewo ɖa be woaɖakplɔ David vɛ, ke Mikal gblɔ be: “Ele dɔ lém.”
ENGLISH: 14 And Saul sent messengers to get David; and she said “He is sick.”

EWE: 15 Ale Saul dɔ amewo ɖa be woaɖakpɔ David ɖa gblɔ be: “Miyi ɖakɔ eya kple aba la vɛ nam ne woawui.”
ENGLISH: 15 And Saul sent the messengers to see David, with the commission “Bring him up to me in the bed to be put to death”;

EWE: 16 Esi dɔlaawo va la, wokpɔ terafim legba la le abaa dzi, eye avɔ si wolɔ̃ kple gbɔ̃fu le eƒe tade.
ENGLISH: 16 and the messengers went in and found the teraphim in the bed and the goat’s-hair netting at its head.

EWE: 17 Eye Saul bia Mikal be: “Nu ka tae nèflum alea, eye nèɖe asi le nye futɔ ŋu wòsi dzo?” Mikal ɖo eŋu na Saul be: “Eyae gblɔ nam be: ‘Ðe asi le ŋunye madzo!
ENGLISH: 17 And Saul said to Mical “What did you turn on me like that for, and let my enemy go so that he has made his escape?” and Mical said “It was he; he said to me ‘Let me go; do you want me to kill you?’”

EWE: Ne menye nenema o la, mawu wò.’” 18 Ke David si yi Samuel gbɔ le Rama. Eye wògblɔ nu siwo katã Saul wɔe la nɛ. Eye eya kple Samuel wodzo yi ɖanɔ Nayot.
ENGLISH: 18 And David fled away and made his escape, and came to Samuel at Ramah and told him everything that Saul had done to him; and he and Samuel went and lived at Nothab-Ramah;

EWE: 19 Emegbe wova gblɔ na Saul be: “Kpɔ ɖa!
ENGLISH: 19 and Saul was told “David is to be found at Nothab-Ramah.”

EWE: David le Nayot le Rama.” 20 Enumake Saul dɔ amewo ɖa be woaɖalé David vɛ. Esi wokpɔ nyagblɔɖila tsitsiwo wole nya gblɔm ɖi, eye Samuel nye tatɔ le wo nu la, Mawu ƒe gbɔgbɔ va Saul ƒe dɔlawo dzi, ale be woawo hã wote nuwɔwɔ abe nyagblɔɖilawo ene.
ENGLISH: 20 And Saul sent messengers to get David; and they saw the assemblage of prophets under the power and Samuel standing over them, and a divine spirit came upon Saul’s messengers and they too fell under the power.

EWE: 21 Esi wova gblɔe na Saul la, enumake edɔ ame bubuwo ɖa, eye woawo hã wote nuwɔwɔ abe nyagblɔɖilawo ene.
ENGLISH: 21 And they told Saul, and he sent other messengers, and they too fell under the power; and Saul kept on and sent a third party of messengers, and so did they.

EWE: Eya ta Saul gadɔ ame hatsotso etɔ̃lia ɖa, eye woawo hã wɔ nu abe nyagblɔɖilawo ene. 22 Mlɔeba eya ŋutɔ hã yi Rama. Esi wòɖo vudo gã si le Seku gbɔ la, ebia be: “Afi kae Samuel kple David le?” Woɖo eŋu be: “Wole Nayot le Rama.”
ENGLISH: 22 And Saul was angry, and he too went to Ramah, and came to the cistern of the threshing-floor on the scalp and asked “Where are Samuel and David?” and the man he asked said “You will find them at Nothab-Ramah.”

EWE: 23 Esi Saul le mɔa dzi tso afi ma yina Nayot si le Rama la, Mawu ƒe gbɔgbɔ va eya hã dzi, eye wòyi azɔlia dzi hele nu wɔm abe nyagblɔɖila ene va se ɖe esime wòɖo Nayot le Rama.
ENGLISH: 23 And he went there to Nothab-Ramah, and a divine spirit came upon him too, and he went along, under the power as he went, till he came to Nothab-Ramah;

EWE: 24 Eye eya hã ɖe eƒe awuwo ɖi, eye wòwɔ nu abe nyagblɔɖila ene le Samuel ŋkume, eye wòɖe ama mlɔ anyi ɖi ŋkeke blibo kple zã blibo ma katã. Esia tae wogblɔna be: “Ãa, Saul hãe le nyagblɔɖilawo domea?”
ENGLISH: 24 and he too threw off his clothes and was under the power before Samuel, and fell down naked and lay so all that day and all night; this is why they say “Is Saul also among the prophets?”

EWE: 1 Samuel
ENGLISH: 1 Samuel

EWE: 20 Eye David si tso Nayot le Rama va Yonatan gbɔ hebiae be: “Nu kae mewɔ?
ENGLISH: 20 And David fled away from Nothab-Ramah.

EWE: Vo kae meda, eye nu vɔ̃ kae mewɔ ɖe fofowò ŋu, hafi wòle didim be yeaɖe nye agbe ɖa?”
ENGLISH: And he came and said in conversation with Jonathan “What have I done? what is my crime? what wrong have I done before your father, that he is hunting for my life?”

EWE: 2 Yonatan ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Nede megbe xaa! Mèle kuku ge o. Kpɔ ɖa! Fofonye mawɔ nu gã alo nu sue aɖeke, ne megblɔe nam o. Nu ka ŋuti fofonye aɣla nu sia ɖem?
ENGLISH: 2 And he said to him “Away with the thought! you are not to die; why, my father does not do anything great or small without disclosing it to me, and how should my father conceal this thing from me? there is nothing to it.”

EWE: Nu sia madzɔ o.” 3 Ke David gaka atam gblɔ be: “Fofowò nyae nyuie be, mèlɔ̃a nu le gbɔnye o, eya ta agblɔ be: ‘Mele be Yonatan nanya naneke tso eŋu ne wòavee o.’
ENGLISH: 3 But David answered again “Your father knows perfectly well that you like me, and he thinks ‘Let Jonathan not know this, for fear he should be pained’; but, by Jehovah and by your life, I am just about a pace from death.”

EWE: Ke zi ale si Yehowa le agbe, eye wò hã èle agbe la, nye kple ku dome megadidi o!” 4 Yonatan gagblɔ na David be: “Nu sia nu si nàgblɔ la, mawɔe na wò.” 5 Eye David gblɔ na Yonatan be: “Kpɔ ɖa! Etsɔe nye dzinu yeye, eye wòle nam godoo be mabɔbɔ nɔ anyi aɖu nu kple fia la; do mɔm madzo aɖaɣla ɖokuinye ɖe gbe me, va se ɖe ŋkeke etɔ̃lia ƒe fiẽ.
ENGLISH: 4 And Jonathan said to David “What would you suggests? and I will do it for you.” 5 And David said to Jonathan “Here it is new moon tomorrow, and I should sit down with the king to eat: give me leave of absence, and I will conceal myself out on the range till the third evening.

EWE: 6 Ne fofowò de dzesii be nyemeli o la, ekema gblɔ be: ‘David bia mɔ le gbɔnye be yeaƒu du ayi yewo de Betlehem, elabena ƒome blibo la le ƒevɔ sa ge le afi ma.’
ENGLISH: 6 If your father should miss me, say ‘David asked leave of me to run to his city Bethlehem, because all the clan has an annual sacrifice there.’

EWE: 7 Ne egblɔ be: ‘Enyo!’ la, ekema wò dɔla ŋu fa.
ENGLISH: 7 If he says ‘All right,’ your servant is safe; but if he is angry, be sure I am in for trouble from him,

EWE: Ke ne edo dziku la, ekema nyae be eɖo tame vɔ̃ ɖe ŋunye. 8 Eya ta ve wò dɔla nu, elabena wò kple wò dɔla mieɖo Yehowa ƒe nubabla me. Ke ne meda vo la, ekema wò ŋutɔ wum.
ENGLISH: 8 and act a friend’s part by your servant (since you have taken your servant into a pledge in the name of Jehovah) and if there is crime in me, kill me yourself: what should you bring me to your father for?”

EWE: Nu ka ŋuti nàkplɔm ayi na fofowò?” 9 Yonatan ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Nede megbe xaa be mawɔ nu ma tɔgbi ɖe ŋuwò! Ne menyae be fofonye ɖo tame vɔ̃ ɖe ŋuwò la, ɖe nyemagblɔe na wò oa?”
ENGLISH: 9 And Jonathan said “Away with the thought; if I do find that trouble is due to come upon you from my father, of course I will tell you of it.”

EWE: 10 Eye David bia Yonatan be: “Ne fofowò da gbe ɖe gbɔwò ɖe, ame kae agblɔe nam?”
ENGLISH: 10 And David said to Jonathan “Who shall tell me if your father gives you a hard answer?”

EWE: 11 Yonatan gblɔ na David be: “Wò ya va míayi gbe me.” Ale wo kple eve la woyi gbe me.
ENGLISH: 11 And Jonathan said to David “Come out on the range”; and the two of them went out on the range.

EWE: 12 Eye Yonatan gblɔ na David be: “Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la, nanye ɖasefo, be etsɔ ɣealewoɣi, alo ŋkeke etɔ̃a gbe la, mate fofonye ƒe nu me ase. Ne susu nyui le esi ɖe David ŋu la, ekema ɖe nyemadɔ ame ɖe wò woava gblɔe na wò oa?
ENGLISH: 12 And Jonathan said to David “Jehovah the God of Israel be witness: when I sound my father, right away tomorrow, and find that he is or is not well-disposed toward David, then I will send to you and give you notice.

EWE: 13 Ke ne fofonye di be yeawɔ vɔ̃ wò, gake nyemeva gblɔe na wò o hedo mɔ wò le ŋutifafa me o la, ekema Yehowa nefia Yonatan, eye wòagafiae ɖe edzi.
ENGLISH: 13 Jehovah do so to Jonathan, and more, but if my father is thinking fit to do you mischief I will give you notice and send you off to go where good shall betide you.

EWE: Yehowa nenɔ kpli wò abe ale si wònɔ kple fofonye ene.
ENGLISH: And may Jehovah be with you as he has been with my father;

EWE: 14 Eye ne megale agbe la, ɖe màɖe Yehowa ƒe amenuveve afiam, eye ne meku hã màɖee afiam oa?
ENGLISH: 14 and if I should still be alive, I hope you will befriend me for Jehovah’s sake; and if I should be dead,

EWE: 15 Eye wò amenuveve la nu megatso le aƒenye me o tegbee, ne Yehowa ɖe David ƒe futɔwo katã ɖa le anyigba dzi gɔ̃ hã.”
ENGLISH: 15 you will never cut off your friendship from my family, nor, when Jehovah cuts off David’s enemies each of them from the face of the earth,

EWE: 16 Eya ta Yonatan bla nu kple David ƒe aƒe gblɔ be, “Yehowa abia akɔnta tso David ƒe futɔwo si.”
ENGLISH: 16 Jonathan be cut off from alongside David’s family; and may Jehovah hold David’s enemies to account.”

EWE: 17 Ale Yonatan gana David ka atam nɛ ɖe lɔlɔ̃ si wòtsɔ lɔ̃e la dzi, elabena elɔ̃e abe ale si wòlɔ̃ eya ŋutɔ ɖokui ene.
ENGLISH: 17 And again Jonathan swore David, in the love that he had for him, because he loved him the same as himself.

EWE: 18 Eye Yonatan gblɔ nɛ be: “Etsɔe nye dzinu yeye, eye woade dzesii be mèli o, elabena wò zikpui atsi ƒuƒlu.
ENGLISH: 18 And Jonathan said to David “Tomorrow it is new moon, and you will be missed because your seat will be vacant.

EWE: 19 Woagade dzesi wò anyimanɔmanɔ la wu le ŋkeke etɔ̃a gbe, eya ta yi afi si nèbe ɖo tsã la, eye nànɔ kpe sia xa.
ENGLISH: 19 And the third day lie very low, and come to the place where you concealed yourself on the day of the affair, and sit down beside yonder mound;

EWE: 20 Mada aŋutrɔ etɔ̃ ɖo ɖe kpea xa, abe nanee medzidze da ene.
ENGLISH: 20 and I will shoot roving arrows to one side of it, roving at a mark.

EWE: 21 Ne medɔ subɔvi aɖe ɖa la, magblɔ be: ‘Yi ɖadi aŋutrɔawo.’ Ne megblɔ na subɔvia be: ‘Kpɔ ɖa! Aŋutrɔawo le axawò afii, fɔ wo’ la, ekema va, elabena zi ale si Yehowa le agbe la, efia be ŋuwò fa, vɔ̃ aɖeke madzɔ ɖe dziwò o.
ENGLISH: 21 And I will send the boy and tell him ‘Go find the arrow’; if I say to the boy ‘Here, the arrow is this side of you; pick it up,’ come, because you are safe and there is nothing afoot, by Jehovah.

EWE: 22 Ke ne megblɔ na ɖekakpui la be: ‘Kpɔ ɖa! Aŋutrɔawo le ŋgɔwò ɖaa’ la, ekema dzo, elabena Yehowa do mɔ wò.
ENGLISH: 22 But if I say to the boy ‘There, the arrow is beyond you,’ go, because Jehovah has sent you away.

EWE: 23 Ke nya siwo nye kpli wò míegblɔ la, Yehowa nenɔ nye kpli wò dome tegbee.”
ENGLISH: 23 And as to the promise you and I have given, Jehovah is between you and me forever.”

EWE: 24 Eye David ɣla eɖokui ɖe gbea me.
ENGLISH: 24 And David concealed himself on the range; and new moon came, and the king sat down to his meal.

EWE: Esi dzinu yeye ɖo la, fia la bɔbɔ nɔ eƒe zikpui dzi be yeaɖu nu. 25 Fia la bɔbɔ nɔ teƒe si wònɔna edziedzi le glia ŋu.
ENGLISH: 25 And the king sat in his place as usual, in the wall seat, and Jonathan was in front and Abner sat at Saul’s side, and David’s place was vacant.

EWE: Yonatan dze ŋgɔe, eye Abner bɔbɔ nɔ Saul xa, ke David ƒe nɔƒe ya tsi ƒuƒlu. 26 Saul megblɔ nya aɖeke gbe ma gbe o, elabena ebu be: ‘Nanee dzɔ, ale be eŋu mekɔ o.
ENGLISH: 26 And Saul said nothing that day, because he thought “He has had something happen; he is not clean because he has not purified himself.”

EWE: Ɛ̃, anye eŋutie mekɔ o.’ 27 Eye le ŋkeke evea gbe, si nye ŋkeke si kplɔ dzinu yeyea ɖo dzi la, David ƒe nɔƒe la gatsi ƒuƒlu kokoko. Eye Saul bia via Yonatan be: “Nu ka tae Isai vi la meva nua ɖuƒe etsɔ kple egbe siaa o?”
ENGLISH: 27 And on the day after the new moon, the second, David’s place was vacant, and Saul said to his son Jonathan “How comes it Jesse’s son did not come to the meal either yesterday or today?”

EWE: 28 Yonatan ɖo eŋu na Saul be: “David ɖe kuku nam be maɖe mɔ na ye yeayi Betlehem.
ENGLISH: 28 And Jonathan answered Saul “David got leave of me for a trip to Bethlehem,

EWE: 29 Eye wògblɔ be: ‘Meɖe kuku, na mayi, elabena míaƒe ƒomea le vɔ sa ge le dua me, eye nɔvinyee ɖo du ɖem. Eya ta ne ève nunye la, ekema meɖe kuku, na maƒu du ayi aɖakpɔ nɔvinyewo ɖa.’
ENGLISH: 29 and said ‘Give me leave of absence, because we have a clan sacrifice in the city, and here my brothers have summoned me; now please let me get off to see my brothers’; that is why he has not come to the king’s table.”

EWE: Esia tae meva fia ƒe kplɔ̃ ŋu o ɖo.” 30 Ale Saul do dɔmedzoe ɖe Yonatan ŋu vevie gblɔ nɛ be: “Wò nyɔnu dzeaglã ƒe vi, menyae nyuie be, ètia Isai vi la be nàtsɔ ado ŋukpe ɖokuiwò, eye nàdo ŋukpe dawò.
ENGLISH: 30 And Saul was angry at Jonathan and said to him “You son of disorderly girls, don’t I know you are associated with Jesse’s son to bring yourself to grief, yourself and your mother’s nakedness?

EWE: 31 Elabena ŋkeke ale si Isai vi la le agbe le anyigba dzi la, wò ŋutɔ kple wò fianyenye la miali ke o.
ENGLISH: 31 because just as long as Jesse’s son is alive above ground your kingship will not be secure.

EWE: Eya ta dɔ, ne woaɖakplɔe vɛ nam, elabena edze na ku.”
ENGLISH: Now send and fetch him to me, for his life is forfeit.”

EWE: 32 Ke Yonatan bia fofoa Saul be: “Nu ka tae woawui ɖo? Nu kae wòwɔ?”
ENGLISH: 32 And Jonathan answered his father Saul “What should he die for? what has he done?”

EWE: 33 Enumake Saul da akplɔ be yeatɔe, eye Yonatan dze sii be ye fofo ɖoe kplikpaa be yeawu David.
ENGLISH: 33 and Saul hurled his spear at him to kill him; and Jonathan knew his father was bound to put David to death.

EWE: 34 Enumake dzi ku Yonatan vevie wòtso le kplɔ̃a ŋu, eye meɖu abolo le dzinu yeye ƒe ŋkeke evelia dzi o, elabena David ƒe nya la te ɖe edzi, eye eya ŋutɔ fofoa do ŋukpee.
ENGLISH: 34 And Jonathan rose from the table in anger, and ate no food the second day of the moon, because he was pained about David, because his father had insulted him.

EWE: 35 Esi ŋu ke la, Yonatan dze mɔ yi gbe me le teƒe si eya kple David woɖo ɖi be yewoakpe le, eye ɖekakpui dzaa aɖe si nye eƒe subɔvi la nɔ eŋu.
ENGLISH: 35 And in the morning Jonathan went out on the range to keep his appointment with David, taking a small boy with him,

EWE: 36 Eye wògblɔ na eƒe subɔvi la be: “Meɖe kuku, ƒu du yi ɖadi aŋutrɔ siwo da ge mala.”
ENGLISH: 36 and said to his boy “Run and find the arrows I shoot.”

EWE: Subɔvi la ƒu du yi, eye Yonatan da aŋutrɔ la to eta.
ENGLISH: As the boy was running he shot an arrow to go beyond him;

EWE: 37 Esi subɔvia ɖo afi si aŋutrɔ si Yonatan da la dze la, Yonatan do ɣli ɖe subɔvi la yome gblɔ be: “Alo menye aŋutrɔ lae nye ema ɖaa le ŋgɔwò oa?”
ENGLISH: 37 and when the boy came to the place where the arrow Jonathan had shot was, Jonathan called after the boy “Why, the arrow is beyond you.”

EWE: 38 Eye Yonatan gado ɣli ake ɖe subɔvia yome be: “Ðe abla! Netsɔ! Mègatɔ o!” Eye Yonatan ƒe subɔvi la yi ɖafɔ aŋutrɔawo heva eƒe aƒetɔ gbɔ.
ENGLISH: 38 And Jonathan called after the boy “Be quick, hurry up, don’t stand still”; and Jonathan’s boy picked up the arrow and brought it to his master,

EWE: 39 Ke subɔvia menya nu si le edzi yim o; negbe Yonatan kple David koe nya.
ENGLISH: 39 the boy not knowing anything only Jonathan and David knew the idea.

EWE: 40 Emegbe Yonatan tsɔ eƒe aʋawɔnuawo na eƒe subɔvi la gblɔ nɛ be: “Tsɔ wo yi dua me.”
ENGLISH: 40 And Jonathan gave his boy the equipment he had, and said “Go take it into the city”;

EWE: 41 Esi subɔvia dzo la, David do go tso afi ma lɔƒo, le anyiehe gome. Eye wòdze klo tsyɔ mo anyi zi etɔ̃, eye wogbugbɔ nu na wo nɔewo hefa avi ɖe wo nɔewo dzi, ke David ƒe avifafa nu sẽ wu.
ENGLISH: 41 and the boy went in, and David stood up from beside the mound and threw himself down flat on his face and did reverence three times; and they kissed each other and wept for each other till broad day.

EWE: 42 Eye Yonatan gblɔ na David be: “Heyi le ŋutifafa me, elabena mí ame evea míeka atam le Yehowa ƒe ŋkɔ me be: ‘Yehowa nenɔ nye kpli wò dome, eye wòanɔ nye dzidzimeviwo kple wò dzidzimeviwo dome tegbee.’” Ale David tso dze mɔ, eye Yonatan hã yi dua me.
ENGLISH: 42 And Jonathan said to David “Go, and good betide you; and as to what we have both sworn in Jehovah’s name, Jehovah shall be between you and me, and between your descendants and mine, forever”; and David went away, and Jonathan went into the city.

EWE: 1 Samuel
ENGLISH: 1 Samuel

EWE: 21 Emegbe David va nunɔla Ahimelek gbɔ le Nob. Ahimelek vɔ̃ eye wòdo go va kpe David hebiae be: “Nu ka ŋuti wò ɖeka koe va, eye ame aɖeke mele ŋuwò o?”
ENGLISH: 21 And David came to Nob, to Priest Ahimelec; and Ahimelec came in alarm to meet David, and said to him “How comes it you are alone and nobody with you?”

EWE: 2 David ɖo eŋu na nunɔla Ahimelek be: “Fia lae de gbe aɖe asi nam, eye wògblɔ nam be, ‘Ame aɖeke meganya naneke le nya si gbe mele dɔwòm ɖo kple gbe si mede asi na wò la ŋu o.’ Eye mewɔ ɖoɖo kple nye ɖekakpuiawo be míado go le teƒe aɖe.
ENGLISH: 2 And David said to Priest Ahimelec “The king gave me an order and said to me ‘Let nobody know anything of the matter that I am sending you on and have given you orders for’; and I have made an appointment with my men for such and such a place.

EWE: 3 Eya ta ne abolo atɔ̃ le asiwò la, ekema tsɔ wo nam, alo nu sia nu si nàkpɔ ko.”
ENGLISH: 3 And now what have you on hand? give me half a dozen cakes of bread in my hand, or whatever there is.”

EWE: 4 Ke nunɔla la gblɔ na David be: “Abolo dzodzro aɖeke mele asinye o, gake abolo kɔkɔe ya li; ne ɖekakpuiawo mede nyɔnu gbɔ le ŋkeke siawo me o ko.”
ENGLISH: 4 And the priest answered David “I have no everyday bread, but sacred bread there is, if the men have only kept themselves from womankind.”

EWE: 5 David ɖo eŋu na nunɔla la be: “Wotsri nyɔnu na mí abe ale si wònɔ tsã esime meyi aʋa ene. Ne dɔdeasi dzro aɖe koe wònye ɣemaɣi evɔ ɖekakpuiawo ŋuti kɔ la, ɖe wo ŋuti makɔ egbe sia wu esi míeva dɔ tɔxɛ sia gbe oa!”
ENGLISH: 5 And David answered the priest “O, but we are barred from womankind as we used to be; when I left, the men’s things were in a sacred condition though it was everyday business they were on how much more when today it is every way sacred!”

EWE: 6 Ale nunɔla la tsɔ abolo kɔkɔe la nɛ, elabena abolo aɖeke mele afi ma o, negbe ŋkumeɖobolo si woɖe le Yehowa ŋkume be woatsɔ abolo yeye aɖo eteƒe le gbe si gbe woɖee ɖa la ko.
ENGLISH: 6 And the priest gave him sacred, because there was not any bread there except the showbread that had been removed from before Jehovah to put on hot bread on the day when it was taken.

EWE: 7 Ke Saul ƒe subɔviwo dometɔ ɖeka, si wosika ɖi le Yehowa ŋkume la, nɔ afi ma gbe ma gbe.
ENGLISH: 7 And there was a man there that day who was one of Saul’s servants, detained before Jehovah; his name was Doeg the Edomite, the fighting man of Saul’s shepherds.

EWE: Eŋkɔe nye Doeg, Edomtɔ la, eye wònye Saul ƒe lãkplɔlawo ƒe amegã. 8 Eye David gblɔ na Ahimelek be: “Akplɔ alo yi aɖeke mele gbɔwò afi sia oa?
ENGLISH: 8 And David said to Ahimelec “And is there not in your hands here such a thing as a spear or a sword? because I did not take with me either my sword or my other things, since the king’s affair was urgent.”

EWE: Nyemetsɔ nye yi alo nye aʋawɔnuwo ɖe asi o, elabena ehiã be woakpɔ fia ƒe nya la gbɔ kpata.” 9 Nunɔla la gblɔ be: “Filistitɔ Goliat, ame si nèwu le Ela Bali me la ƒe yi koe li, eyae nye esi ŋu wobla avɔ ɖo, le kɔmewu la megbe.
ENGLISH: 9 And the priest said “The sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you killed in Terebinth Vale there is that, wrapped in a cloak behind the ephod; if you would take that for yourself, take it; for there is no other on these premises but that.”

EWE: Eye David gblɔ be: “Etɔgbi aɖeke meli o. Tsɔe nam.”
ENGLISH: And David said “There is none like that; let me have it.”

EWE: 10 David dze mɔ gbe ma gbe henɔ sisim le Saul nu, eye mlɔeba wòva Gat-fia Akis gbɔ.
ENGLISH: 10 And David rose and fled from Saul that day, and came to King Akish of Gath.

EWE: 11 Eye Akis ƒe subɔviwo gblɔ nɛ be: “Menye David siae nye anyigba la ƒe fia oa? Alo menye eya ŋue woɖu ɣe le nɔ gbɔgblɔm be: ‘Saul wu ame akpewo, David ya wu ame akpe ewowo’ oa?”
ENGLISH: 11 And Akish’s officers said to him “Why, this is David, the king of the country; the one of whom they sing in the dances ‘Saul has killed by the thousand, David by the ten-thousand.’”

EWE: 12 Nya siawo ɖe fu na David ƒe dzi, ale be wòde asi Gat-fia Akis vɔvɔ̃ me ŋutɔ.
ENGLISH: 12 And David took note of these words and became very much afraid of King Akish of Gath,

EWE: 13 Eya ta edo tsu eɖokui le wo ŋkume henɔ aɖaʋanu wɔm le wo dome. Eye wònɔ fli tem ɖe dugbo la ƒe ʋɔtruwo ŋu, eye ade nɔ tsyɔtsyɔm ɖe ge me nɛ.
ENGLISH: 13 and pretended to them that his wits were unsettled, and drummed on the gates and let his saliva run down on his beard.

EWE: 14 Mlɔeba Akis gblɔ na eƒe subɔviwo be: “Esi miekpɔ be ame sia le aɖaʋanu wɔm ɖe, nu ka tae miekplɔe vɛ nam?
ENGLISH: 14 And Akish said to his officers “There, when you see an insane man, why do you bring him to me?

EWE: 15 Alo aɖaʋatɔe le hiãyem hafi miekplɔe vɛ be wòava nɔ aɖaʋanu wɔm le gbɔnyea? Ðe wòle be ame sia nage ɖe nye aƒe mea?”
ENGLISH: 15 Am I short of lunatics, that you bring that fellow to play his insane tricks around me? is that creature to come into my house?”

EWE: 1 Samuel
ENGLISH: 1 Samuel

EWE: 22 David dzo le afi ma hesi yi agado si le Adulam la me. Esi nɔviawo kple fofoa ƒemetɔwo katã see la, woyi egbɔ le afi ma.
ENGLISH: 22 And David went away from there, and escaped to the fastness of ʽAdullam; and his brothers and all his kin heard of it, and they went down and joined him there.

EWE: 2 Eye ame siwo katã le xaxa me kple fenyilawo kpakple ame siwo katã dɔme le vevem la ƒo ƒu ɖe eŋu, eye wòzu woƒe tatɔ. Ame siwo le eŋu la anɔ ame alafa ene.
ENGLISH: 2 And every man who was in a desperate pinch, and every man who was involved in debt, and every man with a grievance, gathered around him, and he became chief over them; and there came to be about four hundred men with him.

EWE: 3 Emegbe David dzo le afi ma yi Mizpe le Moab, eye wògblɔ na Moab-fia be: “Meɖe kuku, na fofonye kple danye nanɔ mia gbɔ, va se ɖe esime manya nu si Mawu awɔ nam.”
ENGLISH: 3 And David went from there to Mispeh-Moab and said to the king of Moab “Let my father and mother come out and be among you till I know what God will do with me”;

EWE: 4 Ale wògblẽ wo ɖe Moab-fia gbɔ, eye wotsi egbɔ ŋkeke siwo katã David le agado la me.
ENGLISH: 4 and he brought them into the presence of the king of Moab, and they stayed with him all the time David was in the fastness.

EWE: 5 Emegbe nyagblɔɖila Gad gblɔ na David be: “Mèganɔ teƒe ma o. Dzo yi Yuda-nyigba dzi.” Ale David dzo, eye wòva Heret-ve me.
ENGLISH: 5 But the prophet Gad said to David “You are not to stay in the fastness; go into the country of Judah”; and David went, and came into Hereth Badlands.

EWE: 6 Saul se be woke ɖe David kple ame siwo le eŋu la ŋuti.
ENGLISH: 6 And Saul heard of it, because David and the men who were with him were well known.

EWE: Ɣemaɣi Saul bɔbɔ nɔ Gibea le tamarisk-ti te le togbɛ la dzi, elé eƒe akplɔ ɖe asi, eye eŋumewo katã le tsitre ƒo xlãe.
ENGLISH: And Saul was at Gibeah sitting under the tamarisk on the height, with his spear in his hand and all his officers standing by,

EWE: 7 Eye Saul gblɔ na eŋume siwo le tsitre ƒo xlãe la be: “Mi Benyamin viwo, meɖe kuku, miɖo to miasee. Ðe miesusu be Isai vi la ana anyigbawo kple waingblewo mia?
ENGLISH: 7 and Saul said to his officers who were standing by “Listen, Benjamites: is Jesse’s son going to give all of you fields and vineyards and make all of you captains over a thousand or over a hundred,

EWE: Ðe wòaɖo mi katã amegãwo ɖe ame akpewo nu alo ɖe ame alafawo nua? 8 Mi katã mieɖo nugbe ɖe ŋunye! Ame aɖeke mefi tofi nam esime nye ŋutɔ vinye bla nu kple Isai vi la o! Eye mia dometɔ aɖeke mese veve ɖe nunye, ne wòava fi tofi nam be, nye ŋutɔ vinye na nye subɔvi tso ɖe ŋunye heva de xa ɖi nam, abe ale si wòle egbe sia ene o.”
ENGLISH: 8 that all of you have conspired against me and there is nobody to give me notice when my son leagues with Jesse’s son, and there is nobody who aches for me and gives me notice when my son sets up my servant against me as an underhand enemy, as he is doing today?”

EWE: 9 Eye Doeg Edomtɔ si tɔ ɖe afi ma henye tatɔ le Saul ŋumewo nu la ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Mekpɔ Isai vi la wòva Ahimelek, Ahitub vi gbɔ le Nob.
ENGLISH: 9 And Doeg the Edomite, who was standing by Saul’s officers, answered “I saw Jesse’s son come to Ahimelec the son of Ahitub at Nob,

EWE: 10 Ebia gbe Yehowa nɛ; ena mɔdzinuɖuɖui. Eye wòtsɔ Goliat, Filistitɔ la ƒe yi nɛ.”
ENGLISH: 10 and he put a question to Jehovah for him and gave him provisions, and gave him Goliath the Philistine’s sword.”

EWE: 11 Enumake fia la dɔ be woayi aɖayɔ nunɔla Ahimelek, Ahitub vi la kple nunɔla siwo katã le fofoa ƒe me le Nob la vɛ.
ENGLISH: 11 And the king sent to summon Priest Ahimelec the son of Ahitub and all his kin, the priests at Nob, and they all came to the king.

EWE: Ale wo katã wova fia la gbɔ. 12 Eye Saul gblɔ be: “Ahitub vi, meɖe kuku, ɖo to nàsee!”
ENGLISH: 12 And Saul said “Listen, son of Ahitub”; and he said “Yes, sire.”

EWE: Eɖo eŋu be: “Mele to dzi, nye aƒetɔ.” 13 Saul biae be: “Nu ka tae wò kple Isai vi la mieɖo nugbe ɖe ŋunye, nètsɔ abolo kple yi nɛ, eye nèbia gbe Mawu nɛ?
ENGLISH: 13 And Saul said to him “Why have you and Jesse’s son conspired against me, you giving him bread and a sword and putting a question to God for him, standing up against me as an underhand enemy, as you are doing today?”

EWE: Etso ɖe ŋunye hede xa ɖi nam, abe ale si wòle egbe sia ene.” 14 Eye Ahimelek ɖo eŋu na fia la be: “Ame kae le wò dɔlawo dome si wɔa nuteƒe abe David ene? Fia ƒe to kple ŋuwòdzɔlawo ƒe amegã, si ŋu wodea bubui le aƒewò me ye wònye.
ENGLISH: 14 And Ahimelec answered the king “And who among all your majesty’s officers is like David, enjoying your confidence and son-in-law to your majesty, and admitted to private audience, and honored in your house?

EWE: 15 Egbee nye zi gbãtɔ si mebia gbe Mawu nɛa? Nya si gblɔm nèle nede megbe xaa tso gbɔnye!
ENGLISH: 15 Have I begun today to put questions to Jehovah for him? away with the thought!

EWE: Fia megada nya ɖe eƒe subɔvi kple fofonye ƒe aƒe blibo la katã dzi o, elabena wò subɔvi menya naneke kura tso nu siawo katã ŋu o.”
ENGLISH: Your majesty must not charge anything against your servant or any of my kin, for your servant knows nothing of all this, nothing great or small.”

EWE: 16 Ke fia la gblɔ be: “Ahimelek, wò kple fofowò ƒe aƒe la katã miaku.”
ENGLISH: 16 And the king said “You die, Ahimelec, you and all your kin.”

EWE: 17 Eye fia la gblɔ na dzɔla siwo le tsitre ƒo xlãe la be: “Mite yi, ne miawu Yehowa ƒe nunɔlawo, elabena wowɔ ɖeka kple David! Wonya be esi dzo, ke womefi tofi nam o!”
ENGLISH: 17 And the king said to the runners who stood by “Turn to and put the priests of Jehovah to death, because they too have been backing David, and because they knew he was in flight and did not give me notice”; but the king’s officers would not put out their hands to cut down”; the priests of Jehovah.

EWE: Ke fia la ƒe subɔviwo medi be yewoado asi ɖa ada nu Yehowa ƒe nunɔlawo o. 18 Eye fia la gblɔ na Doeg be: “Trɔ nàda nu nunɔlawo!” Enumake Doeg, Edomtɔ la trɔ heda nu nunɔlawo. Ewu ŋutsu blaenyi vɔ atɔ̃, siwo do aklalakɔmewu gbe ma gbe.
ENGLISH: 18 And the king said to Doeg “Turn to, yourself, and cut the priests down”; and Doeg the Edomite turned to and cut the priests down himself, and put to death that day eighty-five men who carried linen ephods;

EWE: 19 Etsɔ yi ɖasi Nob, si nye nunɔlawo ƒe du la gɔ̃ hã: etsɔ yi wu ŋutsuwo kple nyɔnuwo, ɖeviwo kple vi nonowo, nyiwo kple tedziwo kpakple alẽwo siaa.
ENGLISH: 19 and in Nob, the priests’ city, he massacred everybody without quarter, man and woman, child at play and baby at the breast, ox and donkey and sheep, without quarter.

EWE: 20 Ke Ahimelek, Ahitub vi, ƒe vi ɖeka, si ŋkɔe nye Abiatar ya si ɖadze David yome.
ENGLISH: 20 And one son of Ahimelec the son of Ahitub, named Abiathar, escaped, and fled away to follow David.

EWE: 21 Abiatar gblɔ na David be: “Saul wu Yehowa ƒe nunɔlawo.”
ENGLISH: 21 And Abiathar told David that Saul had killed the priests of Jehovah;

EWE: 22 Eye David gblɔ na Abiatar be: “Menyae gbe ma gbe be esi Doeg, Edomtɔ la nɔ afi ma ta la, eyina egblɔ ge na Saul godoo.
ENGLISH: 22 and David said to Abiathar “I knew that day that Doeg the Edomite was there, that he would be telling Saul; I have turned to to kill every soul of your family.

EWE: Nyee ɖi fɔ le ame siwo katã wowu le fofowò ƒe me la ta. 23 Wò ya nɔ gbɔnye. Mègavɔ̃ o, elabena ame si le wò agbe dim la le nye hã nye agbe dim, eya ta makpɔ tawò.”
ENGLISH: 23 Stay with me, do not be afraid, because the one who is hunting for your life is the one who is hunting for mine; for you are in safe-keeping with me.”

EWE: 1 Samuel
ENGLISH: 1 Samuel

EWE: 23 Emegbe wova gblɔ na David be: “Kpɔ ɖa, Filistitɔwo le aʋa wɔm kple Keila, eye wole nuku siwo le nukuƒoƒeawo ham.”
ENGLISH: 23 And they told David “Here are the Philistines making war on Keilah, pillaging the threshing-floors.”

EWE: 2 Eye David bia gbe Yehowa be: “Mayi aɖasi Filistitɔ siawoa?”
ENGLISH: 2 And David put the question to Jehovah “Shall I go and strike these Philistines?” and Jehovah said to David “Go and strike the Philistines and save Keilah.”

EWE: Yehowa ɖo eŋu na David be: “Yi ɖasi Filistitɔwo, eye nàxɔ na Keila.” 3 Ke David ƒe amewo gblɔ nɛ be: “Kpɔ ɖa!
ENGLISH: 3 And David’s men said to him “We are in fear right here in Judah how much worse it will be when we go to Keilah against the Philistine line of battle!”

EWE: Míele vɔvɔ̃m le Yuda afi sia tso, ne wòahanye keke Keila kee míayi aɖaho aʋa ɖe Filistitɔwo ƒe aʋalɔgowo ŋua?” 4 Eye David gabia gbe Yehowa ake.
ENGLISH: 4 And again David put the question to Jehovah, and Jehovah answered him “Go right down to Keilah, for I am giving the Philistines into your hands.”

EWE: 5 Eya ta David kple eƒe amewo yi Keila, eye wòwɔ aʋa kple Filistitɔwo; ekplɔ woƒe lãhawo dzoe, eye wòwu wo dometɔ gbogbo aɖewo, eye David xɔ na Keilatɔwo.
ENGLISH: 5 And David and his men went to Keilah and made war on the Philistines and drove their cattle, and killed a great number of them; and David saved the inhabitants of Keilah.

EWE: 6 Esi Abiatar, Ahimelek vi si yina David gbɔ le Keila la, etsɔ kɔmewu ɖe asi yii.
ENGLISH: 6 And when Abiathar the son of Ahimelec had fled to David to Keilah, an ephod had come down in his hand;

EWE: 7 Emegbe wova gblɔ na Saul be: “David va Keila.” Eye Saul gblɔ be: “Mawu tsɔe de asi nam, elabena eva tu eɖokui ɖe du si nu agbo kple gameti le la me.”
ENGLISH: 7 and Saul was told that David had gone into Keilah, and Saul said “God has put him into my hands, since he has shut himself in, going into a city with gates and bars,”

EWE: 8 Ale Saul yɔ eƒe amewo katã ƒo ƒu be woaho aʋa ɖe Keila ŋu ahaɖe to ɖe David kple eƒe amewo.
ENGLISH: 8 and Saul summoned all the people to war, to go down to Keilah to besiege David and his men;

EWE: 9 Esi David se be Saul le vɔ̃ ɖom ɖe ye ŋu la, egblɔ na nunɔla Abiatar be: “Tsɔ kɔmewu la va afii.”
ENGLISH: 9 and David learned that it was against him Saul was brewing mischief, and said to Priest Abiathar “Bring the ephod.”

EWE: 10 Eye David gblɔ be: “Oo Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu, wò subɔvi se be Saul le didim be yeava Keila ahatsrɔ̃ du la le tanye.
ENGLISH: 10 And David said “Jehovah, God of Israel, your servant hears that Saul is trying to come to Keilah to destroy the city on my account.

EWE: 11 Ðe Keilatɔwo ƒe kplɔlawo atsɔm ade asi nɛa?
ENGLISH: 11 Will the burghers of Keilah give me up to him? will Saul come down as your servant has heard?

EWE: Ðe Saul ava, abe ale si wò subɔvi see enea?
ENGLISH: Jehovah, God of Israel, tell your servant.”

EWE: 12 David gabia be: “Ðe Keilatɔwo atsɔ nye ŋutɔ kple nye amewo ade Saul sia?”
ENGLISH: 12 And Jehovah said “He will.”

EWE: Yehowa ɖo eŋu be: “Woatsɔ mi ade esi.”
ENGLISH: And David said “Will the burghers of Keilah give me and my men up to Saul?” and Jehovah said “They will.”

EWE: 13 Enumake David kple eƒe ame siwo anɔ ŋutsu alafa ade la dzo le Keila henɔ yiyim ko, womenya afi si tututu yim wole o.
ENGLISH: 13 And David and his men, about six hundred strong, left Keilah and went where they happened to; and Saul was told that David had escaped from Keilah, and he gave up going out.

EWE: Esi wova gblɔ na Saul be David si dzo le Keila la, megaxa ho o. 14 David nɔ gbea dzi le teƒe siwo yiyi sesẽ, eye wònɔ tonuto la me le Zif gbedzi. Eye Saul dii ɣeawokatãɣi, gake Yehowa metsɔe de asi nɛ o.
ENGLISH: 14 And David lived in the wilderness, in the fastnesses.And he lived in the highland, in the wilderness of Ziph; and Saul was looking for him all the time, but God did not give him into his hands;

EWE: 15 Eye David nya be Saul le tsatsam le ye dim be yeawu esime David nɔ Hores le Zif gbedzi.
ENGLISH: 15 and David was afraid because Saul had come out to hunt for his life. And David was in the wilderness of Ziph at Horeshah,

EWE: 16 Yonatan, Saul vi yi David gbɔ le Hores be yeado ŋusẽe be wòaɖo ŋu ɖe Yehowa ŋu.
ENGLISH: 16 and Jonathan the son of Saul went off to Horeshah to David and encouraged him in the name of God,

EWE: 17 Eye wògblɔ nɛ be: “Mègavɔ̃ o, elabena fofonye Saul ƒe asi matu wò o, eye wò la, àzu fia ɖe Israel dzi, ke nye la manye evelia anɔ ŋuwò; fofonye Saul hã nyae alea.”
ENGLISH: 17 and said to him “Do not be afraid, Saul my father will not get his hands on you; you will reign over Israel and I shall be second to you; Saul my father knows himself it is so.”

EWE: 18 Eye wo ame evea wobla nu le Yehowa ŋkume, eye David tsi Hores, ke Yonatan ya dzo yi aƒe me.
ENGLISH: 18 And the two of them pledged themselves to each other before Jehovah; and David remained at Horeshah, and Jonathan went home.

EWE: 19 Emegbe Zif ŋutsuwo yi Saul gbɔ le Gibea ɖagblɔ nɛ be: “David va be ɖe mía gbɔ le teƒe siwo yiyi sesẽ le Hores, le Hakila togbɛ la dzi, le Yesimon ƒe anyiehe.
ENGLISH: 19 And the Ziphites came up to Saul at Gibeah, saying “David is keeping himself concealed in our country in the fastnesses at Horeshah, on the sides of Hakilah Hill south of the Jeshimon;

EWE: 20 Eya ta Oo fia, ɣesiaɣi si nèdi be yeava la, va, eye míatsɔe ade asi na fia la.”
ENGLISH: 20 so now at your pleasure to come down, your majesty, come down, and it shall be our part to put him into your majesty’s hands.”

EWE: 21 Eye Saul gblɔ be: “Yehowa neyra mi, elabena mienyo dɔme nam.
ENGLISH: 21 And Saul said “Jehovah bless you that you had mercy on me!

EWE: 22 Meɖe kuku, migayi ɖadii tsitotsito, ne miakpɔ teƒe si tututu wòle kple ame si kpɔe le afi ma, elabena wogblɔ nam be edze aye ŋutɔ.
ENGLISH: 22 Go get more preparations made, and look and make sure of the place for him, where his feet will be hampered for they tell me he does play the slyest tricks

EWE: 23 Eye midze agbagba mianya afi siwo katã wòbena ɖo, eye miatrɔ ava gbɔnye ava ɖo kpe edzi nam. Mayi kpli mi; eye ne ele anyigba la dzi la, ekema nye hã madii tsitotsito le Yuda ƒe ame akpeakpewo katã dome.”
ENGLISH: 23 look and make sure of any of the lurking-places where he hides, and come back to me at Nacon, and I will go with you: if he is in the country, I will hunt him out among all the thousands of Judah.”

EWE: 24 Ale wotso dze Saul ŋgɔ yi Zif, esime David kple eƒe amewo le Maon gbedzi le Araba, le Yesimon ƒe anyiehe.
ENGLISH: 24 And they came away and went to Ziph before Saul; and David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, in the Rift Valley, south of the Jeshimon.

EWE: 25 Emegbe Saul kple eŋumewo va edi ge. Esi wogblɔe na David la, enumake eɖi yi agakpe la gbɔ henɔ Maon gbedzi.
ENGLISH: 25 And Saul and his men went to look for him; and they told David, and he went down to the cliffs and lived in the wilderness of Maon.

EWE: Esi Saul see la, eti David yome yi Maon gbedzi. 26 Esi Saul va to la ƒe akpa ɖeka la, David kple eƒe amewo hã le to la ƒe akpa kemɛ.
ENGLISH: 26 And Saul heard of it, and pursued David into the wilderness of Maon; and Saul went on this side of a mountain and David and his men on that side.

EWE: Eya ta David wɔ kaba be yeasi le Saul nu, le ɣeyiɣi sia me la, Saul kple eƒe amewo ɖe to ɖe David kple eƒe amewo be yewoalé wo.
ENGLISH: And as David was going in headlong haste to get away from Saul, and Saul and his men were hemming David and his men in to capture them,

EWE: 27 Kasia dɔla aɖe va Saul gbɔ va gblɔ be: “Va kaba, elabena Filistitɔwo va ƒo ɖe anyigba la dzi!”
ENGLISH: 27 a messenger came to Saul to say “Come quick, because the Philistines have raided the country”;

EWE: 28 Enumake Saul gbugbɔ le David yome, eye wòyi ɖakpe aʋa kple Filistitɔwo.
ENGLISH: 28 and Saul turned back from pursuing David, and went to face the Philistines.

EWE: Esia tae woyɔ teƒe ma be Kaklãgakpe.
ENGLISH: Because of this they call that place Division Cliff.

EWE: 29 Eye David dze mɔ tso afi ma yi ɖanɔ teƒe siwo yiyi sesẽ le En-Gedi.
ENGLISH: 29 And David went up from there and lived in the fastnesses of ʽEn-Gedi.

EWE: 1 Samuel
ENGLISH: 1 Samuel

EWE: 24 Esi Saul nya gbɔ tso Filistitɔwo yometiƒe ko la, wova gblɔ nɛ be: “Kpɔ ɖa! David le En-Gedi gbedzi.”
ENGLISH: 24 And when Saul came back from pursuing the Philistines they told him “David is in the wilderness of ʽEn-Gedi.”

EWE: 2 Eya ta Saul ɖe ŋutsu tiatia akpe etɔ̃ le Israel blibo la dome heyi be yeadi David kple eƒe amewo le agamegbɔ̃gakpewo dzi.
ENGLISH: 2 And Saul took three thousand picked men out of all Israel and went to look for David and his men along the Ibex Rocks,

EWE: 3 Saul va ɖo alẽkpo siwo wotsɔ kpe wɔ la gbɔ le mɔ to, afi si agado aɖe le, eye wòyi ɖe eme be yeade afɔdzi, sigbeɖe David kple eƒe amewo bɔbɔ nɔ agado la ƒe mlɔenu.
ENGLISH: 3 and came to the sheepfolds by the roadside. There there was a cave, and Saul went in to ease himself; and David and his men were at the back of the cave sitting down.

EWE: 4 David ƒe amewo gblɔ nɛ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, esiae nye ŋkeke si dzi Yehowa le gbɔgblɔm na wò be: ‘Metsɔ wò futɔ la de asi na wò, be nàwɔ nu sia nu si dze ŋuwò la ɖe eŋu.’”
ENGLISH: 4 And David’s men said to him “Here is the day of which Jehovah said to you ‘I am giving your enemy into your hands, and you shall do with him as you think best.’”

EWE: Eye David wɔ dzaa yi ɖalã Saul ƒe awu ʋlaya si ŋu abɔ mele o la toga.
ENGLISH: And David rose and cut off the flap of Saul’s robe quietly;

EWE: 5 Ke emegbe la, David ƒe dzi lã kpo, le esi wòlã Saul ƒe awu ʋlaya la toga ta.
ENGLISH: 5 but after that David’s conscience pricked him for having cut off the flap of Saul’s robe,

EWE: 6 Eya ta egblɔ na eƒe amewo be: “Mesɔ le Yehowa ŋkume be mawɔ nu sia ɖe nye aƒetɔ, si nye Yehowa ƒe amesiamina la ŋu ahado nye asi ɖe egbɔ o, elabena Yehowa ƒe amesiaminae wònye.”
ENGLISH: 6 and he said to his men “Jehovah forbid the thought of my doing such a thing to my sovereign, Jehovah’s anointed, as to lay hands on him, because he is Jehovah’s anointed.”

EWE: 7 Eya ta David ƒe nya siawo na eƒe amewo dze akɔ anyi, eye meɖe mɔ na wo be woawu Saul o.
ENGLISH: 7 And David reprimanded his men and would not let them rise to attack Saul; and Saul rose and left the cave and went along the road.

EWE: Eye Saul do le agado la me helé eƒe mɔ. 8 Emegbe David tso hedo le agado la me, eye wòdo ɣli yɔ Saul gblɔ be: “Nye aƒetɔ fia!” Esi Saul nyè kɔ kpɔ megbe la, David bɔbɔ tsyɔ mo anyi hede ta agu.
ENGLISH: 8 And after that David rose and went out of the cave and called after Saul “Your majesty!” and Saul looked back, and David bowed his face to the ground and did reverence.

EWE: 9 Eye David bia Saul be: “Nu ka tae nèle amewo ƒe gbe sem be: ‘Kpɔ ɖa, David le wò vɔ̃ dim’?
ENGLISH: 9 And David said to Saul “Why do you listen to men’s words ‘David is looking for a chance to injure you’?

EWE: 10 Kpɔ ɖa, wò ŋkuwo kpɔ ale si Yehowa tsɔ wò de asi nam egbe sia le agadoa me hafi. Ke esi ame aɖe gblɔ nam be mawu wò la, mekpɔ nublanui na wò, eye megblɔ be: ‘Nyemado asi ɖe nye aƒetɔ gbɔ o, elabena Yehowa ƒe amesiamina wònye.’
ENGLISH: 10 This day you have seen with your own eyes how Jehovah gave you into my hands today in the cave, and I refused to kill you, but spared you and said ‘I will not lay hands on my sovereign, because he is Jehovah’s anointed and my father.’

EWE: 11 Fofonye, kpɔ wò awu ʋlaya toga si le asinye me la ɖa, elabena esime melã wò awu ʋlaya toga la, mate ŋu awu wò hafi. Azɔ dze sii, eye nàkpɔe be nyemeɖo be mawɔ nu vevi aɖeke wò alo adze aglã o, eye nyemewɔ nu vɔ̃ aɖeke ɖe ŋuwò hã o, evɔ wò ya èle yonyeme tim vevie be yeaɖe nye agbe ɖa.
ENGLISH: 11 Yes, see the flap of your robe in my hands! for by my cutting off the flap of your robe and not killing you you may see for yourself that I have no fault or offense upon my hands, and have not misconducted myself toward you; but you are trying to take my life.

EWE: 12 Yehowa nedrɔ̃e le nye kpli wò dome, eye Yehowa nabia hlɔ̃ wò nam, ke nye ŋutɔ nye asi ya made ŋuwò o.
ENGLISH: 12 Jehovah shall give judgment between us, and Jehovah shall avenge me on you; but my hands shall not be laid on you.

EWE: 13 Abe ale si blematɔwo ƒe lododo aɖe gblɔe ene la, ‘Nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ tsoa ame vɔ̃ɖiwo gbɔ,’ ke nye ŋutɔ nye asi made ŋuwò o.
ENGLISH: 13 As the proverb of the ancients says, knavery comes from knaves; but my hands shall not be laid on you.

EWE: 14 Ame ka gɔ̃ yome timee Israel-fia la le? Ame kae nènya ɖe nu? Avu kukua? Axɔ̃ ɖeka pɛa?
ENGLISH: 14 Whom has the king of Israel come out against? whom are you pursuing? a dead dog, a single flea.

EWE: 15 Yehowa nanye ʋɔnudrɔ̃la, ne wòadrɔ̃e le nye kpli wò dome; akpɔ eme, eye wòaʋli tanye, eye wòadrɔ̃ nye nya nam ahaɖem tso asiwò me.”
ENGLISH: 15 And Jehovah shall be arbiter, and give judgment between us, and uphold my rights and give me justice against you.”

EWE: 16 Eye esi David gblɔ nya siawo nɛ vɔ la, Saul gblɔ be: “Vinye David, wò gbee nye esia?” Eye Saul wó avi kple ɣli.
ENGLISH: 16 And when David finished saying these things to Saul, Saul said “Is that your voice, son David?” and Saul wept aloud,

EWE: 17 Eye wògblɔ na David be: “Tɔwò dzɔ wu tɔnye, elabena èwɔ nyui nam, ke nye ya mewɔ vɔ̃ ɖe ŋuwò.
ENGLISH: 17 and said to David “You are more honest than I, because you have done good to me and I harm to you;

EWE: 18 Èɖe nyui si nèwɔ nam la fia egbe, elabena esi Yehowa tsɔm de asi na wò la, mèwum o.
