ENGLISH: 18 and it is a great good deed you have done to me today, that Jehovah put me into your hands and you did not kill me.

EWE: 19 Ame kae ake ɖe eƒe futɔ ŋu, eye mawɔ nu vevii o? Yehowa atsɔ nyui aɖo eteƒe na wò, le nu si nèwɔ nam egbea ta.
ENGLISH: 19 When a man finds his enemy and lets him go unmolested Jehovah will repay you with good for this day, what you have done to me.

EWE: 20 Kpɔ ɖa, menyae be èle fia ɖu ge godoo, eye Israel ƒe fiaɖuƒe la ali ke ɖe asiwò me.
ENGLISH: 20 And now, I know you are to be king and the kingship over Israel is to stand permanently in your hands:

EWE: 21 Eya ta ka atam nam le Yehowa ŋkume be màtsrɔ̃ nye dzidzime si ava ɖe yonyeme la ɖa o, eye màtsrɔ̃ nye ŋkɔ ɖa gbidigbidi le fofonye ƒe me hã o.”
ENGLISH: 21 now swear to me by Jehovah that you will not cut off my descendants after me and that you will not root out my name out of my family”;

EWE: 22 Eye David ka atam na Saul; emegbe Saul dzo yi aƒe me.
ENGLISH: 22 and David swore to Saul.

EWE: Ke David kple eƒe amewo gatrɔ yi teƒe si yiyi sesẽ la.
ENGLISH: And Saul went home, and David and his men went up to the fastness.

EWE: 1 Samuel
ENGLISH: 1 Samuel

EWE: 25 Emegbe Samuel ku; eye Israel blibo la katã va ƒo ƒu hefae, eye woɖii ɖe eƒe me le Rama.
ENGLISH: 25 And Samuel died, and all Israel gathered and wailed for him and buried him at his home in Ramah.

EWE: Eyome David tso heyi Paran gbedzi.
ENGLISH: And David moved, going down to the wilderness of Paran.

EWE: 2 Ke ŋutsu aɖe nɔ Maon, eye eƒe dɔwɔƒe le Karmel. Ŋutsu sia nye kesinɔtɔ, alẽ akpe etɔ̃ kple gbɔ̃ akpe ɖeka le esi, eye wònɔ fu kom na eƒe alẽwo le Karmel ɣemaɣi.
ENGLISH: 2 And there was a man at Maon whose ranch was at Carmel: the man was very wealthy, had three thousand sheep and a thousand goats; and he was having a sheepshearing at Carmel.

EWE: 3 Ŋutsua ŋkɔe nye Nabal, eye srɔ̃a ŋkɔe nye Abigail. Nyɔnua sea nu gɔme, eye wòdze tugbe, ke ŋutsua ya nye ŋlɔmitɔ eye meɖɔ ʋu o; enye Kaleb ƒomea me tɔ.
ENGLISH: 3 The man’s name was Nabal, and his wife’s Abigail; the wife was beautiful and sensible, the husband harsh and ill-conditioned; he was a Calebite.

EWE: 4 David se le gbea dzi be Nabal le fu kom na eƒe alẽwo.
ENGLISH: 4 And David heard in the wilderness that Nabal was shearing his sheep;

EWE: 5 Ale David dɔ ɖekakpui ewo hegblɔ na wo be: “Miyi Karmel, ne mieyi Nabal gbɔ la miado gbe nɛ nam.
ENGLISH: 5 and David sent ten young men, and David said to the young men “Go up to Carmel, and when you come to Nabal’s ask him in my name how he does,

EWE: 6 Eye miagblɔ nɛ be: ‘Míedi lãmesẽ kple agbe didi na wò, eme nenyo na aƒewòmetɔwo, eye eme nenyo na nu siwo katã le asiwò.
ENGLISH: 6 and say ‘So may you live, yourself well and your family well and all that is yours well.

EWE: 7 Mese be èle fu kom na wò lãwo. Esime wò alẽkplɔlawo va nɔ mía gbɔ la, míewɔ nu vevi aɖeke wo o.
ENGLISH: 7 Now I have heard that you are having a shearing: now those shepherds of yours have been with us, and we did not bully them, and nothing of theirs was missing all the time they were at Carmel.

EWE: Eye woƒe naneke mebu le ŋkeke siwo katã wonɔ Karmel o. 8 Bia wò ŋutɔ wò ɖekakpuiawo se, ne woagblɔe na wò. Ve nye ɖekakpuiwo nu, elabena ŋkeke nyui dzie míeva.
ENGLISH: 8 Ask your men and have them tell you, that my men may have your goodwill, since we have come on a happy day; please give what you can to your servants, and to your son David.’”

EWE: 9 Eye David ƒe ɖekakpuiawo va gblɔ nya siawo katã na Nabal le David ƒe ŋkɔ me.
ENGLISH: 9 And David’s men came and said to Nabal in David’s name all these words, and rested.

EWE: Esi woƒo nu vɔ la, 10 Nabal gblɔ na David ƒe dɔlawo be: “Ame kae nye David, eye ame kae nye Isai vi la? Le egbeŋkeke siawo me la, subɔvi geɖewo le sisim le woƒe aƒetɔwo gbɔ.
ENGLISH: 10 And Nabal answered David’s followers “Who is David, and who is Jesse’s son? there are too many slaves today that are turning brigands by their masters’ fault.

EWE: 11 Ðe matsɔ nye abolo kple nye tsi kpakple nye lã si mewu na nye fukolawo la ana ame siwo ame aɖeke menya afi si wotso gɔ̃ hã oa?”
ENGLISH: 11 And am I to take my bread and my wine, and my meat that I have slaughtered for my shearers, and give them to men from I don’t know where?”

EWE: 12 Eye David ƒe ɖekakpuiawo trɔ dzo yi ɖagblɔ nya siawo katã nɛ.
ENGLISH: 12 And David’s men turned and went their way, and came back and told him all these words.

EWE: 13 Enumake David gblɔ na eƒe amewo be: “Mia dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe neta yi!” Ale wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe ta yi, eye David ŋutɔ hã ta yi, eye ŋutsu alafa ene dze David yome, ke wogblẽ ŋutsu alafa eve ɖe agbaawo gbɔ.
ENGLISH: 13 And David said to his men “Belt on your swords”; and they belted on their swords, and David too belted on his, and about four hundred men went up behind David, while two hundred stayed with the things.

EWE: 14 Ke Nabal ƒe subɔvi ɖeka va gblɔ na Nabal srɔ̃ Abigail be: “Kpɔ ɖa, David dɔ amewo tso gbea dzi be woava di nyui na míaƒe aƒetɔ, ke eda gbe ɖe wo gbɔ hedzu wo.
ENGLISH: 14 And one of Nabal’s men told Nabal’s wife Abigail “Here has David sent men out of the wilderness to congratulate master, and he jawed them.

EWE: 15 Evɔ ŋutsuawo wɔ nyui geɖe na mí. Womewɔ nu vevi mí o, eye naneke hã mebu na mí le ŋkeke siwo katã míenɔ gbea dzi kpli wo la o.
ENGLISH: 15 But the men were very good to us, and we were not bullied, and did not miss anything, all the time we were going with them while we were out on the range:

EWE: 16 Gli wonye nɔ mía ŋu zã kple keli le ŋkeke siwo katã míenɔ wo gbɔ nɔ lãhawo kplɔm.
ENGLISH: 16 they were a wall for us both night and day all the time we were with them tending the sheep.

EWE: 17 Eya ta bu nu si nàwɔ ŋu, elabena woɖo vɔ̃ ɖe míaƒe aƒetɔ kple eƒe aƒe blibo la katã ŋu, elabena yakamee míaƒe aƒetɔ nye, eye nuƒoƒo nɛ sesẽna.”
ENGLISH: 17 Now make up your mind what you will do; for master and all his family are in for trouble, and he is too much of a reprobate to speak to.”

EWE: 18 Eya ta Abigail wɔ kaba tsɔ abolo alafa eve, wain ze gã eve, alẽ atɔ̃ siwo wowu la ƒe lã, nuku tɔtɔe seya atɔ̃, waintsetse ƒuƒu bolo alafa ɖeka kple gbotsetsebolo alafa eve, eye wòtsɔ wo katã do agbae na tedziwo.
ENGLISH: 18 And in haste Abigail took two hundred cakes of bread and two skins of wine and five cooked sheep and seven pecks of roasted grain and a hundred clusters of raisins and a hundred cakes of figs, and put them on donkeys

EWE: 19 Eye wògblɔ na eƒe dɔlawo be: “Midze ŋgɔnye; mele mia yome.” Gake megblɔ nya aɖeke na srɔ̃a Nabal o.
ENGLISH: 19 and said to her men “Go over ahead of me: I will be coming after you”; but she did not tell her husband Nabal.

EWE: 20 Esi wòdo tedzi la ɖi abu ɖo toa xa yina la, kasia David kple eƒe amewoe nye ema gbɔna, eye wòyi ɖado go wo.
ENGLISH: 20 And as she was riding on her donkey and going down screened by the mountainside, she found David and his men coming down to meet her;

EWE: 21 Ke David gblɔ be: “Dzodzroe medzɔ ame sia ƒe nuwo katã ŋu le gbea dzi. Eƒe nuwo katã dometɔ ɖeka pɛ hã mebu o, evɔ wòtsɔ vɔ̃ ɖo nyui teƒe nam.
ENGLISH: 21 and she met with them while David was thinking “It is all for nothing I have guarded in the wilderness everything that belonged to this man, and of all that belonged to him nothing was missing: he has repaid me bad for good.

EWE: 22 Eya ta Mawu nefia David ƒe futɔwo, eye wòagafia wo ɖe edzi, ne eƒe ŋutsuwo dometɔ aɖe atsi agbe hafi ŋu nake fĩ!”
ENGLISH: 22 God do so to David’s enemies, and more, if by morning I leave of all that belongs to him any male person.”

EWE: 23 Esi Abigail nya kpɔ David ko la, ewɔ kaba ɖi le tedzi la dzi, eye wòtsyɔ mo anyi ɖe David ŋkume hebɔbɔ de ta agu.
ENGLISH: 23 And Abigail saw David and dismounted from her donkey in haste, and threw herself down on her face before David and did reverence on the ground,

EWE: 24 Eye wòbɔbɔ ɖe eƒe afɔnu gblɔ be: “Nye aƒetɔ, vodada la nanɔ dzinye; meɖe kuku, na wò dɔlanyɔnu naƒo nu, eye se wò dɔlanyɔnu la ƒe nyawo.
ENGLISH: 24 and threw herself on his feet and said “On me be the offense, sir; but let your servant speak in your hearing, and listen to your servant’s words.

EWE: 25 Nye aƒetɔ, meɖe kuku, mègatsɔ Nabal yakame sia ƒe nya de tame o, elabena eya kple eƒe ŋkɔe sɔ. Eŋkɔe nye Nabal, eye movidzɔdzɔ tso aƒe ɖe egbɔ.
ENGLISH: 25 You must not mind that reprobate Nabal, sir, because he is just like his name: Nabal means curmudgeon, and curmudgeonliness is his nature; but I your servant did not see the young men you sent, sir.

EWE: Ke wò dɔlanyɔnu mekpɔ nye aƒetɔ ƒe ɖekakpui siwo nèdɔ ɖa la o. 26 Eya ta nye aƒetɔ, zi ale si Yehowa le agbe, eye wò hã nèle agbe la, Yehowae xe mɔ na wò be nàgaɖi ʋufɔ, atsɔ wò ŋutɔ wò asi abia hlɔ̃e o.
ENGLISH: 26 And now, sir, by Jehovah and by your life, Jehovah has restrained you from getting into bloodguilt and from letting your own hands relieve you: now may your enemies, and those who wish my lord ill, be as Nabal is.

EWE: Eya ta wò futɔwo kple ame siwo le nye aƒetɔ ƒe gbegblẽ dim la nazu abe Nabal ene. 27 Ke azɔ xɔ nunana sia si wò dɔlanyɔnu tsɔ vɛ na nye aƒetɔ la na ɖekakpui siwo le nye aƒetɔ yome.
ENGLISH: 27 Now, then, let this token of goodwill that your servant has brought to my lord be given to the young men who accompany my lord in his movements.

EWE: 28 Tsɔ wò dɔlanyɔnu ƒe dzidada kee dzro, elabena Yehowa atso aƒe si anɔ anyi ɖaa la na nye aƒetɔ, elabena Yehowa ƒe aʋawo wɔmee nye aƒetɔ le, eye womekpɔ nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ le mewò le wò agbemeŋkekewo katã me o.
ENGLISH: 28 Pardon your servant’s crime; for Jehovah will make my lord a secure house, because my lord is fighting Jehovah’s battles and there is nothing bad in your record as long as you have lived.

EWE: 29 Ne ame aɖe tso be yeati yowòme, aɖe wò agbe ɖa la, ekema woabla nye aƒetɔ ƒe agbe ɖe agbekplo me wòanɔ dedie le Yehowa wò Mawu gbɔ, ke ada wò futɔwo ƒe agbe abe akafo mee wòdee da ene.
ENGLISH: 29 And men have stood up against you to persecute you and hunt for your life, but my lord’s life shall be wrapped up in the bundle of the living in the keeping of your God Jehovah, and your enemies’ lives he shall sling out in the cup of a sling.

EWE: 30 Ne Yehowa wɔ nu nyui siwo katã ƒe ŋugbe wòdo na nye aƒetɔ eye wòɖo wò kplɔlae ɖe Israel nu la,
ENGLISH: 30 And when Jehovah does for my lord just as he has promised you good, and appoints you warden over Israel,

EWE: 31 mave wò alo aɖu dzi na wò be yekɔ ʋu ɖi dzodzro, alo yetsɔ ye ŋutɔ yeƒe asi bia hlɔ̃e o. Eya ta ne Yehowa na eme nyo na nye aƒetɔ la, nàɖo ŋku wò dɔlanyɔnu la dzi.”
ENGLISH: 31 my lord will not have this as a matter for misgiving and unrest, to have shed blood without cause and to have let my lord’s own hands relieve him; and Jehovah will do you good, and you will remember your servant.”

EWE: 32 Eye David gblɔ na Abigail be: “Woakafu Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu la, ame si dɔ wò egbea be nàva do gom!
ENGLISH: 32 And David said to Abigail “Blessed be Jehovah the God of Israel, who sent you to meet me today;

EWE: 33 Woakafu wò aɖaŋudzedze, eye woakafu wò, ame si xe mɔ nam egbe sia be nyemeɖi ʋufɔ alo tsɔ nye ŋutɔ nye asi bia hlɔ̃e o.
ENGLISH: 33 and blessed be your good sense, and blessed you, who have checked me this day from getting into bloodguilt and from letting my own hands relieve me.

EWE: 34 Ke zi ale si Yehowa, Israel ƒe Mawu, ame si xe mɔ nam be magawɔ nu vevi wò o la le agbe la, ne menye ɖe nèwɔ kaba va do gom o la, anye ne ŋutsu aɖeke magasusɔ na Nabal hafi ŋu nake o.”
ENGLISH: 34 But, by Jehovah the God of Israel, who has restrained me from doing you harm, if you had not been quick about coming to meet me, by morning not a male person of Nabal’s would have been left.”

EWE: 35 Eye David xɔ nu siwo wòtsɔ vɛ la hegblɔ nɛ be: “Heyi aƒe le ŋutifafa me. Kpɔ ɖa, mese wò gbe, eye mawɔ nu si nèdi la na wò.”
ENGLISH: 35 And David took from her hands what she had brought him; and to her he said “Go up to your home, it will be all right: see, I have obeyed you and favored you.”

EWE: 36 Emegbe Abigail va Nabal gbɔ, ke Nabal ɖo nuɖukplɔ̃ gã aɖe nɔ dzidzɔ kpɔm le eƒe me abe fia ene, eye Nabal ƒe dzi le dzidzɔ kpɔm, eye wòmu aha vlevlevle.
ENGLISH: 36 And Abigail came home to Nabal and found him having in his house a wassail like the king’s; and Nabal was jolly and very drunk; and she did not tell him a thing, great or small, till the morning light.

EWE: Ke Abigail megblɔ nya aɖeke nɛ o va se ɖe esime ŋu ke. 37 Esi ŋu ke, eye wain la kɔ le mo na Nabal la, srɔ̃a gblɔ nya siawo nɛ.
ENGLISH: 37 But in the morning, when the wine had gone out of Nabal, his wife told him these things; and his heart died in him, and he turned to a stone.

EWE: 38 Anɔ abe ŋkeke ewo ene emegbe la, Yehowa ƒo Nabal eye wòku.
ENGLISH: 38 And in about ten days Jehovah smote Nabal, and he died;

EWE: 39 Esi David se be Nabal ku la, egblɔ be: “Woakafu Yehowa, ame si drɔ̃ nye nya nam heɖe nye vlodoame ɖa eye wòɖem tso Nabal si me, eye mena eƒe subɔla wɔ vɔ̃ o, ale be Yehowa trɔ Nabal ƒe nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ la va eya ŋutɔ ƒe ta dzi!”
ENGLISH: 39 and David heard that Nabal was dead, and he said “Blessed be Jehovah, who has upheld my rights against Nabal in the matter of the insult I suffered, and who held back his servant from mischief and sent Nabal’s mischief back on his own head.”

EWE: Eye David dɔ ame ɖa be woaɖaƒo nu kple Abigail na ye, ne yeaɖee.
ENGLISH: And David sent a proposal of marriage to Abigail;

EWE: 40 Eye David ƒe dɔlawo va Abigail gbɔ le Karmel heƒo nu kplii be: “David dɔ mí ɖe gbɔwò be yeaɖe wò nàzu ye srɔ̃.”
ENGLISH: 40 and David’s servants came to Abigail at Carmel and addressed her, saying “David sent us to you to get you for his wife.”

EWE: 41 Etso enumake, eye wòbɔbɔ hetsyɔ mo anyi gblɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, eƒe kosie menye; melɔ̃ be manye dɔlanyɔnu aklɔ afɔ na nye aƒetɔ ƒe subɔviwo.”
ENGLISH: 41 And she stood up and did reverence with her face to the ground, and said “Your servant is a waiting-maid to wash the feet of my lord’s servants”;

EWE: 42 Eye Abigail wɔ kaba de eƒe tedzi dzi, eye eƒe dɔlanyɔnu atɔ̃ le eyome; eye wòkplɔ David ƒe dɔlawo ɖo yi, eye wòzu srɔ̃a.
ENGLISH: 42 and Abigail set out at once, riding on her donkey, with her five maids going behind her, and followed David’s messengers and became his wife.

EWE: 43 Do ŋgɔ la, David ɖe Ahinoam si tso Yezreel, eye nyɔnu eveawo siaa va zu srɔ̃awo.
ENGLISH: 43 David took Ahinoʽam of Jezreʽel too; and they both became his wives.

EWE: 44 Ke Saul tsɔ vianyɔnu Mikal, si nye David srɔ̃ la, na Palti, Lais vi, ame si tso Galim.
ENGLISH: 44 But Saul had given his daughter Mical, David’s wife, to Palti the son of Layish, of Gallim.

EWE: 1 Samuel
ENGLISH: 1 Samuel

EWE: 26 Emegbe Zif ŋutsuwo va Saul gbɔ le Gibea gblɔ be: “David be ɖe Hakila togbɛ si dze ŋgɔ Yesimon la dzi.” 2 Eye Saul tso hedze mɔ yi Zif gbedzi, eye Israel ŋutsu tiatia akpe etɔ̃ kpe ɖe eŋu, ne woadi David le Zif gbedzi.
ENGLISH: 26 And the Ziphites came to Saul at Gibeah, saying “David is keeping himself concealed on the sides of Hakilah Hill, in front of the Jeshimon; 2 and down went Saul to the wilderness of Ziph, and three thousand men with him, the picked men of Israel, to look for David in the wilderness of Ziph;

EWE: 3 Saul va ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Hakila togbɛ si dze ŋgɔ Yesimon la dzi, le mɔ to. Ɣemaɣi la, David le gbea dzi, eye wòse be Saul ti ye yome va gbea dzi.
ENGLISH: 3 and Saul camped on the side of Hakilah Hill, in front of the Jeshimon, by the roadside; and David was living in the wilderness, and saw that Saul had come to the wilderness after him.

EWE: 4 Eya ta David dɔ ŋkutsalawo ɖa, ne woakpɔ ɖa be Saul va nyateƒe hã.
ENGLISH: 4 And David sent out scouts and learned that Saul had come to Nacon;

EWE: 5 Emegbe David tso yi afi si Saul ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖo, eye David kpɔ afi si Saul mlɔ, kple afi si Abner, Ner vi si nye eƒe aʋafia la hã mlɔ; Saul mlɔ anyi ɖe asaɖa la me, eye ameawo ƒo xlãe godoo.
ENGLISH: 5 and David went off and came to the place where Saul was camped. And David saw the place where Saul and his general Abner the son of Ner were lying: Saul was lying in the cart-stand, and the people were camped around him.

EWE: 6 Eye David bia Ahimelek, Hititɔ kple Abisai, Zeruya vi Yoab nɔvi be: “Ame kae ayi Saul gbɔ le asaɖa la me kplim?” Abisai ɖo eŋu be: “Mayi kpli wò.”
ENGLISH: 6 And David spoke up and said to Ahimelec the Hittite and Serujah’s son Abishai, Joab’s brother, “Who will go down with me to Saul in the camp?” and Abishai said “I will go down with you.”

EWE: 7 Eye David yi ameawo gbɔ le zã me, eye Abisai kpe ɖe eŋu; eye kpɔ ɖa, Saul mlɔ anyi dɔ alɔ̃ le asaɖa la me hetsɔ eƒe akplɔ tu anyi le eƒe tade; Abner kple aʋawɔlaawo mlɔ anyi ƒo xlãe.
ENGLISH: 7 And David and Abishai came to the people in the night, and found Saul lying asleep in the cart-stand with his spear sticking in the ground at his head, and Abner and the people lying around him.

EWE: 8 Eye Abisai gblɔ na David be: “Mawu tsɔ wò futɔ de asi na wò egbea. Eya ta meɖe kuku, na matsɔ akplɔ la amimii ɖe anyigba zi ɖeka pɛ ko, nyemadae zi eve o.”
ENGLISH: 8 And Abishai said to David “God has put your enemy into your hands today; now let me pin him to the ground with his own spear at one stroke, and not give him a second.”

EWE: 9 Ke David gblɔ na Abisai be: “Mègawui o, elabena ame kae aka asi Yehowa ƒe amesiamina ŋu, eye maɖi fɔ o?”
ENGLISH: 9 But David said to Abishai “Do him no violence; for who can lay hands on Jehovah’s anointed and go unpunished?”

EWE: 10 Eye David gagblɔ be: “Zi ale si Yehowa le agbe la, Yehowa ŋutɔ awui, alo eƒe ŋkeke ade wòaku loo alo ayi aʋa woawui.
ENGLISH: 10 And David said “By Jehovah, but Jehovah shall smite him, or his day shall come and he shall die, or he shall go down to a battle and meet his end.

EWE: 11 Nede megbe xaa tso gbɔnye le Yehowa ŋkume be mado nye asi ɖe Yehowa ƒe amesiamina la gbɔ!
ENGLISH: 11 Jehovah forbid the thought of my laying hands on Jehovah’s anointed; now take the spear at his head and the jug of water and let us get away.”

EWE: Eya ta meɖe kuku, tsɔ akplɔ si le eƒe tade kple tsizea, ne míadzo.” 12 Eya ta David tsɔ akplɔ kple tsize la le Saul ƒe tade, eye wodzo. Ame aɖeke mekpɔ wo alo nya, alo nyɔ hã o, elabena wo katã wodɔ alɔ̃ klenee, elabena Yehowa na wodɔ alɔ̃ yi eme ʋĩi.
ENGLISH: 12 And David took the spear and the jug of water at Saul’s head, and they made their way out, without anybody’s seeing them or knowing of it or waking up, because a trance from Jehovah had fallen on them.

EWE: 13 Eye David yi go kemɛ dzi ɖatɔ ɖe to la tame le adzɔge, eye wo kpli wo dome didi.
ENGLISH: 13 And David went over to the other side, and stood a long way off on the top of the mountain, with a great distance between;

EWE: 14 Eyome David yɔ aʋawɔlaawo kple Abner, Ner vi gblɔ be: “Abner, màtɔ oa?”
ENGLISH: 14 and David called out to the people and to Abner “Hallo there, Abner!” and Abner answered “Who are you, calling out to the king?”

EWE: Eye Abner bia be: “Wò ame kae nye ema le ɣli dom ɖe to me na fia la?” 15 Eye David gagblɔ na Abner be: “Menye ŋutsue nènye oa? Ame kae de nuwò le Israel? Ekema nu ka tae mèdzɔ wò aƒetɔ fia la ŋu o?
ENGLISH: 15 And David said to Abner “You are a man that is a man, are you, and nobody equal to you in Israel? and why did you not guard his majesty? because one of the people has been in to do violence to his majesty;

EWE: Elabena aʋawɔlawo dometɔ ɖeka va be, yeawu wò aƒetɔ fia la. 16 Mèwɔe nyuie o.
ENGLISH: 16 this is not a good record you have made.

EWE: Zi ale si Yehowa le agbe la, miedze na ku, elabena miedzɔ miaƒe aƒetɔ, si nye Yehowa ƒe amesiamina la ŋu o.
ENGLISH: By Jehovah, you are candidates for death for not having guarded your sovereign, Jehovah’s, anointed.

EWE: Azɔ kpɔe ɖa be, afi kae fia la ƒe akplɔ kple tsize si nɔ eƒe tade la le?”
ENGLISH: Now see where the king’s spear is, and the jug of water that was at his head.”

EWE: 17 Saul dze si David ƒe gbe, eye wòbia be: “Vinye David, wò gbee nye ema?” David ɖo eŋu be: “Nye aƒetɔ fia, nye gbee.”
ENGLISH: 17 And Saul recognized David’s voice, and said “Is that your voice, son David?” and David said “It is, your majesty.”

EWE: 18 Eye wògblɔ kpee be: “Nu ka tae nye aƒetɔ nya eƒe dɔla ɖe nu, nu kae mewɔ, eye nu vɔ̃ ka tututue mewɔ?
ENGLISH: 18 And he said “What is your majesty pursuing his servant for? what have I done, and what fault is there upon my hands?

EWE: 19 Azɔ meɖe kuku, nye aƒetɔ nese eƒe dɔla ƒe nyawo: Ne Yehowae dɔ wò ɖe ŋunye la, ekema nexɔ nye nuɖuvɔsa, ke ne amegbetɔwoe la, ekema aɖi wo ŋu le Yehowa ŋkume, elabena wonyam ɖa egbea tso Yehowa ƒe domenyinu la gbɔ, le gbɔgblɔm be, ‘Yi ɖasubɔ mawu bubuwo.’
ENGLISH: 19 Now, your majesty, listen to your servant’s words: if Jehovah has set you on against me, let him accept an offering; but if it is men, cursed be they before Jehovah, because they have banished me from being connected with Jehovah’s, estate, as much as to say ‘Go worship other gods.’

EWE: 20 Eya ta mègana woakɔ nye ʋu ɖe anyigba si le adzɔge tso Yehowa ŋkume la dzi o, elabena Israel-fia do go yi axɔ̃ ɖeka pɛ di ge, abe ale si wotia tegli yome le towo dzi ene.”
ENGLISH: 20 Now may my blood not fall from Jehovah’s presence to the earth; for the king of Israel has come out to seek my life as a hawk chases a partridge on the mountains.”

EWE: 21 Saul gblɔ nɛ be: “Mewɔ nu vɔ̃. Vinye David, trɔ va, elabena nyemagawɔ nu vevi wò azɔ o, le esi nye agbe xɔ asi le ŋkuwòme egbe sia ta.
ENGLISH: 21 And Saul said “I did wrong; come back, son David, for I will do you no more harm, seeing that you valued my life this day; I acted foolishly, I was very deluded indeed.”

EWE: Vavãe, mewɔ bometsinu, eye meda ƒu ŋutɔ.” 22 David gblɔ nɛ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, fia ƒe akplɔ lae nye esi.
ENGLISH: 22 And David answered “Here is the king’s spear for one of the men to come over and get;

EWE: Na ɖekakpuiawo dometɔ ɖeka nava xɔe. 23 Yehowae aɖo eteƒe na ame sia ame ɖe amea ŋutɔ ƒe dzɔdzɔenyenye kple nuteƒewɔwɔ nu, elabena Yehowa tsɔ wò de asi nam egbe sia, gake nyemedi be mado asi ɖe Yehowa ƒe amesiamina la gbɔ o.
ENGLISH: 23 and Jehovah will repay each man his honesty and loyalty, when Jehovah gave you into my hands today and I would not lay hands on Jehovah’s anointed.

EWE: 24 Kpɔ ɖa, ale si ko wò agbe xɔ asi le ŋkunyeme egbea la, nye hã nye agbe axɔ asi le Yehowa ŋkume nenema ke eye wòaɖem tso nye xaxawo katã me.”
ENGLISH: 24 And, as I thought much of your life this day, so may Jehovah think much of mine, and deliver me out of all distress.”

EWE: 25 Eye Saul gblɔ na David be: “Woayra wò, vinye David. Àwɔ nu gãwo, eye àkpɔ dzidzedze hã.”
ENGLISH: 25 And Saul said to David “Bless you, son David: do you shall and achieve you shall.”

EWE: Ale David lé eƒe mɔ, eye Saul hã gbugbɔ yi enɔƒe.
ENGLISH: And David went on his way, and Saul back to his place.

EWE: 1 Samuel
ENGLISH: 1 Samuel

EWE: 27 Ke David gblɔ le eƒe dzi me be: “Mele Saul ƒe asi me tsi ge gbe ɖeka. Nu nyuitɔ si mawɔe nye be masi ayi Filistitɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi; ekema Saul magadim le Israel-nyigba blibo la dzi azɔ o, eye mado le esi me.”
ENGLISH: 27 And David said to himself “Now I shall come to my end at Saul’s hands someday or other: there is nothing for it but to escape to the Philistine country and have Saul despair of getting me by looking for me any longer in all the territory of Israel, and so escape out of his hands”;

EWE: 2 Ale David kple ŋutsu alafa ade siwo le eŋu la dze mɔ yi Akis, Maok vi si nye Gat-fia la gbɔ.
ENGLISH: 2 and over went David, he and six hundred men who were with him, to Akish the son of Maʽoc, the king of Gath.

EWE: 3 Eye David nɔ Akis gbɔ le Gat, eya kple eƒe amewo, ame sia ame kple eƒemetɔwo. David kple srɔ̃a eveawo, siwo nye Ahinoam si tso Yezreel, kple Abigail, Karmel nyɔnu la, si nye Nabal ƒe ahosi.
ENGLISH: 3 And David lived at Gath with Akish, he and his men and their families, David with his two wives Ahinoʽam the Jezreʽelite and Abigail the widow of Nabal the Carmelite;

EWE: 4 Emegbe wova gblɔ na Saul be David si yi Gat, eya ta megadii azɔ o.
ENGLISH: 4 and Saul was told that David had fled away to Gath, and he no longer looked for him.

EWE: 5 Eye David gblɔ na Akis be: “Ne ève nunye la, ekema na woana teƒem ɖe anyigba la ƒe duviwo dometɔ ɖeka me, ne manɔ afi ma.
ENGLISH: 5 And David said to Akish “Please let them give me a place to live in in one of the cities on the wolds: why should your servant live at the capital with you?”

EWE: Nu ka tae wò subɔvi anɔ fiadua me kpli wò?” 6 Eya ta Akis tsɔ Ziklag nɛ gbe ma gbe.
ENGLISH: 6 And Akish that day gave him Siklag; so Siklag has belonged to the kings of Judah to this day.

EWE: 7 Ɣeyiɣi didi si David nɔ Filistitɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi la le ƒe ɖeka kple ɣleti ene.
ENGLISH: 7 And the length of time that David lived in the Philistine countryside was a year and four months.

EWE: 8 Eye David kple eƒe amewo yina ɖadzea Gesurtɔwo kple Girzitɔwo kpakple Amalektɔwo dzi, elabena wonɔ anyigba si tso Telam va ɖo Sur ɖado ɖe keke Egipte-nyigba dzi ke la dzi.
ENGLISH: 8 And David and his men went up and raided the Geshurites and the ʽAmalekites (for those were the primitive populations of the country as you come to Shur and down to Egypt);

EWE: 9 Ne David yi ɖadze duawo dzi la, megblẽa ŋutsu alo nyɔnu aɖeke ɖe agbe o, eye wòtsɔa alẽwo, nyiwo, tedziwo, kposɔwo kple nudodowo gbɔna vaa Akis gbɔ.
ENGLISH: 9 and David would devastate the country, and not leave alive man or woman, and take flocks and herds and donkeys and camels and clothing. And he came back and came to Akish,

EWE: 10 Eye Akis bianɛ be: “Afi ka mieyi ɖadze amewo dzi le egbea?” David ɖoa eŋu be: “Yuda ƒe anyiehe, alo Yerameltɔwo ƒe anyiehe alo Kenitɔwo ƒe anyiehe.”
ENGLISH: 10 and Akish said “Where did you raid today?” and David said “Against the Judahite South and the Jerahmeelite South and the Cainite South.”

EWE: 11 David menaa ŋutsu alo nyɔnu aɖeke tsia agbe, ne wòakplɔ ava Gat o, elabena egblɔ be: “Ne woagaƒo nu le mía ŋu agblɔ be: ‘Ale kple ale David wɔ’ o.”
ENGLISH: 11 And David would leave not a man or woman alive to bring to Gath, “for fear they should tell on us.”

EWE: (Aleae wòwɔ le ŋkeke siwo katã me wònɔ Filistitɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi.)
ENGLISH: So David did, and such was his custom, all the time he lived in the Philistine countryside.

EWE: 12 Eya ta Akis xɔ David dzi se, eye wògblɔ na eɖokui be: ‘Ele ʋeʋẽm ɖe eƒe dukɔ Israel, azu nye subɔvi ɖaa.’
ENGLISH: 12 And Akish had confidence in David, thinking “He has given mortal offense to his people Israel, and will be my subject always.”

EWE: 1 Samuel
ENGLISH: 1 Samuel

EWE: 28 Le ŋkeke mawo me la, Filistitɔwo ƒe aʋakɔ la va ƒu asaɖa anyi be yewoawɔ aʋa kple Israel.
ENGLISH: 28 And in those days the Philistines gathered their armies for a campaign, to attack Israel; and Akish said to David “Understand that you go out with me in the army, you and your men.”

EWE: Eya ta Akis gblɔ na David be: “Nyae be wò kple wò amewo miayi aʋa la kpli mí.” 2 David ɖo eŋu na Akis be: “Wò ŋutɔ ènya nu si wò subɔvi awɔ.”
ENGLISH: 2 And David said to Akish “So you shall know for yourself what your servant does”; and Akish said to David “So I will appoint you my permanent lifeguard.”

EWE: 3 Ɣemaɣi la, Samuel ku, eye Israel blibo la katã fae, eye woɖii ɖe Rama le eƒe du me.
ENGLISH: 3 And Samuel had died, and all Israel had wailed for him and buried him in his city Ramah.

EWE: Eye Saul ɖe ŋɔliyɔlawo kple nukalawo katã ɖa le anyigba la dzi.
ENGLISH: And Saul had expelled from the country all the spirit-mediums of different kinds.

EWE: 4 Filistitɔwo ƒo ƒu heva ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Sunem. Eya ta Saul hã ƒo Israel blibo la nu ƒu, eye wova ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe Gilboa.
ENGLISH: 4 And the Philistines gathered and came and encamped at Shunem; and Saul gathered all Israel, and they encamped at Gilboaʽ.

EWE: 5 Esi Saul kpɔ Filistitɔwo ƒe asaɖaa la, vɔvɔ̃ ɖoe, eye dzika tso eƒo ŋutɔ.
ENGLISH: 5 And Saul saw the Philistine army, and was afraid and utterly unnerved;

EWE: 6 Togbɔ be Saul biaa gbe Yehowa hã la, Yehowa meɖoa eŋu nɛ to drɔ̃e me loo, to Urim la dzi loo, alo to nyagblɔɖilawo dzi o.
ENGLISH: 6 and Saul put questions to Jehovah, but Jehovah did not answer him either by dreams or by the Urim or by the prophets.

EWE: 7 Mlɔeba Saul gblɔ na eƒe dɔlawo be: “Midi nyɔnu ŋɔliyɔla aɖe nam, ne mayi aɖabia nu ta se le egbɔ.” Eye eƒe dɔlawo gblɔ nɛ be: “Kpɔ ɖa!
ENGLISH: 7 And Saul said to his officers “Look me up a medium that I can go to and inquire of her”; and his officers said to him “There is a medium to be found at ʽEn-Dor.”

EWE: Nyɔnu ŋɔliyɔla aɖe le En-Dor.” 8 Eya ta Saul trɔ eƒe dzedzeme hedo awu bubuwo, eye eya kple ŋutsu eve woyi nyɔnu la gbɔ le zã me. Eye wògblɔ be: “Meɖe kuku, ka nu nàyɔ ame si mayɔ na wò la nam.”
ENGLISH: 8 And Saul disguised himself and put on different clothes, and went, he and two men with him, and came to the woman in the night and said “Use your power as medium for me, and bring me up the one I tell you to.”

EWE: 9 Ke nyɔnua gblɔ nɛ be: “Kpɔ ɖa, ènya nu si Saul wɔ la nyuie, ale si wòɖe ŋɔliyɔlawo kple nukalawo ɖa le anyigba la dzi. Ekema nu ka tae nèle mɔ̃ trem nam ne woawum?”
ENGLISH: 9 But the woman said to him “Now you know what Saul did, how he extirpated the different kinds of mediums out of the country, and why are you shooting at my life?”

EWE: 10 Saul ka atam nɛ le Yehowa ƒe ŋkɔ me be: “Zi ale si Yehowa le agbe la, fɔɖiɖi aɖeke manɔ dziwò le nya sia me o!”
ENGLISH: 10 But Saul swore to her by Jehovah, “As Jehovah lives, you shall not suffer for this matter”;

EWE: 11 Eya ta nyɔnua biae be: “Ame kae nàdi be mayɔ avɛ na wò?” Eɖo eŋu be: “Yɔ Samuel vɛ nam.”
ENGLISH: 11 and the woman said “Whom shall I bring up for you?” and he said “Bring me up Samuel.”

EWE: 12 Esi nyɔnua kpɔ “Samuel” la, edo ɣli sesĩe eye nyɔnua bia Saul be: “Nu ka tae nèflum?
ENGLISH: 12 And the woman saw Samuel, and gave a loud cry and said “Why did you deceive me, when you are Saul?”

EWE: Evɔ wònye wòe nye Saul hafi!” 13 Ke fia la gblɔ nɛ be: “Mègavɔ̃ o; nu kae nèkpɔ?”
ENGLISH: 13 And the king said to her “Do not be afraid; but what did you see?” and she said to him “I saw a god coming up out of the earth.”

EWE: Nyɔnua ɖo eŋu na Saul be: “Mekpɔ ame aɖe si le abe mawu aɖe ene wòle dodom tso anyigba me.” 14 Enumake ebiae be: “Aleke eƒe dzedzeme le?” Eɖo eŋu be: “Ame si do gbɔna la nye amegãɖeɖi, eye wòdo awu ʋlaya si ŋu abɔ mele o.”
ENGLISH: 14 And he said to her “What did he look like?” and she said “An old man is coming up, wrapped in a robe”; and Saul knew it was Samuel, and bowed his face to the ground and did reverence.

EWE: Enumake Saul dze sii be “Samuel” ye, eya ta ebɔbɔ tsyɔ mo anyi. 15 Eye “Samuel” bia Saul be: “Nu ka tae nèɖe fu nam, be nèna woyɔm vɛ?” Saul ɖo eŋu be: “Meɖo xaxa gã aɖe me. Filistitɔwo le aʋa wɔm kplim, evɔ Mawu hã ʋu le gbɔnye, eye megaɖoa nya ŋu nam to nyagblɔɖilawo dzi loo alo drɔ̃e me o; eya tae meyɔ wò be nàgblɔ nu si mawɔ la nam.”
ENGLISH: 15 And Samuel said to Saul “Why have you disturbed me with bringing me up?” and Saul said “I am in a very hard case, with the Philistines making war on me and God gone away from me and not answering me any longer either through the prophets or by dreams; and I have called you to let me know what to do.”

EWE: 16 Eye “Samuel” gblɔ be: “Fifia si Yehowa gblẽ wò ɖi hezu wò futɔ ɖe, nu ka tae nèle nu biamem?
ENGLISH: 16 But Samuel said “And why should you ask me, when Jehovah has gone away from you and become your enemy?

EWE: 17 Yehowa awɔ abe ale si tututu wògblɔ to dzinye ene: Yehowa adu fiaɖuƒe la le asiwò atsɔ ana hawòviwo dometɔ ɖeka si nye David.
ENGLISH: 17 And Jehovah has done as he said by me he would, and torn the kingship out of your hands and given it to a rival of yours, David.

EWE: 18 Esi mèɖo to Yehowa ƒe gbe o, eye mèna eƒe dziku helĩhelĩ va Amalek dzi o tae Yehowa le nu siawo wɔm wò egbea ɖo.
ENGLISH: 18 As you did not obey Jehovah and wreak his anger on the ʽAmalekites, therefore Jehovah has done this thing to you this day;

EWE: 19 Azɔ hã, Yehowa atsɔ Israel kple wò ŋutɔ ade asi na Filistitɔwo, eye etsɔ la, wò kple viwòŋutsuwo miava do ɖe gbɔnye.
ENGLISH: 19 and Jehovah has also given Israel with you into the Philistines’ hands.

EWE: Yehowa atsɔ Israel ƒe aʋakɔ la gɔ̃ hã ade asi na Filistitɔwo.”
ENGLISH: And tomorrow you and your sons shall be with me; the army of Israel too Jehovah will give into the Philistines’ hands.”

EWE: 20 Enumake Saul tsra ɖe anyigba dremu eye vɔvɔ̃ ɖoe ŋutɔ le “Samuel” ƒe nyawo ta. Eye ŋusẽ aɖeke megale eŋu o, elabena meɖu nu ŋkeke blibo la kple zã blibo la katã o.
ENGLISH: 20 And Saul was dumbfounded, and fell full length on the ground, and was greatly afraid at Samuel’s words; he had no strength in him either, because he had not eaten food all day and all night.

EWE: 21 Esi nyɔnua va Saul gbɔ hekpɔ be nya la ɖe fu nɛ ale gbegbe la, egblɔ nɛ be: “Wò dɔlanyɔnu ɖo to wò gbe, eye metsɔ nye agbe de afɔku me hewɔ nu siwo nègblɔ nam.
ENGLISH: 21 And the woman came to Saul and saw that he was in utter consternation; and she said to him “Here your servant has obeyed you, I have taken my life in my hand and listened to the things you proposed to me;

EWE: 22 Eya ta meɖe kuku, ɖo to wò dɔlanyɔnu ƒe gbe. Na matsɔ abolo vi aɖe aɖo akɔwòme nàɖu, ale be ŋusẽ naɖo ŋuwò nàtrɔ adzo.”
ENGLISH: 22 now take your turn to obey your servant, and let me set a bit of bread before you, and eat something so as to have some strength in you when you go on your way”;

EWE: 23 Ke egbe gblɔ be: “Nyemaɖu nu o.”
ENGLISH: 23 but he refused, and said “I will not eat.”

EWE: Ke hã, eƒe dɔlawo kple nyɔnu la siaa ƒoe ɖe enu. Mlɔeba eɖo to wo, eye wòtso le anyigba hebɔbɔ nɔ aba dzi.
ENGLISH: But his servants urged him, and so did the woman; and he obeyed them, and rose from the ground and sat down on the bed.

EWE: 24 Ke nyivi dami aɖe le nyɔnu la si le aƒea me. Eya ta ewɔ kaba tsoe, eye wòku wɔ blui hetsɔe mè amɔwɔ maʋamaʋã bolo.
ENGLISH: 24 And the woman, who had a tied-up calf in the house, killed it in haste and took meal and kneaded it up and baked it into matzoth,

EWE: 25 Eye wòtsɔ wo ɖo Saul kple eƒe dɔlawo kɔme woɖu. Emegbe wotso dzo le zã ma me.
ENGLISH: 25 and presented it before Saul and his servants, and they ate, and went off that night.

EWE: 1 Samuel
ENGLISH: 1 Samuel

EWE: 29 Filistitɔwo ƒo woƒe aʋakɔwo katã nu ƒu ɖe Afek, eye Israel-viwo hã ƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe tsidzɔƒe si le Yezreel gbɔ.
ENGLISH: 29 And the Philistines gathered all their armies to Aphek, while the Israelites were encamped at the spring in Jezreʽel.

EWE: 2 Filistitɔwo ƒe kplɔlawo kple woƒe aʋakɔwo va le yiyim alafaalafa kple akpeakpe, eye David kple eƒe amewo nɔ wo megbe hekpe ɖe Akis ŋu va yi.
ENGLISH: 2 And the Sarns of the Philistines were passing in review by hundreds and by thousands, and David and his men passing in the rear with Akish;

EWE: 3 Ke Filistitɔwo ƒe amegãwo gblɔ be: “Nu ka dim Hebritɔ siawo le?”
ENGLISH: 3 and the captains of the Philistines said “What do these Hebrews mean?”

EWE: Akis ɖo eŋu na Filistitɔwo ƒe amegãwo be: “David, Israel-fia Saul ƒe subɔvi, si le gbɔnye afi sia ƒe ɖeka kple nanewoe nye esia lae. Eye nyemekpɔ vɔ̃ aɖeke le eŋu tso gbe si gbe wòsi va gbɔnye va se ɖe egbe sia o.”
ENGLISH: And Akish said to the captains of the Philistines “Why, this is David, King Saul of Israel’s officer, who has been with me this year or two, and I have never had any fault to find with him from the day he transferred his allegiance to me till this day.”

EWE: 4 Ke Filistitɔwo ƒe amegãwo do dziku ɖe eŋu, eye wogblɔ nɛ be: “Na ŋutsu la nagbugbɔ. Na wòagbugbɔ ayi afi si nètsɔ nɛ la. Mègana wòayi aʋa la kpli mí o, ne wòagava trɔ ɖe mía ŋu le aʋa la me o.
ENGLISH: 4 But the captains of the Philistines were incensed, and said to him “Have the man go back, back to his place where you stationed him, and not down with us into the battle, and we shall not have him for an antagonist in the battle.

EWE: Nu kae ame sia awɔ atsɔ adze eƒe aƒetɔ ŋu, ne menye be wòawu míaƒe ame siawo oa?
ENGLISH: And what should the fellow pacify his sovereign with? would it not be with those men’s heads?

EWE: 5 Alo menye David sia ŋue wodzi ha le heɖu ɣe nɔ gbɔgblɔm be: ‘Saul wu ame akpewo, David ya wu ame akpe ewowo’ oa?”
ENGLISH: 5 Why, this is the David of whom they sing in the dances ‘Saul has killed by the thousand, David by the ten-thousand.’”

EWE: 6 Eya ta Akis yɔ David gblɔ nɛ be: “Zi ale si Yehowa le agbe la, ame dzɔdzɔe nènye, eye ɖe medi be nàyi kple nye aʋakɔa le aʋahohoa me hafi, elabena nyemekpɔ vɔ̃ aɖeke le ŋuwò tso gbe si gbe nèva gbɔnye va se ɖe egbe sia o. Gake Filistitɔwo ƒe kplɔlawo ya meka ɖe dziwò o.
ENGLISH: 6 And Akish called David and said to him “By Jehovah, I think you are all right, and I should like to have you go in and out with me in the army, because I have found nothing wrong with you from the day you came to me till this day; but the Sarns do not like you.

EWE: 7 Eya ta gbugbɔ yi le ŋutifafa me, be nàgawɔ nu si madze Filistitɔwo ƒe kplɔlawo ŋu o.”
ENGLISH: 7 Now go back in friendship, and do not displease the Sarns of the Philistines.”

EWE: 8 Ke David bia Akis be: “Nu ka ta, nu kae mewɔ? Nu gbegblẽ kae nèkpɔ le wò subɔvi ŋu tso gbe si gbe meva ŋkuwòme va se ɖe egbe sia?
ENGLISH: 8 And David said to Akish “But what have I done, and what fault have you had to find with your servant from the first day I was with you till this day, that I am not to come and fight your majesty’s enemies?”

EWE: Nu ka tae nyemayi aɖawɔ aʋa kple nye aƒetɔ fia ƒe futɔwo o?” 9 Akis ɖo eŋu na David be: “Nye ya menyae be ame nyui nènye, abe mawudɔla ene.
ENGLISH: 9 And Akish answered David “I know I think you are all right, right as a god’s angel; only the captains of the Philistines have said ‘he shall not go up with us into the battle.’

EWE: Ke Filistitɔwo ƒe amegãwoe gblɔ nam be: ‘Mègana wòayi aʋa la kpli mí o.’ 10 Eya ta wò kple wò aƒetɔ ƒe subɔvi siwo va kpli wò la, mifɔ ŋdi kanya miadzo ne xexea me nya kɔ ko.”
ENGLISH: 10 Now, the first thing in the morning, you and your sovereign’s subjects that came with you go to the place where I stationed you, and do not take anything vicious into your head, because you stand all right with me; go the first thing in the morning, as soon as you have light.”

EWE: 11 Eya ta David kple eƒe amewo fɔ ŋdi kanya hedze mɔ yi Filistitɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi, ke Filistitɔwo ho yi Yezreel.
ENGLISH: 11 And the first thing in the morning David went off, he and his men, to go back to the Philistine country; and the Philistines went up to Jezreʽel.

EWE: 1 Samuel
ENGLISH: 1 Samuel

EWE: 30 Esime David kple eƒe amewo gbɔ va Ziklag le ŋkeke etɔ̃a gbe la, wokpɔe be Amalektɔwo va dze anyiehe gome kple Ziklag dua dzi, eye wosi Ziklag hetɔ dzoe.
ENGLISH: 30 And when David and his men came to Siklag on the third day, the ʽAmalekites had raided the South and Siklag, and had sacked Siklag and burned it down,

EWE: 2 Eye woɖe aboyo nyɔnuwo kple ame siwo katã le dua me, ɖeviwo kple tsitsiawo siaa. Womewu ame aɖeke o, ke boŋ wokplɔ wo dzoe.
ENGLISH: 2 and carried off the women and everybody in it, great and small; they did not kill anybody; and they herded them up and went on their way.

EWE: 3 Esi David kple eƒe amewo va dua me la, wokpɔ be wotɔ dzoe, eye woɖe aboyo wo srɔ̃wo kple wo viŋutsuwo kpakple wo vinyɔnuwo.
ENGLISH: 3 And David and his men came to the city and found it burned down and their wives and children carried off;

EWE: 4 Eya ta David kple ame siwo le eŋu la fa avi kple ɣli, va se ɖe esime avia meganya le fafam na wo o.
ENGLISH: 4 and David and the people he had with him raised their voices and wept till there was no longer any power to weep in them.

EWE: 5 Woɖe aboyo David srɔ̃ eve siwo nye Ahinoam si tso Yezreel, kple Abigail, si nye Karmeltɔ Nabal ƒe ahosi.
ENGLISH: 5 And David’s two wives were carried off, Ahinoʽam the Jezreʽelite and Abigail the widow of Nabal the Carmelite.

EWE: 6 Nya la te ɖe David dzi ŋutɔ, elabena ameawo gblɔ be yewoaƒu kpee, elabena ŋutsuawo do dziku vevie le wo viŋutsu kple wo vinyɔnu siwo wokplɔ dzoe ta.
ENGLISH: 6 And David was in a very hard case, because the people were proposing to stone him, because all the people were furious over their children.

EWE: Ke David tsɔ Yehowa eƒe Mawu la do ŋusẽ eɖokui.
ENGLISH: But David took courage in his God Jehovah.

EWE: 7 Eye David gblɔ na nunɔla Abiatar, Ahimelek vi la be: “Meɖe kuku, tsɔ kɔmewu la va afii nam.”
ENGLISH: 7 And David said to Priest Abiathar the son of Ahimelec “Bring the ephod for me.”

EWE: Eye Abiatar tsɔ kɔmewu la vɛ na David. 8 Eye David bia gbe Yehowa be: “Mati adzoha sia yomea? Matu woa?” Eɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Ti wo yome, elabena àtu wo godoo, eye àxɔ miaƒe nu sia nu si wotsɔ dzoe la le wo si.”
ENGLISH: 8 And David put the question to Jehovah “Shall I pursue these raiders? should I catch them?” and he said to him “Do: catch you shall and rescue you shall.”

EWE: 9 Enumake David dze mɔ kple ŋutsu alafa ade siwo le eŋu la, eye wova ɖo Besor-tɔʋu la gbɔ, eye ame aɖewo tsi afi ma.
ENGLISH: 9 And David went, he and six hundred men who were with him, and they came to Besor Arroyo; and he left two hundred men there,

EWE: 10 Eye David kple ŋutsu alafa ene la ti wo yome, ke ŋutsu alafa eve, siwo ŋu ɖeɖi te belibeli ale gbegbe be womate ŋu atso Besor-tɔʋua o la, tsi anyi.
ENGLISH: 10 and he pressed on the pursuit, he and four hundred men; and two hundred men stayed, who were too dead to cross Besor Arroyo.

EWE: 11 Wova ke ɖe Egipte ŋutsu aɖe ŋu le gbe me. Eye wokplɔe va David gbɔ hena aboloe be wòaɖu, eye wona tsii be wòano.
ENGLISH: 11 And they found an Egyptian out on the range and took him to David, and gave him food, which he ate, and water to drink;

EWE: 12 Wona gbotsetsebolo kakɛ ɖeka kple waintsetse ƒuƒu bolo eve hãe.
ENGLISH: 12 and they gave him a cake of figs and two or three clusters of raisins, and he ate and his spirit came back to him for he had not eaten food nor drunk water for three days and three nights.

EWE: Eye wòɖui, eye ŋusẽ gaɖo eŋu, elabena ŋkeke etɔ̃ kple zã etɔ̃e nye ema meɖu abolo alo no tsi o. 13 Eye David biae be: “Ame ka ƒe amee nènye, eye afi kae nètso?”
ENGLISH: 13 And David said to him “Whom do you belong to, and where are you from?” and he said “I am an Egyptian boy, slave to an ʽAmalekite man, and my master left me behind because I was taken sick three days ago.

EWE: 14 Míeyi ɖadze Keretitɔwo ƒe anyiehe kple Yuda-nyigba kpakple Kaleb ƒe anyiehe nyigbawo dzi, eye míetɔ dzo Ziklag.”
ENGLISH: 14 We had raided the Cretan South and the Judahite and the Calebite, and Siklag we had burned down.”

EWE: 15 Eye David biae be: “Àkplɔm ayi adzoha sia gbɔa?” Eɖo eŋu be: “Tà Mawu nam be, màwum o, eye màtsɔm ade asi na nye aƒetɔ o; ekema makplɔ wò ayi adzoha sia gbɔ.”
ENGLISH: 15 And David said to him “Will you take me down to these raiders?” and he said “Swear to me by God that you will not put me to death nor give me up to my master, and I will take you down to these raiders.”

EWE: 16 Eya ta ekplɔe yi afi si wokaka ɖe anyigba la katã dzi, le nu ɖum le nu nom hele aglo tum le aboyonu gbogbo siwo katã woha tso Filistitɔwo ƒe anyigba kple Yuda-nyigba dzi la ta.
ENGLISH: 16 And so he did; and they found them all over the ground at random, eating and drinking and holidaying with all the immense booty that they had taken from the Philistine country and the country of Judah.

EWE: 17 Eye David si wo tso fɔŋli va se ɖe fiẽ, eye wòtsrɔ̃ wo; wo dometɔ aɖeke mesi o, negbe ɖekakpui alafa ene siwo do kposɔ la koe si.
ENGLISH: 17 And David killed them from twilight to dark and gave no quarter: not a man of them escaped except four hundred young men who mounted camels and made off.

EWE: 18 Eye David xɔ nu siwo katã Amalektɔwo ha la, eye David xɔ srɔ̃a eveawo hã.
ENGLISH: 18 And David rescued everything that the ʽAmalekites had taken; and David rescued his two wives;

EWE: 19 Naneke mebu o, woxɔ ɖeviwo kple ame tsitsiwo, wo viŋutsuwo kple wo vinyɔnuwo kpakple nu sia nu, si woha. David xɔ nu sia nu gbɔe.
ENGLISH: 19 and nothing of theirs was gone, from the smallest thing to the greatest and to sons and daughters, and from booty to everything that had been taken from them: David recovered everything.

EWE: 20 David kplɔ alẽhawo kple nyihawo, eye wokplɔ wo dze woawo ŋutɔwo ƒe lãhawo ŋgɔ.
ENGLISH: 20 And he took all the sheep and cows, and they drove them before him and said “This is David’s booty.”

EWE: Eye wogblɔ be: “David ƒe aboyonue nye esia.” 21 Emegbe David va ɖo ŋutsu alafa eve, siwo ŋu ɖeɖi te belibeli ale gbegbe be womete ŋu kplɔ David ɖo o, eye wona wotsi Besor-tɔʋua nu la gbɔ, eye woyi ɖakpe David kple ame siwo le eŋu la.
ENGLISH: 21 And David came to the two hundred men that had been too dead to follow David, and whom he had had stay at Besor Arroyo; and they came out to meet David and the people he had with him, and came up to the people and asked how they had got on.

EWE: Esi David gogo ameawo la, ebia woƒe agbe ta se. 22 Ke ame vlowo kple yakame siwo le ŋutsu siwo kplɔ David ɖo yi dome la gblɔ be: “Esi womeyi kpli mí o ta la, míana aboyonu si míexɔ la ƒe ɖeke wo o, ke boŋ wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe nekplɔ srɔ̃a kple viawo ko ne wòadzo.”
ENGLISH: 22 And all the good-for-nothing reprobates among the men who had gone with David answered “Since they did not go with us, we will not give them any of the booty we have recovered except each man’s wife and children: they may take that drove along and go.”

EWE: 23 Ke David gblɔ be: “Nɔvinyewo, migawɔ alea o!
ENGLISH: 23 But David said “You shall not do so, brothers, with what Jehovah has given to us and kept us safe and given into our hands the raiders that had come against us.

EWE: Yehowae tsɔ nu siawo na mí, ekpɔ mía ta, eye wòtsɔ adzoha si va dze mía dzi la de asi na mí. 24 Eye ame kae aɖo to mi le nya sia me? Ke ame si de aʋa la ƒe gome nasɔ kple ame si tsi agbawo gbɔ la ƒe gome. Ame sia ame naxɔe sɔsɔe.”
ENGLISH: 24 And who would listen to you on this proposition? for the share of the one who goes down to the fight is equal to the share of the one who stays with the things: they are to share together.”

EWE: 25 Eye tso gbe ma gbe dzi la, nya si David gblɔ la zu se kple ɖoɖo le Israel va se ɖe egbe sia.
ENGLISH: 25 And thenceforth he made it a usage and a law for Israel to this day.

EWE: 26 Esi David va ɖo Ziklag la, eɖo aboyonu la ƒe ɖe ɖe Yuda ƒe ametsitsi siwo nye exɔlɔ̃wo hegblɔ be: “Mixɔ nunana sia tso Yehowa ƒe futɔwo ƒe aboyonuwo me.”
ENGLISH: 26 And David, coming to Siklag, sent parts of the booty to his friends the elders of Judah, with the message “Here is a token for you out of the booty from Jehovah’s enemies”:

EWE: 27 Eɖoe ɖe ame siwo le Betel, ame siwo le Ramot le Negeb kple ame siwo le Yatir,
ENGLISH: 27 to those in Bethul and those in Ramoth-Negeb and those in Jattir

EWE: 28 ame siwo le Aroer, ame siwo le Sifmot kple ame siwo le Estemoa,
ENGLISH: 28 and those in ʽArʽarah and those in Siphmoth and those in Eshtemoaʽ

EWE: 29 ame siwo le Rakal, ame siwo le Yerameltɔwo ƒe duwo me kple ame siwo le Kenitɔwo ƒe duwo me,
ENGLISH: 29 and those in Racal and those in the Jerahmeelite cities and those in the Cainite cities

EWE: 30 ame siwo le Horma, ame siwo le Borasan kple ame siwo le Atak,
ENGLISH: 30 and those in Hormah and those in BorʽAshan and those in ʽAthac

EWE: 31 ame siwo le Hebron kple teƒe siwo katã David kple eƒe amewo to.
ENGLISH: 31 and those in Hebron and to all the places where David had roved, he and his men.

EWE: 1 Samuel
ENGLISH: 1 Samuel

EWE: 31 Filistitɔwo nɔ aʋa wɔm kple Israel. Eye Israel ŋutsuwo si le Filistitɔwo nu, eye wo dometɔ geɖe tsi aʋa le Gilboa To dzi.
ENGLISH: 31 And the Philistines fought the Israelites, and the men of Israel ran before the Philistines, and fell stabbed through on Mount Gilboaʽ.

EWE: 2 Filistitɔwo ɖe Saul kple viaŋutsuwo ɖe nu, eye Filistitɔwo wu Yonatan, Abinadab kple Malki-Sua, siwo nye Saul viwo.
ENGLISH: 2 And the Philistines kept close after Saul and his sons; and the Philistines killed Saul’s sons Jonathan and Abinadab and Malk-Shuaʽ.

EWE: 3 Aʋa la nu sẽ ŋutɔ ɖe Saul dzi, eye aŋutrɔdalawo va ke ɖe eŋu, eye aŋutrɔdalawo de abi eŋu vevie.
ENGLISH: 3 And the onslaught on Saul was fierce, and the shooters (bowmen) hit him, and he was badly hurt by the shooters.

EWE: 4 Eya ta Saul gblɔ na eƒe adekplɔvi be: “Ðe wò yi ne nàƒo ɖem, ne aʋamatsomatsotɔ siawo nagava aƒo nu ɖem ahawɔ funyafunyam o.” Ke eƒe adekplɔvi la melɔ̃ o, elabena enɔ vɔvɔ̃m ŋutɔ.
ENGLISH: 4 And Saul said to his squire “Draw your sword and run me through with it, for fear those uncircumcised fellows should come and amuse themselves with me”; but his squire would not, because he was too much afraid.

EWE: Eya ta Saul tsɔ yi la hedze enu.
ENGLISH: But Saul took his sword and threw himself on it;

EWE: 5 Esi Saul ƒe adekplɔvi la kpɔ be Saul ku la, eya hã dze eƒe yi nu, eye wòku kplii.
ENGLISH: 5 and his squire saw that Saul was dead, and he too threw himself on his own sword and died with him.

EWE: 6 Ale Saul kple viaŋutsu etɔ̃awo, eƒe adekplɔvi la, kpakple eƒe amewo katã ku gbe ma gbe.
ENGLISH: 6 And Saul and his three sons and his squire died on that day.

EWE: 7 Esi Israel-vi siwo le balimenuto la kple Yordan nutoa me kpɔ be Israel ƒe aʋawɔlawo si, eye Saul kple viaŋutsuwo ku la, wogblẽ duawo ɖi hesi, eye Filistitɔwo va nɔ wo me.
ENGLISH: 7 And the men of Israel on the other side of the Vale and of the Jordan saw that the men of Israel had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, and they left their cities and fled, and the Philistines came and lived in the cities.

EWE: 8 Le ŋufɔke esi Filistitɔwo va nu ɖe ge le ame tsiaʋawo ŋu la, wokpɔ Saul kple viaŋutsu etɔ̃awo woku ɖe Gilboa To la dzi.
ENGLISH: 8 And on the next day the Philistines came to strip the killed, and found Saul and his three sons fallen on Mount Gilboaʽ.

EWE: 9 Eye wotso ta le Saul nu, ɖe eƒe aʋawɔnuwo le eŋu, eye wodɔ ame ɖo ɖe Filistitɔwo ƒe anyigba dzi godoo be woagblɔe le woƒe trɔ̃wo ƒe me kple dukɔ blibo la me.
ENGLISH: 9 And they cut off his head and stripped off his equipment and sent them around through the Philistine country to bring the news to their idols and the people,

EWE: 10 Wotsɔ eƒe aʋawɔnuwo va da ɖe Astoretwo ƒe me, eye wotsɔ eƒe ŋutilã kukua ku gli ŋu le Bet-San.
ENGLISH: 10 and put his equipment in the temple of ʽAshtart; and his body they pegged to the wall of Beth-Shan.

EWE: 11 Esi Yabes-Gileadtɔwo se nu si Filistitɔwo wɔ Saul la,
ENGLISH: 11 And Jabesh in Gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul;

EWE: 12 ŋutsu aʋawɔlawo katã tso, eye wozɔ mɔ zã blibo la yi ɖaɖe Saul kple viawo ƒe kukuawo le Bet-San ƒe gli ŋu. Wotsɔ wo yi Yabes, eye wotɔ dzo wo le afi ma.
ENGLISH: 12 and all the bravest men set out and made an all-night march and took the bodies of Saul and his sons from the wall of Beth-Shan and brought them to Jabesh and burned them there,

EWE: 13 Emegbe wotsɔ woƒe ƒuwo yi ɖaɖi ɖe tamarisk-ti si le Yabes la te, eye wotsi nu dɔ ŋkeke adre.
ENGLISH: 13 and took their bones and buried them under the tamarisk tree at Jabesh, and fasted seven days.

EWE: 2 Samuel
ENGLISH: 2 Samuel

EWE: 1 Le Saul ƒe ku megbe la, David trɔ va Ziklag le esime wòɖu Amalek dzi megbe, eye wònɔ afi ma ŋkeke eve.
ENGLISH: 1 And after Saul’s death David, coming back from defeating the ʽAmalekites, stayed at Siklag two days.

EWE: 2 Le ŋkeke etɔ̃a gbe la, ŋutsu aɖe tso Saul ƒe asaɖa me va, awu vuvu le eŋu, eye ke le tame nɛ.
ENGLISH: 2 And on the third day in came a man from the army, from Saul, with his clothes torn and earth on his head; and on coming to David he threw himself down on the ground and did him reverence.

EWE: Esi wòva ɖo David gbɔ la, ebɔbɔ tsyɔ mo anyi enumake. 3 Eye David biae be: “Afi kae nètso?”
ENGLISH: 3 And David said to him “Where do you come from?” and he told him “From the Israelite army; I am one that got away.”

EWE: Eɖo eŋu be: “Israel ƒe asaɖa la mee mesi tso.” 4 David gabiae be: “Aleke nuwo va yii?
ENGLISH: 4 And David said to him “What was it that happened? tell me.”

EWE: Meɖe kuku, gblɔe nam.” Eye wògblɔ be: “Dukɔ la si le aʋa la nu, eye dukɔ la me tɔ geɖe tsi aʋa. Saul kple via Yonatan hã ku.”
ENGLISH: And he said that the people had been routed in the battle, and that many of the people had fallen and were dead; and that Saul and his sons were dead.

EWE: 5 Eye David bia ɖekakpui si le nyaa gblɔm nɛ la be: “Aleke nèwɔ nya be Saul kple via Yonatan ku?”
ENGLISH: 5 And David said to the young man who brought him the report “How do you know that Saul and his son Jonathan are dead?”

EWE: 6 Ðekakpuia ɖo eŋu be: “Nanetɔe la, meva Gilboa To la dzi, eye mekpɔ Saul wòziɔ ɖe eƒe akplɔ ŋu; eye tasiaɖamdolawo kple sɔdolawo va tui.
ENGLISH: 6 And the young man who brought the report said “I happened by chance to be on Mount Gilboaʽ, and found Saul supporting himself on his spear, and the chariotry and cavalry overtaking him;

EWE: 7 Esi wòtrɔ kpɔm la, eyɔm, eye metɔ be: ‘Nyee nye esi!’
ENGLISH: 7 and he turned and looked behind him and saw me, and called to me, and I said ‘Here I am’;

EWE: 8 Eye wòbiam be: ‘Ame kae nènye?’ Meɖo eŋu be: ‘Amalektɔe menye.’
ENGLISH: 8 and he said to me ‘Who are you?’ and I said to him ‘I am an ʽAmalekite.’

EWE: 9 Eye wògblɔ be: ‘Meɖe kuku, te ɖe ŋunye, ne nàwum, elabena mele veve sem ŋutɔ, eye agbe gale menye ko.’
ENGLISH: 9 And he said to me ‘Come and stand over me and give me my death; for I have been taken with dizziness while my life was still all in me.’

EWE: 10 Eya ta mete ɖe eŋu hewui, elabena menya be anyi si wòdze la, menye agbenɔtɔe o. Eye meɖe fiakuku si le eta kple abɔgɛ si le eƒe abɔ, be matsɔ wo vɛ na nye aƒetɔ le afi sia.”
ENGLISH: 10 So I stood, over him and gave him his death for I knew he could not live after he had fallen and took the diadem that was on his head and an armlet that was on his arm, and brought them to your highness.”

EWE: 11 Eye David dze eƒe awuwo; eye ŋutsu siwo katã le eŋu hã dze woƒe awuwo.
ENGLISH: 11 And David took hold of his clothes and tore them, and so did all the men that were with him;

EWE: 12 Eye wofa konyi, fa avi hetsi nu dɔ va se ɖe fiẽ le esi Saul kple via Yonatan kple Yehowa ƒe dukɔ la kpakple Israel ƒe aƒe la tsi yi nu ta.
ENGLISH: 12 and they wailed and wept and fasted till evening over Saul and over his son Jonathan and over Jehovah’s people and over the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.

EWE: 13 Eye David bia ɖekakpui si le nyaa gblɔm nɛ la be: “Afi ka tɔe nènye?” Eɖo eŋu be: “Amalektɔ aɖe si nye amedzro la ƒe vie menye.”
ENGLISH: 13 And David said to the young man who had brought him the report “Where are you from?” and he said “I am the son of an ʽAmalekite immigrant.”

EWE: 14 Eye David gblɔ nɛ be: “Nu ka tae mèvɔ̃ be nàdo asi ɖa awu Yehowa ƒe amesiamina la o?”
ENGLISH: 14 And David said to him “How is it you were not afraid to put out your hand to make away with Jehovah’s anointed?”

EWE: 15 Eye David yɔ ɖekakpuiawo dometɔ ɖeka gblɔ be: “Te ɖe eŋu nàda nui.” Ale wòda nui ƒu anyi wòku.
ENGLISH: 15 And David called one of the men and said “Come and cut him down”; and he stabbed him to death.

EWE: 16 Eye David gblɔ nɛ be: “Wò ʋu nanɔ wò ŋutɔ wò ta dzi, elabena wò ŋutɔ wò nue ɖi ɖase ɖe ŋuwò be, ‘Nyee wu Yehowa ƒe amesiamina la.’”
ENGLISH: 16 And David said to him “Your blood is on your own head, because your own mouth testified against you, saying ‘It was I who gave Jehovah’s anointed his death.’”

EWE: 17 Eye David kpa konyifaha sia le Saul kple via Yonatan ŋu,
ENGLISH: 17 And David sang this lament for Saul and his son Jonathan:

EWE: 18 eye wògblɔ be woafia konyifaha sia si nye “Aŋutrɔdaha La” Yuda viwo.
ENGLISH: 18 To teach the sons of Judah.

EWE: Woŋlɔe ɖe Yasar ƒe agbalẽ me:
ENGLISH: N.B. Written in the Book of the Upright.

EWE: 19 “Oo Israel, wowu ame siwo nye atsyɔ̃ na wò le wò togbɛwo dzi.
ENGLISH: 19 Israel, the antelope is speared on thy heights: how have champions fallen!

EWE: Aleke ŋusẽtɔwo dze anyi ale! 20 Migagblɔe le Gat o; Migaɖe gbeƒãe le Askelon ƒe ablɔwo dzi o, Ne Filistitɔwo ƒe vinyɔnuwo nagakpɔ dzidzɔ o, Ne aʋamatsomatsotɔwo ƒe vinyɔnuwo nagatso aseye o.
ENGLISH: 20 Do not tell of it in Gath, do not give out the news in the streets of Ashkelon, lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.

EWE: 21 Mi Gilboa Towo, Zãmu alo tsi megadza ɖe mia dzi o, Eye agblewo megawɔ woatsɔ edzi kutsetsewo awɔ nudzɔdzɔ kɔkɔewo o, Elabena afi mae wogblẽ kɔ ɖo na kalẽtɔwo ƒe akpoxɔnu le, Saul ƒe akpoxɔnu, ale be womegasi ami nɛ o.
ENGLISH: 21 Mountains in Gilboaʽ, may there never be dew nor rain on you, mountains of death; for champions’ shields were left uncared-for there, Saul’s shield unanointed with oil.

EWE: 22 Ame siwo wowu la ƒe ʋu, kalẽawo ƒe ami: Yonatan ƒe aŋutrɔ metrɔna ɖa le wo ŋu o, Eye Saul ƒe yi hã metrɔna gbɔna dzodzro o.
ENGLISH: 22 From blood of the slain, from the fat of champions, Jonathan’s bow never drew back, and Saul’s spear came never empty home.

EWE: 23 Saul kple Yonatan, ame malɔ̃nugbɔ siwo ƒe nu nyoa ame ŋu le woƒe agbenɔɣi, Wo dome mema le ku me hã o. Woɖea abla wu hɔ̃, Wosesẽ wu dzata.
ENGLISH: 23 Saul and Jonathan, the loved and the winsome, were not separated in their life and in their death; swifter than vultures they were, more stalwart than lions.

EWE: 24 Mi Israel vinyɔnuwo, mifa avi na Saul, Ame si ta avɔ dzĩ siwo nya kpɔ na mi, eye wòɖo atsyɔ̃ na mi Eɖo atsyɔ̃ na miaƒe nudodowo kple sikanuwo.
ENGLISH: 24 Daughters of Israel, weep for Saul, who clothed you in scarlet with luxury, who topped your clothing with golden jewelry.

EWE: 25 Ao, aleke kalẽawo tsi aʋa ale!
ENGLISH: 25 How have champions fallen amid the battle!

EWE: Wowu Yonatan ɖe wò togbɛwo dzi!
ENGLISH: Jonathan is speared on thy heights.

EWE: 26 Tɔwò le veyem, nɔvinye Yonatan, Wò nu nyoa ŋunye ŋutɔ! Wò lɔlɔ̃ nam ƒo nyɔnuwo ƒe lɔlɔ̃ ta sãsãsã.
ENGLISH: 26 I am distressed for thee, my brother Jonathan; thou wast to me very winsome, wonderful in thy love to me beyond the love of women.

EWE: 27 Aleke wɔ kalẽawo tsi aʋa, Eye aʋawɔnuwo nu yi ale!”
ENGLISH: 27 How have champions fallen and weapons of war been lost!

EWE: 2 Samuel
ENGLISH: 2 Samuel

EWE: 2 Emegbe David bia gbe Yehowa be: “Mayi Yuda duawo dometɔ ɖeka mea?” Yehowa ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Yi.” Eye David gabia be: “Afi kae mayi?”
ENGLISH: 2 And after this David put the question to Jehovah “Shall I go up into one of the cities of Judah?” and Jehovah said to him “Go up.”

EWE: Egblɔ be: “Yi Hebron.” 2 Ale David kple srɔ̃a eveawo yi afi ma: Ahinoam si tso Yezreel kple Abigail, si nye Karmeltɔ Nabal ƒe ahosi. 3 David kplɔ ŋutsu siwo le eŋu la hã yii, wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe kple eƒemetɔwo, eye wonɔ Hebron nutoa ƒe duwo me. 4 Eye Yuda ŋutsuwo va si ami na David le afi ma be wòaɖu fia ɖe Yuda ƒe aƒe la dzi.
ENGLISH: And David said “Where shall I go up to?” and he said “To Hebron.” 2 And David went up there, and also his two wives, Ahinoʽam the Jezreʽelite and Abigail the widow of Nabal the Carmelite; 3 and David brought up his men who were with him, each one with his household, and they took up their residence in the cities of Hebron; 4 and the men of Judah came and anointed David there as king over the house of Judah.

EWE: Wogblɔ na David be: “Yabes-Gileadtɔwoe ɖi Saul.”
ENGLISH: And they told David “It was the men of Jabesh in Gilead that buried Saul.”

EWE: 5 Eya ta David dɔ amewo ɖo ɖe Yabes-Gileadtɔwo hegblɔ na wo be: “Yehowa neyra mi, elabena mieve miaƒe aƒetɔ Saul nu heɖii.
ENGLISH: 5 And David sent envoys to the men of Jabesh in Gilead, saying to them “Jehovah bless you that you did this act of friendship by your master Saul, and buried him.

EWE: 6 Eya ta Yehowa neve mia nu eye wòawɔ nuteƒe na mi. Nye hã mawɔ nyui na mi le esi miewɔ nu sia ta.
ENGLISH: 6 And now, may Jehovah do friendlily and faithfully by you; and I too will do well by you for your having done this thing.

EWE: 7 Azɔ misẽ ŋu, eye miwɔ kalẽ, elabena miaƒe aƒetɔ Saul ku, eye nyee Yuda ƒe aƒe la si ami na be manye yewoƒe fia.”
ENGLISH: 7 Now keep up a stout heart, and show yourselves stalwart men; for Saul your sovereign is dead.

EWE: 8 Ke Saul ƒe aʋafia Abner, Ner vi la, kplɔ Saul vi Is-Boset tso tɔ la yi Mahanayim,
ENGLISH: Furthermore, the house of Judah have anointed me king over them.”

EWE: 9 eye wòtsɔe ɖo fia ɖe Gileadtɔwo, Asurtɔwo, Yezreeltɔwo, Efrayimtɔwo, Benyamintɔwo kple Israel blibo la dzi.
ENGLISH: 8 And Abner the son of Ner, Saul’s general, took Saul’s son Ishbaal and carried him over to Mahanaim 9 and installed him as king over Gilead and the Ashurites and Jezreʽelites, and over Ephraim and Benjamin and all Israel.

EWE: 10 Saul viŋutsu Is-Boset xɔ ƒe blaene esime wòzu fia ɖe Israel nu, eye wòɖu fia ƒe eve. Ke Yuda ƒe aƒe la ya nɔ David yome.
ENGLISH: 10 Ishbaal the son of Saul was forty years old at his accession to the throne of Israel, and reigned two years, except that the house of Judah was on David’s side.

EWE: 11 David ɖu fia ɖe Yuda ƒe aƒe la dzi le Hebron ƒe adre kple ɣleti ade.
ENGLISH: 11 And the days that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah amounted to seven years and six months.

EWE: 12 Emegbe Abner, Ner vi kple Saul vi Is-Boset ƒe amewo ho tso Mahanayim yi Gibeon. 13 Eye Yoab, Zeruya vi kple David ŋumewo hã ho, eye wova do go le Gibeon ta la to; akpa ɖeka nɔ ta la ƒe go ɖeka dzi, eye evelia hã nɔ go kemɛ dzi.
ENGLISH: 12 And Abner the son of Ner and the soldiers of Ishbaal the son of Saul set out from Mahanaim to Gibeon; 13 and Joab the son of Serujah and David’s soldiers went out and met with them by the reservoir of Gibeon.

EWE: Yoab ɖo eŋu be: “Na woatso.” 15 Ale wotso hetso ta la le woƒe xexlẽme nu, ame wuieve nye Saul vi Is-Boset ŋumewo tso Benyamin, eye ame wuieve nye David ŋumewo. 16 Eye wolé ta na wo nɔewo, eye wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe ƒo eƒe yi ɖe nɔvia ƒe axadame, ale be wo katã wodze anyi zi ɖeka. Eye wona ŋkɔ teƒe ma be Helkat-Hazurim; ele Gibeon.
ENGLISH: And they sat down these on one side of the reservoir and those on the other; 14 and Abner said to Joab “Let us have the boys step out and give us an exhibition”; and Joab said “Let us.” 15 And they stepped out and were counted off, twelve for Benjamin and Ishbaal the son of Saul, and twelve of David’s soldiers; 16 and each took hold of the other’s head and planted his sword in the other’s side, and they fell together; and that place was called the Rock Lot in Gibeon.

EWE: 17 Aʋa la nu sẽ ŋutɔ gbe ma gbe, eye David ŋumewo si Abner kple Israel ŋutsuwo.
ENGLISH: 17 And it was a very hard battle that day; and Abner and the men of Israel were beaten by David’s soldiers.

EWE: 18 Zeruya vi etɔ̃awo, Yoab, Abisai kple Asahel hã nɔ afi ma; Asahel ƒe afɔ tsɔna abe sãde le gbe me ene.
ENGLISH: 18 And the three sons of Serujah were there, Joab and Abishai and ʽAsahel; and ʽAsahel was as swift-footed as any gazelle on the range.

EWE: 19 Eye Asahel nya Abner ɖe nu, eye medze ɖe ɖusime alo miame le Abner yome o. 20 Esi Abner nye kɔ kpɔ megbe la, egblɔ be, “Asahel, wòe nye ema?” eye wòɖo eŋu be, “Nyee.” 21 Eye Abner gblɔ nɛ be: “Dze ɖe ɖusime alo miame, ne nàlé ɖekakpuiawo dometɔ ɖeka, eye nàtsɔ nu si nèɖe le eŋu la na ɖokuiwò.” Ke Asahel medi be yeatrɔ le eyome o. 22 Eye Abner gagblɔ na Asahel be: “Trɔ le yonyeme. Nu ka tae mada nu wò aƒu anyi?
ENGLISH: 19 And ʽAsahel pursued Abner, not turning to the right or to the left from his chase of Abner; and 20 Abner turned back and said “Is that you, ʽAsahel?” and he said “Yes.” 21 And Abner said to him “Turn to your right or your left and get hold of one of the men and take his spoils”; but ʽAsahel would not turn off from chasing him.

EWE: Aleke mawɔ agakpɔ nɔviwò Yoab ŋkume?” 23 Ke egbe tɔtrɔ, eye Abner tsɔ akplɔti la ƒe megbe tɔ dɔme nɛ, eye akplɔ la ŋɔe do go ɖe eƒe dzime; eye wòdze anyi heku enumake. Eye ne ame sia ame va ɖo afi si Asahel dze anyi ku ɖo la, etɔna ɖi. 24 Eyome Yoab kple Abisai nya Abner ɖe nu.
ENGLISH: 22 And Abner said again to ʽAsahel “Turn off from chasing me; what do you want me to strike you down for? how could I show my face to your brother Joab?” 23 But he refused to turn off; and Abner hit him below the waist with the back end of the spear, and the spear came out behind him; and he fell down and died on the spot.

EWE: Esime ɣe nɔ to ɖom la, wova Ama togbɛ, si le Gia ŋgɔ le Gibeon gbedzimɔ dzi la dzi.
ENGLISH: And all who came to the place where ʽAsahel had fallen and died stopped.

EWE: 25 Eye Benyamin viwo ƒo ƒu ɖe Abner ŋu hezu hatsotso gã ɖeka le afi ma, eye wotɔ ɖe togbɛ aɖe tame. 26 Eye Abner yɔ Yoab gblɔ be: “Ðe yi anɔ nuɖuɖu dzi ɖaa? Mènyae be vevesese ko wòahe vɛ oa?
ENGLISH: 24 But Joab and Abishai pursued Abner, and as the sun was setting they came to Ammah Hill, that is in front of Giah on the way to the wilderness of Gibeon; 25 and the sons of Benjamin rallied behind Abner and formed a single bunch, and made a stand on the top of a hill.

EWE: Ɣekaɣie nàgblɔ na ameawo be woatrɔ le wo nɔviwo yome?” 27 Eye Yoab gblɔ be: “Zi ale si Mawu vavã la le agbe la, ne menye ɖe nèƒo nu o la, anye ne etsɔ ŋdi hafi ameawo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe nagbugbɔ le nɔvia yome.” 28 Azɔ Yoab ku lãdzo, eye eƒe amewo dzudzɔ Israel yome titi, eye aʋaa ke.
ENGLISH: 26 And Abner called out to Joab “Shall swords always be eating? do you not know that it will be bitter afterward? how long before you will tell the men to turn back from chasing their brothers?” 27 And Joab said “By God, if you had not spoken, it would have been in the morning that the men broke off each chasing his brother.” 28 And Joab sounded the horn, and all the men halted and made no further pursuit of the Israelites, and did no more fighting.

EWE: 29 Abner kple eƒe amewo zɔ to Araba zã blibo la katã, eye wotso Yordan-tɔsisia hezɔ to bali blibo la me, eye mlɔeba wova Mahanayim.
ENGLISH: 29 And Abner and his men made an all-night march in the Rift Valley that night, and crossed the Jordan and went through the whole Bithron and came to Mahanaim.

EWE: 30 Esi Yoab trɔ le Abner yome la, eƒo ameawo katã nu ƒu. Eye ame wuiasieke hekpe ɖe Asahel ŋu megale David ƒe amewo dome o. 31 Ke David ŋumewo ɖu Benyamin kple Abner ƒe amewo dzi, eye wowu ame alafa etɔ̃ blaade le wo dome.
ENGLISH: 30 And Joab turned back from chasing Abner and gathered all the men, and there were missing of David’s soldiers nineteen men and ʽAsahel; 31 and David’s soldiers had killed of the Benjamites and of Abner’s men three hundred and sixty men.

EWE: 32 Wokɔ Asahel yi ɖaɖi ɖe fofoa ƒe yɔdo si le Betlehem la me. Yoab kple eƒe amewo zɔ zã blibo la katã, eye woɖo Hebron le ŋdi.
ENGLISH: 32 And they took up ʽAsahel and buried him in his father’s tomb at Bethlehem; and Joab and his men made an all-night march, and the daylight found them at Hebron.

EWE: 2 Samuel
ENGLISH: 2 Samuel

EWE: 3 Aʋa nɔ Saul ƒe aƒe la kple David ƒe aƒe dome eteƒe didi; eye David nɔ ŋusẽ kpɔm ɖe edzi, ke Saul ƒe aƒe la nɔ gbɔdzɔgbɔdzɔm ɖe edzi.
ENGLISH: 3 And the war between Saul’s house and David’s was a prolonged one; and David grew stronger and stronger, and Saul’s house weaker and weaker.

EWE: 2 Ɣemaɣi la, wodzi ŋutsuviwo na David le Hebron: eƒe ŋgɔgbevie nye Amnon, si Ahinoam, Yezreel nyɔnu la dzi.
ENGLISH: 2 And sons were born to David in Hebron; and his eldest was Ammon, by Ahinoʽam the Jezreʽelite,

EWE: 3 Via eveliae nye Kileab, si Abigail, ame si nye Karmeltɔ Nabal ƒe ahosi la dzi, eye etɔ̃liae nye Absalom, si Maaka, Gesur-fia Talmai vinyɔnu dzi.
ENGLISH: 3 and his second Kileab by Abigail the widow of Nabal the Carmelite, and the third Absalom the son of Maʽacah the daughter of King Talmai of Geshur,

EWE: 4 Eneliae nye Adoniya, si nye Hagit vi, eye atɔ̃liae nye Sefatiya, si nye Abital vi.
ENGLISH: 4 and the fourth Adonijah the son of Haggith, and the fifth Shephatiah the son of Abital,

EWE: 5 Adeliae nye Yitream, si David srɔ̃ Egla dzi. Ame siawoe wodzi na David le Hebron.
ENGLISH: 5 and the sixth Jithreʽam by David’s widow ʽEglah; these were born to David in Hebron.

EWE: 6 Esime aʋa si nɔ Saul ƒe aƒe kple David ƒe aƒe dome nɔ edzi yim la, Abner nɔ ŋusẽ dom eƒe ɖoƒe le Saul ƒe me.
ENGLISH: 6 And while the war between Saul’s house and David’s was going on Abner was doing his best by Saul’s.

EWE: 7 Ke ahiãvi aɖe nɔ Saul si, si ŋkɔe nye Rizpa, eye wònye Aya vinyɔnu. Emegbe Is-Boset bia Abner be: “Nu ka tae nèdɔ fofonye ƒe ahiã gbɔ?”
ENGLISH: 7 And Saul had had a concubine named Rispah the daughter of Aijah; and Ishbaal the son of Saul said to Abner “How comes it that you have gone in to my father’s concubine?”

EWE: 8 Eye Abner do dziku vevie le Is-Boset ƒe nyawo ta hegblɔ be: “Avu ƒe tae menye le Yuda?
ENGLISH: 8 and Abner was very angry at Ishbaal’s words, and said “Am I a dog’s head?

EWE: Meve fofowò Saul ƒe aƒe kple nɔviawo kpakple exɔlɔ̃awo nu va se ɖe egbe, eye nyemetsɔ mi de asi na David o; eye wòa nèle nya hem ɖe ŋunye egbea be meda vo le nyɔnu ta?
ENGLISH: Today I am doing favors to the house of your father Saul, down to his brothers and his personal friends, and have not handed you over to David; and you are calling me to account today for this fault about the woman.

EWE: 9 Eya ta Mawu nefia Abner ne wòagafiae ɖe edzi, ne nyemewɔ na David abe ale si tututu Yehowa ka atam nɛ ene:
ENGLISH: 9 God do so to Abner, and more, but I will do for David as Jehovah has said to him,

EWE: 10 be yeaxɔ fiaɖuƒe la le Saul ƒe aƒe la si, eye yeali ke David ƒe fiazikpui ɖe Israel kple Yuda dzi tso Dan va se ɖe Beer-Seba o fĩ!”
ENGLISH: 10 to carry the royal power away from Saul’s house and to set up David’s throne over Israel and over Judah from Dan to Beer-Shebaʽ.”

EWE: 11 Eye Is-Boset megate ŋu gblɔ nya aɖeke tsɔ ɖo eŋu na Abner o, elabena enɔ evɔ̃m.
ENGLISH: 11 And he was not able to give Abner any further answer, because he was afraid of him.

EWE: 12 Ale Abner dɔ amewo ɖo ɖe David enumake gblɔ be: “Ame ka tɔe anyigba la nye?”
ENGLISH: 12 And Abner sent messengers to David saying “Make terms with me, and you shall have my hand with you to turn over all Israel to you.”

EWE: Eye wògblɔ kpee be: “Bla nu kplim, eye mawɔ nu sia nu si mate ŋui atrɔ Israel blibo la katã ɖe ŋuwò.” 13 Eɖo eŋu be: “Enyo ta! Mabla nu kpli wò.
ENGLISH: 13 And he said “Very well; I will make terms with you; I only make one demand on you you shall not see my face unless when you come to see my face you bring Saul’s daughter Mical.”

EWE: 14 Azɔ hã, David dɔ amewo ɖo ɖe Saul vi Is-Boset gblɔ be: “Gbugbɔ srɔ̃nye Mikal, si ta metsɔ Filistitɔwo ƒe aʋanuyi alafa ɖeka na ɖo la nam.”
ENGLISH: 14 And David sent envoys to Ishbaal the son of Saul with the message “Give me my wife Mical whom I betrothed for a hundred Philistine foreskins”;

EWE: 15 Eya ta Is-Boset dɔ woɖakplɔe le srɔ̃a Paltiel, Lais vi gbɔ vɛ.
ENGLISH: 15 and Ishbaal sent and took her from her husband, from Paltiel the son of Layish.

EWE: 16 Ke srɔ̃a dze eyome nɔ avi fam kplɔe ɖo va ɖo keke Bahurim ke. Eye Abner gblɔ nɛ be: “Trɔ yi aƒe me!”
ENGLISH: 16 And her husband went with her, weeping as he went along behind her, as far as Bahurim; then Abner said to him “Now go back,” and he went back.

EWE: Enumake wògbugbɔ. 17 Ke Abner ɖo du ɖe Israel ƒe ametsitsiwo be: “Ɣeyiɣi aɖee nye esia miedi be David nanye fia ɖe mia nu.
ENGLISH: 17 And Abner had been holding communication with the elders of Israel, telling them “You were already wanting to have David for king over you a while ago:

EWE: 18 Miwɔe azɔ, elabena Yehowa gblɔ na David be: ‘Nye subɔla David ƒe asi dzie mato aɖe nye dukɔ Israel tso Filistitɔwo kple woƒe futɔwo katã si me.’”
ENGLISH: 18 now act on it; for Jehovah has said to David ‘By the hands of my servant David I will save my people Israel out of the hands of the Philistines and of all their enemies.’”

EWE: 19 Eye Abner ƒo nu na Benyamin viwo hã. Emegbe Abner yi ɖagblɔ nu siwo katã dzi Israel kple Benyamin ƒe aƒe blibo la lɔ̃ ɖo la na David le Hebron.
ENGLISH: 19 And Abner also passed the word to Benjamin, and Abner also went to bring word to David at Hebron of all that had been agreed to by Israel and by all the house of Benjamin.

EWE: 20 Esi Abner kple ŋutsu blaeve siwo le eŋu la va David gbɔ le Hebron la, David ɖo kplɔ̃ na Abner kple eŋumeawo.
ENGLISH: 20 And Abner came to David at Hebron with twenty men, and David gave a banquet to Abner and the men who were with him;

EWE: 21 Eye Abner gblɔ na David be: “Na mayi aɖaƒo Israel blibo la katã nu ƒu ɖe nye aƒetɔ fia ŋu, ne woabla nu kpli wò, ne nànye fia ɖe nu sia nu si nèdi la dzi.”
ENGLISH: 21 and Abner said to David “I am going to bring all Israel together to your majesty to exchange pledges with you, and you shall be king with absolute power”; and David dismissed Abner, and he went away on friendly terms.

EWE: Eya ta David do mɔ Abner wòdzo le ŋutifafa me. 22 Ɣemaɣi tututu la, David ƒe dɔlawo kple Yoab yi ɖadze ame aɖewo dzi trɔ gbɔna, eye wohe aboyonu geɖe gbɔe.
ENGLISH: 22 And in came David’s soldiers and Joab from a raid, bringing a great deal of plunder with them; but Abner was not in Hebron with David, because David had dismissed him and he had gone away on friendly terms.

EWE: Ke Abner megale David gbɔ le Hebron o, elabena edo mɔe wòdzo yina le ŋutifafa me. 23 Esi Yoab kple eŋumeawo gbɔ la, wogblɔ na Yoab be: “Abner, Ner vi, va fia la gbɔ, eye wòdo mɔe wòdzo yina le ŋutifafa me.”
ENGLISH: 23 And when Joab and all the forces that were with him came in, they told Joab “Abner has been to the king, and he has dismissed him and he has gone away on friendly terms.”

EWE: 24 Eye Yoab yi fia la gbɔ gblɔ be: “Nu kae nye esi nèwɔ? Abner va gbɔwò. Nu ka tae nèdo mɔe wòdzo nenema ko?
ENGLISH: 24 And Joab went to the king and said “What have you been doing? here Abner came to you, why did you dismiss him and let him go off?

EWE: 25 Ènya Abner, Ner vi la nyuie, ɖe wòva be yeava ble wò, ne yeanya wò afɔɖeɖewo ahanya nu siwo katã wɔm nèle.”
ENGLISH: 25 you know Abner the son of Ner, and that he came to inveigle you and to find out your goings out and your comings in, and to find out everything that you are doing.”

EWE: 26 Eya ta Yoab dzo le David gbɔ hedɔ ame ɖo ɖe Abner yome, eye wotrɔe tso Sira tsido la gbɔ gbɔe; gake David ya menya o.
ENGLISH: 26 And Joab went out from David’s presence and sent messengers after Abner, and they brought him back from the cistern of Sirah without David’s knowledge.

EWE: 27 Esi Abner trɔ va Hebron la, Yoab ɖe kpɔe woge ɖe dugbo la me be yeaƒo nu kplii. Ke eƒo yi ɖe dɔme nɛ le afi ma wòku le esi wòwu nɔvia Asahel ta.
ENGLISH: 27 So Abner came back to Hebron, and Joab took him aside into the recess of the gate to speak with him quietly, and there with a thrust below the waist he stabbed him to death for the blood of his brother ʽAsahel.

EWE: 28 Esi David see emegbe la, egblɔ be: “Nye kple nye fiaɖuƒe míeɖi fɔ le Abner, Ner vi, ƒe ʋu me o le Yehowa ŋkume tegbee.
ENGLISH: 28 And David heard of it afterward, and said “I and my kingdom will be innocent of the blood of Abner the son of Ner before Jehovah forever;

EWE: 29 Netrɔ va Yoab ƒe ta kple fofoa ƒe aƒe blibo la dzi. Eye ŋutsu afuɖɔla alo kpodɔléla alo ŋutsu ɖetitrela alo ame si tsi yi nu loo alo dɔwuitɔ nu megatso le Yoab ƒe me o!”
ENGLISH: 29 may it light on the head of Joab and on all his kin, and may Joab’s family never be without men infected with discharges and leprosy, and men that take to the spindle, and men that fall by the sword, and men that lack bread,”

EWE: 30 Ale Yoab kple nɔvia Abisai wu Abner elabena ewu wo nɔvi Asahel le aʋa me le Gibeon.
ENGLISH: 30 Joab and his brother Abishai having killed Abner because he was the death of their brother ʽAsahel in battle at Gibeon.

EWE: 31 Eye David gblɔ na Yoab kple ame siwo katã le eŋu la be: “Midze miaƒe awuwo, mita akpanya, eye mifa konyi le Abner ta.” Eye Fia David ŋutɔ gɔ̃ hã dze amekukugba la yome.
ENGLISH: 31 And David said to Joab and to all the people that were with him “Tear your garments and tie sackcloths around your waists, and wail before Abner”; and King David walked behind the bier.

EWE: 32 Woɖi Abner ɖe Hebron; eye fia la fa avi hehehe le Abner ƒe yɔdo to, eye ameha la hã fa avi sesĩe.
ENGLISH: 32 And they buried Abner in Hebron; and the king raised his voice and wept at Abner’s grave, and all the people wept.

EWE: 33 Eye fia la kpa konyifaha na Abner gblɔ be: “Ðe Abner aku abe yakame enea?
ENGLISH: 33 And the king sang a dirge for Abner, “Was Abner to die as a rascal dies?

EWE: 34 Womebla asi na wò o, Eye womede kunyowu afɔ na wò o. Èku abe ale si wokuna ɖe hlɔ̃dolawo si me ene.” Ale ameawo katã gafae ɖe edzi wu.
ENGLISH: 34 Your hands were not bound, nor your feet brought to the shackles: as one falls before ruffians you fell”; and all the people wept again over him.

EWE: 35 Emegbe ameha blibo la tsɔ abolo vɛ na David esi zã medo haɖe o be woafa akɔ nɛ, ke David ka atam be: “Mawu nefiam, eye wòagafiam ɖe edzi, ne made abolo alo nu bubu aɖe nu me hafi ɣe naɖo to fĩ!”
ENGLISH: 35 And all the people came to get David to take bread while it was yet day; and David said “God do so to me, and more, if before the sun sets I taste bread or anything at all.”

EWE: 36 Eye ameha la katã kpɔe, eye wòdze wo ŋu. Nu sia nu si fia la wɔ la dze ameha la ŋu.
ENGLISH: 36 And all the people understood, and it pleased them: like everything that the king did, it pleased all the people.

EWE: 37 Ameha la katã kple Israel blibo la dze sii gbe ma gbe be, menye fia la gbɔ wòtso be wowu Abner, Ner vi la o.
ENGLISH: 37 And all the people, and all Israel, knew that day that it was not a plan of the king’s to kill Abner the son of Ner.

EWE: 38 Eye fia la gblɔ na eŋumewo be: “Ðe mienyae be amegã kple ame ŋkuta aɖee ku egbea le Israel oa?
ENGLISH: 38 And the king said to his servants “Do you not know that one of the chieftains and great men of Israel has fallen today?

EWE: 39 Togbɔ be nyee wosi ami na mezu fia hã la, megbɔdzɔ egbea, Zeruya viŋutsu siawo sesẽ nam akpa. Yehowa neɖo eteƒe na vɔ̃wɔla ɖe eƒe nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ la nu.”
ENGLISH: 39 And I today am David, and anointed king, but these men, the sons of Serujah, are too much for me: Jehovah repay the criminal appropriately to his crime.”

EWE: 2 Samuel
ENGLISH: 2 Samuel

EWE: 4 Esi Saul vi Is-Boset se be Abner ku le Hebron la, dzi ɖe le eƒo, eye dzidzi ƒo Israel-viwo katã.
ENGLISH: 4 And Ishbaal the son of Saul heard that Abner had come to his death in Hebron, and he lost heart, and all Israel were in consternation.

EWE: 2 Ke ŋutsu eve, siwo nye adzohawo ƒe tatɔwo, le Saul vi la si: ɖeka ŋkɔe nye Baana, eye evelia ŋkɔe nye Rekab. Wonye Beerottɔ Rimon viwo tso Benyamin ƒomea me. (Elabena wobua Beerot hã kpena ɖe Benyamin ŋu tsã.
ENGLISH: 2 And there were two men whom Ishbaal the son of Saul had as captains of raiders, one named Baʽanah and the other named Recab, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite (of the sons of Benjamin; Beeroth too is counted as belonging to Benjamin,

EWE: 3 Ke Beerottɔwo si yi Gitayim, eye wozu amedzrowo le afi ma va se ɖe egbe sia.)
ENGLISH: 3 and the Beerothites have fled away to Gittaim and are living there as immigrants to this day).

EWE: 4 Ke viŋutsu aɖe le Saul vi Yonatan si, si ƒe atawo tu. Exɔ ƒe atɔ̃, esime du tso Yezreel va le Saul kple Yonatan ŋuti, eye edzikpɔla kɔe si, eye esi wòle kplakplakpla dzi le sisim la, ɖevi la ge, eye wòzu wɔmetɔ.
ENGLISH: 4 And Jonathan the son of Saul had a crippled son: he was five years old when the news about Saul and Jonathan came from Jezreʽel, and his nurse took him up and fled, and with her haste to flee he fell and was lamed; and his name was Meribaal.

EWE: Eŋkɔe nye Mefiboset. 5 Ke Beerottɔ Rimon viwo, Rekab kple Baana, yi Is-Boset ƒe me le ŋdɔkutsu dzatsɛ, esi wònɔ ŋdɔlɔ̃ dɔm.
ENGLISH: 5 And the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Recab and Baʽanah, went and entered Ishbaal’s house at the hottest part of the day, while he was lying down for his noon rest:

EWE: 6 Woyi aƒea me abe ame siwo gbɔna lu tsɔ ge ene, eye woƒo nu ɖe dɔme nɛ; ke Rekab kple nɔvia Baana si dzo.
