EWE: 2 Wokpɔ woŋlɔ ɖe agbalẽa me be, Mordekai ye ʋu go fiaŋume eve, siwo nye Bigtana kple Teres, ame siwo nye agbonudzɔla siwo ɖo nugbe be yewoawu Fia Ahasweros.
ENGLISH: 2 And he had seven sons and three daughters born to him.

EWE: 3 Fia la bia be: “Nu kae wowɔ tsɔ de bubu Mordekai ŋu, eye nu kae wowɔ tsɔ da akpe nɛ le esia ta?” Eye fiaŋume siwo subɔnɛ la ɖo eŋu be: “Womewɔ naneke nɛ o.” 4 Emegbe fia la bia be: “Ame kae le xɔxɔnua?”
ENGLISH: 3 And his stock was seven thousand sheep and goats and three thousand camels and five hundred yoke of cattle and five hundred donkeys, and a very large body of servants; and that man was the largest proprietor among all the Easterners.

EWE: Ke edzɔ be Haman va fiasã ƒe xɔxɔnu gotatɔ la me be yeagblɔ na fia la be woahe Mordekai ɖe ati si yetu nɛ la ŋuti. 5 Eye fia la ƒe dɔlawo ɖo eŋu nɛ be: “Haman ye tɔ ɖe xɔxɔnua.”
ENGLISH: 4 And his sons used to go and make a banquet, one day at each one’s house, and invite their three sisters to eat and drink with them; 5 and when the banquet-days had gone the round Job used to send and hallow them, and the first thing in the morning offer a burnt-offering equal in number to all of them, because Job thought “Maybe my sons sinned and cursed God in their hearts.”

EWE: Eya ta fia la gblɔ be: “Mina wòage ɖe eme.”
ENGLISH: Job was doing things like that all the time.

EWE: 6 Esi Haman ge ɖe eme la, fia la biae be: “Nu kae woawɔ na ŋutsu si ŋu fia di be yeade bubui?”
ENGLISH: 6 And one day the angels came to present themselves before Jehovah, and the Adversary too came among them.

EWE: 7 Eya ta Haman ɖo eŋu na fia la be: “Ŋutsu si ŋu fia di be yeade bubui la,
ENGLISH: 7 And Jehovah said to the Adversary “Where did you come from?”

EWE: 8 woatsɔ fiawu si fia la dona kple sɔ si fia dona, si ƒe ta fiakuku le la avɛ.
ENGLISH: 8 And Jehovah said to the Adversary “Did you take notice of my servant Job? because there is nobody on earth like him, a conscientious and upright man, fearing God and keeping clear of bad actions.”

EWE: 9 Woatsɔ awua kple sɔa ade fia ƒe amegã bubumewo dometɔ ɖeka si, woado awua na ŋutsu si ŋu fia la di be yeade bubui la, eye woana wòado sɔa ato dua ƒe ablɔ me. Eye woanɔ ɣli dom le eŋgɔ be: ‘Alea wowɔ na ŋutsu si ŋu fia la di be yeade bubui lae nye esi.’” 10 Enumake fia la gblɔ na Haman be: “Netsɔ! Tsɔ awua kple sɔa nàwɔ abe ale si tututu nègblɔe ene na Yudatɔ Mordekai si bɔbɔ nɔ fia ƒe agbo nu. Mègana naneke nato le nya siwo katã nègblɔ la me o.”
ENGLISH: 9 And the Adversary answered Jehovah “Is it for nothing that Job is God-fearing? 10 haven’t you kept up a fence all round him and his family and everything that belongs to him, blessed the work of his hands, and his stock have multiplied in the country? 11 but put out your hand and strike everything that belongs to him and see if he will not curse you to your face.”

EWE: 12 Emegbe Mordekai gbugbɔ va fia la ƒe agbo nu, ke Haman ɖe abla yi aƒe me kple nuxaxa, eye wòtsyɔ nu ta.
ENGLISH: 12 And Jehovah said to the Adversary “Here, everything that belongs to him is at your disposal; only do not put out your hand to him.”

EWE: 13 Eye Haman gblɔ nu siwo katã dzɔ ɖe edzi la na srɔ̃a Zeres kple exɔlɔ̃wo katã.
ENGLISH: And the Adversary went out from Jehovah’s presence; 13 and one day when his sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine at their oldest brother’s 14 house a messenger came to Job and said “The cattle were plowing and the donkeys grazing beside them, 15 and the Sheba tribe came down and took them and massacred the men; there was only I that escaped alone to bring you word.” 16 While this one was still speaking the next one came and said “God’s fire fell out of the sky and burned the sheep and goats and the men and ate them up; there was only I that escaped alone to bring you word.” 17 While this one was still speaking the next one came and said “The Chaldeans arranged three columns and raided the camels and took them and massacred the men; there was only I that escaped alone to bring you word.” 18 While this one was still speaking the next one came and said “Your sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine at their oldest brother’s house, 19 and there from across the wilderness came a great wind and hit all four corners of the house, and it fell on the young folks and they are dead; there was only I that escaped alone to bring you word.”

EWE: Eye eƒe nunyalawo kple srɔ̃a Zeres gblɔ nɛ be: “Ne Yuda vidzidzie Mordekai, ame si ŋkume nète toyiyi le nye la, ekema màte ŋu aɖu edzi o, ke boŋ àyi to le eŋkume godoo.”
ENGLISH: 20 And Job stood up and tore his robe and sheared his head, and threw himself on the ground and did reverence 21 and said “Naked I came out of my mother’s body and naked I go back there.

EWE: 14 Esi wokpɔtɔ nɔ nu ƒom kplii la, fiaŋumewo va ɖo, eye wowɔ kaba kplɔ Haman yi kplɔ̃ si Esta ɖo la ŋu.
ENGLISH: Jehovah gave and Jehovah took. Jehovah’s name be blessed!” 22 With all this Job did not sin nor find fault with Jehovah.

EWE: Esta
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 7 Ale fia la kple Haman va kplɔ̃ si Fianyɔnu Esta ɖo la ŋu.
ENGLISH: 2 And one day the angels came to present themselves before Jehovah, and the Adversary too came among them, and presented himself before Jehovah.

EWE: 2 Esi wonɔ kplɔ̃ ŋu nɔ wain nom le ŋkeke evea gbe la, Fia la gabia Esta be: “Fianyɔnu Esta, nu kae nèbe yeabia?
ENGLISH: 2 And Jehovah said to the Adversary “From where did you come?”

EWE: Woatsɔe ana wò. Eye nu ka dim nèle? Ne nye fiaɖuƒea ƒe afã gɔ̃ hãe la, woatsɔe ana wò!”
ENGLISH: And the Adversary answered Jehovah “From ranging through the earth and walking about in it.”

EWE: 3 Eye Fianyɔnu Esta ɖo eŋu be: “Oo fia, ne ève nunye, eye wònyo fia ŋu vavã la, ekema meɖe kuku ɖe nye agbe, eye nàxɔ na nye dukɔ la.
ENGLISH: 3 And Jehovah said to the Adversary “Did you take notice of my servant Job? because there is nobody on earth like him, a conscientious and upright man, fearing God and keeping clear of bad actions; and he still holds on to his principles, and you were trying to influence me to wipe him out for nothing.”

EWE: 4 Elabena wotsɔ nye kple nye dukɔ la dzra, be woatsrɔ̃ mí, woawu mí, eye woagblẽ mía dome.
ENGLISH: 4 And the Adversary answered Jehovah “Skin over skin, and over his person a man will give everything he has.

EWE: Gake mesɔ be woaɖe mɔ ɖe xaxa sia ŋu o, elabena agblẽ nu le fia la ŋu.” 5 Eye Fia Ahasweros bia Fianyɔnu Esta be: “Ame kae?
ENGLISH: 5 But put out your hand and hit his bones and flesh, and see if he will not curse you to your face.”

EWE: Afi kae ame si do dzi be yeawɔ nu sia la le?” 6 Esta gblɔ be: “Adikãtɔ kple futɔ lae nye Haman vɔ̃ɖi sia.”
ENGLISH: 6 And Jehovah said to the Adversary “Here, he is at your disposal; only look out for his life.”

EWE: 7 Ke fia la tso le kplɔ̃a ŋu kple dziku heyi fiasã la ƒe abɔ me, eye Haman hã tso be yeaɖe kuku na Fianyɔnu Esta ɖe yeƒe agbe ta, elabena ekpɔe be fia la ɖo tame be yeahe to na ye.
ENGLISH: 7 And the Adversary went out from Jehovah’s presence and struck Job with a malignant eruption from foot to crown, 8 and he took a piece of broken crockery to scrape himself with.

EWE: 9 Eye Harbona, ame si nye fiaŋumewo dometɔ ɖeka, gblɔ be: “Haman tu ati be yeahe Mordekai, ame si ƒo nu heɖe fia ƒe agbe la ɖe eŋu.
ENGLISH: And as he sat in the ashes 9 his wife said to him “Are you still holding on to your principles? curse God and die.”

EWE: 10 Ale wohe Haman ɖe ati si wòtu ɖe Mordekai ŋu la ŋuti, eye fia ƒe dzikua nu fa.
ENGLISH: 10 But he said to her “You talk as any reprobate would. Are we to accept the good at God’s hands and not accept the bad?”

EWE: Esta
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 8 Gbe ma gbe Fia Ahasweros tsɔ Haman, Yudatɔwo ƒe futɔ la ƒe aƒe na Fianyɔnu Esta; eye Mordekai va fia la ŋkume, elabena Esta gblɔ ale si eya kple Mordekai do ƒomee la nɛ.
ENGLISH: 3 After this Job opened his mouth and cursed his day,

EWE: 2 Eye fia la ɖe eƒe ŋkɔsigɛ, si wòxɔ le Haman si la tsɔ na Mordekai.
ENGLISH: 2 and said

EWE: 3 Esta gaƒo nu kple fia la, eye wòtsyɔ mo anyi ɖe eƒe afɔnu fa avi heɖe kuku bia be wòatrɔ Agagitɔ Haman ƒe tame vɔ̃ kple nugbe si wòɖo ɖe Yudatɔwo ŋu la.
ENGLISH: 3 “Perish the day on which I was to be born, and the night that said ‘A man is conceived’!

EWE: 4 Eye fia la do sikafiatikplɔ la ɖe Esta, eye Esta tso hetɔ ɖe fia la ŋkume.
ENGLISH: 4 Be that day darkness; let God not concern himself with it from above and no brightness beam into it.

EWE: 5 Eye wògblɔ be: “Ne edze fia ŋu, eye wòve nunye, ne nya la sɔ le fia ŋkume, eye nye nu nyo eŋu la, ekema nena woaŋlɔ agbalẽ atsɔ ate fli ɖe agbalẽ siwo tame vɔ̃ ɖola Haman, Agagitɔ Hamedata viŋutsu la ŋlɔ be woatsrɔ̃ Yudatɔ siwo le fiaɖuƒea ƒe nutowo katã me la me.
ENGLISH: 5 Let darkness and gloom claim it, let clouds settle over it, let eclipses overwhelm it.

EWE: 6 Elabena aleke mate ŋu akpɔ vɔ̃ si ava nye dukɔ dzi la teƒe, eye aleke mate ŋu akpɔ nye ƒometɔwo ƒe tsɔtsrɔ̃ teƒe?”
ENGLISH: 6 That night let blackness take; let it not form part of the days of the year nor come into the count of the months.

EWE: 7 Eya ta Fia Ahasweros gblɔ na Fianyɔnu Esta kple Mordekai Yudatɔ la be: “Kpɔ ɖa!
ENGLISH: 7 O be that night bleak and bare, let no jubilation come into it;

EWE: 8 Azɔ miate ŋu aŋlɔ agbalẽ ɖe Yudatɔwo nu ale si nyo mia ŋu le fia ƒe ŋkɔ me, eye miatsɔ fia ƒe ŋkɔsigɛ atre enu, elabena se si woŋlɔ le fia ƒe ŋkɔ me, eye wotsɔ fia ƒe ŋkɔsigɛ tre enu la, womate ŋu atrɔe o.”
ENGLISH: 8 Let day-cursers lay a curse on it, those who are ready to rouse Leviathan.

EWE: 9 Eya ta woyɔ fia la ƒe agbalẽŋlɔlawo ɣemaɣi, le ɣleti etɔ̃lia, si nye Sivan, ƒe ŋkeke blaeve vɔ etɔ̃lia dzi; eye woŋlɔ se siwo katã Mordekai de la ɖe agbalẽ me na Yudatɔwo, nuto gã dziɖulawo, nutodziɖulawo kple amegã siwo le nuto vovovoawo dzi ɖum, tso India va se ɖe Etiopia, siwo le nuto alafa ɖeka blaeve vɔ adrewo me, eye woɖoe ɖe nuto sia nuto le eƒe nuŋɔŋlɔ nu ɖe dukɔ sia dukɔ le eƒe gbegbɔgblɔ me, ɖe Yudatɔwo ŋutɔwo ƒe nuŋɔŋlɔ nu, kple woƒe gbegbɔgblɔ me.
ENGLISH: 9 Let its twilight-stars be dark, let it hope for light and there be none,and let it not descry the eyelashes of the dawn,

EWE: 10 Eŋlɔ agbalẽa le Fia Ahasweros ƒe ŋkɔ me, etsɔ fia ƒe ŋkɔsigɛ tre enu, eye wòtsɔ agbalẽ siwo woŋlɔ la de ame dɔdɔ siwo doa fia ƒe sɔ ɖidu siwo womla ɖe fia ƒe dɔwo wɔwɔ ŋu, si ɖo ɖa.
ENGLISH: 10 Because it did not shut the doors of the body I was in and shut off torment from my eyes.

EWE: 11 Fia la ɖe mɔ na Yudatɔ siwo le du vovovoawo katã me le agbalẽawo me be woaƒo ƒu, aʋli woƒe agbe ta, eye woatsrɔ̃ aʋakɔ alo dukɔ alo nuto si me tɔwo atso ɖe wo ŋu la, eye woawu wo ahaɖe wo ɖa, ɖeviwo kple nyɔnuwo siaa, eye woaha woƒe nuwo.
ENGLISH: 11 Why was I not to die in birth, come out of my mother’s body and perish?

EWE: 12 Woawɔ esia le ŋkeke ɖeka dzi, le Fia Ahasweros ƒe fiaɖuƒea ƒe nutowo katã me, le ɣleti wuievelia, si nye Adar, ƒe ŋkeke wuietɔ̃lia dzi.
ENGLISH: 12 How came it that knees welcomed me, and breasts for me to suck?

EWE: 13 Agbalẽa me nyawo nazu se le nuto vovovoawo katã me.
ENGLISH: 13 For now I should be lying down quiet, asleep and so at rest,

EWE: 14 Ame dɔdɔ siwo doa fia ƒe sɔ ɖiduwo la, wɔ kaba dze mɔ heɖe abla le fia ƒe gbeɖeɖe nu.
ENGLISH: 14 With kings and statesmen of earth who built for themselves sites that lie waste

EWE: Wode se sia le Susan mɔ́ la hã me. 15 Ke Mordekai dzo le fia la ŋkume, ele fiawu si wotsɔ avɔ blɔ kple aklala tɔ la me, eye wòɖɔ sikafiakuku gã aɖe hedo awu ʋlaya si wotsɔ avɔ biɖibiɖi kple aɖabɛ dzĩtɔ tɔ.
ENGLISH: 15 Or with generals who owned gold, who filled their houses with silver,

EWE: Eye dzidzɔ kple aseyetsotso xɔ Susan du la me. 16 Eye wònye gbɔdzɔe, dzidzɔ, aseyetsotso kple bubu na Yudatɔwo.
ENGLISH: 16 Or like an abortion tucked underground I should not exist, like infants that had never seen light.

EWE: 17 Eye le nuto vovovoawo katã kple du vovovo siwo katã me fia la ƒe nya kple eƒe sea de me la, Yudatɔwo kpɔ dzidzɔ, wotso aseye, woɖo kplɔ̃ hetu aglo.
ENGLISH: 17 There wicked men forbear to rage, and there exhausted men rest, 18 Prisoners are at ease together, hear no overseer’s voice. 19 Small and great are there, and a slave is free from his owner.

EWE: Eye anyigbaa dzi nɔlawo dometɔ geɖewo gblɔ be yewozu Yudatɔwo, elabena Yudatɔwo ƒe ŋɔdzi lé wo.
ENGLISH: 21 Who wait for death and it is not there, and hunt more industriously for it than for buried treasure,

EWE: Esta
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 9 Le ɣleti wuievelia, si nye Adar, ƒe ŋkeke wuietɔ̃lia dzi, esime ɣeyiɣi de be woawɔ fia la ƒe nya kple eƒe se la dzi, le ŋkeke si Yudatɔwo ƒe futɔwo nɔ mɔ kpɔm be yewoaɖu wo dzi la, nuwo va trɔ bubui, ale be Yudatɔwo boŋ va ɖu ame siwo lé fu wo la dzi.
ENGLISH: 4 And Eliphaz the Temanite answered

EWE: 2 Yudatɔwo ƒo ƒu ɖe woƒe duwo me le Fia Ahasweros ƒe fiaɖuƒea ƒe nutowo katã me be yewoatu nu kple ame siwo le yewoƒe gbegblẽ dim la, eye ame aɖeke mete ŋu nɔ te ɖe wo nu o, elabena woƒe ŋɔdzi lé dukɔwo katã.
ENGLISH: 2 “Shall we try a word to you? you will be impatient, but who can keep in words?

EWE: 3 Amegã siwo katã le nutoawo me, nuto gã dziɖulawo, nutodziɖulawo kple ame siwo wɔa fia ƒe dɔwo la kpe asi ɖe Yudatɔwo ŋu le esi Mordekai ƒe ŋɔdzi lé wo ta.
ENGLISH: 3 Here you have been schooling many and nerving slack hands;

EWE: 4 Elabena Mordekai zu amegã le fia ƒe aƒe la me, eye eƒe ŋkɔ ɖi de fiaɖuƒe la ƒe nutowo katã me, elabena Mordekai le gã zum ɖe edzi ɖaa.
ENGLISH: 4 Your words set a stumbling man on his feet and you braced failing knees;

EWE: 5 Yudatɔwo tsɔ yi dza woƒe futɔwo katã, wowu wo eye wotsrɔ̃ wo; wowɔ ame siwo lé fu wo la ale si dze wo ŋu.
ENGLISH: 5 Now that it comes to you you are impatient; it touches you and you are disconcerted.

EWE: 6 Le Susan mɔ́ la me la, Yudatɔwo wu ame alafa atɔ̃.
ENGLISH: 6 Is not your piety your reliance and your conscientious life your hope?

EWE: 7 Wowu Parsandata, Dalfon, Aspata,
ENGLISH: 7 Remember: what innocent man has perished, where were upright men annihilated?

EWE: 8 Porata, Adaliya, Aridata,
ENGLISH: 8 As I see it, those who plow villainy and sow trouble reap it;

EWE: 9 Parmasta, Arisai, Aridai kple Waizata,
ENGLISH: 9 They perish by God’s breath, are made an end of by the air from his nostrils.

EWE: 10 ame siwo nye Haman, Hamedata vi si lé fu Yudatɔwo la, ƒe vi ewoawo hã. Gake esi wowu wo la womeha woƒe nuwo o.
ENGLISH: 10 The lion’s roar, the voice of the king of beasts, and the two-year-old lion’s teeth, are broken,

EWE: 11 Wova gblɔ ame siwo wowu le Susan mɔ́ la me gbe ma gbe la ƒe xexlẽme na fia la.
ENGLISH: 11 The great lion perishes for lack of prey, and the lioness’s cubs lose touch with each other.

EWE: 12 Eye fia la gblɔ na Fianyɔnu Esta be: “Yudatɔwo wu amewo le Susan mɔ́ la me, eye wotsrɔ̃ ame alafa atɔ̃ kple Haman viŋutsu ewoawo.
ENGLISH: 12 “And a word once stole upon me, my ear took in a whisper of it,

EWE: Woawɔ edzi.” 13 Esta gblɔ be: “Ne enyo fia ŋu la, ekema wòaɖe mɔ na Yudatɔ siwo le Susan be woawɔ ɖe egbe ƒe se la dzi etsɔ hã; eye woahe Haman viŋutsu ewoawo ɖe ati ŋu.”
ENGLISH: 13 In thoughts brought by night visions when trances fall on men.

EWE: 14 Eya ta fia la ɖe gbe be woawɔe nenema. Wode se le Susan, eye wohe Haman viŋutsu ewoawo ƒe kukuawo ɖe ati ŋu.
ENGLISH: 14 A terror beset me, and a quaking, and terrified every bone in me,

EWE: 15 Yudatɔ siwo le Susan la gaƒo ƒu ake le ɣleti Adar ƒe ŋkeke wuienelia dzi, eye wowu ame alafa etɔ̃ le Susan, gake womeha woƒe nuwo o.
ENGLISH: 15 And a breeze ran over my face, made the hair on my flesh prickle up:

EWE: 16 Ke Yudatɔ susɔe siwo le fiaɖuƒea ƒe nutowo me la ƒo ƒu, eye woʋli woƒe agbe ta.
ENGLISH: 16 It stood there, but I could not make out what it looked like; There was a form before my eyes, I heard a hushed voice:

EWE: 17 Esia va eme le ɣleti Adar ƒe ŋkeke wuietɔ̃lia dzi, wogbɔ ɖe eme le ɣletia ƒe ŋkeke wuienelia dzi, eye wowɔe wòzu kplɔ̃ɖogbe kple dzidzɔkpɔgbe.
ENGLISH: 17 ‘Is a human being to be more in the right than God, a man to be cleaner than his Maker?

EWE: 18 Yudatɔ siwo le Susan la ƒo ƒu le ɣletia ƒe ŋkeke wuietɔ̃lia kple ŋkeke wuienelia dzi, eye wogbɔ ɖe eme le eƒe ŋkeke wuiatɔ̃lia dzi, wowɔe wòzu kplɔ̃ɖogbe kple dzidzɔkpɔgbe.
ENGLISH: 18 Why, he does not trust his own servants and charges his angels with frailties;

EWE: 19 Esia tae Yudatɔ siwo le duviwo me le nuto bubuawo me la wɔ ɣleti Adar ƒe ŋkeke wuienelia wòzu dzidzɔkpɔgbe, kplɔ̃ɖogbe kple aglotugbe, si dzi woɖoa nuɖuɖu ɖe wo nɔewo le.
ENGLISH: 19 How much more those who inhabit houses of clay! such as have their foundations on the earth and are beaten down before a moth,

EWE: 20 Mordekai ŋlɔ nudzɔdzɔ siawo ɖi, eye wòɖo agbalẽ siwo wòŋlɔ la ɖe Yudatɔ siwo katã le Fia Ahasweros ƒe fiaɖuƒea ƒe nutowo katã me, esiwo le kpuiƒe kple didiƒe siaa.
ENGLISH: 20 Between morning and evening they are shattered, are lost for all time without anyone’s noticing it.

EWE: 21 Eɖoe na wo be ɣleti Adar ƒe ŋkeke wuienelia kple eƒe ŋkeke wuiatɔ̃lia nanye ŋkekenyui eye woanɔ eɖum ƒe sia ƒe,
ENGLISH: 21 A fiber pulls out within them and they die unaccountably.’

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: Enye ame dzɔdzɔe si wɔa nuteƒe, evɔ̃a Mawu, eye wòtsri nu vɔ̃ɖi.
ENGLISH: 5 “Call: is there one that will answer you? and to which of the Holy Ones will you turn?

EWE: 2 Wodzi ŋutsuvi adre kple nyɔnuvi etɔ̃ nɛ.
ENGLISH: 2 For vexation kills an ignorant man and jealousy brings a simpleton to death.

EWE: 3 Eƒe lãhawo le alẽ akpe adre, kposɔ akpe etɔ̃, nyi akpe ɖeka kple tedzi alafa atɔ̃ hekpe ɖe subɔvi gbogbo aɖewo ŋu.
ENGLISH: 3 I have seen an ignoramus take root,but suddenly the ground he stood on was lost.

EWE: 4 Viaŋutsuwo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe ɖoa kplɔ̃ le eƒe me le ŋkeke si wòɖo edzi la dzi.
ENGLISH: 4 His sons are far from succor, are overborne in the gate and there is no deliverer;

EWE: 5 Eye ne kplɔ̃ɖoŋkekeawo wu enu keŋ la, Hiob dɔa ame ɖa wòkɔa wo ŋu.
ENGLISH: 5 What they have harvested a hungry man eats, and thirsty men gulp their abundance.

EWE: 6 Eva eme gbe ɖeka be Mawu vavã la ƒe viwo va tsi tsitre ɖe Yehowa ŋkume, eye Satana hã le wo dome va.
ENGLISH: 6 For misfortune does not come out of the earth nor trouble sprout from the soil;

EWE: 7 Eye Yehowa bia Satana be: “Afi kae nètso?”
ENGLISH: 7 For man breeds trouble, and sparks fly high.

EWE: 8 Yehowa bia Satana be: “Èlé ŋku ɖe nye subɔla Hiob ŋua?
ENGLISH: 8 But I would apply to Deity and state my problem to God,

EWE: 9 Satana ɖo eŋu na Yehowa be: “Dzodzroe Hiob vɔ̃a Mawua?
ENGLISH: 9 Who does things great and inscrutable, wonderful things in uncountable number,

EWE: 10 Ðe menye wòe tɔ kpɔ ɖe eya ŋutɔ kple eƒe aƒe kpakple eƒe nuwo katã ŋu godoo va kpe oa?
ENGLISH: 10 Him who gives rain over earth and sends water over all outdoors,

EWE: 11 Gake ne èdo wò asi ɖa gblẽ nu siwo katã le esi dome la, aƒo fi ade wò le wò ŋutɔ wò ŋkume godoo.”
ENGLISH: 11 While he sets lowly men on high and men that wore black mount to triumph;

EWE: 12 Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Satana be: “Kpɔ ɖa, eƒe nuwo katã le asiwò me. Ðeko mègade asi eya ŋutɔ ŋu o!”
ENGLISH: 12 Who frustrates shrewd men’s plans, and their hands do nothing that makes sense;

EWE: 13 Gbe ɖeka esi Hiob viŋutsuwo kple vianyɔnuwo nɔ nu ɖum henɔ wain nom le wo nɔvi tsitsitɔ ƒe aƒe me la,
ENGLISH: 13 Who catches wise men in their own shrewdness, and crafty men’s policy goes rash.

EWE: 14 ame dɔdɔ aɖe va Hiob gbɔ va gblɔ nɛ be: “Nyiawo nɔ agble ŋlɔm, eye tedziawo nɔ gbe ɖum le wo xa,
ENGLISH: 14 In the daytime they meet with darkness and they grope as if in the night at noon,

EWE: 15 kasia, Sabatɔwo va dze wo dzi helé wo, eye wowu subɔviawo kple yi. Nye ɖeka pɛ koe te ŋu si, be mava gblɔe na wò.”
ENGLISH: 15 And he saves from their swords an orphan and from a strong man’s hands a needy man,

EWE: 16 Esi ame sia ganɔ nuƒoƒo dzi la, ame bubu va do hegblɔ be: “Mawu ƒe dzo ge tso dziƒo va dze alẽawo kple subɔviawo dzi hefiã wo keŋkeŋ!
ENGLISH: 16 And the poor man comes to have hope and foul play shuts its mouth.

EWE: 17 Esi ame sia mekpɔ wu eƒe nyaa nu o la, ame bubu va do hegblɔ be: “Kaldeatɔwo ƒe adzoha etɔ̃ va dze kposɔawo dzi helé wo, eye wowu subɔviawo kple yi.
ENGLISH: 17 Happy the man whom God corrects; do not reject Shaddai’s discipline;

EWE: 18 Esi ame sia hã mekpɔ ɖe nu le eƒe nyaa me o la, ame bubu hã va do hegblɔ be: “Viwòŋutsuwo kple viwònyɔnuwo nɔ nu ɖum henɔ wain nom le wo nɔvi tsitsitɔ ƒe aƒe me.
ENGLISH: 18 For he hurts and he bandages, He mangles and his hands heal.

EWE: 19 Kasia, ya sesẽ aɖe ƒo tso gbedzinuto me va lɔ xɔ la ƒe dzogoe eneawo ɖe eme, ale wòmu dze ɖeviawo dzi woku.
ENGLISH: 19 In six distresses he will deliver you and in seven no harm shall touch you;

EWE: Nye ɖeka pɛ koe susɔ, be mava gblɔe na wò.” 20 Ale Hiob tso dze eƒe awu, elũ ta, eye wòbɔbɔ tsyɔ mo anyi
ENGLISH: 20 In famine he will have paid your ransom from death and in war from the power of the sword;

EWE: 21 gblɔ be: “Amama menɔ hafi do tso danye ƒe dɔ me, Eye amamae maganɔ ayi. Yehowae na, eye Yehowae gaxɔe.
ENGLISH: 21 When a tongue scourges, you shall be hidden, and you shall not be afraid of havoc when it comes.

EWE: Woakafu Yehowa ƒe ŋkɔ ɖaa.” 22 Le nu siawo katã me la, Hiob mewɔ nu vɔ̃ alo bu fɔ Mawu be ewɔ nu gbegblẽ o.
ENGLISH: 22 At havoc and at starvation you shall laugh, and of the wild beasts you shall not be afraid, 23 Because you have your pact with the stones of the field and the wild beasts have made peace with you.

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 2 Emegbe esi ŋkeke la ɖo be Mawu vavã la ƒe viwo nava tsi tsitre ɖe Yehowa ŋkume la, Satana hã le wo dome va tɔ ɖe Yehowa ŋkume.
ENGLISH: 6 But Job answered

EWE: 2 Eye Yehowa bia Satana be: “Afi kae nètso?” Satana ɖo eŋu na Yehowa be: “Metso tsatsa ge le anyigba dzi kple tsa ɖi ge le edzi.”
ENGLISH: 2 “If only my vexation were to be weighed and they were to take up my catastrophe altogether on the scales,

EWE: 3 Yehowa bia Satana be: “Èlé ŋku ɖe nye subɔla Hiob ŋua? Ame aɖeke mede enu le anyigba dzi o.
ENGLISH: 3 Because it would then outweigh the sand of the sea! that is why my words were so rash.

EWE: 4 Ke Satana ɖo eŋu na Yehowa be: “Ŋutigbalẽ ɖe ŋutigbalẽ teƒe, eye amegbetɔ atsɔ nu sia nu si le esi la ana ɖe eƒe agbe ta.
ENGLISH: 4 For I have Shaddai’s arrows in me, their poison drinking out my spirit; God’s overwhelmings are in the field against me.

EWE: 5 Gake ne èdo wò asi ɖa ka asi eƒe ƒu kple eƒe ŋutilã ŋu la, aƒo fi ade wò le wò ŋutɔ wò ŋkume godoo.”
ENGLISH: 5 Will a wild ass bray over greensward or a cow moo over its mess of barley?

EWE: 6 Eye Yehowa gblɔ na Satana be: “Kpɔ ɖa, ele asiwò me. Ðeko mègaɖe eƒe agbe ɖa o!”
ENGLISH: 6 Is flour paste to be eaten without salt, or is there flavor in marshmallow?

EWE: 7 Ale Satana dzo le Yehowa ŋkume, eye wòna ƒoƒoe vɔ̃ɖi aɖe te Hiob tso eƒe afɔƒome va se ɖe eƒe dzodome.
ENGLISH: 7 My appetite refuses to touch, loathes my food like the discharges of my disease.

EWE: 8 Eye wòbɔbɔ nɔ dzofi me hetsɔ sonu gaglɛ nɔ ŋuti kumee.
ENGLISH: 8 If only what I ask would come, and God would give what I am hoping for,

EWE: 9 Mlɔeba srɔ̃a gblɔ nɛ be: “Ègalé wò nuteƒewɔwɔ me ɖe asi kokokoa?
ENGLISH: 9 And God would be pleased to fell me, would turn his hand loose and finish me off!

EWE: Gbe Mawu, ne nàku!” 10 Ke egblɔ nɛ be: “Èle nu ƒom abe nyɔnu bometsila ene. Ðe míaxɔ nu nyuiwo tso Mawu vavã la gbɔ, evɔ míaxɔ gbegblẽawo ya oa?”
ENGLISH: 10 And it would yet be my comfort, and I should break away in the pang that he does not spare, because I have never hushed up the say of the Holy One.

EWE: 11 Hiob xɔlɔ̃ etɔ̃, siwo nye Temantɔ Elifaz kple Suatɔ Bildad kpakple Naamatɔ Zofar, wose nya vɔ̃ siwo katã dzɔ ɖe edzi, ale wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe tso enɔƒe va.
ENGLISH: 11 What is my strength, that I should wait? and what is my end, that I should be patient?

EWE: 12 Esi wokpɔe le adzɔge ɖaa la, womekpɔe dze sii o.
ENGLISH: 12 Or is my strength the strength of stones? or is my flesh bronze?

EWE: 13 Eye wobɔbɔ nɔ egbɔ le anyigba ŋkeke adre kple zã adre.
ENGLISH: 13 Or do I have in me no help for myself and are sensible ideas knocked out of me?

EWE: 14 Kple anyigbadzifiawo kpakple woƒe adaŋudelawo,Ame siwo tu teƒe siwo zu aƒedowo fifia la na wo ɖokuiwo,
ENGLISH: 14 One who fails to get friendship from his friend will leave off the fear of Shaddai.

EWE: 15 Alo kple amegã siwo si sika le,Ame siwo ƒe xɔwo me yɔ taŋ kple klosalo.
ENGLISH: 15 My brothers have played false like an arroyo, like a bed of arroyo-streams that run off,

EWE: 16 Alo nu ka tae nyemele abe fugege si le ɣaɣla ene,Abe vidzĩ siwo mekpɔ kekeli aɖeke kpɔ o ene o?
ENGLISH: 16 That are black with winter weather, on which snow goes out of sight;

EWE: 17 Afi mae ame vɔ̃ɖiwo gɔ̃ hã dzudzɔ agbodzedze le;Afi mae ame siwo nu ti kɔ na la le ɖiɖim ɖe eme le.
ENGLISH: 17 At the scorching time they are wiped out; in the heat they disappear from their place;

EWE: 18 Afi mae gamenɔlawo katã ŋu vo le; Womegasea ame siwo zia wo dzi be woawɔ dɔ ƒe bublu o.
ENGLISH: 18 The line of their course twists about, they go up into nothingness and are lost.

EWE: 19 Ame tsɛwo kple ame ŋkutawo siaa sɔ le afi ma, Eye kluvi vo tso eƒe aƒetɔ si me.
ENGLISH: 19 The wayfarers from Teman were looking,the caravans from Sheba were hoping for them;

EWE: 20 Nu ka tae wònaa kekeli ayaɖula,Eye wònaa agbe ame siwo le veve sem helĩhelĩ?
ENGLISH: 20 They were disappointed because they had relied on them; they came to them and were discomfited.

EWE: 21 Nu ka tae ame aɖewo le ku dim, evɔ wògbe vava?
ENGLISH: 21 You have now been the same to me; you see a horror and are afraid.

EWE: 22 Wo ame siwo tsoa aseye, Eye woglina kple dzidzɔ ne wokpɔ ɖiƒe.
ENGLISH: 22 Was I saying ‘Give me’ or ‘Pay a tip for me out of your means

EWE: 23 Nu ka tae wònaa kekeli ŋutsu si ƒe mɔwo bu ɖee, Ame si ŋu Mawu tɔ kpɔ ɖo?
ENGLISH: 23 And get me off out of a foeman’s hands and ransom me out of the hands of ruffians’?

EWE: 24 Elabena hũɖeɖe xɔ ɖe nuɖuɖu teƒe nam, Eye nye ŋeŋe kɔna ɖi abe tsi ene.
ENGLISH: 24 Instruct me and I will be silent; make it clear to me what missteps I have made.

EWE: 25 Elabena nu si dzia ŋɔ nam lae dzɔ ɖe dzinye, Eye nu si vɔ̃m mele la dzɔ ɖe dzinye.
ENGLISH: 25 How telling are frank utterances! but what does correction from you correct?

EWE: 26 Nyemekpɔ ŋutifafa, tomefafa alo gbɔdzɔe aɖeke o, Negbe xaxawo sɔŋ ko.”
ENGLISH: 26 Do you think of correcting talk? but a despairing man’s say amounts to wind.

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 4 Eye Temantɔ Elifaz ɖo eŋu be:
ENGLISH: 7 “Does not a man have a term of duty on earth,and is not his time like a hired hand’s?

EWE: 2 “Ne ame aɖe di be yeagblɔ nya aɖe na wò la, ɖe dzi aku wòa?
ENGLISH: 2 Like a slave panting for a shadow and a hired hand looking forward to his pay,

EWE: Elabena ame kae agbe nuƒoƒo? 3 Nyateƒee èxlɔ̃ nu ame geɖewo, Eye nèdoa ŋusẽ alɔ gblɔdɔwo.
ENGLISH: 3 So I have been assigned moons of futility and nights of trouble are counted off for me.

EWE: 4 Wò nyawo léa ame siwo katã le anyi dzem la ɖe te, Eye nèdoa ŋusẽ klo beliwo.
ENGLISH: 4 When I lie down I think ‘When can I get up?’ evening stretches on, and I have all I can hold of tossing till daybreak.

EWE: 5 Azɔ esi wòdzɔ ɖe dziwò la, eglo wò; Etu wò ŋutɔ azɔ, eye dzi ɖe le ƒowò.
ENGLISH: 5 My flesh is clothed in maggots and clods; my skin sets and liquefies.

EWE: 6 Ðe wò mawuvɔvɔ̃ mena dzi ɖo ƒowò oa?
ENGLISH: 6 My days go faster than a shuttle and come to an end with no sort of hope.

EWE: Ðe wò nuteƒewɔwɔ mena mɔkpɔkpɔ wò oa? 7 Meɖe kuku, bu eŋu kpɔ: Ame maɖifɔ ka nue yi kpɔ?
ENGLISH: 7 Remember, God, that my life is a breath of wind; my eye will never get back to seeing good;

EWE: 8 Nu si mekpɔe nye be, ame siwo dea nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ ƒe agble, Kple ame siwo ƒãa xaxa la, nu ma kee woaŋe.
ENGLISH: 8 The eye of him who is seeing me will not behold me, while your eyes are on me I am gone.

EWE: 9 Mawu ƒe ŋɔtimegbɔgbɔ tsrɔ̃a wo, Eye ne eƒe dziku fla la, wo nu yina.
ENGLISH: 9 A cloud clears up and goes off; just so one who goes down to the world below will never come up.

EWE: 10 Dzata ɖea gbe, eye dzatavi xlɔ̃na, Ke woŋea aɖu na dzata sesẽwo gɔ̃ hã.
ENGLISH: 10 He will never come back to his house and his place will not greet him again.

EWE: 11 Dzata kuna ne mekpɔ nu lé o, Eye dzataviwo kana hlẽna.
ENGLISH: 11 I on my part will not check my mouth, will speak in the distress of my spirit, will protest in the ache of my heart.

EWE: 12 Wotsɔ nya aɖe vɛ nam dzaa, Eye nye to se eŋuti dalĩ.
ENGLISH: 12 Am I a sea, or a sea-monster, that you set a watch over me?

EWE: 13 Le zãŋutega si na nye susu tɔtɔ ŋutɔ la me, Esime amewo yi alɔ̃ me ʋĩi,
ENGLISH: 13 When I think ‘my bed will comfort me, my couch will help carry my grievance,’

EWE: 14 Dzidzi ƒom vevie, Eye ŋɔdzi lém de nye ƒutome ke.
ENGLISH: 14 You dismay me with dreams and overwhelm me with visions,

EWE: 15 Gbɔgbɔ aɖe va to ŋkunyeme; Ðadoe ɖo to ɖe ŋunye.
ENGLISH: 15 And my soul chooses strangling, rather death than my woes.

EWE: 16 Etɔ ɖi, Ke nyemekpɔ eƒe nɔnɔme dze sii o. Nɔnɔme aɖe va tɔ ɖe ŋkunyeme; Ðoɖoe zi toŋtoŋ, eye azɔ mese gbe aɖe be:
ENGLISH: 16 I will not take it; I shall not live forever; let me be, because my days are a puff of air.

EWE: 17 ‘Ðe amegbetɔ si kuna ate ŋu anye dzɔdzɔetɔ wu Mawua?
ENGLISH: 17 What is man that you should make much of him and fix your attention on him

EWE: Alo ɖe ame ate ŋu anɔ dzadzɛ wu Ewɔla?’ 18 Kpɔ ɖa!
ENGLISH: 18 And inspect him every morning, test him every moment?

EWE: 19 Ʋuu keke wòahayi anyixɔmenɔlawo, Ame siwo gɔme woɖo anyi ɖe ke me, Eye wogbãa wo bɔbɔe abe agbagblaʋui ene nye gea?
ENGLISH: 19 How long will you never glance away from me, not let up long enough for me to swallow my spittle?

EWE: 20 Wogbãa wo gudugudu tso ŋdi va se ɖe fiẽ; Wo nu yina tegbee, eye ame aɖeke menyana gɔ̃ hã o.
ENGLISH: 20 I sinned; what am I doing to you, Keeper of man? Why do you set me as a thing in your way and have me as a load to carry,

EWE: 21 Ðe womele abe agbadɔ si ƒe kawo wotso ene oa?
ENGLISH: 21 And not pardon my crime and set my guilt aside?

EWE: Wokuna le numanyamanya me.
ENGLISH: For right off I shall be lying in the clay, and you will go in quest of me and I shall not be there.”

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: Kɔkɔetɔawo dometɔ ka ŋue nàtrɔ ɖo?
ENGLISH: 8 And Bildad the Shuhite answered

EWE: 2 Elabena dzikuléle ɖi awu bometsila, Eye ŋubiabiã awu numanyala.
ENGLISH: 2 “Till when will you keep up this talk and shall the words of your mouth be a big wind?

EWE: 3 Nye la, mekpɔ bometsila wòdo ke, Kasia woƒo fi de eƒe aƒe.
ENGLISH: 3 Will Deity play tricks with justice or Shaddai with right?

EWE: 4 Dedienɔnɔ le adzɔge le viawo gbɔ o, Wofanya wo le dugbo la nu, eye xɔnametɔ aɖeke meli na wo o.
ENGLISH: 4 If your sons sinned against him he let them bear the consequences of their crime;

EWE: 5 Dɔwuitɔwo ɖua eƒe nuku si wòxa, Woɖea esi tsi ŋùwo me gɔ̃ hã, Eye mɔ̃ ɖea woƒe nunɔamesiwo.
ENGLISH: 5 If you will direct your quest toward Deity and beseech Shaddai,

EWE: 6 Elabena menye ke mee vɔ̃ miena tso o, Eye menye anyigba tumee xaxa dona tso o.
ENGLISH: 6 If you are pure and right-minded he will rouse for you now and revive your righteous standing,

EWE: 7 Elabena wodzia amegbetɔ be wòakpe hiã, Abe ale si dzoxi dzona yia dzi godoo ene.
ENGLISH: 7 And your past will have been little and your future will be right ample.

EWE: 8 Ne nyee wònye la, anye ne matrɔ ɖe Mawu ŋu, Anye ne matsɔ nye nya ade asi na Mawu,
ENGLISH: 8 For ask a past generation and observe their fathers’ researches,

EWE: 9 Ame si wɔa nu gã siwo me dzodzro meli o, Nu wɔnuku siwo mele xexlẽ me o.
ENGLISH: 9 Because we are yesterday’s growth; we do not know; for our days on earth are a shadow.

EWE: 10 Enaa tsi dzana ɖe anyigba dzi, Eye wòdea tsi gbewo.
ENGLISH: 10 Will not they instruct you, tell you, and bring out words from their hearts?

EWE: 11 Edoa ame tsɛwo ɖe dzi, Eye wòxɔna na blanuilélawo hekɔa wo ɖe dzi.
ENGLISH: 11 Will papyrus stalks make a jungle in anything but a morass? will reeds thrive without water?

EWE: 12 Egblẽa ayetɔwo ƒe ɖoɖowo me, Ale be woƒe asinudɔwo medzea edzi o.
ENGLISH: 12 Still unripe, unplucked, before any grass they dry out.

EWE: 13 Eléa nunyalawo le woawo ŋutɔwo ƒe ayedzedze me, Ale be ame drãwo ƒe ɖoɖowo me gblẽna.
ENGLISH: 13 Such are the paths of all who forget Deity, and the hope of an irreligious man comes to nothing,

EWE: 14 Viviti dona ɖe wo le ŋkeke me, Eye wonɔa asi tsam le ɣeɖota abe zã mee ene.
ENGLISH: 14 One whose reliance is a gossamer and the object of his confidence is a spider’s tent.

EWE: 15 Eɖea wɔnamanɔŋutɔwo tso yi, si le woƒe nu me la nu, Eye wòɖea ame dahe tso ame sesẽ si me,
ENGLISH: 15 He leans on his house and does not stand, takes hold of it and does not get on his feet.

EWE: 16 Ale be mɔkpɔkpɔ va sua ame tsɛ la si, Ke ɖoɖoe zina le ame madzɔmadzɔwo ya nu.
ENGLISH: 16 He is lush before the sun and his runners run out over his garden,

EWE: 17 Kpɔ ɖa! Dzidzɔtɔe nye ame si Mawu kaa mo na; Eya ta mègagbe Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la ƒe amehehe o!
ENGLISH: 17 His roots are matted about a stone-heap, he takes hold of a structure of rocks.

EWE: 18 Elabena enaa ame sea veve, gake eblaa abi la; Egbãa ame, gake eƒe asi daa gbe le eŋu.
ENGLISH: 18 If He annihilates him from his place it will disavow him, ‘I never saw you.’

EWE: 19 Aɖe wò tso xaxa ade me, Eye le adrelia me hã, nu vevi aɖeke mawɔ wò o.
ENGLISH: 19 That is the triumphant climax of his career, and another sprouts up from the ground.

EWE: 20 Aɖe wò tso ku si me le dɔŋɔli, Eye wòaɖe wò tso yi si me le aʋaŋɔli.
ENGLISH: 20 Deity does not repudiate a conscientious man nor lend a hand to evil-doers.

EWE: 21 Aɣla wò tso aɖeɖiƒoame me, Eye ne gbegblẽ va la, màvɔ̃ o.
ENGLISH: 21 He will yet fill your mouth with laughter and your lips with hurrahs.

EWE: 22 Àko gbegblẽ kple dɔwuame, Eye màvɔ̃ anyigbadzilã wɔadãwo o.
ENGLISH: 22 Those who hate you will be wrapped in shame, and wrong-doers’ tent will be nowhere.”

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 6 Eye Hiob ɖo eŋu be:
ENGLISH: 9 But Job answered

EWE: 2 “Ne ɖe woada nye vevesese le nudanu me bliboe Eye woatsɔe akpe ɖe nye fukpekpe ŋu ada le nudanu me ɖe!
ENGLISH: 2 “Certainly, I know it is so, and how is a human being to be in the right with Deity?

EWE: 3 Elabena ele kpekpem fifia wu ƒutake. Esia tae mele nu ƒom kple adã ɖo.
ENGLISH: 3 If he chooses to argue a case with him he will not answer him one point out of a thousand.

EWE: 4 Elabena Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la ƒe aŋutrɔwo ƒo ɖem, Eye nye gbɔgbɔ le woƒe aɖi nom; Mawu ƒe ŋɔdzidodowo tre ɖe nu ɖe ŋunye.
ENGLISH: 4 Wise in heart and mighty in strength, who has defied him and remained safe and sound?

EWE: 5 Ðe gbetedzi xlɔ̃na ne ekpɔ gbe dama le ɖuɖuma, Alo ɖe nyitsu xlɔ̃na ne ekpɔ nu le ɖuɖuma?
ENGLISH: 5 Him who displaces mountains before they know it, as he has overthrown them in his anger;

EWE: 6 Ðe woaɖu nu vɔvɔ dzemadeea, Alo ɖe vivi aɖe le atimitsi mea?
ENGLISH: 6 Him who shakes earth loose from its place and its pillars quiver;

EWE: 7 Megbe asikaka nu siawo ŋu. Wole abe ɖi ene le nye nuɖuɖu me.
ENGLISH: 7 Him who says a thing to the sun and it does not break out, and seals off stars;

EWE: 15 Womate ŋu aɖo dzi ɖe nɔvinyewo ŋu o, elabena wole abe vuvɔŋɔli me tɔʋuwo ene, Abe vuvɔŋɔli me tɔʋu siwo va miena la ene.
ENGLISH: 15 I who if I were in the right would not answer, would beg as a favor for what was my right.

EWE: 16 Tsikpe na wo me blu, Eye sno si nyina bè ɖe wo me.
ENGLISH: 16 If I called and he answered me I would not believe that he would give ear to my voice,

EWE: 17 Ne kuɖiɣi ɖo la, tsi meganɔa wo me o, womiena ƒiaƒiaƒia; Ne dzomeŋɔli ɖo la, wo me ƒuna kplakplakpla.
ENGLISH: 17 He who deals me hurts in a tempest and multiplies my sores for nothing,

EWE: 18 Wotrɔ mɔ na woƒe toƒewo; Wosina yia gbegbe, eye wo nu yina.
ENGLISH: 18 Does not let me get back my breath but gives me all the bitter mouthfuls I can hold.

EWE: 19 Tema-sihawo le ŋu tsam na wo; Saba mɔzɔhawo le mɔ kpɔm na wo.
ENGLISH: 19 As for stark strength, there it is! but as for judgment, who will set me a date?

EWE: 20 Woɖu ŋukpe elabena woƒe mɔkpɔkpɔ zu dzodzro; Wova ɖo afi ma, ke ɖeko woƒe mo wɔ yaa.
ENGLISH: 20 If I am in the right my own mouth will put me in the wrong; I am virtuous and he has made a crook of me.

EWE: 21 Aleae miawo hã miele nam; Miekpɔ ale si gbegbe nye fukpekpea dzi ŋɔe, eye vɔvɔ̃ ɖo mi.
ENGLISH: 21 I am virtuous I do not think of my person I want nothing of my life

EWE: 22 Ðe megblɔ be miana nanem, Alo miatsɔ miaƒe kesinɔnuwo ƒe ɖe anama?
ENGLISH: 22 It is all one; therefore I say, he makes a clean sweep of virtuous man and rogue.

EWE: 23 Ðe mebia be miaɖem tso ketɔ la si me, Alo miaxɔ nam tso ŋutasẽlawo si mea?
ENGLISH: 23 If a scourge brings sudden death he makes fun of innocent men’s despair.

EWE: 24 Mifia num, ekema mazi ɖoɖoe; Vo si meda la, miɖee fiam.
ENGLISH: 24 A country is given into a rogue’s hands; he covers its judges’ faces.

EWE: 25 Nya dzɔdzɔewo mevea ame o ɖe! Ke viɖe kae le miaƒe mokanamewo ŋu?
ENGLISH: 25 And my days are swifter than a runner, have gone off without seeing anything good,

EWE: 26 Nye nyawo ŋue miebe yewoadi vodada lea, Ame si mɔkpɔkpɔ bu ɖo, si le nu ƒom ɖe yamea?
ENGLISH: 26 Have passed like reed boats, like a vulture shooting toward food

EWE: 27 Ekema miadzidze nu ɖe tsyɔ̃evi ya dzi bɔbɔe ŋutɔ, Eye miadzra mia xɔlɔ̃wo gɔ̃ hã bɔbɔe!
ENGLISH: 27 If I say I will forget my grievance, will quit my dismalness and brighten up,

EWE: 28 Azɔ mitrɔ miakpɔm, Elabena nyemada alakpa le mia ŋkume o.
ENGLISH: 28 I quail at all my woes, I know I shall not be acquitted.

EWE: 29 Meɖe kuku, migbugbɔ bu eŋu​ migabu fɔm madzemadzee o​ Ɛ̃, migbugbɔ bu eŋu, nye dzɔdzɔenyenye gakpɔtɔ li.
ENGLISH: 29 I am the one to be found guilty what should I take useless trouble for?

EWE: 30 Ðe nya totro aɖe le nye aɖe dzia?
ENGLISH: 30 If I take a snow bath and clean my hands with alkali,

EWE: Alo ne meɖɔ nu veve kpɔ la, ɖe nyemadze sii oa?
ENGLISH: 31 Then he will dip me in a mudhole and my garments will abominate me.

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 7 “Ðe menye hloloetsotso dzi koe amegbetɔwo le le anyigba dzi oa, Eye ɖe eƒe ŋkekewo mele abe apaɖila ƒe ŋkekewo ene oa?
ENGLISH: 10 My soul loathes being alive; I will quit grieving to myself, I will speak in the ache of my heart.

EWE: 2 Ele vɔvɔli dim vevie abe kluvi ene, Eye wòle eƒe fetu lalam vevie abe apaɖila ene.
ENGLISH: 2 I will say to God ‘Do not declare me guilty, let me know what you are prosecuting me for.

EWE: 3 Ale ɣleti dzodzrowo sɔŋ koe su asinye, Eye zã siwo yɔ fũu kple hiãkame koe wotsɔ nam.
ENGLISH: 3 Does it do you good to deny justice, to repudiate what your hands have toiled on and beam upon the policy of wrong-doers?

EWE: 4 Ne memlɔ anyi la, megblɔna be, ‘Ɣekaɣi gɔ̃e mele fɔfɔ ge?’
ENGLISH: 4 Do you have a mortal’s eyes or see as mankind sees,

EWE: 5 Nye ŋutilã katã dze nyé, eye wòƒo ke; Abi xɔ nye ŋutilã katã ŋu hele tsi tsyɔm yoyoyo.
ENGLISH: 5 Are your days like a human being’s days or your years like a man’s days,

EWE: 6 Nye ŋkekewo le du ɖim wu avɔlɔ̃ʋu, Eye wo nu yi mɔkpɔkpɔ aɖeke manɔmee.
ENGLISH: 6 That you hunt up my guilt and make a search for my sin,

EWE: 7 Ðo ŋku edzi be nye agbe nye ƒuƒu dzro ko, Be nye ŋkuwo magakpɔ dzidzɔ akpɔ gbeɖe o.
ENGLISH: 7 Notwithstanding your knowledge that I shall not prove to be doing wrong and there is nobody to deliver out of your hands?

EWE: 8 Ŋku si kpɔam fifia la magakpɔm azɔ o, Wò ŋkuwo adim, ke nyemanɔ anyi o.
ENGLISH: 8 Your hands molded me and made me; afterward you swing round and wipe me out.

EWE: 9 Ale si alilikpo kakana hebunae la, Nenemae ame si yia Tsiẽƒe la, megagbɔna o.
ENGLISH: 9 Remember that you made me in clay and are putting me back in the loam.

EWE: 10 Magatrɔ ava eƒe aƒe me azɔ o, Eye eƒe nɔƒe magadze sii azɔ o.
ENGLISH: 10 Did you not pour me like milk and curdle me like cheese,

EWE: 11 Eya ta nyemalé nye nu o. Maƒo nu le nye gbɔgbɔ si le nu xam la ta; Mafa konyi le nye vevesese helĩhelĩ la me!
ENGLISH: 11 Clothe me with skin and flesh and frame me with bones and sinews,

EWE: 12 Atsiaƒue menyea, alo ƒumelã klitsue menye, Hafi nèɖo dzɔla ɖe ŋunyea?
ENGLISH: 12 Make life in me, befriend me, and your thoughtfulness guarded my spirit

EWE: 13 Ne megblɔ be, ‘Nye dɔƒe afa akɔ nam; Nye aba aɖe nye dzimaɖitsitsi dzi akpɔtɔ nam la,
ENGLISH: 13 And you had these things hidden in your heart; I know you have had this in mind.

EWE: 14 Ekema ètsɔa drɔ̃ewo doa vɔvɔ̃ nam Eye nètsɔa ŋutegawo doa ŋɔdzi nam,
ENGLISH: 14 If I sinned you would watch me and not acquit me of my guilt;

EWE: 15 Ale be medina be gbɔgbɔ natsi ƒonye, Ɛ̃, be maku wu nye ŋutilã sia.
ENGLISH: 15 If I did wrong, woe to me; or right, I should not lift up my head, Eating my fill of indignities and drinking my fill of misery,

EWE: 16 Menyɔ ŋu nye agbe; nyemegadi be manɔ agbe o. Ðe asi le ŋunye, elabena nye ŋkekewo le abe ƒuƒu ene.
ENGLISH: 16 Or if I bridled up you would hunt me like a lion and come back to your mysterious dealings with me,

EWE: 17 Nu kae amegbetɔ nye, be nàtsɔ ɖe le eme nɛ, Eye nàtsɔ susu aɖo eŋu?
ENGLISH: 17 Confront me with new witnesses and multiply your grievances against me, mobilize fresh divisions against me.

EWE: 18 Nu ka tae nànɔ ŋku lém ɖe eŋu ŋdi sia ŋdi Eye nànɔ edom kpɔ aɖabaƒoƒo sia aɖabaƒoƒo?
ENGLISH: 18 And why did you bring me out of a womb? I should have perished and no eye have seen me,

EWE: 19 Mèle ŋku ɖe ge ɖa le ŋunye oa, Eye mèle asi ɖe ge le ŋunye mami ta teti oa?
ENGLISH: 19 Been as if I had not existed, been taken from mother’s body to grave.

EWE: 20 Ne mewɔ nu vɔ̃ la, nu kae magblẽ le wò, Ame si léa ŋku ɖe amegbetɔwo ŋu la ŋuti?
ENGLISH: 20 Is not my lifetime small? leave off, glance away from me and let me brighten up a little

EWE: 21 Nu ka tae màtsɔ nye dzidadawo ake, Eye màɖe asi le nye vodadawo ŋu o?
ENGLISH: 21 Before I go, never to return, to a land of darkness and gloom,

EWE: Elabena eteƒe madidi o mayi ketu me, Àdim, ke nyemanɔ anyi o.”
ENGLISH: 22 A land of sable dusk, gloom and disorder, that beams sable rays.’”

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 8 Eye Suatɔ Bildad ɖo eŋu be:
ENGLISH: 11 And Sophar the Naʽamathite answered

EWE: 2 “Va se ɖe ɣekaɣi nànɔ nu ƒom alea? Wò numenyawo nye ya ʋuduʋudu sɔŋ ko!
ENGLISH: 2 “Is quantity of talk to go unanswered, or a loose-tongued man to pass for having right on his side?

EWE: 3 Ðe Mawu ate nya dzɔdzɔe ɖe toa, Alo ɖe Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la atrɔ gbo dzɔdzɔenyenyea?
ENGLISH: 3 Are your fine words to silence men, and are you to scoff uncriticized

EWE: 4 Ne viwòwo wɔ nu vɔ̃ ɖe eŋu la, Enana wohea woƒe aglãdzedze ŋuti to na wo;
ENGLISH: 4 And say ‘My doctrine is flawless and I was irreproachable under your eyes’?

EWE: 5 Gake ne ɖe nàtrɔ ɖe Mawu ŋu Eye nàƒo koko na Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la be wòave ye nu,
ENGLISH: 5 But I would that God would speak and open his lips to debate with you,

EWE: 6 Ne ɖe nèle dzadzɛ hele dzɔdzɔe vavã la, Anye ne eɖo to wò xoxo Eye wòagada wò ɖe nɔƒe si nèdze na.
ENGLISH: 6 And tell you the secrets of wisdom, because he is double in sense! Know that God is overlooking part of your guilt!

EWE: 7 Eye togbɔ be wò gɔmedzedze nɔ nyaŋui hã, Àva nye gã le etsɔme.
ENGLISH: 7 Will you explore God or exhaustively investigate Shaddai?

EWE: 8 Taflatsɛ bia nya dzidzime siwo do ŋgɔ, Eye nàlé ŋku ɖe nu siwo ŋu wo fofowo ke ɖo la ŋu kpɔ.
ENGLISH: 8 Higher than the sky what will you do? deeper than the realm of death what will you know?

EWE: 9 Míawo la, etsɔviwo ko míenye, eye míenya naneke o, Elabena vɔvɔli koe míaƒe agbemeŋkekewo nye le anyigba dzi.
ENGLISH: 9 Its measure is longer than the earth and wider than the sky.

EWE: 10 Ðe womafia nu wò Ahagblɔ nu si wonya la na wò oa?
ENGLISH: 10 If he goes past and locks a door and convenes a court, who will turn him back?

EWE: 11 Ðe aƒla atsi nyuie ne mele tsiteƒe oa? Ðe aɖa awɔ nyuie ne mekpɔ tsi oa?
ENGLISH: 11 For he knows paltry men and sees villainy without paying attention.

EWE: 12 Ne metsi ɖo sisi me haɖe o hã, Atre ƒuƒu na gbe bubuawo katã.
ENGLISH: 12 But an empty-headed man gets brains when a wild ass’s colt is born human.

EWE: 13 Aleae wònɔna na ame siwo katã ŋlɔ Mawu be, Elabena ame si mevɔ̃a Mawu o ƒe mɔkpɔkpɔ nu ayi,
ENGLISH: 13 If you condition your heart and spread out your hands to him,

EWE: 14 Eƒe dziɖoɖo ɖe nu ŋu mele ɖeke me o, Eye eƒe ŋuɖoɖeŋu le belii abe yiyiɖɔ ene.
ENGLISH: 14 If there is villainy in your hands put it far away, and let foul play not lodge in your tents,

EWE: 15 Aziɔ ɖe eƒe xɔ ŋu, ke manɔ te o; Adze agbagba be yeaku ɖe eŋu, ke mali ɖi o.
ENGLISH: 15 Why, then you will lift your face out of discredit and be in hard straits and not be afraid,

EWE: 16 Ele abe ati si kpɔ tsi hewɔ nyuie le ɣetotoe nu ene, Eye wòɖe alɔ hevu nyuie le eƒe abɔ me.
ENGLISH: 16 Because you will forget trouble, will remember it like water that has run past,

EWE: 17 Eƒe kewo ɖo wo nɔewo me le kpe siwo li kɔ ɖi la me; Eye wòdia nɔƒe le kpeawo dome.
ENGLISH: 17 Life will stand up to surpass noontime, dusk will be like daybreak,

EWE: 18 Gake ne wohoe ɖa le eteƒe la, Ekema teƒea agbe nu le egbɔ ahagblɔ be, ‘Nyemekpɔ wò kpɔ o.’
ENGLISH: 18 And you will rest assured, because there is hope, will look about at everything and go to bed in security

EWE: 19 Ɛ̃, aleae enu ayii; Eye ati bubuwo amie ɖe eteƒe.
ENGLISH: 19 And lie with no one to alarm you, and many will seek your favor.

EWE: 20 Mawu megbea nu le nuteƒewɔlawo gbɔ o; Eye mekpena ɖe nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔlawo ŋu o, 21 Elabena agana nukoko nayɔ wò nu me fũu Eye wòana aseyetsotso nayɔ wò nuyiwo taŋ.
ENGLISH: 20 But wrong-doers’ eyes will wear out with watching, they will not have any place left to run to, and their hope will be exhaustion of heart.”

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 9 Hiob ɖo eŋu be:
ENGLISH: 12 But Job answered

EWE: 2 “Nyateƒee, menya be nenemae wòle.
ENGLISH: 2 “You are indeed a people with whom wisdom will die!

EWE: 3 Ne ame aɖe di be yeahe nya kplii hã la, Ame ma mate ŋu aɖo nya ɖeka pɛ hã ŋu nɛ le nya akpe dome o.
ENGLISH: 3 I have brains like you, am not inferior to you, and who does not have things like these on hand?

EWE: 4 Dzi nyanu le esi, eye eƒe ŋusẽ tri akɔ. Ame kae ate ŋu adze aglã ɖe eŋu, eye nu vevi mawɔe o?
ENGLISH: 4 ‘A butt for his neighbor’s laughter’ am I, ‘one who called on God and he answered him, an honest conscientious man is a butt.’

EWE: 5 Emlia towo ɖa, ke amewo menyana o; Etrɔa wo bua anyi le eƒe dziku me.
ENGLISH: 5 ‘To the thinking of one who is at ease, disaster is to be pooh-poohed; for one whose foot is giving way it is a solid certainty.’

EWE: 6 Eʋuʋua anyigba le enɔƒe, Ale be eƒe sɔtiwo ʋuʋuna kpekpekpe.
ENGLISH: 6 ‘Marauders’ tents prosper and there is security for those who disturb Deity, for the one who brings God in his hand.’

EWE: 7 Eɖea gbe na ɣe be wòagaklẽ o Eye wòxea ɣletiviwo ŋkume;
ENGLISH: 7 But ask beasts and they will inform you, the birds of the air and they will tell you,

EWE: 8 Eya ɖekae kekea dziƒowo me, Eye wòzɔa ƒutsotsoe kɔkɔwo dzi.
ENGLISH: 8 Or crawlers of the earth and they will inform you, and the fishes of the sea will tell you the story:

EWE: 9 Ewɔ Ayis, Kesil, kple Kima ɣletivihatsotsowo Kple anyiehe ɣletivihatsotsowo;
ENGLISH: 9 Who does not know by all these that Jehovah’s hand made this,

EWE: 10 Ewɔa nu gã siwo me dzodzro meli o, Kple nu wɔnuku siwo mele xexlẽ me o.
ENGLISH: 10 In whose hand is the soul of everything living and the breath of all flesh of men?

EWE: 11 Eto ŋunye va yi, eye nyemete ŋu kpɔe o; Etso eme va yi, ke nyemedze sii o.
ENGLISH: 11 Does not an ear test words and a palate do its tasting of food?

EWE: 12 Ne edu nu le ame si la, ame kae ate ŋu agbe nɛ?
ENGLISH: 12 In graybeards is wisdom, and length of life is intelligence

EWE: 13 Mawu mafa eƒe dziku nu o; Ame siwo naa kpekpeɖeŋu Rahab gɔ̃ hã abɔbɔ ɖe ete.
ENGLISH: 13 With him is wisdom and efficiency, his are skill and intelligence.

EWE: 14 Ke aleke nyea mawɔ aɖo nya ŋu nɛ? Afi kae makpɔ nyawo le atsɔ ahe nya kplii?
ENGLISH: 14 Where he demolishes, there is no rebuilding; he locks a man up and there is no unlocking;

EWE: 15 Ne tɔnye dzɔ hã la, nyemate ŋu aɖo nya ŋu nɛ o.
ENGLISH: 15 When he shuts off the water, it dries out; he lets it loose and it tears up the earth.

EWE: Ðe maƒo koko na nye ʋɔnudrɔ̃la boŋ be wòakpɔ nublanui nam. 16 Ne meyɔe la, ɖe wòatɔ nama?
ENGLISH: 16 With him are might and sagacity; to him belong misled and misleader.

EWE: 17 Elabena etsɔa ahom gbãam gudugudu, Eye wònaa nye abiwo sɔa gbɔ ɖe edzi yakatsyɔ.
ENGLISH: 17 One who sets counselors to going stripped and judges to running wild,

EWE: 18 Ena mede gbɔgbɔ ge do kpoe; Eye wòtsɔa veve yɔa ko nam.
ENGLISH: 18 Undoes kings’ control and ties a loincloth on their waists,

EWE: 19 Ne ŋusẽ ƒe nyae wònye la, ke eyae nye ŋusẽtɔ la.
ENGLISH: 19 One who sets priests to going stripped and upsets immemorial status,

EWE: 20 Ne tɔnye dzɔ la, nye ŋutɔ nye nu abu fɔm; Ne melé nye nuteƒewɔwɔ me ɖe asi hã la, abu fɔm.
ENGLISH: 20 One who makes reliable men’s tongues slip and takes away old men’s sagacity,

EWE: 21 Ne melé nye nuteƒewɔwɔ me ɖe asi hã la, nyemaka ɖe ɖokuinye dzi o; Megbe nu le nye agbe sia gbɔ.
ENGLISH: 21 One who pours contempt on nobles and slackens irresistible men’s girdles,

EWE: 22 Nya ɖeka koe li. Esia tae megblɔna be, ‘Etsrɔ̃a ame maɖifɔ kple ame vɔ̃ɖi siaa.’
ENGLISH: 22 One who unveils abysmal things out of darkness and brings gloom to light,

EWE: 23 Ne tsi aɖɔ kpata awu ame le vo me hã la, Ame maɖifɔwo ƒe xaxa la aɖi kokoe nɛ.
ENGLISH: 23 One who makes nations immense and destroys them, spreads out folk upon folk and leaves them lying,

EWE: 24 Etsɔ anyigba la de asi na ame vɔ̃ɖiwo; Etsyɔa nu ŋku dzi na ʋɔnudrɔ̃la siwo le edzi. Ne menye eyae wɔe o ɖe, ke ame kae?
ENGLISH: 24 One who turns aside the minds of the heads of the populace and sets them wandering in pathless nothingness,

EWE: 25 Nye ŋkekewo le du dzi wu duƒula gɔ̃ hã; Wova yi kabakaba nu nyui aɖeke makpɔmakpɔe.
ENGLISH: 25 Groping in unlighted darkness; and he makes them wander about like a drunken man.

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 10 “Nye agbe le ŋu nyɔm nam. Eya ta matrɔ nye dzimaɖitsitsiwo aƒo ɖi bababa.
ENGLISH: 13 There, my eye has seen everything, my ear has heard and understood it;

EWE: Maƒo nu le nye vevesese helĩhelĩ la ta! 2 Magblɔ na Mawu be: ‘Mègabu fɔm o.
ENGLISH: 2 I too know the same things you know, am not inferior to you.

EWE: 3 Ðe wòaɖe vi aɖe na wò be nàwɔ fu ame, Be nàgbe nu le wò ŋutɔ wò asinudɔwɔwɔ gbɔ Eye nàkpɔ ŋudzedze ɖe ame vɔ̃ɖi boŋ ƒe adaŋudede ŋua?
ENGLISH: 3 But I am speaking to Shaddai and would like to argue with Deity.

EWE: 4 Menye amegbetɔ ƒe ŋkuwoe le asiwò o ɖe!
ENGLISH: 4 But you are whitewashers, quack doctors all of you.

EWE: 5 Ðe wò ŋkekewo le abe amegbetɔ ƒe ŋkekewo enea, Alo ɖe wò ƒewo le abe amegbetɔwo tɔ ene,
ENGLISH: 5 Would that you would hold your tongues so that it should become wisdom for you!

EWE: 6 Be nànɔ nye vodadawo me kum tsitotsito, Eye nànɔ ŋku kem ɖe nye nu vɔ̃wo mea?
ENGLISH: 6 Hear out my argument and listen to the contentions of my lips!

EWE: 7 Ènyae nyuie be nyemeɖi fɔ o; Eye ame aɖeke mate ŋu axɔm le asiwò me o.
ENGLISH: 7 Will you talk unfairly for Deity and stream out fraud for him?

EWE: 8 Wò ŋutɔ wò asiwoe nètsɔ mèm hewɔm, Ke azɔ èbe yeatsrɔ̃m ɖikaa.
ENGLISH: 8 Will you be partial to his side, or champion Deity’s cause?

EWE: 9 Meɖe kuku, ɖo ŋui be anyie nètsɔ mèm, Ke azɔ èna megatrɔ zu anyi.
ENGLISH: 9 Is it a good thing that he should investigate you, or would you hoax him as one hoaxes a man?

EWE: 10 Ðe mètrɔm kɔ ɖi bɔbɔbɔ abe notsi ene, Eye nèna mebla abe notsi babla ene oa?
ENGLISH: 10 He will be calling you to account if you show private partiality.

EWE: 11 Èfa ŋutigbalẽ kple lãkusi ɖe ŋunye, Eye nède ƒuwo menye hetsɔ lãmeka titriwo lɔ̃m kpe.
ENGLISH: 11 Should not his majesty overwhelm you and the dread of him fall upon you?

EWE: 12 Èna agbem eye wò lɔlɔ̃ nam nu metsi o; Eye nètsɔ beléle tɔxɛ dzɔ nye gbɔgbɔ ŋu.
ENGLISH: 12 Your memorable sayings are proverbs of ashes, your shield-bosses turn out to be crockery.

EWE: 13 Evɔ nèɖo nu siawo dzaa be yeawɔ. Menyae nyuie be nu siawo tso gbɔwò.
ENGLISH: 13 Be still, and I will do the talking, come what may.

EWE: 14 Ne mewɔ nu vɔ̃wo la, wò ŋku anɔ ŋunye, Eye màtsɔ nye vodada akem o.
ENGLISH: 14 I will pick up my flesh in my teeth, take my life in my hand.

EWE: 15 Ne meɖi fɔ nyateƒe la, ekema baba nam! Eye ne tɔnye dzɔ hã la, nyemate ŋu afɔ ta dzi o, Elabena vlododo kple fukpekpe yɔm fũu.
ENGLISH: 15 Suppose he slays me: I will not wait, I will just argue my course to his face.

EWE: 16 Ne mefɔ ta dzi la, àɖem ɖe nu abe dzata ene Eye àgaɖe wò ŋusẽ afia ɖe ŋutinye.
ENGLISH: 16 He will become salvation to me too, because an ungodly man will not be admitted before him.

EWE: 17 Àɖo ɖasefo yeyewo ɖe ŋunye Eye àgado dziku ɖe ŋunye ɖe edzi, Ale be fukpekpe natre ɖe fukpekpe nu nam.
ENGLISH: 17 Hear my word, do, and take my demonstration into your ears.

EWE: 18 Ke nu ka tae nèna medo tso vidzidɔ me ya? Ðe wòle be maku hafi, anye ne ŋku aɖeke mekpɔm o.
ENGLISH: 18 Here I have formulated my case: I know I am the one that will turn out to be in the right.

EWE: 19 Anye ne mele abe ame si menɔ agbe kpɔ o ene; Anye ne wotsɔm tso danye ƒe dɔ me yi ɖaɖi.’
ENGLISH: 19 Who will join issue with me? for I would now hold my tongue and pass away.

EWE: 20 Ðe nye ŋkekewo mele ʋɛ oa? Neɖe asi le ŋunye; Neɖe ŋku ɖa le dzinye, ne makpɔ gbɔdzɔe vie,
ENGLISH: 20 Only do not do two things with me, then I will not screen myself from your face:

EWE: 21 Hafi madzo, eye nyemagatrɔ agbɔ o, Hafi mayi anyigba si do viviti tsiɖitsiɖi dzi,
ENGLISH: 21 Take your hand away from me and let your terror not overwhelm me,

EWE: 22 Ayi anyigba si dzi viviti do ɖo tsiɖitsiɖi, Afi si blukɔ kple tɔtɔ le, Afi si kekeli gɔ̃ hã nye blukɔ le.” Hiob 11:1-20 11 Naamatɔ Zofar ɖo eŋu be:
ENGLISH: 22 And call, and I will answer; or I will speak, and return me a reply.

EWE: Ðe ame aɖeke magbe nya na wò ɖe wò alɔmeɖenyawo ta oa?
ENGLISH: 23 How much of guilts and sins do I have? let me know my crime and sin.

EWE: 4 Èle gbɔgblɔm be, ‘Kpɔtsɔtsɔ mele nye nufiamewo ŋu o, Eye medza le ŋkuwòme.’
ENGLISH: 24 Why do you veil your face from me and count me as an enemy of yours?

EWE: 5 Ke hã, ne ɖe Mawu ŋutɔ ake nu, Eye wòaƒo nu na wò ɖe!
ENGLISH: 25 Would you terrorize a driven leaf or chase dry straw,

EWE: 6 Ekema aɖe nunya ŋuti nya ɣaɣlawo afia wò, Elabena nunya vavãtɔ keke ta ŋutɔ.
ENGLISH: 26 That you list bitter things against me and saddle me with the guilts of my boyhood

EWE: 7 Ðe nàte ŋu ake ɖe Mawu ƒe nu goglowo ŋu Alo anya nu sia nu tso Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la ŋua?
ENGLISH: 27 And set my feet in the stocks, and watch all my paths, and mark a line round the soles of my feet

EWE: 8 Ekɔ gbɔ dziƒo ŋu sãsãsã. Nu kae nàte ŋu awɔ?
ENGLISH: 28 And he is like a worn-out water-bag, like a moth-eaten blanket.

EWE: Egoglo kura wu Tsiẽƒe.
14 Ne nu vɔ̃ɖi le asiwò me la, tsɔe ƒu gbe ɖe adzɔge ke, Eye nu madzɔmadzɔ aɖeke meganɔ wò agbadɔ me o.
ENGLISH: 14 “Man, the woman-born, has a scanty lifetime and an overload of difficulties.

EWE: 2 “Nyateƒee, miawo koe nyaa nu, Eye ne mieku ko la, nunya hã nu yi kpli mi!
ENGLISH: 2 Like a flower he came out and wilted, fled away like a shadow and does not stand.

EWE: 3 Nye hã mesea nu gɔme. Nyemebɔbɔ ɖe anyi wu mi o, Ame kae menya nu siawo o?
ENGLISH: 3 Upon even this you open your eyes and summon him to appear against you for trial!

EWE: 4 Mezu alɔmeɖenu na xɔ̃nyewo, Nye, ame si le Mawu yɔm be wòatɔ nam.
ENGLISH: 4 Who shall produce a clean thing out of unclean? not one.

EWE: 5 Ame si le dziɖeɖi me la doa vlo hiãkame, Esusuna be ame siwo ƒe afɔ meli sesĩe o koe hiã tuna.
ENGLISH: 5 If his time is decided, you have his number of months, you have drawn his bounds and he is not to go beyond,

EWE: 6 Adzoblasuwo ƒe agbadɔwo ŋu fa, Eye ame siwo doa dziku na Mawu la le dedie, Ame siwo ƒe mawu le woƒe asiwo me.
ENGLISH: 6 Glance away from him and leave off till, like a hired man, he takes the satisfaction of his day.

EWE: 7 Taflatsɛ, bia lãwo se, eye woafia nu wò; Kple dziƒoxewo hã, eye woagblɔe na wò.
ENGLISH: 7 For there is hope for a tree: if it is cut down, it starts again, and its shoot will not fail to come;

EWE: 8 Alo trɔ ɖe anyigba ŋu, ekema afia nu wò; Eye ƒumelãwo atoe na wò.
ENGLISH: 8 If its root grows old in the ground and its trunk dies in the soil,

EWE: 9 Wo dometɔ kae menya be Yehowa ƒe asie wɔ esia o?
ENGLISH: 9 At the scent of water it will sprout and make a twig like a young tree newly set.

EWE: 10 Eya si mee nu gbagbewo katã ƒe agbe, Kple amegbetɔwo katã ƒe gbɔgbɔ le.
ENGLISH: 10 But a man dies and lies lifeless; a human being breathes his last, and where is he?

EWE: 11 Ðe to medoa nya kpɔna, Abe ale si aɖe ɖɔa nu kpɔna ene oa?
ENGLISH: 11 Water goes away from a sea and a river dries off and out,

EWE: 12 Menye ame tsitsiwo gbɔe nunya tso aƒe ɖo oa? Eye menye agbe didie hea gɔmesese vanɛ oa?
ENGLISH: 12 And a man lies down and will not get up; till the sky wears out they will not wake nor rouse from their sleep.

EWE: 13 Eya sie nunya kple alɔkame sesẽ le; Adaŋudede kple gɔmesese bɔ ɖe esi.
ENGLISH: 13 O that you would stow me away in the world below, screen me till your anger turned back, fix a date for me and remember me!

EWE: 14 Ne egbã nane la, womegatea ŋu tunɛ o; Nu si wòtu la, ame aɖeke mete ŋu ʋunɛ o.
ENGLISH: 14 If a man dies will he come to life? I would wait all the time I had to serve till my relief came;

EWE: 15 Ne eɖo asi tsidzadza dzi la, ku ɖina; Eye ne eɖe asi le eŋu la, eɖɔna ɖea anyigba la.
ENGLISH: 15 You would call and I would answer you; you would have a yearning for the work of your hands.

EWE: 16 Eya sie ŋusẽ kple nunya vavãtɔ le; Eye etɔe ame si tra mɔ kple ame si kplɔ ame trae la siaa nye;
ENGLISH: 16 For then you would be counting my steps, not watching for my sin,

EWE: 17 Enana adaŋudelawo tsia afɔ ƒuƒlu, Eye wònana ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo tsia bome.
ENGLISH: 17 My crime would be packed up under seal, and you would whitewash my guilt.

EWE: 18 Etua ka si fiawo tsɔ bla amewo la ɖa, Eye wòtsɔa alidziblaka blaa ali dzi na wo.
ENGLISH: 18 “But a mountain tumbles down, wears out, and a rock shifts from its place;

EWE: 19 Enana nunɔlawo zɔa afɔ ƒuƒlu, Eye wòɖea zi le ame siwo ƒe ŋusẽ li ke la te;
ENGLISH: 19 Water pulverizes stones; a cloudburst washes away soil; and you have crushed man’s hope.

EWE: 20 Edea ga nu na aɖaŋuɖola bibiwo, Eye wòɖea nunya le tagbɔ na ame tsitsiwo;
ENGLISH: 20 You force him permanently out, and he goes; you change his face and turn him off.

EWE: 21 Etrɔa vlododo kɔna ɖe bubumewo dzi, Eye wònana ŋusẽtɔwo gbɔdzɔna;
ENGLISH: 21 His sons rise to honor and he does not know it, or sink into insignificance and he does not find out about them;

EWE: 22 Eɖea nu goglo siwo le viviti me la ɖe go, Eye wòhea blukɔ vaa kekeli nu;
ENGLISH: 22 Only his flesh feels pain upon himself and his soul is mournful over himself.”

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 13 “Nyateƒee, nye ŋku kpɔ nu siawo katã, Nye towo see eye wose wo gɔme.
ENGLISH: 15 And Eliphaz the Temanite answered

EWE: 2 Nu si mienya la, nye hã menyae; Nyemebɔbɔ ɖe anyi wu mi o.
ENGLISH: 2 “Would a wise man answer with windy ideas and fill himself up with east wind,

EWE: 3 Ke madi be maƒo nu kple Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la ŋutɔ; Madi be maʋli ɖokuinye ta le Mawu gbɔ.
ENGLISH: 3 Arguing with unserviceable talk and useless phrases?

EWE: 4 Ke miele ŋunye gblẽm kple alakpanyawo; Gbedala dzodzrowo mi katã mienye.
ENGLISH: 4 You, besides, are breaking up fear of the Deity and lessening thoughtfulness before him,

EWE: 5 Ne ɖe miazi ɖoɖoe kura la, Anye ne woabui nunyae na mi hafi.
ENGLISH: 5 Because your guilt is tutoring your mouth and you choose artful men’s language.

EWE: 6 Meɖe kuku, mise ɖokuinyenuɖenyawo, Eye milé to ɖe nye nuyiwo ƒe kokoƒoƒowo ŋu.
ENGLISH: 6 Your own mouth shall prove you in the wrong, not I, and your own lips shall testify against you.

EWE: 7 Ðe miagblɔ nya madzɔmadzɔ ɖe Mawu nua, Eye ɖe miaƒo nu alakpatɔe ɖe enua?
ENGLISH: 7 Are you the first of men to be born? were you brought forth before the hills?

EWE: 8 Ðe miebe yewoade edzi, Alo be yewoaxɔ nya ɖe Mawu vavã la nua?
ENGLISH: 8 Did you listen into God’s private conference and sequester some wisdom for yourself?

EWE: 9 Ne edzro mia me kpɔ la, ɖe eme anyo na mia? Alo ɖe miaflui abe ale si woflua amegbetɔ enea?
ENGLISH: 9 What do you know that we do not, perceive that we are not aware of?

EWE: 10 Aka mo na mi godoo, Ne miete kpɔ be yewoade ame dzi le adzame;
ENGLISH: 10 We have among us graybeard and patriarch, further on in years than your father.

EWE: 11 Ðe eƒe gãnyenye mana miadzo haha Eye eƒe ŋɔdzi nalé mi oa?
ENGLISH: 11 Are Deity’s consolations too little for you, and talk that is easy on you?

EWE: 12 Miaƒe nya gã nya gãwo nye lodonya gbɔlowo sɔŋ; Miaƒe ametakpɔnuwo nye anyi dzro ko.
ENGLISH: 12 Why does your heart carry you away, and what do your eyes fasten on,

EWE: 13 Mizi ɖoɖoe le ŋkunyeme, ne maƒo nu. Eye nu sia nu si be yeadzɔ ɖe dzinye la, nedzɔ!
ENGLISH: 13 That you send your breath back to Deity and pour phrases out of your mouth?

EWE: 14 Nu ka tae metsɔ ɖokuinye de afɔku me, Eye metsɔ nye agbe ɖo nye asiƒome?
ENGLISH: 14 What is man that he should be pure and that one born of woman should be in the right?

EWE: 15 Togbɔ be awum hã la, makpɔ esinu; Maʋli ɖokuinye ta le eŋkume.
ENGLISH: 15 Here, he does not put trust in his holy ones and sky is not pure to his eyes,

EWE: 16 Eya koe axɔ nam, Elabena mawumavɔ̃la aɖeke mava eŋkume o.
ENGLISH: 16 To say nothing of an abominable and degenerate being, a man who drinks rascality like water.

EWE: 17 Milé to ɖe nye nyawo ŋu nyuie; Miƒu to anyi miase nye nyagbɔgblɔwo.
ENGLISH: 17 “I will show you; give me a hearing; I have recognized this and will tell you about it,

EWE: 18 Kpɔ ɖa! Metsɔ nye nya va tu anyi; Menyae nyuie be tɔnye adzɔ.
ENGLISH: 18 What wise men state and their fathers have not kept back.

EWE: 19 Ame kae ate ŋu ahe nya kplim? Ðeko maku nenye be mezi kpi!
ENGLISH: 19 They had the country given to them alone, and no stranger came through among them.

EWE: 20 Oo Mawu, nu eve ko biam mele tso asiwò, Ekema nyemaɣla ɖokuinye le ŋkuwòme o:
ENGLISH: 20 All a wrong-doer’s life he is in expectation, the number of years that are laid up for the violent man.

EWE: 21 Ðe wò asi si sẽ ɖe dzinye la ɖa, Eye mègana ŋɔdzi si le ŋuwò la natso dzika ƒo nam o.
ENGLISH: 21 Sounds of dread are in his ears, in peace there is a ravager coming to him;

EWE: 22 Wò ya yɔm ko, ne matɔ na wò; Alo na nye boŋ maƒo nu, ne wò nàɖo eŋu nam.
ENGLISH: 22 He does not count on coming back out of darkness, and he is marked for the sword;

EWE: 23 Agɔ kae medze, eye nu vɔ̃ kae mewɔ? Na manya nye dzidada kple nye nu vɔ̃.
ENGLISH: 23 He has an appointment to be a meal for a kite; he knows his disaster is a settled thing;

EWE: 24 Nu ka tae nèɣla wò ŋkume ɖem, Eye nèle buyem wò futɔe?
ENGLISH: 24 A day of darkness will overwhelm him, distress and hard straits will overpower him, like a king ready for the onslaught,

EWE: 25 Ðe nèbe yeado voɖi na aŋgba dzro si ʋu ya la Alo anya ahɔ̃liti ƒuƒu dzro ɖe nua?
ENGLISH: 25 Because he stretched out his hand against Deity and blustered against Shaddai,

EWE: 26 Elabena èle nutsotso sesẽwo ŋlɔm ɖi ɖe ŋunye, Eye nèna mele nye ɖevime vodadawo ŋuti fe xem.
ENGLISH: 26 Running at him headlong with thick shield-fronts.

EWE: 27 Èbɔ pã nye afɔwo, Èléa ŋku ɖe nye mɔwo katã ŋu tsitotsito; Eye nède dzesi nye afɔɖoƒewo katã.
ENGLISH: 27 Because he covered his face with fat and put on flesh in his waist,

EWE: 28 Eya ta amegbetɔ nyunyɔ abe nu vóvo ene, Abe avɔ si agbagblaʋui ɖu keŋ ene. Hiob 14:1-22 14 “Amegbetɔ nyɔnu tɔ dzidzia, Eƒe agbe le kpuie eye wòyɔ fũu kple fukpekpe.
ENGLISH: 28 And planted himself in extirpated cities, houses that were never to be lived in, which had been made ready to become heaps of stones,

EWE: 4 Ame kae ate ŋu ana ame dzadzɛ nado tso ame si mele dzadzɛ o me? Ame aɖeke mate ŋui o!
ENGLISH: 29 His means shall not be rich, shall not grow up to stalks, shall not bend ears earthward;

EWE: 7 Elabena mɔkpɔkpɔ li na ati gɔ̃ hã. Ne wolãe la, agadze, Eye eƒe alɔwo magbe toto o.
ENGLISH: 30 He shall not get out of darkness; flame shall dry up his shoot, and his buds shall blow off in the wind;

EWE: 8 Ne eƒe ke do xoxo le to me, Eye eƒe takpo ku ɖe to me hã la,
ENGLISH: 31 Let him not trust to rambling futility, for futility will be his purchase;

EWE: 9 Ne tsi nya ʋẽ ɖee ko la, agadze; Eye wòagato alɔ abe ati fẽ ene.
ENGLISH: 32 His fronds shall wither untimely and his new fronds not grow verdant;

EWE: 10 Ke ne ame ku la, wotsɔnɛ mlɔa anyi wɔnamanɔŋutɔe; Ne amegbetɔ mia nu la, afi kae woagakpɔe le?
ENGLISH: 33 He shall blast his berries like a grapevine and drop his blossoms like an olive-tree.

EWE: Womanyɔ o, va se ɖe esime dziƒo nu yi, Eye womanyɔ wo tso woƒe alɔ̃dɔdɔ me o.
ENGLISH: 34 For a godless man’s company is stony ground, and fire has devoured the tents of bribery;

EWE: 14 Ne ame ku la, ɖe wòagagbɔ agbea? Le nye dziziziŋkekewo katã me la, manɔ lalam Va se ɖe esime gbɔdzɔe nava nam.
ENGLISH: 35 There is breeding of trouble and giving birth to villainy, and inside them fraud is shaping up.”

EWE: 15 Àyɔm, eye matɔ na wò.
16 Ke fifia la, èle nye afɔɖeɖewo xexlẽ dzi; Nye nu vɔ̃ ko ŋue nèléa ŋku ɖo.
ENGLISH: 16 But Job answered

EWE: 2 “Ðe nunyala atsɔ nya gbɔlowo sɔŋ aɖo nya ŋua, Alo ɖe wòatsɔ ɣedzeƒeya ayɔ eƒe dɔ mea?
ENGLISH: 2 “I have heard plenty like that; you are plaguy comforters all of you.

EWE: 3 Mokanamenyawo ɖeɖe maɖe vi aɖeke o, Eye tsɔɖui aɖeke mele nuƒoƒo gbɔlo me o.
ENGLISH: 3 Is there any end to windy talk? or what is galling you, that you answer?

EWE: 4 Èna mawuvɔvɔ̃ me gbɔdzɔ, Eye nèna ŋugbledede le Mawu ŋu yi to.
ENGLISH: 4 I too might speak as you do if your souls were in the place of mine; I might string phrases together about you and shake my head over you;

EWE: 5 Elabena wò vodada ye fiaa mɔ nya si nègblɔna, Eye nètia nuƒoƒo ayetɔe.
ENGLISH: 5 I might brace you up with my mouth, and the comfort of my lips might check

EWE: 6 Wò ŋutɔ wò nue le fɔ bum wò, menye nyee o; Wò ŋutɔ wò nuyiwoe nye ɖasefo ɖe ŋuwò.
ENGLISH: 6 If I speak my pain is not checked, and if I refrain what passes away from me?

EWE: 7 Wòe nye ame gbãtɔ wodzi loo, Alo ɖe nètre dzɔdzɔ na togbɛwoa?
ENGLISH: 7 He has just tired me out now; you have laid all my company desolate,

EWE: 8 Ðe nèsea Mawu ƒe nya ɣaɣlawoa, Alo wò ɖeka gbɔ koe nunya tso aƒe ɖoa?
ENGLISH: 8 And you have gripped me, it has become a witness, and my leanness stands up against me, testifies to my face.

EWE: 9 Nu ka koŋ nènya, si míawo ya míenya o? Nu ka gɔmee nèse, si gɔme míawo ya míese o?
ENGLISH: 9 His anger tore me and flung me down; he ground his teeth at me; my foe sharpens his eyes for me.

EWE: 10 Ta ƒowɔ kple amegãɖeɖiwo le mía dome, Ame siwo tsi wu fofowò gɔ̃ hã.
ENGLISH: 10 They have opened their mouths at me, insolently struck my cheeks, collected in full force against me.

EWE: 11 Ðe Mawu ƒe akɔfanyawo, Alo eƒe nya siwo wògblɔ tufafatɔe la, mesɔ gbɔ na wò oa?
ENGLISH: 11 The Deity gives me up to a foul-player and thrusts me into the hands of wrong-doers.

EWE: 12 Nu ka tae nèna wò dzi le blewòm, Eye nu ka tae wò ŋku biã hɛ̃ le dziku me?
ENGLISH: 12 I was in quietness and he jerked me, took me by the back of my neck and burst me, And sets me up for his target,

EWE: 13 Elabena ètrɔ wò dziku ɖe Mawu ŋu, Eye nèna nya siawo tɔgbi le dodom le nuwò.
ENGLISH: 13 his marksmen surround me, And he cuts through my kidneys unsparingly, lets my gall run out on the ground,

EWE: 14 Nu kae amegbetɔ nye, be wòanɔ dzadzɛ, Alo be nyɔnu tɔ dzidzia nanye ame dzɔdzɔe?
ENGLISH: 14 Wounds me with wound across wound, runs at me like a warrior.

EWE: 15 Kpɔ ɖa! Mexɔ eƒe kɔkɔetɔwo ke hã dzi se o, Eye dziƒowo ŋutɔ hã medza le eŋkume o.
ENGLISH: 15 I have stitched a sackcloth on my hide and run my horn into the clay,

EWE: 16 Ʋuu keke wòahayi ame nyɔŋu, ame vlo, Ame si le nu madzɔmadzɔ nom abe tsi ene la nye gea?
ENGLISH: 16 My face is inflamed with weeping and there is gloom over my eyelashes,

EWE: 17 Magblɔe na wò sea; ɖo tom! Na magblɔ nu si teƒe mekpɔ la na wò,
ENGLISH: 17 For no violence that I have on my hands; and my prayer is pure.

EWE: 18 Nu si nunyalawo se tso wo fofowo gbɔ, Eye womeɣla eƒe ɖeke o.
ENGLISH: 18 Earth, do not cover my blood, and let there be no place for my outcry!

EWE: 19 Woawo koe wotsɔ anyigba la na, Eye ame tutɔ aɖeke meto wo dome o.
ENGLISH: 19 Even now my witness is there, in the heavens, and I have my voucher aloft,

EWE: 20 Ame vɔ̃ɖi kpea fuwo ƒe fu le eƒe ŋkekewo katã me, Le ƒe siwo katã wodzra ɖo ɖi na ŋutasẽla la me.
ENGLISH: 20 My friend is my interpreter; to God my eye drips,

EWE: 21 Esea gbeɖiɖi dziŋɔwo le eƒe to me; Adzoblasuwo va dzea edzi le ŋutifafaɣi.
ENGLISH: 21 That he would arbitrate for a man with a God and between a human being and his fellow.

EWE: 22 Mexɔe se be yeasi le viviti la nu o; Elabe yi koe le elalam. 23 Ele tsatsam le nuɖuɖu dim​ afi kae ɖe le?
ENGLISH: 22 For a few years are to come and I shall go on the track I shall not come back on.

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 16 Hiob ɖo eŋu be:
ENGLISH: 17 My spirit is blighted, my days are snuffed out, graves are mine.

EWE: 2 “Mese nya siawo tɔgbi geɖe. Akɔfala siwo doa nuxaxa na ame koe mi katã mienye!
ENGLISH: 2 Decidedly I have triflers about me and my eyes grow tired resting on their ungovernableness.

EWE: 3 Ðe nya gbɔlo siawo nu ava tsoa?
ENGLISH: 3 Give yourself bail for me; who would there be to strike into my hand?

EWE: Nu kae ve wò be nèle nya ŋu ɖom alea? 4 Nye hã mate ŋu aƒo nu abe miawo ke ene.
ENGLISH: 4 For you have kept their hearts closeted from sense; therefore you will not set them on high.

EWE: 5 Gake ɖe matsɔ nye numenyawo ado ŋusẽ mi, Eye nye akɔfanyawo afa dzi na mi boŋ.
ENGLISH: 5 He notifies friends for a share, and his sons’ eyes are worn out with looking and longing.

EWE: 6 Ne meƒo nu la, nye vevesesea dzi maɖe akpɔtɔ o, Eye ne mezi ɖoɖoe hã, ɖe wòafa nama?
ENGLISH: 6 But you have set me up for a byword of peoples, and I am a phenomenon before them,

EWE: 7 Ke azɔ ena wɔna vɔ le ŋunye; Eye wòtsrɔ̃ nye aƒekɔ la katã.
ENGLISH: 7 And my eyes are dim with vexation and my figure dissolves like a shadow.

EWE: 8 Wò asi su dzinye hã, eye wòzu ɖaseɖiɖi, Ale be meɖi ku eye nye kuɖiɖi sia tso hele ɖase ɖim ɖe mo nam kã.
ENGLISH: 8 Upright men will stand aghast at this, and an innocent man be stirred up against an ungodly;

EWE: 9 Eƒe dɔmedzoe vuvum ʋayaʋaya, eye wòlém ɖe dɔme. Eɖua aɖukli ɖe ŋunye.
ENGLISH: 9 But a right-doer will hold his course and a cleanhanded man grow increasingly resolute.

EWE: 10 Woke woƒe nu baa ɖe ŋunye, Eye woƒo tome nam vlodoametɔe; Wolɔ hoo ɖe ŋunye.
ENGLISH: 10 But you may all come again and I shall not find a wise man among you.

EWE: 11 Mawu gblẽm ɖe ŋutsuviwo si me, Eye wòtsɔm de asi na ame vɔ̃ɖiwo.
ENGLISH: 11 My days have gone past; I am annihilated; my heartstrings are snapped.

EWE: 12 Meli bɔkɔɔ, gake egbãm nyanyanya; Elé ʋume nam, eye wòtsɔm xlã ɖi megbã ʋayaʋaya; Etsɔm ɖo nudzidzea na eɖokui.
ENGLISH: 12 They make night into day, ‘light is near, coming away from darkness.’

EWE: 13 Eƒe aŋutrɔdalawo ƒo xlãm; Eŋɔ nye ayikuwo nublanuimakpɔmakpɔe; Egbã nye vevegoe kɔ ɖe anyi.
ENGLISH: 13 If I hope, the realm of death is my house; I have made up my couch in the darkness;

EWE: 14 Eŋɔm flofloflo; Elũ ɖe dzinye abe aʋawɔla ene.
ENGLISH: 14 I have called decay my father, the maggot my mother and sister,

EWE: 15 Metɔ akpanya do, Eye meɖi nye bubu ɖe ke me.
ENGLISH: 15 And where is hope of mine? and who is to behold good fortune of mine?

EWE: 16 Mefa avi ʋuu nye mo do ʋusrã, Eye blukɔ tsyɔ nye aɖabawo dzi,
ENGLISH: 16 Will they go down with me to the realm of death? or shall we go underground together?”

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 18:1-21 18 Suatɔ Bildad ɖo eŋu be:
ENGLISH: 18 And Bildad the Shuhite answered

EWE: 2 “Ɣekaɣi gɔ̃ miadzudzɔ nya siawo gbɔgblɔ?
ENGLISH: 2 “How long will you be snaring phrases?

EWE: Mise nu gɔme, ekema míate ŋu aƒo nu.
ENGLISH: See the point, and afterward we may talk.

EWE: 3 Nu ka ŋuti woabu mí lãwoe, Eye míezu bometsilawo le mia ŋkume?
ENGLISH: 3 How comes it we seem like cattle to your eyes,

EWE: 4 Ne èvuvu ɖokuiwò ʋayɛʋayɛ le wò dɔmedzoe me hã, Ðe woagblẽ anyigba la ɖi le tawò, Alo ɖe agakpe aho le eteƒea?
ENGLISH: 4 you that tear yourself in your anger? Is earth to be forsaken on your account, and a rock shifted from its place?

EWE: 5 Ɛ̃, ame vɔ̃ɖi ƒe akaɖi atsi, Eye eƒe dzo mabi o.
ENGLISH: 5 A wrong-doer’s light does go out, and the blaze of his fire gives no radiance.

EWE: 6 Kekeli si le eƒe agbadɔ me ado viviti, Eye akaɖi si le etame hã atsi.
ENGLISH: 6 Light turns dark in his tent, and his lamp goes out over him.

EWE: 7 Eƒe azɔlizɔzɔ kãkãkã la me agbɔdzɔ, Eye eya ŋutɔ ƒe adaŋudede aƒui anyi.
ENGLISH: 7 His vigorous steps will be cramped and his own purposes will upset him,

EWE: 8 Elabena eƒe afɔ akplɔe ade ɖɔ me, Eye wòazɔ ade afɔ ɖɔkawo me.
ENGLISH: 8 For he runs his feet into a net and walks along on wickerwork.

EWE: 9 Mɔ̃ alé afɔkpodzi nɛ; Mɔ̃ka alée sesĩe.
ENGLISH: 9 A trap will grip his heel and a noose clutch him.

EWE: 10 Woɣla adoboli ɖe anyigba nɛ, Eye wotre mɔ̃ ɖe etoƒe.
ENGLISH: 10 The cord for him is hidden on the earth and the snare for him along the path.

EWE: 11 Ŋɔdzinuwo doa voɖi nɛ le goawo katã me Eye woyɔnɛ ɖe nu kplikplikpli.
ENGLISH: 11 On all sides wraiths overwhelm him and chevy him wherever he goes.

EWE: 12 Ŋusẽ vɔ le eŋu kura, Afɔku ana wòanɔ ya mum sagasaga.
ENGLISH: 12 His vigor is famished and calamity stands ready for his weakening.

EWE: 13 Eƒe lãyi vɔ le eŋu; Dɔléle vɔ̃ɖitɔ kekeake ɖu eƒe abɔwo kple afɔwo.
ENGLISH: 13 His skin is eaten away by disease; the firstborn of death eats his members.

EWE: 14 Wohee do goe le eƒe agbadɔ si me wòle dedie le la me, Eye wokplɔe yi na ŋɔdziwo ƒe fia.
ENGLISH: 14 He is torn out of his tent, what he trusted to, and is marched to the king of wraiths.

EWE: 15 Ame tutɔwoe anɔ eƒe agbadɔ me; Woakaka dzokpe ɖe eƒe aƒe dzi.
ENGLISH: 15 There shall be living in his tent something that is not his; brimstone shall be sprinkled over his lands.

EWE: 16 Eƒe kewo aƒu le to me, Eye eƒe alɔwo ayrɔ le dzi.
ENGLISH: 16 His roots shall die out underneath and his twigs wither overhead.

EWE: 17 Womagaɖo ŋku edzi le anyigba dzi o, Eye woaŋlɔ eƒe ŋkɔ be le ablɔwo me.
ENGLISH: 17 The memory of him is lost from earth and there is no name of his over the wide world.

EWE: 18 Woatu asii tso kekeli me aɖo ɖe viviti me Eye woanyae ɖa le anyigba wɔnu la dzi.
ENGLISH: 18 He is pushed out of light into darkness and sent flitting out of the world.

EWE: 19 Vi alo dzidzime aɖeke manɔ esi le eƒe dukɔ la dome o, Eye ame aɖeke makpɔtɔ nɛ ɖe enɔƒe o.
ENGLISH: 19 He has neither chick nor child among his people nor any survivor in the places he has visited.

EWE: 20 Ne eƒe ŋkeke de la, Ɣetoɖoƒetɔwo ƒe nu aku Eye dzidzi aƒo Ɣedzeƒetɔwo.
ENGLISH: 20 Over the day that comes for him men of the west shall stand aghast and men of the east be taken with a shudder.

EWE: 21 Esiae dzɔna ɖe nu gbegblẽ wɔla ƒe agbadɔ dzi Eye aleae ame si menya Mawu o la ƒe nɔƒe zunae.”
ENGLISH: 21 Altogether such are the dwellings of a malefactor, and like this is the place of one who knows not Deity.”

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 19 Eye Hiob ɖo eŋu bena:
ENGLISH: 19 But Job answered

EWE: 2 “Va se ɖe ɣekaɣie mianɔ nuxaxa dom na nye luʋɔ, Eye miatsɔ nyawo anɔ dzi gbãm nam?
ENGLISH: 2 “How long will you make my soul miserable and beat me down with phrases?

EWE: 3 Zi ewo sɔŋ ye nye esia mieka mo nam; Ŋu mele mia kpem be miele nu tum kplim alea o.
ENGLISH: 3 This is ten times you have been humiliating me, you are not embarrassed to keep saying spiteful things about me.

EWE: 4 Eye ne nyateƒee wònye be meda vo hã la, Dzinyee vodada la anɔ.
ENGLISH: 4 But even take it that I really have made a misstep: it is with me my misstep is lodged.

EWE: 5 Ne vavãe miebe yewoakɔ mia ɖokui ɖe dzi agbɔ tanye, Eye miebe medze na vlododo sia la,
ENGLISH: 5 If you are really taking high ground with me and proving my ignominy against me,

EWE: 6 Ekema minyae be, Mawue kplɔm trae, Eye wòtsɔ eƒe ɖɔ ɖem.
ENGLISH: 6 Know that it is God has done the unfair thing by me and set his toils round me.

EWE: 7 Kpɔ ɖa! Mele ɣli dom be, ‘Ŋutasesẽe!’ ke wometɔ nam o; Mele ɣli dom be woaxɔ nam, ke wometso afia dzɔdzɔe nam o.
ENGLISH: 7 Suppose I cry murder, I am not answered; I shout an appeal and there is no administration of justice.

EWE: 8 Eɖo gli xe mɔ nam, nyemate ŋu aflɔe o; Ena viviti do ɖe nye toƒewo keŋ.
ENGLISH: 8 He has walled off my road and I cannot pass; he has spread darkness over my paths.

EWE: 9 Eklo bubu le ŋunye Eye wòɖe fiakuku le ta nam.
ENGLISH: 9 He has stripped my honor off me and taken away the crown from my head.

EWE: 10 Egbãm kɔ ɖi, eye nunye yi kura; Eye wòho nye mɔkpɔkpɔ abe ati ene.
ENGLISH: 10 He tears down every side of me, and I am gone, and he has cleared away my hope like a piece of timber.

EWE: 11 Eƒe dziku fla ɖe ŋunye, Eye wòle buyem eƒe ketɔe.
ENGLISH: 11 He is angry with me and thinks of me as he does of his foes.

EWE: 12 Eƒe aʋakɔwo ƒo ƒu va ɖe to ɖem, Eye woƒu asaɖa anyi ɖe nye agbadɔ ŋu godoo.
ENGLISH: 12 His raiders come on unitedly and have built their road against me and are camped round my tent.

EWE: 13 Eɖe nye ŋutɔ nɔvinyewo ɖa le ŋunye, Eye nye ame nyanyɛwo trɔ ɖa le ŋunye.
ENGLISH: 13 He has set my brothers to standing aloof from me, and my acquaintances are altogether estranged from me.

EWE: 14 Xɔ̃nye veviwo gɔ̃ hã megali o, Eye ame nyanyɛ kekeake hã ŋlɔm be.
ENGLISH: 14 My nearest and dearest have quit, my housemates have forgotten me,

EWE: 15 Amedzro siwo va dze aƒenye me kple nye kosiwo ke hã le buyem ame tutɔe; Mezu amedzro le wo ŋkume.
ENGLISH: 15 And my serving-maids think me a stranger, I seem to them a foreigner.

EWE: 16 Meyɔ nye dɔla, gake metɔ o; Metsɔ nye nu ɖe kuku nɛ be eƒe dɔme natrɔ ɖe ŋunye.
ENGLISH: 16 I have called my slave and he does not answer I beg him for favors with my own mouth.

EWE: 17 Nye nu me le ya ɖem ɖe srɔ̃nye, Eye mele ʋeʋẽm ɖe nɔvinyewo.
ENGLISH: 17 My breath is hateful to my wife and I smell foul to the sons of my body.

EWE: 18 Ðeviwo ke hã le vlo domem; Ne menya tso ko la, wotea fewuɖuɖu le ŋunye.
ENGLISH: 18 Even children think nothing of me; let me stand up, they talk at me.

EWE: 19 Xɔ̃nye veviwo katã tsrim vevie, Eye ame siwo melɔ̃na la tso ɖe ŋunye.
ENGLISH: 19 All my bosom friends abhor me, and whom I loved have turned on me.

EWE: 20 Nye ŋutigbalẽ kple lãkusi lé ɖe nye ƒuwo ŋu, Eye meku kloe.
ENGLISH: 20 My bones stick to my skin, and I come off with my flesh in my teeth.

EWE: 21 Oo, mi xɔ̃nyewo, mikpɔ nye nublanui, mikpɔ nublanui nam dzro, Elabena Mawue do asi ɖe gbɔnye.
ENGLISH: 21 Be kind to me, be kind to me, you friends of mine, because God’s hand has touched me.

EWE: 22 Nu ka ŋutie miele yonyeme tim abe Mawu ke ene, Hele nu tum kplim madzudzɔmadzudzɔe?
ENGLISH: 22 Why is it you chase me down as Deity does and can never get enough of my flesh?

EWE: 23 Oo, ne ɖe woahaŋlɔ nye nyawo ɖi, Oo, ne ɖe woahade wo agbalẽ me ɖe!
ENGLISH: 23 O that what I have to say were written down, were registered in a document,

EWE: 24 Ne ɖe woatsɔ ganuŋlɔti kple tsumi, Aɖe wo ɖe agakpe dzi tegbee la, ne anyo ŋutɔ!
ENGLISH: 24 With iron pen and lead, carved in rock forevermore!

EWE: 25 Elabena menyae nyuie be nye xɔnametɔ le agbe; Ava mlɔeba, eye wòatɔ ɖe anyigba dzi.
ENGLISH: 25 But as for me, I know my vindicator is alive, and one in future will stand up above ground,

EWE: 26 Togbɔ be nye ŋutigbalẽ gblẽ keŋkeŋ, Evɔ mekpɔtɔ nye ŋutilã hã la, makpɔ Mawu,
ENGLISH: 26 And behind my skin, which has borne this, out of my flesh I shall behold God,

EWE: 27 Nye ŋutɔ makpɔe, Nye ŋutɔ nye ŋkuwo akpɔe, menye ame bubu o. Gake le ememe la eglom!
