ENGLISH: 27 Whom I shall behold for myself; it will be my eyes that saw, and not a stranger my heart is spent in my bosom!

EWE: 28 Elabena miele gbɔgblɔm be, ‘Mɔ ka nue míele eyome tim le?’ Esi miebe nya la ƒe kè le gbɔnye.
ENGLISH: 28 When you think ‘What of his shall we chase down and find ground for a case in him?’

EWE: 29 Yi nedo dzikatsoƒoe na miawo ŋutɔwo, Elabena yi wotsɔna hea toe na vodalawo; Ne mianyae be ʋɔnudrɔ̃la aɖe li.”
ENGLISH: 29 Quail on your own account for fear of a sword, because those are offenses to bring down the sword, so that you may know there is an arbiter.”

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 20 Eye Naamatɔ Zofar ɖo eŋu be:
ENGLISH: 20 And Sophar the Naʽamathite answered

EWE: 2 “Nu siwo le fu ɖem na nye susue ƒoe ɖe nunye be maɖo nya ŋu Elabena metsi dzodzodzoe le ɖokuinye me.
ENGLISH: 2 “For that my thoughts give me response, and by reason of it I am hurried on.

EWE: 3 Mese mokaname aɖe si nye dzu nam; Eye nye nugɔmesese ƒoe ɖe nunye be maɖo eŋu.
ENGLISH: 3 I hear a tutoring that humiliates me and wind rather than sense answers me

EWE: 4 Ðe wòle be nànya esia xoxoxo, Elabena aleae wòle tso esime wowɔ amegbetɔ ɖe anyigba dzi,
ENGLISH: 4 Have you known this from of yore, since man was set on earth?

EWE: 5 Be ame vɔ̃ɖiwo ƒe aseyetsotso nu mesena yina o, Eye be ɣeyiɣi kpui aɖe koe mawumavɔ̃la ƒe dzidzɔ nɔa anyi.
ENGLISH: 5 For wrong-doers’ caroling is shortsighted, and an ungodly man’s merrymaking is momentary.

EWE: 6 Ne eƒe gãnyenye kɔ yi ɖatɔ dziƒo ke, Eye eƒe ta yi ɖatɔ alilikpowo hã la,
ENGLISH: 6 If he lifts his crest to the sky and his head touches the cloud,

EWE: 7 Aɖo agu ɖikaa abe eya ŋutɔ ƒe afɔdzi ene; Ame siwo kpɔnɛ tsã la agblɔ be, ‘Afi kae wòle?’
ENGLISH: 7 Like his dung he perishes utterly; those who saw him say ‘Where is he?’

EWE: 8 Enu ayi abe drɔ̃e ene, eye womagakpɔe o; Abú kura abe zãmeŋutega ene.
ENGLISH: 8 Like a dream he takes wing and one cannot find him; he flits away like a vision of the night.

EWE: 9 Ŋku si kpɔe la magakpɔe akpɔ o, Eye eƒe nɔƒe hã magakpɔe azɔ o.
ENGLISH: 9 An eye has glimpsed him, but does so no more, and his place will not behold him again.

EWE: 10 Viawo adi be ame dahewo nave yewo nu, Eye eya ŋutɔ ƒe asi atrɔ kesinɔnuwo ana amewo.
ENGLISH: 10 His sons must give satisfaction to poor men, his hands give back his goods.

EWE: 11 Ðekakpuimeŋusẽ kpɔtɔ le eƒe ƒuwo ŋu, Ke atsɔe ayi ketu me.
ENGLISH: 11 His bones are full of his virility, but with him it lies down in the clay.

EWE: 12 Ne nu vɔ̃ɖi vivina le nu me nɛ, Eye wòɣlae ɖe eƒe aɖe te,
ENGLISH: 12 If evil is sweet in his mouth, he hides it under his tongue,

EWE: 13 Ne ele enu vivim eye wògbe asiɖeɖe le eŋu Eye wòkpɔtɔ le nu me nɛ hã la,
ENGLISH: 13 Saves it up, will not let go of it, keeps it snug in the roof of his mouth,

EWE: 14 Eƒe nuɖuɖu atrɔ azu veve le dɔ me nɛ; Eye wòatrɔ azu ƒli ƒe aɖi le lãme nɛ.
ENGLISH: 14 His dinner turns in his bowels, he has vipers’ gall within him,

EWE: 15 Emi kesinɔnu, ke adzɔe; Mawu aɖee tso eƒe dɔ me ke.
ENGLISH: 15 He has swallowed wealth but must throw it up, Deity ousts it from his stomach.

EWE: 16 Ano ƒli ƒe aɖi; Eye dzakpata ƒe tsó awui.
ENGLISH: 16 He sucks vipers’ poison, a sand-adder’s tongue will kill him.

EWE: 17 Magakpɔ tɔʋuwo akpɔ o, Magakpɔ tɔʋu siwo me anyitsi kple notsi kpekẽ le sisim le la o.
ENGLISH: 17 He must never look on outflows of oil, streams of honey and clabber.

EWE: 18 Agbugbɔ nu siwo su esi la ana, eye maɖu wo o; Maɖu viɖe si wòkpɔ tso eƒe asitsatsa me o.
ENGLISH: 18 Because of old age he will not swallow what he has spent his strength on, he will not be gay in proportion to the wealth he has traded for,

EWE: 19 Elabena egbã ame dahewo gudugudu hegblẽ wo ɖi; Exɔ aƒe si metso o la sesẽe.
ENGLISH: 19 Because he victimized and abandoned poor men, stole a house, and does no building on it.

EWE: 20 Gake makpɔ gbɔdzɔe aɖeke le eɖokui me o; Eye eƒe kesinɔnuwo maxɔ nɛ o.
ENGLISH: 20 Because he had no quiet in his stomach, in his wishes he let nothing get away,

EWE: 21 Naneke masusɔ nɛ wòaɖu hamham o; Esia tae nu madze edzi nɛ eteƒe nadidi o.
ENGLISH: 21 There was nothing left over from his eating, therefore his good time will not persist.

EWE: 22 Ne nu bɔ ɖe esi kpaŋkpaŋ la, hiã atui; Eye vɔ̃ aƒo ɖe edzi bibibi.
ENGLISH: 22 In his full plenty let him come into distress, all the force of trouble come over him.

EWE: 23 Ne eɖu nu ɖi ƒo la, Ekema Mawu atrɔ eƒe dziku helĩhelĩ akɔ ɖe edzi, Eye wòadudui akɔ ɖe edzi wòaɖo keke eƒe dɔkawo me ke.
ENGLISH: 23 Let him have his bellyful, let Him turn His anger loose on him and shower it on him into his entrails.

EWE: 24 Ne esi le gayibɔlãnuwo nu la, Akɔbliŋutrɔwo aƒo ɖee.
ENGLISH: 24 He takes flight from arms of iron; a bow of bronze drives through him;

EWE: 25 Eho aŋutrɔ si ƒo ɖe dzime nɛ, Ehe lãnu dadzo la doe tso eƒe vevegoe me, Eye ŋɔdzi lée.
ENGLISH: 25 He pulls and it comes out of his back, comes flashing away from his gall.

EWE: 26 Viviti tsiɖitsiɖi le eƒe kesinɔnuwo lalam; Dzo si ame aɖeke meƒlɔ ɖo o la afiãe keŋkeŋ; Eye afɔku dziŋɔ le ame si kpɔtɔ ɖe eƒe agbadɔ me la lalam.
ENGLISH: Terrors are upon him; 26 all darkness lurks for him. Let an unblown fire consume him, feed on survivors in his tent;

EWE: 27 Dziƒo aklo nu le eƒe vodada dzi; Eye anyigba atso ɖe eŋu.
ENGLISH: 27 Let the heavens uncover his guilt and earth be an adversary to him;

EWE: 28 Tsiɖɔɖɔ akplɔ eƒe aƒe adzoe; Tsidzadza gãe wòanye le Mawu ƒe dzikudogbe la.
ENGLISH: 28 Let the progeny of his house be swept out of the country, drifted wreckage on the day of His anger.

EWE: 29 Esiae nye ame vɔ̃ɖi ƒe gome tso Mawu gbɔ, Eƒe domenyinu si Mawu dzra ɖo ɖi nɛ.”
ENGLISH: 29 This is a wicked man’s lot from God, and the estate named for him by Deity.”

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 21 Hiob ɖo eŋu be:
ENGLISH: 21 But Job answered

EWE: 2 “Milé to ɖe nye nyawo ŋu nyuie; Eye mina esia boŋ nanye akɔfafa tso mia gbɔ nam.
ENGLISH: 2 “Do hear what I have to say, and let this be your comforting.

EWE: 3 Migbɔ dzi ɖi nam maƒo nu; Eye ne meƒo nu vɔ la, ekema miate ŋu aɖe alɔme le ŋunye faa.
ENGLISH: 3 Bear me, and I myself will speak; and after I speak you shall make your fun.

EWE: 4 Amegbetɔe mele konyi fam naa? Ne amegbetɔe la, magate ŋu agbɔ dzi ɖia?
ENGLISH: 4 Is my grievance against man? and how should I not be impatient?

EWE: 5 Mitrɔ mo ɖe gbɔnye, miaƒe nu neku; Eye mitsɔ asi ɖo nu.
ENGLISH: 5 Face toward me and stand aghast and lay your hands over your mouths!

EWE: 6 Ne mebu nu sia ŋu la, eɖea fu nam vevie, Eye medzona nyanyanya.
ENGLISH: 6 And if I bethink myself I am in consternation, and a shudder seizes my flesh.

EWE: 7 Nu ka tae ame vɔ̃ɖiwo yia edzi nɔa agbe, Wotsina kua amegã, eye woƒe kesinɔnu dzina ɖe edzi?
ENGLISH: 7 How comes it that wrong-doers live, come to advanced age and are still notably robust?

EWE: 8 Wo viwo nɔa wo ŋu ɣesiaɣi, Eye wokpɔa woƒe dzidzimeviwo.
ENGLISH: 8 Their posterity is firmly established before them; their offspring is numerous under their eyes.

EWE: 9 Woƒe aƒewo le dedie, ŋɔ medzia wo o, Eye Mawu mehea to na wo kple eƒe ameƒoti o.
ENGLISH: 9 Their houses are at peace from dread, and God’s cudgel is not on them.

EWE: 10 Woƒe nyitsuwo meyɔa asi dzodzro o; Woƒe nyinɔwo dzina, eye fu megena le wo ƒo o.
ENGLISH: 10 His bull covers and does not miss, his cow calves and does not slink.

EWE: 11 Wo viŋutsuwo doa go abe lãha ene, Eye wo vi suewo nɔa kpo tim nɔa yiyim.
ENGLISH: 11 They let out their brats like sheep and goats, and their children caper about.

EWE: 12 Wodzia ha ɖe axatsɛ kple saŋku ŋu Eye wonɔa dzidzɔ kpɔm ɖe dze ƒe ɖiɖi ŋu.
ENGLISH: 12 They sing with tambourine and lyre and make merry to the sound of the pipe.

EWE: 13 Woɖua agbe le woƒe agbemeŋkekewo me Eye woyia Tsiẽƒe le ŋutifafa me.
ENGLISH: 13 They wear out their days in comfort, and all of a sudden they go down to the world below.

EWE: 14 Ke wogblɔna na Mawu vavã la be, ‘Ðe asi le mía ŋu!
ENGLISH: 14 And they have said to the Deity ‘Get out of our way, we do not care to know your courses.

EWE: Míedi kura be míanya wò mɔwo o. 15 Ame kae Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la nye, be míasubɔe?
ENGLISH: 15 What is Shaddai that we should worship him, and what good should we do when we invoked him?’

EWE: Viɖe kae wòanye na mí be míadze sii?’ 16 Menyae be woƒe dzidzedzekpɔkpɔ mele woawo ŋutɔwo si me o.
ENGLISH: 16 Here it is not in their hands that their comfort lies, wrong-doers’ principles are far from him

EWE: Ame vɔ̃ɖiwo ƒe adaŋudede metsɔ gbɔnye o. 17 Zi nenie ame vɔ̃ɖiwo ƒe akaɖi tsina? Zi nenie afɔku dzɔna ɖe wo dzi?
ENGLISH: 17 How often do wrong-doers’ lamps go out and their calamity come upon them, cords grip them by his anger,

EWE: 18 Ðe wova le abe gbe ƒuƒu si ya lɔ ɖe nu ene kpɔa, Alo abe tsro si ahom kplɔ dzoe ene kpɔa?
ENGLISH: 18 Do they become like straw before a wind and like chaff that a gale filches?

EWE: 19 Mawu ana vɔ̃wɔla ƒe tohehe natu viawo; Gake Mawu neɖo eteƒe nɛ, ne wòanya ale si wòle.
ENGLISH: 19 Let him not lay his misfortune away for his sons; let him pay it up to himself and let him know it.

EWE: 20 Eya ŋutɔ ƒe ŋkuwo nekpɔ eƒe gbegblẽ teƒe, Eya ŋutɔ neno Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la ƒe dɔmedzoe helĩhelĩ la.
ENGLISH: 20 Let his eyes see his calamity and let him drink ire of Shaddai.

EWE: 21 Elabena ɖe wòagatsɔ ɖe le eƒe aƒemetɔ siwo wògblẽ ɖe megbe la ƒe nya me Nenye be woɖe eƒe dzinuwo ƒe xexlẽme dzi kpɔtɔa?
ENGLISH: 21 For what concern has he for his family after him, when his number of months has been cut off?

EWE: 22 Ðe ame aɖe ate ŋu afia nunya Mawu, Esi wònye eyae drɔ̃a ʋɔnu ame siwo le ɖoƒe kɔkɔwoa?
ENGLISH: 22 Should one teach the Deity knowledge, when it is he judges those on high?

EWE: 23 Ame aɖe ya aku esi wòkpɔtɔ le ŋusẽ blibo me, Esime eƒe tome fa, eye wòɖe dzi ɖi bɔkɔɔ,
ENGLISH: 23 This one dies in perfect soundness, all quiet and at ease,

EWE: 24 Esime eƒe atawo da ami nyuie, Eye ŋusẽ le eƒe ƒuwo ŋu.
ENGLISH: 24 His crocks are full of milk and the marrow of his bones has its drink,

EWE: 25 Gake ame bubu ya anɔ nu xam ʋuu atsɔ akui, Esime eya mese nu nyui aɖeke ƒe vivi kpɔ o.
ENGLISH: 25 And that one dies in bitter soul and has never eaten a comfortable meal;

EWE: 26 Wo kple evea siaa woayi ketu me, Eye nyéviwo anyè atsyɔ wo kple evea dzi.
ENGLISH: 26 Together they lie down on the clay and maggots cover them over.

EWE: 27 Kpɔ ɖa! Menya nu siwo tututu susum miele Kple tame vɔ̃ siwo ɖom miele be miatsɔ adze agɔ le dzinye.
ENGLISH: 27 Here, I know your ideas and such designs as you contemplate against me,

EWE: 28 Elabena miebe, ‘Afi kae ame ŋkuta la ƒe aƒe le, Eye afi kae agbadɔ si me ame vɔ̃ɖiwo nɔ la hã le?’
ENGLISH: 28 That you say ‘Where is an aristocrat’s house? and where are wrong-doers’ dwellings?’

EWE: 29 Ðe miebia nya mɔzɔlawo se kpɔ oa? Eye ɖe miedzro woƒe nuteƒekpɔkpɔwo me nyuie,
ENGLISH: 29 Have you not asked travelers, and do you not recognize their tokens?

EWE: 30 Be wokpɔa ame vɔ̃ɖi ta le vɔ̃dzɔgbe Eye woxɔna nɛ le dɔmedzoedogbe oa?
ENGLISH: 30 That the bad man is kept back on the day of calamity, gets the better of the day of wrath?

EWE: 31 Ame kae aɖe eƒe zɔzɔme agblɔ ɖe mo nɛ kã, Eye ame kae aɖo nu si wòwɔ la teƒe nɛ?
ENGLISH: 31 And who tells him of his course to his face? and if he has done a thing who pays him back?

EWE: 32 Ne wokɔe yi ameɖibɔ me la, Woanɔ eƒe yɔdo ŋu dzɔm.
ENGLISH: 32 And he is brought to burial and his mound is attended to.

EWE: 33 Bali me anyikɔwo avivi enu, Eye ameƒomea katã dze eyome, Abe ame siwo do ŋgɔ nɛ, siwo mele xexlẽ me o la ene.
ENGLISH: 33 Arroyo clods are sweet to him, and all men pour along after him and innumerable before him.

EWE: 34 Nu ka tae miatsɔ nya gbɔlowo anɔ akɔ fam nam? Miaƒe ŋuɖoɖowo nye beble sɔŋ ko!”
ENGLISH: 34 And how are you to comfort me with thin air, when your answers sift down to unreliability?”

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 22 Temantɔ Elifaz ɖo eŋu be:
ENGLISH: 22 And Eliphaz the Temanite answered

EWE: 2 “Ðe ame ate ŋu anye viɖenu na Mawua? Ðe viɖe le ame si si gɔmesese deto le la ŋu nɛa?
ENGLISH: 2 “Is a man to be serviceable to God? why, it is to himself that a capable man is serviceable.

EWE: 3 Ðe Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la tsɔa ɖe le wò dzɔdzɔenyenye mea? Alo ne fɔɖiɖi mele wò zɔzɔme ŋu o la ɖe wòɖea vi nɛa?
ENGLISH: 3 Does Shaddai have any concern that you should do right, or any profit when you follow a conscientious course?

EWE: 4 Ðe wòahe to na wò, Eye wòakplɔ wò ayi ʋɔnui le wò mawuvɔvɔ̃ ta?
ENGLISH: 4 Would it be for your piety that he would reprove you and arraign you for judgment?

EWE: 5 Ðe menye esi wò nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔwo sɔ gbɔ Eye seƒe meli na wò vodadawo o tae oa?
ENGLISH: 5 Is it not that your wickedness is greatand your guilt infinite,

EWE: 6 Elabena èxɔ awɔbanu le nɔviwòwo si yakatsyɔ, Eye nèɖe avɔ le amewo ŋu wotsi ama.
ENGLISH: 6 Because you demand pawns of your brothers without reason and strip off naked men’s garments,

EWE: 7 Mènaa tsi ame siwo ŋu ɖeɖi te la wonona o, Eye nètea abolo dɔwuitɔwo.
ENGLISH: 7 Do not give a drink of water to a fainting man and refuse bread to a hungry man,

EWE: 8 Anyigba la zu ame si si alɔkpa sesẽ le la tɔ, Eye ame ŋkutae nɔa edzi.
ENGLISH: 8 But a strong-handed man has the country for his own, and an influential man is to live in it;

EWE: 9 Ke èɖo ahosiwo ɖa asi gbɔlo, Eye nèna tsyɔ̃eviwo ƒe alɔ me tu.
ENGLISH: 9 You turn widows away empty-handed and batter orphans’ arms?

EWE: 10 Esia tae woɖo mɔ̃ ƒo xlã wò, Eye ŋɔdzi léa wò le vo me;
ENGLISH: 10 That is why there are traps around you and dread throws you into sudden consternation,

EWE: 11 Esia tae viviti do ɖe wò ale gbegbe be mègate ŋu le nu kpɔm o, Eye tɔɖɔɖɔ va tsyɔ dziwò ɖo.
ENGLISH: 11 Light has turned dark for you, you cannot see, and spray of water covers you.

EWE: 12 Ðe Mawu mele dziƒo ʋĩi oa? Eye kpɔ afi si ɣletiviwo katã le ɖa, be wo gbɔ metsɔ o.
ENGLISH: 12 Of course, God stands high in the heavens and sees the heads of the stars, lofty though they be,

EWE: 13 Ke wòa nègblɔ be: ‘Nu ka gɔ̃e Mawu nya? Ðe wòate ŋu akpɔ nu to blukɔ me adrɔ̃ ʋɔnua?
ENGLISH: 13 And you think ‘What does God know? will he judge through thick air?

EWE: 14 Alilikpowo xe eŋkume, ale be mele nu kpɔm o, Ðeko wòɖia tsa le dziƒo gobaa la.’
ENGLISH: 14 Clouds are a screen to him and he will not see; and he will be walking the vault of the heavens.’

EWE: 15 Ðe nèbe yealé mɔ xoxo, Si dzi ame vɔ̃ɖiwo to la me ɖe asia?
ENGLISH: 15 Will you keep to the foul-players’ path, the one villains have trodden,

EWE: 16 Wo, ame siwo wotsrɔ̃ ɖa hafi woƒe ɣeyiɣi de, Ame siwo ƒe gɔmeɖoanyi tsiɖɔɖɔ kplɔ dzoe?
ENGLISH: 16 Who were seized untimely, a river pouring upon their foundation,

EWE: 17 Ame siwo gblɔna na Mawu vavã la be: ‘Ðe asi le mía ŋu!
ENGLISH: 17 Those who said to Deity ‘Get out of our way’ and ‘What should Shaddai do to us?’

EWE: Nu kae Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la ate ŋu awɔ mí?’ 18 Evɔ wònye eyae tsɔ nu nyuiwo yɔ woƒe xɔwo me taŋ hafi.
ENGLISH: 18 When it was he that had filled their houses with good things; wrong-doers’ principles are far from him.

EWE: 19 Ame dzɔdzɔewo akpɔe, eye dzi adzɔ wo, Ame maɖifɔwo aɖe alɔme le wo ŋu be:
ENGLISH: 19 Honest men see and are glad, and an innocent man derides them:

EWE: 20 ‘Wotsrɔ̃ míaƒe ketɔwo ɖa keŋ, Eye dzo afiã woƒe nu susɔewo keŋkeŋ.’
ENGLISH: 20 ‘They are positively annihilated, every mother’s son, and fire has consumed the last remnant of them.’

EWE: 21 Dze xɔlɔ̃e, ne nànɔ ŋutifafa me; Ekema nu nyuiwo asu asiwò.
ENGLISH: 21 Get used to him and on good terms with him; by that what comes to you will be good.

EWE: 22 Xɔ se si do tso eƒe nu me, Eye nàdzra eƒe nyawo ɖo ɖe wò dzi me.
ENGLISH: 22 Take an instruction from his mouth and lodge his say in your heart.

EWE: 23 Ne ètrɔ va Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la gbɔ la, ekema agaɖo wò te; Ne ète nu madzɔmadzɔ wɔwɔ ɖa xaa tso wò agbadɔ gbɔ,
ENGLISH: 23 If you go back to Shaddai, humbling yourself, put foul play far off from your tent,

EWE: 24 Ne ètsɔ wò sika kɔ ɖe ke me, Eye nèkɔ Ofir sika ɖe kpewo me le tɔʋe me la,
ENGLISH: 24 Lay ore in dust and Ophir gold among arroyo rocks,

EWE: 25 Ekema Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la azu sika na wò, Kple klosalo nyuitɔ na wò.
ENGLISH: 25 Then Shaddai will be your nuggets and peak-silver to you.

EWE: 26 Ekema Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la ƒe nu anyo ŋuwò vevie, Eye àwu wò mo dzi na Mawu.
ENGLISH: 26 For then you will be happy over Shaddai and raise your face to God,

EWE: 27 Àƒo koko nɛ, eye wòaɖo to wò; Eye àwɔ wò adzɔgbeɖeɖewo dzi.
ENGLISH: 27 You will invoke him and he will hear you and you will be paying your vows,

EWE: 28 Nu sia nu si nèɖo be yeawɔ la adze edzi na wò, Eye kekeli aklẽ ɖe wò mɔwo dzi.
ENGLISH: 28 And you will decide on a thing and have it hold good for you, and light will be beaming over your paths.

EWE: 29 Elabena ne èƒo nu dadatɔe la, abɔbɔ wò ɖe anyi, Ke axɔ na ame si bɔbɔ eɖokui ɖe anyi.
ENGLISH: 29 For he brings low the lofty and proud man, and the man of downcast eyes he saves.

EWE: 30 Axɔ na ame maɖifɔ la; Eya ta ne wò asi me dza la, ekema axɔ na wò godoo.”
ENGLISH: 30 He will bring to safety one who is not innocent, and he shall be brought to safety by the cleanness of your hands.”

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 23 Hiob ɖo eŋu be:
ENGLISH: 23 But Job answered

EWE: 2 “Egbe hã mato nyatoƒoe; Ŋusẽ vɔ le ŋunye le nye hũɖeɖe ta.
ENGLISH: 2 “Today too my complaint is rebellion! my hand lies heavy on my moans.

EWE: 3 Oo, ne ɖe menya afi si makpɔ Mawu le ɖe!
ENGLISH: 3 If only I knew how to find him, come to his seat!

EWE: 4 Matsɔ nye nya aɖo eŋkume Eye mana nye nu me nayɔ fũu kple ɖokuitaʋlinyawo;
ENGLISH: 4 I would formulate my case before him and fill my mouth with arguments;

EWE: 5 Makpɔ ale si wòaɖo eŋu nam Ne mase nya si wòagblɔ nam.
ENGLISH: 5 I should find out what points he would make in answer to me, should see what he would say to me.

EWE: 6 Ðe wòatsɔ eƒe ŋusẽ triakɔ la awɔ avu kplima? Ao ɖe! Aɖo tom godoo.
ENGLISH: 6 Would he maintain his contention against me by superior strength? not he, he would just pay attention to me.

EWE: 7 Ekema ame dzɔdzɔe aɖɔ wo kplii dome ɖo, Eye nye Ʋɔnudrɔ̃la agblɔ be tɔnye dzɔ, ne nyaa natɔ ɖe afi ma.
ENGLISH: 7 There I should have one who was candid arguing with me, and I should definitively get clear from my judge.

EWE: 8 Gake ne meyi ɣedzeƒe la, mele afi ma o; Ne megatrɔ gbɔ hã, nyemele ekpɔm o.
ENGLISH: 8 Here I go east and he is not there, and west and I do not perceive him,

EWE: 9 Ne ele dɔ wɔm le miame la, nyemate ŋu akpɔe o; Ne edze ɖe ɖusime hã, nyemakpɔe o.
ENGLISH: 9 I look for him in the north and do not behold him, swing round to the south and do not see him,

EWE: 10 Ke hã enya nye mɔwo nyuie. Ne edom kpɔ vɔ la, ŋunye adza abe sika nyuitɔ ene.
ENGLISH: 10 While he knows which way I stand; were he to test me, I should come out like gold.

EWE: 11 Nye afɔ to eƒe toƒewo tututu; Melé ɖe eƒe mɔwo ŋu, eye nyemedze ɖe aga o.
ENGLISH: 11 My foot holds on to his tracks, I watch his course and do not swerve,

EWE: 12 Nyemetrɔ ɖa le se siwo do tso enu la gbɔ o. Medzra eƒe numenyawo ɖo nyuie wu ale si wodi tso asinye.
ENGLISH: 12 From the command of his lips I do not shift, in my bosom I have laid up the say of his mouth.

EWE: 13 Ne eɖo nane be yeawɔ la, ame kae ate ŋu axe mɔ nɛ? Nu si dzroe wòbe yeawɔ la, ewɔnɛ.
ENGLISH: 13 But when he has his mind made up who will turn him back? he hankers and he acts.

EWE: 14 Elabena awɔ nu siwo katã wòɖo ɖe ŋunye la ade goe, Eye nu siawo tɔgbi bɔ ɖe esi.
ENGLISH: 14 For he will go through with what he has marked out for me, and has in store plenty of things like that.

EWE: 15 Esia tae metɔtɔ le eya amea ta; Ne mebu eya amea ŋu la, megavɔ̃nɛ ɖe edzi.
ENGLISH: 15 That is why I am affrighted at him; I realize the situation and stand in dread of him,

EWE: 16 Mawu na dzi ɖe le ƒonye, Eye Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la na vɔvɔ̃ ɖom.
ENGLISH: 16 And Deity has unnerved me and left me terror-struck.

EWE: 17 Gake viviti la mena ɖoɖoe zi le nunye haɖe o, Nenema kee nye blukɔ si tsyɔ mo nam la hã.
ENGLISH: 17 For I do not break down at darkness and at being covered with blackness.

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 24 “Nu ka tae Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la meɖo ɣeyiɣi ɖi o? Nu ka tae ame siwo dze sii la menya eƒe ŋkeke o?
ENGLISH: 24 “How comes it times are not reserved by Shaddai and those who know him do not behold his days?

EWE: 2 Ame aɖewo ŋea liƒo ɖe eme; Wodaa adzo lãhawo hekplɔa wo yia woƒe gbeɖuƒee.
ENGLISH: 2 These displace boundary-marks, steal a flock and pasture it,

EWE: 3 Wokplɔa tsyɔ̃eviwo gɔ̃ hã ƒe tedzi dzonɛ Eye woxɔa ahosi ƒe nyi sesẽe wɔa awɔbanui.
ENGLISH: 3 Drive off orphans’ donkeys, take a widow’s cow and hold it as a pawn,

EWE: 4 Wotua asi ame dahewo ɖa le mɔ dzi; Eye wɔnamanɔŋutɔ siwo le anyigbaa dzi la sina bena na wo.
ENGLISH: 4 Force needy men off the road; earth’s downtrodden go into hiding together.

EWE: 5 Ame dahewo ɖoa gbe nɔa nuɖuɖu dim abe gbetedzi le gbedzi ene; Wotsana le gbegbe nɔa nuɖuɖu dim na wo viwo.
ENGLISH: 5 They go out in the wilderness like wild asses in their activities in quest of anything that can be eaten; he has desert wastes as food for the boys.

EWE: 6 Ame bubu ƒe agble mee woxaa nu le, Eye wofɔa nuku dzɔdzɔ le ame vɔ̃ɖi ƒe waingble me.
ENGLISH: 6 On the range they make a harvest of its cattle-feed, they go through a wicked man’s vineyard for belated grapes.

EWE: 7 Womlɔa anyi amama le zã me avɔ makpɔe; Eye naneke mele wo si woatsyɔ le vuvɔ me o.
ENGLISH: 7 They pass the night naked for want of clothing and coverless in the cold.

EWE: 8 Tsi ƒoa wo le towo dzi belee; Esi bebeƒe aɖeke meli o ta la, wokuna ɖe agakpewo ŋu.
ENGLISH: 8 They are wet with mountain rainstorms and hug rocks for lack of shelter.

EWE: 9 Woɖea tsyɔ̃evi gɔ̃ hã ɖa le no nu sesẽe; Eye woɖea avɔ si le ame dahe ŋu gɔ̃ hã wɔa awɔbanui.
ENGLISH: 9 They steal orphan from breast and take in pawn a poverty-stricken man’s baby.

EWE: 10 Ale wotsi ama le yiyim le esi avɔ mele wo si o ta, Eye wole dɔmeɣi hegatsɔ nuku bablawo ɖe ta.
ENGLISH: 10 They go about naked for want of clothing, and while they go hungry they carry shocks of grain,

EWE: 11 Wodagbana le ŋdɔgbe le gliwo domee; Wofiãa wain le wainfiãƒewo gake tsikɔ ganɔa wo wum.
ENGLISH: 11 Between their walls they press oil, they tread winepresses and go thirsty.

EWE: 12 Kudɔƒolawo le ŋeŋem le dua me; Eye ame siwo ŋu wode kubii la ƒe ɣli le ɖiɖim, Gake Mawu mebui be nane gblẽ le eŋu o.
ENGLISH: 12 Out of cities dying men groan and souls of men mortally wounded shriek. And God does not find any fault.

EWE: 13 Ame aɖewo li siwo tsia tsitre ɖe kekeli ŋu; Womedzea si eƒe mɔwo o, Eye womezɔa eƒe toƒewo o.
ENGLISH: 13 Those are rebels against light, do not recognize its routes nor settle in its paths.

EWE: 14 Ne ŋu ke la, amewula tsona; Eye wòwua wɔnamanɔŋutɔ kple ame dahe, Ke le zã me la, efia fi.
ENGLISH: 14 When it is not light a murderer stands up, kills a downtrodden and needy man; and in the night a thief goes about.

EWE: 15 Ŋutsu ahasitɔ ya ƒe ŋku le anyinutsyɔɣi ŋu, Egblɔna be, ‘Ame aɖeke makpɔm o!’ Eye wòtsyɔa nu mo.
ENGLISH: 15 And an adulterer’s eye watches for dusk, thinking ‘No eye will espy me,’ and he muffles up his face.

EWE: 16 Adzogliwo dzea zã ɖe aƒewo ŋu; Wodoa ʋɔ ɖe wo ɖokuiwo nu le ŋkeke me.
ENGLISH: 16 One breaks into houses in the dark.

EWE: Womelɔ̃a kekeli ƒe nya o.
ENGLISH: By day they shut themselves in; they make no acquaintance with light;

EWE: 17 Elabena agudzedze le na wo abe viviti tsiɖitsiɖi ene; Elabena wonya ale si blukɔ ƒe ŋɔdzi léa amee la nyuie.
ENGLISH: 17 For alike are morning to them and gloom, because they are familiar with the wraiths of gloom.

EWE: 18 Gake wo nu yina kaba abe tɔsisie kplɔ wo dzoe ene. Woaƒo fi ade anyigba ƒe akpa si nye woƒe gome. Womagatrɔ ayi woƒe waingblewo me o.
ENGLISH: 18 He is light on the surface of water; their share in the land shall be cursed; a treader shall not turn to their vineyard.

EWE: 19 Ale si kuɖiɖi kple dzoxɔxɔ kplɔa sno si lólo dzonae la, Nenemae Tsiẽƒe hã kplɔa nu vɔ̃ wɔlawo dzonae!
ENGLISH: 19 Drought, heat too, steal snow-water; the realm of death, who have sinned.

EWE: 20 Dadaa aŋlɔe be, nyéviwo aɖui; Womagaɖo ŋku edzi azɔ o.
ENGLISH: 20 The womb that fashioned him will forget him, his loftiness will not go on to be remembered, and foul play breaks like a piece of wood.

EWE: Eye woaŋe ame madzɔmadzɔ abe ati ene. 21 Etafaa konɔ, Eye wòwɔa fu ahosi.
ENGLISH: 21 One who does injuries to a barren woman that bears no children, and no good to a widow,

EWE: 22 Mawu atsɔ eƒe ŋusẽ aɖe ŋusẽtɔwo ɖa; Togbɔ be wole tsitrenu hã, kakaɖedzi meli be woanɔ agbe o.
ENGLISH: 22 And drags down needy men by his power, stands up and does not put faith in living;

EWE: 23 Mawu ɖea asi le wo ŋu wokana ɖe wo ɖokuiwo dzi hebuna be yewole dedie, Gake eƒe ŋkuwo le nu sia nu si wowɔna ŋu.
ENGLISH: 23 He grants him to have confidence and reliance, and his eyes are on their courses.

EWE: 24 Woado wo ɖe dzi ɣeyiɣi kpui aɖe, kasia wo nu ayi. Wobɔbɔa wo ɖe anyi eye woɖea wo ɖa abe ame bubu ɖe sia ɖe ko ene; Eye woŋea wo abe ale si woŋea nuku le nuŋeɣi ene.
ENGLISH: 24 They have been lofty a little while, and there is nothing of them and they are laid low, collapse like alkali-sorrel, and are cut down like heads of grain.

EWE: 25 Azɔ ame kae ate ŋu aɖe aʋatso nam, Alo agblɔ be nye nyawo mele eme o?”
ENGLISH: 25 If not, then, who will show me up as a liar and reduce my claims to nothing?”

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 25 Suatɔ Bildad ɖo eŋu be:
ENGLISH: 25 And Bildad the Shuhite answered

EWE: 2 “Dziɖuɖu le esi, eye ŋusẽ triakɔ le esi; Eɖo ŋutifafa anyi ɖe dziƒo.
ENGLISH: 2 “Dominion and terror are about him; he makes peace in his realms aloft.

EWE: 3 Ðe xexlẽme li na eƒe aʋakɔwoa? Eye ame ka dzie eƒe kekeli meklẽna ɖo o?
ENGLISH: 3 Is there any counting his regiments? and over whom does his light not stand up?

EWE: 4 Ekema aleke amegbetɔ anye dzɔdzɔetɔ le Mawu ŋkume, Alo nyɔnu tɔ dzidzia ŋu nadza le eŋkume?
ENGLISH: 4 How is a human being to be in the right with Deity? and how is one born of woman to be pure?

EWE: 5 Ne dzinu ke hã mekɔ le eŋkume o, Eye ɣletiviwo gɔ̃ hã medza le eŋkume o ɖe,
ENGLISH: 5 Here the very moon is not bright and stars are not pure to his eyes,

EWE: 6 Ke amegbetɔ si kuna, si nye nyévi, Kple amegbetɔvi si nye ŋɔvi ko ya ɖe?”
ENGLISH: 6 To say nothing of a human being, a maggot; of a son of mankind, a worm!”

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 26 Hiob ɖo eŋu be:
ENGLISH: 26 But Job answered

EWE: 2 “Oo, aleke nèhekpe ɖe ŋusẽmanɔsitɔ ŋue nye esi!
ENGLISH: 2 “What a help you have been to one without strength, what a salvation to an arm without energy,

EWE: Aleke nèhexɔ na alɔ beli lae nye esi! 3 Aleke nèheɖo aɖaŋu deŋgɔ na ame manyanui ale!
ENGLISH: 3 What a counselor to one without wisdom, and in what abundance you have imparted common sense!

EWE: 4 Ame kae nèle nu ƒom na, Eye ame kae dɔ wò be nàgblɔ nya siawo?
ENGLISH: 4 Whom have you told what to say? and whose breath came out from you?

EWE: 5 Ame siwo ku, eye ŋusẽ aɖeke megale wo ŋu o gɔ̃ hã dzona nyanyanya; Woɖiɖi ɖe anyi wu tsiwo kple wo me nuwo gɔ̃ hã.
ENGLISH: 5 The shades writhe underneath the water and its denizens.

EWE: 6 Tsiẽƒe le ƒeƒle le Mawu ŋkume, Eye tsɔtsrɔ̃ƒe le nuvo.
ENGLISH: 6 The realm of death lies naked before him and the land of the gone forever has no cover.

EWE: 7 Ekeke dziehedziŋgɔli me ɖe yame, Eye meku anyigba la ɖe naneke ŋu o;
ENGLISH: 7 He stretches the north over vacancy, hangs earth on nothing,

EWE: 8 Eblaa tsiwo ɖe eƒe alilikpowo me, Ale be alilikpoawo megbãna le woƒe kpekpeme ta o;
ENGLISH: 8 Bundles up water in his thunderclouds and the cloud does not tear under it,

EWE: 9 Exea eƒe fiazikpui la ŋkume, Ekekea eƒe alilikpo ɖe edzi.
ENGLISH: 9 Encloses the face of the full moon, spreading his cloud over it.

EWE: 10 Eɖe liƒo godoo ɖe tsiawo dzi; Eɖo seƒe ɖi na kekeli kple viviti.
ENGLISH: 10 He has drawn a boundary circle on the face of the water at the extremity of light, where it meets darkness.

EWE: 11 Dziƒosɔtiwo ke hã ʋuʋu; Eye ne eblu la, wodzona kpekpekpe.
ENGLISH: 11 The pillars of the sky rock and are confounded at his rebuke.

EWE: 12 Eƒe ŋusẽ nana atsiaƒu dzea agbo, Eye wòtsɔ eƒe nunya gbã ƒumelã klitsu la gudugudu.
ENGLISH: 12 By his power he stirred the sea and by his understanding he mangled Rahab.

EWE: 13 Etsɔ eƒe yagbɔgbɔ na dziŋgɔli me kɔ; Eƒe asi ŋɔ da si dzi asi mesuna bɔbɔe o la.
ENGLISH: 13 By his wind the sky is swept bare,and his hand pierced the elusive snake.

EWE: 14 Kpɔ ɖa!
ENGLISH: 14 There, these are the edges of his course,

EWE: Esiawoe nye eƒe mɔwo ƒe nugbɔ ko; Eye nya si míese le eŋu la nye dalĩdodo ko! Ke ame kae ate ŋu ase eƒe gbeɖeɖe sesẽ la gɔme?”
ENGLISH: and what a whispered thing it is that we hear of him! but the thunder of his energies who may perceive?”

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 27 Hiob gayi eƒe nyawo dzi be:
ENGLISH: 27 And Job further struck up his lay and said

EWE: 2 “Zi ale si Mawu, ame si gbe afiatsotso nam la le agbe, Eye Ŋusẽkatãtɔ, ame si do vevesese nam la le agbe,
ENGLISH: 2 “By the Deity, who has brushed aside my rights, and Shaddai, who has embittered my life,

EWE: 3 Zi ale si gbɔgbɔ kpɔtɔ le menye Eye Mawu ƒe gbɔgbɔ le ŋɔti me nam la,
ENGLISH: 3 When my breath was still all in me and God’s wind in my nostrils,

EWE: 4 Nye nuyiwo magblɔ nya vlo aɖeke o; Eye nye aɖe magblɔ alakpanya aɖeke o!
ENGLISH: 4 My lips shall not speak amiss nor my tongue voice false pretenses.

EWE: 5 Nyemabu mi ame dzɔdzɔewoe gbeɖe o! Nyemaɖe asi le nye fɔmaɖimaɖi ŋu va se ɖe esime maku o!
ENGLISH: 5 Away with the thought of my putting you in the right; till I breathe my last I will not throw off my conscientiousness.

EWE: 6 Malé nye dzɔdzɔenyenye me ɖe asi, eye nyemaɖe asi le eŋu akpɔ o; Zi ale si mele agbe la, nye dzi mabu fɔm o.
ENGLISH: 6 I hold fast to my righteous cause and will not loosen my hold; my heart feels no remorse for any of my days.

EWE: 7 Nye futɔwo nenɔ abe ame vɔ̃ɖiwo ene, Ame siwo tso ɖe ŋunye la nenɔ abe nu gbegblẽ wɔlawo ene.
ENGLISH: 7 May my enemy be in the state of a wrong-doer and my adversary in that of a knave!

EWE: 8 Elabena mɔkpɔkpɔ kae li na mawumavɔ̃la ne wohoe ɖa, Alo ne Mawu ɖe eƒe agbe ɖa?
ENGLISH: 8 For what is an ungodly man’s hope when God is cutting off and pulling out his soul?

EWE: 9 Ðe Mawu ase eƒe ɣlidodo Ne eɖo xaxa mea?
ENGLISH: 9 Will Deity hear his cry when distress comes upon him,

EWE: 10 Alo ɖe wòakpɔ dzidzɔ ɖe Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la ŋua?
ENGLISH: 10 Or will he be happy over Shaddai, call on God on every occasion?

EWE: Ðe wòanɔ Mawu yɔyɔ dzi ɣesiaɣia? 11 Mafia nu mi tso Mawu ƒe ŋusẽ ŋu; Nyemaɣla Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la ƒe naneke ɖe mi o.
ENGLISH: 11 I will instruct you as to the Deity’s hand; what Shaddai has in mind I will not conceal from you.

EWE: 12 Kpɔ ɖa! Ne ŋutegae mi katã miekpɔ la, Ekema nu ka tae miaƒe nyawo nye nya gbɔlowo sɔŋ?
ENGLISH: 12 Here you have all of you seen the sights, what do you go into flights of fancy for?

EWE: 13 Esiae nye ame vɔ̃ɖiwo ƒe gome tso Mawu gbɔ; Domenyinu si ŋutasẽlawo axɔ tso Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la gbɔ.
ENGLISH: 13 This is a wicked man’s lot in the Deity’s plan, and the estate violent men are to get from Shaddai.

EWE: 14 Ne viawo dzi ɖe edzi hã la, woatsi yi nu, Eye eƒe dzidzimeviwo makpɔ nu aɖu wòasu wo o.
ENGLISH: 14 If his sons are numerous, the sword is for them, and his offspring will not have their fill of bread.

EWE: 15 Dɔvɔ̃ akplɔ ame siwo susɔ nɛ la ayi yɔ me, Eye woƒe ahosiwo mafa wo o.
ENGLISH: 15 His survivors will be buried in death and his widows will not weep.

EWE: 16 Ne eli kɔ klosalo ɖi abe ke ene Eye wòƒo nudodowo nu ƒu abe tsu ene hã la,
ENGLISH: 16 If he piles up silver like earth and lays up clothing as if it were clay,

EWE: 17 Aƒo wo nu ƒu baa, Gake ame dzɔdzɔewoe ado wo, Eye ame maɖifɔwoe ama eƒe klosalo.
ENGLISH: 17 He will lay it in and an honest man will wear it and innocent men share the silver among them.

EWE: 18 Xɔ si wòtu la, anɔ abe agbagblaʋui ƒe azitsro ko ene, Abe agbadɔ si dzɔla tu la ene.
ENGLISH: 18 He has built his house like a spider’s, like a booth a watchman makes.

EWE: 19 Kesinɔtɔe wòanye hafi amlɔ anyi, ke hã maƒo naneke nu ƒu o; Ne eʋu ŋku la, eƒe nu sia nu nu ayi.
ENGLISH: 19 He goes to bed rich, but is so no more; he opens his eyes and it is not there.

EWE: 20 Ŋɔdzi alée le vo me abe tɔɖɔɖɔ ene; Ahom alɔe ɖe nu le zã me.
ENGLISH: 20 Dissolution descends upon him like water; in the night a gale snatches him,

EWE: 21 Ɣedzeƒeya akɔe adzoe; Eye wòakplɔe adzoe le enɔƒe.
ENGLISH: 21 An east wind picks him up and he goes, and it sweeps him out of his place.

EWE: 22 Esime wòle agbagba dzem be yeasi le eƒe ŋusẽ nu la, Ava ƒo ɖe edzi sesĩe, eye makpɔ nublanui nɛ o.
ENGLISH: 22 He pelts him unsparingly; he is in constant flight from his hand.

EWE: 23 Asi akpe ɖe eta, Eye wòanɔ enɔƒe alia aku ɖe eŋu.
ENGLISH: 23 He strikes his hands together over him and whistles at him from his place.

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 28 “Klosalokuƒe li, Eye sikalóloƒe hã li;
ENGLISH: 28 “For there is a mine for silver and a place for gold that they wash out.

EWE: 2 Wokua gayibɔ le to me, Eye kpe mee wolóloa akɔbli tsonae.
ENGLISH: 2 Iron is taken out of earth,and one melts stone to copper.

EWE: 3 Amegbetɔ xɔa ŋusẽ le viviti si; Wodia tomenu le goawo katã me keŋkeŋ, Le blukɔ kple viviti tsiɖitsiɖi me.
ENGLISH: 3 Man has set an end to darkness, and to every extremity he ransacks stone of blackness and gloom.

EWE: 4 Woɖe do wòyi to ʋĩi tso amenɔƒe gbɔ, Teƒe siwo metsɔ afɔ gbɔ o, siwo mele nyanya o; Afi mae ame siwo wotsi ɖe yame la saa agba ɖiɖina yina.
ENGLISH: 4 An intruding people breaks into ravines that were forgotten by feet; they suffer privations, they rove from men

EWE: 5 Anyigba la dzie nuɖuɖu miena ɖo; Ke woguglua anyigbaa tume abe ale si dzo guglua nui ene.
ENGLISH: 5 To a country from which bread has gone out and whose underpart turns to be like fire,

EWE: 6 Eƒe kpewo mee safir-kpe le, Eye eƒe kewɔ mee sika le.
ENGLISH: 6 A place whose stones are malachite and which has clods of gold,

EWE: 7 Xe ƒonu aɖeke menya afi ma mɔ o; Eye aʋako ƒe ŋku hã mekpɔe kpɔ o.
ENGLISH: 7 A path no bird of prey knows nor has a kite’s eye glimpsed it,

EWE: 8 Lã wɔadã meto edzi kpɔ o; Dzata meka afɔ edzi kpɔ o.
ENGLISH: 8 Which boldest beasts have not trodden nor lion passed along it.

EWE: 9 Amegbetɔ tsɔa asi gbaa kpe sesẽwo; Eɖea kè le towo te womuna.
ENGLISH: 9 He puts his hand to the pyrite rock, turns mountains up by their roots;

EWE: 10 Eɖea mɔ ɖe agakpewo tome; Eye eƒe ŋkuwo kpɔa nu xɔasi ɖe sia ɖe.
ENGLISH: 10 He rips out channels among the rocks, and his eye sees everything valuable.

EWE: 11 Exea mɔ na tsi ƒe toƒewo Eye wòhea nu ɣaɣlawo vaa kekeli nui.
ENGLISH: 11 He explores the sources of rivers and brings to light an undiscovered thing.

EWE: 12 Ke nunya ya, afi kae woakpɔe le, Eye afi kae nye gɔmesese hã tsoƒe?
ENGLISH: 12 But where is wisdom to be had from, and what is the place for insight?

EWE: 13 Amegbetɔ aɖeke menya ale si gbegbe wòxɔ asii o, Eye womekpɔnɛ le agbagbeawo ƒe anyigba dzi o.
ENGLISH: 13 No man knows the road to it, and it is not to be found in the land of the living.

EWE: 14 Tsi goglo la be: ‘Mele menye o!’ Atsiaƒu hã be: ‘Mele gbɔnye o!’
ENGLISH: 14 The deep says ‘it is not in me’ and the sea ‘I do not have it here.’

EWE: 15 Womate ŋu atsɔ sika nyuitɔ aƒlee o; Eye womate ŋu ada klosalo ɖe eƒe home nu o.
ENGLISH: 15 Solid gold is not to be given for it nor silver to be weighed out as its price;

EWE: 16 Womate ŋu atsɔ Ofir sika aƒlee o, Alo atsɔ oniks-kpe kple safir-kpe xɔasiwo aƒlee o.
ENGLISH: 16 It is not to be balanced against nuggets from Ophir, against the most precious beryl, or lapis lazuli;

EWE: 17 Womate ŋu atsɔ sika kple ahuhɔ̃e asɔ kplii o; Eye womate ŋu atsɔ sikaze nyuitɔ aɖɔlii o.
ENGLISH: 17 Gold and glass will not match it, a thing of red gold be an exchange for it;

EWE: 18 Womayɔ adzagba kple kristalo-kpe ŋkɔ gɔ̃ hã ɖe eŋu o, Elabena nunya kotoku ɖeka xɔ asi wu dzonu xɔasi kotoku ɖeka.
ENGLISH: 18 Pearls and alabaster are not to be mentioned, and wisdom is more of a prize than coral;

EWE: 19 Womate ŋu atsɔ Kus ƒe topaz-kpe asɔ kplii o; Womate ŋu atsɔ sika nyuitɔ gɔ̃ hã axe fe ɖe eta o.
ENGLISH: 19 The Nubian chrysolite will not match it, nor against pure nugget-gold is it to be balanced;

EWE: 20 Ke afi ka gɔ̃e nunya dzɔ tso, Eye afi kae nye gɔmesese hã tsoƒe?
ENGLISH: 20 And where does wisdom come from? and what is the place for insight?

EWE: 21 Ele ɣaɣla ɖe agbagbeawo katã ƒe ŋkuwo, Eye wòle ɣaɣla ɖe dziƒoxe dzodzoewo hã.
ENGLISH: 21 It lies out of sight of any living thing and screened from the birds of the air.

EWE: 22 Tsɔtsrɔ̃ kple ku hã be: ‘Wobewobe koe míese kple to.’
ENGLISH: 22 Death and the land of the gone forever say ‘We have heard a hearsay of it.’

EWE: 23 Mawue nya egbɔ mɔ; Eya koe nya enɔƒe,
ENGLISH: 23 God understands the road to it, he knows the place for it,

EWE: 24 Elabena eyae kpɔa anyigba ƒe mlɔenuwo ke, Eye wòkpɔa nu siwo katã le dziƒoa te.
ENGLISH: 24 Because he looks to the ends of the earth, sees under all the sky,

EWE: 25 Esi wòɖo ya ƒe ŋusẽ anyi Eye wòdzidze tsiwo,
ENGLISH: 25 Determining a weight for the wind and proportioning the water by measure.

EWE: 26 Esi wòwɔ ɖoɖo na tsidzadza Eye wòɖe toƒe na ahom kple dziɖegbe la,
ENGLISH: 26 When he made a law of nature for the rain and a course for the lightning of thunder,

EWE: 27 Ɣemaɣi kee wòkpɔ nunya, eye wòɖee fia; Eɖoe anyi, eye wòdzro eme kpɔ.
ENGLISH: 27 Then he saw it and described it, made it sure and thoroughly searched it out,

EWE: 28 Eye wògblɔ na amegbetɔ be: ‘Kpɔ ɖa! Yehowa vɔvɔ̃e nye nunya, Eye vɔ̃tsitsri ye nye gɔmesese.’”
ENGLISH: 28 And he said to man ‘Here, fearing the Lord is wisdom and shunning what is bad is insight.’”

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 29 Eye Hiob gayi eƒe nyawo dzi be:
ENGLISH: 29 And Job further struck up his lay and said

EWE: 2 “Oo, ɖe wòanɔ nam abe ale si wònɔ le dzinu tsãtɔwo me ene, Abe ŋkeke siwo me Mawu nɔ tanye kpɔm ene;
ENGLISH: 2 “Would that I were as in old-time months, as in the days when God watched over me,

EWE: 3 Esime wòna eƒe akaɖi klẽ ɖe nye ta dzi, Eye eƒe kekeli kplɔam to viviti me;
ENGLISH: 3 When he let his lamp beam over my head and by his light I walked through darkness!

EWE: 4 Esime menɔ ame me, ŋusẽ nɔ ŋunye, Esime menɔ ƒomedodo me kple Mawu le nye agbadɔ me;
ENGLISH: 4 As I was in my days of ripeness, when God had a fence round my home,

EWE: 5 Esime Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la gale gbɔnye, Esime vinyewo katã ƒo xlãm!
ENGLISH: 5 When Shaddai was still with me, my boys were around me,

EWE: 6 Esime nye afɔtoƒewo nyea notsi kpekẽ ɖeɖe sɔŋ, Eye agakpe dudua ami kɔna ɖi nam bɔbɔbɔ;
ENGLISH: 6 When my callers washed their dust off in clabber and rocks on my grounds poured rills of oil.

EWE: 7 Esime medona yia dua ƒe agbo nu Hebɔbɔna nɔa anyi ɖe zikpui dzi gli le ablɔ me ɖe,
ENGLISH: 7 When I went out of gate to town, prepared to take my seat in the square,

EWE: 8 Ne ɖekakpuiwo kpɔm la, wotena yia adzɔge, Eye ame tsitsiwo ke hã tsona ɖe tsitrenu.
ENGLISH: 8 Young men saw me and hid and graybeards rose and stood;

EWE: 9 Amegãwo tsoa woƒe nyawo dzi; Eye woɖoa asi nu.
ENGLISH: 9 Captains checked what they had to say and laid hand on their mouths;

EWE: 10 Gbɔgblɔ buna ɖe ame ŋkutawo; Eye woƒe aɖe léna ɖe aŋɔme na wo.
ENGLISH: 10 Magistrates’ voices hid and their tongues stuck to the roof of their mouths.

EWE: 11 Ame sia ame si se nye nyawo la kafuam, Eye ame siwo kpɔm la ƒoa nu nyui tso ŋunye.
ENGLISH: 11 For ears heard and deemed me happy, eyes saw and bore witness to me,

EWE: 12 Elabena mexɔna na ame dahe si le ɣli dom, Tsyɔ̃evi kple ame si xɔnametɔ aɖeke meli na o la.
ENGLISH: 12 That I brought a downtrodden suppliant out of trouble, and an orphan, and one whom none would help;

EWE: 13 Ame si ɖo kudo nu la ƒe yayra nɔa dzinye, Eye menaa ahosi ƒe dzi kpɔa dzidzɔ.
ENGLISH: 13 The blessing of one who was perishing came upon me and I set a widow’s heart caroling.

EWE: 14 Metaa dzɔdzɔenyenye abe avɔ ene; Eye nye nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔ le abe awu ʋlaya kple tablanu ene.
ENGLISH: 14 I clothed myself in right, and like a robe and tiara justice clothed me.

EWE: 15 Ŋku menye na ŋkuagbãtɔ Eye afɔ menye na bunɔ.
ENGLISH: 15 I was eyes for the blind man, and feet for the lame man was I.

EWE: 16 Fofo menye na ame dahewo; Medoa ame manyamanya ƒe ʋɔnunya gɔme.
ENGLISH: 16 I was a father to the needy, and investigated the claims of the man I did not know

EWE: 17 Mefea glã na nu gbegblẽ wɔla la Eye meɖea nu si dzi wòkpe aɖu ɖo la le aɖutɛ me nɛ.
ENGLISH: 17 And smashed a knave’s fangs and knocked prey out of his teeth.

EWE: 18 Megblɔna be, ‘Nye ŋutɔ nye aƒe mee maku le, Eye nye ŋkekewo asɔ gbɔ abe kekui ene.
ENGLISH: 18 And I thought I should breathe my last with my nestlings and have my days as numerous as the sand,

EWE: 19 Maɖe kè wòade tsi gbɔ, Eye zãmu adza ɖe nye alɔwo dzi zã bliboa.
ENGLISH: 19 With my roots spreading out to water and dew on my twigs through the night,

EWE: 20 Nye bubu anɔ yeye zum ɣesiaɣi, Eye manɔ aŋutrɔ si le asinye me la dada dzi.’
ENGLISH: 20 My honors fresh about me and my bow coming new in my hand.

EWE: 21 Amewo ɖoa tom hekpɔa asinye nu, Eye wozia ɖoɖoe sea nye aɖaŋuɖoɖo.
ENGLISH: 21 They listened for me and waited, kept still to get my advice;

EWE: 22 Ne meƒo nu vɔ la, nya aɖeke meganɔa wo si woagblɔ o; Eye nye nyawo gena ɖe woƒe towo me bɔlɔɔ.
ENGLISH: 22 After my word they did not speak again, and my discourse came sprinkling down on them.

EWE: 23 Wolalaam abe ale si wolalaa tsidzadza ene; Eye wokea woƒe nu baa abe adatsie wokee na ene.
ENGLISH: 23 They waited for me as if for rain and held their mouths wide open for a spring shower.

EWE: 24 Ne meko alɔgbɔnu na wo la, womexɔnɛ sena o; Ale si mekɔa mo ɖe wo la nana dzi ɖoa wo ƒo.
ENGLISH: 24 I gave them a laugh, they did not believe; and my face shone, they did not let theirs fall.

EWE: 25 Nyee fiaa mɔ wo abe woƒe tatɔ ene, Menɔ abe fia ene le eƒe aʋakɔwo dome, Abe ame si faa akɔ na konyifalawo ene.
ENGLISH: 25 I chose their course and sat as head,and lived like a king in a raiding-party, as if he were comforting mourners.

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 30 “Ke azɔ la, wole koyem Wo, ame siwo menye xoxo na, Ame siwo fofowo nyemalɔ̃ be Woanɔ nye lãkplɔvuwo gɔ̃ hã ŋu hafi o.
ENGLISH: 30 But now my juniors are laughing at me, whose fathers I had rejected for placing with my sheep-dogs.

EWE: 2 Vi kae woƒe alɔkpa sesẽ la ɖe nam? Woƒe ŋusẽ vɔ.
ENGLISH: 2 Of what use was even the strength of their hands to me, men in whom solid vigor was lost, gaunt with destitution and starvation?

EWE: 3 Hiã kple dɔwuame na ŋusẽ vɔ le wo ŋu; Wokukoa kuɖiɖinyigba Afi si zu aƒedo kple gbegbe.
ENGLISH: 3 Those who gnaw arid downs, the emesh of blast and blight,

EWE: 4 Wodaa dzegbe le avekɔewo me; Eye ati dodoewo ƒe kee nye woƒe nuɖuɖu.
ENGLISH: 4 Who pluck alkali-sorrel, wormwood leaves, and have broom-roots for their bread;

EWE: 5 Wonyaa wo ɖa le ame dome; Amewo doa ɣli ɖe wo ta abe fiafitɔwo ene.
ENGLISH: 5 They are driven out of a community, they yell at them as they would at a thief.

EWE: 6 Wova nɔa baliwo, Dowo kple agadowo me.
ENGLISH: 6 They have to live in the sides of arroyos, in holes in the ground and between stones.

EWE: 7 Wodoa ɣli le avekɔewo me; Wotigi wo ɖokuiwo ɖe dzawo te.
ENGLISH: 7 They bray between wormwood bushes, snuggle together under weeds.

EWE: 8 Movitɔ kple yakame ƒe viwoe wonye, Wonya wo ɖa le anyigba la dzi.
ENGLISH: 8 Sons of rascals, sons of nobody that can be named, they are whipped out of the country.

EWE: 9 Azɔ la, wodoa vlom le woƒe hadzidziwo me; Eye mezu alɔmeɖenu na wo.
ENGLISH: 9 And now I am the butt of their jingles and have become a byword of theirs.

EWE: 10 Wonyɔa ŋum, wole adzɔge tso gbɔnye; Eye woɖea ta ɖe mo nam faa.
ENGLISH: 10 They abhor me, stand far away from me, do not keep their spit out of my face.

EWE: 11 Elabena Mawu na nye ŋusẽ gbɔdzɔ, eye wòbɔbɔm ɖe anyi, Ale be wowɔa nu sia nu si dze wo ŋu la le ŋkunyeme.
ENGLISH: 11 For he has undone my bowstring and made me helpless, and they loosen their reins before me.

EWE: 12 Nu vlo wɔha tso ɖe ŋunye le nye ɖusime; Wona mede afɔ du me Eye woxe mɔ nam be yewoagblẽ donyeme.
ENGLISH: 12 On the right a horde stand up, unsettle my footing, and build their tracks of calamity against me.

EWE: 13 Wogblẽ nye toƒewo Wona nye xaxa la kpe ɖe edzi, Eye ame aɖeke meli aɖo asi wo dzi hã o.
ENGLISH: 13 They tear up my path, do great work for catastrophe, have nobody to help them.

EWE: 14 Wolũ ɖe dzinye abe gli gbagbã mee woto ene; Wolɔ hoo to gbagbãƒewo va ƒo ɖe dzinye.
ENGLISH: 14 They come like coming through a broad breach, roll along under the crash of ruin.

EWE: 15 Ŋɔdzi nye tsyɔm; Woɖe nye bubu ɖa abe yae kplɔe dzoe ene, Eye nye xɔname nu yi abe alilikpo ene.
ENGLISH: 15 Dissolution turns upon me, my dignity is chased off as if by the wind, and my hope of succor passes like a cloud.

EWE: 16 Azɔ agbe le vɔvɔm le menye, Hiãŋkekewo tum.
ENGLISH: 16 And now I have my life draining out, days of suffering are gripping me,

EWE: 17 Le zã me la, nye ƒuwo me ɖuam ƒuƒuƒu, Eɖuam madzudzɔmadzudzɔe.
ENGLISH: 17 In the night my bones are being dug away and my sinews get no repose.

EWE: 18 Enu sẽ ɖe dzinye ale gbegbe be nye awu trɔ ɖeƒomevii; Emia ve nam sesĩe abe nye awu ƒe kɔme ene.
ENGLISH: 18 My garment takes strong hold, lies snug on me like the neck of my shirt.

EWE: 19 Mawu tu asim ƒu ba me; Ale be mezu ke kple afi ɖeɖe.
ENGLISH: 19 He has laid me for clay, and I am made like earth and ashes.

EWE: 20 Medoa ɣli be nàxɔ nam, ke mètɔna nam o; Metso ɖe tsitrenu, ke ɖeko nèle kpɔyem dũu.
ENGLISH: 20 I clamor to you and you do not answer me; I stand there and you observe me,

EWE: 21 Ètrɔ zu ŋutasẽla ɖe ŋunye; Ètsɔ wò alɔkame sesẽ la dze dzinye.
ENGLISH: 21 You turn brutal toward me, you wreak your grudge on me with the vast strength of your hand.

EWE: 22 Èkɔm ɖe dzi ale be ya kɔm dzoe; Eye nènyamam le ahom me.
ENGLISH: 22 You pick me up into the air, ride me on the wind, let storm toss me.

EWE: 23 Elabena menyae nyuie be àtsɔm ade asi na ku, Ne mayi xɔ si me agbagbeawo katã ƒoa takpli ɖo la.
ENGLISH: 23 For I know you will bring me back to death, to the rendezvous of everything alive.

EWE: 24 Gake ame aɖeke megaƒoa ame si gbã gudugudu, Esi wòle ɣli dom be woaxɔ na ye le xaxaɣi o.
ENGLISH: 24 Only he does not lay hands on a heap of ruin; or by his disaster will there be lucre for them?

EWE: 25 Ðe nyemefa avi ɖe ame siwo ɖo xaxa me la ta oa? Ðe nyemexa nu ɖe ame dahewo ŋuti oa?
ENGLISH: 25 I did weep for the man who was having a hard time, my soul grieved for the needy man;

EWE: 26 Menɔ mɔ kpɔm na nyui, ke vɔ̃ boŋ ye va; Menɔ kekeli sinu kpɔm, ke viviti boŋ ye do.
ENGLISH: 26 I hoped for good, and evil came; I awaited light, and murky darkness came.

EWE: 27 Nye dɔ me le totrom hegbe emedzedze; Hiãŋkekewo va ƒo ɖe dzinye.
ENGLISH: 27 My vitals are boiling, never still; days of suffering confront me.

EWE: 28 Melé blanui le yiyim; nyemekpɔ kekeli aɖeke o. Metso le ha la dome le ɣli dom be woaxɔ nam.
ENGLISH: 28 I go in mourning without sunshine, stand up and clamor publicly.

EWE: 29 Mezu agbotoewo nɔvi, Kple golowo ƒe zɔhɛ.
ENGLISH: 29 I am brother to jackals and fellow to ostriches.

EWE: 30 Nye ŋutigbalẽ nyɔ tsiɖitsiɖi hele fofom le ŋunye, Eye nye ƒuwo me ʋu dzo hɛ̃ le dzoxɔxɔ la ta.
ENGLISH: 30 My skin blackens and comes off, and my bones are hot with fever.

EWE: 31 Konyifafa ko ŋue nye saŋku ɖina ɖo, Eye nye kpẽ ɖina avigbee.
ENGLISH: 31 And my lyre has turned to mourning and my pipe to the voices of weepers.

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 31 “Mebla nu kple nye ŋkuwo. Ekema aleke wɔ nye ŋku aganɔ ɖetugbui ŋu madzemadzee?
ENGLISH: 31 “I put my eyes under a contract, and how was I to take notice of a maiden?

EWE: 2 Nu kae anye nye gome tso Mawu si le dziƒo la gbɔ, Alo domenyinu kae atso Ŋusẽkatãtɔ si le dziƒo ʋĩi la gbɔ nam?
ENGLISH: 2 And what is God’s allotment from above and Shaddai’s assignment from on high?

EWE: 3 Ðe afɔku mele nu gbegblẽ wɔla lalam, Eye vɔ̃ mele nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔlawo dzɔm oa?
ENGLISH: 3 Is it not calamity for a knave and mishap for villains?

EWE: 4 Ðe eya ŋutɔ mele nye zɔzɔme kpɔm, Eye wòxlẽa nye afɔɖeɖewo katã oa?
ENGLISH: 4 Does not he see my courses and count all my steps?

EWE: 5 Ðe meƒo ɖokuinye ɖe alakpanuwɔna me kpɔa? Eye ɖe nye afɔ tsɔna ɖe beble ŋua?
ENGLISH: 5 If I walked with false pretense and my foot hurried toward fraud,

EWE: 6 Mawu nedam le nudanu dzɔdzɔe me; Ekema adze si nye fɔmaɖimaɖi.
ENGLISH: 6 Let God weigh me in a fair balance and know about my conscientiousness.

EWE: 7 Ne nye afɔ tra ɖa le mɔ la dzi Alo nye dzi kplɔ nu si nye ŋkuwo kpɔ ɖo Alo nye asiwo ƒo ɖi la,
ENGLISH: 7 If my tread has swerved from the course and my eye has followed my heart and anything has stuck to my hands,

EWE: 8 Ekema maƒã nu ame bubu naɖu, Eye woneho nye nu siwo meƒã.
ENGLISH: 8 Let me sow and another eat,and what grows for me be uprooted.

EWE: 9 Ne nyɔnu aɖe flu nye dzi, Eye mede xa ɖe hanyevi ƒe ʋɔtru nu la,
ENGLISH: 9 If my heart has been inveigled after a woman and I have lain in wait at my friend’s doorway,

EWE: 10 Ekema srɔ̃nye netu wɔ na ame tutɔ, Eye ŋutsu bubuwo nedɔ egbɔ.
ENGLISH: 10 Let my wife grind for another and others crouch over her.

EWE: 11 Elabena ema anye ŋukpenanuwɔwɔ, Eye wòanye vodada si dze na tohehe le ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo ŋkume.
ENGLISH: 11 For that would be lewdness, it would be guilt to come before a court.

EWE: 12 Anye dzo si abi nu ahagblẽ nu, Eye wòafiã nye nuwo katã va se ɖe woƒe kè gbɔ ke.
ENGLISH: 12 For that is a fire that would eat down to the land of the gone forever and take out the roots of all my produce.

EWE: 13 Ne mete nye kluvi alo nye kosi ƒe nya dzɔdzɔe ɖe to, Esi nya ɖo nye kpli wo dome la,
ENGLISH: 13 If I refused the rights of my slaves when they had a dispute with me,

EWE: 14 Ekema ne Mawu bia gbem la, nu kae mawɔ? Eye ne ebia akɔntam ɖe, aleke maɖo eŋu nɛ?
ENGLISH: 14 What should I do when Deity stands up, and when he is punishing what answer should I make to him?

EWE: 15 Ðe menye Ame si wɔm le vidzidɔ me la kee wɔ woawo hã oa? Eye menye Ame ma kee trɔ asi le mía ŋu hafi wodzi oa?
ENGLISH: 15 Did not he who made me in a mother’s body make them, and was it not one who worked us into shape in the womb?

EWE: 16 Ne mete ame dahewo ƒe didiwo wo Eye mena ahosiwo ƒe ŋkuwo lé blanui;
ENGLISH: 16 If I withheld what poor men wanted and let a widow’s eyes wear out with looking and longing,

EWE: 17 Ne nye ɖeka koe ɖua nu si mekpɔ Eye mekua ŋɔ tsyɔ̃eviwo;
ENGLISH: 17 And ate my snack alone and an orphan did not eat part

EWE: 18 (Elabena tso nye ɖevime kee tsyɔ̃evi nɔ gbɔnye tsi abe fofoa gbɔ wònɔ ene, Eye tso nye ɖevime kee mefiaa mɔ ahosi);
ENGLISH: 18 (For from my boyhood I raised him as a father would, and ever since my birth I helped her along),

EWE: 19 Ne mekpɔ ame wòle tsɔtsrɔ̃m le avɔ manɔamesi ta Alo ame dahe si mekpɔ avɔ atsyɔ o;
ENGLISH: 19 If I saw one perishing for lack of clothing and that a needy man had nothing to cover him,

EWE: 20 Ne meyram o, Evɔ wònye nye alẽfuvɔ de dzo lãme nɛ hafi;
ENGLISH: 20 If his back did not bless me and he get warmth out of the fleeces of my sheep,

EWE: 21 Ne menyè asi ɖe tsyɔ̃evi ŋu, Esi mekpɔe le dugbo la nu be ehiã nye kpekpeɖeŋu la;
ENGLISH: 21 If I shook my fist at a quiet man because I saw I had friends in court,

EWE: 22 Ekema nye abɔ nege le abɔgba ŋu, Eye nye abɔ neŋe ɖe abɔklugui nu.
ENGLISH: 22 May my arm drop off from its shoulder, may it be broken through its long bone.

EWE: 23 Elabena mevɔ̃ afɔku si tso Mawu gbɔ la, Eye nyemate ŋu anɔ te ɖe eƒe gãnyenye nu o.
ENGLISH: 23 For Deity’s calamity is a thing I dread, and I cannot cope with his majesty.

EWE: 24 Ne meɖo dzi ɖe sika ŋu, Alo megblɔ na sika nyuitɔ be, ‘Ŋuwòe mele dzi ɖom ɖo!’
ENGLISH: 24 If I have made gold my reliance and spoken of kethem as my confidence,

EWE: 25 Ne mekpɔa dzidzɔ le esi nye nunɔamesiwo sɔ gbɔ, Le esi nu bɔ ɖe asinye kpaŋkpaŋ ta;
ENGLISH: 25 If I was gladdened because my wealth was great and I had a great deal at my disposal,

EWE: 26 Ne mekpɔ ale si ɣe le keklẽm, Alo mekpɔ ale si dzinu le yiyim le atsyɔ̃ me;
ENGLISH: 26 If I saw the light as it beamed and the moon walking sublimely

EWE: 27 Eye mena wofi nye dzi le adzame, Ale be megbugbɔ asi ɖo ɖe wo tsɔ subɔ wo la;
ENGLISH: 27 And I was secretly so simpleminded that my mouth kissed my hand,

EWE: 28 Ekema anye vodada si dze na tohehe le ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo ŋkume, Elabena afia be megbe Mawu vavã si le dziƒo la.
ENGLISH: 28 That too would be guilt to come before a court, for I should have been lying to Deity above.

EWE: 29 Ðe mekpɔ dzidzɔ ɖe nye futɔ aɖe ƒe tsɔtsrɔ̃ ŋu kpɔa, Alo dzi dzɔm le esi vɔ̃ dzɔ ɖe edzi ta kpɔa?
ENGLISH: 29 If I was glad of a disaster to one who hated me and was elated because evil had found him

EWE: 30 Nyemena nye nuyi wɔ nu vɔ̃ o, Eye nyemedi eƒe ku to ɖiŋudodo nɛ me o.
ENGLISH: 30 Why, I did not let my throat sin asking his life with a curse;

EWE: 31 Aƒenyemetɔwo gblɔna be, ‘Ame kae ate ŋu afia asi ame aɖe be, eya meɖu eƒe nu ɖi ƒo kpɔ o?’
ENGLISH: 31 If the men of my tent did not say ‘Who will bring somebody that has not had all he wanted of his meat?’

EWE: 32 Amedzro aɖeke metsia xexe dɔna o; Mena nye ʋɔ le ʋuʋu ɖi na mɔzɔlawo.
ENGLISH: 32 No visitor from abroad spent the night in the street; I opened my doors to the wayfarer.

EWE: 33 Ðe metsyɔ nu nye dzidadawo dzi abe ale si ame bubuwo wɔnɛ ene, Ale be meɣla nye vodada ɖe nye awu ƒe kotoku me kpɔa?
ENGLISH: 33 If in human fashion I covered up my crime, burying my guilt under my cloak,

EWE: 34 Ðe mevɔ̃na na ale si amehawo awɔ nui, Alo ɖe ƒome bubuwo ƒe vlodoame dzia ŋɔ nam, Ale be mezia ɖoɖoe eye mevɔ̃na be mado ɖe gotaa?
ENGLISH: 34 Because I stood in awe of a great crowd and the contempt of clans dismayed me,And I kept quiet, not going out of the doorway

EWE: 35 Oo, ne ɖe ame aɖe aɖo tom ɖe! Anye ne made asi nya siwo megblɔ la te. Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la neɖo eŋu nam!
ENGLISH: 35 I wish I had someone to hear me!Here is my signature, let Shaddai answer me!And a bill that my opponent had written,

EWE: 36 Anye ne malée ɖe abɔta; Mablae ɖe ta abe atsyɔ̃tablanu ene.
ENGLISH: 36 wouldn’t I carry it on my shoulder,lace it on as a crown for me!

EWE: 37 Mana nye afɔɖeɖe ɖe sia ɖe ŋuti kɔntae; Mazɔ abe fiavi ene ate ɖe eŋu.
ENGLISH: 37 I would report to him the number of my steps, would receive him as a lord high steward should.

EWE: 38 Ne nye anyigba afa avi ɖe ŋutinye, Eye nye agblewo katã afa avi nam hoo;
ENGLISH: 38 If my soil cries out against me and its furrows are weeping together,

EWE: 39 Ne meɖu eme kutsetse femaxee, Alo mena anyigba la tɔwo tsi dzodzodzoe la;
ENGLISH: 39 If I have eaten its strength without paying money and have let the life go out of its owners,

EWE: 40 Ekema ŋù nemie ɖe lu teƒe nam Eye gbe si ʋẽna kũu nemie ɖe ƒo teƒe nam.”
ENGLISH: 40 Instead of wheat let briers come out, and instead of barley nightshade.”

EWE: Hiob ƒe gbe dze anyi.
ENGLISH: End of the words of Job.

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 32 Ale ŋutsu etɔ̃ siawo dzudzɔ nyaŋuɖoɖo na Hiob, elabena Hiob ka ɖe eɖokui dzi be yele dzɔdzɔe.
ENGLISH: 32 And these three men left off answering Job, because he felt that he was in the right.

EWE: 2 Ke dzi ku Elihu, Buzitɔ Barakel vi, si tso Ram ƒomea me la vevie. Edo dziku ɖe Hiob ŋu vevie be ebu eɖokui dzɔdzɔetɔe wu Mawu.
ENGLISH: 2 And Elihu the son of Barakel the Buzite, of the clan of Ram, was angry: angry at Job for making himself out in the right against God,

EWE: 3 Edo dziku ɖe Hiob xɔlɔ̃ etɔ̃awo hã ŋu vevie le esi womekpɔ ŋuɖoɖo gbagbe aɖeke o, ke boŋ wobu fɔ Mawu ta.
ENGLISH: 3 and angry at his three friends for not finding an answer, and putting God in the wrong.

EWE: 4 Nyawo nɔ Elihu si gake elala be Hiob nawu eƒe nyawo nu, elabena wo katã wonye xoxo nɛ.
ENGLISH: 4 And Elihu had waited for Job in the talk because they were older than he,

EWE: 5 Esi Elihu kpɔe be ŋuɖoɖo aɖeke mele ŋutsu etɔ̃awo si o la, dzi kui vevie.
ENGLISH: 5 but Elihu saw that the three men had no answer in their mouths, and was angry.

EWE: 6 Eye Elihu, Buzitɔ Barakel vi, ƒo nu hegblɔ be: “Nye ya ɖevi ko menye, Ke miawo la ame tsitsiwoe mienye. Esia tae melé ɖokuinye kpoo, Eye mevɔ̃ be maɖe nu si menya la agblɔ na mi.
ENGLISH: 6 And Elihu the son of Barakel the Buzite answered “I am a youngster and you are gray-bearded men; that was why I was bashful and afraid to state my view among you.

EWE: 7 Megblɔ be, ‘Tsitsi neƒo nu, Eye ƒe geɖe neɖe nunya fia.’
ENGLISH: 7 I thought ‘Let days speak and number of years disclose wisdom.’

EWE: 8 Gake Mawu ƒe gbɔgbɔ si le amegbetɔ me, Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la ƒe gbɔgbɔ, ye naa gɔmesese.
ENGLISH: 8 But it is a spirit in man, after all,and Shaddai’s breath makes them understand things.

EWE: 9 Menye tsitsi koe wɔa ame nunyala o, Eye menye tsitsiawo koe nya nu si le eteƒe o.
ENGLISH: 9 It is not men of many days that are wise nor old men that understand what is right.

EWE: 10 Eya ta mebe, ‘Miɖo tom, Ne nye hã maɖe nu si menya la agblɔ na mi.
ENGLISH: 10 So I say, Hear me;I too will state my view.

EWE: 11 Kpɔ ɖa! Melala mieƒo nu; Meɖo to se miaƒe susuwo, Le ɣeyiɣi siwo katã me mienɔ nya si miagblɔ la dim.
ENGLISH: 11 Here I did wait for your words,listened for your discernments,Till you should hunt out something to say,

EWE: 12 Nye to nɔ mia ŋu, Ke mia dometɔ aɖeke mete ŋu ɖee fia Hiob be edze agɔ, Alo ɖo eƒe nyawo ŋu nɛ o.
ENGLISH: 12 and applied my attention to you,And found Job had nobody to confute him,to answer his say, among you.

EWE: 13 Eya ta migagblɔ be, ‘Míeke ɖe nunya ŋu; Mawue kpe edzi, menye amegbetɔ aɖekee o.’
ENGLISH: 13 For fear you should say ‘We have discovered wisdom,’ Deity shall put him to rout, not a man.

EWE: 14 Esi wònye be medo nya aɖeke ɖe gbɔnye o ta la, Nyemafɔ nya le miaƒe nyawo me atsɔ aɖo eŋu nɛ o.
ENGLISH: 14 And he has not marshaled points against me, nor will I answer him with what you said.

EWE: 15 Wotsi yaa, nya aɖeke megale wo si woagblɔ o; Gbɔgblɔ bu ɖe wo.
ENGLISH: 15 “They were dismayed, no longer made any answer, their phrases had moved out,

EWE: 16 Melala, ke womegale nu ƒom o; Ðeko wotɔ ɖi, womegale nya aɖeke gblɔm o.
ENGLISH: 16 And was I to wait when they were not speaking, when they were at a standstill, no longer made any answer?

EWE: 17 Eya ta nye hã magblɔ tɔnye sinua; Nye hã magblɔ nu si menya,
ENGLISH: 17 I will make the answer that is my portion, I too will state my view,

EWE: 18 Elabena nyawo le asinye fũu; Gbɔgbɔ si le menye ye le eƒom ɖe nunye.
ENGLISH: 18 For I am full of things to be said,the spirit in my waist is putting me under a strain,

EWE: 19 Nye dɔ me le abe wain si nu wotu nu ɖo ene, Abe lãgbalẽgolo yeye si di be yeawó ene.
ENGLISH: 19 I feel my waist like wine that is not being opened; as with skins of new wine, an explosion is coming.

EWE: 20 Mina maƒo nu, ne mavo! Make nye nuyiwo aɖo nya ŋu.
ENGLISH: 20 I will speak and get relief, will open my lips and answer.

EWE: 21 Nyemade ame aɖeke dzi o; Alo aɖɔ kesekuku na ame aɖeke o,
ENGLISH: 21 May I not show partiality to any man; and to no human being will I pay compliments,

EWE: 22 Elabena nyemenya ale si woɖɔa kesekuku na amee o; Anye ne nye Wɔla aɖem ɖa kaba.
ENGLISH: 22 For I do not know how to pay compliments; my Maker might easily snatch me away.

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 33 “Azɔ Hiob, meɖe kuku, se nye nyawo, Eye nàlé to ɖe nye nyawo katã ŋu.
ENGLISH: 33 But hear what I have to say, Job, and give ear to all my words.

EWE: 2 Kpɔ ɖa! Make nu azɔ; Eye nye aɖe aƒo nu.
ENGLISH: 2 Here I am opening my mouth, my tongue is speaking under its roof,

EWE: 3 Nye nyawo aɖe ale si nye dzi me dza afia, Eye nye nu agblɔ nu si menya le anukware me.
ENGLISH: 3 My say is the sincere expression of my heart and my lips utter the best of their knowledge.

EWE: 4 Mawu ƒe gbɔgbɔe wɔm, Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la ƒe agbegbɔgbɔe na mele agbe.
ENGLISH: 4 Deity’s spirit made me and Shaddai’s breath put life into me.

EWE: 5 Ne ele ŋuwò la, ɖo eŋu nam; Tsɔ wò nyawo va ŋkunyeme; va dze avu ɖi.
ENGLISH: 5 Answer me if you can, join issue and stand up to me.

EWE: 6 Kpɔ ɖa! Ðeko mele abe wò ene le Mawu vavã la ŋkume; Nye hã tsue wotsɔ mèm.
ENGLISH: 6 You will find me to be in the same relation to Deity as you; I was kneaded out of clay as you were.

EWE: 7 Eya ta mègana nye ŋɔdzi nalé wò o, Eye nye nyawo megawu tsɔtsɔ na wò o.
ENGLISH: 7 Here will terror of me not overwhelm you nor my duress weigh you down.

EWE: 8 Ke wò nyawo ge ɖe to me nam, Ɛ̃, wò nyawo ɖi mese be:
ENGLISH: 8 “Only you said in my hearing, I heard a sound of such words,

EWE: 9 ‘Mele dzadzɛ, dzidada aɖeke mele ŋunye o; Ŋunye kɔ, eye vodada mele ŋunye o.
ENGLISH: 9 ‘I am pure, free from crime, I am clear and have no guilt about me.

EWE: 10 Ke hã, Mawu kpɔa nane le ŋunye godoo; Ebuam eƒe futɔe.
ENGLISH: 10 Here he is inventing antagonisms against me and counting me as an enemy of his,

EWE: 11 Ebɔa pã nye afɔwo; Eléa ŋku ɖe nye mɔwo katã ŋu tsitotsito.’
ENGLISH: 11 Setting my feet in the stocks and watching all my paths.’

EWE: 12 Gake medi be mana nànya be, tɔwò medzɔ le nya sia me o: Mawu nye gã wu amegbetɔ.
ENGLISH: 12 Here you are not right in this, I answer you, because God is more than man.

EWE: 13 Nu ka tae nèle nya hem ɖe eŋu? Esi mele wò nyawo katã ŋu ɖom na wò o taea?
ENGLISH: 13 How come you setting up a case against him because he does not answer all your words?

EWE: 14 Elabena Mawu gblɔa nya zi ɖeka, kple zi eve, Togbɔ be amewo meɖoa to o hã,
ENGLISH: 14 For Deity speaks once for all and does not repeat it a second time.

EWE: 15 Le drɔ̃e me, le zã ƒe ŋutega me, Esime amewo yi alɔ̃ me ʋĩi Esime wole alɔ̃ dɔm le woƒe abawo dzi.
ENGLISH: 15 In a dream, a vision of the night, when trances fall on men, in slumbers on the bed,

EWE: 16 Ɣemaɣie wòʋua to na wo Eye wòkua eƒe nufiamewo ɖe to me na wo,
ENGLISH: 16 Then he makes disclosure to men and dismays them with sights that they see,

EWE: 17 Ne wòana amegbetɔ naƒo asa na nu gbegblẽ wɔwɔ Eye wòakpɔ ame ta be wòagado eɖokui ɖe dzi o.
ENGLISH: 17 To turn away man from his doings and prune away pride from a man,

EWE: 18 Mawu ɖea eƒe luʋɔ tso yɔdo si me, Kple eƒe agbe, be wòagatsi yi nu o.
ENGLISH: 18 Hold back his life from the grave and his being from rushing upon destruction.

EWE: 19 Vevesese zua mokaname na ame le eƒe aba dzi Eye wònaa eƒe ƒuwo nɔa eɖum ƒuƒuƒu,
ENGLISH: 19 And he is admonished by pain on the bed and the discord in his bones is perpetual,

EWE: 20 Ale be nuɖuɖu nyɔa ŋu nɛ, Eye wògbea nuɖuɖu nyuiwo gɔ̃ hã.
ENGLISH: 20 And his inclination loathes bread and his appetite the food it naturally craves.

EWE: 21 Lã vɔ le eŋu, ale be meganya le kpɔkpɔm o, Eye eƒe ƒu siwo medzena tsã o la tsi anyi glaŋ.
ENGLISH: 21 His flesh gets too wasted to look at and his bones so bare nobody will look at them,

EWE: 22 Eƒe luʋɔ ɖo kudo nu vɔ, Eye eƒe agbe dze ku ƒe dɔtsɔlawo si me vɔ.
ENGLISH: 22 And his life is near to the grave and his being to the place of the dead.

EWE: 23 Ne dɔla aɖe li nɛ, Nyanuɖela ɖeka le akpe dome, Ne wòagblɔ nu si le dzɔdzɔe na amegbetɔ,
ENGLISH: 23 If he has over him an angel, an interpreter, one out of a thousand, to tell man his right course,

EWE: 24 Ekema Mawu vea enu, eye wògblɔna be: ‘Ðee, ne wòagayi yɔdo me o! Elabena mekpɔ tafe!
ENGLISH: 24 And he is gracious to him and says ‘Let him off from going down to the Pit; I have been given satisfaction,’

EWE: 25 Eƒe ŋutilã negazu yeye wu ale si wònɔ le eƒe ɖevime; Eƒe ɖekakpuimeŋusẽ negaɖo eŋu.’
ENGLISH: 25 His flesh will grow plumper than in childhood; he will come back to his youth.

EWE: 26 Aɖe kuku na Mawu, eye wòakpɔ ŋudzedze ɖe eŋu, Eye wòakpɔ Eŋkume ahatso aseye, Eye Mawu agbugbɔ eƒe dzɔdzɔenyenye aɖo te na amegbetɔ.
ENGLISH: 26 He will invoke God and God will accept him, and he will see his face with shouts of joy; and he will give the man back his standing for righteousness.

EWE: 27 Ekema ame ma agblɔ na amewo be, ‘Mewɔ nu vɔ̃, eye metrɔ gbo nu si le dzɔdzɔe, Gake womeɖo eteƒe nam abe ale si dze ene o.
ENGLISH: 27 He will sing before men and say ‘I sinned, I turned fair play to foul, and he did not give ma measure for measure,

EWE: 28 Eɖe nye luʋɔ, be wòagayi yɔdo me o, Eye nye agbe akpɔ kekeli.’
ENGLISH: 28 He has redeemed my life from passing into the Pit, and my being has the sight of the light.’

EWE: 29 Kpɔ ɖa! Nu siawo katãe Mawu wɔna Na ame zi eve kple zi etɔ̃,
ENGLISH: 29 Here Deity does all these things twice over, three times, with a man,

EWE: 30 Ne wòaxɔe tso yɔdo si me, Ne agbe ƒe kekeli naklẽ ɖe edzi.
ENGLISH: 30 To turn his life back from the Pit to be lighted with the light of life;

EWE: 31 Oo Hiob, ƒu to anyi! Ðo tom!
ENGLISH: 31 Listen, Job, hear me, be silent for me to speak.

EWE: Zi ɖoɖoe, ne mayi nuƒoƒo dzi. 32 Ke ne nya aɖe le asiwò nàgblɔ la, ekema gblɔe nam.
ENGLISH: 32 If there is anything to be said, answer me; speak, because I should like you to be in the right.

EWE: 33 Gake ne nya aɖeke mele asiwò o la, ekema ɖo tom; Zi ɖoɖoe, ne mafia nunya wò.”
ENGLISH: 33 If there is not, hear me yourself; be silent and let me acquaint you with wisdom.”

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 34 Eye Elihu gblɔ yi edzi be:
ENGLISH: 34 And Elihu answered

EWE: 2 “Mi nunyalawo, mise nye nyawo; Eye mi nu geɖe nyalawo, miƒu to anyi ɖe ŋunye.
ENGLISH: 2 “Wise men, hear my words; give ear to me, men of knowledge;

EWE: 3 Elabena to doa nya kpɔna Abe ale si aɖe ɖɔa nu kpɔna ene.
ENGLISH: 3 For ears test words and a palate tastes food.

EWE: 4 Mina míada nya dzɔdzɔe akpɔ; Mina míatso nya me le mía dome le nu si nyo la ŋu.
ENGLISH: 4 Let us pick out rights and come to an understanding of what is good,

EWE: 5 Elabena Hiob gblɔ be, ‘Tɔnye dzɔ, Ke Mawu gbe afiatsotso nam.
ENGLISH: 5 Because Job says ‘I am virtuous but Deity has taken away my rights;

EWE: 6 Aʋatso kam mele esi mebe woatso afia dzɔdzɔe nama? Gbedada mele nye abi la ŋu o, evɔ wònye nyemedze agɔ aɖeke o hafi.’
ENGLISH: 6 Against my rights I am to be lying and I have a festering arrow in me without a crime.’

EWE: 7 Ame kae gale abe Hiob ene, Si noa alɔmeɖeɖe abe tsi ene?
ENGLISH: 7 Who is such a man as Job, who drinks scurrility like water

EWE: 8 Ele nu vlo wɔlawo dome Edea ha kple ame vɔ̃ɖiwo.
ENGLISH: 8 And takes the route to fellowship with villains and to company with criminals?

EWE: 9 Elabena egblɔ be, ‘Meɖea vi aɖeke na amegbetɔ Ne edze agbagba be yeadze Mawu ŋu o.’
ENGLISH: 9 Because he says ‘It is of no advantage to a man to be on good terms with God.’

EWE: 10 Eya ta mi ŋutsu nugɔmeselawo, miɖo tom: Mawu vavã la mawɔ nu vɔ̃ɖi akpɔ o, Eye Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la mawɔ nu gbegblẽ gbeɖe o!
ENGLISH: 10 So, men of sense, hear me: away with the thought of wrong-doing on Deity’s part, foul play on Shaddai’s,

EWE: 11 Elabena eɖoa eteƒe na ame ɖe eƒe nuwɔwɔ nu Eye wòhea ame ƒe nuwɔnawo me tsonu vaa edzi.
ENGLISH: 11 For he will pay man back appropriately to what he does, and give each one the experiences proper to the path he takes.

EWE: 12 Nyateƒe matrɔmatrɔe wònye be, Mawu mewɔa nu vɔ̃ɖi o; Eye Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la mebaɖaa afɔ na nya dzɔdzɔe o.
ENGLISH: 12 In real truth Deity does not do wrong nor Shaddai play tricks with justice.

EWE: 13 Ame kae tsɔ anyigbaa de asi nɛ, Eye ame kae ɖoe xexe blibo la nu?
ENGLISH: 13 Who put him in charge of earth? and who established the whole universe?

EWE: 14 Ne etsɔ eƒe ŋku ɖo wo ŋu, Ne egbugbɔ ƒo woƒe gbɔgbɔ kple agbegbɔgbɔ nu ƒu ɖe eɖokui gbɔ la,
ENGLISH: 14 If he should draw his spirit back to himself and take up to himself his breath,

EWE: 15 Amegbetɔwo katã atsrɔ̃, Eye amegbetɔ agatrɔ azu anyi.
ENGLISH: 15 All creatures of flesh would expire together and man would go back to clay.

EWE: 16 Eya ta ne gɔmesese le asiwò la, ekema se nya sia; Lé to ɖe nye nyawo ŋu nyuie.
ENGLISH: 16 And if you are in your senses, listen to me; give ear to the point I make.

EWE: 17 Ðe ame si lé fu nya dzɔdzɔe ate ŋu aɖu dzia? Alo ɖe nàbu fɔ ŋusẽtɔ si nye nu dzɔdzɔe wɔla?
ENGLISH: 17 Is it even to be that one who hates justice holds sway or a great right-doer does wrong?

EWE: 18 Ðe nàte ŋu agblɔ na fia be, ‘Yakame nènyea,’ Alo na bubumewo be, ‘Ame vɔ̃ɖiwo mienyea’?
ENGLISH: 18 He who says ‘reprobate’ to a king and ‘iniquitous’ to noblemen,

EWE: 19 Ke Ame aɖe li si medea amegãwo dzi o Eye melɔ̃a kesinɔtɔ ƒe nya wu ame dahe o, Elabena eƒe asinudɔwɔwɔe wo katã wonye.
ENGLISH: 19 Who does not defer to generals nor recognize a prominent man before a poor man, because they are all the work of his hands?

EWE: 20 Wotea ŋu kuna kpata le zãtiƒe; Woƒona tititi, eye womiaa nu; Woɖea ŋusẽtɔwo gɔ̃ hã ɖa, ke menye kple amegbetɔ ƒe asi o.
ENGLISH: 20 They die in a moment, at midnight; he touches prominent men and they pass by, and removes a formidable fighter without turning a hand.

EWE: 21 Elabena Mawu ƒe ŋku le amegbetɔ ƒe mɔwo ŋu, Eye wòkpɔa eƒe afɔɖeɖewo katã.
ENGLISH: 21 For his eyes are on a man’s courses and he sees all his steps;

EWE: 22 Viviti alo blukɔ aɖeke meli, Si me nu vlo wɔlawo abe ɖo o.
ENGLISH: 22 There is no darkness, no gloom, that villains may be veiled in.

EWE: 23 Elabena Mawu meɖoa ɣeyiɣi ɖi na ame aɖeke, Be wòava ʋɔnu le ye ŋkume o.
ENGLISH: 23 For a man does not have a date set him to go to Deity for a trial;

EWE: 24 Egbãa ŋusẽtɔwo gudugudu esi mehiã be wòaku nya gɔme hafi o Eye wònana ame bubuwo xɔna ɖe wo teƒe.
ENGLISH: 24 He breaks great men without an investigation and sets up others in their place.

EWE: 25 Elabena enya nu siwo wɔm wole; Etua asi wo ƒua anyi le zã me, eye wogbãna gudugudu.
ENGLISH: 25 So he is aware of their works, and overthrows in the night and they are beaten down.

EWE: 26 Eƒoa wo le woƒe vɔɖivɔ̃ɖi ta, Le afi si ame sia ame ate ŋu akpɔ wo le,
ENGLISH: 26 For wrong-doers he cuffs them in a place with spectators,

EWE: 27 Elabena wotrɔ le eyome Eye womegatsɔ ɖeke le eƒe mɔ aɖeke me o;
ENGLISH: 27 Seeing that they had turned off from following him and not been regardful of any of his courses,

EWE: 28 Wona ame dahewo do ɣli nɛ, Ale be wòse wɔnamanɔŋutɔwo ƒe ɣlidodo.
ENGLISH: 28 Bringing in before him a poor man’s outcry and letting him hear the outcry of downtrodden men.

EWE: 29 Ne Mawu zi ɖoɖoe la, ame kae ate ŋu abu fɔe? Ne eɣla eƒe mo la, ame kae ate ŋu akpɔe? Eɖaɣlae ɖe dukɔ loo alo ɖe amegbetɔ o, nya ɖeka ma ke koe,
ENGLISH: 29 But if he is quiet who is to condemn? or if he veils his face who is to behold him? be it over a nation or over a man alike,

EWE: 30 Ne mawumavɔ̃la nagaɖu dzi Alo be wòatre mɔ̃wo na dukɔ la o.
ENGLISH: 30 That an ungodly man may not be king, a people’s trap.

EWE: 31 Elabena ɖe ame aɖe agblɔ na Mawu be, ‘Wohe to nam, evɔ nyemewɔ nu gbegblẽ aɖeke hafi o;
ENGLISH: 31 For does he say to Deity ‘I bear; I will not do harmful things;

EWE: 32 Ðe nu si kpɔm nyemele o la fiam; Eye ne nu gbegblẽ aɖee mewɔ la, ekema nyemagawɔe azɔ oa’?
ENGLISH: 32 What I do not see, teach me yourself; if I have done amiss I will not keep on’?

EWE: 33 Ðe Mawu aɖo eteƒe na wò le wò didi nu esi nègbe eƒe afiatsotsoa?
ENGLISH: 33 Was he to make requital on the basis of your ideas, that you are vetoing?

EWE: Wòe atso nya me, menye nyee o. Azɔ gblɔ nu si nènya nyuie la nam.
ENGLISH: For you are to choose, not I; what you know, speak out!

EWE: 34 Ŋutsu nugɔmeselawo Ŋutsu siwo si gɔmesese le siwo le to ɖomem la agblɔ be,
ENGLISH: 34 Men of brains will say to me, and a wise man who hears me,

EWE: 35 ‘Hiob menya nya si gblɔm wòle o, Eye gɔmesese mele eƒe nyawo me o.’
ENGLISH: 35 Job speaks not by knowledge and his words do not run by common sense.

EWE: 36 Ne ɖe woado Hiob akpɔ wòade edeƒe, Le esi wòle nya ŋu ɖom abe ame vɔ̃ɖiwo ene ta ɖe!
ENGLISH: 36 Let Job be kept under test permanently for answers that put him among villains!

EWE: 37 Etsɔ aglãdzedze kpe ɖe eƒe nu vɔ̃ ŋuti; Esi akpe fewuɖutɔe le mía ŋkume, Eye wògblɔ nyawo fũu ɖe Mawu vavã la ŋu!”
ENGLISH: 37 For he adds rebelliousness to his sin, slaps his hands between us and talks volubly to the Deity.”

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 35 Elihu gblɔ yi edzi be:
ENGLISH: 35 And Elihu answered

EWE: 2 “Èka ɖe edzi tututu be wò nya dzɔ esi nèle gbɔgblɔm be, ‘Tɔnye dzɔ wu Mawu tɔa’?
ENGLISH: 2 “Do you think this right, say ‘my good case before Deity,’

EWE: 3 Elabena èle gbɔgblɔm be, ‘Vi kae wòaɖe na wò? Ðe wòanyo nam wu ne ɖe mewɔ nu vɔ̃a?’
ENGLISH: 3 That you ask how it benefits you, ‘What good do I get more than by my sinning?’

EWE: 4 Maɖo eŋu, Maɖo eŋu na wò kple xɔwò siwo le gbɔwò.
ENGLISH: 4 I give you the answer, and your comrades with you,

EWE: 5 Fɔ mo dzi nàkpɔ dziƒo, Kpɔ alilikpo siwo le tawòme boo la ɖa.
ENGLISH: 5 Look at the sky and see, and behold the ether so high above you;

EWE: 6 Ne èwɔ nu vɔ̃ la, nu kae nàgblẽ le eŋu? Eye ne wò vodadawo dzi ɖe edzi la, nu kae nèwɔ nɛ?
ENGLISH: 6 If you have sinned what are you doing to him, and if your crimes are many what effect has it on him?

EWE: 7 Ne èle dzɔdzɔe la, nu ka tsɔm nèle nɛ; Alo nu ka xɔm wòle le asiwò?
ENGLISH: 7 If you have done right what are you giving to him, or what is he getting at your hands?

EWE: 8 Amegbetɔ si le abe wò ene koe wò nu vɔ̃ awɔ nane na, Eye amegbetɔviwo dzi koe wò dzɔdzɔenyenye awɔ dɔ ɖo.
ENGLISH: 8 Your wrong-doing pertains to a man like yourself and your right-doing to a human being.

EWE: 9 Amewo doa ɣli le teteɖeanyi ta; Wodoa ɣli be woaxɔ na yewo le ŋusẽtɔwo ƒe amedziɖuɖu ta.
ENGLISH: 9 They cry out over the great number of denials of justice, they clamor over powerful men’s high hand,

EWE: 10 Gake ame aɖeke megblɔna be, ‘Afi kae Mawu, nye Wɔla Gã la, Ame si nana kafukafuhawo ɖina le zã me la le?’ o.
ENGLISH: 10 And one has not said ‘Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night,

EWE: 11 Eyae nye Ame si fiaa nu mí wu anyigbadzilãwo, Eye wònana míedzea nunya wu dziƒoxe dzodzoewo.
ENGLISH: 11 Who teaches us more than the beasts of earth and makes us wiser than the birds of the air?’

EWE: 12 Amewo doa ɣli, gake meɖoa eŋu na wo o, Le ame vɔ̃ɖiwo ƒe dada ta.
ENGLISH: 12 It is there that they cry unanswered because of the pride of bad men,

EWE: 13 Mawu ƒe to menɔa kokoƒoƒo gbɔlowo ŋu o; Eye Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la doa toku wo.
ENGLISH: 13 All in vain Deity does not hear and Shaddai does not regard it.

EWE: 14 Hafi wòa nànɔ gbɔgblɔm be yemele ekpɔm o! Wò nya la le eŋkume, eya ta kpɔ esinu.
ENGLISH: 14 Even when you say you do not behold him, he has the case before him and you are to wait for him.

EWE: 15 Elabena medo dziku bia akɔnta ame loo; Alo tsɔ wò nuƒoƒo dzimagbɔɖitɔe la vevie o.
ENGLISH: 15 And now because he does not set his anger to work he does not thoroughly know the offense!

EWE: 16 Hiob ya, ɖe wòke eƒe nu baa dzodzro; Edudu nyawo kɔ ɖi bababa, ke menya nya si gblɔm wòle o.”
ENGLISH: 16 But Job is opening his mouth to let out air, uttering big phrases without knowing what he is talking about.”

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 36 Elihu yi eƒe nyawo dzi be:
ENGLISH: 36 And Elihu said further

EWE: 2 “Gagbɔ dzi ɖi nam vie, ne maɖe nu me na wò, Elabena nyawo gali magblɔ ɖe Mawu nu.
ENGLISH: 2 “Wait a bit and I will show you, for there is more to say for God.

EWE: 3 Magblɔ nu sia nu si menya, nyemagblẽ ɖeke ɖi o, Eye maɖee afia be nye Wɔla la tɔe dzɔ.
ENGLISH: 3 I will take a broad view and credit my Maker with doing right.

EWE: 4 Elabena nye nyawo menye alakpa kura o; Ame si ƒe nunya de blibo la tsɔ ɖe gbɔwò kpuie.
ENGLISH: 4 What I have to say is no falsification; you have with you one who is sincere in his views.

EWE: 5 Ŋusẽtɔe Mawu nye, eye megbea ame aɖeke o; Eya sie gɔmesese deto le.
ENGLISH: 5 Lo, Deity is supreme and will not be disdainful, supreme in power of mind.

EWE: 6 Maxɔ ame vɔ̃ɖi aɖeke ɖe agbe o, Ke boŋ atso afia dzɔdzɔe na ame si wote ɖe anyi.
ENGLISH: 6 He will not let a wrong-doer live and will give downtrodden men their rights.

EWE: 7 Meɖea ŋku ɖa le ame dzɔdzɔewo ŋu o; Eɖoa wo zi dzi le fiawo xa, eye wòdoa wo ɖe dzi ɖaa.
ENGLISH: 7 He will not minimize his attention to a right-doer, but with kings will enthrone them permanently, and they shall be exalted.

EWE: 8 Gake ne wode kunyowu wo Eye fukpekpe ƒe ka bla wo la,
ENGLISH: 8 And if they are bound in fetters, caught in cords of misery,

EWE: 9 Eɖea nu si wowɔ la fiaa wo, Si nye vo siwo woda, le dada ta.
ENGLISH: 9 He tells them of their doings and their offenses, that they were overweening,

EWE: 10 Eʋua to na wo be woaxɔ ɖɔɖɔɖo Eye wògblɔna na wo be woatrɔ tso woƒe mɔ vɔ̃wo dzi.
ENGLISH: 10 And makes disciplinary disclosures to them and says they are to turn back from vileness.

EWE: 11 Ne woɖo toe hesubɔe la, Ekema eme anyo na wo le woƒe agbe me katã, Eye woƒe ƒewo awu enu nyuie.
ENGLISH: 11 If they listen and submit they shall finish their days in good living and their years in comfort;

EWE: 12 Ke ne womeɖo to o la, ekema woatsi yi nu, Eye woaku le numanyamanya me.
ENGLISH: 12 But if they do not listen they will rush upon destruction and come to their end by lack of knowledge.

EWE: 13 Ame siwo mevɔ̃a Mawu le woƒe dziwo me o la léa dziku ɖe dɔme. Ne ede ga wo hã, womedoa ɣli be woaxɔ na yewo o.
ENGLISH: 13 But men of godless heart take to anger, do not cry out petitions when he binds them;

EWE: 14 Woƒe agbe nu atso le ɖekakpui dzodzoe me, Le esi wobɔa ha kple ŋutsu siwo gbɔ ŋutsuwo dɔna le gbedoxɔ me ta.
ENGLISH: 14 Their vital spark shall die off in youth and their lives as do sodomite boys.

EWE: 15 Ke Mawu ɖea ame siwo le fu kpem la tso woƒe fukpekpewo me; Eye wòʋua to na wo le teteɖeanyiɣi.
ENGLISH: 15 He rescues an unfortunate man in his misfortune and makes disclosures to them in privations.

EWE: 16 Ahe wò ɖa tso xaxa me Ayi gbadzaƒe afi si nàvo le, Atsɔ nuɖuɖu damiwo aɖo kplɔ̃ na wò atsɔ afa akɔ na wò.
ENGLISH: 16 And he has been enticing you out of the mouth of distress too,unconstrained roominess under it, and the setting down of your table full of rich food.

EWE: 17 Ekema wò dzi adze eme ne wodrɔ̃ ʋɔnu ame vɔ̃ɖiwo; Ne wotso afia helé nya dzɔdzɔe me ɖe asi.
ENGLISH: 17 And you are full of the sentence on a wrong-doer; judgment and sentence take hold,

EWE: 18 Gake kpɔ nyuie be dɔmedzoe nagahe wò de fewuɖuɖu me o, Eye mègana zãnu gã nakplɔ wò atrae o.
ENGLISH: 18 For let not choler entice you into mockery nor abundance of composition-money deflect you.

EWE: 19 Ðe wò ɣlidodowo Alo wò dagbadagba aɖe wò tso xaxa mea?
ENGLISH: 19 Will your clamor take effect without distress, and all exertions of strength?

EWE: 20 Mègatsi dzi ɖe zã ƒe dodo ŋu, Esime amewo búna le wo nɔƒewo o.
ENGLISH: 20 Do not pant for the night, to have peoples go up where they stand.

EWE: 21 Kpɔ nyuie be nàgatrɔ ɖe nu vɔ̃ɖi ŋu o, Be nàgatsɔ ema aɖɔli fukpekpe o.
ENGLISH: 21 Beware, do not turn to depravity, for you have been preferring this to suffering.

EWE: 22 Kpɔ ɖa! Mawu ƒe ŋusẽ do eya amea ɖe dzi; Nufiala kae de enu?
ENGLISH: 22 Lo, Deity shows himself supernal in his strength; who is such a preceptor as he?

EWE: 23 Ame kae fia mɔe, Alo gblɔ nɛ be, ‘Nu si nèwɔ la menyo o’?
ENGLISH: 23 Who has appointed his course for him, and who has said ‘You have done amiss’?

EWE: 24 Ðo ŋku edzi nàdo eƒe dɔwɔwɔ ɖe dzi, Dɔwɔwɔ si ŋu amewo dzi ha le.
ENGLISH: 24 Remember to extol his work, of which men have sung.

EWE: 25 Ameƒomea katã kpɔ esia kple ŋku, Amegbetɔwo kpɔnɛ dũu tso adzɔge.
ENGLISH: 25 All mankind view it, man looks at it from afar.

EWE: 26 Ɛ̃, Mawu lolo wu ale si míate ŋu anya; Eƒe ƒewo ƒe agbɔsɔsɔ gbɔ míaƒe gɔmesese ŋu.
ENGLISH: 26 Lo, Deity is great beyond our knowledge; the number of his years is incalculable.

EWE: 27 Ehea tsi toŋtoŋwo yia dzii; Wozua tsidzadza tso eƒe afu me;
ENGLISH: 27 For he takes away drops from the sea to filter as rain for his mist,

EWE: 28 Ale be alilikpowo dzanɛ; Eye wodzana ɖe amegbetɔwo dzi bababa.
ENGLISH: 28 Which the heavens let trickle down and let drop upon many a man.

EWE: 29 Ðe ame aɖe ate ŋu ase ɖoɖo si nu alilikpowo le, Kple ale si dzi ɖea gbe tso eƒe agbadɔ me la gɔmea?
ENGLISH: 29 Or does one understand the spreading of clouds either? the resoundings of his bower?
