EWE: 30 Kpɔ ale si wòklẽa eƒe dzikedzo ɖe edzii, Kple ale si wòtsyɔa nu atsiaƒu ƒe gogloƒewo dzii ɖa!
ENGLISH: 30 Lo, he spreads his mist about him and covers mountaintops.

EWE: 31 Elabena woawoe wòtsɔna léa dukɔwo ɖe te; Eye wònaa nuɖuɖu wo le agbɔsɔsɔ me.
ENGLISH: 31 For by them he provisions peoples, gives food on a great scale.

EWE: 32 Etsyɔa asi dzikedzo dzi, Eye wòɖonɛ ɖe afi si wòdi.
ENGLISH: 32 He covers a stone with light and orders it to strike a mark,

EWE: 33 Eƒe gbeɖeɖe le boblo domee, Lãhawo gɔ̃ hã le boblo dom ame si gbɔna.
ENGLISH: 33 Assailing mischief and wrong and wreaking jealous anger on foul play.

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 37 “Esia na nye dzi lã kpo Eye wòle tsotsom kpokpokpo.
ENGLISH: 37 My heart is alarmed too at this and jumps out of its place.

EWE: 2 Miɖo to eƒe gbe ƒe gbeɖeɖe Kple bublu si le dodom tso eƒe nu me la nyuie.
ENGLISH: 2 Hear, hear the commotions of his voice and what comes as a mutter from his mouth!

EWE: 3 Enana wòɖina le dziƒo bliboa katã te Eye eƒe dzikedzo dea anyigba ƒe mlɔenuwo.
ENGLISH: 3 He sends it abroad under all the sky and his light over the edges of the earth.

EWE: 4 Gbe ɖina sesĩe ɖe eyome; Eɖea gbe ŋusẽtɔe, Eye ne eƒe gbe ɖi la, megaxea mɔ nɛ o.
ENGLISH: 4 Behind it a voice roars; he thunders with his sublime voice and does not hold them back when his voice is heard;

EWE: 5 Mawu ɖea gbe nukutɔe; Ewɔa nu gã nu gã siwo gbɔ míaƒe gɔmesese ŋu.
ENGLISH: 5 Deity thunders with his voice wondrously.

EWE: 6 Elabena egblɔna na sno be, ‘Dza ɖe anyigba dzi,’ Eye wògblɔna na tsidzadza gãwo be, ‘Ðuɖu kɔ ɖe anyi yoo.’
ENGLISH: He does things great beyond our knowledge, 6 For he says to the snow ‘Fall to earth’ and showers down his mighty rains.

EWE: 7 Mawu ɖoa asi amewo katã ƒe dɔwo dzi, Ne amegbetɔwo katã nadze si Eƒe dɔwɔwɔwo.
ENGLISH: 7 He seals up every human being’s hands that all men may know his work;

EWE: 8 Gbemelãwo sina bena Eye wonɔa woƒe bebeƒewo.
ENGLISH: 8 And beasts go into coverts and lodge in their dens.

EWE: 9 Ahom tuna tsoa eƒe xɔgã me, Eye dzieheya kplɔa vuvɔ vanɛ.
ENGLISH: 9 Out of the Chamber comes a gale and out of Mezarim cold weather.

EWE: 10 Mawu ƒe gbɔgbɔ nana be tsiwo blana, Eye tɔ gbanaawo blana zua tsikpe.
ENGLISH: 10 By Deity’s breath ice is put in and the breadth of water is in curbs.

EWE: 11 Ɛ̃, etsɔa tsi doa agba na alilikpo; Ekakaa eƒe dzikedzo ɖe alilikpowo me;
ENGLISH: 11 Also he loads a cloud with refreshment, cloudy sky scatters his fall rain,

EWE: 12 Wotrɔna ƒoa xlã godoo ɖe eƒe mɔfiafia nu; Wowɔa nu sia nu si ƒe se wòde na wo le anyigba bliboa dzi.
ENGLISH: 12 And it goes circling about by his guidance that they may do all that he orders them to over the world on the ground,

EWE: 13 Eɖanye be wòatsɔ ahe to loo, atsɔ ade tsi anyigbaa loo Alo atsɔ aɖe amenuveve afia o, enana wòvaa eme.
ENGLISH: 13 If for a cudgel, if for his earth, if for kindness he sends it to its goal.

EWE: 14 Oo Hiob, lé to ɖe esia ŋu; Tɔ sẽe, ne nàlé ŋku ɖe Mawu ƒe nukudɔwo ŋu nyuie.
ENGLISH: 14 Give ear to this, Job; stand still and realize Deity’s wonders.

EWE: 15 Ènya ale si Mawu fiaa mɔ alilikpowo Kple ale si wònana dzi kea dzo tsoa eƒe alilikpowo mea?
ENGLISH: 15 Do you know how God lays their charge on them and the light of his clouds beams out?

EWE: 16 Ènya ale si alilikpo wɔna lina ɖe yamea? Esiawoe nye Ame si ƒe nunya de blibo la ƒe nukudɔwo.
ENGLISH: 16 Do you know about the hovering of clouds, the wonders of him who is faultless in skill?

EWE: 17 Nu ka tae wò awuwo me xɔ dzo, Le ɣeyiɣi si me anyieheya na anyigba dzi fa?
ENGLISH: 17 Will you whose clothes grow hot when earth has quietness from the south

EWE: 18 Ðe nàte ŋu akpe ɖe eŋu miakeke dziŋgɔli Si sesẽ abe gahuhɔ̃e ene la mea?
ENGLISH: 18 Be with him to consolidate heavens strong as a metal mirror?

EWE: 19 Gblɔ nya si míayi aɖagblɔ nɛ la na mí; Míate ŋu akpɔ nya aɖeke agblɔ o, le esi míele viviti me ta.
ENGLISH: 19 Let us know what to say to him; we cannot get it in order for darkness.

EWE: 20 Ðe woayi aɖagblɔ nɛ be medi be maƒo nua? Alo ɖe ame aɖe gblɔ nya aɖe si wòhiã be wòasea?
ENGLISH: 20 Is he to be told the story of my speaking? or does any man think of being swept away?

EWE: 21 Womate ŋu akpɔ kekeli gɔ̃ hã o, Togbɔ be ele keklẽm le yame hã, Va se ɖe esime ya ƒo va yi eye wòƒo alilikpoawo ɖa hafi.
ENGLISH: 21 And now they do not see light, it is a bright spot in the heavens; but a wind goes over and clears them.

EWE: 22 Keklẽ si le abe sikatsyɔ̃ɖoɖo ene dzena le dziehe wokpɔna; Mawu ƒe gãnyenye wɔ nuku ŋutɔ.
ENGLISH: 22 From the north comes resplendence; over God there is a refulgence that is terrible.

EWE: 23 Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la gɔme sese gbɔ míaƒe ŋutete ŋu; Eƒe ŋusẽ tri akɔ, Eye eléa ʋɔnu dzɔdzɔe dɔdrɔ̃ kple dzɔdzɔenyenye blibo me ɖe asi ɣeawokatãɣi.
ENGLISH: 23 Shaddai our minds do not reach to him, ample in strength and justice and great in right-dealing; he will not victimize.

EWE: 24 Eya ta ele be amegbetɔwo navɔ̃e. Elabena mevea ame siwo bua wo ɖokuiwo nunyalawoe la nu o.”
ENGLISH: 24 So men fear him; he does not take notice of any wise-headed men.”

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 38 Eye Yehowa ɖo eŋu na Hiob le ahom me be:
ENGLISH: 38 But Jehovah answered Job out of the tempest

EWE: 2 “Ame kae nye esia si le nu tsyɔm nye adaŋudede dzi Hele nu ƒom numanyamanyatɔe?
ENGLISH: 2 “Who is this that is befogging a discussion by phrases without knowledge?

EWE: 3 Meɖe kuku, tso nàbla ali dzi abe ŋutsu ene; Ne mabia nya wò nàɖo eŋu nam.
ENGLISH: 3 Gird your loins like a man so that I may ask you questions and you inform me.

EWE: 4 Afi kae nènɔ esime meɖo anyigba la gɔme anyi?
ENGLISH: 4 Where were you when I laid the foundation of earth? tell, if you have competent knowledge.

EWE: Ne ènyae la, ekema gblɔe nam. 5 Ame kae ɖo eƒe dzidzemewo, ènyaea? Alo ame kae da dzidzeka nɛ?
ENGLISH: 5 Who determined its dimensions? for you know! or who stretched a measuring-line over it?

EWE: 6 Nu ka mee woƒo eƒe anyinɔwo ɖo, Alo ame kae ɖo eƒe dzogoedzikpe,
ENGLISH: 6 On what were its under-foundations planted? or who laid its cornerstone

EWE: 7 Esime ŋukeɣletiviwo gli kple dzidzɔ, Eye Mawu viwo katã do dzidzɔɣli?
ENGLISH: 7 While the morning stars shouted together and all the angels hurrahed?

EWE: 8 Ame kae do ʋɔ ɖe atsiaƒu nu Esi wòdo tso vidzidɔ me,
ENGLISH: 8 Who enclosed the sea with doors when it came bursting out of the womb,

EWE: 9 Esime metsyɔ alilikpo nɛ, Eye mexatsa blukɔ ɖe eŋu abe avɔ ene,
ENGLISH: 9 When I made clouds its clothing and thick air its wrapping

EWE: 10 Esime meɖo seƒe nɛ Eye mede gametiwo kple ʋɔtruwo enu,
ENGLISH: 10 And broke a boundary for it and set a bar and doors,

EWE: 11 Eye megblɔ be, ‘Afi sia ko nàva se ɖo, màgbɔ eŋu o; Afi siae wò tsotsoe kpakawo ase ɖo’?
ENGLISH: 11 And said ‘You are to come to here but not beyond, and here the pride of your waves shall break’?

EWE: 12 Èɖe gbe na ŋu be wòake kpɔ, Alo èfia agudzedze eƒe nɔƒee kpɔ,
ENGLISH: 12 Did you ever in your life command a morning, let a dawn know its place

EWE: 13 Ne wòalé anyigbatogawo Aʋuʋui be ame vɔ̃ɖiwo nahlẽ ɖa le edzia?
ENGLISH: 13 To take hold of earth’s edges that wrong-doers may be shaken out of it?

EWE: 14 Eƒe nɔnɔme trɔna abe tsu si to nutrenu te ene, Eye edzinuwo dzena nyuie abe nu si woɖe ɖe avɔ dzi ene.
ENGLISH: 14 It takes shape like clay printed with a stamp, and colors like a dress,

EWE: 15 Ke woxɔ ame vɔ̃ɖiwo ƒe kekeli le wo si, Eye woŋe woƒe alɔ si wodo ɖe dzi la.
ENGLISH: 15 And wrong-doers have their light withheld, and a high-raised arm is broken.

EWE: 16 Ðe nède atsiaƒu dzɔƒewo kpɔa, Alo ɖe nèɖi tsa yi tsi ƒe gogloƒewo kpɔa?
ENGLISH: 16 Have you come to the sources of the sea and gone inspecting through the deep?

EWE: 17 Ðe woɖe ku ƒe agbowo fia wò kpɔa, Alo ɖe nèkpɔ viviti tsiɖitsiɖi ƒe agbowo kpɔa?
ENGLISH: 17 Have the gates of death been laid open for you, or the gatemen of gloom been afraid at sight of you?

EWE: 18 Èse ale si gbegbe anyigba la kekee gɔmea?
ENGLISH: 18 Have you applied your attention to the breadths of earth? tell, if you know it all.

EWE: Ne ènya nu siawo katã la, gblɔe mase. 19 Kekeli gbɔ mɔ ɖe? Afi kae nye viviti nɔƒe,
ENGLISH: 19 In which direction does light have its home, and which is the place for darkness?

EWE: 20 Ne nàkplɔ wo ayi woƒe anyigba dzi, Eye nànya woƒe aƒe me mɔ?
ENGLISH: 20 Because you get it at its domain and are expert in the paths to its house.

EWE: 21 Ðe wodzi wò ɣemaɣi be nàyi esia nya ge Le esi nètsi xɔ ƒe geɖe taa?
ENGLISH: 21 You know, because you were born then and the number of your days is great!

EWE: 22 Ðe nède sno ƒe nudzraɖoƒewo kpɔa, Alo ɖe nèkpɔ kpetsi ƒe nudzraɖoƒewo kpɔ,
ENGLISH: 22 Have you been into the reserves of snow, and seen the reserves of hail

EWE: 23 Esiwo medzra ɖo ɖi ɖe xaxaɣi, Aʋaŋkeke kple aʋakpegbe ŋua?
ENGLISH: 23 Which I am holding back for a day of crisis,a day of battle and war?

EWE: 24 Mɔ ka dzie kekeli tona klẽna, Eye afi kae ɣedzeƒeya tona ƒona ɖe anyigba dzi?
ENGLISH: 24 In which direction is wind divided, east wind scattered over earth?

EWE: 25 Ame kae ɖe toƒe na tsiɖɔɖɔ, Eye wòɖe mɔ na dzikedzo kple dziɖegbe,
ENGLISH: 25 Who laid out a system of channels for floods and a course for the lightning of thunder,

EWE: 26 Ne wòana tsi nadza ɖe teƒe si ame aɖeke mele o, Ðe gbedzi, afi si amegbetɔ aɖeke mele o,
ENGLISH: 26 To send rain on a country without a man, a wilderness with no human being in it,

EWE: 27 Ne wòadzra teƒe siwo zu gbegbe la ɖo nyuie, Eye wòana gbe namie?
ENGLISH: 27 To satisfy the hunger of blasted and blighted places and to make a thirsty place grow vegetation?

EWE: 28 Ðe fofo le tsidzadza sia, Alo ame kae dzi ahũdzadza?
ENGLISH: 28 Does the rain have a father? or who brought dewdrops to birth?

EWE: 29 Ame ka ƒe dɔ mee tsikpe do tso, Eye dziƒoketsiwo ya ɖe, ame kae dzi wo
ENGLISH: 29 Out of whose body did the ice come? and who gave birth to hoarfrost?

EWE: 30 Esime tsiwo ŋkume sẽ abe kpe ene, Eye tsi goglo la ŋgɔ bla zu tsikpe?
ENGLISH: 30 Water masks itself like a stone and the surface of the deep coheres.

EWE: 31 Ðe nàte ŋu asa Kima ɣletivihatsotso ƒe kawo, Alo atu Kesil ɣletivihatsotso ƒe kawoa?
ENGLISH: 31 Shall you be tying the laces of the Pleiades or unhitching the traces of Orion,

EWE: 32 Ðe nàte ŋu akplɔ ɣletivihatsotso adoe le eƒe ɣeyiɣi dzi Alo afia mɔ Ayis ɣletivihatsotso la kple viawoa?
ENGLISH: 32 Making Mazzaroth come out at its time and guiding Aldebaran with its sons under it?

EWE: 33 Ðe nènya dziƒo ƒe sewoa, Alo ɖe nàte ŋu ana eƒe ŋusẽ naɖu anyigba dzia?
ENGLISH: 33 Do you know the laws of the sky or are you ordaining its supervision of the earth?

EWE: 34 Ðe nàte ŋu akɔ gbe dzi ado ɣli na alilikpo Ne wòana tsi natsyɔ dziwòa?
ENGLISH: 34 Will you send your voice aloft to the cloud and have a spray of water cover you?

EWE: 35 Ðe nàte ŋu adɔ dzikedzowoa? Ale be woava gblɔ na wò be, ‘Míawoe nye esia!’
ENGLISH: 35 Will you send lightnings abroad, and have them go and say to you ‘Here we are’?

EWE: 36 Ame kae tsɔ nunya de alilikpowo me, Alo ame kae na gɔmesese yamenu wɔnukuwo?
ENGLISH: 36 Who implanted wisdom in the ibis? or who gave discernment to the cock?

EWE: 37 Ame ka sie nunya le be wòaxlẽ alilikpowo, Alo ame kae ate ŋu atrɔ dziƒotsizewo abu anyi
ENGLISH: 37 Who counts in wisdom the threads of mare’s-tail clouds,and the water-bags of the sky who tips down

EWE: 38 Ale be kewɔ nazu bafifi Eye anyikɔwo nalé ɖe wo nɔewo ŋu?
ENGLISH: 38 When loam runs into metal and clods cling together?

EWE: 39 Ðe nàte ŋu ada ade alé nu na dzata, Alo afa dɔwuame nu na dzataviwo
ENGLISH: 39 Will you hunt prey for a lioness and fill the need of two-year-old lions

EWE: 40 Ne wotsyɔ akɔ ɖe bebeƒewo Alo de xa ɖe wo nɔƒewoa?
ENGLISH: 40 When they are down in the lairs,sitting in ambush in a covert?

EWE: 41 Ame kae dia nuɖuɖu na akpaviã, Ne viawo le xɔxlɔ̃m na Mawu be wòaxɔ na yewo, Eye wole tsatsam le esi naneke meli woaɖu o ta?
ENGLISH: 41 Who gets its provision ready for the raven when its young are clamoring to Deity, wandering about in want of food?

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 39 “Ðe nènya ɣeyiɣi si agamegbɔ̃ dzia via?
ENGLISH: 39 Do you know crag ibexes’ birth, watch does’ calving?

EWE: Èkpɔ zinɔ ƒe vidzidzi teƒe kpɔa? 2 Ðe nèxlẽa ɣleti siwo fu nɔa wo ƒoa?
ENGLISH: 2 Do you count the months they fill out, and know their birth-date?

EWE: Alo ɖe nènya ɣeyiɣi si tututu wodzia via? 3 Wobɔbɔna dzia vi, Eye woƒe kuléle nu tsona.
ENGLISH: 3 They crouch down, detach their young, let go what they have been hampered with;

EWE: 4 Ŋusẽ ɖoa wo viwo ŋu, eye wotsina le gbe me; Wodzona, eye womegagbɔna vaa wo gbɔ o.
ENGLISH: 4 Their children are robust, grow big in the wilds, go out and never come back.

EWE: 5 Ame kae na ablɔɖe gbetedzi, Eye ame kae tu kae?
ENGLISH: 5 Who set free a wild ass and unhitched an onager’s halter,

EWE: 6 Metsɔ gbegbe wɔ aƒe nɛ Eye dzenyigbae nye enɔƒe.
ENGLISH: 6 Of which I have made desert the home, alkali plains the habitation?

EWE: 7 Hoowɔwɔ si ɖina le du me la ɖia kokoe nɛ; Mesea lãkplɔla ƒe ɣlidodo o.
ENGLISH: 7 It laughs at town noises, hears no vociferations of a driver.

EWE: 8 Etsana dia gbeɖuƒe le togbɛwo dzi Eye wòdia gbe mumu ɖe sia ɖe yome mɔ.
ENGLISH: 8 It explores mountains as its pasture and searches after any green thing.

EWE: 9 Ðe gbenyi alɔ̃ asubɔ wòa? Alo ɖe wòatsi wò lãkpo me adɔa?
ENGLISH: 9 Will a ure be willing to work for you or come to your crib for the night?

EWE: 10 Ðe nàte ŋu ade ka gbenyi be wòaŋlɔ agble, Alo ana wòagudu bali me le yowòmea?
ENGLISH: 10 Will you tie a yoke on him with cords or will he harrow vales after you?

EWE: 11 Ðe nàɖo ŋu ɖe eƒe ŋusẽ geɖe la ŋu Ahatsɔ wò dɔ gãwo agblẽ ɖe esi mea?
ENGLISH: 11 Will you put confidence in him because his strength is great,and leave to him the results of your toil?

EWE: 12 Ðe nàɖo ŋu ɖe eŋu wòatsɔ wò agblemenukuwo agbɔe na wò Ahaƒo enu ƒu ɖe wò nukuƒoƒea?
ENGLISH: 12 Will you rely on him to come back, get in your seed to your threshing-floor?

EWE: 13 Golo ƒoa eƒe aʋala kpakpakpa dzidzɔtɔe, Evɔ ɖe woate ŋu atsɔ eƒe aʋala kple eƒe fu asɔ kple damixe tɔa?
ENGLISH: 13 An ostrich’s wing is for pleasure; or is it a kindly pinion and plume,

EWE: 14 Elabena egblẽa eƒe azi ɖe anyigba, Eye wònana ke dea dzo wo me.
ENGLISH: 14 When she leaves her eggs on the ground and warms them on the earth,

EWE: 15 Eŋlɔna be be woate ŋu aɖo afɔ wo dzi woagbã, Alo be gbemelã aɖe ate ŋu azɔ wo dzi.
ENGLISH: 15 And has forgotten that feet will smash them and wild animals tread them to pieces?

EWE: 16 Ewɔa ŋlɔmi le viawo ŋu, abe menye etɔwoe wonye o ene; Mevɔ̃na be yeƒe agbagbadzedze azu dzodzro o.
ENGLISH: 16 She is hardhearted to her young as if they were not hers; her labor goes for nothing without alarming her,

EWE: 17 Elabena Mawu na nunya bɔe Eye mena gɔmesese aɖekee o.
ENGLISH: 17 Because God has made her unmindful of wisdom and given her no allowance of sense.

EWE: 18 Gake ne etso, ƒo aʋala la, Sɔ kple edola ƒe nu ɖia kokoe nɛ.
ENGLISH: 18 The minute she goes off high she laughs at the pony and its rider.

EWE: 19 Wòe na ŋusẽ sɔa? Wòe ɖo kɔdza kɔ ŋu nɛa?
ENGLISH: 19 Do you give the ponies mettle? do you clothe their necks with mane?

EWE: 20 Àte ŋu ana wòati kpo abe ʋetsuvi enea? Eƒe ŋɔtimetudada dzia ŋɔ.
ENGLISH: 20 Do you set them in commotion like grasshoppers? the thrill of their snorting is a terror.

EWE: 21 Etsɔa afɔ kaa anyigba le bali me, eye wòtia kpo kple ŋusẽ; Elũna ɖe aʋa me.
ENGLISH: 21 They paw in the vale and are joyous, go out in strength to meet an armament,

EWE: 22 Ŋɔdzi ɖia kokoe nɛ, eye mevɔ̃a naneke o. Megbugbɔna ɖe megbe le yi nu o.
ENGLISH: 22 Laugh at terrors and are not dismayed, and do not turn back before swords.

EWE: 23 Aŋutrɔ ŋkɔ le ɖiɖim le eƒe axadzi; Nenema kee nye akplɔ kple akplɔvi siwo le dzo dam la hã.
ENGLISH: 23 On them ring quiver, spearhead, and javelin.

EWE: 24 Etia kpo kple dzidzɔ helɔnɛ ɖe eme, Eye megatea ŋu lalana ne aʋakpẽ ɖi o.
ENGLISH: 24 Twitching and fidgeting they pit the earth and do not believe there is a sound of a ram-horn.

EWE: 25 Ne aʋakpẽ nya ɖi ko la, egblɔna be, ‘Eɖo dzi vɔ!’ Esea aʋa ƒe ʋeʋẽ tso adzɔge ʋĩi Esea aʋafiawo ƒe gbeɖeɖe kple aʋaɣli.
ENGLISH: 25 At every ram-horn they say ‘Ha!’ and scent battle afar, thunder of captains and cheering.

EWE: 26 Wò nunya nue xe ƒonu dzona yia dzi ʋĩi, Eye wòkea eƒe aʋalawo ɖoa ta anyiehea?
ENGLISH: 26 Is it by your sagacity a hawk takes wing, soars off to the south,

EWE: 27 Alo wò gbeɖeɖe nue hɔ̃ dzona yia dzi Hewɔa atɔ ɖe kɔkɔƒea?
ENGLISH: 27 Or is it by your direction that a vulture goes high and that it sets its nest aloft,

EWE: 28 Eye wò gbeɖeɖe nue wònɔa agakpe dzi hetsia afi ma dɔna, Eye wòtsɔa agakpe tsakliwo tome wɔa eƒe bebeƒea?
ENGLISH: 28 Perches on a crag and spends the night on a crag-tooth and a fastness,

EWE: 29 Afi ma wòtsona dia nuɖuɖu; Eƒe ŋkuwo kpɔa nu le didiƒe ʋĩi ke.
ENGLISH: 29 Searches from there for food, its eyes looking far away,

EWE: 30 Viawo noa ʋu; Eye afi si ame tsiaʋawo le la, afi mae wònɔna.”
ENGLISH: 30 And feeds its chicks with blood, and where there are corpses, there the bird is?”

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 40 Yehowa yi edzi gblɔ na Hiob be:
ENGLISH: 40 And Jehovah answered Job

EWE: 2 “Ðe vɔ̃eɖenamela ate ŋu ahe nya kple Ŋusẽkatãtɔ la? Ame si be yele nya gbem na Mawu la neɖo eŋu.”
ENGLISH: 2 “Does an admonisher dispute with Shaddai? let him who corrects God answer it.”

EWE: 3 Hiob ɖo eŋu na Yehowa be:
ENGLISH: 3 And Job answered Jehovah

EWE: 4 “Kpɔ ɖa! Nyemedze o.
ENGLISH: 4 “Here I am, insignificant what reply should I make?

EWE: Nya kae matsɔ aɖo eŋu na wò?
ENGLISH: I lay my hand on my mouth.

EWE: Meɖo asi nu. 5 Meƒo nu zi ɖeka, eye meɖe nu le eme; Meƒo nu zi eve, eye nyemagagblɔ nya aɖeke akpee o.”
ENGLISH: 5 I did speak once, but will not answer and twice; but I will do it no more.”

EWE: 6 Eye Yehowa ƒo nu na Hiob le ahom me be:
ENGLISH: 6 And Jehovah answered Job out of a tempest

EWE: 7 “Meɖe kuku, bla ali dzi abe ŋutsu ene, Ne mabia nya wò nàɖo eŋu nam mase.
ENGLISH: 7 “Gird your loins like a man so that I may ask you questions and you inform me.

EWE: 8 Ðe nàte ŋu atsɔ nya ɖe nye dzɔdzɔenyenye ŋua? Ðe nàbu fɔm ne tɔwò nàdzɔa?
ENGLISH: 8 Will you even quash my judgment, hold me in the wrong so that you may be in the right?

EWE: 9 Ðe wò alɔkame sesẽ de Mawu vavã la tɔ nua, Alo ɖe nàte ŋu aɖe gbe abe eya enea?
ENGLISH: 9 Or do you have an arm like God’s, do you thunder with a voice like his?

EWE: 10 Ekema tsɔ ŋutikɔkɔe kple gãnyenye ɖo atsyɔ̃e; Eye nàta bubu kple atsyɔ̃.
ENGLISH: 10 Bedeck yourself with dignity and sublimity, robing yourself in majesty and splendor,

EWE: 11 Trɔ wò dziku helĩhelĩ la ƒo ɖi; Di dadalawo katã ne nàɖiɖi wo ɖe anyi.
ENGLISH: 11 Hurl the rages of your anger, and see every proud one and bring him low,

EWE: 12 Di dadalawo katã ne nàbɔbɔ wo ɖe anyi, Eye nàfanya ame vɔ̃ɖiwo le afi si wole.
ENGLISH: 12 See every overweening one and humble him, crumple wrong-doers where they stand,

EWE: 13 Ði wo katã ɖe ke me; Eye nàbla wo ɖe teƒe ɣaɣla,
ENGLISH: 13 Bury them in the ground together, envelop their faces in sod,

EWE: 14 Ekema nye ŋutɔ malɔ̃ ɖe edzi na wò, Be wò nuɖusi ate ŋu axɔ na wò.
ENGLISH: 14 And I too will praise you that your right hand has made good your cause.

EWE: 15 Kpɔ Behemot si mewɔ abe wò ke ene la ɖa. Eɖua gbe abe nyi ene.
ENGLISH: 15 Here is Behemoth, that I made with you; it eats grass like cattle.

EWE: 16 Kpɔ ŋusẽ si gbegbe le eƒe ali me Kple ŋusẽ triakɔ si le eƒe ƒodokawo me ɖa!
ENGLISH: 16 Here is the strength in its back and the vigor in the muscles of its belly.

EWE: 17 Elia eƒe asike abe sederti ene; Eƒe atagbomeka titriwo lɔ̃ ɖe wo nɔewo me.
ENGLISH: 17 It holds its tail stiff as a cedar; the sinews of its hams are ropy.

EWE: 18 Eƒe ƒuwo le abe akɔbliga siwo me do le ene; Eƒe afɔwo sesẽ abe gayibɔkpɔtiwo ene.
ENGLISH: 18 Its bones are copper pipes, its backbone like a bar of iron.

EWE: 19 Eyae nye gbãtɔ le Mawu ƒe dɔwo dome. Ewɔla koe ate ŋu atsɔ yi ɖe eŋu.
ENGLISH: 19 First of Deity’s undertakings is this, made as he was bringing on his chisel.

EWE: 20 Elabena nuɖuɖu miena ɖe towo dzi nɛ, Afi si gbemelãwo katã ɖia adzrɔ le.
ENGLISH: 20 For mountains bear growth for it, and all beasts of the wilds play there.

EWE: 21 Ŋùtiwo tee wòmlɔna, Eye wòbena ɖe aɖawo me, le tɔba me.
ENGLISH: 21 Under jujube-trees it lies, in a blind of reeds and morass,

EWE: 22 Ŋùtiwo doa vɔvɔli ɖe edzi, Amuti siwo le tɔʋuwo to la ƒo xlãe.
ENGLISH: 22 Jujube-trees cover it with its shade, arroyo poplars surround it.

EWE: 23 Ne tɔwo nyra hã, dzika metsoa eƒo o. Ne Yordan-tɔsisi le ƒoƒom ɖe nu ŋu nɛ hã, eɖea dzi ɖi bɔkɔɔ.
ENGLISH: 23 Suppose a river overflows, it is not nervous; it is undaunted though a Jordan bursts against its mouth;

EWE: 24 Ðe ame aɖe ate ŋu alée esime wòfɔ ŋku ɖe edzi gãa, Alo aƒo ga ɖe ŋɔti me nɛa?
ENGLISH: 24 In its eyes it takes it; it has its nose bored with baits.

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 41 “Ðe nàte ŋu atsɔ ƒu aɖe Leviatan Alo atsɔ ka abla eƒe aɖe ate ɖe nu me nɛa?
ENGLISH: 41 Will you pull Leviathan about with a fishhook and press its tongue down with a line?

EWE: 2 Ðe nàte ŋu ade ka ŋɔti me nɛ, Alo atsɔ ƒu aŋɔ eƒe glãa?
ENGLISH: 2 Will you run a rush through its nose and punch its gills with a thorn?

EWE: 3 Ðe wòaƒo koko na wò zi geɖe, Alo ɖe wòaƒo nu na wò kple gbe blewua?
ENGLISH: 3 Will it give you profuse appeals for grace, or speak submissively to you?

EWE: 4 Ðe wòabla nu kpli wò, Ne nàxɔe wòazu wò kluvi le eƒe agbe me katã?
ENGLISH: 4 Will it make terms with you and you take it as permanent slave?

EWE: 5 Ðe nàfe kplii abe xevi enea, Alo ɖe nàde kae na viwònyɔnuviwoa?
ENGLISH: 5 Will you play with it as you would with a bird and tie it up for your girls,

EWE: 6 Ðe nudzralawo atsɔ woƒe adzɔnuwo aɖɔliia?
ENGLISH: 6 Cooperators bargain over it, divide it between dealers?

EWE: 7 Ðe nàte ŋu atsɔ ʋã aŋɔ eƒe ayi Alo atsɔ akplɔ atɔ eƒe taa?
ENGLISH: 7 Will you fill its skin with darts, its head with fish-harpoons?

EWE: 8 Ka asi eŋu kpɔ; Àkpɔe be avu blibo wòanye, eye màgawɔe akpɔ gbeɖe o!
ENGLISH: 8 Lay your hand on it, think of fighting do not try it again.

EWE: 9 Ne ewɔ na wò be yeate ŋu akpe edzi la, ke èble ɖokuiwò.
ENGLISH: 9 Here his expectation has been belied, at the very sight of it he is sent flying,

EWE: Ekpɔkpɔ ɖeɖe dzaa adzi ŋɔ na wò. 10 Ame aɖeke make atsɛ aʋuʋui o.
ENGLISH: 10 He is not fierce enough to rouse it and who will stand his ground before me?

EWE: Ke ame kae ate ŋu anɔ te ɖe nunye? 11 Ame kae tre nunanam, ne maɖo eteƒe nɛ?
ENGLISH: 11 Who has confronted me and come off safe and sound? under all the sky mine he is.

EWE: Nu siwo katã le dziƒo bliboa te la, tɔnyee. 12 Nyemagbe nuƒoƒo le eƒe ŋutinuwo, Eƒe ŋusẽ kple eƒe nɔnɔme dzeani la ŋu o.
ENGLISH: 12 I will not be silent as to its members,and the matter of powerfulness, and the symmetry of its build.

EWE: 13 Ame kae aflo eƒe akpa le eŋu?
ENGLISH: 13 Who uncovers the surface of its coat? who will get inside its double coat of mail?

EWE: Ame kae ate ŋu aɖo eƒe glãwo me? 14 Ame kae ate ŋu ake eƒe nu?
ENGLISH: 14 Who opens the doors of its mouth? the circuit of its teeth is a terror.

EWE: 15 Tsro trikpawo ɖo ɖe eƒe dzimegbe, Wolé ɖe wo nɔewo ŋu kpaɖikpaɖi.
ENGLISH: 15 Its back is ridged with shields, closed in tight sealing,

EWE: 16 Wodre ɖe wo nɔewo ŋu ale gbegbe Be ya gɔ̃ hã mate ŋu ato wo me o.
ENGLISH: 16 One coming up to another with no gap intervening,

EWE: 17 Ðe sia ɖe lé ɖe nɔvia ŋu; Woƒo ɖe wo nɔewo me ale gbegbe be womate ŋu ama wo me o.
ENGLISH: 17 Each keeping contact with the next, inseparably linked.

EWE: 18 Eƒe nyènye ɖeɖe dzaa kea dzo, Eye eƒe ŋkuwo klẽna hɛ̃ abe agudzedze ene.
ENGLISH: 18 Its sneezing sends beams of light and its eyes are like the eyelashes of the dawn;

EWE: 19 Dzoƒaɖewo dona tso eƒe nu me; Dzoxiwo hlẽna ŋeŋeŋe.
ENGLISH: 19 Out of its mouth fly torches, sparks of fire escape;

EWE: 20 Dzudzɔ tuna tso eƒe ŋɔti me Abe dzokpo si me wodo ketidzo ɖo ene.
ENGLISH: 20 Out of its nostrils smoke streams out like that from a heated pot and rushes.

EWE: 21 Eƒe gbɔgbɔ naa aka léa dzo, Eye dzoƒaɖewo dona tsoa eƒe nu me.
ENGLISH: 21 Its breath sets coals ablaze, and a flame comes out of its mouth.

EWE: 22 Ŋusẽ geɖe le eƒe kɔ me, Eye ŋɔdzi tia kpo le eŋgɔ.
ENGLISH: 22 Force lodges on its neck and despair bounds before it.

EWE: 23 Eƒe ayi mlɔ wo nɔewo dzi; Wolé ɖe wo nɔewo ŋu kpaɖii be womeʋãna o.
ENGLISH: 23 The underparts of its flesh cling fast, are immovably welded on.

EWE: 24 Eƒe dzi sẽ abe kpe ene, Ɛ̃, esẽ abe té si dzi wotua nu le ene.
ENGLISH: 24 Its heart is solid as a stone and solid as a lower millstone.

EWE: 25 Ne etso la, dzidzi ƒoa ŋusẽtɔwo gɔ̃ hã; Ne eʋã eɖokui la, woluluna.
ENGLISH: 25 At its rearing up heroes quail, at bone-breaking strokes they fall into dismay.

EWE: 26 Ne yi va tui la, mekpea edzi o; Eye akplɔ, ga biɖoe alo aŋutrɔ hã meɖia naneke nɛ o.
ENGLISH: 26 One who hits it with a sword finds that that does not bite, a spear nor a bolt nor a mail-piercer.

EWE: 27 Gayibɔ le nɛ abe gbe ƒuƒu ko ene, Akɔbli abe ati si nyunyɔ ene.
ENGLISH: 27 It thinks iron is threshed straw and bronze rotten wood.

EWE: 28 Aŋutrɔ menyanɛ ɖe nu o; Akafokpe le nɛ abe ahɔ̃liti ko ene.
ENGLISH: 28 A shaft from a bow will not put it to flight; stones from a sling turn to straw for it.

EWE: 29 Ebua kpo abe ahɔ̃liti ene, Eye akplɔ ƒe ʋɔlulũ ɖia kokoe nɛ.
ENGLISH: 29 A club counts as a straw for it, and it laughs at the vibration of a javelin.

EWE: 30 Eƒe dɔmegbɔ le abe sonu gaglɛ ɖaɖɛwo ene; Eɖea fli ɖe ba me abe luƒotasiaɖam ene.
ENGLISH: 30 Under it are sharp chips of crockery; it runs a toothed plank over mud.

EWE: 31 Enana tɔ gɔme fiẽna wlɔwlɔwlɔ abe nuɖaze me ene; Eblua atsiaƒu abe amiɖaze me ene.
ENGLISH: 31 It makes ooze boil up like a pot, makes sea like a perfumer’s saucepan.

EWE: 32 Enana etoƒe le tɔ dzi klẽna le eyome; Ale tɔa dzi funa kpii abe ta ƒowɔ ene.
ENGLISH: 32 It leaves a shining wake behind it; one thinks the deep is gray-haired.

EWE: 33 Etɔgbi aɖeke mele anyigba dzi o, Nuwɔwɔ si ŋɔ medzina o lae wònye.
ENGLISH: 33 Over the earth there is nothing that masters it, it that is made to be without dismay.

EWE: 34 Eklẽa ŋku ɖe nu sia nu si doa eɖokui ɖe dzi la.
ENGLISH: 34 Every high one fears it; it is king over all proud beasts.?

EWE: Hiob
ENGLISH: Job

EWE: 42 Eye Hiob ɖo eŋu na Yehowa be:
ENGLISH: 42 And Job answered Jehovah

EWE: 2 “Azɔ menyae be àte ŋu awɔ nu sia nu Eye naneke meli nàɖo, si màte ŋu awɔ o.
ENGLISH: 2 “I know that you can do everything and nothing you may think of is impossible to you.

EWE: 3 Ègblɔ be, ‘Ame kae nye esia si le nu tsyɔm nye adaŋudede dzi numanyamanyatɔe?’ Nyateƒee, meƒo nu, esi nyemese nuwo gɔme o, Elabena wonye nu siwo wɔ nuku ale gbegbe, siwo nyemenya o.
ENGLISH: 3 Who is this that is muddling a discussion without knowing anything about it? so I have been asserting things I do not understand, things too mysterious for me, which I do not know:

EWE: 4 Ègblɔ be, ‘Meɖe kuku, ɖo to, ne maƒo nu. Mabia nya wò nàɖo eŋu nam.’
ENGLISH: 4 ‘Listen, and I will speak; I will put questions; inform me.’

EWE: 5 Wogblɔ nya le ŋuwò mese, Ke azɔ la, nye ŋkuwo kpɔ wò.
ENGLISH: 5 I had heard of you by hearsay, but now my eye has seen you;

EWE: 6 Esia tae melɔ̃ ɖe edzi be nyemegblɔe nyuie o, Eye metrɔ dzi me le ke kple afi me.”
ENGLISH: 6 Therefore I recant and repent in the ashes on the ground.”

EWE: 7 Esi Yehowa gblɔ nya siawo na Hiob vɔ la, Yehowa gblɔ na Temantɔ Elifaz be: “Medo dziku ɖe wò kple xɔ̃wò eveawo ŋu vevie, elabena miegblɔ nyateƒea tso ŋunye abe ale si nye subɔla Hiob wɔe ene o.
ENGLISH: 7 And after Jehovah had spoken these words to Job, Jehovah said to Eliphaz the Temanite “I am angry with you and your two friends because you did not speak soundly about me as my servant Job did.

EWE: 8 Eya ta milé nyitsu adre kple agbo adre miayi nye subɔla Hiob gbɔ, ne miasa numevɔ ɖe mia ɖokuiwo ta. Eye nye subɔla Hiob nado gbe ɖa ɖe mia ta. Eya ƒe kukuɖeɖee mase hafi nyemaɖo eteƒe na mi ɖe miaƒe bometsitsi la nu o, elabena mieto nyateƒe le ŋunye abe ale si nye subɔla Hiob wɔe ene o.”
ENGLISH: 8 Now take seven steers and seven rams and go to my servant Job and offer them as burnt-offering for yourselves and let my servant Job pray for you, and see if I will do him the personal favor of not ill-treating you because you did not speak soundly of me as my servant Job did.”

EWE: 9 Eya ta Temantɔ Elifaz, Suatɔ Bildad, kple Naamatɔ Zofar yi ɖawɔ abe ale si tututu Yehowa gblɔ na wo ene. Eye Yehowa se Hiob ƒe gbedodoɖa.
ENGLISH: 9 And Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Sophar the Naʽamathite went and did as Jehovah had told them to, and Jehovah did do the favor for Job.

EWE: 10 Esi Hiob do gbe ɖa ɖe exɔlɔ̃awo ta vɔ la, Yehowa ɖe Hiob ƒe xaxawo ɖa eye wòna Hiob gazu kesinɔtɔ.
ENGLISH: 10 And Jehovah came back to Job when he prayed for his friends; and Jehovah added double to everything that belonged to him.

EWE: Yehowa ɖo nu siwo katã nɔ esi tsã la teƒe nɛ zi gbɔ zi eve. 11 Eye nɔviaŋutsuwo kple nɔvianyɔnuwo katã kpakple eƒe ame nyanyɛwo katã va egbɔ heɖu nu kplii le eƒe aƒe me. Wodo baba nɛ hefa akɔ nɛ le vɔ̃ siwo katã ŋu Yehowa ɖe mɔ ɖo wova edzi la ta. Eye wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe na ga kple sikasigɛe.
ENGLISH: 11 And all his brothers and sisters and all his former acquaintances came to him and ate bread with him in his house and lamented over him and comforted him for all the disaster Jehovah had brought upon him, and gave him a keshitah each and a gold earring each.

EWE: 12 Ale Yehowa yra Hiob le eƒe agbenɔƒe mamlɛawo me wu ale si wònɔ le gɔmedzedzea, ale be alẽ akpe wuiene, kposɔ akpe ade, nyi eveve teƒe akpe ɖeka kple tedzinɔ akpe ɖeka va su Hiob si.
ENGLISH: 12 And Jehovah blessed Job’s later life more than his earlier, and he had fourteen thousand sheep and goats and six thousand camels and a thousand yoke of cattle and a thousand donkeys;

EWE: 13 Wogadzi viŋutsu adre kple vinyɔnu etɔ̃ nɛ.
ENGLISH: 13 and he had seven sons and three daughters,

EWE: 14 Ena ŋkɔ nyɔnuvi gbãtɔ be Yemima, evelia be Kezia, etɔ̃lia be Keren-Hapuk.
ENGLISH: 14 and named one daughter Jemimah and the second Kesi’ah and the third Keren-hap-Puk;

EWE: 15 Womekpɔ nyɔnu dzetugbe aɖeke le anyigba la katã dzi kpɔ abe Hiob vinyɔnuawo ene o, eye wo fofo na domenyinu wo ɖe wo nɔviŋutsuwo dome.
ENGLISH: 15 and there were no women so beautiful as Job’s daughters to be found in all the country; and their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers.

EWE: 16 Le nu siawo megbe la, Hiob ganɔ agbe ƒe alafa ɖeka blaene, eye wòkpɔ viawo kple tɔgbuiyɔviawo va se ɖe dzidzime enelia dzi.
ENGLISH: 16 And Job lived after this a hundred and forty years, and saw his sons and his sons’ sons to four generations.

EWE: 17 Hiob tsi, eye agbenɔnɔ ɖi kɔ nɛ hafi wòku.
ENGLISH: 17 And Job died an old man, having lived as long as he cared to.

EWE: Lododowo
ENGLISH: Proverbs

EWE: 1 Israel-fia Salomo, David vi, ƒe lododowoe nye esiawo:
ENGLISH: 1 The proverbs of Solomon the son of David,

EWE: 2 Ne woadze nunya eye woaxɔ amehehe; Ne woase nya goglowo gɔme;
ENGLISH: king of Israel, 2 For knowing wisdom and instruction,

EWE: 3 Ne woaxɔ hehe si naa gɔmesese deto sua ame si, Ne woawɔ nu dzɔdzɔe, abu nuwo ŋu nyuie ahawɔ nu si le eteƒe;
ENGLISH: for understanding sentences of insight, 3 For getting instruction in the successful practice

EWE: 4 Ne ame makpɔnuteƒewo nadze aɖaŋu; Ne ɖekakpui nadze nunya eye tamebubuŋutete nasu esi.
ENGLISH: of honesty and justice and rectitude, 4 For giving shrewdness to simpletons,

EWE: 5 Nunyala asee, eye wòasrɔ̃ nu geɖe akpee; Eye nugɔmesela axɔ mɔfiame nyuitɔwo,
ENGLISH: knowledge and practicality to a boy, 5 While a wise man hears and adds to his lore

EWE: 6 Ne wòase lododowo, abebubuwo, Nunyalawo ƒe nyawo kple woƒe adzowo gɔme.
ENGLISH: and an expert acquires technique; 6 For understanding proverb and paradox,

EWE: 7 Yehowa vɔvɔ̃e nye sidzedze ƒe gɔmedzedze.
ENGLISH: 7 Fear of Jehovah is the first thing in knowledge.

EWE: Bometsilawoe doa vlo nunya kple amehehe.
ENGLISH: Wisdom and instruction ignoramuses despise.

EWE: 8 Vinye, se fofowò ƒe amehehe, Eye mègagbe dawò ƒe nufiame o.
ENGLISH: 8 Listen, son, to your father’s instruction,

EWE: 9 Elabena seƒoƒotsihe dzeani wònye na wò ta Kple kɔgɛ nyui na wò kɔ.
ENGLISH: and never abandon your mother’s teachings, 9 Because they are a becoming garland for your head

EWE: 10 Vinye, ne nu vɔ̃ wɔlawo le nuwò blem la, mègalɔ̃ ɖe edzi o.
ENGLISH: and a necklace for your throat. 10 My son, if sinners are inveigling you do not consent.

EWE: 11 Ne wogblɔ be: “Yi kpli mí.
ENGLISH: 11 If they say “Come with us,

EWE: Na míade xa akɔ ʋu ɖi.
ENGLISH: let us lay an ambush for bloodshed,

EWE: Na míanɔ adeklo dzi ɖe ame maɖifɔwo ŋu dzro ko.
ENGLISH: set a trap for an innocent man for nothing;

EWE: 12 Na míami wo agbagbee abe ale si Tsiẽƒe mia amee ene, Míami wo bliboe abe ale si wònɔna na ame siwo yina aʋli me ene.
ENGLISH: 12 We shall swallow them alive like the grave, sound and whole like men going down to the world below;

EWE: 13 Na míaxɔ woƒe nu veviwo katã; Míatsɔ aboyonu ayɔ míaƒe xɔwo me taŋ.
ENGLISH: 13 We shall come across all sorts of valuable goods,

EWE: 14 Va wɔ ɖeka kpli mí, Ale be míama nu siwo míeda adzoe la sɔsɔe.”
ENGLISH: fill our houses with booty; 14 You shall get an even split, we will have one purse for all,”

EWE: 15 Vinye, mègayi kpli wo o.
ENGLISH: 15 My son, do not walk on a road with them,

EWE: Mègaɖo afɔ woƒe toƒewo o,
ENGLISH: keep your foot off their path,

EWE: 16 Elabena woƒe afɔ tsɔna ɖe nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ ŋu; Eye wozãna ɖe ʋukɔkɔɖi ŋu.
ENGLISH: 16 Because their feet are running to evil and hurrying to shed blood.

EWE: 17 Ne woɖo ɖɔ ɖi na xevi le xevia ŋkume la, dzodzroe.
ENGLISH: 17 For it is for nothing that the net flutters

EWE: 18 Esia tae ame siawo dea xa ɖi ɖe ʋukɔkɔɖi ŋu ɖo; Wobena be yewoaɖe amewo ƒe agbe ɖa.
ENGLISH: before the eyes of any bird, 18 And they are laying ambushes for their own blood,

EWE: 19 Aleae ame siwo katã dia viɖe ƒoɖi la ƒe mɔwo le, Ke viɖe ƒoɖi la aɖe ame siwo ƒe asi su edzi la ƒe agbe ɖa.
ENGLISH: setting traps for their own lives. 19 Such is the fate of whoever grasps at gain; it takes its owners’ life.

EWE: 20 Nunya vavãtɔ le ɣli dom le kpɔdomee.
ENGLISH: 20 Wisdom holloos on the street,

EWE: Eƒe gbe le dzi dem le ablɔwo me.
ENGLISH: sends out her voice in the squares,

EWE: 21 Ele ɣli dom le ablɔ siwo dzi zinyenye le la ƒe dzogoe dzi.
ENGLISH: 21 Calls out at the crowded corners,

EWE: Ele gbɔgblɔm le dua ƒe agbowo nu be:
ENGLISH: says her say in the city at the gates,

EWE: 22 “Va se ɖe ɣekaɣi mi ame manyanuwo mianɔ numanyamanya dzi?
ENGLISH: 22 “How long, simpletons, will you love simpleness,

EWE: Va se ɖe ɣekaɣi mi fewuɖulawo mianɔ dzidzɔ kpɔm ɖe fewuɖuɖu ŋu?
ENGLISH: and cynics like to be cynical,

EWE: Eye va se ɖe ɣekaɣi mi bometsilawo mianɔ fu lém sidzedze?
ENGLISH: and fools hate knowledge?

EWE: 23 Nye mokaname neʋã mi.
ENGLISH: 23 You should turn back at my admonition;

EWE: Ekema matrɔ nye gbɔgbɔ akɔ ɖi na mi; Mana mianya nye nyawo.
ENGLISH: I would stream my spirit for you, would make my words known to you.

EWE: 24 Esi meyɔ mi gake miegbe, Meke nye abɔwo me na mi gake mia dometɔ aɖeke mede nu eme nam o,
ENGLISH: 24 Since I have called and you refused,

EWE: 25 Miedo toku nye aɖaŋuɖoɖowo katã, Eye miegbe nye mokanamewo.
ENGLISH: held out my hand and nobody listened, 25 And you neglected my advice

EWE: 26 Nye hã mako nu ne vɔ̃ dzɔ ɖe mia dzi; Maɖe alɔme le mia ŋu ne nu si dzia ŋɔ na mi la dzɔ,
ENGLISH: and would not have my admonition, 26 I on my part will laugh at your calamity,

EWE: 27 Ne nu si dzia ŋɔ na mi la va mia dzi abe ahom ene, Ne vɔ̃ ɖi kpe mi abe ahomya ene, Eye hiã kple xaxa tu mi.
ENGLISH: will make fun when what you dread comes, 27 When what you dread comes like a thunderstorm and your calamity arrives like a gale,

EWE: 28 Ɣemaɣi la, woayɔm gake nyematɔ o; Woadim vevie gake womakpɔm o,
ENGLISH: when distress and hard straits come upon you; 28 Then they will call me and I will not answer,

EWE: 29 Elabena wolé fu sidzedze, Eye wometia Yehowa vɔvɔ̃ o.
ENGLISH: they will go in quest of me and not find me. 29 Inasmuch as they hated knowledge

EWE: 30 Wogbe nye aɖaŋuɖoɖowo; Wodo vlo nye mokanamewo katã.

EWE: 31 Mekpɔa dzidzɔ ɖe eƒe anyigba si wòwɔ be woanɔ edzi la ŋu, Eye nyemelɔ̃a nu le amegbetɔviwo gbɔ kura o.
ENGLISH: 31 Playing with nature all over his earth,

EWE: 32 Azɔ vinyewo, miɖo tom; Dzidzɔtɔwoe nye ame siwo léa nye mɔwo me ɖe asi.
ENGLISH: and my pleasure was among mankind. 32 And now, sons, listen to me

EWE: 33 Miɖo to amehehe, ne miadze nunya, Eye migagbee gbeɖe o.
ENGLISH: happy are those who keep on my courses. 33 Hear instruction and be wise,

EWE: 34 Dzidzɔtɔe nye ame si ɖoa tom, Ame si dona ɖe nye ʋɔtruwo nu kaba gbe sia gbe, Ame si lalana le nye ʋɔtrutiwo nu;
ENGLISH: and do not neglect it. 34 Happy a man who listens to me, attent at my doors day by day,

EWE: 35 Elabena ame si ƒe asi tum la, eƒe asi tu agbe, Eye Yehowa akpɔ ŋudzedze ɖe eŋu.
ENGLISH: watching the jambs of my portal, 35 Because he who finds me has found life

EWE: 36 Ke ame si mebuam ɖe ɖeke me o la wɔa nu vevi eɖokui, Eye ame siwo katã léa fum la, ku lɔ̃m wole.”
ENGLISH: and obtained favor from Jehovah, 36 But he who sins against me is victimizing himself; all who hate me love death.”

EWE: Lododowo
ENGLISH: Proverbs

EWE: 9 Nunya vavãtɔ tu eƒe xɔ; Ekpa eƒe sɔti adreawo ɖe eŋu.
ENGLISH: 9 Wisdom has built her house, has shaped her pillars seven,

EWE: 2 Etrɔ asi le eƒe lã ŋu; Etɔtɔ eƒe wain; Eye wòɖo eƒe kplɔ̃ hã.
ENGLISH: 2 Has killed animals for her meat, mixed her wine,

EWE: 3 Edɔ eƒe dɔlanyɔnuwo ɖa Ne woado ɣli le dua ƒe kɔkɔƒewo be:
ENGLISH: set her table too, 3 Has sent her girls, calls out

EWE: 4 “Ame sia ame si si nuteƒekpɔkpɔ mesu o la, neva dze afii.”
ENGLISH: on the crests of eminences in the city 4 “Who is a simpleton? let him come this way;

EWE: Egblɔ na ame si si tagbɔ mele o hã be:
ENGLISH: brainless? that I may say to him

EWE: 5 “Va ɖu nye abolo.
ENGLISH: 5 ‘Come, have some of my dinner

EWE: Eye nàno wain si metɔtɔ la.
ENGLISH: and drink some of the wine I have mixed.

EWE: 6 Ðe asi le numanyamanya ŋu, ne nànɔ agbe; Eye lé gɔmesese ƒe mɔ tsɔ tẽe.”
ENGLISH: 6 Leave off simpleness and have life,

EWE: 7 Ame si le fewuɖula ɖɔm ɖo la kplɔa ŋukpe ƒua eɖokui, Eye ame si le mo kam na ame vɔ̃ɖi la awɔ nu vevi eɖokui.
ENGLISH: and tread the road of discretion.”’ 7 He who offers instruction to a cynic gets dishonor for himself, and he who admonishes a wicked man, it is his discredit.

EWE: 8 Mègaka mo na fewuɖula o; fu ko wòalé wò.
ENGLISH: 8 Do not admonish a cynic, for fear he should hate you;

EWE: Ka mo na nunyala boŋ, eye alɔ̃ wò.
ENGLISH: admonish a wise man and he will love you.

EWE: 9 Fia nu nunyala, eye aganya nu ɖe edzi.
ENGLISH: 9 Give to a wise man and he will be wiser yet;

EWE: Fia nu ame dzɔdzɔe, eye agasrɔ̃ nu geɖe akpe esi wònya.
ENGLISH: advise a right-minded man and he will add to his lore.

EWE: 10 Yehowa vɔvɔ̃e nye nunya ƒe gɔmedzedze, Eye sidzedze Kɔkɔetɔ lae nye gɔmesese.
ENGLISH: 10 The beginning of wisdom is to fear Jehovah,

EWE: 11 Elabena nyee ana wò agbemeŋkekewo nasɔ gbɔ, Eye woadzi wò agbenɔƒewo ɖe edzi.
ENGLISH: and to know the Holy is discretion. 11 For by me your days shall be many

EWE: 12 Ne èdze nunya la, wò ŋutɔe nunya sia aɖe vi na, Gake ne ènye fewuɖula la, wò ɖeɖee akpɔ emetsonua.
ENGLISH: and years of life shall be added to you. 12 If you are wise, you are wise for yourself; and are you cynical, you will carry the consequences alone.

EWE: 13 Nyɔnu movitɔ doa aƒa.
ENGLISH: 13 Foolishness is boisterous;

EWE: Mebua nu ŋu yia ŋgɔe o, eye menya naneke o.
ENGLISH: simplemindedness knows no shame;

EWE: 14 Ebɔbɔ nɔ eƒe aƒe ƒe mɔnu, Le zikpui dzi le dua ƒe kɔkɔƒe,
ENGLISH: 14 And she sits at the door of her house,

EWE: 15 Le ɣli dom le ame siwo tso eme va yina la yɔm, Le gbɔgblɔm na ame siwo lé woƒe mɔ tsɔ tẽe la be:
ENGLISH: in a chair on eminences in the city, 15 To call to passersby, those who are treading their ways,

EWE: 16 “Ame sia ame si si nuteƒekpɔkpɔ mesu o la, neva dze afii.”
ENGLISH: 16 “Who is a simpleton? let him come this way;

EWE: Egblɔ na ame siwo katã si tagbɔ mele o hã be:
ENGLISH: and brainless? that I may say to him

EWE: 17 “Tsi si wofi la, ɖe wòvivina, Eye vivimenuɖuɖu ɖe wòle ŋanaŋana.”
ENGLISH: 17 ‘Stolen water is sweet and bread behind a screen is delicious’”

EWE: 18 Ke womenyae be ku le afi ma o, Be Tsieƒe ƒe gogloeƒe kee ame siwo wòkpe la le o.
ENGLISH: 18 But he does not know there are ghosts there; her guests are in the deeps of the realm of death.

EWE: Lododowo
ENGLISH: Proverbs

EWE: 10 Salomo ƒe lododowo.
ENGLISH: 10 The Proverbs of Solomon.

EWE: Vi nyanu doa dzidzɔ na fofoa, Ke vi tsibome nyea nuxaxa na dadaa.
ENGLISH: A wise son gladdens a father, but a foolish son is misery to his mother.

EWE: 2 Kesinɔnu si wokpɔ to mɔ fitifiti dzi la maɖe vi aɖeke o, Ke dzɔdzɔenyenyee aɖe ame tso ku me.
ENGLISH: 2 A wrong-doer’s hoards do no good, but right-doing delivers from death.

EWE: 3 Yehowa mana dɔ nawu ame dzɔdzɔe la o, Ke ame vɔ̃ɖi ya, mana nu si le edzrom la nasu esi o.
ENGLISH: 3 Jehovah will not let a right-doer go hungry, but wrong-doers’ hankering he will balk.

EWE: 4 Asi si wɔa alɔgblɔdɔ la, hiã atui, Ke asi si doa vevie nu la hea kesinɔnu vanɛ.
ENGLISH: 4 He who does things with slack hand grows poor;

EWE: 5 Vi nyanu ƒoa nuwo nu ƒu le dzomeŋɔli, Ke vi ŋukpenanuwɔla dɔa alɔ̃ yia eme ʋĩi le nuŋeɣi.
ENGLISH: but energetic men’s hands enrich. 5 A capable son is stowing things away in summer;

EWE: 6 Yayrawo ava ame dzɔdzɔe ƒe ta dzi, Ke ŋutasesẽ ɣla ɖe ame vɔ̃ɖiwo ƒe nu me.
ENGLISH: a worthless son lies fast asleep in harvesttime. 6 There are blessings for a right-doer’s head,

EWE: 7 Ŋkuɖoɖo ame dzɔdzɔe dzi anye yayra, Ke ame vɔ̃ɖi ya ƒe ŋkɔ anyunyɔ.
ENGLISH: but outrage covers up wrong-doers’ mouths. 7 The memory of a right-doer is for a blessing,

EWE: 8 Ame si si dzi nyanu le la alɔ̃ axɔ nufiame, Ke woafanya ame si gblɔa bometsinya la.
ENGLISH: but wrong-doers’ names will decay. 8 A man of wise heart takes orders,

EWE: 9 Ame si ƒe zɔzɔme ŋu fɔɖiɖi mele o la anɔ dedie, Ke ame si ƒe mɔwo glɔ̃ la asi atui.
ENGLISH: but a man of ignorant lips makes trouble. 9 One who walks plainly walks safely,

EWE: 10 Ame si miaa ŋku ɖe ame ayetɔe la hea nuxaxa vanɛ, Eye woafanya ame si gblɔa bometsinya la.
ENGLISH: but one who tangles his courses will be shown up. 10 A winker gives woe,

EWE: 11 Ame dzɔdzɔe ƒe nu la, agbevudo wònye, Ke ŋutasesẽ ɣla ɖe ame vɔ̃ɖiwo ƒe nu me.
ENGLISH: but an outspoken reprover brings soundness. 11 An honest man’s mouth is a fountainhead of life;

EWE: 12 Fuléle dea dzre aƒe, Ke lɔlɔ̃ tsyɔa dzidadawo katã dzi.
ENGLISH: but outrage covers up wrong-doers’ mouths. 12 Hate starts quarrels,

EWE: 13 Nugɔmesela ƒe nuyiwo dzie wokpɔa nunya le, Ke ameƒoti li na ame si si tagbɔ mele o la ƒe medome.
ENGLISH: but love covers over all offenses. 13 On an intelligent man’s lips wisdom is found;

EWE: 14 Nunyala dzraa sidzedze ɖo, Ke bometsila ƒe nuyi hea gbegblẽ vanɛ.
ENGLISH: but a cudgel is the thing for a brainless man’s back. 14 Wise men keep knowledge under cover;

EWE: 15 Hotsuitɔ ƒe kesinɔnuwoe nye du sesẽ nɛ.Hiãtɔ ƒe ahedadae nye eƒe gbegblẽ.
ENGLISH: but an ignorant man’s mouth is ruin close at hand. 15 A rich man’s goods are his strong city;

EWE: 16 Ame dzɔdzɔe ƒe dɔwɔwɔ hea agbe vanɛ; Ke ame vɔ̃ɖi ƒe dɔwɔwɔ hea nu vɔ̃ vanɛ.
ENGLISH: the destitution of poor men is their ruin. 16 What a right-doer has worked on goes for life;

EWE: 17 Ame si xɔa amehehe la nye agbemɔ, Ke ame si do toku ɖɔɖɔɖo la kplɔa amewo trana.
ENGLISH: a wrong-doer’s produce, for sin. 17 He who lives up to lessons is on a road to life,

EWE: 18 Ame si ɣla fuléle ɖe dzi me la, alakpatɔ wònye, Eye ame si kakaa ameŋugblẽnya la, bometsilae.
ENGLISH: but he who ignores admonition is off the track. 18 Lying lips cover up hatred;

EWE: 19 Dadaƒu megbea nuƒoƒo vivivo me o, Ke ame si kpɔa eƒe nuyiwo dzi la, aɖaŋudzelae.
ENGLISH: but he who gives out scandal is a fool. 19 In multiplicity of words offense will not be lacking;

EWE: 20 Ame dzɔdzɔe ƒe aɖe le abe klosalo nyuitɔ ene, Ke ame vɔ̃ɖi ƒe dzi mele ɖeke me o.
ENGLISH: but he who keeps his lips under restraint is acting sensibly. 20 An honest man’s tongue is sterling silver;

EWE: 21 Ame dzɔdzɔe ƒe nuƒo nyia ame geɖe, Ke bometsilawo kuna le numanyamanya ta.
ENGLISH: wrong-doers’ brains are worth little. 21 An honest man’s lips shepherd many;

EWE: 22 Yehowa ƒe yayrae wɔa ame kesinɔtɔ, Eye metsɔa vevesese aɖeke kpena ɖe eŋu o.
ENGLISH: but ignoramuses die by lack of brains. 22 Jehovah’s blessing is what makes one rich,

EWE: 23 Ŋukpenanuwɔwɔ nyea fefenu na bometsila, Ke nunya le nugɔmesela si.
ENGLISH: and pains add nothing extra. 23 Committing enormity is just fun to a fool,

EWE: 24 Nu si vɔ̃m ame vɔ̃ɖi le la, eyae adzɔ ɖe edzi; Ke woawɔ ame dzɔdzɔewo ƒe didi dzi na wo.
ENGLISH: and so is wisdom to an intelligent man. 24 What a wrong-doer stands in terror of is what will come to him;

EWE: 25 Ne ahom tu va yi la, ame vɔ̃ɖi la nu ayi, Ke ame dzɔdzɔe ya ali ke abe gɔmeɖoanyi ene tegbee.
ENGLISH: but honest men’s desire will be granted. 25 When a gale has gone past, a wrong-doer is not there;

EWE: 26 Ale si aha tsitsi le na aɖu kple dzudzɔ le na ŋku la, Nenemae kuviatɔ le na ame si dɔ dɔe.
ENGLISH: but an honest man is permanently fixed on his foundation. 26 As is vinegar to the teeth and as is smoke to the eyes,

EWE: 27 Yehowa vɔvɔ̃ dzia agbenɔƒewo ɖe edzi, Ke ame vɔ̃ɖiwo ya ƒe agbenɔƒewo dzi atso kpo.
ENGLISH: so is the idler to those who send him. 27 The fear of Jehovah adds days;

EWE: 28 Ame dzɔdzɔewo ƒe mɔkpɔkpɔ hea dzidzɔ vanɛ, Ke ame vɔ̃ɖiwo ƒe mɔkpɔkpɔ nu ayi.
ENGLISH: but wrong-doers’ years will be shortened. 28 Right-doers’ prospect is gladness;

EWE: 29 Yehowa ƒe mɔ nye mɔ́ sesẽ na fɔmaɖila, Gake enye gbegblẽ na vɔ̃wɔlawo.
ENGLISH: but wrong-doers’ hope will be lost. 29 Jehovah is a citadel to a man of conscientious course

EWE: 30 Womana ame dzɔdzɔe nadze anyi akpɔ o, Gake ame vɔ̃ɖiwo ya maganɔ anyigba la dzi o.
ENGLISH: but ruin to villains. 30 A right-doer will be unshaken forever, but wrong-doers will not have a lodgment in the country.

EWE: 31 Nunya doa go tso ame dzɔdzɔe ƒe nu me, Ke woalã alakpaɖe la ya ɖa.
ENGLISH: 31 A right-doer’s mouth bears crops of wisdom,

EWE: 32 Ame dzɔdzɔe ƒe nuyi gblɔa nya dzeto, Ke ame vɔ̃ɖi ƒe nu gblɔa nya tovo.
ENGLISH: but a mischief-making tongue will be cut out. 32 A right-doer’s lips know courtesy,

EWE: Lododowo
ENGLISH: Proverbs

EWE: 11 Nudanu amebatɔ nye ŋunyɔ na Yehowa, Ke nudanu si de pɛpɛpɛ la dzea eŋu.
ENGLISH: 11 Cheating scales are what Jehovah detests,

EWE: 2 Ne ɖokuidodoɖedzi do mo ɖa la, ŋukpe hã dzea eyome godoo, Ke ame siwo nyaa afi si woƒe ŋutete se ɖo la si mee nunya le.
ENGLISH: and a full-standard weight is what he approves. 2 Comes pretentiousness, comes dishonor;

EWE: 3 Nu dzɔdzɔe wɔlawo ƒe fɔmaɖimaɖie fiaa mɔ wo, Ke ame mawɔnuteƒewo ƒe nu fitifiti wɔwɔe atsrɔ̃ wo.
ENGLISH: but wisdom is on the side of modest men. 3 Straightforward men’s conscientiousness will guide them,

EWE: 4 Viɖe aɖeke manɔ ame ƒe kesinɔnuwo ŋu le dzikudogbe o, Ke dzɔdzɔenyenyee aɖe ame tso ku me.
ENGLISH: but faithless men will be upset by their wickedness. 4 Property does no good on a day of wrath,

EWE: 5 Ame maɖifɔ ƒe dzɔdzɔenyenyee taa mɔ dzɔdzɔe nɛ, Ke ame vɔ̃ɖi ŋutɔ ƒe vɔ̃ɖinyenyee aƒui anyi.
ENGLISH: but right-doing delivers from death. 5 A conscientious man’s rectitude will smooth his course,

EWE: 6 Nu dzɔdzɔe wɔlawo ƒe dzɔdzɔenyenyee aɖe wo, Ke ame mawɔnuteƒewo ƒe dzodzrowoe dea wo asi.
ENGLISH: but a wrong-doer will fall by his tendency to wrong. 6 Straightforward men’s rectitude will deliver them,

EWE: 7 Ne ame vɔ̃ɖi ku la, eƒe mɔkpɔkpɔ nu yina; Eye ŋuɖoɖo ɖe eƒe ŋusẽ ŋu hã nu yina.
ENGLISH: but faithless men will be caught by their greed. 7 At man’s death hope perishes

EWE: 8 Woɖea ame dzɔdzɔe tso xaxa me, Eye ame vɔ̃ɖi xɔna ɖe eteƒe.
ENGLISH: and the prospect vigor gave is lost. 8 An honest man is rescued out of distress

EWE: 9 Xɔsegbela tsɔa eƒe nu gblẽa ehavi dome, Ke sidzedzee wotsɔna ɖea ame dzɔdzɔewo.
ENGLISH: and a rogue goes in instead. 9 By an ungodly man’s mouth his neighbor is ruined,

EWE: 10 Ame dzɔdzɔewo ƒe nu nyui wɔwɔ nana du kpɔa dzidzɔ, Ke ne ame vɔ̃ɖiwo nu yi la, aseye ɖina.
ENGLISH: but by knowledge honest men are rescued. 10 When good things happen to honest men a town jubilates,

EWE: 11 Nu dzɔdzɔe wɔlawo ƒe yayra doa du ƒe ŋkɔ ɖe dzi, Ke ame vɔ̃ɖiwo ƒe nu nana wogbãnɛ ƒua anyi.
ENGLISH: but when rogues perish there is shouting. 11 By upright men’s blessing a town stands tall,

EWE: 12 Ame si si tagbɔ mele o la doa vlo ehavi, Ke nugɔmesela zia kpi.
ENGLISH: but by rogues’ mouths it is demolished. 12 A brainless man despises his neighbor,

EWE: 13 Ameŋugblẽla nɔa tsatsam nɔa go ʋum nya ɣaɣla, Ke ame si dzi woate ŋu aka ɖo ɣlaa nya.
ENGLISH: but an intelligent man holds his tongue. 13 A tattler discloses confidences,

EWE: 14 Ne mɔfiafia nyui meli o la, dukɔ dzea anyi, Ke aɖaŋuɖola geɖewo dzie wotona kpɔa dzidzedze.
ENGLISH: but a man of trusty spirit covers a matter up. 14 By not having political skill a people falls;

EWE: 15 Ame si da megbe na ame tutɔ wòdo ga la, eme manyo nɛ o, Ke ame si gbe asinana ɖe ɖoɖo dzi la anɔ dedie.
ENGLISH: but preservation comes by plenty of advisers. 15 One comes to grievous harm because he has gone security for a stranger;

EWE: 16 Nyɔnu si wɔ ame la ƒe asi sua bubu dzi, Ke ŋutsu ŋutasẽlawo ya kesinɔnu koe sua wo si.
ENGLISH: but he who hates hand-strikers has nothing to fear. 16 A gracious woman holds honor,

EWE: 17 Ame si nyoa dɔme la le nyui wɔm na eya ŋutɔ ɖokui, Ke ŋutasẽla hea xaxa vaa eya ŋutɔ ɖokui dzi.
ENGLISH: but aggressive men will control riches. 17 A friendly man is befriending himself;

EWE: 18 Ame vɔ̃ɖi xɔa beblefetu, Ke ame si ƒãa dzɔdzɔenyenye la xɔa fetu vavã.
ENGLISH: but a cruel man is breeding trouble for his own flesh. 18 A wrong-doer makes illusory revenue,

EWE: 19 Ame si léa nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔ me ɖe asi la le agbemɔ dzi, Ke ame si tia nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ yome la le kumɔ dzi.
ENGLISH: but he who sows the seed of right, real wages. 19 Firmness in the right makes for life;

EWE: 20 Ame siwo ƒe dzi metoa mɔ ɖeka o la ƒe nu nyɔa ŋu na Yehowa, Ke ame siwo ƒe zɔzɔme ŋu fɔɖiɖi mele o la ƒe nu nyoa eŋu.
ENGLISH: but one who chases after evil does this for his own death. 20 Men crooked in their hearts are what Jehovah detests,

EWE: 21 Ka ɖe nya sia dzi be: Womagbe tohehe na ame vɔ̃ɖi o, Ke ame dzɔdzɔewo ƒe viwo ya ado le eme.
ENGLISH: and men conscientious in their courses are what he approves. 21 Hand on hand a vicious man will not be cleared,

EWE: 22 Nyɔnu dzetugbe si gbea susu ŋu dɔ wɔwɔ, Le abe ha si sikaŋɔtigɛ le ŋɔti na ene.
ENGLISH: but right-doers’ descendants escape. 22 A beautiful but wrong-headed woman

EWE: 23 Ame dzɔdzɔewo ƒe dzimedidi hea nyui vanɛ, Ke ame vɔ̃ɖiwo ƒe mɔkpɔkpɔ hea dziku vanɛ.
ENGLISH: is a gold ring in a hog’s nose. 23 Honest men’s desire is pure kindness,

EWE: 24 Ame aɖe naa nu faa, ke egadzina ɖe edzi nɛ; Ame aɖe hã vea nu ale gbegbe, ke ahe ko wòdana.
ENGLISH: but rogues’ hope is truculence. 24 There is such a thing as one who scatters but has more and more;

EWE: 25 Eme anyo na dɔmenyotɔ, Eye ame si naa amewo ƒe dzi dzea eme la, woana eya hã ƒe dzi nadze eme.
ENGLISH: but one who scrimps unduly is headed only for want. 25 A generous soul will get plenty of oil,

EWE: 26 Ame si miaa asi ɖe bli dzi la, amewo ado ɖiŋu nɛ, Ke ame si tsɔe na woƒle la, woayrae.
ENGLISH: and a man who gives water freely, plenty of water for himself. 26 One who refuses to sell grain the people will curse,

EWE: 27 Ame si le nyui yome tim la, eƒe nu anyo ame ŋu, Ke ame si le vɔ̃ dim la, vɔ̃ ava edzi godoo.
ENGLISH: but there will be blessings for the head of one who does sell it. 27 One who goes after good is going to find God’s favor,

EWE: 28 Ame si le dzi ɖom ɖe eƒe kesinɔnuwo ŋu la adze anyi, Ke ame dzɔdzɔewo awɔ vlɔvlɔvlɔ abe aŋgba ene.
ENGLISH: and one who hunts for harm will have it come to him. 28 He who puts confidence in his riches, he will fall,

EWE: 29 Ame si he vɔ̃ va eƒe aƒe dzi la, ya anye eƒe domenyinu, Eye bometsila anye subɔla na ame si si dzi nyanu le.
ENGLISH: but right-doers will bud out like leaves. 29 One who breeds trouble for his house will have an estate of air;

EWE: 30 Ame dzɔdzɔe ƒe kutsetse nye agbeti, Eye ame si ɖea luʋɔwo la, nunyalae.
ENGLISH: and an ignoramus is slave to a man with a wise brain. 30 The fruit of right-doing is bark from a tree of life,

EWE: 31 Kpɔ ɖa, ne woɖoa eteƒe na ame dzɔdzɔe le anyigba dzi la, Ke ɖe womaɖo ame vɔ̃ɖi kple nu vɔ̃ wɔla ya ƒe nuwɔna teƒe na wo oa?
ENGLISH: but rascality takes lives away. 31 Here an honest man has a narrow margin of well-being how much more a rogue and sinner!

EWE: Lododowo
ENGLISH: Proverbs

EWE: 12 Ame si lɔ̃a amehehe la, elɔ̃a sidzedze, Ke ame si lé fu mokaname la, menyaa nu o.
ENGLISH: 12 One who loves being instructed loves knowledge; but one who hates being corrected goes stupid.

EWE: 2 Ame nyui ƒe nu dzea Yehowa ŋu, Ke ebua fɔ ame si ɖoa susu vɔ̃wo ɖe tame.
ENGLISH: 2 A kindly man will obtain favor from Jehovah,

EWE: 3 Nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ mana ame nali ke akpɔ o, Ke womaho ame dzɔdzɔe ya gbeɖe o.
ENGLISH: but a schemer he will condemn. 3 Man is not set firm by wrong-doing;

EWE: 4 Srɔ̃nyɔnu zazɛ̃ nye fiakuku na srɔ̃a, Ke srɔ̃nyɔnu ŋukpenanuwɔla nye ŋuɖui le ƒutome na srɔ̃a.
ENGLISH: but right-doers’ roots are unshaken. 4 A worthy wife is her husband’s crown,

EWE: 5 Ame dzɔdzɔewo ƒe tamesusuwo le eteƒe, Ke ame vɔ̃ɖiwo ƒe mɔfiafia nye beble ɖeɖe sɔŋ.
ENGLISH: but a worthless one is like a rot in his bones. 5 Honest men’s plans are for legitimate procedure;

EWE: 6 Ame vɔ̃ɖiwo ƒe nyawo trea azã ɖi, Ke nu dzɔdzɔe wɔlawo ƒe nyawo xɔa wo ɖe agbe.
ENGLISH: rogues’ tactics are fraud. 6 Rogues’ words are an ambush for bloodshed,

EWE: 7 Ne woho ame vɔ̃ɖiwo la, womaganɔ anyi o, Ke ame dzɔdzɔewo ya ƒe aƒe anɔ te ɖaa.
ENGLISH: but upright men’s mouths deliver them. 7 Upset rogues and they are nowhere;

EWE: 8 Woakafu ame si kea eƒe nu le nunya me, Ke woado vlo ame si ƒe dzi metoa mɔ ɖeka o.
ENGLISH: but honest men’s house will stand. 8 A man will be praised in proportion to his good judgment;

EWE: 9 Ame si wobuna ame tsɛe, gake subɔvi le esi la Nyo wu ame si ƒoa adegbe, gake nuɖuɖu mele esi o.
ENGLISH: but a dizzy-headed man will come into contempt. 9 A nobody who owns a slave

EWE: 10 Ame dzɔdzɔe léa be na eƒe aƒemelãwo, Gake ame vɔ̃ɖiwo ƒe nublanuikpɔkpɔ gɔ̃ hã nye tagbɔsesẽ.
ENGLISH: is better than a pretentious man short of bread to eat. 10 A right-minded man knows the wants of his animal;

EWE: 11 Ame si dea eya ŋutɔ ƒe agble la, aɖu nu aɖi ƒo, Ke ame si tia nu maɖinuwo yome la, tagbɔ mele esi o.
ENGLISH: but vicious men’s feelings are brutal. 11 One who works his ground will have plenty of bread;

EWE: 12 Nu si nu vlo wɔlawo lé la le ŋu biãm na ame vɔ̃ɖi, Ke ame dzɔdzɔe la le abe ati si tsea ku ene.
ENGLISH: but one who runs after unpractical things lacks brains. 12 Love for wrong-doing is a net for bad men;

EWE: 13 Ame vɔ̃ɖi ƒe nya vlowo nyea mɔ̃ ɖenɛ, Ke ame dzɔdzɔe ya dona le xaxa me.
ENGLISH: but honest men’s root is permanent. 13 In crime of the lips is a disastrous snare,

EWE: 14 Ame ƒe nu ƒe kutsetse hea nu nyuiwo vana nɛ taŋtaŋ, Eye eƒe asinudɔwɔwɔ ahe viɖe geɖe avɛ nɛ.
ENGLISH: but an honest man gets out of the pinch. 14 Out of the fruit of a man’s mouth he will have his fill of good,

EWE: 15 Bometsila ƒe mɔ dzɔna le eya ŋutɔ ŋkume, Ke nunyala xɔa aɖaŋuɖoɖo.
ENGLISH: and the dealing of one’s hands will come back to him. 15 A know-nothing’s course seems all right to him,

EWE: 16 Bometsilae mesaa dzikudodo o, Ke aɖaŋudzela ya doa toku dzudzu.
ENGLISH: but he who listens to advice is wise. 16 A know-nothing’s pique is displayed on the spot,

EWE: 17 Ðasefo nyateƒetɔ gblɔa nya si le eteƒe, Ke aʋatsoɖasefo daa alakpa.
ENGLISH: but a shrewd man covers up a dishonor. 17 Who utters reliable facts shows the right;

EWE: 18 Nuƒoƒo eŋumabumabui le abe yitɔame ene, Ke nunyalawo ƒe aɖe daa gbe le ame ŋu.
ENGLISH: but a false-speaking witness, a cheat. 18 There is such a thing as a man whose jabber is like sword-stabs;

EWE: 19 Nyateƒenuyi ali ke tegbee, Ke aʋatsoɖe ya nu mesena yina o.
ENGLISH: but wise men’s tongue is healing. 19 A lip of truth will stand fast forevermore,

EWE: 20 Beble le dzi me na ame siwo ɖoa nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ, Ke ame siwo doa ŋutifafa ɖe ŋgɔ la kpɔa dzidzɔ.
ENGLISH: but a tongue of falsehood for an instant. 20 There is double-dealing in the hearts of those who are cooking up harm,

EWE: 21 Vɔ̃ aɖeke maɖi kpe ame dzɔdzɔe o, Ke vɔ̃ aƒo go ame vɔ̃ɖiwo wòade edeƒe.
ENGLISH: but those who confer on wholesome policy have happiness. 21 No trouble will be brought upon a right-doer;

EWE: 22 Yehowa nyɔa ŋu alakpanuyiwo, Ke ame siwo wɔa nuteƒe la ƒe nu dzea eŋu.
ENGLISH: but wrong-doers are full of evil. 22 Lips of falsehood are what Jehovah detests,

EWE: 23 Aɖaŋudzela dzraa eƒe sidzedze ɖo, Ke bometsila ƒe dzi doa boblo eƒe bometsitsi.
ENGLISH: but men who act truly are what he approves. 23 A shrewd man covers up knowledge,

EWE: 24 Veviedola ƒe asie aɖu dzi; Ke kuviatɔ ƒe asie awɔ kluvidɔ.
ENGLISH: but fools’ hearts bawl ignorance. 24 Energetic men’s hands will have control,

EWE: 25 Nuxaxa le dzi me ɖe wòtea ame ƒe dzi ɖe anyi, Ke nya nyui nana dzi kpɔa dzidzɔ.
ENGLISH: but slackness will come to servitude. 25 Worry in a man’s heart depresses it,

EWE: 26 Ame dzɔdzɔe ƒe ŋku nɔa eƒe lãnyiƒe ŋu, Ke ame vɔ̃ɖiwo ƒe mɔ kplɔa wo tranae.
ENGLISH: but thinking of a good thing gladdens it. 26 A right-doer will hunt up his pasture,

EWE: 27 Kuviawɔwɔ mekplɔa ame yia adegbe o, Ke veviedodo la, nu xɔasi wònye na ame.
ENGLISH: but the course wrong-doers are on will make them lose their way. 27 Slackness does not broil his game;

EWE: 28 Dzɔdzɔenyenye ƒe mɔ kplɔa ame yia agbe me; Eƒe mɔ menye kumɔ o.
ENGLISH: but energy treats a man’s goods as worth caring for. 28 On the highway of right there is life,

EWE: Lododowo
ENGLISH: Proverbs

EWE: 13 Vi nyanu sea fofoa ƒe amehehe, Ke fewuɖula mesea nyagbename o.
ENGLISH: 13 A wise son a father’s instruction,

EWE: 2 Ame ƒe nu ƒe kutsetse ana wòakpɔ nu nyuiwo aɖu, Ke ame mawɔnuteƒewo ƒe dzimedidi nye ŋutasesẽ.
ENGLISH: but a cynic hears not a rebuke. 2 Out of the fruit of a man’s mouth he will eat good,

EWE: 3 Ame si kpɔa eƒe nuyiwo dzi la kpɔa eƒe agbe ta, Ame si kea eƒe nuyiwo baa la, dzea gbegblẽ me.
ENGLISH: but faithless men’s appetite is for outrage. 3 He who keeps watch of his mouth is guarding his life;

EWE: 4 Nu dzroa kuviatɔ vevie, gake makpɔ naneke o, Ke veviedola aɖi ƒo nyuie.
ENGLISH: he who throws his lips open comes to ruin. 4 An idler has an appetite and finds nothing,

EWE: 5 Ame dzɔdzɔe léa fu alakpanya, Ke ame vɔ̃ɖi ƒe nuwɔna hea ŋukpe kple vlodoame vanɛ.
ENGLISH: but energetic men’s appetite will find plenty of oil. 5 An honest man hates a false word,

EWE: 6 Dzɔdzɔenyenye kpɔa ame si ƒe zɔzɔme ŋu fɔɖiɖi mele o la ta, Ke vɔ̃ɖinyenye ƒua nu vɔ̃ wɔla anyi.
ENGLISH: but a rogue leaves you disappointed and abashed. 6 Right-doing keeps safe a man of conscientious course,

EWE: 7 Ame aɖewo doa kesinɔtɔ wo ɖokui, evɔ naneke mele wo si hafi o; Ame aɖewo hã doa hiãtɔ wo ɖokui, evɔ nu bɔ ɖe wo si hafi.
ENGLISH: but sin upsets wrong-doers. 7 There are such things as a man who makes himself out rich and there is nothing at all there,

EWE: 8 Kesinɔnu ame tsɔna ɖea eƒe agbe, Ke hiãtɔ ya mesea ŋɔdzidoname aɖeke o.
ENGLISH: of goods. 8 A man’s riches buy off his life;

EWE: 9 Ame dzɔdzɔewo ƒe kekeli klẽna nyuie, Ke ame vɔ̃ɖiwo ƒe akaɖi atsi.
ENGLISH: but a poor man hears not a rebuke. 9 Right-doers’ light is merry, and wrong-doers’ lamp goes out.

EWE: 10 Dzre sɔŋ koe ɖokuiŋudzedze hena vanɛ, Ke nunya tso aƒe ɖe ame siwo dia aɖaŋuɖoɖo gbɔ.
ENGLISH: 10 A man with nothing in him will start a squabble by self-will; but wisdom is with men who take advice.

EWE: 11 Kesinɔnu siwo wokpɔ kaba la nu mesẽna yina o, Gake ame si ƒo nuwo nu ƒu ʋɛʋɛʋɛ la tɔ adzi ɖe edzi.
ENGLISH: 11 Property got together in a rush will shrink; but one who gathers bit by bit will make much.

EWE: 12 Mɔkpɔkpɔ si meva eme kaba o nana dzi sea veve, Ke didi si va eme la, agbeti wònye.
ENGLISH: 12 An expectation long drawn out breeds sickness in the heart; but a desire that comes true is bark from a tree of life.

EWE: 13 Ame si doa vlo nuxlɔ̃ame la, akpɔ etɔ nua, Ke ame si dea bubu sedede ŋu la, woaɖo eteƒe nɛ.
ENGLISH: 13 One who despises a word will have to give security; but one who fears a commandment, he will go safe.

EWE: 14 Nunyala ƒe nufiafia la, agbevudo wònye, Eɖea ame tso ku ƒe mɔ̃tetrewo me.
ENGLISH: 14 A wise man’s precept is a spring of life

EWE: 15 Gɔmesese nyuitɔ nana wokpɔa ŋudzedze ɖe ame ŋu, Ke nu fitifiti wɔlawo ƒe mɔ dzi le glidzaglidza.
ENGLISH: for keeping away from the snares of death. 15 Tact gives charm;

EWE: 16 Aɖaŋudzela wɔa nu le nunya me, Ke bometsila doa boblo eƒe bometsitsi.
ENGLISH: but faithless men’s course is to perdition. 16 Any shrewd man acts by knowledge;

EWE: 17 Dɔtsɔla vɔ̃ɖi dzea vɔ̃ me, Ke duxɔla wɔnuteƒe daa gbe le ame ŋu.
ENGLISH: but a fool spreads out ignorance. 17 An unscrupulous messenger tumbles one into disaster,

EWE: 18 Ame si doa toku amehehe la, ahedada kple ŋukpee ava edzi, Ke ame si lɔ̃na woɖɔnɛ ɖo la ŋue woade bubui.
ENGLISH: but a trustworthy courier is healing. 18 Poverty and dishonor, who neglects instruction;

EWE: 19 Didi si va eme la vivia ame nu, Ke vɔ̃tsitsri menyoa bometsilawo ŋu o.
ENGLISH: but one who observes admonition will come to high standing. 19 A desire realized is sweet to the soul;

EWE: 20 Ame si zɔna kple nunyalawo la, adze nunya, Ke ame si dea ha kple bometsilawo la, eme manyo nɛ o.
ENGLISH: but avoiding anything bad is what fools detest. 20 Go with wise men and become wise;

EWE: 21 Nu vɔ̃ wɔlawo yomee vɔ̃ tina, Ke nunyoname nyea teƒeɖoɖo na ame dzɔdzɔewo ya.
ENGLISH: but one who cultivates fools will come to harm. 21 Disaster pursues sinners,

EWE: 22 Ame nyui gblẽa domenyinu ɖi na viawo ƒe viwo, Ke woadzra ame vɔ̃ɖi ƒe kesinɔnuwo ɖo ɖi na ame dzɔdzɔewo.
ENGLISH: but comfortable prosperity rests with honest men. 22 A good man will bequeath an inheritance to children’s children,

EWE: 23 Hiãtɔ ƒe agble naa nuɖuɖu geɖe, Ke nu madzɔmadzɔ wɔwɔ kplɔnɛ dzonae.
ENGLISH: but a sinner’s wealth is stored away for an honest man. 23 Plenty of food, poor men’s sod-breaking;

EWE: 24 Ame si vea nu le eƒe ameƒoti gbɔ la lé fu via, Ke ame si lɔ̃a via la hea to nɛ ale si dze.
ENGLISH: but there is such a thing as one that is swept away without justice. 24 He who holds back his stick hates his son,

EWE: 25 Ame dzɔdzɔe ɖua nu wòɖia ƒo nɛ, Ke ame vɔ̃ɖiwo ya tsia dɔmeɣi.
ENGLISH: but he who loves him goes in quest of it as a discipline. 25 A right-doer eats all his appetite wants,

EWE: Lododowo
ENGLISH: Proverbs

EWE: 14 Nyɔnu si dze nunya vavã la tua eƒe aƒe, Ke nyɔnu tsibome tsɔa eya ŋutɔ ƒe asi gbãnɛ.
ENGLISH: 14 Women’s wisdom builds its house, but foolishness is demolishing it with her own hands.

EWE: 2 Ame si ƒe mɔwo le dzɔdzɔe la vɔ̃a Yehowa, Ke ame si toa mɔ fitifitiwo dzi la doa vloe.
ENGLISH: 2 He who fears Jehovah goes straightforwardly, but he who despises him takes dodging courses.

EWE: 3 Bometsila ƒe nuƒoƒo dadatɔe le abe ameƒoti ene, Ke nunyalawo ƒe nuyiwo akpɔ wo ta.
ENGLISH: 3 In a know-nothing’s mouth there is a switch for his own back, but wise men’s lips guard them safe.

EWE: 4 Ne nyiwo meli o la, lãto me nɔa dzadzɛ, Ke nyitsu ƒe ŋusẽe nana wokpɔa agblemenu geɖe.
ENGLISH: 4 With no cattle there is a clean manger, but there is plenty of produce by a horned beast’s strength.

EWE: 5 Ðasefo wɔnuteƒe mada alakpa o, Ke aʋatsoɖasefo ya daa alakpa ɣesiaɣi.
ENGLISH: 5 A trustworthy witness will not lie, but a false witness breathes lies.

EWE: 6 Fewuɖula dia nunya ʋuu doa kpoe, Gake sidzedze sua nugɔmesela ya si bɔbɔe.
ENGLISH: 6 A cynic hunts for wisdom and does not find any,

EWE: 7 Te ɖa le bometsila gbɔ, Elabena màkpɔ nunya aɖeke le eƒe nu me o.
ENGLISH: but knowledge is an easy thing to a man of sense. 7 Go face to face with a foolish man,

EWE: 8 Aɖaŋudzela ƒe nunyae nana wòsea mɔ si dzi wòle la gɔme, Ke bometsilawo ƒe movidzɔdzɔ blea wo.
ENGLISH: and you have not known lips of knowledge. 8 A shrewd man’s wisdom consists in understanding his course;

EWE: 9 Bometsilawo tsɔa woƒe fɔɖiɖi wɔa nukonyae, Ke nu dzɔdzɔe wɔlawo lɔ̃na ɖe ame nɔewo dome dzadzraɖo dzi.
ENGLISH: but the stupidity of fools, in cheating. 9 Reprobates’ homes are held guilty,

EWE: 10 Ame ƒe dzi nya eya ŋutɔ ƒe vevesese, Eye ame bubu aɖeke mate ŋu ama eƒe dzidzɔ kplii o.
ENGLISH: but upright men’s houses are accepted. 10 A heart knows its own grief,

EWE: 11 Ame vɔ̃ɖiwo ƒe aƒe atsrɔ̃ gbidii, Ke nu dzɔdzɔe wɔlawo ƒe agbadɔ ali ke ɖaa.
ENGLISH: and a stranger does not mix in its gladness. 11 Wrong-doers’ house will be rooted out,

EWE: 12 Ame aɖewo ƒe mɔ dzɔ le woawo ŋutɔ ŋkume, Ke eƒe nuwuwu nye ku ƒe mɔ.
ENGLISH: 12 There is such a thing as a road that lies smooth before a man but the last part of it is the recesses of death.

EWE: 13 Ne veve le ame ƒe dzi me hã, wotoa egbɔ koa nu, Eye dzidzɔ tea ŋu wua enu ɖe nuxaxa me.
ENGLISH: 13 Even in laughter a heart will feel pain, and the sequel of gladness is sorrow.

EWE: 14 Ame si ƒe dzi tra mɔ akpɔ eƒe nuwɔnawo me tsonu, Ke woaɖo eteƒe na ame nyui hã ɖe eƒe nuwɔnawo nu.
ENGLISH: 14 A man of recreant heart will have his fill out of his courses, and a good man out of his practices.

EWE: 15 Ðekemanyala xɔa nya sia nya dzi sena, Ke aɖaŋudzela léa ŋku ɖe eƒe afɔɖeɖewo katã ŋu.
ENGLISH: 15 A simpleton believes every word, but a shrewd man considers his steps.

EWE: 16 Nunyala ɖɔa ŋu ɖo, eye wòƒoa asa na vɔ̃, Ke bometsila tsia dzi, eye wòkana ɖe eɖokui dzi.
ENGLISH: 16 A wise man is afraid and gets out of the way of harm,

EWE: 17 Ame si doa dziku kabakaba la wɔa bometsinu, Ke woléa fu ame si bua nuwo ŋu nyuie.
ENGLISH: but a fool is hotheaded and confident. 17 A quick-tempered man acts foolishly,

EWE: 18 Ðekemanyala ƒe domenyinue nye bometsitsi, Ke woɖɔa sidzedze na aɖaŋudzelawo abe kuku ene.
ENGLISH: but a practical man bears. 18 Simpletons come in for an estate of ignorance,

EWE: 19 Ame vlowo abɔbɔ ɖe ame nyuiwo ŋkume, Eye nenemae ame vɔ̃ɖiwo hã awɔ le ame dzɔdzɔewo ƒe agbowo nu.
ENGLISH: but shrewd men crown themselves with knowledge. 19 Bad men are brought low before good men

EWE: 20 Ame dahe haviwo ke hã léa fui, Gake xɔlɔ̃ bɔ ɖe kesinɔtɔ si.
ENGLISH: and wrong-doers are at a right-doer’s gates. 20 A poor man is hateful even to his friend;

EWE: 21 Ame si doa vlo ehavi la le nu vɔ̃ wɔm, Ke dzidzɔtɔe nye ame si vea ame tsɛwo nu.
ENGLISH: but there are many to love a rich man. 21 One who despises his neighbor is sinning,

EWE: 22 Ðe ame siwo ɖoa vɔ̃ ɖe tame la metraa mɔ oa?
ENGLISH: 22 Practitioners of evil are on the wrong track indeed,

EWE: Ke wotsɔa amenuveve kple nuteƒewɔwɔ ɖoa eteƒe na ame siwo ɖoa nyui ɖe tame.
ENGLISH: but practitioners of good work in friendship and loyalty.

EWE: 23 Kutrikuku ɖe dɔwɔwɔ ŋu hea viɖe vanɛ, Ke nu kpoloe ƒoƒo ɖeɖe la, ɖeko wònaa wodaa ahe.
ENGLISH: 23 By any hard work there will be a clear profit;

EWE: 24 Nunyalawo ƒe fiakukue nye woƒe kesinɔnu; Ke bometsilawo ƒe movidzɔdzɔe nana wogatsia bome ɖe edzi.
ENGLISH: but lip-talk comes only to a deficit. 24 Wise men’s crown is shrewdness,

EWE: 25 Ðasefo nyateƒetɔ xɔa ame ɖe agbe, Ke aʋatsoɖasefo daa alakpa ɣesiaɣi.
ENGLISH: but fools’ garland is foolishness. 25 A true witness is a lifesaver,

EWE: 26 Kakaɖedzi sẽŋu le Yehowa vɔvɔ̃ me, Eye sitsoƒe wòanye na viawo.
ENGLISH: but a lie-blower is a disappointment. 26 In the fear of Jehovah is a strong reliance,

EWE: 27 Yehowa vɔvɔ̃ nye agbevudo, Enana woƒoa asa na ku ƒe mɔ̃tetrewo.
ENGLISH: and to one’s children that will be a refuge. 27 The fear of Jehovah is a spring of life

EWE: 28 Fia ƒe atsyɔ̃ le dukɔ ƒe agbɔsɔsɔ me, Ke ne teviwo mele dziɖula si o la, edome gblẽna.
ENGLISH: for keeping away from the snares of death. 28 In the numerousness of a people is a king’s majesty,

EWE: 29 Ame si medoa dziku kabakaba o la, nugɔmesese bɔ ɖe esi, Ke ame si megbɔa dzi ɖi o la ɖea eƒe bometsitsi fiana.
ENGLISH: but in lack of folk is a potentate’s ruin. 29 A patient man shows great intelligence,

EWE: 30 Dzi fatu naa agbe ametia, Ke ŋuʋaʋã nye ŋuɖui le ƒuwo me.
ENGLISH: but an impatient man conspicuous foolishness. 30 A placid heart is life in the flesh,

EWE: 31 Ame si le ame tsɛ tafam la doa vlo Ewɔla, Ke ame si vea ame dahe nu la dea bubu Eŋu.
ENGLISH: but passion is a rot in the bones. 31 One who denies a poor man his rights is insulting him who made him;

EWE: 32 Ame vɔ̃ɖi ƒe vɔ̃wɔwɔ atutui aƒu anyi, Ke ame dzɔdzɔe akpɔ sitsoƒe le eƒe fɔmaɖimaɖi me.
ENGLISH: but he who is honoring him shows favor to a needy one. 32 A rogue is knocked over by his viciousness,

EWE: 33 Nunya tso aƒe ɖe nugɔmesela ƒe dzi me, Ke bometsila doa boblo etɔ.
ENGLISH: but an honest man finds refuge in his conscientious life. 33 In a sensible man’s heart wisdom rests,

EWE: 34 Dzɔdzɔenyenye doa dukɔ ɖe dzi, Ke nu vɔ̃ dea ŋukpe mo na dukɔwo.
ENGLISH: but in fools’ bosoms it is known. 34 Right-doing uplifts a nation,

EWE: 35 Subɔvi si wɔa nu le nunya me la ƒe nue dzea fia ŋu, Ke edoa dziku ɖe esi wɔa ŋukpenanu ŋu.
ENGLISH: but sin is a disgrace to any folk. 35 A capable official will have a king’s approval, but a worthless one will be his rage.

EWE: Lododowo
ENGLISH: Proverbs

EWE: 15 Nyaŋuɖoɖo fafɛ tsia dziku nu, Ke gbedaɖeamegbɔ nana dɔmedzoe flana.
ENGLISH: 15 A soft answer wards off ill temper, but a harsh word brings up anger.

EWE: 2 Nunyala ƒe aɖe wɔa sidzedze ŋu dɔ nyuie, Ke bometsitsi dona le bometsilawo nu gbẽgbẽgbẽ.
ENGLISH: 2 Wise men’s tongues know what is what, but fools’ mouths stream ignorance.

EWE: 3 Yehowa ƒe ŋku le afi sia afi, Eléa ŋku ɖe ame vlowo kple ame nyuiwo siaa ŋu.
ENGLISH: 3 Jehovah’s eyes are in every place, keeping a lookout over bad men and good.

EWE: 4 Aɖe fafɛ la, agbeti wònye, Ke nya totro nana mɔkpɔkpɔ buna ɖe ame.
ENGLISH: 4 Calmness of tongue is bark from a tree of life, but upsetting in it means a fracture in the spirit.

EWE: 5 Bometsila doa vlo fofoa ƒe amehehe, Ke aɖaŋudzela lɔ̃na xɔa ɖɔɖɔɖo.
ENGLISH: 5 A know-nothing is contemptuous of his father’s training,

EWE: 6 Kesinɔnu bɔ ɖe ame dzɔdzɔe ƒe aƒe me, Ke nu si su ame vɔ̃ɖi si hea xaxa vaa edzi.
ENGLISH: but one who observes admonition will grow shrewd. 6 A right-doer’s house has in it plenty of capital;

EWE: 7 Nunyalawo ƒe nuyiwo kakaa sidzedze, Ke bometsilawo ƒe dzi ya mele alea o.
ENGLISH: but in a wrong-doer’s produce trouble breeds. 7 Wise men’s lips sprinkle knowledge,

EWE: 8 Ame vɔ̃ɖiwo ƒe vɔsa nye ŋunyɔ na Yehowa, Ke ame dzɔdzɔewo ƒe gbedodoɖa dzea Eŋu.
ENGLISH: but fools’ hearts are not right. 8 Wrong-doers’ sacrifice is what Jehovah abominates,

EWE: 9 Ame vɔ̃ɖi ƒe zɔzɔme nye ŋunyɔ na Yehowa, Ke ame si tia dzɔdzɔenyenye yome lae wòlɔ̃na.
ENGLISH: but upright men’s prayer is what he accepts. 9 What Jehovah abominates is a wrong-doer’s course;

EWE: 10 Amehehe tena ɖe ame si gblẽ mɔ la ɖi dzi, Ke ame sia ame si lé fu mokaname la aku.

ENGLISH: the upshot is irrelevance and humiliation. 14 A man’s spirit weathers his ailment,

EWE: 18 Nudzidze tsia dzre nu, Eye wòtsoa nya me na hoʋlila sesẽwo.

EWE: 19 Nɔvi si ŋu woda vo ɖo la tri akɔ wu du sesẽ, Eye dzre aɖewo le abe mɔ́ sesẽ ƒe gameti ene.
ENGLISH: and separates formidable opponents. 19 A brother is more of a salvation than a strong city,

EWE: 20 Ame ƒe nu ƒe kutsetse ana wòaɖi ƒodo; Nu siwo do tso eƒe nu me la aɖi ƒo nɛ.
ENGLISH: and kinsfolk are equal to castle bars. 20 Out of the fruit of a man’s mouth his stomach will have its fill,

EWE: 21 Ku kple agbe le aɖe la si me; Ame siwo lɔ̃a ezazã la aɖu eƒe kutsetse.
ENGLISH: and of the produce of his lips he will get all he can hold. 21 Death and life are in the hands of the tongue,

EWE: 22 Ame si kpɔ srɔ̃nyɔnu nyui la, eƒe asi su nu nyui dzi, Eye amenuveve wònye tso Yehowa gbɔ nɛ.
ENGLISH: and those who love it will eat the fruit of it. 22 Who has found a wife has found a good thing

EWE: 23 Ame dahe ɖea kuku ne ele nu ƒom, Ke kesinɔtɔ daa gbe ɖe ame gbɔ.
ENGLISH: and obtained favor from Jehovah. 23 A poor man talks beseechingly,

EWE: 24 Xɔlɔ̃ aɖewo li siwo gblẽa wo nɔewo dome, Gake xɔlɔ̃ aɖewo kuna ɖe ame ŋu wu ame nɔvi gɔ̃ hã.
ENGLISH: a rich man answers imperiously. 24 There are friends for company, and there is such a thing as a loving friend that sticks tighter than a brother.

ENGLISH: Proverbs

ENGLISH: 19 Better a poor man leading a conscientious life than a man of crooked lips, he being a fool.

EWE: 2 Sidzedze ƒe ame si manɔmanɔ menyo o, Eye ame si tsia klokloklo la wɔa nu vɔ̃.
ENGLISH: 2 When a soul has not knowledge it is not good either,

EWE: 4 Kesinɔnuwo hea xɔlɔ̃ geɖe ɖe ame ŋu, Ke xɔlɔ̃wo kana le ame dahe ŋu.

EWE: 7 Ame dahe nɔviwo ke hã léa fui; Aleke wɔ exɔlɔ̃wo ya maka le eŋu o!

EWE: Enɔa wo yome ɖea kuku na wo, gake womedea nu eme nɛ o.

EWE: 8 Ame si si nunya su la lɔ̃a eɖokui.
ENGLISH: 8 One who invests in brains loves his life;

ENGLISH: 9 A false witness will not be held guiltless

ENGLISH: and a lie-blower will perish. 10 Luxury is not befitting for a fool;

EWE: 11 Ame si sea nu gɔme nyuie la, medoa dziku kabakaba o, Eye atsyɔ̃ wònye nɛ be wòaŋe aɖaba aƒu agɔdzedze dzi.
ENGLISH: much less is ruling over generals for a slave. 11 For a man to exercise patience is good business, and to pass over offenses is an adornment to him.

EWE: 12 Fia ƒe dziku le abe dzata ƒe gbetete ene, Ke eƒe amenuveve le abe zãmu si dza ɖe gbewo dzi ene.

EWE: 13 Vi tsibome hea gbegblẽ vaa fofoa dzi, Eye srɔ̃nyɔnu dzrewɔla le abe xɔ si le ɖuɖum ɖaa ene.
ENGLISH: 13 A foolish son is a catastrophe to his father, and a woman’s wrangles are a steadily dribbling leak in the roof.

EWE: 14 Aƒe kple kesinɔnuwo nye domenyinu tso vifofowo gbɔ, Ke srɔ̃nyɔnu nyanu la, Yehowa gbɔe wòtsona.

EWE: 20 Se aɖaŋuɖoɖo, eye nàxɔ amehehe, Ne nàdze nunya le etsɔ si gbɔna me.
ENGLISH: 20 Listen to advice and accept instruction,

EWE: 21 Nu geɖewoe amegbetɔ ɖona ɖe eƒe dzi me, Gake Yehowa ƒe adaŋudedee ava eme.
ENGLISH: in order that you may be wise in future. 21 A man has plenty of ideas in his mind,

EWE: 22 Atsyɔ̃e wònye na ame ne elɔ̃a ame tso dzi me; Eye enyo be woanye hiãtɔ wu be woanye alakpatɔ.
ENGLISH: but Jehovah’s plan is what stands. 22 A man’s goodwill is his friendliness,

EWE: 23 Yehowa vɔvɔ̃ kplɔa ame yia agbe me; Ame si vɔ̃nɛ la aɖe dzi ɖi; vɔ̃ aɖeke mava edzi o.
ENGLISH: and a poor man is better than a liar. 23 Fearing Jehovah leads to life,

EWE: 24 Kuviatɔ de asi nuɖugba me; Etsɔtsɔ de nu me gɔ̃ hã zu dɔ nɛ.
ENGLISH: and one passes the night with a full stomach, unvisited by harm. 24 An idler has buried his hand in the dish,

EWE: 25 Ƒo fewuɖula, ekema ame makpɔnuteƒe adze nunya, Ka mo na nugɔmesela, ekema sidzedze geɖe asu esi.

ENGLISH: happy his children after him!

ENGLISH: 18 Ideas become effective by forethought;
