EWE: 13 Eɖo dzo ɖa tso dzi ɖe nye ƒuwo me, eye wòge ɖe nye ƒuwo katã me.
ENGLISH: 13 See God’s work; for who is able to set straight what he crooks?

EWE: Medze dɔ ŋkeke blibo la katã. 14 Etsɔ eƒe asiwo ƒo ƒu nye vodadawo hebla wo abe kɔkuti ene. Etsɔ wo ku kɔ nam, eye ŋusẽ vɔ le ŋunye.
ENGLISH: 14 On a day of good be in a good mood, and on a day of evil see: God made this too to go with that, with a view to man’s not finding out anything that is to follow.

EWE: 15 Yehowa tsɔ nye kalẽtɔwo katã ƒu gbe le donyeme.
ENGLISH: 15 I have seen everything happen in my days of nonsense.

EWE: Eyɔ takpekpe ɖe ŋunye, ne woagbã nye ɖekakpuiwo gudugudu. Yehowa fanya Yuda ɖetugbui leaƒe la le wainfiãnu me.
ENGLISH: There is such a thing as a right-doer perishing in his right-doing, and there is such a thing as a wrong-doer getting a long life in his wrong-doing.

EWE: 16 Nu siawo tae mele avi fam ɖo; nye ŋkuwo le aɖatsi fam yoyoyo. Elabena ame si afa akɔ nam, alo ana gbɔdzɔem la, le adzɔge. Vinyewo tsrɔ̃, elabena futɔ la ƒe alɔ de dzi. 17 Zion ke eƒe abɔwo me; gake ame aɖeke meli afa akɔ nɛ o. Yehowa dɔ Yakob ƒe ketɔ siwo katã ƒo xlãe la ɖe eŋu. Yerusalem zu ŋunyɔnu na wo. 18 Yehowa tɔ dzɔ, elabena eƒe sewo ŋue medze aglã ɖo. Mi dukɔwo katã, misee, ne miakpɔ nye vevesese la. Nye ɖetugbui leaƒewo kple nye ɖekakpuiwo yi aboyo me.
ENGLISH: 16 Do not be an extreme right-doer and do not go in excessively for wisdom: why turn anchorite? 17 Do not go to extremes in doing wrong, and do not be foolish: why die before your time? 18 Better hold on to this and not let go of that, because one who fears God will get through with all of it.

EWE: 19 Meyɔ lɔ̃nyelawo, gake wogbe vava.
Nye nunɔlawo kple nye ametsitsiwo ku le dua me, Esime wole nu dim be yewoaɖu, ne yewoatsi agbe.
ENGLISH: Wisdom is stronger for the wise man than any ten autocrats that there have been in the city.

EWE: 20 Oo Yehowa, kpɔ ɖa, meɖo xaxa me. Nye dɔ me le totrom.
ENGLISH: 20 For there is no human saint on earth that does what is good and never sins.

EWE: Gake àna ŋkeke si nèɖe gbeƒãe la naɖo, ale be woawo hã woanɔ abe nye ene. 22 Woƒe nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔwo katã neva ŋkuwòme, eye nàtu nu kpli wo vevie, Abe ale si nètu nu kplim vevie le nye dzidadawo katã ta ene.
ENGLISH: 21 Do not take notice, either, of all words that are spoken, that you may not hear your slave curse you; 22 for you know yourself that many times you yourself have cursed others.

EWE: Konyifahawo 2:1-22
ENGLISH: 23 All this I probed by wisdom.

EWE: Etsɔ Israel ƒe atsyɔ̃ la xlã ɖe anyi tso dziƒo.
ENGLISH: I thought I would be wise; but that was too far off for me.

EWE: 2 Yehowa mi Yakob ƒe nɔƒewo katã nublanuimakpɔmakpɔe.
ENGLISH: 24 What is is far off and deep, deep; who is to find it out?

EWE: Egbã Yuda vinyɔnu la ƒe mɔ́ sesẽwo ƒu anyi le eƒe dziku helĩhelĩ me. Eɖiɖi wo ɖe anyi hegblẽ kɔ ɖo na fiaɖuƒe la kple eƒe amegãwo.
ENGLISH: 25 I have gone about, my heart and I, to know and to explore and search out wisdom and science, and to know wrong to be folly, and fooling to be craziness.

EWE: 3 Etsɔ dziku helĩhelĩ ŋe Israel ƒe ŋusẽ katã ɖa. Ehe eƒe nuɖusi ɖe megbe esi futɔ la va, Ebi le Yakob abe dzobibi si fiãa nu sia nu si ƒo xlãe la ene.
ENGLISH: 26 And I find a bitterer thing than death: woman, whose heart is toils and nets and whose arms are fetters; one whom God finds good will get clear of her, but a sinner will be caught on her.

EWE: 4 Ebi eƒe dati abe futɔ ene; eƒe nuɖusi sɔ gbe abe ketɔ ene; Ele woƒe ame veviwo katã wum.
ENGLISH: 27 See, this I have found, says Koheleth, putting one thing with another to get a result, 28 that my soul still searched and I did not find.

EWE: Etrɔ eƒe dɔmedzoe ƒo ɖe Zion vinyɔnu ƒe agbadɔ me abe dzo ene.
ENGLISH: One out of a thousand of mankind I found, but a woman among all these I never did find.

EWE: 5 Yehowa zu abe futɔ ene; Emi Israel. Emi eƒe xɔ tsralawo katã; Egbã eƒe mɔ́ sesẽawo katã.
ENGLISH: 29 This alone, see, I did find: that God made man straight, but they have hunted out many contrivances.

EWE: Etsi eƒe ŋkekenyui la nu.
ENGLISH: Ecclesiastes 8:1-17

EWE: 8 Yehowa ɖoe be yeamu Zion vinyɔnu la ƒe gli aƒu anyi.
ENGLISH: 8 Who is like the wise man? and who knows the explanation of a thing?

EWE: Eda dzidzeka. Mehe eƒe asi ɖe megbe le tsɔtsrɔ̃ hehe vɛ ŋu o.
ENGLISH: A man’s wisdom puts light into his face, and the hardness of his face is changed.

EWE: Eye wòna kpoƒuƒu kple gli le konyi fam. Ŋusẽ vɔ le wo kple eve la siaa ŋu.
ENGLISH: For he does anything he chooses to, 4 inasmuch as a king’s word is authoritative, and who will say to him “What are you doing?”

EWE: 9 Eƒe agbowo ɖo agu. Egblẽ eƒe gametiwo heŋe wo. Eƒe fia kple eƒe amegãwo le dukɔwo dome.
ENGLISH: 9 All this I saw, keeping my mind on all the work that was done under the sun, at a time when man had control of man to his own harm.

EWE: Se aɖeke meli o; eƒe nyagblɔɖilawo gɔ̃ hã mekpɔ ŋutega aɖeke tso Yehowa gbɔ o. 10 Zion vinyɔnu ƒe ametsitsiwo bɔbɔ nɔ anyigba hezi ɖoɖoe.
ENGLISH: 10 And then I saw wrong-doers buried, and coming in, out of a holy place, and their bad record forgotten in the city.

EWE: Nye dɔ me le totrom. Nye aklã dudu ɖe anyigba le nye dukɔ la ƒe vinyɔnu ƒe anyidzedze ta, Elabena ɖeviwo kple vidzĩwo le ƒenyi kum le dua ƒe ablɔwo me. 12 Wole wo dadawo biam be, “Abolo kple wain ɖe?”
ENGLISH: This too is nonsense, 11 that sentence on evil-doing is not quickly executed; therefore the hearts of mankind are altogether determined to do evil, 12 inasmuch as a sinner does evil all along and has a long life

EWE: Esime wole ƒenyi kum le dua ƒe ablɔ me eye wole abe ame si ŋu wode abi ene, Esime woƒe agbe nu nɔ tsotsom le wo dadawo ƒe akɔnu. 13 Nu ka mazã wòanye ɖase nam Oo Yerusalem vinyɔnu, nu kae matsɔ wò asɔ kplii? Oo, Zion ɖetugbui leaƒe, nu kae matsɔ wò asɔ kplii, ne mafa akɔ na wò? Elabena wò abi la keke abe atsiaƒu ene.
ENGLISH: though I do know that for those who fear God there will be good inasmuch as they stand in fear before him, 13 but for the wrong-doer there will not be good and he will have no long life, like a shadow, inasmuch as he does not stand in fear before God.

EWE: Ame kae ate ŋu ada gbe le ŋuwò? 14 Ŋutega siwo wò nyagblɔɖilawo kpɔ na wò la nye alakpa kple beble, Eye womeklo nu le wò vodada dzi ne woaxe mɔ na wò aboyomeyiyi o, Ke boŋ wokpɔa alakpaŋutega eye wogblɔa ameflunyawo na wò.
ENGLISH: 14 There is a piece of nonsense that is done on earth, that there are right-doers to whom there happens what is suitable to wrong-doers’ work and there are wrong-doers to whom there happens what is suitable to right-doers’ work. I say this is nonsense too.

EWE: 15 Ame siwo katã tso eme va yina la sia akpe ɖe ŋuwò tsɔ ɖua fewu le ŋuwò. Ewɔa moyaa na wo wolia aku heʋuʋua ta ɖe Yerusalem vinyɔnu la ŋu gblɔna be: “Du si ŋu wogblɔna le tsã be, ‘Enye tugbewo ƒe tugbe, anyigba blibo la ƒe dzidzɔ’ lae nye esia?”
ENGLISH: 15 And I praise merrymaking, inasmuch as there is nothing good for man under the sun but to eat and drink and make merry, and he will have that to go with him for his trouble through his time of life which God has given to him under the sun.

EWE: 16 Wò futɔwo katã ke nu baa ɖe ŋuwò.
ENGLISH: 16 When I applied my heart to knowing wisdom and seeing all the business that is done on earth

EWE: Wolia aku hele aɖukli ɖum le gbɔgblɔm be: “Míemii.
ENGLISH: for day and night it does not get even a glimpse of sleep

EWE: Eva ɖo azɔ, eye míekpɔ eteƒe!” 17 Yehowa wɔ nu si wòɖo la; ewɔ eƒe nya dzi de goe, Nya si wògblɔ tso blema ke. Egbã nu ƒu anyi nublanuimakpɔmakpɔe. Ena dzi dzɔ futɔ la le tawò; ena wò ketɔwo kpɔ ŋusẽ.
ENGLISH: 17 I saw all God’s work, how man cannot make out all the work that is done under the sun, inasmuch as man puts himself to trouble looking into it but does not make it out, and even if the wise man professes to know he cannot make it out.

EWE: Konyifahawo
ENGLISH: Ecclesiastes

EWE: 3 Nyee nye ame si kpɔ fukpekpe teƒe le eƒe dziku helĩhelĩ ƒe ameƒoti la ta.
ENGLISH: 9 For I took all this into my heart, and my heart saw all this, that the righteous and the wise and their doings are in God’s hands: neither love nor hate does man know about.

EWE: 2 Enyam, eye wòna mezɔ viviti me, ke menye kekeli me o.
ENGLISH: 2 Everything that has gone before them is nonsense, as there is one fate for all, for the right-doer and the wrong-doer, and for the clean and the unclean, and for the sacrificer and the nonsacrificer; the good man is like the sinner, the swearer like him who is afraid of swearing.

EWE: 3 Ɛ̃, etrɔ eƒe asi ɖe ŋunye atraɖii ŋkeke blibo la. 4 Ena wɔna vɔ le nye ŋutilã kple nye ŋutigbalẽ ŋu; Eŋe nye ƒuwo.
ENGLISH: 3 This is a bad thing in all that is done under the sun, that there is one fate for all; and also the hearts of mankind are full of evil, and they have craziness in their hearts through their lives; and afterward, to the dead, 4 for who is there that has a choice As to all the living there is something to depend on; for a living dog is thereby better than the dead lion.

EWE: 5 Eɖe to ɖem; etsɔ aɖi veve kple fukpekpe ƒo xlãm.
ENGLISH: 5 For the living know they are to die, but the dead do not know a thing, and no longer get any reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.

EWE: 6 Ezi dzinye mebɔbɔ nɔ viviti me, abe ame siwo ku gbe aɖe gbe ke ene.
ENGLISH: 6 Both their love and their hate and their ardors are lost in the past, and they no longer have a part, forever not, in anything that is done under the sun.

EWE: 7 Eɖo gli ɖe ŋunye, be magate ŋu asi o; Ede akɔblikunyowu kpekpewom.
ENGLISH: 7 Go, eat your bread in merriment and drink your wine with happy heart, because God has already given his approval to your doings.

EWE: 8 Eye ne medo ɣli nɛ vevie be wòaxɔ nam la, egbea nye gbedodoɖawo sese.
ENGLISH: 8 At every time be your clothes white and oil not scanty on your head.

EWE: 9 Etsɔ kpe fufuwo xe mɔ nam; Egɔdɔ̃ nye toƒewo.
ENGLISH: 9 Gaze on life with a wife you love, all the days of your nonsensical life that God has given to you under the sun; all the days of your nonsense, because that is the portion you get by living and by your trouble that you take under the sun.

EWE: 10 Edea xa ɖi nam abe sisiblisi ene, abe dzata si le adeklo dzi ene.
ENGLISH: 10 Everything that comes within your reach to do with your powers, do; because there is no action nor purpose nor knowledge nor wisdom in the world below, where you are going.

EWE: 11 Ehem ɖa le mɔ me, eye wòvuvum ʋayaʋaya. Ena mezu aƒedo.
ENGLISH: 11 I came back seeing under the sun that the race does not go to the swift nor the battle to the crack fighters, neither does bread go to the wise, neither do riches go to the longheaded, neither does popularity go to the knowing, because time and chance happen to all of them.

EWE: 12 Evu eƒe da me, eye wòdzidze aŋutrɔ ɖe dzinye. 13 Eƒo eƒe daku me aŋutrɔwo ɖe nye ayikuwo.
ENGLISH: 12 For man does not know his time either: like the fishes, that are gripped by a disastrous net, or like the birds, that are gripped by the trap, like them mankind are trapped in a disastrous time when it falls upon them suddenly.

EWE: 14 Mezu nu ɖikokoe na amewo katã, mezu ha le nu na wo wole dzidzim ŋkeke bliboa. 15 Etsɔ nu vevewo ɖi ƒo nam, ena atsa yɔm fũu.
ENGLISH: 13 This too I saw of wisdom under the sun, and it was great to me: 14 a small city, and few men in it, and there came to it a great king and surrounded it and built great towers against it; 15 but he found in it a wise poor man, and he preserved the city by his wisdom; but people did not remember that poor man.

EWE: 16 Ena kpekui ŋe aɖu nam; Etigim ɖe dzofi me.
ENGLISH: 16 And I say, wisdom is better than prowess, but the poor man’s wisdom is despised and his words are not listened to.

EWE: 17 Èna ŋutifafa bu ɖem; meŋlɔ nu nyui be.
ENGLISH: 17 Wise men’s words in quiet are heard better than the screams of a ruler among fools.

EWE: 18 Ale megblɔ be: “Nye atsyɔ̃ nu yi, eye mebu mɔkpɔkpɔ le Yehowa me.”
ENGLISH: 18 Wisdom is better than weapons of battle.

EWE: 27 Enyo na ŋutsu be wòatsɔ kɔkuti le eƒe ɖevime.
ENGLISH: But one bungler brings the loss of a great deal of good.

EWE: Konyifahawo
ENGLISH: Ecclesiastes

EWE: 4 Aleke sika si le keklẽm, sika nyui la, nyɔ vĩi ale! Aleke wokaka kpe kɔkɔewo ɖe kpɔdomeewo ƒe dzogoewo katã dzi ale!
ENGLISH: 10 Dead flies taint perfumer’s oil with foul-smelling bubbles; a little foolishness outweighs wisdom and standing.

EWE: 2 Zion ƒe vi veviwo, ame siwo ƒe dadame sɔ kple sika si ŋu wodza, Aleke wobu wo abe anyize, Si nye zemela ƒe asinudɔwɔwɔ ene!
ENGLISH: 2 A wise man’s heart is toward his right, but a fool’s heart toward his left.

EWE: 3 Agbotoewo ke hã naa no wo viwo wonona, Ke nye dukɔ vinyɔnu ya ƒe tagbɔ sẽ, abe golo le gbedzi ene.
ENGLISH: 3 And even on the road as the foolish man is walking his brains give out and he tells everybody he is foolish.

EWE: 4 Vi nono ƒe aɖe lé ɖe nu me nɛ le tsikɔwuame ta. Ðeviwo biaa abolo, gake ame aɖeke menaa wo o.
ENGLISH: 4 If the ruler’s temper rises against you, do not leave your position; for coolness quiets down great faults.

EWE: Ame siwo wotaa aɖabɛ na tsã la mlɔ aɖukpo dzi. 6 Nye dukɔ vinyɔnu la ƒe tohehe kpe wu tohehe si va Sodom dzi le eƒe nu vɔ̃ ta, Du si wotrɔ bu anyi le aɖabaƒoƒo ɖeka me, eye ame aɖeke meli akpe ɖe eŋu o. 7 Eƒe Naziritɔwo le dzadzɛ wu sno, wofu wu notsi.Wo ŋu biã wu soe; wo ŋu zrɔ̃ abe safir-kpe ene.
ENGLISH: 5 There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, seeming like a blunder that originates among the autocrat’s officers: 6 foolishness is put in many lofty positions and rich men sit in low places; 7 I have seen slaves on horseback and chieftains walking on the ground like slaves.

EWE: Woƒe ŋutigbalẽ lé ɖe woƒe ƒuwo ŋu kpaɖii; eƒu abe nake ene. 9 Ame siwo tsi yi nu la tɔ nyo wu ame siwo tsi dɔwuame si me, Ame siawo ɖi ku glaŋ, le esi agblemenuwo ƒe hiã ƒo ɖe wo abe yi ene ta.
ENGLISH: 8 He who digs a pit falls into it, and he who breaks down a wall has, a snake bite him; 9 he who takes out stones gets hurt by them; he who splits wood is in danger by it.

EWE: 10 Nyɔnu siwo ƒe dɔme trɔna ɖe ame ŋu ke hã ƒe asiwo ɖa woawo ŋutɔwo ƒe viwo. Wozu abe nuxaxabolo ene na amewo le nye dukɔ vinyɔnu la ƒe anyidzeɣi.
ENGLISH: 10 If the iron has grown dull and he has not whetted, then he exerts himself; but wisdom is an advantage for giving efficiency.

EWE: 11 Yehowa ɖe eƒe dɔmedzoe la fia; Etrɔ eƒe dziku helĩhelĩ ƒo ɖi. Edo dzo ɖe Zion, eye wòfiã eƒe gɔmeɖoanyiwo.
ENGLISH: 11 If the snake bites without having been charmed, one is no better off for having a skilled tongue.

EWE: 12 Anyigbadzifiawo kple anyigba la dzi nɔlawo katã mexɔe se Be ketɔ la kple futɔ la age ɖe Yerusalem ƒe agbowo me hafi o.
ENGLISH: 12 The words of a wise man’s mouth are ingratiating, but a fool’s lips swamp him.

EWE: 13 Nu siawo katã dzɔ le eƒe nyagblɔɖilawo ƒe nu vɔ̃wo, eƒe nunɔlawo, Ame siwo kɔ ame dzɔdzɔewo ƒe ʋu ɖi le eme ƒe vodadawo ta.
ENGLISH: 13 The first words of his mouth are foolishness and the last of it is a bad case of craziness; 14 and the foolish fellow makes a lot of talk.

EWE: Woƒo ʋu,Ale be ame aɖeke mete ŋu ka asi woƒe avɔwo ŋu o. 15 Wodo ɣli ɖo ɖe wo be: “Mite ɖa! Mia ŋu mekɔ o! Mite ɖa! Mite ɖa! Migaka mía ŋu o!”
ENGLISH: Man does not know what will happen, and who is to tell him what is to come after him? 15 The fool’s trouble tires him out, as he does not know enough to walk to town.

EWE: 17 Fifia gɔ̃ hã míaƒe ŋkuwo kpɔ mɔ na xɔname wòglo. Míekpɔ mɔ na xɔname ʋuu tso dukɔ si mate ŋu axɔ na ame o la gbɔ. 18 Futɔwo le ŋku lém ɖe míaƒe afɔɖeɖe ɖe sia ɖe ŋu ale gbegbe be zɔzɔ le míaƒe ablɔwo me zu dɔ.Míaƒe nuwuwu gogo; míaƒe ŋkekewo vɔ, elabena míaƒe nuwuwu ɖo.
ENGLISH: 16 Alas for you, country whose king is a boy and whose generals eat in the morning! 17 Happy are you, country whose king is a son of nobles and whose generals eat at a regular hour, for strength and not for drinking! 18 By indolence the timbers sag, and by unlifted hands the roof leaks.

EWE: 19 Mía yometilawo ɖe abla wu hɔ̃ le yame. Woyɔ mí ɖe nu le towo dzi; wode xa ɖe gbedzi na mí.
ENGLISH: 19 They get up meals for fun, and wine makes life merry, and money provides an answer for everything.

EWE: 20 Asi su míaƒe ŋɔtimegbɔgbɔ, Yehowa ƒe amesiamina la dzi le woƒe ʋe gã la me, Eya, ame si ŋu míegblɔ le be: “Míanɔ eƒe vɔvɔli te le dukɔwo dome.”
ENGLISH: 20 Do not misspeak a king even mentally, nor a rich man in your bedchambers, for the birds of the air will convey the sound and the winged will carry word.

EWE: Konyifahawo
ENGLISH: Ecclesiastes

EWE: 5 Oo Yehowa, ɖo ŋu nu si dzɔ ɖe mía dzi la. Ðo ŋku anyi nàkpɔ ale si wodo ŋukpe míi ɖa.
ENGLISH: 11 Let your bread go out over the water, for in the long run you will find it.

EWE: 2 Míaƒe domenyinu la trɔ zu ame tutɔwo tɔ, míaƒe aƒewo zu amedzrowo tɔ.
ENGLISH: 2 Give share to seven and even to eight, because you do not know what there will be of disaster on the earth.

EWE: 3 Míezu tsyɔ̃eviwo, tɔ mele mía si o. Mía nɔwo le abe ahosiwo ene.
ENGLISH: 3 If the clouds get full of a shower they empty it out on the earth; and if a tree falls toward the south, or if toward the north, in the place where the tree falls, there it will be.

EWE: 4 Ðe míedzea tsi hafi nona, eye ɖe míeƒlea míaƒe nakewo.
ENGLISH: 4 One who watches the wind will not sow, and one who views the clouds will not reap.

EWE: 5 Ame siwo yɔ mí ɖe nu la gogo mí; Ðeɖi te mía ŋu belibeli, gake míekpɔ gbɔɖeme aɖeke o.
ENGLISH: 5 As you do not know what is the course of the spirit into bones in the body of the pregnant woman, so you will not know the working of God who works everything.

EWE: 6 Míebɔbɔ ɖe Egipte te kple Asiria te, be míakpɔ abolo aɖu aɖi ƒo.
ENGLISH: 6 In the morning sow your seed and at evening do not rest your hand, because you do not know which will do right, whether this or that or both of them alike will be good.

EWE: 7 Mía tɔgbui siwo wɔ nu vɔ̃ la, megali o, ke míawoe le woƒe vodadawo tsɔm.
ENGLISH: 7 And the light is sweet, and it does the eyes good to see the sun; 8 for if man lives many years he is to be merry in all of them.

EWE: 8 Kluviwo le mía dzi ɖum azɔ; ame aɖeke meli aɖe mí le wo si me o.
ENGLISH: 8 Perfect nonsense, says Koheleth; everything is nonsense.

EWE: 9 Míedea míaƒe agbe afɔku me hafi kpɔa míaƒe abolo gbɔnɛ, elabena yi le gbedzi.
ENGLISH: 9 And in addition to Koheleth’s being a wise man he taught knowledge to the people besides, and, weighing and probing, edited many proverbs.

EWE: 10 Dɔ wu mí vevie ale gbegbe be míaƒe ŋutigbalẽ ʋu dzo hɛ̃e abe kpodzo ene.
ENGLISH: 10 Koheleth aimed to find interesting language and write straightforward truths.

EWE: 11 Wogblẽ srɔ̃nyɔnuwo le Zion, kple ɖetugbui leaƒewo le Yuda duwo me.
ENGLISH: 11 Wise men’s words are like goad-points, and such as are taken up into collections are like driven nails; they are given from one shepherd.

EWE: 12 Wode ka woƒe amegãwo ƒe asiwo tsi ɖe yame, eye womede bubu ametsitsiwo ŋu o.
ENGLISH: 12 And in addition to these things, my son, take warning: of making many books there is no end, and studying much is a fatigue to the flesh.

EWE: 13 Ðekakpuiawo lé té ɖe ta, eye ɖeviwo dze anyi le nakegba te.
ENGLISH: 13 Last word; all is heard: fear God and keep his commandments, for this is the whole of man.

EWE: 14 Ametsitsiwo vɔ le dugbo la nu; ɖekakpuiwo megale ha ƒom o. 15 Míaƒe dzi dzudzɔ aseyetsotso; míaƒe ɣeɖuɖu trɔ zu konyifafa.
ENGLISH: 14 For God will bring every action under a judgment covering every unknown circumstance, be it good or be it bad.

EWE: Daniel
ENGLISH: Song of Solomon

EWE: 1 Le Yuda-fia Yehoyakim ƒe fiaɖuɖu ƒe ƒe etɔ̃lia me la, Babilon-fia Nebukadnezar va Yerusalem, eye wòɖe to ɖee.
ENGLISH: 1 Solomon’s Song of Songs

EWE: 2 Eye Yehowa tsɔ Yuda-fia Yehoyakim kple Mawu vavã la ƒe aƒe la me nu aɖewo de asi nɛ, ale be wòtsɔ wo yi eƒe mawu ƒe me le Sinar-nyigba dzi.
ENGLISH: 2 Let him give me kisses from his mouth, for your love is better than wine.

EWE: 3 Eye fia la de se na eŋumewo ƒe tatɔ Aspenaz be wòakplɔ Israel-vi aɖewo hekpe ɖe fia ƒe dzidzimeviwo kple bubumewo ƒe vi aɖewo ŋu vɛ.
ENGLISH: 3 Your oils are good to smell; your name is Turak oil; therefore the girls love you.

EWE: 4 Woanye ɖekakpui siwo nu mewɔ afi aɖeke na o, siwo dze ɖeka, wonyaa nu, sidzedze le wo si, wosea nu gɔme nyuie, eye woate ŋu asubɔ le fiasã me.
ENGLISH: 4 Draw me after you; we will run;bring me into your chambers, king! We will be gay and glad in you;

EWE: Ame siawoe woafia Kaldeatɔwo ƒe nuŋɔŋlɔ kple gbegbɔgblɔe.
ENGLISH: we think more of your love than of wine; rightly they love you.

EWE: 5 Azɔ hã, fia la ɖoe be woana woƒe gbe sia gbe nuɖuɖu wo tso fia la ƒe nuɖuɖu viviwo kple wain si wònona me.
ENGLISH: 5 I am dark but handsome, daughters of Jerusalem, like Kedar’s tents, like Solomon’s curtains.

EWE: Woana hehe wo ƒe etɔ̃, ale be le ƒe siawo ƒe nuwuwu la, woasubɔ fia la. 6 Ke Yuda-toa me tɔ aɖewo le wo dome, woawoe nye Daniel, Hananiya, Misael kple Azariya.
ENGLISH: 6 Do not notice how dark I am, how the sun has taken a look at me; My mother’s sons were cross with me, set me to watch the vineyards; my own vineyard I did not watch.

EWE: 7 Eye fiaŋumewo ƒe amegã la tsɔ ŋkɔ na wo; Daniel tɔe nye Beltesazar, Hananiya tɔe nye Sadrak, Misael tɔe nye Mesak, eye Azariya tɔe nye Abednego.
ENGLISH: 7 Tell me, you whom my soul loves, where you are pasturing your flock, where you are having them lie down at noon; Why should I be like a girl wandering at random by your comrades’ flocks?

EWE: 8 Ke Daniel ɖoe le eƒe dzi me be yematsɔ fia ƒe nuɖuɖu viviwo kple wain si wònona la agblẽ kɔ ɖo na ye ɖokui o.
ENGLISH: 8 If you do not know, most beautiful among women, Go out on the track of the sheep and pasture your kids by the shepherds’ tents.

EWE: 9 Eye Mawu vavã la na fiaŋumewo ƒe amegã la ve Daniel nu hekpɔ nublanui nɛ.
ENGLISH: 9 To a pony in the Pharaoh’s chariots I liken you, sweetheart.

EWE: 10 Gake fiaŋumewo ƒe amegã la gblɔ na Daniel be: “Mele vɔvɔ̃m na nye aƒetɔ fia, ame si ɖo miaƒe nuɖuɖu kple miaƒe nunono nam.
ENGLISH: 10 How handsome your cheeks with face-chains, your neck with beads!

EWE: Ke ne ekpɔ be miaƒe dzedzeme vloe wu ɖekakpui bubuawo tɔ ɖe?
ENGLISH: 11 We will make you gold face-chains with silver studs.

EWE: Esia ana madze agɔ le fia la dzi.” 11 Ke Daniel gblɔ na dzikpɔla si fiaŋumewo ƒe amegã la ɖo Daniel, Hananiya, Misael kple Azariya nu la be: 12 “Meɖe kuku, do wò subɔviwo kpɔ ŋkeke ewo, ne woana amagbewo mí míaɖu kple tsi mí míano; 13 emegbe nàtsɔ míaƒe dzedzeme asɔ kple ɖekakpui siwo ɖua fia ƒe nuɖuɖu viviwo la ƒe dzedzeme, eye nàwɔ na wò subɔviwo ɖe nu si nàkpɔ la nu.”
ENGLISH: 12 While the king was at his table my nard gave its scent. 13 My truelove is to me the package of myrrh lying between my breasts through the night.

EWE: 14 Eya ta elɔ̃ ɖe woƒe biabia la dzi, eye wòdo wo kpɔ ŋkeke ewo.
ENGLISH: 14 My truelove is to me a cluster of henna-flowers in the vineyards of ʽEn-Gedi.

EWE: 15 Le ŋkeke ewo megbe la, woƒe dzedzeme nyo wu, eye woƒe lãme wɔ nyuie wu ɖekakpui bubu siwo katã ɖua fia ƒe nuɖuɖu viviwo.
ENGLISH: 15 Ah, you are beautiful, sweetheart, ah, you are beautiful, your eyes are doves.

EWE: 16 Ale dzikpɔla la naa amagbe wo ɖe fia ƒe nuɖuɖu viviawo kple wain la teƒe.
ENGLISH: 16 Ah, you are beautiful, truelove, winsome too; our couch too is verdant.

EWE: 17 Ke Mawu vavã la na sidzedze kple gɔmesese deto ɖekakpui ene siawo le nuŋɔŋlɔ ƒomevi ɖe sia ɖe kple nunya gome; ke wona Daniel ya sea ŋutegawo kple drɔ̃ewo katã ƒomevi gɔme.
ENGLISH: 17 The beams of our house are cedars, our rafters are cypresses.

EWE: Daniel
ENGLISH: Song of Solomon

EWE: 2 Le Nebukadnezar ƒe fiaɖuɖu ƒe ƒe evelia me la, Nebukadnezar ku drɔ̃ewo, eye wòtsi dzodzodzoe, ale be alɔ̃ bu ɖee.
ENGLISH: 2 I am a narcissus on the plain, a lily in one of the vales.

EWE: 2 Eya ta fia la ɖe gbe be woayɔ akunyawɔlawo, afakalawo, dzotɔwo kple Kaldeatɔwo vɛ, ne woalĩ fia ƒe drɔ̃eawo nɛ.
ENGLISH: 2 Like a lily among the briers, such is my sweetheart among the daughters.

EWE: Eye wova tsi tsitre ɖe fia la ŋkume.
ENGLISH: 3 Like an apple-tree among the trees on the rocks, such is my truelove among the sons.

EWE: 3 Eye fia la gblɔ na wo be: “Meku drɔ̃e si na metsi dzodzodzoe elabena medi be mase drɔ̃e la gɔme.” 4 Eye Kaldeatɔwo gblɔ na fia la le Aramgbe me be: “Fia nenɔ agbe tegbee.
ENGLISH: I am eager to sit in his shade and his fruit is sweet to my palate.

EWE: Lĩ drɔ̃e la na wò subɔviwo, ekema míaɖe egɔme.”
ENGLISH: 4 He has brought me to the winehouse, and his banner over me is love.

EWE: 5 Fia la gblɔ na Kaldeatɔwo be: “Nu si meɖo tame kplikpaa be mawɔe nye esi: Ne mielĩ drɔ̃e la heɖe egɔme nam o la, ekema woafli mi kakɛkakɛe, eye miaƒe aƒewo azu nugododeƒewo.
ENGLISH: 5 Refresh me with raisins, recover me with apples, because I am breaking down with love.

EWE: 6 Ke ne mielĩ drɔ̃e la heɖe egɔme la, ekema miaxɔ nunanawo kple teƒeɖoɖo tso gbɔnye, eye made bubu geɖe mia ŋu.
ENGLISH: 6 His left arm clasps my head and his right embraces me.

EWE: Eya ta milĩ drɔ̃e la nam, eye miaɖe egɔme.” 7 Wogagblɔ zi evelia be: “Fia la nelĩ drɔ̃e la na eƒe subɔviwo, ekema míaɖe egɔme.”
ENGLISH: 7 I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles or the wild does, Not to wake love or rouse it up till it so please.

EWE: 8 Fia la gblɔ be: “Menyae nyuie be ɣeyiɣi ko dim miele, elabena mienya tame si meɖo kplikpaa.
ENGLISH: 8 My truelove’s step! here he comes Leaping along the mountains, bounding along the hills;

EWE: 9 Ne mielĩ drɔ̃e la nam o la, ekema tohehe ɖeka koe li na mi katã.
ENGLISH: 9 My truelove seems like a gazelle or a young deer.

EWE: Ðe mieɖoe be yewoagblɔ alakpanyawo kple ameflunyawo nam va se ɖe esime nuwo natrɔ. Eya ta milĩ drɔ̃e la nam, ekema manyae be miate ŋu aɖe egɔme.”
ENGLISH: Here he is standing outside the wall of our house, Gazing through the windows, glancing through the lattices.

EWE: 10 Kaldeatɔwo ɖo eŋu na fia la be: “Amegbetɔ aɖeke mele anyigba dzi, si ate ŋu awɔ nu si dim fia la le o, elabena fiagã alo nutodziɖula aɖeke mebia nu sia tɔgbi tso akunyawɔla alo afakala alo Kaldeatɔ aɖeke si kpɔ o.
ENGLISH: 10 My truelove speaks up and says to me “Up, sweetheart; come on, my beauty,

EWE: 11 Nu si biam fia le la sesẽ, eye ame aɖeke meli ate ŋu agblɔe na fia la o, negbe mawuwo ko, ame siwo nɔƒe mele amegbetɔwo dome o.”
ENGLISH: 11 For the winter is over, the rains are past and gone,

EWE: 12 Esia na dzi ku fia la, eye wòdo dɔmedzoe helĩhelĩ heɖe gbe be woawu Babilon nunyalawo katã.
ENGLISH: 12 The flowers on the ground are out, song-time has come in and the turtledove’s note is heard in our country;

EWE: 13 Esi wòde se be woayi aɖawu nunyalawo la, wodi Daniel kple eƒe zɔhɛwo hã be woawu.
ENGLISH: 13 The fig-tree has its fruit-buds out and the blooming grapevines are fragrant.

EWE: 14 Ɣemaɣi la, Daniel tsɔ aɖaŋudzedze kple nunya ƒo nu kple fiaŋudzɔlawo ƒe amegã Ariok, ame si tso be yeawu Babilon nunyalawo.
ENGLISH: Up, sweetheart; come on, my beauty. 14 My dove in the crannies of the cliff, in the covert of the rock-ledge, Let me see your form, let me hear your voice, Because your voice is sweet and your form is lovely.”

EWE: 15 Ebia amegã Ariok be: “Nu ka tae fia la de se sesẽ sia ɖo?”
ENGLISH: 15 “Catch foxes!

EWE: Eye Ariok gblɔ nya la na Daniel.
ENGLISH: Little foxes are damaging vineyards, and our vineyards are blooming!”

EWE: 16 Eya ta Daniel yi fia la gbɔ ɖabiae be wòana ɣeyiɣi ye, ne yeaɖe drɔ̃ea gɔme na fia la.
ENGLISH: 16 My truelove is mine and I am his, who pastures his flock among the lilies

EWE: 17 Emegbe Daniel yi aƒe me, eye wògblɔ nya la na eƒe zɔhɛ Hananiya, Misael kple Azariya.
ENGLISH: 17 Till the day grows breezy and the shadows take flight.

EWE: Eye egbɔe kekeli le. 23 Oo tɔgbuinyewo ƒe Mawu, meda akpe na wò hele kafuwòm,
ENGLISH: Truelove, come round and do like a gazelle Or a young deer on the mountains of Bether.

EWE: wòe nye sikata la.
ENGLISH: Song of Solomon

EWE: 3 Fia Nebukadnezar wɔ sikalegba si kɔ abɔklugui blaade, eye wòkeke abɔklugui ade.
ENGLISH: 3 On my bed of nights I looked for the one that my soul loves, looked for him and did not find him.

EWE: Eye wòlii ɖe Dura tagba le Babilon fiaɖuƒea ƒe nuto me. 2 Eye Fia Nebukadnezar dɔ amewo ɖa be woaƒo nuto gã dziɖulawo, nuto sue dziɖulawo, nutodziɖulawo, adaŋudelawo, kesinɔnuwo dzi kpɔlawo, ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo, nyadrɔ̃lawo kple nutoawo katã dzi kpɔlawo nu ƒu, ne woava kɔ legba si Fia Nebukadnezar li la ŋu.
ENGLISH: 2 Let me stand up and go round in the city in the streets and the squares Looking for the one that my soul loves; I looked for him and did not find him.

EWE: 3 Ale nuto gã dziɖulawo, nuto sue dziɖulawo, nutodziɖulawo, adaŋudelawo, kesinɔnuwo dzi kpɔlawo, ʋɔnudrɔ̃lawo, nyadrɔ̃lawo kple nutoawo dzi kpɔlawo katã va ƒo ƒu, be woakɔ legba si Fia Nebukadnezar li la ŋu.
ENGLISH: 3 The watchmen that go round in the city found me: “Have you seen the one that my soul loves?”

EWE: Eye wotsi tsitre ɖe legba si Nebukadnezar li la ŋgɔ.
ENGLISH: 4 I had got a little past them when I found the one that my soul loves.

EWE: 4 Eye gbeƒãɖela la do ɣli sesĩe be: “Oo amehawo, dukɔwo kple gbegbɔgblɔ ɖe sia ɖe dolawo, wole se dem na mi be, 5 ne miese lãdzo, dze, gakasaŋku, saŋku, kasaŋku, dze nuevee kple haƒonu vovovoawo ƒe ɖiɖi la, ekema miabɔbɔ ade ta agu na sikalegba si Fia Nebukadnezar li la.
ENGLISH: I caught hold of him, did not let go of him Till I brought him to my mother’s house, to my parent’s chamber. 5 I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles or the wild does, Not to wake love or rouse it up till it so please.

EWE: 6 Ame si mabɔbɔ ade ta agu o la, woatsɔe aƒu gbe ɖe kpodzo si le bibim flaflafla la me enumake.” 7 Eya ta esi dukɔwo katã se lãdzo, dze, gakasaŋku, saŋku, kasaŋku kple haƒonu vovovoawo ƒe ɖiɖi ko la, amehawo, dukɔwo kple gbegbɔgblɔ ɖe sia ɖe dolawo katã bɔbɔ de ta agu na sikalegba si Fia Nebukadnezar li la.
ENGLISH: 6 Who is this coming up out of the wilderness like columns of smoke, Perfumed with burnings of myrrh and frankincense,with every powder money can buy? 7 Here comes Solomon’s bed, Sixty champions round it, champions of Israel,

EWE: 8 Ɣemaɣi la, Kaldeatɔ aɖewo va tso Yudatɔwo nu.
ENGLISH: 8 All of them sword-wielders, men trained to war, Each with sword on thigh against night alarms.

EWE: 9 Eye wogblɔ na Fia Nebukadnezar be: “Fia nenɔ agbe tegbee.
ENGLISH: 9 King Solomon has made himself a palanquin of wood from the Lebanon,

EWE: 12 Ke Yudatɔ aɖewo li, siwo nètsɔ ɖo Babilon dziɖuɖudɔwo nu, siwo nye Sadrak, Mesak kple Abednego.
ENGLISH: 10 Made its legs of silver,its back of gold, Its seat of purple, its body inlaid with ebony.

EWE: Oo fia, ŋutsu siawo medea bubu aɖeke ŋuwò o. Womesubɔa wò mawuwo o, eye wogbe tadede agu na sikalegba si nèli la.”
ENGLISH: 11 Daughters of Jerusalem, go out and gaze at King Solomon In the wreath his mother put on him on his wedding-day, the day of his heart’s gladness.

EWE: Eya ta wokplɔ ŋutsu siawo va fia la ŋkume.
ENGLISH: Song of Solomon 4:1-16

EWE: Ke ne miegbe tadede agu nɛ la, ekema woatsɔ mi aƒu gbe ɖe kpodzo bibi la me enumake.
ENGLISH: 4 Ah, you are beautiful, sweetheart, ah, you are beautiful.

EWE: Eye mawu kae ate ŋu aɖe mi tso asinye me?”
ENGLISH: Your eyes are doves behind your veil.

EWE: Woɖo eŋu na fia la be: “Ɛ̃, fia.” 25 Egblɔ be: “Kpɔ ɖa!
ENGLISH: Your hair is like a flock of goats that overflow a Gilead mountain.

EWE: 28 Eye Nebukadnezar gblɔ be: “Woakafu Sadrak, Mesak kple Abednego ƒe Mawu, ame si dɔ eƒe dɔla ɖa wòva ɖe eƒe subɔlawo.
ENGLISH: 2 Your teeth are like the flock for clipping as they come up from the washing, Flock where they all have twins and not one has lost a lamb.

EWE: 3 Eƒe dzesiwo lolo, eye eƒe nukunuwo tri akɔ loo!
ENGLISH: 3 Your lips are like scarlet thread and your mouth is lovely.

EWE: Eƒe fiaɖuƒe nye fiaɖuƒe mavɔ, eye eƒe dziɖuɖu li tso dzidzime yi dzidzime.
ENGLISH: Your temple is like a segment of pomegranate behind your veil.

EWE: 4 “Nye, Nebukadnezar, menɔ aƒenye me bɔkɔɔ, eye nuwo dze edzi nam le nye fiasã me.
ENGLISH: 4 Your neck is like David’s tower built for an armory, With the thousand shields hung on it, all the bucklers of the champions.

EWE: 5 Meku drɔ̃e, si na vɔvɔ̃ ɖom. Nu siwo mekpɔ le susu me esime mele nye aba dzi kple ŋutega siwo mekpɔ la do voɖi nam.
ENGLISH: 5 Your two breasts are like two fawns, a gazelle’s twins That pasture among the lilies

EWE: 6 Eya ta meɖe gbe be woakplɔ Babilon nunyalawo katã ava ŋkunyeme, ne woaɖe drɔ̃e la gɔme nam.
ENGLISH: 6 till the day grows breezy and the shadows take flight. I wend my way to the mountain of myrrh and to the hill of frankincense.

EWE: 7 “Ɣemaɣi la, akunyawɔlawo, afakalawo, Kaldeatɔwo kple ɣletivimefakalawo va.
ENGLISH: 7 You are beautiful all of you, sweetheart, and there is nothing wrong about you.

EWE: Esi melĩ drɔ̃e la na wo la, womete ŋu ɖe egɔme nam o. 8 Mlɔeba Daniel, ame si wotsɔ nye mawu ƒe ŋkɔ Beltesazar na, eye mawu kɔkɔewo ƒe gbɔgbɔ le eme la, va ŋkunyeme; eye melĩ drɔ̃e la nɛ be:
ENGLISH: 8 With me from Lebanon, bride, with me from Lebanon you shall come, You shall look off from the top of Amana, from the tops of Shenir and Hermon, From lions’ haunts, from leopards’ mountains.

EWE: 9 “‘Oo Beltesazar, akunyawɔlawo ƒe tatɔ, menyae be mawu kɔkɔewo ƒe gbɔgbɔ le mewò, eye nya ɣaɣla aɖeke meli si sẽ na wò akpa o.
ENGLISH: 9 You have driven me out of my senses, my sister, bride; you have driven me out of my senses with one of your eyes, with one bead of your necklace.

EWE: 10 “‘Ŋutega siwo mekpɔ esi mele nye aba dzi lae nye esi: Meɖo ŋku anyi, eye kpɔ ɖa, mekpɔ ati aɖe le anyigba titina, si kɔ ŋutɔ.
ENGLISH: 10 How pretty is your love, my sister, bride! how much better than wine is your love, and the scent of your oils than all spices!

EWE: 11 Ati la tsi, eye wòsesẽ, ekɔ yi ɖatɔ dziƒowo, eye wòle dzedzem le anyigba bliboa ƒe afi sia afi.
ENGLISH: 11 Your lips drip purest honey, bride; you have honey and milk under your tongue, and the scent of your clothes is like that of Lebanon.

EWE: 12 Eƒe aŋgbawo nya kpɔ, eƒe tsetse sɔ gbɔ, eye nuɖuɖu le edzi na nu gbagbewo katã.
ENGLISH: 12 A locked garden is my sister, bride, a locked garden, a sealed water-spring.

EWE: 13 “‘Meɖo ŋku anyi le ŋutega siwo mekpɔ esime mele nye aba dzi la me, eye mekpɔ dzɔla kɔkɔe aɖe ɖi tso dziƒo.
ENGLISH: 13 Your sprays are an orchard of pomegranates and priceless fruits, plants of henna and nard,

EWE: 14 Edo ɣli sesĩe gblɔ be: “Milã ati la ƒu anyi, eye milã eƒe alɔwo. Midudu eƒe aŋgbawo, eye mika eƒe tsetseawo hlẽ!
ENGLISH: 14 Nard and saffron, sweet flag and cinnamon, with all frankincense-bearing trees, Myrrh and eaglewood with all rarest spices.

EWE: 15 Ke migblẽ eƒe takpoea ɖe to me, eye mitsɔ gayibɔ kple akɔbli blae ɖe gbe me.
ENGLISH: 15 The spring in my garden is a well of living water and a flow from Lebanon.

EWE: 16 Woatrɔ eƒe dzi, be wòaganye amegbetɔ ƒe dzi azɔ o, eye wòazu abe lã ƒe dzi ene, va se ɖe esime ɣeyiɣi adre nava yi nɛ.
ENGLISH: 16 Wake, north wind, and come, south, blow through my garden, let its spices flow.

EWE: 29 Le dzinu wuieve megbe la, enɔ tsa ɖim le Babilon fiasã la tame.
ENGLISH: Let my truelove come into his garden and eat its priceless fruits.

EWE: Ànɔ gbemelãwo gbɔ.
ENGLISH: Song of Solomon

EWE: 5 Fia Belsazar ɖo kplɔ̃ gã aɖe na eƒe amegãwo dometɔ akpe ɖeka, eye wòno wain le wo ŋkume.
ENGLISH: 5 I come into my garden, my sister, bride, gather my myrrh with my balsam, Eat my honeycomb with my honey, drink my wine with my milk.

EWE: 2 Esi wain ɖo mo na Belsazar la, egblɔ be woatsɔ sikanu kple klosalonu siwo fofoa Nebukadnezar lɔ tso gbedoxɔ si nɔ Yerusalem me la vɛ, ne fia la kple eƒe amegãwo, srɔ̃awo kple eƒe ahiãwo nano nu le wo me.
ENGLISH: Eat, friend, drink and carouse, truelove! 2 I was asleep but my heart was awake: the sound of my truelove knocking!

EWE: 3 Ale woyi ɖatsɔ sikanu siwo wolɔ tso gbedoxɔ, si nye Mawu ƒe aƒe, si nɔ Yerusalem me la vɛ, eye fia la kple eƒe amegãwo, srɔ̃awo kple eƒe ahiãwo no nu le wo me.
ENGLISH: “Open to me, my sister, my sweetheart, my dove, my ideal, Because my head has got full of dew, my locks of night drops.” 3 “I have taken off my tunic; how can I put it on?

EWE: 4 Wono wain, eye wokafu mawu siwo nye sika kple klosalo, akɔbli, gayibɔ, ati kple kpe.
ENGLISH: 4 My truelove put his hand through the hole and my bosom was in a turmoil over him.

EWE: 5 Kasia wokpɔ amegbetɔ ƒe asibidɛ wòle nu ŋlɔm ɖe fiasã la ƒe gli si wosi akalo na la ŋu le akaɖitia ŋgɔdze, eye fia la kpɔ asi si le nua ŋlɔm la.
ENGLISH: 5 I stood up to open for my truelove, and my hands were dripping with myrrh And my fingers with myrrh that went over to the handles of the bolt.

EWE: 6 Ale fia la ƒe mo fu kpii, eye eƒe tamesusuwo do ŋɔdzi nɛ, eƒe ali le ƒoƒom, eye eƒe klowo le wo nɔewo ƒom kpakpakpa.
ENGLISH: 6 I did open for my truelove, but my truelove had turned round and gone. The life had gone out of me at his speaking; I looked for him and did not find him, called him and he did not answer me.

EWE: 7 Eye fia la do ɣli sesĩe be woakplɔ afakalawo, Kaldeatɔwo kple ɣletivimefakalawo vɛ.
ENGLISH: 7 The guards that go round in the city found me, beat me, wounded me; The guards of the walls took my mantle off me.

EWE: 8 Eye fia la ƒe nunyalawo katã va, ke womete ŋu xlẽ nuŋɔŋlɔa ne woahayi egɔme ɖe ge na fia la o.
ENGLISH: 8 I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, if you find my truelove, To what you are to tell him: that I am breaking down with love.

EWE: 9 Ale vɔvɔ̃ ɖo Fia Belsazar ŋutɔ, eye eƒe mo fu kpii; eƒe amegãwo hã tɔtɔ.
ENGLISH: 9 “What sort of truelove is yours, most beautiful among women?

EWE: 10 Ke esi fianyɔnu la se fia kple eƒe amegãwo ƒe nyawo la, eyi kplɔ̃ɖoƒe la enumake. Eye fianyɔnu la gblɔ be: “Fia nenɔ agbe tegbee.
ENGLISH: What sort of truelove is yours, that you adjure us like that?” 10 My truelove is white and red, outstanding among ten thousand.

EWE: 11 Oo fia, ŋutsu aɖe le wò fiaɖuƒe la me, si me mawu kɔkɔewo ƒe gbɔgbɔ le.
ENGLISH: 11 His head is nuggets of red gold; his locks are waving, black as a raven.

EWE: 12 Elabena Daniel, ame si fia la tsɔ ŋkɔ na be Beltesazar, ƒe susu ɖa ale gbegbe, sidzedze kple gɔmesese le esi, eɖea drɔ̃ewo kple adzowo gɔme, eye wòɖea nya sesẽwo gɔme.
ENGLISH: 12 His eyes are like doves by dingles of water, bathed in milk and laid in settings.

EWE: Eya ta na woayɔ Daniel vɛ, eye aɖe egɔme.” 13 Ale wokplɔ Daniel va fia la ŋkume.
ENGLISH: 13 His cheeks are like beds of sweet herbs growing perfumers’ stock; His lips are lilies that drip flowing myrrh.

EWE: Eye fia la bia Daniel be: “Wòe nye Daniel, aboyome siwo fofonye, fia la, kplɔ tso Yuda vɛ la dometɔ ɖeka? 14 Mese le ŋuwò be, mawuwo ƒe gbɔgbɔ le mewò, eye wokpɔe be sidzedze, gɔmesese kple nunya deto le asiwò.
ENGLISH: 14 His arms are cylinders of gold set with jasper; His waist is a block of ivory overspread with sapphires.

EWE: 15 Wokplɔ nunyalawo kple afakalawo va ŋkunyeme be woaxlẽ nuŋɔŋlɔ sia, ne woaɖe egɔme nam, gake womete ŋui o.
ENGLISH: 15 His legs are pillars of marble resting on bases of red gold. The look of him is like the Lebanon, admirable as the cedars.

EWE: 16 Ke mese le ŋuwò be ètea ŋu ɖea nya ɣaɣlawo gɔme, eye nèɖea nya sesẽwo hã gɔme.
ENGLISH: 16 His talk is luscious and everything about him fascinating.

EWE: Gake maxlẽ nuŋɔŋlɔ la na fia la, eye maɖe egɔme nɛ.
ENGLISH: This is my truelove and this is my friend, daughters of Jerusalem.

EWE: Daniel
ENGLISH: Song of Solomon

EWE: 6 Dario kpɔ be enyo be yeaɖo nuto gã dziɖula alafa ɖeka blaeve be woanɔ fiaɖuƒe blibo la nu.
ENGLISH: 6 “Which way did your truelove go, most beautiful among women?

EWE: 2 Eye wòɖo amegã etɔ̃ wo nu, ame siwo dome Daniel le, ale be nuto gã dziɖula siawo natsɔ nyatakaka anɔ yiyim na wo, ne fia la nagabu naneke o.
ENGLISH: Which way did your truelove turn? and we will look for him with you.” 2 My truelove went down to his garden, to the beds of sweet herbs, To crop the gardens and pick lilies.

EWE: 3 Eye Daniel va ƒo amegãwo kple nuto gã dziɖulawo ta le nu sia nu me, elabena eƒe susu ɖa ŋutɔ, eye fia la ɖoe be yeatsɔe aɖo fiaɖuƒe blibo la nu.
ENGLISH: 3 I am my truelove’s and my truelove is mine, who pastures his flock among lilies.

EWE: 4 Ɣemaɣi la, amegãwo kple nuto gã dziɖulawo le mɔnu dim le Daniel ŋu atraɖii, ne woakpɔ nya aɖe le eŋu le dɔ siwo wòwɔna le fiaɖuƒea me la me, ke womete ŋu kpɔ nya alo nu tovo wɔwɔ aɖeke le eŋu o, elabena enye ame si dzi woate ŋu aka ɖo, eléa fɔ ɖe dɔ ŋu, eye mewɔa nu fitifiti aɖeke o.
ENGLISH: 4 You are beautiful, sweetheart, as Tirsah, lovely as Jerusalem, terrible as the aurora.

EWE: 5 Eya ta ŋutsu siawo gblɔ be: “Míele nya aɖeke kpɔ ge le Daniel sia ŋu o, negbe le nu siwo ku ɖe eƒe Mawu ƒe se la ŋu me ko.”
ENGLISH: 5 Turn your eyes off me, for they overpower me. Your hair is like a flock of goats that overflow Gilead.

EWE: 6 Ale amegã siawo kple nuto gã dziɖulawo lɔ hoo va fia la gbɔ gblɔ nɛ be: “Fia Dario nenɔ agbe tegbee.
ENGLISH: 6 Your teeth are like a flock of ewes as they come up from the washing, Flock where they all have twins and not one has lost a lamb.

EWE: 7 Oo fia, fiaɖuƒe la ƒe amegãwo katã, nuto sue dziɖulawo kple nuto gã dziɖulawo, adaŋudelawo kple nutodziɖulawo, de adaŋu be woade se le fia ƒe ŋkɔ me, eye wòaɖo kpe edzi be, ame sia ame si abia nu mawu alo amegbetɔ aɖe le ŋkeke blaetɔ̃ me, ne menye wò ko o la, woatsɔe aƒu gbe ɖe dzatawo ƒe do me.
ENGLISH: 7 Your temple is like a segment of pomegranate behind your veil.

EWE: 8 Eya ta fia, de se sia eye nàde asi ete, ne tɔtrɔ naganɔ eŋu o ɖe Mediatɔwo kple Persiatɔwo ƒe se, si me wometea fli ɖo o la nu.”
ENGLISH: 8 Sixty are queens and eighty concubines, and maids innumerable;

EWE: 9 Ale Fia Dario de asi nuŋɔŋlɔ la kple se la te.
ENGLISH: 9 One is my dove, my ideal,her mother’s one is she,her parent’s pure one she.Girls saw her and felicitated her,queens and concubines, and praised her.

EWE: 10 Ke esi Daniel nya se be wode asi nuŋɔŋlɔa te ko la, eyi aƒe me, eye wòge ɖe eƒe xɔtaxɔ si ƒe fesrewo trɔ ɖo ɖe Yerusalem gome la me.
ENGLISH: 10 Who is this that looks out like dawn, beautiful as the moon, clear as the sun,terrible as the aurora?

EWE: Eye wòdzea klo doa gbe ɖa hekafua eƒe Mawu zi etɔ̃ gbe ɖeka le eŋkume, abe ale si ko wòwɔnɛ ɖaa ene. 11 Ɣemaɣi ŋutsu siawo ge ɖe edzi zi ɖeka ʋla hekpɔ Daniel wòle koko ƒom hele amenuveve biam le eƒe Mawu ŋkume.
ENGLISH: 11 I went down to the nut-garden to look over the things starting in the arroyo, To see if the grapevines had broken out their buds,if the pomegranates had blossomed.

EWE: 12 Eya ta wova fia la gbɔ heɖo ŋku fia ƒe sededea dzi nɛ be: “Oo fia, menye ɖe nède asi sea te be, ame sia ame si abia nu mawu alo amegbetɔ aɖe le ŋkeke blaetɔ̃ me, ne menye wò ko o la, woatsɔe aƒu gbe ɖe dzatawo ƒe do me oa?”
ENGLISH: 12 I did not know;my soul had made me ʽAmmi-Nadib’s chariots.

EWE: 15 Mlɔeba ŋutsu siawo lɔ hoo va fia la gbɔ gblɔ nɛ be: “Oo fia, nyae be, Mediatɔwo kple Persiatɔwo ƒe se wònye be, se alo ɖoɖo ɖe sia ɖe si dzi fia la ɖo kpee la, womatrɔe o.”
ENGLISH: 13 7:1 Come back, come back, Shulammite;come back, come back, and let us have a look at you.What sight of the Shulammite would you have?

EWE: 18 Emegbe fia la dzo yi eƒe fiasã me.
ENGLISH: In the camp dance!

EWE: Daniel
ENGLISH: Song of Solomon

EWE: 7 Le Babilon-fia Belsazar ƒe ƒe gbãtɔ me la, Daniel ku drɔ̃e, eye wòkpɔ ŋutegawo le eƒe aba dzi.
ENGLISH: 7 7:2 How beautifully your feet tap with the shoes, daughter of a nobleman!

EWE: Eye wòŋlɔ drɔ̃e la ɖi; eŋlɔ nyawo katã ɖi tsitotsito.
ENGLISH: The swing of your hips is like bangles made by an artist’s hands.

EWE: 2 Daniel gblɔ be: “Mekpɔ le nye ŋutegawo me le zã me, eye kpɔ ɖa, dziƒo ƒe ya eneawo le atsiaƒu gã la nyamam.
ENGLISH: 2 7:3 Your navel is like a stirring-bowl may there be no lack of wine-mixture!Your waist is like a heap of wheat set round with lilies.

EWE: 3 Lã gã ene do tso atsiaƒu la me, eye woto vovo tso wo nɔewo gbɔ.
ENGLISH: 3 7:4 Your two breasts are like two fawns, a gazelle’s twins.

EWE: 4 “Gbãtɔ le abe dzata ene, eye wòto hɔ̃ ƒe aʋala.
ENGLISH: 4 7:5 Your neck is like the Ivory Tower.

EWE: Mele ekpɔm, va se ɖe esime wotu eƒe aʋalawo le eŋu, wokɔe dzi tso anyigba, eye wona wòtɔ ɖe afɔ eve dzi abe amegbetɔ ene, eye wotsɔ amegbetɔ ƒe dzi nɛ.
ENGLISH: Your eyes are like the reservoirs at Heshbon at the Bath-Rabbim gate. Your nose is like the Lebanon tower looking out on the Damascus side.

EWE: 5 “Eye kpɔ ɖa, lã evelia si le abe sisiblisi ene la do. Wokɔe dzi ɖe akpa ɖeka, eye wòtsɔ aɖu lé agbaƒuti etɔ̃ ɖe nu; eye wogblɔ nɛ be: ‘Tso nàɖu lã geɖe.’
ENGLISH: 5 7:6 Your head stands on you like Carmel, and the strands of your head are like purple; a king is fettered in the threads.

EWE: 6 “Eyome meɖo ŋku anyi, eye kpɔ ɖa, lã bubu aɖe si le abe lãklẽ ene, gake wòto aʋala ene ɖe dzime abe xevi ene la do.
ENGLISH: 6 7:7 How beautiful you are, how winsome, love, daughter of delight!

EWE: 7 “Emegbe meɖo ŋku anyi le ŋutega me le zã me, eye kpɔ ɖa, lã enelia do; eɖi vɔvɔ̃, ŋɔdzi le eŋu, eye wòsesẽ ŋutɔ, eto gaɖu kakowo.
ENGLISH: 7 7:8 This figure of yours is the likeness of a palm tree; and your breasts, of clusters.

EWE: Eto vovo tso lã bubu siwo do ŋgɔ nɛ la gbɔ, eye wòto dzo ewo. 8 Meɖe ŋku ɖe dzoawo, eye kpɔ ɖa, dzo bubu si nye dzo sue aɖe, to ɖe wo domee, eye woho dzo gbãtɔawo dometɔ etɔ̃ le eŋgɔ.
ENGLISH: 8 7:9 I think I will climb the palm tree, take hold of its bunches of fruit, And let your breasts be like clusters of the grapevine and the scent of your breath like that of apples,

EWE: 9 “Meɖe ŋku ɖee va se ɖe esime wotsɔ fiazikpuiwo va li anyi, eye Ame Si Li Tso Gbe Aɖe Gbe Ʋĩi Ke la bɔbɔ nɔ anyi.
ENGLISH: 9 7:10 And your mouth like the best wine, running smoothly for my throat, gliding through my lips and teeth.

EWE: 10 Dzotɔsisi aɖe le sisim le eŋgɔ.
ENGLISH: 10 7:11 I am my truelove’s and his impulse is toward me.

EWE: Woɖi ʋɔnu, eye woke agbalẽwo. 11 “Ɣemaɣi la, meɖo ŋku anyi le nu kpɔm le dadanya siwo gblɔm dzo la le ta; meɖe ŋku ɖee va se ɖe esime wowu lã la, eye wotsɔ eƒe ŋutilã la na be woatɔ dzoe.
ENGLISH: 11 7:12 Come on, truelove, we will go out on the range, pass the night in the villages,

EWE: 12 Ke woxɔ dziɖuŋusẽ le lã susɔeawo si, eye wona ɣeyiɣi kple azãgbe si woayi edzi anɔ agbe ase ɖo la wo.
ENGLISH: 12 7:13 Be in the vineyards the first thing in the morning seeing if the grapevines have broken out their buds, Have come into bloom, if the pomegranates have blossomed.

EWE: 13 “Meɖo ŋku anyi le ŋutega me le zã me, eye kpɔ ɖa, ame aɖe gbɔna kple dziƒolilikpowo abe amegbetɔvi ene; eye wona wòva Ame si li tso gbe aɖe gbe ʋĩi ke la gbɔ, eye wokplɔe va eŋkume.
ENGLISH: There I will give you my love. 13 7:14 The mandrake-apples are giving their scent, and at our doors are all sorts of fine fruits; New and last year’s too, truelove, I have laid up for you.

EWE: Daniel
ENGLISH: Song of Solomon

EWE: 8 Le Fia Belsazar ƒe fiaɖuɖu ƒe ƒe etɔ̃lia me la, nye Daniel, mekpɔ ŋutega aɖe le esi mekpɔ va yi la megbe.
ENGLISH: 8 If only you were the same as a brother of mine, one that had sucked my mother’s breasts!

EWE: 2 Mekpɔ ŋutega la, eye esime mele ekpɔm la, mele Susan mɔ́ si le Elam nuto me la me; eye mekpɔ le ŋutega la me be mele Ulai-tɔsisi la to.
ENGLISH: Finding you in the street, I would kiss you; they would not despise me either. 2 I would lead you, would bring you to my mother’s house, to the chamber of her who gave me birth.

EWE: 3 Esi mefɔ mo dzi la, kpɔ ɖa, agbo aɖe tɔ ɖe tɔsisi la to, eye wòto dzo eve. Dzo eveawo didi, ke ɖeka didi wu evelia, eye legbeetɔ lae nye mamlɛtɔ si to.
ENGLISH: I would give you a drink of perfumed wine, of my pomegranate-wine. 3 His left arm clasps my head and his right embraces me.

EWE: 4 Mekpɔ agbo la wòle eƒe dzowo dam ɖo ta ɣetoɖoƒe kple dziehe kpakple anyiehe gome, eye lã aɖeke mete ŋu nɔ te ɖe enu o, eye ame aɖeke metea ŋu xɔa ame le esi me o.
ENGLISH: 4 I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, why should you wake love or rouse it up till it so please?

EWE: 5 Ke esi mele eŋu bum la, kpɔ ɖa, gbɔ̃tsu aɖe tso ɣetoɖoƒe va anyigba blibo la katã dzi, eye eƒe afɔ mele anyigba kam o.
ENGLISH: 5 Who is this coming up from the wilderness leaning on her truelove?

EWE: Eye dzo titri aɖe le gbɔ̃tsu la ƒe ŋugbladome.
ENGLISH: Under the apple-tree I waked you up; it was there your mother bore the birth-pains for you, there she bore the birth-pains, brought you to birth.

EWE: 6 Eɖo ta agbo dzoevee, si mekpɔ wòle tsitre ɖe tɔsisia to la gbɔ; eye wòlũ ɖe edzi kple ŋusẽ le dziku me.
ENGLISH: 6 Lay me like a seal over your heart, like a seal on your arm; For love is violent as death, jealousy hard as the grave; Its flashes are flashes of fire, Jehovah’s flame-throwing.

EWE: 7 Mekpɔe wònɔ tetem ɖe agbo la ŋu, eye dzi kui ɖe eŋu. Etu dzo agbo la ƒu anyi heŋe eƒe dzo eveawo, eye ŋusẽ aɖeke mele agbo la ŋu be wòanɔ te ɖe enu o.
ENGLISH: 7 Much water cannot quench love, and rivers will not sweep it away; If a man were to give all the goods in his house for love they would just despise him.

EWE: 8 Ke gbɔ̃tsu la do eɖokui ɖe dzi ale gbegbe, eye esi ŋusẽ ɖo eŋu la, eƒe dzo gã la ŋe; eye dzo ene to ɖe eteƒe trɔ ɖe dziƒo ƒe ya eneawo dzi.
ENGLISH: 8 “We have a little sister and she has no breasts; what shall we do for our sister on the day when she is to be spoken for?

EWE: 9 Eye dzo sue bubu aɖe to tso wo dometɔ ɖeka me, eye wòlolo ŋutɔ hetrɔ ɖe anyiehe kple ɣedzeƒe gome kpakple Atsyɔ̃nyigba la gbɔ.
ENGLISH: 9 If she is a wall we will build silver battlements on her, but if she is a door we will board her up with cedar planks.”

EWE: 10 Eto helolo va ɖo keke dziƒoʋakɔ la gbɔ, ale be wòna aʋakɔ la me tɔ aɖewo kple ɣletivi aɖewo ge dze anyigba, eye wòtu afɔ wo dzi.
ENGLISH: 10 I am a wall and my breasts are like the towers; then I was in his eyes like one who finds peace.

EWE: 11 Edo eɖokui ɖe dzi ɖe aʋakɔwo ƒe Amegã la gɔ̃ hã ŋu, exɔ gbe sia gbe vɔsa la le esi, eye wogbã eƒe kɔkɔeƒe si wòɖo anyi la.
ENGLISH: 11 Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-Hamon; he gave the vineyard to keepers, each to bring in a thousand shekels of silver.

EWE: 12 Wotsɔ aʋakɔ aɖe de esi hekpe ɖe gbe sia gbe vɔsa la ŋu le dzidada ta; eléa nyateƒe ƒua anyi, eye wòwɔ nu wòdze edzi nɛ.
ENGLISH: 12 I have my own vineyard before me; the thousand for you, Solomon, and two hundred for those who keep its fruit safe!

EWE: 24 Akpɔ ŋusẽ gã, ke menye to eya ŋutɔ ƒe ŋusẽ me o. Agblẽ nu eteƒe makɔ o, eye wòakpɔ dzidzedze le eƒe nuwɔwɔwo me.
ENGLISH: 13 You that are sitting in the garden, comrades are listening for your voice; let me hear it.

EWE: Atso ɖe amegãwo ƒe Amegã la gɔ̃ hã ŋu, ke woagbãe ame ƒe asi manɔmee.
ENGLISH: 14 Off with you, truelove, and do like a gazelle Or a young deer on the spice mountains.

EWE: Daniel
ENGLISH: Lamentations

EWE: 9 Le Dario, si nye Ahasweros Mediatɔ la ƒe vi, ame si wotsɔ ɖo fiae ɖe Kaldeatɔwo ƒe fiaɖuƒe la nu ƒe ƒe gbãtɔ me
ENGLISH: 1 How lonely she sits, the city great in people! she has become like a widow, the great among the nations.

EWE: 2 le eƒe fiaɖuɖu ƒe ƒe gbãtɔ me la, nye Daniel, melé ŋku ɖe agbalẽawo me hekpɔe dze sii le Yehowa ƒe gbe si va na nyagblɔɖila Yeremiya nu be, Yerusalem ƒe aƒedozuzu la anɔ anyi ƒe blaadre.
ENGLISH: Princess among the provinces, she has come to serfdom. 2 She is weeping in the night, has tears on her cheeks; there is not a comforter for her out of all her lovers, all her friends have played her false, become enemies to her.

EWE: 3 Eya ta metrɔ mo ɖe Mawu vavã Yehowa ŋu, ne matsɔ gbedodoɖa, kokoƒoƒowo kple nutsitsidɔ adii, eye meta akpanya hebɔbɔ nɔ dzofi me.
ENGLISH: 3 Judah has gone to an expatriate life because of destitution and overwork; she has settled among the nations but not found a resting-place; everybody who was hunting her down has come upon her in a tight place.

EWE: 4 Medo gbe ɖa na Yehowa nye Mawu heʋu eme be:
ENGLISH: 4 The roads to Sion are mourning not to have people coming in to the holy dates; all her gates are desolate, her priests are moaning, her maidens are sorrowing, and she is in bitter grief.

EWE: “Oo Yehowa, Mawu vavã kple Mawu gã si ŋu ŋɔdzi le, ame si wɔa eƒe nubabla dzi eye wòvea ame siwo lɔ̃nɛ kple ame siwo léa eƒe sededewo me ɖe asi la nu, 5 míewɔ nu vɔ̃, míeda vo, míewɔ nu tovo, eye míedze aglã; míetra ɖa le wò sededewo kple wò ʋɔnudɔdrɔ̃wo ŋu.
ENGLISH: 5 Her foes are in control, her enemies are untroubled, because Jehovah has reduced her to misery for her multitude of crimes. The children in her have gone into foreign slavery before the foe.

EWE: 6 Míegbe toɖoɖo wò subɔla nyagblɔɖilawo, ame siwo ƒo nu kple míaƒe fiawo, míaƒe amegãwo, mía tɔgbuiwo kple dukɔ la me tɔwo katã le wò ŋkɔ me.
ENGLISH: 6 And all the stateliness of the daughter of Sion has gone out of her, her generals have become like deer that find no pasture and have gone along strengthless before a pursuer.

EWE: 7 Oo Yehowa, tɔwò dzɔ, ke míawo, Yuda ŋutsuwo kple Yerusalem nɔlawo kpakple ame siwo katã le Israel, ame siwo le kpuiƒe kple didiƒe le anyigba siwo katã dzi nèka wo hlẽ ɖo le woƒe nuteƒemawɔmawɔ na wò ta la, mía tɔe nye ŋukpe, abe ale si wòle egbe sia ene.
ENGLISH: 7 Jerusalem remembers her days of misery and homelessness when her people were falling by a foeman’s hand and she had no helper; foemen saw her, laughed over her extinction.

EWE: 8 “Oo Yehowa, mía kple míaƒe fiawo, míaƒe amegãwo kple mía tɔgbuiwo tɔe nye ŋukpe, elabena míewɔ nu vɔ̃ ɖe ŋuwò.
ENGLISH: 8 Jerusalem did sin, so she has become a piece of garbage; all who had been honoring her hold her cheap because they have seen her nakedness; she too moans and retreats backward.

EWE: 9 Ke Yehowa, mía Mawu, èkpɔa nublanui helɔ̃a tsɔtsɔke, ke míawo míedze aglã ɖe ŋuwò.
ENGLISH: 9 She has her defilement on her skirts; she did not bethink herself of her future. She has come down extraordinarily; there is nobody to comfort her.

EWE: 10 Míeɖo to Yehowa mía Mawu ƒe gbe hezɔ le eƒe se siwo wòde na mí to esubɔla nyagblɔɖilawo dzi la nu o.
ENGLISH: 10 A foe has spread his hand over all she held dear; for she has seen heathens come into her sanctuary, of whom you commanded “you shall not have them come into the assembly.”

EWE: 11 Israel blibo la da wò Se la dzi, eye wote ɖe aga hegbe wò gbe sese, ale be nètrɔ fiƒode kple atam siwo woŋlɔ ɖe Mawu vavã ƒe subɔla Mose ƒe Se la me kɔ ɖe mía dzi, elabena míewɔ nu vɔ̃ ɖe Mawu ŋu.
ENGLISH: 11 All her people are moaning, hunting for bread, have given what they held dearest for food to bring back life. See, Jehovah, and look, because I stand cheap.

EWE: 12 Ewɔ eƒe nya si wògblɔ ɖe mía kple míaƒe dziɖulawo ŋu la dzi, esi wòhe vɔ̃ gã aɖe va mía dzi; womewɔ nu si wowɔ le Yerusalem la tɔgbi le dziƒo bliboa te kpɔ o.
ENGLISH: 12 Not toward you, all passersby! look and see if there is a hurt like mine that has been inflicted on me, the sorrow Jehovah gave me in his day of anger.

EWE: 13 Vɔ̃ siawo katã dzɔ ɖe mía dzi, abe ale si woŋlɔe ɖe Mose ƒe Se la me ene, ke míeɖe kuku na Yehowa mía Mawu be wòakpɔ nublanui na mí ahaɖe asi le míaƒe vodadawo ŋu o, eye míese wò nyateƒe la gɔme o.
ENGLISH: 13 From aloft he sent fire down into my bones, he spread his net for my feet, drove me backward, struck me desolate, sick all day.

EWE: 14 “Eya ta Yehowa ƒe ŋku le te, eye wòhe vɔ̃ va mía dzi, elabena nu siwo katã Yehowa mía Mawu wɔ la le dzɔdzɔe; ke míawo míeɖo to eƒe gbe o.
ENGLISH: 14 He paid attention to my offenses; they interwove in his hands, they came up over my neck, he brought my strength to a fall.

EWE: 15 “Azɔ, Oo Yehowa mía Mawu, wò, ame si tsɔ alɔ sesẽ kplɔ wò dukɔ tso Egipte-nyigba dzi, eye nèwɔ ŋkɔ na ɖokuiwò abe ale si wòle egbe sia ene, míewɔ nu vɔ̃, míewɔ nu tovo.
ENGLISH: The Lord gave me into the hands of those against whom I cannot stand up. 15 The Lord has spurned all my braves within me, has called a convention against me to mangle my young men, trodden winepress for Judah’s maiden daughter.

EWE: 16 Oo Yehowa, míeɖe kuku, wò dziku kple wò dɔmedzoe nu nefa ɖe wò du, Yerusalem, wò to kɔkɔe la ŋu, le wò nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔwo katã ta; elabena Yerusalem kple wò dukɔ la zu vlodonu na ame siwo katã ƒo xlã mí le míaƒe nu vɔ̃wo kple mía tɔgbuiwo ƒe vodadawo ta.
ENGLISH: 16 Over these things I weep, my eye streams down water, because far away is any who would comfort me, would bring me back to life, my sons are desolate because an enemy is in power.

EWE: 17 Azɔ, Oo mía Mawu, se wò subɔla ƒe gbedodoɖa kple eƒe kokoƒoƒo, eye na wò mo naklẽ ɖe wò kɔkɔeƒe si zu aƒedo la dzi le wò ŋutɔ ɖokuiwò ta, Oo Yehowa.
ENGLISH: 17 Sion spreads out her hands, has no comforter. Jehovah has commissioned Jacob’s foes all round him, Jerusalem has become a piece of garbage among them.

EWE: 18 Oo nye Mawu, ƒu to anyi nàsee!
ENGLISH: 18 Jehovah is in the right, because I had disobeyed him.

EWE: Ke ŋku nàkpɔ nɔnɔme sesẽ si me míele, kple ale si du si ŋu woyɔ wò ŋkɔ ɖo la zu aƒedoe la; elabena menye míaƒe nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔ tae míele kuku ɖem na wò ɖo o, ke boŋ wò nublanuikpɔkpɔ geɖeawo tae.
ENGLISH: Listen, all peoples, and see my hurt! My maidens and young men have gone into foreign slavery.

EWE: 19 Oo Yehowa, see.
ENGLISH: 19 I called to my lovers; they failed me.

EWE: Oo Yehowa, tsɔe ke.
ENGLISH: 21 Listen when I moan!

EWE: Oo Yehowa, lé to ɖe eŋu, eye nàwɔe!
ENGLISH: I have no comforter.

EWE: Oo nye Mawu, mègahe ɖe megbe o le wò ŋutɔ ɖokuiwò ta, elabena wò ŋkɔe woyɔ ɖe wò du kple wò dukɔ la ŋu.”
ENGLISH: All my enemies hear of my calamity, they rejoice because you acted. Bring the day you have announced and let them be like me!

EWE: 20 Esi megale nuƒoƒo dzi, le gbe dom ɖa hele nye nu vɔ̃ kple nye dukɔ Israel ƒe nu vɔ̃ me ʋum, eye mele Yehowa nye Mawu ƒe amenuveve biam ɖe nye Mawu ƒe to kɔkɔe la ta, 21 esi megale gbe dom ɖa hele nu ƒom la, ŋutsu Gabriel, ame si mekpɔ le ŋutega me tsã la, va gbɔnye le fiẽvɔsaɣi esime ɖeɖi te ŋunye belibeli. 22 Ena mese egɔme eye wògblɔ be:
ENGLISH: 22 Let all their viciousness come before you and treat them as you treated me for all my crimes.For my moans are many and my heart is sick.

EWE: Daniel
ENGLISH: Lamentations

EWE: 10 Le Persia-fia Kores ƒe ƒe etɔ̃lia me la, woɖe nya aɖe fia Daniel, ame si ŋkɔe nye Beltesazar; nya la nye nyateƒe, eye wòku ɖe aʋawɔwɔ gã aɖe ŋu.
ENGLISH: 2 How the Lord in his anger clouds Sion’s daughter in, has thrown the magnificence of Israel from sky to earth, and not remembered his footstool on his day of anger!

EWE: Ese nya la gɔme, eye wòse nu si wòkpɔ la gɔme. 2 Le ŋkeke mawo me la, nye Daniel mexa nu kwasiɖa etɔ̃ sɔŋ.
ENGLISH: 2 The Lord has unsparingly swept off all Jacob’s meadows, has in his wrath demolished the fortifications of the daughter of Judah, has laid in the dust, desecrated, a kingdom and its generals.

EWE: 3 Nyemeɖu nu nyui aɖeke o, lã alo wain aɖeke mede nu me nam o, eye nyemesi ami o, va se ɖe esime kwasiɖa etɔ̃ la katã wu enu.
ENGLISH: 3 In his anger he has chopped off every horn of Israel’s, turned his right hand backward before an enemy, and blazed in Jacob like a flaming fire devouring on all sides.

EWE: 4 Le ɣleti gbãtɔ ƒe ŋkeke blaeve vɔ enelia dzi, esime mele tɔsisi gã, si nye Tigris to la, 5 mefɔ mo dzi eye mekpɔ ŋutsu aɖe si do aklalawu, eye wòtsɔ Ufaz sika bla ali dzi.
ENGLISH: 4 He has bent his bow like an enemy, brought up his right hand like a foe, and killed all that were a delight to the eye; on the tent of the daughter of Sion he has poured his choler like fire.

EWE: 6 Eŋuti le abe krisolit ene, eye eƒe mo le abe dzikedzo ene, eƒe ŋkuwo le abe akakati bibiwo ene, eƒe abɔwo kple eƒe afɔwo le abe akɔbli si le dzo dam ene, eye eƒe nuƒoƒo le ɖiɖim abe amehawo ƒe hoowɔwɔ ene.
ENGLISH: 6 And he has ruthlessly dismantled her lodge like a shack in a garden, has ruined her meeting-place, Jehovah has caused meeting-day and sabbath to be forgotten in Sion, and in his angry hostility has contemned king and priest.

EWE: 7 Nye Daniel ɖeɖe koe kpɔ ŋutega la; ame siwo le ŋunye ya mekpɔe o. Ke hã, wodzo nyanyanya ŋutɔ, ale be wosi yi ɖabe.
ENGLISH: 7 The Lord has repudiated his altar, ignored his sanctuary, given up to an enemy the walls of her palaces; they made a noise in Jehovah’s house that sounded like an annual feast.

EWE: 8 Nye ɖeka koe susɔ eye esi mekpɔ ŋutega wɔnuku sia la, ŋusẽ vɔ le ŋunye, nye dzedzeme trɔ ɖe ƒomevii, eye wɔna vɔ le ŋunye keŋkeŋ.
ENGLISH: 8 Jehovah planned to wreck the walls of the daughter of Sion; he stretched a line, did not turn his hand back from sweeping it down, and let bulwark and wall mourn, forlorn together.

EWE: 9 Eye mese eƒe nuƒoƒo; ke esi mese eƒe nuƒoƒo la, metsyɔ mo anyi heyi alɔ̃ me ʋĩi.
ENGLISH: 9 Her gates have sunk into the earth; he has destroyed and shattered her bars; her king and generals are among the nations; there are no rulings on religion; her prophets too have not found any vision from Jehovah.

EWE: 10 Gake asi aɖe ka ŋunye, eye wòʋuʋum mefɔ ɖe nye klo kple asi dzi.
ENGLISH: 10 The elders of the daughter of Sion sit silent on the ground, have put earth over their heads, have belted on sackcloths; the maidens of Jerusalem have put their heads down on the ground.

EWE: 11 Eye wògblɔ nam be: “Daniel, wò, si nye ame vevi, lé to ɖe nya siwo magblɔ na wò la ŋu. Azɔ tsi tsitre ɖe tewòƒe, elabena wodɔm ɖe gbɔwò.”
ENGLISH: 11 My eyes are used up in tears, my vitals are boiling, my heart runs out of me for the broken bones of the daughter of my people, when little boy and baby collapse in town squares;

EWE: Esi wògblɔ nya siawo nam la, metsi tsitre hele ƒoƒom kpakpakpa. 12 Eye wògblɔ nam be: “Daniel, mègavɔ̃ o.
ENGLISH: 12 They say to their mothers “Where is some grain and wine?” while they faint away in city squares like a man mortally wounded, while their life runs out in their mothers’ laps.

EWE: Tso gbe si gbe nètsɔ wò dzi ɖo gɔmesese ŋu, eye nèbɔbɔ ɖokuiwò le wò Mawu ŋkume la, wose wò nyawo, eye wò nyawo tae meva ɖo. 13 Ke Persia-fiaɖuƒe la ƒe amegã tsi tre ɖe ŋunye ŋkeke blaeve vɔ ɖekɛ sɔŋ.
ENGLISH: 13 What shall I quote to you, what shall I compare you to, daughter Jerusalem? what shall I parallel to you to comfort you, maiden daughter of Sion? for your mauling is great as the sea; who shall heal you?

EWE: Ke Mikael, amegãwo ƒe tatɔwo dometɔ ɖeka, va kpe ɖe ŋunye; eye menɔ Persia-fiawo gbɔ le afi ma. 14 Ke azɔ meva be mana nànya nu si ava dzɔ ɖe wò dukɔ la dzi le ŋkekeawo ƒe nuwuɣi, elabena ŋkeke siwo ava va la ŋue ŋutega la ku ɖo.”
ENGLISH: 14 Your prophets have furnished you futile and unctuous visions, have not spoken out about your guilt to bring you back but have given you visions that are delusion, futility, and exile.

EWE: 15 Ke esi wòle nya siawo gblɔm nam la, mede mo to, eye gbɔgblɔ bu ɖem.
ENGLISH: 15 All passersby struck their hands together over you, whistled and shook their heads at the daughter of Jerusalem: “Is this the city that was spoken of as perfect in beauty, a joy to all the earth?”

EWE: 16 Eye ame aɖe si ƒe nɔnɔme le abe ŋutsu ene la ka asi nye nuyiwo ŋu, ale meke nu, eye meƒo nu gblɔ na ame si le tsitre ɖe ŋgɔnye la be: “Oo nye aƒetɔ, nu si mekpɔ la na dzidzi ƒom, eye ŋusẽ vɔ le ŋunye.
ENGLISH: 16 All your enemies opened their mouths wide at you, whistled and ground their teeth, said “We have made a clean sweep; this is just the day we were hoping for; it has turned up, we see the sight.”

EWE: 17 Ke aleke nye aƒetɔ ƒe dɔla awɔ aƒo nu kple nye aƒetɔ? Elabena ŋusẽ aɖeke megale ŋunye fifia o, eye gbɔgbɔ aɖeke megakpɔtɔ ɖe menye o.”
ENGLISH: 17 Jehovah has done what he designed, finished up his dictate that he ordained from olden days, demolished unsparingly, gladdened your enemies over you, given your foes a high horn.

EWE: 18 Ame si ƒe nɔnɔme le abe ŋutsu ene la gaka asi ŋunye hedo ŋusẽm.
ENGLISH: 18 Their hearts cried out to the Lord hotly; daughter of Sion, pour down your tears like a flooded brook day and night, take no anodyne, let your eyeball never be still.

EWE: 19 Eye wògblɔ be: “Oo wò, si nye ame vevi, mègavɔ̃ o. Ŋutifafa na wò. Sẽ ŋu, ɛ̃, sẽ ŋu.”
ENGLISH: 19 Stand up and clamor in the night, at each new watch, pour out your hearts in Jehovah’s face like water, raise your hands to him for the lives of your boys and girls who have fainted away with hunger at the tops of all the streets.

EWE: Esi wònɔ nu ƒom kplim la, ŋusẽ ɖo ŋunye, eye megblɔ azɔ be: “Nye aƒetɔ neƒo nu, elabena èdo ŋusẽm.” 20 Eye wògblɔ be: “Ènya nu si koŋ ta meva gbɔwò ɖoa?
ENGLISH: 20 See, Jehovah! look whom you have handled so! or should women eat their own fruit, their petted children? or should priest and prophet be killed in the Lord’s sanctuary?

EWE: Ne medzo la, Hela-megã ava. 21 Ke hã, magblɔ nu siwo woŋlɔ ɖe nyateƒegbalẽa me la na wò.
ENGLISH: 21 Boy and old man are lying on the ground in the streets; my maidens and young men have fallen by the sword; on your day of anger you killed, slaughtered, had no mercy.

EWE: Ame aɖeke medo alɔm le nya siawo me o, negbe miaƒe amegã Mikael ko.
ENGLISH: Those that I had petted and brought up my enemy has swept away.

EWE: Daniel
ENGLISH: Lamentations

EWE: 11 “Ke nye la, metso be mado ŋusẽe atui ɖo, le Mediatɔ Dario ƒe ƒe gbãtɔ me.
ENGLISH: 3 I am the man that saw hardship by the cudgel of his wrath.

EWE: 2 Azɔ magblɔ nyateƒe la na wò: “Kpɔ ɖa!
ENGLISH: 2 Me he drove along to go darkling, unlighted.

EWE: 3 “Eye fia sẽŋu aɖe ado eye eƒe dziɖuƒe akeke ta, eye wòawɔ nu si dze eŋu.
ENGLISH: 3 Only at me all day he kept turning back his hand.

EWE: 4 Gake ne enya do ko la, woagbã eƒe fiaɖuƒe la, eye woamae ɖe dziƒo ƒe ya eneawo nu, ke menye na eƒe dzidzimeviwo o, eye menye ɖe ŋusẽ si wòtsɔ ɖu dzii la hã nu o; elabena woaho eƒe fiaɖuƒe la atsɔ ana ame bubuwo, ke menye woawo o.
ENGLISH: 4 He wore away my flesh and skin, shattered my bones,

EWE: 5 “Ŋusẽ aɖo anyiehefia, si nye eƒe amegãwo dometɔ ɖeka ŋu; gake ame bubu akpɔ ŋusẽ wui, eye wòatsɔ ŋusẽ gã si keke ta wu ame kemɛ ƒe dziɖuŋusẽ la aɖu dzii.
ENGLISH: 5 Built siege-works against me and surrounded my head with hard experiences,

EWE: 6 “Le ƒe aɖewo megbe la, woawɔ ɖeka kple wo nɔewo, eye anyiehefia vinyɔnu ava dziehefia gbɔ, be woabla nu.
ENGLISH: 6 Seated me in places of darkness like men long since dead.

EWE: 7 Eye alɔ adze tso nyɔnu la ƒe kè me axɔ ɖe fia la teƒe, eye wòava aʋakɔ la gbɔ aho ɖe dziehefia ƒe mɔ́ sesẽ la ŋu, atso ɖe wo ŋu ahaɖu wo dzi.
ENGLISH: 7 He walled me off so that I could not get out, made my fetters heavy.

EWE: 8 Atsɔ woƒe mawuwo, woƒe galegbawo, klosalonu kple sikanu xɔasiwo kpakple aboyomewo ayi Egipte.
ENGLISH: 8 Withal when I cried and clamored he shut off my prayer.

EWE: Anɔ adzɔge na dziehefia, 9 si ava anyiehefia ƒe fiaɖuƒe la me hena ƒe aɖewo, ke agbugbɔ ayi eya ŋutɔ ƒe anyigba dzi.
ENGLISH: 9 He walled up my road with masonry, kept me making detours.

EWE: 10 “Ke viawo adzra ɖo na aʋawɔwɔ, eye woaƒo aʋakɔ gã aɖe nu ƒu.
ENGLISH: 10 An ambushed bear he was to me, a lion under cover.

EWE: 11 “Dzi aku anyiehefia la wòaho aɖawɔ aʋa kple eya, si nye dziehefia la; aƒo ameha gã aɖe nu ƒu, ke woatsɔ ameha la ade asi na fia kemɛa.
ENGLISH: 11 My roads he filled with briers and tore my flesh, laid me desolate.

EWE: 12 Eye woakplɔ ameha la adzoe.
ENGLISH: 12 He strung his bow and set me up like a target for the arrow,

EWE: 13 “Dziehefia la atrɔ agbɔ ava ƒo ameha gã aɖe nu ƒu wòasɔ gbɔ wu gbãtɔ; eye le ɣeyiɣiawo ƒe nuwuwu, le ƒe aɖewo megbe la, ava kple aʋakɔ gã kple aʋawɔnu geɖewo.
ENGLISH: 13 Sent in the contents of his quiver into my waist.

EWE: 14 Ame geɖewo atso ɖe anyiehefia la ŋu ɣemaɣi. “Woakplɔ mia devi sẽŋutawo ayi be woana ŋutega aɖe nava eme; ke womate ŋu anɔ te o.
ENGLISH: 14 I became a butt for the laughter of all my people, for their jingles all day long.

EWE: 15 “Dziehefia ava ƒu kpo, eye wòaxɔ du si ŋu gli sesẽwo le.
ENGLISH: 15 He filled me up with bitter greens, gave me wormwood-juice for refreshment,

EWE: 16 Ame si ho ɖe eŋu la awɔ nu si dze eŋu, eye ame aɖeke manɔ te ɖe enu o.
ENGLISH: 16 And rasped my teeth with gravel, thrust me down in the ashes.

EWE: 17 Aɖoe kplikpaa be yeatsɔ yeƒe fiaɖuƒe la ƒe ŋusẽ katã ahoe, eye wòabla nu kple fia ma; awɔ nu si wòdi la ade goe.
ENGLISH: 17 And you banned my soul from welfare; I forgot such a thing as good,

EWE: Vinyɔnu la manɔ te o, eye makpɔtɔ anye fia ma tɔ o. 18 Agatrɔ ɖe ƒutanyigbawo ŋu, eye wòaxɔ geɖewo.
ENGLISH: 18 And said “my continuance is lost, and my expectation from Jehovah.”

EWE: 19 Agatrɔ ɖe eya ŋutɔ ƒe anyigba ƒe mɔ́ sesẽwo ŋu, ke akli nu adze anyi, eye womagakpɔe o.
ENGLISH: 19 The recollection of my miserable and homeless state is wormwood and opium.

EWE: 20 “Ame aɖe axɔ ɖe eteƒe, ame si ana adzɔxɔla natsa le fiaɖuƒe dzeani la me, gake le ŋkeke ʋɛ aɖewo megbe la, woatsrɔ̃e, ke menye le dziku alo aʋa me o.
ENGLISH: 20 Recollect my soul does, and is downhearted within me.

EWE: 21 “Ame ɖigbɔ aɖe axɔ ɖe eteƒe, eye womade fiaɖuƒe la ƒe bubu eŋu o; ava esime woɖe dzi ɖi bɔkɔɔ, eye wòatsɔ numevivi axɔ fiaɖuƒe la.
ENGLISH: 21 This I will bring back to mind, will therefore wait,

EWE: 22 Ke woakplɔ aʋakɔ siwo gbagba ɖi la adzoe le eya ta, eye woatsrɔ̃ wo; abe ale si woatsrɔ̃ nubabla ƒe Kplɔla la ene.
ENGLISH: 22 Jehovah’s friendlinesses, that they are not exhausted, that his sympathy has not come to an end,

EWE: 23 Le nu si wobla kplii ta la, anɔ alakpa dam, eye wòaho atsɔ dukɔ sue aɖe akpɔ ŋusẽe.
ENGLISH: 23 New every morning; great is your loyalty.

EWE: 24 Age ɖe fiaɖuƒea ƒe nuto siwo me kesinɔnuwo bɔ ɖo la me esime woɖe dzi ɖi bɔkɔɔ, eye wòawɔ nu si fofoawo kple tɔgbuiawo mewɔ o.
ENGLISH: 24 Jehovah is my portion, my soul has said; therefore I will wait for him.

EWE: 25 “Atsɔ aʋakɔ gã aɖe adzi eƒe ŋusẽ ɖe edzi ahado ŋusẽ eƒe dzi ɖe anyiehefia ŋu, eye anyiehefia la hã atsɔ aʋakɔ gã nyadri aɖe ŋutɔ adzra ɖo ɖe aʋa la ŋu.
ENGLISH: 25 Jehovah is good to those who hope in him, to a soul that betakes itself to him.

EWE: Ke manɔ te o, elabena woaɖo nugbe ɖe eŋu. 26 Ame siwo ɖua nu kplii lae ana wòadze anyi.
ENGLISH: 26 Good it is that one wait, and in silence, for Jehovah’s salvation.

EWE: 27 “Fia eve siawo ƒe dzi atrɔ ɖe nu gbegblẽ wɔwɔ ŋu, eye woanɔ kplɔ̃ ɖeka ŋu anɔ alakpa dam na wo nɔewo.
ENGLISH: 27 Good it is for a man that he carry a yoke in his youth,

EWE: 28 “Atsɔ nu geɖewo atrɔ ayi eƒe anyigba dzi, eye eƒe dzi atso ɖe nubabla kɔkɔe la ŋu.
ENGLISH: 28 Sit alone and be still because it was laid on him,

EWE: 29 “Ne ɣeyiɣi ɖoɖi la de la, agatrɔ ava, eye wòaho ɖe anyiehenyigba ŋu.
ENGLISH: 29 Put his mouth in the dust,perhaps there may be hope,

EWE: Ke fifia ya manɔ abe tsã ene o, 30 elabena Kitim tɔdziʋuwo aho ɖe eŋu, eye woabɔbɔe ɖe anyi.
ENGLISH: 30 Give his cheek to the one who strikes him, take his fill of humiliation.

EWE: 31 Alɔwo ado tso eme; woagblẽ kɔ ɖo na kɔkɔeƒe la, si nye mɔ́ sesẽ la, eye woatsi gbe sia gbe vɔsa la nu.
ENGLISH: 31 For the Lord will not repudiate man forever,

EWE: 32 “Atsɔ numevivinyawo akplɔ ame siwo wɔa nu vɔ̃ɖitɔe hedaa nubabla la dzi la ade xɔsegbegbe me.
ENGLISH: 32 For if he causes misery he will have sympathy in accordance with his great friendliness,

EWE: 33 Ke ame siwo si gɔmesese deto le le dukɔ la dome ana gɔmesese nasu ame geɖewo si.
ENGLISH: 33 For he does not arbitrarily grind down sons of man and bring them to misery.

EWE: 34 Ke ne wona wokli nu la, woakpe ɖe wo ŋu vie; eye ame geɖewo atsɔ numevivi ava wɔ ɖeka kpli wo.
ENGLISH: 34 To beating down underfoot all earth’s prisoners,

EWE: 35 Woana ame siwo si gɔmesese deto le la dometɔ aɖewo nakli nu.
ENGLISH: 35 To warping the law against a man in the face of the Most High,

EWE: 36 “Fia la awɔ nu si dze eŋu, eye wòado eɖokui ɖe dzi ahado gã eɖokui ɖe mawu sia mawu ŋu; agblɔ nya wɔmoyawo ɖe mawuwo dzi Mawu la ŋu.
ENGLISH: 36 To circumventing a man in his suit over his rights, the Lord does not assent.

EWE: 37 Mabu fofoawo ƒe Mawu ɖe ɖeke me o, eye mabu nyɔnuwo ƒe nu malɔ̃nugbɔa ɖe ɖeke me o.
ENGLISH: 37 Who is there that says a thing and has it come when the Lord has not ordered it?

EWE: 38 Atsɔ ŋutikɔkɔe ana mawu si le mɔ́ sesẽwo me boŋ; atsɔ sika, klosalo, kpe xɔasiwo kple nu veviwo ade bubu mawu si fofoawo menya o la ŋu.
ENGLISH: 38 Do not evils and good come out of the mouth of the Most High?

EWE: 39 Aɖo ŋu ɖe dutamawuwo ŋu ahawɔ nu ale si wòdi ɖe mɔ́ sesẽ siwo li ke wu la ŋu.
ENGLISH: 39 What should a living man bemoan, a man over his sin?

EWE: 40 “Le nuwuɣi la, anyiehefia akpe kplii, eye woanɔ wo nɔewo tutum, eye dziehefia atsɔ tasiaɖamwo, sɔdolawo kple tɔdziʋu geɖewo ava dze edzi; ava ƒo ɖi bibibi ato wo dzi abe tsiɖɔɖɔ ene.
ENGLISH: 40 Let us search our course and examine it, and come back to Jehovah.

EWE: 41 Ava Atsyɔ̃nyigba la hã dzi, eye woana dukɔ geɖewo nadze anyi.
ENGLISH: 41 Let us hold up our hearts in our hands to Deity in heaven.

EWE: 42 Anɔ eƒe asi dom ɖa ɖe anyigbawo ŋu; eye Egipte-nyigba la mato le eme o.
ENGLISH: 42 We were criminal and disobedient; you did not forgive.

EWE: 43 Akpɔ ŋusẽ ɖe kesinɔnu ɣaɣla siwo nye sika kple klosalo kpakple Egipte ƒe nu veviwo katã dzi.
ENGLISH: 43 You overspread us with anger and pursued us, you killed without mercy.
