EWE: 2 Kpɔ ɖa, mena nèle sue le dukɔwo dome;Wodo vlo wò vevie.3 Wò dzi ƒe dadae ble wò,Wò ame si le agato me,
ENGLISH: 2 Here, I have made you little among the nations; greatly despised you are.

EWE: Eye nèle kɔkɔƒewo hele gbɔgblɔm le wò dzi me be: ‘Ame kae atutum aƒu anyi?’
ENGLISH: 3 Your self-confidence has deluded you, perched in the crannies of the cliffs with your lodgment on the towering heights, that say to yourself “Who will bring me down to earth?”

EWE: 4 Ne èwɔ nɔwòƒe ɖe dzi ʋĩi abe hɔ̃ ene,Alo nèwɔ atɔ ɖe ɣletiviwo dome hã la,Matutu wò aƒu anyi tso afi ma,” Yehowa ye gblɔe.
ENGLISH: 4 If you go high as the vulture and have your nest set between the stars, from there I will bring you down, quoth Jehovah.

EWE: 5 “Ne fiafiwoe dze dziwò, alo adzoblasuwoe va le zã me ɖe, (Aleke gbegbee woatsrɔ̃ wòe nye esi!) Menye nu ale si nu dim wole koe woafi oa? Alo ne wainxalawoe ƒo ɖe dziwò la, Ðe womakpɔtɔ ɖe ɖi oa?
ENGLISH: 5 If thieves came to you, if night marauders how you are blotted out! would they not steal what they had occasion for? if grape-gatherers came to you would they not leave after-pickings?

EWE: 6 Oo, kpɔ ale si gbegbe wodi Esau ƒe amewo tsitotsitoe ɖa!
ENGLISH: 6 How ʽEsau is hunted out, his coverts pried into!

EWE: Kpɔ ale si gbegbe wodi eƒe kesinɔnuwo heha woe ɖa! 7 Wonya wò ɖo ɖe keke liƒo dzi ke. Ame siwo katã bla nu kpli wò la ble wò. Ame siwo le ŋutifafa me kpli wò la ɖu dziwò. Ame siwo ɖua nu kpli wò la aɖo ɖɔ ɖe tewò,
ENGLISH: 7 All the men you had treaties with have sent you to the boundary; the men who were at peace with you have deluded you, overpowered you; they have laid your bread as a trap for you; he has no sense in him.

EWE: Ke màdze sii o. 8 Yehowa be: “Ðe nyematsrɔ̃ nunyalawo ɖa le Edom
ENGLISH: 8 Shall I not on that day, quoth Jehovah, do away with wise men in Edom and good judgment in ʽEsau’s highland?

EWE: Kple gɔmesese ɖa le Esau tonuto la me gbe ma gbe oa? 9 Oo Teman, ŋɔdzi alé wò aʋawɔlawo,
ENGLISH: 9 and your champions shall be dismayed, Teman, so that ʽEsau’s highland shall be without a man by carnage.

EWE: Elabena woawu wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe le Esau tonuto la me. 10 Ŋukpe anyè atsyɔ wò Le ŋuta si nèsẽ le nɔviwò Yakob ŋu la ta,
ENGLISH: 10 For the outrage to your brother Jacob shame shall cover you and you shall be done away with forever:

EWE: Eye woatsrɔ̃ wò ɖa tegbee. 11 Gbe si gbe nètɔ ɖe adzɔge, Gbe si gbe ame tutɔwo ɖe aboyo eƒe aʋakɔ, Esime amedzrowo ge ɖe eƒe agbowo me, eye wodzidze nu ɖe Yerusalem dzi la,
ENGLISH: 11 in the day when you stood by, in the day when strangers were carrying off his strength and foreigners had come into his gate and were casting lots over Jerusalem, you too were like one of them.

EWE: Wò hã èwɔ nu abe wo dometɔ ɖeka ene. 12 “Mele be nàkpɔ nu si dzɔ ɖe nɔviwò dzi le ŋkeke si vɔ̃ dzɔ ɖe edzi la kple dzidzɔ o, Mele be nàkpɔ dzidzɔ le gbe si gbe Yuda viwo nɔ tsɔtsrɔ̃m o,
ENGLISH: 12 And do not gloat over your brother’s day on his day of mishap; and do not rejoice for the sons of Judah on the day they are perishing; and do not talk jauntily on a day of distress;

EWE: Eye mele be nàɖu fewu le wo ŋu le woƒe xaxagbe o. 13 Mele be nàge ɖe nye dukɔ ƒe agbo me le gbe si gbe vɔ̃ dzɔ ɖe edzi o, Mele be nàfɔ ŋku ɖe xaxa si va edzi la dzi le gbe si gbe vɔ̃ dzɔ ɖe edzi la o,
ENGLISH: 13 do not go into my people’s gate on their day of calamity, do not be another to gloat over his ills on his day of calamity, and do not put your hand to his wealth on his day of calamity;

EWE: Eye mele be nàdo asi ɖe eƒe kesinɔnuwo gbɔ le gbe si gbe vɔ̃ dzɔ ɖe edzi o. 14 Mele be nàtɔ ɖe mɔ dzevee nu be yeawu eƒe sisilawo o,
ENGLISH: 14 and do not stand in ambush to cut off those of his who are escaping; and do not in a day of distress hand his survivors over to their fate.

EWE: Eye mele be nàtsɔ eƒe ame siwo tsi agbe la ade asi le xaxagbe o. 15 Elabena Yehowa ƒe ŋkeke si dzi wòatso ɖe dukɔwo katã ŋu la tu aƒe.
ENGLISH: 15 For Jehovah’s day is near upon all the nations: as you have done you shall be done by; your dealings shall come back on your own head.

EWE: Nu si tututu nèwɔ la kee woawɔ wò hã. 16 Elabena ale si mienɔ aha nom le nye to kɔkɔe la dzii la, Nenema kee dukɔwo katã anɔ nye dɔmedzoe la nom abe aha ene ɖaa.
ENGLISH: 16 For as you have drunk on my sacred highland all the nations shall drink all the time, drink and talk at random and be as if they never had been;

EWE: Eye woanɔ abe ame siwo medzɔ kpɔ o la ene. 17 Ke ame siwo si la anɔ Zion To la dzi, Eye wòazu teƒe kɔkɔe;
ENGLISH: 17 but on Mount Sion there shall be escape, and it shall be sacred, and the house of Jacob shall dispossess their dispossessors.

EWE: Eye Yakob ƒe aƒe la axɔ nu siwo nye wo tɔ la. 18 Yakob ƒe aƒe la anye dzo, Yosef ƒe aƒe la anye dzoƒaɖe, Eye Esau ƒe aƒe la anye ahɔ̃liti, Woatɔ dzo wo woafiã. Esau ƒe aƒe la me tɔ aɖeke matsi agbe o;
ENGLISH: 18 And the house of Jacob shall be fire and the house of Joseph become flame, and the house of ʽEsau become stubble; and they shall catch to them and eat them up, and the house of ʽEsau shall have no survivor, because Jehovah has spoken.

EWE: Elabena Yehowa ŋutɔe gblɔe. 19 Woaxɔ Negeb, kple Esau tonuto la, Sefela kple Filistitɔwo ƒe anyigba. Woaxɔ Efrayim-nyigba kple Samaria-nyigba,
ENGLISH: 19 And they shall take possession of the South, ʽEsau’s highland, and the lowlands, the Philistines; and they shall take possession of the countryside of Ephraim and the countryside of Samaria, and Benjamin Gilead.

EWE: Eye Benyamin axɔ Gilead. 20 Eye Israel-viwo, ame siwo woɖe aboyoe tso gli sia gbɔ la, Axɔ nu siwo nye Kanaantɔwo tɔ la va se ɖe keke Zarefat ke.
ENGLISH: 20 And the deported population of Halah (this is for the sons of Israel) shall dispossess the Canaanites to Sarephath, and the deported Jerusalemites in Asia Minor shall take possession of the cities of the South.

EWE: Eye Yerusalem ƒe aboyome siwo nɔ Sefarad la axɔ Negeb duwo. 21 Eye xɔnametɔwo ava Zion To la dzi, Ne woadrɔ̃ ʋɔnu Esau tonuto la,
ENGLISH: 21 And saviors shall come up into Mount Sion to do justice on ʽEsau’s highland; and the empire shall be Jehovah’s.

EWE: Yona
ENGLISH: Jonah

EWE: 1 Yehowa ƒe gbe va na Yona, Amitai vi be: 2 “Tso nàyi Niniwe du gã la me, eye nàgblɔ nye ʋɔnudrɔ̃gbedeasi nɛ elabena eƒe nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ va ɖo ŋkunyeme.”
ENGLISH: 1 And Jehovah’s word came to Jonah the son of Amittai, 2 “Go off to the great city Nineveh and preach against it, because its wickedness has come up before me”;

EWE: 3 Ke Yona tso be yeasi le Yehowa nu ayi Tarsis; eye wòva Yopa hekpɔ tɔdziʋu aɖe si yina Tarsis. Ale wòxe fe heɖo ʋua be yeasi le Yehowa nu ayi Tarsis kpli wo.
ENGLISH: 3 and Jonah stood up to get away to Spain out of Jehovah’s presence, and went down to Joppa and found a ship sailing for Spain, and paid his fare and went aboard to sail with them to Spain out of Jehovah’s presence.

EWE: 4 Eye Yehowa lɔ ya sesẽ aɖe trɔ ɖe atsiaƒu la dzi, eye ahom gã aɖe tu le atsiaƒu la dzi ale be tɔdziʋua di be yeagbã.
ENGLISH: 4 But Jehovah launched a great wind over the sea, and there came very rough weather on the sea, and the ship was ready to be wrecked;

EWE: 5 Tɔdziʋumedɔwɔlawo vɔ̃, eye wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe de asi eƒe mawu yɔyɔ me be wòaxɔ na ye. Eye wonɔ tɔdziʋua me nuwo fɔm nɔ gbe ƒum ɖe atsiaƒua me be wòanɔ wodzoe.
ENGLISH: 5 and the sailors were afraid, and each cried to his god, and flung into the sea the things they had in the ship, to have it be easier on them; but Jonah had gone down into the hold and lain down and was fast asleep.

EWE: Gake Yona ya yi tɔdziʋua gɔme hemlɔ anyi dɔ alɔ̃ yi eme ʋĩi. 6 Eye ʋumefia la te ɖe eŋu gblɔ nɛ be: “Nu ka ƒe alɔ̃ dɔm wò ya nèle? Fɔ nàyɔ wò mawu!
ENGLISH: 6 And the captain came where he was and said to him “What are you about, fast asleep? get up and call out to your god, maybe the god will have some consideration for us and we shall not be lost.”

EWE: Ðewohĩ Mawu vavã la akpɔ nublanui na mí, be míagatsrɔ̃ o.” 7 Eye wogblɔ na wo nɔewo be: “Miva, mina míadzidze nu, ne míanya ame si ta vɔ̃ sia le dzɔdzɔm ɖe mía dzi ɖo.”
ENGLISH: 7 And they said to each other “Come on, let us cast lots and know on whose account we are having this bad luck”; and they cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.

EWE: Ale wodzidze nu, eye nudzidze la dze Yona dzi. 8 Eye wobiae be: “Míeɖe kuku, gblɔe na mí, ame ka tae vɔ̃ sia le dzɔdzɔm ɖe mía dzi ɖo?
ENGLISH: 8 And they said to him “Please tell us what errand you are on and where you are going from, what country you are from and what people you belong to.”

EWE: 9 Eɖo eŋu na wo be: “Hebritɔ menye, eye mevɔ̃a Yehowa, dziƒo ƒe Mawu, Ame si wɔ atsiaƒu kple anyigba ƒuƒui la.”
ENGLISH: 9 And he said to them “I am a Hebrew, and revere Jehovah, the god of the heavens, who made the sea and the land.”

EWE: 10 Ale vɔvɔ̃ gaɖo ŋutsuawo ɖe edzi, eye wobiae be: “Nu kae nèwɔ?”
ENGLISH: 10 And the men were in great fear, and said to him “What is this you have done?” because the men knew he was trying to get away out of Jehovah’s presence, because he had told them.

EWE: (Ŋutsuawo va nyae be Yehowa nue wòle sisim le, elabena egblɔe na wo.) 11 Eye wobiae be: “Nu kae míawɔ wò, be atsiaƒua nadze akɔ anyi na mí?”
ENGLISH: 11 And they said to him “What are we to do to you to have the sea calm down?” because the sea was getting stormier and stormier.

EWE: Elabena ƒu la ƒe nyanyra nu le sesẽm ɖe edzi. 12 Egblɔ na wo be: “Mikɔm ƒu gbe ɖe atsiaƒua me, ekema atsiaƒua adze akɔ anyi na mi; elabena menyae be tanyee ahom sesẽ sia va mia dzi ɖo.” 13 Ke ŋutsuawo ku ʋua kple ŋusẽ be yewoaɖi go; gake womete ŋui o, elabena ƒu la nɔ nyanyram ɖe edzi eye yaƒoƒo la nɔ wo kpem.
ENGLISH: 12 And he said to them “Pick me up and fling me into the sea to have the sea calm down; for I know it is on my account you are having this great storm.” 13 And the men rowed to get back to land, but could not, because the sea was getting stormier and stormier against them.

EWE: 14 Eye wodo ɣli yɔ Yehowa gblɔ be: “Ao, Yehowa, Oo, míeɖe kuku, mègana míatsrɔ̃ le ŋutsu sia ta o!
ENGLISH: 14 And they called out to Jehovah “Please, Jehovah, may we not perish for this man’s life, and do not charge us with shedding innocent blood, because you, Jehovah, did as you preferred”;

EWE: Eye mègabu fɔ mí ɖe ʋu maɖifɔ ta o, elabena Yehowa, wò ŋutɔe wɔ nu si dze ŋuwò!” 15 Ale wokɔ Yona ƒu gbe ɖe atsiaƒua me; eye atsiaƒua dze akɔ anyi.
ENGLISH: 15 and they picked Jonah up and flung him into the sea, and the sea stopped raging.

EWE: 16 Eye ŋutsuawo vɔ̃ Yehowa ŋutɔ, eya ta wosa vɔ na Yehowa heɖe adzɔgbe nɛ.
ENGLISH: 16 And the men conceived a great fear of Jehovah, and made a sacrifice to Jehovah and made vows.

EWE: 17 Azɔ Yehowa dɔ tɔmelã gã aɖe wòmi Yona, ale Yona nɔ tɔmelã la ƒe dɔme ŋkeke etɔ̃ kple zã etɔ̃.
ENGLISH: 17 And Jehovah provided a great fish to swallow Jonah; and Jonah was in the fish’s stomach three days and three nights.

EWE: Yona
ENGLISH: Jonah

EWE: 2 Eye Yona do gbe ɖa na eƒe Mawu Yehowa tso ƒumelã la ƒe dɔme, 2 eye wògblɔ be:
ENGLISH: 2 And Jonah prayed to his God Jehovah from the fish’s stomach,

EWE: “Medo ɣli yɔ Yehowa le nye xaxa me, eye wòtɔ nam. Medo ɣli tso Tsiẽƒe ʋĩi ke be nàxɔ nam.
ENGLISH: 2 and said “I called out of my distress to Jehovah, and he answered me; out of the heart of the realm of death I shouted; you heard my voice.

EWE: Èse nye gbe. 3 Esi nètsɔm ƒu gbe ɖe gogloeƒe, ɖe atsiaƒu titina la, Ƒu dzeagbo la ŋe tsyɔ dzinye.
ENGLISH: 3 And you threw me in the ooze in ocean’s abyss, a river enclosing me; all your surges and waves passed over me;

EWE: Wò tsi kpakawo kple ƒutsotsoewo katã to tanye yi. 4 Eye megblɔ be: ‘Wonyam ɖa le ŋkuwòme!
ENGLISH: 4 And I thought ‘I am banished from before your eyes, how am I anymore to look to your holy temple?’

EWE: Aleke mawɔ agakpɔ wò gbedoxɔ kɔkɔe la?’ 5 Tsiwo ŋe tsyɔ dzinye eye nye agbe ɖo afɔku me;
ENGLISH: 5 Water enveloped me choking off my life, the deep enclosed me, weeds were wrapped round my head.

EWE: Gbewo xatsa ɖe ta nam. 6 Meyi to de towo ƒe agunu ke. Anyigba ƒe gametiwo do ɖe nunye tegbee, Ke èɖe nye agbe do goe tso do la me, Oo Yehowa nye Mawu.
ENGLISH: 6 To the sockets of mountains I went down, the earth had its bars over me forever; And you brought up my life from dissolution,Jehovah, my God.

EWE: 7 Esi nye agbe nu nɔ tsotsom la, Yehowae nye Ame si dzi meɖo ŋkui. Eye nye gbedodoɖa ɖo gbɔwò le wò gbedoxɔ kɔkɔe la me.
ENGLISH: 7 When my soul failed me I remembered Jehovah, and my prayer went in to him in his holy temple.

EWE: 8 Ame siwo ku ɖe legba maɖinuwo ŋu la gblẽ woƒe lɔlɔ̃ vavã tsoƒe ɖi.
ENGLISH: 8 Those who attend to futile superstitions are leaving their help,

EWE: 9 Ke nye la matsɔ akpedagbe akafu wò eye masa vɔ na wò. Mawɔ adzɔgbe si meɖe la dzi. Yehowa gbɔe xɔname tsona.”
ENGLISH: 9 but I with voice of thanksgiving will sacrifice to you,what I have vowed I will pay as salvation-offering to Jehovah.”

EWE: 10 Eye Yehowa de se na tɔmelã la, ale wòyi ɖadzɔ Yona ɖe gota.
ENGLISH: 10 And Jehovah told the fish what to do, and it vomited Jonah out to the land.

EWE: Yona
ENGLISH: Jonah

EWE: 3 Eye Yehowa ƒe gbe va na Yona zi evelia be: 2 “Tso nàyi Niniwe, du gã la me, eye nàɖe gbeƒã gbedeasi si megblɔ na wò la nɛ.”
ENGLISH: 3 And Jehovah’s word came to Jonah a second time 2 “Go off to the great city Nineveh and preach to it what I dictate to you”;

EWE: 3 Eya ta Yona ɖo to, eye wòtso yi Niniwe le Yehowa ƒe nya la nu.
ENGLISH: 3 and Jonah went off to Nineveh in accordance with Jehovah’s word.

EWE: Ke Niniwe nye du gã aɖe, eye ŋkeke etɔ̃e woazɔ hafi ate ŋu akpee ɖo.
ENGLISH: And Nineveh was a stupendously great city, a three days’ walk;

EWE: 4 Eye Yona yi du la me hezɔ ŋkeke ɖeka to dua me nɔ gbeƒã ɖem be: “Esusɔ ŋkeke blaene ko ne woatsrɔ̃ Niniwe.”
ENGLISH: 4 and Jonah began going into the city, going one day’s walk in, and preached “Forty days more and Nineveh is overthrown.”

EWE: 5 Ale Niniwetɔwo xɔ Mawu dzi se, eye woɖe gbeƒã be ame sia ame, tso tsitsiawo dzi va se ɖe ɖeviwo dzi, natsi nu adɔ ata akpanya.
ENGLISH: 5 And the men of Nineveh believed God and proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloths, from the greatest to the least of them;

EWE: 6 Esi gbedeasia ɖo Niniwe-fia gbɔ la, etso le eƒe fiazikpui dzi heɖe eƒe fiawu ɖi, eye wòta akpanya hebɔbɔ nɔ dzofi me.
ENGLISH: 6 and the word reached the king of Nineveh, and he stood up off his throne and laid off his grandeur and covered himself with a sackcloth and sat on the ashes,

EWE: 7 Azɔ hã ena woɖe gbeƒã le Niniwe ɖe fia la kple eƒe amegãwo ƒe sededea nu be,“Amegbetɔwo alo lãwo, eɖanye nyi alo alẽ o, dometɔ aɖeke megade naneke nu me o.
ENGLISH: 7 and had proclamation made in Nineveh by authority of the king and his magnates “Let man and beast, cattle and sheep, not taste anything, not be pastured, and not drink water,

EWE: Womegaɖu nu loo alo ano tsi o. 8 Amegbetɔwo kple lãwo siaa nata akpanya; eye woaƒo koko na Mawu, eye woaɖe asi le woƒe zɔzɔme vɔ̃ɖi kple ŋutasẽnuwɔwɔwo ŋu.
ENGLISH: 8 and cover themselves with sackcloths, man and beast, and call out loudly to God, and turn back from their wicked ways and from their ill-gotten gains;

EWE: 9 Ðewohĩ Mawu vavã la agbugbɔ abu nu si wòɖo be yeawɔ la ŋu, eye wòaɖe asi le eƒe dɔmedzoe helĩhelĩ la ŋu be míagatsrɔ̃ o!”
ENGLISH: 9 who knows but God will turn back and repent, and desist from his anger, and we shall not perish?”

EWE: 10 Esi Mawu vavã la kpɔ nu si wowɔ, ale si woɖe asi le woƒe zɔzɔme vɔ̃ɖi la ŋu la, Mawu vavã la gbugbɔ bu vɔ̃ si wòbe yeahe vɛ la ŋu, eye megahee vɛ o.
ENGLISH: 10 And God saw their actions, that they turned back from their wicked ways, and God repented of the evil he had threatened to do to them, and did not do it.

EWE: Yona
ENGLISH: Jonah

EWE: 4 Ke esia medzɔ dzi na Yona kura o, ale dzi kui vevie.
ENGLISH: 4 And Jonah took it very hard and was angry,

EWE: 2 Eya ta edo gbe ɖa na Yehowa be: “Oo Yehowa, esia ŋu pɛ mebu esime menɔ mía de! Esia tae medo ŋgɔ si yina Tarsis ɖo; elabena menyae be Mawu veveseɖeamenula kple nublanuikpɔla nènye, mèdoa dziku kabakaba o, eye wò lɔlɔ̃ si nu metsina o sɔ gbɔ, eye vɔ̃wɔwɔ vea wò.
ENGLISH: 2 and prayed to Jehovah “Now, Jehovah, was not this what I said while I was still on my own soil? that was why I tried to head it off by getting away to Spain, because I knew you were a deity kindly and tenderhearted, patient and very friendly, and would repent of the evil.

EWE: 3 Eya ta Oo Yehowa, meɖe kuku ɖe nye agbe ɖa, elabena ne meku la, enyo wu be manɔ agbe.”
ENGLISH: 3 And now, Jehovah, take my life away, because it is better I should die than live.”

EWE: 4 Eye Yehowa biae be: “Ðe wòsɔ be nàdo dɔmedzoe nenema gbegbea?”
ENGLISH: 4 And Jehovah said “Thoroughly angry, are you?”

EWE: 5 Eye Yona do le dua me yi ɖabɔbɔ nɔ dua ƒe ɣedzeƒe gome. Etu agbadɔ ɖe afi ma be yeanɔ eƒe vɔvɔli te ahakpɔ nu si ava dzɔ ɖe dua dzi la ɖa.
ENGLISH: 5 And Jonah went out of the city and established himself out in front of the city, and made himself a booth there and sat down in the shade under it till he should see what would happen to the city.

EWE: 6 Eye Yehowa Mawu dɔ goeka aɖe be wòamie ado vɔvɔli ɖe Yona dzi, ne wòana gbɔdzɔe tso eƒe xaxa la me. Eye Yona kpɔ dzidzɔ ɖe goeka la ŋu ŋutɔ.
ENGLISH: 6 And Jehovah provided a gourd vine, and it came up over Jonah to be a shade over his head, to free him from his trouble; and Jonah was very glad for the vine.

EWE: 7 Ke esi ŋu ke, eye agu dze la, Mawu vavã la dɔ ŋɔ aɖe wòva ɖu goeka la, eye wòyrɔ.
ENGLISH: 7 And Jehovah God prepared a worm at daybreak the next day, which attacked the vine and it dried up;

EWE: 8 Esi ɣe dze la, Mawu dɔ ɣedzeƒeya xɔdzo aɖe ɖa, eye ɣe ɖu Yona ƒe ta, ale be nu te eŋu belibeli. Eye wòbia be yeaku nɔ gbɔgblɔm be, “Ne meku la, enyo wu be manɔ agbe.”
ENGLISH: 8 and when the sun rose God prepared a scorching east wind, and the sun struck on Jonah’s head, and he collapsed and asked for death and said “it is better I should die than live.”

EWE: 9 Eye Mawu bia Yona be: “Ðe wòsɔ be nàdo dɔmedzoe nenema gbegbe le goeka la taa?”
ENGLISH: 9 And God said to Jonah “Thoroughly angry about the gourd vine, are you?” and he said “I am thoroughly angry, fit to die.”

EWE: Eɖo eŋu be: “Esɔ be mado dɔmedzoe, dɔme le veyem ale gbegbe be medi be maku.” 10 Ke Yehowa gblɔ be: “Wò la, goeka si ŋu mèwɔ naneke le o, mèkpɔ edzi wòtsi o, emie le zã ɖeka me, eye wòku le zã ɖeka me la ƒe nu le vewòm.
ENGLISH: 10 And Jehovah said “You feel benevolent toward the vine, which you had not worked on nor raised, a one-night growth and a one-night loss;

EWE: 11 Ðe Niniwe, du gã si me amewo le wu ame akpe alafa ɖeka blaeve, eye womenya nyui kple vɔ̃ o, hekpe ɖe lã geɖewo ŋu, la ƒe nu mavem oa?”
ENGLISH: 11 and was I not to feel benevolent toward the great city Nineveh, in which there are more than a hundred and twenty thousand human beings that do not know their right hand from their left, and many beasts?”

EWE: Mika
ENGLISH: Micah

EWE: 1 Esiae nye Yehowa ƒe gbe si va na Mika si tso Moreset, le ŋutega si wòkpɔ ku ɖe Samaria kple Yerusalem ŋu le Yuda-fia siwo nye Yotam, Ahaz kple Hizkiya ŋɔli:
ENGLISH: 1 Jehovah’s word which came to Micah the Morashtite in the times of Kings Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah, of Judah, which he beheld against Samaria and Jerusalem.

EWE: 2 “Mi dukɔwo katã, misee! Oo anyigba kple edzinuwo katã, miƒu to anyi, Eye Yehowa si le eƒe gbedoxɔ kɔkɔe me,
ENGLISH: 2 Listen, all peoples; give attention, earth and what it holds; and let Jehovah be witness against you, the Lord out of his holy temple.

EWE: Aƒetɔ Dziɖulagã Yehowa, nanye ɖasefo ɖe mia ŋu. 3 Kpɔ ɖa, Yehowa ɖi tso enɔƒe gbɔna;
ENGLISH: 3 For here is Jehovah coming out of his place and coming down and treading on earth’s heights;

EWE: Ava zɔ anyigba ƒe kɔkɔƒewo. 4 Towo alólo gbanaa le ete, Eye baliwo afe Ahalólo abe anyixe le dzo nu ene,
ENGLISH: 4 and the mountains shall melt down under him and the vales shall split, like wax before a fire, like water spilled on a slope.

EWE: Anɔ abe ale si tsi sina ne ele aga ɖim ene. 5 Yakob ƒe aglãdzedze tae nu siawo katã dzɔ ɖo,
ENGLISH: 5 For Jacob’s crime is all this, and for the sins of the house of Israel.

EWE: Israel ƒe aƒe la ƒe nu vɔ̃wo tae. Ame ka gbɔe Yakob ƒe aglãdzedze tso? Menye Samaria ye oa?
ENGLISH: Who is Jacob’s crime? is not Samaria? and who is Judah’s heights? is not Jerusalem?

EWE: Menye Yerusalem ye oa? 6 Eya ta mana Samaria nazu glikpo atsi gbe me, Azu waingbledeƒe; Malɔ eƒe kpewo akɔ ɖe bali me,
ENGLISH: 6 And I will make of Samaria a ruin in the open country, a place to plant vineyards, and spill her stones into the valley and uncover her foundations.

EWE: Eye mana eƒe gɔmeɖokpewo natsi ƒeƒle. 7 Woagbã eƒe legbawo katã gudugudu, Eye woatɔ dzo nunana siwo katã wòkpɔ le gbolowɔwɔ me. Matsrɔ̃ eƒe trɔ̃wo katã. Elabena gbolowɔwɔ mee wòto kpɔ nu siawo,
ENGLISH: 7 And all her carvings shall be smashed, and all her tips burned down, and all her idols I will reduce to a desolation, because out of a prostitute’s tips they were gathered and to a prostitute’s tips they shall go back.

EWE: Eye gbolowoe woagatsɔ wo axe fe na.” 8 Eya ta mafa avi sesĩe ahaƒu asi nu; Maɖe ama ahazɔ afɔ ƒuƒlu. Manɔ xɔxlɔ̃m abe agbotoewo ene,
ENGLISH: 8 For this I will wail and howl, go stripped and naked; I will make a wailing like the jackals and a mourning like the ostriches,

EWE: Eye mafa konyi abe golowo ene. 9 Elabena gbedada mele eƒe abi la ŋu o. Eva ɖo keke Yuda ke.
ENGLISH: 9 because her wound is desperate, for it goes in to Judah, it reaches my people’s gate, Jerusalem.

EWE: Dɔvɔ̃ la va ɖo nye dukɔ ƒe agbo nu, eva ɖo Yerusalem. 10 “Migagblɔe le Gat o; Migafa avi kura o.
ENGLISH: 10 Do not weep; at Beth-le-ʽAphrah I have daubed myself with earth.

EWE: “Mimli le ke me le Bet-Afra. 11 Mi Safir nɔlawo, miɖe ama, eye miatso eme ava yi kple ŋukpe. Zaanan nɔlawo ya medo go o.
ENGLISH: 11 Pass, dame of Shaphir, in the shame of nakedness; Saanan’s dame is not left out; the wail at Beth-ha-Esel takes its starting-point from you.

EWE: Konyifafa axɔ Bet-Ezel, eye wòana sitsoƒe nabu ɖe mi. 12 Elabena Marot nɔlawo le mɔ kpɔm na nyui,
ENGLISH: 12 For the dame of Maroth has waited for good, when evil had come down from Jehovah to the gate of Jerusalem.

EWE: Ke vɔ̃ ye ɖi tso Yehowa gbɔ va Yerusalem ƒe agbo la nu. 13 Oo mi Lakis nɔlawo, mitsi sɔwo ɖe tasiaɖam ŋu. Miawoe nye Zion vinyɔnu ƒe nu vɔ̃ ƒe gɔmetoto,
ENGLISH: 13 Hitch up the blood-horse to the chariot, dame of Lakish; she was the beginning of sin for the daughter of Sion, because in you were discovered the crimes of Israel.

EWE: 14 Eya ta miatsɔ nunanawo ado mɔ Moreset-Gat.
ENGLISH: 14 So you shall give good-bye gifts to Moresheth-Gath.

EWE: Akzib xɔwoe flu Israel-fiawo.
ENGLISH: The houses of Aczib are a disappointment to the kings of Israel.

EWE: 15 Oo Maresa nɔlawo, magakplɔ amedziɖula la ava ƒu wò.
ENGLISH: 15 I will yet bring you your possessor, dame of Mareshah; to ʽAdullam shall Israel’s glory come.

EWE: Israel ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe la ade Adulam ke. 16 Lũ ta kokoe le viwò malɔ̃nugbɔawo ta. Lũ ta wòanɔ abe akaga tɔ ene,
ENGLISH: 16 Go bald and shorn for your delicate children, extend your baldness like a vulture, because they are deported from you.

EWE: Mika
ENGLISH: Micah

EWE: 2 “Baba na ame siwo ɖoa nu gbegblẽ wɔwɔ ɖe ta me, Ame siwo bua nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ ŋu le woƒe abawo dzi! Ne agu dze la, wowɔnɛ,
ENGLISH: 2 Ha, they who plot villainy and commit mischief on their beds, and when morning light comes they do it because they have the ability!

EWE: Elabena ŋusẽ le wo si. 2 Agble dzroa wo, eye woxɔnɛ sesẽe; Ne aƒee dzro wo la, woxɔa eya hã; Wotafaa ŋutsu xɔa eƒe aƒe,
ENGLISH: 2 and they desire fields and steal them, houses and carry them off, and victimize husband and house, man and estate.

EWE: Eye wobaa ame xɔa eƒe domenyinu. 3 Eya ta ale Yehowa gblɔe nye esi: ‘Kpɔ ɖa, meɖoe be mahe gbegblẽ ava ƒome sia dzi, eye miate ŋu asi le enu o.
ENGLISH: 3 So Jehovah says, Here I am for this clan a misfortune from which you shall not extricate your necks, and you shall not go upliftedly, because it is a bad time.

EWE: Miaganɔ zɔzɔm glodzoeglodzoe o; elabena ɣeyiɣi vɔ̃ wònye. 4 Gbe ma gbe la, amewo ado lo ɖe mia ŋu, Eye woafa konyi vevie ɖe mia ŋu. Woagblɔ be: “Wogblẽ mía dome keŋkeŋ! Ena nye dukɔ ƒe gome yi ame bubu si me kpɔ ale si wòxɔe le asinyee ɖa!
ENGLISH: 4 On that day they shall strike up a lay about you and lament a lamentable lament “Ravaged are we; he changes off my people’s portion; how it shifts away from me! to those who carry us off as slaves he divides our lands.”

EWE: Ema míaƒe agblewo na ame mawɔnuteƒewo.” 5 Eya ta ame aɖeke manɔ asiwò ada dzidzeka
ENGLISH: 5 So there shall be no one of yours who measures a line by lot in Jehovah’s assembly.

EWE: 6 Wole gbɔgblɔm be, “Midzudzɔ gbeƒãɖeɖe!
ENGLISH: 6 “Do not preach!”

EWE: Mele be woaɖe gbeƒã nya siawo o; Womado vlo mí o!”
ENGLISH: Preach or not preach, for these disgrace will not fall back.

EWE: 7 Oo Yakob ƒe aƒe, gbɔgblɔmee wole be:
ENGLISH: 7 Is the house of Jacob cursed?

EWE: “Ðe Yehowa ƒe gbɔgbɔ megagbɔa dzi ɖi oa?
ENGLISH: Has Jehovah grown impatient or are these his doings?

EWE: Ðe nye nyawo mewɔa nyui na ame siwo ƒe mɔwo le dzɔdzɔe oa?
ENGLISH: Do not my words deal kindly with him who walks right?

EWE: 8 Azɔ nye ŋutɔ nye dukɔ tso ɖe ŋunye abe futɔ ene. Mieɖe atsyɔ̃ɖonu xɔasiwo kple awuwo siaa
ENGLISH: 8 But of late my people is standing up as an enemy; you strip off robe, cloak, mantle from unsuspicious passersby as if by law of war.

EWE: Le ame siwo tso eme va yina dziɖeɖitɔe la ŋu, abe ame siwo gbɔ tso aʋa ene. 9 Mienya nye dukɔ la ƒe nyɔnuwo ɖa le woƒe aƒe siwo gbɔ womelɔ̃a nu le o la me.
ENGLISH: 9 The women of my people you expel from their dainty houses; you take my adornment forever off from their little children.

EWE: Mieɖe nye atsyɔ̃ ɖa le viawo ŋu tegbee. 10 Mitso miadzo, elabena menye gbɔɖemeƒee nye afi sia o.
ENGLISH: 10 Be off, for this is not the resting-place; owing to uncleanness you will be smitten with a baleful ruin.

EWE: Esi wòzu du makɔmakɔ ta la, woagbãe, woagbãe eteƒe makɔ o. 11 Ne ame si kplɔ ya kple alakpadada ɖo hekaa aʋatso la gblɔ be, “Magblɔ nya ɖi ku ɖe wain kple aha muame ŋu” la,
ENGLISH: 11 If a man running a course of wind and falsehood should say lyingly “I will preach wine and beer to you” he would be the preacher for this people.

EWE: Ekema eyae anye dukɔ sia ƒe nyagblɔɖila! 12 Oo Yakob, maƒo mi katã mia nu ƒu; Maƒo Israel ƒe ame susɔeawo nu ƒu godoo. Mana woanɔ anyi ɖekae, abe alẽha le alẽkpo me ene, Abe lãha le lãnyiƒe ene;
ENGLISH: 12 I will collect all Jacob, I will gather the remnant of Israel; I will put them together like sheep in a pen, they shall be a thronging mass of humanity like a flock in the middle of a corral.

EWE: Eye amewo ƒe hoowɔwɔ axɔ afi ma keŋ.’ 13 Gligbãla adze wo ŋgɔ; Woalɔ hoo ato agbo la nu ado go. Woƒe fia adze wo ŋgɔ, Eye Yehowa adze wo ŋgɔ.”
ENGLISH: 13 The burster has gone up before them; they have burst it, they have trodden out a gate and gone out by it, and their king has gone on before them and Jehovah at their head.

EWE: Mika
ENGLISH: Micah

EWE: 3 Megblɔ be: “Mi Yakob ƒe tatɔwo, Kple mi Israel ƒe aƒe ƒe kplɔlawo, meɖe kuku, misee.
ENGLISH: 3 And I said “Listen, heads of Jacob and chieftains of the house of Israel: is it not your business to know justice?

EWE: Menye miawoe wòle be mianya nu si le dzɔdzɔe oa? 2 Ke mieléa fu nyui, eye mielɔ̃a vɔ̃;
ENGLISH: 2 haters of good and lovers of evil, eaters of my people’s flesh that have stripped their skin off them and cracked up their bones

EWE: Mievuvua ayi le amewo ŋuti, eye miefloa lã le woƒe ƒuwo ŋu. 3 Mieɖua nye dukɔ ƒe lã hã,
ENGLISH: 3 and carved them as if in a kettle, like meat contained in a caldron.

EWE: Abe nu si woɖa le ze me ene, abe lãkɔ le nuɖaze me ene. 4 Ɣemaɣi la, woayɔ Yehowa be wòaxɔ na yewo, Gake matɔ na wo o. Aɣla mo ɖe wo ɣemaɣi
ENGLISH: 4 Then they will cry to Jehovah, and he will not answer them but will veil his face from them at that time because they have taken to vicious practices.

EWE: Le woƒe nuwɔna vɔ̃ɖiwo ta. 5 Ale Yehowa gblɔ ɖe nyagblɔɖila siwo kplɔa nye dukɔ tranae, Ame siwo ne woɖo aɖu nane dzi la, woɖea gbeƒã ‘Ŋutifafa!’
ENGLISH: 5 Says Jehovah about the prophets that mislead my people, that bite with their teeth and proclaim peace, and against him who does not put something in their mouths they declare a war:

EWE: Ke ne ame aɖe mede naneke nu me na wo o la, ekema wohoa aʋa ɖe eŋu lae nye esi: 6 ‘Zã gbɔna dodo ge na mi, ale be miagakpɔ ŋutega aɖeke o; Viviti le dodo ge na mi, ale be miaka afa o. Ɣe aɖo to ɖe nyagblɔɖilawo,
ENGLISH: 6 Therefore you shall have night cutting off vision and darkness cutting off soothsaying, and the sun shall go down on the prophets and the day turn black over them,

EWE: Eye ŋkeke ado viviti ɖe wo. 7 Ŋukpe alé ŋutegakpɔlawo, Eye nukalawo ƒe mo atsi dãa. Wo katã woatsyɔ nu woƒe nutage dzi,
ENGLISH: 7 and the seers shall be disappointed and the soothsayers abashed, and they shall all veil their lips, because there is no answer from God.

EWE: Elabena ŋuɖoɖo aɖeke metso Mawu gbɔ o.’” 8 Ke nye ya la, le Yehowa ƒe gbɔgbɔ ta, ŋusẽ,
ENGLISH: 8 But I am full of strength and decision and vigor to tell Jacob his crime and Israel his sin.

EWE: Ne magblɔ Yakob ƒe aglãdzedze nɛ, eye maʋu go Israel ƒe nu vɔ̃ nɛ. 9 Mi Yakob ƒe aƒe la ƒe tatɔwo Kple mi Israel ƒe aƒe la ƒe kplɔlawo, meɖe kuku, misee,
ENGLISH: 9 Listen to this, heads of the house of Jacob and chieftains of the house of Israel, that detest justice and put kinks in whatever is straight,

EWE: 10 Mi ame siwo tsɔ ʋukɔkɔɖi tsò Zion hetsɔ nu madzɔmadzɔ wɔwɔ tsò Yerusalem.
ENGLISH: 10 that build Sion by bloodshed and Jerusalem by foul play

EWE: 11 Eƒe kplɔlawo drɔ̃a ʋɔnu le zãnuxɔxɔ ta, Eƒe nunɔlawo fiaa nu le fetu ta, Eye eƒe nyagblɔɖilawo gblɔa nya ɖi le ga ta. Evɔ woziɔna ɖe Yehowa ŋu nɔa gbɔgblɔm be: “Ðe Yehowa mele mía dome oa?
ENGLISH: 11 her heads give the decision they are bribed to, and her priests the rulings they are hired to, and her prophets the predictions they get money for, and they lean on Jehovah and say “Do we not have Jehovah in our midst? no mischief will come upon us.”

EWE: Vɔ̃ aɖeke mava mía dzi o.” 12 Eya ta le miaƒe nuwɔnawo ta Woaŋlɔ Zion abe agble ene, Yerusalem azu glikpo, Eye gbedoxɔ la ƒe to azu togbɛ toave.
ENGLISH: 12 So on your account Sion shall be plowed for field land, and Jerusalem shall be ruins and the Temple Mount a height of broken rocks and scrub trees.

EWE: Mika
ENGLISH: Micah

EWE: 4 Le ŋkeke mamlɛawo me la, Yehowa ƒe aƒe ƒe to la Ali ke sesĩe ahakɔ ta agbɔ towo ŋu, Eye wòaƒo togbɛwo ta;
ENGLISH: 4 And in the future days the mountain of Jehovah’s house shall be set at the head of the mountains, lifted above hills, and peoples shall stream to it.

EWE: Eye dukɔwo aƒo zi ɖe eŋu. 2 Eye dukɔ geɖewo ava agblɔ be: “Miva míayi Yehowa ƒe to la dzi, Míayi Yakob ƒe Mawu ƒe aƒe la me. Afia eƒe mɔwo mí, Eye míazɔ eƒe toƒewo.” Elabena sedede atso Zion,
ENGLISH: 2 And many nations shall go and say “Come and let us go up to Jehovah’s mountain, to the house of the God of Jacob, to have him instruct us in ways of his that we may go in his paths,” because from Sion instruction shall go out and Jehovah’s word from Jerusalem.

EWE: Eye Yehowa ƒe nya atso Yerusalem. 3 Atso afia na dukɔ geɖewo, Eye wòatso nya me na dukɔ sesẽwo va se ɖe didiƒe ke. Woatsɔ woƒe yiwo atu agblenuwoe, Eye woatsɔ woƒe akplɔwo atu hɛ gobɛwoe. Dukɔ magatsɔ yi ɖe dukɔ ŋu azɔ o,
ENGLISH: 3 And he shall give judgment between many peoples and pronounce verdicts for numerous nations to a great distance, and they shall pound their swords into hoes and their spears into pruninghooks; nation shall not take up sword against nation, and they shall never again learn war.

EWE: Eye womagasrɔ̃ aʋawɔwɔ azɔ o. 4 Wo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe abɔbɔ nɔ eƒe wainka kple eƒe gboti te bɔkɔɔ, Eye ame aɖeke mado voɖi na wo o,
ENGLISH: 4 And they shall sit each man under his grapevine or his fig-tree with no one to alarm them, for the mouth of Jehovah of Armies has promised it;

EWE: Elabena aʋakɔwo ƒe Yehowa ƒe nue gblɔe. 5 Dukɔwo dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe azɔ le eƒe mawu ƒe ŋkɔ me,
ENGLISH: 5 because all the peoples go every man in the name of his own god, but we go in the name of our God Jehovah forever and ever.

EWE: Ke míawo ya míazɔ le Yehowa mía Mawu ƒe ŋkɔ me ɖaa tegbee. 6 Yehowa be: “Gbe ma gbe la, Maƒo ame siwo le bu tɔm la nu ƒu,
ENGLISH: 6 On that day, quoth Jehovah, I will bring in what was breaking down and bring together what was straying and what I had hurt,

EWE: Kple ame siwo mewɔ fui la nu ƒu. 7 Mana ame siwo le bu tɔm la nasusɔ, Eye ame siwo wonya ɖo ɖe didiƒe la nazu dukɔ sesẽ; Eye Yehowa aɖu fia ɖe wo dzi le Zion To la dzi,
ENGLISH: 7 and make what was breaking down into a remnant and what was ailing into a strong nation, and Jehovah shall be king over them on Mount Sion thenceforth forever.

EWE: Tso fifia yi mavɔmavɔ me. 8 Ke wò la, Oo lãhawo ƒe gbetakpɔxɔ, Wò, Zion vinyɔnu ƒe togbɛ, Dziɖuɖu gbãtɔ atrɔ ava na wò,
ENGLISH: 8 And you, Migdal-ʽEder, castle hill of the daughter of Sion, to you shall come the first dominion, a kingdom for the daughter of Jerusalem.

EWE: Ɛ̃, Yerusalem vinyɔnu ƒe fiaɖuƒe la, atrɔ ava na wò. 9 Azɔ nu ka ŋutie nèle aƒa dom ale? Ðe fia aɖeke mele mewò oa, Alo ɖe wò aɖaŋuɖola ku,
ENGLISH: 9 Now why are you raising a shout? have you no king in you, or is your counselor lost, that pangs like those of a woman in childbirth have seized you?

EWE: Hafi nèle veve sem abe nyɔnu si le ku lém enea? 10 Oo Zion vinyɔnu, ƒo togotogoe nànɔ ŋeŋem Abe nyɔnu si le ku lém ene, Elabena àʋu le dua me aɖanɔ gbe me. Eye àyi Babilon ke, Afi mae woaxɔ na wò le;
ENGLISH: 10 Be in pangs and burst out, daughter of Sion, like a woman in childbirth, for now you are to go out of town and find quarters in the fields, and come to Babylon: there you shall be rescued, there Jehovah will bring you off out of your enemies’ hands.

EWE: Afi mae Yehowa agbugbɔ wò aƒle tso wò futɔwo si me le. 11 Azɔ dukɔ geɖewo aƒo takpli ɖe ŋuwò; Eye woagblɔ be: ‘Migblẽ kɔ ɖo na Zion,
ENGLISH: 11 And now many nations have come together against you, those that say “Let her be polluted and let us gloat over Sion,”

EWE: Eye mina míaƒe ŋku nakpɔ nu si adzɔ ɖe Zion dzi.’ 12 Ke womenya Yehowa ƒe susuwo o, Womese eƒe tameɖoɖowo gɔme o;
ENGLISH: 12 not knowing Jehovah’s ideas nor understanding his plan, that he has gathered them like sheaves to a threshing-floor;

EWE: Elabena aƒo wo nu ƒu abe ale si woƒoa nukubablawo nu ƒu ɖe nukuƒoƒe ene. 13 Oo Zion vinyɔnu, tso nàfanya nu; Elabena mana wò dzo nazu gayibɔ, Eye mana wò afɔkliwo nazu akɔbli, Eye àgbã dukɔ geɖewo gudugudu;
ENGLISH: 13 stand up and thresh, daughter of Sion, for I will make your horns iron and your hoofs I will make bronze, and you shall batter many peoples to powder and devote the winnings from them to Jehovah and their wealth to the Lord of all the earth.

EWE: Mika
ENGLISH: Micah

EWE: 5 “Oo vinyɔnu si dzi futɔwo dze, Èle ɖokuiwò sim azɔ; Woɖe to ɖe mí.
ENGLISH: 5 Now let the daughter of Gedor fence herself, they have laid siege to us; with a rod they will beat the judge of Israel on the Jawbone.

EWE: Wotsɔ ati ƒo tome na Israel ƒe ʋɔnudrɔ̃la la. 2 Oo wò, Betlehem Efrata, Wò, si le sue akpa be woabu ɖe Yuda ƒe duwo dome la, Mewòe ame si anye dziɖula le Israel la ado tso nam,
ENGLISH: 2 And you, Beth-Ephratha, tiniest among the thousand of Judah, out of you shall come one to be ruler in Israel, his origins being from of old, from ancient days.

EWE: Ame si dzɔɣi tso blemablema ke, tso gbe aɖe gbe ʋĩi ke. 3 Eya ta Mawu atsɔ wo ade asi
ENGLISH: 3 So he will give them up till the time that one has borne a child.

EWE: Eye dziɖula la nɔvi mamlɛawo atrɔ agbɔ va Israel-viwo gbɔ.
ENGLISH: And the rest of his brothers shall come back to the sons of Israel.

EWE: 4 Atso, eye wòakplɔ wo le Yehowa ƒe ŋusẽ Kple eƒe Mawu Yehowa ƒe ŋkɔ ƒe gãnyenye me. Eye woanɔ anyi dedie,
ENGLISH: 4 And he shall stand and shepherd in Jehovah’s might and in the pride of the name of his God Jehovah; and they shall be settled, for then shall he be great to the ends of the earth.

EWE: Elabena eƒe gãnyenye ade anyigba ƒe mlɔenu ke. 5 Ahe ŋutifafa vɛ. Ne Asiriatɔ la va míaƒe anyigba dzi, eye wòɖo afɔ míaƒe mɔ́ sesẽwo me la,
ENGLISH: 5 (And this shall be peace: when Assyria comes into our country and treads on our soil, we shall set up against him seven shepherds and eight dukes of men,

EWE: Míawo hã míadɔ lãkplɔvi adre, ɛ̃, amegã enyi tso amegbetɔviwo dome ɖe eŋu. 6 Woatsɔ yi ɖe Asiria-nyigba la
ENGLISH: 6 and they will shepherd Assyria’s country with swords and Nimrod’s country with falchions.)

EWE: Kple Nimrod ƒe anyigba la ŋu le eƒe agbowo nu. Eye ne Asiriatɔ la va míaƒe anyigba dzi,
ENGLISH: And he shall deliver us from Assyria when it comes into our country and treads on our territory.

EWE: Eye wòɖo afɔ míaƒe nutoa me la, aɖe mí tso esi me. 7 Yakob ƒe ame mamlɛawo anɔ dukɔ geɖewo dome, Abe zãmu tso Yehowa gbɔ Kple tsidzadza ɖe gbe dzi, Si mekpɔa ame aɖeke sinu o,
ENGLISH: 7 And in the midst of many peoples the remnant of Jacob shall be like dew from Jehovah, like showers on herbage, that does not await a man nor stand waiting for human beings; and among the nations,

EWE: Eye melalaa amegbetɔviwo o la ene. 8 Yakob ƒe ame mamlɛawo anɔ dukɔwo dome, Woanɔ ameha geɖewo dome Abe dzata le gbemelãwo dome ene, Abe dzatatsui si ne eto alẽhawo dome la, Wòdzea nu dzi hevuvua nu,
ENGLISH: 8 in the midst of many peoples, the remnant of Jacob shall be like a lion among game in the badlands, like a two-year-old lion among flocks of sheep, which, if it passes, pounces and makes its kill and nobody can rescue.

EWE: Ke xɔnametɔ aɖeke menɔa anyi o la ene. 9 Woado wò alɔ ɖe dzi ɖe wò ketɔwo ŋu,
ENGLISH: 9 Your hand shall go high over your foes, and all your enemies shall be extirpated.

EWE: Eye woatsrɔ̃ wò futɔwo katã.” 10 Yehowa be: “Gbe ma gbe la,
ENGLISH: 10 And on that day, quoth Jehovah, I will extirpate your ponies from your midst and destroy your chariots,

EWE: Matsrɔ̃ wò sɔwo le dowòme, eye magblẽ wò tasiaɖamwo. 11 Matsrɔ̃ duwo le wò anyigba dzi,
ENGLISH: 11 and extirpate the cities of your country and demolish your fortresses,

EWE: Eye magbã wò mɔ́ sesẽwo katã aƒu anyi. 12 Matɔ te wò dzosasa,
ENGLISH: 12 and I will extirpate the witchcraft you ply and you shall have no fortune-tellers,

EWE: Eye akunyawɔla aɖeke maganɔ mewò o. 13 Matsrɔ̃ wò legbawo kple wò trɔ̃sɔtiwo le dowòme,
ENGLISH: 13 and I will extirpate your carvings and obelisks out of your midst and you shall no longer do reverence to the work of your hands,

EWE: Eye màgade ta agu na wò asinudɔwɔwɔwo azɔ o. 14 Maho wò Aserawo ɖa le dowòme,
ENGLISH: 14 and I will uproot your asherahs out of your midst and stamp out your idols.

EWE: Eye matsrɔ̃ wò duwo. 15 Mabia hlɔ̃ dukɔ siwo meɖo tom o la Le dɔmedzoe kple dziku me.”
ENGLISH: 15 And in anger and resentment I will take vengeance on all the nations that have not listened.

EWE: Mika
ENGLISH: Micah

EWE: 6 Meɖe kuku, mise nya si gblɔm Yehowa le. Tso, nàtsɔ wò nya va towo gbɔ,
ENGLISH: 6 Listen to what Jehovah is saying: “Stand up, upbraid the mountains and let the hills hear your voice.

EWE: Eye na togbɛwo nase wò gbe. 2 Mi towo, mise Yehowa ƒe ʋɔnunya, Mi anyigba ƒe agunuwo hã misee, Elabena nya le Yehowa kple eƒe dukɔ la dome;
ENGLISH: 2 Listen, mountains, to Jehovah’s upbraiding, and give ear, foundations of earth, because Jehovah has a case against his people and is having it out with Israel.

EWE: Israel ye wòle nya he ge kplii: 3 “Nye dukɔ, nu kae mewɔ wò? Eye fu kae meɖe na wò?
ENGLISH: 3 My people, what have I done to you and how have I overtasked you? testify against me.

EWE: Ðo eŋu nam. 4 Elabena mekplɔ wò tso Egipte-nyigba dzi, Meɖe wò tso kluviƒe me;
ENGLISH: 4 For I brought you up out of Egypt and ransomed you out of the slave-quarters, and sent before you Moses, Aaron, and Miriam.

EWE: Medɔ Mose, Aron kple Miriam wodze ŋgɔwò. 5 Oo nye dukɔ, meɖe kuku ɖo ŋku nu si Moab-fia Balak ɖo be yeawɔ, Kple ale si Bileam, Beor vi, ɖo eŋu nɛ la dzi Ðo ŋku nu siwo dzɔ tso Sitim va se ɖe Gilgal Ale be nàdze si Yehowa ƒe nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔwo.” 6 Nu kae matsɔ ɖe asi ado ɖe Yehowa ŋkume, Ava de ta agu na Mawu dziƒoʋĩtɔ la? Ðe matsɔ numevɔsa blibowo
ENGLISH: 5 My people, remember what King Balak of Moab proposed and what answer Balaam the son of Be’or gave him, and from the Acacias to the Gilgal, in order to know Jehovah’s loyal work.” 6 With what shall I advance to Jehovah, pay homage to the transcendent God? shall I advance to him with burnt-offerings, with yearling calves?

EWE: Kple nyivi siwo xɔ ƒe ɖeka la ɖe asi ado ɖe eŋkumea? 7 Ðe agbo akpewo Kple amitɔʋu akpe nanewo adze Yehowa ŋua? Ðe matsɔ nye ŋgɔgbeviŋutsu ana ɖe nye dzidadawo ta
ENGLISH: 7 will Jehovah accept thousands of rams, millions of rivers of oil? shall I give my eldest son for my crime, the fruit of my wife for the sin of my soul?

EWE: Kple nye dɔmevi ana ɖe nye nu vɔ̃ taa? 8 Oo amegbetɔ, egblɔ nu si nyo la na wò. Eye nu ka dim Yehowa le tso asiwò? Eya koe nye be nàwɔ nu dzɔdzɔe, nàlɔ̃ nu si le eteƒe la wɔwɔ,
ENGLISH: 8 He has told you, man, what is good; and what does Jehovah demand from you but to do justice and love friendliness and walk sanely with your God?

EWE: Eye nàbɔbɔ ɖokuiwò ɖe anyi ahazɔ kple wò Mawu! 9 Yehowa le du la yɔm; Ame si si nunya vavãtɔ le la avɔ̃ wò ŋkɔ.
ENGLISH: 9 Hark, it is Jehovah’s voice as he calls out to the city and sets forth good sense, saying “Listen, tribe and meeting of the city:

EWE: Miɖo to ameƒoti la kple ame si dɔe la. 10 Ðe kesinɔnu madzɔmadzɔ
ENGLISH: 10 am I to forget the wrong-doer’s house, ill-gotten hoards and a detestable short bushel?

EWE: Kple efa nudzidzenu si mede o, si nyɔ ŋu gale ame vɔ̃ɖi ƒe aƒe me kokokoa? 11 Ðe ŋunye akɔ ne nudanu amebatɔ
ENGLISH: 11 am I to clear him for wrongful scales and a bag of cheating weights?

EWE: Kple nudakpe ameflutɔ le nye akplo mea? 12 Elabena ŋutasesẽ yɔ eƒe kesinɔtɔwo fũu, Eye dua me nɔlawo kaa aʋatso;
ENGLISH: 12 city whose rich men are full of outrage and its inhabitants talk falsehoods and the tongues in their mouths are all disloyalty!

EWE: Alakpaɖe le nu me na wo. 13 “Eya ta maƒo wò ade abi ŋuwò,
ENGLISH: 13 And I on my part have dealt you devastatingly prostrating blows for your sins.

EWE: Eye mana nàzu aƒedo le wò nu vɔ̃wo ta. 14 Àɖu nu, ke màɖi ƒo o; Wò dɔme aɖi gbɔlo. Àlɔ nuwo adzra ɖo, ke màte ŋu akpɔ wo ta woanɔ dedie o,
ENGLISH: 14 You are to eat and not have your hunger satisfied, and it will give you the colic; and to displace and not bring safe off, and what you do bring off I will give to the sword.

EWE: Eye nu si nètsɔ dzoe la, matsɔe ade asi na yi. 15 Àƒã nu, ke màŋe nu o. Àɖa ami, ke màkpɔ ami azã o;
ENGLISH: 15 You are to sow and not reap; you are to tread olives and not rub yourself with oil, and grape-juice and not drink wine.

EWE: Eye àfiã wain hã, ke makpɔ wain ano o. 16 Elabena miewɔa Omri ƒe ɖoɖowo dzi eye miewɔa Ahab ƒe aƒe ƒe nuwɔnawo katã, Eye miezɔna ɖe woƒe adaŋudedewo nu. Esia ta mana nàzu ŋɔdzinu, Woalia aku ɖe dua me tɔwo ŋu; Eye dukɔwo ƒe vlodoame anɔ dziwò.”
ENGLISH: 16 And you observe ʽOmri’s usages and every fabrication of Ahab’s house, and go by their plans, so as to have me make you a desolation and its inhabitants a whistling, and have you bear the taunts of peoples.”

EWE: Mika
ENGLISH: Micah

EWE: 7 Baba nam! Elabena mele abe Ale si wònɔna ne woxa dzomeŋɔlikutsetsewo Eye wofɔ waintsetse siwo woxa la ƒe susɔewo vɔ ene, Waintsetse aɖeke meli woaɖu o,
ENGLISH: 7 Woe is me, for I am like fruit-harvest time, like after-picking time in the vintage: there is no cluster to eat, I hanker after a rare-ripe fig.

EWE: Eye gbotsetse ŋgɔgbea si dzroam aɖeke meli o! 2 Nuteƒewɔlawo nu yi le anyigba la dzi; Ame dzɔdzɔe aɖeke mele amegbetɔwo dome o. Wo katã wode xa ɖi ɖe ʋukɔkɔɖi ŋu.
ENGLISH: 2 Godly men are lost from the earth, and there is not an upright person among mankind; they are all watching their chance for bloodshed, they are each trying to get his brother in a net.

EWE: Ame sia ame ɖo ɖɔ na nɔvia. 3 Woƒe asi bi ɖe nu vɔ̃ɖi wɔwɔ me; Amegã dia viɖe, Ʋɔnudrɔ̃la drɔ̃a ʋɔnu ɖe fetu ta, Ame ŋkuta gblɔa nu si dzronɛ,
ENGLISH: 3 They have put their hands in good shape for bad work; the general is soliciting and the judge is acting for a consideration, and the great man is asserting his own personal desire,

EWE: Eye wosɔa nu wɔnɛ. 4 Ame nyuitɔ si le wo dome le abe ŋù ene,
ENGLISH: 4 and they twist the good into the tangle like bushes too straight for a hedge.

EWE: Wò gbetakpɔlawo ƒe ŋkeke, si nye wò akɔntanagbe ava. Ekema amewo atɔtɔ keŋ.
ENGLISH: On the day of your lookouts your punishment is coming; now will be their bewilderment.

EWE: 5 Migaxɔ miaƒe zɔhɛ dzi se o. Alo aɖo ŋu ɖe mia xɔlɔ̃ vevi ŋu o.
ENGLISH: 5 Do not trust a friend, do not rely on a chum, guard the frontier of your mouth against the mate that rests in your arms;

EWE: Nya nuƒoƒo le ame si le wò akɔnu la gbɔ. 6 Elabena viŋutsu doa vlo fofoa, Vinyɔnu tsona ɖe dadaa ŋu, Lɔ̃xoyɔvi tsona ɖe lɔ̃xoa ŋu;
ENGLISH: 6 for son cheapens father, daughter stands up against mother, daughter-in-law against mother-in-law, a man’s enemies are the men of his house.

EWE: Ame ƒe futɔwo nye eƒe aƒemetɔwo. 7 Ke nye la, manɔ ŋu tsam na Yehowa.
ENGLISH: 7 But I will watch for Jehovah, wait for the God of my salvation; my God will hear me.

EWE: Nye Mawu aɖo tom. 8 Oo nye futɔ, mèganɔ dzidzɔ kpɔm le tanye o. Togbɔ be medze anyi hã la, magafɔ;
ENGLISH: 8 Do not be glad for me, enemy; when I fall I get up, when I sit in the dark Jehovah gives me light.

EWE: Togbɔ be mele viviti me hã la, Yehowa anye kekeli nam. 9 Mewɔ nu vɔ̃ ɖe Yehowa ŋu, Eya ta mado dzi atsɔ eƒe dziku,
ENGLISH: 9 I will bear Jehovah’s displeasure, because I have sinned against him, till he champions my rights and does justice for me.

EWE: Va se ɖe esime wòadrɔ̃ nye nya ahatso afia dzɔdzɔe nam. Akplɔm ado ɖe kekeli nu;
ENGLISH: He will bring me out to the light; I shall feast my eyes on his loyal work,

EWE: Makpɔ eƒe dzɔdzɔenyenye. 10 Nye futɔ hã akpɔe,
ENGLISH: 10 and my enemy shall see it and shame shall cover her, she who is saying to me “Where is your God Jehovah?”

EWE: Eye ŋu akpe ame si gblɔ nam be: “Afi kae Yehowa wò Mawu la le?” Nye ŋkuwo akpɔ nyɔnu la.
ENGLISH: My eyes shall see her fate; now she shall become a trampled thing like street mud.

EWE: Azɔ woafanyae abe ba le kpɔdomee ene. 11 Anye ŋkeke si woaɖo wò gliwo,
ENGLISH: 11 There is a day for building your fences; that day limits shall be far off;

EWE: Gbe ma gbe la, woakeke wò liƒowo ɖe enu. 12 Amewo atso keke Asiria kple Egipte duwo me Ava gbɔwò gbe ma gbe,
ENGLISH: 12 that is a day when your gems shall come in, from Assyria to Egypt and from Egypt to the River;

EWE: Tso atsiaƒu nu yi atsiaƒu nu, tso to ɖeka gbɔ yi bubu gbɔ. 13 Anyigba la aɖi gbɔlo le edzinɔlawo ta,
ENGLISH: 13 and the earth shall become a desolation on account of its inhabitants, out of the fruit of their practices.

EWE: Le woƒe nuwɔnawo me tsonuwo ta. 14 Tsɔ wò atikplɔ kplɔ wò dukɔ, alẽha si nye wò domenyinu Si le eɖokui si le ave me, le atikutsetsebɔ me.
ENGLISH: 14 Pasture your people with your staff, the sheep that are your estate, dwellers in the solitude of the bush, in the midst of Carmel; let them pasture Bashan and Gilead as in days of yore;

EWE: Na woaɖu gbe le Basan kple Gilead abe le blemaŋkekewo me ene. 15 “Mana wòakpɔ nukunuwo
ENGLISH: 15 as in the days of your coming out of Egypt show us wonders.

EWE: Abe le ŋkeke siwo me nèʋu tso Egipte-nyigba dzi ene. 16 Dukɔwo akpɔ nu siawo, eye ŋu akpe wo, togbɔ be ŋusẽ geɖe le wo ŋu hã. Woatsɔ asi aɖo nu;
ENGLISH: 16 Let nations see and be ashamed of all their might; let them lay hand on mouth, let their ears be dumb.

EWE: Eye woƒe to aku. 17 Woaɖuɖɔ kewɔ abe dawo ene; Ŋɔdzi alé wo woasi ado tso woƒe bebeƒewo abe nu gbagbe siwo tana le anyigba dzi ene. Woanɔ ƒoƒom kpakpakpa ava Yehowa mía Mawu la gbɔ,
ENGLISH: 17 Let them lick dust like a snake, like crawlers of the earth let them wriggle out of their coverts; to our God Jehovah let them come in dread, and be afraid of you.

EWE: Eye woavɔ̃ wò.” 18 Mawu kae le abe wò ene, Wò ame si tsɔa vodada kena, eye mèléa ŋku ɖe wò domenyinu mamlɛa ƒe dzidada ŋu o? Malé dɔmedzoe ɖi ɖikaa o, Elabena amenuveve nyoa eŋu.
ENGLISH: 18 Who is a deity like you, pardoning guilt and passing over crime for the remnant of his estate, not holding his anger forever, because he takes pleasure in friendliness;

EWE: 19 Agakpɔ nublanui na mí; axɔ ŋusẽ le míaƒe vodadawo si.
ENGLISH: 19 coming back to his tenderness for us, conquering our guilt?

EWE: Àtsɔ woƒe nu vɔ̃wo katã aƒu gbe ɖe atsiaƒu ƒe gogloeƒe.
ENGLISH: You will throw all our sins into the oozy deeps of the sea,

EWE: 20 Àwɔ nuteƒe na Yakob, Eye àve Abraham nu, Abe ale si nèka atam na mía tɔgbuiwo tso blemaŋkekewo me ene.
ENGLISH: 20 you will accord to Jacob the loyalty, to Abraham the friendship, that you swore to our fathers from of old.

EWE: Nahum
ENGLISH: Nahum

EWE: 1 Nya ɖe Niniwe ŋu: Elkostɔ Nahum ƒe ŋutegagbalẽ:
ENGLISH: 1 The boding for Nineveh; the book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.

EWE: 2 Yehowa nye Mawu si biaa ɖokuitsɔtsɔna blibo, eye wòbiaa hlɔ̃; Yehowa biaa hlɔ̃, eye wòdoa dɔmedzoe. Yehowa biaa hlɔ̃ eƒe futɔwo,
ENGLISH: 2 Jehovah is a jealous deity and takes revenge; Jehovah takes revenge and is fierce in temper; Jehovah takes revenge on his foes and bears his enemies in mind.

EWE: Eye wòléa dɔmedzoe ɖi na eƒe futɔwo. 3 Yehowa medoa dziku kabakaba o, eye ŋusẽ gã le esi,
ENGLISH: 3 Jehovah is patient and powerful, and Jehovah does not acquit an offender.

EWE: Ke Yehowa magbe tohehe ne ehiã o. Eƒe mɔ to ya ʋuduʋudu kple ahom me,
ENGLISH: His walk is in gale and tempest, and clouds are the dust of his feet;

EWE: Eye alilikpo dodowo le abe ʋuʋudedi ene le eƒe afɔ te. 4 Ebluna ɖe atsiaƒu ta wòmiena; Enana tɔsisiwo katã me tsiwo miena. Basan kple Karmel yrɔ,
ENGLISH: 4 He speaks sternly to the sea and dries it out, and dries off all the rivers; Bashan wilts, and Carmel, and the young leafage of Lebanon stands forlorn.

EWE: Eye Libanon seƒoƒowo yrɔ. 5 Towo ʋuʋu le eta, Eye togbɛwo lólo gbanaa. Anyigba adzo kpekpekpe le eŋkume,
ENGLISH: 5 The mountains quake at him, and the hills surge, And the earth is in commotion before him, the world and all who inhabit it.

EWE: Anyigba la kple edzinɔlawo katã. 6 Ame kae ate ŋu anɔ te ɖe eƒe dziku nu?
ENGLISH: 6 Before his hostility who may stand, and who stand up amid the heat of his anger?

EWE: Atrɔ eƒe dziku aƒo ɖi abe dzo ene, Eye agakpewo akaka le eta.
ENGLISH: His choler is like a stream of fire, and the rocks break down before him.

EWE: 7 Yehowa nyo, mɔ́ sesẽ wònye le xaxagbe. Enya ame siwo sinɛ tsona.
ENGLISH: 7 Jehovah is good for a citadel in the day of distress; Jehovah knows those who take refuge in him,

EWE: 8 Atsɔ tsiɖɔɖɔ atsrɔ̃ du ma ɖa keŋkeŋ,
ENGLISH: 8 and carries them through cloudbursts.

EWE: Eye viviti anya eƒe futɔwo ɖe nu.
ENGLISH: He makes a finish of those who stand up against him, and chases his enemies into darkness.

EWE: 9 Nugbe kae miaɖo ɖe Yehowa ŋu? Ele nu tsrɔ̃ ge keŋkeŋ.
ENGLISH: 9 What do you plan against Jehovah? he is making a finish;distress will not stand up twice;

EWE: Xaxa mado ta ɖa zi evelia o. 10 Elabena woɖo wo nɔewo me abe aŋɔka ene, Eye wole abe ame siwo mu aha ene;
ENGLISH: 10 for even briers matted in a tangle, and soaked as they can be, will be eaten up like stubble fully dry.

EWE: Ke hã, woafiã keŋkeŋ abe ahɔ̃liti ƒuƒu ene. 11 Mewòe ame si ɖo nugbe ɖe Yehowa ŋu,
ENGLISH: 11 Out of you came one who planned mischief against Jehovah, who proposed a vicious policy.

EWE: Eye wòɖoa aɖaŋu gbɔlo la, ado tso. 12 Ale Yehowa gblɔe nye esi: “Togbɔ be ŋusẽ le wo ŋu ale gbegbe, eye wosɔ gbɔ taŋtaŋ hã la, Woalã wo ɖa; wo nu ayi.
ENGLISH: 12 Says Jehovah, If waters gush out and rage withal, so do they subside and pass off; I did grind you down, I will not again.

EWE: Mana nàkpe fu, ke emegbe nyemagana nàkpe fu azɔ o. 13 Azɔ maŋe eƒe kɔkuti ɖa le dziwò,
ENGLISH: 13 And now I will break his yoke-bow off from you and snap your tether.

EWE: Eye matso eƒe kawo le ŋuwò. 14 Se si Yehowa de ɖe ŋuwòe nye esi: ‘Dzidzime aɖeke madzɔ tso wò ŋkɔ me azɔ o. Matsrɔ̃ legbawo kple galegbawo ɖa le wò mawuwo ƒe me.
ENGLISH: 14 And Jehovah will give a commission against you: there shall not again be any of your name engendered; out of the house of your gods I will eradicate carving and casting; I will make your grave a dunghill.

EWE: Maɖe yɔdo na wò, elabena ènyɔ ŋu.’ 15 Kpɔ ɖa! Du nyui xɔla, ame si ɖea gbeƒã ŋutifafa, Ƒe afɔwoe nye ema ɖo towo dzi. Oo Yuda, ɖu wò ŋkekenyuiwo, wɔ wò adzɔgbeɖeɖewo dzi, Elabena yakame aɖeke magava to mewò azɔ o. Woatsrɔ̃e ɖa keŋkeŋ.”
ENGLISH: 15 There on the mountains are the feet of a messenger of good news, a herald of peace: celebrate your feasts, Judah, pay your vows, for never again shall the reprobates pass through you, they are done with, they are extinct.

EWE: Nahum
ENGLISH: Nahum

EWE: 2 Ame si kaa amewo hlẽna la va ƒo ɖe dziwò. Dzɔ mɔ́ sesẽawo ŋu. Nɔ mɔ dzi kpɔm.
ENGLISH: 2 A hammer has come in your face: mount guard, keep a lookout on roads, brace waists, rally strength to the utmost.

EWE: Bla ali dzi, dzra ɖo kple wò ŋusẽ katã. 2 Elabena Yehowa agbugbɔ Yakob ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe aɖo te Wòanɔ abe Israel ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe ene, Elabena nuhalawo ha wo;
ENGLISH: 2 For Jehovah has brought back Jacob’s pride like Israel’s, because riflers had rifled them and had wrecked their branches.

EWE: Eye wotsrɔ̃ woƒe wainkawo. 3 Eƒe kalẽtɔwo ƒe akpoxɔnu biã hɛ̃, Eƒe aʋawɔlawo le awu dzĩ helĩhelĩ me. Eƒe tasiaɖamŋugawo le dzo dam Le aʋakpablagbe,
ENGLISH: 3 His champions’ shields are reddened, stalwart men in scarlet; steel was softened in fire on the day of his making ready, and cypresses were made to reel.

EWE: Eye wole akplɔ siwo wotsɔ sesewuti kpa la nyèm. 4 Tasiaɖamwo le zi nyèm le kpɔdomeewo. Wole du dzi le yiyim le gbɔgbɔm le ablɔwo me.
ENGLISH: 4 In the open the chariots are running wild, they are hurtling through the suburbs; their look is like torches, they shoot along like lightning-flashes.

EWE: Wole keklẽm abe akakatiwo ene hele dzo dam abe dzikedzowo ene. 5 Fia la ayɔ eƒe amegãwo. Woanɔ nu klim anɔ yiyim.
ENGLISH: 5 He remembers his heroes; they stumble in their going; they hurry to the wall and the barricade is got ready.

EWE: Woɖo mɔxenu la ɖi. 6 Tɔsisiawo ƒe agbowo aʋu,
ENGLISH: 6 The river gates are opened and the palace collapses,

EWE: Eye fiasã la alólo. 7 Wotso nya me xoxo: Woklo nu le eŋu, Wokplɔe yi aboyo me, eye eƒe kosiwo fa konyi;
ENGLISH: 7 and madame is made to stand exposed, with her slave-girls droning like pigeons’ notes, drumming on their chests.

EWE: Wole xɔxlɔ̃m abe ahɔnɛwo ene, eye wole akɔta ƒom. 8 Niniwe le abe ta si tsi yɔ fũu ene tso edzɔɣi; Ke azɔ la, wole sisim. Wodo ɣli be, “Mitɔ! Mitɔ!”
ENGLISH: 8 And Nineveh is like a reservoir of water with its water running out; “stop, stop,” but no one turns his face.

EWE: Gake ame aɖeke menyè kɔ o. 9 Miha klosalo; miha sika! Elabena kesinɔnuwo sɔ gbɔ taŋtaŋ.
ENGLISH: 9 Plunder silver, plunder gold, and there is no end of the supply, fortunes in every kind of choice article.

EWE: Nu vevi vovovoawo sɔ gbɔ ɖe eme fũu. 10 Woɖi gbɔlo dua, eye wòtsi ƒuƒlu hezu aƒedo! Vɔvɔ̃ na dziwo lólo gbanaa, klowo tɔ gu, eye aliwo katã le ƒoƒom,
ENGLISH: 10 Clearing out, cleaning out, clawing out, and hearts melting down and knees giving way and cramps in all backs, and all their faces are contorted.

EWE: Mowo katã da tu. 11 Afi kae dzatawo nɔƒe, si dzatatsuiwo ɖua nu le, Afi si dzata dona tso hekplɔa viawo,
ENGLISH: 11 Where is the lions’ lair, that was feeding-place for the two-year-olds, where walked lion, lioness, lion’s cub with no one to alarm it?

EWE: Eye ame aɖeke medoa voɖi na wo o la le? 12 Dzata vuvua nu ale si nu ade viawo nu, Eye wòmiaa ve na lãwo tsɔ vanɛ na eƒe dzatanɔwo.
ENGLISH: 12 the lion tore up as much as his cubs wanted and broke necks for his lionesses, and filled his holes with prey and his lairs with carcasses.

EWE: 13 “Kpɔ ɖa, metso ɖe ŋuwò,” aʋakɔwo ƒe Yehowa ye gblɔe,
ENGLISH: 13 Have at you, quoth Jehovah of Armies!

EWE: Wò dzatatsuiwo atsi yi nu. Mana wò nuléle nu natso le anyigba dzi, Eye womagase wò ame dɔdɔwo ƒe gbe azɔ o.”
ENGLISH: I will smoke out your thicket, and swords shall eat up your two-year-olds, and I will rid earth of your kills, and the sound of your roar shall not be heard again.

EWE: Nahum
ENGLISH: Nahum

EWE: 3 Baba na du si kɔa ʋu ɖi la. Amebeble kple adzodada yɔe fũu.
ENGLISH: 3 Ha, bloody city, all trickery, full of prey, never without a kill!

EWE: Nuléle mevɔna le eme gbeɖe o! 2 Sɔƒokawo ŋkɔ le ɖiɖim, tasiaɖamfɔwo ƒe hoowɔwɔ le ɖiɖim,
ENGLISH: 2 Hark, a sound of whips, a sound of wheels jarring, and galloping ponies and jumping chariot!

EWE: Sɔwo tsɔ du, eye tasiaɖamwo le du dzi. 3 Sɔdolawo de sɔ dzi, yiwo le dzo dam, akplɔwo le dzo sim, Aʋatsilawo sɔ gbɔ eteƒe mekɔ o, eye ame kukuwo li kɔ ɖi gleglegle, Seƒe meli na ame kukuwo o.
ENGLISH: 3 rearing horse and flame of sword and lightning of spear and multitudes of dying and masses of corpses; there is no end of the bodies, they stumble on the bodies,

EWE: Wole ame kukuwo klim. 4 Esia dzɔ le gbolo la ƒe gbolowɔwɔ vivivo ta, Eya si nye nyɔnu dzetugbe si blea ame nu, eye wònye dzosala bibi,
ENGLISH: 4 for the multitudinous debaucheries of the handsome prostitute, mistress of witchcraft, who blotted out nations with her debaucheries and clans with her witchcraft.

EWE: 5 Aʋakɔwo ƒe Yehowa be, “Kpɔ ɖa!
ENGLISH: 5 Have at you, quoth Jehovah!

EWE: Maklo avɔ le ŋuwò akɔ ɖe mo na wò, Mana dukɔwo nakpɔ wò ama, Eye fiaɖuƒewo nakpɔ wò ŋukpeƒe.
ENGLISH: I will turn your skirts up over your face and let nations see your nakedness and clans your ignominy,

EWE: 6 Malɔ gbeɖuɖɔ akɔ ɖe ŋuwò, Eye maɖi gbɔ wò;
ENGLISH: 6 and I will throw carrion over you and make you an object of disdain and a spectacle.

EWE: Mana nàzu nukpɔkpɔ. 7 Ame sia ame si akpɔ wò la asi le gbɔwò agblɔ be: ‘Wogbã Niniwe! Ame kae afa nɛ?’
ENGLISH: 7 And everyone that sees you shall make off, and say “Nineveh is smitten! who is to lament her? where shall I look for comforters for you?”

EWE: Afi kae makpɔ akɔfalawo le na wò? 8 Wòe nyo wu No-Amon, si bɔbɔ nɔ Nil-tɔʋuwo toa? Tsi ƒo xlãe godoo;
ENGLISH: 8 Are you to be better than Amon’s Thebes, seated on the branching Nile with water around her, whose wall was a bulwark of sea, consisted of sea;

EWE: Atsiaƒue nye eƒe kesinɔnu, eye atsiaƒue nye gli nɔ eŋu. 9 Etiopia kple Egipte nye eƒe ŋusẽ triakɔ, si teƒe mekɔ o.
ENGLISH: 9 whose forces the Nubians were, and the Egyptians, no end of them; whose auxiliaries were Put and the Libyans?

EWE: Put kple Libiatɔwoe xɔna nɛ. 10 Ke hã woɖe aboyoe; Eyi aboyo me. Wotsɔ viawo hã xlã ɖe nu le kpɔdomeewo ƒe dzogoewo katã dzi. Wodzidze nu ɖe eƒe bubumewo dzi,
ENGLISH: 10 She too went to slavery in exile; she too had children’s brains dashed out at every street-end, and over her aristocrats they threw lots and all her great men were chained in fetters.

EWE: Eye wode kunyowu eƒe amegãwo katã. 11 Wò hã àmu aha; Àyi aɖabe.
ENGLISH: 11 You too shall overdrink and be stupefied; you too shall hunt for a refuge from an enemy.

EWE: Eye àdi sitsoƒe tso futɔ la nu. 12 Wò nɔƒe sesẽwo katã le abe gboti siwo dzi kutsetse ɖiɖi gbãtɔwo le ene;
ENGLISH: 12 All your fortresses are trees with rareripe figs, if they are shaken they drop into an eater’s mouth;

EWE: Ne woʋuʋu wo la, woage ɖe eɖula ƒe nu me. 13 Kpɔ ɖa! Wò aʋakɔwo le abe nyɔnuwo ene le dowòme. Wò anyigba ƒe agbowo aʋu gbadzaa na wò futɔwo.
ENGLISH: 13 you find your people women in you; the gates of your country are thrown open to your enemies, fire has consumed your bars.

EWE: Dzo afiã wò agbowo ƒe gametiwo. 14 Du tsi kɔ ɖi, elabena wole to ɖe ge ɖe wò! Na wò nɔƒe sesẽwo nagasẽ ɖe edzi. Ge ɖe agbi me nànya anyi;
ENGLISH: 14 Draw yourself water for a siege; strengthen your fortresses; get into the mud and trample clay, handle a brick-mold;

EWE: Na kpetsonu nasɔ gbe. 15 Le afi ma gɔ̃ hã la, dzo afiã wò, Yi atsrɔ̃ wò. Aɖu wò abe ale si ʋetrawo ɖua nui ene.
ENGLISH: 15 there fire will consume you, swords will make an end of you, they will eat you up like marching grasshoppers.

EWE: Ɛ̃, ƒo wò amewo nu ƒu miasɔ gbɔ kpaŋkpaŋ abe ʋetsuviwo ene! 16 Èna wò asitsalawo sɔ gbɔ wu dziƒoɣletiviwo.
ENGLISH: 16 Come on in masses like marching grasshoppers, come on in masses like flying grasshoppers; you have drawn more traders than there are stars in the sky the hoppers cast their skins and take wing.

EWE: Ke ʋetrawo ɖea tsro hedzona dzona. 17 Ŋuwòdzɔlawo le abe ʋetsuvi ene, Eye wò asrafomegãwo le abe ʋetsuviwo ƒe ha ene. Wodze ɖe glikpɔwo ŋu le gbe si gbe vuvɔ le wɔwɔm. Gake ne ɣe dze ko la, wodzona dzona;
ENGLISH: 17 Your policemen are like grasshoppers and your clerks like young grasshoppers that camp in the hedges on a cold day; the sun is up and off they go, and there is no knowing what place they were in.

EWE: Eye ame aɖeke menyaa afi si wole o. 18 Oo Asiria-fia, wò lãkplɔviwo le akɔlɔ̃e dɔm; Wò bubumewo tsi wo nɔƒewo. Woka wò amewo hlẽ ɖe towo dzi,
ENGLISH: 18 Your shepherds are drowsy, king of Assyria, your heroes are asleep; your people are scattered over the mountains with no one to draw them together.

EWE: Eye ame aɖeke meƒo wo nu ƒu o. 19 Màkpɔ gbɔdzɔe aɖeke le wò fuwɔame la me o. Abi si nèxɔ la maku gbeɖe o. Ame siwo ase nya le ŋuwò la asi akpe ɖe tawò; Elabena ame ka ŋue wò vɔ̃wɔwɔ atraɖii la megblẽ nu le o?”
ENGLISH: 19 There is no healing for your broken bones; your wound is gangrened; all who hear about you will clap their hands over you for over whom has not your vileness taken its course continually?

EWE: Habakuk
ENGLISH: Habakkuk

EWE: 1 Nya si woɖe fia nyagblɔɖila Habakuk le ŋutega me:
ENGLISH: 1 The boding that the prophet Hambakuk beheld.

EWE: 2 ‘Oo Yehowa, va se ɖe ɣekaɣi manɔ ɣlidodo dzi be nàxɔ nam, gake nàgbe esese?
ENGLISH: 2 How long, Jehovah, shall I have been clamoring and you not listen, shall I cry foul play and you not interfere?

EWE: Va se ɖe ɣekaɣi manɔ yɔwòm be nàxɔ nam le ŋutasesẽ ta, evɔ nàgbe nudede eme? 3 Nu ka tae nèna mele nu vlo wɔwɔ teƒe kpɔm?
ENGLISH: 3 why do you show me villainy and look on at mischief, and I am confronted with rapine and outrage, and disputes break out and raise quarrels?

EWE: Eye nu ka tae dzrewɔwɔ kple avuwɔwɔ bɔ?’ 4 Eya ta se la me gbɔdzɔ, Eye wogbe nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔ kura. Elabena ame vɔ̃ɖi ɖe to ɖe ame dzɔdzɔe,
ENGLISH: 4 Therefore religion is numbed, and justice comes out nevermore, because a criminal brings numbers against the one who has right on his side and therefore justice comes out on the wrong track.

EWE: Esia ta nu dzɔdzɔe trɔ gbo. 5 “Miɖe ŋku ɖe dukɔwo dome, miakpɔ nu! Miaƒe nu neku mianɔ nu kpɔm gãa;
ENGLISH: 5 See among the nations, look, be mystified, be mazed: for he is doing a deed in your days that you will not believe when it is told;

EWE: Eye ne wogblɔe na mi hã la, miele edzi xɔ ge ase o. 6 Elabena kpɔ ɖa, manyɔ Kaldeatɔwo, Dukɔ sẽŋuta si tsia klokloklo. Wozɔna toa anyigba ƒe gbadzaƒewo
ENGLISH: 6 for here he is setting in motion the Chaldeans, the truculent and hasty nation that goes through the length and breadth of earth to take possession of abodes that do not belong to it.

EWE: Be woaxɔ nɔƒe siwo menye wo tɔ o la. 7 Ŋɔdzi kple vɔvɔ̃ le wo ŋu.
ENGLISH: 7 It is terrible and formidable; it looks to itself for its laws and its standing;

EWE: Woawo ŋutɔwoe wɔa sewo eye wodia gãnyenye na wo ɖokui. 8 Woƒe sɔwo ƒua du wu lãklẽ,
ENGLISH: 8 and its ponies are swifter than leopards and brisker than evening wolves, and its horsemen come from far, they fly.

EWE: Eye wonyrana wu amegãxi le zã me.
ENGLISH: Like vultures hurrying to eat,

EWE: Wole du dzi abe ale si hɔ̃ dea agba anyi va ƒoa nui ene. 9 Wo katã wova ɖe ŋutasesẽ ŋu.
ENGLISH: 9 it all comes for outrage; their massed faces are toward the east; and it has gathered up slaves like the sand,

EWE: Eye wolɔa aboyomewo abe ke ene. 10 Woɖea alɔme le fiawo ŋu, Eye wokoa amegãwo. Mɔ́ sesẽ ɖe sia ɖe ɖia kokoe na wo;
ENGLISH: 10 while it gibes at kings and takes potentates for its butt; it laughs at every fortification and has piled up earth and taken it,

EWE: Woƒua kpo ɖe eŋu hexɔnɛ. 11 Emegbe wohona dzona abe ya si ƒo va yi la ene, Gake woaɖi fɔ,
ENGLISH: 11 then taken breath and passed on, and made this strength of its own its god.

EWE: 12 Oo Yehowa, ɖe mèli tso gbe aɖe gbe ke oa?
ENGLISH: 12 Are you not from of old, Jehovah?

EWE: Oo nye Mawu, nye Kɔkɔetɔ, mèkuna o.
ENGLISH: God of my devotion, you will not die.

EWE: Oo Yehowa, wòe ɖo wo be woadrɔ̃ ʋɔnu; Nye Agakpe, wòe ɖo wo be woahe to.
ENGLISH: Jehovah, you established him for judgment and planted him as a rock for correction.

EWE: 13 Wò ŋkuwo dza ale gbegbe be màte ŋu anɔ nu gbegblẽ wɔwɔ kpɔm o, Eye màte ŋu anɔ vɔ̃ɖinyenye teƒe kpɔm o. Nu ka tae nèle nu fitifiti wɔlawo kpɔm,
ENGLISH: 13 Why should you, too clean-eyed to see wickedness and unable to look at mischief, look on at faithless men, lie still while a rascal chews up a more honest man,

EWE: Eye nèzia kpi ne ame vɔ̃ɖi mi ame si le dzɔdzɔe wui la? 14 Nu ka tae nèwɔ amegbetɔ abe ƒumelãwo,
ENGLISH: 14 and have made mankind like fish in the sea, like insects without a government?

EWE: Abe atsiaƒumenu gbagbe siwo nu dziɖula aɖeke mele o la ene? 15 Etsɔa ƒu hea nu siawo katã ɖe go.
ENGLISH: 15 he brings them all up with a hook, hauls them in in his net, gathers them in his seine.

EWE: Etsɔa eƒe ɖɔ ɖea wo,
ENGLISH: Therefore he is glad and gay;

EWE: Esia tae wòkpɔa dzidzɔ hetsoa aseye ɖo. 16 Esia tae wòsaa vɔ na eƒe ɖɔ, Eye wòsaa vɔ na eƒe asabu ɖo;
ENGLISH: 16 therefore he sacrifices to his net and burns incense to his seine, because by those his takings are fat and his diet rich;

EWE: Eye nunyiame le eƒe nuɖuɖu me. 17 Ðe wòanɔ ɖɔdada dzia?
ENGLISH: 17 is he therefore to empty his net and be always killing nations unsparingly?

EWE: Habakuk
ENGLISH: Habakkuk

EWE: 2 Matsi tsitre ɖe nye gbetakpɔƒe la, Eye matɔ ɖe kpoƒuƒu la tame. Manɔ ŋudzɔ, ne makpɔ nya si wòagblɔ to dzinye,
ENGLISH: 2 I will stand at my post and station myself on guard and be on the lookout to see what he will say by me and what response I shall make to my reproach.

EWE: Kple nya si magblɔ ne eka mo nam. 2 Eye Yehowa ɖo eŋu nam be: “Ŋlɔ ŋutega la ɖi, eye nàɖee ɖe kpe gbadzɛwo dzi wòadze nyuie,
ENGLISH: 2 And Jehovah answered me and said “Write a vision and set it forth clearly on the tablets to be read swiftly;

EWE: Ale be ame si kɔ gbe dzi le exlẽm la nate ŋu axlẽe bɔbɔe. 3 Elabena azãgbe li na ŋutega la,
ENGLISH: 3 for there is yet a vision for the date, to depose of the end, and it will not lie.

EWE: Ne etsi megbe hã la, nɔ esinu kpɔm! Elabena ele eme va ge kokoko.
ENGLISH: If it delays, wait for it; for come it will, and not be belated.”

EWE: Mahe ɖe megbe o! 4 Kpɔ ame si dana la ɖa; Nu dzɔdzɔe wɔwɔ aɖeke mele eya amea me o.
ENGLISH: 4 Now in the timeserver he takes no satisfaction, but the honest man shall live by his steadfastness;

EWE: Ke ame dzɔdzɔe ya ƒe nuteƒewɔwɔ ana wòanɔ agbe. 5 Esi wain nye ameflula ta la, Ŋutsu dadala maɖo eƒe taɖodzinu gbɔ o. Ekeke eƒe dzodzrowo abe Tsiẽƒe ene; Ele abe ku ene, eye metea ŋu ɖia ƒo o. Ele dukɔwo katã nu ƒom ƒu,
ENGLISH: 5 how much less shall a faithless brute be pleasing, a haughty man, who has distended his appetite like the grave, being like death insatiable, and has gathered in all the nations and swept up all the peoples!

EWE: Eye wòle ƒu ƒom amewo katã na eɖokui. 6 Ðe ame siawo katã mado hamelo ahagblɔ nyamenya atsɔ asi ahama ɖe eŋu oa? Woagblɔ be: ‘Baba na ame si ƒo nu geɖe siwo menye etɔ o la nu ƒu Ɣekaɣi wòayi esia wɔwɔ dzi ase ɖo?
ENGLISH: 6 Shall not all these strike up a lay of him and propound a satire on him, and say “Ha, you who amass for how long? what is not yours, and load yourself up with things you have taken in pawn!

EWE: Baba nɛ, elabena fe ko nyim wòle ɖe edzi! 7 Ðe wò fetɔwo mava do zi ɖeka kpoyi oa? Woatso eye woaʋuʋu wò sesĩe,
ENGLISH: 7 Will not your creditors stand up suddenly and your worriers wake, and you be for their pillaging?

EWE: Eye àzu nuhaha na wo. 8 Esi nèha dukɔ geɖewo ta la, Dukɔwo ƒe susɔeawo katã aha wò, Le ameʋu si nèkɔ ɖi Kple ŋuta si nèsẽ le anyigba la
ENGLISH: 8 Because you have despoiled many nations, all the rest of the peoples shall despoil you, for bloodshed of men and outrage to earth, town and all who live in it.

EWE: Kple du la kpakple emenɔlawo ŋu ta. 9 Baba na ame si dia viɖe ƒoɖi na eƒe aƒe, Ne wòawɔ atɔ ɖe kɔkɔƒe,
ENGLISH: 9 “Ha, you who make hurtful winnings for your house, placing your nest aloft, to come off safe out of the clutch of disaster!

EWE: Ale be wòasi le vɔ̃ nu! 10 Èɖo nu si ahe ŋukpe va wò aƒe dzi la ɖe tame.
ENGLISH: 10 You have contrived shame for your house, maiming many peoples and letting your life be the forfeit;

EWE: Esi nètsrɔ̃ dukɔ geɖewo ta la, èwɔ nu vɔ̃ ɖe ɖokuiwò ŋu. 11 Elabena kpe ado ɣli le gli me,
ENGLISH: 11 for stones will cry out from walls, and joists out of woodwork will back them up.

EWE: Eye daɖedzi axee le xɔtiwo me. 12 Baba na ame si tsɔ ʋukɔkɔɖi le du tsom,
ENGLISH: 12 “Ha, you who build a city by bloodshed and found a town by foul play!”

EWE: Eye wòtsɔ nu madzɔmadzɔ wɔwɔ li ke dui! 13 Kpɔ ɖa!
ENGLISH: 13 (Is not that from Jehovah of Armies?)

EWE: Ðe menye aʋakɔwo ƒe Yehowa gbɔe wòtso be dukɔwo nadze agbagba dzodzro hena dzo,
ENGLISH: “And peoples toil to feed fire, and folk upon folk spends itself bootlessly.”

EWE: Eye dukɔwo naku kutri dzodzro oa? 14 Elabena Yehowa ƒe ŋutikɔkɔe ŋuti sidzedze axɔ anyigba la dzi,
ENGLISH: 14 (For the earth shall be full of knowledge of Jehovah’s glory like water that covers a sea.)

EWE: Abe ale si tsi yɔ atsiaƒu mee ene. 15 Baba na ame si na nane ehavi wòno Eye wòtsɔ dziku kple dɔmedzoe kpe ɖe eŋu be wòamu,
ENGLISH: 15 “Ha, you who have your friend drink out of your bowl and your bag, and befuddle him too, in order to look at their nudity!

EWE: Ne wòakpɔ eƒe ama! 16 Vlododo aɖi ƒo na wò ɖe bubu teƒe. Wò hã noe, ne nàklo nu le wò aʋamatsomatso dzi. Kplu si le Yehowa ƒe nuɖusi me la atrɔ ava gbɔwò,
ENGLISH: 16 You are fuller loaded with ignominy than with glory; drink yourself and show off your uncircumcised body; the cup in Jehovah’s right hand shall come round to you, and shabbiness come over your glory.

EWE: Eye ŋukpe atsyɔ wò bubu dzi; 17 Elabena ŋuta si nèsẽ le Lebanon ŋu, Kple wò nu gbegblẽ si do ŋɔdzi na lãwo la ava dziwò, Le ameʋu si nèkɔ ɖi Kple ŋuta si nèsẽ le anyigba la
ENGLISH: 17 For the outrage to Lebanon shall cover you, and the havoc of beasts shall dismay you, for bloodshed of men and outrage to earth, town and all who live in it.”

EWE: Kple du la kpakple emenɔlawo ŋu la ta. 18 Viɖe kae le nu kpakpɛ ŋu Hafi ekpala kpae, Viɖe kae le galegba kple alakpanufiala la ŋu, Hafi ewɔla ɖoa ŋu ɖe eŋu,
ENGLISH: 18 Of what use is a statue that its sculptor should have carved it, a bronze and a lying oracle that its modeler should have put his confidence in it, so as to make dumb trumperies?

EWE: Eye wòwɔa mawu maɖinu siwo meƒoa nu o? 19 Baba na ame si le gbɔgblɔm na ati be, “Nyɔ!” Alo na kpe maƒonu be, “Fɔ!
ENGLISH: 19 Ha, you who say to wood “Wake up, stir yourself!” of silent stone “That will give instructions”!

EWE: Fia nu mí”! Kpɔ ɖa, wofa sika kple klosalo ɖe eŋu,
ENGLISH: There is that cased in gold and silver, with no soul within it.

EWE: Ke gbɔgbɔ kui ɖeka hã mele eme o. 20 Ke Yehowa le eƒe gbedoxɔ kɔkɔe la me.
ENGLISH: 20 But Jehovah is in his holy temple: silence before him, all the earth!

EWE: Habakuk
ENGLISH: Habakkuk

EWE: 3 Nyagblɔɖila Habakuk ƒe gbedodoɖa si nye konyifaha:
ENGLISH: 3 (A prayer of the prophet Hambakuk in dithyrambics.)

EWE: 2 Oo Yehowa, mese nya le ŋuwò. Oo Yehowa, wò dɔwɔwɔ na vɔvɔ̃ ɖom. Gbɔ agbe wò dɔwɔwɔ le ƒeawo me! Ðee fia le ƒeawo me.
ENGLISH: 2 Jehovah, I have heard your story, have feared, Jehovah, at your dealing; As years draw on bring it to life, as years draw on making it known, fiercely remembering tenderness.

EWE: Ðo ŋui nàkpɔ nublanui le wò dzikudoɣi. 3 Mawu tso Teman va,
ENGLISH: 3 God is coming from Teman, the Holy from the highlands of Paran.

EWE: (Sela) Eƒe bubu xɔ dziƒowo keŋ; Eye eƒe kafukafu yɔ anyigba dzi taŋ.
ENGLISH: (Selah) His majesty covers the sky and the earth is full of his praise,

EWE: 4 Eƒe keklẽ le abe ɣe ƒe keklẽ ene. Keklẽ eve do tso eƒe asi me,
ENGLISH: 4 And there is under him a radiance like fire, he has beams of light at his side, and there is the hiding of his power.

EWE: Afi si eƒe ŋusẽ be ɖo. 5 Dɔvɔ̃ dze eŋgɔ,
ENGLISH: 5 Before him goes pestilence, and back of him firebolts go out.

EWE: Eye asrãdɔ sesẽ le eƒe afɔɖeɖewo yome. 6 Etɔ ɖi heʋuʋu anyigba la. Ekpɔ nu, eye wòna dukɔwo dzo nyanyanya. Blematowo kaka keŋkeŋ, Eye gbe aɖe gbe togbɛwo ŋe dze eme.
ENGLISH: 6 He halts, and earth trembles; He sees, and nations flinch; And primeval mountains burst, immemorial hills stoop,

EWE: Aleae eƒe mɔwo le tso keke blemablema ke. 7 Mekpɔ Kusan ƒe agbadɔwo le xaxa me.
ENGLISH: 7 The packtrains of ‘Us are alarmed, the caravans of Ishbak are dismayed, The homes of Cushan are disquieted, the tents of the Midianite country.

EWE: Midian-nyigba ƒe agbadɔvɔwo dzo nyanyanya. 8 Oo Yehowa, tɔsisiwo ŋue dzi le kuwòm helĩhelĩ ɖoa, Tɔsisiwo ŋuea? Alo atsiaƒu ŋue nèdo dɔmedzoe ɖoa? Elabena èdo wò sɔwo;
ENGLISH: 8 Are you angry with the rivers, Jehovah, or is your wrath against the sea, That you are riding your ponies, your victory-bringing chariot,

EWE: Wò tasiaɖamwo ɖu aʋa dzi. 9 Èɖe wò dati ɖe go hena wòsɔ gbe.
ENGLISH: 9 With your bow stripped bare, your quiver crammed with shafts?

EWE: Woka atam ɖe wò atikplɔawo ŋu.
ENGLISH: [Selah] Earth splits into rivers,

EWE: Ètsɔ tɔsisiwo ma anyigba lae. 10 Towo kpɔ wò, eye wodzo kpekpekpe le vevesese me. Tsi gã dza hesi va yi. Tsi goglo la ɖe gbe.
ENGLISH: 10 mountains have seen you, they writhe, Clouds pelt down water, the deep utters its voice, The sun forgets its lofty radiance,

EWE: Eye wòdo eƒe alɔwo ɖe dzi. 11 Ɣe kple ɣleti tɔ ɖe wo nɔƒe le dziƒo ɖaa. Wò aŋutrɔwo lũ ʋɔ abe kekeli ene.
ENGLISH: 11 the moon stands still in its lodge, At the light of your arrows as they go, at the radiant flash of your spear;

EWE: 12 Èzɔ to anyigba la dzi le dɔmedzoe helĩhelĩ me.
ENGLISH: 12 In hostility you tread earth, in anger you trample nations.

EWE: Èfanya dukɔwo le dziku me. 13 Èho be nàxɔ na wò dukɔ, be nàɖe wò amesiamina la. Ègbã ame vɔ̃ɖi ƒe aƒe la ƒe tatɔ gudugudu. Etsi ƒeƒle tso gɔmeɖoanyi dzi va se ɖe etame.
ENGLISH: 13 You have gone out for the succor of your people, to give victory to your anointed; You have shattered head from wicked man’s house, baring foundation to neck; (Selah)

EWE: (Sela) 14 Ètsɔ eya ŋutɔ ƒe aʋawɔnuwo ŋɔ ta na eƒe aʋawɔlawo Esi wonyè zi va be yewoakam ahlẽ. Wotso aseye be yewoavuvu wɔnamanɔŋutɔ la le bebeme.
ENGLISH: 14 You have pierced with his shafts the heads of his warriors coming tempestuously to scatter me, Their exultation as if to eat up a wretch in concealment.

EWE: 15 Ètsɔ wò sɔwo to atsiaƒu la me,
ENGLISH: 15 You have trod your ponies in the sea the clay of great waters.

EWE: To tɔ gã gbanaa dzeagbowo me. 16 Mesee, eye nye lãme ƒo; Esi mese nyaa la, nye nuyiwo nɔ ƒoƒom. Nyunyɔ ɖo nye ƒuwo me; Nye afɔwo nɔ ƒoƒom le tenye. Ke hã, menɔ anyi kpoo lala xaxagbe la,
ENGLISH: 16 I heard, and my body quivered, my lips purred aloud; Decay comes into my bones, my insteps quiver under me, I moan at a day of distress to come for a nation that raids us.

EWE: Elabena egbɔna dukɔ siwo tso ɖe mía ŋu la dzi. 17 Togbɔ be gboti maƒo se o, Eye wainkawo matse o; Togbɔ be amiti mawɔ o, Eye agblewo mana nuɖuɖu o; Togbɔ be alẽwo avɔ keŋ le kpo me,
ENGLISH: 17 For fig-trees are bearing no fruit and nothing grows on the grapevine, Olive-trees’ work is disappointing and terraces are making no food, Sheep have disappeared from fold and there are no cattle in the stalls.

EWE: Eye nyi aɖeke manɔ nyikpowo me o hã la; 18 Nye ya matso aseye ɖe Yehowa ŋu;
ENGLISH: 18 But I will glory in Jehovah, I will exult in my God of salvation;

EWE: Makpɔ dzidzɔ ɖe nye xɔname ƒe Mawu la ŋu. 19 Aƒetɔ Dziɖulagã Yehowae nye nye ŋusẽ; Ana nye afɔwo nanɔ abe zinɔ tɔ ene, Eye wòana mazɔ le kɔkɔƒewo.
ENGLISH: 19 The Lord Jehovah is my vigor, and makes my feet like a wild doe’s and makes me tread the heights. (of the Director; with string accompaniment.)

EWE: Zefaniya
ENGLISH: Zephaniah

EWE: 1 Esiae nye Yehowa ƒe gbe si va na Zefaniya, si nye Kusi vi, Gedaliya vi, Amariya vi, Hizkiya vi, le Yuda-fia Yosiya, Amon vi, ŋɔli:
ENGLISH: 1 Jehovah’s word which came to Sephaniah the son of Cushi the son of Gedaliah the son of Amariah the son of Hezekiah in the time of Josiah the son of Amon, king of Judah.

EWE: 2 Yehowa be, “Matsrɔ̃ nu sia nu ɖa le anyigba la dzi keŋkeŋ.
ENGLISH: 2 I will take off everything off the face of the earth, quoth Jehovah:

EWE: 3 Matsrɔ̃ amewo kple lãwo siaa. Matsrɔ̃ dziƒoxe dzodzoewo kple ƒumelãwo, Maɖe nuɖianuwo ɖa eye matsrɔ̃ ame vɔ̃ɖiwo;
ENGLISH: 3 I will take off man and beast, I will take off the birds of the air and the fish of the sea, and the stumbling-blocks with the wicked, and I will extirpate mankind off the face of the earth, quoth Jehovah.

EWE: Maɖe amegbetɔwo ɖa le anyigba la dzi,” Yehowa ye gblɔe. 4 “Mado nye asi ɖa ɖe Yuda Kple Yerusalem nɔlawo katã ŋu, Eye maɖe nu siwo susɔ na Baal la dometɔ ɖe sia ɖe ɖa,
ENGLISH: 4 And I will stretch out my hand over Judah and over all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and exterminate from this place the kin of the Baal and the kith of the komers,

EWE: Matutu dutamawuwo ƒe nunɔlawo ŋkɔ ɖa, eye matsrɔ̃ alakpanunɔlawo le teƒe sia; 5 Matsrɔ̃ ame siwo dea ta agu na dziƒonuwo le xɔwo tame,
ENGLISH: 5 and those who do reverence on the roof to the legions of the sky, and those who do reverence to Jehovah and swear by Malcam,

EWE: Gake wogakaa atam na Malkam hã; 6 Matsrɔ̃ ame siwo trɔ le Yehowa yome,
ENGLISH: 6 and those who fall back from following Jehovah and those who have not gone looking for Jehovah nor resorted to him.

EWE: Kple ame siwo medi Yehowa yome mɔ alo bia eta se o.” 7 Mizi ɖoɖoe le Aƒetɔ Dziɖulagã Yehowa ŋkume, elabena Yehowa ƒe ŋkeke la tu aƒe.
ENGLISH: 7 Silence because of the Lord Jehovah, because Jehovah’s day is near; because Jehovah has prepared for a sacrifice, has hallowed his guests.

EWE: Yehowa dzra vɔsa ɖo, eye wòkɔ ame siwo wòkpe la ŋu. 8 “Ava eme le Yehowa ƒe vɔsagbe la be, matso ɖe amegãwo,
ENGLISH: 8 And on the day of Jehovah’s sacrifice I will punish the generals and the royal family and all that wear foreign clothing,

EWE: Fiaviwo kple ame siwo katã doa dutatɔwo ƒe awu la ŋu. 9 Gbe ma gbe la, matso ɖe ame siwo katã liana yia kpui la dzi,
ENGLISH: 9 and I will punish on that day everyone who leaps over a threshold, those who fill their master’s house with outrage and fraud.

EWE: Ame siwo tsɔa ŋutasesẽ kple amebeble yɔa woƒe aƒetɔwo ƒe xɔwo taŋ la ŋu. 10 Gbe ma gbe ɣli aɖi tso Tɔmelãgbo la nu, Asiƒunu aɖi tso du la ƒe Akpa Evelia,
ENGLISH: 10 And on that day, quoth Jehovah, there shall be the sound of an outcry from the fish gate and a howling from the second quarter and a great crashing from the hills.

EWE: Yehowa ye gblɔe. 11 “Mi Maktes nɔlawo, mifa avi sesĩe, Elabena wotsrɔ̃ asitsalawo katã;
ENGLISH: 11 Howl, inhabitants of the hollow, because all the people of Canaan are cut off; all those who were laden with silver are exterminated.

EWE: Woɖe klosalodalawo katã ɖa. 12 Ɣemaɣi la, matsɔ akaɖi atsa le Yerusalem tsitotsito, Eye mabia akɔnta ame siwo ɖe dzi ɖi bɔkɔɔ hele gbɔgblɔm le woƒe dzi me be, ‘Yehowa mele nyui alo vɔ̃ wɔ ge o.’ 13 Woaha woƒe kesinɔnuwo, eye woƒe aƒewo azu aƒedo. Woatu xɔ, ke womanɔ wo me o;
